name: University of Alabama in Huntsville
reviews: ['Great university to attend and gain knowledge and real world experience in the field of your choice. Beautiful campus with many parking. My cousin attended here and got her degree in Communications. She says the program (her professors) prepared her for workforce and made her learning experience a pleasant one. She credits her academic advisors for helping her with internships and job placement. I also remember her talking about how U of Alabama Huntsville helped her come out her shell to meet nice people from all backgrounds who have become lifelong friends. This a great university with rice history to find your true calling in the world. A+', 'This college is a hidden gem here in North Alabama. The area is beautiful. The campus is nice and clean everywhere. Constant construction and continued growth should be the norm for this campus for several years to come. My money and my kid goes to UAH. GO CHARGERS!!!!', "The overall atmosphere is toxic among students and professors alike. There is favoritism, backstabbing, unhealthy competition, false accusations, cliquey behavior, and an overall sense of disgust for anyone who doesn't fit their culture. There is also a lot of discrimination. Don't expect title IX to protect you here. Also don't expect the ADA to protect you either. Stay far away.", "Advising is horrible if your in engineering. Not very accommodating for students that focus better on a one on one meeting than back and forth emails that take buisness days to get back to. If the issue is too many students wants one on one advising, just hire more advisors, you're a big university, do better for your students and their future. We want guidance not more confusion on top of all our studies.", 'UAH has gone above and beyond for me when I needed help. I have loved all my professors and my advisor. As a nontraditional student, I was a little intimidated coming here from Calhoun, but I am so glad I chose UAH to finish my English degree. It’s a STEM-heavy school, yes, but don’t discount the College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences—you will have a great support system over there if you choose to go that route. I am going to law school next year, and thanks to the people at UAH, they made that a possibility for me. I’m graduating in December and I will be a very proud alumni. Go Chargers 💙🐴']

name: The University of Alabama
reviews: ["Beautiful campus full of people who genuinely wanted to be there. We visited the Engineering school and it's very impressive with a broad array of research labs and facilities for students clubs.", "Beautiful campus. Grounds and buildings well maintained. We went into several different halls and such. Very nice spaces. While I wish we had caught his name, a professor from the Engineering school stopped by our table at the Furg - realizing we were there for student orientation, he asked if we had any questions.  He sure didn't have to, but really impressed me that he thought to spend a few minutes with us.", "I have been to this campus twice now! I stayed at the on-campus hotel both times and the amenities were great. I also really appreciated all the signage on the campus. I'm a career readiness speaker and when I travel somewhere, I often don't know where to go. This campus has AWESOME signage!", 'Absolutely appalled by the history tied to this institution.\nWhat happened with the syphilis experiments conducted in Alabama was one of the most inhumane, unethical acts ever done under the name of “research.” Human lives were treated as disposable, and the suffering of innocent people was ignored for decades. It’s shameful that such a tragedy was ever associated with a place of learning. A university should stand for truth, compassion, and ethics — not exploitation. The fact that this even happened is horrifying. Institutions involved in such acts should have been held fully accountable and permanently shut down.', 'The University of Alabama (UA), located in Tuscaloosa, is a prestigious public research university known for its strong academic programs, vibrant campus life, and storied traditions. Established in 1831, UA offers a wide range of undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs across disciplines such as business, engineering, law, education, and the sciences.']

name: Central Alabama Community College
reviews:
['Played Pickleball and watched grandbabies.. The place was nice and clean. Very quiet..', 'Graduated in 2013 still in 2024 have not received my diploma (that I paid for) and I have tried to get it multiple times and was told "well organizations will look at your transcripts anyway". Very disorganized and most office workers aren't willing to do anything for you. My transcripts also got messed up somehow and now after 2 overseas deployments trying to go back to school has become a nightmare!!', "Professors were amazing!! I'd give the professors a 5 star review if I could. The staff tried to be helpful, most the time, but they never answered their phone calls. I was mostly left on my own to figure out things. I also hated that the book store was online, and so was CACC's merch store, and you had to order within a certain timeframe. No  cafeteria, so I had to eat out all the time, which sucked after awhile. There was no social life at this community college, not even by a little. This college didn't have much to offer for me except passing basic courses. I wish this college had more of a social life, especially. I felt very lonely at this college, and no student deserves to feel that way in college.", 'This place shouldn't even be called a school. They have caused me so much suffering the last few years. I got a loan to go here, and it was a huge mistake. I'm just now getting it paid off, even though I dropped out 6 months in. Im probably going to have to get a lawyer to get the rest on my money back. Half of my so called "professors" were extreamly rude, refused to help me with anything. Eventhough I was paying 500 dollars for the class I felt very unwelcome. The final straw is when I had a sprained ankle, and I pulled up next to the door, to literally go 30 feet to drop a paper off on a desk, in the 30 seconds of doing it, a fat rent a cop is flying across the parking lot, to cut me off, and illegally detain me and give me a ticket. Literally parked there for less then one minute. I could not deal with this usurpitation, it took everything I had not to break that punks neck.

If you are a young man or women, and you are unsure about what you should do in your life. Don't let people pressure you into going to college. Take a year or two off, and work if you need too. College cost a ridiculously large amount of money, because the government basically guarantees it to anyone who wants to go. Make sure you are on a path to a successful and fulfilling career. It took me 5 years in the real world to pay back a 5000 dollar loan. If you are going to college. You better be sure that you WILL be able to get a good job, making in excess of 36,000 a year, or you will not be able to afford you loan.

There are also much better colleges and trade schools you can go to. Dont waste your money on this place.', 'Very nice for a small college']

name: Auburn University at Montgomery
reviews: ['At first AUM was a dream, as time went on it became so difficult to even feel welcomed there anymore. You can have a married couple living together on campus but oh no once a engaged couple tries to it’s a problem, you can’t have opposite gender sleepovers, can’t smoke when you’re above the age, can’t drink if you have an underage roommate, when everyone breaks those rules if you’re not the best known person on campus it’s a living hell, let’s not forget if you have a problem with a roommate and you report it you’re immediately the problem 🤦🏻\u200d♀️ this campus is the worse Montgomery campus you could choose. name: South University-Montgomery
reviews: ['The staff at South University Montgomery campus are nothing short of amazing, they are so kind and always looking for a way to help the students. When my grandma passed they sent me a card with well wishes and it was really  the sweetest thing ever. I’m so sad I have to go. They are so patient and supportive, I would definitely recommend this campus to any aspiring students out there who’s looking for a community who cares about your education just as much as you.', "There is a high turnover rate with the staff so it seems as if the academic advisors and teachers are always changing. Furthermore,  financial aide staff is not helpful. They are not knowledgeable about any topics. The supervisor is rude and only has one person working under her who doesn't know much. The classes are good though and aren't too big which allows for more one on one instruction. If they had better staff working in Financial aide then I would give them 4 stars.", "Absolutely loved SUM and all of the staff and teachers I had the pleasure of working with! Got my bachelor's in business and was successful due to all of the one on one assistance and encouragement I received! Though expensive, I highly recommend them, especially for older adults who are looking for a small classroom setting. Veteran and financial aid assistance is also available...", "The main reason I attended this college was because with my major (criminal justice), an internship was included in the program. I was looking forward to having some hands-on experience & possibly a foot in the door. Unfortunately, they weren't giving internships at the time not long before I graduated. If I'd known that, I never would've attended this expensive school!", 'This is the worst school that I\'ve attended. During the first quarter in nursing school, I had a teacher that didn\'t teach us anything! The whole class thought that she just didn\'t care because at the end of the school quarter, she left. There were only two great instructors in the whole nursing program and they left. The staff members in the office always said that we were welcomed to come talk to them about anything  but we (my cohort) didn\'t know who to trust. After exams, our grades would get out to other cohorts by an instructor that wasn\'t even teaching the class. I had a situation that I couldn\'t help and I was told that I couldn\'t attend clinical for that day and to write a 10 page paper while several of the others got away with it. When I had a meeting about it, the program director went off subject and started looking at my past grades and said that he was doing that to everyone. That was a lie. He came off very prejudiced to me. I saw another review saying and that he talked down on students and I agree 100%. He\'s racist. I was told by an instructor to my face that the people in the office were trying to get people like me ("Black") out of the program and I believed her. I also had another problem on an exam about which race of people were more likely to get sickle cell. The instructor said with me being "black", I should have gotten that question correct. It was very offensive. Racist! The staff is very unprofessional and nothing is kept confidential. Teachers were changing answers on exams and they chose who they wanted to let through in the program. Policy requires students to get full clinical hours in order to graduate. False! People graduated without full clinical hours. People even got by with being late to several clinicals. The dean of the school isn\'t any help. The staff sticks together. They don\'t care about the students. They only care about the money and sticking together. Tuition is very expensive so I wouldn\'t waste my time or money. Trust the reviews that you read because I wished I would have. I would have never attended this school. Like I said, they pick and choose who they let through. Everyone is not treated equally. People don\'t know the half of everything you have to deal with in the nursing program. They (staff) always get defensive when you speak up and try to tell them how you feel about certain things in the program. If you do decide to go to this school, RECORD meetings and everything for proof. It\'s sad to say that you have to do that, but just giving you all a warning. If there is a problem that needs to be resolved, speak up as a CLASS. Don\'t leave anyone hanging. People were scared to speak on things because they knew how the staff was and thought that they would do something sneaky. I wrote this review because several people have asked me about this school, so here you go.']

name: Coastal Alabama Community College
reviews:
["I went there today to attend the #URKEYS2DRV Teen Driver Summit. This was supported by State Farm, Drive Safe Alabama, ASF Foundation, Safe Kids Alabama, Children's of Alabama, ALDOT, ABC Board, and more! There were so many wonderful groups there, and the event was absolutely incredible! Thank you so much to everyone invoked and a huge Thank You to Coastal Alabama Community College in Bay Minette for hosting sunch an amazing event for our soon to be and new to driving kids!", 'My daughter went here. Great campuses and community!', 'This is an excellent educational institution with a caring, student driven faculty. I met with the president today and he really impressed me. The instructors are all dedicated to student success.', 'I went here back in the early 1990s when it was known as “Faulkner State Community College”, mainly to save money.  In all honesty, I didn’t have too good of an experience and regarded Faulkner as just a glorified high school but what made things worse was when I transferred to the University of South Alabama I lost a lot of credits, putting me back to being a freshman and delaying my graduating for almost a year!

Well folks, I’m here to tell you in the 30 years since that happened absolutely nothing has changed about that place except the name. My daughter went to Coastal and is now finishing her nursing degree at South Alabama.  30 years is a long time for things to change…I figured Coastal would have gotten with the times and when you go to transfer EVERYTHING should transfer, especially in state. Like my situation back then she lost about a year’s worth of credits delaying her graduating by a year.

That’s OK because there will not be a third time! My youngest daughter was thinking about going to Coastal but after what we experienced 30 years apart from one another, the brakes were slammed on that! She is now working on her degree at South Alabama where she doesn’t have to worry about losing credits. I should have heeded my mother’s advice when she told me a long time ago “fool me once shame on you, fool me twice shame on me” and I have been kicking myself since.  Aside from that, I was not surprised to learn other people had gone here, transferred to other colleges in state only to lose credits which calls in the question is Coastal really a community college or just a place where money gets laundered!?

My advice to anyone, if you go to Coastal do so at your own risk! Aside from that, when my daughter went to have her credits transferred Coastal seemed like it was nothing but organized chaos leaving her highly frustrated because nobody over there in administration seemed to know what was going on. When you finally did talk to someone, they constantly dragged their feet And did not take into consideration, the time was taking and things needed to be done right away.  That certainly isn’t the case at the University of South Alabama where when you call there you get an answer right away and not give a runaround  Between me, and my oldest daughter, we have been successful in turning upwards of 15 people away from Coastal after they learned of our experience and will continue to share our story with future prospective students.

Bottom line: Unless you have time to waste and money to burn avoid Coastal Alabama Community College like the plague or you’ll be sorry! 👎👎', 'Unassuming looking building with great people inside!!! Went student camp once it was awesome!!! Every time I’ve been here I learned about Jesus and had an amazing time']

name: Faulkner University
reviews:
['The Christian church attaches great importance to reconciliation, emphasizing the reconciliation between man and God, and between man and the world. In Christ the Mediator we can mend broken relationships, but now of course we must mend the scarred nature and mend the broken relationship between man and nature. Therefore, the church reminds mankind not only to cherish all things, but also to be kind to all things.
They kicked out our Mexican 🇲🇽 restaurant and quickly built an American fried chicken fast food with no peace talks and no plans to let us go and destroy the harmonious coexistence of nature.', 'I’ve had a really great experience with Faulkner University so far, and I wanted to share it. One of the standout things for me has been how responsive and personable everyone is. If I need anything at all, I can just pick up the phone, and they connect me right away to someone who actually knows my case and what I’m working on. It’s got this small-town feel in the best possible way. Everything I’ve needed has been handled quickly and smoothly, and it’s been a really nice experience so far. I’ll definitely update more as I go along, but for now, I just wanted to say how appreciative I am of their approach!', 'I’m very disappointed with the Graduation Department at Faulkner University. I am a dedicated student with only four classes left to earn my BA in Business Management, and I’ve worked extremely hard to get to this point. Unfortunately, I missed the graduation conferral deadline because I didn’t check my student email regularly. I understand that they sent 2–3 reminder emails with no phone calls, but as I explained, I am a full-time student, full-time business owner, active duty military member, and full-time family man.

My schedule is beyond demanding, and I had hoped the university would show some understanding and flexibility given my circumstances. Not to mention, I just got back from my deployment in South Korea.
Instead, I was told there was nothing they could do to help me, which feels discouraging after years of commitment to this institution. I wish Faulkner’s Graduation Department would take a more student-centered approach and work with individuals who are genuinely trying to complete their degree but face unique time constraints. A little empathy and willingness to make an exception would go a long way in supporting hardworking students like myself.', 'The parking lot had puddles, and for many days after the rain, there was a lot of standing water. The construction site inside was filthy, with white foam particles flying everywhere, metal fences lying on the ground, and a huge trash can.', 'On a college tour. Loved the total experience! Enjoyed meeting the staff and students who were all so welcoming.  Enjoyed the chapel service. And appreciated the attention to detail that the counselors showed regarding the info shared.  Would be proud to have my child attend.']

name: George C Wallace State Community College-Hanceville
reviews:
["Came down for the high school games for regional state basketball tournament. The gym is very nice and clean. Seats comfortably. Food choices seem good. My suggestions for improvement is definitely have way better sigage on the main roads and college roads where to turn and proceed to get to the gym. A small printer sign 1 foot off the ground does not cut it. Large eye level to drivers is required in ALL DIRECTIONS to help people to find it. I was disappointed you had temporary ticket booths to charge for parking on a public funded college. Tax dollars has already paid for for the parking and yet you charge again over and over for people to park with no passes out when in fact multiple teams from sane school plays at different times. That should not happen. I do like you accept cash for admission because doing go fan app only is totally crap to make people who do not have smart phones not be able to attend public sporting events. That's a class action law suit coming to force people to use go fan only. As a graduate of Wallce State... I was disappointed in these things and hope the campus administration corrects this for next time.", 'Wallace State Community College has completely changed my life through its welding program. When I enrolled, I was looking for a skill that could provide stability and long-term career opportunities. What I found was much more than that. I found structure, discipline, confidence, and a clear direction for my future.

The welding program at Wallace State is one of the best decisions I have ever made. The instructors truly care about their students and push us to be our best every single day. They do not just teach us how to weld — they teach us how to read blueprints, understand safety standards, follow proper procedures, and take pride in our craftsmanship. I have learned MIG, FCAW, TIG, and other advanced welding techniques that prepared me for real-world work environments.

One of the most impressive things about Wallace State’s welding program is its one hundred percent job placement rate. That shows how respected the program is in the industry. Employers know that when they hire a Wallace State graduate, they are getting someone who is trained, skilled, and ready to work. That reputation means everything.

Since starting here, I have gained certifications, improved my technical skills, and developed a stronger work ethic. The hands-on training environment allows students to practice daily and build confidence in their abilities. I love it here because I can see myself growing. Every week I am better than I was before.

Wallace State did more than teach me welding and it also changed my life around. It gave me direction, purpose, and opportunities I did not have before. I am proud to be part of this program, and I am grateful for everything it has taught me.

Sincerely,
Zarrius Greer', 'Great day and accomplishment for my daughter  Addison  Nolen Garnett she received her pinning  after all the  hard work and studies at WALLACE STATE  as a Registered Nurse  they are there to help you  achieve your dreams .', "A greedy company run just like any other. They don't care about their students, only money. They charged me for a class I wasn't even enrolled in and say I need proof I wasn't in the class as if my lack of attendance isnt proof, so I will be transferring to a more honorable provider of education. The staff is rude. This is not the first college I have attended and honestly Im shocked by how they treat their students compared to where I went before. Ill take my tuition elsewhere.", "This is my Freshmen year. I've been taking online courses. Today was my 1st ever visit to campus. Everyone I got to meet was very friendly and helpful. I'll have an on campus course in the Spring."]

name: George C Wallace State Community College-Selma
reviews: ["You're more likely to get a 5 star robbery attempt than a decent education here.\n\nBut the cafeteria has good food though.", "Not the place for me but nothing but high marks for the Nursing Program. The staff is on point and demand nothing but the best from their students. They take their responsibility of training future healthcare workers seriously and want to make sure students are fully prepared to meet and exceed the needs of their patients. If you are not prepared or don't have time to study, don't even apply!", "Wallace is a great place to get your basics. I wish they offered a wider variety of classes, but it is on par for what you'd expect at any community college. They offer many programs to help the community as well.", "I'm not normally one to get hung up on names, but are you serious?!  A community college in Selma, Alabama, birthplace in earnest of the American Civil Rights movement, named after George C. Wallace?!", 'Wallace Selma Nursing Program is not as good as it was 5 years ago, the RN & LPN Program is so unorganized and unprofessional, the staff doesn’t care about the students. The exams are so inaccurate and not passable. If you really want to be a Nurse don’t go to Wallace Selma.']

name: Herzing University-Birmingham
reviews: ['Wow!!! I honestly don’t know where to start! Mr. Aundra Jones is God sent! You can tell he really cares about his students! He spoke very clearly about the school, course requirements, etc! I had such a great experience with him. He is very knowledgeable and supportive throughout the entire enrollment process. What could’ve been a stressful process wasn’t at all! It was so smooth and I’m so looking forward to starting school and having him in my corner! I appreciate his willingness to help me with anything. He answered all my questions and made sure I had a clear understanding of everything. I appreciate his professionalism and dedication to helping me succeed! Thank you Mr. Jones! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!! If I could’ve gave more stars, I would have!', 'It’s a must that I express my gratitude for Hope Ball, the enrollment coordinator at Herzing University. She has went over and beyond to assist me with my educational goals at Herzing. Sometimes I felt like I didn’t know who to call or contact and I was able to contact her and get things handled. If you’re seeking enrollment or need help, don’t hesitate to reach out and request Ms. Hope Ball, she’s patient, empathetic and supportive.', 'The admissions and re-entry process is great. A huge thank you to my re- entry advisor  Taylor Garza on helping me get back into Herzing. It was a smooth and easy process and she was there every step of the way. Thank you Taylor!', 'I have a wonderful experience getting enrolled into my LPN class. Stacie Perkins Admission Advisors was so helpful from the beginning and provided my with everything I need to get me prepared for my TEAS test and keep encouraging me even when I thought I wasn’t going to do well and keep in touch all the way up to orientation. Max my Enrollment Coordinator was also very helpful when I had questions with portal issues and class schedules. ☺️', 'The staff at Herzing University has been nothing lees than amazing.  Brittany Rivers did a phenomenal job in helping me to navigate the enrollment process.  She executed a seamless warm handover to Student Accounts.  Kenneth Howard walked me through the student portal and ensured I understood how to navigate the system. He took time to ensure all of my prerequisites were satisfied.  Matthew Miller was a tremendous help in acquiring funding for me.  The staff has presented a wonderful and lasting impression on me.  Great job Herzing!']

name: Huntingdon College
reviews: ['The instructors are great. The atmosphere in general is positive. However, that ends at the business office. The business office systems are terrible and appear to be outdated. They want you to go by paper billing but refer back to their online system. The staff does not communicate well via writing or even verbal. There are a few individuals that have a terrible attitude and feel like they can speak condescending towards their student because they are young and naive. They’re adamant about collecting fees even though their system contradicts one another. We specifically ruled out schools that had bad reviews with their business office. Unfortunately, it’s difficult to make changes once your child has started at an institution. If you plan to pay for your child’s education without student loans, you may want to rethink this place and explore other colleges. I’m definitely thinking of that at this point…', 'Watched a football game here tonight (a friend\'s daughter is in the marching band.) For a relatively small college, the football field is "cozy." They could stand to add a few more bleachers on the visitor\'s side, and the concessions is cash-only (I had no cash 🙄). Having said that, it was a nice family friendly atmosphere.', 'My daughter loves the atmosphere of the campus and has made it her top 2 choice for continuing her athletics and education!', 'Beautiful Campus with friendly students and staff!', "My daughter is just getting started there, but I have to say that the whole experience is about as painless as it gets. Well, besides the cost. But college expensive everywhere. The campus is beautifully and the staff is outstanding! If it turns out to not be such a great experience after four years, I'll update this review. If you you're considering it, go check it out in person, meet the staff, see the campus."]

name: Heritage Christian University
reviews: ['One of the best places to get a degree in biblical studies and train for local ministry. HCU offers a wide variety of options for minors (undergraduate) and emphases (graduate). In addition, the core curriculum in both the graduate and undergraduate are balanced and challenging. You can get a quality degree both on-campus and via distance learning. This wonderful university will bless you in many ways should you choose to take or audit classes.', 'I graduated from HCU in 2021 with a Bachelor’s in Biblical Studies and loved the experience so much because of the knowledge, concern, and Christian love of the professors and administrators that I am now working toward a Master of Divinity with emphasis in Biblical Interpretation and Theology.', "I am a graduate of HCU, Class of 1998, and would highly recommend HCU to anyone wishing to strengthen their Bible knowledge. To be honest,  not sure what difficulties/lackings or other things that Anna Adams is referring to in her review. I have come back after 17 years to work with HCU and continue my education because they are VERY Biblically sound. Sure, some classes use books not published by members of the church of Christ, but since when does the church of Christ have the corner on the truth, historical writings, or Biblical interpretation.  Any good university is going to use the resources available to properly educate it's students. Same with Faulkner, Harding, Freed-Hardeman, and other respected brotherhood universities. Also, the student-staff relationships are beyond compare, and very enriching. All activities and devotionals are open to both staff and students alike. Nothing is done here unless it would be pleasing to the Lord. In my opinion, if you want a sound, Biblical, Bible based education recognized around the world, then HCU is the place. I highly recommend it for people of all ages. Come and see for yourself!", "My daughter got a top rate education here.  I am so proud of her.  Funny thing when her mom died in a horrible hand gliding accident she took to Jesus like a duck to a pond.  Whereas my faith is as dead as a cold fish.\nThe schools Indoctrination of faith is a 10 out of 10.  My daughter's relationship with her divine pretend friend is borderline fanatical now.\nOverall, a great affordable education with maybe a tad too much Jesus.", 'I graduated from Heritage Christian University with a BA in Biblical Studies. This is a focused, private, Bible college with a singular focus on biblical education. I believe the current administration is doing great things and headed the right direction.']

name: J. F. Drake State Community and Technical College
reviews:
["Today I had a very horrible experience with what sounded like a older black guy in admissions. Very rude , not a good listener and not professional at all. And this is coming from a black woman. Admissions is the first impression and my expectations weren't met at all. If he doesn't want to do his job and give a good first impression he shouldn't be the voice of your company.", 'BEWARE SUPRISE BILLING!!!!

RESOLVED: After being sent to voicemail on the phone, I had to drive up to figure it out where it was explained to me they Undercharged me on tuition and I still had to pay. They said it was a "glitch" in the system.

I have been attending this school since Summer 2024. Set to graduate with 2 certificates Spring 2026.
I have always paid my tuition on time with no issues. (Spring 2026 included, I had settled what I had owed on 12/04/25)
I am now being charged 131$ for "developmental tuition."
I have already had this semester paid and they added it on 12/31/25.
I went through the accounty activity on ALL of my semesters and this is the ONLY semester where I have a charge for "developmental tuition"
Adding this 5 days before school starts in insane.

I received an email today saying I had an undue balance due the same day (one day before classes start) for 131$', 'Blackness & Black conditions Dr. Bakin Art exibit was a phenomenal event. Amazing exhibit and great forum for questions and discussion. The artist was enlightening and his art really portrays and focuses on the African American experience. I enjoyed his perspective and discussion teaching and exposing the students, professors, and community alike is essential and this was a wonderful exhibit and speach', 'I found that the so many of the staff were willing to go so far above what their jobs required in order to help me. I was a minority at Drake, an HBCU, and I always felt like everyone was working for my success.', 'Had nst testing today. Mrs Donyale was professional and pleasant per usual!']

name: Jacksonville State University
reviews: ['Enjoyed participating in 2026 Transition U at JSU. Teacher candidates joined classroom teachers to host engaging learning activities for h.s. students with disabilities...Good teamwork!', 'As a student at JSU, I can firmly say that this school is incredible. The learning environment is wonderful. The staff is friendly. The students have tons of opportunities excel both academically and through extra curricular / social events. If you’re deciding whether or not this is the school for you, make the right choice and come to JSU.', "If you're trying to figure out which college to go to and this one is on your list join them for a tour and check it out. This school has so much to offer!", 'Campus is pretty and staff is amazing. Daughter will be attending in the fall and I believe JSU will be a great school for her', 'I have been to this campus several times and it is beautiful.   Friendly people and students with great attitudes!']

name: Jefferson State Community College
reviews: ["Just finished my first semester back in school and I'm extremely happy with my teachers and how much it cost. I've never done this well in school and I have to give some credit to the staff for that. That being said what is seen in some reviews here about the financial aid office and advising office there are some hiccups in the process.  I did have a slight issue with transcripts being registered in but it was also a bit last minute and depending on the time of day you call it can be hard to get ahold of people. I still believe always going in person goes a long way and with me doing that I had no real issues getting set up in my classes.", 'Love this school! Great educators, advisors & adult program. A great place to start your educational journey, especially for transfer students looking into 4-year universities afterwards.', 'I’m coming back to school after being out for a while, and was expecting a great experience but it has not turned out that way so far. I was dropped from a class for no reason. I paid on time, and I did the assignments asked of me on time. I put in a re-instatement form got approved and guess what my class still was not there! I was told it was a glitch, but even after I was supposedly back in the class I still can’t see anything! It’s been almost a week, and I am falling behind on assignments because of an error that should already be fixed. I feel like my money is literally being stolen right now, and nothing has been done about it.', "My issue is the unprofessionalism of some of the instructors. I am in my late 30s and they will speak to me as if I'm a child. Even when reported, nothing is done about it. I am truly disgusted by it and if they treat me this way, just imagine how they treat high schoolers in dual enrollment and recent high-school graduates. The difference is WE are PAYING the instructors to educate US. Instructors are NOT our bosses. Instructors should be REPRIMANDED. Those who we report our issues to that do nothing should be REPRIMANDED. I increased my course load to graduate sooner so I can stop dealing with JSCC employees sooner. I take classes online and in-person. The online classes are the worst. Instructors get on students about sending unprofessional emails and they will literally use all caps and exclamation points in emails, which is technically yelling and should not be used in emails (something you learn in middle school). I can't put too many specifics because some issues are personal and this is my last semester. I'm avoiding being reprimanded for talking against the school. If you plan on or are attending JSCC, do NOT let staff intimidate you. You are NOT a child (even if you are, do not allow them to). YOU are paying the school. Even if you get grants/financial aid, YOU are giving them YOUR money. Not the other way around. YOU are putting money in their pockets. YOU have a voice. YOU are paying for your education. YOU are paying instructors that basically WORK FOR YOU, they're just hired by the school. If you're having issues with any staff members, keep documentation (keep emails or document day, time, and statement of what occurred). You have great staff members but the disrespect of some of the instructors, overshadows the greatness of some because of how badly they treat you. Please write reviews (the good, bad and ugly) on the school. Good luck on your education and I wish you all the best on your journey.", "The financial aid office is a joke. No one answers the phone and now they make you leave a message. No matter how many messages you leave no one will return the call. I have had to submit documents multiple times because they say they have not been received. The financial aid staff are condensending and take forever to process your paper work no matter how early you submit it. It's very frustrating to receive your aid well after classes start and they ask you to pay upfront and you will get reimbursed when your information is processed. Well, if I had the money to pay for it all upfront then I wouldn't need aid. Professors are great despite the unprofessional office staff."]

name: John C Calhoun State Community College
reviews:
['I’ve had good experiences with CCC in the past as a teenager.. but when wanting to return as a 30 year old adult I was extremely disappointed with advising. I’ve had a long successful career in dentistry that I wanted to move further into with a degree, I was highly motivated and confident, but once meeting with Regina Jacob’s I left, sat in my car and cried. The first thing she said to me was “I don’t know if you’re sure what you want” this being my first time speaking to her or being on campus since 2013/2014. I was questioned about my career and how I know I want to do it (based on my chosen major at age 19 and not on my current age and long term career) I was made to feel like I don’t take it seriously ( based on my grades at 19) I was talked to as someone unmotivated and unsure and was not listened to. She absolutely made me question my worth and my choice of going to college again. Questions weren’t answered and mostly I was pushed into registering for classes without conversation of those classes. And this may also had been because she was looking to leave early that day (as she told others before taking me back) and rushed through our visit.. I spoke to another advisor who gave very different answers and recommendations than Regina that I felt made more sense and he was great (that was conversation over email) but once going to meet with someone in person I was met with Regina who only persuaded me by her demeanor to not move forward with Calhoun community college. I have other options for my career in dentistry and while I can continue to pursue them without CCC, it is so disappointing how that meeting went and how unhelpful it was. Had I been the 19 year old who was unsure of their future, their parents were helping pay for their education, and had such a lack of life experience I would understand her questioning and hesitancy. But to be so unhelpful, unkind, and hesitant with an adult regarding their current career, whom would be paying for their education themselves, it was more than anything disrespectful. I feel an opportunity for CCC would be advisors specifically for adults in a different point of their life than young new students. Or better communication training.', 'What is the problem with your Testing Center faculty?

The treatment my boyfriend received at this testing center was completely unacceptable. After taking the Accuplacer exam, one of the older women who works there spoke to him in a demeaning, condescending manner when printing his results, as if placing into English 101 or Math 098 meant he was unintelligent or incapable of going to college. This is a community college, for crying out loud.

These placement scores are extremely common — I received the same. Does everyone who has to take these courses get treated like they’re incapable? This employee’s behavior crossed the line into public shaming and was completely inappropriate for an educational environment. Students come to a testing center nervous enough as it is — they should not be met with judgment, sarcasm, or disrespect. Why is a grown adult bullying and shaming someone anyway? Grow up.

This staff member should NOT be working with students if she cannot show basic professionalism. I have formally reported this incident and expect it to be addressed. No one deserves to be treated this way. Thank you for crushing dreams.', 'We went today to Callhoun at Wymn Drive ,Huntsville to look for help to fill a form about financial aid for my son and Christy in the Financial Aid area was very helpful and friendly with us.', "After experiencing Dr. Wilson and Ms. Crayton's clown show that they call surgical technology, I can no longer recommend this institution. I had very good grades but I will not take part in a program that throws rules, guidelines, and education out the window for the sake of teachers' egos. I've got a degree previously from Calhoun, and a degree from Auburn University as well. It's a shame that this institution has gone down hill this badly. It may just be the Surgical Technology department, but I will never come back to this school. I couldn't believe the misinformation being taught to be honest. I had to hold my tongue constantly to avoid stepping on the teacher's ego when I knew she was teaching information that was wrong. Both teachers were both actively trying to get the other fired at the time that I left as well which further echoes the unprofessionalism that takes place in this program. Ms. Crayton asked us multiple times to go to the Dean about Dr. Wilson's total lack of effort. She bad-mouthed him constantly in our classes (which he deserves, but is still very unprofessional). Avoid this program at all costs. It's 100% not worth it.", "This review is specific to BUILDING 9  - TESTING VENTER & ADULT EDUCATION, office # 109.  This is where I went yesterday to take my exam for selling Life & Health Insurance.  The testing center was quiet and spread out enough that I didn't notice anyone else was in the room while I was testing.  They provided a noise-canceling headset which also helped.  The computer monitors where adjustable, as were the chairs.  They provide lockers for you to keep your personal items safely locked away during your testing time.
The waiting area and the bathroom facilities were clean and comfortable.  Parking is right in front of the building.  Directions to find the testing center were concise.
I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND this testing center.  I have tested as PSI in Nashville in the past, and it wasn't nearly as nice, clean, or professional and friendly."]

name: Lawson State Community College
reviews: ['They beg u to sign up for classes, don’t communicate or will halfway communicate, change things last minute all while u fill out FAFSA, just for them to TAKE your money & DROP all your classses. BEWARE BECAUSE THEY WILL NOT HELP YOU! All they do is send a bunch of emails that lead you nowhere! I have yet to speak to an actual Human being in person or on the phone. All they do is emails. 🤦🏾\u200d♀️ just go to Jeff state, I did their CMA program, I will gladly just go back for nursing. At least they are organized.', 'I am about to get my Curinary Arts degree great people that work here awesome teachers that really care about your success I truly appreciate everyone that has helped me along the way go Cougars ❤️💯', 'Lisa Robison denied my helping me and was very rude. Twirled her finger beat on the desk and was very unprofessional. Besides that Lawson is a great school very impatient n unprofessional people.', 'I attend Lawson state, I wish I didn’t. Unprofessional staff, Office administration doesn’t care about you and give poor useless instructions. Rooms and buildings falling apart. Teachers from my experiences generally nice people who care about you and your education. If you’re a parent and you care about your child’s future do not send them here. Adults save your money.', 'Im 43 and just now figuring out what I want to do with my life. Im so grateful Lawson State is giving me the opportunity to do what I love!']

name: University of West Alabama
reviews: ['Visited with my son for a college tour. Enjoyed the overall experience.  Everyone we met was friendly and helpful. And our tour guide was WONDERFUL! The information received about the university as well as the available programs is exactly what we need to make a decision on  where my son will eventually attend. Good day !!!', "Worst experience ever! The professors are very unprofessional! This is the only school I've been to that did not care about you having a full time job! They would literally give you 5 days to complete 3-4 essays including 30+ page research papers!! Then, if you ever drop a class, you better keep an eye on it because i dropped a class halfway through because I couldn't keep up! After the semester ended, I received a letter in the mail stating I owed for this class! I contacted the school thinking it had to be an error and this lady argued me down claiming I never dropped the course even though I had evidence that I did! If you want to know the truth, I found out through a reliable source that the school was hurting financially and they were doing this in an attempt to receive extra funds! They woukd show your student loan where you dropped it and they would tell you you didnt so they woukd receive double payment for that course.", 'If I could give out a zero for this school I would. I have never experience a so called "University" to use excuses on my transcript they have got. My transcript was sent by the other college but UWA stated to me that the transcript was incomplete...So I have been waiting for a month and two weeks for UWA to give me an update of the matter. So while I am waiting for the transcript to clear my classes will begin the following week. I see that I\'m not the only one who has this problem and it\'s very clear that this so called university does not care about some incoming students that affect what they do to us. The off putting salution they gave me is to reregister next semester. Well I got a better idea, I feel that this school should be investigated and retrain. If you are a student that has a choose to go to another school please save yourself the time and money and go somewhere else.', 'Spent 2 of my college years here.  Excellent staff and well maintained campus.  Shout out to 96-98 3rd floor Speith Hall!  We ran that jokers!', 'I’ve been waiting for my transcripts to be evaluated for a month and couple of weeks . I’ve never experienced such unprofessional guidelines. I have miss two start dates for the RN BSN. I’ve been to multiple universities and never has it taken this long to complete a transcript evaluation. This school doesn’t even offer a RN MSN degree to specialize as a Nurse Practitioner. You would think they would take the BSN enrollment more seriously before they lose students to other schools that do offer those other programs. What an embarrassment I would not recommend.']

name: Lurleen B Wallace Community College
reviews: ["The LBW College has a wonderful nature trail to walk around and view the beautiful scenes of the pond with the gorgeous selection of fish and turtles. It also has a water fountain in the middle of the pond on the trail which is also the golf course of the college. I recommend any and everyone to go and take a hike around it. It's a really nice and peaceful, relaxing place to go to by yourself or with your family.", 'We went for a Cyber Security conference hosted by the college. Lunch was provided and the presentation was very good!', 'This is the community college of Andalusia, Alabama,where I am currently enrolled. There are wonderful people here. The academic counselor happens to be my favorite,a very caring woman. My next favorite would have to be the art instructor. A very honest ,upbeat,down to earth kind of lady. These are very special and " down to earth" ladies with magnificent talents!! LBWCC is very fortunate to have them. Go Saints!!', 'Not bad it was a good two years. The wifi was bad for the whole 2 years. I had some of the best teachers and that outweighed the 2 bad teachers I had. Lots of community stuff to do. Everyone was very helpful and they cared unlike at the high school up the road.', 'Andalusia Dance recital was held in the Dixon Center. Nice facility. Andalusia Dance has class and grace. Enjoyable event.']

name: Marion Military Institute
reviews:
['I spent a year there back in ‘82. Cannot believe how much the facility has  improved program has always been top-notch. But the addition of the fire and rescue and other RTC programs. My stepson is taking it lightly duck to water.', 'Yea the program seems by what I witnessed and heard is a pretty good one what I really like is that in the classrooms they would focus more on 1 on 1 teacher student time', 'My son is looking to attend the Air Force Academy and MMI came highly recommend!  Our congressman had a service academy event and as we spoke with each one, they all had amazing things to say about MMI and how it prepared cadets to attend the academies.   Everyone we have met at the school has our son’s best interest at heart and is focused on his success.   This school has the backing of some super successful people and is one of the few options that the US government will also pay for sponsored prep for the academies.  Highly recommend a visit if it is a school you are considering', "My son will be attending Marion Military Institute (MMI) this fall under the SAP (Service Academy Program) as a non-sponsored cadet. Although he did not receive a congressional nomination during his senior year of high school, we now believe MMI offers the best path toward earning one.

He was awarded a full athletic scholarship for track and field, which is a testament to both his hard work and the opportunities MMI provides. From the beginning, the staff have been incredibly helpful, responsive, and supportive—addressing every question and concern we've had along the way.

The academic and military curriculum mirrors the rigor of the U.S. Service Academies, and I have full confidence in the program’s direction under LTC Bowen’s leadership. The curriculum is designed to reflect the academic and physical rigor of the U.S. Service Academies, and I feel fully confident in sending my son here to strengthen his candidacy for an appointment at USNA or USMA.", 'My son graduated from MMI May 25.  We are so thankful for the experience.  He was treated so well, and learned so much.  I know His time there will help him in his future career.']

name: Miles College
reviews:
['Beautiful campus, clean, secured entrance and exit. Has campus security. Had Sororities and fraternities. New construction. This College has a lot to offer. The college is world renowned.', "My husband attended this college in the Fall of 1989. He hadn't been back since then. We happened to be in town for a Southern University A&M Baton Rouge SWAC Basketball Championship game and decided to swing by Miles.
My husband was Floored by all of the improvements and additions to the campus. When he attended the campus only had two forms Male/Female and the football field looked like a practice field full of dirt without the stadium.
It was so nice to see that Miles had come such a long way. The surrounding houses can leave you depressed however.
Overall, progress was made with many more to come I'm certain", 'Nice! The people are warm, helpful, and very friendly! Great band and clean campus!', "It was a great experience to visit the campus and watch the game.Except for the alumni or trustee that works the ticket booth are rude!! Mrs Knight's and others are a little overboard with the students. She's over aggressive with the students especially when they are members of the band. I watched her handle them very aggressively!!! These days are not the time for that.", 'Great place, very helpful staff. Good dining facility. We were there to attend a spiritual retreat during the memorial weekend and everyone from Miles college, including the President were extremely kind and helpful. They went beyond the call of duty to make our weekend memorable. Thanks, Miles college!']

name: University of Mobile
reviews: ['Great campus! I was there chaperoning a camp group. My daughter might be interested in this school.', 'Great place to walk in shade. Between semesters and most of summer there is little student activity so you need only check in at the entrance and walk the campus. Weekdays restrooms and water refill stations can be accessed in the main central building.', 'Small school big school atmosphere very clean safe campus be prepared to show your ID to get on campus.', 'Pretty campus--looks easy to get around.', 'I LOVED IT HERE! I WENT HERE FOR A COLLEGE TOUR AND IT WAS BEST ONE THAT IVE EVER WENT TO! They have so many opportunities to choose from! Really good food! And really nice people there! My favorite person there was ms rhiannon! She was so welcoming and kind❤️']

name: University of Montevallo
reviews:
['We to preview day. We loved the campus and area around the school. It had the small town feel. Daughter likes that the classes were small. The campus is more hilly than other we have visited.', "The campus is frequently noted for its aesthetic and unique, antique architecture. A nice place to walk and meditate.
This university is Alabama's only public liberal arts institution and emphasizes critical thinking and research. A good option far from large cities", "I love the campus it's beautiful. Also the students and staff are all so great !
MONTEVALLO has my vote for the best school of the arts in Alabama !
And I just happen to know these two  exceptional young men. I call them my boys !!!!", 'Wonderful small town university. Of course it is on the outskirts of Birmingham so it's not really a"small town" university.  Anyway it's still an excellent school. I attended a musical production put on by the school drama department. It was an excellent show done in their newly renovated performing arts center. A top notch production.', 'Really beautiful.  A great place for photos.  I was there Spring Break and I had the campus to myself']

name: Northwest Shoals Community College
reviews: ['I don\'t understand why they have an instructor teaching machine tool technology when that person has no clue how to nor ever has run a cnc lathe. He "teaches" what he learns from YouTube. Go ask him a simple trigonometry question. The guy can barley run a 3 axis vertical milling machine yet people pay good money to learn this trade here. I like the guy but he has no business teaching machine tool technology to anyone. Graduates actually learn the trade once on the job. It isn\'t suppose to work that way. It goes to show that it\'s all about money. No one really earns a degree anymore. You just go buy one. This country is circling the bowl. If you are considering learning a trade here, seriously reconsider this location.', "I am getting my gen eds here so I can transfer to a 4-year. It is pretty affordable and there are tons of Opportunities for scholarships and grants! The CCAMPAS is one of them and it helps pay almost 90% of my childcare so I can focus on school! It's cheaper than UNA and there are a lot of class options between the two campuses and online. Definitely worth it for students like me!", 'Wonderful Metallica Scholars concert. Great music, great outdoor space and convenient parking. I look forward to many more from the college.', 'The staff is always super friendly and they keep everything so clean and organized.', 'Amazing teachers who are hands on. Financial aid department is horrible though and needs to be revamped.']

name: University of North Alabama
reviews:
["UNA has progressed since I started and is a college I might have actually enjoyed starting if I weren't finishing. They do have an outdoor center that allows the students to check out kayaks and a Friends of International Students outreach as well now.

When I first started, I was paying monthly and the time came when I finished my basics but was an undecided major because I didn't know what I wanted to do and my advisor told me in my meeting with her that I really needed to have a major and that I should know what I wanted to do by then (I was only 22) and if I didn't then there wasn't really much she could help me with. My most recent advisor for my career was much better at advising me.

The staff was 50/50. Most of the professors are really good at explaining their material and passionate about what they do. Sadly, my favorite history professor was an adjunct so was only around for that semester. Unfortunately, the majority of the basics professors are the ones that really lacked in making me want to stay there. We had one professor that would count us absent even if a few minutes tardy, which makes first year students feel like they might as well not even be in the class if they're unable to find parking and running late.

Graduation, though exciting after so many years was also really irritating. After thousands of dollars and twelve years of working towards my Bachelor's while working full-time, my graduation ceremony had a 6-person maximum. My mom, dad, partner, and three grandparents were able to attend. My three siblings, one of which just started this same college, my step dad, my step grandmother, and all the other people that had supported me were unable to see me walk in person because they're so strict about attendance. Their only response was that they could watch it via live stream as if 1) everyone happened to have access to the internet (which we didn't at my parent's house) and 2) that it was the same thing as seeing the first in three generations achieve a college degree. With as much money as I had spent on getting the degree, I really wanted to be able to have everyone that helped me (mentally and financially) watch me recieve it. To top it all off, the graduation ceremony was delayed by 2 hours, which we didn't find out until we got there so my partner who had only been able to get the morning off work for, had the leave halfway through because of the delay.

Less recent, yet, equally irritating: The cost. The fees are ridiculous: mandatory transportation fee for a bus that never came anywhere near my apartment, recreation facility fee for a pool and gym I was unable to use, technology fee though I used my own laptop, camera, Internet, etc.

Most obvious: the parking. Absolutely atrocious. Freshmen can't even park on campus, they have to use a parking deck downtown. Everyone else that is allowed on campus or near the university needs to come an hour or two early to circle the parking lot(s)/deck(s) like a vulture to find anything within 5 minutes of their class starting as there's definitely twice as many students as there are parking spots.

Not so much a problem for everyone: online classes. For a university that states to have to capability of getting a completely online degree, there are an awful lot of classes unable to be taken online and an equally disappointing amount of classes that are only offered once every two years that make timely degrees a bit hard. This was a selling point for me coming back for my degree while working and ended up being a hassle to actually take classes.

The nicest thing about this University is the aesthetics (even though it is too spread out to efficiently get to classes across campus) and they do offer the IDS degree that makes it easier to graduate for someone that swapped majors too many times while still getting a customized program of study that focuses on the things that would actually be needed for their career.", "UNA is a great college. A small town but there's most things anyone would need nearby. Friendly people and a great atmosphere. name: Bishop State Community College
reviews:
['My experience with the advising department at Bishop State Community College has been consistently disappointing. Advisors play a critical role in helping students navigate their academic path, yet the level of support provided has fallen short of what students deserve.

Advisors are often difficult to reach, and when they do respond, the information given is sometimes incomplete or inconsistent. This creates unnecessary confusion for students who are trying to register for classes, understand degree requirements, or stay on track. Delayed communication has caused avoidable stress and missed deadlines.

Another serious concern is the way some advisors interpret student behavior. I’ve witnessed and experienced situations where normal nervousness — which is completely understandable when students are seeking help — was misinterpreted as agitation. This kind of misguiding profiling not only discourages students from asking questions, but also creates an environment where they feel judged rather than supported. Advisors should be trained to recognize the difference between anxiety and hostility, especially in a college setting where many students are already overwhelmed.

Bishop State has potential, but the advising system needs significant improvement. Better training, clearer communication, and a more student‑centered approach would make a meaningful difference in helping students feel respected, understood, and properly guided.', "Leticia and her supervisor is so incompetent. Leticia will just tell you anything to get you off the phone and doesn't follow up when told of her mistake she will rage bait her supervisor and then the supervisor will do the same. name: Shelton State Community College
reviews:
['I am writing to formally document my experience and to state my decision to discontinue my sister’s college application process with Shelton and proceed with another institution.

I want to begin by emphasizing that I approached this process with courtesy, patience, and professionalism at all times. I invested a significant amount of time, effort, and personal resources to ensure that my sister’s international application was completed accurately and in compliance with all stated requirements. Unfortunately, my experience working with Wyetta has been deeply disappointing and has raised serious concerns about her qualifications, competency, and ability to effectively perform the responsibilities of her role.

Based on my interactions throughout this process, I found Wyetta to be fundamentally unprepared and unqualified to manage international student applications. Her handling of basic requirements, communication expectations, and follow-up responsibilities fell far below any reasonable professional standard. At no point did I feel that the process was being managed with the level of organization, clarity, or accountability required for something as consequential as an international college application.

One of the most concerning issues involved the transcript evaluation requirement. As you are aware, international students from non-English-speaking countries are required to submit a transcript evaluation completed by a NACES-accredited institution. I complied fully with this requirement, paying over $250 for the evaluation and official delivery of the documents to Shelton. According to confirmed delivery records, these documents were received by Shelton in November. Despite this, Wyetta never acknowledged receipt of the documents, nor did she provide confirmation after multiple follow-up attempts. I maintain a complete paper trail documenting the delivery and my repeated efforts to obtain confirmation.

In addition to this failure, communication throughout the process was inconsistent, incoherent, and at times entirely nonexistent. Emails frequently went unanswered, guidance lacked clarity, and timelines were never clearly communicated. This pattern of silence and disengagement is not an isolated incident but something I observed repeatedly over the course of our interactions. Being “ghosted” during a time-sensitive admissions process is unacceptable, particularly when financial costs and strict deadlines are involved.

The lack of transparency, failure to follow through on basic administrative responsibilities, and absence of professional communication demonstrated a disregard for both the applicant and the time invested in this process. It is especially troubling that Shelton would associate its institutional image with an individual whose performance reflects such a significant lack of preparedness and professionalism.

Given the cumulative impact of these issues—poor communication, lack of accountability, failure to confirm receipt of critical documents, and clear deficiencies in competency—I have lost confidence in the support being provided. Continuing under these circumstances would have placed my sister’s academic future at unnecessary risk.

For these reasons, I have decided to move forward with another institution that demonstrates the level of professionalism, clarity, and reliability that international students deserve.

I am sharing this feedback not out of hostility, but out of responsibility, in the hope that it leads to meaningful review and improvement within your admissions processes.', "worst school ever! you will regret coming Here! I don't understand the good reviews here! they are probably lies!", "My wife went through the nursing program. She loved it. She feels like the program really prepared her for her license. I am currently in the HVAC/R program at night. I am glad they have this program at night since I work full time. I feel like the instructors are very knowledgeable. Some of the classes are hybrid and some completely online. That makes it easier for people who work during the day to complete the program. A former state board member told me Shelton State's HVAC program is very good. I wish they had more trades programs at night though. I believe the only other complete program at night is welding.", "Huge waste of time and money.  The only saving grace to this institution is the Fredd Campus. The Martin Campus is not flexible at all, and forget about taking online courses thinking that it will be more flexible. There is much more homework and it is a lot more strict than in person classes.  Do not take online courses, they do not care if you have a full time life, you better bend to their will or fail the class.  If you try to contact anyone regarding any issues, no one will help; you will simply get a very automated and diplomatic response.  Being on the President's and Dean's list means nothing and neither does being in Phi Theta Kappa. I was told C's get degrees, so don't even try to work hard.", "Literally the worst school ever. The advisors do absolutely nothing to help you. When you call they just tell you what you want to hear and don't help at all. I called last week to make sure everything was in order for me to sign up for classes and I was told yes. This morning I go to sign up and there is a hold on my account keeping from signing up. I missed out on the classes I wanted to take because their staff is incompetent. Highly pissed off right now. Then I could not even get ahold of anyone who could take the hold off"]

name: H Councill Trenholm State Community College
reviews:
['On February 3, 2026, I contacted the registrar’s office and spoke with someone named Jackie, who I believe may be Jacqueline Allen. I am trying to obtain a copy of my academic record from 1998. Although I attempted to access it through Parchment, I was unable to retrieve my record.
On Monday, February 2, around 9:00 a.m., I first called the office and was advised to send a formal email with the required information and submit a payment. I sent the email that same morning, but I did not receive any follow up response. Later that afternoon, about one to two hours before the office closed, I left a voicemail after no one answered my call.
On the morning of February 3, I called again several times with no answer and left another voicemail. I still did not receive a response until approximately 30 minutes before this report, when I finally spoke with Jackie. She confirmed that my email had been received, but I was not given an explanation as to why no response had been provided.
I was informed that there is no definite timeline for receiving my digital record, but that a physical copy could take four to six weeks. I explained that I do not need a physical copy and that I specifically need a digital version, which I am unable to access through Parchment. I also asked why my record is unavailable through that system, but did not receive a clear answer.
I was then told that I still need to pay the $25 fee, which is not an issue. Because I felt my questions were not being addressed, I asked to speak with someone else. I was transferred to the business office to submit payment, but no one answered. I left another voicemail and am currently waiting for a response.
At this point, I am very disappointed with the lack of communication and professionalism, particularly regarding unanswered calls and emails. Although I graduated in 1998, I urgently need access to my digital record for applications that are closing this week. I clearly communicated the urgency of this matter, yet my concerns did not seem to be taken seriously.
Something needs to change.', 'This is probably the worst place when is comes to communication. Students are completely ignored on matters of registration and financial aid. When you do finally get someone they have an attitude. My niece has had at her student record before calling her with wrong information. One person tells her one thing then another person tells her another. I would avoid this school at all cost.', 'Horrible communication!!!

Financial department was not helpful as they do not know until the last minute of your financials and push you to take loans. My BIGGEST issue at troy was that the scheduling needs to be revised. Shorter classes more days a week should not be done for concentration courses but rather longer times and maybe 2-3 days to be able to FINISH testing and succeed in courses, my professors half of the time had to stop the class due to time and tell the whole class to look it up online which is an awful way to teach.
