['The place is Pretty solid, it’s amazing how we have a university here, but it doesn’t have many bus stops, one for the entire campus, which is pretty big considering walking in winter.', "If you're a working adult and want to take classes then have a look at night classes at the University of Alaska Anchorage (UAA).  If you're out of high school and plan to live with friends or your parents then you can't beat the convenience of a local campus.  Online classes aren't for everyone, so consider UAA for the traditional higher education experience.

I wish the University Center was located on main campus, but space is an issue around UAA.  Checkout the new buildings on campus and some of the upgrades to the older buildings.  During the summer this campus looks beautiful with all the flowers.  Sadly finding food on campus is nearly impossible, so bring your lunch and relax at one of the many picnic tables.

If this review was helpful please click the Like button.", 'If you can avoid this college please do. I have attended 3 and this is by far the worst. Parking is ridiculously expensive asking like $200 and over for a parking pass. Speaking to an advisor is a joke. I kept getting passed around and then they push appointments to be a phone call. Their website is not student friendly. They changed my degree midway through adding and taking away courses so now I have pointless credits. I have heard from several people now that this is very common of UAA. Trust me there are better colleges out there. I maintained a 3.8 GPA until starting UAA. Partly on me and partly on the fact that they will throw teachers in last minute to teach a course and they admit they had to scramble the course material which usually ended up being overload for beginners classes.', "I have been to a handful of universities, and UAA is by far the most disorganized and unhelpful. Staff can't help you- you're going to have to make a dozen phone calls to even begin to sort out your own financial aid or what courses you need to take for your degree. Making appointments for consultation is a waste of time because you're going to get treated like an Incel for asking the questions that you have and ultimately get nowhere by the end of it. I've never seen a college extinguish so many ambitious youths so quickly. If you're seeking for a straight forward experience look elsewhere.", 'love my local university! Go Seawolves 💚⭐️']

name: Alaska Bible College
reviews:
['Very good college. I am almost through their Bachelor degree, and would recommend them to anyone.', "I am always partial to colleges who are located next to the town's visitor's center.", 'They have a new address now.

248 E. Elmwood Ave.
Palmer, AK 99645']

name: University of Alaska Fairbanks
reviews:
["I love UAF! I received a top-quality education from professors who love to teach, and I learned a lot! It is a beautiful and peaceful campus located on the pristine ancestral lands of the Dena'ina people of the lower Tanana River.", "UAF is doing right! Their dual enrollment for my lower 48 kid was awesome during covid. They have distance learning rock solid. Now that the kiddo is an Alaska resident, the facilities are awesome. They have been remodeling dorms and they are some of the better ones of some 30 colleges that I've been too in the past 30-35 years.
You can't go wrong with any of their science disciplines, as studying and working in the Arctic exposes you to a unique  environment that science plays a significant role.
The administration and faculty are all very approachable. They actually CARE ABOUT THE STUDENTS AND WANT THEM TO SUCCEED, a thing that is lacking at many universities. Student life is very engaging, even at -40!", 'Great campus. Has a lot of cool trails behind the dorms. The woods center has some pretty good food to.', "I had straight A's in my upper division courses last semester over 99%. And I'm not allowed to take summer courses which I enrolled in and were supposed to start today because of some harassment by the Staff at Kodiak College. I reached out to ORCA through UAF and still have a hold on my account. Looks like I'm going to a different College. I'm going to have to take legal action. Don't trust UAF or Kodiak College, they don't care about their students not even the successful ones.", "I really like this school! Alaska is a unique place and have always wanted to visit, but as Alaska's flagship school, UAF has many graduate-level programs I'm interested in!
Fun fact, it's where students stand in front of the sign in summer clothes when it's minus 40 outside!"]

name: University of Alaska Southeast
reviews: ['Easy to work with teachers & admin staff. Teachers work with individual students to help get classes completed & understood.\nA great example to the other colleges in the system!!', "I've been thinking a lot about UAS lately. I was here for 2 years in 2014-2016. I attended mostly to get some of my electives done before transferring to a larger school, and almost all of my credits did transfer. The campus is beautiful, there are some nice trails, it's near a harbor. The housing was really nice. I had a room to myself in a suite with one other bedroom but did not talk to my roommates much. Sol Neely was such a wonderful professor in particular and I was sad to hear about his death. My dad died during the last part of my time at this school and every single one of my professors was so kind, as well as the students. I learned a lot here and often think back to how impressed I am that there was such quality education in such a small school. Many of the things I learned there have stuck with me just as much as my larger university education.", 'Worst set of schools in the entire United States\nThey like to hold students hostage basically not giving them what they need to transfer to other schools outside of Alaska sadly the advisors don’t advise or advocate for students especially Native American students. My daughter was told she could take classes from all campuses and it would make one complete GPA but that was faulty information because that’s not what happened she ended up getting all As and her GPA should have been a 3.2… this was not the case… she ended up with a 2.9 at UAS…. 2.75 at UAA and 2.0 at UAF… non of these she can get into a better university with… and was told oh well if you spend $$$ we can over time get you where you want to be GPA wise… And was told by an advisor that “ Native students should just stay at native schools”', "UAS is great to attend in person. I did so for about 3 years. As soon as I moved to only online classes my advisor was less than helpful. After calling him and sending him soooo many emails I never heard a response. Because of him I was unable to start my fall classes this year and my scholarships were taken away. All because my advisor wouldn't take the time to reply to me. I had a hold on my account because I had switched to all online classes and needed my advisor to approve it. Because I had moved out of Juneau I couldn't just go in and find my advisor. None of the student resource centers were helpful either. UAS is a GREAT school..if you attend in person", "Confused staff and educators that don't seem to care about the curriculum make this school the place to go if you're not particularly concerned about learning. A school that provides undergraduate research, and nothing else. Literally, nothing else; no tech program, no media program, no sports program, a vanishing art program...I could go on. Throughout my degree there were many times I would reflect and become sad; I felt like I was wasting my money, wasting my time, and not learning. I'm not saying it's going to be like this for everyone. I am just sharing my experience."]

name: Alaska Pacific University
reviews:
["APU and Alaska in general are really special places, and I would like to possibly do an MBA here.

I mean look at the other pictures of this place throughout the year, especially in the fall! So beautiful!

I've never been to Alaska as of 2024, but coming from Florida and doing undergrad in Colorado, I have always wanted to visit or even live in Alaska. It's definitely one of my favorite states! So I believe that doing grad school here will help me make that decision for myself.

Thank you!", 'I graduated from APU in 2014 with my Bachelor's in Earth Science. I was beneficial enough to "stumble" across the university during my university search shortly after high school. Coming from a small town in northwest Georgia I was worried about traveling across the country and attending a small liberal arts school in Alaska, but after arriving the residence life staff and the university were beyond welcoming. The school offers "active learning" courses that give students a perspective to learning that goes beyond the confines of a classroom. During my studies, I was able to study earth science first hand from the volcanoes on the big island of Hawaii or the gold mines of Alaska. I would highly recommend the university to any perspective student that wants an active learning experience and true faculty engagement.', 'APU is a World-Class University. It offers excellent course choices for new students locally and internationally. Exceptional instructors. I would highly recommend Alaska Pacific University to those that are serious about getting the best education that is tailored to their needs and professional goals. Keep Up To The Great Work APU', "Update: One positive thing about this University is that they read their ratings. About a month or two months after I posted this, APU finally added their school onto Army Ignite. I still wouldn't recommend it to anyone that's in the military due to their expensive tuition and the lack of experienced  VA workers.

If you’re in the military (especially in the Army) then save your time.

I heard great things about APU, hence why I applied to go here for the Spring semester of 2022. I’m in the Army and use Army Ignite to pay for my courses. The VA department knew that they needed to upload files to have APU available on Army Ignite and failed to so. Not to mention that this school charges around $4k a course, so you would have to be responsible to pay for some of it out of pocket. I was working on resolving this issue for A MONTH. Had I known it was going to be like this, I would’ve went to UAA.

In conclusion, save your time/money.", 'LOVE LOVE ! Extremely hygienic! Clean atmosphere, overall general hospitality and always an experience worth my patients!
Overall probably the best area for my obgyn to be stationed. Lots of medical clinics in this area.']

name: Arizona State University Campus Immersion
reviews:
['Beautiful campus and fun to explore. The commitment to the biophilic design within the campus is very intricate and beautiful to look at. Would recommend going here if campus attraction and things to do were high on your bucket list', "Awesome college experience! Received my bachelor's degree and ten years later received a master's degree. The school is constantly evolving, adapting new learning,  and staying on top of skills employers are looking for. Highly recommend taking a tour for students who haven't decided which college to attend 🤔
There are hundreds of clubs and organizations to be a part of. Getting insights on college life from current students is invaluable part of the campus tours. My son will be attending ASU soon and I cant wait to see him start his journey at my alma mater. Go Devils!", 'ASU Tempe campus has a pretty huge and beautiful that the students can enjoy their campus life with academics, athletics, clubs, classmates,. friends, and so on. Especially, for academics, a tutor system is so organized that any student who needs a study support can take it.
One of my friends recommends me watch a football game which will be a super excited.
Great college!', "GORGEOUS CAMPUS w/ MODERN EDGE! ASU almost felt like it was too good to be true when my family and I drove through it. This is the definition of a college city, the Tempe Campus is HUGE. There's tons of housing, education facilities, and sports venues. Some of them are by the Town Lake! All of the buildings looked fresh and inviting.

I visited during the off-season (winter break) and people were still roaming the campus enjoying the many amenities and eateries nearby (or should I say inside?). It seems like ASU is the heartbeat of Downtown Tempe, I never felt overwhelmed, I just felt this warm, scholastic pride for Tempe's esteemed campus.

I definitely want to visit Mullet Arena soon to see some Sun Devils hockey!", 'Very modern looking school located downtown Phoenix. Several large building in the campus. Seem to have gotten donation for Walter Cronkite school of journalism.']

name: Arizona Western College
reviews: ["Beautiful campus. Went to register and the proposed was super easy.  I applued for the TRIO program and received great information and help navigating the application process. I feel confident that I will have great success at this school. I am a returning student and I'm so happy that they made me feel comfortable returning after 20 years. Thank you AWC ⭐", 'Enjoying a community theatre musical for a  Taste of Broadway! Our tickets came with a full on serve yourself dinner (with seconds, too)! Dessert was carrot cake and chocolate cake. The creamy  lasagnia was so delicious. The chicken with mushroom brown gravy was wonderful. One of our daughters was in the musical. OF COURSE SHE SANG THE BEST! LOL.  🤣😂🎶🎵🏆Actually, everyone did SO AMAZING! What a delightful treat rather than to be home literally crying  and bawling about world events. Tonight was a beautiful escape. Plz help sponsor your local youth theatre. We need more!', 'Beautiful campus, Fara the dog loves the grass. Thank you!', 'Horrible experience with this college. From scheduling courses to driving 30 minutes away for no reason, getting books before they finally shut down their library. Having a full time job makes this place even worse. Good luck trying to communicate with any person for information because none of them ever know the answers even giving false information (like open close times) my experience here has been an absolute nightmare. At 8 they said oh it is is building T4 called the Professor 5 times 2 voice mails explaining why I could not make there on time,, waited for him until 1pm, he never returned any phone call. They the only college here I believe thats why tgey treat people like that. Very bad organization no good.']

name: University of Arizona
reviews:
['Went in February so temperature was very nice and manageable! Cold on first day in the morning (high 30s) all the way back up to 70s on our last day! Absolutely gorgeous campus.', "Haven't been to the campus in nearly 30 years. Really enjoyed the campus tour and orientation for freshman. The staff and volunteers made for a great experience for parents and students. Best wishes to all the students...have a blast!", "Great university! I miss being there sometimes since it's my alma mater! 🙏 Great times with great people learning about wonderous things!

Best,

Michael Angelo Cortez", 'This Campus is Beautiful 😍 the staff is so nice and the overall feel is such a delight. Easy to get around and meet people. Handicap parking all over campus and tons of shade from the beautiful trees. Make sure to make it to a Wildcats game too.', 'It was 1968 and Mr. Anderson led a debate team from Valley High in Las Vegas to University of Arizona. Adrian and I had been up all night tripping on LSD we bought from freaks driving a white van. They picked us up hitchhiking near the university and immediately we were described as “weird Margarets” which was an appellation that became a life long in joke. Most notably one of the freaks broke a cork bulletin board over Adrian. The trails were awesome and I totally tripped on being a Margaret. Next day I was still flashing. Got to the debate room and there was a single fly vexing my mood. In debate you lose points for lack of composure and the fly was molesting me till I opted to swallow it. Grossed out but unbeaten, I want to shout out to my partner who fulfilled his dream of becoming a lawyer. His obituary, not that long ago, extolled a high minded liberal and I just want to say, I am proud of Stephen Swander. Thank you google maps for giving us this platform of place, truly the place to be.']

name: Central Arizona College
reviews: ["I repeatedly called left messages and even sent emails trying to get this college to send me any information about their music recording/engineering program for my son.  Even the academic administrator for this department would not reply to my messages. The desk clerk told me I could come in and do it tour. Yes, well, as I told them, we are in Florida.The reason why I am calling and asking for a information packet is because we would like to know if my son would like to attend the program. Obviously, we can't just pop in and do a tour. Apparently this college isn't very interested in gaining students? If their academic standards are anything like their service standards, I guess we're better off!", "Impossible to contact, impossible to navigate website. SO frustrating. Practically holding my financial aid hostage from another school by not cancelling my aid here so I can't attend class.", "I'll give it another go, yay for education. That Confederacy vs United States instead, should be resolved in Gettysburg VA, on the battlefield! Ha!!", "Unfortunately, my experience at Central Arizona College has been extremely disappointing. My financial aid was delayed for over a month due to poor communication between staff, which caused unnecessary stress. I also returned a product to the bookstore for a refund, only for it to 'mysteriously' go missing. Most of the actual education I've received has come from my own efforts, primarily through YouTube, since much of the class material consists of outdated videos—some nearly a decade old, which are also available on YouTube. If you're considering this school, I highly recommend investing your time and money in a better educational institution that prioritizes quality and student support. P.S.  Do not buy online access from the bookstore for your courses wait and buy it directly from the site!\nit is way cheaper $80 versus $120.", 'Now, in rolling for CDL training, I am doing a refresher course after twenty years']

name: Cochise County Community College District
reviews:
["i've been taking classes at Cochise for 3 years now, and overall it's been pretty good. I do think there can be a professionalism problems amongst the instructors, but it's nothing too crazy. It's a solid community college. It's important to know that some classes are only offered at the main campus in Douglas, but there's a good selection here as well.", 'Do not go here if you are affiliated with the military or white. After a dispute over grades escalated to the point that the college scheduled a meeting with a lawyer, I have been "encouraged" not to attend anymore. 4 "doctors" and 3 deans failed to give any reasoning for my grades, and argued against discrimination/retaliation because "You're not a protected class" despite being a 90% disabled veteran (a protected class). Either A) Cochise college does not think that white people have rights or B) they intentionally failed me so that I would have to reattend, and they could get more GI Bill money out of me. The only reason that I don't sue, is because I can't afford it. Cochise College NEEDS to be put under new management that understands AND FOLLOWS the law.

And now they are continuing to harass me. How is this "school" allowed to operate?', 'This is a review of the campus physical grounds and architecture only. A very beautiful campus for a local community college. I thought the architecture particularly of the science building was very interesting. The views of Miller and Carr Peaks were spectacular. The grounds were immaculate Nice landscaping. The library building had beautiful landscaping. Just a very pretty campus and also I believe the University of Arizona has a mini campus alongside.', 'Poor communication from financial services led to an early dismissal and non-completion of my degree.
The instructors likely are not Teachers, but Aides or Students themselves.
The English curriculum still relies on religious material.
Absolutely a *just out of highschool* institution.', "No way for a wheelchair to get from car to sidewalk they don't think about disabled people ada act."]

name: Eastern Arizona College
reviews: ['Terrible experience as a parent of a minority (black) young lady it was seemingly discriminative. Financial aid made various mistakes two semesters straight. Counselor made errors on schedules causing incorrect payments from financial aid and balances from each semester. No resolution or help. Teachers were rude or dismissive. I’m originally from Mississippi and I thought this was something that doesn’t happen in Arizona based on the 5+ years I’ve lived here but this rural town definitely made me know it exists all over. Very unwelcoming environment and nothing but issues.', "They changed their enrollment process and it's a mess. It's VERY HARD to enroll in classes now. Why make it such a hard process to enroll now? Whomever you paid to redo the schools website for myEAC (Gila Hank) did a horrible job and didn't know what they were doing. Until they fix it or change it back the review stands. Small but beautiful campus. Very good learning environment. Faculty are very supportive of students. Students have a positive and serious attitude towards learning and building lasting relationships.']

name: Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University-Prescott
reviews:
['Really a neat experience. Bought tickets a few months ago as a birthday gift to my husband. Lived in Prescott for many years but has never been. We viewed The Artic at the planetarium and we had a wonderful time.', 'This school sends its students to fly circles over Cottonwood’s neighborhoods all day, everyday. Our community airport is in the middle of town — not at the edge of town like many places. If the sun is up, there’s almost never a quiet moment.

This school has zero regard for residents the next valley over.', "A modern, technically-advanced campus ideal for studying engineering or anything related to aviation. Embry-Riddle is widely recognized in the aerospace and defense field, and I'm proud to call myself an alumnus. The one downside is that this campus is in a somewhat remote location.", 'PATHETIC  institute .. Deeply DISAPPOINTED
This is not a place where a student truly learns or feels supported. My friend studied here, and during his illness, the university showed ZERO care or accommodation. It’s HEARTBREAKING  to see an institution IGNORE the well-being of its own students. . Even the campus feels sooo BORINNNNGGGG..Google should honestly allow ZERO stars for such institutions', 'Toured the campus & flight line today with my daughter. SO SO underwhelmed & disappointing. Seriously this is part of THE Embry Riddle??? (And yes, I knew it was regional campus). 100% the worst campus tour I’ve ever been on. So little information given. Just very poorly organized & run. The campus is just pieced together, overcrowded & the aviation technology seems lacking. And crazy expensive. Really disappointed. I would NEVER EVER send my kid here.  I would give it 0 stars if I could. Don’t bother.']

name: Glendale Community College
reviews:
['Glendale Community College has a decent campus overall, but the hills are extremely steep. I feel like it would be really tiring to walk up and down those slopes every day. The school itself seems fine, but the terrain makes daily commuting pretty challenging.

Something to keep in mind if you prefer a flat and easily walkable campus.', 'Glendale Community College (GCC) offers a solid educational experience with a strong focus on student success and transfer opportunities. The campus is clean, well-maintained, and features updated facilities, including modern classrooms and a helpful library. Professors are generally supportive and knowledgeable, especially in popular programs like nursing, business, and the arts. The college also provides a range of student services such as tutoring, counseling, and career guidance. While parking can be a bit challenging during peak hours, the overall atmosphere is welcoming and student-focused, making it a great choice for those starting their academic journey.', 'Adventist Health Center is conducting a Vaccine center at The Glendale Community College in the parking structure at the top of the hill right off of the 2 Fwy Off the Mountain exit. The staff are very helpful. There is very clear and strict mandates on masks and health protocols. Please follow signage and bring your masks. You will need your ID for check in.
The nurses are very helpful and many of them have worked in the ER with patients and have seen the effects of the pandemic. So most of them are very happy to administer the vaccine and help prevent the spread of this terrible disease.
We are all so happy to share the change in the world and grow together. There is Hope and these are the people that are here to spread that hope.
3👍🏼’s out of 3👍🏼’s the staff and Nurses are very helpful and thoughtful.', 'Best Community College in California! Amazing professors and a school that takes care of their students.', "The staff at this school exhibit a concerning lack of professionalism and diligence. They seem unwilling to put in the necessary effort, often providing incorrect information and resorting to blaming students for their own shortcomings. Classes are abruptly canceled mere days before the semester begins, displaying a lack of foresight and consideration for students' schedules. Additionally, encounters with staff members can be characterized by rudeness and incompetence, creating a hostile environment for students.

It's imperative to hold them accountable for their actions and demand better treatment. If you want your concerns to be taken seriously, it's essential to reciprocate the same level of assertiveness and firmness in your interactions with them. From mishandling important documents that could jeopardize an entire semester to issuing incorrect grades, this institution fails to meet even the most basic standards of competence and professionalism. In my experience, it stands as one of the worst community colleges in Los Angeles County."]

name: Grand Canyon University
reviews:
["I HIGHLY DO NOT RECOMMEND GCU! They do not care about the student, just the money.
I was told that I could get my masters online for teaching English Language Leaners (Their TESOL Program). My state said that it did not qualify as a masters and there was more that I had to do but that I could get an endorsement.  Fast forward, I need a form completed for MY state verifying the program I attended through AZ and they refused to complete it
Now I cannot get an endorsement either and now I must seek legal action  as all they have to offer is an apology.  Apologys won't cover my debt or get me the endorsement I seeked as they enrolled me under false pretenses.", "Absolutely horrible. This University has to have the WORST policies to ever be enforced at any institution in recent history. I use military tuition assistance to pay for my schooling, as such, I'm required to submit a request for said tuition assistance for every class I take. The tuition assistance request must be made 7 days prior to the class start date. This wouldn't be an issue if the University ensured that students are aware of classes that they have been registered for. However, the schools policy states that councelors are not required to inform students when they are registered for a class. The councelors will simply register you for a class without notifying you that they've registered you. Even after explaining that I need to be consulted personally prior to registering me for classes due to how my Tuition Assistance works, my student councelor has continued to register me for classes without my knowledge. This has resulted in me frantically attempting to request to withdraw from classes because I didn't have enough time to apply for Tuition Assistance. Going further into GCUs policy's, it says that full tuition can only be refunded if you ask to drop the class before it starts. This combination of idiotic policy's creates a situation where students are unable to withdraw from their classes prior to their start date due to the fact that NO ONE TOLD THE STUDENT THAT THEY WERE REGISTERED! Thus, causing the student to incur the fee associated with dropping the class during the first week of the course. The most aggravating part of trying to navigate this system, is that even when you request to withdraw before the class start date, the counselors might just forget or decide not to remove you! This has happened with my past 2 classes, where I have requested that I be removed from the class, but then I go into Halo (GCUs version of Canvas), and find that I'm still in the class and the class has already started. It was an absolute nightmare trying to escape paying the stupid fee for a mistake that the councelors made. What was even worse, the first time that this happened was during the government shutdown. There was no guarantee that I was going to get paid and no way for me to even try to request Tuition assistance. Despite this, when I attempted to explain the situation to the councelors I was rebuffed several times and told that there was nothing that they could do. After a week or two completely stressing out over how I was going to pay the fee and rent without knowing if I was going to get paid at all that month, I finally explained my situation in a way that the councelors understood to the point that they were willing to waive the fee. After that whole debacle I requested that I be removed from all future classes because I no longer wanted to attend classes at GCU. Now today Dec 1, I've been made aware that I was registered for another class without my prior knowledge and it started today! I'm separating from the military soon and won't be getting paid my same wage. I'm desperately trying to get all my paperwork in order so I can get back home for Christmas this year. I don't need to be needlessly stressing out over having to drop a class from a University that I explicitly told that I want nothing to do with.

TLDR: DON'T GO TO SCHOOL HERE!!!!", 'would not recommend this school for a masters program. it has been nothing but a headache to deal with student services and the lack of support given when my dad passed away last year is concerning. I wish NAU offered the CMHC program fully online because I had a much better experience with them for my undergrad in social work.', 'I was invited to an orientation as a prospective PhD candidate. This was a pleasant trip and very informative. We had a full day of activities and they included breakfast, lunch and dinner. Excellent itinerary which was time conscious and included a campus tour. We had the opportunity to visit the campus bookstore which was a treat. I have applied for the upcoming semester and encourage all students  seeking a BA, MA and especially PhD to seriously consider a Grand Canyon University. The admission counselors were very helpful and answered all my questions with no hesitation and basically the follow up that I have received since I left the campus is incredible. That type of support is really needed will you try to finish your PhD and I am excited to be called a member of the Grand Canyon University community. Go Lopes!', 'I’ve been enrolled at Grand Canyon University for about a year, and my experience has been disappointing. I was initially led to believe that my degree would cost about half of what I’m actually being charged. Once enrolled, I found that tuition and fees were much higher than expected, and communication about financial aid was unclear. The school promotes itself as a Christian university, but I found that some professors teach from perspectives that differ from traditional Christian doctrine. The only course that strongly incorporates biblical principles is a mandatory $4,000 university class, which feels inconsistent with GCU’s advertised mission. What concerns me most is the handling of financial aid. A loan was requested under my name without my authorization, and despite multiple attempts to speak with leadership, I was given the runaround with no resolution. Students also have very little control over their aid and loan management.
I truly hope GCU takes accountability, improves transparency, and aligns its actions with the values it promotes.']

name: GateWay Community College
reviews:
['Been trying to figure out an account balance for MONTHS now so I can transfer to continue education and keep getting a runaround from everyone. First was the payment office telling me to contact Registrar, then registrar (I believe Raven was who I spoke to, she was very kind though) says to submit an appeal, both offices were aware that I was dealing with a balance from the academic year of 2023, Appeals emails me back to say they refuse to address appeals for anything other than the current year, so why did I get a run around from everyone else? Completely unprofessional and a massive lack of communication between departments, keep this in mind if you’re going to proceed with transferring to another college and you have a personal situation that prevents you from attending classes.', "Beautiful building.👍Gateway is well maintained, it has friendly staffs who are willing to help you and guide you through your school journey. Gateway has a lot of space and there's not a lot of noise in order to study in a really good environment. I wouldn't like to see anything change because I liked everything about the Gateway Campus.", 'I love this school. The professors, deans, and overall staff ate absolutely amazing. I graduated in May, and the best decision I made was to come to Gateway. It is easy to find your way around the building and has easy access to  lots of restaurants. The cafeteria has amazing food as well.', 'I visited Gateway Community College to get information and apply for classes, but from the moment I arrived, I was treated with complete disrespect. The security staff spoke to me in a rude and dismissive way, with clear attitude, as if I was bothering them just by walking in.

When I tried to ask questions about applying, the staff was not welcoming or helpful. They made the process confusing, gave me the runaround, and acted like they didn’t want to assist me. I felt discriminated against simply because English is my second language. Instead of trying to help, they were impatient, dismissive, and condescending.

I also called several times for help, and every time the people on the phone were rude, unprofessional, and acted like they didn’t care. Some didn’t even know how to answer basic questions and clearly didn’t want to help.

Based on my experience, I do not recommend Gateway. If this is how they treat someone who’s just trying to apply, I can’t imagine how they treat their actual students', "If I could give negative stars I would, this school is nasty in terms of its customer service, no one knows anything, departments don't communicate with each other so you will get a thousand different answers and some of the professors can't even speak or write basic English in courses that would require clear communication for you to pass!!  (This isn't xenophobic as I am an immigrant, it's just a true observation). They don't care, you won't feel welcomed here and most of the times you're gonna have to teach yourself. They will give you wrong information and advice and set you back years!!! Do not send your children here, do not enroll!! Can't say I didn't warn you guys."]

name: Mesa Community College
reviews: ['This is my first semester here. I currently work between 30-35 hours a week. I currently taking 3 in person classes & 1 online class. I was super nervous & had a lot of anxiety. The staff & students are really nice & redirect you if you have any questions or concerns. This my third 3 week here. The first week I was overwhelmed because I was trying to understand everything. Now it is my 3rd week here, I feel perfectly fine & comfortable. Just thought I’d share my experience. The professor’s are really great & informative.', 'I regret going to this school. I was forced to drop a class due to the death of a close family member, and my SAP appeal was denied with no compassion or flexibility. During this same period, I was experiencing homelessness and severe financial hardship, which the school completely disregarded. The administration is incompetent and disorganized—my personal high school transcript has been “missing” for six months. I have followed up at least six times through emails and calls and have been completely ignored with no response. Being ghosted by administration while dealing with major life crises is unacceptable. This school lacks empathy, accountability, and basic administrative competence. I would strongly advise prospective students to look elsewhere. There was a professor sexually harassing students and guess what? He still teaches there.', "They don't care about their students or their mental health. Denied me financial aid for 2 semesters, even after I get diagnosed with ADHD they will not consider a 2nd appeal. During COVID and the few semesters that followed I had withdrew from the same class a few times. This semester I got diagnosed with ADHD and tried to come back strong with a good head on my shoulders and brought my GPA up past 2.0. Yet this wasn't enough as my pace of progression was down to 40% which turned into 48% this semester. NO way can I afford 3 more semesters before it gets to 67%. I got an A in the class I had attempted multiple times weighing down my pace of progression so much. The first ever A I've ever got on my transcript. You would think a COMMUNITY college would slightly understand the mental health implications of something like COVID on a young student. I was only 20-22 living all by myself depressed with 0 peers. You can change everything, go to the doctor and make all the right decisions but MCC will not care. Maybe I did mess up a little and withdrew, but its withdrew not failed, never expected it to cost me this much. I tried to come back and worked hard for a year getting my work done while working full time and it still is not enough even after getting diagnosed with ADHD. Now I probably will have to find a different school which is sad cause MCC is a nice community college.", 'My sister completed the nursing program before me. She would come home and we would talk about her experiences within the program and how it would relate to real patient care. I was a CNA at the time and later decided to apply to the program. I was accepted to the CEP program, which means I can simultaneously pursue another degree while working towards my RN associates. I am currently working on my MSN through GCU which MCC allows students to work towards at a discounted rate.\nI have obtained a job as a new grad RN at a rural hospital and have been able to apply evidenced-based care within my practice. I learned a LOT during my schooling with MCC and enjoyed all the faculty. The faculty brough many enlightening experiences, perspectives, and insight as to how they safely delivery high quality patient care. I would recommend this program to any prospective nurse considering entering into this wonderful field. The staff have many ways to setup students for success you just need to be okay with asking for help and you will be guided to the right resource. I am glad to say that I am a MCC Alumni and have attained more knowledgeable colleagues.', 'The college is academically strong; however, my experience with the International Students Office was disappointing. I faced ongoing delays and poor communication, which directly affected important processes. Unfortunately, this situation became a major reason for my decision to leave the college. I hope the administration addresses these issues to better support international students.']

name: Dine College
reviews: ["Unless you're wanting a BA degree in being a Medical Transport Driver, id recommend not wasting your time and money here", "I don't recommend to go to school here for a degree. The campus is in need of repairs such as the NHC building sliding doors being broken. It requires you to manually slide them open and closed. There's often plumbing issues in the dorms such as toilets backing up. In my dorm hall the water was brown for 3 days due to pipes bursting someplace on campus, not all halls were effected. Sometimes the power goes out when it's really windy for 15 minutes or so. You could get a good or bad resident advisor for your dorm, such as them enforcing the quiet hours and making you whisper even in your room. There's a curfew at 11pm, if caught outside you could be written up. The parking lot for the dorm students also gets locked up at 11pm and you will have to ask security to open it up. Some faculty is exemplary and other's are lacking very much. I hate to say it but the older Navajo instructors aren't very good with technology. One instructor never replied to emails and wanted us to text them instead. The school pays adjunct faculty very low and it doesn't help the high turnover of faculty and students. They do dorm inspections maybe twice a semester which requires you to move everything 1 foot from the walls which is a hassle. Some dorm rooms have issues with their heating systems. There is no AC in the rooms. Some dorm halls have an annoying security system beeping sound every minute in the entryway. They do a fire safety drill at a random time which is super inconvenient and adds to the stress of living there.  The school pretty much only has the cafeteria to offer food. It isn't the greatest quality and is hit or miss depending on the day. I would describe it as middle school lunch most days. Sometimes vegetables and rice is undercooked or bland. Other times it's unfilling. A small selection of sandwiches and salads from the coffee shop can be found.  Students will get Mexican food at lunch from a vendor at the local gas station. The gas station food is pretty much the only other option. It's selection is hit or miss and costs more than you would expect. It's inconvenient that there's no local stores for groceries and other needs for dorm living. Overall the school is really only decent for the young who are being introduced to college, adulthood and want to stay on the Reservation for family.", 'I have been to the Christmas community dinner and the price is unbeatable for all u can eat crab buffet, delicious smoked salmon, amazing chocolate & cheese was my favorite, I have so much to say but finish with this I will be back again, thank you.', 'The food is always fresh and reasonably priced. We love the warriors coffee shop. Great coffee and service', 'I really love 💘 being at Dine College in Tsaile Arizona.  Wonderful memories, wonderful staff and wonderful people. Thank you  Dine College in Tsaile Arizona for the best 3 years of my life. I miss you all.']

name: Northern Arizona University
reviews:
["With my 4 years here I never met a single professor that is nice. Whenever I required help for classes the ACS never had anyone who could help me and didn't even try to aid me. The on campus housing wasn't bad, maintenance was always quick. The campus itself is beautiful, but how it's run and the people there aren't the best. Biggest annoyance is that they dont allow students the use of turnitin even though many teachers preach about how nice AI is with helping students learn. If you want to get food on the qeekends and you use teansfer meals good luck. The only options are on opposite sides of campus. It's better and much cheaper to starve yourself than deal with their food. Unless you're getting a good scholarship I would even consider NAU.", 'Great School!

Focused on overall student education, engagement and social well being.  NAU is a top-notch school,  providing a safe environment; where all are welcomed. Excellent dedicated degree programs. Mindset of striving towards a better you; resulting ina better future for all.  😉', 'I am a 2021 Psych grad and had the very best experience I could have hoped for. The professors were amazing, and my academic counselor was exceptional. I am now 11 weeks away from graduating from an MSN program in another state, and I can see the difference between the universities. NAU prepared me for graduate school, and I hope to have the opportunity to teach one of their nursing classes.', 'Beautiful campus if you don’t live there.  All dorms stink and have major problems. They need to invest some of that money into housing!!', 'My recent experience with Northern Arizona University’s graduate admissions process was disappointing and confusing. I applied for an online master’s program that aligned well with my background, and after investing significant time, effort, and money—ordering transcripts, completing the application, and ensuring every requirement was met—I was informed that I was not accepted because the program was “full.”

This explanation simply doesn’t make sense. Spring semesters usually have fewer applicants, and the major I applied for is not a high-demand program. Additionally, because it is fully online, enrollment capacity is rarely an issue. It felt more like an indirect way of rejecting my application than a genuine limitation. What made this even more discouraging is that NAU did not give me any specific reason for the rejection beyond the vague claim that the program had no space.

I have all required prerequisites, strong academic standing, and multiple master’s degrees, including advanced technical programs. With my background and education, I’ve had no issues being accepted into other universities, including highly reputable and competitive institutions. This made NAU’s explanation even more questionable. I’ve never once encountered an online program that was “full,” nor been rejected without a clear, specific reason.

If the program truly was at capacity, NAU should have clearly communicated this before allowing applicants to spend money and time submitting materials. Most universities either close applications once capacity is reached, offer waitlist options, or provide conditional acceptance. NAU did none of these, and nothing in the application portal indicated limited availability.

As a working professional balancing career responsibilities and advanced studies, transparency is essential. Instead, I was left feeling misled and that my efforts were wasted. Given my academic experience—and the fact that I have been accepted without issues into multiple respected institutions—this was a surprising and discouraging outcome.

While I respect Northern Arizona University’s academic reputation, this experience left a negative impression. I hope NAU improves its communication and admissions transparency so future applicants are not left facing the same avoidable confusion and frustration.']

name: Prescott College
reviews:
["I felt compelled to write this review after reading the last two negative reviews about Prescott College. I have been enrolled in the Clinical Mental Health Counseling program since the fall of 2021, and my experience has been generally positive. As a non-traditional student, I have appreciated the program's focus on preparing students for their counseling licensure. Reflecting on my time at Prescott, I can confidently say that the college’s emphasis on equipping students for this career path is genuine and effective.

It’s true that online programs can sometimes feel tedious due to engagement requirements, but I’ve found that the experience is truly what you make of it. As someone who worked full-time while pursuing my degree, the flexibility and asynchronous nature of the classes were crucial. This structure allowed me to complete coursework on my own schedule, often late at night, while still engaging with peers through group projects and online discussions. The balance worked well with my lifestyle.

The faculty at Prescott have been consistently engaged, compassionate, and creative. While not every instructor was my favorite, I only had one negative experience throughout my time in the program. The vast majority of the professors I worked with were impressive, inspiring, and deeply supportive. I am grateful for this master’s program, which made it possible for me to earn my degree while continuing to work full-time.

Coming from a large state school in undergrad, I was struck by the level of support I received at Prescott. From the registrar to the Financial Aid office, the staff was attentive and helpful, a stark contrast to my experience at a bigger institution. As an out-of-state student, I was able to visit the campus in person, and I was pleasantly surprised by what I found. Prescott’s campus is a hidden gem, a small, historic liberal arts college nestled among the boulders of Prescott. As a geology enthusiast, I always make time to visit the Grand Canyon when I’m in the area, and the natural beauty of the region adds to the charm of the college.

Initially, I was concerned that Prescott might not be well-known on the East Coast, but I’ve found that the program has a strong reputation among those familiar with it. In fact, the first counseling facility I was hired at was founded on the West Coast and recognized the quality of Prescott’s program. I also recently passed the CPCE, a requirement for graduation and proof that this CACREP program turns out well rounded students.

The college’s emphasis on social justice and environmental awareness is not just lip service, it’s woven into the curriculum and encouraged in practice. This focus has set Prescott apart from other counseling programs I’ve encountered, and I value the emphasis on systemic change and advocacy.

I highly recommend Prescott College to self-motivated adult students who are looking to earn their master’s degree without putting their lives on hold. If you’re someone who values flexibility, self-paced, supportive environment, and a program that aligns with social justice and environmental values, Prescott is an excellent choice. That said, if you’re looking to build a strong social network during grad school, it may require extra effort, as the program is designed for independent learners. However, I’ve enjoyed getting to know my peers through group projects and have made valuable professional connections along the way.

Overall, my experience at Prescott College has been transformative, and I am grateful for the opportunity to grow both personally and professionally through this program.", 'I attended Prescott College for only one year, way back in 1999.  However it was a year that totally changed my life, my direction, and my ability to believe in myself.  The Professors, Staff, and fellow students were incredible, and the independence that the college afforded was so unlike any other college experience I have seen or heard of.  (I have since been a Professor at three Colleges/Universities) I wish more students would be able to experience the kind of focused, self-directed learning that Prescott College allowed.   Although I left Prescott to pursue other directions, it will forever hold a very special place in my heart.', 'RUN AWAY quickly if you’re considering the online Clinical Mental Health Graduate degree program and value integrity, education, and justice. By far one of the lowest quality “educational” experiences I’ve ever had. Please do your research and check out other programs, because this one isn’t in alignment with its mission statement. For the high price tag and low quality, save your time, money, and mental health, because this isn’t the place.

During recruitment, they’ll point out the statistics about students’ exam passing percentages, but I urge you to look more closely at the program completion rates…. It’s low and for a reason. With the acceptance rate being high, for a reason.

Also, from what I witnessed, faculty and staff retention within the program was laughable. Not sure how this program is still accredited, because the number of professors I witness come and go appeared rather high.

This is a business and poorly run at best. Once deemed the school that “won’t die”, but in my opinion probably should.

The infrastructure lacks the necessary resources to provide quality, thus leaving the students with subpar book recommendations with irrelevant material, a lack of support from both faculty and staff, along with mind numbingly boring and pointless forum posts with several courses including the SAME 4 question prompt. The same four questions people, in several courses and with different professors. It seems lazy and when I pointed that out to the former associate Dean of the department and self proclaimed “gatekeeper”, who ironically could be used as case study on ethics in regards to her clinical work, got rather defensive of said questions in question.

The professors nor cohort have the capacity to connect despite it being a helping profession. There are those that try their best; however, unfortunately, this system doesn’t appear to assist anyone, not even those on the payroll.

So, again if you value quality and education look elsewhere, because this isn’t it, from what I’ve experienced.

If you value critical thinking, run faster.
So many of my peers voiced being “afraid” to speak up about anything from fear of “punishment” by others including faculty, staff, and students due to the brainwashed institutionalized “woke” ideologies being forced upon them. No conversation just condemnation…. Huh doesn’t sound like justice to me.

And if that isn’t enough, ask them about how they manage their finances. Your tuition is being used to support the development of several other programs in a seemingly unsustainable way, but hey one of the buildings got a new paint job.

Perhaps the undergraduate experience is better, but I’ve heard grievances and complaints about administration not addressing issues and concerns, but am unable to speak on that.

What I can speak on is how it appears as though this program’s approach is unethical and unsupportive if you don’t fit into their academic boxes. They say you have flexibility and freedom, but you don’t. If you question anything, one runs the risk of punishment by the “gatekeepers”. They are the game masters and one must abide by their rules despite how nonsensical and contradictory they may seem. Authoritarianism?

This program doesn’t appear to facilitate quality counselors. Those that can write a 10-12 page academic paper aren’t necessarily the ones that make for quality counselors. If you actually care about the counseling field, consider practically any other program out there besides this one. Trust me, you’ll be glad you looked elsewhere.

Edit: for fun, I recommend checking out the college’s tax filings on the IRS website. Prescott College is a private school with nonprofit status. Here’s their EIN: 86-0294012
Check out how much they paid for marketing. I wonder if they spent a fraction of that on cybersecurity. By the way, while also enrolled, there was a security breach that compromised sensitive data which is more than likely being sold on the dark web. Thanks Prescott College glad you could pay your head of marketing so well.', 'Changed my life. They gave me a second chance at an education/life that was so unfamiliar but made perfect sense. It all made sense, why I never “got” school. Our orientation was camping at the bottom of the Grand Canyon... who can say that? Prescott college told me I could do whatever I wanted to if I worked for it. Now a decade later, I can say I’m a much better person for going to PC, with such amazing professors and humans. I’m now an MSW, and going for my LCSW (Clinical Social Work). Thank you for helping me become someone who believes in themselves.', 'Current student and I am loving the hands on inclusive approach of faculty members. Your classroom is unbound with experiential learning at its finest. I have been inspired by fellow students and staff and honestly feel prepared after completing my undergraduate degree. If you love the outdoors, embrace close community, care for the environment and want control of your educational direction this college is for you!']

name: Scottsdale Community College
reviews:
['Semi-decent community college for what it is. Out of all the community colleges, I definitely like this one the most, mainly because of convenience. However, it lacks useful faculty, resources, and clubs. In comparison, Mesa CC had a ton of clubs to choose from amongst their many established campuses, but the Dobson one had more than SCC has currently active, and for Scottsdale, I thought they’d have more when initially choosing this as my primary college, especially for pre-meds. I took a BIO class at Mesa and was taken aback by how my teacher was encouraging us to pursue the clubs offered there and research opportunities. Scottsdale's selection of BIO teachers is the same every semester, with no variety in that department whatsoever. Definitely look around at the other community colleges if you want more active faculty, club facilitators, and student body. Resource-wise pertaining to internships and jobs, you can join a Canvas group centralized on what you're studying. However, they posted this too-good-to-be-true "opportunity" from "Vector Marketing," which is like a total scam! I couldn't believe they actually posted that in one of the communities (business, I think?) on Canvas. Now, for my assigned advisors, I've had the misfortune of dealing with, simply are terrible! My whole time I've been here, I've put together my entire course schedule each semester, except for my first semester when I trusted those vultures to take into consideration my time, money, and willingness of how much I wanted on my plate. They're also extremely snarky and brag about their experience of being advisors for over TWENTY YEARS!!! I'm transferring to the four-year uni's and my counselor made the effort to reach out to me before I could get a chance to reach out to them and scheduled me into my courses a year in advance. I was in awe considering the support SCC's advisors gave me. Now for assignments pertaining to the writing center available on campus and online, it's a hit or miss. I got one feedback on my assignment in which the learning facilitator of the writing center let her anger consume her judgment of my paper and gave me a bunch of marks that were just point-blank invalid, especially since she didn't do background research on the stuff I mentioned and just commented on whatever she perceived was wrong based on her opinion. I submitted the assignment w/o correction to my teacher, and she graded it with full marks, so even if I made the "corrections" according to the writing center's "feedback," it wouldn't have mattered.\xa0The teacher's vary depending on the class you take. You can get bad ones and good ones. After taking classes all over the Maricopa Community College system, I can say most of them suck. Most of the time you're just teaching yourself because some respond late and also expect the best out of you (especially no ai use while also secretly using it themselves) and making spelling/grammar errors on quizzes that are critical to your grade since missing one question brings your grade down a whole level. I once had a quiz question that had two of the same answers while simultaneously not displaying the correct answer. The instructor was not lenient and expected everyone to just take the hit on their grade percentage. I suggest doing thorough research on the rate my professor website. Sometimes it's helpful and sometimes it's not, but you can get a good idea of whether a teacher is worth taking. The hardest part of graduating from college isn’t the curriculum itself; it’s the teachers.

The positives are the bookstore employees and guys in carts on campus (I'm sorry, I'm unsure of what their occupation title is), but they're chill and super nice. name: University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff
reviews:
['I attended this university because I believed in its mission and legacy. There are strong programs here, especially their favorites agriculture, nursing, and certain teaching and STEM areas. Those departments receive visible support and structure.

However, the overall professional infrastructure needs immediate improvement.
The most urgent issue is career development and degree value
Right now, professional support feels inconsistent across majors. Some programs have strong pathways. Others lack:

* Professional clubs tied to careers
* Industry partnerships
* Clear internship pipelines
* Structured alumni mentorship
* Consistent employer engagement

An annual job fair is not enough in 2026.
The job market has shifted. Since 2023, hiring has become:

* Skills-based
* AI-influenced
* Credential-heavy
* Highly competitive

Students cannot afford to graduate without clear direction. Degrees must be evaluated by:

* Job placement rates
* Median starting salaries
* Long-term return on investment

If a program does not lead to economic mobility, it must be restructured. College is too expensive for students to leave unsure of how they will earn a living.

There is also a need for stronger coordination across departments. Units feel siloed. Career services, faculty, and administration must work together intentionally. Professional development should be embedded into the academic culture, not treated as an add-on.

Merit-based scholarships also need to be strengthened. High-performing students should automatically receive financial recognition based on GPA. Many institutions do this as a standard practice. It improves retention and motivates excellence.

Housing conditions require urgent attention as well. Concerns include:

* Poor bathroom conditions
* Pest issues
* Aging dorm infrastructure

Living conditions directly affect:

* Mental health
* Academic performance
* Retention

If housing quality does not improve, pricing should reflect that reality.

This university has legacy and potential. But legacy alone is not enough in today’s economy.

To remain competitive and protect students’ futures, the institution must urgently:

* Build stronger, consistent career pipelines
* Ensure equity and support across all majors or cut the certain major
* Tie degrees to measurable economic outcomes, reevalute them  yearly
* Strengthen merit-based financial recognition
* Upgrade housing standards

The longer these issues go unaddressed, the harder it will be to retain students and remain competitive. Improvement is possible, but it needs to happen now.', 'I love my HBCU. My Dear Mother. Come experience the love and become Part of the Pride.', 'Visited one time with family members. It is a beautiful place and an ideal university for someone who wants to get a good quality education, while living a smaller city. The campus is well organized and centrally located to different shops. I feel like a person would enjoy this environment while receiving a good education', "Provided opportunities I would have never gotten if I had not attended, I met Life long friends and had the opportunity to visit them in there hometown. Ive gotten job opportunities because of Alumni that attended. It was just over all a lifetime great experience that I'm glad I experienced thanks UAPB", "This school has the WORSE financial aid department in my opinion that I have ever experienced, they awarded me someone else's scholarship, did not notify me until a month later, and then hassled me about reimbursement (plus informed me that I would not be able to start the next school year until it was paid). Incompetence is an understatement.  I thought I would love my experience at an HBCU, but I am now wishing that I would have just stayed in Conway."]

name: Arkansas State University-Beebe
reviews: ['Excellent school. Dr Battershell sparked my interest in chemistry. I went on to Jonesboro and got a masters in chemistry and then on to Kansas City and got my degree in osteopathic medicine. I owe it all to Beebe. .', 'My "Temporary Advisor" scheduled me for a class I didn\'t need the first semester I was there. I didn\'t know I didn\'t need the class until I finally got to see my real advisor a month later and he said it was too late to switch out. That was a waste of money. When I was letting my real advisor schedule my classes for me I ended up 3 classes short of what I needed to get my degree and he failed to inform me that if I changed from a 3 credit P.E. (even though I only need 1 hour) to a 2 hour, I would loose my scholarship. Another waste of money. I had to take a summer class to get part of my scholarship back. The class started right before I had the money saved, I was only $150 short, and they kicked me out the second day. So here I am setting up my fall schedule. $1,400 seems cheap for two sciences and a fine arts. However, if i don\'t have the full payment by the day before class they kick me out. There are payment options. For this amount it will be over $350 a month, starting the day before class! I am doing this on my own, working full time while trying to get a degree. This school is sucking its working students dry!', 'The school doesn\'t care enough to assist students in dire needs with obtaining financial aid in a timely fashion or assisting students with disabilities. Only a few of the teachers I encountered were helpful and reasonable...the rest would rather take the first opportunity to tell you to drop if you have any issues (even if your only issue is related to not receiving financial aid for supplies). The school won\'t refund if they push you to drop a class...or if you are failed due to lack of supplies from financial aid issues. Last term, I didn\'t get my aid until school was over...this term...the month before the end (so if you need aid to attend...choose elsewhere!!). None of the supplies and additional labs/observations are listed on the roster when you sign up (like textbooks are)...so you don\'t know until you\'ve wasted money on the book and entered that there are hidden fees. Most teachers choose not to answer (especially not in a timely fashion in order to not be late on assignments...which they also do not give full credit for...even though you were waiting on their response to multiple requests for help) or give snarky responses of "google does wonders" even though the assignment gives a website...with conflicting data and you\'re unsure which set of numbers to use (as one example). Two terms of financial aid issues...and tons of credit card and bank fees later...and now I cannot get the degree...no longer eligible for aid. I had all A\'s before...4.0...and all the completed work was excellent. To top it off, their online program is a mess...blackboard issues with no mobile access, old assignments with dead links and mixed up, pasted questions, deadlines that are erratic and constant (rather than having the freedom online is supposed to offer), apathetic teachers that, among many things, don\'t utilize the calendar tool (so you have to hunt through link after link to be sure no work or test was added)...etc. They will screw you over and not even take the time to reply (in most cases) or assist you...for your sanity and to have a chance to better yourself...choose a better online option (I cannot speak for all in-person classes but between the student forums and the physical class I took, I do not recommend that either...with teachers choosing not to show up, respond or send a message about not being there...and only finding out from a taped paper on the door after you waste a trip)!! Oh...and back when I was a military spouse and saw my husband off to Iraq, the teachers stated they would allow make-up of midterms and assignments upon my return...they lied...failed me...and the school never attempted to fix the issue after contacting them repeatedly. They want the money from having students but not to actually work on making it a good experience.', 'The director is never there to their job, and financial aid is basically two people trying to deal with the whole school. YOU WILL HAVE TO give them all of their paperwork at least 3 times because they always lose it. Worst administration I’ve ever seen at a school.', "Beautiful campus excellent staff & professors! reviews: ['There is a good amount of age and race diversity in this small campus. There are fun social events as well as opportunities to listen to various speakers every few weeks throughout the semester (with snacks provided). It is also a beautiful and well maintained campus. name: Arkansas State University Mid-South
reviews: ["This review is in regards to the disc golf course and not the college itself. The course was uneventful and hardly worth the time. There are very few holes with any sort of technical shots involved. It really came down to how far you can throw your disc. The majority of holes followed the perimeter of soccer fields and many were along side roads, driveways and parking lots. If it was busy or the lots were full of cars, I wouldn't recommend playing even though the before mentioned were considered out of bounds. Many tee pads were far away from the previous basket, making it a hike between holes (not the worse thing). Signage was the best part of this course. Once you find the main map, the layout is fairly simple (which wasn't the case for me at first; played 12-18 before seeing the map). The course is also split by the main road and as someone else suggested, play the front 9 and drive over to the other parking lot to play the back 9. I'd only suggest playing this course if you live in the area and there are no other courses around. This course design feels as if the sports director of the college designed the course without having ever played the sport. But they did work with what they had. Oh and be prepared for water on the course after heavy rain fall. name: Ouachita Baptist University
reviews:
['Beautiful Campus.
Extremely friendly people at, and working at, the football game.', 'Parking for the game today was chaotic.  Stadium and services there were great.', "My four years at Ouachita Baptist University were truly memorable. Even returning to campus is always a pleasant experience, thanks to the welcoming atmosphere and friendly students and staff. It's an exciting place to learn and grow, making it a standout choice for higher education.", 'OBU is awesome 😎 The upward bound program is amazing 😍', 'Ouachita Baptist University gave me an incredible education and wonderful social network in which to grow. Intellectually and academically, I was challenged to consider other view points even though my professors themselves were Christian. The university understood that being Christian in orientation does not mean that the university should shelter students from other religions, philosophies, or so called "secular" methods. Instead, I was encouraged to explore, think, and question everything. It was a very positive and intellectually stimulating environment.

By contrast, when I studied at a top 100 university for my master's degree, many of my classmates there (who had attended famous schools like Oxford, Yale, University of Paris, etc.) simply did not have basic knowledge of history or philosophy which at Ouachita was a part of the core curriculum. I was astounded at how better prepared I was for graduate school than my classmates who had gone to famous name brand schools.

Class sizes are small. Teachers will engage you for hours in the hallways debating and discussing any subject. Many teachers live nearby which facilitates even more educational opportunities for the ambitious student who seeks them.

I strongly recommend an education at Ouachita Baptist University. If you are a Christian, your faith will be challenged and deepened. If you are not a Christian, then your worldviews will also be pushed and prodded.

Hopefully, I will continue to always strive towards knowledge and truth like Ouachita taught me to do.']

name: Arkansas State University Three Rivers
reviews:
['Mr.Bratton at this college is a pretty sucky character. Everytime I am in class or at the bookstore he always has an insult to say and is never satisfied. He claimed I was a bad role model but couldn’t back it up or answer me. Then proceeds to try and insult my mechanic knowledge just because I wouldn’t help him on his ford f250 . He likes to take sides to the females a lot over males in automotive class. I wouldn’t of commented this but it’s just never ending with him.', 'I have never written a review before, but someone very close to me had an experience with this nursing program that was so discouraging that I feel obligated to share it. The program’s leadership shows no empathy or flexibility when real-life emergencies occur nor do they take accountability for giving incorrect information over the phone.

First, the student was told over the phone while checking to make sure that all of his stuff was submitted that a mandatory meeting was the 14th when in reality it was the 13th. On the 12th the student had to have emergency dental work and on the 13th had to go back to the dentist for another emergency stemming from the work done on the 12th. Later in the day on the 13th the student received a called that he had been removed from the program completely. He met with the dean, Melinda Sanders to discuss everything that occurred in an effort to get back into the program. Instead of offering support or reasonable accommodations, she completely shut down everything that he told her. For a school that claims to train future healthcare professionals, the lack of compassion was shocking. You would expect an institution built on the values of care, understanding, and patient advocacy to extend the same courtesy to its own students, but that was not the case.

The policies are unnecessarily strict, enforced without context, and seem more focused on maintaining rigid control than actually helping students succeed. I say this because Sanders’s only reasoning for not allowing the student back in the program was that the school must maintain strict deadlines.  Life happens, and a truly supportive program would work with students, not punish them, during their most vulnerable moments.

Second, and what’s truly astonishing is that this student was on the waitlist to start the program in August and attended every single mandatory meeting without issue and was not granted admission. Nothing, and I meant nothing mattered to Sanders other than her strict adherence to deadlines.

Also, just a few things that the student was told while in the program that expand on the lack on empathy and understanding is that if you miss a clinical day you have to pay $150 to make it up even if weather conditions are bad. The school explained that if an instructor can make it you should be able as well.

If you’re considering this school, think carefully about how important empathy and student support are to you. This experience causes the program to fall far short.', "This post is specifically for Danielle Brown at ASU Three Rivers in Malvern. Thank you for going above and beyond today! I called a random number to find help because no one was answering the student account or financial aid office for the past 2 days. I emailed student account this morning and by the end of the day still hadn't received an email. Mrs. Brown did not stop until she connected me with the correct person to solve 2 of my problems and she didn't have to! She could've transferred me to the correct places voicemail! Thank you for taking time out of your day to assist me, even though it was not your area! ASUTR, you have a great jewel there!", 'We toured here today with our son. Caleb was a fantastic tour guide. Caleb had an answer for each question we asked and gave the handouts to have physical copies of answers to our questions. We had a great experience and our son will be enrolling for fall courses.
