name: Southeast Arkansas College
reviews:
['This institution has few decent instructors and relatively inexpensive programs.  I've never been much of a goody two-shoe, but I've always busted my butt to make the grades in school.

So, out of all the classes I've taken, I've got several A's and a B.  Then there's this F for the Biology class I had with Shanely.  From where?  Science is my favorite subject!  I've been working in the medical field since I graduated from Heritage College with my LMT in 2011. I then went on to receive my NREMT in 2017 at the AFTA in Camden.

Long story short (sort of): They supposedly changed the location of our final exam on the last day, but it was nowhere to be found and I was given an F for the class. My letter grade in this class was a B prior to this "Final."

Just a heads up before you read on: This is the longer version of my story.

When I showed up to our normal classroom there was a sign on the door indicating we were to take the exam in another specified room in the McGeorge building.  On arrival, there was no one in the classroom, the lights were off, and I was scratching my head.  Dismayed, I went looking into every other classroom to see if maybe I'd find anyone familiar. They were nowhere to be found!

I eventually went to the reception office at the Northeast corner of the campus to ask if they had any clue where my class or exam might be. They called around and looked at a few books/clipboards but couldn't figure it out or tell me anything.
I felt defeated and helpless, so after returning to our original room to make sure I didn't misread the sign on the door, I left.  It might not be a huge deal, but I'm stuck with a false letter grade on my record that I don't deserve.

Apart from this experience, my time here wasn't too bad.  I got a few prereqs out of the way for a low price and was on my way.  I've given the 1-star rating because no one should have to deal with the helplessness I have in dealing with this situation.

Note: The dates in the transcript screenshot aren't showing correctly for the transferred courses since they aren't in the system at UAM. My Seark debacle happened in 2013 at the age of 19.', 'If you want an easy certificate to earn that isn’t going to break your wallet, this is the place. Especially their CNA and Phlebotomy programs (shout out to Mrs. Elliott and Mrs. Lyons)

They offer great financial aid packages and scholarships that will pay for your full tuition and then some.', 'Nursing program is an unorganized nightmare, and I hope the state board never gives them back their accreditation. Not only did they fire teachers midway through the semester leaving us with no instructor, but they had non nursing staff proctor exams over material that had nothing to do with what we studied. Clinical rotations were a joke. We performed no skills outside of your basic nursing assistant care, and students were allowed to pretty much say and do whatever they wanted creating  negative atmosphere with no repercussions. The ones who survived the summer, were quickly told that the program would voluntarily withdraw their accreditation status due to low nclex scores, and downplayed the issue.', 'The worse nursing program ever! I know several students that have went here for nursing and their turnover rate is ridiculous. These students have left their jobs and families to be apart of an unorganized program. I wouldn’t recommend this school for their nursing program at all. Like I said, I haven’t attended the college, but I know SEVERAL students and good students at that who have attended and have went through it here. In my opinion, their nursing program definitely need to be investigated.', 'I had a bad experience there two years in a row. Not a good experience If they still have the same instructors there. Camp and McBride was some horrible individuals for them to be in the nursing field. They cannot teach and they act like you should already know things.']

name: University of Arkansas-Pulaski Technical College
reviews: ['These people steal your money. I took an 8 week course with inclusive access for the books. However my teacher never made the book available and didn’t respond for 3 weeks to give me access. So I dropped the course. However the school is still making me pay 1200$ for the class they never gave my book for and the instructor never taught. Absolute scam of a school for people just trying to better their lives. Oh and I appealed it and was supposed to receive a response mid December however it’s January 6th now and every attempt I have made to get an answer has been met with long holds over the phone where they eventually just hang up. It’s impossible to even talk to anyone in records and in the registers office about it. Like I said, absolute scam of a school. Don’t let these people steal your money, you are better off going to UALR.', 'The premises are spacious, and the interior is well-maintained and pleasant. However, the staff handling adult education inquiries lacked professionalism. Correspondence via email was inadequate, and despite my visit on the appointed day, it was unexpectedly canceled without any notification. I had to adjust my work schedule but ended up having my plans disrupted. This level of disappointment and negligence is unacceptable and should not be overlooked. I suggest exploring alternative educational institutions and facilities for adult education before considering this option.', 'I don’t understand the purpose of having a phone and advising people to contact departments that simply do not answer. For the sake of PTC, I’m going to assume that they’re short staffed in Admissions, Advising and Records. I have never been told “your estimated wait time is 3 minutes” so many times in my life! I hope the success rate isn’t equivalent to the success rate of communication here. Hire me! I’ll answer the phones. My goodness!', 'I have not experienced any of the problems of not being able to get anything done. I simply went to the school and talked to the appropriate people and from start to finish i was enrolled and ready to go in two weeks. This is a great community college and now that they are in the U of A system its awesome that the transistion to a 4 year is so seemless. I highly recommend this school if someone doesnt want to take out a buch of loans starting out. And the teachers and staff have been very helpful and friendly. Its always easier to do something in person.', 'Pulaski Technical college is literally a blessing to go too. Ive attended two additional colleges besides Pulaski Technical College for 3 years. I wasn’t even close to finishing school at all until, I started at Pulaski Technical College last November of 2019. I was open to starting at another college although, for a reason. I didn’t seem to get any further at all until, I met Mrs. Sandy and Mrs. Stephanie. they are literally the greatest the teachers and there are no words to express just how thankful I truly am to have had the chance to have them both as my teachers.']

name: University of Arkansas Hope-Texarkana
reviews: ["In my opinion the school is a nice school with great people. Without a place to review their bookstore I must come here. I have never been so displeased with a bookstore in my entire life. The opt in opt out thing is ridiculous. In case you don't know this already this is where you must choose to rent all your books or none of your books from the bookstore. Some people may be like oh that's not so bad because they are $20 a credit hour so usually $60 or $80 for classes with a lab. That's fine and all except you can BUY most of the books for cheaper than $60 or $80. I could forgive all this because I can go online and buy them. However I've seen 3 instances where the bookstore refused to give the ISBN number to students for the books they need for their class. Plus right now my wife is going through nursing school and they want her to sign a contract that says that she will pay for all the books through them for the year and they will hold them for her. Now financial aid will pay for them in the spring ... We don't know about the summer or fall yet because of our financial changes. Unlike the other books in their rental program most of these books are a lot more expensive. She gets to keep most of them as well. The two most expensive ones however are supposed to be returned... That's the school bookstore for you.", "The University of Arkansas is growing and expanding in positive ways and into Texarkana.  This outstanding campus is located on U of A Way near UAMS' new medical site.  The university is near the Four States Fairgrounds and across from a local park, Bobby Ferguson Park.  It's rapidly getting ready to stand on it's on and the signs have already changed to U of A at Texarkana.", "Went here for a few years it's small, teachers were nice and helpful. name: Southern Arkansas University Main Campus
reviews:
["Southern Arkansas University is truly a lovely place. I am going into my senior year this August and am do excited to see what it has in store for me.

Freshman year was a little hard, but SAU has several activities for you to get to know people and make friends (a few of them are mandatory).

I'm in the Honors College which has allowed me to experience several interesting field trips and allowed me to travel abroad to France for 1 week.

Deana Taylor is wonderful. Take a moment to introduce yourself to her because she will help you throughout your time at SAU.

It's a growing community, but everybody seems to be close here (and friendly).

The cafeteria recently expanded and has gotten much better food.

The older dorms are okay, but I definitely suggest the newer dorms, University Hall, Honors North (not South), or The Village.

I'm going for my BBA in Marketing and love it so far. The professors are helpful and the courses (at least the marketing courses) are quite interesting!

If you feel like giving up after your first year  just know this: after my freshman year I was suicidal. I hated life and didn't want to continue on. I moved home for the summer and got healthier. I was around family and good friends and it completely reshaped my life. I am now graduating in one year, have a marketing internship this summer, am in a healthy and loving relationship, and cannot wait to see where life takes me. College can be hard at first, no matter where you are. Make a friend, reach out to others, call your family, and get out there. Get involved. You've got this, and SAU is a great place to start your adult journey.", "It has been 18 years since I stepped foot on campus. The café has been expanded, they have changed the meal policies to better accommodate people from all ethnic backgrounds. You can get meals to-go if being around tons of people isn't your thing. Cheap and good food. 10/10 would recommend.", 'Perfect, most cost-effective university! Everyone (but the head of the nursing department) is professional and friendly!', "I graduated from SAU in 2000. My education was a great preparation for career success. My daughter is now attending SAU as an Honor student. SAU is expanding and offering many diverse options. I'm proud to be a Mulerider & continuing the tradition. I encourage potential students to tour the campus. We are so pleased SAU now waives out of state tuition for Claiborne Parish as well as other bordering counties and parishes. Based on generous academic scholarships, SAU costs less than an in state school with Honors TOPS and additional academic scholarships. The cost difference was not the only reason we chose SAU but certainly a contributing factor. This school offers the hands on attention of a private school with the value of a state school.  Come see what SAU has to offer before deciding on your college.", "My son was supposed to be in the first engineering class or so we were told. The advisor had him take classes he didn't need to take. And yes I was involved in the process. Three years later they still dont have an engineering accreditation even though its in their degree plans. They put him down as physics with an engineering emphasis. This is not an engineer. They can never tell me how much his school is going to cost until halfway through the semester. I had to pull him out and enroll him in a real school."]

name: College of Alameda
reviews:
['Visited the campus.  It is a small college with nice staff.  The facilities are nice!  Transportation is good with many bus lines servicing the campus!  I enjoyed the visit!', 'This is my favorite college! Although it doesn’t have some classes I need, it’s the best college I have seen.

This college truly stands out as a gem among Bay Area schools. From the moment you step on campus, you feel the good vibes — the atmosphere is peaceful, welcoming, and full of positive energy. The beautifully maintained gardens and clean surroundings reflect the care and pride the community takes in the environment.

The professors here are exceptional, with many holding PhDs and bringing a wealth of knowledge and passion into the classroom. But what makes this place even more special is the people — students, staff, and faculty alike are warm, friendly, and genuinely supportive. You can feel that everyone here wants each other to succeed.

Compared to other colleges like Laney, Merritt, Berkeley City, or SF City College, this school shines with its outstanding resources and generous book grants that help students thrive without financial stress. The counselors are some of the best — caring deeply about students’ emotional well-being, academic progress, and personal growth.

It’s no wonder students here feel happy, motivated, and empowered. This is more than just a college — it’s a community where people grow together.', "the admin & record lady with very dark lip stick and wavy hair, she's very impolite and unhelpful, making things harder than it should be.
very frustrated experience.", 'Great campus, clean classrooms and facilities, amazing staff and plenty of classes and courses to pick from', "The atech department is 5/5 I lolove all the staff there. They work on customer cars too at a labor rate of 25 an hour. Why it gets 4/5 is because they just shutdown the book store. You must goto laney for scantrons and and books, and since they don't have the classes it'll have to be ordered."]

name: Allan Hancock College
reviews:
["Im halfway done with AHC and I have absolutely no regrets with choosing to go here. With all the programs offered and the helpful staff and environment it made being away from school for 10 years and 3 kids later not so hard. Im in the CARE program for parents and apart of the Learning Assistance Program for extra support and financially it has its benefits as well as a student. I feel cared for and I know where to go if I need help. You get the results that you put into your education. The only way out of poverty is through an education. The EOPS department has gone above and beyond for me and my family. I mainly do online classes, but there's only been one class I had to go to in person for my specific degree because of the lab needed. So glad I went to my local community college.", 'First year back in many moons. It was a learing curve for sure since everything is online. Took a min to learn the Canvas app and navigate thru the school website. The good thing is they do have very friendly staff that is very willing to help. Which made it a much more user friendly experience. The campus is easy to understand and navigate thru and the amenities are top notch.', "A bit late for a review, but better late than never. Started here Fall 2016 as a non-traditional student. I transferred to Cal State Channel Islands Fall 2019. In the 2.5 years I was at AHC, I met some wonderful, amazing people. The school has a reputation for being the college version of a feeder school. In other words, students can start here and get into places like Cal Poly, or indeed any of the other Cal State or UC Schools if they work hard and play their cards right. That definitely isn't the case elsewhere.There's tons of scholarships and support programs available with a good chance of getting accepted as well. Like most things in college, you get out of it what you put into it. The only downside is it's a bit of a commuter school. When classes let out, the place turns into a ghost town because most of the students commute in and have part time jobs along with studying. That being said, the teachers and counselors really do care about the students here.", "I just finished my first semester as a returning student.  I am very impressed with the improvements the college has implemented since I have been away.  Each department has implemented strategies which will allow students to have more effective communication channels and will allow them to have a higher success rate.  The student body Government is doing great and developing awesome new community leaders in the process.  People here are super accepting of people's diverse backgrounds and this is a great place to go to learn about our culture in a safe environment for people from all walks of life.

I am super proud to be a student at Allan Hancock College and I am looking forward to the next semester.  Hancock is now offering a program offered by them through Cal Poly San Luis Obispo called 2 + 2.  This allows Hancock to offer students the ability to get a four yearw degree in Sociology and Business!  I am a business major and I am way happy about this and will look forward to new four year degree offerings.

The Hancock bookstore is operated by Follett, who has a long and proud history providing text materials to education for years.  They are a great resource and I am so happy to have such a prestigious institution helping us get the materials we need to be successful.

Thank you Allan Hancock College for providing such a safe and awesome educational experience for anyone who wishes to enrich their educational experience with a tradition of excellence in providing the best instructors and classes that are available for any person who wants to better themselves with no exception!", 'I attended AHC and played on the soccer team.  This was a while back but my overall experience there was great.  Easy parking, not over crowded and the counselors were great in assisting me as I transferred to Cal Poly.  Save some cash and go to AHC!!!!!  Worth it.']

name: American River College
reviews:
["I have visited the application lab at American River College about three or four times this month. Each time, I noticed that the staff are professional in appearance, wearing heels and professional clothing. However, their behavior does not seem to match their appearance. Some staff members have been rude and unfriendly. I observed girls speaking negatively about others and not offering help unless they favor someone. During my visits, which have totaled five, I felt quite upset about how some girls behave. I have seen others facing similar issues. I believe the staff at the lab lack professionalism; many only focus on their appearance rather than assisting students properly. It's important that the college trains its employees better, especially those in the application lab and financial aid office. Respect and helpfulness should be priorities. Staff should treat all visitors with kindness, regardless of appearance, and recognize that they represent the college. Right now, I feel disappointed and unwelcome, which has made me decide not to use the services there anymore.
They speak favorably and offer help only to people they personally like, while others are ignored. Instead of focusing on education or student support, the attention is placed on appearance—such as makeup, clothing, which is completely irrelevant.

This raises a serious concern about whether American River College prioritizes education or favoritism. I specifically experienced discrimination from two young female staff members who openly treated me differently. Their behavior appeared to be influenced by bias related to language and religion.

I clearly heard them speaking negatively about me in another language, assuming I would not understand. When I addressed it and informed them that I do understand the language, I expressed that this behavior was inappropriate and unfair", 'Nice staff but rude counselors. Most low star reviews will agree with me. The staff and professors here are pretty nice and helpful but I haven’t had one nice counselor ever sense I attended here and I’m in my final semester. These counselors are unprofessional and I have seen 4 different ones. I originally thought it was just one mean one when I first attended but after seeing 4 I come to realize the school needs to restaff there counseling department. My old CC counseling department had to help me with my classes for ARC from a completely different district. This is how unprofessional the councilors are here and that’s very embarrassing. Also I keep sending my transcripts to the correct email and ARC still claims they don’t have a record of them.', "I love studying here!!!
Everyone always willing to help, everything is accessible and easy.
There are free books in library, lots of places to study inside or outside, water, very clean toilets with hygiene items.
I'm very grateful to workers who planted these extremely beautiful flowers we have in our college.
I really love walking in parks, so I really enjoy walking around campuses
You can choose good professors from ratemyprofessor website.
All of them are really helpful in my nursing journey.
I became an A grade student in this college and I have honors for good GPA
College is accessible for me and now it's free because of the FAFSA which they can help you apply to", 'if I could rewind time, I absolutely would have chosen ARC over the disaster that is UC Davis.

UC Davis looked great on paper — respected UC, good rankings, etc. But the reality? Overpriced, toxic, and full of ego-fueled nonsense. Professors were checked out, advisors were unreachable, and the entire place ran on cliques and politics. Career support was a joke. I got a degree and zero direction.

I’ve spoken with ARC students who got practical, affordable, and actually supportive education — for a fraction of what I paid. While I was drowning in student debt and academic gatekeeping, they were building skills and transferring out with real options.

So no, I didn’t go to ARC. But if you’re stuck choosing between a “prestigious” name like UC Davis and something grounded like ARC — don’t fall for the brand. Learn from my mistake. Go where people care….', 'Terrible counseling experience with Mays J counselor. Very rude and condescending during the entire practice. Unprofessional. As someone who’s graduated from this college it’s very disappointing seeing the counselor treat my wife so poorly. After explaining the situation, Mays J chooses to be rude and unhelpful over the situation. It’s my wife’s first time at college and just trying to prepare for her program. And 2nd guessing her after she chooses every program or classes needed for her road map of success. We remained professional of course just wish she did the same and not try to talk down on my wife for trying to just get started.']

name: Antelope Valley Community College District
reviews:
['Let me start by saying the campus is very nice and clean! The admissions and financial aid staff, on the other hand, is pretty much useless. They are decently friendly, but it seems like no one at the desk is ever authorized to actually do anything aside from taking your info down and saying they’ll reach out to you (no one ever reaches out, by the way, shocker). I’ve visited over 8-10 times in the last 5 months, and the "higher-ups" are always out of the office or in meetings—every single time.

I applied in August 2025 and it took 2 weeks and 3 visits just for them to even find my application because it supposedly got "filed into spam." Most CCs take 48 hours MAX. Because of that "spam incident," my financial aid was severely delayed.

Even though I’m a California native, they flagged me as a non-resident and said they needed my official high school transcripts to prove it. Contacting LAUSD for transcripts is a nightmare and takes 3-4 months, but the admissions supervisor gave me a verbal green light to take my Fall classes anyway. She promised they would backdate the waiver and clear the non-resident tuition once the transcripts arrived.

I finally brought my transcripts in today, and now they’re saying it’s 50/50 if the dean will even honor that since the Fall semester is already over. To make it worse, the dean has been out for the last 2 days and they had no idea when she’d even be back. They refused to even schedule an in person appointment with her for me. I even offered to set it for this Friday or even weeks out and told them they could just call to cancel if she wasn’t in, and they still said no. If someone is going to be out indefinitely, they need to bring in someone else to fill in and handle their responsibilities! I understand things and emergencies happen, but there is still business to be handled.

Now they’re saying they can guarantee Spring will be cleared, but I can’t enroll in any classes until the $500 Fall balance is paid. What sense does that make?? Had I known this would happen, I never would’ve enrolled for Fall, but I trusted the supervisor’s word.

I’m beyond disappointed. The staff is friendly, but they need a new chain of command if the bosses are always gone. It shouldn’t be this hard to better my future. I’m now pursuing enrollment at another college because I can’t deal with this faulty system anymore.

Advice to future students: save yourself the headache and explore other schools if you can. If you do happen to end up here DO NOT  take verbal promises here. Get everything time-stamped and in writing or you’ll end up stuck with a bill you weren't expecting.', 'Great school to achieve academic success, there are a lot of programs that offer assistance paying for classes. name: Bakersfield College
reviews:
['I attended UC Davis, and honestly, it was one of the most disappointing and unhealthy academic environments I’ve experienced. Despite its reputation, the culture felt far more toxic than collaborative. Instead of genuine mentorship or intellectual growth, I encountered cliques, academic politics, and a lot of performative behavior. Decisions often seemed driven by ego, networking games, and optics rather than student development or real career outcomes.

What stood out most was how shallow the intellectual culture often felt. There was a strong sense of academic arrogance without the substance to back it up. Many people relied heavily on the school’s name rather than actual critical thinking or competence, yet were quick to dismiss or undermine those who genuinely challenged ideas or demonstrated real ability. Truly capable or independent thinkers were often treated harshly, while mediocrity was rewarded as long as it fit the social and political mold. There was very little self-awareness, and few people seemed to recognize their own limitations.

Support was minimal where it mattered most. Advisors were overextended, professors often felt detached, and the guidance students received was generic and impersonal. If you weren’t already well-connected or positioned at the very top, it was easy to fall through the cracks. The system seemed to reward visibility and conformity more than intelligence, effort, or potential.

The financial side makes it even harder to justify. The cost is enormous, yet many graduates leave earning about the same as an Uber driver, which raises serious questions about value and return. A prestigious name doesn’t mean much when it fails to translate into meaningful career stability or long-term growth.

Bakersfield College, by contrast, was refreshingly honest and grounded. It emphasized real skills, real outcomes, and actual learning. Professors were accessible and invested, advisors knew my name, and the environment encouraged progress instead of posturing. The education was hands-on, career-oriented, and built to help students move forward without unnecessary ego or gatekeeping.

When it comes to return on investment, the difference is obvious. Bakersfield College prepared me to earn, transfer, and grow—without crushing debt, wasted time, or false promises.

If I could go back, I would skip UC Davis entirely and start at Bakersfield College. For me, it delivered more value, more support, and a far more realistic and respectful path forward.', 'Just needed to write this review. When you call the direct number to get a hold of them, it’s like the girls have a problem with the other girls. I’ve called literally eight times straight and no answer and they kept hanging Up the phone because it would ring two times then three times then one time & etc.  I told my husband can he call And lord and behold, they answered the first ring because It had  a guy’s name as the caller ID. If you are triggered by the same gender as you, you really need a new job. So unprofessional And weird.', "Seriously. Tell your IT team to review their firewall for emails. You guys are often blocking edu domains and custom domains. It's very difficult as a researcher speaking with students or responding to your students who inquire about my work.", 'attended UC Davis and honestly, it was one of the most overrated and toxic experiences of my academic life. The environment was full of mediocrity and full of backstabbing, not collaboration. Instead of support and mentorship, I found cliques, politics, and a lot of performative academics and ass kissing and ego driven decision that did nothing to help my actual career.

And let’s talk about money—UC Davis costs upwards of $35,000+ a year. For what? A name brand that doesn’t guarantee a job, especially when half the “guidance” comes from overbooked advisors and disconnected professors. If you’re not in the top 5% or already well-connected, it’s easy to get lost and left behind.

Bakersfield College, on the other hand, is honest, affordable, and practical. I paid less than $2,000 a year, got hands-on training, real-world career pathways, and transfer options that didn’t bankrupt me. I had professors who actually cared, a flexible schedule, and advisors who knew my name.

ROI? Not even close. BC set me up to earn, transfer, and grow—without crushing debt or wasted time.

If I could go back, I’d skip UC Davis entirely and go straight to Bakersfield College. That’s the truth.', "I am having the worst time here. The BC advisor, Brynn, is screwing me up so badly by taking classes I don't need and didn't tell me that I need 60 units to graduate, and that's both in early childhood and General Education. I tried another BC counselor, and she hasn't responded to me in three weeks! They are useless. I am not getting any guidance or anything except for Brynn telling me to take classes that I don't need and putting me into this statistics class without telling me that I needed to take intermediate algebra before taking this class. And I told her I haven't taken a math class in years, and I am bad at math, and she won't listen to me. She is refusing to answer my emails and refusing to see me. I told her about this English teacher who gave me all the points for my assignments, and the teacher went back and regraded all of it, and Brynn did nothing. I just found out that I need to take General Math 101 before I take other math classes, and of course, Brynn didn't tell me that either. I have to have other people tell me what I should take because these counselors aren't doing their damn job. Brynn and other counselors need to be better at their or BC should fire them. I told Brynn I won't transfer to Cal State but she's gonna try and make me put in a transfer. Once again, she and everyone at BC aren't listening to me. I am being ignored by everyone. I can't find the dean's name anywhere on the site. Don't come here!"]

name: Cabrillo College
reviews:
['Cleanliness is definitely not a priority at this campus. While the outside of the school is surrounded by beautiful trees, the overall campus is filthy and outdated. There are ants in the library. The cafeteria has an unpleasant odor. The tables and chairs are sticky, and the floors are unclean in the cafeteria. There are also no visible cleaning supplies available for students to wipe down tables before or after eating which adds to the unsanitary environment. The bathrooms are equally disappointing outdated and not enough space just crowded dirty, a lack of basic supplies. The unpleasant smell and poor maintenance make it uncomfortable to use them, traffic builds up in the morning and afternoon better off taking classes in the Watsonville campus or online.', 'I’m a first year student at Cabrillo college and have been having a terrible time as a new student. Their staff is lacks communication and is rude for some reason. I would not recommend coming here unless you want to wait on people who can’t respond to simple emails and people who will give you a snarky and rude attitude!', "Easy to study on this library. Amazing views from almost the entire campus! Happy it's nearby.", "This is one of the most beautiful campuses I have ever been on. It is quite hilly and large too, with so many elevation changes that stairs and elevators are a way of life here. Student parking can be a bit far from class sometimes, since priority was given to foot/ bike travel when this place was built.

This community college has many program choices, focusing on STEAM, dental and nursing, with a budding horticulture program that is well worth a visit + a construction program that prepares students for estimating and project management. They run on a semester system.

One can simply achieve their standard Associates degree here, e.g. business, liberal arts, etc. or, go after one of the concentration programs. A visit with an academic counselor will help sort that out.

The cafeteria offers a few culinary options, such as an internal taqueria station, prepackaged sushi rolls and salads, fresh fruits, a salad bar and regular diner-style foods. There is an over priced cafe in the main quad area, with often sassy workers. Follow the sound of a playlist blasting from a Bluetooth speaker to find it.

The culture is very liberal, which can be supportive but exhausting when everyone needs to be a victim that needs to be heard. The campus resources are hit or miss; the NEST is almost worthless, the accessibility center is extremely helpful, the tutoring HUB is a grade-saver when some class subjects are difficult to grasp alone, the bike co-op is a nice idea but doesn't get a lot of use, the veteran support seemed a little lacking, EOPS is very helpful, Guardian Scholars is supportive. There is a daycare center onsite, so parents of little ones have no excuse. There are more, I just can't remember them all. The campus bookstore is recently shutdown, so now all textbook orders are handled online. Not sure I like that part.

Ultimately, this is a beautiful place to spend one's day learning and building long lasting skills, networks and friendships.", 'I went here for three years. Cabrillo’s classes and great professors helped me prepare to transfer to a UC, and for that I’m very grateful! I didn’t have much contact with the counseling department and found my own research for transferring to be far more helpful. The ASC (accessibility support center) was very helpful for my accommodation needs. Reasonable tuition prices. It is a campus where everyone pretty much does their own thing, but I liked it here.']

NOT worth the debt, quality of classes is terrible in general, don’t go if you can.', 'I was disappointed to see that in one of this college’s graduation projects, students featured several companies without properly verifying the information. As a result, the final report included misleading or inaccurate details about those companies. What’s more concerning is that the supervising teacher, Jess (Yun Tien) Wen, not only approved the project but even shared it publicly on LinkedIn, despite the factual inaccuracies.\n\nThis reflects a serious lapse in academic integrity and responsibility - from both the students and the teacher. When educators fail to emphasize ethics, research standards, and accountability, students graduate without the critical skills or mindset needed in the real world. And when new graduates struggle to find jobs or face rejection for poor professional standards, it’s often a reflection of what they were - or weren’t - taught. Teachers play a major role in shaping employable, trustworthy graduates, and negligence in academic guidance directly contributes to that failure.', 'Not worth the the money. Expensive, dorms are dirty. More interested in charging you for services than teaching. I should have gone to Sci Arc! Mistreat Handicap people. The facility is not well equipped for wheel chairs. A very anti Jewish vibe. Administration threatened all professors about speaking against anti Jewish sentiment.', 'I have only taken two semesters here and I can confidently say that there are alot of really amazing talented students and it is a shame that they are wasting their potential at an institution like this. Maybe it\'s the location of the school but the dorms cost way too much for what you get and on top of that they don\'t offer summer classes for alot of the courses, so they incourage students to transfer credits from a different institution if they want to take classes in the summer. Also one day I was told there is a hold and I can\'t register for courses because my highschool diploma isn\'t valid since it needs to be sent directly from the school isnt that something you mention to a student early on before they\'re enrolled at the school???There are a few really amazing professors but other than that this institution is a joke and if you are interested in going into debt and not growing as an artist then this is the perfect place for you!! Having said that you can grow as an artist anywhere it\'s all up to what you make of things but sometimes the environment has an effect and this school is more concerned with making as much money with as less consequences than actually worrying about their students, and having their students "clean up" after semester ends is also a bit insane considering how much money they make off of students and they couldn\'t even hire or pay someone to do that, so all and all if you are interested in the cool printing and art equipment that they have (which also costs money) then maybe this school is for you otherwise I don\'t recommend going here.']

name: California Lutheran University
reviews:
['Great, private university in Thousand Oaks, California. Our daughter spent three years there in the sun lit foothills of northern Los Angeles. They are intimate and have many outreach programs for their students. They also have a great psychology program.', 'Although this is a private university, my toddler boys love walking this campus and visiting the water stream to listen to frogs and just to visit. It’s a beautiful campus and quiet during weekends. They also took swim lesson here. Lovely relaxing atmosphere', "High School and not so large that you feel like you're just another number. It's a cozy campus where everyone feels more like a community than an institution. The atmosphere is more about the student getting as much education and experience from the campus than just passing or getting a grade. It's not competitive, it's more cooperative where others help each other to succeed. I really did love going to school here and the resources and experience I gained are true treasures. The professors here are wonderful and the art community in this campus is wonderful.", "CLU has a beautiful campus, with native landscaping that is labeled to identify the species. we enjoy taking long walks around and through the campus.

There's a walking bridge the crosses over Olsen Road so students and faculty do not have to travel longer distances than necessary, and it also connects the northern portion of the campus to the southern. They have several new buildings, including a state-of-the-art cafeteria, gymnasium with weight room, and a museum.

In the summer months, prior to the pandemic, the Kinsmen Company hosts Shakespearean plays in the campus park, complete with a full stage and professional actors. Patrons can take a picnic dinner and purchase wine and beer before the play or during intermissions. Seats are on the grass, on blankets or on low-backed lawn chairs

The Los Angeles Rams also train on the northern part of the CLU campus in a cordoned-off section that houses their training facility.

I encourage a trip to visit the CLU campus if you're in the area.", 'Terrible staff, res life at this university was one of the most disappointing and unprofessional departments I’ve ever dealt with. In my experience, their behavior was downright shady constantly giving vague answers, dodging responsibility, and acting like basic communication was too much to ask. The whole situation felt intentionally confusing, almost like they were hoping I’d just give up.

What made it even worse was the attitude. Instead of owning their mistakes, they were disrespectful, dismissive, and somehow tried to twist everything around to make themselves look like the victims. It was honestly unbelievable to watch adults in a professional setting behave this way.

If you expect transparency, respect, or even the bare minimum of competence, do yourself a favor and avoid dealing with Res Life here. My experience was a complete mess from start to finish.']

name: California State University-Bakersfield
reviews:
['A Strong Foundation for My Career

I graduated from CSUB last year with a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, concentrating in Accounting, and I’m incredibly grateful for the experience. The professors were knowledgeable, approachable, and genuinely invested in student success. The coursework was challenging yet practical, and it provided a strong foundation that has prepared me well for both graduate studies and real-world opportunities.

The campus has a welcoming atmosphere, with plenty of resources available — from tutoring centers to career services — that helped me stay on track and feel supported throughout my journey.

CSUB was the perfect place to complete my undergraduate degree, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a quality education in a supportive environment.', 'Amazing experience. CSU Bakersfield doing Covid vaccines for anyone that wants one. All thats needed is photo ID. Very professional, very friendly, and very quick staff. The entire time from parking in the abundant parking spaces to walking to the facility, waiting in line, getting the show, waiting the 15 minutes, and leaving was less than an hour. Thank you to everyone the set up, ran, and administered  the vaccines. Your staff are the real heros. The participants even were on point by following the guidelines to make the experience enjoyable.', 'School is cool, but we gotta add another collaborative zone (speaking area) to the library. I be going to the second floor and I can’t find a seat. Bru if you are just one person stop sitting in the booths. Also reduce my tuition, yall tripping.', 'January 10, 2025 -  CSUB Road Runner
Aquatics
My daughter at first loved it ; then they started adding too many kids per class , this is harder for one coach to concentrate on each kid progress.
My daughter eventually lost interest because of this on july 2024 .
Unfortunately my daughter has had some psychological issues to which she’s seeing a professional; it was suggested for her to try again her favorite sport.
At the beginning of January 2025 I contacted Mr. Ryan B. ( the head coach) ; at the time he was polite and gave her a one day swimming test , next day I paid the $140 + fee for the month; the only thing he said was if I ever wanted to cancel I need to give two weeks notice.
Unfortunately my daughter had a nervous episode the next day not wanting to go back; the psychologist told me that it was not a good idea to force her. I emailed Mr. Ryan about possibly canceling since she didn’t take a single class only the testing day.
Mr. Denied my money back , I asked if I could at least get half back ( $ that can still help with my daughter’s treatment) I am a single mom with no job , I have a disability, I am trying to help my daughter the best I can with her health issues.
Mr. Ryan said that only extreme cases he will give the $ back , I tried a higher up , but he said that he was the only person to talk to.
Yes I am upset, but I also want to warn others about this place , money seems to be a priority for them , not the kids and families', "There really isn't anything wrong with csub per day, as a student there are many helpful things, such as information and individuals that are widely available."]

name: California State University-Stanislaus
reviews:
['Beautiful campus! Great place to walk. Just watch out for goose/duck poop', 'I went here for my Bachelors degree and now for my graduate. Everything for my Bachelors was smooth but it seems quality has gone down here significantly or maybe it's just because I'm in graduate school.

I have run into a multitude of issues here with a few things that I had to do for my graduate program. Most significantly, my MPN did not show up in the Financial Aid office system. I have been getting the run around with it and getting very little response.

I was first referred to the loan coordinator with nothing but a first name only. Then, after searching for it myself, I emailed over the course of 2 weeks, I emailed 2 times with no response.

I also called twice in that time. First time, I was told that they were doing something on the backend and I should check back in 24-48 hours. I checked back in 48 hours and was told it would be fixed by "Thursday" which was 3 days from that point in time. Thursday comes and goes and still nothing.

I understand being bombarded or out of their control, but there is no excuse to have zero correspondence (beyond being told to just wait) with students regarding loan issues. Emails ignored, etc.

This is the lives and futures of real life people that are impacted. Sometimes, housing and other basic life needs are also impacted. There should definitely be more than "just wait" being given over the phone through another staff member.

Overall, I have to say that the experience has been a disappointment. I will update review if it improves, but my issue has yet to be resolved and the process has been nothing short of frustrating.

On another note, my professors seem great and invested in their students.', 'It’s a huge blessing knowing little ones are in such good hands while also being part of the Stan State community.

Highly recommend this center for families looking for quality childcare and early education.', 'Great college, beautiful campus. On my way to getting my bachelors, has a less expensive tuition than most colleges.', 'Come here for community events all the time. 4th of july was a hit. Came today for their fall carnival. Awesome our kids had a blast. All the students were into what they were doing. Thank you for contributing to the comminity.']

name: California State University-San Bernardino
reviews:
['Graduated (B.A Phil) in one of the worst times (COVID)- not CSUSB's fault - but after being rejected to over a dozen entry level positions on campus. I had to realize that not all majors are treated the same, and you do have to choose wisely when it comes to school. In many ways, CSUSB could have more support to their students (i.e having support/career building programs per the individual's major). but without going to CSUSB - I wouldn't have met my wife and created my family; so at the end, it must not have been too bad.

Just be careful with what you are studying and make sure you understand what resources are available to you (a known issue that currently exists (i.e not all students knowing about the "DEN"/ their Food assistance program & etc.)', 'csusb's bachelor's degree/program in administration supply chain management program is a joke and completely unprofessional. I called and spoke with their secretary/receptionist and the "dean" of the program who laughed at me and mocked my serious questions about the program. Like other people said, you get what you pay for. It's no surprise that cal state schools are inferior compared to UC schools.', "School is a joke, the entrepreneurship program is laughable. Was the easiest and worst class I've ever taken. Anyone that takes the simplest business class will already know more than what you will here. The instructors preach about starting a business but none of them even have a business. Not to mention the insane fees you will pay on top of your tuition (mine were 2k for one class). Stay away and go to a real school.", 'If you’re actually smart — not just GPA-smart, but independent-thinker, challenge-the-system, ask-better-questions smart — CSUSB will support you. Here, people respect hard work, original thinking, and quiet ambition. There’s no pretentious act, no herd mentality — just real students, real professors, and degrees that mean something.

Now let’s talk about UC Davis.

UC Davis is where originality goes to die. If you question anything — the system, the group narrative, the shallow “woke” activism that only exists on Canva slides — you’re instantly labeled “problematic.” It’s a campus full of groupthink, where being truly intelligent makes you a threat, not an asset.

Want to explore unpopular ideas? Want to push boundaries in science, politics, or tech? Too bad — Davis isn’t interested in thought, just compliance. It rewards people who follow the script and punishes anyone with the guts to think differently. It’s like intellectual prison with compost bins.

And what do you get for playing their game? Ten years after enrollment, you’re lucky if you’re making $54K pre-tax. That’s the reward for swallowing your brain and joining the hive mind.

Meanwhile, CSUSB grads are moving up — building careers in healthcare, education, business, tech — without the ego, without the debt, and without pretending to be elite.

If you value authenticity, intelligence, and actual outcomes, CSUSB is the real one. UC Davis is just a loud, self-congratulatory echo chamber where the truly smart either get silenced — or leave.', 'This is the best school that I’ve ever been to in my life and they help you with every single thing and it is so worth coming to, and if I could go back in time, I would come to the school before attending community college']

name: California State University-Chico
reviews:
['California State University, Chico is one of the few universities that still feels real. It’s not driven by hype or image. Students here get genuine support, grounded education, and a strong sense of community. It’s a place where you’re treated like a person, not just a number or marketing metric. Critical thinkers are encouraged. Practical learning is prioritized. You graduate with skills that matter and a mindset built for real success—not just superficial accolades.

In contrast, UC Davis has increasingly become a performative and image-driven institution. The school projects excellence, but much of it is surface-level—built on branding rather than substance. It markets itself heavily and builds a reputation that doesn’t always match the student experience. Many bright, independent minds end up feeling stifled, while those who conform to the system—regardless of merit—rise more easily. It rewards appearances and safe thinking more than originality or depth.

At Chico State, students develop sharp thinking and are allowed to be themselves. At Davis, there’s a strong culture of performance over authenticity. It’s polished on the outside, but often lacking the academic soul that truly empowers students. If you want real value, real people, and a campus culture that doesn’t just pretend to care—Chico State is the better choice.', 'Miss this beautiful campus and place so much. Hope I get to go back here someday and listen to the creek flowing through campus', "I was super excited to start in the fall of 2024, but the city is not great. For Chico being home to a university, they take no pride in keeping their town safe and clean. The campus is beautiful, but there are a lot more better CSUs in California. All the buildings are super outdated, no diversity in the city, students are rude and entitled, homless everywhere, horrible drivers, weird locals, incidents almost every single day, and the neighorhoods surrounding the univeristy are trashed and suspicious. They push you to move into streets that are close to campus which are the worst areas to live in with the most crime and homeless roaming around. I have had several suspicious people walk by my home while living in Chico and get personal belongings stolen. Several incidents that have occurred i.e, shootings at student apt complexes, random gunshots at night, and several other incidents. There is nothing to do in Chico and anybody who says otherwise is lying to you. Unless you like to be outdoorsy and have the time and money to be driving up to lakes and parks then Chico is fit for you, but no student is going to be driving 1.5-3 hours just to get to a decently sized city that has more food and entertainment to do and that is why every student just goes out to all the dirty nasty bars in Chico. Its a mid school and city, I wouldn't recommend anyone to attend yet alone live in the city.", 'As a visitor, the campus is a beautiful place to visit. CSU facilities staff does an excellent job of maintaining all of the grounds and buildings. I felt safe on campus.', 'i LOVE Chico State! Great school. Everyone works together to serve the students.']

Dahlia mom', 'I came to this school and it is constantly changing. Especially with the pandemic slowly bringing things back. They are remodeling plenty and the campus is beautiful and very spread out. You can enjoy the little critters and plenty of flowers and trees to stare at. This school has plenty of history and beautiful views. Wether you came to this school or want to come to this school, it is definitely in a great centralized location with plenty of amenities both on and off campus.

Bulldog born, Bulldog bread 🐾', "Review of California State University, Fresno

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

California State University, Fresno, commonly known as Fresno State, is an exceptional institution that offers a diverse and comprehensive educational experience. Located in the heart of California's Central Valley, Fresno State provides a vibrant campus life, rigorous academic programs, and a supportive community for students from all walks of life.

The university's campus is beautiful, with well-maintained grounds and state-of-the-art facilities. The Henry Madden Library, one of the largest in the CSU system, is a standout feature, offering extensive resources and a conducive environment for study and research. Additionally, the campus boasts modern classrooms, labs, and recreational facilities, ensuring students have access to everything they need for a well-rounded education.

Fresno State is renowned for its strong academic programs, particularly in areas such as agriculture, business, engineering, and health sciences. The faculty here are dedicated and knowledgeable, often going above and beyond to support their students' academic and personal growth. Small class sizes allow for personalized attention and foster a collaborative learning environment.

One of the university's unique highlights is its agricultural program, which includes the 1,000-acre campus farm. This hands-on learning environment provides students with invaluable practical experience and has earned Fresno State a reputation as a leader in agricultural education.

The student life at Fresno State is vibrant and inclusive, with numerous clubs, organizations, and events that cater to a wide range of interests. The Student Recreation Center, the Save Mart Center, and Bulldog Stadium provide ample opportunities for students to engage in sports, fitness, and entertainment. The university's commitment to diversity and inclusion is evident in its various cultural centers and programs that support underrepresented groups.

Fresno State also has a strong connection to the local community, offering various outreach programs and opportunities for students to engage in community service and internships. This not only enhances students' educational experiences but also helps them build valuable professional networks.

Overall, California State University, Fresno, is a fantastic place to pursue higher education. Its combination of excellent academic programs, supportive faculty, modern facilities, and a vibrant campus life makes it an ideal choice for students seeking a well-rounded and enriching university experience. Whether you're interested in academic excellence, personal growth, or community engagement, Fresno State has something to offer.", 'Beautiful place!
The library is amazing!
Restrooms are spacious and well maintained. Handicap accessible.', 'Very fun wine, grape, and raisen festival with live band, line dancing and line dancing lesson']

name: California State University-Fullerton
reviews:
["Went there for a womens basketball game. Parking in the structure was nice and easy plus it's very close to the gym so that was nice. It does cost $4 an hour (on weekdays, weekends are free) to park there. The gym is real nice, music was definitely hype - the DJ plays great music, really keeps the energy up, concession stand is questionable i dont suggest the pretzel or the coffee, easy restrooms, everyone was friendly and helpful. Support your college athletes! TUSKS UP!!", 'The buildings of CSU Fullerton which are beautiful look more modern structure than other colleges. I visited there with my son who said CSU Fullerton is located in the middle of Los Angeles area which is really convenient going everywhere. How nice.', 'I took my son to visit this Campus,he loves it,so big,clean,all Campus so green with trees and plants. And they have big garden with ponds inside 25 acres. We walk a lot, to know the buildings and it feels safe.', 'Being the first person in my family to attend a university, I was genuinely excited and wanted to have a positive experience here. Unfortunately, the number of fees and constant new charges has made this extremely difficult. I just paid $1,849 in tuition, and the very next day another $1,319 charge appeared on my account. I have not even had the chance to register for my classes, yet my account is already on hold for an overdue balance. It is frustrating to feel like I am being penalized immediately after making a payment. My account is frequently placed on hold because new or unclear charges keep getting added, and it feels overwhelming.

On top of this, the quality of the education has been disappointing. The coursework has felt minimal, and I have learned very little in most of my classes. Also, paying for parking on weekends when the school is empty feels like another cash grab. It does not feel aligned with the cost I am paying or the expectations I had when enrolling. I would transfer if I could, but I am only a few classes away from completing my program. Based on my experience, I would recommend looking into other schools.', 'California State University (CSU) is the largest public university system in the United States, with 23 campuses spread across California. It serves around 460,000 students and employs about 56,000 faculty and staff. CSU is known for its affordability, diversity, and focus on practical education and workforce development.

Key Points:

1. Campuses: Includes popular ones like CSU Long Beach, San Diego State University, and CSU Los Angeles.

2. Programs: Offers undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees in various fields, including business, engineering, arts, sciences, and education.

3. Tuition: Relatively affordable compared to private institutions, with financial aid options available.

4. Diversity: One of the most ethnically and culturally diverse university systems in the nation.

5. Mission: Emphasizes access to quality education, community service, and practical career training.

Let me know if you’re looking for information about a specific campus or program!']

The consensus among those I’ve spoken with highlights a remarkable balance between academic rigor and a genuine, inclusive community spirit that makes every student feel they truly belong. Many people in my circle frequently commend the university’s knack for fostering real-world skills, particularly noting how the diverse faculty brings invaluable industry insights directly into the classroom. It is truly heartening to see an institution remain so steadfastly committed to affordability and social responsibility while simultaneously expanding its reputation as a powerhouse for innovation and career readiness. Ultimately, the positive buzz surrounding the "Pioneer" spirit is well-founded, as the university continues to prove itself as a transformative force for anyone dedicated to their professional and personal evolution.', 'Dear Admission

Central America.', "Is there a nice campus Queen not very crowded people are friendly and they're always doing something it's nice up in the hills", "Easy to get to, plenty of parking. I was looking for international students admissions,  which took some driving around and friendly people to redirect me. Some areas of the campus looked like it needed maintenance (tennis courts, stadium) but overall the buildings looked modern/well kept. It's helpful to use the online university map as a reference.", 'California State University, East Bay is a hidden gem in the CSU system. Don’t let the quiet reputation fool you—CSUEB delivers on every front that matters: quality teaching, accessibility, affordability, and real-world preparation. Professors here care about students, offering smaller class sizes and direct support. The diversity on campus isn’t just a statistic—it’s a true strength, enriching classroom discussions with global perspectives and fostering a welcoming, inclusive environment.

The location in the East Bay offers proximity to Silicon Valley and San Francisco without the overwhelming price tag. There’s a strong sense of community here that’s hard to find at bigger, impersonal institutions. For anyone looking to get a meaningful, career-focused education without being drowned in student debt, CSUEB is a seriously smart choice.

Now let’s talk about UC Davis. Sure, it’s a big-name UC. But what does that prestige really get you? Huge lecture halls, overworked professors, and a hyper-competitive culture that can grind students down. For all the hype, UC Davis feels like a machine—processing thousands of students with little regard for individual growth. When you factor in the massive cost, the pressure cooker atmosphere, and the bureaucratic sprawl, it’s hard to justify the price tag. I’d rate UC Davis ABS — Absolutely Bloated System.']

name: California State University-Long Beach
reviews:
['Beautiful place to go to university. Good energy and they are building. Will be next level when finished.', "This university is on the affordable side and they offer so many fields of study that other nearby universities don't offer. It is closer to the ocean and it's bustling with life. However, the recent politics of this school were not good.

The university raised the tuition to construct a nicer area (that didn't need renovation), rather than use that money to improve and expand programs, or improve student life (Air conditioning for the Art building for example). The restaurants before 2020 were filled with people and all kinds of food you can buy. Now, it's deserted because they closed all of the restaurants. Some of the dorm rooms are poorly managed at times, based on what some people tell me.

Before all of that, I came to this university during high school, and I knew I wanted to go here, but I feel like it's becoming more of a shell of itself. Maybe I am being dramatic.

They also didn't let graduates walk after the COVID pandemic. Despite everything being in person, they didn't let graduates walk in attempts to save money. I don't know if that part was resolved.

The professors were great and I miss them. Despite the buildings having an overall theme with style, some of the architecture is unique in their own. I love the psychology building.", "It's far more expensive now then when I attended but still great value, great faculty and beautiful campus. Population density of Long Beach is also much greater these days thanks to housing incentives and you will see homeless people lighting it up broad daylight in the immediate areas around campus sometimes but also more taco street vendors. There's used to be a guy is trying to sell you speakers in the parking lot out of a van, he was trying so hard.", 'Beautiful college campus in the heart of Long Beach. The campus classroom buildings all have different characteristics from those that are modern to those that still have vintage aesthetic qualities to them. The campus is packed with students but the area and space is vast enough to feel comfortable while walking to and from classes. Everyone looks focused and ready to learn! name: University of California-Irvine
reviews:
['This school bullied an autistic young male adult. He tried so hard to fit in on the first day, and they told him, "If you keep doing this (pretending to be an extrovert and smile like a goofball because apparently his neutral face makes people think he's angry and triggers people to yell at him and comment on how quiet he is), you'll do great at this campus!" So you couldn't accept him as he is? You have to expose him just like that? In a social event, the event organizer asked a distasteful question, "Who is most likely going to shoot up a school?" and everyone in that event said it would be him. Well, guess what, you may have ruined this young male adult's life and career opportunities. You are probably married with a successful career, but know this, Class of 2010 to 2014: you thrived because you bullied and ostracized a student just like yourself, who just wanted to fit in and belong in the college campus just like you. But you are absolutely wrong because he has never shot up a school or caused societal harm to anyone like you hoped that guy who is (insert your labels here) would end up doing. But he never did. You have his blood on your hands.', 'The University of California, Irvine, situated at the heart of the dynamic Orange County landscape, is consistently portrayed in my professional and social circles as a premier vanguard of technological and medical innovation, where the iconic circular campus design fosters a unique sense of interconnected scholarly focus. From numerous insightful dialogues with local industry leaders and successful alumni, it is abundantly clear that UCI provides a substantive, high-caliber environment, frequently lauded by my acquaintances for its exceptional ability to merge rigorous computer science research with a deeply respectful, community-oriented approach to education. It is truly heartening to observe how the institution maintains such a transparent and ethical dedication to sustainability and social mobility, qualities that the broader public increasingly recognizes as the defining hallmark of the "Anteater" legacy’s global ascent. Many people I know personally highlight the campus's sophisticated synthesis of safe, suburban stability and cutting-edge intellectual ambition as a merytorically superior asset that uniquely prepares graduates for the complexities of the modern workforce. Ultimately, in the collective view of the Southern California academic community, UCI stands as a distinguished pillar of public research, rightfully respected for its elegant ability to cultivate a new generation of visionaries who are as technically proficient as they are socially responsible.', 'Great campus. Instructions about reaching there while avoiding toll roads and parking on the weekend could be more clear.', 'The Great Deception: My Child's Experience at UC Irvine

They call it the happiest campus. They show us shiny brochures and beautiful buildings. They talk about world-class academics and passionate professors. And for a moment, we believe it. We believe our kids are heading to a place of opportunity, a place that values their well-being.

Then we see the reality.

We're not talking about bad grades or tough classes. We’re talking about basic human needs. We’re talking about the absurd cost of simply existing on this campus. My daughter, like so many other students, is being failed by the very institution we were told to trust.

Part 1: The High Price of Hunger
The university's meal plan is nothing short of a scam. We pay over $800 for 35 meals and a handful of credits that are only good at a few, overpriced spots. Do the math. At an average of $15 a meal, that gives my daughter less than two meals a day for an entire month! It’s a disgrace.

This isn’t just a complaint—it’s a systemic issue. This deceptive pricing validates a recent study by the California Student Aid Commission, which found that university meal plans are deficient, providing students with only about 13 out of 21 meals a week. How can a university claim to foster bright minds when it leaves them to fend for themselves, short on food and short on funds?

This financial burden becomes even more absurd when you consider that the USDA’s own guidelines for federal food assistance implicitly define a full meal plan as providing more than 50% of three meals a day. A standard that UCI's plan clearly fails to meet.

Part 2: The Campus of Contradictions
The problems don’t stop there. This is a campus that restricts bicycles on its sprawling, hilly landscape, forcing students to walk long distances or wait for inefficient shuttles. Why? For "pedestrian safety," they say. But I’ve seen the same administration turn a blind eye to murderous e-scooters weaving through crowds, putting everyone at risk.

The irony is not lost on me. A campus built for movement and fresh air is a contradiction—a place that actively discourages the very thing that makes campus life convenient and healthy for so many.

Part 3: The Unlivable Living Spaces
Finally, let's talk about the apartments. On the outside, they look modern and new. But on the inside, they are a gut punch of decay and neglect. My daughter's apartment building is riddled with old, rotting wood and paper-thin walls. The dining area—a place for food—is a magnet for ants. Ants! A huge irony is that UCI calls themselves the Anteaters, yet the place is crawling with ants! It's a sickening joke—the mascot is supposed to be a hunter of the very pest they can't seem to eliminate, especially in the dining area. It's almost as if the name itself mocks the reality of living here.

Just as bad, there are no refrigerators, no fans, no heaters. It’s a breeding ground for frustration, an insult to the cost of attendance.

Why does a world-class university perpetuate this gap between the haves and have-nots?

A Call to Action: We Will Not Be Silent

My daughter may not be complaining, but I am. And I know she is not alone. Every student and parent facing these same issues has a choice: stay silent or speak up.

This isn’t a small issue. It’s a matter of dignity. It's about being treated fairly by an institution that is supposed to be nurturing our children. It's time for the University of California to stop hiding behind its glossy image and address these core failures.

To the passionate students of UCI: This is your moment. Your future is not just about a degree—it’s about using your voice to create real change. Document the conditions. Take photos. Share your stories. Use change.org. Let’s build a movement that will force the administration to listen. Let’s show them what true leadership looks like.', 'UC Irvine doesn’t just hand out diplomas — it shapes professionals.
It’s where ambition meets precision, and ideas turn into impact. From business and computer science to engineering and biology, UCI builds thinkers who execute. The research output is elite, the academics demanding, and the culture one of quiet drive — not noise, but depth.

At Irvine, you earn your ground. You’re challenged by peers who care, faculty who push, and a system that rewards initiative. You leave with credentials that matter, and a reputation that travels. UCI’s alumni don’t just graduate — they advance.

And then there’s UC Davis.

Let’s be honest — it’s coasting on branding, not backbone. It promises excellence, then buries you in red tape and groupthink. You’ll spend more time navigating bureaucracy than mastering your craft. The classes are bloated, the feedback slow, and originality gets you side-eyed instead of celebrated.

You’ll find plenty of people — but few with pulse.
It’s a system that produces survivors, not standouts.

As for return? UC Davis’s 10-year ROI sits around $58 K pre-tax in California — that’s roughly $30 K in real terms if you factor in cost of living. Mediocrity shouldn’t cost that much. Prestige? It’s a logo — not leverage.

At UC Irvine, you earn respect.
At UC Davis, you earn excuses.

So if you’re choosing between the two:
Go where progress happens.
Not where it’s promised.

UCI wins. UC Davis doesn’t even make the lineup.']
