name: California Institute of the Arts
reviews:
['In 2018, I visited the California Institute of the Arts for my university trip.

CalArts is the most prestigious institution in California. I had a tour around the school, looked at some student artwork and the campus was astonishing. I first heard of CalArts in “The Pixar Story” where some alumni attended there and later employed at Disney such as John Lasseter, John Musker and Brad Bird. It was such a wonderful visit to CalArts.', "Located in the Santa Clara area of California in the United States, the California Institute of the Arts was formed by the merger of the Chouinard Art Institute, which was established in 1921, and the Los Angeles Conservatory of Music, which was established in 1883, and is an art colleage where art and music coexist.

The alumni association was founded in 1965 by Walt Disney's younger brother, Roy Disney, and is now considered the most prestigious college with the most expensive tuition and the best professors, faculties and graduates in the field.

There are majors of Art & Technology,
Program in Art, Photography and Media, and Graphic Design.", 'This is purely a review of the guided campus tour for high school students, not the teaching or student experience.

My child had CalArts at the top of her college list for the last three years.  We finally visited in 2025.  And after the tour she left in tears, saying she’s not going to even apply.

Some positives.  The surrounding setting is beautiful.  The reputation is excellent.  The admission rate is low, meaning they are very selective.  The school has all the arts covered: animation, fine arts, sculpture, music, painting, ceramics, puppetry, acting, directing, lighting, etc.

Now for the tour experience.  The inside of this place is as crummy as an underfunded middle school.  Old lockers fill the halls (never explained by the guide), doors and windows with peeling paint, worn surfaces everywhere, old lighting, empty rooms, etc.  I’ve been in/on more than a dozen college campuses in my lifetime and this is the only one that has felt like a school on the verge of bankruptcy.  But, obviously, they aren’t.

The art that we saw was bad.  Sculptures, drawings, ceramics, woven art.  It looked like struggling 8th graders who wanted to be Artists some day.  Meat hanging from strings? Female warriors fully dressed except for pants, revealing male genitalia? Ceramic bowls that look exactly like my own kids’ Mother’s Day gifts when they were 6?

We looked out a window at “The Wild Beast”, a beautiful concert building.  But we weren’t allowed to go inside?

We stood outside and the guide pointed to some apartments across the parking lot.  She took three minutes to explain that these were dorms, but there’s also an apartment complex “15 minutes away” where they put underclassmen.  Then she asked if we had any questions, and when no one had any, she said “oh thank God.”

The lobby has a men’s and women’s restroom.  But the rest of the school has “gender neutral” bathrooms…that include urinals and stalls so we can all pee together.

The school encourages self-expression, like any art school.  Apparently, however, 75% of the self expression on the walls was all about sex.

My daughter’s interest was animation, and even the guide called it “the most prestigious program here”.  But when we got to the animation wing, we were told that we couldn’t “go in” or “see anything.”  And then we walked away.  No discussion, no details.

Our tour had over a dozen kids and their parents.  Several times the guide asked if we had any questions.  At no point in the tour did a single student or parent have a question.  And when it was over everyone dispersed.  Very blah.
Let’s be clear - with an acceptance rate this low, the leadership at CalArts doesn’t really care about making a good impression on these high school kids.  But as a parent, my takeaway was that this school has so much money and such a good reputation that they have become a haven for wandering minstrels, itinerant artists, and lost souls.  Basically, a bunch of 19-20 year olds who just want to make art, and don’t care if they live with their parents or tend bar to pay the bills.  My daughter wants a career in animation.  She’s serious about creating characters, telling stories, and using her talents, the latest technology, and top-notch education to make it happen.  CalArts may be that place, but you’d never know it from the tour.', 'I want to be an artist   at the red  river college', 'They had a large grass area as well as a place for people to sit on concrete seats. It was a bring your own food put your blanket on the grass and enjoy the show. It was a great show.']

name: California State University Maritime Academy
reviews: ['My former roommate attended the Maritime Academy (before Cal Poly SLO merger i think). He was former Coast Guard (or US Navy?). He lived off campus and rode a bicycle to school (his girlfriend took their car for commute to her job, so had no on-campus parking tickets or impounds as described in other reviews). He graduated and got a license to crew and pilot barges, and seems to have done ok with it.', "Don't. It's not what it used to be. Expect to be screwed by the academic advisor you didn't know you had. Enjoy the prison like dorm experience and garbage food you're required to pay for. Embrace the campus security that exists entirely to write parking tickets, because you aren't paying enough already. Hope your vehicle isn't broken into or vandalized, because they won't do anything about it, but they will threaten you.\n\nIts all about the money, which also neatly describes Vallejo and Solano county. Don't come here. I can't say east coast options are better, but they'd have to work hard to be worse.", 'This school is amazing. I am so proud that my daughter attends here. She loves it.', 'Beautiful campus with fantastic academics and the highest return on investment of any University in CA.', "CSU Maritime is an amazing educational institution. The campus is beautiful. They have top of the line training facilities with some of the best maritime simulators in the world. Their engineering program is bar none. Every CMA graduate that wants a job will find a job, and will probably find a good job. CMA has a broad course selection ranging from navigation sciences to engineering and international business. Recently CSU Maritime merged with Cal poly San Luis Obispo. I'm confident this will make the school even better."]

name: Canada College
reviews:
['We drove through the college and enjoyed a view of this relaxing campus. Stopping at the parking lot offers a great view of the ocean and the Mountains.
The buildings are well
Armed and easy to find.
We found van accessible wheelchair parking in lots that did not Indicate the need for university decal or payment.
Enjoy these views', 'This review is not about the academics of Cañada College or it’s admissions process, but rather the grounds and walkability. The aesthetics of Cañada College are simply beautiful. The college is set up high with panoramic views all around the campus. The buildings architecture is modern and strikingly beautiful. A great place to walk because it gives you opportunity for stairs, hills, and flat ground. A great workout!', "It was Canada's Junior College theater. All the seats were perfect. Not a bad seat in the house so to speak.", 'Nice campus on a hill with a great view of Silicon Valley where you can see from the 🌉 San Mateo Bridge to the 🌉 Dumbarton Bridge

Went for MonkeyPox vaccine and they also do corona in their parking lot 🅿️', 'Let me save you some time and money: UC Davis was not worth it. After 10 years and over $58,000 sunk into that so-called “world-class” education, what do I have to show for it? Stress, student debt, and a degree that no one cares about unless you already have connections.

You think you’re joining a top-tier academic environment, but you’re actually walking into a snake pit of performative intellectualism, bloated egos, and hollow prestige. Professors don’t teach—they publish. Advisors don’t advise—they dodge emails. The system is built to reward the top 5% and ignore everyone else. If you’re not born into a network, you’re invisible.

And the students? Let’s be honest: it’s not a hub of brilliance. A lot of them are just coasting on the name, following checklists, and pretending they’re future CEOs while relying on group projects they barely contribute to. The UC name doesn’t make you smart. It makes you pay—for branding, for bureaucracy, for an outdated idea of success.

Meanwhile, Cañada College—a small, honest, community college in the Bay Area—delivered more real education, more support, and more opportunity than UC Davis ever did. I spent a fraction of the cost, got direct access to professors who actually knew how to teach, and found real career pathways that didn’t require selling my soul or taking on crushing debt.

At Cañada, I wasn’t lost in a crowd of 30,000. I wasn’t just another number in a lecture hall. I was taught by people who cared, guided by advisors who knew my name, and supported every step of the way. The ROI? Off the charts—because I walked away with skills, clarity, and zero debt.

If I could go back, I wouldn’t waste a second on UC Davis. It was an overpriced illusion that delivered nothing. Cañada College was the real thing—affordable, practical, and powerful.

UC Davis students and grads can keep pretending it’s worth it. But if your degree costs you $58,000+ and still doesn’t guarantee a job or direction in life… maybe it’s not the smart choice after all.']

name: College of the Canyons
reviews:
['COC is an amazing place. They offer so much equity to the community. Thanks to their adult re-entry program, the EOPS office, and all of the caring professors I was able attain my AA-T degree in psychology. I graduated with multiple university offers, including UCLA. I highly recommend checking out this campus, it was an answered prayer for me. Go Cougars! 💙🙏🏽', 'Phenomenal school. In this rare case, you don’t get what you pay for. Better professors than IVY league schools for 1% of the tuition. Valencia campus much bigger than Canyon Country. Great services such as mental health services. Library and TLC are good. Skilled football team. Great school, thank you for making Santa Clarita even better.', 'This review is long overdue. COC is an amazing school. Just a little background, I homeschooled my daughters and had them start taking classes at LAVC at 14 yrs old then move over to COC at 16 yrs old (you have to be 16 to attend for some weird reason). Utilizing dual enrollment as a high school student , the classes were also free as an added bonus.

It was an amazing experience for all my daughters as they were able to earn college credit while also fulfilling high school requirements, have time to figure out their passions - and all have done extremely well, built lasting relationships with their professors here and utilized all the myriad of resources available (the TLC here offers free in person and online tutoring for students - an amazing perk).

One of my daughters (who transferred to CSUN for Art) even had professors at CoC who were also teaching at Cal Arts. My other daughters are in STEM majors - all have done extremely well, transferred or will be transferring to universities and got a better education than I felt like I did at UCLA (no joke).

The amount of resources available at COC is astounding and the professors are top notch (many of them also teach at CSUN, CSU Fullerton, Cal Poly Pomona etc). There is also a little advertised engineering club which is affiliated with Cal Tech/ JPL and for the students who participate, this is counted as an internship, with opportunities to have their project selected by NASA and participate in a launch.

I feel that a lot of people don’t understand that not every successful university path has to begin as a freshman at a 4 year school. Overall I can’t say enough wonderful things about this school - it has worked out so well for our family :)', 'College Of The Canyons is a great place for your education. The college is located in the Santa Clarita Valley. They have two campuses. The main campus is located on the west side and the second is on the east side of the Santa Clarita Valley. Both campuses are places for your epic education experience. I highly recommend that you visit these campuses to see the benefits it will bring you and your family at a very low cost. Priceless benefits.', 'This is a great local community college, and will hopefully become an accredited University some time soon. Great facilities, with lots of growth and expansion recently. Nice performing arts center and a huge new parking structure.']

name: Cerritos College
reviews:

Half of the reviews are positive and the other half are negative but there lies. Not true.
Trust me I know.
———————————————————————
Only a person who likes to criticize and complain says negative things when it’s not true and they don’t care at all.
The person who lies and lies. Is just someone who is not a good person.', 'Do not choose this school for the dental hygiene program. The instructors here are not actually teaching. They provide no slides, no clear guidance, and simply read word-for-word from the textbook during lectures. Instead of proper instruction, they make students draw teeth and mouths or piece together puzzles of oral radiology images—calling this ‘interactive learning.’ They also rely on students with prior work experience to teach those without experience, rather than fulfilling their own responsibility to educate.

On top of this, students are forced to read an overwhelming workload—on average 5 chapters per book, across 11 different books—yet still walk into lectures without knowing what the focus is supposed to be. My cousin enrolled and paid $11,000 in tuition, only to regret it immediately. Within the first week, she was overwhelmed, crying daily, sleeping only 3 hours a night, and under constant stress with no clear direction.

Please consider this a sincere warning: research carefully before enrolling. This program is not worth the financial or emotional toll', 'Can this school get more funding for laptops? We had to share laptops in class because we needed to a program use for stats class.', 'My daughter  just started college, hate that one of her class in online, which make it harder for her to understand and when she ask for help, teacher sends her video,(algebra) really, smh n still needs help, counsler ,takes awhile to responds, and now she missed a test due to personal absent, she was dropped, (algebra)class, wow ceritos  college, ,, seems worse college  ever, also ,gotta pay for books, and yes its also online  books, pay for teacher test booklet too, rip off,i guess  teachers just gettin lazier,', 'Been a while since I’ve been to this campus, the new buildings are amazing!']

reviews: ['Nice experience excellent team work they help a lot so kindly', 'OTHTC High Desert Ultra (50K) Race, held at Cerro Coso Community College  each year in early December, not to be missed! name: Chabot College
reviews:
["The programs at Chabot College are extremely helpful (Eops, NextUp, Guardian Scholars) and I am grateful for all the counselors that helped me to get to the point of graduating; but the Admissions & Records Office constantly messes important paperwork up. (Lost transcript forms, writing the incorrect address on important forms ). The Financial Aid office at times messes up your disbursement (as I've had to pay for a semester out of pocket before; then had to go to the office to fight them for my money back.)

(In my honest opinion, some of the people in these offices have nasty energy attached to them and should watch the way they're  talking to these students. We're confused...this is a whole new world for us.)

I've had to come to the school 4-5 times after I graduated to check on the transcript form I filed to see if it was done correctly (they lost the first form I filled out & paid for)

I will say Chabot has gotten more strict on their identification policy. (when I first started in 2022, they allowed you to show them your student ID). But...Students can no longer use their Student ID Card @ the Financial Aid Office & Admissions and Records Office.

One of my professors told us that Chabot has been recieving a lot of fake students enrolling to try to recieve financial aid.

Overall, Chabot is great.

Lots of classes to choose from, attentive & caring counselors, most of the professors are kind, helpful and want you to succeed in life.

[here's a tip]: make friends! Don't be shy, because we're all here for the same thing! learning/growth! The best thing we can do is help eachother. I'm leaving Chabot with friends I've made from being in programs and study groups!

Something else I'd like to put out there for students & parents, is to make sure you use your voice and keep record of all important documentation here.

Colleges need to be held accountable for messing up too, thats how people fix things... by making mistakes.

Anyway...Grateful for my time at Chabot, peace out & good luck to all future gladiators  ✌️ ☮️  August 2025", 'HORRIBLE communication. Went back and forth for almost three months regarding my admission for transfer credit of one online winter course. Would take a week to respond to me after I would email back within the hour. No way to talk to someone on the phone. Told me after months that they could not admit me unless I went in person which is 8 hours away from me. I now have no options left as. 0/10', 'If you are looking into taking classes in the bay to pursue your college education I suggest schools in the peralta district like Alameda Or Merritt. Not only is chabot a terrible option to continue your education as the counselors give awful advice in order to prolong your stay, but certain teachers take pride in failing students (I’ve heard first hand). Not only that but class capacity is at an all time high with often more students than chairs. During registration it’s extremely frustrating as someone students result to botting just to get the specific classes they need. Lastly the campus security are extremely rude and unhelpful. One example of this was when I was verbally attacked and harassed over a ticket I had no reason for receiving due to the dispenser being out of order. All around this school is a clown show with ~70% of staff not caring about you in the slightest and look forward into making your life more difficult. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND!', 'Worst community college experience ever.

Absolutely 0 accessible student services. Nobody picks up calls, nobody responds to emails. The professors are either decent or outright terrible. If you or your child does go, make absolutely sure you pick a major that prioritizes in-person learning, because the remote courses and resources are an absolute scam and only exist to prop up tenured "professors" that think they own the world.

If I could rate it 0 stars, I would.', 'True definition of a Community college. Resources for the community, clean, respectful atmosphere, and really support the students.']

reviews:
['Chapman is a fantastic school. In 15 years I have seen the transformation of a great university. I attend the Economic Forecast and enjoy the campus life, the Musco Center is breathtaking. Unique & incredible community in heart 🧡 of Orange County CA is home to outstanding progressive academics.

name: City College of San Francisco
reviews:
['City College of San Francisco is what higher education is supposed to look like when it’s actually serving students instead of performing for rankings and donors. The focus is on teaching, skill-building, and real outcomes. Classes are practical, instructors are engaged, and students are there to learn, transfer, or get to work—not to posture or play prestige games. For the cost, the value is obvious and immediate.

Comparing that to places like UC Davis makes the difference impossible to ignore. UC Davis operates like academic theater: polished messaging, endless buzzwords, and a lot of self-congratulation, but surprisingly little substance underneath. CCSF doesn’t waste time pretending to be elite—it just does the job. UC Davis, by contrast, spends enormous energy staging excellence rather than delivering it.

At CCSF, students are grounded, focused, and outcome-driven. At UC Davis, too much of the culture revolves around image, signaling, and bragging, with graduates often leaving confident in the brand but weak in practical competence. One institution prioritizes learning and utility; the other prioritizes appearances.

City College of San Francisco proves that real education doesn’t need hype, inflated tuition, or bureaucratic spectacle. It delivers substance without the performance—and that alone puts it miles ahead of universities that mistake reputation for value.', "City College of San Francisco (CCSF) is a community institution with real integrity. It doesn’t try to sell you prestige—it earns your respect through quality teaching, support systems that actually function, and a diverse student body that’s motivated and resilient. Whether you're transferring to a four-year university or leveling up your career, CCSF gives you real tools, real value, and real progress. It’s a space where hard work pays off and independent thinkers are respected, not suppressed.

By contrast, UC Davis often feels like a polished performance—more focused on reputation management than meaningful education. It wears the UC badge proudly, but that badge doesn’t guarantee depth. Many students find themselves stuck in giant lecture halls, chasing validation in a system that prioritizes image, not inquiry. Creative, sharp, or unconventional minds can feel boxed in—told to fit the brand rather than think freely. It's a place where surface-level achievement is often rewarded more than real intellectual effort.

At CCSF, students are seen. They're supported, challenged, and encouraged to grow on their own terms. UC Davis, by contrast, often seems more invested in looking successful than actually being transformative. The result? An education that feels disconnected from reality—expensive, branded, and not always worth the hype.

If you care more about becoming skilled and capable than just collecting a name-brand diploma, City College of San Francisco is the smarter, more honest choice…", 'I feel very happy to have earned my diploma from CCSF.
Education itself wasn’t my biggest obstacle — it was the hatred that some professors had toward me and expressed without any hesitation, even though I was paying them to educate me, not to hate me.
This has been one of the most racist places I’ve ever been.
But I’m proud because I managed to overcome it and walk out of there with my head held high, with my Food Service Manager diploma, and without hating them for failing in their attempt to make my life miserable during my time at that depressing institution.', 'Most of the instructors at this college will not accept class add requests. They are rude and mean. The waiting list is not worth since you can be on it for months and they will never give you a spot. Not enough courses for all the demands.', "I've only ever been inside the Multiuse Building and the Rec Center for a swim class at Ocean Campus.

City College multiple sites across San Francisco and classes are offered both in person, hybrid, and online (sync and asynchronous).

Languages like Spanish, Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese, German, Italian, French, and Tagalog are regularly offered, although sessions are fewer for higher level courses. Except for Spanish and Mandarin, the expectation is that you'll transfer to an institution with more advanced level classes.

The college has a number of defunct certificate programs and cool classes that are no longer offered, eg app and game design in the computer science department.

The Ocean campus is walking distance from Balboa Park Station, a terminus for the K, M, and J trains + the BART trains going toward Daly City/Millbrae/SFO. There's also a ton of parking, although it isn't all free.

The community college is free if you're an SF resident. You pay some or all your tuition upfront, and it's refunded throughout the semester (that's been my experience).

I was able to register and get my account working in very little time.

Taking CS classes that use the Hills computer for submitting homework are hell on earth. Not all professors explain how to access the College's SQL database or how to remote login into the terminal. In those situations, you wonder why you're taking a class in the first place since you need to do 99% of your learning and troubleshooting on your own.

I've only used the counseling services to get my units approved or to schedule my graduation, but the few counselors I've interacted with are very helpful and proactive.

If you want to save money before transferring, you can't go wrong with City College. If you just want to take a class for fun or work on a certificate, there are tons of useless courses on computer networking / frontend development, paralegal stuff, construction management, and basically every Math course you'd want before upper level engineering / science stuff."]

name: University of Silicon Valley
reviews:
['Highly recommend the MBI program at USV!

I joined the pilot MBI cohort right after the new leadership took over, and honestly it’s been a great experience. The faculty is incredibly supportive and focused on student success. The biggest advantage is that you don’t have to wait to be a senior to get real work. Through USV, I have been given multiple opportunities to work on live client projects with companies such as Logitech and have secured a contracts to build AI-powered stakeholder intelligence system, netting over $25k in a single semester. I am now actively using the school's resources to launch my own startup. If you are looking for real engineering experience and a return on your investment before you graduate, this is the place to be.", 'I’m having a great experience at this university, which prioritizes collaboration, adaptability, and innovative approaches to problem-solving while fostering a supportive and inclusive community. The faculty and staff are not only knowledgeable but genuinely approachable, always listening to student feedback to enhance learning and tailor teaching methods to our needs. What sets this university apart is its forward-thinking approach, continually evolving to align with technological advancements and societal changes, preparing students for the future. As a veteran, this institution has been a strong foundation during my transition from active duty to civilian life. The staff and professors have offered invaluable support, and the veteran community here is welcoming, and we check in on one another, ensuring no one ever feels alone. I definitely recommend this university to anyone seeking a transformative and enriching educational journey.', 'DO NOT GO HERE. They promote AI art like its their job. The students and staff alike are friendly and helpful. I've felt welcome from day of stepping foot on campus.", "Compton college is good I love it I've been here for 2 years got my associate's degree no school is perfect but this one's all right give me a second chance to life", 'As a former professor and student here I can say that Compton College has been consistently disappointing in providing the education students expect. While some professors are excellent and genuinely committed to helping students succeed, many leave due to inadequate support and poor administrative oversight. Instruction in several courses does not fully prepare students with the knowledge and skills they need, and navigating different departments can be confusing because information is often incomplete or inconsistent. Programs like free food distribution are helpful, but they cannot replace the need for strong academic instruction and guidance. Some members of the administration have been unhelpful in responding to student concerns, which undermines the college’s mission to serve the community. Overall, the institution often falls short in supporting students effectively, and it is disheartening to see a college with the potential to positively impact its community struggle in this way. For those looking to take a few classes to meet transfer requirements, caution and selectivity are advised, but for pursuing a full degree, other schools in the Los Angeles Community College District—such as Long Beach City College, El Camino College, and Cerritos College—provide more consistent guidance, stronger resources, and a better overall educational experience. Man easy money ya think 🤔", "It's a great college, this is my first semester in CCC, I'm studying the ESL and I've felt so much better in my English.Thank you Contra Costa College and thank you professors.", 'I visited this campus twice recently and was really impressed with the faculty, administration, and sense of community I felt and experienced at this college! I attended an amazing poetry reading in the college library and met professors, a dean, students, administrators, and the college president. Everyone was so kind and welcoming. I could tell that they all really care about education and helping students! The campus is also really pretty with a lot of green spaces and places to meander as well as contemplate deeply. Such a happy place dedicated to higher learning!!', "Contra Costa College is one of those rare institutions that actually lives up to what education should be about: opportunity, integrity, and growth. It doesn’t pretend to be something it’s not—it simply delivers. Whether you're starting your academic journey, changing careers, or pushing for something bigger, CCC gives you a strong foundation. Faculty care, resources are targeted, and there’s a culture that rewards real effort and real intelligence—not just appearances.

Compare that to UC Davis, which has increasingly become a performative institution built on image rather than impact. While it talks a big game—about innovation, diversity, excellence—the lived experience for many students doesn’t reflect that. It’s a system that favors those who fit the mold and discourages those who challenge it. Critical thinkers are often boxed in, while surface-level performance is applauded. The learning environment can feel hollow—more focused on prestige than progress.

At Contra Costa College, bright minds are encouraged, not filtered out. There’s no need to posture or play political games—you just learn, grow, and move forward. UC Davis, by contrast, can feel like a place where keeping up appearances matters more than actual achievement. If you value authenticity, affordability, and real support—CCC is a far wiser investment."]

name: Cosumnes River College
reviews:
["I went to the CRC Counseling office for a drop in due to counselors never being available. After waiting for one and a half hours with no movement on the queue, I asked to be switched online. The long wait is understandable though because I went to a drop in. There were two ladies in the front. I asked the young lady if she knew the time range for a wait so I can keep an eye out for the email. The young lady was super sweet. BUT the older lady was so rude!!! They need to retrain her on manners. Avoid her at the counseling office and go to the young lady instead!!", 'The process of trying to get a counselor is absolutely ridiculous! I gave up and decided to stay at sac city because there is no way my peace was going to be taken. The staff seem very friendly. The college is aesthetically cute but be prepared to lose your mind just to get an appointment with the counselor. I still have yet to get one. They tell you to go online and then online tells you there’s no appointment and give you a number to call and that number just rings until it tells you they cannot assist you and refer you back to the website or to go in person and in person then tells you  to please go on the website and add CRC(sounds easy) Then Another person tells me that was incorrect. I need to redo my application and then add CRC wait 24 - 48 hours to make sure it’s been added or a counselor cannot see me. And the way to make sure your application was processed is calling that number that no one ever picks up. Or emailing the college. I just called sac city back and got an appointment with the counselor right away. Back to Sac city it is!', 'I really enjoyed myself and was able to relax and post some discount codes. Being able to focus on school and health.', 'My base school was scc, which I live right next to, but I travel to crc because of the environment! I feel completely safe and have met so many people I consider "mentors" or role models through this school! The campus is beautiful! The counselors are also easier to meet with.', "Cosumnes River College is one of the smartest choices you can make if you're serious about your future and don't want to waste time or money. The classes are affordable, the campus is welcoming, and the instructors actually teach — not just collect a paycheck while chasing tenure like you’ll see at big-name schools.

CRC gives you room to breathe and grow without all the ego, red tape, and fake academic politics. You’re treated like a real person, not a statistic.

Compare that to UC Davis: overpriced, bureaucratic, and full of surface-level “harmony” that hides how disconnected and competitive the system really is. Unless you're in a narrow range of high-demand majors (and even then, good luck getting into the right labs or networks), the return on investment is embarrassingly low. Students graduate tens of thousands in debt with no clear career path, while the school keeps pushing fluff and optics over results.

CRC respects your time, your budget, and your potential. If you’re smart and strategic, start here and don’t let big-name branding fool you — UC Davis is not worth the hype for most people."]

name: Diablo Valley College
reviews:
["This is a great Community College. The teachers and faculty are amazing, they go above and beyond for the students. I've come here as a 40+yr old student for the Culinary Arts/ Hospitality Associate of Science Degree for Transfer and was lucky enough to start when Chef Prater head of the Culinary Arts program has taken over and instating a Culinary Curriculum that he's spent 10 years developing, along with Chef Oscar they've developed an amazing very technical, hands on, business and service program that is designed to teach us not just how to cook but why we cook, the science and art of this passion based career. If you're considering a Culinary Arts degree I highly recommend coming to DVC and at least check it out, you'll be impressed I guarantee it. I'm happy and proud to be a student here at DVC.", 'I went to UC Davis expecting rigor, mentorship, and a strong intellectual culture. What I actually encountered was an environment that felt bloated by reputation and thin on substance. Collaboration was more slogan than reality. Instead, the campus culture revolved around cliques, internal politics, and people performing intelligence rather than practicing it. Decisions—academic and otherwise—often seemed driven by ego and hierarchy, not by what actually helped students grow or succeed.

What made it worse was the disconnect between confidence and competence. Many students leaned heavily on the UC label as proof of ability, yet struggled with basic critical thinking or accountability. Those who thought independently or demonstrated real skill were often met with resistance or hostility, while average performance was rewarded as long as it didn’t disrupt the status quo. There was little self-awareness and even less humility.

Support systems didn’t compensate for this. Advisors were overwhelmed, professors were frequently inaccessible, and career guidance felt vague and detached from reality. If you weren’t already connected or highly visible, it was easy to be overlooked. For an institution that demands so much financially, the payoff was questionable—especially when many graduates walk away earning about the same as an Uber driver.

Then there’s Diablo Valley College.

DVC was the opposite in almost every meaningful way. It was efficient, focused, and unapologetically practical. Despite being a community college, it consistently sends a large number of students to UC Davis—often better prepared than those who started there as freshmen. At DVC, instruction emphasized mastery, not image. Professors were present, standards were clear, and students were expected to actually understand the material.

Advising at DVC was personal and strategic. Counselors worked with students to build realistic transfer plans, not vague aspirations. The environment rewarded effort, discipline, and growth rather than networking or academic theater. There was no inflated ego—just people trying to move forward intelligently.

When you strip away branding and look at outcomes, Diablo Valley College delivered more value than UC Davis ever did. It respected students’ time, intelligence, and finances while quietly doing the work UC Davis takes credit for.

If I had to choose again, I’d start at DVC without hesitation. It offered clarity, preparation, and real return—things UC Davis promised but never truly delivered.', 'DVC is a great school. Among many programs, it provides an excellent low cost Dental Hygiene school that is open to public patients.', 'Beautiful campus. Many walks of life. Teachers and staff may not be reasonable at times but its generally good for an education.  Already had 2 friends transfer, you can go your own pace.', 'Really don’t like how theres no visitor parking. I’m a Veteran trying to sign up for classes and I wasn’t informed about $4 daily parking permits or even a $40 parking violation fee.']

Worth a visit just to explore the grounds. As a graduate student there, I can also recommend their program.', 'The student body is very diverse—racially, culturally and age-wise. The professors are dedicated and caring. The campus and surrounding area is beautiful. The library is filled with interesting books—some very old. The cafeteria has tasty food.']

name: East Los Angeles College
reviews:
['As an international student, I have received so many help from the international students office! There are plenty of school events for enriching students’ life!!! The environment is cool! I love the professors here! The classes schedule is various and plenty of choices!!!', 'Loved my classes! Took animation classes here! And got my degree in animation. I got lots of good benefits here. Started during covid, they were very informative if you actually open the canvas notifications. Campus was beautiful!', "Disappointing Experience with Admissions Process and Communication

I recently had a frustrating experience with the admissions process at ELAC. To make a long story short, they don’t even have a proper operator, which makes it frustrating to get any help. I was told by a representative at the welcome center that they don't answer voicemail calls, and that I need to physically come to the college to get assistance. As someone with a busy schedule, this is not feasible. To add insult to injury, the customer service I've received so far has been subpar. Unreturned phone calls and lack of clear communication have made this process incredibly stressful. I'm disappointed in the level of service ELAC is providing to its prospective students. Hopefully, the college can work on improving their communication and customer service to better support students like me.", 'Great school for transfers! ELAC has given me so many different opportunities. I have always been supported and guided by counselors and alumni alike. Given opportunities for internships, networking, federal work study, financial aid assistance, transfer talks, field trips with MESA, clubs, a safe environment, free food passes, a free shuttle, free tutoring, free merchandise, not to mention the low cost of tuition and other fees. Most of the professors here are really great. As of now I am attending UCLA to pursue my major in Linguistics and Computer Science. ELAC continues to strive for the best in helping ALL students succeed. I couldn’t have asked for much more. You receive so much assistance here and it only continues to grow.. but you do have to go and reach out for it. Stay engaged and you’ll reap the rewards. Best community college in the entire district.

Go Huskies!', 'Nice campus
Two large parking structures on both ends of college
Lots of restaurants within walking distance in Atlantic Square']

name: Evergreen Valley College
reviews: ['Fave college I went to including 2 different CSUs. The campus is gorgeous, the caf food is delicious, and the professors care SO MUCH. There are some very talented lecturers here. Shout out Professors Brian Gott and Paul Stamp!!! ❤️❤️❤️', 'A beautiful environment and I’ve been here only tennis and pickle ball. The ambience is pure bliss and I really like their parks and sports facilities.', 'Evergreen Valley College offers a student-centered experience anchored in academic support and community involvement. The campus is clean, modern, and thoughtfully designed, featuring quiet study spaces, dedicated resource centers, and approachable faculty. Programs like Enlace and robust tutoring services help students thrive, whether they’re preparing for transfer or building foundational skills.\n\nOutside of academics, the college also serves as a familiar starting point for local youth activities. Each year, Scouts gather here for the beginning of their annual meeting, using the space as a meeting point before heading to their next destination. The open layout and accessible location make it a practical and welcoming environment—not just for learning, but for launching meaningful community experiences.', 'Review pickleball only - awesome, well lit courts. Folks super friendly and welcoming... only draw back are occasional smokers, whose smoke seems to overtake the area?', "4/19/2022 Front renovations complete. Very pleasing in the night light. name: FIDM-Fashion Institute of Design & Merchandising
reviews:
['I graduated from FIDM in 2010. Although I ultimately pursued a career in the medical field rather than fashion, I remain incredibly grateful for the foundation FIDM provided—particularly the Financial Aid Department.

Thanks to the guidance and support I received back in 2008, I was fresh out of high school and was able to establish an AMAZING agreement with my loan provider that has continued to support me through my current journey in nursing school. The financial aid team truly held my hand through this process, and their dedication made a lasting impact on my educational path.

While I may not be working in fashion, I will always sing the praises of FIDM’s Financial Aid Department. Your commitment to student success has helped set me up for future educational success, and for that, I sincerely thank you.', 'Awesome campus in downtown LA! I was there for my first time last week at an event they hosted. This video below was taken on the 4th floor deck of one of their main buildings.

Also highly recommend checking out their on-campus museum!', 'money hungry school. this school is great until it comes to needing any kind of help with advisement or services. This institute puts on a front about caring and your best interest at heart until you actually get accepted and it’s as if your on the back burner. They take and take and give about 10%. The fees go beyond what is expected. When seeking help it’s extremely hard and there’s a lack of professionalism within the school. You can learn here but just know they take a lot more then they offer.', "If I could rate less than one star, trust that I would. I heavily appreciate spending x amount of money to attend this private university. Only to arrive out of the blue to commemorate my experience as an alumni from 2016. And security from all entrances refused me access without an appointment. Why would I want an appointment? The career center didn't help me out to get any job anyways, even when I was attending. I simply wanted to view the design shadow boxes on the second and fourth floors, that the students pride themselves on. Don't spend your time or money ladies!  Choose FIT (fashion institute of technology in nyc). I choose FIDM over FIT, such a mistake, such a pity. I don't care to associate with this college, I'm not even proud to be an alumni anymore. Shouldn't even be allowed to call themselves a university. That would require them to actually care about their students after their successes and accomplishments. Which they certainly do not. Unless money is involved.", 'This school is exceptional. It is not for everyone. Everyone thinks just because it's a fashion school, it's a "Barbie" school, it will be easy. This school is tough and fast pace because it teaches you what things are really going to be like in the industry. If you are hard working and know what you want you will succeed in this school. The teachers are experienced and are there to push you to your highest potential. It just takes a mature, hard working person. And that's what employers are looking for.']

name: Feather River Community College District
reviews: ['This school issued out money to a person who stole my DOB and info. name: Foothill College
reviews:
['If I had been there 15 years ago for taking the placement test that had to do with the TTW program, I wish I might visit there. On summer 2013, I had met two females, Rita the adapted kinesiology instructor and Pat Hyland the dean. During my fall quarter, I saw Pat Hyland again like meeting again. Besides that, I saw Pat Hyland as a guest speaker before on fall 2013 quarter. When I come, I’m hopeful that I’ll see them again. I’m sure that they’ll recognize my name, Joshua Jun class of 2014 in TTW', "Foothill College is an amazing place with a beautiful campus, and many positive aspects. However, there are areas that could use improvement. One suggestion is to choose better deans who are empathetic and understanding of students' concerns, rather than dismissing them or making students feel that their worries are insignificant.

Additionally, the college should consider hiring more competent faculty members for the accounting team and those responsible for overseeing tutoring centers. Unfortunately, some staff members seem to play the victim and inadvertently put students in difficult situations. It's important for colleges to hire professionals rather than individuals who act immaturely.

Furthermore, the college should conduct thorough background checks on potential hires to ensure they prioritize student safety. This is crucial in maintaining a secure environment for all students.

The mental health services at the college also need improvement, specifically by hiring more therapists, especially women of color. While this is not meant to be a discriminatory statement, the current staff is predominantly middle-aged Caucasian women, who may not fully understand the complex issues that BIPOC students face. The mental health system needs to become more trauma-informed and responsive to diverse needs.

Lastly, the Disabilities Resource Office requires more resources and support for students with disabilities. It's vital that these students receive the proper attention and care they deserve, rather than being overlooked.

Overall, Foothill College must strive to do better. Students are investing their hard-earned money in their education, and they deserve a supportive and understanding environment.

Let's fight for systemic justice in educational systems!", 'Sprawling community college in a nice central location on the peninsula. Was there for a soccer game, and the facilities looked well-maintained. The roads are a bit windy and could be confusing at times. Plenty of parking spaces.', "Foothill college is literally the best community college out there. The teachers are, in my opinion, world class and always go out of their way to provide students with a robust education. Also, it's affordable and excellent for achieving your goals.

Also, the school has a fitness center open to the community. It provides amazing equipment and with monthly and semester installments, it's an affordable alternative to mainstream gyms.", "This is the coolest college I could have landed at. Not only is the curriculum new, this school gives people the gateway into the real world of business, tech, and the humanities with what's most current and easiest to understand. I must top that with the WHOLE staff cares. I have yet to find an instructor who doesn't devote their entire being into the care of each of their students thank you Foothill for helping immensely in creating who I am today! To infinity and beyond!"]

name: Fresno City College
reviews: ["Great, I had to visit several times. I had to enroll and deal with paperwork issues and a native American grants application. Everyone there is helpful and nice. It's a great place to have to spend time and deal with. The transit to city college is better than other routes but watch for busses that don't catch each other drive by without seeing you.", 'One of the best places in the country to start or continue your professional career. Love the campus and the staff. Every staff member and instructor is very professional and kind.  A wide variety of programs in many fields.', 'It is a beautiful school. The Old Administration Building is a classic structure.', 'The lady in the records office could not have been more more helpful. Her expertise in willingness to assist was exceptional. My only gripe is that their lack of signage means you have to walk all over campus to try to figure out where you need to be. The campus is very clean and attractive and there’s a lot of parking but only if you have a permit.', 'I\'ve had two "college careers" here. One after high school and before I transferred to Fresno State, and one recently to learn web design. It\'s still an affordable option to learn new job skills or transfer to a university. Just make sure to seek out help if you need it (It\'s always available, just keep at it), and this can be a good, affordable alternative to going straight to a university for a bachelor\'s degree.']

name: Fresno Pacific University
reviews: ['Debbie in the mail room  withheld my medicine from me that I needed BEFORE class. Right after winter break, not even the second day of school in the second semester I lost my student id during break. Debbie refused to type in my manual number and she told me to come back later even though I told her I had class', "If you're new to campus, I’d suggest avoiding Art as your advisor. Not everyone may have the same experience, but this was mine. As a first time visitor to the Campus, I was left feeling challenged as yo how I was going to find the office/building I was looking for.  In fact, I wound up leaving because nobody could assist me.\nTo be fair, I went back a couple of days later after my contact on campus sent me the map link and I found the office with no problem.  Beautiful Campus,  pleasant non-treatening police presence, God filled Staff and students.  Who wouldn't want to get lost here?  LQTM, it wasn't that bad, really. It provides a slower paced experience, positive atmosphere, and strengthens your religious beliefs as well as challenging them. I was impressed by how much I learned in non religious aspects as my field is psychology and I feel confident graduating here knowing I got the best college experience.', "I had an incredibly frustrating experience at FPU when my boyfriend mistakenly took my car key with him after dropping him off for class, and he was unreachable due to a broken phone. Despite being listed as an emergency contact and even with his mother's verification, the registrar's office refused to assist me in paging him/locating him or even providing his class schedule. Their lack of concern and unwillingness to help in a genuine emergency situation was shocking and disappointing."]

name: Glendale Community College
reviews:
['Glendale Community College has a decent campus overall, but the hills are extremely steep. I feel like it would be really tiring to walk up and down those slopes every day. The school itself seems fine, but the terrain makes daily commuting pretty challenging.

Something to keep in mind if you prefer a flat and easily walkable campus.', 'Glendale Community College (GCC) offers a solid educational experience with a strong focus on student success and transfer opportunities. The campus is clean, well-maintained, and features updated facilities, including modern classrooms and a helpful library. Professors are generally supportive and knowledgeable, especially in popular programs like nursing, business, and the arts. The college also provides a range of student services such as tutoring, counseling, and career guidance. While parking can be a bit challenging during peak hours, the overall atmosphere is welcoming and student-focused, making it a great choice for those starting their academic journey.', 'Adventist Health Center is conducting a Vaccine center at The Glendale Community College in the parking structure at the top of the hill right off of the 2 Fwy Off the Mountain exit. The staff are very helpful. There is very clear and strict mandates on masks and health protocols. Please follow signage and bring your masks. You will need your ID for check in.
The nurses are very helpful and many of them have worked in the ER with patients and have seen the effects of the pandemic. So most of them are very happy to administer the vaccine and help prevent the spread of this terrible disease.
We are all so happy to share the change in the world and grow together. There is Hope and these are the people that are here to spread that hope.
3👍🏼’s out of 3👍🏼’s the staff and Nurses are very helpful and thoughtful.', 'Best Community College in California! Amazing professors and a school that takes care of their students.', "The staff at this school exhibit a concerning lack of professionalism and diligence. They seem unwilling to put in the necessary effort, often providing incorrect information and resorting to blaming students for their own shortcomings. Classes are abruptly canceled mere days before the semester begins, displaying a lack of foresight and consideration for students' schedules. Additionally, encounters with staff members can be characterized by rudeness and incompetence, creating a hostile environment for students.

It's imperative to hold them accountable for their actions and demand better treatment. If you want your concerns to be taken seriously, it's essential to reciprocate the same level of assertiveness and firmness in your interactions with them. From mishandling important documents that could jeopardize an entire semester to issuing incorrect grades, this institution fails to meet even the most basic standards of competence and professionalism. In my experience, it stands as one of the worst community colleges in Los Angeles County."]

reviews: ["I've been a student at Grossmont College for three years now; I took classes at different colleges, but I didn't receive the education I received here.\nMost the instructors are well prepared and care about the learning of the student and the learning outcome more than the grade; because of course, grade is  not everything!\nAs of fall of 2018, I have taken a total of 101 units for different majors, and they were amazing.", "Angela NGO is the absolutely worst professor I've ever had. name: Harvey Mudd College
reviews: ["Really a great college. name: California State Polytechnic University-Humboldt
reviews: ['Moved a kid into the dorms and everyone was so incredibly knowledgeable, kind, helpful..... it was almost surreal. The campus is beautiful. So many trees! Love the architecture.  There also seems like there is a lot of support for students.  Fingers crossed it stays amazing as time goes on.', 'I am an alumni here. I studied forestry and come to find out it was a wasted degree. I should have worked for a local arborist and worked my way up, instead I struggled in college for a degree that was relatively useless. Yes, I did use it to make $100,000/year when I got out and before I did, but I think in forestry its better if you just work for an arborist and earn your ISA certified arborist. During my time here the police stalked me and bothered me, girls reported me to the dean and I had these dean meetings. This college supports you if you are female, black, hispanic, native american, etc. Being white and male is okay, but you get targeted here. It\'s just a very inappropriate culture. A professor I had Jeffrey Kane wanted to give me a C on my final project that I worked with the Department Chair of Forestry on and when I complained about it he said "Well what kind of grades do you normally get" I also had a professor Andrew Stubblefield lower my grade at his will without me turning in or missing an assignment. That felt wrong. This college is due for a civil rights lawsuit against them. Just my words after going here for 8 years. I had many positive encounters, but these were some highlight able negative ones. Make good decisions. Decide what those are for yourself. Hopefully you make it out and do well in life. Your fellow Alumni.', 'Beautiful campus. Graduation event was nice and organized. This area is wonderful.', 'Great place to get an education. Location is like no other', 'How dare you not honor Charles Bellos wishes after he endowed his estate to you']

name: Humphreys University-Stockton and Modesto Campuses
reviews: ["Small but excellent college. The accelerated program makes it easy to forget details from one class to the next, but it allows the student to complete their degree faster. name: Irvine Valley College
reviews:
['I visited Irvine Valley College yesterday and was really disappointed. The campus felt more like a collection of temporary container buildings rather than a proper college environment. The facilities were outdated, and nothing about the place felt welcoming or well-maintained.

The accessibility was also poor — getting around the campus didn’t feel convenient at all. Based on this experience, I’ve decided to look into other community colleges instead.

Definitely not what I expected.', 'Once I needed to take a PSYCHOLOGY class in the summer and only ended up in Professor Susan Gil's' class because every other section was full and I thought, 'How bad could it be?'

This class was a whole circus... She would show up late with these crusty PowerPoints from 2015 of 200 pages, complains about her schedule and how "overworked' she is and how her ADHD makes it impossible for her to stay organized. If you ask a question she hits you with the classic, 'Do your own research,' as if we didn't pay actual MONEY to be taught. Girl, WE are the ones researching while YOU sit there reading off PowerPoints you copy and pasted during the Obama administration.

I have no idea how they still hires her. She never grades anything on time-like literally weeks go by and the gradebook is just empty. No feedback, no comments, nothing. She's super aggressive for no reason too. One time a kid asked about a canvas assignment that had magically disappearedand she snapped and said she could 'call security' if people kept 'acting up.

And forget getting help. Prof. Susan Gil literally never answers emails, never clarifies anything, and then acts shocked when everyone is confused. Honestly feels like she uses grades as revenge when she's having a bad day. By mid-semester HALF the class had dropped.. Honestly, overall the campus is actually not that bad, but particular individual?...

NOT worth the money, the stress, or the brain cells I lost. Take it at another college.', "I just couldn't hate phone verification more. I don't have signal at home or on campus, so i have no access to my canvas, neither my homework or zoom class link. Each time I want to login, I have to wait until I have signal. I don't know if this truly prevents terrorist threat from us, IT DOES NOT HELP US AT ALL!", 'My experience with Irvine Valley College’s Admissions and Records office has been the worst I’ve had in higher education. I filled out my FAFSA eight months in advance, corrected my residency after returning from a year of military service, and ensured my college of record and catalog year were listed as IVC 2025—yet none of that transferred correctly when IVC and Saddleback switched to the new Ellucian MySite platform in Fall 2025. The system change completely messed up my records, and instead of being helpful or accommodating, the A&R office was dismissive and unresponsive.

For nearly two months, I had to fight to fix a simple records issue that jeopardized my financial aid. Every call ended with being placed on hold, hung up on, or redirected to Saddleback College—only to be told it was IVC’s responsibility. Student workers handled calls without proper training, and no one followed up until I finally CC’d the Vice President on my emails. Only then did they act.

As an Irvine native, I chose IVC because of its strong reputation, but this experience has been incredibly disappointing. The A&R office’s lack of professionalism, accountability, and urgency caused unnecessary financial stress and made what should’ve been a simple fix into a months-long ordeal. Students deserve better from an institution that claims to prioritize excellence.', 'Here's a fun question - How much time does it take to register for some classes at IVC?

Even if you're not a degree pursuing student, the answer is apparently at least 3 months. The Admissions department is an absolute clown show as you can see from some of the reviews below.

First you need to email them after you've already submitted an application, just to ask them to actually process your application - a process that many, many other schools have been able to figure out without requiring additional input from the student.

Then someone replies to my email saying I need a registration time for Spring 2026 with a "Have you been assisted already?" when clearly no one has replied.

Then I get someone asking me for my student ID, and only my student ID.

Then I get passed off to someone else who tells me I need to submit a legal ID, just so they can pass off the work to the next person who has to answer.

This is ridiculous, I've been fighting this Admissions department to register for classes AT YOUR COMMUNITY COLLEGE SINCE AUGUST AND IT'S NOW OCTOBER. ARE YOU KIDDING ME IVC?']

Edit:

The last class I took from them, online, featured more bizarre harassment—i.e. transcript fraud. reviews: ['I came to tour Laney College during an enrollment event advertised on television and because they offered free tuition for the  fall 2023 semester. name: La Sierra University
reviews:
['La Sierra is overpriced. Like genuinely expensive compared to most universities, and it does not feel like you get that value back.

Campus life is basically dead. When you walk around, you’ll barely see students. It feels like a ghost town, and honestly that makes the place feel weirdly unsafe, because there’s just nobody around. It’s empty in a way that doesn’t feel peaceful, it feels off. Even the random stuff you see is strange, like the other day there was a Jeep that had crashed into a tree and it just sat there for two days. That made no sense and it honestly felt like Jurassic Park.

The classes are hit or miss, but the biggest issue is the forced religion requirements. This is an SDA Christian university, and they make that very clear. You’re required to take religion classes, and you’re also expected to go to chapel on Tuesdays. I’ll be real, I like faith, and chapel can be a good thing, but the fact that it’s mandatory makes it feel more like a chore than something meaningful. I’m here to take my classes and move on.

The campus facilities also feel old. Some buildings are honestly kind of smelly, and a lot of classrooms feel like basic high school rooms. It doesn’t always feel like a real college environment.

There also aren’t many good study areas around campus. You would think studying outside would be a peaceful option, but most of the seats are in the scorching sun, and a lot of them are covered in spider webs or bird poop. So being outdoors and studying is basically not an option.

Also, the security presence can be unprofessional. I was studying in the business building at night around 10:30 pm, and a heavyset security guard barged in and kicked everyone out rudely. No greeting, no basic respect, just cleared the room like we were doing something wrong. We were literally just studying. I’ve also pulled up to the front entrance kiosk and seen some of the student workers in pajamas or looking sloppy in hoodies, acting like they don’t care. It does not feel professional. I’ve also seen campus security pull people over for minor stop sign issues, which feels excessive compared to the actual issues on campus.

Now for the positives. The campus is small, but it’s pretty. It has a nature vibe even if it’s not really “nature.” It’s also insanely easy to get around. I can walk from one end of the university to the other in about five minutes or less, which is honestly amazing. I also like that it’s gated, so it feels safer than a lot of other campuses.

The library is actually really nice too. It’s peaceful, it feels secure, and it’s one of the best places to be on campus.

The fitness center hours feel weirdly limited. For something that has card access, it should be open longer.

The president also seems like a genuinely nice guy. Every time I see him, he’s friendly and greets people, and some of the staff are the same way. They feel approachable, and I do appreciate that.

Parking is free, which is a big plus. For how expensive this school is, at least you can park without paying and usually park wherever you need to.

And the only downside to the pretty gated campus vibe is the coyotes. There are so many running around it feels like a whole pack lives there.', "I went there to attend a baseball game. Nice field, the seating was difficult on my back. The campus looks very well maintained. Next time I'll bring my own chair.", 'very expensive for the same amount of education that you will get in public school. on top of that the stuff lives on the students mistakes... if you do something wrong expect everyone will talk about you', 'I attended La Sierra from 1972-1974.  As a 17 year old freshman, I was very homesick for my family and my community.  The educational experiences were wonderful, and I was subsequently accepted to the School of Dentistry at Loma Linda University to further my education and career goals!  I wouldn’t change any of it…best years of my life!', 'While I wasn’t a student there luckily, I have spent time on the campus and interacted with staff and student. There is zero campus life (which for me is actually prefer) but despite that, I have reason to rate it as low as we can go. Very expensive. Very understaffed. Basically paying to be taught by other students cause all the professors are stretched to thin. I went to events and I thought they hadn’t started yet, only to find out no one ever comes. The education department is the most incompetent and uncaring from what I’ve seen and heard. Seems they are actively trying to screw up the lives of future teachers. When the school closes the community will benefit.']

name: Southern California University of Health Sciences
reviews:
['Just finished taking General Chemistry with the lab and I can say that was one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had when it comes to school.  This is supposed to be a general course, but the amount of work and the level of work required did not feel like a general course.  I’ve taken biochemistry at this school, and it was not as strenuous as this general chemistry course.  The lab, which is a 1 unit course, had more work than the lecture course.  Professor Sanchez listed a rubric for the lab notebook entry and then requires more than what the rubric states for a 20/20.  My notebook entries ended up being about 8 pages long each time.  The lecture course had so much work, there isn’t enough time in a week to watch the lecture videos, do the homework and read, especially if you’re working and/or have a family to take care of.  The first exam, the average score was a 60/100.  If most people are barely cracking a D on an exam, there’s something wrong with the class.  It also doesn’t make sense to have 45 minutes for 5 mathematical questions for the quiz and then 1 1/2 hours for the exam with 40 questions.  I highly advise against taking a lecture and a lab, I was aiming for As but was fortunate to finish both with Bs.  Even looking past my grades, it is incredibly strenuous to complete all the work and study in the given time.  I had to limit myself to about 5 hours of sleep each day for 5 weeks so that I could have enough time to complete all the work and learn the material.  Hard to justify paying $2200 to have such a hard time with a general course.  Safe to say, I won’t be taking any more classes at SCUHS.', 'I took the physiology and microbiology courses for prerequisites,  and would definitely recommend any courses under Professor Cauilan. She responds quickly to messages, explains difficult concepts in an efficient manner, and presents lecture material in a way that maximizes understanding. I cannot speak for the reviews on other courses, but can definitely say that courses under Professor Cauilan were worth it!

For asynchronous classes, it is all about how you want to study and pace the course.', "worst online class experience of my life. I have a four year degree from SFSU and am pursuing a graduate degree. I needed a chem class as a pre requisite. Chose SCUHS for the tutoring included.

The class structure is horrible. I feel like they set you up to fail in order to get you money AGAIN. Do not go here if you just need medical pre requisites.

Also, I'm saying this as someone who really enjoys going to school. I got mostly A's in my undergraduate degree, (B's my last year because I needed to work a lot). I'm not saying this as a lazy student who doesn't like to learn or work hard in class. Literally worst money I've spent on school in my entire academic career.", 'Man what a terrible experience. Feels like a money scam. The class average for our lecture exam for Chem 1 was a 43, but no corrections were allowed.. So half the class had to drop or end up failing. DO NOT SIGN UP THIS IS A PURE MONEY GRAB.', "I would advise against their accelerated courses. The tuition was $1600 for a primarily textbook based course. It's not suitable if you don't learn well that way. It's a scam at best. The staff is also disorganized and don't seem to care about your grievances. It's all about the money and not you as a student/person."]
