name: Newschool of Architecture and Design
reviews:
['I’m a recent graduate with a BA in Interior Architecture from NewSchool. I still remember my first campus visit. I was just walking around the neighborhood when I decided to stop by the building and ask for a tour. It was summertime, so the school was quiet, but the enrollment team welcomed me with open arms.
I even got to meet Elena, who was the Dean of Design at the time. She was so kind and genuine, and her Italian accent made me feel instantly at ease, especially since I’ve always been a little self-conscious about my own. She told me not to worry, because many of the professors at NewSchool come from different parts of the world. That stuck with me. I’ve always loved diverse environments, and I knew right then that this was a place where I could belong and grow.
NewSchool isn’t your traditional school—and that’s what makes it special. To thrive here, you have to be open to change and willing to be challenged in new ways. You’re encouraged to think for yourself, question conventions, and carve your path. It’s not always easy, but that’s what makes the experience powerful.
Throughout my time at NewSchool, most of my professors were incredibly supportive. I was a full-time student while also working full time, and many of them went out of their way to help me balance both. Architecture school is demanding—you need passion, resilience, and a real commitment to your goals. But what makes NewSchool stand out is how much the faculty cares. They understand that every student is different, and they truly want you to succeed.
Now that I’ve graduated and joined the NewSchool team professionally, I’ve had the chance to see even more of the transition the school is going through. I believe NewSchool is evolving in a direction that reflects the real world—diverse, innovative, and forward-thinking. Change isn’t always easy, especially in a creative field, but I believe the leadership here understands what the future demands.
Since the passing of Marvin J. Malecha, many have stepped up to carry on his legacy. The pandemic also brought big challenges to higher education. But through it all, NewSchool continues to push forward—and I’m proud to be part of that journey.
If you’re someone who wants to think differently, who embraces diversity, and who’s ready to grow not just as a designer but as a person, then I think you’ll find your place here, just like I did.', "I have been going to Newschool for three years now and I feel extremely fortunate. I have met some of the most passionate, intelligent, and design-minded instructors here. I am continuously amazed by all of the wonderful opportunities that Newschool has to offer. As a student who is very involved, Student Council President, AIAS member, Library Aid, and Student Life Aid, I can say that the complaints that I've heard always come from those who expect to be handed things. With any school, this is not, and should not be, the case. Newschool provides you with the tools and it is up to students to take advantage of them. If you don't have the drive to do so, this is not the school for you. The school has undergone serious change and has improved immensely over the last 3 years. I foresee this trend continuing.", "I attended the NewSchool of Architecture & Design for their Architecture program. I was impressed with the faculty's expertise and dedication to helping students succeed. The curriculum was comprehensive and provided a well-rounded education in architectural theory and practice. The school's emphasis on hands-on learning and real-world projects offered valuable practical experience. The close-knit community fostered collaboration and personal growth. Overall, I had a positive experience at the NewSchool and would encourage aspiring architects to consider it.", "It's better than California College of Arts. I attended 2 years and was disappointed. NewSchool is up and coming for sure.", 'Paying a lot of money here for my online degree program to learn that all my online peers just copy and paste things from chatgpt/AI generated answers for our assignments, and it seems like the teachers have not picked this up. Some faculty staff are nice, most are hostile and are not respectful of your time.']

name: Occidental College
reviews: ['Just graduated from Occidental in 2025 and could not be more pleased with my experience. The most amazing professors, great class sized, enormous opportunities (I studied abroad fully funded, held two research fellowships, and had a translation published), and wonderful financial aid. So glad I picked this school.', 'Nice campus. Alot of foliage. JESUS said, " I AM the way, the truth and the life and no one comes to the FATHER but by ME."', 'My younger sister attends school here and absolutely loves it. Such a beautiful campus and helpful staff! Love visiting!', "Graduated in '87 and look back at my 4 years at Occidental as giving me a strong foundation for life.  Took some adjusting coming from a CA public education (academically speaking) but being taught how to learn by not limiting yourself to only one point of view...that's liberal arts for you.  End up knowing a little about a lot.  And so glad to this day I took advantage of the Oxy in Washington program apart from D.C. in August weather.", 'A magical college campus in Los Angeles! Reason. Critical thinking. Global perspectives. Social justice.  This is a happy place in Eagle Rock and I encourage you to check it out.  Also great for an afternoon walk - with or without a dog!']

name: Ohlone College
reviews:
['I am proud to be an alumni of this great college!  It was a great experience!  I highly recommend this college for the first two years of their college journey or to those, like myself, who just want to return to college again!', 'Great scenery and campus, also decent learning facilities!', "Ohlone college parking lot . Lots of parking but why start from 6AM .. now it's free from 6 am  to 11 pm .. beautiful view of mission peak in early morning .. weather was cold and foggy and lots of wind but still enjoying hike as always ..", "I would like to share my deep frustration with the enrollment process at Ohlone College.

I have previously taken courses at De Anza College, where the enrollment system is clear, straightforward, and efficient. In comparison, my experience with Ohlone has been extremely disappointing due to its confusing, bureaucratic, and inefficient processes.

Despite following all instructions, I have been unable to register for courses. When I reached out for help, I was often redirected to different departments, receiving generic, unhelpful responses that wasted my time but never solved the problem.

For example, after completing my English placement test, I was told by a counselor that I was eligible to select my desired courses. However, the system still classified me as an ELI student and blocked my registration, forcing me to contact yet another department.

The most frustrating part is that I applied for the new semester months ago, yet I am still not enrolled.

Every attempt to get assistance has been met with bureaucratic replies, or I'm told to make an appointment with a counselor. Ironically, the online appointment system doesn't even work—it keeps logging me out and won’t let me schedule anything.

I know how to use enrollment systems. At De Anza, everything went smoothly, so this is not a user error. Despite my patience and persistence, my efforts to enroll in courses at Ohlone have been exhausting and deeply disappointing.

Frankly, I would not recommend Ohlone College to my friends based on this experience. As of today, I am still unable to join the classes I applied for.

I hope this feedback reaches someone who truly cares about resolving these ongoing issues.", "Awesome campus right on a hill. The topography makes for an awesome view of the bay. Lots of new and tall buildings, and trails nearby. This campus is especially beautiful in the spring. When it comes to classes, it's alright. I do think their canvas class pages tend to be VERY cluttered with too much stuff compared to other bay area colleges, it can be quite overwhelming. But that's not what a review of the maps place is for."]

name: Orange Coast College
reviews:
["Orange Coast College (OCC) is a great place for anyone who wants to learn and enhance their skills. They have a many course offerings and very convenient schedules. The subjects are relevant to the current business environment and can help an individual to become job ready. Our experience with their Adult Education team is fantastic! They are very prompt in responding to queries and are very student centric. Ms Sara Martinez, Jose Castrejon, Mindy, Abby, Karen & Richard are excellent. Whether its getting access to books and study resources or getting guidance regarding the logistics, the entire team is always ready to help. Recently I met a 63 year old student who had just got his certificate of completion after finishing the Patient Aide Program and he shared his positive experience with the Adult Education department. They are a living example of the OCC motto 'We'll help you get there'. I highly recommend OCC.", 'Orange Coast College is an amazing institution! The teaching staff is incredibly knowledgeable in their fields and truly dedicated to student success. The programs are well-structured, and the college offers some of the most advanced certifications available in Southern California. I highly recommend OCC to anyone looking to further their education and career with a supportive and forward-thinking community.', 'The administrative staff I’ve had the displeasure of dealing with at the school are not very competent, are cynical and downright rude, including the financial aid office staff and the admissions and records staff.

If you ever want to know what the rest of your experience will be like at an institution, always see what your interactions are like.

The lack of accountability, empathy and helpfulness are all you need to know. They try to profit off shoddily built housing for students at exorbitant prices. Just remember, education is a business, and if they don’t run a good business, students (customers) can take their business elsewhere.', 'Very nice campus a lot of new buildings and looks some new construction starting.', "I came here to get certified for a new profession.  I paid $800 to take this course and $400 for course equipment.  One professor was a perfectionist, unhelpful, and disrespectful.  Instead of studying for three months and getting certified, 80% of the class and I failed.  I felt cheated out of my money.  Midway through another course, the security threatened to arrest me for carrying a knife.  They don't have signs prohibiting knives, you're just supposed to magically know.  They treated me as though I intended on using that knife to kill people.  I used that knife to cut plastic wrap, tape, and food.  Almost paid a lawyer $1,000 to come to the school.  After failing that course, I met with administration to discuss my performance.  They asked how I wanted to proceed.  I said I never wish to return.  I had two other professors here.  Both I had no issues with."]

name: Otis College of Art and Design
reviews:
['Honestly the school will go out of it’s way to make sure the students know what programs and tools they need to use in order to improve their skills. The professors are tough but for the right reasons. My only issue with the school is that they forced me to take a covid booster 2 days after I got over covid. Even though I was only taking classes online. Other than that the school is pretty great and I’d recommend it!', "Don't sign up for noncredit classes as you will not receive any grades. I took typography, web design and other classes mixed with storyboarding and Maya, but now that I transferred outside of Los Angeles, and I'm taking art classes I'm seeing a huge difference. I wasn't getting thorough training nor skills.

As a new students, I should have been urged to get credit classes so I could transfer or get credits, otherwise why would they charge 1k for each class while no history to it.

I thought at least, I had access to the job board, but one time I was trying to post a job on there, the girl in charge was  unfriendly and then when I told her that I usually check opportunities on there she blocked my access immediately.
Although I was actually a student in Otis,  she claimed  that this is strictly for their full-time students, which is untrue, because the former employee gave me a full access and she blocked it.

So then I wouldn't be taking further classes there because I'm wasting my money , instead I  would go to workshop or an Institute.

The professors were cool, a few were in tht industry and a few were outdated as in typography and storyboarding.", "If you're into majors that involve fashion, toys, packaging, woodworks, digital & physical media, animation, computers, etc. I cannot stress enough now good Otis is in not only helping you with these subjects, but also giving you skills to where you can find work that isn't just in the major/field you chose. The campus is relatively small and it isn't hard to navigate around the area.

However, for those who don't have a credit card, I would recommend that you bring your own food or get a credit card because both the cafeteria and the Cafe are credit only, no cash.", "Nice Clean campous.  The staffs are focused on the student's success.  They are more geared for employment than art promotion, is the impression I received after extensive interrogations :).  You should expect to land a job upon graduations, as the school puts a lot of efforts into getting jobs.", "Otis is a great alternative to Art Center. It's a friendlier environment and the student body is suited to for students coming from high school and community college. The new addition to the campus is really going to change the environment and make it even more communal because they are now going to offer on camps dorms. The education is awesome and like anything you need to work hard to receive the full benefits."]

name: Oxnard College
reviews: ["📚At Oxnard College, I studied ESL (English as a second language). In general, the buildings are beautiful and the classrooms are well-equipped. 📱The library provides free books and iPads for students. ‼️However, opinions about the teachers vary. I have never encountered a worse teacher than German Bermudez! ⛔️He is very arrogant, unfriendly, and the atmosphere in his class is always tense! ❌He speaks with a strong Latin accent, and he never explains new words. He always speaks quickly, and he gives strict deadlines for homework that you can't complete (on an iPad), which other teachers don't do. 👎As I was informed, he used to be a student and now he's a tutor, which is why he has a sense of grandeur. I am very disappointed that the college doesn't have control over who they hire…\n☝️Additionally, I would like to recognize the most excellent teacher in this college, Patricia Viveros! ❤️She always smiles, jokes with her students, and is very helpful in explaining new words!👩🏼\u200d🎓👨\u200d🎓 Her lessons are easy and fun, and the atmosphere is friendly! She is a great teacher with a lot of experience and a kind heart! ✨Her teaching methods make it easy to understand and learn English! I would recommend her as the best teacher ESL in Ventura County! 📖🇺🇸🫶🫶🫶", "I am attending Ventura County Community College's to complete prerequisites for the Radiology technician program at Moorpark College. Some of my classes are taken at Oxnard College. While the campus is very nice with lots of shade and parking, some of the staff have been incredibly unhelpful. The financial aid department has been the worst. I have been appealing things over and over, and they do not bother try to see that I have updated my financial aid appeal. Also, one day, I went to the academic counseling office during regular hours and was told all the counselors were at a meeting. Common sense would be to have at least one person available, but zero common sense. The head academic counselor, however, was incredibly helpful after I called later on in the week. Overall, I do not recommend you attend any of the community colleges in Ventura County. They are incompetent, unhelpful, and do not seem willing to go the extra mile in their jobs.", 'Oxnard College Academic Guidance Counselor Ms. Jennifer Ruppert is truly one of a kind. She is one of the most genuine, caring, and supportive individual I’ve had the pleasure of working with. She approaches her role with such grace and elegance, making every interaction feel thoughtful and meaningful. Ms. Ruppert wholeheartedly cares about her students—not just academically or professionally, but personally as well. Her encouragement and unwavering support have made a lasting impact on my journey. Oxnard College & VCCCD are incredibly fortunate to have her.', 'Oxnard College is a welcoming and supportive place for students. The campus is clean and well-maintained, with plenty of space to study, relax, or connect with others.\nThe professors and staff are knowledgeable and genuinely care about student success, making classes engaging and accessible. There are also great resources available, from the library to student services, which help make the college experience smooth and positive.', 'GREAT School. If you want to come take a few classes. This is the best place for you']

name: Hope International University
reviews: ['HIU is a pretty good to remain with a small number of enrollment (about 1,000 students) that I can imagine each class size should be smaller like less than 1:10 ratio. The student might close with each other including the professors.', "I graduated from Hope in 2012.   I started out as a transfer student and lived off campus but by my second year at HIU I fell in love with the community so much that I moved into the dorms.   I made life long friends while at Hope....got individual attention from my professors....and was able to grow as a leader.   For me a smaller Christian campus was a welcomed change after going to a university with 20,000 students where no one knew my name and I felt lost    I'm thankful for my time at Hope and got a college experience where I was able to go on missions trips, worship freely with my friends, and dig into the Bible in ways that where both challenging and rewarding at the same time.", 'We would not recommend this university unfortunately to anyone. There are better schools in Biola, APU, even Chapman. God bless your decision.', 'I raised my 5 children differently. Yes we homeschool, yes our eldest also attended public school part of her education years. We thought we were truly signing on to a Christian campus with a Christian dance team that was not the case. My daughter‘s dance coach was often late with a Starbucks in her hand though if a team member was late there was no grace shown. There was also favoritism. I feel the coach has a lot of maturing to do in her own private life, and that it influenced how she dealt with her team. Our daughter is highly intelligent and was in the honors ministry program and she did make The Dean’s list, though we only stayed 1 semester. There is so much that goes on in those dorms. They are not supervised. The food is the worst food that I have had personally, some of the stuff she brought with her when she came home (almost every weekend because it was so boring there) we tossed in the trash if.\nSo prospective parents high school graduates and families if you want to attend a school that will gladly take your money feed you less than quality food and allow so much sinful things to happen in their own dorm room and on their own campus then come here. PaPa God might have you here to bring more change but please pray before attending.', 'This school gets a one star because I can not give it a Zero. My main concern for this school is safety and security. There is absolutely no Campus Safety at this school despite what they advertise online. While I was there an entire athletic team had there phones stolen from an intruder on the campus. No one on the campus including the staff takes charge to keep doors locked and also expect campus security guards to open doors for anyone who asks. The staff doesn’t require any ID or credential check. Online it says the security guards are "professionals" yet don\'t even require a simple guard card to work there. Homeless people surround the school and are often found sleeping in class rooms, using drugs on campus, destroying school property or threatening to harm people on the campus or simply creeping around the dorm area. (In some cases they’ve even accessed the dorms!) The Staff encourage students to enter rooms or areas during closed hours(even if it’s late at night) and require security to open it for them and as a result the doors are left unsecured. Don\'t be fooled by this campus and there behavior of sweeping the crime rate under the rug. This is not an issue of the actual security guards, this issue is from the top! The leaders of this school have no regard for campus safety what so ever. The security guards are treated poorly by the staff and require security to work by there protocols even if it’s not best for the safety of the campus.']

name: Pacific Union College
reviews:
['Beautiful campus but the dorms need renovations.
$2.2M needed for Newton. 10-20K/room for the other dorms. $149M needed for entire PUC renovation.', "Visited this college for a women's ministry retreat. Beautifully landscaped and well kept. By flings are quite old but kept up modestly. Very hilly campus with lots of stairs.", "Class of 1981 AS Nursing and 2001 BSN. I was 25 when I first came to PUC after living on my own in my own apt since 18. I lived in the dorm the first time and the second time because of my age i had to live in the apts that are for married students. My experience was wonderful I came to PUC starting the summer quarter it was cheaper. I just read all the reviews and it was upsetting to me to have to read all the complaining. PUC is a 7th day Adventist college if you do not want to behave like a christian while you are there then don't go there. You do not go to college so you can have girls in your room. If you want a hamburger drive down the hill and get one the same for drinking and all the else you want to do. But do not run down my college because you are too immature to follow a few rules for 4 years which is nothing. I was never locked in, the dean let me stay out as long as i liked because she knew she could trust me, even when she knew i was with a man. yes i eat meat, i need to because of health reasons, i bought my own. Jewelry? yes i wore it before going to PUC but guess what? I put it in a safe deposit box in the bank while i was in college along with my red nail polish (not really but you get the point). The point of getting a Christian education is to get to know Jesus, God and the Holy Spirits work and what purpose He has for your life. After what God and Jesus gave up for you you can't give up a few things while at college. I bet those of you complaining were sent there by parents that did it because they cared about you and were trying to keep you out of trouble. So grow up! Be grateful you got to go to such a beautiful college with such great people. There are many many kids that would give up way more than you did to go to any college. I worked for years saving my money to go back to school and PUC was worth every penny and when i die they get the rest of my money to help the kids that will appreciate it like i did. I made wonderful friends there. But best of all i learned the true gospel of Jesus Christ through wonderful people like Pastor Venden and Dr. Desmond Ford. Glory be to God. Come soon Lord Jesus. LINDA FISCHER", 'Great institution all together! They were very helpful in meeting my financial needs with scholarships. As an international student, I must say that PUC made it possible for me to continue my education in the USA.', "Do you want a college that is incompetent in its financial department and can't even figure out a return statement? Do you want a college that 'masquerades' itself as a moral, upstanding, and open minded place of learning? Do you want a college that leaves you to 'believe' that they are for the 'greater good'? Do you want a college that has a food service for students that can potentially send them to the hospital, then BILL you for the mishap? Then this is the school for you!

Don't be fooled by the beautiful outside campus of this place, the dorms are poorly maintained(walls have peeling paint, there is always a musty smell, there are constant blackouts, the furniture given to students are borderline unusable AND if they break guess who gets charged?, the beds look like they belong to a 1950's prison cell and feel as if they violate all forms of health and safety), the buildings for some classes are equally poorly maintained and some have not been updated (i.e. no A/C in the middle of summer! Constant blackouts, various damaged walls, windows look like they belong in a war museum).

BUT the best part is their financial department! They lead you to believe that you are getting a top notch service for the low low price of $38,000 a quarter!!! Oh let's not forget to pile on tons of unnecessary 'extras', want to use your own medical plan to cover yourself? NOPE sorry you're using the school's medical plan that has LIMITED coverage!

How about a food plan that has food to help students get through the year in the middle of nowhere? NOPE sorry, you're using the school's cafeteria that has a RENOWN reputation of health violations (rodents and insects in the food? That's the LEAST of your worries, just hope the food doesn't send you to the hospital like it did to me!)

But let's not forget that this is a religious institution! Surely they have upstanding morals and beliefs right? To develop students to think for themselves, God, and lead a world where their students are the standard for humanity. WRONG, that's what they want you to believe! After being there, I can tell you how much discrimination there is for people that do not follow their religion heavily, the school is not out to help students, they are out to establish their dominance as a religion. The institutions that they associate themselves with are related to their religion, which is fine, but at the same time they are a business scheme out to make money. Only they are not as subtle. After this school where do you plan to go? Of course, the infamous Loma Linda University or Andrews! BUT, let's do a comparison. If these schools(PUC,Loma Linda, etc.) had such a reputation why is it that after I transferred for various health reasons and other problems that almost ALL of the colleges I went to after DID NOT accept various courses? Oh right, cut corner education! I'm not saying their professors are bad, no, in fact that was the highlight of the school. The professors truly are great people and out for the students' benefit, but they have no say in how the school is run and don't realize the reality of what the school is doing.

So, my TL;DR to people: Save your money and go to a quality school for a fraction of the cost if you care about your children and whoever you intend to send to this sorry excuse for a school with piss poor living conditions."]

name: Palomar College
reviews:
['Do your own research on transfer requirements—because the advising here clearly won’t. I trusted my counselor, followed their course plan, and wasted time and money on classes that didn’t count toward transfer. If you go here, assume your “two-year” path may quietly turn into four.', "I used to attend school there, but now I take my dogs for a walk there sometimes. We go through the hills and trails at the arboretum. It's beautiful with tall trees, and a lot of shade. They have many unique plants and shrubs throughout, very interesting to see.", "Affordable start to furthering education.
Wish I were still local; I would consider completing my schooling through Palomar so I could finally have a degree in hand for the 'some college' I received after high school.

Thanks to the faculty and other staff there for helping further my education.
-Alyssa", 'I've been a student (intermittently) here since 2010. As someone that loves learning and the overall "school" atmosphere, I feel extremely fortunate that I get to be a student at Palomar College; "lucked out", I would say.

The teachers are magnificent and have the potential to change your life forever (I know a few that have for me already*).

You can get help with enrollment fees with through the BOG Waiver - all my classes end up being free because of it. Parking permits 1/2 off also.

The school is modern and always improving. Their buildings are stylish and unlike anything I've seen anywhere else. Each is unique, yet somehow they all come together to form a beautiful campus.

I truly look at this campus like a second home. I love going here.

(Parking can suck, that's a big reason why I try to only stick to night classes 🤓) ➡️ HOWEVER! They now have a brand new parking GARAGE! I haven't used it yet, as I am only doing evening classes, but I can only imagine how much it helps everyone be able to find parking! It is nice to know that they actually do care about the problems we face throughout college life & do what they can to help make it as comfortable & as enjoyable as possible!
UPDATE (3/19/18)!! I started using the parking garage and it is AWESOME!!! Security cameras coming soon! This school keeps on getting better and better!!

'Safety' is also another big thing here that they take seriously. They make sure to inform us students on a regular (& when, if necessary) basis all the details regarding our options when it comes to being and staying safe throughout our education at Palomar. They have their own (actual/legit) police force that is on duty 24/7 & a direct emergency line to call any hour day or night. They provide free escorts to anyone needing or just wanting a little extra piece of mind walking to their car or anywhere around campus. Every class locks from the inside by a button next to the teacher's phone that keeps anyone from getting in in case of an active shooter or anything else putting students at harm, & when they lock, it sends a signal to the Palomar Police with the location of the room, etc. etc. I could go on but you get it, they care & work hard to keep us safe! 🤗

* AJ Professor Jack Hook, AJ Professor Leeyann Chapman, COMM Professor Wendy Nelson & LS Professor Lisa Burns; just to name a few! ;)', 'This campus is lovely and the staff are professional, courteous and competent. There are numerous parking lots making it quite convenient even for late arriving students or for those who take classes during peak hours. The natural sciences building is quite impressive as is the landscaping and labeling of the plants and trees.
This school is a gem!']

name: Pasadena City College
reviews:
['Pasadena City College is one of the best community colleges I’ve visited. The campus is extremely well-maintained, with modern facilities and a clean, welcoming atmosphere. The city of Pasadena also feels very safe, which makes the campus environment even better.

Everything is built on flat ground, so walking around the campus is super comfortable and enjoyable. Overall, PCC left a great impression on me, and it stands out among community colleges for both quality and environment.', 'Pasadena City College is a textbook example of what a community college should be: practical, focused, and genuinely committed to student outcomes. The instruction is clear, the expectations are real, and the emphasis is on learning skills that actually transfer—to universities, careers, or both. Faculty teach instead of perform, and students are there to do the work, not posture for a brand.

Put next to that, UC Davis looks like academic theater. It’s heavy on slogans, reputation, and carefully staged impressions, but light on real return. Prestige is constantly advertised, yet too much of the culture revolves around signaling, networking, and playing institutional roles rather than building competence. The machinery is massive, the bureaucracy endless, and the payoff often underwhelming.

At PCC, education feels grounded and honest. Students are focused, instructors are accountable, and progress is measurable. At UC Davis, there’s far more emphasis on looking impressive than being effective—more performance than substance, more branding than results.

Pasadena City College doesn’t pretend to be elite, and that’s exactly why it succeeds. It delivers real value without hype. UC Davis insists on prestige while staging excellence instead of consistently producing it. When judged by usefulness, ROI, and actual learning, PCC comes out ahead—and the contrast makes UC Davis’s theatrical nature impossible to ignore.', 'Our experience with PCC has shown us that the administration does not really care about their students.  Their visions and values statement sounds good but they do not put it into practice.  They are very disorganized and unhelpful in taking care of their students educational needs. PCC seems is
just a waste of time, money and effort.', 'Great school!  I went there back in 1992 as a foreign student and then transferred to USC after 3 semesters with a GPA of 3.80.  Teachers and staff are passionate about their work and most students are spending quality time studying in a lovely campus.', 'I attended UC Davis, and despite all the hype, it turned out to be one of the most overrated and discouraging academic environments I’ve experienced. The reputation suggests excellence, but the reality felt very different. The culture leaned heavily toward cliques, internal politics, and surface-level achievement rather than real intellectual growth or collaboration. Instead of mentorship, there was a lot of posturing—people protecting status, chasing approval, and making ego-driven decisions that did little to help students build real careers.

What surprised me most was how hollow the academic confidence often felt. There was plenty of arrogance tied to the UC name, but not much depth behind it. Independent or genuinely capable students were frequently dismissed or treated harshly, while conformity and optics were rewarded. Many people seemed unaware of their own limits, yet quick to judge others. It created an environment where mediocrity was normalized, but real ability was inconvenient.

Support structures didn’t help much either. Advisors were overloaded, professors were often detached, and guidance felt impersonal. If you weren’t already plugged into the right circles or comfortably at the top, you were easy to overlook. For a school that costs so much and markets itself as elite, the lack of meaningful support was hard to justify—especially when many graduates end up earning about the same as an Uber driver.

Now compare that to Pasadena City College.

PCC was practical, grounded, and transparent about what it offered—and it delivered. Despite being a community college, it functions as one of the largest and most reliable feeders into UC Davis, which says a lot about where the real preparation happens. At PCC, professors were engaged, instruction was hands-on, and the focus was on building actual skills and clear transfer pathways. Advisors were accessible, knew students personally, and helped map out realistic plans instead of vague promises.

The difference in value was obvious. PCC respected students’ time, intelligence, and financial reality. There was no inflated ego, no obsession with appearances—just education that worked. It prepared students to transfer, earn, and move forward strategically without burying them in debt or false prestige.

When you look at outcomes rather than branding, Pasadena City College outperformed UC Davis in every way that mattered to me. If I could do it over again, I’d choose PCC without hesitation. It offered more honesty, more support, and a far better return on investment than UC Davis ever did.']

name: Riverside City College
reviews:
['Riverside City College is honestly a very nice choice  ! 🎓

As a student here, I can say RCC has been a really positive experience from day one. The campus is clean, modern, and filled with life there’s always something going on, whether it’s student events, clubs, or just people hanging out and studying together. It feels like a real community, not just a place to take classes.

some professors are so passionate about what they teach and genuinely care about their students. They’re approachable and go out of their way to make sure you understand the material, which makes a huge difference when you’re trying to stay motivated. The staff are also super helpful from counseling to financial aid, they actually take time to help you out instead of brushing you off.

RCC also offers great programs for transferring to universities and building a solid foundation for your career. I’ve met people who’ve gone on to amazing schools and jobs, and it really shows how much opportunity this place creates.

On top of that, the environment is welcoming and diverse you meet people from all walks of life, and everyone’s trying to better themselves. It’s inspiring and keeps you focused.

The only bad thing i encountered like every other college you do encounter some professors that just don’t want to be there and they enjoy failing students instead of actually helping them out but the college gives you longer time for you to drop the class the Deans are just so wonderful and considerate.

Also the college itself carries so much resources that you can use making study easier on everybody.

If you’re looking for a place that truly supports your growth, Riverside City College is it.', 'We traveled all the way from across the country to attend a dive competition at Riverside Community College — spending thousands of dollars on flights, hotels, and event costs — only to come away with a parking ticket.

This happened in the middle of summer, when the college isn’t even in session, and in a stall that wasn’t labeled or marked in any way. As visiting families supporting student-athletes, we expected a more welcoming and organized environment. Instead, we were penalized for parking in a space that gave absolutely no indication of being restricted.

It’s extremely disappointing that a college hosting national events would treat out-of-town guests this way. We hope the administration reviews their parking policies and signage, so other families don’t have to go through this frustrating experience.', "Fantasia Premiere Night was incredible! I will be looking at a different college for my education.', "I attended in the late 90's .Now the campus is so organized seems like a small enough campus to learn and succeed  in today's economy."]

name: San Diego City College
reviews:
['I absolutely love City College ', 'San Diego City College has become one of the most beautiful and inspiring campuses in the area. Over the years, it has grown tremendously — not just in size, but in presence. The architecture blends modern design with open, welcoming spaces, and the landscaping gives the entire campus a calm, university-level atmosphere.
Walking through the courtyard areas feels less like a typical community college and more like a four-year university. The newer buildings are clean and thoughtfully designed, with glass, natural light, and updated technology that make it feel current and forward-moving. At the same time, the campus still maintains its accessibility and sense of community.
It is impressive to see how much the college has invested in growth and improvement. The expansion of academic programs and facilities reflects that progress. For anyone considering continuing their education, this campus offers both opportunity and an environment that feels motivating and elevated.
Now let’s zoom out for a second. Campuses matter. Environment shapes behavior. There is research in environmental psychology showing that physical space affects motivation, focus, and even identity formation. When a community college looks and feels like a university, it subtly raises expectations — of the institution and of the students. That matters.', "I haven't attended classes here, not yet anyways, but I am staying nearby temporarily and I adore this campus and the ideas expressed around the campus - on signs, artwork, billboards, etc ...

I went to Mesa College back in 2010-2013, and look back at it as one of the best schools I've ever attended.

Unlike UC San Diego, the classes are not so huge that human connection is impossible. Things are small and tidy, and feel more supportive of actual scholarship.

I use the free wi-fi on the campus sometimes, and although some look at me like some freeloading bum, I'm actually working on some things, and pretty sure I'm using the campus for it's intended purpose.

I've returned to San Diego after a decade away, since getting my BA at UCSD back in 2013, and hope to take a few classes here.", 'Great experience at this college. Abnormal psychology class really amazing with a dedicated, very good professor. She does all she can to help students succeed. Admin is professional too. The only drawback is parking. Almost impossible to find parking despite paying for the permit.', "I'm going to look into taking classes here. I like that it's close by"]

name: San Diego Miramar College
reviews:
['My experience at San Diego Miramar College genuinely derailed my life after leaving the military.

As a veteran transitioning out of service, I trusted this school to handle enrollment and financial aid properly. From the beginning, my schedule was mishandled. Counselors repeatedly mis-scheduled me, failed to correct the errors, and then blamed me for the consequences. The problems were never rightfully resolved.

I was forced to take out FAFSA loans in order to remain enrolled, despite using my GI Bill. I did not want additional federal debt, but I was told it was necessary to stay registered. As a direct result of these administrative failures, I have incurred over $5,000 in debt, experienced housing instability, and ultimately had to return to my hometown to rebuild.

The academic experience did not justify the cost or the disruption to my life. Many classes consisted primarily of PowerPoints or videos created by other professors, with minimal engagement or practical instruction. It did not feel like a hands-on or career-focused education.

After leaving, I attended a trade-focused program and had significantly more success — especially in resume development and actually entering my job field. The difference in practical value was night and day.

San Diego Miramar College was, for me, a complete waste of time and financially devastating. Veterans and students relying on financial aid deserve accurate guidance, accountability, and real educational value. That was not my experience here.', 'Miramar has the best counselors out of any college I have ever been to. If you are lucky enough to work with Ron or Anh, they are some of the most caring and incredible people I have ever had the pleasure of working with, and they truly want what is best for the students. Once you show up for your scheduled appointment, they will prompt you to reschedule as “they are not sure what you are talking about.” Save yourself the hassle of getting scammed and go to a real accredited college.', "Miramar College is an amazing CC a great stepping stone towards transferring to a 4 year university or just working on skills. The small class sizes are a huge plus, as they make it easy to get to know your professors and receive personalized attention. Overall, it's a wonderful place to learn and grow. Highly recommend:)"]

more than effort, more than grind—

a presence rare to find.
At SDSU she doesn’t just attend,
she adds, she builds, she grows,
a hardworking queen with vision,
someone every campus knows.
A special soul, a steady light,
proof of what this place can be—
Ella Katherine isn’t just a student,
she’s part of the university.', 'The collective sentiment among my peers and the wider San Diego professional community suggests that San Diego State University is much more than just a beautiful campus on Campanile Drive; it is a vital engine for regional innovation and leadership. From countless discussions with neighbors and former students, I’ve gathered that the "Aztec" experience is defined by a rare synergy between high-level research initiatives and a deeply ingrained culture of student mentorship. It is heartening to see an institution that stays so authentically committed to public service while simultaneously climbing the ranks of national academic prestige with such grace. God bless every people this campus future. Only a black male shuttle driver is very rude. Another driver is very kind', "I had a generally positive experience here, aside from spending two of my four years online due to COVID. I do sometimes wonder what the full four-year on-campus experience would’ve been like, because the campus itself is essentially a resort. The facilities, gym access, and overall environment genuinely support a healthy lifestyle, and honestly, that alone could justify a portion of the tuition.

Academically, I can only speak for the engineering and business programs, since that’s where most of my coursework was. I should also note that I wasn't the most engaged student and didn’t take full advantage of every resource offered - so part of my experience falls on me.

The business school, however, feels outdated in certain areas. Real Estate and Accounting are strong departments with knowledgeable staff, including some standout professors with real industry experience. But if you're pursuing entrepreneurship, be aware: many instructors haven’t built or currently run businesses. Much of the curriculum leans heavily on theory rather than practical application. The program tends to reflect traditional brick-and-mortar business models and doesn’t meaningfully address online commerce, digital marketing, or the current direction of the business world.

If your goal is to start a business, you'd be better off beginning right now. You don’t need to take classes here to do that, and in some cases, the tuition money might serve you more directly if invested into your own startup. On the other hand, if you're interested in finance, real estate, or accounting, you may find a clearer return on your investment.

Overall, I enjoyed my time here. Did I get a financial return on my degree? Not really. Did the degree help me in the job market? In my experience, no - I didn’t have a single employer ask about it. But when all the information you could ever need is already available online, you start to question what college is truly for. Education is part of it, but the experience, independence, community, and personal growth matter just as much, if not more. And for those reasons alone, I would still go back and do it again.", 'I didn’t attend USD, but after spending time at UC Davis, I genuinely wish I had gone to a place like this.

University of San Diego actually follows through — small class sizes, strong support, personal attention, and a campus culture that seems built for real growth, not academic performance art.

At UC Davis, it’s the opposite. The branding is everywhere — the results are not. Advising is slow, career services are a checkbox, and you’re left on your own to figure out how to make a $30K-per-year education translate into anything meaningful.

Let’s talk outcomes:
USD grads regularly break into law, business, and leadership pipelines.
UC Davis grads? Median income 10 years after enrollment is just ~$58k after recent year heavy inflation. That’s barely above entry-level — after a decade. You could match that working retail without student debt.

Davis sells prestige. USD seems to offer support, clarity, and preparation. I never got that at Davis — just automated emails, generic workshops, and professors who were too busy publishing to teach.

USD = personal, practical, outcome-driven.
UC Davis = bureaucratic, bloated, and underdelivering.

If you’re looking at both: skip the UC fantasy and go where students actually thrive. USD looks like the real deal. UC Davis is just expensive trial and error', "Insider here. Go elsewhere for a better education!!! The campus is beautiful, but the beauty stops there. Behind the surface is a hypocritical organization that protects the powerful and tramples over everyone else. Students pay $60k/year to be taught by old professors who checked out 30 years ago and haven't updated their courses since then. The university is plagued by scandals. There are plenty of other universities that provide a better education at a more reasonable price without the hypocrisy and lack of values!"]

name: San Francisco State University
reviews:
["Honestly, if you're going to Stanford, you're getting ripped off. SFSU is the greatest college in America, possibly in the whole world. Very affordable, small classes and dedicated professors. The campus is cool and the mascot has the juice. Stop simping for Ivy Leagues and get with the program.", 'Honest Review of SFSU Mechanical Engineering (With Business Perspective)

I’m a Mechanical Engineering student at SFSU, and my girlfriend is a Business major with a Marketing emphasis. After progressing through most of our degrees and comparing experiences with peers at other schools, we both feel that San José State University (SJSU) would have been the better choice for both majors, mainly due to stronger education quality, alumni networks, and industry pipelines.

On paper, SFSU Mechanical Engineering offers many upper-division electives, but in reality only about 4–6 are offered per semester, usually with one section each. This problem also applies to core classes, not just electives. With recent class cuts, most required courses have only one professor and one section, leaving little flexibility if instruction quality or organization is poor. Missing or failing a course can easily delay graduation. Single-professor dependency is one of the biggest structural risks in this program.

A clear example is ENGR 410 (Process Instrumentation and Control). Although ENGR 410 + its lab are required for graduation, the lab was last offered in Spring 2024 and has not appeared for roughly two years. As a result, students may be forced to replace the requirement with ENGR 447 (Automatic Control Systems) + its lab, pushing them into a more difficult and theory-heavy path due to scheduling failures. This is a program planning issue, not a student issue.

The main problem is not that the program is too hard. Engineering should be rigorous. The issue is that the rigor is poorly aligned with how engineers are hired and evaluated in industry. Many upper-division courses (core and elective) are extremely theory-heavy, focused on textbooks, formulas, and exams, with limited hands-on or project-based work. As a result, students often leave not practically prepared for industry unless they aggressively self-train outside the curriculum. I’ve seen similar theory-heavy issues at UC Davis, but when combined with SFSU’s weaker industry reputation, the outcome is worse.

Many lower-division engineering courses are not meaningfully hands-on and could reasonably be offered online or hybrid. Greater online availability would improve flexibility, reduce bottlenecks, and better serve commuters and working students. I’ve found it far more efficient to take many lower-division courses at community colleges, where online options are common, and then transfer them in.

Some professors are unorganized or not student-centric, which becomes far more damaging when there is only one section and no alternative instructor. In contrast, schools like SJSU benefit from greater course redundancy, stronger employer presence, and established alumni pipelines that reduce uncertainty at graduation.

If I could redo everything, I would complete 2 years at community college, then transfer to either a school with a lighter, flexible curriculum to focus on skills, or a school with strong pipelines and alumni connections (like SJSU). SFSU is sometimes described as an “easy ride,” but I strongly disagree—limited sections, single-professor dependency, and theory-heavy instruction make it hard to justify, especially when students must still independently build employable skills.

I don’t yet have a full-time Mechanical Engineering role, but I’m actively applying and improving my skills. Once I gain industry experience, I plan to update this review. While engineering hiring doesn’t heavily emphasize prestige, new-grad pipelines absolutely matter, and that’s something I underestimated.

Prospective students should carefully research their major, core + lab availability, alumni outcomes, pipelines, total cost, and job market demand. Concrete improvements that would significantly help include online/hybrid lower-division courses, hands-on/project-based upper-division courses, guaranteed lab availability, and more redundancy for required classes. Choose the school that best supports career outcomes—not just the degree.', 'I was really excited to attend but overall it wasn’t much different than community college at least for Gen ed. my excitement peaked week 4 and by week 11 of the semester I realized what was ahead of me and how the school is kind of a crazy mess. Having ethnic studies tie their bodies to the Muni tracks and an on campus anti abortion protest with bloody pictures was definitely a bit much And not made better by the pleasant Marchant booths the fallowing week. name: University of San Francisco
reviews: ['The University of San Francisco, anchored at 2130 Fulton Street, is frequently highlighted in my social and professional circles as a premier bastion of Jesuit education, where the "Change the World from Here" motto is substantively reflected in its rigorous social sciences and nursing programs. From numerous dialogues with alumni and community partners, it is evident that USF provides an intellectually vibrant yet deeply ethical environment, often praised by my acquaintances for its unique ability to combine world-class academic standards with a profound, respectful focus on social justice and urban engagement. It is truly heartening to observe how the institution maintains such a transparent dedication to holistic student development, a quality that is widely recognized as a catalyst for the impressive professional integrity of its graduates within the competitive Bay Area landscape. Ultimately, in the general consensus of informed San Franciscans, the university stands as a distinguished hallmark of moral and academic leadership, rightfully respected for its elegant ability to cultivate a diverse student body that is as merytorically proficient as it is compassionate.', 'EVERYONE.... from the students to the staff treated us with the highest self regard and always offered their help. Security treated us like human beings and I had several fruitful conversations with strangers all over campus during "move-in day ".  USF!', "The University of San Francisco (USFCA) has been instrumental in shaping my academic and personal journey. The experience I gained here is truly invaluable. USFCA not only provided me with knowledge but also fostered progressive thinking and personal growth. The professors were exceptional, and the staff, especially shout out to literally everyone at the Career Services department who provided invaluable support. Although I've contemporarily moved to Vietnam, I am forever grateful for the opportunities and relationships I developed at USFCA.", 'Great campus and grounds to walk. Nice easy elevation gain with beautiful landscaping.  Neighborhood has nice architecture & homes to walk as well.', 'Beautiful campus\nLocated across from the Golden Gate Park, the University of San Francisco is one of the must-visit spots in your SF trip.']

name: San Joaquin Delta College
reviews: ["I always enjoy Delta. You can never feel like an outcast. It is a melting pot where most people are helpful and supportive. There are a few bad apples of course. The younger one's straight from highschool with kid mentalities. If you have disabilities there are places to aid you and lots of people willing to help. The culinary cuisine is always tempting, but unfortunately since COVID the cafeteria has been closed and it had incredible breakfast burritos and more. Now they have gas station food and the thriving Java Juice with Starbucks coffee. Classes a great, Professor's are very understanding and supportive and the clubs are incredible. Danner Hall, (The food court/rec room is awesome. Couch, chairs and a TV to hook up gaming consoles to play as well as having tournaments. They have a great Police force, excluding one who sped through a crosswalk I was about to cross. But even the groundskeepers are super nice. I easily recommend taking a class or two, or three. Lastly, as a student you have the opportunity to go once a week to the student pantry where they let you get limited food items to help during the week. Also, once a month they have a farmers market that gives out a variety of goods in the Shima 2 parking lot. Check the student pantry for more details. Delta also has 3 Theaters. And one in particular is the Alfred Muller Theater where I filmed a play for him just before he passed away. Great man. There is so much more I can say, but I recommend checking it out for yourself. All (respectful people) are welcome. In N Out is right across the street too. So... Why wait. Go get enrolled.", "This place is a damn maze. No signs to point you in what direction to get to your destination. Police staffs are not friendly and not helpful at all. If you're a first time student. I highly recommend you to explore the campus beforehand so you'll know which parking lot you'll be at and where your class building is located.", "I've attended delta (6 months) for only 1 reason, becuase it was closer to my home, however during the time I applied to delta it was covid time. Everything was told to be done digitally. now its 2026, yet they've havn't solved my problem. They say that you can walk in on wednesdays to meet with a counselor but when I showed up they told me all appointments were books at 8:30 am and that they have walk-ins for the 2 weeks startinng next week. Fast forwarding to the week, I call the counseling department at broad daylight but no one picked up. There whole administration system sucks. I'm so glad I made the decision to transfer to a different Community college right away to complete my GE.", "Parking is a bit wild, you'll always find parking at the back of the school. Use the maps posted in different areas of the school.  A good school that is to the point. Some hallways and exits lead to areas you didnt think, but everything is pretty accessible.", "Today my daughter & I spoke to a few people regarding her starting on campus class.  Delores in the library,  Graciela in the EOPS office were super helpful.  There were a few others but I didn't catch their names.  I can't wait to see my daughter enjoy her college experience! Culinary here she comes!"]

name: San Jose City College
reviews: ["San José City College is a great starting point for anyone looking to explore new academic or career paths. I’ve visited the campus during transfer expos and community events, and the staff always seemed genuinely invested in helping students succeed. The Jaguar Market is a standout resource—offering free groceries and essentials—and the counseling team is approachable and knowledgeable. Class sizes are small, which makes it easier to connect with instructors and get personalized support.\n\nThe campus is clean and accessible, though the surrounding area can feel a bit sketchy at times—especially in the evenings. Still, the college does a good job of creating a safe and welcoming environment. There’s a strong sense of community here, especially during cultural events and student-led activities. Whether you're aiming to transfer to a four-year university or just want to build new skills, SJCC offers a supportive and flexible space to grow. Just be sure to stay proactive and take advantage of the many resources available.", 'Closing campus on 11/10/25 "for" Veteran\'s Day even though the holiday is on the 11th is a giant middle finger to the many Veterans who attend this school.', 'Beautiful junior college. Staffs at admissions office are super friendly.', "Ok, it's very hard for me to rate a school, especially one I have been to, mix ideas due to I did had a couple of great teachers while studying here,  administration is terrible no help from this people,  none student working programs only facades, the math teachers are the worst I've ever seen and the tutoring department is bad lacks a lot of coordination and not enough tutors. If you are not that good with math, don't go here,  You will fail, and to be honest, most Bay Area colleges are like that,  go outside, and you will succeed.  This college doesn't care about students' period. It's  just another business."]

name: San Jose State University
reviews:
['I got into this school as a freshman last semester and while I’d say I’ve enjoyed my time here so far, I’ve several different caveats that many people who may be wanting to attend this school should know about.

This university overall is a fantastic place if you’re going to be majoring in engineering or business because the campus literally works with different tech companies and you’d have a decent chance of landing a job or an internship at the very least before you even graduate.

However, the downsides are that this school has a serious issue with safety because I’ve never felt any more anxious studying in the MLK library with a bunch of homeless people going into there to access the computers for free and with all the incidents that happened just last week. Be sure to carry a pepper spray if you can because the UPD sure takes a lot of time to respond.

Also you may have to spend time learning outside the classroom because some professors here are just god awful who don’t know or have the passion to teach their students despite having fancy degrees and extensive experience in their field. Have the decency to hire professors who have the passion and desire to actually teach their students SJSU!', "It's okay for a place to study but if you don't know how to deal with crazy homeless people or not to stare then I wouldn't recommend it. Also always wash your hands regardless if it looks clean because 80% of the time it's not. Great spots to study on the 8th floor by the windows (if not taken already lol)", "Financial Aid office is a joke. I transferred in as a junior and only received $370 from my Cal Grant B and was told to just take out loans for financial support. I make less than 30,000 a year and I'm already in debt just trying to pay for simple things like car insurance, housing and food. If you're expecting to have financial support while taking classes here, you better lower those expectations. Not to mention the professors are awful teachers. The Python programming course is ridiculous. Only one professor for the students who are fulfilling the online degree program and he writes his instructions in an undecipherable code. I'm spending way too much money just to have to turn to YouTube tutorials.", 'A truly unhelpful school which does not care about the wellbeing of its students. Money is their only concern, as for example administration continues talks of implementing new and additional fees under the guise of improved services.

The classrooms are unclean and stale, many professors are terrible and cannot handle nor care about students, yet university administration refuses to take action. The campus is not very safe, and incidents are exceedingly common. College education is meant to be superior, but, at least here, it ends up being significantly worse than previous schooling.

Remember, this is just another greedy institution; I am warning you against giving them your money.', 'The firing of a tenured professor for her pro-Palestinian activism represents a serious breach of academic freedom, fairness, and the core mission of a public university. Tenure exists to protect faculty from retaliation for holding or expressing controversial views, yet the university’s decision effectively punishes lawful political speech and sets a dangerous precedent for viewpoint-based censorship. Selectively applying conduct rules to silence certain political perspectives undermines trust, chills open inquiry, and restricts the diversity of ideas essential to higher education. Public universities have a responsibility to uphold free expression and foster an environment where faculty and students can engage with complex global issues without fear of reprisal; this action betrays that responsibility and damages the integrity of the institution']

name: College of San Mateo
reviews:
['College of San Mateo delivers real education without pretending to be something it’s not. The instruction is practical, structured, and aimed at outcomes—transfer readiness, workforce skills, and actual competence. Faculty are focused on teaching, students are there to do the work, and progress is tangible. For the cost, the value is straightforward and honest.

Put next to that, UC Davis comes across as academic theater. It leans heavily on reputation, slogans, and carefully staged impressions, but the return on investment often doesn’t justify the hype. Bureaucracy is massive, messaging is polished, and “excellence” is constantly advertised—yet outcomes frequently feel underwhelming.

At College of San Mateo, learning is grounded and functional. Expectations are clear, effort is rewarded, and results matter. At UC Davis, too much of the culture revolves around signaling, networking, and institutional performance rather than building durable skills or independent capability.

College of San Mateo proves that education doesn’t need prestige branding or spectacle to work—it just needs focus, accountability, and commitment to students. UC Davis insists on the spectacle, often mistaking appearance for value. Side by side, it’s hard not to see which institution is actually delivering education and which one is busy staging it.', 'Another track and field event for the Bay Area, Senior Olympic’s in the books. Wonderful weather today with unlimited views of the Bay for the track bleachers.', 'This review is not on the academics or admissions of The College of San Mateo but the walkability of the campus. The College of San Mateo is a beautiful place to walk and exercise with lovely panoramic views. A great place to get exercise with hills, stairs, and flat areas to walk.', 'Jazz on the hill at College of San Mateo has always been a vibe and is the kick off to the summer music festival season.', 'There are some amazing high tech headquarters in Silicon Valley but most are off limits to the public. Apple in Cupertino. Google in Mountain View. Facebook in East Palo Alto. Amazon basically everywhere. But the cool thing about the College of San Mateo is that it is public land funded by local tax revenues that ordinary people can visit. No need to be Mark Zuckerberg or Elon Musk or Jeff Bezos or some other billionaire like the Google founders. It’s prime real estate for sure. The best land for miles around. But you can actually visit with your kids. Get in some steps on your iPhone Health app. Steve Jobs would have loved it. It’s as American as apple pie and as enduring as eternity.']

name: Santa Clara University
reviews:
["Santa Clara University
A really nice campus. Beautiful buildings, well maintained and very clean. It has a historic feel with plenty of architectural buildings to appreciate. We didn’t go inside any of them just walked around campus. There is an old church that may be worth a look. You can walk-on campus but to visit the campus by car you have to get a visitor parking pass either by the entry or go to the security booth. The security were very nice and will give you a map of the campus.

The campus exudes a sense of affluence, and it's evident that there's wealth here. While walking around, we came accross a teacher's meeting were all the teachers were very well dressed. They looked more like professionals in corporate attire than your typical brainy educators. The neighborhood around the campus is well-maintained and felt safe. The campus atmosphere felt friendly but also a bit preppy. Despite that, the campus is definitely worth a visit, as it's beautiful.", 'Santa Clara University at 500 El Camino Real is widely regarded in the Silicon Valley community as an exceptional institution where a Jesuit-inspired moral compass perfectly aligns with the cutting-edge demands of the tech industry. From various discussions with neighbors and alumni, it is clear that the university’s reputation for cultivating "men and women for others" is more than just a motto; it is a lived reality reflected in the high ethical standards and leadership skills of its graduates. Friends whose children have attended often praise the stunning, mission-style campus as a serene backdrop for an education that offers unparalleled access to industry-leading internships and professional networks. In professional circles, the consensus is that SCU consistently produces well-rounded individuals who possess both the technical prowess and the critical thinking necessary to navigate today’s complex global landscape. It is truly heartening to hear so many firsthand accounts of how this university empowers its students to integrate professional success with a genuine commitment to social responsibility and community service.', 'Santa Clara University (SCU) is a respected private Jesuit university located in the heart of Silicon Valley, known for its blend of strong academics, ethical leadership, and community engagement. Programs span arts and sciences, business, and engineering, and the university emphasizes critical thinking, social justice, and real‑world learning—encouraging students to explore internships and research opportunities right in one of the world’s most innovative regions. The board of director recently signed an agreement with ODosta Store to serve Microsoft and Partner Network Software license to their Students at the discount price.', 'Santa Clara University is an exceptional place to learn and grow. The campus is beautiful and welcoming. Professors are knowledgeable, supportive, and genuinely invested in student success.', 'Gorgeous campus, I come walking here every day. Gardens and flower beds are immaculate. Love it. There’s bathrooms by the parking lot on Lafayette as well as next to the science building. They’ve been mostly locked over Covid and distance learning. Security guards on campus are usually patrolling around, it’s well lit with emergency phones. Don’t use the vending machine by the science building, it’s been faulty for years lol. There’s a Safeway close by but you can’t bring a picnic and linger if you’re not a student. You can walk around and use the benches etc and take photos. If you use a professional photographer they’ll ask for a permit. The art museum is free and worth a visit. It’s been closed with Covid though.']

name: Santa Monica College
reviews:
['I was really impressed with Santa Monica College. The campus has a lot of modern, updated buildings, and you can tell they’re still investing heavily in improvements—there are quite a few construction areas where older buildings are being replaced with new, modern facilities, which I think is a great move for the school’s future.

The facilities overall are excellent, and one thing I especially appreciated is the free underground parking, which makes commuting so much easier. The campus feels clean, organized, and well-designed, and it shows that SMC is constantly upgrading to give students a better environment.

Overall, it’s a very solid campus with great facilities and a forward-thinking approach to development.', 'I entered UC Davis expecting a serious academic environment—one built on rigor, collaboration, and mentorship. What I found instead was an institution propped up by reputation more than results. The culture felt crowded with ego, politics, and surface-level ambition. Collaboration was talked about constantly but rarely practiced. Too often, success seemed tied to appearances, social positioning, and knowing the right people rather than actual competence or effort.

What stood out was the gap between confidence and capability. Many students carried an inflated sense of intelligence simply because of the UC label, yet showed little depth or curiosity when challenged. Independent thinkers or genuinely strong students were frequently dismissed, sidelined, or treated harshly for not fitting into the dominant academic culture. There was very little awareness of personal limits, and questioning the system—or outperforming it quietly—was not welcomed.

The lack of meaningful support only reinforced this. Advisors were stretched thin, professors were often inaccessible, and career guidance felt disconnected from real-world outcomes. For an institution that costs so much and markets itself as elite, the results were underwhelming—especially when many graduates end up earning about the same as an Uber driver.

Santa Monica College, by contrast, was grounded, disciplined, and results-oriented. Despite being a community college, it consistently sends a large number of well-prepared students to UC campuses, including UC Davis. At SMC, the focus was on mastery and momentum, not branding. Classes were demanding in the right ways, professors were engaged, and students were expected to actually learn—not just signal achievement.

Advising at SMC was intentional and personal. Counselors helped students build concrete transfer plans and career pathways, not vague narratives about prestige. The environment rewarded focus, work ethic, and clarity of goals rather than ego or academic theater.

When you compare outcomes instead of logos, Santa Monica College delivered far more value than UC Davis. It respected students’ time, intelligence, and finances while quietly producing students who were better prepared and more resilient.

If I had to do it again, I’d choose Santa Monica College without hesitation. It offered structure, accountability, and a real return on investment—things UC Davis promised loudly but failed to deliver consistently.', "i love my school.

From the head of the program to the only career counselor assigned to this pathway lack the necessary qualifications for their positions and have engaged in behavior that is manipulative and unprofessional.

Not just for outside people but also it can help new students or ESL Students.
I liked to see the Aquatics and Tennis courts.  There was a lot of constructions going on on multiple areas . It's still manageable to drive through and also a good sign that this College is growing.
I can't say to much about the education programs in detail, but what I saw , that it is acceptable average.', 'Constantly have issue with admissions. Despite being a student off and on over 15 years, you have to re-enroll anytime there’s a break in attendance. This triggers a “mandatory” 4 hour counseling session to discuss career objectives. I have a career! All I need is some continuing education classes! And the counseling department is of zero help. In my last interaction, I asked to speak with a someone else and was told everyone was busy, then she hung up on me.', "The classes and professors are hit or miss, you often have to feel it out the first two weeks and pray you withdraw or stay in time. It's overcrowded and often you can't get the classes you need in time because you're not high enough priority. Main issue being the administration. As a student who has graduated, and been accepted into my transfer school, they haven't sent my transcript despite being petitioned while I was enrolled there. It's aggravating because I now have to wait another semester to get into my degree, due to their negligence/oversight. It's disappointing yet unsurprising. It's difficult to communicate with the admin or counselors.", "I've heard so many wonderful things about Sierra through my friends...however, their online courses are horrible. If you want to attend Sierra online, don't do it!! Staff communication isn't very good, and the professors have a difficult time communicating with students, and you'll find yourself having issues with aggressive professors. I would recommend going to Sierra in-person instead of online. Such a shame!"]

name: Simpson University
reviews:
["Went here 15 years ago and studied English. I loved my life at Simpson, the English Department (gone now except for one professor) and the spiritual growth as well as the community and was happy to drive my sister down to attend 15 years later. The campus is showing age in some areas. The dorms needed to be repainted in the actual rooms and outside, the walls were beat up, but the feel is the same. Everyone is friendly, it feels safe, the classrooms appear well kept, the grounds are beautiful.

I do wish my department remained. Honestly, I wouldn't have gone there if they hadn't had English 15 years ago. Probably would have went to Master's instead. I'm glad they had it back then and I got a quality, well rounded education with multiple view points in Literary Theory, which I haven't seen in my friends that were English majors from public colleges and universities.", 'A joke of a private school that charges the tuition of an Ivy League school while holding the rank of #177 in their category. When you pay your professors $26 an hour, you get crappy professors. What happened to "Do not bind the mouths of the kine that tread out the grain"?', '1st. It is mandatory that you live on campus unless you’re over 24 years old, or are married. Get ready to spend $10,000 on that. Every semester.
2nd. Have an issue with your dorm life/situation? Too bad! You’ll just have to get over it :) I didn’t have a light in my bathroom for 2 weeks! (And maintenance filed that the light was fixed)
3rd. Do you have any possible questions about the financial aspects of the institution? Good thing no one on campus will answer them! In fact there is a student that answers the phones and I am nearly positive that they tell her her job is to inform the caller that no one is available. They are known to wrongfully up charge students, and even charge them for housing when they live off campus. The money is taken from your loans immediately but have fun trying to get it back!', 'Nice campus! Great wrestling', 'W school, my favorite part is the cafe']

name: College of the Siskiyous
reviews: ["COS Choir and jazz summer camp is incredibly beneficial for kids. It builds friendships, improves musical abilities, encourages confidence, teamwork, and fun, creative way to express themselves. I'm so grateful for this program!👏🏻👏🏻👏🏻", 'My  youngest son graduated\nFriday.   COS is the most beautiful campus 😍', 'The faculty at this college is top notch.
