Hopefully there will not be any cancellation of classes for any reason. (Cough cough covid)"]

name: Skyline College
reviews:
["Perched in San Bruno, Skyline College offers a scenic campus with strong academic programs and a welcoming atmosphere. The facilities are modern and well-equipped, with dedicated spaces for tutoring, career services, and student life. Staff are approachable and responsive, making it easy to get support whether you're a new student or preparing to transfer. The college emphasizes equity and inclusion, with programs tailored to diverse learning needs.

Transfer pathways to CSU and UC schools are clearly outlined, and the campus hosts regular workshops to help students stay on track. The surrounding views of the Bay Area add to the appeal, and the community vibe makes it easy to connect with peers and faculty. Whether you're attending a class, joining a club, or meeting with an advisor, Skyline feels organized and student-centered", 'I do not recommend attending classes here. I graduated from a 4 year college on time and with no issues, but when I tried to take a few courses here it was non-stop registration issues. I registered for 3 courses and immediately paid the $695 fees so I wouldn’t get dropped but a few hours after paying that $695, a $17 fee was added on and I had no idea. Because I didn’t know about the $17 and therefore didn’t pay it, I was dropped from all the courses and only found out because I had a meeting with my counselor and he couldn’t see any of my classes. I tried to talk to multiple people for help on the situation and everyone but my counselor was absolutely no help and told me to get on the waitlists. After getting on the waitlists (waitlisted #4, #22, and #24) for classes that I was previously enrolled in, I was removed from all the waitlists with no email or any notice. The professors sent emails saying to show up the first day but I was removed from the waitlists before any of the classes even started. No one has been any help. This was the worst experience ever. 0/10 do not give your money to this school. Skyline college still has my $695.', 'I’m leaving this review to help future transfer students avoid the confusion I experienced.

I proactively asked a counselor before enrolling whether a Computer Science course would count toward my UC transfer goals. Articulation was confirmed, but I was not informed that the course would not count toward financial-aid-approved units unless added to my SEP.

That distinction was never explained, and it later caused serious issues with my financial aid status. Counseling and financial aid appear to operate in separate lanes, and students are left to discover critical details after the fact.

My advice to future students: get written confirmation from both Counseling and Financial Aid before enrolling in any course that is not explicitly required for your major.

The school may work for some, but for transfer-focused CS students who rely on financial aid, the lack of coordination and clarity made this a frustrating experience.', "The track is open for public use if you're willing to brave the chilly February winds!  Also, Parking Lot P has a COVID Clinic on site if anyone needs testing for travel and the like...", 'Let me tell you how I do love this college. It’s incredible!!! Last semester, I still believed that Skyline was a quite quiet college because students and staffs  might be affected by the foggy and cold weather all the time. I wanted an active college where has very energetic generations of students. Since that ideas had popped up in my mind, I chose CSM for my first semester even though it takes me 20-30 minutes to get there while I drive to Skyline in 5 minutes. But in Spring 2020 semester, I wanted to try it out. I signed up 2 classes. First day at school, I have a lot of confusions about facilities and the system, but from students to staffs, all of them were super nice and friendly to help me out. I could grab whoever I met on my path, and they showed me very detailed information. My professors are awesome, too. Very kind and passionate. Overall, people here are not low energy like I thought before.']

name: San Bernardino Valley College
reviews: ['My grandson to be gave his teacher a 3 months notice that he was getting married on a specific date.  His teacher had scheduled a test on that date and would not allow my grandson to take it at an earlier or later date.  Get a zero if he wasn\'t there.  Have a granddaughter who goes to Yale and she is attending the wedding.  Yale gave her a whole week off and worked with her studies schedule.  SBVC supports this teachers" decision.  What does this say about caring about the student.   This is a real life situation and thankful he wasn\'t ill or hospitalized.', "I attended here from 1991-1998 and earned my first AA. SBVC was a great start to my academic career. Now, there has been declining enrollment, not unaffected by the Pandemic. While professors remain the bright spot, it appears that student services, in general, leaves much to be desired. Unfortunately, there exists much unnecessary 'red tape' in getting expedited services. Policies are stuck in the 1990s. Counselors are NEVER available. 30 years ago, there were always 2 counselors working nights who would see students until 7pm on a walk-in basis. What the hell happened? Beautiful campus with new buildings; but this place is a shell of itself. It gives the impression that this school does not care about students. So disappointing.", "There was a Planetarium offering a tour of our Universe lead by 'Major' Tom. It was Groovy Gr8 & we got to handle an ancient meteorites before stepping outside to view (through telescopes) Jupiter & 4 of Jupiter's moons & then the Orion Nebula.\nI've been on Mother Earth,  Terrafirma for me at 6 decades & I'd not seen any of these heavenly bodies before last night. Thanks 'Major' Tom & SBVC Valley College 😎✌🏽☮️", 'Amazing place of learning.  I came for welding. I had Mr.John King as our teacher and instructor but he was much more than that. He was a mentor and cared about each of us who actually were there to learn. The school is amazing and the staff are very helpful.  Your never too old to go back to school. I recommend this place completely. 👌', 'I first had a sour attitude about attending this school since it was never an option on attending swell as just graduating and expecting the environment to be "high school 2.0".  When I attended my very first semester. my attitude changed to neutral as it seemed my expectations were far from true.  As I am halfway completed with my degree as well as a year away from getting started with my transfer process, it took me a lot of realization that sbvc is just a college.  Despite the surrounding location being in a not so nice area, the campus itself is gorgeous and very calming, unless there are events being held.  The counselors are encouraging and want everyone to succeed.  The professors that I have had treat me with respect.  So far, I am mentally well to attend my courses no matter what I am going through.  I\'m glad I gave this college a chance as it is preparing me for the career field and a smooth transition to a 4 year university.']

name: Solano Community College
reviews:

name: Sonoma State University
reviews: ["I enjoyed taking Psychology classes here and finishing my Bachelor's degree years ago. It's a mellow university. Nice teachers. Some great classes. Housing on campus. The Green Music Center has wonderful events. Overall, a lovely campus and school in the CSU system.", "Just started at SSU as a transfer student from SRJC and I am blown away by the beauty surrounding this campus! All of the teachers and students I've interacted with have been amazing! I'm loving this school!", 'Best food I’ve ever eaten at a university/camp. I’m honestly sad to leave it! So many yummy veggies, so many options, SUCH GOOD ICECREAM, and the best staff', "Love this school, it's truly beautiful. Foods always great and they have a pretty decent amount of vegetarian options. The staff and faculty are amazing and extremely welcoming. Best choice I ever made transferring here. Although regretfully they don't have family housing which made it very hard for me as a parent to find housing. The Lobos cafeteria is an awesome place to drink beer and do homework. Where the school really lacks is the nonexistent connection between staff/students. It is overtly political, which is cool if you are far left, but if you are indifferent or conservative, forget about it. Parking is pretty bad but that’s every university.']

name: South Coast College
reviews:
["South Coast College is an excellent trade school that has multiple fields of interest to choose from.  I graduated from their Court Reporting program back in 2014.  The teachers are diligent,  knowledgeable, and encourage students through the classes.  They are always available and happy to answer questions or take time to hear any concerns and advise how you can move forward. If you are even curious about what South Coast College has to offer, it's worth your time and efforts to set up a tour to get a first-hand look and insight of what they have to offer.", 'The teachers and staff here are amazing! They overly prepare you for your state exams, making your state exam process smooth and fun! I’m honored to have graduated from South Coast College and would recommend this school to anyone who is ready to jump into a new career.', 'When I decided I wanted to become a court reporter, I looked into accredited, superior schools in Southern California . South Coast College was the only physical establishment that hit all the checks on my list. South Coast has such a helpful, hands-on staff that I never felt in the dark about anything, which was very important for me in an educational setting. I qualified for the CSR Examination and graduated in 2.5 years. If you want to be successful in a good career, check out the court reporting program at South Coast. They have other credible programs as well.', "I loved the hands on experience I received from this school. Every teacher knows your name and wants to help you succeed. They take their time after classes to give you extra guidance. The atmosphere was always positive and uplifting. They all help you to try to pass as well as help to keep you motivated when you're not passing. Because I went to South Coast, I've been able to have a very successful career in the few years I've been a reporter, and I have them to thank for everything I've accomplished. So thank you, South Coast, for all that you did and continue to do each day!", 'I love and loved South Coast College. The best thing about it was its staff.  From its court reporting instructors to its paralegal program, everything is taught and intended to provide the student with the best opportunity to leave its halls with knowledge superlative to that of students from anywhere else.

What are your chances of obtaining a position in the legal office as a court reporter, paralegal or legal assistant? That is probably what I should have asked myself prior to obtaining a "less-than-godly" student loan! I graduated mentally prepared - but financially not quite ready to work at the rate at which most legal firms hire those fresh out of school!

Although I work in a field completely unrelated to that in which I was trained (I graduated from the paralegal program and am one of two people now running a surgical company.) I maintain the hope that I will become an integral part of a firm, foundation or group that will recognize my training. Hats off to you, SCC, the "best little college in California!"']

Love a college with no responsibility."]

name: Southern California Institute of Architecture
reviews:
["The School that Changed a City

I write this review not as an alumni but as an Angeleno.

When the Sci-arc moved to its current location from Marina del Rey in 2000 the surrounding neighborhood was empty, desolate, and filled with crime and homeless.  People say there are three things that fuel a thriving community: housing, dining, and schools.  It has been almost over a decade since housing and restaurants slowly and carefully moved in, but it wasn't until Sci-arc finally purchased the build that it rented for so many years.

That catapulted the community into the fast lane.  Housing sky rocked, hip restaurants and boutique stores moved in, mega complexes started to get built.  It's a milestone that changed the entire eastside of Los Angeles.

Architects Home Grown

The connective tissue between Sci-arc and downtown Los Angeles is undeniable and beneficial to both parties.  Students and faculty architects are deeply engrained in the current rising of Downtown Los Angeles.", 'Fitting to see they can't seem to crack the lists of top architecture schools, trophies just for placing I guess, although one of the highest tuition costs in the country doesn't seem justified if the prestige isn't really all that great with hiring firms. Not as advertised in my opinion (though they do seem to self-advertise heavily), it is a good old boys club as far as I am concerned, intelligence takes a backseat and only a handful of students who play that game will really thrive from a system like that.
They seem to take whoever they can get, with a very high acceptance rate for an "elite" school. In my own experience making the mistake of attending the MArch2 program for two semesters, the literacy rates were dreadful, "easiest A you'll ever get" I had heard a few times in conversation when I mentioned that it bothered me some of my graduate peers struggled to read English at a supposedly elite educational institution in the United States.
For how "competitive" they lauded the student body to be when I voiced complaint, in my architectural theory classes most of the students could hardly read written English, much less participate their words in any meaningful discussion with professors who struck me as the incredibly elitist type that could care less who they're teaching. After all it's not like they will remember many of the student livestock, mostly mislead into coming from overseas, once they've paid for the last semester of extremely over-priced tuition.
It's also worth mentioning that the studio instructors browbeat students into spending what I always considered a second tuition cost on supplies, pedestals, expensive 3d-prints due most classes, and in render-farm credits necessary to finish animated assignments. The burden of most of those payments is thrown damn near entirely on the student. Just in case I haven't supplied enough of a warning, have fun with your sorry excuse for a workspace. That's right, each student was given what was called a desk made out of a few trash pieces of plywood or particle board that must be some sort of minimalist inside-joke between the faculty.
Maybe with the previous dean it was a better situation, but Hernan has not been very impressive. But again that's just my opinion, perhaps if they were more transparent concerning graduate job placement statistics, or lack thereof...
1/5 Avoid Like The Plague', 'Basically sci-arc is a scam especially their edge-program. They shouldn’t open stuff like fiction and entertainment, as far as I most student goes bankrupt after enrolling that program! Imagining a film school teaching architecture design then congratulations you will never able to compete with the real architect. Anyway, they only benefit for their selves, for example my professor do scam and make more than 150K per year, so he bought a houses in LA in just 2 years. Do go there, you will be put into a trap and it takes you few years or you never strong enough to go out from the trap.', 'The school that is proud of their high number international students!
I don’t know about others, I was clearly misled by chair of admission who told me I will be hired to work on a project that the institute has won, located in South of Paris. He explained how lucky I would be to be able to work while I study as other students had to look for work after graduation. It was a lie. After I arrived I had to ask about the project multiple times, and eventually I was told it has been a miscommunication. A miscommunication! No projects. So it was only a small lie to get me on board. The lies still continue in every occasion. I’d say this school is highly unethical in many ways. Also, you will use broken chairs and desks made of cheap materials. Stay away.', 'Sciarc is simply a scam. They really need to redefine their purpose as they don’t seem to understand they don’t train architects in any way. They train artists (who 3D model wired buildings only) or maybe they know but still pretend they are training architects.
The tuition is extremely high (unless you have money to through out of the window and have time to kill) and since the school is not popular (they heavily self advertise otherwise and fake their rank but do not believe everything you read please), they literally take in anyone (I repeat anyone) who applies (and pays). In sciarc it is very popular to bump into students who seem totally out of place, if you feel they are indeed out of place, consider the possibility that you may be the one who is out of place!
Companies do not like to hire from sciarc either unless they look for “CAD monkeys” (sorry but this is the truth) for $4 to $6 per hour. (So sorry)
Some call sciarc an “OPT SHOP” too since foreign students who plan want to stay in the US enroll to sciarc to take benefit from the 3 year OPT.
Not recommended.']

name: University of Southern California
reviews:
['Very nice campus. However, the building style are pretty much same styles within the campus.  This place is so well maintained it is so clean.

I saw at least 10 security guards within my one hour visit. And the whole campus is well confined within its own boundaries. I believe it must be very safe within the campus.

It is a private school and has lots of good programs. The tuition is not cheap.  I think that is why they can maintain such a good program and environment.', 'Beautiful campus filled with amazing minds. I really loved the building styles and the way campus is maintained. It’s a tough university to get into for a reason.
Best part is the free Lyft rides they offer their students during the night to maintain safety, that is something I have never heard before.
I would love to visit this campus again.', "A beautiful campus with a Romanesque revival architecture. Makes for a unique scholarly - progressive - modern look. During school season the campus is bursting with life in every corner, while during the summer and off-seasons it is quiet and tranquil. It's not a massive campus but not small either. It takes 10-15 minutes to walk from side to side. Restaurants, cafes and other food and drink places are all around campus, with 3-4 starbucks cafes in and around the campus. The new construction of the USC village has made such a positive contribution to the whole ambience of the campus. Unfortunately, the surrounding area, while improving, is still not the best.", "If you're looking for a stunning campus with a rich history and world-class facilities, look no further than the University of Southern California (USC). This prestigious university boasts one of the most beautiful campuses in the country, with a mix of stunning architecture, lush greenery, and modern amenities that create a truly unforgettable experience.

One of the highlights of USC's campus is the architecture. From the stunning red brick buildings of the original campus to the modern glass-and-steel structures of the new buildings, every inch of the university is designed with both beauty and functionality in mind. The iconic Bovard Auditorium, the ornate Doheny Memorial Library, and the sleek and modern Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism are just a few of the many buildings that make up this breathtaking campus.

But it's not just the architecture that makes USC such a special place. The university is also incredibly well maintained, despite being located in the heart of downtown Los Angeles. The lawns are always impeccably manicured, the buildings are sparkling clean, and the walkways are well-lit and easy to navigate.

Despite being located in the middle of a bustling city, the campus feels like a peaceful oasis. The tall palm trees, colorful flowers, and bubbling fountains create a tranquil environment that is perfect for studying, relaxing or just hanging out.", 'USC was a prestigious private research university in LA. The University Park campus was a fenced campus that was uncommon in American universities (The Rockefeller University was fenced and closed to the public). Due to the pandemic, all visitors would receive temperature checking and answer questions on the virus infection symptoms. Campus looks clean and beautiful with the majority of the red-brick buildings uniformly erected on the campus in which more than a dozen schools and institutes were set inside.']

name: Taft College
reviews: ['I recommend Taft college to anyone I can. Class sizes are small and easy to get into. I would highly recommend Dr Abbas J for anatomy and physiology. reviews: ['We visited for one of their barbecue tour days. It was awesome. You will have the chance to talk directly with the Director of Admissions. She is incredibly knowledged. name: Ventura College
reviews:
['Ventura College has two campuses. This is the main campus in Ventura offers a full range of academic programs, library services, student support, and sports facilities. It is the primary location for most students.', 'One of the best community colleges around. Definitely a great place to start or continue your academic career journey. Very beautiful campus, super large too. Nice buildings all over, tons of places to sit and work or take a break inside and outside. Definitely recommend everyone to check this college out in person. They also have a swap meet here in the parking lot on the weekends. Also worth checking out if in the area. Good deals and some good food. One of the many great places and things about Ventura California.', 'Ventura College is a great place for learning and personal growth. The campus is beautiful, well-maintained, and easy to navigate, with plenty of open spaces to relax and study. The atmosphere is welcoming and supportive, making it a comfortable environment for students.
The professors and staff are helpful, knowledgeable, and truly care about student success. There are a wide variety of programs, classes, and activities to fit different interests and goals. The resources provided, such as the library, tutoring centers, and student services, are excellent and very useful.
Ventura College also offers a strong sense of community, with events and clubs that help students connect and get involved. reviews:

Berkeley College encourages a strong focus on career development from start to finish. Highly recommend!", 'I was warned about Berkeley college but I didn’t listened and  now I have learned my lesson.

Attending this school the school cost were almost $13k my financial aid would cover atlease half and the rest of 6,000 would be cover by students loans.

I would totally recommend this school. Wish I had the nerve to take out more loans but I've had enough with the loans I have. Thank you Berkeley College for making me feel like I was home, and doing everything possible for me to graduate. I truly appreciate it."]

name: Walden University
reviews:
['I am currently a student at Walden University, and the only reason I remain enrolled is because the program can be completed online. Outside of the classes themselves, the overall administrative experience has been extremely frustrating.

The biggest problem is how disorganized and fragmented the system is. Getting a clear answer or speaking with the right person is unnecessarily difficult. Students are constantly bounced between departments such as financial aid, billing, advising, and cost of attendance. Each department frequently says they cannot help and directs you somewhere else. Even basic questions can turn into multiple emails and phone calls because no one seems able to address issues across departments.

Another major problem is the lack of responsiveness and urgency. It is extremely rare to reach someone in real time who can actually resolve an issue. Most representatives say they need to escalate the problem to a supervisor or manager, but those supervisors are almost never available to speak directly and often do not follow up afterward. This leaves students stuck waiting with no real updates or accountability.

In my case, a financial aid refund that should have been straightforward took approximately two and a half months to resolve. I was charged for a class that I was not enrolled in. The error was clearly visible on the billing statement itself. I even sent the document back with the incorrect charge marked so the issue could be clearly seen. Despite this, responses from billing repeatedly stated that the charges were correct instead of addressing the actual problem being pointed out. Being told the billing was correct while looking at the same document showing the error was incredibly frustrating.

The billing portal itself also adds to the confusion. Instead of providing a clear summary of tuition, fees, financial aid, and refunds, the system shows a running ledger of transactions. Even though there are different sections in the portal you can click through, it still does not clearly explain what you are actually being charged for or how credits are applied to your account.

Another frustrating part of the experience is the difference between enrollment and being an actual student. During enrollment, the enrollment specialist is extremely responsive and easy to reach by phone, text, or email at almost any time. Once you are officially enrolled, that access disappears. The enrollment specialist cannot assist with most issues anymore, and students are left trying to navigate a system where it is difficult to reach the correct department or get timely responses.

Walden is based in Minnesota, while many students live in completely different states. Because of this, students cannot simply walk into an office to resolve issues in person. When the phone system is unhelpful, responses are delayed, and departments redirect students elsewhere, it creates a system where getting help becomes unnecessarily complicated.

The online flexibility of the program is useful, but the administrative side of the university — including communication, billing transparency, and follow-through — creates a very frustrating experience for students.', 'My experience with Walden has been extremely positive. I am attending for Business Administration Degrees and plan to obtain my Doctorate from them in Public Administration. While my experience is online only and through Tempo, class work and  expectations have been clearly provided. I have a turn around time from my professors in 2-3 days, including emails that come in over the weekend or prior to holidays. I have had 1-2 more "difficult professors" but they have been respectful and clear on what I was doing not to expectation. Was it enjoyable to re-do work, no, but to think the road to growth will not have bumps in it is a delusion.

I see a few people with Financial Aid trouble/issues. I have used Financial Aid at Walden and found the process to be easy and the assistance to be helpful.

My Coach Melanie is fantastic and I will be disappointed to lose her when I go for my doctorate. That being said she is always quick to email or jump on a call, even when my kids are melting down in the background. I have been met with kindness and genuine compassion.

I have also transferred credits from a AA and they were all approved, it took some hoop jumping to get the transcripts through Parchment, but  it was only a short delay and worth waiting for.

As far as "for-profit" institutions there is a lot of help/resources and so many people that really want you to do well. I believe the best investment you can always make is in yourself and I believe Walden like with anything is 100% what you put into it.

In short I think the University is worth the money, and I think the education is quality.', 'This school has the potential to be great. The classes are well designed, and the instructors are knowledgeable, intentional, and supportive. Unfortunately, poor communication and slow administrative processes significantly impact the overall experience.
During my Master’s practicum, my site supervisor and I were notified of site approval just two days before the required start date, despite repeated emails and requests for updates. Although the program claims to offer field experience support, communication is limited to email, and responses direct students to lengthy, generic lists that often do not address specific questions. There is no way to escalate concerns or speak directly with someone.
At the end of the program, my degree, along with many others, was withheld for 20 days. This delayed our ability to apply for state requirements, which already take weeks to process, and directly affected our income. I was told a manager would call, but no one ever did. Additionally, final grades were posted 11 days after classes ended, even though we were repeatedly told that no extensions would be granted and grades would be posted promptly.
With stronger communication and more efficient administrative support, this school could truly live up to its potential.', 'I had a great time at my graduation on 7/11/2025. It was not just a graduation, it was an experience to remember; it was a celebration that will resonate with me for years. I met people worldwide as we shared this historical event. Walden knows how to celebrate your accomplishment. The event was well-organized and was a non-stop party. Thanks, Walden, for honoring us in style, class, and dignity.', 'Since I initially applied, my phone has been inundated with phone calls and texts from Tammy Byerly, who's a representative for Walden University. While I submitted all of the required documents needed to process my application, she has deliberately refused to process it without a phone call to "confirm some information and to assure we are placing students in the correct degree plan, start date etc". I do not personally require any hand-holding, or assistance in this matter, I am a US Army Veteran, and am capable of making my own decisions. I am attempting to apply to a graduate level program, this isn't my first rodeo. Stop wasting people's time and money.']

name: West Los Angeles College
reviews:
['The literal worse experience of my life. Do not give these people your information nor sign up for anything. Unprofessional incompetent staff. No care for students they are using you for financial aid. Reporting to Trump because I’ve never seen such fraud waste and abuse. Beware do not gone here, do not waste your time or energy. I’m reporting to whomever to can find and making sure to give 0 stars across the board. Horrible, horrible, horrible', 'If I could give zero stars, I would. I’ve been at West LA College for two years. Calling or emailing staff is consistently ignored. What could take 15 minutes over the phone turns into a 1 hour cross-town inconvenience just to get help and not be helped. When I finally reach someone, I encounter unprofessional behaviors such as counselors smelling strongly of marijuana  and excuses for not answering, like ‘I was on lunch.’ Time-sensitive processes, especially for students and veterans relying on GI Bill and FAFSA funds for basic living needs, are a constant battle. The rage bait is real at WLAC. The ambiance feels like a funeral, which may explain why nothing runs efficiently. I now take all my classes at their sister school to avoid this campus. 0/10.', 'This is one of 9 LACCD colleges. I’ve earned several certificates in Real Estate and Hospitality. I attempted to also earn a certificate in Business, but some classes are only offered at one of the 9 other campuses - which is where a problem may arise. There is a 50/50 chance that you take your course at one of the 9 sister colleges and WLAC won’t accept it. This happened to me when taking Business English at ELAC because it’s hardly offered at WLAC. The district is not well correlated. I’m now finishing up turning my certificates into AA degrees.

Financial Aid office is usually quick to respond to emails. Loans may be delayed a month into the semester. Cal Grants are also delayed 4-7 weeks in. Some grants like the Student Success Completion Grant are not always awarded like other colleges because the district runs out of state funds.

Book store does not always carry your books which can make your EOPS voucher pointless.

Overall, I love that I’m able to complete an AA degree online without having to attend in person. I just wish the school and district correlated their classes. I originally chose WLAC in 2022 because it was ranked as one of California’s best community colleges to obtain an AA degree online. You can also attend in person for many classes.', "I was only there to watch a women's volleyball match, so I did not see very much of it. What I saw was nice. The gym was well taken care of and the bathroom was clean. Near the gym they have airplanes and at least 1 helicopter. Everyone I met there was nice.  I only gave a 4 because my exposure was limited, but it looks very nice.", 'Ok so I don’t go here but I live across from here. Across from the football field, ish. There is a small sliver of the balloona creek or La river or whatnot between us that makes it a pain to get to the college. Because there’s no crossing, so you have to walk a good 3/4 of a mile around the perimeter to make your way to the actual entrance of the college. This seems like a fairly useless review and it is, given that I’m not a student and have no actual comment to its facilities or campus culture, etc, but I can say as a close neighbor - they do have a killer marching band. I love it. I can hear them (tho it’s contained, I could easily ignore if I needed to sleep or whatnot) and l quite like the drumline rhythms as an accompaniment to my sputtering through morning chores. Anyway, I’ve also heard that this is a decent school, feeds well into the ucs and state system. Semi environmentally depressing grounds, but not the worst. (Im looking at you cal state Fullerton, the city of Ontario, large swathes of Azusa).']

name: West Valley College
reviews:
['The administration office staff are super nice, especially Ana, is so helpful and efficient. She guided my parents through the entire process with patience and care. You can truly tell she has a big heart for students. Highly appreciated!', "I've been to and stayed in Royce Hall dormitory before Demolition and rebuilding at San Jose State University campus. West Valley College campus is so much more relaxing to traverse as a tetraplegic paralyzed in a wheelchair with Rolling Hills and oak trees and shade during the hot days, it's so much more relaxing atmosphere and not so many people to try to avoid accidentally running into with my wheelchair. Even though there are more accessible features at San Jose State I'm much more thoroughly enjoyed West Valley Community College. Thank you so much for a great experience.", 'The campus itself is top tier. I attended a semester of the UAS program and found it to be a huge letdown.

Professor Cruz had no idea what he was doing most of the time.  Tech issues and long rambling tangents were constant in class. Extremely unprofessional and disorganized. The only positive his courses offer is at-home access to ARCGIS Pro and Drone2Map where you can use the internet to teach you how to use these programs because he simply doesn't know how. We were told we'd get to do hands on activities and tours of drone factories and all those events were cancelled. We were taught very little and told to use ChatGPT to figure out how to do everything.

Mendelsohn is bad at teaching and his low-effort online course straight up sucks. There are far better online options available for ground pilot school, many for a similar price and you can do them at your own pace much faster with better study materials and no poorly designed homework assignments or error filled quizzes to worry about.

I do NOT recommend the UAS program at this school. You can learn ARCGIS and DroneDeploy online, and you can get your part 107 in a couple weekends of self study. The program offers little useful help to people who are struggling and is comically easy for someone who is smart enough to learn on their own. Furthermore, the program offers no pipeline for employment and only promises to let you "build your portfolio" with useless rice paper for tasks that you'll have to learn on the job anyways. Their certificate is literally worth no more than the paper it's printed on and their degree option isn't transferable.

Also admissions and records here doesn't have a contact phone number and is difficult to get ahold of and not helpful via email.

Worst community college experience I've ever had.', 'Applied for winter last year. Never got an email back after sending what was required and I missed the semester deadline because I couldn’t register (needed an ID # which I never was sent). Be aware of this because they do handle this poorly.', 'West Valley College has some amazing professors who really know their stuff and genuinely care about students. It’s a great environment for learning, whether you’re starting out or working toward a transfer. The community here is supportive, and the staff are always ready to help. Overall, it’s a solid choice if you want quality education and a campus that feels like a second home.']

reviews: ['Westmont College is a beautiful, well-kept campus nestled in a stunning town, with an amazing and caring staff. Like others have said, if you don't fit the stereotype of people there, you will struggle to make lifelong friends. Sure, everyone there is really nice, but that's about it. If you are an adventurous, spontaneous person who is afraid of being average (not in the academic sense, rather in your approach to life) you will have a hard time fitting in at Westmont. People there are very similar to each other, it's hard to describe the exact personality but everyone is very sheltered/homeschooled type kids. If you are a STEM major, DO NOT GO TO WESTMONT. Especially engineering, the program is a joke compared to other colleges. My high school had far better engineering. Don't make the same mistake I did and waste $20k.", 'Nice campus and small religious college. Class sizes are small for a great learning experience. Another perk I found is that the professors seem kind and caring."]

reviews:

The library does look pretty. But during the 10 hour orientation, the tour guides were rude and bossy. Small campus too, not a lot of food choices.
If you want to know what you are getting out of here, look up the notable alumni. Who are those people? Yes, we have never heard of them.

Speaking from my side of the view, so don't get offended.", 'I recently published a book and two months ago I called this library and asked if they would accept it as a donation. If you deal with libraries often this is the absolute worst kind to deal with -- I still don't know if a library is even there because it's in a closed-off area and could be people squatting a building. I don't recommend dealing with these people at all.']

name: Adams State University
reviews:
['If you are looking for an online counselor education program to become a therapist, I cannot recommend this one in good faith. I had some good professors and their program is organized. But they are not up to date with the requirements of other states. Only Colorado's.

If you are out of state, they will tell you to look up yourself and when you have questions they will just direct you to the state board. This mentality cost me a job opportunity because I did look it up online. I thought I understood. But because I had no one to ask my questions to, I just picked the national credential exam that bust suited my focus (like it said to do online), the NCMHE. And no one at Adams made it explicit that I can only take one exam before graduation. But my state requires you to take both the NCE and NCMHE but needs the NCE first before you can work under supervision. Because I took the wrong test (NCMHE not the NCE) I lost a job opportunity because my site did not want to wait 3 or 4 months for me to take the NCE exam.

So if you are ok with that kind of treatment, go to Adams State, I guess. But they really had an attitude of "figure it out, kid" while giving messaging that they are "there to help you".

And if you need academic accommodations, it's like that too. You have to let your professors know ahead of time that you are using your accommodations? Like if I had the mental space to do extra work like writing a professor asking for help before every assignment then I would not need the accommodations.

So I cannot recommend the Counseling Education program for people who live out of the state of Colorado or people who need academic accommodation. Like I said, they say they will help you. The messaging is feel good, warm vibes. But in practice, you really are on your own for getting what you need out of the program. And that really sucks given how much money the program is getting from you.', 'Nicely kept campus. Great place to pursue some degrees. The campus is well maintained. Support by the community is very strong. It has all the things students need to study and have a good degree without major distractions. It is not a party university and there are not a ton of businesses and other things that would make students be wasting time. People there are very friendly and welcoming. The Alamosa community as a whole is a welcoming community that values and embraces everyone.', "For a campus that has international students, they really help you feel at home here!!  Beautiful landscapes, along with friendly, intelligent staff make this a top choice!! Thank goodness for their Adam's Promise, which made University a possibility for our son!! 🙏💚", "This institution needs to review it's policies and cut the red tape. There are many areas of improvement, and opportunity for innovation.  I will only mention a few. This institution has a low graduation rate when compared to it's peers, it is probably because they don't help students succeed, and their policies in essence set a student up to fail rather than succeed; often giving students the runaround. Their staff is not knowledgeable and not professional. This could be addressed through professional development programs implemented at all levels of the institution. I wish I would have not wasted my time and money at this  institution longer to graduate because of arbitrary administrative policies. There are better educational options for less money! Great improvements to the aesthetics and captures the San Luis Valley's natural beauty. This and a few professors are the only positive thing I can share about my experience. Cut the politics and focus on your students!", 'SBDC was a wealth of information.
Carmona Escobar was amazing']

name: Aims Community College
reviews:
['Up before the sun to catch the hot air balloons 🎈 at Aims Community College this morning! My friend might not be a morning person, but I, the quintessential early bird, took it all in stride. Just means more coffee for me while I waited! ☕ It was totally worth it, though. Seeing all the colorful balloons fill the sky was so cool!

#HotAirBalloon #EarlyBird #BalloonFestival #AimsCommunityCollege #ColoradoLife #ColorfulSkies #MorningAdventures #NotAMorningPerson #WorthTheWait #OptOutside', 'Aims Community College in Greeley, Colorado, is one of the top 100 community colleges in the United States, and for good reason. Its reputation for academic excellence is matched by its uniquely charming campus, featuring an array of small, eclectic buildings that create a welcoming and distinctive learning environment.

The engineering and chemistry departments are standouts, offering top-tier programs that rival those at larger institutions. During my time at Aims, I pursued a degree in pre-engineering and engineering drafting, creating detailed designs for CAD 101/102 and advanced 200-level design classes.

Equally impressive is the chemistry department, where the instructors’ passion for teaching and ability to simplify complex topics set them apart. In my class, which included about 23 pre-nursing students, the energy and dedication of the faculty were unmatched. The pre-nursing program’s seamless transition into the University of Northern Colorado is a testament to the program’s quality and preparation. The chemistry faculty were instrumental in helping students succeed, leaving a lasting impact with their supportive and inspiring teaching.

Aims Community College combines academic rigor, a supportive environment, and a beautiful campus, making it an outstanding choice for students pursuing their goals in engineering, nursing, or any other field. It’s a place where students can truly thrive, thanks to the dedication and expertise of its faculty.', "I was a recipient of their FREE TAX SERVICE'S  this last year....they madec2 paper copies of my financial papers and tax forms...they gave one copy to a STRANGER who also was there...they didn't apologize and left it up to me to Block my taxes and forms for future scams...
I expressed my disappointment,  anger for their lack of concern...it was like  OH WELL...please be very careful if you use their free tax services coming up.....", 'Aims put on such a great graduation yesterday. Great job AIMS! Congratulations to all the graduates 🎓!', 'At first, it can seem like a confusing campus, but the super friendly staff are more than willing to get you pointed in the right direction and to your destination! Combine that with amazing professors who care deeply about the subjects they teach and the success of each of their students and you got yourself an awesome recipe for success!']

name: Arapahoe Community College
reviews: ["The 42nd Annual Colorado Concours d'Elegance & Exotic Sports Car Show was awesome!", 'A little concrete utopia with eclectic and kindhearted professors and students. The education is robust and inexpensive, and the campus offers lots of services and opportunities.', 'Mostly everything is great. Currently I have an issue with my Bio Fundamentals class. name: Bel-Rea Institute of Animal Technology
reviews:
['The campus is very nice and intimate but because the instructors do not have teaching degrees the classes are often non comprehensive. They expect you to work but you have no time because of the constant studying. Some of the instructors were very demeaning and made people feel stupid for asking questions, something that should never happen in a school.', 'I attended this school at the age of 23 and went for the entire two years. This school was next to impossible. Previous college experience was 100x more positive than this schooling. The female"professors" were rude,unprofessional and seemed to almost want to set students up for failure.
Never have I had such an experience as I did the two years at Bel-Rea.
I wish the experience was more positive and fulfilling as my past schooling was. The price I paid for this school, is to me now, EMBARRASSING.
But as always others will have a much more positive experience. I recommend other schools.', "Very good little school, in a safe area. As a graduate I can honestly say your chances of getting a job once graduated are EXTREMELY high. More than half our graduating class already had jobs lined up BEFORE graduating.
In regards to the actual schooling experience there is definitely a little of the good, the bad, and the fantastic.
For the good the campus has undergone some fantastic renovations, with an extra classroom added and some cosmetic work to one of the buildings. In class there is an appropriate amount of hands on experience (the school has a wide variety of on-campus animals to work with), but this school really goes above and beyond to line up volunteer and shadowing experiences right into your hands, especially if you feel you need more practice, AND these are fantastic networking opportunities! In addition, this school offers AMAZING laboratory classes. You learn an incredible amount but I will not lie--these courses are challenging! But the experience you gain is a major factor in why so many facilities hire this school's graduates.
For the bad, most of it comes down to the scale of the facility. Because it is a small campus it does allow everyone to become a tight-knit little community, but at the same time it limits staff flexibility. Because it is not a larger campus the limitations on staff also limit the scheduling times for classes. You WILL have a flexible schedule, it just won't be as flexible as you think. Mostly because the quarterly schedule makes you feel like you're moving at a breakneck pace. This isn't necessarily an issue for most students, but for students with children this can be particularly difficult to work around, especially if it is a single parent household. In addition there are some course policies that can be rather harsh, but most of this is necessary for both the school's accreditation and for the fairness to other students. If you go here you will be frustrated at least once, but I think it's a small sacrifice when you know you will have a job at the end of it all. Which is hard to say for some universities!

And for the AMAZING it has to be the staff. They want you to succeed and they want you to be honest. (Seriously, they are blood-hounds for cheating--they will find you, and they will kick you out. A common saying at the school is that if you are willing to cheat to pass a test, who knows what you'll do to an animal. And this is extremely accurate.) They want you to be a good vet tech and they want to know you did it honestly. The professors give lots of opportunities to help struggling students and guidance from their personal experience.  If you work hard they will be there to help.In addition the administrators are awesome too! Sometimes life throws a curveball and interrupts your studies, but the administrators do their best to help accommodate. They can help you with almost anything. Counseling, finding roommates, adjusting schedules,  and in general just helping sort your life out!

Ultimately, I would highly recommend this school! I have a few nitpicks here or there, and a couple of moments I remember were frustrating, but in the end I am satisfied with my education. AND the staff will be there to help if you ever need guidance navigating the job market, both before and after you graduate!", "I'm so glad after retiring from the military that I used my 9/11 GI bill to attend Bel Rea! The classes were difficult but the school has in place many unique tools to help students succeed. Personally, I used tutoring services provided by other students and teachers then became a tutor myself. There were many job and volunteer opportunities available that reinforced the curriculum which helped me to obtain my dream job only 3 weeks after graduating! Thank you Bel Rea! If you are serious about becoming a Veterinary Technician I strongly recommend Bel-Rea Institute of Animal Technology.", "Bel Rea has really taught me a lot. The curriculums can be challenging but the teachers are always there to help. I really enjoyed my studies at Bel Rea because faculties are friendly and they make it worth your while. It's not a walk in the park but I felt I was prepare for anything after that. Thank you so much Bel Rea."]

name: University of Colorado Denver/Anschutz Medical Campus
reviews: ['Here for my kids surgery and 4 week stay. Had amazing doctors, amazing nurses and an amazing team! We have been well taken care of! The only issue we’ve had was a female security personnel that apparently misplaced her midol.. and food is a little spendy. But the campus is nice with a quiet little garden area to decompress in. Outdoor seating for having meals outside. I highly recommend this hospital for your kiddos stay!', 'The absolute worst ever. They just have multiple teams discussing treatment options with no one in charge, allowing a patient to lay in a bed for up to two weeks and have no treatment plan whatsoever. If given a choice, I would go anywhere other than this hospital.', 'They have always bern good for us. Their oncology fept saved a good friend of ours with csncer. Their trials have given her 15 more years.', "We haven't have this level of care ever . The staff the nurses the doctors awesome. The best hospital in Colorado.", 'On August 12 I took my wife to Anshutz for labs. She has been battling cancer for 6 years. The labs were not good and they sent her to the CARE Emergency Center around 1:30 PM. We were greeted there by Nurse Petra Shelest, probably the most professional and competent nurse ever. She hardly left Cindy’s side and between her and Kaycee she was rarely left unattended. Any request for warm blankets or anything else were quickly met. Around 5:30 PM my wife’s oxygen fell and she exhibit irregular heartbeat. The decided a chest xray was needed and Petra personally wheeled her in a wheel chair to the other end of the facility. Around 6:30 symptoms escalated and they determined she needed to be admitted. Petra again wheeled her up to the seventh floor Oncology Unit. Due to shift changes and other issues no one was there to check her in. Petra stayed well past her scheduled quitting time until she was sure Cindy was being care for. I would strongly recommend her for any and all honors or rewards that can be given.\nDarrell Dinkel']

name: University of Colorado Colorado Springs
reviews:
["I love UCCS so much, it's such a wonderful school. I am currently in my fourth undergrad year here, began in Fall 2022, and so far my experience is overall very positive. The campus is extremely beautiful, the classes are very interesting and insightful, there are a lot of resources that are very helpful, and so on. In my personal opinion, I also really love the Dining facilities, and the clubs and orgs are pretty cool, etc. Overall I feel a strong sense of belonging and community here. It's such a wonderful school and I knew since I first toured here, that it was the right school for me.

There are some downsides of course, which some are not too bad because there are ups and downs everywhere, but some things need to improve. In my freshman year, everything was so magical and I felt so excited about everything, but after that, I felt less cared about. I think UCCS is improving on that but for a while, it felt like they only really cared about their freshmen. I also feel like the Springs in general makes it hard to commute if you don't have a car, even if you live close by off campus, and on campus housing can get ridiculously expensive. But of course, the magic still stays with me in my heart and I feel like I belong on this campus. But, I feel like it could do as much for sophmores, juniors, seniors, superseniors (year 5, 6, 7... depending), nontraditional students, and of course graduate students, all as much as they do for freshmen.

I found my place here and I am so glad I chose this school. I love everything about it, and I resonate with the personal and professional development, fueling success, finding a sense of belonging, and so many more of UCCS's values. We also have beautiful mountain views, great places around the Springs to go to and visit, there are wonderful employment opportunities, and so on. I really like it here and I highly recommend this school. Overall, it's a very awesome school! Normally I'd give it 5 stars, it's just more that the housing can be so expensive and that the vibe changes everywhere every single year. It also feels like, or at least used to feel like even more, that Freshmen were the most cared about groups of students. It feels like it dies down after some time... Sometimes.", "This school is just another example of the subtle racism that Colorado is known for. If you aren't white, expect to be passed over, ignored, treated like you don't exist while your white classmates only talk to other white classmates. It's great being right in the middle of a group of white people like in labs, and they refuse to ask you anything while they get everything wrong. Top notch learning experience, even if it isn't about the subject of the class.", "Just saying hello to my favorite school and thanking it for all the support that it has given me to graduate. Thank you.

I scored 4/5. The experience was great, not perfect, and I would absolutely recommend enrolling and graduating. The college rests on the side of the mountain and its view is breathtaking, you can see the entire side of the city from the campus. It's nice! Visit there sometime!", 'This school supports sexual harassment, bullying, and pretty much any crime under the sun. This institution has a lot of issues as everyone else already pointed out. But in recent years, it has really become an unsafe place to be. There is no concern for student safety, to the point where I would consider the people in charge to be "anti safety." Campus police just ride around and yell at random people, or spend most of their time in the dinning halls. Students have to worry about campus staff and their "predatory" nature. Shootings get swept under the rug. And when the university catches any flack, they send emails to everyone about "institutional standards" and mental health resources. As student of 8 years, I never thought I would be so happy to graduate and leave this awful place.', 'The campus is set at edge of the colorado rockies... beautiful. Mostly it is calm, peaceful.  Some RUDE STUDENTS have zero respect for handicap parking, however.']

name: Spartan College of Aeronautics and Technology
reviews: ['Well... My father and other colleagues trained here and went on to become 747 Captains with major airlines! That was back in the day. Pilots are needed in the job pipeline and Spartan should perhaps look for govt. help with funding to provide more aircraft and support and check pilots for this college. This is needed for our nation, to have well qualified pilots who are experienced and know what they are doing!! Who are your Senators and Congress rep. people to get funding assistance?!', 'The facility made several promises that they failed to keep. After completing the NDT program, I was instructed to return to my previous position as a maintenance machinist. It seems all they care about is your money, and their placement program is ineffective. I would advise against attending this school if you are considering a career in aviation, as they are relying on a reputation that has long since faded.', 'One of the best Aviation school in the US.. great tutors and always helpful to students..', 'I strongly advise against attending Spartan Flight School due to a range of issues that left me both financially and educationally set back. The pay for Certified Flight Instructors (CFIs) is extremely low—only $19 an hour, with a slight increase to $22 for multi-engine instruction. This discourages quality teaching, and in some cases, CFIs have signed off on training that wasn’t actually completed. The management is unsupportive and more focused on profits than students’ success. When I struggled financially, the chief pilot dismissed my concerns and threatened instructors who helped students with financial issues.\nSpartan is understaffed and poorly equipped, with over 400 students and just one Designated Pilot Examiner (DPE), causing delays in checkrides. The aircraft fleet is small, resulting in frequent lesson cancellations. The scheduling system is flawed, with favoritism and poor communication adding unnecessary stress. Overall, Spartan prioritizes money over quality education. I recommend looking into other schools like TCC or Part 61 options for a better training experience.', 'Rope  swings with little airplanes that have flight simulator on the screen that buzz light year u right on to a full speed tread mill that launches you into a going down tread mill to a strait treadmill  hitting the run way with your skinny wheel bike racing tires is my idea of flight training']

name: University of Colorado Boulder
reviews:
['Beautiful campus!

Spent time here in the summer. See the photos.

They have a space exhibit at old main, a planetarium, an observatory, and many other things to see and do.

The buildings all share a unified stone and red tile them on the roof.

They also do walking tours.', 'One of the most beautiful campuses I have visited. Spectacular landscape with mountains on the side, and the buildings are uniquely colored due to locally sourced limestone. Highly recommend for few hours to be spent here to anyone passing by Boulder.', "Our son is a student at CU Boulder and we couldn't be more happy with his decision to be a buff.   A fantastic academic institution with a diverse student population and (in my opinion) the prettiest campus in the world.    Absolutely love the place!", "The stately, majestic campus of one of the great universities of the American West. I must admit that I'm a little biased toward Colorado Boulder, having grown up in the Colorado front range region, but returning to this campus, I am even more impressed by its magnificence and its sprawling beauty than I was when I was younger. The campus is a wonderful, lively place to wander around and explore, seeing a variety of new sites ranging from a scale model of the solar system to a lovely little prairie like area that has carrots growing in it. This is a place that feels constantly surprising, and it's never boring when you are walking through it, yet the campus feels remarkably unified. Despite the differences in when the buildings were constructed, they all feel cohesive, and they all have that specific reddish-brown stone color that glows in the mountain sunlight, making the campus look both like a site for true learning and comprehension and a distinctly Colorado place that could not exist anywhere else. I highly recommend coming here if you are in the area, and if you are considering going to the University of Colorado Boulder, I guarantee you that you will enjoy your time at this campus.", 'Expensive to attend as in state student despite edicts on education. Campus is pretty but overrun by homeless like most of Boulder. Some good programs and teachers though.']

name: Colorado Christian University
reviews:
['I do not recommend this University for military or prior military individuals. Their finance department is a complete soup sandwich and only ONE student advisor is assigned for the entire military community. They mischarged the VA for my classes then sent me a bill to be paid immediately for over 4k. As a disabled veteran I asked for a little time to pay it off and they declined. Placed a hold on my student account until their mistake is paid off. Not to mention I called and emailed several times during my transition from active duty to VA.', 'CCU is an excellent place for our growing young adults.  It is Bible based and the students seem to love the professors.  If you look up Christian Universities and Colleges, CCU is at the top of the list for staying focused on Christ.  The student apartments are absolutely amazing as well.  And the food, at least when parents are on campus, is first rate.', 'As a recent graduate of Colorado Christian University (CCU), I feel it’s important to share my genuine experience for the benefit of prospective students. When I first heard about CCU back in high school, I was excited by the idea of attending an academically challenging university that claimed to be rooted in Christian values. I truly believed it was the place where I was meant to grow both intellectually and spiritually.

Although I transferred in as a junior pursuing my degree in Computer Information Systems, my initial enthusiasm quickly met reality. Unfortunately, I found the student culture to be far less welcoming than expected. In my experience, many students seemed judgmental and unkind, especially toward those who did not fit into what I would describe as the "ideal CCU mold." Rather than fostering a Christ-centered, inclusive community, the environment often felt exclusive and critical.

Regarding the faculty, my experiences were mixed. Some professors were absolutely incredible—wise, compassionate individuals who went above and beyond to support their students. I am grateful for the relationships I built with them and will continue to value those connections. However, others did not embody the values they professed, which was deeply disappointing.

What concerns me most is the direction I witnessed the university heading during my time there. Rather than focusing on spiritual development and student well-being, there appeared to be a growing emphasis on financial interests. Several student support services—including academic advising, the career center, and even campus security—were significantly reduced or cut altogether while I was enrolled.

I did not remain silent about these issues. Before graduating, I personally brought my concerns to the new university president, who had publicly invited students to share feedback. Unfortunately, my outreach was ignored. I also spoke with the dean of students, only to be met with justification for inappropriate conduct. I was told directly, “I do not engage with students to enforce the rules”—a response that, in my view, reflects a failure of leadership in a role meant to advocate for students.

Despite these challenges, if asked whether I would choose CCU again knowing what I know now, my answer would still be yes—but for different reasons. While my experience at CCU was far from what I had hoped for, it was there that I met my spouse and learned valuable, though difficult, lessons about people, faith, and leadership.

I share this perspective not out of bitterness, but in the hope that it will help others make informed decisions about whether CCU is the right fit for them.', "I cannot even begin to express all the amazing things at CCU: the staff, the students, the vibe, the housing options, the education, the community connections, the growth and learning of each individual, the building of relationships between themselves and God and the enormity of friends.

Just left our youngest 1200 miles from home as a freshman at CCU. Lots of emotions flood the moment, but above all joy and anticipation knowing she is surrounded and supported by God's love and those that model exactly that.", 'Absolutely phenomenal school all inclusive and i highly recommend!']

name: Colorado School of Mines
reviews:
['Professors are usually great, but the administration is really juicing extra out of you for each semester. They charge you fees to be in clubs, but the clubs don't get very much (if any) of that money. They charge $600 for the rec center, but many of the machines are broken for weeks, and it's usually very overcrowded. They charge you $600 in fees to park, and the parking is always full, so you end up parking somewhere else anyways.

I even pay them $700 per year to build new buildings that I'm not allowed in without special access (which I don't have). I pay $300 per year for sports teams I don't care about.

"Mandatory Fees" don't cover all the fees you'll be required to pay (parking, for instance), tuition gets hiked up by $3,480 compared to what is listed on the CoA website, and, even after all of that, they usually don't provide me with all of the resources required to take the class.

TLDR: Professors are good, campus is pretty nice, but they will find ways to make you pay them money that would require a PhD just to come up with.', 'Our kids were thrilled to see the massive amounts of gems and minerals in this place. It is extensive and fun to look at. When you think you’re done, there’s a downstairs as well. Just park close - or enjoy walking through the entire campus… which we’d also fun too!', 'As visitor prospective, this campus seems small and limited spaces but views are beautiful, designed areas are not easy to find and understand, campus polices seem aggressive in patrol which could be better safety or too many issues around campus', 'I want to learn gold panning. this school is the best choice', 'My husband and I just met a couple who attends your school they had a blowout to the lake we never exchanged names but we want to say we hope they got home safely and to  get back to school safely this week. You produce smart kids we hope we cross paths with these smart kids  again.']

name: Colorado State University-Fort Collins
reviews:
['⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Worth Every Mile – Exceptional Care from Dr. Zacharie Wund, Alexa Wing, and the CSU Veterinary Teaching Hospital

We live in Utah and made the drive all the way to Colorado so our dog could be seen at the Colorado State University Veterinary Teaching Hospital — and it was absolutely the best decision we could have made.

After being quoted nearly $18,000 by MedVet in Salt Lake City (SLC) for an interhepatic liver shunt surgery, we decided to seek a second opinion. From the very first call, the compassion and professionalism from Dr. Zacharie Wund and student Alexa Wing stood out. They took the time to explain our dog’s diagnosis, the surgical options, and what to expect each step of the way. Their honesty, patience, and genuine care immediately gave us confidence that our pup was in the best hands possible.

When we arrived at CSU, we were greeted with warmth and understanding. Dr. Wund’s calm, confident manner and surgical expertise were truly remarkable. The surgery was a complete success, and our dog is now thriving — happy, healthy, and full of life again.

Alexa Wing deserves special recognition. She went above and beyond in every way — updating us daily, answering every question with kindness and detail, and making us feel supported throughout this emotional journey. Her compassion and professionalism are exceptional, and it’s clear she has a very bright future ahead in veterinary medicine.

What amazed us most was that our total cost at CSU was less than one-third of what MedVet quoted — yet the care, communication, and outcome were in a completely different league.

Driving from Utah to Colorado was absolutely worth it. If your pet is facing a complex diagnosis or you want care from people who truly treat your animal like family, go to CSU. They combine world-class veterinary expertise with genuine heart.

Thank you, Dr. Zacharie Wund, Alexa Wing, and the entire CSU Veterinary Teaching Hospital team, for giving our dog a second chance at life — and giving us hope when we thought we had none. 💜🐾', "Colorado State University in Fort Collins, Colorado is a beautiful campus. The Rocky mountains have the backdrop and Northern Colorado weather, getting any better?

Great football stadium. We're going to CSU Rams games.

Even if you're not going to school here, it's a beautiful campus to walk around on.

Lots of trees on campus so that you can take a break in the shade as well as benches, tables, etc.", 'I graduated in Food Science at Colorado State in 2011.  The education in the classroom and in life that I received while I attended university was life changing.  I met some of the best people I have had in my life and I pursued my love for nutrition and food science while I was there.  My degree opened up many doors for me in my career in the brewing industry and at the time the undergrad brewing course was one of the only ones in the country.  I am so glad I attended CSU and I can say without a doubt my life and career would not be the same had I not gone here.  I am still a season ticket holder and while I miss the old stadium, having a beautiful new stadium on campus is pretty nice!  Go Rams!', 'My daughter and I visited the campus as it currently ranks number 3 for Veterinary Medicine.

The staff was genuine, sincere and gracious.  They setup one on one meetings to make the visit extremely personal.

They appeared to have the students best interest at heart and even supplied a full day parking pass.

The facilities appeared updated and state of the art.  They were heads and shoulders above our visit at Texas aTm.

The only prevention of a five star rating was partially our fault as we were unable to get a tour of the school of medicine.', "Honestly, although I rarely write a bad review, I feel like I should in this case to warn/inform other families who are spending their money at CSU. My daughter chose to attend CSU for a variety of reasons. She graduated with the highest GPA in the history of her HS, so she's no slouch. She is pursuing pre-med and/or engineering.

Her professors so far have been very poor. They don't prepare the students for the exams. My daughter has taken numerous practice exams, skipped many social activities to study, and has sought extra help to prepare for the exam. She sits down to take it and information on the exam wasn't in the lecture or the reading. As an educator for 30 years, this is EXTREMELY poor pedagogy.

And, so far, her professors regularly use profanity and act unprofessional in other ways. We will seriously consider whether CSU is the right fit for her going forward. We are very disappointed so far. Parents and prospective students: be warned, be aware.

CSU, you can do better."]

name: Colorado Technical University-Colorado Springs
reviews: ["I love this school. I had actually attended 3 other schools both in person and online before finding this one. I am currently a two time Alumni currently working on my Masters degree! I got both my Associates and Bachelors here. I honestly don't know how anyone can have a bad experience with this school. I have had some professors that were less favorable than others, but then some were just amazing. The Live Chats give me anxiety so I usually only view the archives. This school has been perfect for me with work and kids and adhd and pets. lol I will always recommend and always come back.", "I graduated CTU in 2023 with a 4.0. I would have to give this University 2 stars simply because even though I was able to graduate with a 4.0, I have not been able to land a career using my degree. I have a Bachelor's in Business Administration with a focus on Finance. I have applied to thousands of positions with no luck. You would think that even with a small unknown college that I would have had some luck, but nobody is willing to give me a chance. I can only assume that this is because CTU must not be as well known as the let on or companies have known that you get a subpar education while you are there. I am a very intelligent person but I thought that these classes were a little easy, which is probably why I was able to get a 4.0. I would not go here if I was you. Pick a well known University. Might as well, you will still be paying just as much for your education and someone might actually hire you when you are finished.", 'CTU really has some work to do. I began furthering education with them, just for them to tell me they cannot verify my high school education and will not allow me to continue my education. Why would you allow a student to start, when you don’t have everything needed? I called the registrars office and informed them my school has been permanently closed  and has not replied to my request for my transcripts. I’ve reached out to my state department of education and they provided me contact information to retrieve my transcripts. I have yet to get a response. They literally have an office to find this information, yet, I’m still stuck doing the work. How do you hold a student responsible for something that’s out of their control? I despise ever applying for this school', 'I had an awesome experience!!! It was well organized and the CTU staff was so supportive and friendly. I felt so loved and they made me feel so good about my accomplishments!! I really appreciate CTU for an amazing experience!!!', "I love this school. It's straight to the point: doing and learning. I greatly appreciate that it doesn't have distractions like Greek Life or smoothie bars. It's humble, simple and effective. Thank you, CTU."]

name: Community College of Aurora
reviews: ["This school may not be glamorous, but it's strong. I've gone far in life now, and I can atribute all of my success to the environment, the dedication of the instructors, and the quality of the courses. The admin team is there for you too! This whole school just wants to see you become the best version of yourself possible, and they work incredibly hard to see that happen. You won't regret attending CCA, and if you put in the work this school will launch you into a terrific future!", 'I have taken prerequisites at a few community colleges around the Denver metro and CCA is the worst. I have run into many issues including needing to pay for and take 19.5 more credits at CCA even though my prerequisites are finished, being told by the financial aid office that I wasn’t getting any aid and to take out student loans, and then a month later I DID end up getting financial aid, as well as being dropped from two classes in two different semesters for being one day late on starting a payment plan due to not getting paid until Friday. (Payment plan was due by Thursday) they would not let me back into these classes once kicked out!  This has pushed my “plan” to finish these stupid extra credits back two semesters! I work full time, am struggling to pay for my respiratory therapy program, clinicals, as well as these “necessary” cca classes, and don’t have anyone to ask to cover me until I can reimburse. This has been such a burden financially and on my mental health. I’m doing all I can to improve my life and it just feels like this school could not care less about their students, they just want their money. Look at other schools/programs and only come here as a last resort!', "It has been a pleasure to attend Community College of Aurora as I have pursued additional coursework to enhance my degrees. The staff personnel has been supportive throughout the entire process, making the experience seamless and positive. For example, the staff members managing the cashier's office, advising, registration, and front desk. I am grateful for the high-quality instruction combined with the opportunity to refine my academic qualifications in such a welcoming and professional environment.", 'Awesome new building. Still in progress but has everything first responder training needs. Simulated amublance, all BLS and ALS training tools you can think of.', "Everything outside of their science department is great.
