name: Community College of Denver
reviews:
["I wouldn't recommend online courses as professors and Sparc are a complete joke! The professor I am referring to is named Carolina Gonzalez-Berrios and the Sparc supervisor of the biology depart is Fleur Bond. Now I must say as I sit here it is starting to feel more race targeted with the lack of investigating the Sparc supervisor did. I suffered a loss of a stepson in November 2025 and wasn’t made reasonable accommodation in regard to exam. I had already completed more than half the assignments before the time they were expected. However, I was given 30% and that didn’t add up to the work submitted before deadlines due to some technical issues I struggled with the exams which there were only 2 of them. I also missed maybe 2 labs however again more than half assignments were completed and turned in before DEADLINES. The Sparc supervisor just sided with the professor but lacked any reasons for my grade being so low as the work submitted doesn’t add up to the grade received and they both really added to the heartache I was and still am suffering from losing my stepson. Ultimately both failed in aiding me in anyway and the excuses given are unreasonable, especially due to the fact my other teacher made the reasonable accommodations even giving me more time to study for exams after the loss of my stepchild. They felt I assuming during my 2 weeks off I was studying for the exam instead of planning a funeral and grieving while travel back and forth from New Mexico to Colorado as the funeral was in New Mexico! At this point I have moved forward with the knowledge of these 2 individuals being quite shitty and that’s my nice description of them. I am hoping the color of my skin didn’t play a role in such a decision to not investigate and not give me the grade I deserved but we will never know!! However, I 100% recommend the in person classes as the teachers or more understanding when they can see you and you have more direct access to them versus the online mess and nonsense. I hope this is helpful and gives an insight to the whole online and Sparc nonsense. Also the Sparc supervisor ignored me until I had Tina Garcia reach out to her in which she was really passive once she reached out. Tina Garcia is a saint though she did her part and more.", 'The most ongoing, worst experience I’ve had with the college, There have been multiple instances of the employees and teachers flat out, not helping any students, including myself with anything whether it be financial aid, parking citations or anything of the matter that involves money! Transferring financial aid from MSU to CCD was a complete nightmare as nobody on either side had any idea what they were doing, They needed three people on one computer just to figure out how to transfer money from one account to another! And I haven’t even brushed upon how awful the professors are when it comes to any student aid, I had an English 101 professor who quit not even after one semester because it Because it was “too much” not to mention that she would end classes super early, almost an hour early And would sometimes Even cancel classes is very often because “not many people were there” And she “didn’t see a reason to teach a small class if everyone wasn’t gonna pick up on it the day after“. Not to mention the fraudulent activity that’s been going on in the parking administrative offices, They tried doubling my parking ticket on two different days Claiming that I parked in the seventh Street garage without paying, but most of my classes are on the Cherry Creek building So I don’t know why I would be in the seventh Street garage?? And for one of my parking tickets that was dismissed, they put it as upheld on the Auraria campus even though it was dismissed! I don’t know what kind of fraudulent activities have been going on over there for who knows how long but I’m getting sick of it', 'DO NOT GO TO SCHOOL HERE OR SEND YOUR CHILDREN TO SCHOOL HERE! I am in an unnecessarily stressful situation because no one I have contacted at this institution has taken any accountability for their mistakes. You do not want to attend a school that allows students to be ignored instead or being helped by people simply doing their jobs correctly. Aside from 3 fantastic professors in the paralegal department, this entire situation from start to finish has been a nightmare. Their financial aid office and cashier's office "DO NOT COMMUNICATE" in any way about tuition payments or aid received. That is absolutely insane. I have earned a BA and an MA and GradCert, and I have never experienced a school that allows their programs to run the way this one does. It's chaotic and not a place to invest in your education.', 'I began CCD with genuine excitement and passion for art and design. I wanted to learn, grow, and be part of a creative community. Instead, I experienced a culture filled with favoritism, retaliation, and discrimination.
At CCD, if one professor dislikes you, others seem to follow. I was treated unfairly simply for speaking up and staying true to myself. One professor wrongly accused me of turning on the classroom lights when it was actually another student she favored—and she said nothing to him. Later, she remade my artwork and asked whose was better, turning what should have been a supportive classroom into a competition.
Another professor made inappropriate gestures and used to wink at me. When I didn’t respond to his advances, his attitude completely changed. A different instructor mocked my Catholic faith and openly talked about performing rituals with other faculty members, which made the environment feel spiritually and emotionally unsafe.
When I reported these behaviors, I was treated as the problem instead of the victim. The administration protected their colleagues instead of helping students. I was forced to redo projects I had already completed just to earn the grades I deserved, while others received leniency.
The mistreatment even extended beyond the classroom. The advisor, Lynne, treated me poorly when I expressed interest in taking another class after graduation. She questioned how I would pay for it, even though financial matters weren’t part of her job. Her tone and attitude made it clear that jealousy and bias influenced how some staff treated students with scholarships or ambition.
I wanted to go back to school so badly, but the way I was treated made it impossible. Now, a year later, I’m happy to finally write this review. I’ve found peace in moving forward and no longer carrying fear or self-doubt from that experience.
Despite everything, I graduated. It wasn’t easy—I left that school shaken—but I also left stronger, wiser, and proud that I never gave up. I learned that standing for truth can make people uncomfortable, but it’s always better to walk away with integrity than stay silent in a corrupt environment. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS SCHOOL BUT IF YOU END UP COMING HERE…
To future students: document everything, stay grounded in your values, and never let anyone intimidate you into silence. When you stay true to yourself, no one can take your light or your power away.', 'Randomly disables my whole account for no reason. States I need to prove my identity after attending school for over a year and literally being employed as a work study for the school. Extreme inconvenience as I dont go to main campus and none of my courses are there yet im forced to show up in person to prove im real.']

name: University of Denver
reviews:
["As a proud University of Denver alum, I am thrilled to share how incredible this campus is. The blend of historic charm and modern facilities creates an inspiring atmosphere, surrounded by lush green spaces and breathtaking views of the Rockies. It’s more than just a place to study—it’s a place to grow and create lasting memories. Whether you're a prospective student or simply visiting, DU’s vibrant and picturesque campus is sure to captivate your heart!", 'One of the most prominent and premier institutes for higher education in Denver area. DU is known for law, business and humanities programs across usa. The campus is comparatively small but very nice and well maintained. I love going to the campus. Will highly recommend a visit', 'The University of Denver recommended an online class through a third party to obtain a certificate in cyber security and ethical hacking. It’s called Partners to Success. The 100 hour course provides a certificate, with resume writing but no job hunting assistance. We signed my son up for this course, and this is what happened.
After speaking to the registration person in charge, since their employees work from home in different locations across the country, and discussing the fees, when I called to make a payment they said the fees increased from 2850.00 to 3470.00, and have been in affect for several months. Since it’s an ongoing program one can register any time. It took two weeks to begin because my son couldn’t log in since they had entered the wrong country code. Then another week to start because they had entered the wrong phone number. The labs with the videos were not accessible because of their glitches, and the professor never answered my son’s email after several attempts, to which the administrator stepped in to help with google face time. After the second video, the complicated homework instructions were over several pages and you can’t go back to look at them, only shutting down the screen and rebooting the lab instructions and taking photos on your phone was the answer. There were no simulations or examples to complete the homework. After more calls and emails we were told to use two screens and
Open the e book but the ebook was
Nowhere to be found. After more emails we were directed to another administrator who never answered her phone, voicemails or emails. I was instructed to reply to ‘all’ so everyone could know what was going on. Each lab is timed, and if you need more time, you must request it and another week goes by. The entire course must be finished within four months plus if one needs to retake a timed text, that’s another $400.00.
You waste a lot of time requesting help, nobody answers including the professors, whom they guarantee a response within 48 hours. The website is confusing, complicated and shuts down by early evening so it’s inaccessible. They offer a full refund within the first 30 days but good luck with that. They send you to the administrator’s refund department that does not answer their voicemails or emails. There is literally nobody to talk to. Yes the one human I did speak with was friendly but with this program being spread out all over the United States and possibly abroad, it’s a dysfunctional organization that is both frustrating and expensive. There are many alternatives online and if you do pay 3470.00 and want a refund good luck. I’m waiting for visa to resolve this. For that price you could hire a private tutor or the class should have a professor available 8-5 Monday through Friday. They might change the name of this online class through a third party. Right now it’s called Partners for Success. Be careful with this program. It’s not worth it.', "It has a beautiful campus and many parks around it. Good for dogs walks and socializing with social distancing. It's well maintained. Academically, I haven't studied at DU, so not much aware of programs they offer, but heard from many that it's one of top school for law.", "I believe that it is fundamental that a person speaks not merely by word but performs their acts by deed. The Josef Korbel School and the broader University of Denver campus should be embarrassed by its inaction and ineptitude in regards to the situation in which I find myself. As a campus that preaches “Prepare for Purpose,” I have faced prejudice and outright oppression. I would like to think that such an institution would fight for the rights of a former student who has had his human rights violated as defined by United Nations international human rights law.

The Nelson Mandela rules were violated by the Jefferson County Sheriff's Jail against me. Further, the Nelson Mandela rules were adopted as state law in Colorado in 2017. This violation of human rights law against me is indisputable and I have extensive and ample evidence to prove the culpability of the law enforcement officers involved.

Law enforcement misconduct against me has escalated to the point of having an officer within the Denver Police District 1 Station threaten false arrest against me for attempting to report her for a crime. This occurred within the station which is heavily recorded as well as having personal video footage of the incident. Such an act by an officer of the law is a violation of the Fourth Amendment of the United States Federal Constitution.

I have appealed to the university in regards to my situation but they have been unresponsive at best. I have experienced complacency, dishonesty, and outright criminal activity by law enforcement throughout this process. The judiciary, which allowed the torture to occur while I was under its supervision and openly protesting during its occurrence, has also chosen inaction up to this point.

These champions of social change and progress are nothing more than cloistered hypocrites who have allowed these offenses to occur in their own back yards. Law enforcement has openly and willfully broken the law against me several times but the university and its staff have not utilized their resources to assist or defend me against this instance of State tyranny.

*To note: I have also filed formal complaints at the local, state, and federal level. As the violation is defined as a crime against humanity by UN international human rights law I have also filed complaint with the International Criminal Court."]

name: Metropolitan State University of Denver
reviews:
['If you’re planning on going to MSU Denver, here’s what to expect (and what not to).

What not to expect: cheap parking, great food, or an “awesome” campus atmosphere. The vibe isn’t tight-knit it’s basically like a community college branded as a university. Also, brace yourself for some freezing days because it’s Colorado, after all. And if you’re hoping for exciting city life right outside campus, the clubs and bars nearby are honestly pretty mid.

What to expect: A nice, clean campus that feels safe overall. It’s one of the most affordable universities in the area, and the professors here genuinely want you to succeed. You’ll find great resources, friendly staff, and if you put yourself out there, some really good friends.

MSU Denver might not have the “traditional college” feel, but it’s a solid, down-to-earth place to learn and grow especially if you’re motivated and make the most of what’s here.

MSU Denver shares its campus with CU Denver and CCD, which honestly kind of sucks sometimes. It makes the place feel a bit disconnected — like three separate schools just coexisting instead of one strong community. Still, I genuinely think MSU has the potential to become Colorado’s coolest school if they invested more in building a better campus atmosphere and stronger student life (i.e dorms, events, greek life, food, etc) The programs and professors are already great (IMO), it just needs that extra spark to make people want to hang around and be part of it.

PS: Red White and Blue is not it please change the colors😭', 'I came to MSU Denver hoping for support. Because of my underprivileged background, I was upfront about my situation and asked for extra resources. Instead of encouragement, the program director told me I would need to change my educational goals and that my background would never allow me to succeed in her program.

Those words could have ended my academic journey. Instead, they pushed me toward a university next door that welcomed me, supported me, and believed in me. I graduated with honors and walked with distinction — in the very field MSU Denver said I had no place in.

It is heartbreaking that students who are already navigating difficult circumstances are turned away here rather than lifted up. Every staff interaction I have had has left me feeling dismissed and devalued. I hope no one else is made to feel the way I was. #NotABrickInTheWall', "You know, eight years ago, it was a completely different University. The faculty the staff and the resources had so much more structure to them. Fast forward present day.It's a garbage university, not a reflection upon the professors.The professors are excellent. Far more helpful than any resources they can hope to provide on campus. I dropped out of the honors program due to being mistreated by female faculty members. I reached out for counseling support and they failed me for the last two years. I'm now one year out from getting my undergraduate in psychology, and I can honestly tell you that the professors have been more help than any of the resources provided.

The student body is full of kids who absolutely have no life experience.Other than criticizing putting down, and prejudging people based off of nothing that they have any life experience on. I'd highly recommend go to a different state or avoid this university entirely. It's a joke.

The cops don't do their jobs either, and all they have is nothing but discrimination, harassment, and ridicule. They don't even come talk to the student body when they have questions. For the last two days, there's been a cop that follows me in the morning, just before one of the buildings open, and he doesn't get out to come talk to me or check on me or see how i'm doing.He just sits in his car and stares at me for more than ten minutes, which is harassment because it's a tension.I never asked for and I never wanted. As I said before, highly recommend not coming to MSU Denver.", "Worst tuition in the state. Over charges with junk fees and forces you to pay for their medical insurance, they lies about payment plans. If you set up a payment plan they'll make you pay down your tuition under 20% of the balance if you want to schedule classes, that is not a payment plan. What a scam. If you have another opportunity to attend a different school you should go there. I would not recommend this place. Turn around and run away from this place!!! Horrible administration practices!", 'update to recent response: rowdy’s corner has been nearly impossible to get food from this semester due to increasing student demand so this being the sole active solution is still an incredibly disappointing response from a university. from the school survey that was issued about a week and some change ago , there were updates on there being a request to send proof of snap benefits to receive a 50 dollar gift card ⚰️ and  then silence. this is absolutely repulsive.

this school is an absolute joke. there have been weeks of public announcements about SNAP benefits being defunded for students, and instead of preparing in advance to support the many students ya’ll know rely on them because there are papers everywhere on campus with instructions and assistance for getting students to apply…the school’s big solution is a three-question “survey” to brainstorm “creative ideas.”
it’s very much giving we have concepts of thoughts and prayers for ya’ll. ☠️

food stamps are set to be cut tomorrow, and this is the level of preparedness they have for their own students who keep this place running with their overpriced tuition for what the actual experience is here.

it’s beyond disappointing. this institution somehow has the funding to open a brand new campus restaurant and pursue multiple expansion projects but when it comes to actual student welfare? suddenly there’s no plan, no urgency, and no accountability. the priorities couldn’t be any clearer: appearances over the students they claim
to care “so much” about.']

name: Morgan Community College
reviews:
['Very helpful staff and teachers. If you have a problem, it’s going to be solved quickly and efficiently.', 'I signed up for GED classes and I felt the whole sign up process was messed up. I didn't hear back from her most of the time. I asked if I needed materials or books and never got a response.
I tried to sign up to just take the exams and pay for them myself through MCC limon, but they told me no I couldn't do that. I had to go through Fort Morgan.
The day of class (virtual) I didn't receive any kind of contact, then after the class I was sent an online calculator, to which I responded "never got zoom link"
The next day I was invited to class. The entire class was spent on helping 1 girl with her understanding of a math problem and felt like I was listening in to a tutoring session. That's how most of them went.
Everything was YouTube videos on how to do the problems, which I can look up myself.
When my children got covid and I informed them I wouldn't be in class I received a few emails questioning MY dedication.
Then, halfway through classes a book is mentioned. Funny I was never told about that and then even later I was asked about my study guide, again, something I never received.
I was told numerous times upon registration that I would be able to test in Limon, where I live, and then later I was told I had to go to fort Morgan. (This would require numerous day trips which I couldn't do). Yet, in class another person from Limon was told her could test here, so idk why I was told I had to go there...
My final straw was when I got on for class 5 mins early and the teacher and registration lady were discussing how I would most likely fail the test. I was livid and hurt. If I'm not doing well in class, thats on the teacher. I didn't learn 1 single thing through those classes and I'm extremely irritated by the whole experience.', 'A beautiful community college facility with awesome staff and welcoming folks.  MCC brings countless benefits to the area in many facets of local educational needs', 'This community college is a big asset for the local area. As with most community colleges, degree options are limited. A very friendly and student-focused staff.', 'This is a city county community college excellent facility we rented a room for the day at $130 large room for a political meeting excellent facilities excellent it']

name: Naropa University
reviews:
["UPDATE: I emailed three offices at Naropa because their Google account told me to reach out.  No response.  My 1 star review stands (with 3000 views, I just saw).  Do yourself a favor and just read some good spiritual books, pray, serve the poor, and meditate as you see fit.  Save yourself the ten to twenty grand.

One of my biggest regrets of my 20s.
I stopped going for a year because going online was driving me insane.

No one checked in on me and I'm 10s of thousands of dollars in debt from a place that:
1. Pretends like you're part of a community that loves you but clearly doesn't actually care
2. Doesn't really take education seriously
3. Puts pictures of their god all over the place--he assaulted women and they doublethink by supporting #MeToo

You can find out anything they're teaching you by yourself.  They introduced me to a few good books and I liked my Sufism class, but other than that, the Kabbalah guy will force you to read his personal books in class and then hawk his extra spiritual classes for classes that are at least cheaper than going to Naropa.", "I attended Naropa for two semesters to pursue a Psychology degree. The teachers and courses were unique, thought-provoking and wonderful to work with. However, you'll be paying a VERY high price for those qualities.

I enrolled in Naropa because of the scholarship they offered me and because of what I had heard about their programs. However, I came to find out (a week before my first semester ended) that a student will not be eligible for any scholarships without a cleared FAFSA form.

The Finance department is awful. They don't communicate well and don't set students up to succeed.
I attended most of my summer 2024 semester (thinking that financial aid worked out & scholarships were applied) just to find out (a week before the semester ended) that no financial aid was applied (therefore no scholarships can be applied) despite me reaching out on this several times throughout the semester.

I tried to work with the Finance department but couldn't meet their requirements for paying off the balance. If you cannot pay off the balance immediately or commit to a very aggressive payment plan ($1500+ a month), Naropa immediately sends the balance to collections. I did their online program for two semester and received a collections bill for $19,093.75.

For a school that's meant to be so big on mindfulness/balance/humanity, their Finance Department is severely lacking and put me in a very bad spot financially. This is an incredibly expensive school when you can source most of the knowledge you'll learn through their recommended books.

If you choose to attend this school, I highly recommend being very proactive about making sure that financial aid goes through before you commit to any classes for the semester.", 'I hope they get shut down. Sky high tuition, unprofessional faculty, lacking CACREP accreditation.', "Setting aside the fact I met my wife there, which was outside Naropa's purview, I could not be happier with my Naropa education.  During my 20+ year clinical career since earning my Master's degree there, I have been struck by how well trained I was.  I am much more comfortable doing group therapy and sitting with individuals suffering from extreme states of mind than many of my colleagues, even those who have been doing the work as long or longer than me.  That is because of my training at Naropa.  Also, my personal growth journey there was hard to beat, on top of the excellent clinical training.  If I had gone to Naropa ONLY to grow as a person, I'd be happy with the experience.  Same is true if I'd gone ONLY to become a therapist.  The fact that I was 100% happy with BOTH elements leads to a five star review and a very happy life both personally and professionally.  And yes I had to take on loans; and yes as with all private schools it's not cheap; and yes their endowment does not allow for much financial aid.  But you know what?  I know from having been on the STAFF after I graduated, no one is getting rich at Naropa.  It costs a lot to run a private school, especially in Boulder.  So I have no issue with it and I recommend Naropa highly.", "I earned my undergraduate degree from Naropa University in the late 90's in Religious Studies and Writing and Poetics. Both students and faculty were passionate about the programs offered and this created a lively atmosphere for learning. When the program was over it seemed to have come too quickly, the sign of a good experience. Years later, I feel that Naropa's contemplative bent has enabled me to continually feel enriched by whatever life brings me next. Studying there instilled within me a deep sense that it's not what happens but how you meet what happens that matters most."]

name: Northeastern Junior College
reviews: ['Both our boys played summer basketball leagues here in this facility. We enjoyed it and the upstairs walking track is a bonus. Lots of good memories here. I have to stop and reminisce when I’m in town on showings.', 'Friendly area. Very clean. And the cafeteria food is the best!', 'I really enjoyed my time here at NJC beginning to take my classes after high school.  Made friends, started my journey to higher levels of education.  Yet, my college algebra professor was interesting....  toward midsemester all the males were out of the class (either dropped or withdrew) due to immediately lowering or terrible grades. Other female friends who attended the class said they experienced the same thing in other semesters, and often the professor would invite them to have "discussions" and he would introduce them to his son and it was obvious he was trying to set them up with them.\n\nOther than that. name: University of Northern Colorado
reviews: ['I thought it was a great school until I went to DU for my Master\'s program. I should have went there for my undergrad too. I regret my choice of ever going to UNC. The professors do not get back to you for reference letters which is a bummer when you think that you got along so well with them and you just get ghosted. They also do not prepare you at all for the "real world". Career services is literally laughable. They just give you the handshake resource which is a horrible way to find a job. Do better UNC.', 'Maybe one of the best studios I saw in Denver. The instruments are almost brand new, Steinway piano… Focal monitors & also the gear they use to teach music production are new stuff too.', 'Expect to pay about $2000 in fees in addition to tuition and books. Maybe even more if you are a first time student or transfer student. Three of the fees recieved were all for the same exact thing but just added three times. Very frustrating to get an education without going into crippling debt.', 'Love this place. My daughter feels at home while in school here', "I went to school at UNC. It's a good school! name: Pikes Peak State College
reviews:
['I attended Pikes Peak Community College from 2019 to 2021, and my experience was very mixed. My first semester was especially painful. I lost my grandmother and had to travel out of state for her funeral. When I returned, my English Composition I professor told me that I “shouldn’t have gone” and that it would’ve been better for me to stay and attend class instead of being with my family. Hearing that after losing someone so important to me was devastating. It became extremely hard to even walk back into her classroom.I couldn’t withdraw because the deadline had already passed, so I stayed and ultimately failed the class. The environment felt discouraging, and I noticed she seemed more invested in the male students than the female students, which made the class even harder to be in.I eventually retook English Composition I with a different professor, and the difference was night and day. I went from failing with an F to earning a B+, and I finally felt supported and understood. That experience showed me how much a compassionate, fair professor can impact a student’s confidence and success.I also want to highlight that my Communication professor was one of the best instructors I’ve ever had. I loved that entire class. The environment was positive, engaging, and respectful, and it reminded me that good faculty truly do make a difference. Outside of the classroom, the library and tutoring center were wonderful. The staff there were kind, patient, and genuinely invested in helping students succeed.However, when COVID‑19 hit, everything shifted online in the middle of the semester. Despite losing access to in‑person resources, facilities, and the campus experience we were paying for, the school continued charging the same tuition and fees. I felt the situation was handled poorly, and that students should have received some form of tuition adjustment or support during such a major disruption.Ultimately, the combination of insensitive faculty experiences, inconsistent support, and the way the COVID transition was handled led me to leave Pikes Peak. While there were a few bright spots—especially my Communication class and the tutoring center—my overall experience was not positive. Based on what I went through, I cannot fully recommend Pikes Peak Community College.', "Seriously the most worthless college. The staff is far from helpful and has no follow through. I've reached out to Balinda numberous times with no contact back, I wasted over an hour with her just on passwords. You'll have better luck nailing water to a tree than getting help from the staff. Getting my transcripts and going somewhere where the staff truly supports students looking to further their education.", 'A joke. You try to talk to people to get enrolled get told to go online instead. Some of us would prefer to talk to people. I finally was able to get a meeting with a real person and was told id be contacted for classes and never heard from anyone. No calls no emails they enrolled me to the school but never got my classes. Now the courses i needed are full thanks for nothing useless staff. Ill make sure i continue to talk down about this place and recommend people look else where', "I've been going to this school for two years now and I will admit I haven't been the greatest student but I still kept trying to keep my head high and continue with my education. But it's gotten to the point that registering for classes is a major pain in the butt and a major source of anxiety for me. Everytime I've tried to register for classes each semester I'm met with a different problem one after another that I've had to constantly make an appointment with advisors who struggled at their job just to go to a school that charges 2,000$ for only two classes", 'If you’re expecting an insanely high quality university, look elsewhere. Although, I feel PPSC outweighs other local options.

Affordable, Military Friendly.  ☑️
Recently changed from community to state. ☑️
Helpful staff members (sometimes long-winded, but it gets done). ☑️
Ample variety of courses. ☑️']

name: Pueblo Community College
reviews:
['I attended Pueblo Community College for about one to two years (2021-2023) pursuing an Associate of Applied Science in Behavioral Health with an Addiction Recovery emphasis. My goal was to use this degree to enter PCC’s Medical Sonography program, which is the only program in Colorado that allows students to use financial aid for sonography. Unfortunately, my experience at PCC was extremely disappointing and emotionally draining.The Behavioral Health/Addiction Counseling program was especially difficult because there was only one professor teaching all of the addiction counseling courses. These courses were often one‑credit, two‑week classes, or required being on campus for up to three full days from 8 AM to 5 PM. This was nearly impossible to manage while working full‑time and commuting from Colorado Springs, yet the professor offered no flexibility or support.I completed around eight courses with this professor, and she failed me in the majority of them. Even when I communicated my circumstances—such as my mother battling breast cancer—my requests for reasonable extensions were denied.The final course I took with her was the most unprofessional experience I’ve ever had in higher education. She changed the scheduled in‑person class to a Zoom meeting only a week before, then sent out a poll to reschedule the date due to personal issues. The new date was one I was not available for, but I still rearranged my life to attend. During the Zoom session, she required cameras to be on even if students were driving. When I turned my camera on and muted myself for safety, she removed me from the meeting. I emailed her repeatedly asking to be let back in—she said she would, but never did. I had already completed all coursework and only needed the final approval from that Zoom session to pass. She failed me anyway.When I contacted the school to report what happened, I was told I “shouldn’t have been in that class” because of missing prerequisites—despite the fact that I was already enrolled, attending, and completing the work. The entire situation felt disorganized and dismissive.On top of that, my academic advisor assured me that the Behavioral Health degree would qualify me for the Medical Sonography program. After completing nearly half of the degree, I spoke directly with the program director, who told me it would not qualify me. I was devastated. I had spent years working toward a dream I’d had since I was 15, only to be told the degree path my advisor recommended would not get me there. The alternatives they suggested—such as a Medical Assistant degree—made no sense, especially since you don’t even need a degree to become a medical assistant.I also experienced moments where the program felt inconsistent and poorly managed. For example, one required three‑day in‑person course was suddenly shortened to one day “just because,” and I had to attend despite being in severe pain from endometriosis. Missing that day would have resulted in an automatic failure. No student should be put in that position.Overall, my experience at Pueblo Community College was chaotic, unsupportive, and emotionally exhausting. Between the lack of structure, the misinformation from advising, and the discriminatory and inflexible behavior from the addiction counseling professor, I cannot recommend PCC to anyone—especially students who are working, commuting, or trying to pursue a healthcare pathway.', 'Ahh the allure of online classes, the ultimate in convenience.  The freedom to complete course content when it fits into your busy schedule.  Just be aware, the college upcharges for this.  You can see it in their tuition chart.

BUT what they don’t disclose, written in any of their web pages, or verbally with your advisors, instructors, department chairs and literally any staff member you might bump into, is that if you are taking courses that require third-party assignment and test proctoring (this includes any course in the health sciences) you will essentially need fiber optic internet service to use the proctoring service.

Happy with your high-speed DSL service that has always been there for you?  Well NOT good enough for PCC’s third party proctoring service.

The other thing an unsuspecting student learns is that if EVERYTHING isn’t just right with your computer, the required web browser and extensions, and if you don’t access this third party proctor in JUST THE EXACT RIGHT WAY, none of the stuff will work for you.  NONE OF IT.

Oh sure, PCC has 24-7 tech support and the proctoring outfit has a customer support email and phone number, but good luck with all that.  Your level of ‘help/support’ is literally dependent on who is on the other side of the line at the moment (IF anyone is actually there).

I would rather walk 100 miles on broken glass and tetanus inducing rusty nails, than deal with this abomination of a proctoring outfit.  You would be better off jumping from the highest Colorado 14teener and landing on a bed of metal spikes, covered in the most potent, concentrated neurotoxin, submerged in hydrochloric acid, filled with electric eels, sharks, and the most viscous piranhas known to man, than have to deal with all the headaches associated with  the PCC third party online assignment and test proctoring outfit.', 'The school itself is great! However the dental hygiene program is a JOKE. Poorly run and designed for failure. I graduated and love my career but would never wish the hazing and trauma I received during the 2 year program on anyone. Now that a program has opened up in the Spring.. Choose wisely.', 'I will give 3 stars because the Fremont campus was phenomenal and I got my general studies from there. That being said I was in the dental hygiene program at the Pueblo campus  and it was highly abusive. I can account for multiple instances where my hand was slapped, dental instruments were thrown at me, and not to mention the favoritism and belittling from instructors. Unless you’re a favorite, you will not graduate from the program and money and time will be wasted. If you plan on going to dental hygiene school, please consider another institution.', 'Both myself and my daughter are graduates of PCC. Just read the College and Foundation Community report for 2025, so many exciting advances to meet our community and national work force needs for generations to come!! I was so grateful for the impact of PCC in our family achievements.
Thank you for your continued expansion of meeting the educational needs of our future!
Darlene']

name: Red Rocks Community College
reviews:
["I've never been a student or staffer at RRCC, but I'm an art lover and I've been visiting the campus for many years to take in the Art Department's periodic exhibitions.

These were originally presented on the basement walls surrounding the Department's classrooms and offices, but more recently a formal art gallery has been created in the spaces surrounding the Community Room. This is immediately to your right as you go in the main entrance to the College.

The new gallery is quite nice. There's a long, rectangular space and also a rotunda-like area immediately outside the Community Room. Be sure you go through the double doors at the rear of the front gallery to get into the second space. The gallery is open during all campus hours. Occasionally the rear doors are locked, but if you call Campus Security, they will be happy to let you in.

The gallery presents student work, but also shows featuring the Lakewood community interspersed with material of regional and sometimes greater significance. It's a bit of a drive for me, but the campus is pretty and a visit to the gallery makes for a relaxing afternoon.", 'Red Rocks community college offers poor communication. I struggled with adding and dropping classes to the point where I could not get anyone to help me with adding or dropping classes. Therefore, I dropped my classes. I then was sent to collections with no communication from the school that money was even owed. Then when filing my taxes when my tax returns came back, the returns were returned to Red Rocks community college. I then reached out to the school to let them know that this should’ve not happened because I did not take any classes at the school. Because of the lack of help I received from the school, they were able to take my money. I am able to put in a appeal to see if they will grant me to takeoff what I owe them. But I will not be receiving the money that they took in the first place back. I would advise anyone who intends to go to Red Rocks community college to avoid going here for the poor lack of communication and the money that they will take from you because of the lack of communication. There are much better schools within the community that will help communicate and help you to understand and get the education that you Deserve.', 'Professors are usually incredible but the way the records office treats students is absolutely unacceptable. It took a full year for them to begin processing my transcripts (despite submitting them in person WITH a member of records) and the people working in the records office were unimaginably rude. I love the classes but would think twice about ever recommending the school for that reason.', 'This school has very poor communication and organization. I recently moved to Colorado and applied to Red Rocks to continue my education. When I was enrolling, I clearly told the admissions staff that I did not yet have a Colorado ID because appointments were booked months out. I was told, “Oh no, you’re fine,” and they went ahead and enrolled me in classes anyway.Throughout the semester, I repeatedly checked with the financial aid office, almost daily, asking if everything was okay. Each time I was told that everything looked fine and that I just needed to wait. Because of this, I paid out of pocket for books and a computer, trusting that my aid and residency status were handled.Halfway through the semester, no one flagged any issues. Then at the end of the semester, I suddenly received a $4,000 bill and was told that I was listed as a non-resident. This was extremely frustrating because if I had been told earlier to bring back my Colorado ID or additional documentation, I would have done so immediately.Even after I provided my Colorado ID, student records refused to correct the issue. Now I’m stuck with a $4,000 balance due to their mistakes, and I can’t even move forward with school because of it.This situation could have been completely avoided with proper communication and accountability. Instead, I was misinformed, reassured incorrectly, and left to deal with the financial consequences. Very disappointing experience.', "While attending this school I was going through some very difficult times and some very challenging transitions. I forget who my sociology teacher was but her name began with an M I want to say her name is Mary if you ever have the opportunity to take her class I strongly encouraged taking her class as she's the one that has completely changed the way I perceive the world and others around me and even just the way that I think and process and function as an adult today. Miss Gina in the first generation department for student support I and forever thankful for you and I forget the other person's name you work with that's unbelievably full of spunk but I am happy to report I am almost graduated with my degree and I really truly hope our paths cross professionally someday! And thank you to Caitlin in the student life department for being my boss when I was a working student and all your patients while I was in a not healthy position in my life you are very patient and very understanding and I really hope that you show other students the same support even if it's just letting them walk away in silence because it is for their safety I fully fully and thankful to have had the support of staff from everyone at this community college I cannot think of a better community college to send my daughter when she is of age to start higher education! 💖"]

name: Regis University
reviews:
['I was a student at Regis for a little over a year. I would talk with fellow students on campus about Jesus Christ and the administration placed me on academic probation. The administration (Dean of Students Erica Ingalls) stated they had no religion and the missions office (Kyle Turner, Tamara Boynton, Kari Kloos) stated that there is no difference between any religions. They want to strong arm students into silence if they do not agree with the universities stance rather than actually exchanging ideas. They state they want to protect their students, but in reality they merely want to induct them into their own beliefs. They even state on their website that Regis is an inter-faith dialogue campus, but my dialogues were interrupted by campus security and then led to formal hearings that burdened my family and other students who testified that I had acted respectfully and their class times were not interrupted. Do not go to Regis if you want to grow in the Christian faith, they will lead you astray or persecute you to no end.', 'The home page on Regis' website says, "Examine your heart, challenge your mind and question the status quo. Join a community ready to aid you on your journey to discovering what you believe in and how you can make a difference in the world," yet, they persecute their own students who share the Gospel on campus. Their mission statement on the About page says they "more just and humane world through transformative education
at the frontiers of faith, reason and culture," but how is it just and humane to go after your own students for sharing the essential truth you were founded upon?

Is Regis still faith-based? And which faith? The Gospel of Jesus Christ ... or secular pluralism and political correctness?

"But if serving the Lord seems undesirable to you, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve ..." [Joshua 24:15]', 'I never attended. I didn’t even apply. They are the most AGGRESSIVE marketers. I inquired about their MSN FNP program and proceeded to get calls at 8AM almost every day! I also got frequent text messages.
Even when I asked to be taken off the call list, I continued to get calls. Even as many as TWICE a day! I would NEVER apply here if this what they think is acceptable behavior.', 'The administration is having disciplinary hearings for my friend, a student there, because he was telling the Gospel to other students. They say they don’t want Muslims to be offended by it.', "I would give Regis a negative star rating if I could.

I attended about 8 years ago and had no issues. I re-enrolled in January and have had nothing but issues. From getting people to return my call for enrolling to now, 7 months later, getting a $2,000 fee because they supposedly mistakenly gave me a scholarship (that they told me I got when I enrolled) and then reversed it causing me to get late fees and have a large balance now that my student loans won't cover. Many classes are disorganized and frustrating.

AFTER I enrolled in CIS they told me they are completely cancelling this degree program because they don't have enough students enrolling.  It's now a mad dash to make sure I'm enrolled in every class because they won't be offering them again. I looked into transferring to CU Denver and they are requiring I send syllabus's for nearly all my Computer courses because they're considered unidentifiable.  I was mixed between going to CU and Regis and apparently I made the wrong choice.

Spend your money at a better school than Regis. They are laying people off like crazy and are such a mess. This is too expensive of a path to be so poorly managed by them. So disappointed in them."]

name: Rocky Mountain College of Art and Design
reviews:
['ANY OTHER COLLEGE WOULD BE BETTER!!!

UPDATE: Since meeting with the Chairman of the Interior Design program things have gotten significantly worse and everything discussed in the meeting appears to be a lie because the instructor has gotten worse and has provided even less feedback and continues to disregard what the Pre-Made Courses require him to do. Instead he messages the class to say that his feedback is not necessary and we should do what we like with the assignment. My BIGGEST concern is why I am paying THOUSANDS for a college to not do their job or provide real instruction to their students. The course information and resources are available, but the courses are so vague that you need the instructor to provide further information so you can meet their specific expecations. Otherwise, you will be given a poor grade sometimes with an explanation of why, but not always.

IT has been a joke, instead of helping with resources available on the websites the first thing they ask is, "did you reach out to your professor?" I'm not really sure how my professor can help me with online library resources so no. I had a couple ok instructors, 1 that was absolutely amazing!!! And then one that made it blantly obvious the instructors only job is to grade assignments. That's it. Not teach the materials just grade assignments and give feedback if they so chose. The interior design program is accredited, but you teach yourself the materials.', 'I attended the online program for 3D Animation & Fine Arts. The classes were awesome. Lots of experimentation with many forms of art. I was more of a traditional 2D animator at first and ended up having a fond liking to 3D animation towards the end of my tenure with the school. However after graduation the school immediately became unhelpful and useless. The exit counsel did nothing to help me find any jobs post graduation. All the licenses for the software programs expired and they offered no help or discount or special programs for alumni. I’ve practically lost all my memory of how to use Maya and Mudbox because the software is far to expensive to get. It’s been nearly a decade since I graduated and I have found no work in the field I went to school for. It has been absolutely miserable and frustrating! I basically wasted my time and racked up $70k in student loans just to work at a basic job. I’m furious and wish I could go back in time and take it all back. You get trained in programs you won’t really find a job in. And as time passes you forget what you were taught. I’m extremely unsatisfied and zero stars is the true rating this school deserves for the neglect it has for it’s alumni!😡😡😡😡😡😡😡😡', 'I filed an official report against another student because they had looked through my phone and they continuesly ignored my boundaries by taking photos of me despite me telling them to stop several times even in front of other faculty. These were intentional calculated pattern that make me feel unsafe at RMCAD.

When I presented what I documented to the appropriate faculty and mentioned my justifiable fear for my safety, the faculty dismissed the perpetrator’s actions as "just microaggressions."

Edit: This same student had brandished a weapon against me in the student parking lot unprovoked and under the pretence of going to grab lunch. I have reason to believe that she and her friend had planned this.', 'I’d like to state that I do believe you get a quality education from this college having gone here myself. My daughter has been attending for her BA in FA. The education is adequate and beneficial.

The financial aid for this college has been a whole situation through the course of her education. It is May and my daughter has been contacting the financial aid department to try to square up entirely for her education since Thanksgiving 2024. Between their response time, their communication and misinformation, they ended up giving her $12,000 and telling her everything was paid and two weeks later 14 emails later they sent her a bill for thousands of dollars. It’s taking a toll on her mental health, especially when she just graduated and finished finals. This is not exactly setting her up for success.!

Numerous mails, and phone calls later, they put us in touch with the financial aid department who said they could not help her. Who also stated that they did not show her receiving a check.

It would be nice to have more adequate communication and somebody who can actually solve the problem within a term at this school. It hasn’t happened yet and $65,000 later I am disappointed.

Hopefully someone will reach out with a solution and change this for us, and hopefully, you don’t have a similar situation.', 'The reviews almost stopped me from a great experience here.From the registration process, to class work and communicating with my professors, I’ve had nothing short of an amazing experience. I’ve learned so much in the short time that I went to RMCAD and graduated with my BA in Fine Arts today. Yes, it was a lot of work but with that work I’ve learned so much and accomplished what I came to do. All of my instructors were knowledgeable, gave great feedback and answered all of my questions. I can vouch 100% for the music production program and have no doubt that all of their other programs are just as amazing!']

name: Colorado State University Pueblo
reviews:
["Transferring for a more preferred degree path, Register  office was both rude and unhelpful. Got PCC to transfer my transcript and tell me what my GPA was so I could transfer easy. Their office refused to do both and called me ignorant for not knowing that they could not help. They could not even recommend where to go next, insisting parchment was the right choice. That would be great but they closed my account and thus my ease of access to that platform.
The whole system is a mess, do not expect any help from administration or work study's.", "I applied as a resident of Colorado and was accepted. However they changed me to a non-resident due to my ID being out of state. I have lived and paid taxes here for 4 years. They did not notify me of the change in residency status - I found out when I got the bill that was 2X larger than expected and at that point it was past the date for petitioning for residency. They claim it is because of state legislation, however I attended Pikes Peak State College as a resident for 2 years before transferring.

I edited this from a 1 star to a 3 star because they did end up changing my residency status after telling me they couldn't change it, but again- I wasn't notified of the change so I could approve my COF to be used towards tuition. I appreciate the change, but part of the issue is lack of communication.", 'Man some of the staff here are RUDE AS HELL. name: Pickens Technical College
reviews:
["I just graduated from their Culinary Arts class last month and here is what I have to say about it. They have pretty decent communication and got back to me pretty quickly whenever it came to emailing them or going to the office in Building B for help. Once I saw one dude who worked there go through multiple buildings to find and help someone understand something they asked about after researching it. There is also a Starbucks and another place that serves food in the lounge and staff were kind and treated us like family 👍. My teacher was also nice and although she hasn't ever worked in food service, she has surprisingly taught me a lot about cooking and my mom who has worked in food service for years, can confirm that I learned the basics and some advanced cooking methods. The class was fun and challenging most days and some days were pretty easy. The uniform is comfortable, although most of us had to roll up the bottom of our pants for them to fit properly. It was easy to navigate to my class unlike some classes. The teacher was a really light grader so you don't have to worry too much about that. You mainly have to worry about showing up on time. You mostly learn how to follow complex recipes and be creative sometimes. It is mostly hands on but occasionally we did some writing assignments and even learned a bit about the world and history. It is also accessable for people with disabilities and I know that because one of my classmates was legally blind and another one had only one leg. And they both were given accommodations and were treated well. As long as you follow the basic rules like having your school ID on you, wearing your uniform, and making sure you have your book and knife kit/basic supplies, you are basically set. And I bought a different brand knife kit that was cheaper and they allowed it and you can borrow their books and knife kits if you want for the year rather than buy them because they are kind of expensive. I graduated this class as an honors student and I got into the college a few days into the year because they didn't have enough students and still got all A's and All of the credits and a 4.0 GPA somehow. It was mostly because I had perfect attendance and the class was easy though lol. And if you want to see most of what we cooked, I posted it on my Instagram at arielwillcutt17 so y'all can have a heads up👍. All in all, if you take this class I'm sure you'll do great 👍.", 'That front desk lady was so rude!! I was just calling about information concerning a program, and they didn’t add that one piece of information I needed. She keeps telling me, “I don’t know, ma’am.” I guess if you don’t know, just transfer me to someone who does, right? Well, she didn’t. She kept telling me she doesn’t know and was very impatient with me. I’m no longer applying, and the reviews told me everything I needed to know, so thank you for not answering me.', 'Hello my name is Marina orozco I came to this school for other programs I love it a lot everyone is helpful. Mostly Daniel he is very helpful also was Kevin from finical aid highly recommend this school.', 'Made this mistake of choosing this program as part of  a mental health treatment plan. Attempted to set up accommodations and got told that I didn’t sound capable. I could’ve been. with the right support. Now I’m just a pissed off former student who was already struggling mentally watching the program I wanted to complete slip through my fingers and move on without me. I paid  3k for nothing. Cool. Won’t be back. The subject is ruined for me as well. Thanks!', "One of the most disappointing academic experiences I’ve had. The lack of communication and support is unreal. Grades not being updated from 1st semester due to a honest mistake , but still not fixed.
The SMALL BUSINESS MANAGEMENT  program I enrolled in looked promising online, but once I started, I realized how misleading it was, things we never did  etc. . They have you add skills and experience to your resume that you didn’t actually gain — which is embarrassing and damaging when you're job hunting. Employers expect you to know things the program barely touches on, Things are just signed off weather its done or not . Plus , employers are looking for a minimum of an Associates Degree , not a Certificate.  Invest your money into a real
Let’s be real: the only solid skill we walked away with was how to do a basic W-2 form for taxes. The rest? We were told to “just Google it.” The instructor meant well, but was constantly unprepared and clearly overwhelmed and still learning himself . We often had to teach ourselves or rely on outside resources to learn what we needed. Most of the course was though on free online videos.
On top of that, the program mixes high school students with adult post-secondary students in the same classroom — which might work in theory, but in reality, it creates a chaotic and unprofessional learning environment. It’s hard to focus when you're dealing with classroom drama and immaturity.

Bottom line? If you're serious about your education and want real job readiness, and education , this is not the place. I don’t recommend this program to anyone, even if your looking to just open your business , if that's the case , ChatGPT will be your best friend .  There is about a handful of students looking for a refund due to the disappoint experience ."]

name: Trinidad State College
reviews: ['I "received" a GRANT and when I called and verified that it intended for me and not tuition I was told YES it was intended for me. Which I thought was a saving grace since my post 9/11 documents weren\'t processed which was a whole headache in itself. Well at the end of the freaking semester I get a email saying it was a clerical error despite me calling and verifying. Was no option for payment plan. And has since be sent to collections/law office where almost 1500 in fees has been added on it . Never solely trust the information given', 'Solid 4 stars\n\nTheir facilities aren’t the best but the professors here genuinely put in their all. They care about your success both in and outside of their classroom. My educational experience here was much better than at Pueblo Community college. Go Trojans!', 'My alma mater. Still one of the most beautiful campuses I’ve seen. Great two year electronics and computer degree. Served me well.', 'Although the teachers(the few that are left) are good most classes are online or hybrid. You might as well just go  to school completely online. The school expects students to pay in full for classes at one time no matter the amount because there\'s "no payment plan option" even though the ONLY bill you receive is one that is stamped "past due- due immediately". I\'ve heard many people going through similar things. Students turn in their student loan paperwork just to find out the next semester that they can\'t enroll for classes due to the irresponsibility of the office staff for either losing or just simply not putting through their student loan paperwork they handed them. Then staff doesn\'t even contact you if they lose it. Awesome, right? Students will try to enroll the next semester and the office staff will then let you know (last minute and way too late) that you owe hundreds, thousands or however much money (depending on your classes) before you can even go back to school. How can one expect to achieve much here when the staff can\'t hardly complete their jobs?', 'Gorgeous areas to park n watch wildlife!! Everything is sooo green and beautiful this year!! ❤️❤️']

name: Western Colorado University
reviews: ['Small class sizes, kind and knowledgeable professors, beautiful and safe location.', 'The football "undefeated" team. Don\'t know how to take a loss. name: Albertus Magnus College
reviews: ['Awesome school, small classroom settings. Everyone is friendly. You feel right at home there. Everyone is available to you and will help you with whatever you need. Lectures are welcoming and ensures you are on top of what needs to be done and that you understand what is being taught.', 'Was an okay college, kind of expensive for what they offered. I also signed up during the pandemic, so the experience that I had was drastically different than an experience someone else would have in 2023, opposed to 2020, when I went there. Just keep that in mind. Most of the professors were really kind and caring, I didn’t have a problem with the majority of them. Seemed like a very nice place to be if you want something smaller, and it was a bit expensive for the things they were offering there. If you’re looking to not pay as much as the national average, or stay within some type of budget, it also can be a good place to be. it is private though, for the people who are wondering. I never got to finish, the pandemic made it quite difficult and lonely for me, so that was offputting, and I didn’t have a roommate either, they dropped out before they even started.. it was empty in my room, didn’t really like the vibe. Needed someone else to lighten the mood for sure, that’s what was hard about the pandemic too. We couldn’t chill in each other‘srooms and stuff, no outsiders could come into the dorms either. It was a time that will never be forgotten.', "If you want your kid to be disrespectful...to be high and drunk and smoking on a sporting event, this is your college.  Security is a joke.  They are afraid of the students.  They don't even take pride in their school,  throwing their garbage and disposable masks on the ground.  Security smell like booze.  Very disappointing.  I was asked to bring my vaccination card and advices that they enforce mask wearing for all events.  Yet no one had masks.  If they can not follow their own rules, how would you expect them to protect your children??", "I don't like small colleges, but this school wasn't too bad. Like any school, nothing will ever be perfect. As Dr. Camille begins his tenure as the new president of the school, I'm confident that things will head in a better direction. He's passionate about the students being successful and the school having a active presence in the community. You won't regret the education you receive, but maybe your pockets will... #fearlessfalcons", 'Quality education! I believe Dr. Camille will take this school to the next level, while maintaining the integrity and enhancing the culture. Go Falcons!']

name: University of Bridgeport
reviews:
['Honestly worst admissions experience I’ve ever had. I’ve been going back and forth with the finance department and admissions to get simple questions answered, such as potential class times, as I was hoping to do part time at night. They have been absolutely unhelpful in this matter. I have had many communications with various departments and none have given any response except “sign up”.

They keep emailing me and texting me to sign on RELENTLESSLY but refuse to answer even the most simple questions when prompted. Definitely not worth the money', "A Disruptive Force in Global Education – Bold, Accessible, and Visionary

The University of the People is more than an institution, it's a movement. As someone with a deep background in development, consulting, and systems thinking, I see UoPeople as a strategic disruptor in the global education ecosystem.

In an age where student debt, institutional exclusivity, and rigid academic systems limit potential, UoPeople boldly redefines access. It dares to democratize higher education through an innovative model that is tuition-free, fully online, and internationally diverse.

Their rapid growth is no accident; it’s a testament to intelligent systems, strategic partnerships (like with UNESCO, Yale, and Google), and mission-driven design. The curriculum is rigorous, the learning environment is highly collaborative, and the peer-to-peer model fosters critical thinking and resilience.

What impresses me most is their relevance. UoPeople equips learners with practical, globally applicable skills at a fraction of the cost, especially in fields like Business Administration, Computer Science, and Health Science. The university doesn’t just give degrees, it builds digital-age problem solvers.

Is it perfect? No system is. But for those willing to work hard, think critically, and build global networks, UoPeople is a powerful launchpad.

T M
Entrepreneur | Consultant | Education Reformer | Digital Strategist", 'I attended this university (ELI) about 15-20 years ago.
I had never broken a window in the party room of the dormitory where I used to lived, but I was forced to pay for the glass in the window that someone had cracked when they were drunk.
I could not accept this decision and went to protest, but principal (at the time)
did not accept it,so I moved to a different school.

The teachers were unique and interesting.', "Since coming to UB as a transfer, I honestly really love it. My major is International Political Economy and Diplomacy, and in every class there always many international students, which creates a rich environment for discussion. I can personally attest that the professors are extremely helpful and because the school is so small there is plenty of one on one interaction. Even though this is my first semester I already feel extremely connected with the school. A huge focus the professors harp on is future careers, and we get plenty of advice on resumes and interviews and such. I'm honestly proud to be at this school and am very happy with my decision.", 'I graduated in 2016 from UB with a Master of Science in counseling.  I had the best professors who were supportive and provided guidance with every step of my journey.  My daughter recently graduated with her Masters in Criminal Justice and my youngest son is now in his second year.  Purple Knights to the world! I would recommend UB to anyone seeking higher education.']

name: Central Connecticut State University
reviews:
['The budget option to UCONN. Still met some good professors and there's a ton of events you can attend if you don't have a day job.

Support resources are a bit lacking and some departments have very few professors. So if you don't like one, you can get stuck with them for several courses because they're the only one available for courses you need to take for your degree.

Also be mindful of what courses you take for each term, some courses are only available in specific terms or "irregularly" so plan carefully and loop in your department chair when needed.

CCSU has an underfunded feel, but it's also cheaper than other CT schools and not a bad option for students on a budget.', 'I do not recommend their teaching program. It is poorly organized, and they expect you to quit your job in order to student teach, something that is simply unrealistic today. Instead of pushing people out of the profession, programs should be supporting the next generation of educators. They need to modernize, update their approach, and meet the needs of their students.

How can you tell someone to quit their job, and if they can’t pay rent, suggest they go to a homeless shelter? That is unacceptable.', "Very pretty and huge campus. Lots of students and the staff is absolutely welcoming. Can't wait to start my classes", 'Very comfortable, nicely scaled college of ~5,000 full-time undergraduates, with broad academic offerings and a faculty focused on students and teaching first. Eminently walkable campus that is vibrant even on weekends with 2/3 of first-year students living on campus and 1/4 overall with lots of walkable private housing. Comprehensive athletics program from intramural to mid-major NCAA varsity sports with a bit of an “old school”, pre-big money feel. A little under the radar but it’s definitely worth a thorough visit. Do the tour but also sit in on a few classes, visit the library and the art museum, eat at Hilltop Cafe, you just might find your perfect college fit.', 'Continuing Education sessions are really interesting.  Classes and delicious lunches/dinners are $25. Worth it.']

name: Charter Oak State College
reviews:
["I recently graduated from Charter Oak State College with my bachelor’s degree, and I am now continuing my education by pursuing my master’s. My experience at Charter Oak has been overwhelmingly positive, and I’m grateful for the flexibility and support the college provided throughout my journey.

When I started at Charter Oak, I transferred in with 90 credits but needed 120 to complete my degree. The college made the transfer process smooth and efficient, accepting my previously earned credits and helping me build a clear plan to finish my remaining requirements. The advisors were always responsive and knowledgeable, making it easy to stay on track academically while balancing work, life, and future goals.

The courses were well-structured, engaging, and designed for adult learners. I appreciated the focus on real-world application, especially as I prepared to transition into graduate-level study. Charter Oak’s online format allowed me to work at my own pace without sacrificing the quality of my education.

Overall, Charter Oak State College was the perfect fit for my academic needs. It provided an affordable, flexible, and supportive pathway to earning my bachelor's degree and prepared me well for my master’s program. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable and student-centered online college experience.", 'I think this program is a great option for an affordable degree, especially if you have way more than the usual 60 credits that are allowed for transfer. They take up to 87. I was able to get into graduate school at SUNY Purchase after I finished here.', 'After graduating from Capital Community College in Fall 2022, I was hesitant to continue my education due to concerns about student loan debt. Charter Oak State College quickly eased those fears. The Financial Aid Office informed me about a scholarship for CT community college graduates, making my education affordable. The diverse class offerings and outstanding support from my academic advisor, who guided me toward future opportunities, made my experience exceptional. While I’ll miss Charter Oak, I’m proud to soon be an alumnus of this incredible institution!', "There are a lot of areas where I think Charter Oak State College could improve but, the fact of the matter is, I got my BS here and probably spent less than 5,000 dollars. TOTAL! All these people complaining about the cost of higher education need to look at schools like Charter Oak. They have little in the way of credit-residency requirements -- I was only required to take eight credits in-house -- and they let you test out of as many credits as you like. For a fast, self-directed learner such as myself, it was perfect. My only caution is that I've found it very difficult to get into graduate school with my degree, despite some excellent grades and standardized test scores. The world still isn't prepared for educational paradigms like this.", 'I did have a helpful advisor, however, the financial aid (FA) department was difficult to get in touch with. I had to go down to the New Britain office in person 3 times and then call & email the office several times before getting even one issue resolved. After a year of their callous responses, I sent an email to the FA office to complain. They basically responded to me by calling me a liar and trying to discredit me! It was terribly unprofessional.

Charter Oak treated me as just another faceless number. The lack of personalization and unfriendly response from the employees showed me that I did not matter. I felt mistreated on their end. Don’t waste your money on a school that will refuse to hear you out and better their efforts. I wasn’t even looking for anything in return; I just wanted them to know that they needed improvement. Instead, they lost me as a student at their school.']
