name: Porter & Chester Institute of Hamden
reviews:
['I attended this school last year and it worst the worst experience of my life I was doing the LPN program. Julie the nursing director is probably the worst person I ever came in contact with once they get all the money that’s when their true colors show they are extremely unprofessional she would come from breaks smelling like cigarettes. She never cared about our future at all. What she has put me through was emotional trauma I left my job to be a student here ,I made sacrifices to be here only to be left with false hopes and fake promises .the school has worst teachers they get annoyed when asking them questions or don’t know it at all your basically teaching your self and to make it worse they will purposely fail you if speak up about the issues. Julie never helped but just threatened students. She wasnt fair at all .And to think that she is a nurse and should want to see the next generation of nurses succeed but she prepares for you to fail …Its truly sad ….and Im pretty sure the school is aware which makes the situation worst ….they are money grabbers and I want to warn you and I don’t people to experience the headache and stress , and the emotional trauma I faced at the hands of these people please look into other programs there is so much other places to pursue your nursing career !!!', 'I attended the HVAC program thru the VA and I have been nothing but disappointed in the institution. Especially with how long the va takes to get you settled and enrolled, I feel like I burned months of my life waiting to get education just for the school to let me down.
My instructor Karl (with a k) was a cool dude but the other aspects of the school were subpar.
Context:
• I was given the wrong time to attend classes (full time residential 4pm instead of 6pm) and wasn’t made aware until my 3rd week. By then I was somewhat behind due to missing labs and lectures.
•1 instructor for 50+ students
• I was put into a classroom of 50+ students whom some of which were already well ahead in the program.
• The materials/tools provided to us were dated and not readily available for the # of students in the class. For a 32-34k tuition that’s not acceptable. Other students stopped showing up because the curriculum overall is a mess.

In the end, I’m more so mad at myself for not doing my due diligence in researching other schools in the area like Entech and even Lincoln Tech. I expressed this all to my va representative and Thank God I don’t have to go thru the whole process again. I would advise the school to improve the overall quality and organization of education.
Was allowed to keep the Chromebook tho so I guess that deserves a star.', "Do not enroll. Save your money. The lpn program is extremely difficult and only about 1/3 of the starting classes will finish, getting ahold of administration to express concerns is next to impossible. It's a straight scam. They sell this 15 month dream to victims knowing full well the majority of them will not finish. Goodwin college is 18 months, and has better reviews. in hindsight ALL lpn programs should be 18 months or longer. Don't destroy you're credit at this school. Charging me 800$ for a couple cheap materials, cheap ugly uniforms that rip. You can only miss 42 hours in the 18 months and when I tell you, if you are 1 minute late to class, they will dock you that minute.", 'This campus is very well ran .The director of the school is very fair person. As long as you doing what you’re supposed to be doing he will be more lenient with you  .I graduated from the electrical program in January. In my opinion the instructor Mr. Strazza, is the best electrician in the state.I was very lucky to have him as my instructor ! I learned a lot. I recommend this school to people that are ready to take on the challenge and not make excuses! As for the other trades the other students seem to enjoy  them. I was not paid to write this lol I truly believe in this school and enjoyed my time there !', "I had a great experience with the electrical department in Hamden. Awesome teachers and a brand new facility with separate industrial and residential areas that are large and well built. I had all the supplies I needed and always knew I had the support of my teachers who gave me multiple perspectives to learn all the theoretical and practical skills I needed to feel comfortable on a job site

I was the only woman in the class and felt totally comfortable and welcomed.

You're given lots of time to work in the lab and lots of extra time after school as well. We got to learn extra skills like how to operate a scissor lyft and got to work with brand new PLCs too. Its on you to take the initiative but all the support you'd want or need is there if you want to learn. Every campus is different and you'll hear a lot of different P.O.Vs but taking this course totally changed my life and I feel so grateful I got the chance to experience it.

All the office staff are kind and helpful.

From my own personal experience with P&C I'd 100% recommend the electrical department in Hamden"]

name: University of Connecticut
reviews: ['The University of Connecticut is a fantastic school with a lively campus and a strong academic reputation. The professors are supportive, and the variety of programs offers something for everyone. UConn’s campus is beautiful, and the school spirit is incredible, especially with all the sports events. It’s the perfect place for both learning and making lasting memories!', 'Beautiful campus.  Go to the Dairy Bar, amazing ice cream and cheeses!', 'Sept 2021 pics. You don\'t have to be a student to enjoy the free, beautiful grounds of this campus. Bring your family or go solo. There\'s something for everyone here. Horse barn hill has a trail so you can walk around and explore the "dairy" part of campus. Stop at the dairy bar for their homemade ice cream. Walk around the campus and enjoy the beautiful grounds, old buildings. Attend a sporting event, ie., men\'s soccer matches are $5pp, free parking. Bring a book or a picnic and sit and enjoy the quiet, floral grounds. College Kids are in session right now but they\'re doing their own thing. I\'ve been visiting the campus 6x in past 8 weeks and it\'s been amazing.', "What a wonderful campus to have. First, the huskies are always building. However, it's a nuisance since it removes parking for basketball games. The education of the people here is good and there are numerous sports arenas. The buildings, specifically the new dorm project is far away from the center. The museum of puppetry is appreciated. Old UCONN pre COVID would be a 5, but post COVID more like a 4.", "Beautiful campus in a town completely dedicated to supporting the college campus. Even though it's a campus of 19,000 students, it feels small enough as not to be completely overwhelming. We took my daughter up for a college tour, and we were very impressed with this Top 25 public university."]

name: Goodwin University
reviews:
['The LPN program at Goodwin had both positive and negative aspects. The most positive experience was the relationships formed with classmates, and many of the instructors were genuinely supportive and willing to help students succeed.

However, I was part of the first full-time LPN cohort, and the program was extremely challenging due to ongoing organizational issues. There was a high turnover rate among instructors, frequent last-minute changes, and a general lack of communication. Administrative staff often could not provide clear or accurate answers to important questions. We were explicitly told by the head of the nursing program that we were the “guinea pigs” for the program and that any improvements would benefit future cohorts rather than our own.
Despite these challenges, I successfully completed the program. One of the most concerning issues occurred one week before graduation, when we were informed that all outstanding balances had to be paid in full or placed on a payment plan in order for transcripts to be released. One week after graduation, we were then informed that students were responsible for paying to have their transcripts sent, as the university would not cover this cost. I graduated on December 18, 2025, and I am still unable to schedule my NCLEX. Due to delayed communication from the university, my transcript was sent to the state without my clinical hours included. As a result, I remain unable to test and am currently awaiting clarification from Goodwin regarding why my clinical hours were omitted and how they will be sent.
Given that Goodwin offers multiple nursing programs that follow the same state testing process, it is unclear why the LPN program has faced such significant issues. Based on my experience, I would strongly encourage prospective students to consider other options if available.', 'So far I am having a great experience here! I ESPECIALLY like that when you call , you can actually talk with someone!!!!! Everyone here has been so helpful,  registering for clases is so easy , and the advisors are helpful.  If you have to send a request for information,  they respond  fast.  This has been the best college experience ive had . Goodwin please keep up the good work!', 'I’m currently a student at Goodwin, my experiences have been great when talking about the education aspect, my only complaint would be the front desk person, Shanya, the first person you interact with besides the security. She was very rude and had an attitude when asking me about my physical student ID which has no been set up as of current because I take full online courses. I have only gone into the school for the bookstore which I will now be ordering my books online. After that brief interaction, with her manager supposedly right there,  they all laugh as if this is highschool. Do better Goodwin, you pride yourself on being a welcoming community, and that starts with the front desk. As a single mom just trying to better myself I am deeply disappointed.', "I'm currently enrolled. It's been a wonderful experience up until a class I was taking this semester. The front end individuals have been incredibly helpful and professional. However, there is a professor there who is unprofessional and their conduct needs to be addressed. I've turned to several outlets and nothing has been done. I dropped that individual's class and care less to continue looking for support on this issue. It's a shame some students concerns go ignored. Not s good way to run your school.", 'My experience at Goodwin University has unfortunately been disappointing. I would rate it a 2/10. The cost of attendance is extremely high, and despite being marketed as “single-mom friendly,” my experience has not aligned with that message. I have been enrolled at this institution for over four years and still have not been able to complete my degree, largely due to inconsistent guidance and unclear communication.

Each staff member I’ve interacted with has given different information, making it difficult to navigate my academic path. The lack of consistency, professionalism, and genuine support has created unnecessary setbacks and financial strain. It has been disheartening to feel that instead of helping students advance in their careers, the system often leaves them overwhelmed with additional debt.

I truly hope the university will improve its communication, support services, and overall commitment to student success moving forward.']

name: Eastern Connecticut State University
reviews: ['Amazing professors. Dining hall is mid- sometimes good, they try to have a good variety but sometimes it’s not to my liking. Student center food court is really great tho. Students can be really nice or really mean but the school does a lot to promote community. Campus is beautiful.  Lots of opportunities. Cool events.', 'Recently, our Family went on a tour of the beautiful Eastern Connecticut University campus for our son and we fell in love with the campus layout and the warm staff!', "It was an alright experience, but this University stops at nothing to beg for money after you graduate, as if you haven't paid enough while you attended.  Prepare for non-stop phone calls, emails, etc. that you never asked for.  They've even resorted to selling overpriced Alice in Chains tickets.  Leave me alone.", 'I was a student here for 3 years and I’m proud that I even made it that long. The best description of this school that I can give, is high school for adults and social work majors. Eastern says they are all abt diversity and inclusion and I say womp womp to that.  UConn, just 15min up the road, is arguably the most diverse and high achieving school in New England. If you want the full college experience do NOT go here, for your own sake. Listen to me or listen to your peers say the same thing I just did over the course of 4 years till it sticks in your head.', 'I have literally never regretted a decision more in my life. Joke school with terrible staff and student employees that treat you like children shaped garbage cans. Save yourself time and money, don’t go,']

name: University of Hartford
reviews:
['The University of Hartford is a fantastic institution that combines quality education with a supportive and engaging campus environment. The faculty are knowledgeable, approachable, and committed to helping students succeed academically and personally.

The campus is well-maintained, modern, and provides an excellent atmosphere for learning, research, and extracurricular activities. I particularly appreciate the university’s focus on innovation, career readiness, and holistic student development.

Whether you’re interested in academics, athletics, or community involvement, the University of Hartford offers resources and opportunities to grow in all areas. I highly recommend University of Hartford to anyone seeking a well-rounded and enriching university experience.', "The University is very expensive, and I believe additional parking fees make it even harder for students who are already struggling financially. Many students live on their own and work after classes just to afford tuition, bills, and basic needs. I think the school should consider reducing extra fees just like parking space  and focusing on the most essential courses that directly support students' majors. I hope the university becomes more understanding of students’ financial challenges.", "I've been going here almost 5 years and I ultimately cannot recommend it. The education is ok but they won't hesitate to nickel and dime you over petty technicalities. This is my experience while participating in their MBA program. Needless to say, I won't be speaking favorably about this school and won't be making any future donations.", 'Wonderful university. Great opportunities and experiences for our daughter. Doing their best under these difficult and abnormal times to bring our kids together. name: Mitchell College
reviews: ['Very lovely small college that my grandson goes to London excellent', 'Best College in Connecticut! Amazing faculty, staff, students, and administration. The campus in the beach are absolutely beautiful. Highest rating possible for a great education.', 'This college is located on the beautiful New London coastline. From the moment you step foot on their campus, there is an overwhelming sense of family.  The atmosphere is welcoming, as positive relationships are evident, and encompassed by student success.', 'Back when I was a pizza delivery boy no student at Mitchell college ever tipped more than a few cents. Compare this with the kids at Conn College who are decent and would toss a buck or two and say "thank you". For this reason Mitchell gets  one star reviews FOREVER', 'My son attended this college, because of the “resources” and staff we were promised they had. Boy were we wrong. First, no one answers the phone and there is no communication between staff, parents and kids. The first day of my son’s attendance, was horrific. I entered his assigned room to bring his items into it and the kids were drinking and doing drugs. Yes, you read that correct. My son was severely bullied and left without a room or place to sleep for a weeks and I had to Uber him home because I could not get anyone from the college to pick up the phone or respond to an e-mail to ensure he had a safe place to sleep. The reason he did not have a room was because he came home for a weekend and got hospitalized for a concussion. When he returned the room was vandalized and smelled of something so foul it was not livable. When I did get ahold of a counselor she stated she could not get anyone to get back to her about getting my son a room to live in. This went on for weeks. The staff not once spoke to my son, went to check on the room or do any form of investigation. Of course, later on they stated that they in fact did, which could not be farther from the truth. The bullying and fact that my son had a room that had been trashed by a fellow roommate when my son was away became so stressful that my son dropped out. When I finally went to go pick up his belongings my heart was broken. His clothes and belongings had been vandalized, most of his items stolen and the room had been sprayed with some form of “stink bomb”. Not one staff member ever entered the room to see the severity of the situation.\nThe school took zero responsibility and turned the blame on my son. I want to mention that my son and I chose this school because of a mental illness and the resources promised to him. However, it is quite the opposite. There is a lack of resources, communication and no one is checking on the safety of the students, like in my son’s situation.\nThere is much more that went on during his short stay at Mitchell but I write this review to warn parents so that they are aware and can make their own educated decision. I know if we could do it all over again we would never have chosen this college.']

name: University of New Haven
reviews:
['As an Indian international student, I feel utterly scammed by the University of New Haven. They lure you in with easy admissions, charge insane tuition (~$45K/year), and then set you up to fail in the first semester with brutal grading and zero remedial support. No second chances, no extra exams—if you bomb a course, you’re screwed and risk deportation on your F-1 visa. It’s like they bank on your tuition and don’t care if you sink. Advisors are MIA, and the international student office is a joke—good luck getting help. The campus feels like a cash grab, especially for Indians who make up most of the grad programs. How does CT and the U.S. let this place operate? It’s accredited, sure, but it’s a predatory system that preys on our dreams and wallets. Save your money and avoid this hellhole!', 'The beauty of this school is not just about  the academic excellence and great facilities, but the diversity; it’s almost as if every nationality is represented here. Everyone is friendly from the students to the academic staffers, non-academic staffers, to the school security operatives.
When I visited this school I observed  wheelchair accessibility is greatly adhered to in this institution. I also noticed there’s a 24/7 Wells Fargo Bank ATM point on this campus. Consequently, you will always have access to cash.

When you school here you also get to enjoy the magnificence of New Haven, West Haven and most of all New York City, since it’s just less than an hour ride with your car or via the Metro-North Train. This school is pretty close to road and be easily noticed from a vehicle in normal traffic.

#NewHaven #WestHaven #UNH #University #AcademicsExcellence #CT #Connecticut #OnGoogleMaps #Google #LetsGuide #GreatFacilities #WheelchairAccessible #Knowledge', "UNH is a Good University, did Masters in Environmental Engineering from here (2014-16), Campus looks neat.

In Environmental Engineering Department Dr. Agamemnon Kutsospyros, Professor  Emese Hadnagy and visiting Professor Gulsah Tuna were really good at teaching.

Celebrated Dr. AK's birthday on Feb 25 2014

Frank Cahill's Presentation in Prof. Emese Hadnagy's Engineering Hydrology course was good (Sample video uploaded)", 'It’s a beautiful atmosphere with a lot of tree and plants , experience faculty and  football ground and with  huge Jim', "I attended this university between the years of 2019 and 2023. Earned a B.S. in Criminal Justice (January 2021) and a M.S. in National Security (December 2023).

The one star:
A stellar education taught among two programs. Common characteristics include various learning formats and knowledgeable instructors. I also appreciated the wide scope of material covered in each degree program, and the opportunity to ask questions via email as a follow up to something that was covered in an assignment or lecture. An academic improvement I STRONGLY suggest is that industry recognized/accepted credentials, certifications, and or licenses be included in each program's curriculum where applicable (plus university wide). The main reason is because in both job searches after each program, a lack and absence of these continues to hinder my ability to satisfy job requirements (as of 11/26/2025). Whether this implementation occurs from within university, encouragement by employers, or by NECHE, something must happen. Because if employers are requiring applicants to have these in the post pandemic era, how can UNH graduates without them be desirable amongst other applicants who have them? Anyhow, for this and identical reasons, I strongly recommend the university pursue this revision. The ROI for students will increase greatly. Still unemployed as of this edited review btw.

Switching to the other side of the 1 star:
My reasons are unfortunately one too many. As a commuter student, I can honestly attest that unless the student lives within a 30-minute radius of campus and has immediate access to a vehicle, it is difficult to persuade or advocate that a social experience life will follow suit. By this I mean as someone who lived in northern Connecticut for both programs, I frequently missed out on many extracurricular activities. Reasons range from simply being too tired after class to simply not being on campus when an event occurred. Compounding this was that after a solid attempt in spring 2019 to immerse myself with the university’s LASA (Latin America Students Association) group, I ceded failure. They chose to continue socializing amongst pre-existing circles rather than include me. This remains difficult to talk about without getting upset. In addition, this was the onset in which I felt my own Hispanic-Latino identity work against me for the second time in my life. I consequently felt out of place often and sad to know that I did not have a place of belonging at UNH where they market themselves as a place of DEI. (How contrary it really was considering Hispanic/Latino status was supposed to be a beneficiary of DEI). It's more hurtful to know that other diverse people were sought out and valued more than others. Major double standard here. Anyhow, these repetitive letdowns amplified more and more and consequently affected my ability to see persevere. As a result, I failed even more. When my final graduate semester began (fall 2023), I accepted that there was no more opportunity for improvement. I focused on more joyful-rewarding things off campus. Such as visits to NYC. (Here I was more successful on the basis that my age and identity were more desirable and valued in the places and things I pursued).

Bottom line now:
I came to UNH as a transfer student. Spent one semester in university housing and quickly realized that there were too many things working against me. My time came and went well before I arrived. Winter commencement was canceled some time ago by the school. But that is a minor compared to the others described above. Some support was offered or pursued along the way to improve things. But to no avail was most of it successful.

I also want to point out that because of my double below-average experience at UNH, I did not entertain nor accept the university's offer to attend the spring's 2024 commencement ceremony.  To do so would have been another saddening experience for all to see and validated the university's values at my expense.

(Edited November 2025)."]

name: Porter & Chester Institute
reviews:
['I personally don't like to write a bad review; however, I am doing this because this school is too horrible. From the very beginning, she should just pull me aside instead of embarrassing me in front of the whole call. In the end, I just want to say that people's college life maybe only once in life and DON'T LET THIS SCHOOL TO RUIN YOUR COLLEGE MEMORY', 'Horrible program. My daughter is in the program. Her teacher left last month due to a family emergency since then they have had nothing but issues. We are paying good money to be here. They have had 6 different teachers who are unorganized, have power points that the students don’t have and when they bring it to the higher ups they blame the students saying “you have your book” like they are supposed to become nurses off the book. They haven’t had any of the emails for the random subs they have had so they have no one to ask questions.  Ben the dean doesn’t care. There are MULTIPLE students failing since they haven’t had a set teacher and it states in our guideline we have “the right to have an organized curriculum and responsible instructor prepared to teach” which they haven’t.', 'To whom may concern :

A little more than a year and a half ago I spoke with a guy named Rafael, which is the director of this facility and he took it upon himself to delete my application based on me asking concerning questions about the course. I I take it either. He didn’t have time or he wasn’t in the mood to considerate the questions I have for him. Very unprofessional. Ever since I’ve been trying to get to start an application, but it’s been unsuccessful. Also spoke to someone named Cheryl. I believe she’s a higher up but unfortunately I don’t know if it’s due to her busy schedule or something else but I’ve left plenty of voicemails and there hasn’t been a Reply. This is going to be my second year, trying to apply but in this facility there seems to be no interest in helping people. Every time I go people seem to just be sitting around chitchatting and all I get is “ No Worries .Will email you or will call you “ . It’s been about two months since the last time I spoke with someone and I’m still waiting to receive a call. Is unfortunate for me that this is the only institute that offers the course I want.

I wouldn’t wish this on anybody that’s trying to Progress.', 'worst "trade school" by far and the biggest waste of time and money. you can get a better education for a way lower cost than 25k anywhere else. the "teachers" here aren't even qualified or taught to teach. im in welding during the day, and all my "teacher" does is sleep all day or take his teachers pet everywhere with him to do projects, that none of us are allowed to do. not for nothing as well, but the class is overbooked -- we have say 11 welding booths and 15 students, and the students who have to share booths with others because of this issue get yelled at and harassed by the teacher for just sitting around doing nothing, when all we are doing is waiting for our turn to weld. i would highly recommend pursuing other options, the only thing that this school offers you is a welding jacket and a couple of tools, which can all be bought at harbor freight for a hundred or so dollars. oh, and good luck if you are hard of hearing, because the teacher in the day welding class has a thick spanish accent and a lisp, and gets irritated when you dont understand him. class is also supposed to run from 7:30-3:00, when in actuality it runs from 7:30-1:30, sometimes 2:00, and only ever near 3:00 when corporate is in the building. biggest waste of time and money ever.', "Don’t Go There!! I regret every single day having studied at this school. They don't teach you anything; you have to learn everything on your own by watching YouTube videos while the instructor watches Netflix on the computer. Thanks to what I was able to learn on the street, I was able to help my classmates in any way I could... They say they'll help you get a job, but they never call you back after you finish the course. I FEEL LIKE THEY ONLY USED ME TO STEAL MY MONEY.  Now I owe the state $19,000 and have no hope of getting a job in the electrical field.

I felt very sorry looking at students who knew absolutely nothing and had no one to teach them."]

name: Post University
reviews: ["Despite all of the bad reviews for this school, I had a really good experience throughout my time attending Post University. I was enrolled at a 4 year university but moved across the country and found that a fully online program fit my schedule a lot better. Post accepted about 60 transfer credits from my previous university and I thought that was very fair, I only ended up losing out on a handful of credits. The transition was very easy, Frank worked with me over the phone to get me enrolled and kept in touch until I was assigned a student advisor. My advisor was extremely helpful, kind, and easy to get in contact with. We communicated often through text where he would check in, send updates about upcoming enrollment dates, and even just check-in if it looked like I hadn't been as active as usual. I was pleased that I had the same advisor for majority of my time here, he even personally called me once to congratulate me on doing well in my courses! I was enrolled as a military dependent student, with this I received free books with all of my courses and they were automatically ordered for me at the time of enrollment each term. I did not have any issues with Financial Aid, they were always straight forward with what they needed from me and I received refunds from my grant promptly.\n\nAll in all, I had a great experience with Post and received my Bachelors degree in October. I understand my experience differs greatly since I was not a first time college student and was already educated in navigating online platforms and financial aid, but with any University or online program it is important to remember to advocate for your own success as a student.", 'I Love this University!! I had no problems with them at all!! They let me have a term off for family reasons. Just want to say this school is awesome!!! I am almost getting my degree in Accounting (4 more classes) and going for my certificate in forensics accounting also. The students advisors and financial aid advisors has been great!! The instructors has been amazing for each class I have taken!! If you are looking for a great university to go, Post University is the one!! GO EAGLES!!!!!!!!!!🦅🦅🦅💜💜💜🦅🦅🦅', "I used to attend this school to work on my master's degree in education. I had a terrible professor who should not be a professor. I reported them and wanted to withdraw from the school. The school ended up releasing me, which I had wanted since I was not pleased with everything about it. This school asked me if I wanted to come back, but I told them I was not interested in coming back after having a bad experience attending the school. But I received my master's degree and earned very high grades like A's and B's in my classes, as I have for many years at another college. This school needs to be shut down, and I advise students not to attend this school.", 'I am in my second term at Post University, and I have found the staff to be second to none. If I have an issue, I talk to my advisor, and it is generally resolved before I hang up the phone. Excellent financial aid advisors as well.', "I am not the type of person to leave negative reviews, but you people have been spamming my inbox and calling me nonstop for over a week now! I told you people the first time that I'm not interested in applying to the Business Administration school, this is unacceptable. I have blocked their number multiple times and they still find a way to call me, it doesn't matter how many times I repeat I'm not interested. I AM NOT INTERESTED. This is harassment. I don't know if the woman answering the phone is an AI Bot or not, but she ignores me every time I ask her not to call me."]

reviews: ['Was on a university tour with my high school students today. They were so nice and welcoming. The campus is absolutely beautiful. name: Sacred Heart University
reviews:
['Physics, chem, and bio departments are a joke. The university is dirt cheap with hiring professors that multiple biology courses have TWO sections at most. It is such a struggle for both staff and students to just get into required courses when it comes time for class registration. This uni has more than enough money especially seeing as they DO NOT PAY PROPERTY TAX. Please work better on focusing where you allocate your money, for the sake of everyone who PAYS TO BE HERE.', "Don't attend this school. They brainwash you to think that the staff is here to help you. Know one cares about the student. You can't get in touch with registrar. You don't have any form of guidance when it comes to any staff at Sacred Heart.
Once they take your money, your a goner. I graduated from this school and this was by far the worst university experience in my life. They are better universities in Connecticut that don't charge an arm & a leg.
Actual good ones that guide the student and have actually people answer phone calls. I feel like the staff does whatever they want because there are no consequences for screwing students over.
Parents of freshmans, stay away from this mediocre school.", "Has very nice grounds. The tour guide did a very nice job of showing everyone around in the hot sun. She spoke very clearly and explained everything very well. They seemed very accommodating to everyone's needs. They have a chapel so that students can pray or go to Mass(or whatever other religion they may practice) right next to the dorms. Very beautiful place would recommend a visit to Sacred Heart University.", 'Beautiful campus. Very supportive of students.', 'Sacred Heart was a decent university to attend but its not great.
The professors and student body are a mixed bag. Some of the professors are bad and not very engaging, some are decent and do a decent job, and some are great. The academic programs are a mixed bag depending on what you peruse. The nursing and marketing programs are great, but some of the "smaller" programs are mixed. The students are also similar in the sense of unfriendly to friendly.
The main academic building and some other older buildings  are run down, and tired, and stick out like a sore thumb in comparison to the newer buildings. Specifically the main academic building with 63's dining hall probably hasn't been updated or renovated since the early 2000's.
The newer building's are modern and sheik and appealing. The residential buildings are similar- they are either really run down or outdated, or they are really nice, depending on which dorm your assigned. Most are relatively newer and nice.
The SHUttles are also pretty effective and do the job for students who may not drive or don't have a car.
The food options SUCK. 63's (the buffet style restaurant) is  mediocre at best. "The Market" does the job for a oncampus cafe. Linda's is decent for a quick in and out place for grab and go food. Similarly, JP's is also a decent place for a diner like setting - probably the best place on campus for food options! Einstein's is also as good.']

name: University of Saint Joseph
reviews: ['Definitely not grateful for how my athlete brother is treated on the team. I repeat do not send you children to this school for athletics as they have favorites and may never give your children or siblings a chance to play. Do not waste your money at this school. Can’t understand how someone’s goes from being a captain to not playing for three years yet being on the team that plays statistics to cover / protect themselves. I am beyond disappointed in USJ and I would not recommend anyone to send their aspiring athletes for any sports at that school especially basketball', 'Everyone on campus that I have dealt with has maintained so much professionalism, the professors here really go out of their way to be helpful. I wish it were cheaper, but you get what you pay for, this school is definitely worth the money! The tutoring department is amazing!', 'Excellent school for both women and men.  The university offers several degree programs with a strong emphasis on education and nursing as well as many other options.', "I recently was enrolled in the graduate cohort for reading and writing.  I have been teaching for almost 10 years and found most of the classes insulting. I felt I knew more than the cohort professors and learned very little new. Many of the text books were from early 2000.  Considering the vast changes in LA recently, I felt many classes provided information that was not up to curent reading philosphies and/or research. The rubrics were so convoluted that the professors couldn't figure them out or they did not pertain to the topic. Many classes were spent going back and forth over the rubrics only to have them change again. Knowing what I do now, I would not waste the money, but would have done an on-line course for 1/3 the price.", "As a current junior undergraduate at the University of Saint Joseph in West Hartford, CT, I am very happy here. I came to USJ as a shy, timid girl without the confidence to speak up in class. I am now a confident woman that isn't afraid to voice my opinion or share my insights. USJ has given me the platform to grow as a person and to realize exactly what I want out of college and out of life. In the past, I have always been unsure what the future would hold for me but ever since I've been at USJ my path has become more clear. I would recommend attending USJ to any woman interested in getting, not only a college education, but a chance to grow as a person, which is something not most colleges can offer."]

name: Southern Connecticut State University
reviews:
['They have dumbed this place down so much that instead of reading challenging academic articles they are now showing YouTube videos and having you read the teachers past lectures written out instead of reading challenging academic papers. The teachers are doing all of the work to simplify the courses for the students because they are so devolved and have the attention span of a goldfish. In other words, if there is a 30-page reading, the teacher will post up a 3-page summary of the reading so the students just read that as oppose to reading the whole chapter.
Between the giant "Black Lives Matter" banner, the toilet seats up in the women’s bathroom, the zombied out children all carrying or wearing between one to five electronic devices, I can't wait to get out of this place.  I don't know how many white students, Asian students, Indian, or Latino students want to ride up to a school with a giant "Black Lives Matter" banner on the building. That is a slap in the face to all other racial groups. The college should be completely neutral. Whites are 60% of the population, Blacks are 10% of the population. Colleges are a business. A good business person is going to cater to the majority, not the minority. Stupid is as stupid does.', 'I am deeply disappointed with the way Southern Connecticut State University handles student well-being. There is a noticeable lack of concern for students’ physical and mental health, and support services often feel secondary to financial priorities. The university needs to take student safety and mental health far more seriously. At this point, the environment feels unsafe and unsupportive, and meaningful improvements are long overdue… avoid staying on campus.', 'This university is so overrated. The on campus staff people are indifferent, treat you like a commodity and don’t care about supporting you. There is no sufficient student parking available unless you come super early in the morning and the parking attendants are rude and obnoxious for no reason. You end up parking elsewhere. The amount of tests and exams per semester is atrocious, the professors don’t adequately cover those topics and there is too much for you to self study. Some professors don’t answer your emails at all, others are too short and vague in their responses.', 'I knew I shouldn’t have chose this school once I visited it in person. I should have left AS SOON after they told me to withdraw all of my classes the first semester I came. That’s why the graduation retention rate is so low! There’s LACK of support, don’t take student’s mental health seriously, until it’s last minute. It’s a money grab school. Most will discourage you.

If you stay on campus housing, the area is not pleasing, there are cops all over campus because it’s that bad. Sometimes the school would have shooting alerts. I honestly felt so unsafe. I had two roommates who were bullying me.

Some professors/instructors will fail who they want, they have favorites. Please don’t take professor/instructor Bradley. Every time she would talk to me she would give me an annoyed and disgusted look on her face. She was so rude.

It’s not the end for me though! I just didn’t want to be apart of this school or even graduate here. But if you choose this school, good luck seriously.', 'I spent weeks calling the school, calling the people in charge of the program I was accepted into, sending emails all just to register for classes. No one ever got back to me. I was not able to register for classes.

The woman answering the phone in the graduate admissions department was extremely rude to me and completely unhelpful. Truly no desire to help me. She purposely spoke to me as if I was bothering her. Sighing loudly and scoffing when all I was doing was asking for help.

I am truly genuinely heartbroken and disappointed in the treatment that I received from this school. No one has ever treated me so horribly.

I sadly realize this is not a school I want to be part of.']

name: Trinity College
reviews: ["Beautiful Trinity College - a stunning architectural beauty.  Entrance through any of the arches is transforming, leaving behind the traffic noise, step into a contemplative atmosphere of quiet and intelligence.  We frequent there for concerts, and this time for a film in their period theater.   Having attended very pleasant state school, I've often wondered, if I were intelligent enough, what it would have been like to walk onto that campus as a student.  Of the current students, I wonder if they pause long enough to appreciate the beauty of their surroundings.   A required course should be an appreciation of what those who have gone before have designed and built for today's students.", "We came for my daughter to look at and talk to the school and the athletic department. It's an amazingly beautiful campus. A liberal arts college with an engineering department. Definitely a contender for next year. Quite a way from Colorado. 😃", "One of the, if not the most inspiring commencement ceremonies I have ever been to. Very diverse faculty great students. The place is beautiful and it's a wonderful institution. Cheers to the walking under the elms!", "Perhaps one of the most beautiful college campuses in the country. It's majestic setting on a bluff overlooking the City must be experienced.", 'The campus is stunning and do not miss the chapel.  The trees there are enormous.  Lovely campus!']

name: Wesleyan University
reviews: ['Very interesting Van Vleck  observatory is open to the public for hands on tour every Wednesday evening. 8- 9 pm  (Be sure to check the website first ).Located next to the Olin library on Wesleyan campus Middletown CT. Fun visit ☺️', 'My 50th reunion was great. Remains a challenging and exciting place.', 'Would I sell my soul to get admitted here? Yes.\nUpdate: I GOT IN WOOHOO!!!!', 'Beautiful campus. Great atmosphere. Nice town', 'Excellent liberal arts college in CT']

name: Western Connecticut State University
reviews: ['Offers everything all of the private northeastern liberal arts colleges that charge 60k plus a year offer at a fraction of the cost. A hidden gem of a university', 'My honest  this is the worst college that you can ever attend. It’s a shame that living in the same city for a  very long time I feel has been the worse experience with Western Connecticut State University for the second time!! So bad!! Western Connecticut State University discriminate students with Grants  scholarships. They not professional lack of communication, discrimination upside down. Also, if you are Spanish or have a Spanish last name, you might think twice before you waste your time going through the process because they also discriminate once they find out that you Hispanic and has a grant scholarship. Don’t waste your time with Western Connecticut State University.', 'One of the worst college you can go to. The RA’S are out of control. Especially the RA Zion. MOST UNQUALIFIED PERSONNEL TO RUN A DORM POINT BLANK GUY SHOULD BE FIRED', 'I take courses as an audit student.  I have a Ph.D. in Romance Languages and am a senior (80), who takes courses in concert chorale and jazz piano at WCSU. I am thrilled to be a part of WCSU!', "Got my MBA here. The faculty is quite smart and is genuinely interested in your success. Specifically, the marketing, supply chain, and finance professors are top notch. If you get the opportunity to study abroad for Taiwan, which is available as an undergrad as well, absolutely do it. Amazing people to network with and friends that came out of class, overall very rewarding experience.\nI spent a year and change at the school, and I'd go again if I found the need to go back to school."]

name: Yale University
reviews: ['I had such a beautiful experience visiting Yale University with my friend. The campus is absolutely stunning — the historic architecture, peaceful courtyards, and lively student atmosphere make it feel both inspiring and welcoming. Walking around together made it even more special; every corner feels like a picture perfect moment. We especially enjoyed exploring the Yale University Art Gallery and the Yale Peabody Museum both were incredible and such a great bonus since they’re open to the public. It’s the perfect place for a relaxing walk filled with history, culture, and great conversations. Highly recommend visiting and taking a guided tour! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐', 'I was unaware of the scale that Yale University has. It’s quite literally an entire city. We walked for miles and block after block, building after building was just another Yale owned building. The architecture is truly incredible to see on these buildings. Hillhouse Avenue is full of beautiful houses turned into Yale buildings.', 'A very nice school with nice brown bricks buildings. There are a lot of police cars along side the school and its boundaries, and the light always keep lighting. There are also many security guards walking in the school area. The bad things are 1) the streets is not very clean, there are many trash on the streets; 2) there are some people walking with hammers, or other tools ; 3)the free parking varies, some 5pm, some 7pm. Be safe when visiting.', 'Our family has been here many times for various middle school and high school classes (highly recommend). But for the trip we took the admissions tour for our rising senior daughter and did the info session and really enjoyed it! The campus is so beautiful, and it was great learning more about applying and life on campus.', "Such a GRAND school. Just to step foot onto this campus, I felt immediately smarter, haha! The architecture of the buildings really is magnificent.  Like stepping back in time, seeing the huge columns, inscription into the buildings, grand doorways, and old-fashioned windows definitely play the part. Overall, it was such a nice visit just walking around the campus on a Saturday rainy afternoon. A lot of students were walking around as well. If you're ever visiting this area, I definitely recommend visiting this school."]

name: Delaware Technical Community College-Terry
reviews:
["I ran in the Del Tech Chocolate 5k Run/Walk in Dover, DE today. It was the best 5k I've ever participated in..EVER... well organized, ample and close parking, clean, wonderful volunteers, the best after party ever... The T-shirts smelled like chocolatel!!! So creative and cool design.  If this run is an example of how students are treated and educated, this is the place to attend, folks!!!", 'I truly appreciated the honest and warm help that I received from a woman name Angel. I was in need of my transcripts and she went the extra mile to help me succeed. She provided excellent customer services and hospitality from the heart.', 'I know a lot of people left reviews but I wanted to leave one more recent in the hopes people will see it. Stick with me here !
First things first, the classes were good and education was fine.
HOWEVER and this is a big however I dropped out of courses because it just wasn’t for me. Fast forward almost a year later, me being under the impression I was dropped out and done because no one ever communicates properly, I get an email stating I will be send to collections. I try to find out more and no one is willing to help me. No one is able to provide proper cause and why this is happening. I was told I didn’t drop out properly and that would be my fault. It wouldn’t be their job to follow up and help me. They said there is nothing I can do, to the answers of why no one said anything for a year that I had a balance was a simple " I don’t know "
I made peace with having to pay that money since no one wants to help me. However now I am running into the problem of getting send around, having been told three different things, stating I can’t set up a payment plan it would have to be in full( I was told something else two days ago ) by God knows when for no one can get me an exact date when I will be send to collections.
- With that I am owing a lot of money which I didn’t know I did for almost a year. And no one cares because I quote " not their job, your problem " my problem of coming up with a lot of money by " date unknown "

No one wants to help. Everyone just gives the solution of "  just pay the money ".  This is by far one of the most outrageous experiences I have ever had.
Please make sure if you do attend, get everything in writing and properly laid out otherwise it’s your word against theirs and they don’t care about your word.', "Well organized health event. Some informative classes. Free lunch and many vendors offering all kinds of takeaways and information on their services. Can't wait until next year's event. Great day for anyone who has diet restrictions our lives with someone with such needs.", 'I attended the Minority SBA event and learned a lot, while making professional contacts. A great day for all and hopefully one that will continue. Del Tech had a wonderful conference facility that was easy to find and access.']

name: Delaware State University
reviews:
['I transferred to this place from a PWI in hopes for a better, non toxic environment I couldn’t have been more wrong and I regret that decision every single day on this college . First of all the foreign professors are very racist and discriminate towards the black students in an HBCU !!! and don’t even bother reporting it because the school is not going to do anything about it. 97% of the departments don’t pick up their phone calls or even answer emails if you’re lucky you might get a reply in a month and don’t even get me started on the housing department horrible!!! and I’m in one of the most recent constructed housing but we keep having issues with everything the shower water is brown so I had to get a filtered shower head and communication is terrible I worked in a daycare and the toddlers had better communication in all, This is a place I wouldn’t even recommend to my worst enemy pls for the sake of your mental health don’t come here i have just been here for a semester and I’m considering transferring out I feel horrible because I was so happy to come here', 'If the way the admissions department and certain advisors ignore calls and emails indicates the experience my son will have going to this school I may have to transfer him out ASAP. If you have a question about admissions don’t bother calling and leaving a message because they will not call you back. Advisors ignore emails as well. I don’t know what year this school went down hill but it’s starting off horribly for my son who is about to start school. I went to this school in 2004 and it IS NOT the same. It seems they need new staff and training courses for their employees.', 'The on-boarding  process  was a tad bit cumbersome,  but much much better than other schools.
The environment  was serene  and  the students  were  more welcoming.
So far so good!', 'I was so proud and filled with excitement when I got accepted to DSU back in 1998. I attended from 98-2000 and was heartbroken that I had decided to leave, due to issues with my student loans not being dispersed in a timely manner, or at all. My mother had to drive down from Newark, Delaware and give one of the ladies in the financial aid office a lesson in math, and before you know it, I got my last few classes paid for and a refund before transferring to the University of Delaware, which was an absolutely better decision.

What also broke my heart was seeing all these beautiful black and brown people, with so much promise, throw away their futures to keep up some image, and mentality from the streets. Fights and shootings were normal occurrences and I just had to go.

I hope it’s gotten much better, and the leadership there understands that they have a piece of the future if Black America in their hands, that they have an opportunity to help mold and forge into what can potentially help advance and have an immense and powerful impact for future generations of all (and especially black and brown) people in this country and future generations to come.', 'The WORST school I have EVER come across as a student. Their communication is horrible, the right hand has no idea what the left is doing, they always promise things will improve and things will happen but they NEVER do! Example 1, ECHS or ECS, which is DSUs attempt to draft high school kids into DSU, was suppose to be held at a temporary placement at an old hotel for its first year, they have been open now for about ten years. I was told they were suppose to start an FNP program this fall and that they only need a director but its "gonna start" 2024 fall semester. Still no such program that is active. Spoke with numerous faculty there during the spring/summer, to prepare for the fall 2024 semester, at least 10, still til this day I have no idea who my counselor was suppose to be, they never told me. I personally know a student at ECS class of 24', which is ran by DSU, who got a FULL RIDE AND TURNED IT DOWN!!!! Why? You guessed it, a clustered mess with horrible communication. How awful are you when students would rather pass up a full ride then deal with the chaos! Look at their pass rate of students and their retention rates. HORRIBLE once again!!! I myself was accepted to DSU, but I was so frustrated I rescinded my application because to start on a good step was just impossible with lack of good support from faculty. Look at the stats if you don't believe me. The are federally mandated to report. I ended up going to another University in Wilmington who is nationally accredited and my lowest grade in all of my classes is a 97%. I bust my butt and the communication is great, staff is responsive and NOT using student helplines ran by students who really don't know about classes or what it involves for each major and apparently staff. You call the school I chose and you actually talk to faculty and not just have to put in case numbers and emails and hope to get it resolved eventually. O and when I originally went into a "mandatory" meeting in Dover, DE. I was told o it,s not mandatory to be here. So missed work for no reason. O and was told by admissions, this class "should" work!!!! Talked to ANOTHER faculty member who said no that won't work who told you that, O ADMISSIONS did!!!!! Unreal, I took a whole summer semester to get ready for DSU, and I took a losses of time and a monetary value, but then I'll deal with that than unorganized chaos. Go somewhere else!!!!! You have been warned.']

name: University of Delaware
reviews:
['U Delaware tour for our daughter, who recently got an acceptance letter. Figured we should visit to help her consider if she’s actually interested!', 'Worthless degrees. I had to pay $2000 to take a class where all we did was create a LinkedIn profile. Because learning LinkedIn is a skill needed for a masters in finance. Administration never answers the phone. Never calls back when you leave voicemails. If you graduate, be prepared to be harassed for money endlessly regardless of whether you want it or not.', 'My wife went here. She seems to have had a dandy good old time. I suspect under age drinking occurred. But should say she is very successful now, so clearly some teaching happened as well.', 'Went here to attend a band competition. The baked goods here were awesome!! Very nice stadium and seem like a pretty nice area as well.', "My Amazing Experience at the University of Delaware!
I can't say enough good things about my time at the University of Delaware. Choosing a college is a huge decision, and I feel so lucky that I ended up here. It truly has been the perfect place for me to grow, learn, and make lifelong friends.

The academics are top-notch. I was challenged in my classes, but the professors were always so supportive and accessible. They're not just experts in their fields; they genuinely care about their students' success. I always felt like they were invested in me and my future, which made a huge difference. The variety of programs and research opportunities available is incredible, and I felt well-prepared for my career path long before graduation.

Beyond the classroom, the campus itself is just beautiful. Walking through the Green is something I never got tired of. There's always something happening on campus, from club activities and sporting events (Go Blue Hens!) to concerts and festivals. It has a vibrant, energetic atmosphere, but it still feels like a close-knit community. I found my people here and made memories I'll cherish forever.

Newark is also the perfect college town. Main Street has everything you need—great coffee shops for studying, amazing restaurants, and cute shops. It's all right there, within walking distance.

If you're looking for a university that offers a fantastic education, a lively and welcoming campus culture, and a true sense of community, I wholeheartedly recommend the University of Delaware. It's an experience I wouldn't trade for anything."]

name: Goldey-Beacom College
reviews:
['Unique small college experience.

The campus is beautiful year-round. All classes are held within one large building, and professors are engaging and have experience in the subjects they teach.

Excellent campus setup for dorm residents, commuters, and working professionals alike; quick access to classes, not to mention easy & FREE parking!

I love the new library setup. Great study areas and new study pods. Even though most study resources are available online, I enjoy using the library to catch afternoon rays by the windows while studying and sharing ideas & experiences with fellow students & faculty.

I highly recommend GBC! ⚡️📚💻📝🏫❤️🎓', 'Great school!! My sons high school plays their home games there. Definitely going to look into it when he graduates.', 'Daughter loves it, I love it.  Great college.  Small, affordable, and they have so much to offer the students.  Feels like my daughters second home.

She is on scholarship for volleyball and was loved watching he play.  The atmosphere during the games was so much fun.  Campus is really beautiful during the fall season.', 'The best four years of my life, surrounded by the most genuine, intelligent, and compassionate faculty and staff. There’s a reason why so many faculty members are still there!

10/10 would recommend!', 'Great school for adults seeking a business degree. The 7 week accelerated classes are great for full time working adults. It would have taken me double the time to complete the degree at Del-Tech.']

name: Wilmington University
reviews: ['Less online learning and more in person learning, the campus is a ghost town. Where are all the people, so can have a real college experience and network.', 'Would like to see the school be a stronger, more consistent neighbor. There are occasional issues like litter in the surrounding area, and while the school does support some local programs, the way that support is handled can feel uncertain and hard for community groups to plan around. There also seem to be inconsistencies in how the school addresses certain neighborhood-adjacent matters, and more transparency and consistency would go a long way. Overall, we hope the school takes a more proactive approach to partnering with and supporting the local community.', 'Worst institute where I lost my 3 years. They made scam and did fraud with us. They said Business Analytics is a STEM degree. But suddenly some of the students got RFE as our institute is not STEM. Then university did not help any of them. They informed to the authority that they will not be STEM anymore. But we invested our 3 years as a STEM course. But they did not support us for this issue. They blamed on USCIS and did not make any formal email as it will be an evidence. Then again we keep so many evidence. But still they ruined our life', 'Excellent environment to study and excel. Enhanced courses and tailored teaching. Instructors with much expertise. Amazing university for career growth and skill development.', "You won't get a job in cybersecurity. Don't believe what they tell you. I fell for it. Get a degree in something that is in-demand. The market is way oversaturated with people that want to get in the field. Entry level jobs want 5 years of experience. It's a joke. They can be demanding because there's hundreds of people for every 1 job out there. Please do literally anything else."]

name: American University
reviews:
['I love American University. My daughter just graduated with a BA in international studies and minors in environmental science and computer science.  The college is located in s safe area of DC, the research professors in the international studies school are passionate and the school also has semester abroad, which is an amazing programs to Brussels (UN) and other part of the world. Highly recommend this college; money well spent.', 'American University — Washington, D.C.

American University is a beautiful, well-organized, and intellectually vibrant campus located in one of the most livable areas of Washington, D.C. The architecture blends classic collegiate style with modern facilities, creating an atmosphere that feels both traditional and forward-looking. The main quad is peaceful, filled with trees and well-maintained lawns, and it’s common to see students studying outdoors when the weather is pleasant.

Academically, AU stands out for its commitment to global engagement and interdisciplinary education. The professors are approachable, and many of them bring real-world policy and legal experience into the classroom. The Washington College of Law, in particular, has excellent resources for students pursuing careers in international law, business law, and technology law. The campus is also well connected to downtown D.C. via the Metro and several shuttle routes, making it convenient to attend events, internships, or professional meetings around the city.

Outside academics, the environment feels inclusive and community-oriented. The student services are efficient, the library is open late, and the athletic facilities are modern and well kept. Cafeteria food is decent by university standards, and there are good coffee spots nearby. Overall, American University provides an excellent balance of academic rigor, professional opportunity, and a comfortable, welcoming atmosphere for students from around the world.', "We only took the college tour so take everything with a grain of salt.
We loved that AU has a traditional college layout with quad and everything even though it is still with DC.
Almost all the facilities look new and well kept. They had the nicest dorm rooms as well.
They had the best orientation of all the schools we've gone to so far. Molly, our guide, was great.", "American University is a special place, in every iteration of the word haha. The people and teachers are unique, the education is rigorous, the campus is compact and beautiful, the facilities can be a hit or miss but are overall good, and much more. There's always something to complain about, but that's the case anywhere. I enjoyed my four years here!", "American is a gem of a school tucked into a remote section of DC.  It's a super safe area.
If your look for a quaint school with big city resources AU is the perfect blend."]

name: The Catholic University of America
reviews: ["The Catholic University of America, anchored at its sprawling and serene campus at 620 Michigan Ave NE, is consistently portrayed in my community and professional circles as a unique crossroads of timeless tradition and modern intellectual discovery. From numerous thoughtful exchanges with alumni and local scholars, it is merytorically evident that CUA offers a substantive and deeply supportive environment, frequently lauded by my acquaintances for its exceptional ability to integrate rigorous classical philosophy with high-level research in fields like architecture, social work, and canon law. It is truly commendable to observe how the institution maintains such a transparent and respectful dedication to its foundational values while actively engaging with the contemporary challenges of the nation's capital, a quality that many people I know personally cite as the defining reason for the school’s lasting influence. Ultimately, in the collective view of informed D.C. residents, the university stands as a distinguished hallmark of moral and academic leadership, rightfully respected for its elegant ability to foster a community of scholars who are as ethically grounded as they are intellectually ambitious.", 'I am a healthcare traveler from New Jersey, working at MedSTAR hospital for a few months and noticed this beautiful campus not far, so spent a few hours walking around and enjoying the architecture, the memorial statues and the Basilica Cathedral. Seems like a great location with the easy access from several points and if you’re looking for a great place to do a walk or explore, definitely worth your time to visit this location. Looking forward to it touring the inside of the Basilica next time I visit there. Definitely opportunities for some awesome photos.', 'Beautiful campus with nice open space & convenient access from Brookland/CUA Metro Station. We walked through the campus from Metro to the Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception.', 'Great Orientation days!!!! Very well organized. I feel blessed to be able to send my kid this school.', 'Beautiful European style Catholic Basilicata. Highly recommend a visit with a hour or two to walk around.']

name: University of the District of Columbia
reviews:
['If I could give this place negative stars I would, my biggest regret in life is going to this school. From the staff, to the head of the school they’re all absolutely incompetent. I need a copy my of transcripts for the past month I’ve been calling the school and not a single office answers, either by phone or email. All the staff does is sit on their behind and collect checks. This place is a disgrace to academics.', 'Honestly, apply to another university. Don’t go here. You may not graduate or end up wasting a huge amount of time /money trying to get into the right classes and not having much direction from counselors. I got my BA in another state but I’ve decided to take an entry level chem class this Fall 2025. I applied to this school on June 7th as a non-degree student. I submitted my transcript & got an email to allow 2 weeks for admissions to process it. Great. A month later, and I heard nothing. So I called and emailed the admissions office and no one responded. No one answered my emails or voicemails. I had to take time off work to show up in person to the student registration office. The front desk was curt & unfriendly. The student counselor who came to see me acted like I was the inconvenience. (There were no other students in the office). She told me they didn’t have my application and then found it in 2 minutes after actually looking up my name. She asked for my transcripts and then found them when she again looked up my name. Then she actually admitted me to the school. She gave me no further steps. Didn’t offer me a contact to registering for classes (I have found you need admin approval to register for classes). I had to look it all up myself only to be told the online info was outdated. I finally got a hold of a student success advisor. It’s been a full week of me calling and emailing him to ask for him to put me into an ‘intro to chem class’. I have had to call and email him every day to hopefully get a little closer to registering for an entry level class. I provided him my transcripts, the exact classes I wanted, and reached out to the professors and he has emailed me a 4th time to ask me yet again what classes I would like to register for. I’m losing my mind. This whole process has taken so long that I might not be able to register on time for this fall semester. I am a full grown adult who is good at administration and I worry how any beginner student can successfully register & excel in this school when staff is incompetent & offer no assistance whatsoever. If I could advise you, I would tell you to apply to a school with staff that is excited & helpful to register you. And no, this staff is not over worked. They have about 3,000 students to look after. My last university had 35,000 and they were far more helpful and responsive. UDC needs to step it up. I’m so disappointed.
Update: The Student Success Advisor got me registered for classes. I start next Monday. So far, no staff that has registered me has directed me to any sort of student orientation packet. So i’ll have to ask & find out but by bit how their student portal works. Just not feeling set up for success.', "Udc's tuition is competitively priced. I've been fortunate enough to get my undergrad here. Parking can be hassle but overall the goal is education and that you will get here.", "There are some good professors and lots of nice people, but the people in charge of administration are the worse, the worse in the sense that you never hear from them when you need them. They don't answer emails or calls, you have to Google what they look like and try to catch them around their office just to get your answer. Not professional at all.", 'UDC sells itself on affordability, and while it is indeed the cheapest school in the city this is for a reason. UDC is a LAST RESORT SCHOOL.

While this place is indeed accredited and has some qualified professionals, the institution ideology is more focused on collecting federal dollars and grant money than providing a meaningful opportunity to achieve professional success after college. I did not fulfill my goals BECAUSE of UDC, but more so in SPITE of their best efforts to make every step of the process as painful as possible.

The administrative arm of this institution seems hellbent on making the lives of any student who dares come ask for help into the equivalent of torture. Communication is universally nonexistent and the ubiquitous "SYSTEM" they use to address your concerns is ALWAYS "down". Financial Aid will ALWAYS be late. Student Accounts will charge out-of-state tuition to an in-state student, while their account literally says in-state designation, for 4 years with no recourse even from the President of the University himself. They won't even APOLOGIZE for charging someone tens of thousands of dollars extra. Student Accounts will hold onto private loan money 3+ months after it has been disbursed to the school, while giving no indication that they ever received the money and continuing to threaten and harass for payment. They will put multiple separate administrative holds on a paid-cleared account to prevent registration even when in totally good standing, and since that system is down they cannot remove the holds or even tell you why it is still there. Nobody even knows who removes them apparently.

Using the online support ticket is useless because it is seldom that somebody contacts you about the request you submitted.

Advisors will force you to take unnecessary classes that are not on your program schedule, sometimes multiple times. At the same time, and despite advising being mandatory before every. single. semester, you cannot rely on the advisors to give meaningful advice that will assure you have the credits you need to graduate on time.

Research professors are largely not engaging their students in the experience, which is weird considering how small the STEM cohort is in relation to the amount of faculty. Most don't come to campus the required 4 days a week and none of them are consistently on time.

The school of engineering only announces guest speakers the same (or next) day they are speaking; same goes with scholarships, internships, and career opportunities. Despite most of these kind of things taking a few days to complete the application or plan for they usually give you less than 24 hours.

My professor and department chair, Dr Paul Cotae, had no qualms disparaging my desired career path; even going so far as to call me greedy and lazy; and if this is not indicative of the faculty culture it is also worth mention that professors do not return grades for assignments and some not even for tests. But that is ok, because you could do absolutely nothing but show up in most of these courses and still get a B! Some professors like Dr Hongmei Dang bump all grades a letter by default, counting an 80% as an A and 70% as a B!

There are no meaningful professional development opportunities for the engineering school despite it being one of the largest and best-funded on campus. There is zero alumni involvement, no employment drives for seniors, and the only real shot the school provides Engineers at helping you seek the career you desire is at a single STEM conference (BEYA) that one could attend on their own and free of charge. Very few employers visit campus to hire or pipeline talent despite being surrounded by some of the biggest firms in the world.

This is a LAST RESORT SCHOOL!']

name: Gallaudet University
reviews: ['Awesome stay and felt comfortable. Reading and speaking sign helped. Could learn more, yet I have what I need. Thanks for the stay. Remember the golden lock that I had left and the note. Pursue your dreams. Charlie.', 'Gallaudet University is a beautiful, outstanding, cultured giant of innovation. I cannot say enough good things about it. It is located on FL avenue in DC. It is 144miles from central va. There is on campus housing, and off campus options.  The school has a vast history and a bright future. Absolutely amazing.', 'Surprising find in DC. Clean and welcoming. Unfortunately my toilet tank ran all night and leaf blowers on campus woke me up before 8:00am. Had no idea that there was a National Deaf Life museum in DC that is on campus as well.', "Great campus and even better institution for the deaf/hard of hearing. I visited the campus after taking a class in ASL because I was just very interested and wanted to explore the famous university itself! They use American Sign Language as their first language. Gallaudet University is truly a safe and open space for the deaf/hard of hearing. It's also located in a great spot and many people living in DC actually know how to sign!", 'I had an interaction with a person named Christine Wood, I would hate to say my interaction has been nothing but rude, condescending and discriminatory. I do not believe this university stands for racism and values diversity. Wish the administration would do something about these types of behavior.']

name: George Washington University
reviews:
['George Washington University, strategically anchored at 2121 I St NW, is frequently characterized in my professional and social circles as a premier "metropolitan powerhouse" where the Foggy Bottom campus acts as a seamless extension of the nation’s political and financial nerve centers. From numerous insightful dialogues with alumni and faculty members, it is merytorically evident that GW offers a substantive, high-velocity environment that my acquaintances consistently praise for its unparalleled ability to place students at the literal doorstep of the White House, IMF, and State Department. It is truly impressive to observe how the institution maintains such a transparent and respectful dedication to global engagement, a quality that is widely recognized as the primary engine behind its reputation for producing graduates who are exceptionally savvy in the realms of international affairs and public policy. Many individuals I know personally highlight the university's sophisticated Elliott School of International Affairs as a distinguished hallmark of academic excellence, proving that the institution excels in translating theoretical classroom concepts into real-world diplomatic influence. In the broader consensus of the D.C. community, GW stands as a vital and forward-thinking pillar of higher education, rightfully respected for its elegant ability to cultivate a diverse student body that is both intellectually ambitious and civically responsible. Ultimately, this institution remains a top-tier choice for those seeking a dynamic educational journey that is as much about professional networking as it is about rigorous scholarly pursuit.', 'I graduated here in 1986, and decided to take a walk around campus to see how it had changed. Well, with time some changes occur...the Marvin Center has been stripped of the Marvin appelation, as his mores were inconsistent with what GW stands for now. A majority of the buildings I recall are still standing, if refaced and repurposed.

The campus feel is still intimate. It looks like a welcoming place.', "G.W.U. is a sprawling campus occupying a large area of Foggy Bottom. It's one of the top rated universities in the country. It's a pretty active landscape that typically relys on
the students and State Department employees that encompass much of the area.", 'Not much of a campus like you’d find at a normal college, but the area is decent and mostly clean. The subway stop is right there which is convenient as can be. Huge hospital right there and numerous stores and places to sit around.', "If I could I would give The George Washington University negative -5 star rating. One of the teachers at the university made an extremely racist video talking about how she purposely over charges people of a different race  and gives free service to people thats the same race as her. I reported it to the university and they just ignored it.
