I've had other people who attended the university admit that they've been treated poorly there because of their race and their reports were ignored too. I filed a report and did things the correct way only to be ignored like the 4 other people before me so I've decided to let it be known to the public so they know not to let their kids go there and  become victims too. SHAME ON YOU GEORGE WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY YOU FAILED."]

name: Georgetown University
reviews: ['This campus is surprisingly massive and beautiful. Very prestigious school and beautiful buildings onsite. All around cool place and the location is ideal to local shopping and dining options', 'Georgetown University, anchored by the iconic Healy Hall at 3700 O St NW, is consistently characterized in my professional and social circles as a premier crucible of global diplomacy where a substantive Jesuit heritage seamlessly integrates with high-level international discourse. From numerous insightful dialogues with local policy influencers and successful alumni, it is merytorically evident that the institution provides a high-caliber, intellectually rigorous environment, frequently lauded by my acquaintances for its exceptional ability to bridge the gap between ethical philosophy and real-world political application. It is truly heartening to observe how the university maintains such a transparent and respectful dedication to the "Cura Personalis" principle, a quality that the broader community recognizes as a vital catalyst for the profound sense of civic duty found in its graduates. Many people I know personally emphasize the school\'s sophisticated synthesis of historic prestige and a forward-looking, globally-relevant curriculum as a distinguished hallmark of academic excellence. Ultimately, in the collective view of informed D.C. residents, Georgetown stands as an unrivaled pillar of intellectual and moral leadership, rightfully respected for its elegant ability to shape the next generation of global visionaries.', 'This review is on the campus and walkability of Georgetown University, not the academics, which are indisputably excellent. That said, the campus is a bit worn and in need of some renovations. It’s on a hill so you will get your exercise if you walk here. The buildings are almost all brick with forgettable architecture. Of course the nearby city of Georgetown is lovely and lively so there’s that.', 'Beautiful campus well maintained. Although old it still has many modern buildings and they are always improving. Lots of history there. No subway stop at the campus but nonetheless is worth going over there. Campus bookstore is huge.', "For the record, I didn't go to school here, but I've only heard good things. From a tourist's perspective, there's plenty of neat architecture on campus. It's in one of the older sections of Washington DC, so definitely worth checking out."]

name: Howard University
reviews: ['Howard University is an outstanding institution with strong academic programs and a vibrant intellectual environment. The quality of teaching and research is excellent, and the university offers programs that are both rigorous and impactful. The academic and administrative staff are friendly, supportive, and genuinely helpful, making the overall experience very positive. Howard provides not only a great education but also a strong sense of community and support for student success.', 'Everyone was very helpful. The campus felt very inclusive. Reliable public transportation for students & faculty.', 'Today I went to drop off my niece who’s continuing her second year of pre-med. the experience was amazing. I love how supportive the staff is. They have smooth transition process during moving in season. They were very well organized and had keys, moving carts, parking permits and guidance everywhere. I noticed that minorities are the majority at Howard. Diversity is embraced and everyone is welcomed and respected. I loved how they have sanitation stations everywhere fondue to Covid-19. The application process is easy and they financial aid staff is very helpful. Howard university os affordable and well known school. The dorms are spacious and private. Kitchen is well organized and the bathroom is huge. Campus was a little crowded because it was moving in day, but it was so organized that by 2pm everyone was situated and the streets were cleaned. I recommend this university.', "Howard University is in the process of changing, improving and increasing their level of services they offer their community. GoodLove this place. Had a good experience here. Enjoyed the homecoming Saturday with my daughter. I missed my high school's homecoming but enjoyed Howard's. Sorry DCs Dunbar had to go to the Mecca.Great institution for higher learning. Homecoming 2019 was fun, except for the score of the game.This campus was really nice. The college presentation was concise and thorough.  The presenter seemed knowledgeable and engaging.It seems to be a great place offering a lot of opportunities for young adults of color. Our tour guide was a young lady who is a senior at the school and she was so articulate and presented the information in a way that conveyed her knowledge of the school and also how much you really enjoyed going there. The students on the campus all seemed very happy and friendly.", 'I was on campus for their Homecoming Invocation. It was a very uplifting service. The vocalists were outstanding. The liturgical dancers moved the entire room. The soaker Re. Dr. Michael Eric Dyson was phenomenal.']

name: Trinity Washington University
reviews:
["Beautiful campus with magnificent buildings and statues. Of course you will see Nancy Pelosi's picture in the hallway of the main building!", 'Financially I suppose it’s a decent option but besides that, I cannot come up with any other benefits of attending this school… respectfully. Staff is incredibly hard to get a hold of, they do not care if you’re struggling whether that be in class or mentally. They ignore your emails but when they need something from you, they all of a sudden know how to communicate. You have to make appointments for almost everything, which is understandable, but the appointment time is almost never honored. It seemed more about grades than actually making sure you understood the material.', 'Campus was very pretty but facilities were ageing and  in need of updating. The main issue however were the staff, with the exception of one or two kind ladies in the cafeteria they were exceedingly unhelpful and disrespectful.

Whatever small issue was raised with them, they responded with an agressive attitude and would chastise you for raising an issue with them in the first place.', 'I am a current student at Trinity Washington University and I definitely don’t feel the same way about this school, as i did a few months ago when I started. The school isn’t the worst but I would not say that you get the feeling of a good college experience. I am currently thinking about transferring to another school. So that I don’t create a long review for others to read I will give a bullet overview of what does on/why i want to leave:

- The administration as a whole are not very cooperative, nor do they know how to really help you. Advisors just repeat the same information that you could have found in the Trinity website.
- The food is NOT good. I have seen dining hall workers take food from the dining hall and take it over to the deli which is one building away and charge more for it. They give you a better sandwich if your using flex dollars, but they give a basic sandwich if your using your meal plan.
- Security is not consistent, they pretty much let anyone on campus and don’t ask the necessary questions before having a car proceed to drop off/pick up or parking.
- There are no water fountains in the freshman dorm, which i feel is a health hazard. I feel, if they can get a dollar out of me then they will. It’s either $1.25 - 1.75 for a bottle of water in the freshman building, and Laundry is $1.50 to dry and another $1.50 to dry.

My first semester of freshman year it was clear that the dean didn’t like my professor so she would try and get us to say things negating about her, she would observe her teaching more than i’ve ever seen, and before the second semester was to start she quit.

Trinity is nice in the brochures, and online, but if you come here you will soon realize unfortunately everything is not as it seems.', 'the worst school i have ever been to. All they care about is the money they get from you. the staff are no help at all. community collage appears to be better. the professors are good but the people in the office are rude and mean and all they do is sit around while they drink coffee and talk about their personal life. for any question i asked the answer i got was "I dont know". i am glad i left when i had the chance.']

name: Baptist University of Florida
reviews: ["Baptist University of Florida (BUF) is a private Christian university located in Graceville, Florida, based in Orlando also operates online focusing on Christian values. The academic experience has been for me amazing highly qualified teachers, allowing for more personalized accompaniment during the learning process. The university has accreditation that supports the validity of its academic programs. It's amazing the academic experience I've had and how my global vision has expanded. Thank you for allowing me to belong.", 'I graduated from BUF with a Master’s degree in Theological Studies and am currently pursuing my doctorate at the institution. My experience has been excellent. BUF is a strong academic institution that is clearly rooted in a biblical worldview, which was very important to me. The professors are supportive, knowledgeable, and genuinely invested in their students’ growth, both academically and spiritually. One of BUF’s greatest strengths is its language programs. Students can take classes not only in English, but also in Spanish, Portuguese, and French, which makes the school accessible to a diverse and global student body. I highly recommend BUF to anyone seeking a Christ-centered education with solid academic support.', 'Baptist University of Florida has been an excellent place to pursue my master’s degree. I am very grateful for the scholarship opportunity and for their full accreditation, which reflects the high academic standards of the university. They accepted my international degree without difficulty, and the professors are outstanding knowledgeable, supportive, and truly invested in student success. I highly recommend this university to anyone seeking quality education in a supportive environment.', 'I’ve had a wonderful experience as a student at Baptist University of Florida. The professors are supportive, approachable, and truly invested in student success. The university values faith, excellence, and personal growth. I can’t recommend BUF enough.', 'I have learned so much and grown exponentially in my faith from being here. So thankful for the Lord’s provision in bringing me here! The staff care about you on a personal level and are so encouraging!']

name: Barry University
reviews:
['What can I say: I love Barry. Even though I live way up here in Jax, I commuted down there for classes once a month. It was worth it to me. I’m in the PhD nursing program and I can say it really changed my life. Dr. Jessie Colin, who is also my chair, is the most intelligent and remarkable person I have ever met. The 5 stars is for her and how she is running the doctoral program. Thank you Dr. Colin! The rest of the nursing faculty are also wonderful. Lovely women (too many to name). I’m so glad I made the decision to come to this school. I’ve learned so much that this post would be too long to describe it all! It’s an intellectually challenging program, so be ready to learn.

This school in general really focuses on social justice. If you are not open minded to multi-culturalism and discovering new ways of thinking outside of the norm, this may not be the school for you. I tell people this because I know how the culture is in America today (ignorance is bliss). You have to accept to live the ‘Barry Life’, which is being open to culture and seeking justice for those whose voices might go unheard.

Like some say on other reviews, yes, the area in which the school is in is kinda sketchy. And be prepared, the student parking is awful. The biggest parking lot is a couple blocks away and you have to take a shuttle to get to the campus. It’s a small campus but quite beautiful.', "This school is amazing and not so intense, however it is a very thorough university with its curriculum, and their graduate success rate is very high. I graduated with my bachelor's 2022...now I'm enrolling for the master's program in Aug 2024. I have no doubt I will be in position for another graduation. Go BarryU🎉🎉🎉", 'The University itself is gorgeous, but the area right next to it is really bad I never felt safe they only have security in the front and occasionally in the back. The Motrom Doss hall rooms smelled like mold and I got charged a lot for unnecessary things. Rude RA’s and staff. The program and schooling was really good as well as the professors. But if you want to go to this school you’re better off living off campus.', 'It depends on the program. The health sciences are the toughest, but for a reason; nursing students told me they all received a solid education, that gave them a level of education, very much superior to the level of other nursing programs. I hope I will have a similar experience once I finish my program. The campus is absolutely beautiful. Serene and peaceful, great and beautifully restored art deco architecture, surrounded by stunning local vegetation. Some corners of various buildings demonstrate the original campus feel from the days it was built,  but restored and updated to the standards of tomorrow. So far, though one of my professors was extremely tough, it has been a wonderful experience.(can not comment on housing; I live off campus)', 'Like most schools, they’re more concerned with money and debts than education. VETERANS BEWARE- DO NOT utilize your G.I. Bill benefits here- they always find a way to tell you owe more.']

name: Bethune-Cookman University
reviews: ['Had the pleasure to visit Bethune -Cookman University in Daytona Beach to speak with the Marketing Class of Dr. Eboni Rainey Haynes. The Campus was easy to find and the Dean of Staff was a pleasure to speak with. Pouring into the students about our Entrepreneurial marketing journey in Financial  Services and as a Financial Adviser was uplifting and rewarding. We thank BCU for welcoming @URFinancial Physicians', 'The choir came out to my senior living community in Longwood, FL and had me in tears before they hit chorus! I cannot understand the power that came from those voices. It was a JOYFUL NOISE to say the least and we all truly enjoyed that Sunday visit! May God bless each and every one of you that traveled to our community for this event!!!!', "Daytona Bike Week is awesome and Detroit Randy's Antique motorcycle show is great.", "Loved every moment of the tour. We visited while vacationing Daytona Beach. The staff was absolutely amazing. So friendly, the students as well. Corey was our tour guide and she is vibrant and genuine. My son got to see the dorms. He met the band director. The band students played for us. The greek life was explained in detail. It really made my son's vacation. I can't explain the look of anticipation and joy in his eyes.  Thank you.", 'Visit with new students, friends and family.  Visually a lovely campus. Facilties at the one dorm visited Benson Annex, included unfinished repairs, Being an advance group of athletes and teams, I feel their rooms should have been completely finished. Also, 3  visits over 3 days the elevators  were never cleaned, even though floors in rhe common areas were.\nImprovement is warranted to present this great school to the bestadvantage!']

name: Lynn University
reviews:
['I wish I could say how the classes were but dealing with the admissions department alone made me withdraw from the school altogether. This was my first time going back to school in a long time. I was anxious and stressed already and then there was problem after problem with admissions until ultimately they dropped all my classes without my knowledge. Because of the complete nightmare of an experience that I had with this school, I’ve given up on pursuing a higher education altogether.', 'We went to the concert given by the students and their teachers
It was as good as being in the n y philharmonic orchestra and a lot cheaper by hundreds of dollars

This past Saturday we went to the smaller room in the concert to see a play of Onb by the students and everything works
It was a result of energy and the people who had the ability to remember their lines  for example it was based on the fact that the star of the show became an anonymous advice collomistf. Aka ann lander she annsserzs  lettertt from the trouble people who are in trouble and she has.to  speaking for the. entire  show giodI', 'Lynn offers  a wonderful, safe and beautiful learning experience with a unique approach to scheduling.', "I have attended school here for 3 years and have had nothing but awful experiences. To start, the food is not as good as you hear. Many of my friends freshman year including me got food poisoning multiple times. To add, the financial aid office is AWFUL. They are horrible with communications and have screwed me over more times than I can count. Moving on, my academic advisor has also done nothing to screw me over. I am ending up having to take another year of undergrad because there was so much miscommunication on her part about what classes I needed to take, if I was on track or not, etc. If you take a look at some statistics about Lynn, you will noticed that the acceptance rate is 80% but the graduation rate is 51%. After freshman year, so many students transfer out of lynn because it is not a great school. Another thing that Lynn doesn't tell incoming freshman is that credits DO NOT transfer. That means that if you go through 1 or 2 or even 3 years and want to transfer out, it is almost impossible to get your credits transfer. You would pretty much have to start all over at another school as a freshman. Lynn is totally not worth all the money I have given to this school. I do love the location and being close to the beach, West Palm Beach, and Fort Lauderdale, but other than that I cannot say another good about Lynn. If you are thinking about coming to Lynn, PLEASE do your research about it and ask your admissions counselor so many questions.", 'Beautiful campus. New baseball and softball complexes.']

name: Eastern Florida State College
reviews:
['Eastern Florida State sponsors a youth golf camp in the summer. It is a top-notch program for FREE. The entire staff and volunteers are THE BEST! Kids have an opportunity to learn about golf, respect, and other critical values that are needed for life skills. Thank you for the opportunity. The campus is also very clean, and landscaping is beautiful. The staff is extremely nice and helpful!', "📚Great Teachers📚

I learned so much during my time at EFSC. The classes feel small and specialized, with teachers that really do invest in the success of the students. Through the honor societies, clubs, and opportunities afforded, I was able to achieve my academic goals and graduate satisfied with my investment.

The Cocoa campus is larger than the Titusville campus with more buildings and space. There's a three-story library, a TV station, and entire buildings dedicated to specific specializations, such as health science, veterinary nursing, or HVAC. From art classes and theater, to welding and phlebotomy, there's a bit of everything here. There are also frequent on-campus events to enjoy, including food vendors, live performances, and games.", 'I was told when I enrolled that we would be able to keep our titan e-mails for good, no end. Now after I have already signed up for MULTIPLE accounts with this e-mail address do I get an e-mail saying it would be permanently deleted. Way to keep your word.', "I haven't frequented many community colleges, so I don't know how this truly stacks up. It's clearly an older building, but it seems as though they do the best with what they have, and they seem to do that well. All professors I've met save for one were outstanding, with the exception having the best intentions I'm sure. The campus Cafe is surprisingly decent. Library is oddly empty but also large and available for study, computer access, and printing. The bookstore is small but has friendly staff and most essentials on offer. Student advisors have been helpful, again, save for one. No real complaints here.", '(Alumni review) The EMT/ medic program here has some of the coolest instructors/adjuncts/professors....everyone there is really cool and super professional!']

name: Broward College
reviews:
['Extremely Frustrating Admissions & Enrollment Experience at Broward College
I was originally excited to enroll at Broward College because of their healthcare pathway, especially the Respiratory Care program. What should have been a straightforward enrollment process turned into months of stress, wasted money, and constant delays.
I had to send my transcripts almost five times because Broward kept claiming the documents were “unreadable” or that I was still enrolled in a class I actually completed several semesters ago. This incorrect information blocked me from registering for the semester I wanted. The worst part? Each transcript costs $10, and Broward kept misinterpreting something every other Florida school processed in under three days with zero issues.
The long waits weren’t just online the wait times in the building are ridiculous too. You can be in the cut line for one to three hours just to talk to someone for five minutes. The system is slow, unorganized, and honestly feels like they don’t value students’ time at all.
And this is what I don’t understand:
Why can’t Broward just evaluate the credits I’ve already completed, add them to my degree plan, and then evaluate any new transcripts after I finish the next classes?
That’s how nearly every other college handles transfer credits. It’s simple, it’s logical, and it works. But Broward makes it way harder than necessary.
On top of that, if you’re coming from out of state, be prepared to use almost all of your financial aid just to attend even though their degree completion rates and credit outcomes are not impressive. The value doesn’t match the cost at all.
To make things worse, I even had to schedule a mandatory Zoom meeting just to get registered, which is something no other college required. From the administration building to financial aid to enrollment, every step felt like another obstacle.
Broward was my first choice, but after nearly five months of waiting for them to properly read a standard transcript, I honestly don’t want to attend anymore. No student should have to jump through this many hoops just to enroll.', 'I tried several times to help my daughter access the schedule for classes. No one would answer the phone or answer questions. So we chose another college. Now we’re getting sales calls weekly. What a joke', 'Nothing about this school is good, especially not good enough to require me to download and app on my phone to access the student portal
Definitely not higher education, you think you are some fancy school, absolutely delusional', 'Do not waste your money or time in this place, it’s better to pay more and go somewhere else. I had the worst experience in this place. Their customer service is terrible, cant get a hold of someone, the people you talk to know absolutely nothing so trying to get help is almost impossible. They also made me paid twice for a class when I did nothing wrong, I was withdrawn from a course without notice, even after completing all assignments. If I could give them 0 stars I would. So unprofessional and a waste of money.', 'I have had nothing but great experiences at BC! I’m just finishing up two years here and am excited to continue with them. They are very accommodating of any financial aid delays that may occur and questions they I have. Most staff are knowledgeable and friendly. BC is always requesting feedback and implementing systems to ensure speedy resolutions. School spirit across all campuses and encouragement from President Haile (through his video messages at the start of each school year) can be felt even as an online student. Congrats on being named top 10 in the nation once again! #BCProud']

name: Albizu University-Miami
reviews:
['From my point of view. To share my experience in my daughter’s graduation October 10 in the JLKC, it was terrible. The escalator and elevator from the parking to the center were broken and my mom had to climb stairs, she is 92 y/o. Then I was discriminated by the guard at the entrance about my purse being too big, I left it in the car and when I came in I saw many ladies with purses the same size as mine , incredible. Then I had to request accommodation for my mom as she could not climb the steps to the seats, for that I received assistance. We were very disappointed about how bad looking the stage for the students was. The video of the students sharing their experiences was ok but they should have rehearsed better, they are supposed to be professionals for crying out loud. Please , spend some money in nice flower arrangements, this school is not cheap and the students deserve better. It was not a pleasant experience over all and again, the students deserve better.', 'Horrible management, the people that work there aren’t qualified or available for students. They never answer the phone. They rather email that give you a call. If you need something you need to be on their back to get it done. Not worth it, very expensive & they only are available to have you registered for the next term', 'I recently reached out to this university to inquire about the Psychology program. Unfortunately, my experience with one of their representatives, Mr. Carlos, was deeply disappointing and unprofessional.

From the beginning, Mr. Carlos responded in a tone that came across as dismissive and somewhat rude. I attempted to explain my academic background and interest in the program, hoping to receive some guidance, but he seemed unwilling to listen or engage in a meaningful conversation. Instead, I was met with what felt like a disrespectful attitude and little to no effort to understand my situation.

When I asked about potential admission requirements—such as the TOEFL or SAT—Mr. Carlos vaguely responded that it would "depend on the academic information" I provided. However, his tone and the way he responded made me feel as if he doubted the legitimacy of my academic experience, which came off as not only unprofessional but borderline discriminatory.

I also made it clear that I was interested in a virtual learning option, as I do not reside in Florida. Despite this, he insisted that any further questions would require an in-person visit, offering no real assistance or alternatives for out-of-state students.

Based on my interaction with Mr. Carlos, I cannot recommend this university to prospective students. First impressions matter, and if this is the level of courtesy and support offered at the inquiry stage, I can only imagine how it would feel to actually be enrolled. His attitude alone was enough for me to reconsider and ultimately decide not to pursue my studies at this university.', "It's not a piece of cake to figure out where to park your car if you never been there before", 'I recently spoke with Mr. Carlos Clavijo regarding the online Bachelor’s in Psychology. I was truly excited to learn more about this program, but unfortunately, the experience was deeply disappointing due to his unprofessional attitude.

First of all, he made remarks suggesting that only “smart” people could finish the course earlier, implying that intelligence was the sole factor. When I pointed out that completing a course faster often depends on how much time someone can dedicate, not just intelligence, he dismissively responded with, “Yes, whatever.” That kind of attitude is condescending and unhelpful.

He then asked if my last name was Chávez, like the president in a condescending tone
—an inappropriate and irrelevant comment. When I requested an email with more information, what I received was five short lines, no subject line, and no real effort to provide details. It lacked any sense of professionalism.

With representatives like this, it’s discouraging to even consider applying. This was a very unfortunate experience, especially for someone genuinely interested in pursuing education.']

name: College of Central Florida
reviews:
["Campus is great, and my overall experience has been nice. It is a community college, so I understand the limited options for student life. Please keep in mind the low ratings professors receive. As a student, I have doubts about my ability to achieve here, given the limited options regarding faculty. CF offers several courses needed for transfer, which is great. However, it would be nice if they provided a better selection of professors to guarantee students' success rate.", "Amazing people are very supportive of the students' well-being and safety. Great place to get started on your college path and get your AA as well as many specialties. Huge focus on students' mental health and small classes. Hoping to get my radiography degree in the long run, the testing staff helped me with a test that helped me figure out what path was best for me! Love this place so many things on campus to check out and always something going on! The professors are the best!", 'we have the most incredible experience using this venue in November. It was exactly what we needed. The staff was so incredibly helpful and resourceful. I have not experienced customer service at this level in a long time so thankful to I’ve had such an incredible experience. The venue is beautiful, clean and priced well. We have already booked our next two events here with the anticipation of more incredible experiences. Thank you CF staff for making this possible.', 'Going to CF has honestly been my biggest regret. I’m a first-time college student and from the very beginning I feel like I was set up to fail. Over the summer, my advisor enrolled me in accelerated online classes that I didn’t even need for my degree and never explained that they were accelerated. I ended up failing two out of four classes and was placed on financial aid probation.
The next semester, I made sure to do everything right. I enrolled in four classes that I actually needed, made sure they were not accelerated, and that they were online since I’m in an online degree program. My Intro to Math class was advertised as a Zoom class when I enrolled while on the phone with my advisor. Once the semester started, I emailed the professor because I couldn’t find the Zoom link. He emailed me back apologizing and told me the class had been changed to in person only.
I live an hour away, work full time, and I’m a full-time parent, so attending in person was not an option. The professor tried to help me and contacted the dean to see if I could be switched to one of his online classes, but it was denied because it conflicted with my English class. Since I couldn’t add or drop at that point, the professor gave me an N to avoid a withdrawal on my record.

I passed all my other classes and worked hard to bring my GPA up from a 1.25 to a 3.0. After final grades were posted, I called the financial aid office to make sure I was off probation. They told me I was good to go and even congratulated me. The very next day, I got an email saying all my financial aid was taken away and that I was now on suspension.
I immediately filed an appeal explaining everything, including the fact that the math class was originally listed as Zoom and changed after the semester started. The professor even emailed financial aid backing me up and confirming this was out of my control. Despite all of that, my appeal was denied with little to no explanation, and my full Pell Grant was taken.
This has taken away financial stability for me and my child and has completely crushed my motivation to continue. The lack of communication, accountability, and consistency at this school is unbelievable. I would not recommend CF to anyone, especially first-time students or parents trying to better their lives.', "I’ve been attending CF for almost a year. Throughout this time, I’ve made every effort to be respectful and reasonable, but my experience has been very disappointing. The level of service and support is poor  many staff members seem unwilling to assist and often pass you off to someone else. When you finally reach the right department or person, you’re often met with frustration or disrespect for simply seeking help.

Additionally, I’ve encountered issues with grading that appear to be based on personal opinions rather than clear academic standards, and there seems to be an overall lack of genuine care for students' education and well-being. Unfortunately, it feels as though many employees are simply there for a paycheck, not to support students.

That said, there have been exceptions — my advisor, Bruno, has been incredibly supportive and one of the few people who genuinely cares and strives to help. I sincerely appreciate his dedication. Sadly, my experience with most others has left me very disappointed.do not go here"]

name: University of Central Florida
reviews:
['The University of Central Florida feels more like a hands-on workshop than a quiet classroom. The pace is fast, the standards are demanding, and there’s little room to stay passive. Professors push hard, peers challenge one another, and by graduation you’ve been tested enough that professional life seems far less intimidating. It isn’t always easy, but that intensity is what drives development — progress comes through pressure.

UC Davis presents a very different atmosphere. Its messaging is polished, the marketing is attractive, and the tone is consistently upbeat. Yet underneath, the structure can feel complicated, momentum can lag, and students may find it easy to coast unless they deliberately push themselves. The culture of UC Davis tends to favor blending in and maintaining harmony rather than questioning assumptions or pressing forward, which can leave some feeling they spent more energy navigating the environment than being refined by it. Students who operate at a higher intensity sometimes feel out of sync with that dynamic.

One university approaches education like a forge. UC Davis treats it more like a display window.

Ultimately, the decision comes down to whether a student wants to be molded through challenge — or supported in comfort.', ".

Positive reviews come from admissions counselors at SOUTH UNIVERSITY. BEWARE!!!!!
I had a really bad experience at South University and yes I would agree with the statements about them being all about the money. I was told my transfer credits were approved, BUT once I was enrolled—signed all documents—then they told me that I had to retake more classes $$$ (again, after being “approved”). Tuition is ridiculous, I was charged well over $4,000 for 2 classes. Now they won’t even release my transcripts until I pay off this amount. BE CAREFUL!!!!
The institution is disorganized, and I got mixed information from different people. I never knew who was in charge of anything....
It all seems smooth and nice until you sign up.

BTW I received both As in my classes, this is an honest review based on my experience and it doesn’t come from “someone who’s not doing what they are supposed to”', 'I am an alumni of South University and I only experienced a great experience. There is a student academic progress process in which the students who are not doing well academically will be given the opportunity to improve their grades. If they do not, they will be academically dismissed from the school. The professors care about the students success and help in any way that they can. I highly recommend South University. The tuition if not cheap, but if you are looking for small classes, individualized attention and success...South University is the school for you. I feel that some people on this forum were not doing what they needed to do to be successful and they should own up to it, not blame the school.', "And the only reason they get three stars is because the professors actually care. name: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University
reviews: ['When discussing the academic landscape of Tallahassee with friends and peers, the conversation inevitably turns toward the profound legacy and modern-day excellence of Florida A&M University on Martin Luther King Jr Blvd. The collective sentiment among those I know who have passed through its gates is one of immense pride, particularly regarding how FAMU fosters a unique culture of "Rattler" resilience and top-tier scholarship. I’ve heard countless stories from acquaintances about the university’s exceptional ability to produce high-achieving leaders in pharmacy, law, and engineering, all while maintaining a deeply supportive community that feels more like a family than a standard institution. It is genuinely heartening to see how the faculty prioritizes mentorship, a quality frequently highlighted in community discussions as the secret behind the remarkable professional success of its graduates. Ultimately, the consensus from everyone I trust is that this university remains a cornerstone of empowerment and intellectual rigor, proving itself time and again as a prestigious engine for social mobility and innovation.', 'My cousin attended school here and it proved to be a highly advancing experience. The campus also looks rather nice.', 'The grounds have been improving, the recent improvements in the landscaping, makes the campus a breathtaking sight of history. There are numerous resources for students to thrive in their academics; including mentors, academic coaching, libraries, study rooms, etc. The spacious study rooms are well equipped  with whiteboards where the scholars  have the ability to thrive as a collective. FAMU is well versed in student success and finding one’s identity. It’s a beautiful school, where beautiful dreams can be molded into reality, and where you can be awakened comfortably into the person you are destined to be.', 'One of the best HBCUS out there we visit every year on college tours and have students enroll. They are so friendly and the epitome of southern hospitality im blessed to have been', 'Nice campus, well maintained with a heavy presence in the community. Easy to access, seems to be constantly improving for the students.']

name: Florida Atlantic University
reviews:
["Having closely monitored the trajectory of Florida Atlantic University through the lenses of various friends and local professionals, it is clear that the Boca Raton campus has transformed into a dynamic epicenter for innovation and upward mobility. The prevailing sentiment in my social circles suggests that FAU offers a sophisticated blend of high-level research and a supportive, student-centric culture that is rare for an institution of its size. I frequently hear from acquaintances about the university’s exceptional ability to foster real-world connections, particularly within the business and engineering sectors, ensuring that the transition from the classroom to the Florida job market is both seamless and rewarding. It is heartening to hear firsthand accounts of how the faculty at 777 Glades Road balances academic rigor with a genuine accessibility that makes diverse learners feel empowered to reach their full potential. Based on the many positive testimonials I’ve encountered, there is a profound respect for the way the university serves as a cultural and intellectual anchor for the entire region while steadily climbing the national rankings. One cannot help but be impressed by the university's forward-thinking approach to specialized fields like oceanography and nursing, which many in my network cite as being truly world-class. Ultimately, the consistent feedback from those I trust confirms that FAU is a premier destination for anyone seeking a modern, transformative education that stays deeply attuned to the demands of the 21st century.", "Unfortunately, I have found the environment to be very business and money oriented, with little regard for the students' needs.

If I had the opportunity to choose again, I would opt for another university. Additionally, I have encountered instances where the staff's attitude was quite unpleasant, and when problems arose, they provided no assistance or support. This has been very disappointing.", 'Absolute atrocity of a university. From beginning to end. Not to mention, the process of scheduling an academic advising appointment on Navigate 360 hasn’t worked for years. In general, being a student here has been a frustrating experience. There are not enough professors to teach classes leading to extremely tight schedules offering no flexibility whatsoever. I have had to endure 12 hour days at this uni because of it. On top of having a shortage of professors, a lot of the professors can barely teach. I’ve had professors that seem genuinely confused by what they’re teaching. I’ve had instances where they’ve attempted to teach and explain examples only to look at the solutions and realise they were wrong. Then, going back and reading in an attempt to understand what he’s already supposed to know. I understand making mistakes every now and then, but it was too frequent to justify. Another issue amongst these professors is the habitual use of outdated material (2005-2010), especially in a field that is rapidly growing and changing. There’s so much more I would like to say regarding the professors but I need to address and voice some of my other concerns too. Parking situation is terrible, filthy restrooms in every building (broken toilets, faucets, no soap), some of the classes themselves are disgustingly muggy and warm. As a student here, I feel as if a lot of the funding doesn’t go towards fixing the root problems. Maybe it does but there have been no apparent improvements to the quality of teaching here. At the end of the day, that’s what I’m here for.

On another note, I would like to commend the few well-knowledged professors at this institution. There’s nothing more rewarding than having a professor who truly knows how to teach. One that has a well-structured, well planned out class with up-to-date information. One that challenges you and ensures the future success of each hard-working student. I am highly grateful for professors who are passionate about their jobs and truly know how to teach, and also want to teach.

Overall, I feel failed by this university. Maybe it’s simply an issue with my field of study. There’s a plethora of issues that I didn’t even address. I sincerely don’t recommend studying here. This borderline feels like a scam (I wish I was being dramatic). Do your research and choose wisely, maybe it’s like I stated above, “simply an issue with my field of study.” Back when I was younger, I was reading the reviews on here and saw the mention of “FAU means - find another university.” I disregarded it believing it was dramatised; however, I soon realised how accurate that statement stood to be.', 'I didn't go to FAU, I drove by FAU.
My memory's being a student.There are all good. Professional educators, excellent professors, and core student body that's good.
A lot of changed over to years including now, a football stadium.
I did not think they needed a football stadium, but it seems to attract another set of people willing to spend money there. "Go Owls"', 'A great university,  campus, a great amount of facilities,  and programs.  Good Luck students , study, learn ,stay smarts. You have one. Uno" Opportunity "  take it knows while you can .  Learn languages,  voulenteer when can,  do some kinds exercises,  sports too.   🕺 💃  ⚾️  🏀  🏊‍♂️,   🐈 🐕  🐰.      Do yall have garden there. Make a veggies , garden you have plenty areas.  🍅 🌶 🥗  🫘     ✌️ ❤️']

name: Florida State College at Jacksonville
reviews:
['For the past six months, I visited multiple campuses trying to get enrolled, and the process was frustrating. I felt like I was getting nowhere until I came to this location. The difference was night and day. I had the pleasure of working with Kathy (I believe that was her name), who was incredibly patient, kind, and truly knowledgeable. She took the time to understand what was holding up my enrollment and helped me finally get everything sorted out.

If you’re looking for an advisor who genuinely cares and is ready to guide you through the process, this is the campus to visit. It’ll save you so much time and give you real peace of mind.

I’m officially ready to start school and I couldn’t be more excited!', 'I spent over a year at FSCJ before forming this opinion. Unfortunately, my experience with the staff was consistently poor. Many staff members seemed unfamiliar with their own processes, which often led to enrollment, financial aid, or other administrative errors. There was little to no accountability when mistakes were made, even when the issue clearly originated with staff. Instead, the burden was placed on the student to resolve the problem, requiring significant extra time and effort.

This was especially frustrating as a student with a disability. Accommodations and accessibility concerns were often treated as inconveniences rather than legitimate needs. Communication between departments was weak, and it frequently felt like students with disabilities were pushed aside or expected to repeatedly advocate for support that should have been automatic.

I can’t speak for every program, but the IT program was particularly disappointing. The courses were essentially online classes with required attendance. While most instructors were polite and personable, the quality of instruction was poor. In one class, the instructor played about 15 minutes of a random YouTube video during a three-hour session, with little to no actual teaching. Exams were still given, but the material was never properly covered.

The coursework itself was not original or enhanced—it was the same generic online content offered by many other colleges, but paired with unnecessary administrative headaches. Overall, the school appears poorly managed, with systems that work against students rather than supporting them.

Do yourself a favor and look elsewhere. While some people may have a good experience here, others do not. I would not take the chance of ending up in the latter group.', "The student dean is a joke. Admissions and student advising are impossible to get ahold of, and due to the lack of communication it has caused me more money in taking classes I didn't need. I am counting down the day until I can transfer out of this mess. The dean was my last straw, and her lack of a backbone should be a vivid warning to all incoming students. If you want a decent education, good use of your time, and an administration that listens, save your money and go somewhere else.", 'This has been by far the worst experience I’ve had at any college I’ve attended. Communication from professors was extremely poor, and emails often went unanswered. I did not feel supported academically and will not be completing my program here. I would not recommend this institution based on my experience.', "I apply on 11/25. As of 12/16, I'm still waiting for them to respond  to my application. I have two degrees and attended 3 colleges. I've never had this poor of an experience.

I'm about to ask for a refund of my application fee."]

name: Flagler College
reviews: ["Flagler College is absolutely beautiful. Make sure to take a few hours to tour the historic campus. Originally Flagler's Ponce Hotel, discover how it was converted to an educational institution. Make sure to peek your head in the dining hall to see the Tiffany glass windows. Situated in beautiful St Augustine, make a day of your visit by touring the walkable historic streets surrounding the campus.", 'Not a student but the place is freaky cool too learn about.', 'I toured Flagler College and downtown along with my brother. Architecture of this college is fabulous. Some of the detail is absolutely remarkable. Nice tour available without ever stepping foot on the property. Plenty of photo opportunities. I’d like to see the inside of some of the buildings at some point on a later more in-depth tour.', 'The Flagler College area is absolutely beautiful.   The Spanish architecture is breathtaking.   From the terracotta roofs to the red iron gaits and railings, this place is eye candy.  Walked around and looked at the various hotels and other various buildings, all the same style and flair.  When you tour the downtown Saint Augustine area, venture a little further down to see these sites.', 'Taking the free architectural tour at Flagler College was absolutely fascinating and beautiful! It was like time traveling back to the Gilded Age  where conspicuous luxury and customized environs and decor knew no bounds. Learning the history of the visionary team behind the project and the short amount of time this hotel was completed yielded many surprises for us!']

name: Florida College
reviews: ['Wonderful small for your college on the banks of the Hillsborough River. Place where everyone knows everyone else and the professors are as much friends as teachers. I truly lifetime enriching experience', "I would never send my child here and would urge others considering to do some research about the job opportunities that your child would have after graduating from here. I hate to break it to you but there isn't many reputable employers out there that will want to hire the average student from here as anything other than maybe an associates degree from Florida college is not respectable at all.", "I have known many people that have attended Florida College, from current students to those in their 80s.  Their stories and their lives reflect a consistent message that FC stands apart as an institution of higher learning that puts its focus on God first as well as God having a place in every aspect of the experience there whether it be in the classroom, activities and relationships with students, faculty and staff.  My oldest daughter attends there now and my middle child, Lord willing, will be there in the fall.  I can't think of a better place for a Christian to attend.", 'What a wonderful positive environment for a students foray into the "real world!" God needs to be the center of each one\'s life.', 'A very great place to get an education. The classes are small enough that the teachers are able to provide focused attention to the students. The dorm father for the boys dorm is a very heart warming man.']

name: AdventHealth University
reviews: ['Beautiful campus. Caring healthcare professionals', 'Go anywhere else than AdventHealth University! I completed the online training program for surgical tech (which was a joke) in March. But still haven\'t been placed for my in person training. AdventHealth won\'t even allow me to train there because apparently they know how horrible the school is as well.. They advertise "ready to work in 3-6 months". It has been 7 months and I\'m no where near being able to get a job. Also the certification is a joke. The majority of places want you to have an NBSTSA or NCCT. So don\'t waste your money like I did. Go somewhere that is legitimate.', "I've been to seminole state and Valencia before coming to this school and it has been the best. I've experienced lots of care from my professors and the counselors when I visited one. I really appreciate how friendly the welcome center is and helpful my financial aid counselor is when I do not understand things. I am happy that I am able to grow professionally and educationally because that is what I  see my program is teaching us as well. It is defiantly a christian environment that I am happy to be part of.", 'I am a current student at Adventist University and I do not regret my decision. I have finished my first year of college and can tell you that the professors care about the students and are always available to speak with you with open arms. The staff is friendly and helpful and make it their duty to help you as best as they can. The campus is clean and great and not to mention how it is right next to the Florida Hospital which gives students chances to get that hands on experience. It is great knowing you are surrounded by people who have a similar passion for helping people and an interest in health science professions.', "This school has been very good to me. I remember coming for my first day terrified because I wasn't sure where to go. The faculties and staff are very helpful. Everyone was so friendly and wanted to help me. My professors took time to learn all of our names in the classrooms which is rare for a university. I've been to Valencia and the professors didn't even know I was in their class, even though our classroom was small just like AHU. This school really cares about their students. I do not regret coming here."]

name: Florida Institute of Technology
reviews:
["Review regarding the online experience only:

It must be intentional to make every single part of their system (portal and PAWS) as non-intuitive as humanly possible. I imagine it was some high schoolers project to have numerous systems that don't communicate with each other for hours or even days on end.

Additionally I have emailed 4 different departments or contacts directly listed on FIT's own website and have not received a single response. I don't know if anyone actually works here or not but I imagine they're highly overpaid for doing exactly zero work.", 'I feel 2 stars is being generous. This review is solely based on their online MBA program. From the moment I was accepted, there was zero guidance on how to set up the portal, student email, etc., I didn’t even know what online learning platform they used. There is one advisor for the entire online MBA program and she never introduced herself. When I needed help trying to navigate the portal, website, what learning platform is used, etc she was of no help. I didn’t even know what classes I needed to take. I had to reach out to her to get the document of classes. She never checked in once. I’ve taken 3 classes here and I only hear from her when I reach out. The other departments are also terrible at communication. I feel like I shouldn’t complain because I have a 4.0 and the instructors have been fine but outside of that it’s terrible. I originally was accepted to a university closer to me for my MBA and accepted their offer before Florida got back to me and they were wonderful. Introduction, follow up, guidance, etc — so when I switched to Florida Tech and experienced this, I was shocked a highly regarded school could be this terrible to their students. I also want to mention, I had no access to my Canvas or Paws for the first month I was accepted. IT couldn’t figure it out for awhile then finally did. I also haven’t had any access to my student email from August until currently (Oct 30). I withdrew from my fourth term and will be transferring to a university that actually cares about their students. The only time I had staff reach out to me first was to settle my balance I owe. How convenient.', 'Beautiful campus. Very friendly people.', "Loved my experience here. The professors are wonderful and all the TAs and graduate students were helpful. It's also located in the Space Coast so that's hard to beat. The only downside is that the wifi is kinda bad", "FIT maybe tell your construction workers that it is illegal to block the only entrance and exit to a residential complex. I hope I don't need the police or an ambulance because they won't be able to get in. Let alone all of us trying to go home after an 11 hour overnight shift. They block our complex every single day and every single day I struggle to go home or take my kids to school on time because of the construction. Also tell them to contain their site. I shouldn't have sheet rock at my apartment from your site. Also shouldn't have had to change 3 tires now back to back because of giant nails. This is absolutely ridiculous."]

name: Florida International University
reviews:
['Our group attended a conference at the Ernest Graham Center. The Center includes a one price cafe that offers various food centers. Pizza, Italian pasta and sauces. Delicious tender chicken. Green veggie of beans, and fluffy mashed potatoes.  I chose chicken and juicy pin loin.  The hand crated puesto chips are crisp and delicious.
I enjoyed the desert stations with a parfait, cake, chocolate chip cookies and a vegan cookie. The ice cream machine offers soft serve chocolate, vs ills, and zebra twist for cone  or cup.
The CocaCola fountain drinks are in several places thru the food center as are the 2 ice tea and 2 Poweraid® options
The workers are r tremy friendly and efficient to serve food.
The students here are quiet, serious and polite. Self bussing of dishes and cups.
Entry to the center is accessible either touch pad. Restrooms are accessible with heavy door and dedicated stall and 2 grab bars and 4ftx 5ft space
Aisles are wide and rooms are accessible', 'The new 191-foot FIU pedestrian bridge, replacing the 2018 collapsed structure, is currently under construction by the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT). This $11.4 million, USD-funded project utilizes traditional steel girder construction rather than the previous concrete design, with completion expected in fall 2026. The design features a canopy, elevators, and, importantly, enhanced structural safety measures.
Florida International University in Miami
Florida International University in Miami
+5
Key Details of the New Bridge Construction:
Methodology: Unlike the previous failed attempt which used Accelerated Bridge Construction (ABC), this bridge is being built using traditional steel girders in a six-phase, conventional process.
Location: Spans SW 8th Street (Tamiami Trail), connecting the Modesto A. Maidique Campus with the City of Sweetwater.
Safety & Design: The new design includes a canopy, surveillance cameras for the FIU Police Department, and improved, modern structural components.
Timeline: Construction began in 2024, with fabrication completed by early 2026.
Responsibility: The project is designed and managed by FDOT.
Florida International University in Miami
Florida International University in Miami
+5
Background on the 2018 Collapse
The original 2018 pedestrian bridge was a "concrete truss" design that failed during construction, resulting in six fatalities. That project utilized an accelerated, off-site construction technique known as Self-Propelled Modular Transportation (SPMT) to move the massive, 950-ton structure. The failure was later attributed to significant design errors, where the bridge's, specifically the node where a diagonal member met the deck, was under-designed, creating a structure that lacked necessary redundancy.', "Based on the many insightful conversations I’ve had with South Florida professionals and former students, it is undeniable that Florida International University has become a primary engine of intellectual and economic vitality for the Miami region. The common thread in the feedback I receive from friends is a deep admiration for how the campus on SW 8th Street bridges the gap between a high-energy urban environment and a truly rigorous research-driven education. Many colleagues often highlight the university’s exceptional international focus, noting that its business and global affairs programs are frequently cited by those in the know as some of the most practical and culturally relevant in the nation. It is heartening to hear firsthand accounts of how the faculty members utilize their real-world expertise to mentor a student body that is as ambitious as it is diverse. From what I’ve gathered through community circles, the university maintains a respectful, forward-thinking atmosphere that encourages students to solve local problems with global solutions. One cannot help but be impressed by the consistent success of its graduates, who many of my acquaintances describe as being uniquely prepared for the complexities of the 21st-century workforce. Ultimately, the consensus among those I trust is that FIU isn't just an institution of higher learning, but a sophisticated gateway to opportunity that remains deeply committed to the success of every individual who joins its ranks.", 'My experience with FIU’s Moss School of Construction made it very clear that attention to detail and basic professionalism are not priorities here. I emailed the program with simple admissions questions and received an automatic reply directing me to a second contact for immediate assistance. I followed that instruction the same day.

After that, nothing. No reply from either person for more than four months. Not even an acknowledgment.

When I finally withdrew my interest, the director responded—but his message referenced an “application,” even though I never submitted one. That told me everything I needed to know: the email wasn’t actually read, and the underlying issue was completely missed.

This isn’t a one-off mistake. When two points of contact ignore an inquiry for months, and the director sends a template response without understanding the situation, it reflects a systemic problem. If this is the level of responsiveness before enrollment, I can only imagine how students are treated once they’re actually in the program.

Based on this experience, I won’t be pursuing FIU, and I wouldn’t recommend the program to anyone who expects professionalism or reliable communication.', 'Beautiful university campus and facilities, friendly staff and students.']

name: The College of the Florida Keys
reviews:
['Great place for adults to go lap swimming! Clean and well maintained pool, very calm ambiance and reasonable prices and good schedule that makes it easy to work out for most. So thankful for this pool.', 'The in person dive classes are great. The problem is a lot of the stuff they offer is online— and many of the classes they list as available aren’t regularly offered. They can’t find instructors to cover the classes. If your expectations are low you won’t be disappointed. If you have high expectations you’ll hate it. Wanted to rate it 2/5 stars but you have to go in not expecting much— and that makes it 3/5.', 'This is where Island Living meets Island Learning! The College of the Florida Keys spans for 100 miles and it is very unique because there is something for everyone!
The college offers:
Certificates, Associate and Bachelor’s level, credit and non-credit classes for lifetime learners, entrepreneurs and for those who want to enhance their careers
Online courses
Student Dorms
Student life
Scholarships, grants and payment plans
Project Access program for students with unique abilities
Active military and VA Services
Marine and aquaculture programs
Hospitality and culinary programs
A pool that houses classes and hosts events

Visit the campus or website for a one stop experience where the faculty and staff knows your name.', "If you have a child with a disability, then this is NOT the place for your child. We thought it was, just like many parents thought it was. Many parents paid for certain services and never receiving those services. Nice campus but some of the staff and policies need to be changed. Most parents were told the cost would be close to $17, 000 and it was closer to $24,000 (that's living on campus with the meal plan). Some student mentors do a good job and some don't do anything, but the school will still charge you for it regardless. If your child has a disability, then you're gonna want to find another program and there are many out there.", 'Ah, yes...FKCC, or as I like to call it the "Harvard of all of the colleges in the Florida Keys." It's actually a great little community college with a reasonable amount of academic programs offered for its size. Smaller class sizes allow for more one on one interaction with instructors. Some of the staff can be a bit pokey in Student Services, but that's life in the Keys. Facilities are nice and up to date. I can't comment on the campus dorms as I do not live there. The writing and math labs in the library are awesome for additional tutoring too.']

name: Florida Memorial University
reviews:
['Beautiful campus. The staff in Admissions and Financial Aid were friendly and helpful. I highly recommend the University Tour. It will give you great insight into campus life and academic programs. I was extremely impressed. A hidden gem in South Florida for sure! 😊', "I honestly had to reflect the other day, the best faculty that I had was not at a PWI, but at an HBCU. Never had such caring university professors, who still support their students many years after graduation. I was blessed to earn a degree from this institution, while engaging in several college activities, and journeying with similar persons at the time of my attendance.
*I don't think it's so much about race or color, but the heart of the professors and also how well the operational culture is permeated by institutional values.
*4/5 because campus life could have been a bit safer at times, due to the partying et cetera, but got my education which was my priority.
*May have changed by now, but the old dorms needed an upgrade, may it be funded.🙏🏾
Anywho, great faculty support towards student success.", 'I am an Alumni of FMU and I took my 21 year old Son on a tour of the Campus as he is considering matriculating there and completing his undergraduate and graduate education. Nothing like an HBCU! The Campus is expanding and growing as the Land has been cleared where Prime and Duo once proudly stood! Ahhh the Memories! I also Love seeing the Iguanas on Campus!!!', "Great university ,staff, educational programs, excellent campus.  Wow .. great Jazz Concert.. can't wait for the next one.", 'Florida Memorial University is one of the most unprofessional colleges I’ve ever experienced. The people from the admissions office are very disrespectful, incompetent, and do not provide services when in need. It is a hassle to try & get in contact with someone from any department, nobody ever picks up or returns phone calls! They provide you with incorrect information, keep you on hold then proceed to hang up the phone, and many more. Tasha from the admission offices is very disrespectful & one of the most immature administrators that I’ve ever came across! Education & money is nothing to play about! I will be sure that I get into contact with someone that is above & has higher power,  because this is ridiculous & I feel sorry for the students that attend Florida Memorial University that have to receive this type of treatment on daily basis!']

name: Florida Southern College
reviews: ['Went today to visit Florida Southern College to go on a basic tour of the Frank Lloyd Wright designed building. It was $35 per person for a 60-90 minute tour. We had a very knowledgeable tour guide that showed us inside 3 separate buildings on property, along with walking us through the property explaining the design history behind the campus. Overall it was very amazing to see this historic property still being maintained and properly preserved to this day. It’s hard in central Florida to find such history in architecture.', 'I came to this campus to see the Frank Lloyd Wright buildings. Although they looked great from afar, the condition of the buildings was disgraceful. The buildings are crumbling apart and look like they might just come down on top of you.  I would think they would try to keep these buildings from rotting and crumbling away but everywhere you turn, there is damage and mold. It is so sad to see. They need a ton of money to be poured into constant maintenance of these buildings 365 days of the year. I would not send my children to this school for fear the roof will collapse upon them while attending class.', 'One of my favorite Frank Lloyd Wright designs. Features the largest collection of his buildings. Had an opportunity to tour this campus in the Fall of 2019! I was amazed by the scenery and really enjoyed walking around the campus! I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for something to do while in the area.', 'We took a tour of the Frank Lloyd Wright buildings on campus. It was a great tour and well worth the price. I think it is the largest collection of his buildings.', 'I don’t have much to contribute as far as the educational portion of this location, but the historical architecture is another story. If you’re a fan of Frank Lloyd Wright or architecture in general, you will find numerous gems practically on top of one another. Unfortunately, the structures are in poor condition. Still worth taking a peak.']

name: Florida State University
reviews:
['Loved my time at FSU! My programs challenged me and pushed me to challenge myself and succeed. It did take work and definitely wasn't a cakewalk, but, with effort, the classes were doable. Graduated with a few degrees, so did not have much time for any leisure activities. However, the university offers an expansive variety of extracurriculars and activities for students. I am very glad I chose FSU.

Tips:
•It is a very large university, so you have to be proactive in getting the advice and help you may need.
•For subjects you are having difficulties with, utilize the tutors.
•The book series "For Dummies" is a godsend for difficult subjects.
•Double check that you are meeting all your scholarship requirements every semester!!! Not doing this caused me a lot of problems.
•Make sure you explore ALL your academic and hobbies of interest, even if they don't seem relevant at the moment. Talk with your advisor about this. Examples: foreign language, dance, creative writing, music etc. (If I could go back and start again, I would have taken a different academic pathway, and I wish I would have been given this advice back then.)
•Don't be afraid to take a class completely out of your department for fun. I took dance classes at the university just for fun.
•Either double major or single major with a minor, even if you have to stay at the university a little longer. This way you can get experience in different areas, and one focus can be practical, while the other one can be for passion and fun.
•Have fun, try different hobbies and activities.', "They campus is absolutely gorgeous and we had a great tour here. The area is really nice as well. I can't complain about the weather either since I was born and raised in Florida and it beats the freezing cold. They have good academics and are well recognized, at least in my perspective and I can't see a valid reason I personally wouldn't want to go here - meaning I think it would be a great school to attend. It's also in the states capital, which for my major is a huge perk.", "My son has attended two years at FSU with the associated costs of housing and transportation to and from his home.  He only gets online classes.  We tolerated that his freshman year.  Now his ENTIRE sophomore year are online classes.  FSU even has the gall to charge more for online despite not needing the space or the professors to teach it.  The classes themselves are weak, multiple choice oriented for the most part and lack any educational benefit that you couldn't get from reading a book in the library.  Awful university.", 'This was a great campus to go to. I went here on a field trip and it was the most beautiful campus. The scenery was nice and the buildings were clean and spacious. I highly recommend taking time to go see this university.', 'Wonderful institution with highly renowned and quality professors. Most beautiful campus in the state scattered with aged live-oaks, historic buildings, and an incredible landscape design. Unmatched access to the Florida State Capitol. Tours available through the FSU Visitors Center at the stadium.']

name: University of Florida
reviews: ['Taking into account the numerous glowing conversations I’ve had with alumni and local professionals, it is unmistakable that the University of Florida operates as a premier flagship of academic brilliance in the heart of Gainesville. The collective perspective shared by my friends often highlights a rare synthesis of tradition and cutting-edge discovery, where the "Gator" legacy is backed by world-class research and a truly formidable athletic spirit. It is particularly heartening to hear acquaintances describe the campus as an environment that doesn\'t just demand excellence, but actively provides the networking and technological resources necessary to achieve it. From what I’ve gathered through community circles, the university’s influence extends far beyond the lecture hall, deeply impacting Florida’s economic landscape through its top-tier engineering and agricultural programs. Many people I trust emphasize that the faculty’s commitment to mentorship is a cornerstone of the experience, ensuring that every student feels their potential is being fully realized. One cannot help but admire how the institution manages to maintain such a prestigious national ranking while remaining a welcoming and inclusive home for a diverse student body. Ultimately, the consistent feedback from those in the know suggests that a degree from UF is a badge of honor that opens doors across the globe.', 'Sleep Center now in Medical Bldg. Much preferred location in shopping center, which had less traffic, more easy parking, & was much easier to get too. Folks are caring, professional & friendly in most instances. Check In slow, person missing. Check out slow, person texting. But MEDICAL FOLKS all excellent.', 'The University of Florida offers strong academic programs and a beautiful campus, but my experience was a mix of positives and challenges. Some professors and resources are excellent, yet class sizes can feel overwhelming and getting timely support from administration is sometimes difficult. Campus facilities are good overall, but a few areas could use updates and better maintenance. It’s a solid school with a lot to offer, but there’s room for improvement in organization and student services.', "I know this is a review about the school but idk how else to get my point across lol!! I'm sure this is a wonderful school, but my husband is a HUGE gators fan I mean huge, and he wants to see them in the national championship 🏆 plz!! Do better gators!! He thinks you should replace DJ with the 2nd string!! He's tired of seeing you guys lose plz do better!!!!\n\nLove always a concern wife lol", "Love them they fix all my health issues. Plus they listen at least my Dr.Goode. she's awesome!"]

name: Full Sail University
reviews:
['Full Sail University truly changed my life.

From the moment I joined the ESL program, Full Sail became much more than a school — it was my gateway to understanding American culture and finding my place in it. The staff and professors were always supportive, helping me grow both personally and professionally.

Later, during my Sports Marketing degree, I had the opportunity to dive deep into the world of sports business, learning from passionate instructors and working on real-world projects that shaped my career path.

Today, I can confidently say that Full Sail played a fundamental role in my success. It gave me the tools, mindset, and inspiration to pursue my dreams in the sports industry. I’ll always be proud to be a Full Sail graduate!', "By the time you're reading this it's probably already too late. I would never recommend attending this school, the credits are worthless, the debt - astronomical, and good luck with job placement! Was a 2006-2007 dual major grad, and the training was irrelevant the day we graduated. The textbooks I saved were about as useful as the yellow pages are today (actually less useful). 99% of what you learn can be easily self-taught, save your money for equipment/gear, and pursue your dreams elsewhere. Don't say you weren't warned!", 'I am a student at Full Sail studying remotely from Dallas, Texas. I absolutely love this program. I have been a freelance designer for 5 years, but lacked the technical skills I needed to take my career to the next level. the Inspiring, passionate professors and helpful staff have made my experience top tier.
I have learned so much and am ready to grow my career in graphic design!
10 stars', 'My son attended Full Sail from September 2022 through October 2024 for an accelerated computer science degree. We were told during orientation that recruiters would come in months before graduation to speak with the students offering job prospects and that many would have a position waiting when they graduated , and this did not occur. Upon graduation not only did my son, but many other students that he knows have been unable to get a position in their field. Full Sail did nothing to help them, and I am so highly disappointed in the amount of money and the false advertising and basically bait and switch that we got from this so-called university. My son worked so very hard and even got awards/paid semester for how well his grades were and now he is employed in a completely different type of job not in the field that he worked so hard to get his degree. It is heartbreaking. Shame on you Full Sail.', 'I’m a proud Full Sail graduate with a bachelor’s in Entertainment Business! Full Sail is fast-paced, intense, and immersive just like the real entertainment industry. It’s not for the faint of heart, but if you have grit, passion, and the drive to see it through, you’ll come out stronger, way mire skilled, and ready to thrive in your career!!']

name: Gulf Coast State College
reviews: ['As someone who is trying to apply to the science program at this school. I’m finding it EXTREMELY hard to get in touch with anyone. I have NEVER experienced this with any other school. If your not in person is quite  impossible to get in touch with anyone here. They told me my pathway advisor who is Terri, I’ve applied and sent over my transcript over 3 weeks ago and nothing has been evaluated or posted on to my account. I’m literally this close to not pursue anything at this school and find somewhere else. If you are trying to apply to the health science program just expect to not hear back from nobody.', 'Excellent school providing access and opportunity to anyone who seeks education - for a better job and a better life.  Lowest tuition in the state of Florida and a tremendously generous Foundation who will help most anyone lacking financial resources. reviews:
