reviews:
['Ya, not much to say. Got an education. Some of the teachers and staff were amazing and really care about you.. Egos will go wild and that really shows between support staff and teachers. I gave up and just rolled with the bs as you do. I would have given 0. But those few teachers who actually cared earned my respect and these 2 stars.', 'The staff are so nice and helpful. You can tell they actually like their jobs and helping students. I was there for about 30 minutes today and in that time I spoke to people in both financial aid and cashiering so not a long wait at all. Aside from that taking classes has been a good experience too. I am a busy stay at home parent and sometimes lag behind in classes and most of the instructors have been reasonably  understanding and work with me.', 'I have attended SCF Venice campus for several years. I completed my associate degree in early childhood education there. About a year after that, I was awarded an academic scholarship for the early childhood education bachelor program.

PROS:Beautiful campus.

CONS:When working towards my Associates degree, they some how kept coming up with more and more classes that I “needed to take” in order to earn my diploma. Every time that I asked why I was not told about the added classes prior, I would just get an apology.

When I would email the person I was told to email questions to, they would always forward my email to someone different saying they didn’t handle that question. So it really seems as if no one knows what anyone else does there.

A professor accused me of cheating and gave me 0 on an assignment without any explanation. After weeks of begging her to look over my assignment again, she finally emailed back with a short apology, saying some other students in the class had cheated so she just assumed I had also so she automatically had given me 0 but after looking at my work again, she realized I had not cheated. When I received my scholarship, a woman came to the preschool I work at to give it to me. So she knew where I worked. I completed all of my classes and one of the 3 internship classes. I was then told I would not be allowed to complete the internship because the preschool I work at is not on their “approved internship list”. This makes NO sense to me as I was able to complete my internship for my associates degree at this same preschool. Also, I am confused as to why someone from the college would drive to my preschool to give me the scholarship if they knew my preschool was not approved in the first place. So I basically wasted years working for a degree they knew I would not be able to attain. Not only am I upset that they wasted my time, but also heart broken that I worked so hard for this just to be turned away 9 weeks prior to graduating.

I would never recommend this college to anyone.', 'Called admissions with some questions because I haven’t heard back from them after submitting my application & transcripts and waited for probably 40 minutes to speak with an admissions rep. She got me in touch to the correct department which would be evaluation and evaluation told me that they did not find any classes that could be transferred and I started listing the classes I took and said thats incorrect, she said oh my goodness whoever evaluated this obviously did not evaluate it correctly or at all so now I have to wait again for it to be evaluated correctly and I can finally see my financial aid at this point I don't think I'm interested.", 'Persistent lack of response from VA-certifying official
I’m a veteran at this school. Every time I contact the Veterans Services office I’m told to reach Zenaida Rabi-Menendez, but my calls go straight to voicemail and are never returned. Emails receive only generic replies that don’t address the specific questions I asked . If you’re a prospective student-veteran, plan on extra lead time and be prepared to escalate to the registrar or VA liaison supervisor—because the person listed as the primary certifying official simply does not respond.', 'As a student, I can’t miss the opportunity to fully recommend this amazing College. Specially, Admission and Financial Aid. Every single personnel is super welcoming, professional, diligent and they take care of each student taking in consideration the individual need:
Deborah Escalona
Ligia Sibaja
Dominique Ledger
Thalia Suarez
David Leiton
María Galdamez', 'Miami Dade College delivers something rare in higher education: honesty. The mission is clear, the expectations are explicit, and the outcomes are practical. Instruction is grounded, faculty are accessible, and students are treated as people whose time and money matter. There’s no prestige theater—just education designed to move students forward without burying them in debt or institutional politics.

MDC’s strength is its focus on fundamentals and pathways. Skills transfer. Credits articulate. Students leave better prepared, not just better branded. The college doesn’t pretend to be something it isn’t, and that integrity shows in how effectively it serves a diverse student population aiming for real mobility.

Now contrast that with UM Miller. Miller trades heavily on reputation while delivering an environment saturated with hierarchy and politics. Intellectual rigor is inconsistent, independent thinking is constrained, and conformity quietly outperforms merit. For PhD trainees especially, the outcomes are underwhelming relative to the investment—uneven mentorship, modest research visibility, and placements that rarely justify the cost or the hype.

Where MDC respects student futures, Miller risks diluting them. One institution builds capability and options; the other often builds résumés that rely on name recognition to mask thin substance. MDC is transparent, efficient, and outcome-driven. Miller is prestige-driven, inefficient, and complacent.

If you care about value, preparation, and momentum, Miami Dade College deserves serious respect. UM Miller, despite the branding, too often does not.']

name: University of Miami
reviews:
['Very Disappointing Experience  Lack of Communication and Accountability
Our experience with the University of Miami has been extremely disappointing due to poor communication and a serious lack of responsibility regarding scholarship information.

We were clearly informed and approved for a scholarship with a specific dollar amount, which played a major role in our decision to enroll our daughter. Based on that confirmation, she started classes in good faith. We expected better standards, clearer processes, and accountability from an institution of this reputation.
