Maybe if I was an international student, that this place would be better suited. Maybe if I was for sorority, and fraternity tasks I would have had better luck. Needless to say, I am smart enough, but not popular enough. Respectfully, this school should be more honest about the crime committed on there campus. Have you ever wondered what happens at nighttime in there arena? Maybe my old boss would recollect, but I digress and am strictly stirring up the truth people do not want to accept.

As a PURE American bread individual, this campus is not the hype it gives, and more importantly they do NOT prioritize academic. They completely overlook the intent of a college University, and this is why JU is getting more business.', 'Observing the consistent success of graduates within the Jacksonville business community, it is clear that the University of North Florida has established itself as a premier institution where academic excellence meets a truly personalized student experience. Many of my colleagues and friends who have studied at the 1 UNF Drive campus frequently praise the university for its "Osprey" spirit, which emphasizes a tight-knit environment where students are never just a number in a crowded lecture hall. Based on the many positive testimonials I’ve heard over dinner table conversations, the faculty is highly regarded for integrating real-world Jacksonville industry insights directly into the classroom, particularly in their standout business and healthcare programs. It is heartening to see how the university utilizes its beautiful, nature-rich campus to foster a serene yet intellectually stimulating atmosphere that encourages deep focus and creative collaboration. From what I have gathered through various community circles, the university maintains a respectful and inclusive culture that serves as a vital springboard for those aiming to make a meaningful impact in the regional economy. Ultimately, the overwhelming consensus among local professionals is that UNF offers a sophisticated, high-value education that remains authentically committed to the long-term success of its diverse student body.', 'This school is growing and it has more dorms, and athletic centers. I also find the teacher are professionals and rendering a great education, but unfortunately the bursar, Financial Services are as inept as always. Jenna in FA does not give a parent with granted access to the student information, the final amount due. I know there is a balance, but no statement shows on the improved cashnet site (2026 update) and the student needs to go to ask this information, because somehow they can not verify a parent is authorized to know.', "I am hot pissed! First of all, financial aid was supposed to be disbursed 2 days ago and then they send an email today that they have been double depositing refunds and they will not disburse until February. You all have the right one. I am reporting you to my lender. And so convenient that NO ONE AT THE UNIV IS ANSWERING PHONES TODAY. You do not just get to sit on our money till you all feel like it. This was a mistake by UNF and it is straight BS. I will be leaving this college. Can't even get in touch with anyone by phone. I am done with this BS.

Nice to know students got double their refunds while others are just doing without. Not giving students their money because of a mistake the UNIV made- your fault- DISBURSE EVERYTHING!!!!!!", "I came to this school from NYC where I was born and raised. UNF was fantastic! I love the campus and how it was easy to make friends and how much I fell in love with Jacksonville Florida. I can now call Jacksonville is my second home. Best part about UNF is that it's only 15-20 minutes from the beach."]

name: Nova Southeastern University
reviews: ['I had a very negative experience with the Financial Aid office. I requested information from my own student profile, but they were unable to provide it. I submitted important documents in person, and they were not returned to me, even though I needed them both for my application and for other personal processes. When I asked for a solution, I was told they could not give me the information nor return the document. This shows a lack of respect, organization, and professionalism. I truly hope the office improves its service to students, as these matters are essential and directly impact our education and well-being.', "It was my son's graduation from Coopers City high school 👌 the best graduation presentation and organized secured logistics that I've attended good job from Coopers City officials by picking Nova's Arena to do such a wonderful graduation ceremony!👍", 'NSU has first rate facilities!  I was impressed with the congruence of the shark branding and marketing on all things NSU.  Their staff was welcoming and informative.  If you’re taking the tour, be sure to see the “It pays to be a shark” presentation, which illustrates how scholarships, FL Prepaid, Bright Futures, etc. all chip away at the private school cost.', "Come on people. Wake up. Unless you are in medical school, you are paying tens of thousands of dollars to watch teachers read off of a PowerPoint and write google-able research papers just to only have the degree with no skills. Then having to pay off capitalized student loans while making low income and studying real skills on your own? It's a predatory scam. Get real skills. Get certificates. Get job experience. Don't go to private colleges. So many cheaper options.", 'The admissions office is very unresponsive and unhelpful. After paying the deposit, I tried contacting them many times through email for over a month, but I never received any reply. Very disappointing experience.']

name: Northwest Florida State College
reviews:
["The enrollment for this school was fast and easy. Easier than I expected at least. The test for the initial placement was a pain. It don't sound like that many questions but it takes longer than expected lol. The whole campus looks well maintained. I like the artistic feel of the whole place. Statues, architecture, leaf imprints in some parts of the sidewalk. The course selection is great and had lots of options to befit many different people and personality types. I wish online classes were easier though. With some classes using a newer system and some using an older it can be co fusing going from one site for one class and a different for another.", 'The teachers themselves are absolutely wonderful.

Everything else is such a pain that I'm debating switching to Pensacola. The staff with registration is extremely sassy and the student success center gets frustrated when you try to call for information. Further, the only campus that matters to them is the main campus. Smaller campuses are disgustingly outdated. Our A/C was either off or broken for the whole semester at the Fort Walton campus. The chairs were falling apart. They also have LED signs outside the main campus advertising "FREE MONEY" and "Grants Available" which sounds extremely scam-y, and they are. They make it near impossible to qualify for any financial aid. I work full time to pay for school and it's still not enough due to the fact that any changes are not accommodated. If you don't pay for all your classes at the same time they will drop you out of all your classes, even if you already paid for some. I was emailing registration about stuff and they told me they had taken care of something and notified the proper parties and then left me hanging which screwed over my semester and degree plan. Someone dropped the ball the blamed me for it even after attempting to vouch for myself, then proceeded to ignore me.

TLDR: If you're a perfect person who never needs any help from staff, sure feel good about your decision to go here. Otherwise, prepare for pushback and no refunds or transfer of funds.', 'I see why this school has horrible reviews. I had Maria ( the advisor I was assigned) get me signed up for classes at the end of last year so I would be good to go for spring. I specifically made an appointment with her so I didn’t do anything incorrect. This women put me in a “non degree seeking program” KNOWING I am finishing up the last of the classes I needed and was SEEKING the nursing program. I just found out today by Jeannie that she also never got information uploaded she said she completed. As I sit at Jeannie’s desk today for almost an hour NOTHING was accomplished. I am beyond frustrated but extremely grateful I will not be wasting anymore time at this insane “college” this isn’t my first time attending college so I know this isn’t how things are to be handled. Get some people in this establishment that knows what the hell is going on and how to do there job', 'Pick a different college unless you enjoy being frustrated, lied to, and not taught anything. Lazy staff and teachers. Terrible hours to get ahold of anyone when you do have a problem. Zero accountability for mistakes on their end.', 'God help you if you have a problem with your student account. I have been told "I don't know how to help you" by the help desk multiple times. Well maybe it's time for a new profession then, the help desk isn't for you. They have lost my paperwork multiple times, they will transfer you to another department who will then say we can't help you, they should have helped you in the previous department. No one in the office seems to know how to do anything at all. The professors are all pretty good and it was a professor, not an office worker, that went into the office and helped me more than anyone. It's absolutely absurd. Been fighting with these people for WEEKS to fix the issues with my student account and have been told multiple times, "we don't know what to do". That's your only job as a college, help and get students into classes, come on.']

name: Palm Beach Atlantic University
reviews:
['I am a sophomore here, with a theatre BFA and while I don’t see much of the school itself I have nothing but good things to say about the theatre program. It’s got great classes and all the professors work very hard to personally make sure you do well. I’m able to ask for office hours and I will get detailed personalized advice that is extremely helpful. The great thing about going here too is you get a lot of tech experience, as if you’re not in shows you’re in tech and they hire experts to come in and personally teach you in a hands on learning style. I’ve gotten experience with sound engineers, building props, learning how to pick costumes, leadership roles, painting sets etc all in the time I’m not getting to perform on the stage. I’ve gained a lot of insight and respect from it, and feel like a well-rounded performer. The kindness I’ve experienced from the professors in my learning process is irreplaceable and if you’re looking for a personal and specific school that will care about you as the individual where you can make a place for yourself this is the program for you. I’m extremely happy here and I’m sure many more would also be.', "Palm Beach Atlantic University is a welcoming community that embraces Christians from diverse backgrounds. The university is committed to providing high-quality education while fostering spiritual growth and personal development. I’m grateful to be part of such a supportive environment. Like any institution, PBA isn't perfect, but there are safe spaces for open dialogue and meaningful conversations about change. The campus is also in a fantastic location—with easy access to world-class performances at the Kravis Center and Society of the Four Arts, as well as the nearby beach for those who value connecting with nature and caring for their mental well-being.", 'Can't speak about the education although I do know they're scrapping the theater department as it's not as revenue producing as business. What I also know is they are proving to be very inconsiderate neighbors. The college is situated in a small, historic neighborhood. We have tiny streets. Since PBAU has begun the most recent construction projects, students have been clogging our streets to park all day, every day. PBAU's attitude? Call the police. Nice neighbors. I will never support this institution again. They call themselves Christian? I call them indifferent and self-serving. How about not charging students a fortune to park on their own campus? Typical of these "Christian" institutions, it's all about the money. My son goes to an ivy league college. They charge $200 a year for parking. PBAU? $600 a semester. PBAU is a money mill.', 'This show was amazing. I loved the live vocals. The last one I went to was all instrumental which was fantastic, but to have singing in this one was much more lively and such a great performance. These guys from Miami were amazing… would highly recommend!!!', "Why We Love PBA - A Parent’s Perspective
Palm Beach Atlantic has been an incredible blessing to our daughter and our entire family. The impact this school has on both academics and character development is truly remarkable.
The theater program stands out as a transformative experience. From Stage Movement, which builds confidence and presence, to Stage Craft, where students learn hands-on construction and real-world application, the skills they gain go far beyond the stage. These are life skills that open doors.
Students thrive in an environment where professors bring deep experience and Christ-like mentorship. Academically, the rigor is impressive. Our daughter is currently in Humanities 3, and Professor Chapman brings history to life in ways every parent hopes their child will experience.
The program is immersive - intense academics by day, theater productions by night, with four performances a year. Students learn everything: lighting, stage design, movement, costumes, props, and more. It’s a full creative and intellectual journey.
If you're looking for a place where your child can grow in faith, talent, and intellect — PBA is it. I do not have to be concerned about her finding a career. If I owned a company, a theater major from PBA would be a top hire."]

name: Palm Beach State College
reviews:
['This is my first year at PBSC and dealing with advising has been a nightmare. Expect to be bounced between departments, given wrong information, and spend hours of your day just trying to get basic answers. I had to start documenting my visits and calls because of how disorganized and unhelpful the process became.

As a 19-year-old, I wasn’t taken seriously until I brought my mom with me — after already coming in person over 10 times since Fall 2025. The only bright spots were Ms. Linda, Mr. John, and Ms. Maureen, who were actually professional and helpful.

Professors and classes have been great, but the advising department seriously needs improvement. If you attend PBSC, ask for supervisors and avoid student advisors unless you enjoy misinformation and attitude.', 'My girlfriend called the admissions office to get see if she could get assistance registering for classes. Unfortunately, I was met by a dismissive JoCarol Bines, an "Admissions specialist" at the Lake Worth campus who hung up on her twice after asking her to explain the process to verify in-state residency. She was excited to attend PBSC and had her classes picked out, but this experience is making her reconsider.

I personally attended PBSC in the past and as an alumni, I'm disappointed to see the state of the current admissions office first hand. PBSC, you are better than this! Please help your prospective students instead of dismissing them.', "As a returning student, I love the staff here! Admissions, registration, financial aid, are all very easy to communicate with and I always feel comfortable doing so. The Lake Worth campus is the biggest and my favorite. Advisors are helpful and sweet, professors are debatable but the good ones are really nice, and the cafeteria has great options contrary to what i hear. There's breakfast and lunch and several options for both. The line looks daunting but usually goes very quickly, and the employees are very kind.

Sometimes the campus isn't really sanitary because I'll see the occasional possum every now and then... but one man's trash is another man's treasure, I think they're cute!", 'Love PBSC! As an international student 🧑‍🎓 I enjoyed my time there. Amazing teachers. International admission office is great. They helped me a lot.', 'Does anyone actually review applications at this college? I completed my application over a week ago and have since emailed and left phone messages with no response. Instead of receiving an acceptance confirmation or instructions on how to schedule for the Real Estate Sales Associate Post-Licensing (5493) course, I’ve been getting a series of irrelevant emails.

This experience has been extremely frustrating and disappointing so far. Could someone please look into my application and let me know the next steps?']

name: Pasco-Hernando State College
reviews: ['This is my first semester attending PHSC and I love it! The staff is so helpful from the admissions office, advisors, and most importantly the financial aid office. They are always putting something together for the students. Last week it was free pizza and pumpkin painting. This week it was free wing Wednesday. They even put on a treasure hunt. I’ve never had a school give back to their students so much. I’m proud to be a bobcat!', 'Good place to go to school. There are friendly and knowledgeable staff here. There is also a cafeteria and a library plus a shop for school supplies. This college has lots of outside nature for quiet studying.', 'I have been trying to talk with someone about a program that you offer. When i call i get pushed over to a voicemail. Nobody has called me back.\nYour online info information does not answer any of my questions.\nThis is very unprofessional.', 'Please stop wasting my time I sing up for a zoom meeting to learn more about the EMT program it say it starts at Friday which is today at 10:00am and not one person is there I this close fix to turn you in the corporate office to file a complaint for wasting my time and Play this bull crap games I this close to fixing to switch to a different college area.', 'We toured the campus today with my son as he’s going to be taking some classes there and the campus tour guides were unbelievably informative and so easy going and nice. The campus is beautiful and has come so far since I took a few classes there over two decades ago. Parking is easy and every single staff person we ran into was pleasant and welcoming. The library and art gallery were both very impressive.']

name: Pensacola State College
reviews: ['Graduated with my associates here! Over all experience was great, but I will say the advisors and the “higher ups“ that you have to email to get approved for certain documentation for financial aid or whatever you need. They are a joke its very hard to get information or be directed to the right spot you pretty much have to figure out everything on your own other than that. Great School just need better people working there that are committed to helping students. Trying to fix overlapping financial aid was horrible for me when I transferred and being snappy and having an attitude through an email is crazy.', 'You are awesome, can’t wait to visit and present my work for the 10 years I’ve been doing it.', 'Awesome professors, easy to navigate wedbsite/campus, very good started school.\n\nMy advisor was horrible though. Hoping other people have more success with theirs!', 'The staff in the library are very friendly especially the only male librarian with a long hair. The support they have for veterans is impeccable. I was sad when the retired navy advisor Kevin Kropp left  but Mr. Tilden is doing an amazing job as well. I did not put 5 stars all the way because of my bad experience with one advisor. Not mentioning his name but this retired Air Force set up an appointment with me before the start of semester.  When I called him that day he left his phone at home and his wife answered it. After she gave me his office number, I called him and he told me to call him back after an hour. I called after an hour many times but he never picked up and he did not even respond on my emails. Two of the core values of the AF are Service Before Self and Excellence in all we do but I did not get that from him.', 'Great instructors well funded art dept']

name: Polk State College
reviews:
["Let me speak bluntly: The administration at this school is going to lead to stress in your life. I have never encountered an institution that seems to actively work against student success such as I've encountered here. If you want to get ahold of someone at the department for admissions, financial aid, student services, or the registrar, good luck, sincerely. And if, bless your heart, you choose to sit and play phone tag, or wait on hold, the help desk will likely defer you to another department or answering machine (they are often full or just not set up). It's as if the entire premise of the administrative department was built upon the concept of simply deflecting responsibility to someone else. I'm beginning to understand that this school is understaffed, and I can empathize with that. However, this is an institution with a 100% acceptance rate. Many, many of these students have no prior experience in higher education, which makes these student services CRUCIAL TO THEIR SUCCESS!! If you want to succeed at Polk State College, you absolutely can. But do expect to encounter friction and difficulties along the way, do expect to do your own research and double check every piece of information at every step of the process, because this school will leave you in the dust. I have personally experienced being dropped from all of my classes the week that they began due to an issue with financial aid (I was later able to write an appeal for this). How did I find this out? Through email, right? I mean, this is a HUGE issue. Nope. I found this out because I happened to check on dashboard to see that all of my classes were gone. An entire semester had disappeared overnight. That's all. No call, no email, no notification whatsoever. While I was able to get this issue resolved, it was not without unnecessary headache and tremendous anxiety.
Tread carefully, folks. Your future IS important. Do not downplay your goals, do not compromise on the dreams you have for yourself, and for God's sake, do not let a borderline non-existent administrative department get in your way. Do your due diligence to prioritize your success despite the institutional opposition you may encounter along the way.", "I approve the following message: As an Alumni former student that attended this institution as a Criminal Justice student I can say my program director and my instructors were all professional. Dr. Falconetti, Our Chair, and board of directors of this school all put the students first and during COVID-19 helped me through my financial needs by granting me relief funds that I did not have to pay back and supplied me with $2,000 that helped me pay my bills and needs for school. Hard work pays off if you put in the amount of time and dedication towards your learning  I was awarded 3 scholarships which also assisted in covering books and classes I am only left having to payback $1800 which isn't bad and look at the outcome I got my degree. Sheriff Judd should put more recognition for our Program Director and the professors that instruct in the CJ program I had a great experience with each of you all though I decided to pursue Cybersecurity it was fun being able to learn more on my Law and the Criminal Justice System. This school has earned this review and I will also keep a good word of mouth out for this school and their professionalism to assist students as a disabled student I was able to be successful on campus.", "As a former student (graduated) this places administration sucks. No one answers the phones and no one sends emails. You have to figure out events are happening by googling it. The professors are great. I loved my professors. Except the programming professors and the one odd professor who loves to hang with students outside of school hours. That's was a weird one.

But the trip was fun and now I move on to a university that actually answers phones and emails when needed.", 'I am an alumna of Polk’s nursing program (ASN and BSN) and used to highly recommend this college. Unfortunately, that is no longer the case.

Multiple friends and family members currently attending Polk—across different programs—have experienced severe issues with administration and academic advising. Communication is extremely poor, follow-through is lacking, and students are repeatedly forced to chase issues that the school should be handling.

These problems have had serious consequences. In one case, a student’s graduation was delayed by a year and a half due to administrative negligence, despite repeated attempts to resolve the issue.

Based on these ongoing experiences, I would not recommend this college to anyone.', 'Literally the worst “service” I’ve ever experienced. If you’re even considering online courses don’t waste your time applying here. The departments don’t communicate effectively without one another and the student suffers. You’d think by now with all these technological innovations a state college would be able to provide smooth transitions throughout the admissions process, right? Wrong ! It’s took 5 months for me to be alerted after applying about holds on my account. The website while easy to navigate, has false, misleading, and misplaced information . The website software and encryption in itself is faulty to say the least being that one of the most important pages doesn’t open (the Polk portal) . There also isn’t anything or anyone to explain that error to besides the technical support that you only have access to once you’re a student . I literally am blowing the school up asking what’s going on and what else is needed and searching for the next ACTUAL step . Not what the website says. After the WAIT , knowing my options for classes were pretty much down to nothing, I was given an excuse as to why I couldn’t be a business major with a concentration in IT, like computer science-  or another, and was asked if i would allow them to switch my major to liberal arts , which also was the only way to keep my previously earned credits. All of them. Over it, I obliged. I get in 2 classes late. I’m not able to buy the book for one though . Fafsa never notifies me. The school says nothing. Now the school email that sends more spam mail than anything, is telling me fafsa need me to approve something. The fafsa notification on the website, EMPTY. The approval, needed in the Polk portal , THAT WONT OPEN. You think anyone from financial aid has contacted me ? A follow up from the advisors that I couldn’t get a hold of ? No one ! I Drop the class with no book. And today I of on to complete the work for week 2 , and I’ve been dropped. The webage still won’t open , I’ve already submitted work for this class, it’s too late to begin a 12 week semester with another college, I still have to wait 6 weeks for fast track somewhere else , the inconvenience- PAST AND PRESENT…

It’s like they purposely make the experience horrible so they can eventually get rid of the entire online portion the institution has.']

name: Ridge Technical College
reviews:
['I’m extremely disappointed with the lack of communication from the financial aid office at Ridge Technical College. I was told that Tatiana would follow up with me regarding an update on my financial aid status, and it has now been over two weeks with no call back, no email, and no update.

Financial aid is time-sensitive and incredibly important for students who are trying to plan their education and finances. Waiting this long without any communication is frustrating and unprofessional. A simple phone call or email to provide an update—even if there was no change—would have made a big difference.

I expected better support and responsiveness, especially when it comes to something as critical as financial aid. I hope the school works on improving communication within the financial aid department so future students don’t experience the same issue.', 'I highly recommend the nail specialist program at Ridge Technical College with Ms. Still and Mrs. Bly. They are both amazing teachers and individuals. They put so much time and effort into the program and it shows. Not only did I gain all the required knowledge to become a licensed nail specialist (and then some) but I also I thoroughly enjoyed my time as a student with them. They are very hands on and truly care about the program and their students.', 'I Attended Ridge technical 1979  to 1981 truck and bus diesel mechanics, fire safety, LP gas training, air conditioning and heating and some other shorter courses. Found them to be a great start/foundation to our small business started nearly 40 years ago. Would  highly recommend this school to anyone that wants to make a difference in their livelihood. My son and I have been working together for nearly 10 years now and I have shared what I learned through these courses. Thank you Ridge technical for a lifetime of Success in our family business.', 'I just call to get info on a program that they offer in the speaking Spanish lady answer. With a bad attitude. It’s not free I’ll be paying it’s not a free education so I really don’t get it.what a bad service definitely don’t want to study there.', 'Trying to contact this place is ridiculous. I’m trying to reach student services and it just immediately hangs up the phone without ringing during open hours. So I tried another extension and the lady was so rude. Very angry in tone. I was transferred and of course, no one picked up. I just want to apply for a class, and the website is so buggy. Crazy']

name: Ringling College of Art and Design
reviews:
["My daughter goes to school here and I love it!  Staff are wonderful!  My daughter raves about professors and her program.  Students are given opportunities to participate in conventions pertaining to the specialty, my daughter went to IAAPA.  Guest lecturers happen often.  Professors have great contacts and share info with students.  It has been a very rewarding experience for her.  She's also with like minded students who work very hard.", "Seeing these reviews be incredibly polarized made me want to leave an honest review as a current student.
First off, if you are not ready to pull all nighters, face criticism that may be super harsh, then this school is not for you. This is not a art school in the traditional sense, this is a school that prepares you for industry work. They're gonna lay down the hammer on you and build you up for the inevitable crunch you will receive. If you can't handle the curriculum, then you probably won't be able to handle that work in the future. A lot of the reviews from neurodivergent people point out how hard this school was on them, so if you fit somewhere in that bubble then maybe consider a career change, or freelance.
Now for the price of the school, if you're planning on going here you better not dream of wasting time and slacking off. If you take advantage of the opportunities here and study, build connections with students and faculty, volunteer, you will have an amazing experience. You will grow as an artist and you will be set up for a promising career.
The staff knows what they are doing, obviously you aren't guaranteed to have a lot of chemistry with them, but they all no doubt have years of experience in their fields. They are not bullies, they are here to help you get better, even if that means giving you the most harsh critique you've ever heard in your life (Me personally I've only ever witnessed 1 - 3 people get really harsh feedback, so it's not even a common occurrence)
The school has an amazing career services team. They bring multiple people over a month to give talks, bring recruiters, host job fairs, give resume critiques, all for free, and are still accessible after graduation. My friend already got an internship as a sophomore at a huge company thanks to the schools connections.
The cafeteria food is fine? Some days it's pretty good, other days they'll have food that no one eats. It's the most average college cafeteria food ever.
Now on the darker side, yeah the school is not great at all at handling student misconduct. They are currently being sued for sweeping heavy things under the rug and giving students a slap on the wrist. There are students who are still here who have done horrible things and the school keeps them here. It's a problem that they aren't getting any better at.
To top this all off, the school has a great growing campus, the faculty are great and know what they're doing, if you put in the work, you are guaranteed to grow. There are a few places where the school falls flat, but overall if you're looking for a college experience where you can find good friends, get better at what you do, and want a promising career, then Ringling is probably a pretty good choice. Just please don't waste your money if you go here, a good 30 - 40% (ballpark estimate) of students in the year end up dropping out or transferring. Be prepared to consider if you can afford it and if you think you're capable of putting in the work. Otherwise, it'll be a huge waste of money", 'Was lovely to walk around and dream! The creativity and skill it takes to produce this medium is unreal. These pieces are stunning!', 'The campus is growing and expanding. Several buildings that being built are finished. It is really a nice place to go to school for all of those artist and gamers.', 'It’s a great college with kind faculty, amazing classes and a great community. Ive learned so much about art and design here.']

name: Rollins College
reviews: ['I absolutely love Rollins College. The campus is stunning and makes the perfect backdrop for family photos, engagements, and wedding portraits. The light, the architecture, and the peaceful walkways are always beautiful. If you are looking for a gorgeous location and a photographer to capture your memories, I would love to serve you.\nThe Wandering Storyteller Photography', 'Today I attended a beautiful service in honor of Martin Luther King hosted by Rollins community connections. It was a beautiful service that really highlighted black history with guest speakers, spoken words and musical performances. This was the first time I attended this service and I am looking forward to many more. Thank you', "My son goes to Rollins College and he can't be happier.  Great teachers, wonderful kids, delicious food,  very small up to 15 students classes.", "What a beautiful campus! I absolutely love the trail by the lake - it's perfect for a morning run. All of the wildlife, nature, & fresh air... not to mention the beautiful sunrises... & all of the gorgeous buildings.", 'We have visited dozens of colleges and universities, and Rollins College campus is one of the most beautiful.  The grounds are immaculate and spacious, located on the lake in Winter Park.  While there we visited the Rollins Museum of Art on campus too.']

name: Saint Leo University
reviews: ["If I could give zero stars I would. This college experience the past four years has consisted of awful service from financial and all services provided by this university. If you want to live in a mold infested awfully kept apartment that costs you thousands SLU is your go to, If you want to deal with the worst financial team in creation, go to Saint Leo. Another thing to add is the school is so poorly kept financially that they have to cut almost all teams and organizations they have. To conclude if you are looking for a college in Florida I advise to to look at UCF, SCF, or any other college because this university is awful.\n\nTo add they will not help you when you're in a financial pinch if you don't have a way to pay out of pocket even if you have a loan set up they will refuse to lift a hold to ensure you can register for classes so they back you into a corner and force you to pay large balances out of pocket to ensure you can register.", "I've just started attending here and I'm loving it. Such a great community and everyone is so friendly everywhere you go. I've only been going 4 weeks now and I seem to find someone I can call a friend everywhere I go on campus. The scenery surrounding the campus is absolutely gorgeous as well and as a native of Pasco County I honestly had no idea that a landscape like this was so local until I started attending. I love the slow paced, country living out here and the experience I get being able to learn about the different cultures represented here. I've met Southern people, Northern people, Hispanic people, Caribbean people, European people, Middle Eastern people, and so many other cultures too. It's beautiful to see how understanding and forgiving everyone is of people of different cultures. While it does have some flaws, like losing power pretty often or the sometimes mediocre food in the cafeteria, they are so minor compared to all the great things this school offers. It is easy to get scholarships too. 11 out of 10 I would recommend attending this school. I also would recommend the Honors Program. In addition to getting a huge upgrade on your dorm (your own bedroom and a shared living room!), it's pretty easy to get into, and the classes are so engaging and fun and honestly pretty easy if you like conversation. Shout out to Professor Orlando! I know that there were issues in the past with the school but I have been going under the new President and new leadership and when I see the old reviews saying how terrible the experience was for those people, I cannot believe it. (Also, the food really isn't that bad. I mean, it's college cafeteria food, you can't expect a 5-star gourmet restaurant.) Overall, I'm so glad to be here and this is definitely worth the work to get into the school and get scholarships. Definitely would recommend!", "This is my son's girlfriends school and I went to visit and it's actually really really nice. They've got like their own little town with everything you can think of. Its really nice and I heard the teachers are not to shabby either, that they're good. Is recommended my friends/family to go there, that's why I gave them a 5 star rating.", "This school looks nice and cozy. It appears that there wouldn't be as many distractions as some schools, but you could still receive an education.  The school seems very well kept! I would go here, and I am going to recommend to this a family member.", 'Love this school. Professors are great, campus is beautiful and clean. Lots of students activities and sports.']

name: St Petersburg College
reviews:
['I was enrolled in a few classes here since my home campus is small and doesn't offer everything I wanted to take. My favorite class here was the astronomy lab, as rhis campus has its own planetarium and observatory. My astronomy professor, Professor Joseph, was great. He was humorous and offered a variety of engaging and fun lab activities ranging from telescope viewing nights to physics labs where we manipulated light. The campus itself is well-equipped and well taken care of. This campus also has much more of a "college vibe" if that makes any sense.  😆
As partially stated earlier with Professor Joseph, the staff here are nice. The only negative experience I've ever had with a staff member here was with one of the math tutors who got frustrated with me for not grasping the material quick enough, I guess? I won't specify their name to respect their privacy, but wow that was unacceptable.', 'I’ll be direct. I am paying a lot of money to take this class, and the way students are treated in it is unacceptable.

This course is not challenging in a productive way it is stressful because of how feedback is delivered. Comments are written in ALL CAPS, which does not feel like instruction. It feels like being yelled at. There is a clear difference between constructive criticism and being rude, and this class consistently crosses that line.

I don’t want to state this as a fact, but it genuinely feels like I have to walk on eggshells with everything I post, especially in American Government discussions. When my opinion does not seem to align with the professor’s, I feel like my work is graded more harshly. I have received feedback saying I failed to include things that I specifically remember were not part of the instructions.

When I try to double-check the instructions, I can’t because the original posts and previous assignments are deleted after grading. I checked my other courses, and this is not how they operate. Those assignments remain visible. Removing them makes it impossible to understand expectations, learn from feedback, or feel confident that grading is fair.

Students are spending over $4,000 to take classes . If this were free, maybe the attitude would still be inappropriate but at least understandable. When students are paying thousands of dollars, professionalism is not optional. The way students are spoken to shows a lack of care for the people actually taking the class. I respect this school and teachers that I have don’t get me wrong. My other teachers have been very friendly supportive and amazing here. Especially my counselor she is super sweet. This is a great college.

Only problem I have is:

This American Government course. Students should not feel pressured, intimidated, or afraid to express themselves. Freedom of speech should not feel like a liability in a class built around it.

Students are dealing with real life. I have family from Ukraine who now reside in Poland. I have a grandmother going through cancer. Many students are carrying serious personal stress, and no one deserves added pressure from a professor who is dismissive rather than supportive.

I understand that he  is accomplished and knowledgeable. Being smart or published does not give anyone the right to treat paying students this way. Knowledge without respect does not create a healthy learning environment.

I’ve never experienced a professor like this. And it’s unfortunate, because one class like this can completely overshadow an otherwise positive school experience.

I’m sharing this because I care about my education and because students deserve better.', 'This is my second time enrolling in college. The first time was years ago, before on-line classes were a thing. That college, their  staff, advisors, financial aid office were amazing. With me at every step. Making sure I had everything I needed before deadlines. Advocating for me for financial aid, for example they would constantly tell me if there were other grants or scholarships available.
I mean obviously It did require organization on my part as well, but it felt like they had my back.....like they were working for me in a way. I could completely trust them to help me with everything. Almost like I had a team of people making sure I succeeded.

I had to mention my past experiences so I can share that I know for a fact the support received through spc is garbage.
I feel like a lot of it might be miscommunication or maybe the on-line portal. I had no idea the name of my advisor. I reached out to their financial aid office twice with no response. My transcripts have been sent but nobody has any clue where they are.....and they were sent electronically.
I was so excited to enroll and sign up for classes but I think Im going to just have to walk away. It sucks because my application fee I had to but on my credit card and I just pretty much threw that money away.
I terrified to get in any further with this college.', 'We took the students to look at the  Planetarium. They had such an amazing time, I would love to take them back again. You can take your family on Friday nights and Wednesday nights. Just call SPC for more information.', "This school has been steadily improving for years.  It's amazing to see the school grow.  The cost is very low and they have so many programs. They are connected to USF for things like ROTC.   Where else can you go to school for $3,000-$4,000 a year in 2018?"]

name: Santa Fe College
reviews:
['I visited the International Admissions Office, and they were all so friendly and helpful. I especially want to say a big thank you to Elizabeth Madrigal — she was very friendly, knowledgeable and kind. I was in a hurry to get my acceptance letter, and she helped me with every step and constantly followed up on my application until I got it. She’s one of the nicest people you could ever meet. Thank you to the entire International Admissions Office team!', 'This is by far the worst school I have ever attended. While yes, there are a few very kind professors, most do not care about their students whatsoever and only see you as numbers. The advisors are some of the worst people in the world—not only do they not know their own school’s policies, but they also leave you in the dark about classes, graduation, and transfer requirements.

I started at Santa Fe as a dual enrollment student, and I had to learn how to check everything myself. When I asked for help on where to find policies, transcripts, or credit information, I was either completely ignored or guided to the wrong place. I was intended to graduate from Santa Fe in 2025, but now it has been pushed all the way to early 2027 because my previous advisor had me taking classes that were completely unnecessary for my degree. Even now, my current advisor feeds me information in a delayed and unorganized fashion.

The only time anything has made sense is when I reached out directly to board members, presidents, or heads of departments. It should not be this hard to get an education. No one wants you to succeed here. DO NOT COME. Plus, the parking is horrible!!!!', 'Unimpressive, unresponsive and unhelpful.  I was hoping they would actually care even the slightest to evaluate my transcript - I was wrong.  Furthermore, they lost my PERT testing.  Getting a call back? Yeah right....  As a veteran, purple heart recipient and high valor awardee , I am ashamed of this school and the staff - they are just typical "I don't give a crap bureaucrats".  I went to advising to get some advice on programs and was told they don't do that - a direct quote.  I was told to talk to the employment office.  My question was about the academic work....  I was humiliated and sent away.  I have over 240 credit hours of education and I can't even get registered for a stupid class for a coaching license.', 'I am extremely disappointed with how SF College handles student concerns. Communication is almost nonexistent, emails and calls go unanswered, and when someone does respond, nothing actually gets resolved. It genuinely feels like the administration does not care about its students or the issues they are facing. Because of this lack of support and accountability, I am giving SF College one star, only because I don’t have the option to give less.', 'My son is attending the college on a bright futures scholarship and we have been trying to address his financial aid and no one will do their job. They do not respond to emails or voicemail and when my son sits for hours to be seen in person he is told that they will fix his issues, but there is no follow through. I am filing a formal complaint with The Federal Student Aid program and I suggest if you are having similar issues, you do the same. I will be doing whatever is in my power to get my son transferred to a different school.']

name: Seminole State College of Florida
reviews:
['If I could give this school a 0 star review I would. The professors are great but the rest of the staff from my experience are grossly incompetent. They will tell you one thing then do another. You get an email from them and good luck with getting an answer from them. They put a date in an email for something to happen that date is a lie they say February and they do it in January and don’t tell you. You call them to get help they will tell you all is fine don’t worry and then do the opposite of what they told you no warning or anything. Just tell you that your fine and your email will work then boom kicked out no access and trying to get any thing figured out good luck they will transfer you from department to department and no one has answers no one can help you. Makes me not one to ever attend a class here again it’s sad cause they use to be a great school but they have been going down hill over the past few years.

So here I am again trying to get access to my email that they said I would have access too. Waiting on hold can’t email an advisor or talk to anyone from my email about classes I was looking to take. Can’t access the important emails I need from my email or references I need from there to even talk to a person on the phone cause no access. So, now I’ve been transfer to 4 different departments and sitting on hold an hour now again.

This place is honestly getting worse every year. While I appreciate the advisors and the professors the rest of the staff needs to be replaced with more competent people.

So, here is the warning to any future students get ready to deal with incompetent staff here, get lied to by staff here, get transferred from department to department, and sit on hold for hours on in cause they lied to you. There is a reason why this school has 3.3 stars and falling every year. Won’t be surprised this school has below 3 stars by next year.

I do not recommend this school at all if you want a good college experience, try Valencia or any other college.', 'As a disclaimer, I am no longer attending SSC as I did graduate.

Seminole State College was legitimately the worse experience I have had at any college. Every single semester there was a challenge of patience, as I had to repeatedly jump through hurdles and pester the staff to get the financial aid I was eligible for. I had to fight to get the actual amounts I had signed for each semester when they would try to give me less, where I would have to just happen to be checking to notice the changes. Then I would have to fight to get it disbursed on time.

SSC has terrible communication in general, but especially with its students. I would constantly be fed misinformation or be told one thing by one person and then something conflicting by another. Most of the time I had to figure out the fixes to my issues on my own. To the point where I had been asked how I fixed something by IT once, so they could use it to help others. I even worked there for over a year and experienced firsthand how little the departments of the school knew of what happened in the others, so there was constant miscommunication or even none at all for extended periods.

Currently I am struggling to prove I have withdrawn from the school so the financial aid office will cease attempting to process a grant I was given… despite not being registered anymore with the school. Despite having my actual student account be disabled which even showed proof I had not been enrolled for almost a year. I have contacted the financial aid office and the registrar’s office who have both given me the direct ways to contact exactly who I supposedly needed to contact to solve my issue. This was almost a month ago and I have not had a single response since to any emails.

I cannot proceed any further in continuing my education with another college because the COD system has yet to be updated, so I cannot receive my grants to another school until SSC releases me. I am running out of time due to my next semester at a graduate school beginning soon, and I will be expected to pay thousands out of pocket if I cannot get my aid.

Thanks, Seminole.', "From my daughter's earliest days in elementary school, it was always the plan for her to complete her first two years of college at Seminole State and then use the (outstanding) Direct Connect program to transfer to UCF or another Florida university. My daughter is now in her sophomore year at Seminole State, and we couldn't be more pleased with her experience. The academic rigor is solid, campus life is vibrant, and the faculty and staff are always available and helpful. It's everything we could want from the college experience at a fraction of the cost so many of my daughter's friends are paying. Choice of college is a very personal decision with many factors that go beyond the academic experience, but I absolutely recommend EVERYONE at least tour and consider Seminole State.", 'Seminole State College of Florida is a real nice place. We have a Nice experience to be there. Me my wife and my Eight year kid really enjoyed this visit. We are in Building C for that adult education fair.', 'I enrolled at Seminole State College hoping for a smooth transition into their Medical Information Coder/Biller program. Unfortunately, I encountered repeated issues with poor communication from both Financial Aid and my academic advisor. Despite reaching out multiple times, I received little to no guidance or support, even after officially notifying them of my withdrawal. My final email to my advisor — sent out of courtesy and professionalism — was never acknowledged.

It’s incredibly disappointing to feel disregarded as a student, especially when all I was asking for was basic communication and support. I’ve since withdrawn and will be pursuing my education elsewhere. I hope the school improves how they treat students going forward — especially adult learners trying to better their lives.']

name: Saint Johns River State College
reviews:
["I have went to this college on and off for a few years. Most of the professors and advisors are great, however I've had a few bad experiences with both advisors and professors. It is also hard to get a return call, which makes it feel like your education isn't important. I am not the only one in my family who has had these issues.

SJR State also took away the ability to pursue two programs of study, without any warning, which leaves me and I'm sure many other students in my situation, having to skip semesters and reapply at a later time to finish their degree programs.

I used to love this college, but it is going downhill. If you can't find your preferred program of study at a better college, be prepared to have to skip semesters, especially if you have a nice amount of courses done already.", 'Went here for one semester. Absolutely awful staff, incompetent and rude. Gave me wrong information that cost me multiple times. Had one teacher that was good, the rest of the three classes….sigh…what a joke

I’ll always remind people to never come here, after I ran into a problem where I had gave negative feedback about one of my classes to one of my teachers, the teacher got upset and got the administrators upset and used their power to put a hold on my account preventing me from withdrawing from my classes because I didn’t attend their unaccommodating conduct meeting so they could “talk to me about it.” Am I in junior high school? Am I not paying you thousands of dollars for you to teach me?  Since then, Jack Carter Hall has made it clear he encourages this type of sadistic emotional egotistical behavior by continuing to refuse to accommodate. They do not care. It’s all about the money. Greedy corrupt thing of the past!', "The campus is so fricking gorgeous. Hats off to the grounds keeping crew because they KNOW what they're doing. There are even tags you can scan by the different flora to learn more about them. My big-backed self obviously took photos of the food too- shout out to the rolling stone family grill, it's so yummy!! You can find it in the student union hall with the pool table and arcade games 😊. Love this campus overall, it's so big and I used to get lost but now that I'm more familiar it's relaxing to just walk around and get a feel for the place.", 'It was easy to find, clean, and due to Covid masks are required inside.  My daughter is the first graduating class to receive her AA degree before graduating high school', "So far they've been able to help me with every problem I've had. I've only taken a few classes so far, but all of my professors have been great. Especially my Spanish professor, Dr. Gil makes learning so much fun. I would highly reccomend this professor if you decide to take Spanish to fulfill your language requirements."]

name: South Florida State College
reviews:
['I have been going to the college for a bit now, and it is the most friendly and helpful place I have been to. The staff are always helpful and the classes their always seem to be full with knowledge. Parking is a lot open. And the students have many amazing events to bring out the best of them.', 'I’ve had a frustrating experience with communication and organization here. Counseling and advising rarely call back, and I’ve had to constantly follow up just to get basic questions answered. Applications take forever to process, especially when it comes to getting into programs, which adds unnecessary stress.

The only real benefit of coming here is that it’s more affordable than a university — but that doesn’t excuse the lack of communication or organization. Just because we’re in a small town doesn’t mean students should receive anything less than proper support.

When I first attended a few years ago, things felt more structured. Since then, it seems like it’s been downhill. They no longer offer the EMT program, and overall student support doesn’t feel like a priority anymore. I truly hope the college improves the way they respond and follow through with students.', 'Wildstein performing arts center and enjoyed a fabulous concert US AIR FORCE BAND. Was spectacular and a perfect auditorium.', 'I was referred here by a close friend who is studying at the school for dentistry. The entire experience was great! From the moment I walked in, everybody had a smiling, friendly face. The initial examination was quick and thorough. The pricing is fantastic, and the instructors that guide the students are very knowledgeable and helpful. Everything is very professional and clean. It is a very nice building, and you can tell they have all the best and newest equipment on hand. Even the ceiling tiles are fun while you’re laying in the chair, as they have animal prints engraved in them and other fun things going on! I highly recommend checking it out. It will help a student that is studying dentistry, and you will be given fantastic here at a fantastic price!', 'We were here for a graduation program at the Wildstein Center. The staff were great and worked well together to get people inside and seated. The program was wonderful, and you could tell that the students loved their college president. The program was wonderful, and the center was clean and beautiful. There was plenty of parking and wheelchair accessible entrances.']

name: University of South Florida
reviews:
["Observing the rapid evolution of the University of South Florida over the years, it is clear from the glowing testimonials of my friends and local business leaders that this Tampa-based powerhouse has truly come of age. The general consensus among those I’ve spoken with suggests that USF seamlessly blends the resources of a top-tier research institution with a surprisingly personalized touch that makes the vast Fowler Avenue campus feel like a tight-knit community. Many acquaintances have specifically highlighted the university's prowess in healthcare and innovation, noting how the institution serves as a crucial springboard for graduates entering the competitive Florida job market. It is genuinely impressive to hear firsthand accounts of the faculty’s dedication to student success, where high academic expectations are matched by an equally strong support system for diverse learners. The prevailing sentiment in our local circles is one of immense pride, particularly regarding how the university fosters a culture of global citizenship and forward-thinking problem solving. It’s heartening to see such a vibrant hub of intellectual energy that remains so deeply committed to the economic and social flourishing of the entire region. Ultimately, the positive buzz surrounding the Bulls is entirely justified, as USF continues to redefine what it means to be a modern, impactful public university.", "I should have saved money and went to a local state college. The degree doesn't matter and USF is not prestigious enough to make a difference. Polk State College is an excellent substitute.

Here the classes are too big for you to learn anything, everything is too expensive, and the parking is a nightmare. Honestly one college to AVOID. Having been to Polk State, USF, and UF, I would put this one last on the list.

Thats my 30 thousand dollar lesson. Unless you live close and need a specific degree, its not worth the money.", "They have a wonderful MUSIC program for children in middle and high schools.
AUTUMN WINDS , BAY WINDS AND SUMMER CAMP !
EXTRAORDINARY TEACHERS....
Scholarship funding available as well (  you' ll have to ask for details)
If you have a child interested in advancing in music, this is such a wonderful gift to give them !", 'Had the chance to tour. Beautiful campus. Our young adults seem happy and free as they roamed around. Staff was inviting and the overall feeling you have is everyone seems invested in the future. Awesome school!', "The doctor's here are amazing.  They are very professional and explained everything you need to know in great detail. I like the valet parking and it was only $3."]

name: St. Thomas University
reviews:
['This university has potential, but the lack of support from the business office and financial aid is unacceptable. It is extremely difficult to get in contact with anyone in these departments. Calls go unanswered, and emails often take a week or more for a response , if you get one at all. Students are forced to repeatedly follow up just to receive basic information.

What makes this worse is the lack of communication between staff. You can speak to one representative and get an answer, only to be told something completely different by someone else. It creates confusion, delays, and unnecessary stress for students who are just trying to handle important financial matters.

For a university that expects professionalism and accountability from students, the administrative support should reflect the same standard. Until communication and responsiveness improve, this will continue to be a major frustration for students!', 'Great atmosphere, there is always an amazing event going on there. All the sport teams are exciting to watch', 'Amazing university! Great structure, amazing body of teachers, place clean and very organized! Highly recommended!', "WORST SCHOOL FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS , THINK TWICE!
READ MY STORY!
I completed my bachelor's degree and started my Master's in the fall of 08/25/2023, and just 2 months later, after checking in with the DSO to change my I-20 and my level of education, they terminated me and didn't let me know until now that I went to the DSO office to change my I-20 and asked her to transfer me to another school, now 2 years later and 24 credits of the master level completed i have to return to my country with a 5 year old kid and a wife that i am fully responsible, probably facing immigration issues with the US because someone couldn't reach out or simply see that i was registered and fully enrolled in school!
Their entire staff is unhelpful and will ruin your life as they did with mine! Currently in the task of suing them!", "Great facilities and a great campus!! The football staff were amazing sponsors for today's 6th Annual Orange Bowl Showcase@"]

name: Stetson University
reviews: ["I’m writing this review on behalf of a current athlete’s family to bring attention to ongoing concerns within the cheerleading program's coach. The coach consistently speaks to the team in a harsh and demeaning way, creating an environment that feels more like intimidation than leadership. What should be a supportive and motivating experience has instead become stressful and discouraging for many athletes. These students work incredibly hard and deserve to be treated with respect. I truly hope the university takes this feedback seriously and evaluates the coaching practices in place for the well-being of the team.", "We toured this college for my son, he loved it but we couldn't make the costs work, I expect he would have attended their business school otherwise. Very modern campus, the business related areas we toured were modern. Admissions staff was amazing, very helpful and friendly.", 'this is a small, private university in DeLand, Florida, between Orlando and Daytona. there are a few residence halls and academic buildings, a student union with a dining hall and study spaces, a wellness & recreation center, and a physical & mental health center. there’s also lots of greenery around the campus, making it a beautiful place to walk through.', "It's a really gorgeous campus with unique and beautiful buildings. The people are kind and helpful. It's a smaller campus but it seems to be located in a good area, not too far from Orlando. There's some good family owned restaurants in the area that are excellent to go to.", 'Great nature surroundings and building structures. Me and my family came to a graduation and all the staff was very nice and organize at the beginning but they lost control because the place got to full. But they tried to handle the best of their abilities.']

name: Southeastern University
reviews:
['Graduation ceremony for my daughter today was fantastic , such a beautiful school . The ceremony was on the field for her December graduation and the presentation was on point to include fireworks, key speakers, a singer as we sang a worship song together, the entire presentation was phenomenal as is her staff and school. I highly recommend SEU~', "Update 7.25
Finally there and super happy. In the end they are coming through for the Masters Program. Looking forward to parents weekend drop off. More posts to come.
Update 7.12.22
I still love this school for my kid but have been less than impressed with my own experience getting into Masters program for Nursing. It's been a rough go with little to no communication. I hope its just because its a new program but a month out from when my daughter starts in fall and still know nothing about my program, what classes, cost or when it starts. I'll post an update when I find out more. I hate lowering my rating but have to due to my experience so far.

Amazing campus. I went on a visit for my kid and I want to go.
Update 6.17.22
This place is still amazing. My oldest is going there and I decided to do Grad school there. Hope to teach there one day.
You want a place thats gonna love your kid and want the best for them. Look no further. We have visited several times before making our choice and its always the same no matter who you talk to. They are about supporting your kid through a Christ centered education. Diverse student population. Many of the staff are past alumni.  The list goes on.", "One of the finest campuses I've visited. It is described as an resort styled campus. Lakes on two side. More food on campus than I've seen before. Patrolled 24hrs by security with Deputy sheriffs on campus throughout the day and evening.", "I am studying Sports Media at this college for the next four years. I love it here, and it's a very lively atmosphere. A bonus is that I'm a member of the Athletic Pep Band in the clarinet section, and I've played at SEU Fire Basketball and Football games. I 100% recommend SEU because the experience that you'll have is going to be an amazing one!

I hope that someone will attend this school not because of it's distance from the theme parks, it's because they have a heart to love others and worship our LORD JESUS CHRIST, who loves us as well. You're gonna love it here!", 'Its a shame how poor the customer support is at SEU. As a student I spend 3 weeks trying to get someone to help reactivate my student account to register for class. It has gotten very frustrated and stressful just trying to connect with someone to help.']

name: Tallahassee State College
reviews:
['Devonte is an excellent cashier. While assisting me, he was also training a new associate who was asking questions about a customer. Even while handling both tasks at the same time, he remained patient, professional, and attentive. He showed great integrity and outstanding customer service despite everything going on. He also helped me with a return even though I lost my receipt and did not receive one by email. Thank you, Devonte', 'Quality education at an affordable price! The professors are excellent educators and are committted to helping their students achieve their goals. In fact, all of the staff including the academic and financial aid advisors, and just about anyone else you’ll encounter are quick to offer any assistance they can. Great place to begin your college education!', 'If you are considering TSC’s Nursing program, I urge to carefully consider the following…

The program is presently run by a grossly incompetent administration which is driving it to the ocean floor.

Within the past 6 months, they have terminated at least 2 instructors, one of which was so deplorable, as a nursing instructor, she walked out in the middle of the semester leaving the students unable to perform and learn the material subject matter.  Despite this, the Dean of Students failed several of these students and made them pay for another semester.

PLEASE take heed.  Mark and avoid this program until the present administration is replaced!', 'Staff is Useless. RUDE. Incompetent shouldn’t work for a school if you genuinely don’t care about students. School is just as bad for keeping them employed!', 'Extremely grateful for the opportunity, knowledge, and care I received from TSC. Not only do I believe my career, income & impact have been assisted by what I learned in general, but I also frequently remember the courses and information during real life situations and apply it - even at times subconsciously - to improve my work and life and hopefully the lives of others.

The vast majority of staff and academic counseling were helpful and genuine educators.

The facilities were pretty solid for a smaller college. Will say the athletics needs some more investment, especially for the relative talent rich environment in which TSC is located, and please a JUCO football team. I still am shocked by the amount of potential in even just football specifically that goes by the wayside because of no JUCO opportunities in Florida…

Aside from that TSC helped develop my life and mind for the positive. Great value, the time you put in will pay dividends and highly recommend!']

name: Talmudic College of Florida
reviews: ["The first week at Talmudic University Yeshiva Beit Moshe Chaim brought me a positive experience. The professor interrupted his first-day lecture to share a humorous story about his grandmother's kitchen while explaining a difficult Talmudic term, which made the entire class laugh. The large size of my New York seminary creates an impersonal environment because its teaching staff members enter and leave frequently.\n\nThe classroom environment at this institution felt authentic to me because students maintained genuine friendships with each other. The shuttle service experienced a delay during my time at the institution. The shuttle delay became acceptable because of the free coffee and genuine apologies, which made the campus feel welcoming.", 'Great crowd of boys, out-of-town warm environment maintaining perfect balance, not yeshivishe but from. Incredible staff.', 'i was in this university and its so nice thiere', 'Excellent school caring faculty', 'Great place!']

name: The University of Tampa
reviews:
['I was enrolled in the MBA program at the University of Tampa and was only part of the School of Business. My experience was extremely disappointing and ultimately led me to transfer.

First, the quality of instruction was very poor. Many professors were unprepared, disorganized, and disconnected from real-world business practice. Despite paying premium tuition, I did not feel that I gained practical or applicable skills that justify the cost of the program.

Second—and most concerning—the credit structure is misleading. The MBA program is advertised as 40 credits, completable in 12 months, at $758 per credit hour. However, after starting the program, I discovered (on my own, not through advising) that I was actually required to complete 58 credits to graduate. This information was never clearly communicated beforehand. That is an additional $13,644 in tuition alone, which is a massive and unacceptable surprise for any graduate student.

Third, there are no academic scholarships offered for graduate students, which makes the already expensive program even less accessible.

Fourth, most MBA courses are only 2 credits, which creates serious problems if you decide to transfer. When I attempted to transfer my credits, none of them were accepted, because most graduate programs use 3-credit courses. As a result, I had to retake courses I had already completed. Once I realized I needed 58 credits and that my credits wouldn’t transfer, the decision to leave became very easy.

Finally, the administration and advising are completely incompetent. I did not even have an assigned academic advisor at one point. When I asked questions about registration or degree requirements, I was repeatedly sent from one office to another, with no one taking responsibility or providing clear answers. Everything feels disorganized and inefficient.

On top of all this, Tampa is extremely expensive, housing (both on- and off-campus) is a constant headache, and the school largely caters to students from very wealthy backgrounds.

If you value your time, money, and education, I strongly recommend looking elsewhere than at the University of Tampa.', 'I had a terrible experience at this university. I failed two semesters because I was severely sick and they denied my academic petitions to drop these courses and did not explain why my petition was denied they just told me i can appeal the decision and that i can email their director if i have questions and he is on vacation.', 'Excellent University. Our son is about to graduate and had one of the best life experiences attending there. Campus is beautiful, well maintained and always expanding. As a private university, we found that the overall costs to attend was less than our own so called state schools up north. Always warm and sunny in Tampa!', 'Our daughter attends UT and loves it.  Campus is clean, very nice and safe.', 'My daughter just graduated from University of Tampa. She is happy with her experience. She was mostly happy with her professors and her classes. Classes were smaller size, so that professors knew their students names and communicated well. She was able to find a small job off campus for three years to make herself spending money. Hurricanes were disruptive, but she enjoyed the surprise breaks from school. She studied and did her work timely and received excellent grades.  I feel she is well prepared for her future.']

name: Webber International University
reviews:
['I have been a student at Webber International University since Fall 2023 and in the nursing program for the past 1.5 years. During that time, the program has gone through significant changes. While transitions can be challenging, these changes have ultimately led to meaningful improvements and a stronger, more supportive learning environment.

Nursing Director Jenafer Garcia and her team have truly been at the forefront of this transformation. Their leadership has helped create a more positive, structured, and accepting program that I am proud to be a part of. They genuinely care about their students and consistently demonstrate that their goal is to see us succeed—not just academically, but as future nurses.

WIU is a very athletics-focused campus, and the nursing program makes a strong effort to support student-athletes. The faculty work with students to help them continue participating in their sports while meeting the rigorous demands of the nursing curriculum. That level of understanding and flexibility speaks volumes about their commitment to student success.

I am grateful for the growth the program has experienced and for the dedication of the faculty who continue to invest in our development as we progress through our nursing careers.', 'I am currently a third-semester nursing student, and I am proud to be a part of this program. Throughout my three semesters, it has been very easy to reach my professors during and after business hours. The nursing lab, along with a staff filled with years of experience who guide you through realistic scenarios, makes walking into clinicals feel natural rather than intimidating.
The nursing program also has a 100% NCLEX-RN pass rate. Our classes are smaller, which makes it easier to learn and encourages students to ask questions during lecture. We have completed clinical rotations at HCA Florida Highlands (Sebring), AdventHealth Lake Wales, and Lakeland Regional, gaining experience across various patient care units.
This program allows you to apply what you learn in the lab directly to the clinical setting, while also helping you discover where you belong in nursing after graduation.', "I'm having a very positive experience in the nursing program at Webber International University. The nursing instructors are knowledgeable, supportive, and genuinely invested in student success. They challenge us to think critically while also providing guidance and encouragement throughout the program. The curriculum is rigorous and prepares students well for clinical practice and the NCLEX examination. Clinical experiences are well-organized and offer hands-on learning opportunities that help build confidence and competence in real-world settings.", 'My experience in the nursing program at Webber International University has been both challenging and rewarding. The nursing professors truly care about their students and push us to reach our full potential. They are approachable, responsive, and always willing to help clarify difficult concepts. The program is demanding, but it prepares you to think like a nurse and apply critical thinking skills in clinical situations.', 'Since transitioning from the SAU nursing program to the Webber Nursing program, I had a seamless transition and felt consistently supported by the staff throughout my entire journey. The staff and my peers are incredibly welcoming, and I believe the quality of education has exceeded my expectations. I am confident that I will be the most prepared nurse.']
