reviews:
['I recently applied and spoke with Tomika. She was very informative and extremely helpful in guiding me through the process of applying. As well as helpful in advising me on all of the available options to me from ICT Morrow. It was a refreshingly pleasant experience in a world where customer service seems a lost art.', 'Deciding to go back to school was more than a simple choice for me — it was personal. I’ve got kids looking up to me, depending on me, watching how I move. And I want to be someone they can be proud of. Someone who doesn’t give up. Someone who keeps pushing no matter what. So choosing ICT felt like the first real step toward building a better future for them and for myself.

But right after I paid the registration fee, everything fell apart. My high school diploma couldn’t be found. The only thing on file was my Job Corps diploma, and ICT couldn’t accept that.

I can’t even explain the feeling…
It hit me in a way I didn’t expect.

All I could think was, “I’m trying to do the right thing. I’m trying to better myself for my kids… why does something always have to go wrong?” It felt like another door closing. Another opportunity slipping away. Another moment where I’d have to look at my kids and feel like I failed at something important.

But then… Tomika and Keshana showed up for me in a way I will never forget.

They didn’t treat me like just another student. They didn’t brush me off or act like it was too much work.
They took their time. They searched. They dug through everything they could until they FOUND my real diploma.

That wasn’t just paperwork to me.
That was hope.
That was a second chance.
That was my kids’ future being put back on track.

And they didn’t stop there. They helped me with my testing. They walked me step-by-step through my FAFSA. Anytime I called — nervous, confused, or needing guidance — they answered right away. No attitude. No frustration. Just real support and kindness.

It meant something to me.
Because I’m not used to people going that hard for me.
Especially not people who didn’t have to.

I’m truly, deeply grateful for them. They took a moment that could’ve broken me and turned it into a reminder that good people still exist — people who want to see you win.

And now, because of them, I’m not going into January stressed or uncertain.

He didn’t just teach,he invested his time and energy to ensure that every detail was understood and executed with precision.\nIn a world where rushed instruction is all too common, Mr. McCall stands out as a rare example of someone who truly cares. His commitment to excellence and his insistence on doing things the right way made a lasting impression on me. It's not often you encounter an instructor who treats your success as his own mission.\nIf you're looking for a training experience that combines professionalism, heart, and an unwavering standard of perfection this is it.", 'I completed a 2 day Forklift Training & Certification course with Mr.McCall here at Atlanta Technical College. He was very knowledgeable, patient, stern, professional, and overall positive. I definitely learned a lot. All my classmates were awesome, and we all worked together to help each other pass the course. I will definitely be taking more classes at Atlanta Technical College to further my education & skills.', 'I’m writing this review with tears in my eyes because I never imagined I would feel this broken by a school I trusted with my future. When I started this nursing program, I came with hope, determination, and the belief that hard work would be enough. I sacrificed everything to be here. I studied eight hours a day, I missed time with my children, I quit my job so I could focus. I am in the process of being evicted and losing my car because I was willing to make the temporary sacrifices for the bigger picture. I think the teachers here have lost sight of us being people and not just numbers. I believed this program would help me build a better life for my family. I accepted those sacrifices because I understood they were temporary.I believed the struggle would be worth it. What I did not expect was to feel unsupported, discouraged, and powerless in a program that is supposed to lift students up. Instead of guidance, many of us felt shut out. Instead of mentorship, we felt ignored. Instead of being taught, we were left to figure things out on our own. When students spoke up and asked for fair treatment or clarity, we were made to feel like problems instead of just helping us. It is heartbreaking to pour your entire life into a dream and feel like the people responsible for helping you succeed are unwilling to do so. Many of us entered this program full of passion and left feeling defeated, anxious, and emotionally drained. Nursing school is already hard. It is supposed to be. But it should never feel like students are fighting the program instead of being supported by it. To the single mother or father reading this, to the person working two jobs and studying late at night, to the student who is sacrificing everything to become a nurse,I want you to know that your dream is valid. You deserve a program that believes in you, teaches you, and prepares you, not one that leaves you feeling hopeless. I truly wish someone had warned me before I enrolled.You can become a nurse. But please carefully consider whether this is the place that will help you get there.', 'My experience here was by far the best. Very good course, has all the information needed. Having been trained on several different forklifts myself, Mr. McCall was very patient and informative. The Strive Atlanta program and the Atlanta technical college have been a blessing to me.']

name: Point University
reviews:
['Disorganized. Son had a dual enrollment class that he didn’t get a book for until 3 weeks after the class started. It was blamed on the book distributor but they had his classes wrong the day before classes started even though I had it in writing what he was supposed to be scheduled for. I finally get in touch with a human just for someone in Dominique office (billing) to hang up in my face as well as my husband face when he called. THIS MESSAGE WILL ALSO BE GOING ON ALL SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS AND I WILL TAG THE SCHOOL AS WELL', 'On campus 02.11.24 for Point vs Keiser Men's Lacrosse
Parent group of 20+ from Florida 10+ hours to listen to the student section taunt our players for 2 hours and calling them by name.  This is "chirping" culture on your campus is embarrassing.  These students were not their to watch the game or cheer on your boys, who played great by the way. AD out of town

Guys in the press box we're enjoying it and taking no leadership for the student section we were told "that's a security" problme.

If this is the environment you're fostering it's sad.  This is what I will remember about our visit.  Thanks 1 star.', 'My 1 star rating is not just because I have encountered countless issues, but rather, because addressing issues with Point is nearly impossible. Additionally, in my 2 years with point, I have only received one call back from voicemails left with the different departments of the school. I wouldn’t recommend Point to anyone, and wouldn’t go back to Point even if I had a full-ride scholarship.', 'I am a student here and I had over $200 stolen out of my dorm because housing felt it necessary to change my locks with no notification before doing so and leaving the door unlocked. After reporting it to security they said it was my fault for the theft and they could do nothing about it. School is also extremely unorganized when it comes to credits and there is a reason why so few students graduate from school and transfer by their sophomore year.']

name: Clark Atlanta University
reviews:
['I went to CAU for a field trip recently and I had an amazing time! They always found new ways to entertain me and keep me engaged. name: Berry College
reviews: ["My friend was showing me around the town of Rome and Berry College campus was one of the places we visited. Campus looks gorgeous, almost like something you'd see in medieval Europe or Harry Potter. Plenty of nature trails nearby. Apparently it has the world's largest contiguous campus (27,000+ acrea). Can't speak for the quality of education here but I'd assume its pretty good.", 'Beautiful campus. Large, wide open campus with lots of deer. Very scenic and also has good facilities.', 'Berry is stunningly beautiful. Main campus has the feel of a Southern university, with it’s beautiful traditional architecture and brick buildings and columns. There is SO much green space. The balance of green space to people was the perfect proportion for our family and felt just right, after visiting larger schools like Clemson and UGA. There are SO many ways to get outdoors and be renewed and refreshed by the beauty of nature. The mountain campus is really cool too, as is the older section of campus used primarily as housing, faculty offices, and some parts of the nursing and education programs. They have good dining hall options, great recreational facilities and options, and technology/learning spaces. They offer a wide range of majors, and their agricultural program (including animal sciences) is really good. We did a tour for prospective students and could not have enjoyed it more. Our tour guide was a current Berry student (an ambassador), and he did a super job of showing us the campus and helping us see what life at Berry was like. The students and staff are so down-to-earth and unassuming. We felt welcome and like we belonged. The staff were so helpful and kind. Now, our eldest child is enrolled and thrilled to become a Berry student.', 'Beautiful campus. Like a smaller scale of Duke University. Nice landscapes with beautiful trees and flowers. Magnificent castle uphill. The whole campus was just filled with a classic atmosphere that could bring you back to the old times when campus was a sanctuary of peace, learning and self reflections. Come here to enjoy the walk and the scenery of the campus and read about the history of the establishment of this wonderful school.', 'If you are driving by, there are 40 miles of hiking trails and outdoor areas to keep you buss. I went to school here for undergrad and it is a wonderful school with a student work program that is very unusual and fantastic if you want to try your hand at business. If you are looking for a school with small class sizes and for a liberal arts education, consider looking here. The beauty of the school will draw you in, but the people with convince you to stay.']

name: Brenau University
reviews: ["Honestly after being an online student a Brenau for a full year, you're probably better off choosing another university. For starters, most of the instructors barely interact with you. They claim to respond to e-mails within 24 hours, but for me it takes almost a week to even get a response. No zoom meetings to interact with students as I would like. Second thing, they hardly even have any programs online to choose from. Not even any minors or the option to take up a dual major. Lastly, TUITION SHOULD NOT COST THAT MUCH AS AN ONLINE STUDENT OR COLLEGE STUDENT PERIOD. I am glad I am in the process of transferring to a university that cost nearly four times less than what I am paying per semester at Brenau.", 'The person I spoke with was unexpectedly aggressive and rude. Considering the call was already five minutes late, I found the tone especially disappointing—particularly for a program representing the nursing profession.', 'Great, warm and inviting staff. Clean campus and definitely historic.', 'Small campus with great hospitality.  My daughter loves it at Brenau!', "I wouldn't give this university one star if that were an option. The university seems alright through the enrollment process. The enrollment advisors and success coaches are great. After that you find out how bad the instructors really are as well as the provost and the registrar. All fully accredited master’s programs should be rigorous, but they should not be unbearable. The university crams an entire lifetime of work into seven weeks while claiming to cater to working adults with families. There is no support system whatsoever and the instructors are way too harsh with their grading. My colleagues went to universities with much better recognition and prestige and they were not anywhere near as overwhelmed as I was while attending Brenau. Time management is key, but I do not want to forget to mention that if you become ill and hospitalized for any reason, they will not empathize with you. If you need to submit an appeal to be readmitted to school or to gain financial aid eligibility, I would recommend you do not submit an appeal as they are still going to throw you out anyway even with all of your medical documentation. They are very quick to throw students out of the university with no looking back. Yet they wonder why their retention rate is so low. I would not recommend this school to anyone wanting to pursue a graduate degree. There are better options trust me."]

name: Brewton-Parker College
reviews:
["I'm an international student and this institution was recommended to me. Can someone advise me on whether it's worth enrolling in the program or if I should look for another institution? It's for the Bachelor's Degree in General Business.

Thank you very much.", 'I cannot say one redeeming thing about my experience at BPC. Attended for 2.5 years, only went for baseball.
The head coach was fired. All of the assistant coaches were fired. The best players on the team were kicked off. All of this happened in a year and a half. The program went from A to F.
They hired Ergun Caner, a wonderful Christian man who loved everyone just to force him out soon after due to his ethnicity.
There is nothing to do in this small town, the facilities on campus are nonexistent, the curfews are ridiculous, the amenities are worn down, the atmosphere is bleak, teachers rotate over and over, so there is no consistency, the program had no accreditation; when I transferred, I lost a year of college and had to repeat my prerequisites.
I would not be leaving this review if not for two reasons. Reason the first, 10 years later someone asks me where I attended, so I pull it up to show them. Reason the second, when I pulled it up, I see the school review is 4.5 stars when it is not worthy of the 1 star in this review.', 'Small school. Great people. Very Christ centered. Great nursing program.', 'I went to Brewton-Parker College for two years. I would say it is was great 50% of the time and was awful the other 50% of the time. It was a very small and great christian environment around the professors. Most students were very nice on campus. It was a very kind and accepting environment, but the living situations are awful. The buildings are very old, unclean, and run down on campus. I lived in one complex with seven other guys. This complex only contained two stalls and two showers. It might have just been my experience, but they do not have a huge variety of choice of where you want to live.', "As a college: My brother went here for two years, until the music department was suddenly closed down. Students found out through the local paper, and it was just handled very poorly. However, I have heard the school has improved a great deal since then, which I am glad of, and some of my friends went there after my brother's time there and seemed to like it. We have very few Baptist colleges in Georgia, and I hope this one is a good option for new students.

As a campus: I've been here for camp several different times and found the campus itself to be fairly standard as far as housing goes. Some places were in need of repairs, while some were newer and pretty; basically what you'd normally find at a college campus. The food was pretty standard as well. The grounds themselves are very pretty, including a lake and some special features by the lake. I actually met my husband at a camp here in the pavilion by the lake, and then last August he proposed in the pavilion. It has a lot of history for us, and I think of the place with the warmest of memories (literally and figuratively, as South Georgia's heat in the summer is no joke)!"]

name: West Georgia Technical College
reviews: ['Ms. Amber in the Hospitality program is probably the best professor I’ve ever had. She not only shows she cares by walking through class schedules and helping set up semesters, but by taking time to see how I learn and helping to tailor my learning to it. She makes class engaging and enjoyable with activities and discussions that are relevant and meaningful to the lesson. When I say I haven’t had a teacher like this before I really haven’t. She goes above and beyond to be the best teacher she can be and it shows. The hospitality program is structured well and flows at a smooth pace. I haven’t felt overwhelmed with the work load because she pairs each lesson with one or two assignments that help you to comprehend what you just learned. The projects are not to daunting with check points to make sure you don’t fall behind. We also have an excellent mentorship program where we are paired with a hospitality professional to help refine our skills. Overall I would not have stayed in college if it weren’t for the amazing support I’ve received from all staff especially Ms. Amber.', 'Just graduated today from trucking school & West Georgia Tech is one of the best schools. Mr. Hodge Mr. Leroy Mr. Bruce. Was very outspoken & outstanding thank you for all you do on my last day I was able to fly with the airbrakes test. Very great school to go to pursue your cdl. For everything you have to do for work & job security.', 'I wish I had went to any other college in Georgia. The computer science programs are outsourced through third parties that anyone could sign up for on their own. I had to basically pay WGT to act as a middle man to copy and paste the grades I earned through another party that also required payments to participate. It felt like a massive scam. And the fire science courses were a complete joke. I switched out of the program halfway through because of the “mini-mesters” they started piling on to push people through the program at lightning speed. But really it was for WGT to collect payments at lightning speeds. Again I wish I went anywhere else since they were transitioning to basically an online type of college. University of Phoenix is far more reputable at that point.', "I returned for the Spring semester after 5 years and I have to say I am not pleased this go around. Even though all my information was turned in before deadline, my funds were released late because no one in the FA office knew how to release them. After speaking with the director twice it was taken care of (2 weeks into class). I have had to basically coach everyone through how to handle my courses (which classes can be credited for others/ which classes I need to take) because I do not have an advisor. I was just contacted to be assigned an advisor via email but its a little too late since I am 66% complete with my degree. The staff must be over worked and under paid because they are rude and make you feel like you are a bother. I really feel bad for students that truly need advisement to succeed because you definitely don't get it here. I am actually withdrawing to transfer to another institution. I hope they can get the staff back on track, this use to be a really good school. :(  ***This post is strictly about advisors / admissions / FA office, my class experience has been wonderful and fulfilling. ***)", 'Worst financial aid department I’ve ever dealt with. Not just a one time thing. I’ve been going here off and on for almost ten years. Email is the only form of communication that they actually respond to. When they do reply, often their response is quite rude, especially if you do not understand their explanation and email them back stating so. Terrible customer service.']

name: Clayton  State University
reviews:
['Clayton State University has been great so far. When I need answers and don’t get a response right away, I take the initiative to go in person and ask everything I need to know. I understand that there are many students who need assistance, and I’m eager to stay on top of my education. I’m paying for school, so I make sure I get the information I need to succeed. Overall, my experience at CSU has been very positive, and I give them 5 stars for a strong start. 🧡', 'This shcool is not the same it has evolved in a negative way, The leadership is changing the school into a non " HBCU". be careful who we choose to lead in  these HBCU connected environments. This is not the Clayton University it was 6 years ago', 'As parents of an applicant, we just toured the campus and are impressed. The grounds and buildings appear to be well kept, the common areas are quiet/serene, and every student/employee/parent we encountered was pleasant/extremely helpful.

I would like to mention the following people, as they stood out:

Police officer/Campus police -Assisted with building location when GPS failed
Campus Security/Parking Permit -Patient
Student Center Cafeteria Staff -Provided a multitude of information/help with Smiles!

I left with the feeling that, should my son be accepted, he would be well treated and supported as a member of the student body.', 'I am writing this on behalf of my cousin, who was a dedicated student at Clayton State University and was on track to graduate in December 2024. Unfortunately, their academic journey was abruptly derailed by a deeply disappointing and unfair experience.
My cousin was accused of academic dishonesty, a claim that was later reviewed through available video footage and found to have no supporting evidence. Despite this, the university failed to correct the situation or take any meaningful action to help. Instead, they seemed to brush it off entirely, showing no concern for the truth or for the lasting impact this would have on a student’s future.
Throughout their time at Clayton, my cousin had no prior disciplinary issues and maintained a strong academic record. They deserved a fair and transparent process. Instead, they were met with silence, indifference, and a complete lack of accountability from the institution. This failure in due process has caused my cousin emotional distress, lost opportunities, and a deep sense of discouragement and depression.
Clayton State University should be truly ashamed of how they handled this matter. Students deserve to be treated with respect, fairness, and dignity, especially when their future is at stake.', 'At Night not so good really need more lights but easier to get around in the day time']

name: Columbus State University
reviews:
['Beautiful campus, great degree programs and faculty, extensive community involvement. Definitely check out all of their external programs. An integral pillar of the community that is constantly improving.', 'Like other schools, some of Columbus State University’s staff  is unpleasant to deal with. I don’t recommend coming here, especially if you have to take science classes. You can come here if you want, but keep your options open.', "CSU has been full of great opportunities that I have had the chance to take a part in and I've only been here a year so far! The campus only continues to grow and improve and all of the faculty and staff have been more than willing to help me get to where I need to be. Just like any school, as long as you stay on top of your work, it'll have some of the best times of your life! Can't wait for next year!

Edit-
One year later and I wish I could give it more stars! CSU's professional faculty and wonderful staff always leave me wishing other places were like them! CSU has given me some very valuable education and experiences. Every university has its faults, but with CSU, if you try and make a difference, they'll help you! People like to complain online but never do much in the real world. I've had very few times where something was amiss at this university, but when I addressed it to those that could help, they would do exactly that, and it would be fixed before I even knew it. Learning in the classes here is more fun than it is a chore if I'm honest. The professors really care and the classes are small enough to make real connections. I wish I could speak for everyone, but sadly I can't and am not sure just how true these bad reviews are, but I can attest to my incredible experience at CSU and how it is one of the best schools in the Southeast and definitely a hidden gem to those looking at schools. Still can't wait for another great year as CSU only gets better!

Second Edit-
It has been quite some time since making a review for me! It's been so long, that I graduated a year ago! Crazy stuff, but I still love this university! Through the pandemic, the tough times were made easier by support of the faculty and staff. Before the pandemic though, when this university could shine without limits, it really showed me what I was made of and what I could do in this life. Although smaller than most, CSU is mighty due to its community, support for students, and overall amazing ways of teaching. Looking back, I can tell there were moments where I was learning so much and didn't even realize it. Now that I have graduated, I can only appreciate my time there and wish that the end wasn't so bittersweet. If you are ever thinking of coming here, I would say go for it! Somehow, it is just a place that proves your potential and pushes you into new and better parts of life!", 'If you want to have fun, do not come to this school. It’s the most boring college ever, there’s no party life, the bars around town are boring. They shut down all of the the frat houses. All this school has going for itself is the theater and music department. Don’t recommend if you want a fun college experience. You can barely play music too loud without getting in trouble. This is like highschool for 20 years olds. Like it’s actually sad.', 'This university works magic for the first generation college student and really helps out the family. Thanks for the allowances you make on your students behalf. You all keep my girl safe! and encouraged.']

name: Emory University
reviews:
['Emory University, anchored at 201 Dowman Dr in the lush Druid Hills neighborhood, is consistently celebrated in my professional and social circles as a "Southern Ivy" that masterfully balances a liberal arts soul with the high-octane research power of a global top-tier institution. From numerous substantive discussions with alumni and medical professionals, a clear consensus emerges that the university operates with a merytorical precision, leveraging its unique proximity to the CDC and its world-renowned healthcare system to offer students a truly avant-garde educational experience. My colleagues often remark on the sophisticated, collaborative atmosphere of the Goizueta Business School and the Rollins School of Public Health, noting that the faculty demonstrates a profound dedication to nurturing both intellectual moxie and ethical leadership. In frequent conversations about the Atlanta academic landscape, the public sentiment consistently praises the campus for its remarkable architectural beauty and its role as a vital engine for scientific breakthroughs and social justice. I am particularly struck by the university’s commitment to interdisciplinary learning, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their children transform into compassionate, job-ready professionals within the school’s inclusive and rigorous environment. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration handles its prestigious status with a transparent and visionary hand, ensuring that an Emory degree remains a gold-standard credential across international markets. Reflecting on these consistently positive and grounded testimonials, I view Emory University as a distinguished entity that executes its complex mission with undeniable class, academic integrity, and an inspiring dedication to the betterment of humanity.', 'Writing from my experience as an alumni.

While Emory University provides high-level resources and reports strong overall career outcomes, my experience suggests that students may encounter significant obstacles in securing internships and employment, particularly when seeking early, industry-specific opportunities.

Alumni networks are also weak and loosely connected. Alumni are sparse, generally rare on linkedIn, and hard to get in proper contact with.

The reported employment statistics may overrepresent positive outcomes due to methodological exclusions. According to NACE (National Association of Colleges and Employers), graduates who cannot be reached, do not respond, or whose outcomes cannot be confirmed are excluded from the "Career Outcomes" denominator.

Students who attend, if they do attend, should be prepared to dedicate most of their time to supplementing their career with networking, alumni outreach, and external application efforts.', 'Beautiful impeccable manicured campus buildings and landscapes.  Vibrant engaging atmosphere with much history on display.', "Emory University, located in Atlanta, Georgia, is a prestigious private research institution known for its academic excellence and innovative contributions. The university offers a wide range of programs across undergraduate, graduate, and professional levels, with strengths in fields such as medicine, public health, law, and business.

Emory is celebrated for its cutting-edge research, particularly in areas like biotechnology, global health, and neuroscience. Its close collaboration with institutions like the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) enhances its impact on public health and medical advancements.

The campus combines historic charm with modern facilities, creating an inspiring environment for learning and discovery. Emory's diverse community of students and faculty fosters cultural exchange and intellectual growth. Its alumni network includes influential leaders, Nobel laureates, and pioneers in various fields, reflecting the university's global impact and legacy.", "Beautiful campus. We visited for relatives that were celebrating one of the kid's graduation ceremony. Nice time, well managed considering the volume of attendees."]

name: Georgia Highlands College
reviews: ['Meant to post this review days ago. The Rome campus is beautiful! Very clean, peaceful, and a fun place to hang out with the family! 💙', 'Problem # 1: georgia highlands college is the WORSE school I have ever attended! reviews:

name: Georgia State University
reviews:
['This is a shameful, awful, horrific institution. The fact that public universities have fallen so far is staggering. College-level science professors should speak fluent English.

Online courses should provide lectures. How can you have a Chemistry class with no provided lectures?!

This is absurd and disgraceful; I would even say criminal.

Lanier Tech is better than this school, and I gave Lanier tech a 1-star rating.

This school should lose its accreditation.', 'Georgia State University, woven directly into the vibrant urban tapestry of Atlanta, is frequently celebrated in my professional and social circles as a national model for student success and a transformative engine for upward mobility. From several substantive discussions with local entrepreneurs and alumni, a clear consensus emerges that GSU operates with a merytorical precision that masterfully bridges the gap between high-level academic theory and the fast-paced demands of the Georgia economy. My colleagues often remark on the university’s unique ability to foster a sophisticated, high-performance environment where diversity and innovation are not just buzzwords, but the primary drivers of intellectual growth. In frequent conversations regarding the regional educational landscape, those I trust repeatedly emphasize the university's legendary "Panther" resilience and its pioneering use of data to ensure that no student is left behind. I am particularly struck by the institution's strategic integration with the city's business district, which my acquaintances describe as a decisive advantage for securing top-tier internships and career-defining connections. It is evident from the collective feedback of my network that the administration manages this sprawling metropolitan campus with a transparent and visionary hand, successfully elevating GSU into the upper echelons of public research institutions. Friends who have navigated the Robinson College of Business or the College of Law often point to the faculty’s real-world moxie and their genuine dedication to mentorship as the defining features of their experience. The general sentiment among the community is that the university represents a prestigious and dependable pillar of progress that fulfills its complex mission with undeniable class and social integrity. Reflecting on these consistently positive and grounded testimonials, I view Georgia State University as a distinguished powerhouse that sets a gold standard for the modern, inclusive urban university.', "1975 (!) graduate of the Art Department; transferred from Atlanta College of Art (now SCAD) after two years when intrigued by fiber arts offered at GSU. The school IS downtown, began as a business night school, grew over the years. Stellar art department and academics when I was there. I wonder whether some negative reviews may be due to folks not understanding it is an URBAN campus, not an 'ivy covered' leafy campus. I also wonder whether it has gotten too big, unweildy in some ways? Security? The art building locked up at 10pm each night, and without a car I'd be on buses going home to Midtown but never had a problem; you just have to be aware of your surroundings. I hope the negatives will get addressed so the school's reputation is protected.", 'PLEASE BE VERY AWARE THAT THEY WILL HOLD YOUR DIPLOMA IF YOU HAVE A HOLD ON YOUR ACCOUNT . PLEASE ALSO BEWARE THAT IF YOU TAKE CARE OF HOLD THAT THEY WILL STILL KEEP YOUR DIPLOMA FROM YOU ! The school allowed me to accept a loan that I wasn’t suppose to receive then had me pay it back to then hold my diploma from me .The graduation department told me i would to have to repurchase a diploma I never once received because I was suppose to magically know that I only had one year to contact the graduation department and tell them that I wasn’t able to receive my diploma because I hadn’t payed my loan off as of yet, please be mindful of the young lady Shynece Aldridge in the graduation department who will tell you that it was your responsibility to know a policy that it not connected to your hold information  that I would some how magically know is a resource.', 'I want to sincerely thank the Sgt Nikita Peters  and Joann the communications representative who went far above and beyond to help me locate my lost wallet. From the very first interaction, their patience, compassion, and genuine concern stood out. Sgt Peters took extra time to check multiple locations and never made me feel rushed or dismissed, while Joann the communications staff member stayed engaged and reassuring throughout the process. In a moment of stress, their kindness meant more than they may realize. It is clear they were raised with strong values—kindness, empathy, and service to others.Those lessons clearly live on through the way they care for people in the community. I am deeply grateful and will never forget the humanity they showed me.💚💕👸🏽👸🏽']

name: University of Georgia
reviews: ['The University of Georgia, gracefully centered around the iconic Chapel and Herty Drive in Athens, is consistently hailed in my professional and social circles as a premier public institution that masterfully balances a "Public Ivy" academic rigor with an unrivaled campus spirit. From numerous high-level discussions with alumni and regional leaders, it is clear that UGA operates with a merytorical depth that places it firmly among the nation\'s top 20 public universities, particularly excelling in fields like insurance, real estate, and public affairs. My colleagues often emphasize the university’s unique "experiential learning" mandate, noting that this hands-on approach grants graduates a sophisticated professional moxie that is highly valued by global recruiters. In frequent conversations about the Southern educational landscape, the public consensus repeatedly praises the institution for its vibrant student life and a legendary alumni network that provides a lifetime of career-defining support. I am particularly struck by the university’s strategic research investments, which my acquaintances describe as a transformative force in the state’s economic development and scientific innovation. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages the Athens campus with a transparent, forward-thinking vision, successfully maintaining an elite academic atmosphere while fostering a genuinely inclusive "Bulldog" community. Friends who have navigated the Terry College of Business or the School of Law often point to the faculty’s accessibility and real-world expertise as the decisive factors in their own professional confidence. The general sentiment among the community is that UGA represents a distinguished and dependable powerhouse that fulfills its educational mandate with undeniable class, integrity, and a profound respect for its historic heritage. Reflecting on these consistently glowing testimonials, I view the University of Georgia as a world-class hub of learning that continues to set a gold standard for excellence in the modern era.', 'Fantastic museum! A real jewel of the south. I’m not a artsy or museum going person, but I visited with my daughter who is an art history major to see the American Women in Paris exhibit. While she was studying the paintings I spend 2 full hours thoroughly engage and entertained roaming the other exhibits. There is a lot here to enjoy. Please visit if you can and enjoy a few hours in another world.', 'Did the campus tour with our son.  Admissions team...AWESOME!  Tobey is the best.  Ate at Joe Frank dining hall, food was really good.  Overall fantastic experience.   GO DAWGS@', 'Beautiful campus. A nice mix of social life and classes. Having a business degree from the University of Georgia has always served me well in my career.', 'Great Campus life, amazing memories, awesome local food joints, live music scene and full of life']

name: Gordon State College
reviews:
['Great school with wonderful professors and activities. Would recommend, especially if you are a nursing major.', 'My experience wasn't bad but it wasn't good either and if I had to choose which was more it would be bad. For me I was continuing my education and already had 1 degree from another school so I was already familiar with how the process works. Getting enrolled to start was horrible. Had to take a vacation day from work just to come sit at an unnecessary orientation just because it was policy. Was forced to "check a box". Complete waste of my time. Getting in touch with anyone on the phone in any office other than financial aid was nearly impossible and a few times had to drive down just to get answers to simple questions.  The classes them selves were hit or miss. At the time I attended, the online classes were poorly structured and nearly everyone had near failing grades. The only good note I have is for the in person classes I took. Those were pretty good and the teachers were good people. There were some staff there that generally wanted to help but it's 50/50. Everything considered its probably a really good place for young students fresh out of high-school living on campus but if you're a working parent forget about it.', "Thank you lord!! This day have finally came. My son is in college, he bust his but in high school and now things are about to pay off. This is a great school, I've done my research on this place and even though it's small, they have a big heart!! Today we still had to sign papers and everyone that we encountered was very friendly and helpful and I really appreciate that. My son will fit in, hell he has no choice, his old room is now my workout room! Gordon College is a great school, don't sleep on them.", "Gordon is fantastic. It is beautiful and well cared for. The staff is really a bunch of sweet hearts, in my years here I have NEVER come across one that didn't feel like coming to work that day. They are never condescending and are always helpful. I think they are very choosy who they put in the offices like financial aid, business, registrars etc. I can't say enough good things about them, even when you feel like you are asking too much or being ignorant, they are pleasant. I love the classic college feel but apart from the big city, its perfect and unlike high school i have a ton of school pride!", "I sat with professors and the students of Gordon State College for the New Student Orientation with my son.
Although I am from Cambridge, MA where people from all over the world come to further their Education at Top Universities such Harvard, MIT, and Radcliffe. I pretty much grew up in Harvard as a child and teenager.
What I experienced at Gordon College made me feel like a child again amongst our future World Leaders.
Gordon State College, is a small campus filled with Exceptional Individuals whom truly care for all.
Although it's not my son path to go into college. Gordon made me feel Like I am now ready to continue my education with them. As a returning Student/ Mama.. So since my son wants to explore life, I will now return to college."]

name: Southern Crescent Technical College
reviews: ['I am in the midst of reinstating my nursing license through the nurse re-entry program, and hitches two parts, didactic and clinicals.  I completed the didactic portion with no problems, however this school system doesn’t seem to have any contracts in place with any facilities to complete the clinical portion which is 160 hrs onsite at a hospital/facility.  If I had known this, I would not have chosen this school.  False advertising!!  I’ve asked numerous times about going anywhere in the state of Georgia to finish, I’ve found places what will take me into their facility but the school does not have a decent contracting team to follow through the process.  Money wasted, money could have been making already if completed on time.  I can choose to walk away with no refund and start the process over, lawyer up or wait.  I keep getting the run around emails of they are trying to resolve…..\nlies and false advertising so don’t waste your money.  Criminal acts', "I wouldn't recommend this technical college if I knew it was gonna take almost a year of trying to just enroll and almost impossible to even get a hold of someone on the phone. I would've never even wasted my time on filling out an application. I'm still not enrolled and will be going to a different technical college. Also it almost seems like nobody really knows what to do and they don't seem to care all that much. They deserve 0 stars in all honesty i don't even know how they're still up and running.", 'Worst experience of my life, they never respond to calls or emails. You have to figure out everything on ur own. If you ask questions to ppl in financial aid, or the teachers they get mad and do devious things to stop ur registrations or progression in the class. Everything is unorganized within the class settings they show u nothing, then call u out to embarrass u for being confused. They withhold financial aid for months after starting but don’t supply u with everything u will need in certain classes then ur basically buying out of pocket still all semester.. the schedule time sometimes lies online then wen u sign up and get in class they say a different schedule. U may as well go online somewhere since u can’t get help here, ur mental will pay for it being cheap here 0/10.', 'This school is very poorly run. The financial aid office will not return your calls, if you call anything after 5pm to any of the offices, you will not get an answer. Even the book store doesn’t answer the phone. As someone who works every day of the week, it’s impossible to try to get anything done without taking time off of work. On top of that, if there’s an issue with your account or a mistake made by the financial aid office, no one is going to help you stay in your classes, and you won’t know if there’s anything wrong until it’s too late.\nNo one actually cares about you here. You’re just another number, and nothing is going to get done unless you go there in person. It’s ridiculous how much money you will pay to go there and still be treated like you’re a nuisance. Good luck.', "They are the worst to get in touch with!  I have called and left messages more than a handful of times and no one has returned my call.  How do you speak to someone?  I am wanting to enroll and can't get any help whatsoever!!!  Frustrated!"]

name: Gupton Jones College of Funeral Service
reviews: ['The administrative aspects of the school are seriously lacking. I applied in April 2025. I did not hear back from anybody until July when I reached out. You don’t get to pick the classes you sign up for they just pick them for you and then you can tell them what you don’t want to take but be prepared for seven classes on your schedule. If you get financial aid outside of the federal government make sure you tell them you want the extra money back if there is any. Otherwise they may just assume you don’t want it like they did with me. The school program itself is also heavily focused on funeral directing and the embalming portion just seems like an afterthought.', 'The worse school ever.  I thought it would be convenient being online and a private school. No communication from teachers or Dean ( unless you owe money) went a half of semester without a book and received failing grades after reaching out to multiple staffs…. Wasn’t able to take a final exam because of a system they changed to ( protoru) it’s designed to have someone watch you as you test. After 2  1/2 hours no one showed reached me it to the instructor and Dean nothing happened failed class… emails has to include half of the staff including the president in order to get a response back.. 18 month program will take you 2 to 3 years to complete and teacher make errors give wrong answers and students suffer from it!! I’m\nFighting now for grades and completions….Never recommend this school for anyone… Please stay away.', 'I recently graduated from this institution. They prepared me for a career in funeral service and provided me with the necessary tools to pass the National Board Exams on the first attempt. All of the administrators and staff are very caring and helpful and want you to succeed!', 'March 2022 was daughter’s first time after high school attending college.  She decided to attend GJC.  After receiving her acceptance letter, she called to get an update on her financial aid prior to the start of the semester.  She left a message for a return call from the financial aid office.  Two weeks later, the semester started and my daughter called again inquiring about her financial aid status.  Still no update on financial aid, but she was enrolled in classes and allowed to begin her classes.  I thought that was somewhat out of the ordinary compared to when I attended college.  However,  my daughter and I called and left many messages, spoke to the dean of the college, emailed the financial aid office multiple numerous, and spoke to staff members regarding the status of my daughter financial aid throughout the semester, but to no avail.  The semester has ended and my daughter is still without a financial aid letter!  She decided not to return to GJC due to the lack of communication, unprofessionalism, and the denial of an opportunity to use any financial aid funds books, laptop, etc.  In an effort to obtain a resolution, my daughter will file a formal grievance as well file a complaint with the Department of Education.  I do not recommend this college.', "It's been a number of years since I graduated from Gupton Jones.  I can tell you the school equipped me with the knowledge needed to score in the high percentile on the National Board Exam and to pass my State Board License Exam.  Additionally, early employers found me to be useful and competent at a professional entry level. I highly recommend the school."]

name: Gwinnett College-Lilburn
reviews: ['I am currently an active student here! And let me tell you that this is the place of opportunities and dreams! They work so well with your schedule, teachers are very easy to communicate with, I can consider most of my teachers family. Class rooms aren’t so over crowded so they can definitely work more with you and your questions one and one. The school and teachers very much understand that we are adults and life sometimes hits us hard but they definitely are there to help you get back up! I will definitely be coming back if I need any other degree that they offer here! Especially if it’s a class with Ms.Law (medical billing and coding) she is the best teacher to have! The school and us students definitely need more teachers like her! Overall a 10 out of 5 for me!', 'I am a MBC student. I love everything about this college. I  am getting the support needed from my teachers.', "Attended Gwinnett Vocational College Lilburn back in 2009. Graduated in 2011 as a Massage therapist. Never pursued a career in that field. Just recently dropped by to purchase my diploma since I'm still having to pay off the tuition. The facility itself improved a lot. There used to be a fitness center that seemed to have closed down. Lenny Davis is still the College director & was great to cross paths with him 12 years later.", 'I graduated back in 2018. My instructors were Mr Craig and Mr Crews. They are the best you’ll ever find. I went to 3 different schools for massage. This school was by far the most thorough and I would highly recommend the massage program to anyone. I’m still a therapist and I love what I do.', "It's an amazing school with great teachers and wonderful staff."]

name: Gwinnett Technical College
reviews:
['Great college with amazing instructors. I had both great and tough experiences in my engineering major, but most of the instructors I had were very helpful to my success.
My all-time favorite professor was Mr. Gregory Allen. He is extremely knowledgeable in mathematics. I had him for Calculus I and II, and I learned so much in his classes. He is funny, very kind, and always willing to make time to help students better understand the material.
GTC is truly blessed to have him.', 'Attended Berkmar High-school until sophomore year of 2006, left to attend a private school in Manila Philippines for less than a year; ended up coming back to the USA. Figured I wouldn’t want to waste money I don’t have just to have a high school diploma so I began working in the food industry for two years at 16 years old then got my General Education Diploma just in time that I turned 18 years of age. 2008 would’ve been my graduation date but thank God I skipped the whole unnecessary stress of high school & got an equivalent diploma. Came here few times to register for a college prerequisite but I never got any respond from admission back in 2015. It was a mess but now in 2024 so much improvement had taken place. Tagged along with mama since she’s registering for next semester. Great stuff.', 'Excellent careers to improve in your life. The best option to learn English like Sencondary  Language (ESL) for free. Best ambiance and good teachers.', 'There are a few professors here that actually do their job but unfortunately not many. most of them you will have to go back and check your work yourself and point out where they failed to correct a mistake in the system or do all the checking yourself. Even with financial aid this school is a waste of your money. they will just ignore you complaints about staff who are jut collecting a paycheck for overseeing people teach themselves.', 'Poorly managed and serious lack of professionalism at this so called "College". It is virtually impossible to speak with any staff that will actually know how to assist students with anything. The staff is unmotivated and they have no work ethic. Whoever is managing the operations and procedures of this place is doing a terrible job. You will only ever receive generic email responses, an online service that will infuriate the user, and an endless phone call directory.
Do yourself a favor, CHOOSE A DIFFERENT SCHOOL.']

name: Lanier Technical College
reviews:
['My experience here today was awesome! The staff that I had the pleasure of encountering was so very helpful and compassionate. My family has a continued need to be here and I am so grateful to the friend that referred us here for this purpose. So far, so good and they delivered. Thank you Miss Kim!❣️', 'Do not do not do not waste your money on this school I had a professor ( Jacob gresham) Wait till 10 o’clock at night The day my final was due to tell me where my finals code was accessed. Yeah, I’m calling you out because I busted my ass in this class Just for him to respond to me two hours before my final was due. The school isn’t gonna do anything about it I messaged this dude 11 o’clock in the morning 2 o’clock in the afternoon And he was probably getting hammered. All he sent me was a oh I’m sorry message. Like yeah I didn’t just blow you off all day. I knew your final was due just to tell you at 10 o’clock how to access it. Dude needs to be fired.', 'Very clean and sanitary. Amazing staff. They will make sure that you understand the curriculum. The ammonia operator 1 course was awesome,  definitely going back for more!', 'Professors usually work two jobs and don’t put a lot of effort into their classes. Plus a lot of majors can’t do in person classes despite the college having 3 locations.', 'FOR ANY STUDENT LOOKING TO GET INTO PRACTICAL NURSING GO SOMEWHERE ELSE.
I am a current practical nursing student and My experience has been profoundly disappointing due to consistent unprofessionalism from the instructors. It's clear that student well-being and academic success are not a priority.
From the outset, the program has demonstrated a concerning lack of organization. This disorganization directly impacted my ability to get a good education.
The instructors, in particular, have contributed significantly to this negative environment. I found many to be unresponsive For instance: Emails to instructors went unanswered for days, sometimes weeks, or When I sought help or clarification on complex topics, instructors were dismissive or provided unhelpful responses, or "There was a noticeable lack of empathy or understanding when students faced personal challenges impacting their studies.This lack of support made it incredibly difficult to complete the program.
Furthermore, there were instances where the instructors' conduct was overtly unprofessional. I witnessed instructors making inappropriate comments to students,or There were instances of instructors discussing personal matters irrelevant to the course during class time,or Feedback on assignments was often vague, unhelpful, or delivered in a condescending manner.  Such behavior not only detracts from the learning experience but also creates an uncomfortable and unproductive environment.
The pervasive unprofessionalism and the apparent disregard for students' needs make this program a frustrating and unrewarding experience. Prospective students should be aware of these significant shortcomings before enrolling. I hope these current instructors take into consideration that teaching is not for them and it's time to do something else.']

name: Life University
reviews: ["Beautiful campus. First time visiting the campus is when I'm graduating. ✨️🥹", 'Do not live here the student housing is the worst and I believe it all stems from the people managing it and the insane contract you have to sign to live there. Worst decision I made was to live at the “life student retreat”. They have cockroaches in the walls mold in the vents and the people in charge of housing are the worst don’t expect anything but spending all your money on fees or being notified last minute or not at all of changes that will effect you during school. Again do go here!!! Housing off campus is way cheaper. They lie about it being cheaper. There are way better options off campus if you look!', 'Wait till you see the amount of loans you will come out with from chiropractic school. It’s the worst healthcare investment period. 250k loans at 7% interest with a 65k-75k job. Good luck fellow DC alumni.', 'the amount of clubs on campus is about the only good thing i have to say about it. although i absolutely love chiropractic and the select few professors that make this program tolerable, this program will test you in ways no school should. this program has been called “inhumane” but faculty and staff and that is quite true. the amount of students this program has altered mentally for the worse is not countable, and the only thing that keeps us going is each other and our love for what we do.', 'The school is currently on probation and is at risk of losing its accreditation. Over winter break, all the assistant deans either quit or stepped down. The chief academic officer recently announced her resignation, and the president also stepped down during the same period.\n\nAt this time, most of the leadership—including the dean of students, the president, and the chief academic officer—are serving in interim positions. The institution is overpriced and disorganized. Consider attending Sherman, Life West, New Zealand College of Chiropractic, Barcelona College of Chiropractic, or McTimoney instead.']

name: Chattahoochee Technical College
reviews: ['07/31/2025 I took my twins to get class schedules and help getting back into their online account. We had exceptional assistance from Denita Davis in assisting us. Unfortunately, the other lady with the short hair was rude and short. We were sent to financial aid , student success, and the cashier. name: Herzing University-Atlanta
reviews:

Taylor answered every question I had and always offered reassurance and encouragement. Thanks to her, continuing my educational journey was easy and exciting. I found another school that is more kind to its potential students.

name: Mercer University
reviews: ["I would not recommend this school to anyone who is an in person learner like me. They don't tell you while applying that the majority of their classes are online. No science class should be provided online unless you already have already taken the class. I can see Mercer as being my son's home away from home while advancing in his education.", 'Beautiful campus. Very walkable.y daughter will be starting here fall of 2026.', "Awesome place to visit.  One of the cleanest campuses I've ever visited.   Streets are laid out well.  People are friendly.   Makes me want to go to school again", 'Fantastic university. Small college feel and big university resources.']

name: Morehouse College
reviews:
['Attended a Vespers service, also honoring Joseph Smith Jr, beautiful chapel and choir performance, engaging preachers', 'What an amazing institution of higher learning! The original producers of #BoysToMen !!! Everyone, from campus police, to staff, to professors, instill a sense of royalty, belonging, and extended family into each and every student that attends.

Dear old Morehouse...', 'I had an amazing few days at Morehouse. It’s an institution where at each turn you are immersed in deep history, relentless promise, and innovation. Why dont graduating leaders reinvest in upgrades?', 'It was a great experience  to see so any young men in college  aspiring  a greater  education. So encouraging, not to be bias,but black men striving for excellence.']
