I earned my Christian Teaching degree and then went on to get my Master's in TESOL (Teaching English to Speakers of Languages). Not only did I feel prepared in what I wanted to do, but I Boise Bible taught me the importance of seeing the classroom as a ministry field. In addition, you can't beat the community!", 'BBC is amazing. The campus community is so friendly and welcoming, the music is heart-touching and the professors are so nice. I feel like I became closer to God.']

name: Boise State University
reviews:
['Love BSU! Great sprit, the campus is beautiful and located right on the Boise River! Lots of great food in the area, Students are cool and I enjoy living in the area.', "I thought we played an excellent game against Notre Dame. They were just a little bit faster than we were. I'm very proud of all our players. You guys were awesome!", 'A great school, a beautiful setting along the Boise River, and BLUE TURF!  Stop to see where the legend of the BLUE began.', 'An amazing place to acquire an education. I fully believe that anyone that enrolls in Boise State can achieve what they set their minds to. The professors can provide anything you need (as long as it’s not the math department).

I spent so many years at this University. I started at this university as someone who had already known the area really well. I thought I knew all the ‘ins and outs’ of any community BSU had to offer. I was as partially right as I was mostly wrong. The community here may seem like one that isn’t serious in most social ways but that is only because every student has a need to connect at this university outside of their studies.

If i have learned anything from outside my studies it’s that the people are a major portion of your studies. The small connections we make could mean so much to us in our careers down the line.

Stay at BSU and study hard. Talk to as many people as you can. Advance your future how you want. If this university isn’t for you, consider transferring and stay. You will have a great time with all of the people you connect with. You will find your way through avenues of education you may have never thought interesting to you. You might also find something you are good at that you enjoy, something we are all searching for.

Whether it’s higher education, a nice place to spend hiking in the summer, a place to connect with communities of people you would never talk to otherwise, or simply a place to learn. Boise State University surprised me with all of those. I was greatful to spend so many years there. If you are considering applying, I say go for it and don’t look back. Looking back is fiscally responsible, but looking forward might reveal other things we have all been searching for in life.', 'Fine school, but they would charge you $1 every time you went to class if they thought they could get away with it.']

name: College of Eastern Idaho
reviews:
['This school is a joke, especially their RN program.

I work a full-time M-F job and don’t have the luxury to quit so I can focus on school. Instead, I had no choice but to find a way to juggle both. Before applying and spending money on prerequisites, I tried meeting with an advisor and struggled for months. No one would get on the phone with me or meet in person to answer my questions. When I finally got one on the phone, I was transparent about my situation and was never told the part-time program would not work with my schedule, but instead warned it would be difficult to juggle both. I already knew that going into this, so I proceeded. I completed my prerequisites and the first semester of the program while working. I was devastated to learn that the program is not truly part-time as clinicals starting trim the second semester would be during working hours. Despite pleasing with anyone I could to work with me and give me the opportunity to grab evening or weekend shifts, I was shot down. I wanted this to work so bad and busted my ass to maintain a 4.0 throughout my time at CEI. It’s insane to me that there wasn’t more transparency at the start of the program because I would not have spent my time and money at this school.

Another thing to note during labs outside of class consist of instructors who are useless. I was practicing inserting a GI tube and asked that the instructor on duty assist and she simply instructed me to watch a video. It kind of explains the level of medical care you get in Idaho though. It’s horrifying some of the people in this state who go on to practice medicine.', "I'm currently a student in the energy systems technology program and I absolutely love CEI. All of the staff are the most friendly and helpful people I've met. The school is far more affordable than other universities and I feel like I'm getting a real practical education that will prepare me for a career in the field.", 'I took an ESL class. It was an amazing experience. I am very satisfied with the curriculum Meredith did for us. We made us practicing every areas, reading(Even short novel), speaking, listening, writing(focus on grammar). I highly recommended this program to my friends. Now they are gonna be join next one.', 'I use the grounds about 2 x per week to walk my puppy. They also have the best ice machine in town. My puppy loves eating ice so I am able to get a cup for her there. Peope are friendly overall. There is always a lot of garbage by the automotive building.', 'Nice and clean campus seems to be well organized, the technical department seems very organized with all the tools and the training necessary to be prepared for my job.
The campus was so clean and so organized that I think I will sign my wife up so she can start classes in the fall.
We even showed up before classes were to supposed to start, and the security guard was good about letting us in, it was pretty cold, I hope somebody checked on him cuz he had to walk what seems like miles just to come open the door for us. 😁
Just found out that they are partnering with local highschools to get kids s head start to schooling... Very cool']

name: Idaho State University
reviews:
['I absolutely LOVED going to college here! The people, the atmosphere, the environment, everything about it. I felt safe and was super happy. My first year I lived in the honors dorms. Then the next year I rented a house right off campus by the dome. I took my kids back to visit and walk the campus.

Parking in a lot was difficult because there was an event, but signs were not posted or the lot was not blocked off. I was told even if I paid on my phone, my car could be cited or towed because it was a private event 🤦‍♀️ it would have been nice to have signs posted or block the lot off before hand, better communication and signage would be appreciated. Otherwise my children loved the campus. We went into the student center and student store where the kids bought souvenirs and ISU gear. I would definitely encourage my children to go here someday, if their major of study is here.', 'Parking is so convoluted. It is clean. The museum has some interesting things in it. But my 4btear old son was most excited about the coloring paper.

They lack a lot of dinosaurs.', 'The audiology department is wonderful.
The Speech Department is amazing.
Update: Group makes up speech and neuro difficulties. Which is incredibly important. The staff and faculty are amazing, friendly, easy to work with, and do their best to help people succeed.', 'I went to the LDS church close to campus and meet with the bishop. It was a good meeting. And he was a good man.', 'I loved my education at ISU!...Great nursing program.']

name: University of Idaho
reviews: ['The University of Idaho, situated at 875 Perimeter Drive in Moscow, consistently earns high praise in my professional and social circles as a premier land-grant institution that masterfully balances a high-caliber research profile with a welcoming, student-centered atmosphere. From numerous substantive conversations with alumni and local residents, it is evident that the university serves as a vital intellectual hub, where the faculty’s commitment to academic rigor is matched only by their dedication to mentorship. My colleagues often point to the institution’s exceptional programs in natural resources and engineering as evidence of a curriculum that is both merytorically sound and profoundly relevant to the modern workforce. In frequent discussions regarding the Pacific Northwest’s educational landscape, the public consensus highlights U of I’s unique ability to foster a sense of belonging while driving the state’s economic and scientific innovation. I am particularly struck by the campus’s stunning aesthetic and the "Vandal" spirit, which my acquaintances describe as a powerful force for building lifelong professional networks and community resilience. It is clear from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration operates with a sophisticated, forward-thinking vision, ensuring that the university remains a prestigious and dependable choice for higher education. Reflecting on the consistently positive sentiments shared by my peers, I view the University of Idaho as a distinguished institution that fulfills its educational mission with undeniable class, integrity, and a deep respect for the potential of every student.', "Amazing school with amazing people. I really enjoyed the five years I spent here. The school caters to Law, Agriculture and Sciences mostly. It has really good pricing and sees many out of state students because of this. If your unsure of what school to go to or do not know what you want to do I recommend going here to figure things out as you will have a blast while learning some fascinating material. The school sits only 1/4 mile from downtown Moscow which is a great place to grab a bite to eat or visit the local bike shops. It is also only a 30 minute drive from Moscow Mountain which has great mountain biking and hiking trails. The University of Idaho is a hidden gem. Don't pass it up if given the opportunity to attend.", 'I drive through campus regularly to check out progress on the new basketball arena which is under construction. After the concrete work was completed, progress is going much faster. Interesting, and it is going to be very attractive. Features 100% Idaho timber.', "This is about as Northwest as it gets! In a faraway, secluded corner of the US, University of Idaho offers an exceptionally gorgeous campus, a tightly knit, provincial campus life, amazing outdoor sports & recreation opportunities, opportunity to live as part of a small-town community, and - if academics is your thing - then tranquil peace and great amounts of administrative/academic support for you to study! But really - This university is really about wild spirits and the great, open country around and the magnificent mountains, brooks and rivers that snake all around! Just an amazing experience being here!\n\nIt's too far away from anything of importance - Except maybe Boeing and couple of their suppliers - to be of much significance in terms of landing amazing jobs. But you can always make your own way into Silicon Valley or Amazon at Salt Lake City - If that's your thing. But the university campus life will beat it all. If you want to listen to some amazing jazz or want to engage with reservation Native Americans as they perform their traditional song and dance. Or just want to ride the white waves of the nearby Snake River and go camping in pristine, untouched mountainscapes - This place is definitely for you!", "Brought our granddaughter up her to attend the University of Idaho. GO VANDALS. There was plenty of help to get our truck unloaded, and our grandaughters items taken to her room. The volunteers couldn't have been more friendly and helpful. Got to go find some Vandal gear before we leave town. Wanted to attend the family activities, but time doesnt allow that to happen. Really wanted more info. GREAT JOB TO ALL."]

name: The College of Idaho
reviews:
['Not enough Parking. Street taken and all the spaces in the parking lot. Plan to park far away maybe a block and walk', "I basically had an entire minor where I paid to just do my own personal projects I was already doing. CompSci 0/10

Also they named a newer athletic building after a violent, homophobic, child abusing racist. When it was made clearly evident he simply had a conversation with HR and it was immediately forgotten. Despite repeated incidents the College seem to care more for his popularity with donors than their students' well-being.

Additionally they make you live on campus, buy their terrible meal plans, and good luck holding a full time job when nearly every professor's sending you hours of homework as a substitute for not teaching during actual class time. For how much it costs the non-athlete student with no parental support is at a distinct, almost insurmountable disadvantage.

Great place to send children if you want them to learn about the poor state of modern academia and drown them in expenses.", 'I was sitting at an outdoor table on campus while my wife was in class and a woman approached me and asked if I was a “town person”. She introduced herself as a school staff member and questioned me about why I was there. I felt very unwelcome and she seemed very skeptical that my wife was a graduate student on campus.', "If there were do overs in life I'd go back to school here in a heart beat.  Some of the most memorable times with some of the nicest people you could ever meet in life.  In a matter of a few weeks you got to know most everyone including the professors.  Small class size allowed for more one on one time if needed. 10 day breaks every six weeks allowed for many road trips to new adventures with new friends. Started up their soccer program back in 1985 when enrollment was probably 600+ students from all over the country.", "My daughter graduated this year (2017).  Her teachers know her personally and are actively participating in her future.  She's received a broad education from a school that is nationally recognized with a superior staff.  This was the perfect place for her to grow and spread her wings while enjoying a beautiful campus.  What more could you want?"]

name: Lewis-Clark State College
reviews:
['As a current student, this school sucks. The WIFI hardly works: students are having to be on the guest WIFI to get a relatively stable connection that still disconnects during online exams. One of the residences’ rooms (and probably others) have their own personal wifi routers because of how unstable it is.

The Residence Life Office doesn’t care about the housing nor the care/safety of their students. Starting off with the fact that they severely overbook their housing options; so much so that they are actively putting students into a hotel instead.
There are many health and safety concerns in most of the dorms including (but not limited to):
There’s no AC in one of the halls where it gets to be above 100 degrees during the beginning of the fall semester and end of spring semester. One of the halls not only has black mold in some of the bathrooms, but they also have mice. Both issues have been brought up to the staff, to which there responses were “Just wipe off the mold” and “The mice come in for the same reasons students live there. For warmth and food.” When students go to the staff in charge they are gas lit into believing that they were the ones wrong and not the staff, and in turn, refuse to help with the situation.

This campus is actively speaking of raising their costs, all while programs are actively receiving budget cuts. There is little to no information being put out as to why the costs are increasing, and when there are hearings put out, the school does little to inform students about them. On top of this, due to active program budget cuts, the school is forced to keep on professors and adjunct faculty that are verbally abusive, don’t show any care about their students, and actively show little to no interest teaching.

Overall, it really does seem as though this school cares more about it’s aesthetic than about it’s students.', "I really dislike this college. I took English 102 and working on that class for 30 hours a week I still fell behind. Its not that the work was difficult, there was just so much of it. I would have to writ 12-20 pages a week, and do all of the research and editing for the paper. I ended up falling behind in all of my other classes as I tried to catch up. It is finals week while I am writing this review, and I found out that in addition to a 15 page research paper I have to write I also have to write a 5 page cover letter AND revise all of my previous work in the class. Maybe it is just this class, but I have taken other, supposedly more difficult english classes at other colleges and easily passed those. Be aware. Don't get swamped.", "Today was research admissions and tour the campus day. ALL really great people.  Anyone nervous about attending college,  shouldn't be. These folks are totally friendly and professional. LCSC I'm sure will prove to be the right choice!", 'Visited amphitheater and Art Under the Elms. Lovely campus highlighting local talent.', 'Kids had a fun time at the Christmas basketball camp!']

name: North Idaho College
reviews:
["Curently the college I'm going to, and I love it! The area is beautiful, and I have enjoyed all the classes I have taken here! Most of the food I've tried at the SUB has been good, some meh. I have had some issues in the past with ordering textbooks and dealing with financial aid stuff, but eventually it was all resolved. Overall, a good school I would recommend to anyone.", "This is my current school. I gind it very convenient that it's 15 mins away from home. I am taking their Business Administration program. Here are the professors I can highly recommend to want students to succeed. They are just AWESOME!!

Professor DEAN MILES: Excellent teacher. You can tell he wants to truly invest in his students' learning. He also grades work fairly and makes the lessons/ quizzes pretty easy.

Professor KYLIE TROUT: Mmm... Okay, there's not much to say for this teacher, except SHE IS DA BEST!!! I just took 4 classes this past semester with her, and she is funny, energetic, enthusiastic, and just so joyful! She likes making in-person classes hialrious with her life stories related to class work. She also provides little fidget toys (like pipe cleaners, paper clips, and pens) and lots of free candy!! At first, I thought she was crazy, but I grew to love her in the end. She is always willing to mert with her students, forever telling us her office hours and emailing us with Zoom info. Professor JOHNATHAN FREY: He is nice and his material is great. I blame myself for not passing Eng. 101 with him. He is firm on grades and will make you edit papers as much as you can. His material may be hard to understand, but he as well is willing to guide you through it a bit.", 'Great campus. Amazing staff and wonderful learning environment.', 'The beach behind NIC is the best for building sand castles!', 'Great campus in beautiful CDA. Well maintained, clean facility. Offers great programs and friendly staff.']

name: Northwest Nazarene University
reviews: ['Excellent Noel Christmas program. Beautiful and inspirational concert with lots of variety of singers and Orchestra. Very nicely done and professional. A beautiful ending buy Candlelight singing Silent Night.', 'Both my older kids went here and will be graduating this year!! It was a wonderful experience for us all - lots of memories to cherish!', 'Super friendly students and staff! I love attending school here!', "Great school, truly focused on holistic transformation, just as the mission and vision  outline. Staff and faculty care about their students and they are not just a number in the system. Graduated from here and work here now, Nursing program is great, well known in the community for fostering growth and educating in ways that result in compassionate, well prepared, well rounded nurses. Financial aid, scholarships, and assistance makes tuition cost MUCH MORE REASONABLE THAN PEOPLE EXPECT - if you're at all reach out to the admissions department and they can help you explore options!", "I came here to preform a concert and it was pretty good. It was kind of a pain to get to the holding rooms from the stage because you have to go outside to get there which was especially bad because it was winter but it wasn't the end of the world. Also the restroom is technically wheelchair accessible but is a real pain when there's lots of other people. I know from experience. Other than that I don't really have any complaints."]

name: Brigham Young University-Idaho
reviews:
['It is a tough call.
For students facing financial hardship and mostly focus on working, life at Brigham Young University in Idaho can be especially taxing. Church attendance requirements and other bureaucratic procedures (such as submitting a health waiver every semester to clear holds and dual authentication login) can interfere with the need to continue working and just get in the way. In addition, pervasive social pressure can increase stress and stigma.
There's a certain need to conform to dating, marriage, all that jazz but if you can "put on a mask" like the Joseph Gordon-Levitt quote in The Dark Knight Rises and don't over cater to people pleasing here and kind of soldier through your homework anyway, anything is possible. I'm only leaving a 1 star review because I'm especially exasperated at the extra-supercilious roommates I got handed to deal with this particular semester. You know what they say - all is well that ends well, so it's your call if you have what it takes, or if you're rich it's a "get out of jail free card" so disregard this review if that's you.', 'I came to BYU-Idaho hoping for a merit-based, flexible online program that would complement my full-time role as a software engineer. Instead, I found what feels like a scam wrapped in religious favoritism and outdated infrastructure. This school prioritizes hiring and seemingly advancing LDS members from around the world over actual merit or competence—it's not subtle, and it creates an uneven playing field for anyone who doesn't fit the mold. If you're not deeply embedded in that community, good luck getting fair treatment.
The grading system is a nightmare. They use Canvas, which could be a solid tool, but the rubrics are ancient and riddled with inconsistencies—no clear guidelines, no modern updates, and zero clue from instructors on how assessments are actually evaluated. It's like they're grading in the dark ages: arbitrary feedback, delayed responses, and criteria that shift without notice. As someone balancing a demanding job with another degree in software engineering, this chaos wasted my time and money. I've poured hours into assignments only to get vague deductions that make no sense, all while watching the program drag on without any real support for working professionals.
BYU-Idaho isn't just "messed up"—it's actively harmful to your career and sanity if you're expecting transparency or equity. Save yourself the frustration and look elsewhere (WGU or SNHU are worlds better for tech degrees). I regret every penny spent here. Strongly advise against enrolling.', 'I have been quiet for a long time, but I am done acting like this school is something it is not. My experience here has been full of barriers, judgment, and double standards. They talk about faith, values, and living right, but what they really care about is control and image.

I was followed in the bookstore, ignored when I asked for help, and treated like I should just smile and be the token success story. The behavior I experienced in the bookstore was especially concerning. The director there, a shorter bald man, treated me in a way that made me feel profiled and uncomfortable. In fact, he was recently promoted into that position even though there have been rumors for years about how he treated people in the past, going back eight or nine years. From what I have seen and heard, this should have been looked into a long time ago.

Meanwhile, the same school that preaches about morality and standards looks the other way when students are having sex, smoking weed, partying, and doing things that completely go against what they claim to stand for. There are even guys cuddling in garments in the dorms and nobody says a word, but the minute someone like me speaks up or needs support, it becomes a problem.

They hire student workers with no real world experience, and instead of offering help, they make things harder. They tell you to stay positive, smile, and trust the process, but they do not listen when you are actually struggling. The culture they foster is not healthy. This school is very divided and fake. It feels like they just want people who look good for the brochure, not people who need real support.

This school does not practice what it preaches. It picks and chooses who to protect and who to silence. I am writing this because I want people to see the truth. BYU Idaho needs to do better for all students, not just the ones that fit their image.', 'This is the most amazing university on an incredible campus. The school puts a lot of effort into making this a beautiful and safe place!', 'Buy-I is a fantastic school with a fantastic campus. One of the things I love most about it is that the campus isn’t huge so it is pretty easy to go from class to class and be in time. Some may find that the dress codes and standards are high, which they are, but I think this is what sets those who are serious about getting a great education here apart. I would highly recommend anyone to this school. Grateful that I have had the opportunity to study here.']

Consistently good burgers and great tasting fries, I'll continue to meet the Princess here for lunch anytime schedules our align.", 'Having a wonderful time!! The school and it's curriculum are very impressive and reputable. The housing setup is too spread out and security might be an issue along with the Chicago winters. Overall, it is definitely still a contender.", 'Having a wonderful guest lecture at SAIC.']

name: Augustana College
reviews:
['This college looks impressive on paper and during campus tours, which is exactly why my child chose to attend. Unfortunately, the reality was very different and the decision turned out to be a major mistake.

Students are treated more like high schoolers than college adults, with policies and oversight that feel controlling and out of step with what most families expect from a university.

The most alarming issue, however, is how the school appears to handle rape and sexual assault. From what we witnessed, the system seems to protect perpetrators far more than it protects victims. Individuals accused of serious misconduct appear to face minimal consequences, while victims can feel ignored, blamed, or even vilified for speaking up. That kind of environment discourages reporting and raises serious concerns about student safety.

Drugs and alcohol are also clearly present on campus, yet the systems meant to monitor and address these problems seem ineffective.

We did ask questions about safety and student well-being before enrolling and, unfortunately, believed the reassurances we were given. In hindsight, the reality did not match the rhetoric.

Overall, the college does a very good job marketing itself and creating a positive first impression. Unfortunately, our experience suggests that the reality behind the brochures is far less reassuring. Families considering this school should ask difficult questions about student safety, accountability, and how serious incidents are actually handled.', 'Graduated recently and have been thinking about how Augustana affected me.

I don't drink and at Augustana my self worth plummeted.

They'll tell you "this is how the world works, get used to it," but why then when I moved did I find people who respected me for not drinking?

Greek life is a social hierarchy and if you don't take part few people may want to interact with you.

It's also sad: when kids join Greek life, they change, and if you don't, you get left out.

It's hard to overstate the exclusion and isolation I felt there, and this is from someone who did relatively well in classes, was relatively involved, and am not the first in my family to go there.

On top of all this, many programs are in disarray and now that I'm in work, I notice all the things I failed to learn, that others learned at other schools.

I can't get back the time and money I spent there but the exclusion and sadness I felt there has made me a resilient person.

Do yourself a favor and look for schools where alcohol and Greek life don't run every last aspect of the school.', 'I am a graduate of the Class of 2025. Here’s my experience and observations over the last four years as a student. (Posting this on a burner email)

Financials - As an incoming student I received an appealing financial aid package from Augustana. This enticed me to attend the school over some competitors. Over my four years, tuition and room and board was increased three times (3.5% 2022-2023, 3.85% 2023-2024, 3.38% 2024-2025). I felt this was a bait-and-switch as the scholarships I received in later years did not keep pace with my original financial aid package. I was paying more out of pocket my senior year compared to my freshman year. In addition, any private student loans taken out are a fixed 6.5% rate. I encourage anyone that does attend Augustana to reach out to the financial aid office each year when you receive your new financial aid package and ask for more aid (I was given more aid when I asked).

Education - My overall education experience was good. I learned about many different topics I had not considered before I attended college. The professors were hit-or-miss in some classes so utilizing ratemyprofessor.com was a life saver. Over my four years, there was some professor turnover that I had experienced. It seemed like whenever a new professor was hired they were always an international. The school cannot pay up for good talent. I heard of professors that were not hired because they were offered a salary 2x of what Augustana could offer. Expect foreign professors with a hardy accent teaching some of your classes. I also did enjoy the small class sizes because I felt like I was forced to engage more and it was easier to ask questions.

Housing - Housing is hit-or-miss in your lower-class years. If you are unfortunate enough to live in Andreen or Seminary Hall during your freshman year, I pray for you. You can expect to be miserable the whole year and especially when it is hot outside. There is little to no A/C in those rooms. All the other housing is alright. You are forced to live on-campus for three years so you miss out on better deals of living off-campus with roommates.

Campus Life - There is always some activity happening on campus throughout the school year. I participated in a few clubs which I obtained leadership roles so I think there is something for everyone. My opinion about the cafeteria food is it is not good. Everything is soaked in oil, pre-packaged, and fried. The burgers look nothing like the one shown in the advertisement video on the Augustana Dining website. They’re all thin and frozen. The best food is the dessert.

This review was just my opinion, hopefully it can help you make a more informed decision about the school you may attend. I did receive a job offer before my Senior year began so that is a testament to an Augustana education, though it does depend on your major and career choice.', 'Definitely applying here! Stayed for the IL SCA summer camp and can confidently say this building has 9/10. -1 star for wifi though. Gerber is probably the one with the worst one. Swanson is OK, but not ideal', 'Amazing my sister friend goes here and she loves it']

name: Aurora University
reviews:
['This is a terrible university do not go here. They will act like they care about your future they do not at all. If you don’t have a full ride scholarship package , do not come here. Do not accept the student loan package , you will pay 3 times interest on it when you graduate. Every year the tuition goes up by 400$ a semester. We went from 14400 to 14800 to 15200. They don’t care about you’re professional development and will lie thru there teeth about career development. Unless you have a job in you’re field and you’re being sponsored by you’re employer, it’s all on you to find a job and they will take credit for it without you’re permission. They will not accommodate your work schedule at all, so you are forced to take classes at days and times that don’t work. They recently were in the news for being racist towards a student athlete. If you’re an accountant student, do not come here, go to UIC , some other well known accounting program, you will struggle to land an unpaid internship even because employers do not take them seriously. Definitely don’t come here as a healthcare admin or business major unless you are already in the field, half the students who graduate from here don’t have jobs go to masters school or have to find menial jobs vaguely related to the field. They failed to handle the economic shifts, they are struggling to retain freshman. They lie about there job statistics  , students don’t find jobs in there fields for years. Proffesors are disengaged and disorganized. Some professors will setup zoom classes even though you’ve paid for in person classes. The internship fair is garbage , employers don’t care about you and tell you to go away. Networking sessions are useless and employers have no interest in the students. The university’s bread and butter are transfer adult students and social work majors who also struggle to get hours, experience and jobs unless they already where working. Shame on you Aurora University', 'I would not recommend Aurora University to anyone. I had an awful experience with the administration. I requested to get hours that I had completed within an internship setting signed off on, and they refused to sign off on them and give them to me, even though I had completed a whole semester of hours and passed the class. I feel the school is very racist, biased against people of color, expensive and does not care about their students.', 'Great school. Excellent curriculum. Excellent staff members who truly care about their students and community.', "This review is for the office management.

About 4 years ago I was (luckily) nominated as volunteer academic advisor to my brother's courses at COD.

The experience was so mind-boggling that I often pondered if the (actual)(paid) advisors at COD were alien bodies sent from a galaxy eons away, with hands made of oblique shapes that prohibited them from communicating at anything more then a snails pace or even at all.

So when this week I ventured into another email adventure with AU, I was astonished at the efficiency. Response was within one day & with all the info I needed. Thank you so much!", 'Not many recent reviews here. I got my BSN here. The school is a smaller private university. My classes were just the right size where you can get to know all of your classmates and professors. However, some of the professors were unprofessional in their teachings, so I’m not sure how they were qualified to teach. There were also magnificent professors that would go out of their way in order to see you succeed.

Parking was atrocious before but I’m glad they have a parking garage now. I wished they would have had that when I was in school pre covid. It would have saved me lots of aggravation from finding a parking space. Yeah, there were many times that if you didn’t get there early enough then you would be searching for parking in the nearby neighborhoods. They had many lots before but they got filled up way too fast.

Cafeteria was very decent. The food they served was good, average quality but a nice variety. The labs for doing your nursing skills were superb. The simulation dummy was very helpful and modern. It was used to help you understand how a real patient would be. The clinical sites they sent us ranged from hospitals to nursing homes to schools. The downside is they would send me to Rockford one day and then Chicago the second day. They should have organized it a lot better. Clinical instructors for the most part were very compassionate and attentive in their guidance. The ATI program they used was worthless and not a very good tool for helping nursing students. That was a waste of money in my opinion. I didn’t even use it when studying it for my license.

Tuition was expensive for each semester. For the amount of money they charged, they should have brought in the parking garage sooner and better quality food. I commuted so I didn’t have to stay in the dorms. Overall I give it about a 3.']

name: Southwestern Illinois College
reviews: ['Financial Aid management is rude and disrespectful towards the students. Management didn’t want to appeal a decision “in case I wouldn’t do well in current semester or decided not to continue in my program” and they “didn’t want to potentially “waste time”” on my case.', 'The teachers really make or break this place half of the professors I’ve had almost made me want to drop out and multiple people removed themselves from the classes because of the teacher and other teachers were AMAZING. If you are enrolling into a program here you seem to get great teachers who care about your success but just taking gen ed classes the teachers are really hit or miss. Cheaper and more accessible than SIUE though.', "Financial aid office is terrible with communication. You can actually just wait until your scholarship funds are added to an account and buy all your supplies at half the price on literally any other website or store. Plus you don't have to deal with the attitude from staff members after they make mistakes and blame it on anyone as long as the blame isn't on them. What a joke..", 'Much better than these huge universities just trying to get another dollar and push you through the system. SWIC feels much more genuine with people constantly helping you and caring about you.', 'Affordable, great community resource. Too many cops tho']

name: Black Hawk College
reviews:
['Black Hawk College has recently completed major renovations, and the transformation is impressive.

One of the most exciting upgrades is in their Industrial Manufacturing/Industrial Technology areas. The remodeled facilities are bright, open, and thoughtfully connected — a clear reflection of where modern manufacturing is headed.

I remember visiting years ago when I first started as a Job Shadow Coordinator. Like many traditional shop spaces at the time, it felt dark and dusty — the image many people still associate with manufacturing.

That image is outdated.

Today’s manufacturing environments are clean, technology-driven, and highly skilled workplaces. Black Hawk College’s updated facilities showcase that shift beautifully. They’ve positioned themselves as a leader and a beacon for the future of industrial education.

Well done, BHC — this is exactly the message students, families, and industry partners need to see.', 'Great Staff, Wonderful Environment, A Very Photogenic Building/Landscape!

For those looking to acquire the college legs, Black Hawk offers a wide variety of classes, clubs, sports, and more! Black Hawk is also one of the more affordable schools in the area! As a student, I would highly recommend BHC to anyone of all ages!', 'Happy to send my child here to get gen eds before finishing at a state university. Every employee we have met has been wonderful to interact with so far.', "Blackhawk is a beautiful college that is expanding rapidly. I had the privilege of being part of this expansion. I was putting together all of the new welding booths for their shop classes. I'm very pleased and impressed that they have classes for welding. It's very important to promote our trades. I've been welding for about 28 years and it's made me a lot of money throughout my career as a local #111 ironworker. It's nice to see such a great college realizing the importance of maintaining the quality of craftsmanship in our country. I say Bravo to Blackhawk! Well done!", 'Last year my husband kept submitting the more info thing on the website and no one ever contacted him. Over 4 months he would call and email both locations and no one would respond. I thought maybe it was just him. For last 2 months I keep emailing and submitting the form online. Nothing. No response. It just wants me to sign up for classes. I just want to know the price of a course! This is ridiculous. He wanted to start a course and they didn’t even care enough to respond. They lost the opportunity to get thousands for him to take the welding course. They don’t care. You can email admissions, financial aid, etc. no one will respond. Why even have their emails listed then? If you request more information and insert your contact details why does no one contact you? No emails nothing. I’ve gone to 4 colleges so far in my life and this one has the worst ‘customer service’ most schools are so eager to help you so you can sign up right away and give them money for the courses. Guess even money isn’t enough to get a call back.']

name: Bradley University
reviews: ['Fantastic place to work at. The campus is gorgeous and lots of free parking for visitors. There are quite a few great restaurants within walking distance. The university is well respected by the community.', 'Our son was able to graduate with a bachelors and Masters degrees at the same time. He got a great job offer and generous salary from a large accounting firm afterwards. Small school where the faculty are genuinely interested in student success. Very pleased with his education.', 'Nice campus, friendly students. Very vigilant police. The streets and sanitation department needs to plow, snow storm on 12/13/25 no street was plowed all day.', 'This is from an outside looking in at historical and physical campus of BU. If you are looking for a place to have a beautiful walk around during the daytime, this is a great place. View the buildings and shade trees. Be inspired by the students as they move to their next class, or end their day. The bookstore often has some clearance items if you want to support the local identity and community. Music department offers concerts, so be on the lookout for those. Statue of the founder is available for selfies at most hours. Campus is so close to many food establishments, and I dare say this is not a bad place to meet your friend in gorgeous weather for a healthy chat and walk about.', "Highly do not recommend, if your family is not earning upperclass salary you'd be putting yourself in a bad financial position. The tuition has gone up every semester, and they have discontinued many departments, including math, which is where my major was. Meal plans aren't worth much, especially with overpriced common things like milk, medicine, and supplies. Common areas for my hall were always a mess due to students, and the student services have no transparency.\nIf you simply want a college experience, find another place, because even the smartest student couldn't go here for free."]

name: Carl Sandburg College
reviews: ["If the college/ classes/ programs are run like the application process I've had to go through so far then maybe I won't waste my time. Genuinely appalled and shocked by how disorganized, taxing, and incongruent this application process has been. reviews:

—Lil’ Angels Photography Chicago']

name: University of Chicago
reviews:
['I spent some time exploring the University of Chicago campus recently, and I have to say — it left a strong impression on me. From the moment I walked through the gates, the place feels intellectual and historic in a way few universities do.

The architecture is the first thing that hits you. The Gothic-style buildings, stone archways, and ornate details make the campus look like something out of a classic college movie — almost like a mini-European city tucked into the South Side of Chicago. It feels grand, timeless, and purposeful all at once.

What I loved most was the atmosphere of serious curiosity everywhere you go. You see students deeply engaged in conversation, professors moving between classrooms with stacks of books, and quiet courtyards perfect for reading or reflection. There’s a real culture of inquiry and scholarship here — it’s not just a place to get a degree, it feels like a place that values thinking and learning for its own sake.

The campus isn’t huge, but it’s very walkable and full of little gems — from cozy green spaces and hidden courtyards to impressive libraries that feel almost sacred if you love books. The Oriental Institute Museum and the Reva and David Logan Center for the Arts are just two spots that made me want to linger longer.

Even the vibe of Hyde Park around the university feels like an extension of the school’s personality — diverse, thoughtful, and quietly vibrant without feeling showy. There’s a mix of students grabbing coffee, locals walking through historic blocks, and academic energy that never quite stops.

Overall, my visit to the University of Chicago didn’t just feel like seeing another campus — it felt like stepping into a community that lives and breathes ideas. If you’re into rich academic traditions, beautiful architecture, and an environment that challenges you to think deeply, this place really stands out.', 'Beautiful! Absolutely wonderful place to stay , relatively central! Beds/ Rooms are so
Comfy!  Incredibly polite & helpful staff ! Every single person I came in contact with was a delight and they made my stay stress free ! Will 100% be back in the future.', "One of the great universities of the world, with a campus deserving of it. There's a real commitment to the neogothic and medieval here, even compared to the average American university campus, with elaborate ornamentation and soaring spires and a sense of artistry in every detail, creating a sanctified environment dedicated to learning and the elevated nourishment of the mind. Ivy completely envelops some buildings, with their emphatic verticality and ornate towers, and narrow passages lead into verdant cloistered courtyards that remind me significantly of my time in Scotland. This is a prestigious university but it never feels too showy, just like the old medieval institutions it is modeled on: this is a place of serious and refined study and contemplation.", 'The University of Chicago, anchored at its Gothic-inspired campus at 5801 S Ellis Ave, is consistently characterized in my intellectual and professional circles as a legendary "teacher of teachers," where a substantive devotion to the life of the mind fosters an environment of unparalleled analytical depth. Through numerous insightful dialogues with faculty members and alumni friends, it is merytorically clear that "UChicago" provides an intellectually electric atmosphere, frequently celebrated by my acquaintances for its uncompromising commitment to free expression and the rigorous "Chicago Style" of debate that defines modern economics and sociology. It is truly remarkable to observe how the institution maintains such a transparent and respectful dedication to foundational research, a quality that the broader global community recognizes as the primary reason for its staggering tally of nearly one hundred Nobel Laureates. Many individuals I know personally emphasize the university’s sophisticated synthesis of rigorous theoretical inquiry and practical, world-changing policy application as a distinguished hallmark, proving that its graduates are uniquely equipped to challenge conventional wisdom. The institution's relentless drive toward interdisciplinary discovery is frequently reflected in the success stories shared by my peers, who often highlight the Booth School of Business and the Pritzker School of Medicine as global gold standards. Ultimately, in the collective view of informed observers, the University of Chicago stands as a premier pillar of academic freedom and moral courage, rightfully respected for its elegant ability to cultivate a new generation of visionaries who value truth above all else.', 'The hospital is exceptionally clean and organized. Even though the architecture of the building provides for a cold incredibly huge open space upon entering the building
The receptionist were incredibly friendly, warm and helpful in contrast. Garage parking is taken care of and at a reasonable price by Chicago standards.']

name: City Colleges of Chicago-Kennedy-King College
reviews: ['This is a really great school. Depending on your major, you might have a professor or classmate that may not have a positive experience on your academic journey. Also shout-out to security and the engineers that keep the school running great', 'Love how they transformed Halsted st to an actual campus, I just enrolled in their HVAC program.', 'Worst experience of my life. What a joke.', 'I had a great experience when I went to register for classes today with Ms Regina in admissions. She was very nice and pleasant. She was very much aware of job description. I wish we can have wonderful people like her in the customers service fields today.', "ZERO stars for the financial aid office/department.  All the staff that I was able to talk to were all terrible, like if they came from the same place, with no manners, very unprofessional including the men that's always sitting next to the door doing nothing and just giving the wrong information to the students. reviews: ['I attended a conference at this college with several friends. The college itself is immaculate and well designed. It was clean and the staff were pleasant as well as professional. reviews:
['Where to start.. This was my first steps in this country. Very first English words and help I received there. Staff is nice, always friendly. I hope mr. Henn will read this. I want to say him thank you for your English classes! That was phenomenal. I enjoyed every second in your class.

College is very bright, simple structure, nice base and tasty food in the cafeteria. I love it. Gives me an old warm memories)', "This review is about Spanish lecturer Gina Rios de Nooyer- absolutely terrible teacher, doesn't allow students to use different vocabulary then whats in the book, doesn't teach anything else except whats in the book, for 2 hours she explains half a page , doesn't answer questions considering future subjects , except this she is also rude and arrogant . Her methods of teachings are straight from kindergarten.  I filed complaint against her but Truman didn't give a damn thing about it. After 50 hours with her I can say only few sentences in Spanish. She should be teaching children not adults", 'Today, I was very disappointed with the support I received at Truman College, especially from a teacher named Louise. They were not flexible with my situation just because I cannot participate and interact during the classes for 10 days because of work , I was told I would be withdrawn from the ESL program. This class was very important for me to prepare for my career and pursue my master’s degree.

Now, I have to wait until next year, which feels like a complete waste of time. I truly expected more encouragement and support from the college in helping students achieve their goals.', 'I like this school for many things, but one major concern that I have is the casual Islamophobia from professors here

There have been instances where professors have used class time to bring up irrelevant or misinformed comments about Islam, creating a hostile environment for Muslim students. These discussions are one sided and irrelevant, made worse by the power imbalance which is we are students whose grades are in the hands of these people if we challenge them

I’m not against open dialogue, including about religion.But In a classroom, where professors hold authority, bringing up religion is intimidation and cowardice', 'I’m writing this review because I believe in helping the community and I’m not a fan of dishonesty or manipulation. I’ve been involved with Truman College for almost ten years, and unfortunately, it has deeply affected my life in negative ways. The environment created by some of the staff, especially certain teachers, is extremely toxic, and the management system is both unprofessional and careless.

One of the most disturbing experiences I had was with a teacher named Mr. Dan. He was incredibly disrespectful and unprofessional. He used to send me inappropriate personal messages and repeatedly asked me to buy clothes or items for him — something no teacher should ever request from a student. I tried to ignore these requests politely and repeatedly, but he continued his harassment and threats.

When I reported his behavior to the manager, instead of helping me, they tried to make me feel guilty. They even canceled two of my classes, trying to pressure me into apologizing to the very person who had harassed me. It felt like the school was trying to silence me instead of protecting me.

In my opinion, Truman College operates more like a closed-off family group or mafia rather than an educational institution. They protect each other, ignore complaints, and push students aside. It’s a place where power is abused, and no real accountability exists. Staff members won’t hold each other accountable or accept criticism, and that creates a scary and unhealthy atmosphere.

If you’re someone with big dreams and limited time — if you’re serious about your goals — I strongly advise against enrolling at this college. Truman feels more like a day center for the elderly or unemployed individuals who are just looking to pass time and joke around. If you have no goals, nothing better to do, and just want to socialize for fun, maybe it’s fine. But if you have ambition, this place will only slow you down.']
