name: Columbia College Chicago
reviews:
['don’t waste your time, money or energy here. i waited four years to get the first crack at registering for the classes i wanted to take, just for them to slap me with a surprise hold over a tetanus jab i got over the summer after a workplace injury. no prior notification or anything. no big deal, i immediately updated my new records. it took them days to process it so i was waitlisted for everything i wanted. advisors refused to override the waitlist system so i am stuck taking a bunch of classes im not really interested in to finish out my degree. joke of a school. they make registration a nightmare, raise tuition, and cut all of the interesting programs and then wonder why student retention is so low…. i wish i’d dropped out when i had the chance.', 'My child is currently enrolled here and for years the following has happened:

1. Classes have been canceled mid-semester, screwing students out of credit.

2. Teachers have been laid off mid-semester, also canceling classes or changing the curriculum in the middle of a term.

3. Financial office has deleted payment accounts, resulting in inability to access tuition pages and payment options. Students have had their registrations be put on hold because of this.

4. Financial office is no longer reachable by phone AT ALL. The system hangs up on you every time you call the number. I’m assuming it’s because they are overwhelmed with people who can’t pay tuition, and have had student registration held indefinitely.

I think that the teachers and educators in this college are wonderful, but the administration is killing it. I don’t think we would have applied to this school at all if we’d realized how difficult it would be to register and pay, not to mention have my child earn a major when the classes keep getting eliminated.', 'We had a scheduled tour of Columbia college. Visited a few of their buildings. Great experience overal! Very artsy college in the beautiful downtown area of Chicago.', "Once your student is enrolled it’s crickets other than monthly newsletters. Pretty sure they send out to try to make themselves look good it’s an all a facade. When you have questions there are not any responses. Calls are left unreturned. Calls and waiting time to speak with people have sometimes been over an hour or I get disconnected.  The tuition raises every year. Zero help from Financial Aid. Every inquiry you have they just redirect you everywhere. The cost is astronomical and their educational platform is not very encouraging or educational.  Also when your child has a concern, the college educator's totally just dismiss it. When your child tells you, they’re not learning anything and that the instructors don’t respond to inquiries about classes or questions/concerns until the end of the quarters or semesters is just ridiculous. There’s zero accountability for the educators or staff because they’re protected by their contracts. Terrible educational facility, Don’t waste your hard earned money sending your child here.", 'Worst school ever. Don’t waste your money and go to a real school.']

name: Concordia University-Chicago
reviews: ['My experience at the school has been excellent. I have yet to encounter any issues or imperfections. The onboarding process was extremely smooth, and both the student portal and Blackboard are clean and easy to navigate. It honestly doesn’t get much better than this.', 'In honor for this great university in nowadays. The educational program from there was excellent, even the interaction between the students and professors.\nWe could do whatever we want in the right way to learn...thank you Mr Director Lee Fair. (1989)', "Went to see a graduation. SO uncomfortable in the tiny gym.They offered cookies and juice.  NOTHING WAS GIVEN! Worst graduation ever! Didn't even have a famous speaker and cost the students $200.00 TO WALK!", 'This is an excellent university in a good location just outside Chicago. The grounds are well-maintained. The university employs some outstanding professors and has Christian clergy on staff who promote moral virtue, personal, and professional ethics.  I completed my undergraduate degree and am now taking MBA courses.   I highly recommend Concordia as it has tremendous educational value.', 'I’m not thrilled with this school especially since it could use some updating. Dorms have no air conditioning. I’m hoping that academically I’m praying that my son gets the best education. We will see.']

name: Danville Area Community College
reviews: ["I wish I could give zero stars. Trying to get in touch with anyone at this college is impossible. I've called multiple departments at different times of the day, every day and no one ever answers the phone. It's incredibly frustrating and makes me question how they handle important issues if they can't even pick up a phone. Save yourself the headache and look elsewhere.", 'I go every Friday to the echo tech classroom to hello my brother out with scan time. Always plenty of parking, the building is easy to navigate, and bathrooms are clean. My brother says the program in demanding and professor is amazing.', 'The best College in Vermillion County and surrounding area by far. Lara Conklin and all the staff work hard to give you the best education. They also have great on line courses if your maintaining a family or job. I highly recommend getting your education here!', 'its a decent school. personally i love it. just dont trust their writing center, they will keep you waiting almost 30 minutes just to talk about a root canal. Never reviwed my paper that day.', 'horrible.....although we had an appointment 2 weeks in advance, the counselor kept us waiting almost 2 hours as he was at a basketball tournament at U of I. Finally arrived and couldn\'t have been more rude, rushing us thru the meeting, no doubt not happy that he was called to leave that game. Decided this was NOT the place for my son....he went to KCC, graduated and is working in his field of trade . However, leave it to DACC, they are still sending us 1098-T\'s every year showing my son not only attended school there but got help with tuition. Not true...my son never attended one day of school there. They can\'t even tell me what class he supposedly answered "present" in when rocall was done. Pay out of district tuition if you must.....its worth it to stay out of DACC. Bad enough my tax dollars go there']

name: DePaul University
reviews:
["May come back to update after graduation in June if there are any outlier events worth noting, but overall I have had a mixture of both bad and wonderful experiences at DePaul. Note: I took a 5 year gap due to COVID and am finishing my BA in Sociology.
Teachers: I have had some teachers who have become such an asset to me and have really been guiding forces in my career and others who were completely checked out. Teachers have become way more lax about deadlines and are understanding of students having lives and challenges, which I appreciate! I have been in the field and workforce a long time and I think overall, there is way too much required reading in most classes. More teachers need to offer different types of learning, audio, visual, community based, etc. I know it is important to learn to be critical and digest academic texts, but not everyone learns the same.
Side note- DePaul is stingy with tenured positions. I would love to see that change and for teachers to become core parts of the college. I think it would provide a better sense of community and livelihood for the teachers.
Classes: In my major, there is a lack of flexibility in course offerings for mandatory classes. DePaul forces you to be on campus a lot, which is an outdated, unaccommodating approach for students who have anything else going on in their life like commuting, work, kids, etc. I also think the Sociology track is under supported with the school's focus being on business majors, finance, and media. You would think as a Catholic University there would be more emphasis on serving community and fixing poverty. I also think there could be more of a range of class topics in this field.
Campus and Technology: The Lincoln Park campus is beautiful in every season.
I am glad they have updated security measures around campus now. As far as food options go it is not too bad, but it is a little overpriced, especially for students. The technology used to view degree progression, classes available, and to even call in for support is horrible.  Completely disorganized and most of the employees don't have a helpful attitude. Access to digital course materials and media via the library is lacking. The writing center is great!", 'As expensive of an educational institution as DePaul University is, the communication from the departments are below acceptable. I completed a course in May and was told the grades would be uploaded at the end of the semester, by January 2,2026. As of today my grade has not been updated. It takes an excessive amount of time sometimes days to receive a reply from faculty members such as advisors and financial aid. So far, instructors have been good with communication, everyone else has been unacceptable. Waiting for days to receive a reply or for records to be updated is unrealistic when I think of how much it costs to attend this university. I guess service and assistance isn’t included in the tuition.', "So, let me get this straight:
The university is demolishing historical buildings to build a new athletic facility, cutting staff because of budget cuts, and thinks this is good for the school? Also... Maybe don't build that facility. Maybe, retain your staff.

I got my master's degree here, and I really loved the staff and my time there. I'm extremely upset to see leadership take it in this direction. I feel bad for students who are losing valuable staff members because of a building. Buildings don't teach.", 'I graduated from DePaul University years ago, and I’m saddened by its current trajectory. The administration appears to prioritize international enrollment at the expense of a balanced student body, and the academic environment has grown intolerant of differing viewpoints. I can no longer recommend DePaul to prospective students.', 'A garbage university that could care less about the neighborhood and the city let alone its students. Why demolish vacant properties when you can demolish historic row homes for an athletic department that hasn’t done anything?']

name: College of DuPage
reviews:
['The college itself is well organized, clean, and overall great.

Instructors are either good or bad. My advice.... Before you register for a class look up the professor. This will make a big difference when it comes to your grades, the college has many nice professors who are easy graders, find them. Your best bet is to talk to people and make use of rate my professor. Some classes you have little choice with the professors and some of these professors are tough, rude, and inconsiderate. But for the most part a lot of them from my experience are actually decent people. As a result, I was able to get an A in pretty much all my classes.

No matter what your plans are, your time COD and your experience is dependent on YOU. Make the most of it. Make as many or as few friends as you want. And learn what you can. The college has many benefits so take advantage of them.', 'Excellent, affordable and reliable. This community college is a gem in the western suburbs located in Dupage County. The variety of programs is amazing. The teachers are very well educated. When applying ask for a waiver code and your application can be free. The pre-requisites to start classes at the college are very flexible. They have a wonderful support system called the learning center. They have free tutors in all classes. They offer financial aid and scholarships. Free GED classes. Advising and counseling is free. Registration can be in person or online. Classes are offered in a variety of offerings, online, hybrid, face to face or in person. What more can you ask for? A great college! Check it out.', "One of the worst colleges around. Unprofessional, unknowledgeble, violate federal regulations on a regular basis, chaotic and terribly managed. Try their best to take away your federal financial aid. They do not care about students or their success one bit; all they care about is their enrollment numbers, status and the huge amounts of money pouring in. Faculty are regularly rude with bad attitudes and abuse their positions of power for their own benefit. On top of that, they do not accomodate for students with disabilities as they should, and also do not accomodate for the large enrollment numbers. Routinely put students in uncomfortable and distressing situations due to their lack of care, planning and refusal to fund necessary improvements. And then when you make a formal complaint to administration they collaborate with each other and just pass you around between department directors, giving exactly zero attention to your frustrations. They just truly do not care about the students.

And all of this is without even addressing the poor quality of academics that's provided for students. I believe this school should really be investigated by the Deparment of Education for its corrupt conduct and practices, and totally do not recommend it to anyone looking for a meaningful education experience.", 'Please stop with the misleading advertising promotion I refuse to pay a fee of $20.00 when my student aid should be able to cover it this was a scam bait please remove your advertising promotion or I will flagged it to Google my business as violating there terms of service as scam misleading I will not attend a college that hides stuff from a third party thanks for wasting my time you deserve 0 Stars. I will take my business elsewhere.', 'This is an absolutely horrible place they’re very unorganized and have no clue what’s going on. The management and staff are more confused than the students are. Just go to Harper.

Rather than contacting advising, which is already long and tough process to go through, just stand in the hallways, ask around and find a student that’s taking the program you want to do, ask them what courses and steps you need to take to get into that program.
These advisors aren’t trained to answer or even comprehend what you’re talking about.

Their printing system is absolutely terrible and a headache to deal with. I would rather drive 20 minutes to Glenside public library to print my papers then come back than to deal with their printers.
Just a terrible school overall.

Like I said before just go to Harper or Elgin community college don’t even try and waste you’re time here.']

name: East-West University
reviews:
['East West University (EWU) is a private university in Bangladesh, established in 1996, known for its commitment to quality education and research. It is one of the few private universities to receive permanent government approval and has a permanent campus in Aftabnagar, Dhaka. EWU offers a wide range of undergraduate and graduate programs across 14 departments, aiming to develop skilled professionals with critical thinking skills for both national and international opportunities.
Key features
Establishment and approval:
Founded in September 1996 after receiving permission from the government.
One of the first private universities to get permanent approval from the government.
Campus:
Located in Aftabnagar, Dhaka, after moving from its original Mohakhali campus.
The campus spans a significant area and includes multiple buildings.
Academics and faculty:
Offers 14 departments with both undergraduate and graduate programs.
Has a large number of full-time faculty members, with a significant portion holding Ph.D.s.
Curricula are based on North American universities and are continuously updated.
Rankings and awards:
Ranked as a top university in Bangladesh for quality of education and research by various indexes.
Received the ICT Digital World Award in 2017.
Student development:
Emphasizes providing affordable education and improving access to job opportunities.
Has a Career Counseling Center that helps students with job placement, internships, and professional skills development.
Social and extracurricular:
Has a focus on human values and social responsibility.
Provides scholarships and financial assistance for students, such as the Medha Lalon Scholarship.
Features numerous student clubs and organizations that facilitate extracurricular and mental health activities, such as the East West University Health and Well-being Club.', 'East West University has a beautiful and friendly environment. It is also among the top private universities in Bangladesh. The university strictly maintains all academic rules, so anyone who wants to do well can definitely learn here. EWU has already expanded with many buildings, and I heard that in the future they are planning to establish an even larger permanent campus😍In Sha Allah..', "East West University (EWU) is undoubtedly one of the top-tier private universities in Bangladesh. Established in 1996 by prominent economist Dr. Mohammed Farashuddin, it has built a legacy of academic excellence. While it started in Mohakhali, its current permanent campus in Aftabnagar is modern, spacious, and provides a great environment for learning.
​It's impressive to note that EWU was ranked 3rd in Bangladesh and 64th in the Indian subcontinent by Webometrics (2007), highlighting its strong focus on scientific research and international standards. Highly recommended for Science, Engineering, Business, and Liberal Arts!", 'One of the reputed private universities in Bangladesh. I went there with my colleagues to attend a seminar. We spent a quality time. I want to specially mention the hospitality, we experienced there. We were very impressed by the architectural design of their academic buildings.
In general, it was a well spent day.', "Scholarships & Assistance
East West University offers a variety of scholarships and financial assistance to support students. The university provides merit scholarships that range from full funding to partial tuition waivers. Each semester, the top 10% of students in each batch with a CGPA of 3.97 or above are awarded the EWU Merit Scholarships, valued at 90,000 BDT for undergraduate students and 75,000 BDT for postgraduate students. Additionally, students on the Dean's List are eligible for the Medha Lalon Fund Scholarship, which ranges from 25,000 BDT to 500,000 BDT. The university also offers 28 directorial scholarships each year, valued between 20,000 BDT and 25,000 BDT, for meritorious students with exceptional cases.
For financial aid, students facing financial difficulties, with a CGPA of 3.7 and above, who have completed at least 30 credits in the last three semesters, can apply once a year for support. The financial aid varies from 18,000 BDT to 35,000 BDT. East West University provides a 50% tuition waiver for one sibling pair studying simultaneously at the university, which is worth around 45,000 BDT per year. The university maintains a low tuition fee rate of 4,900 BDT per credit, which varies by department."]

name: Eastern Illinois University
reviews:
['I am so thankful for the incredible support and guidance I’ve received from my academic advisor and professors at Eastern Illinois University. My advisor/professor, Jacqueline Janesku, has been outstanding these past couple of years, always patient, supportive, and encouraging. She not only helped me stay on track academically, but also made me feel like I had a true advocate in my corner.

I also want to give special recognition to some of my professors who made a lasting impact on my journey: Dr. Gordon Tucker, Dr. Misty Rhoads, Jan A. Murphy Morgan, and Dr. Thapaliya. Each of them brought such passion to their teaching and showed a genuine investment in their students’ success. They challenged me to grow, supported me when I needed it, and inspired me with their knowledge and kindness.

All of these individuals have played a huge role in my academic and personal growth. Their encouragement, guidance, and dedication have shaped my college experience in the best way possible, and I feel incredibly fortunate to have had them as part of my journey.', 'Went to EIU to see the homecoming football game. Even though we left at halftime with EIU losing big it was still enjoyable and was worth seeing again. Still looks the same as when I left some 40 years ago.', 'Today, EIU is having a Comic Con at Booth Library and a Band Festival by Lantz Gym area. Go check out the updated campus.', 'I have visited this university because my husband studied there. It was very nice experience for me.
EIU has a welcoming campus environment and a vibrant student life with various organizations and activities. While it may not be as large or well-known as some other universities, it has a solid reputation for its education programs, business school, and the sciences. The campus is also noted for its affordability and strong community feel.', 'Good school, the dorms could use some updating in more ways than one, the dining halls can have their menus revisited and updated for better more nutritional food. Overall an average school.']

name: Elgin Community College
reviews: ['I’ve been in and out of ECC for the past 3–4 years, and I just have to give a HUGE shout-out to the incredible cleaning crew! I recently learned they’re also the team behind setting up almost all events at ECC— Over the last couple of years, the difference has been night and day. The floors have never looked so shiny, and every space feels clean and welcoming. I can’t express enough how much I appreciate walking into a campus that feels safe, clean, and cared for. THANK YOU for the hard work and dedication—it truly makes a difference! I hope this message reaches the right department because you all deserve the recognition!', "I am very upset. I used a vending machine and my drink got stuck. This isn't the first time this has happened. I went to first stop. All I was told was to go to the cafeteria. I did that. They said all I can do is contact the number. Tried that, nothing. Is there really no one that can get this vending machine door open?", "Haven't taken a class yet, but the academic advisor was brief and uninformative.  The halls were decorated in political statements instead of academic.   Hoping the professors stick to knowledge and not propaganda.", "I've technically been associated with ECC because of my dual credit program at SEHS and the credits transferred smoothly to my 4-year college! My friends love it here and their auditorium is very nice and welcoming as well. Their parking lots are MASSIVE which is a huge plus to find parking! Great community college!", 'What are you going to do to protect your students from being kidnapped by ICE?']

name: Elmhurst University
reviews:
['My experience in this University has been great! The campus is pretty safe and the community is very welcoming and kind. Classes have been great as well, professors do go above and beyond to help with what you need. There are tons of different clubs you can join and Greek life is awesome. I highly recommend attending this university.', 'I enjoyed my time at Elmhurst University mostly; I feel as though it has several opportunities despite it being a smaller university. I transferred here from a community college after earning my associate degree and received several generous merit scholarships to attend this school.

I mostly attended psychology and biology courses here; there psychology curriculum was quite expansive, although admittedly, their biology courses required filing a petition to enter every semester given that the volume of students in the biology program exceeded the courses available (e.g., 3 to 5 “upper-level” biology classes offered with a total of 15 to 20 seats open each, but over 100 students with degree focuses requiring these classes).

The school is quite beautiful in the fall and winter. With the addition of their new health sciences building, I anticipate the school will continue to grow and expand its scope. Grateful for the opportunity to have been a Bluejay 🎓🩵', 'Really nice campus and a nice downtown area that is walking distance. Very nice professors and the small campus vibe is very nice. There are many resources here to students to utilize.', 'Currently a student, I adore this university. Inclusive, fun events, good professors. They want their students to succeed and offer many resources (academic, accommodations, mental health services, and more). As a student with a physical disability, I have been accepted and supported by faculty and other students. Genuinely love it here and look forward to continuing my academic journey at EU.', "I don't go here, but the tuition is ridiculous for a mediocre program. However, it brings a lot to the city, from housing to businesses in the downtown area. Nice campus, well kept, with a decent library and paths. Nice to have around."]

name: Eureka College
reviews:
["Very hard to get a five stars out of me. Was very impressed with how I was greeted how they treated my daughter. All the professors were very polite and answered all my questions. The college is definitely one that your child's not going to be lost in the system. Look at several colleges and I think this will be the winner", 'I am an alum. My Mom (alum) and Dad (Dad was attending Bradley) met there. My Aunt & her son went there. So did my Grandfather. So I am a little bias.
But if you are looking for one of the best private school values in the nation... and a atmosphere where you can get to know others and not be a # check out EC.

If that many from one family went EC must be great!

PS If you are into football or another sport there is a good chance they can find academic funds to help you attend. Plus with a enrollment of about 600 there is a good chance of making the varsity team as a walk on...', '"A small college in a small community, where there are no assembly-line diplomas handed out" - Ronald Reagan, class of '32.  The school is small, but close to mid-sized (Peoria, Blomington-Normal) cities as well as a big (Chicago) city to not be so isolated.  Staff is very helpful, education is tailor made so each student can excel where there skill and interests take them.', "Ok, TBH. I don't know much about the college. It is a beautiful campus. Totally came here because it has a lot of Pokemon Gyms & Stops. If you are in town and play. This is the place to go. Happy Cathching!", "Eureka is a liberal arts college dedicated to teaching students to think independently and grow in their thinking. It's a great place for an affordable education. Smaller class sizes with caring faculty and staff make it a great place for students."]

name: Fox College
reviews: ['As a 2020 graduate of Fox the program laid a great foundation for me. I always knew I wanted to pursue to become an OTR, but I had a different journey. The teachers at Fox were caring, firm, and made sure that we actually understood the information which helped me so much in both my Masters and Doctoral programs. I still have relationships with some of the professors to this day based on the amazing, genuine relationships they take the time to build with their students along the journey.', 'I attended Fox Collage’s OTA program class of 2024. The program is well laid out and covers a lot of pertinent information so that you are well prepared as a new clinician. The instructors are wonderful and they each have their own niche and expertise which is helpful when you need the answers to certain questions. They also offer help and are invested in your success wholeheartedly! The classes were small in size that gave a very family feeling which made it easier to come back everyday! With that being said the program itself is very intense 16 month program there is no breaks all gas! Some topics you only cover a couple of days and on to the next thing. The grading scale is higher so you have to work extremely hard to stay a float! There is always an assignment, papers or test due! Your social life will be nonexistent! I would recommend this program to younger people coming right out of high school or people with a good support system! I recommend finding jobs like Uber, Amazon, etc that are flexible because there is no time to work a real job and that becomes frustrating because life still goes on. I also recommend saving money before hand because there will be out of pocket costs you will need to cover. The entire staff at Fox is wonderful and will help if you reach out. Overall I really did enjoy my time at Fox and making long term friendships and relationships with my classmates and instructors.', 'AMAZING OTA Program!!! The professors are GREAT at what they do!!! The program offers you all the resources you’ll need to be successful in your career. I really enjoyed my experience at Fox College, met a lot of great people that I hope to work close by in my future. Everyone on campus is friendly & resourceful. So excited for the learning opportunities, opened my eyes to being apart of something bigger. 10/10 OTA Program !!!', "Good idea if you have no other obligations in life. If you are an adult who is not supported by someone, I would not go to this school. It is for young adults who do not need to work and make money. It is full time, plus homework at night and over most Saturday's and Sunday's. Don't let them fool you, if you have no education with science this will be very hard for you as the program is very fast and offers little help to student's (even though they charge twice as much as a real school that would have tutors). The help they offer is from other fellow student's who are trying to figure out everything as well, so it is a poor situation if you need extra assistance at this school. A few amazing teachers, most though could be easily replaced with better options.", 'when you tour, they tell you exactly what you need to hear & it’s different for everybody. It’s a shame because a lot of students end up hating the career over this greedy program. They don’t offer support & don’t care to drop the minority students.']

name: Governors State University
reviews:
["There are tons of opportunities here. Take advantage of the small campus to build connections and gain experience in your field while earning your degree. The campus is also chef's kiss in the spring time.", 'My first time visiting The campus for the popular stage performance of Shen Yun Excellent Show!!, I was seated in the auditorium for performing arts that area was clean and the restrooms were clean.', 'Great School. The campus is quiet and class sizes are small. Most lectures are in the afternoon and evening hours. This is the perfect place for those who work during the day. My husband had his masters here.', "Counselor education and supervision program. Most rude and unprofessional professors in the world are there. I had very bad experiences in this program's education services. I do not recommend this program to anyone seeking decent education. One professor is mean, rude, and unprofessional. I also noticed that many of their staff act unprofessionally with students. Patricia Robey is the most disrespectful and disgraceful professor I had to deal with. She does not belong in the education system.", 'If your considering this school really weigh out the pros and cons.
Overall, I would never recommend this school. Yeah it is cheaper but is it worth the pain the school will put you through.
Worst  school ever. I obtained my bachelors and masters at a GSU; Many of my friends in the other programs and I agree the most of the teachers  favor students and are extremely bias. Also, some classes are only offered during certain semesters. The following happened to myself and many of my friends at GSU, One of your core classes that you really need in order to graduate is only offered in the fall. When the fall comes around, you’re going to be told that the college could not find an adjunct for the course so it will be offered next year in the fall. That really sucks, especially if your receiving financial aid, now you’re going to  have to take a class you really don’t  need in order to have enough credits to receive your financial aide.
Another problem my peers and I had. You only get 4 tickets for your graduation.  To make matters worse, If you do not finish your program in May. you have to wait forever for your ceremony; my peers and I finished in the winter and we had to wait the following year to walk across the stage.
More so, many classes are offered at night ( 4:30-7:20  and 7:30-10:20) which was convenient for me. However, the cafeteria would be close early. Coming straight from work I would be extremely hungry. Why close the cafeteria at 7pm when many  classes start at 7:30 and get out of class at 10:30?']

name: Greenville University
reviews: ['This is my alma matter and I absolutely loved my experience here. Now, I am 14 years removed, but my experience at Greenville was life changing for the better. Being a Christian, it was the perfect place for me to grow in my faith and be challenged in it as well, with the COR classes all students have to take. With a desire to teach the whole person, days like the all school hike was awesome and you were always given the opportunity to make memories and lifelong friends that were different than you.  I would like to believe that heaven is extremely diverse, and Greenville gives you an opportunity to meet different kinds of people that many “normal” high schoolers might overlook. I also played football and ran track here, so the life of a student athlete was also appealing and fun. Tuition is tuition, I mean it is a private liberal arts university, so that’s why I give it 4 stars instead of 5. Take my opinion with a grain of salt though as I can not speak on the quality of what it is now. I do know that the professors all seek to love like Christ and will do anything for you to help you fulfill your purpose. You will be treated like you matter as the classes are very small and you will be given every opportunity to know and grow your relationship with the creator of the universe who sent his son to die for our sins', 'I had such an amazing preview day experience that I will honestly decide to go to this school. It feels like home away from home with a well-rounded education and social life experience. Thank you faculty for making this day special!', 'Strongly recommend stopping by the Richard Bock Museum. Great place to learn about this very important but little known Illinois artist. Great Museum.', 'I wish I could give this “university” zero stars or perhaps a negative rating. The girls dorm hall is heinous. Major bug issues on the third floor. Subpar education at best. They try to sell you on going here with measly scholarships and the Jesus effect basically. If you are a Christian with loving kindness DO NOT GO HERE. Parents & future students: your child will not be safe here. Campus safety is worthless. This campus is full of Title IX/sexual assault perpetrators. The Dean of students and many other admin are insensitive to students needs and concerns. Also literally nothing to do in this town you will be so bored here. Please go somewhere more affordable that provides a better education.', "I really love this school. Its a small christian liberal arts environment which means you get small class sizes and individual attention. The professors are really nice and love to get to know their students on a personal level. There are a lot of ways to get help outside of the classroom. I am a transfer student here and the advisors made it really easy to transition to this institution.  They reminded me of deadlines and held my hand through every step of the process.The only downsides you would really have to consider is that it is a small town so there aren't a lot of places to go. I also feel that the chapel credits you have to get as a student are a little much."]

name: Highland Community College
reviews: ['Small town..small community...small school but nice apartment style housing..great football coaching staff..nice people in town. Overall I felt comfortable leaving the baby of the family for his first year of college...', 'If the staff would refrain from stereotyping students it could be a decent learning institution. Small town mentality. Such a disappointment.', 'Not the best organization at producing "consistently" and "reliability" out of their students.', "Nice campus, engaged community! Excellent vocal music program and campus life experience! The large on-campus population in a small town makes for a uniquely valuable social growth opportunity for students coming into college.  Small class sizes ensure students are able to be given the one on one interaction time that all data shows to be beneficial.  I was a student here and met friends from all walks of life, from around the country who I'm friends with 20 years later.  The staff and faculty care about the success of their students, both academically and personally.  Like any college experience you will get out what you put into it, but Highland truly offers a unique opportunity for growth during those transition years of a traditional student coming from High School and going on to a 4 year.\n\nI'm also very impressed with how much the technical programs have grown and evolved! Or maybe I just didn't know how cool they were before.  Either way, good stuff!", 'Allison in admissions is extremely rude. She makes the admission process uncomfortable. She clearly does not like her job at all. She gets irritated and frustrated with students when calling with questions regarding enrollment process. If admissions frustrates her so much she should have never gotten a job working with college students.']

name: University of Illinois Chicago
reviews:
['The University of Illinois Chicago is built around immediacy and function. It sits in the middle of a working city, and that reality shapes the academic culture: practical, direct, and tied to professional application. Students are expected to connect coursework to internships, research, healthcare systems, business environments, and public service right away. The tone is not ornamental — it is about building competence you can point to, explain, and use.

UC Davis operates in a very different mode. The campus is expansive, insulated, and supported by a strong institutional reputation, but that scale can dilute the sense of urgency students feel. Navigating administrative layers, large course structures, and a broad, decentralized system can make the experience seem less intentionally driven. Some students say they have to manufacture their own challenge because it is not consistently embedded in the environment itself. In that setting, highly driven individuals sometimes describe the culture as less collaborative than expected, with competition playing out in subtle or discouraging ways rather than through open academic rigor. Critics argue this can leave strong students feeling unsupported or out of sync with the broader pace.

At UIC, the pressure comes from constant proximity to real work and real demands.
At UC Davis, momentum can depend more on how much a student pushes independently within a very large system.

The contrast is between an institution shaped by function and one shaped by scale — and those differences can matter more in practice than they do in rankings.', "Have been in UIC since 2021 and graduated in May 2025. It's a wonderful campus with diverse student populations and a lot of opportunities to offer. They prioritize safety through UIC Safe apps which makes it easier for students with late night classes to commute within or out of campus. There is a welcoming environment for students who stay on or off campus. For those interested in off campus housing, there are a lot of good and affordable apartments located close to campus. Lot of nice restaurants near campus and good train connectivity to downtown Chicago. Would recommend to anyone interested in attending the school.", 'So far a good experience. If you want to make long-term friends, you absolutely need to involve yourself in clubs, organizations, or programs. I think most professors I’ve encountered are generally helpful and want to see you succeed. If you’re considering UIC from out of state, I will caution that you will want to be prepared for being in the heart of Chicago. I feel generally safe, but you will want to always be attentive when taking public transit like the CTA. UIC has its own shuttle system and dedicated blue line stop. It’s an overall well-maintained campus, but you’ll have to seek out any experiences beyond simply education.', "The University of Illinois Chicago, centrally located at 1200 W Harrison St, is consistently recognized in my civic and professional circles as a vital urban engine of opportunity where a substantive commitment to research accessibility meets the diverse energy of a global city. Through numerous insightful dialogues with healthcare professionals and successful tech alumni, it is merytorically evident that UIC provides a high-caliber environment, frequently lauded by my acquaintances for its exceptional ability to host a world-class academic medical center while remaining a deeply respectful and inclusive gateway for first-generation scholars. It is truly heartening to observe how the institution maintains such a transparent dedication to public health and urban development, qualities that the broader Chicago community identifies as the primary catalyst for the university’s status as a top-tier research powerhouse. Many individuals I know personally emphasize the school’s sophisticated synthesis of rigorous scientific inquiry and practical, community-based application as a distinguished hallmark, proving that the campus excels in turning academic potential into tangible social impact. The institution's relentless drive toward innovation is frequently reflected in the success stories shared by my peers, who often mention the unique advantage of studying at a premier public university that is so deeply integrated into the economic fabric of the Midwest. Ultimately, in the collective view of informed observers, UIC stands as a distinguished pillar of American higher education, rightfully respected for its elegant ability to merge a massive institutional scale with a profoundly human-centric mission of transformative growth.", 'Good campus. Great facilities. Listed at rank 151 on World Top 500 universities by Time... Worth to consider as place to continue study']

name: Benedictine University
reviews:
['I attended Benedictine University for two semesters. A discussion regarding the Iraq war manifested, and as a Veteran of the conflict, I felt that I might be able to offer some insight into the class discussion. After informing my classmates and Professor of my status, the Professor said, "You should know all about Abu Gharib then". It was in that moment I knew that I was in the wrong place. It is very hard for me to explain how degrading it was being compared to war criminals, especially after honorable service. Is this how these professors regard military service? Secondly, this same Professor seemed to gloat about how he was tenured and couldn't be fired if he tried. This is the type of person that teaches people what to think, not how to think.

I would never recommend this institution.', "I loved my experience at Benedictine University! I'm proud that I graduated from this school! I loved that the class sizes were small and that you actually got to know your professors. Some of my favorite memories include studying abroad to Morocco with faculty and students, going to NYC for Model UN with our class and winning an award, working in the library, learning all I could about Global Studies and the Arabic language, performing with the Concert Choir, taking voice lessons, and being involved with Catholic-Muslim Dialogue. I had a well-rounded education, and I can tell you all that BenU more than prepared me for grad school at DePaul University as a history MA student. My research skills were refined and honed at BenU, and I'm honored that I was first of all, accepted as a student at Benedictine, and second of all, that I graduated from here! I highly recommend BenU to anyone, especially those that want more of a personal and academic experience out of college as well as the ability to commute to school. Go Eagles!", 'Loved this place and constantly checking its development on Google Map every year as I had left the place 8 years ago. I miss the classrooms, the trading lab, and the professors in this university. Love BenU and eagle for life.', 'Benu is a quaint little university here in the burbs. The teachers and admin are really dedicated to the overall success of the students, whatever their goals may be.

If you’re still trying to decide on what you want to study, it’s a good school too; teachers will help you find your passion.

They need to improve their academic advising, is the only thing, but if you find upperclassmen who can help you navigate your college experience you’ll be fine.', 'Student life is good. But the administration and infrastructure is such poor quality, especially when considering the costs for a student.

Had an awful experience at the financial department office where a worker tried to publicly embarrass me about my financial questions.

The website to take the online courses is hard to use, compared to the website for ASU Online and COD Online.

The basketball court is a joke. Automatic handicap doors are broken. Staff doesn’t know how to get from one place to another.

Spend your hard earned money on a school that’s much better, don’t waste your time at BenU']

name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
reviews:
['I am a proud alumna having graduated in 2016.I had the best of both worlds! A stellar world class education and an amazing social life with a great group of lifelong friends! I will never forget my undergraduate experience at U of I and highly reccommend!! ILLINI FOREVER!!', 'The University of Illinois campus is beautiful, especially Japan House with its serene Japanese garden. I’ve also been studying digital marketing through Coursera, which has been very meaningful. This university is truly amazing!', 'As a parent, it’s that time when we help our children make decisions about the next phase of their lives. For me, sending my child off to college at UIUC was one of the most emotional moments. On the first day, I couldn’t help but cry as I left her on campus, much like I did when I dropped her off at kindergarten. The feeling of letting go is never easy, but looking back, I can say with certainty that UIUC was a wonderful choice for her.

From the very beginning, the campus and community have offered incredible support and opportunities. The professors and lecturers are amazing—engaging and truly invested in their students’ success. There’s always academic help available, whether it’s through tutoring, office hours, or student groups that offer additional support. I was always impressed by how approachable and willing the faculty were to help students succeed.

What stands out most, though, is the sense of safety and care on campus. There’s always someone available to help, even late at night, whether you’re walking around and need assistance or have a concern. UIUC truly seems committed to the well-being of all its students.

For those of you wondering about religious and cultural connections, there is a Hindu temple just 10 minutes away from campus, providing a sense of community and belonging for students who want that connection.

To other parents considering sending their child to UIUC, I want to assure you—it’s a fantastic campus. Don’t worry. The support, education, and experiences your child will have are priceless. You can rest easy knowing they’re in  good hands!', 'I was in UIUC to see off my Nephew.
The university campus is humongous .
The college buildings are awesome , transport system within the university is great(sometimes it takes a long time), there are dedicated bike lanes and accessibility access almost all places
they boast the biggest engineering library .
The orientation program was good and informative, people seem efficient and I am sure teaching staff is also great
There are quite a few frat houses and student quarters around the university
The restaurant selection is great and the university also has multiple on campus food court, and surprisingly have a lot of good vegetarian options as well
Students who really want to learn well can do wonders. Great place to study and enjoy', "Education-wise, it is a good university, but socially, it is a disaster. Far away from everything, and Champaign and Urbana are small cities. There are quite a few opportunities here. If you don't want to study in the cornfields, I suggest you choose a different university."]

name: Illinois Wesleyan University
reviews:
['Proud Alum and staff member. Beautiful campus, excellent faculty and staff -- lots of opportunities and personal attention in a great college town. Small class sizes without feeling like a small school. Seems pricey up front, like all private schools, but very generous with scholarships and grants -- the people here really work to make it affordable for each family.', "Attended the Associated Colleges of Illinois Work & Life Boot Camp on 2/8/2020. The facilities where the event took place spacious, clean and beautiful. The staff was welcoming and one of the things that I especially was thankful for was the signage. Having never been to this institution, I appreciated the signs that pointed us to the parking lots and to the buildings where we'd be. The food that was served was decent. The parts of the campus that we saw were well maintained, up-to-date and nice. It snowed on the day we were there, so the views from the building we were in, were gorgeous.", "We were greeted by the IWU staff and sat down with Admissions counselors who answered all our questions. They were incredibly welcoming and helpful. Then we were given a great campus tour.

The students of the musical theatre department were so friendly and generous with their time. I was deeply impressed with their genuine affection for each other and their school. These students are gifted in their field and already working professionally before graduation.

The faculty is dedicated, knowledgeable and experienced. I would trust them with my child's education and growth as a human being. They genuinely care about their  students and their future. They have created  a supportive and yet academically challenging environment.

A beautiful, small campus.", 'Academically challenging, Professors with small class sizes are top notch; along with a beautiful campus and good golf program.  They tend to preach liberal propaganda but as do all liberal arts programs.  TGOE!', "Wonderful graduation ceramony! They put on a really great day for all the grads. Plenty of snacks and refreshments for all the family's."]

name: Illinois Central College
reviews:
['A STRONG word of warning to any, all, and potential donors and future students to this institution. I encourage you to reach out to current students (especially students in the dental program) about their experiences and their treatment by professors and secretaries. There is a lackluster approach to professionalism and the general want for students to succeed.  My opinion of this institute would be different if these were isolated incidences but these are multiple horror stories by current students. Donors and future students be warned!', 'This is an amazing community college; I learned a lot of useful skills and knowledge while attending. I went for the Automotive Technology program and would not recommend it more. It is by far one of the best programs at the campus. The instructors are very outgoing and understanding. Tom and Todd run one of the best college automotive programs in central Illinois. Without them I would not be the technician I am today. I would highly suggest going through this program if you attend or plan on going to Illinois Central College.', 'I'm sure it's a fine college. I have an issue with the wording on their website involving a federally mandated traffic course. When you get your license, you take defensive driving. When you get a speeding ticket under the age of 25, you take the Alive at 25 NSC federal course. Why are they selling me a generic defensive driving course, when the defensive driving course page online says "Alive at 25" on the page. Then there's a full separate page that says "Alive at 25" and nothing else. I cannot comprehend why they both say "Alive at 25" when one is NOT the Alive at 25 course. Because of the website editor incompetency, I now have to pay a court fee and extend my case because they can't get it together with their website wording.

Was an instant refund stay away. Fix your website and stop playing with people's lives

I changed the stars from 1 to 2 to bypass Google filtering. It's 1 star all day', 'Amazing professors and a quality administration. It made my time here fly by.  Not to mention how much they help their students succeed.  Highly recommend.', 'Great place to easily get a degree. Not a great place to get a valuable education. Classes are inexpensive, the material is easy, they have resources, staff is friendly and if you are a midwesterner then this is a great step up. If you’re from a coastal state you’re going to feel like you’re back in the 6th grade']

name: Illinois College
reviews: ["Wonderful caring staff. They give personalized care for the individual and the college as a whole.  There are many different opportunities that aren't available to all at other universities. The biggest downside is the variety of food in the cafe.  But meal plans are flexible for on-campus restaurants too and take-home boxes of food.  Some dorms have a full kitchen so students can cook for themselves. All of my classmates have been very friendly, the campus is beautiful, and the professors are willing to help to see you succeed.  I really love being at Illinois College and am glad that I made the decision to come here.', 'A college education is something you earn but cannot be given. It does not offer every major a gigantic school can but a student can prepare for almost any career by acquiring a liberal education which teaches how to think and how to continue to learn throughout life.', 'I spent my undergraduate days at IC and I loved every minute of it. name: Illinois Institute of Technology
reviews:

I had 3 academic advisers be unresponsive to me as I enrolled in the program. 2/4 classes had subpar instruction which included classes not occurring from technical difficulties, incorrect homework sets, meandering lectures, and a professor sharing private medical information of one of the students. I suggest considering other alternatives to Illinois Tech for educational opportunities. Be wary of the drop course date and withdrawing before then if needed. This institute is do the agriculture and engineering courses.

name: Illinois State University
reviews:

Excessive fees and limited spaces show that it's not investing in the right amount of infrastructure.", "It was Homecoming at its always a segregated tale of two cities: ISU (Predominately) White Version and The Black Alumni Version. I chose the ladder because it represents the Soul of the institution. To make an integrated effort work you must hsve all parties at the decision making table not in a Whitewashed way but in a true multicultural way. Our tailgate draws everyone. Their activities doesn't.", 'My first review was removed, which just further proves my point that this University is a scamming/stealing joke.
I attended a semester here, after leaving the service. I ran through hoops to get all the paperwork needed for my GI Bill. Completed everything and was told that I was good for the semester.

VETERANS STAY AWAY.', 'Illinois State University (ISU) is a public university  in Normal, Illinois. The university emphasizes teaching and is recognized as one of the top ten largest producers of teachers in the US according to the American Association of Colleges of Teacher Education.[7][8] The university's athletic teams are members of the Missouri Valley Conference and the Missouri Valley Football Conference and are known as the "Redbirds," in reference to the state bird, the cardinal.', 'Redbirds basketball is awesome had a fantastic time at the newly renovated redbird arena. Highly recommend you to take in a game or two this season. Come out and root the redbirds on!!!! Off to a great start victory number one.']

name: Illinois Valley Community College
reviews:
['My experience at IVCC was the most harmful educational environment I’ve ever been in.
Over the course of about a year, I witnessed ongoing bullying by staff (including tutors). It wasn’t an isolated incident. It felt normalized and even encouraged, and it escalated when I asked for help. I was trying to simply get through school and graduate, but instead I spent that year in a constant state of stress.
The most disturbing part was that when I sought support, I felt dismissed and blamed rather than protected. Whether intentional or not, the message I got was that certain staff were going to be protected at all costs, even if it came at the expense of a student’s mental health.
I’m still trying to recover from this years later. I strongly recommend prospective students document everything, advocate for themselves, and escalate concerns outside the tutoring department if needed.', "I'm currently in my 2nd year here and cant say enough good things!! everyone here is super helpful and also the teachers are amazing here. they have something for everyone here and have lots of help for low income students. I will be sad when I have to leave here and transfer to a university.", 'Received my first covid vaccine, and they were so well organized, and helpful. Lines moved very quickly.  Information was clear easy to understand. Follow up appointments made. Great experience over all.', 'I do not know much about the actual college & all that it offers but I did attend a choir concert of my mother in-law at the Illinois Valley Community College Auditorium. The place was very clean, they had temperature check-ins when you walked in & the Auditorium was very pretty and the concert sounded great inside of it.', 'Yea I’m sorry for bringing cash to pay for school!
The guy in the office said really cash! U couldn’t bring anything else like a card or anything else he got mad! I am sorry for bringing cash! I’m sorry that I’m making u do your job! 🤔']

name: John A Logan College

My problems were with Trio and certain instructors who didn"t communicate. Most classes I earned the grade that I deserved. Most instructors were fair and did a great job. Some went above and beyond. name: Joliet Junior College
reviews:
['Overall, this college has a nice campus and a generally positive environment for learning. Many of the faculty members are helpful, approachable, and genuinely want students to succeed. That said, there are a few professors who seem disengaged and are clearly just there to collect a paycheck, which can be frustrating and impact the learning experience. I strongly recommend using RateMyProfessor.com when registering for classes—doing a bit of research can help you avoid those professors and make the most of your time here. I unfortunately chose to overlook the reviews for my 8-week course as I was motivated and wanted to take a risk with this professor, and it has already proven to be a mistake. In such a fast-paced format, professor engagement makes a huge difference, and this course is lacking motivation.', "Joliet Junior College offers an outstanding experience for students, and I’m grateful for my time there.

The psychology and history programs are both fantastic, with professors who are passionate about their fields and truly care about helping students succeed. The courses were engaging, thoughtfully structured, and provided a strong foundation for further study or career paths.

The campus itself is lively and modern. There’s always something happening—clubs, events, and activities that make it easy to get involved and feel connected to the community. The facilities are impressive too, with updated classrooms, beautiful common areas, and a clean, welcoming atmosphere across campus.

One hidden gem is the planetarium, which offers an amazing experience whether you’re attending a class, a show, or a special event. It’s a feature that sets JJC apart and shows just how much the college invests in enriching the student experience.

If you're looking for a place that offers excellent academics, a vibrant campus life, and state-of-the-art facilities, Joliet Junior College is an incredible choice.", 'JJC has an array of classes at very affordable tuition and some amazing professors who care about you… BUT, good luck ever contacting your advisor or any advisor in general… if you do run into any issues regarding a specific professor, the “higher ups” truly do not care.', 'My professors are very nice, everyone is very welcoming, and psychology classes seem to be for me.
My only complaint is that I wish that they refilled the food after it emptied. I saw someone take the last of the stuffed shells before I got a chance.
5/5 stars', 'No one ever gets back to you!!!! Whether it’s through email or leaving a voicemail!! DONT WASTE YOUR TIME on this place!! You’re better off going to another school!!! How the hell do you expect to do business if y’all suck at communicating!! They don’t deserve your money!!!']

name: Judson University
reviews:
["Bible studies shoud be easier and introduce to students in a humbleway. I have to be honest Mr. Alexander is actually turning my student away from Church he is just throwing to much information and expecting to much from the students. Not all students have attended or had Bible studies since young age maybe attended church but not Bible school, this is not Bible introduction he puts students down points out he is being hard because that's how life is outside in the real world but you should also be rewarded for your efforts.
I'm asking the school president or the dean to please attend one of his classes.
Thank you
A very concern parent.", 'Great university. Small enough to where you can know your faculty, but large enough to where you can meet people that aren’t from the same background as you.

Attending will certainly broaden your thought process. Buildings are a little older so they have some unique character which makes it a fun campus. They have a great 18-hole disc golf course there as well!', 'Beautiful school everyone here is very kind and helpful. Teachers really try to help you learn and grow.', "Judson University is a private Christian liberal arts university located along the scenic Fox River in Elgin, Illinois—about 45 miles northwest of Chicago. Known for its strong sense of community and Christ-centered education, Judson offers a welcoming environment for both domestic and international students.

Academics

The university offers over 60 undergraduate and graduate programs, including a unique, accredited architecture program—rare among Christian institutions. Other popular majors include business, psychology, worship arts, education, and design. The faculty are known for being supportive and approachable, often blending academic excellence with a strong faith perspective.

Campus

Judson’s campus spans 90 acres and includes 17 buildings, such as academic halls, dormitories, and recreational facilities. One standout is the Harm A. Weber Academic Center—a LEED Gold-certified building that houses the library and School of Art, Design & Architecture. The campus itself is peaceful and beautifully maintained, with direct access to nature trails along the river.

Arts and Student Life

Judson supports a thriving arts scene. Students can participate in theatre productions, musical ensembles, and visual art exhibitions. The Draewell Gallery regularly showcases student and professional work, and campus events often highlight creative talent across disciplines.

Athletics

Athletically, Judson is home to the Eagles, who compete in the NAIA and NCCAA. The university offers a variety of men’s and women’s sports, including soccer, basketball, volleyball, and track. The Lindner Fitness Center provides up-to-date facilities for both athletes and recreational users.

Community and Mission

Founded in 1963 and named after Adoniram Judson, the first American missionary abroad, the university integrates faith and learning. Its mission is to shape students into leaders who serve with character and purpose in their professions and communities.

Final Thoughts:
Judson University is ideal for students seeking a faith-based, personalized education in a close-knit environment. Whether you're drawn by its respected architecture program, scenic campus, or emphasis on Christian values, Judson offers a unique blend of academic rigor and spiritual formation.", '5/7 perfect score, best wildlife sanctuary I've ever been to the wildlife are free to roam the pastures and walkways. The squirrels and skunks are especially at home even in the buildings. Every once and a while an architecture student can be spotted scampering back to lodging for their brief nights, but one must watch out for the boisterous other majors that scare away the wildlife that belong there. This wildlife sanctuary does have a school encroaching but the ponds are always a relief to see how even after a landfill has been dumped in them they are still "a wildlife preserve".']

name: Kankakee Community College
reviews: ['Attended a seminar here.  Easy to navigate the campus and parking lots.   Great signage.  Once inside, the way to the class was well marked. All of the staff was very nice and accommodating.', 'Its unfortunate that the classes I need are waitlisted. Im forced to reach out to other Colleges around the area so I can take the classes I need to get into the program Im working towards. They only offer one teacher for most classes which forces students to take classes elsewhere or take classes that are not required for their program. They need to hire more teachers to accommodate their students. Because of this, I have to wait until Fall of 2026 to start my program, instead of Spring 2026. I already registered for these classes, but my advisor took me out of them until I took a placement test, which ultimately made me lose my spot.', "Coming from a large university to taking classes here, it was a little different to see such a small campus. On the other hand, it makes everything very convenient and easy to find. The campus is far away from the center of town, so everything is very quiet and peaceful. I can see how it's very easy to study and complete your schooling out here. The staff was very helpful with registration and setting up classes, allowing me to take almost everything online. The few classes I will have to take on campus are easily adjusted to fit my schedule, and there is no hassle or pressure.", "I've taken a few courses fairly recently in order to fill the requirements to sit for the CPA, and my fiance is currently attending. This place has taken an absolute nose dive since I graduated a little under a decade ago. The new president and the board who enable him are more concerned with turning a profit than retaining talented professors, as evidenced by the nearly 60% TURNOVER RATE in some departments. If these students want the quality of their education to improve, they need to file complaints with the Higher Learning Commission until this joke of an institution loses its accreditation. Maybe then they'll start to change course in order to bring this college back to the quality it was under the previous administration. name: Kishwaukee College
reviews:
['I appreciate all the  knowledge we can get her on so many subjects....', 'It’s ok but…They only provided little support The bus system poor No fashion classes+Machines ETC', "This place definitely is strict on Covid-19 protocol and clean. That's alwasy good to know considering the flow of people. I was here for  CDL class and that was in the back lot right by the TOWER, you can't miss it.", 'If you want some actual education beyond just learning how to pass a test, Kish is for you!  I believe if you are willing to learn, the instructors here will teach you!  The experience of the instructors will be an added benefit to your course.  They are not producing test passers.  They are producing drivers.

Value:

Some say that you get what you pay for.  But, this program is quite competitive with their pricing vs. the big CDL companies.  It will be worth your while to entertain getting your CDL at Kish!

Benefits:

Newer Trucks!  They have Volvo tractors which are only a couple years old.  They are well maintained!

Their trailers are sound and properly inspected.

Did I mention the experience of the instructors?  My instructor has over 40 years of industry experience as well as sound knowledge which will help you well past passing your driving exam.

Their administrative person is very prompt at answering questions as you're trying to make a decision.  She will not badger you, like other schools did to me, into attending Kish.  I personally appreciated this since I had been recently laid off and I had enough stress going on.

The setting:

Imagine, if you will, a relaxed environment in the middle of rural DeKalb County.  That is what you get.  The school is surrounded by open farmland.  An idealic setting to learn in!  Ask about Fred "Gear Jammin" Fly... 😂  You will learn to drive big rig in the country, on the open highway, and in the suburbs.  Relaxation is a key to learning and you get that with Kish!

I am very happy with my experience at Kish, and I highly recommend this school vs. the more expensive CDL Mills that just turn out test passers (My personal opinion based upon my research prior to signing up.)  Take it from me.  You will not regret learning to be a DRIVER at Kishwaukee!', "So far I have really enjoyed this school. It has been 20 years since I took college classes. reviews:

name: Lake Land College
reviews:
['As a graduating alum (May 2025) and resident of Shelbyville, my overall experience with Lake Land College has been underwhelming. If your goal is simply to receive a diploma or certificate, this school can check that box. But if you’re genuinely looking to learn, grow, or feel supported—especially as a non-traditional student—you may be disappointed.

Much of what I was taught in my program I had already learned independently through YouTube, Google, and free webinars. The instruction often lacked depth or consistency, classes were either completely self-taught or micromanaged to the point of inflexibility, with little attention to how students actually learn best.

One of the biggest frustrations throughout my time at Lake Land was the poor communication between administrators, staff, and faculty. Simple tasks became unnecessarily difficult because of a lack of coordination or clarity. Processes that should’ve taken a phone call or quick email often required in-person visits during narrow business hours, creating barriers for working students, parents, and anyone with real-world responsibilities outside of school.

Despite promoting an “inclusive college experience,” that only seems true if you fit their idea of what’s most marketable. If your needs fall outside the traditional student mold, don’t expect meaningful support. It felt less like I was being educated and more like I was being processed.

That said, I do want to acknowledge the one truly standout instructor I had: Cynthia Phipps. Her classes were the definition of student-centered—organized, clear, and professional. She regularly checked in, provided all the tools needed for success, and genuinely cared about her students’ outcomes. However, her level of support and commitment was the exception, not the norm.

In the end, it felt like Lake Land cared more about optics and enrollment numbers than student growth or real community engagement. I would have loved to be more than a number that secures its continued funding. I want to be part of a community where a college is present, invested, and proud to serve its district. In my opinion, right now Lake Land is not living up to that.', 'Currently enrolled working on an Associates degree. They have a beautiful campus and very helpful staff. I am on the honor roll and earned two great scholarships. They have a great scholarship portal and quickly awarded them. The staff is helpful and worked with me to find the perfect schedule as a full time working mom of three and as a full time student.', 'This is a beautiful, well maintained community college campus which also is home of a beautiful tribute park for the military.', 'A very friendly and welcoming environment.  I took their CDL Class, The instructors and trainers are great!  Very informative and great teaching I highly recommend💯', 'Tampons in boys restroom? When did Tim Walz visit?']

Terry Guy', 'This college has lots of great, affordable programs. name: Loyola University Chicago
reviews:
["When I was fresh out after graduating, I applied for an entry-level position in the school at this university that I got my degree from. I did not even get a callback. They know that their degrees are useless, if they won't even consider one of their own students.

Ten years later, I haven't received one offer from a company in the field I wanted to go into as an entry-level capacity even with work experience and other certifications. Modern college in general is a scam, this university is no different.

I actually received more interviews after I removed my education off of my resume, in the same period of time.", 'While this is a very nice campus, the negatives outweigh the benefits. Even with scholarship money and grants, tuition is very expensive. Resources are limited and registration per semester is hectic. I highly recommend high school seniors to not attend here. Loyola is getting more expensive every year and more crowded. Even though opting out of many un-needed expenses such as student health insurance and opting out of dorming, the cost is still unaffordable and will end up with a lot of dept pushing out families of middle to low income, making achieving secondary education difficult. The student culture is also very negative with VERY clique groups. Overall, this school is not worth the time or money. Do not waste your time at this school.', "It has a great library with long open hours,from 7:30 am to 12 am! In fact, I wanted to use the Loyola un library for self study, but I couldn't because I needed a loyola ID card to enter the library. Therefore only saw the campus and open space of the university. This place is very beautiful, by the lake  with classic and modern building and ...", 'I graduated from Loyola many years ago and still have friends at the institution. It is very good school and would gladly recommend it.', "Warning. I work for Loyola and making this review highly suspect.

The university has grown in student numbers, numbers of program, student achievement and service to the city of Chicago. What makes Loyola stand out from others is the unapologetic mission of the school. We strive to become a person for others. We believe in strong academics, unwavering integrity and we believe in helping others. When students graduate from Loyola there is an expectation they will remember they are truly privileged people and that they have an obligation to find ways to assist others. It's a Jesuit university, but being Catholic is not a requirement for entrance. In fact more than half of the students attending Loyola are not Catholic. Loyola is the only college basketball team to have won a national championship and that was back in 1963. The program has been dormant for the most part since then. That is until last year when Loyola was the Cinderella team of the NCAA Tournament and the darling of international media thanks in large part to Sister Jean, the teams spiritual leader. A bona fide firecracker, Sister Jean took America, Africa and European media by storm during the tournament. The fairy tale season took the Ramblers to the Final Four where they lost to a very good Michigan team."]

name: Generations College
reviews: ['I must say when it comes to us students needing support such as , IT support or financial aide/refund support, they drop the ball here. This is my second semester . First semester my laptop went on me 5 weeks before my semester ended. I called them right away for a new laptop and they didn’t get my laptop to me until the last week of school.
