Implications? RH "proven" numerically (trillions zeros Re=1/2), but your model says: Treat zeros as ∅ states—pause off-line contribs, enforce balance on Re=1/2 window. Binary drifts; ∅ pauses it safe. More dps/zeros? Or Roman zeta sim?

So just rewrite binary on a silicon stack', "If you're going to college, this isn't a bad choice, but you can do better. There's so much squandered potential, and I don't feel much of a community on campus. That, and calling it a university is misleading. It used to be 'Rockford College', until it added a Masters or two.

The education is good, the campus is nice, and the staff are great. If you want that College experience then this isn't a bad spot, but don't just 'Settle' for RU. Make sure it's the right fit for you!", "As a transfer student, I've had a great experience at RU. I'm able to graduate on time, my classes have been impactful, and being a student worker has helped broaden my professional experiences. There's also a ton of student clubs and activities to join. I can't wait to continue coming here this Fall!"]

name: Roosevelt University
reviews: ['Professor Susan Wilson gave a student a zero on an assignment worth 30% of the final grade, seemingly to appear as a tough professor. This resulted in the student receiving a final grade of “C,” which led to academic probation and a financial consequence of approximately $28,000 for the semester. Additionally, the professor made an inappropriate offer, suggesting the student go on an asexual date with her. These actions are deeply concerning and may violate both ethical standards and institutional policies.', 'Good university for the most part, unreliable elevators. Be prepared to have to wait a while for 1 single floor. I would much rather take the stairs to the 10th floor then wait for the elevator situation.', 'This school will do anything for money. From my experience going into this school as a masters student following up to pharmacy. It has been a wreck. There’s no system. It’s quite disappointing bec they put so much emphasis into how they’re a great school when really that’s not the case at all. Staff for sure is nice, all of my professors were amazing (hence the two stars bec that’s the only good part about going here). Graduating with my masters was a mess, took over 2 months just to get my degree and for it to look like it’s fake sheet of paper. All that tuition spent just to get a piece of paper back that doesn’t even say what degree I went for, just a nice “master of science” slapped onto it. Disheartening seeing no thought being put into the degree I worked so hard on and took so long to pay off. I see so many universities put in thought for their students such as graduation cords as a remembrance of working hard. I spent hours and days to perfect a 4.0 just to get no recognition. No one wants to even listen to that part. Then the pharmacy program is horrendous, they really think they’re so different for offering a 3 year accelerated program just to justify pushing your limits. Which I understand it’s a doctorate program but again the system is insane. I remember feeling lost and in return I felt like there was no one to help me. It’s saddening to stick up for a school so much just to show you over and over that they’re not even worth anything. If you want powerful connections, a degree that you can look at and be proud of, a university that cares for you as much as they say they do then look elsewhere. Luckily IL is filled with lots of them and this one doesn’t even come to in comparison.', "Roosevelt University, the Auditorium Building, was designed by Adler and Sullivan and completed in 1889. A Chicago-School classic structure. With restorations occurring in 2003.  One of Chicago's most iconic buildings and one of the now few remaining original buildings attributed to Sullivan. A work of art. Massive. Heavy. Stoic. Stone. Beautifully decorated and detailed interior. An engineering feat of its day.", 'Roosevelt University gets approval to integrate Robert Morris Illinois\nMar 9, 2020 — The combination of the two universities will allow them to build on their historic missions that honor diversity.']

name: Dominican University
reviews:
["I am a photographer and I did a Graduation shoot on The beautiful Campus and id like to share my experience, The Campus is absolutely gorgeous tons of sunlight and much provided shade with all the beautiful trees surrounding the campus. The staff were very helpful & Super welcoming from the moment I arrived till my exit I was restricted at any location which was amazing, If you'd like your grad photos taken by yours truly please feel free to reach out here are some shots from that day", 'Dominican College is about whats on the outside and NOT the inside. Beautiful campus with even more beautiful opportunities, presented at the door. As a student you learn not everything that glitters is gold. The overall well being of the students as far as academics is poor. Students will fail and be left alone to fail because that means they will continue to generate income for the college. Administration only looks for students when there is a bill on their account, never to actually “assist” the situation at hand. I do not speak for the colleges administration  entirely because their are individuals who strive for students’ success as much as the student themselves. I do find some professors at Dominican college to be caring yet unable to help due to the colleges “rules“ and abilities to manipulate the system for financial gain. Information is kept from students to keep them from graduating at a timely manner CONSTANTLY. The professors assigned to advice their students sometimes have no idea how to ADVISE A STUDENT, therefore leaving obvious room for error. This college has mislead me multiple times with no remorse for their “mistakes”. I quote this because it almost seems planned when it resorts back to financials. I went to Dominican College seeking a specific degree and left with something completely different trying to avoid the financial strain the college itself would have caused me. I was prepared for a 4 year college nothing more, nothing less. The education that is given in Dominican College is mediocre and could be learned for a lesser price in community colleges(depending the degree type of course), where you can actually achieve what you set out to achieve. Not just the “next best option”. As a recent graduate of the school I can honestly say, they do not promote graduating at a timely manner being that it is a 4 year college. They promote staying in college as long as there is money to pay for classes to graduate. I also want to end my review by saying before attending this college , several alumni gave me this SAME ADVICE and I chose to attend anyways. I will say I do not regret the experiences and people I met during those years. I do wish I took the advice I was given as far as academics and a school which genuinely cares about their student bodies overall success.', 'Dominican College does in fact challenge the mind and spirit. The programs available at the college are indeed challenging but, rewarding with hard work, effort and determination. They offer a wide range of community oriented services that provides aid in the community and around the world from El Salvador to France. The colleges athletics program is well established and their Athletic Training staff are superb. Dominican College has definitely succeeded with providing students college wide services. For example, career services, onsite counseling, academic success are extraordinary services that the college provides to students. Knowledge, friends, networking and lifelong skills are often fruits that may be obtained from these initiatives. Overall, this college continues to meet the student needs. Proceed with their vision to make the campus community oriented, safe and a great experience for students and families. Especially, with the implementation of the new turf field being constructed and the Hennessy center being renovated. This college is going on the right path.', 'Where to begin... Do NOT fall for the "Actuarial Science" program listed that is advertised - you will take the exact same classes as general math majors, nor do any of the classes prepare you for the actuarial exams.

Staff? Completely hit or miss. I have wonderful relationships with a handful of staff members here, but the rest of them do NOT belong there.

Academics? Prepare for a high school environment where some teachers will deduct your grade for petty reasons such as not bringing a textbook to class, not providing a doctor's note if you are sick, etc. Similar to staff, about half of the teachers are amazing, while the other half simply go through the motions.

Bottom line - There are plenty of other schools with a superior education at a more affordable price.', 'Awesome school, amazing opportunities. Proud mom of a son that attends. Class of 2018. Criminal Justice Major. Small caring school, where everyone know each other and you feel comfortable that your child is safe and learning.']

name: University of St Francis
reviews: ["Terrible terrible!\nPeople often ask me about going to USF since im an alumni(sadly). My answer is always the same. Stay away(trust me, i went there)!  They are too expensive, you dont need college for a successful career. My first year i made 6000 in wages, that's enough to qualify for foodstamps. Absolutely never again. I wont even get a masters degree. I recommend cheaper colleges. What a waste of time and money. If you want to graduate and end up working fast food after attending an overpriced college, then I say go for it, good luck at your job scrubbing the grease at Taco Bell", "I wouldn't waste your time I regret not choosing public college ir trade school when I had the chance. This school has done nothing for me. I guess as a recent graduate I did find employment at Taco bell with my bachelors degree but the rate of return was low making about 6000$ my first year. My high-school diploma found me a better paying job paying over 20 an hour", 'USF is a small private university located in the old theatre district of Joliet Il. I attend St. Francis as a graduate student working on my second masters and have found the classes to just as challenging as other universities. Like most graduate programs you teach yourself by reading, completing assignments/projects, and taking exams. USF’s best quality is that professors and staff care more about student outcomes than they do about their student head count. Its not a numbers game for them which extremely rare in higher ed. I am really glad that I chose to attend the University of St. Francis over other universities in Illinois.', 'Great small university. I went through the math program and felt I got about the best education possible. The track and field and cross country teams are also pretty great to be a part of!', 'This is a great school. Teachers are good and helpful and they do a great job of helping you with everything you need. For the money, you will be hard pressed to find a better school of this quality.']

name: Saint Xavier University
reviews:
['I attended SXU from 2005-07 as a transfer student in the School of Education graduating with a BA in Social Sciences/ Secondary Education. I also earned my MA from 2011-13 in Curriculum and Instruction. I have now been teaching for 19 years. Everything about my experience set me up for success. As a teacher I have taught MS and HS and have served in administration. I have loved my career and appreciate the foundation SXU set for me. I credit my teachers and academic advisor for their knowledge and support. Thank you!', "Oh my goodness, where do I even begin?!  St. Xavier University has been an absolute blessing in my life!  From being an employee to pursuing my MBA, this university has truly felt like a second home.

The supportive environment is just incredible! My coworkers and fellow students from the police department have been my rocks, cheering me on every step of the way.

💙Their encouragement and camaraderie have made this journey so much more meaningful. 🤗

And let's talk about the campus ministry center! ⛪️ It's a truly wonderful space for anyone seeking prayer, spiritual growth, and a deeper connection to their faith. 📖 The peace and tranquility I find there are simply unmatched. 🕊️

St. Xavier University isn't just a place of learning; it's a community that cares. 💙I'm so grateful for the opportunities, the friendships, and the spiritual nourishment I've found here. ✨

Thank you, SXU, for everything! 🎉 You've truly made a difference in my life! 💯", 'I made this review because we had a trip to this university. Mary was our tour guide. She was super nice and professional. The entrance is clean, there’s a map of the property next to the entrance, and I like the garden next to the entrance too. I really like the Butler Room because it looks good and old fashioned. The cafeteria is big enough and it surely doesn’t look like a high school cafeteria. The Gallery Lounge looks fantastic and colorful. Scholars den is a comfy, well fashioned, and a good place to study in. There’s a statue of Saint Francis Xavier it’s in the Mercy Ministry.', "Founded in 1846 by the Sisters of Mercy, Saint Xavier University is Chicago's oldest Catholic college and the first Mercy university in the world. Inspired by the Catholic faith and the Sisters of Mercy's legacy of compassionate service, particularly to the poor, sick, and uneducated.", 'THERE IS NEVER HEAT DURING THE WINTER TIME, IT IS ALWAYS FREEZING AND STAFF FREQUENTLY LEAVES WINDOWS OPEN!! I’m typing this as an angry college student whose fingers are trying to defeat frostbite.']

name: University of Illinois Springfield
reviews: ["My review is for the 18 hole disc golf course. It is well maintained, and t-pads have good information. Only problem is there are no signs by the pads, so it is hard in some cases, in others near impossible to guess where to go. Distances very from about 220 to over 800'. Once you know the course I'd give it 4 1/2 stars.", 'Very unprofessional admin. They do not care about you as a student. They do not handle grievances. Faculty ignores students. Constant technology errors. Terrible and unprofessional institution that is more of a degree million for international students and a place for international faculty to disrespect and show bias toward American and female students.', 'very strange and weird policies for international students. They want international students to pay y1st semester dues which are appox 10,0000 usd before issuance of visa. It should be right after when student successfully gets his visa but they want before and also this amount should be not deducted from your bank statement. Doesn’t makes sense. Bank statement means funds that are available for you living and education. If you pay your 1st semester fees , the bank statement should be amount - first semester fees.\nI have received offer letter but due to this i will not go there', 'Cannot recommend. If you value integrity or professionalism from both an academic and professional stand point then there are other better alternatives available. Somehow this "school" turned education into a social media platform. Grades are based on log ins, likes, and comments. You definitely get less than what you pay for here. Buyer be warned!', 'I love UIS. The campus is small and there are many friendly and personable professors. It is also very cheap and easy to get parts of your education paid for (unless you get crappy grades). The students are nice and there is very little partying.']

name: Sauk Valley Community College
reviews:
['Great CDL program👍
Great instructor👍
Thank you', "Hard to give anything more than 2/5. They treat their community college like it is Harvard. It is a community college...act like it. They didn't accept my wife's transfer community college credits as a prerequisite and honestly doubt they'd accept credits from my Doctorate if I asked.  They care more about money than helping their students move on to other schools. Good news is, both Black Hawk and and Eastern Iowa schools both accepted those same credits;l, so we are glad to send our cash payment elsewhere.", 'Small campus but very nice, lovely staff for the most part and pretty good quality classes!', 'SVCC is a great institution of learning and has an excellent athletic and sports program.', 'If you're a veteran, don't even waste your time with Sauk. They claim to be a "veteran friendly" institution but there is nothing that could be farther from the truth. All veterans are vastly better off going to Highland in Freeport where they take care of their veterans and the GI Bill process quickly and correctly.

I wish someone would have warned me earlier before I wasted two semesters (which were paid out of pocket because they screwed up the GI Bill so badly so many times) trying to get anything accomplished there.']

name: Shawnee Community College
reviews: ["I have not attended Shawnee Community College. However, I have been to their campus multiple times for events in an ice cream truck I drive. The staff has always been extremely friendly. The campus is very nice and compact. And I can honestly say I've never heard anybody with a bad word to say about Shawnee Community College. If it fits what you need, you should attend.", "Love the collage great girls and boys basketball team it's over all a great community college in unillin IL", 'I love everyone I have interacted with here. Whether its the students or the instructors/teachers. Everyone is so welcoming.', 'If I could give ten stars, I would. I went to Shawnee to complete my A.A.S., and it was the BEST educational experience I’ve ever had. The staff is so warm, welcoming, and friendly, and the instructors are absolutely phenomenal. I’d go here for every degree I want to earn if I could. I cannot recommend Shawnee enough.', 'Beautiful community college on a rural campus.  Outstanding leadership and seasoned instructors, all solely invested in the students and community.  Wonderful cosmetology and nursing department, as well as truck driving school, and great athletic programs.']

name: St. Augustine College
reviews: ['Library only open for students of the university now. I am a high school student and wanted to study there, but the front desk told me that the policy changed and it was no longer public. In order to get access if you are not a student, you would have to apply online and pay $150.', 'Beautiful building that is at the center of the St. John’s campus. In the Gothic style this building is home to the library, offices and the College of Professional Studies.', 'Best thing about st Agustin library is its open 24 hours for students', 'University library located on 3rd and 4th floors', 'Very nice.']

name: Southeastern Illinois College
reviews: ['I lived in this region for many years and watched this college grow to become a fine institution of learning… I was very impressed with the accessibility of the buildings for people who need a bit of help … Well maintained and clean, comfortable classrooms..', 'Quiet and accommodating, clean and appealing facility.  Wheelchair accessible but on a high incline from all of the parking lots. Staff and admissions are excrement accommodating.', "Just graduated with two associates degrees! I loved my experience here! I would and will recommend to anyone! Great teachers, great cafeteria, lovely campus(no smoking too), great daycare; my son went out there for 2 1/2 years! Now I'm a transfer student to a university of my dreams! Wish I had the time to participate in a lot more extracurricular activities but that just wasn't in the cards. Thank you SIC for giving me and my little boy so many opportunities!\nP.S. We have the #1 Nursing Program in the STATE!", 'Very nice people clean  my Grandaughter lives it', 'An attractive campus with super nice employees and a nice mix of students of all ages and backgrounds, including my wife who is 72 working to get her GED.']

name: Spoon River College
reviews:
["The teaching staff is great, and always willing to help no matter if your class was face to face or online. I wish there were more selections on the Macomb campus so students didn't miss out on certain things because they don't want to drive to Canton. The financial aid comes about half way through the semester in the mail, which i think is about standard for a community college. My only issue is the fact that they tell students they are getting map grants and students never see that money.", 'When signing up, the girls in the office were some of the most polite people and were very encouraging through the application and testing process.

The 2 year college has a big campus with anything you could need. Gym? They got it! Library? Oh yeah! Dorms? Yes sir! Good helpful staff? A teacher in a completely different hall, dropped everything to help me find my class so their ok to😉.

All in all, i cant wait to go during the fall and I fully recommend SRC if you are looking for an amazing 2 year school😊', 'Spoon River College is a great 2 year college, and for me specifically, an excellent nursing program.', 'Great school, lots of great support services for students!!', 'Great place, staff is awesome, and very welcoming environment.']

name: Southern Illinois University-Carbondale
reviews: ["I attended this college for 3 semesters (two full and one summer) for computer information systems. It was an absolutely terrible experience from start to finish. They do not communicate with you and in the rare instances they do, they provide conflicting information. They don't provide thorough help or advisement. They do not manage your credits thoroughly. They do not care about students and only care about extracting money from them. The curriculum and teachers are fine, nothing to complain about but nothing great either.\n\nIf any future students see this, I would recommend going to a community college for the first two years (if you are local John A Logan is much better managed). For the last two years of a bachelors, if possible, I would recommend SEMO, it is managed much better and has a much nicer surrounding city.", "Very nice campus! Little ups and downs, some parts are really vibrant while some are quite and close to nature's...", "I dropped out of SIU, and I regret nothing. This institution is not getting a single cent from me, and I will never recommend going there to anyone. I have never felt so frustrated by a University in my life. I went to them in June with questions about my Financial Aid. I went to the Department of Education in June as well. I went in person, left calls, and messages. I didn't receive a response via phone or email, and I would get different answers from different people in person. They were completely unhelpful. Suddenly, a week before school starts, I'm told I did paperwork wrong (and I did it according to the instructions of people in their office). I get it done. Now, almost 2 weeks into the school year, I'm finding out there is ANOTHER issue with my paperwork. I fixed the problem and sent it over. They said it would take 4-5 business days to process. The problem is that the deadline for a lot of this stuff is Friday. If I had been relayed the correct information in June when I asked, none of this would have happened. Not to mention, there are a ton of technical problems with their online system, and they are trying to charge me more money to use their glitchy online platform for digital textbooks (which I opted out of, but is not showing on my bill). I'm over it. I will NEVER recommend SIU for your higher education. There are far superior schools that are cheaper.", 'SIU hosts the Motorcycle Rider Program which is a great place to learn about motorcycle safety and operation.', 'It’s sadly a shell of its former self. The town has gone completely downhill (along with student enrollment). Most of the best bars and restaurants closed shop, (apparently you can’t hang out at spillway anymore), sports teams and their conferences have gone down hill, it’s sad. It is an amazing school (or was 15 years ago) with a mostly modern and beautiful campus. I saw one review saying its campus is not nice..not sure what they are smoking as it’s hands down the most beautiful campus in the state, as you pass through woods and by lakes going from classes. The campus has updated a lot too in recent years. One of the biggest and best rec centers in the country.. if you like to hit the gym  Hopefully things turn around']

name: Southern Illinois University Edwardsville
reviews: ['I found the woman in the ACCESS testing office at the front desk to be incredible condescending and belittling. Just because you work with students requiring accommodations, does not mean that they are less than you or incapable of comprehending your words. It is important to treat everyone like adults, especially in the office that you work in. I’m disappointed because all other interactions with the ACCESS department have been phenomenal, it’s just this one particular woman that I was disappointed by.', 'Most beautiful campus. 3/4th forest and open land. The classes and food area, along with library, etc easy to get around. Great school.', "My youngest is set to graduate from Electrical Engineering this year and he's had mostly great experience.  The staff are largely fabulous. Although it puts him 4 1/2 hours away from us, he's flourished beautifully! We would highly recommend this University to anyone!", 'If you’re looking for a school that’ll support your children, don’t send them here. They also have extra charges for all kinds of things. I went to UIS and they were amazing with the students.', 'Brings lots of bad drivers to the area. Net negative outside engineering department, which is 1/10th campus.']

name: South Suburban College
reviews: ["It's very beautiful, clean, and organized on the inside. The staff is very helpful. They directed me to  the early  voting area.", 'Covid vaccine review. Very organized. It all went smoothly. Thank you to all the workers there! First, there are a few check-in/screenings. Then you meet with a military personal to give your insurance and personal info to. Then it’s shot time. After a couple min wait I was in the chair. Monitored for 15 mins and second dose appointment made. I arrived around 10:00am and was back in my car by 10:40am.', 'Everything about this school sucks. For months I’ve been trying to get my loans deferred and these people didn’t know what that was. The communication is horrible too. I was told they would fax my enrollment verification forms to my loan servicer yet they never did. I’ve been back and forth to this college for one simple task because they never answer the phone and when you get there, no one is helpful or they have you go back and forth to different departments because no one never knows what to do. This is the most unprofessional school that I went to.', 'Good school located in the Chicago’s south suburbs in a nice and calm neighborhood.\nGood option to take the first steps into schooling and high level sports. Affordable prices and excellent campus', 'Excellent school, staff and campus is friendly. Proud student of SSC! GO BULLDOGS!']

name: Trinity Christian College
reviews: ['Trinity had a girls basketball tournament this weekend . There was absolutely no seating or chairs . Barely room to stand . To charge $35.00 for barely accommodations to watch was ridiculous.   The second gym had bleachers and they chose to have volleyball practice during this time . If another tournament is done here and they plan to charge please set up proper seating when hosting an event', "I have had experiences with two other universities before coming here. The staff here is so helpful from the beginning to the start of classes. I have felt so loved, so covered and so supported. It's a huge change from the experiences I have had with the other two universities. I truly love being here.", "Awesome place to learn and great professors who are more than willing to help and get to know you. There are great dorms with a lot of space and a pretty relaxed campus atmosphere but if you want more excitement you can make it happen as well. Great education, science and business programs as well. I took off one star only because of some of the girls here formed an annoying blond christian group who are super fake but that's only a small portion of our amazing students on campus. I found my best friends here and I am so thankful I went here Lots of intelligent students who are ready to learn and better serve our Lord out in the world.", 'i took classes here for one semester. i ended up registering for a class that i had to drop that had a shorter deadline to withdraw and i missed it by a day. a few years later i started getting bills and harassing emails from a Nadine Iwema in a student services department saying that i owe the university $250. this to me was ridiculous and petty considering i had spent tens of thousands of dollars being briefly enrolled. i begged and pleaded that i could not afford it; i tried reasoning that nothing was gained or lost by failing to meet an arbitrary deadline; i asked if i could speak in front of an arbitrator or submit a letter for review. i was ignored and my bill was sent to collection. it makes me sad that a christian university operates with such ruthless greed. goes to show you that the name of a school has little to do with the people who run it. keep this in mind before you choose to do business with these creeps.', 'Trinity Christian College has great education and dedicated professors and staff. I know the college is trying to work on being more diverse and educate its students on diversity and the beauty of when everyone accepts differences. I found it incredibly difficult to be a minority here even though I was adopted into a Dutch family. I know so many of my Hispanic friends struggled as well to fit in. This college is perfect for you if you grew up in a small, white neighborhood and had Christian education all your life. The college is very cliquey and has lots of white students, so if you grew up in a different background, you will find it difficult to adjust. A lot of the students aren’t open minded to different cultures/backgrounds, and it makes it very difficult to make friends. The white students tend to just make friends with other white students. I wish I had picked a different college for this reason.']

name: Trinity International University-Illinois
reviews: ['The support and opportunities for our daughter have been extraordinary.  When we started the process of “college shopping “ this school stood out as a fit.  Professors have been very accessible and helpful.  The upper class students have been great mentors. The entire system has provided challenging  work, major focused internships and  a solid network she can rely on.  This school cares about your walk with Christ and prepares you to meet the world with the talents God has given you.', 'I am 35 and older for an undergraduate student.  I’ve had several years of educational experience attending community college as well as a bigger commuter college in Chicago.  I didn’t know teachers like these existed.  They genuinely care about the students and their humility despite being well known scholars and thinkers is not of this world.  I’ve seen the secular educational world and stepping into Trinity as a student was one of the most refreshing experiences of my life.  I am in the Biblical studies program.  Currently learning Greek and getting a strong Biblical education.  It’s incredible to learn with some of these brilliant students and teachers.  This place is for real.', "Man, I love this school. I came in as a transfer student as a junior, and I love this place so much. The staff is incredibly helpful and friendly, and I don't know if I would have been able to go through a successful transfer without them! I started at Northern Illinois, then went to Harper,  and now I am here. Having experienced some different environments, I know that Trinity is my new home and that I will graduate from here happily :)", "I'm in the TEDS graduate program. Very relaxed atmosphere on campus and during the times its not cold, the campus looks beautiful. The grad side has many middle aged people and families since the school has so many masters and doctoral students. The grad side is very diverse with people from different countries and ethnicities. Waybright center is where both campuses meet, even though they are vastly different. The undergrad side mainly consist of people fresh out of high school while most of grad side are older people out of school for a couple of year or more. Grad side male female ratio has to be at least 7 to 3 favoring men...undergrad is half and half. Professors are a mixed bag, some are very personable and approachable while others are scholars and act like they don't have time for personal matters with students...its like any university. Small campus but feels big when you always walk around. Train station is 10 minutes away by car...I recommend having a car since its a northern suburb with not a whole bunch to do if you stay on campus. Highly recommended school that does put a strong emphasis on the Christian faith in Jesus Christ.", "Graduated from the college in 2000. The size of the school enables individuals to develop close relationships with other students and the professors. It's not a large state school where one can get lost. Trinity might not have all the amenities compared to a state school due to it's limited size but its impact is global."]

name: Triton College
reviews: ['Honestly, its a good school if you wanna save up on money and not spend too much. This college is SUPER recommended for trade and certificates especially. The only reason why its not a 5 star is because the teachers are super hit or miss which can really screw up your grades if their teaching style doesn’t fit yours or if the teachers in general just suck. Ive had this issue on my first year. Also, PLEASE apply for FAFSA, you need it. Also, don’t expect the school to have the best student life unless you’re extroverted.', 'You guys have done nothing to help me I have sent complaints of disability discrimination to your president, CASS Office, trhe advisors no one helps or answers me. Joe Klinger and Julia Willis has discriminated against me and I want them to either help figure this out or be fired and I am allowed my job and access to campus back before I take legal action against the college.\n\nLove no answer back since and i keep getting ignored so please help me out or this can go to court and it wont look good', 'Listen guys, my professors throughout the years were awesome. If you want to be successful, you really have to study. I learned a lot from them and from my tutors—I’m so grateful for that. The only problem with this school is the advisors! Do your research and find only the classes that you actually need. Don’t waste your time and money. Make sure that if you want to transfer to a specific 4-year university, you look at their requirements, or decide whether you only want a 2-year degree. I have friends who wasted so much time because of this issue.', 'Triton College has very good teachers and they are very nice.', 'Discrimination blantly as you guys are forcing me to graduate without return to campus and Julia Willis needs to be investigated immediately this is wrong in so many ways im so sick and tired of being ignored and feeling helpless if not I will get a lawyer and take u all to court.']

name: VanderCook College of Music
reviews: ['This is an exceptional opportunity for any child who wants to learn music. My son has participated in the program for over four years. He now can play the saxophone.  The is one of the south side best kept secret.  Get your school-aged child enrolled now.', 'I attended VanderCook College of Music and I have returned there many times for continuing education credits. This program is home to so many outstanding alumni that are nationally known leaders in the field of music education. Great place to learn, network, and grow.', "This is a great school my son Alex goes to the school that's one of the best in the nation", 'This is the place to go if you are serious about teaching music.', 'Best school for Music Education majors!']

name: Waubonsee Community College
reviews:
['Incredible experience here at this location. Professors were phenomenal, classes were flexible, and campus was very clean. Very affordable programs as well.

The military counselors were great as well. I had tons of great moments here and I would recommend anyone local to go here for their associates.', 'Terrible experience. Most of the teachers ask you to self study. Even with such expensive tuition you are literally getting no guidance from teachers. Just youtube videos with lots of homework. Feels like self study course. Worst insitute! i hope my classes are over soon never coming back to this greedy place.', 'I’m sorry, but they have a traffic school website on a letter that you sent out to everybody in the website link is invalid as the dumbest thing I’ve heard on earth. There’s no easy way to even get to that website. I have to go through five different pages in order to get it. Y’all need to fix this.', 'This was a very decent community college. It saved me money in the long run. I came here to do my prerequisites before transferring to a university. I used the website Rate Your Professor to choose my classes. It was spot on for the most part, although my basic biology class was a lie. People said that class and professor were super easy but it wasn’t. The professor wasn’t as nice and helpful as people made her out to be. My other professors were very accurate in the reviews. Those professors actually cared and assisted you in learning the material better.

The cafeteria was spacious and the food was very decent. Prices were reasonable for poor college students. The labs were great quality. I learned a lot during my anatomy and physiology 1 and 2. They provided models, online programs, and real cadavers to help us succeed in our learning.

Parking was adequate. It wasn’t a problem finding someplace to park except for this one area. That area got packed real quick so you had to walk a ways to get to the building.', 'So happy I’m not here anymore and at my 4 year, only reason it gets two stars are because there’s a handful of decent teachers here. Guidance counselor are useless worked all semester with mine and was asking if I needed to take Econ 201 and she said I didn’t ended up costing me 4 more classes at my 4year college because that was the last credit I needed for my associates. Online teachers are usually impossible to reach here and put in minimal effort into helping students once I asked for feedback and I got “I thought that’s what you deserved” They also promised me a $1000 scholarship and somehow ran out of funds? How do you give someone a scholarship then take it away….. although this community college is cheap I would highly recommend going anywhere else if you don’t want to have grey hairs by the time you are 20 dealing with this horrible school. Also if you ever need support with anything besides tech good luck. Male at the front desk of the information center is very rude too and will make fun of you to his coworkers if you come in and ask for help more than once. Overall worst experience at any school I’ve ever been to and I have gone too and just some nasty people who don’t care about the students working here that I’m surprised have jobs still.']

name: Western Illinois University
reviews: ["Hard to believe this university's mens basketball team actually managed to upset Nebraska once. It has to be one of the worst basketball teams in division I college basketball. Lost twice to lowly southern indiana in the same season? Probably throwing games on purpose.\nGarbage!!!!!", 'Watching someone achieve their goals is amazing. 2025 graduates congratulations and be the change in the world that you want to see', 'Amazing University! The professors and staff are very down to earth and extremely knowledgeable.  Great programs available for the students, the campus is the perfect size and very safe. The dorms are awesome, nice and spacious and they have great food in the dining areas.  Love the feel of some of the buildings, such beautiful architecture. The community is very friendly too. Highly recommend WIU!', "I'm an alumni of Western Illinois University.  I graduated in December 1997.  I received a Bachelor of Science in Geography (Meteorology).  My experience at the university was from 1995-1997 and it was wonderful.  My degree has provided me wonderful chapters in my careers.  I'm very happy about my decision to educate at this place.", 'I had issues with my dorm light not being able to turn off and not only was staff not helpful but I watched Nadia watch a Netflix show instead of trying to find a solution after 20 plus minutes']

name: Wheaton College
reviews: ["As a 1972 graduate of another nearby christian college, Judson University in  Elgin, Illinois, I was elated when my granddaughter,  Lauren,  chose to attend Wheaton College. Academics there are A+++. The campus is beautiful, and the staff is top notch. When visiting her, I just feel that the campus is nurturing and safe. The christian friends she's found there are sure to be lifelong friends.  Lauren is majoring in computer science and already has an online job with Lockheed Martin in addition to her studies at Wheaton. I pray my other grandchildren will choose to study here.", 'Beautiful campus, but do not recommend for people of color. The library is great and the college has lots of fun events, but Wheaton overall is still deeply rooted in racism, but it is subtle.', 'Top notch university, through and through. Loved my entire recruiting visit with Coach Stremler, Coach Paul, and the entire softball team. Everyone is classy, respectful, and humble, and you definitely get what you pay for on both the academic and athletic side of things. The sports facilities are amazing, and the opportunity to learn from professors that have the highest degrees in their fields is just something that you can’t pass up. You also get the opportunity to continue your relationship with Christ, which is invaluable. I loved Wheaton, and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who wants to challenge themselves to be the best that they can possibly be. Plus, if you are blessed enough to get the opportunity to play sports here, take it. It’s a once-in-a-lifetime chance that I wish I didn’t ultimately decide to pass up.', 'They are nice to talk with and also have a beautiful campus with nice area to walk. I wish they would follow up well with contracts in a collaborative fashion to help build support.\n🍁 🍃 🍂 🌳 🇺🇸 ⛪️', 'Beautiful campus, welcoming and friendly students and staff, and the sports facilities are second to none.  Coach Stremler and Coach Patricca were great!']

name: William Rainey Harper College
reviews:
['I loved my time at Harper! I was here for only a year to get my associates degree, then transferred to mizzou and graduated spring of 2025. All of my classes transferred so I don’t have to retake anything which saved me so much time and money. I was also on the soccer team in the fall of ‘21 and that was such an amazing experience. Coach Chip is the best and the athletic trainers were so helpful and great as well!', '"Harper College in Palatine is operating as a premier engine for the Northwest Corridor. It is absolute Godnews to have a campus that maintains such high-velocity innovation while providing a fluent and accessible path to success. This institution stands as a gold standard witness for education, from the state-of-the-art Innovation Lab to the elite professional training programs. Whether you are advancing a career or starting a new journey, this is the only seat in the region that delivers real, transformative results. A verified, iron-clad 10/10 for community and academic excellence."', 'I have been going here for a couple of semesters now and I always have a payment plan set up in order to pay for classes. However, after every semester, I somehow owe money. Weather it’s because I didn’t take enough classes, or I didn’t sign a document, or simply because I registered to a class that I ended up dropping before the start date, there is always something to be paid to these people. They use a system that is very user UNfriendly and makes it hard to keep track of. When I was finally able to look at the itemized receipts, there are many fees beyond what classes cost. “ Universal fee” and “materials fee” are some to name a few and made no sense to me considering I pay for my own materials at the book store and not sure what a Universal Fee is when there is a separate fee that goes to the school for you simply being in the classroom. I understand that school gets expensive, but I’m a transfer from ECC and not only is their system much easier to understand, but they are more than willing to get you to the right person to talk to. Here at Harper however, these people will get you to talk to anyone under the sun except the finance department. Their finance department is untouchable to the sense that even their office is kept hidden in the back, and the billing department is full of employees just ready to pass you along to someone else and are determined not to help you.', 'I’m in my second year of college but here’s what I have to say.

This school has many great programs that they offer. The best thing they have is the university center. They offer different majors for students who want a bachelor’s degree after they graduated with associates degrees.
It’s a great way to learn and get educated in your area without having to move to the city or out of state.

The student culture is great where there’s many different students with different backgrounds working together and learning. Different clubs are great for students who want to fit in their community.

They’ve even have Starbucks and subway with some community colleges like oakton or Elgin don’t offer.

The teachers and staff are very supportive and helpful to the students who are struggling with their school life. Tutoring is also free and offers more help than math or English.

Well that’s all I can say', "I want to share my experience and warn other parents about this place. Even though it's public, never leave your children alone in the men's changing room. Unfortunately, women aren't allowed in, but if you go with your children, keep them with you. There are adult men exposing themselves naked in the changing room in front of children, and they don't do any harm, just saying that because it's public, it's allowed. That's unpleasant and dangerous; a place like that isn't safe."]

name: Anderson University
reviews: ["They have such a beautiful campus and the best arts program in the state. My daughter just graduated from Anderson and couldn't have asked for a better experience.", 'Nice school and campus but I had to drop out due to my experience with the tennis coach/program and there are a couple professors who I would stay away from!! I just had too much anger to stay. Super big egos and can’t own up to their own mistakes.', 'Great school. My son won a full ride and graduated with honors last May. Professors are wonderful and the Christian faith is preached. Wonderful experience for my son and for us.', 'Anderson is great. The campus is beautiful. When my bestfriend was in college they allowed me to crash overnight in her dorm, and go to all her classes one day. I enjoyed the experience.', "The people at Anderson University just make it so special.  We just showed up today to walk the campus and ended up meeting the AU President's wife at the Information Desk. She was so nice to talk to us and make us feel so welcomed. Such a great start to our visit!!"]

name: Ball State University
reviews: ["It's wonderful to have a school of higher learning, Ball State University, in the city of Muncie. BSU draws bright young minds to our town from around the world, enriching the living experience for all residents.", "We had a Great time! BSU is such a beautiful campus. Everyone was very helpful and Nice. We're so excited about this next Journey as a family ❤️", 'Great place to see some nice people who likes the art and music.', 'Dr Reza and Estopinal college was very good for candidates who wants to pursue design and architecture course.', "Beautiful campus-- just gorgeous! The landscaping, layouts and buildings are always a pleasure. See the Owley museum while you're there."]

name: Bethel University
reviews:
['What an amazing college! I attended Bethel through PSEO and had many great professors who genuinely challenged me to become a better student. I also really enjoyed the culture at Bethel working in the Dining Center as a server and getting to meet a lot of great people was a highlight of my experience.

Like anywhere, there were a couple of professors I didn’t love but who doesn’t have that experience? A few rarely showed up, which made it frustrating to drive all the way to campus only to get a last-minute email saying class was canceled or replaced with a simple “what did you do this weekend?” assignment. Overall, though, my experience was very positive.', '05/25/2013 was the day I graduated with a bachelor degree in Nursing and was my last day I set foot in this school!! I was very traumatized by discriminatory experiences I had to endure in order to finish! I was very lost and confused thinking to myself how can a Christian school treats me this way just because of my skin color? I felt less human and I was very miserable. I was very confused because I kept on thinking to myself about the teachings of JC that they will preach at the beginning of each lecture as if they were practicing them to everyone but were only to white students. Whites students were treated as human beings with all the compassion, kindness and empathy, professors were helping them pass classes by giving them questionnaires to practice during the summer if they  were having difficulties with nursing courses. Students like myself were treated like thieves, cheaters and they will put a lot of fear to intimidate you. Whenever you write a paper, they will always single out  papers only  from POC students and look for words that are similar and call on us for plagiarism and give us 0, it was terrible! There were 84 nursing students I believe and only 5 or 6 black students, the remaining were whites so it was easier for them to pick on our papers to look for similar words and call on us for plagiarism! We were treated with no compassion, no empathy whatsoever. These experiences really had a negative impact on my mental health and whenever I try to relive  what I went through in this school I get very anxious as if I was having a panic attack. There was a lot of fear going to Bethel as POC, the  nursing department back in 2013 were 99% white females, and if you are a Poc female, it was a danger zone to be! Going to this school was the WORST experience of my life!!', 'I remember walking through the halls of Bethel University saying “I could live here”. Beautiful scenery, great food! Oh! The food!, quality of education is 🌎 class, they take sports 🥎 seriously 🙌🏽, hostels are homely and the environment is clean. I am not an academic person but if I got a scholarship to Bethel, I would be the most enthusiastic academic individual you’ve ever seen 😂.', "My daughter's academic experience at Bethel is becoming a mess. From the day she set foot on campus, she intended to major in Molecular Biology and Minor in computer science. However, there have been budget cuts and the departments are bare bones. Upper level bio courses have a single section offered once a year or every other year, and this semester, the 4 classes she needed were offered all in the same 2 class periods. She can't even take any classes towards her comp Sci minor because they completely changed the catalog and that obsoleted one of the classes she had already taken and created new class that's a prerequisite for every other comp Sci class she needs, but it isn't even offered in spring. So she's stuck!  This semester she is paying full tuition to take 3 classes because her general Eds are fulfilled and she literally can not find a single class to take that would help her progress toward graduation.
It's been stressful and frustrating, and I wouldn't wish this on any young student...so I'm posting here to try and warn you so you don't make the same mistake.
The campus is nice. The food is good. The professors are great.  But if you can't get a degree, what's the point?", 'Beautiful campus, friendly greeters modern facilities quality every where you look.']

name: Butler University
reviews: ['Great campus with everything in walking distance.Wonderful sports program.Has The Metro as well as Scotty’s right there as well,if your hungry check them out.', 'Attended a show yesterday evening and even in the 3rd mezzanine the seats were great! Very clean and well-kept venue with bathrooms on several levels. Parking garage is close to venue and easily accessible. Would love to bring the family back for another event', 'The campus is beautiful, and the music buildings and concert/recital halls were excellent.  The dormitory where I stayed was clean and spacious. The conference for doublereed players was so well done that several attendees commented on how friendly this gathering was. The workers, both students and local employees, were helpful and completely kind.', 'Not comfortable at all.  Seats are SMALL.  I was pressed against my neighbor the entire show, and in pain from having to sit awkwardly.  Sound in the auditorium is so-so.', 'Good academics, terrible library administration. The worst dean is retired, but was kept on long after the administration was informed about the damage being done to morale, so it’s hard to trust them now.']

name: Calumet College of Saint Joseph
reviews: ['Mostly old building. Most students are litter bugs. Faculty is good, some great.', 'Calumet College of St. Joseph has made my transition back to college great. The Coordinator of Public Safety Program Jaqueline Cruz and Professors are dedicated to our learning experience/achievements. They truly put their students first and I will recommend them anytime.', 'I recently completed my Master of Public Safety Administration from Calumet College of Saint Joseph ("CCSJ"). I reside in the City of Chicago. CCSJ is located in Whiting, Indiana which is a suburb of Hammond near the Indiana/Illinois border. CCSJ is a private, Catholic institution. The sports teams are members of the NAIA governing organization. Allow me to begin by stating that the administration treats students as assets and not as a burden. I\'ve always said that colleges and universities need to stop acting as if they are doing students a favor by letting them attend their respective institutions. Students are essentially customers who are paying a great deal of money for job training. I\'m not sending a child off to college for play time. I\'m sending a child to college to obtain the skills necessary to become a contributing member of society. Administrations need to realize this as do the individual professors. If a student is struggling or not grasping the material then the faculty member needs to help said student - that\'s the point. Students are customers. I\'ve encountered faculty members who think that students should be honored to be enrolled in their classes. That\'s nonsense. So what\'s the point of my diatribe? You don\'t have that elitist attitude here. Dare I say the administration and faculty at CCSJ treat students as family. If you are struggling they will get you help. They work with you throughout the application process, advisement, etc. CCSJ also offers online courses via the ZOOM platform as well as off campus courses as needed. CCSJ has made arrangements for classes in downtown Chicago and Chicago Heights. I can only speak to my program. The content was excellent. The instructors were terrific and many are practitioners in their respective fields. Day and evening classes are offered. CCSJ was my first choice for a MS. Southern Illinois (Carbondale) was my second choice. Both schools are great. Recommended.', 'Great school, where you succeed as a student but also as an individual! Professors are always willing to help you, and they want you to be ready for your work life!', 'Great School!   Completed my under-grad and I didn’t want to stop.  In the process now of completing grad-school and I wouldn’t change a thing.  Thank you CCSJ.']

name: College of Court Reporting Inc
reviews:
['CCR is the absolute best! When I first found my interest in court reporting I didn’t know where to turn or how to even get started. I heard great things about CCR and decided to give it a try. Nicky did a fabulous job getting me started and the teachers were absolutely incredible! I can’t believe how one-on-one they were and genuinely cared about their students. I even had teachers CALL ME, not just email, to tell me how awesome I was doing. 1. I couldn’t have done it without them. 2. You won’t find many schools where a teacher actually calls their students to check in!

Apply at CCR - you won’t regret it!', 'CCR is amazing! As for the negative comment below, court reporting seems to me to be a nitch based career. It is not the schools fault if a person does not have the skills or aptitude. I mean no disrespect by this comment. For example, I could never be a doctor or lawyer no matter how much money I paid or believed  I could or wanted to be. I have gone to school before & the career path was not a great fit for me. CCR has changed my opinion of college and my life for the better and for that I am forever grateful no matter how much debt I may incur or if I finish or not. I am not giving up! Thank you for treating me like family! Thank you CCR!', 'From a former onsite student-  This place at first seems to be really nice.  Faculty preaches about "professionalism" and they do everything they can to tell you that you can succeed in court reporting.  They employ incendiary marketing schemes (i.e recruiting naive Hobart High School students) and tell you that there are tons of "great paying" court reporting jobs all around the world.  Then once you are there you realize everything cost money, it takes WAY more than 2 years to master the skill of stenography, and almost every single faculty member is related to each other.  Almost nobody I started school with here graduated.  Most of the staff here AREN'T EVEN COURT REPORTERS.  They hold unavailing college degrees in disoriented areas.  You take courses such as "Modern History" that is the equivalent to elementary school social studies.  You may be surprised to learn that these colleges of court reporting and court reporting schools have 85% to 90% dropout rates and average graduation rates of 2 to 14 percent.  Do research before attending this school; whether online or onsite.  And be wary of spending a fortune and having nothing but a lifetime of debt.', 'I struggled with their classes because I had reached out to many people for help. And I have emails that never got replied to to prove that.

Let’s just say they were glad to get me out of there. They didn’t even give me a choice of staying or not they just emailed me some exit papers one day.

Waste of my student loans.']

name: DePauw University
reviews: ['Got to visit this college campus on a school counselor bus tour. Our hosts welcomed us with a boxed lunch & answered our questions about majors/programs. We explored different buildings & learned more about the school via our tour guide, a current student. I was pretty surprised at how large the campus is for only having around 2,000 students. Shout-out to a staff member named Barbie who provided me with a Mountain Dew when I was struggling to stay awake without caffeine lol. Also appreciated the gender neutral bathroom!', 'Small town college, well maintained place. Should be great as Black Panther University.', 'The periodic table display is open to the public, and it is an incredible collection with wonderful information on the elements. We enjoyed it thoroughly!!!', 'This place has gone downhill since Rusty left', 'Great school community, very tight knit. Lots to do on campus, big Greek scene, most students are in a fraternity or sorority. Lots of partying. An activity/club exists for everyone. Academics very important, students work hard, spend long hours in the library. Athletics are not stressed, or really supported by the student body. Most students would rather party instead, tailgate > actual game. Greencastle community is lacking, poor relations exist between students and locals.  -Graduated 2011']

name: Earlham College
reviews:
['Do your homework.  I was looking to send my son to a quality,  small Christian college close to Cincinnati but not in the city. Small with a great faculty:student ratio. He would've played sports as he has several offers at some DII schools across the Southeast. The application process proved their is serious lack of professionals operating this school. When attending live webinars, staff and students they had participating also set off alarm bells. For a Christian school, I understand Liberal Arts, but they were more focused on promoting DEI, Transgender, Pride than Biblical foundations and principles.  I thought the whole Quaker experience would be beneficial, turns out they are just looking for anyone that can pay the bill and have a large international student ratio 25%. That's huge for 700 students. It became clear watching conversations on apps like ZeeMee that a solid education and career preparation is not the focus. Their own current students were in groups attacking potential new students applying,  each other, and faculty. There are 2 on the ZeeMee apps that clearly have some mental health concerns.

After the last "virtual" campus visit Live event last weekend, it was the light bulb moment and we withdrew his application immediately.

Each must form their own opinions, I'm just alarmed enough to feel it requires notifying other parents to do your homework. Otherwise, when you see your child on TV at some radical protest event or worse, God forbid, it's not because there wasn't red flags.', 'My child is a sophomore here.  She is finding it to be an amazing educational experience with opportunities to develop a career path beyond any she’s heard of elsewhere.  As a parent, I can’t recommend it more highly!', 'Good experience, well cared for campus, friendly and helpful college administrators, beautiful soccer fields, diverse students and administration.', 'If you wanna send your student to a place where it is a dead community, no 24/7 open hours from cafés to gyms, extreme increase in mental health due to isolation or backstabbing teammates on a sports team this is the right school to go to! If you are looking for a better school with better offers and respects the honest system I highly recommend that you find another school than Earlham College!', "Love the experience, saw old friends and made new ones. Can't believe I waited so long to return."]

name: University of Evansville
reviews:
['I had a very disappointing experience at this university. During my freshman year, I was bullied and treated unfairly by a professor, with little support or accountability from the school.

The tuition and fees are extremely high for the quality of education and student support provided. I regret attending this university and would not recommend this university.', "We went to Braun Stadium here at the University of Evansville, Indiana. The people were very nice and the stadium is absolutely beautiful but unfortunately, the bathrooms were across a lot and in another building. We had to walk through a construction site to get to the bathrooms and the workers were very upset with us. There were no porta potties and that was our only option . It was also way too far for the elderly or disabled people to go. On top of that, the woman's bathroom was locked. Thankfully, there was no one in the men's bathroom. That is the only reason why I gave a low rating.", 'How does a University that claims to be "Private" and "Religious (Methodist)" make it so difficult to find mention of the Universities statement of faith or beliefs on the website.

Can't say I believe the Private Religious University claim. Religion is obviously not the foundation of education here.', 'This is a good University. The people are diverse and most instructors do generally care about your success. It certainly wouldn’t hurt the school to pour back some of the tuition and donations into upgrading the out of date classrooms and dorms. Also, I do think since one is paying a large some of money to go here, teachers should record lectures and post them, to give students more options on sick days or days that are needed for absences. We aren’t paying our friends to keep us up to date. We are paying the school and the staff. Without the students, this school would not exist. Also, that brings me to the thought that the attendance polices are too strict for those students who need to miss for vacation, but are willing to keep up with work online. Hello, we are in the age of technology. These rules are outdated and too demanding for people who are actually paying to be here.', 'Great place for focused studies on a private campus.  Excellent sports teams.  Nice place for conferences as I attended the Diabetes Convention a few years ago for Medtronic, Omnipod, Tandem, and Dexcom.  Nearby to go food places to get some good Chinese or subs.  Bank is close as well.  Nice area and is always clean.  Building are older but still nice.  May be more expensive to attend here but scholarships are nice.  I would recommend this private school.  It is a nice gem to the local area.  Many good things have come from students and staff from this school.']

name: Franklin College
reviews: ['Coming to Franklin College is one of the best decisions I have made. The small campus and class sizes, along with great students, professors and coaches, creates a very personable atmosphere. This atmosphere on campus is one of the main reasons why I chose Franklin in the first place. In addition to my classroom and athletic experiences, Franklin has also been a great place socially. I have built a lot of long lasting friendships during my time here.', 'Great art program - incredible students and staff - David Cunningham still life paintings of rocks is phenomenal', 'I have been at Franklin College now for three years as a student. When I first arrived on campus, I came to get my degree and get out, however, this campus has changed they way I look at college. It is not just a time where students work to obtain a degree, but also a time where students can build themselves as leaders, followers, and individuals. The experiences I have gained at Franklin College will be with me for my life. The academics here are also outstanding. The classroom setting is individualistic. Professors work closely with their students.', 'I absolutely love Franklin College. Campus feels like one giant family. The close-knit environment allows me to not only feel comfortable going to my professors for help but also to be held accountable for the work that I do. Franklin has allowed me to explore fields outside of my major and become a more well-rounded individual. The classwork is rigorous, yet applicable to the real world, allowing me to be better prepared for the graduate school admissions process or beginning my career after graduation.', 'Franklin College gives students the opportunity to grow academically and professionally in a welcoming and close-knit community. Professors have the students best interest in mind and will help them to the best of their ability to achieve their goals. There are many opportunities to get involved on campus and in the community. If I had to make the choice of where to attend college again, I would pick Franklin every time.']

name: Goshen College
reviews: ['More progressive student population than you might expect from a religious college, closer to the actual teachings of Christ. Still,  the college does make their instructors sign a sort of religious pledge, which is kind of uncool.', 'Great college to visit and just see how amazing it truly is. The scholarships programs are extremely good and the teachers are super friendly. Definitely a college to consider attending for your career.', 'This school is very liberal. I would not send my kid here even on a full ride scholarship. I will admit though that sauder hall is a beautiful music venue. It has very nice acoustics and is a great place to take in any variety of concert or musical presentation', 'Goshen College has a progressive, tight knit Christian community that can be hard to understand from the outside.\n\nI just graduated and can attest to the quality of education, lived-out faith of my peers and professors, and campus atmosphere that encourages critical thinking. As a physics major, I got to know my professors on a first name basis,  had internship opportunities every summer, and even spent a semester abroad in Morocco. Beyond imparting technical knowledge, Goshen encourages you to live prophetically and intentionally in a complex world. Highly recommended.', "Culture for service is the motto or was when I went there...indeed Goshen College has a culture of it's own developed by the international outreach that the Mennonites have, this developed its own culture and it is a warm place with excellent education and committed professors and staff all who espouse the mission statement of their church and school.  I enjoyed my time there and made life-long friends, I graduated in 1995."]

name: Grace College and Theological Seminary
reviews: ["Beautiful campus. Wonderful atmosphere.  Just such a positive atmosphere for a young person to grow into a young adult.  Every person we have ever came into contact with genuinely cares about and would stop what they're doing and pray for your child any time. I love visiting just to be in the atmosphere. I can't wait to start attending there this fall. The people are so very friendly and the town is amazing! Our trip got cut somewhat short because one of their student from what I understand was on quarantine and passed away that day. name: Hanover College
reviews:
['Came here for football camp in the summer. Had some good practices, and learned a lot from the Hanover football coaches. They were kind enough to let us stay in the dorms! Food and kitchen staff was 10/10.', '! This program has already dismissed five Black women from the 2025 cohort. Multiple directors and faculty members have resigned from their positions, citing the racism, bias, and systemic unfairness within the administration. Currently, Hanover is facing a lawsuit for systemic racism and sexism within the program. There are two directors in particular who have openly expressed that Black students make them uncomfortable through both words and actions.

Beware: White students who were removed from their fieldwork placements have been given additional chances to remain in the program and be reassigned elsewhere. Yet, when Black students experience challenges in a so-called “mentorship” course, we are not granted those same opportunities or grace.

If you are considering applying to or attending this program be warned. The administration, including Interim Director Aguilar and Theresa Delbert, are money-driven and uphold systems of inequity. Proceed with caution.

They took away our White Coat Ceremony, claiming it wasn’t necessary because they never had one themselves. What they failed to recognize is the incredible amount of work, time, and energy we’ve all invested to get to this point especially for students of color, first-generation college students, and children of immigrants. The lack of understanding and respect for what this moment represents for us speaks volumes.', "What a hidden gem! I took my daughter there only because a coach contacted us. We were welcomed with open arms by her prospective team, had an amazing tour, and really felt how cohesive the student body is. And talk about a gorgeous campus! Top all that off with amazing academics, support throughout their college career and accessibility of the professors...slam dunk! Oh, and don't forget a trip to nearby Madison, the cutest cotton Era small town and stay at the converted cotton mill to hotel. Regardless if she attend, this was an amazing trip!!!!", 'Very beautiful campus.  Helpful and friendly staff. I'm an alumni, started a scholarship to honor a deceased relative and they allowed the funds "largest donor" to make changes to the scholarship without my permission. In my opinion, they chose money from a donor over what is right. Do not donate or trust administration when it comes to money. #MyOpinion']

name: Holy Cross College
reviews:
['This school does absolutely nothing to help students find employment. Most of my twins graduating class friends are either still searching 6 months later, or working in low end service jobs. Save your money, they only care about tuition collection. State colleges are better connected to employers.', 'Went here for a campus tour; the guides, staff and organization were tremendous and very helpful. So good, in fact, that my son applied and went for the interview - which was insightful and very professional. My son was so blown away by the experience that he ended up bypassing the "expected" schools to attend The CHC. We are so glad he did - he loves it and we, as parents, love it for him.', 'You climb that Worcester hill, and before the Gothic spires, before the manicured quad, something stops you cold: Enzo Plazzotta’s bronze hand—68 inches of oxidized metal thrust skyward like a prophet’s warning or a drowning man’s last reach. It’s called The Hand of Christ, but it reads like accusation. That’s Holy Cross in miniature: beauty on the surface, uncomfortable truths murmuring underneath.

The campus dazzles. Mount Saint James earned its nickname—The Hill—through topography that doubles as metaphor: you are always climbing, always reminded of hierarchy, always breathless. The 175-acre arboretum sprawls across dramatic elevation changes. Fenwick Hall’s twin spires (added 1868–1875) puncture the sky with Gothic ambition. Eleven Rodins live here. The architecture shouts permanence, prestige, and a very specific strain of American Catholic aspiration.

But here’s what else they own: a founding story steeped in the economics of enslavement. Thomas Mulledy, Georgetown’s former president, became Holy Cross’s first president in 1843—fresh off being censured for selling 272 enslaved human beings. When fire gutted Fenwick Hall in 1852, the largest rebuilding gift came from Patrick Healy, using $2,300 from his father’s estate—money earned by selling 51 enslaved people. Patrick and his brother James (the school’s first valedictorian) were themselves legally enslaved but passed as white their entire lives—an American arrangement of terror and silence that this institution both enabled and depended upon.

You cannot separate the spires from the ledger. You cannot admire those Rodins without asking who paid—and how.

Today, the college is aggressively selective—21% acceptance rate, down from 43% in 2022—more applicants competing to inherit this gorgeous, compromised space. Controversies swirl like weather fronts: a $25 million donor suing over broken promises, the student newspaper abandoning “Crusader” because it shared a name with a KKK publication, a dispute with the local bishop over Pride flags. In 2019, they ended need-blind admissions. The wealthy climb easier now.

What does it mean to visit? It means confronting American Catholicism’s glittering façade and bloody foundations at once. It means understanding that elite education has always been about who gets to forget and who is forced to remember. From the hilltop, Worcester spreads below—panoramic, possessive, perfect for an institution that spent its first decade debating whether proceeds from enslaved children’s sale were acceptable fundraising.

Go see it. The hand reaches up, the spires reach up—everything here strains toward heaven while rooted in earth that remembers everything. That tension is the American story, and Holy Cross tells it with startling clarity if you look past the purple banners and polished bronze.

The art is world-class. The view is breathtaking. The history is what it is: ours.', 'Save yourself $10,000 a year in vehicle suspension repairs by not going to school here. The number of speed bumps in the parking lot will destroy your car', '[My niece Katie and I had the chance to join a tour this morning, and it was such a great experience! Our tour guides, Ava and Maddie, were fantastic—so friendly, enthusiastic, and interactive. They answered every question and made the tour both fun and informative.

The admissions staff was warm and welcoming, and the campus is absolutely beautiful. The energy and positivity we felt throughout the tour really stood out. Highly recommend this tour to anyone considering the school!']

name: Huntington University
reviews: ["Nice sports area.  Friendly folks..Fun Crossroads Men's Basketball Tournament.", "I went to school here and it's a really great school. Wouldn't have picked any other place. The students and professors are welcoming and really just try to get to know you personally and help you grow. Plus it's beautiful!
