There are also several free concerts put on by the music department or the community orchestra that really are a great experience.', 'Exceptional staff. Your student is not a number here!
Beautiful campus!
They will help your child succeed.
Lovely town to have a your young adult go to school at.
Highly recommend you look at the school', 'Our daughter loves it here. This is a beautiful community and they are very concerned about the young people at the school. There is a noticeable political slant that is unfortunate. A college/university should be a place to explore all points of view not quash/shame one or the other.', 'Simpson College is a liberal arts institution. My kid goes to this school, and really loves it! It has small course sizes and student-to-teacher ratios. Simpson has some top notch scholars with Ivy league education from schools such as Harvard and Stanford. Simpson is located in Indianola, Iowa (which admittedly lacks diversity and culture). Yet, it is a growing city and they are at least "open" to the idea of differing thoughts and cultures. The college is somewhat expensive being of such small stature, but they are overly generous with scholarship opportunities. Simpson promotes their undergraduate research programs as highly competitive. I don't know the actual level of research and societal contributions they are able to make since they are a private institution (aka, lack of incoming public research dollars). However, Simpson has outstanding academic programs. We were sold on Simpson due to our kid's recruiter, named Dave. He's undoubtedly one of the best resources at Simpson. I would highly recommend any student to at least take a campus visit.', 'Great, personalized and hands-on education.  Over and over again Simpson College builds well-rounded individuals whom are ready for the job market.  The close-knit alumni network and proximity to Des Moines make for an excellent home to further your education and broaden your activism.']

name: Southeastern Community College
reviews: ['Populations in rural areas are not always afforded the opportunity to obtain affordable and accessable secondary education. The programs/classes offered here are excellent. In my opinion, the negative reviews reflect experiences that are caused by misunderstanding on the  part of the contributors. We are blessed to have this institution of higher education in Columbus county. (As well as surrounding counties)', 'I love the teachers here they have helped me tremendously! Shout out to Mr Hobbs and Mrs rockenbach!', "You do not want to attend this school it is beyond awful the advisors lie to the students. They have you to take a placement test for classes then they put you in the classes they say you scored to be in then after the classes start they say you weren't eligible to take those classes there then they want you to pay them for having to withdraw from the classes and pay for the books . They lie to get money out of the students. Do not attend here if you want to further your education because you will not go anywhere. Its just awful how this school does students. i will never attend here again", 'Graduate of 1987 class nursing dept. Excellent above and beyond. I developed ms and low immunity,at this time I had to stop work. All instructors from 85,86.and spring of 87 when my. class graduated  They remember us all. Karla', 'Understanding, professional instructors that are willing to help students succeed in their courses as long as the students are using the resources provided to them to understand the material.']

name: Southwestern Community College
reviews: ['Took one class here while taking a gap year from my university and it was very relaxed. The campus is beautiful as they have redone many of the buildings here. The only thing I will say is that it feels like Highschool V2 and feels a bit slow and sometimes communication with professors can be a hassle but a very positive experience nonetheless.', 'If you’re a student transferred from out town, good luck! once you complete your units it will be very HARD to get a hold of someone! I’ve called the Evaluations dept. including the supervisor evaluation leaving voicemail and email and still no contact. I’ve been dealing with this for a year. No one answers their emails and phone numbers!! I’m just a homeless out of town student hoping a better life and this school making it really STRESSFUL!!!!', 'Love the new buildings on campus! My experience at SWC is always been positive, love how spacious the campus is and the Aztec details they put on the building, they have amazing programs and financial aid', 'The price is good and I like the ability to cancel my membership at any time. However, it is very frustrating that they do not enforce rules like keeping students out of the community members locker room, wearing proper shoes in the gym, reminding people to clean the equipment after they use it, and most importantly, locker rooms are not cleaned often. You frequently find hair clumps on the floor and in the sinks, and the floor is rarely ever mopped.', "Took at least 3 weeks to even get registered and another 3 weeks to get a simple password reset for school email. Then they rejected my forms because of their delay so resubmission will most likely take another 3 weeks and I'm simply hoping my target class won't be filled. Love a college with no responsibility."]

name: Upper Iowa University
reviews: ['I did their online MBA. Got top marks. Only thing is, they do nothing to assist with job placement. The degree is meaningless. It will have no impact on your career advancement. Don’t waste your time nor money breaking yourself in this program while working full time for years. It’s all for nothing.', 'Upper university fans did not show good sportsmanship during the dual meet with Maryville, I heard all kinds of things being said to the Maryville wrestlers. Some of the Upper Iowa fans were yelling at the Maryville coach, the referee should have stop the dual and ejected those fans.', 'Neat campus in a really beautiful setting.  Full academic programs and several modern buildings.  Staff are friendly and helpful.  Campus is well maintained.  NCAA DII', "This is the best university I have ever studied. The only reason I transfer was because I couldn't be in cold place. If only the area wasn't that cold and I was comfortable being in cold, I swear to god this is where I would go.\nFriendly people, nice professors, beautiful college, less people and more attention and lot of other benefits. Professor knows you by your name and anytime you need any help, they are there for you. If you have any issue, just call the university and you will be warmly welcomed. I always loved their gym and swimming pool. Good in sports, awesome professors, clean and motivational and inspiring people and also chance of lots of internship. What else would you expect from a university!!", 'For a smaller college I was surprised at the numerous new buildings and amazing campus grounds! Definitely the big college feel but with a small school focus and education. I also realized that they were very military veteran focused. Excellent!']

name: Waldorf University
reviews: ['When I first began pursuing my bachelor’s degree at this college, I didn’t have any major issues. However, as I approached my final courses, things began to change drastically. I was repeatedly told that certain classes were unavailable or that I could only take one course at a time. This constant back-and-forth delayed my graduation by an entire year. Despite my frustration, I decided to give the school another chance and enrolled in a master’s program, a decision I now deeply regret. What should have been an exciting experience turned into an exhausting and discouraging process. The program required only 12 courses, but when I reached my last seven, I encountered the same issues all over again. I attempted to accelerate my progress by enrolling in three courses at once, but my academic adviser, Debra Waldrop, handled the situation unprofessionally and without empathy. She insisted that my degree had to follow a strict 27-month schedule, spacing out my courses so far apart that I wouldn’t finish until late 2026, despite being only seven classes away. After repeatedly explaining my situation, the school asked me to write an essay justifying why I wanted to take more than two courses at a time. I did exactly that, only to be denied again. To make matters worse, they instructed me to pay for two courses that had already begun. Once my payment was processed, I was informed after the start date that one of those courses was actually unavailable. This pattern of dishonesty, poor communication, and lack of accountability has been consistent throughout my time here. I genuinely feel that the school prioritizes keeping students enrolled and paying for as long as possible rather than helping them succeed. At this point, I am not enrolled in any active course, yet I’ve been charged for classes that I cannot even take. I am heartbroken and extremely disappointed by how I’ve been treated. I plan to file formal complaints and explore every available avenue to hold this institution accountable. Please, do your research before choosing to attend this college. My experience has been nothing short of a nightmare.', 'Terrible school for international students. Highly do not recommend. Professors not supportive.  Drug related issues with students every weekend.', 'I love Waldorf University! Attended both residentially for my BA, and online for my MBA. Excellent professors and staff! Highly recommend, especially if you are looking for an intimate classroom setting where the professors care deeply about each student and set-aside time to work with each of them one-on-one.', '2nd experience with Forest City Athletico. A year ago I had a hip replacement & recovered quite easily. This year I had sciatica issues - more demanding physically & mentally. Jenna & staff were amazing in treatment and exercises prescribed - both in session & at home. They are competent, compassionate & encouraging. Highly recommend!', "This school is great! If you have a GI Bill and have had difficulties getting a school to work with you, give Waldorf a call! They took care of everything, checked in with me often while I was waiting for my paperwork, and made the whole process so easy! I attend online; the teachers have a real presence despite the lack of face to face interaction. Everyone I have dealt with has been incredibly helpful! I just did my enrollment for my third term with them; I swear the process took less than five minutes. I couldn't be more pleased to be a student with this University!"]

name: Wartburg College
reviews: ["Iowa doesn't have much there. I think the campus was pretty but they had this one hallway that was creepily empty for sports or something but it was way too big and just a hallway. Also the food was not great.", "I went here for one year. Most of my professors were quite professional, but 2 of them were absolutely atrocious, and a mix-up my professor made landed me with a permanent  F  on my transcript, while my GPA each semester is no lower than a 3.5 . If you ever have a major illness or a tough life situation, or need helpful suggestions from your professors, THEY DO NOT CARE AND DON'T MAKE AN EFFORT TO HELP. Not sure if my experience was just a fluke, but I'm reading all these other comments about how amazing the faculty are, and this is NOT TRUE! Petty music directors, irresponsible professors, lazy office workers. It's the best school you can get in a small, boring town in Iowa. Tuition is also through the roof, especially for the level of education you receive, and tuition just keeps climbing (for what, I'm not quite sure. There is nothing at this school that is worth the amount you pay). Housing is also awful and not accommodating in the slightest. They hardly have enough and don't let people live off campus, most likely because they are losing students and need everyone's money. The only two things I loved about the school were the perpetually mating tortoises in the science courtyard and the W recreational facility. But overall, the campus feels like a glorified high school. College students act like immature teenagers, not a lot of food selection on campus or off campus, and you have to drive 40 minutes to get to a town with anything to do (which STILL sucks). If you like a small-town college with very little to do, cliquey students who NEVER leave campus, small, repetitive food selections, and selfish professors (at least in the music department), this is the school for you!", "Wartburg College is one of only two schools in Iowa that offer music therapy. They have just added a master's program for music therapy as well. The music department in general is fantastic and many students are involved in one ensemble or another, even if they are not music majors. The dining hall, Mensa, offers a wide variety of meal choices at a decent price. Other areas exist on campus to purchase food and drink as well. The W is open for use by students and the public. It has pools, gyms, strength training, etc. It's a great school. There's so much good about it that you just have to come check it out!", "It's pretty and good for a visit. If you're looking to attend there, make sure you plan your budget out and try for as many scholarships as possible to help bring down the price. The people here are great (both in faculty and in students). If you stop to eat, I suggest getting food from the Den and then later get snacks from the Kdit. The W is a very good work out area and I would suggest using it if you get a chance. The art gallery is also always fun to walk around in.", "I graduated from Wartburg in 2016. I had a blast and I grew so much professionally, spiritually (and I'm even Catholic!), and as a person. Wartburg will always be a home for me. I brought my boyfriend (who is from Ohio) to Wartburg for homecoming and he was amazed at how much of a family Wartburg is, and even though he new no one, how welcomed he felt by students, faculty, and staff. President Colson and Christie truly care about their students and you can see that by not only how many events they go to, but how he speaks with students and spends the time to listen to them. Thank you Wartburg, for everything."]

name: Western Iowa Tech Community College
reviews:
['⸻

🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

Michelle and Mike Brown — The Dynamic Duo of Western Iowa Tech

If Western Iowa Tech had superheroes, Michelle and Mike Brown would definitely be it — capes optional, but totally deserved. Whether you’re drowning in deadlines or just need a little extra guidance, these two are the ones who swoop in with exactly the help you need.

Michelle’s attention to detail and calm confidence make even the most confusing processes feel like a breeze. Meanwhile, Mike’s energy and straight-shooter advice cut through the noise and get you back on track faster than you can say “final exam.”

Together, they’re like the peanut butter and jelly of student support — perfectly balanced, surprisingly powerful, and something you didn’t know you needed until you had it. Honestly, navigating school can be tough, but with Michelle and Mike in your corner, it’s way less scary and a lot more manageable.

If you ever find yourself wondering who to turn to at Western Iowa Tech, start here. These two have your back — and then some.', 'Horrible school, they sent a late fee to collections even though I turned in the computer on time. Instead of working with you they instantly flip and turn on you.', 'They are taking money from me and I am no longer a student and have paid all my dues.', "Dont let the graduation rate sway you. This place has phenomenal teachers and tons of help if you look for it and/or ask for it. The tutors have been crucial in my academic success. I wish some more credits would transfer but other than that this place is awesome. Beautiful campus that's always well maintained. Nice disc golf course out back and people are friendly.", 'They offer classes to people of all ages! I started taking classes when I was 16. They work with local high schools to allow high schoolers to get free college. What a cool idea! People and staff are friendly, the other day I had car troubles and one of the professors offered to help. Nice campus! I love the disc golf course!']

name: William Penn University
reviews: ["I ABSOLUTELY LOVED THIS CAMPUS!!! Facility, students, the environment makes u feel so comfortable and welcomed !! Love seeing the students smiling and pleased to be there! Great atmosphere! WPUCT were the cutest and so friendly to my child, they differently won her little heart!! Can't wait to be a parent of a student of WPU!!! Shooting for the stars 🌟", 'Coach Rufus is the man!  Brought in a bunch of basketball recruits and their family and showed them. The royal treatment! I was very impressed by the tour of the campus and the personnel!', "I was recruited to play soccer at William Penn. The coach assured me that the school, facilities and surrounding towns would be just as worth it as the opportunity to play collegiality. I was excited about the opportunity but when I arrived all I was met with was disappointment. The facilities were a joke. We were a college team practicing and playing on one of the worst fields I had ever seen. The buildings on campus are worse. Once I was in the student center and the ceiling actually started falling. There were broken ceiling tiles all over the floor. All of the buildings are filthy and infested with bugs. Even worse than the facilities was the actually education. I had one professor who was actually competent. The rest were a complete joke. 75% of the student population wouldn't have been able to graduate from my high school and so the professors who actually can teach, teach down to that level. If the professors were bad then the faculty is downright worthless. Most departments such as financial aid, counseling, business office, etc are full of people who hate their job. These people are meant to help students but instead anyone who will go into them are made to feel like they are a complete burden on those working. They are not helpful and occasionally downright hostile. Even the dean of the school poses a problem for students. For both myself and other students that I know the dean was incredibly hostile and almost made us pay a lot of money in fees because he tried to get involved in situations he had no business being a part of and over complicating them. William Penn remains in business solely because they offer students the opportunity to play sports. However they prey on students who are afraid to miss out on that opportunity. There are dozens of schools in the surrounding areas alone that will offer students that same opportunity and so much more. These schools have better facilities, friendlier people, and a better education. I lasted one semester at William Penn before leaving and I am not the only one. Out of 45 players on the soccer team (I only use this example because they are the only statistics I know for sure) 13 will return. That number is far too low. If that many students are leaving after one semester there is obviously something wrong with that school.", 'This place changed my life and the lives of so many I went to school with. The leadership core that is implemented in the curriculum prepares students for life. Those that by into it, no doubt experience success long term.', 'I graduated in 2004 and now my son will be starting in fall 2017. Proud to have him experience a great education, lifelong friends, quaint college town and Quaker values.  The best !!']

name: Allen County Community College
reviews: ['Kids on college baseball team were very good ambassadors of Allen. When I asked about the coaching staff one said " coach will be at my wedding" and "i met my best friend here". I wish the baseball portion had a few less kids. So more attention could be focused on their individual play instead of a few reps and then wait for ling periods of time but all in all great experience.', "I love this place! My academic journey started here and I could not be more proud. This place is full of great instructors; if you meet them halfway they will go the extra mile to make sure you get the most out of your college experience. I'm very honored to be a ACCC graduate. -Greg Watt", 'This is a great junior college. The professes are passionate about what they do & the student-to-teacher ratio is really nice. You do feel like more than just a number & you can really explore and find yourself (in terms of finding a major).', 'Classes are smaller and more personable.  Instructors take the time to teach and help you.  Staff is always willing to help and will go out of their way to make it possible to attend classes.  Definitely affordable!', 'The teachers were great however the "support" staff is by far the most incompetent and unmotivated I have ever seen so far. It\'s almost like they don\'t even read the emails they send you. If you have any type of issue other than paying them money good luck. For a community college this small, they do a great job at failing to resolve any issue that you couldn\'t find on an FAQ page. Stay away from this school if your career depends on an education.']

name: Baker University
reviews: ["Poor communication and support from the university for online programs. I graduated from an online Master's program this year, and did not receive a single acknowledgment from anyone, not even the dean of my department. I tried calling for graduation information (phone numbers were incorrectly listed on their site) and emailing (my emails were ignored for 2 months. A very disappointing and frustrating end to all the hard work I put into the program. I would not recommend this university anymore based on my experience.", 'Beautiful campus.  Maple Leaf Festival is a huge draw....lots of craft and food booths.  The ZTA house is a wonderful sorority.', 'great place! but, the beds werent clean at all and there were bugs in the mattresses.', "Nothing but love for 'ol Baker U! Great times here.", 'Very nice school to attend']

name: Barton County Community College
reviews: ["My 23 year old daughter got her 2 year in Dance from here after beginning at Iowa Central and experiencing extreme racism.  While Barton wasn't very diverse, everyone at Barton was kind, welcoming, and inclusive.  When we'd visit we'd get an overwhelming sense of community  and acceptance.  This school was simply amazing and I wish they had an Ultrasound Tech program so I could send my 17 year old there next year!   It will definitely be one of the schools we look at when it's time for my 3 youngest to go to college.  💕", 'This looks like a great college!  All the young people there were so helpful, happy, and uplifting!', 'Excellent instructors, very supportive environment.', 'I wish I could give a better review but I would be lying.  I had many, many issues while going to this school and using my Gi bill only made it more difficult. Lots of the teachers are unresponsive for days-weeks and punish you for waiting on clarification for course work. It also takes them 3-4 weeks to post grades making it very hard to stay enrolled in classes. It would take months for them to verify I was attending and to send the info to the VA. They had me take classes that were not "certified online classes" so to graduate I had to pay $510. They claim to support veterans but they are not a true yellow ribbon school and they do not support veterans as they claim.', 'Absolutely worst school ever! They DO NOT take care of veterans as they claim. It was a complete set-up from the beginning. I enrolled for a class and was told from the school that everything with my Post 9-11 GI bill was fine. AFTER the last day for no-payment withdrawal I was then contacted to be told it wasn’t okay and that I had to pay them 450.00. I was going along with the class like everything was okay only to find out “after the fact” that it wasn’t and since I had already “started” the class there was nothing they can do. Now I’m stuck with a 450.00 debt to them and everyone is saying there is absolutely nothing they can do.']

name: Benedictine College
reviews: ["Benedictine College is a beautiful, faith-filled campus. We received a great tour from Joel and William, two excellent student ambassadors. The student body was so friendly. The food was delicious (we visited on a Friday during Lent, and there were so many meatless choices). Faith opportunities abound everywhere. I wish we had more time to attend mass or pray at Mary's Grotto. Such a beautiful place!", 'This shiny college on the hill is a wolf in sheep clothing. They go all out with tiny details of sending cards and merch and promises of how much they truly care, but if you have any kind of special need they throw you to the wolves. My daughter had a crisis that didn\'t even take place on campus. The college dumped her at the police station and didn\'t allow her to come back on campus unless she was supervised. She had no access to her car, money, or communication as she had left all that on campus. They shamed her for having a crisis and was subjected to a firing squad panel meeting where she learned that could not come back to campus unless she was tested, and proved her worth with check in through their "health" department. She also was told to get her stuff out of the dorms by a certain date or it would be thrown in the trash. They did not help her pack her room up they stayed hidden in their fancy offices and sent thoughts and prayers instead. Do not go here. They are more concerned with their pristine image than the needs of their students.', 'We came from Southern California and took a tour of the college with my husband, daughter (junior) and son (senior). The visit was personalized, well organized and the admission personnel was very friendly and informative. The guide was an upcoming senior. She was able to give us good information about campus life. We also met with Dr. Ramsey and Will Burenheide, admission & financial-aid advisor. I was impressed with the campus, history, hospitality, and most importantly with their commitment to the Catholic faith and values.', "Very beautiful campus and buildings. Excellent university with a growing student population. You will see more pictures by clicking my name or Benedictine College. Also search for Mary's Grotto, St. Benedicts Abbey, St. Benedicts Church. You will see all of my pictures and videos. Great pictures for newcomers, future students, parents, and alumni.", "I love this place, I couldn't imagine going anywhere else.  Its a beautiful campus - everyone who visits, including local and regional sports teams, can't stop talking about how pretty it is.  Especially in the spring and the fall - its a must see.  There are several look out locations on campus behind the Abbey buildings which you can look out over the Missouri River - being on top of a mountain, its a darn cool view.  For the most part, the staff are kind, engaging and just all around great people to be surrounded by.  The community life brought by the students from all walks of life (I am from Virginia but I know people from Florida, California, etc) is authentic.  Most people, if you asked them what their favorite thing about the college is, would say that it is the people/community.  Everyone is friendly and truly cares about one another.  Here you can find true friendship while getting a great, engaging education - I am currently seeking a degree in Theology & Evangelization Catechesis, and I love the professors so far.  Even if this place isn't at the top of your radar, or the location seems bizarre (before coming here, I didn't even really know where Kansas was), give it a try - whether or not you decide to attend, you won't regret it."]

name: Bethany College
reviews: ['Small private Christian college in WV. Close to both OH and PA. The college is welcoming and the community is kind to their diverse population of students. It is a beautiful campus.', 'Beautiful college campus in WV with access to Morgantown, WV, Pittsburgh, PA and points in OH. Smaller school that provides the college experience with individual attention if students need it. Great cafeteria, so many choices. Multiple sports programs at the NCAA III level, PAC conference. Tuition is not ridiculous and 100% of those accepted receive financial aid. Definitely worth considering.', "A beautiful college campus with pleasant staff and a long history dating back into the 1800's I believe. Students attending there come from all over the world. The architecture consists of some old and some new which provides  Bethany college with a beautifully well built atmosphere. Would I reccomend this college to others ??? ABSOLUTELY!!!", 'Bethany College has been everything I could have ever hoped for and more in a school!  I grew up in a small town and was nervous for the “big-time” college atmosphere.  Choosing such a small school made the adjustment much simpler.  The small class sizes, attentive professors, and the opportunity to network through my sorority are only a few reasons that I am a proud Bethanian!  On numerous occasions I have been invited to professors’ homes for classes, networking experiences, and just to show how much they care for their students.  I have always been heavily involved in volunteer work…or so I thought.  When I came to Bethany and joined my sorority I was amazed and proud to see how involved in philanthropic efforts the students, and specifically the Greeks are at Bethany.  Even more important are the real hands on experiences that Bethany offers you.  The campus is small enough that you’re eligible to get involved in things right away.  I’m only a junior and I am the Operations Manager of the radio station on campus.  I have two work study jobs where I have true experience both working in my major and in the high paced work environment that I will becoming a part of in only two more short semesters.  I can never fully express how honored I am to be a part of this history everyday and how proud I am, and will always be, to tell people that I go to Bethany College!', "Can't fill out 1098s that they send to their students correctly. I wouldn't seek education from an institution that can not get this simple task done"]

name: Bethel College-North Newton
reviews: ['Stellar basketball coaching staff!  They really care about their players!', 'A lovely small private college located in North Newton, just a 30 minute drive from Wichita. Easy entrance just off HWY135.  Campus is perfect size with large trees and beautiful limestone buildings. Sports complex & tennis courts are located just North of campus lovely wooded walking paths are available to enjoy. Art building is exciting and bursting with creativity.  Teachers have small classes which aid in learning, polite caring staff & professors and a close/interconnected student base adds a since of pride, respect, and a lot of involvement. I highly recommend this educational institution.', "One of my favorite places on Earth. The people, the place, and the education are top-notch and truly life-changing. My four years here we're unforgettable and the education I received was so beneficial to my growth as a person and citizen. Bethel College is not only an incredible place of education, but also a wonderful family and community.", 'The faculty here are very nice.', "Went to women's basketball game national anthem not played caught Bethany team by surprise I assume because of new. Coach maybe tail wags the dog at your school have not seen that at any of the miaa football games I have attended this year spent quite a lot of money in Newton today eat dinner mom and pop Mexican restaurant filled car up admission both games a pop two candy bars but left at end of first quarter if University does not support our country I will not support them 😡"]

name: Butler Community College
reviews:
['Two years in a row we have received inaccurate bills from the school for my sons courses (joint High school/college). They will charge you if you can not pay their updated bill in full and will not work with you without a fee. They appear to take no responsibility for the inaccuracies, nor will they adjust the bill based on the fact that THEY added something late. While you may think that these things might fall into different billing cycles, they don't seem to care. So be careful and always call about what is on or not on your bill.

Outside of billing, it is worth noting my son and an entire class of students were punished for missing class for a high school function the instructor was not informed about. It was only through several parents complaints to the high school and Butler that this was "fixed". They still blame the students for the event despite the principal of the high school requiring all students to attend the event. Finally, I can not count the number of times my son reported that one of his instructors was very politically biased and shared his views to the class as fact.', 'My kid goes here.

Great music program. Nice, modest dorms.', 'Everyone I have encountered has been very friendly and helpful. If you are unsure of where to go in the mass of buildings, just ask.
I am writing this at a time when we have had bitter cold and snow. I am impressed with their efforts to clear snow and ice!', 'Decent enough place I guess. It’s a cheaper college that’s credited around the US which is nice. The staff are friendly and nice most of the time. Pretty flexible on making your own schedule as long as the class is available at that time or not full. The early college program is a really nice feature. I took it during high school and I’m almost done with my associates degree in I3D Tech at the age of 19. Definitely recommend for anyone in El Dorado or surrounding areas in need of a good and cheaper college education.', 'I had some trouble with a few aspects of getting my course started (mostly operator error) and every time I called or emailed, the service I received was prompt and outstanding. I am ridiculously impressed with the staff at all campus locations. They went above and beyond anything I expected. They were courteous, prompt, helpful, accurate, friendly, and more. I am just really impressed and grateful.']

name: Central Christian College of Kansas
reviews:
['I can not say anything good or bad about their academic program, I would ask, are your sure this is a Christian College? The students vocabulary and conduct in the stands at a recent game would diffinantly say differently. Why have a student monitor, if the ref has to call out the monitor to tell them to have the students watch their mouth? I suggest a name change Central College .', 'They make their way by ripping off the middle class and taking every penny they can. This is the premier Christian racket in Kansas. From the cafe prices to the semester hour price, all a complete racket. Do not go here if you have any other options.', "As a Central alumnus, I could talk about the school and my experience forever. I highly encourage you to take the time to visit and speak with the students and staff. Central isn't for everyone, but it is for students who have a desire to have a personal relationship with Jesus in an academic setting that will test you not only in the classroom but in your everyday life. The school is still working on program diversity, so there are not a lot of majors to choose from. However, Central does have strong education, contemporary Christian music, business, and psychology programs that work well with students from all backgrounds.
Central is a heavily athletic orented school that takes pride in the accomplishments of their student-athletes. Home games create a wonderful atmosphere to be a part of. Also, small settings mean you sit next to the women's soccer goalie in your CCW class and the men's basketball point guard in chapel. The coaches are wonderful to be around and can be found at all athletic activities.
Central's Fine Arts department is by far one of the best kept secrets in town! From the theater productions to the Jazz concerts, the level of talent and creativity is amazing. I think that my favorite part of the arts program are the bands that lead worship in chapel. The bands help to create an atmosphere of worship and light to those who attend. Not to mention, you might hear one of your favorite songs on a day when you really need it.
As I said before, Central isn't for everyone and they are extremely clear about their beliefs and the rules of the school. This is a PRIVATE CHRISTIAN institution. Do not be surprised if you get into trouble for breaking the rules...(firsthand experience). Not to say that they don't extend grace, just know what you are signing up for before you attend. You don't have to be a Christian or religious, you do however have to have respect for the guidelines that are set before you. As long as you do as you're asked and have a positive perspective I think that you will find that there are people who want to help you in everything that you do.
You will meet people who have a terrible opinion and outlook on the school and the people who are associated with Central, but my biggest piece of advice would be to make up your own mind about Central. Don't let others dictate your college experience (myself included). Do what you think is financially, emotionally, spirituality, and  academically right for you.", 'This school doesn’t punish students for gun threats or anything serious like that. But god forbid you have friends over to hang out, they’ll try and accuse you of everything they can think of', 'Very easy to navigate. Dr. She’s Randall profile impressive. Please pray no Trumbly I do not believe God wants or would want him around me.']

name: Colby Community College
reviews: ["Terrible customer service in the student loan department. Nobody could provide info on a loan for the past 12 years, now all of a sudden it's due and nobody can seem to figure out dispersions and principal or interest amounts. This school is absolutely zero help!! Avoid at all costs!!!", 'Had a wonderful and detailed tour with Coach Carter for our interest in the baseball program. Integrity,  potential to partner in growth and community was stressed to our relief. Great new facilities for tennis, pickleball and a very nice outdoor baseball field.', 'There are some problems I have encountered with this school. First off the admissions and financial aid offices were atrocious. Not only did they throw people like myself to the side, but they were rude and had no idea what they were doing. Another is the teachers. While there were a couple of good ones, there were more bad ones than decent ones. Also the advisor I had there was pretty much worthless. He had no guidance and I didn’t think he had a clue what he was doing. Luckily I switched to Hutchinson Community College (who is much better). Overall, my experience with this school was not a very good one.', 'Everything about this place is stressful except the Vet Tech Program itself.  based on fall 2017-spring 2019.  filthy, moldy dorm rooms, poor dorm maintenance support (sewage backed up in the dorm, students left to clean up raw sewage), student workers in the business offices are poorly trained and rude.  Terrible customer service.  These are just a few of our experiences.  Was glad to be finished with the school and the town (poor motel experiences).  As a whole, customer service was lacking everywhere which is sad, since Colby is a town where most people stopping off there will never be back.  They are just passing through.  I had decided to just put it behind us and move on until I had to call the college for tax forms today and I experienced it all over again.  They have some great programs, too bad they are not professionally supported.', 'The dental program there is top notch. I\'m very grateful to Jordan and her instructors who made me feel at ease and comfortable, in a dental suite, I know right? I\'m always nervous and anxious when I go to the dentist for anything. But everyone was so polite and caring, I couldn\'t believe it was a classroom. I\'ve been to "professional" dentists that could learn some lessons from Jordan and her instructors. I had my Xrays taken and I\'m being scheduled for a cleaning. I got good news from the dentist as well. He said I have strong bones and teeth and he complimented me on how young I look for my age. I assured him that it was my reckless abuse of drugs and alcohol that had kept me looking great through the years, but now that I\'ve been in recovery for a decade,  I guess my visage haven\'t waned. So much for the "Portrait of Dorian Grey" idea I had going. Anyway, avail yourself of Free Xrays and a dental hygiene checkup and cleaning at the Colby Community College. It will be a pleasant surprise to your mouth and your wallet and that makes me 😁']

name: Donnelly College
reviews:
['I absolutely loved the staff of Donnelly. Pretty much everyone there is out to help you succeed in all that you do. However, if you are going for a nursing degree, I would recommend going somewhere else. I lived in the dorms above the nursing department in Marion Hall and didn't have any problems except when I went down to the only floor with a water fountain to get fresh, cold water. Patty, the head of the nursing department, repeatedly berated me for coming on "her floor" and told me I wasn't allowed there. After I brought my complaints to the dean of students, all the residents received an email saying that we were "washing dishes in the fountains", and that we weren't allowed to go down there anymore. I would go down to get cold water since we were forced to either drink from warm faucets from either our room or the bathroom, and was filling my cup and just rinsed out what was in it beforehand. I understood that my presence could be distracting, so I took to taking the back route of the dorms so I wouldn't walk past any class. It was only after the new nursing department teacher said I was washing dishes that anything was said to the dorm residents. I understand it's a silly thing to discuss, but it was a major factor in my leaving the school. I would like to see the staff drink warm water that they got from essentially a bathroom sink instead of a water fountain, since the only one that was available was on the first floor.', 'It was one of my best schools I have ever attended. My respects to Mr. Shadfar the teacher of ESL grammar classes god bless him. He invited me to work there cleaning the school and I accepted. I worked there from 6pm to 11pm to close the school. Something strange happened to me. My classmates from ESL were wonder why I accepted that job. They said that it was an old building and it was a hospital, many people died there and not body wanted that job because there was a ghost in the 8th floor a woman in white dress appears there. To hear that I started to be worried about, but I needed the job. During the nights I was really scared to be alone cleaning all hallways and all floors and especially in the basemant. I had to work there on Halloween Oct 31st and it was the scariest night. My boss was a person from Irak. One day I asked him have you ever seen something strange because people say many things about the school that it was a hospital. He told me that only one thing happened to him when we were walking on the 8th floor to the elevator. He said that one day when he was going to check from the highest floor to the first one to be sure there are no students at 11pm he was in the last floor and not body was in the building. He said the elevator went down by itself to the first floor. And the elevator to move down it should be someone in the first floor to push the button. He went downstairs runing and he didnt find anyone there. He was really scare. Other day in the basemant my boss from Irak the responsible from all my commitments showed me in the cafeteria that was the basemant one door that not body opens there. Always is closed. He opened that door  and that door takes you to another bigger basemant. We went there and I could see many old machines It was very scary because I could see all the old things of the hospital including the incinerator machine where the people who died in the hospital were burned it was like a horror movie. We went out and I were so thinking about what I lived there. Nice experience something that I never imagine that could happened. I studied the ESL program and got 500 points in the tofl I took all levels from there and higher and advance level in English. Now I am an English teacher in Mexico I have taught for 15 years and I would like to work as a teacher some day for the ESL program in Donnelly if they give me the opportunity.

God bless this school and all people from there.', 'I graduated from Donnelly in 1995.
I remember Mr. Shadfer at ESL program was the best English teacher ever!
Donnelly and Kansas City were one of my memorable places in my life :)
I would like to thank all the people I met at Donnelly. Thank you so much!
p.s. Please give my regards to Mr. Shadfer. I am back in Japan now :)', "Graduated here in 2015. Small classes, teachers realIy care for their students, and I love how students can work here too! I absolutely love this place-its like a small family, I was sad to go. I spent four years here doing my pre-reqs for nursing.  Only thing is there isn't a lot of classes offered here so I had to go to other colleges while still going here. Another thing is I had to do everything on my own. When I first started thinking about nursing I didn't know where to start and what I had to do. All I knew was that I wanted to go straight for my bachelor's. One of the advisors sent me to go talk to the nursing dept. All the nursing advisor (she no longer works there) was trying to do is convince me to do the LPN program. Once I told her that I wasn't interested in that, that I needed help with what pre-reqs to take, what schools had BSN programs, etc she told me she couldn't help me at all! From that moment on, I had to do my own research -look for schools, what classes to take, how to apply, which required teas test. I even had students interested in nursing come up to me to help them with the process.  Overall, it's a great college in the middle of the city..only thing, give some direction to students. There are other transfer universities besides UMKC.", 'The kindest group of people I have ever had the privilege of knowing. They really care about the students well being and make them the top priority. Truly a wonderful place.']

name: Emporia State University
reviews:
["We attended the Kansas Bandmaster Marching Championship 10/18/2025 that was hosted by ESU and that was the worst experience ever! We have attended many marching competitions at KU, K-State and WU. This is the second year KBA was at ESU and last year was bad, but they defiantly didn't let us down on another horrible experience. I am in charge of our high school's group that feeds the band and at every other facility you are allowed to have 2 vehicles at the location the band sets up their home base, but not at ESU. We pulled in the grass off of Highland St. to get set up and with in minutes the police were there ready to write tickets. There are no parking signs along Highland so we were trying to obey the rules in a manor that seemed most appropriate. So at this point we assumed we could have our 2 vehicle's at this location, but no, not only could we not keep our vehicle's there, but they wouldn't even allow us to stay there and unload. You would think anyone intelligent would have said move off the grass once you get unloaded since we were already parked right where we needed to unload, but wrong, they wanted to write us tickets if we didn't move immediately. So then we moved to the street and the police officers continued to sit there and watch us. I asked them what they needed and they said there is no parking along Highland so they were going to write us tickets for being there. I lost it and asked how in the world we were supposed to get our stuff unloaded and they finally said we could stay there to unload and then go park two blocks away in the overflow parking. We watched numerous other vehicles pull up, turn their flashers on and get out to drop stuff off to one of the other schools and within minutes the police would be there with their lights on pulled up behind them. Why on earth would ESU want to host an event like this and be so unwilling to work with people. We are all just volunteers trying to help the school and kids out and we were getting treated like criminals. Maybe the school needs to either raise their tuition so they don't have to make all of their money off of parking tickets or don't host events.

Worst school ever!!! ESU does not have the parking lot space to host an event of this size but they could make it work if they were more accommodating. I will be getting ahold of KBA and see if they can find a different facility for future events.", "It is a ranked 4 University in Kansas State. The environment is calm and cool. Diversity is the main feature here. Its quite popular in this area and the cost is also a bit lower than any other University in Kansas. People visits it often. Its business school is awesome and ACCSB accredited. They have Cybersecurity lab, IT lab also student friendly assistant.
I hope you'll enjoy the weather, environment.", 'I really enjoy coming here to relax and unwind and just think, the fountains, the pond, and the ducks create an amazing, relaxing atmosphere that just melts the stress away', 'Wonderful experience at the ribbon cutting for the new ESU School of Nursing and Student Wellness Center', 'The nature in Emporia is the best ti me. It has four seasons with different colors. This year there wasn’t any cold like other years and for that we have been able to roam around the city and take a tour of the areas. It gives me joy with different feelings here.']

reviews:

name: Barclay College
reviews:
["Our oldest son goes here.  Free tuition,  small classes, really good theater department, and a fair amount of sports opportunities, too.  Great disc golf course on campus.  Tiny town with a great sense of community.  It's worth a look if you're considering a really affordable faith-based education.  Visit the first weekend in October--there's a lot going on and it's super fun.  We stay at the Best Western or Upland Inn, both in Greensburg (about 10 miles away from  the college) when we go.", 'Yes, you will get a great education in your chosen field, Nursing, Education, Criminal Justice, Business, Ministry and etc.
What makes Barclay College amazing is it becomes family.  It is more than a Bible College, it is a Christian Community where students,and faculty connect with other, the local community, and the World as they learn, encourage, and grow in their the faith in Jesus Christ.', 'Barclay College offers an incredible community of believers and a long history of graduates who have had their lives transformed. I can personally say, through four years of education, I was encouraged and challenged to grow in my faith and saw the same journey play out for so many other students. Some of my Barclay friends are now pastors, youth pastors, missionaries, teachers, nurses, and more. My time there was an unforgettable experience that I will always be thankful for and the relationships that formed will last forever.', 'I received my 4 year degree and made many life changing decisions here.  Although one can never get the exact same positive experience I received here, I do know that God is in the business of continuing to bless this college with the next generation of strong Christ centered individuals with a passion to reach the world for Jesus’ glory.

I hope that if you want practical ministry education with an emphasis on Christ you will consider this school!', 'sadly, I was hoping to feel encouraged to attend Barclay but I felt as I was being judged because of my appearance. Did not get a good feeling from  the psychology advisor he was not welcoming and I didn’t feel comfortable asking him questions. I waited a while to write this review but after coming to another religious college and having the opposite experience I encourage others to do your research. I can see why they offer free tuition must be hard to get students interested.']

name: Friends University
reviews: ['Friends university gave me a new hope. As an adult student returning to college, I wanted to do it my way, while working and being busy with life’s other adventures. Friends was the most ideal place for me. From the advising staff to registrar department, they’re all wanting to help you as much as they could. Absolutely love the administration. They do not want your money and give you something of a degree, they will teach you many things in life.', 'Went to the Ceremony of Lights and it was wonderful.\n\nAlso a 2019 Masters Grad and loved my classes here.', 'The Singing Quakers 100th Anniversary Concert  was Magnificent.', 'I love the campus and had a lovely time at their fall show !', 'Attended The Apprentice Gathering. It was exceptional. Much love to all the authors, staff, and students that make this possible. Thank you, Jim Smith, for your dedication to TAG.']

name: Fort Scott Community College
reviews: ["Saw Jeff Allen in concert here tonight. For those of you who don't know, he's a comedian and he was absolutely hilarious!", "Great school.  I enjoyed my time there a great deal.  Every instructor was very helpful and respected students.  It is very easy to get time one-on-one with them which I've learned isn't necessarily so elsewhere.  They also offer free tutoring for every class(Mr. Dobbins is the best in the business).  The advising office helped me out on multiple occasions and I was even able to work part-time for the college.\n\nI met a lot of great students, faculty, and staff while being there and was sad I had to move on.  As with most things in life however, you will have to put out some effort to find success.  I would strongly recommend this school to everyone!", 'The facility is nice, however, it is extremely unorganized. I went here 11 years ago on a full-ride scholarship and recently decided I wanted to go back to school. I went to get information from the admissions office and they informed me that somehow they must have messed up my scholarship way back then and now I have a balance of $700 I have to pay them before I can even consider going there again. I asked them if they could look up what got messed up in the system for this to happen but they said it was too long ago and there was nothing they could do. I would just have to pay it. I recommend if you do decide to go here to be sure you have them triple check everything in the business office financial department before you sign your life over to them.', 'This college is awful. There are a few decent instructors but there are more crappy instructors then anything. The business office is awful, financial aid office is anything but helpful and are more concern with helping the student athletes then the other students. Speaking of the athletes, they have first dubs on classes and the instructors must let them sit in the front two hours and the other students were told that we were not allowed to sit there. Do not go here if you can avoid it.', 'Hands down, best decision I’ve ever made was picking Fort Scott. The only down side is I wish this school could be a university. Picking a next step college was tough when compared to this school - literally in all areas. I contemplated just getting a second associates! The teachers are hands down amazing, all staff in any department you go to - dining, fees, bookstore are all super friendly. I came down and was on the rodeo team as well and I’ve never had a better head coach at any sport.']

name: Garden City Community College
reviews: ['Runners and families be aware of my experience with Coach Rios. If your student goes to her for help to improve times, they’re told, “there’s no point in discussing past performances.” Ridiculous. My student was also told they could quit college, but she withheld the three-day appeals process in the contract. We also experienced a breach of student privacy among the team with an incident that occurred. There are so many other issues concerning families and anyone who runs.', 'Horrible service. Daughter has struggled with this college to get into the nursing program. They don’t call her back, they don’t email her back , she’s gotten the same reply messages over and over with the same steps to do when she’s already done everything, lady Named JUDY who we are to speak is nowhere to be found and impossible to reach. We have even CC’d other staff members in important emails to get a call back with who we need to speak with to answer our questions and get our daughter enrolled, but it seems they just aren’t interested in her attending there for some reason. Never thought this would happen. Will be filing multiple complaints with the college and city. She Will be staying in DC3, thanks for nothing Garden City College.', "If you plan to live here, don't. They treat you like your in middle school and they think they can do what ever they want with your contracts. The welding program is awsome, it's a great program to take and the instructors are awsome!", 'I’m gonna spend some times here for my education. Honestly, the staffs and faculties are super friendly and helpful. Great people, great environment and great school.', 'My daughter is a little bit of an introvert but GCCC helped her overcome her fears. It was amazing to see her go to her first class not afraid to be there. Almost like sending her to kindergarten again. This time unafraid.']

name: Haskell Indian Nations University
reviews: ["Amazing place! It's so exciting to have number one native American University in the United States an hour away in Lawrence, Kansas! People here are so cool and the vibe is so good!", 'Haskell is a trap, it\'s cheap for a reason!! They only show the nice rooms from the newer building, don\'t be fooled! There is mold in the showers and rooms, missing security and S/RA\'s that don\'t do their jobs so if something serious happens, you\'ll be on your own. Professors are great and the other staff such as library, janitors and serving + kitchen staff are wonderful but the housing head ignores you or from what I heard, belittles. We did get served moldy bread and meals are hit or miss. Room checks say you need a "made bed an d organized desk", thats ridiculous esp considering they turn a blind eye to the moldy peeling caulking strips in the showers and are stingy when they turn on the heat for the rooms. Choose a different uni if you can. Read about the ignored SA reports journal of the uni but there\'s bullying that occurs too.', 'My husband is Haskell alumnus. He took me go around campus and they have a food facility. One day my husband’s tooth so hurts and he needed to get his tooth pulled.  We traveled from Alaska so we didn’t know where to go here in Lawrence, KS but he found out that there was Haskell Health Center and he finally could walk in and get his tooth pulled. Zero bill since he showed his Tribal ID.', "I really enjoyed the festival last Saturday. I really enjoy festivals like this because they allow me to be a part of and learn about others' Indigenous cultural backgrounds and my own Indigenous ancestry. Also, I had fun talking to the staff and students. They were all very nice, especially a student named Jordan who didn't mind spending time with me. I will be driving back again for the next festival and/or any other community events that will take place!", 'We went for the Annual Indian Art Fair. There was an entire field of extremely high quality fine art for sale, along with tribal dance exhibitions and a time for all the children to play inside the Pow Wow circle. It was a great experience.']

name: Hesston College
reviews: ["I learned a lot more than just college education it's a very different environment but its a good place to grow and learn. A very different culture but it's worth it I think. The people I met here I will never forget wonderful people.", 'Great atmosphere super nice staff and friendly students very welcoming, great community', 'Lovely place']

name: Highland Community College
reviews: ['Small town..small community...small school but nice apartment style housing..great football coaching staff..nice people in town. Overall I felt comfortable leaving the baby of the family for his first year of college...', 'If the staff would refrain from stereotyping students it could be a decent learning institution. Small town mentality. Such a disappointment.', 'Not the best organization at producing "consistently" and "reliability" out of their students.', "Nice campus, engaged community! Excellent vocal music program and campus life experience! The large on-campus population in a small town makes for a uniquely valuable social growth opportunity for students coming into college.  Small class sizes ensure students are able to be given the one on one interaction time that all data shows to be beneficial.  I was a student here and met friends from all walks of life, from around the country who I'm friends with 20 years later.  The staff and faculty care about the success of their students, both academically and personally.  Like any college experience you will get out what you put into it, but Highland truly offers a unique opportunity for growth during those transition years of a traditional student coming from High School and going on to a 4 year.\n\nI'm also very impressed with how much the technical programs have grown and evolved! name: Johnson County Community College
reviews:
['If you think about transferring do your own research if your going to out of state. The university that I am going to jccc does not have it listed nor are they partners witch makes since because its community college anyway. Also most classes will not transfer over witch is BS and a waste of time. So if you think of transferring do your research yourself. Also you should have just gone to a University', 'Do NOT take English as a second language here. They will take your money and unapologetically teach you absolutely nothing. My wife’s teacher refuses to help her, repeat herself, or slow her speech down so my wife can learn. She also won’t let her use her translation headphones to even understand what the teacher is trying to say. Also, why would they assign my wife a teacher that doesn’t speak her language? She just gave JCCC another chance for another semester and they paired her with the same unhelpful teacher. She’s only had one class this semester and they will not let her switch or get a refund.', "This is a well-run college. It offers children's art classes as well as teen enrichment classes, college classes and hobby classes. The price is fair and the location is excellent.", "In early 2016 I wanted to change careers. I signed up for a tour, and I was just blown away by how nice this campus is. So, at the age of 39, I was a college student again.

The enrollment process was very easy, and everything could be done online including applying for financial aid. I enrolled in evening classes because I was working during the day. I was interested in a degree with an emphasis on Accounting because I remembered doing well and being interested in the subject when I had to take an Accounting class for a different degree.

As for the quality of the teachers, I was mostly pleased. I took Accounting 1 from Mike Megaris. I loved the energy he brought to the classroom. He was good at staying on point during the lectures. One thing I'd change is doing more problems with him in class because there were several times I came across homework problems that I'm sure weren't explained in class. I took Accounting 2 from Anthony (Tony) Wayne. That was the 1 teacher I didn't like. Anthony wasted so much class time telling stories instead of teaching. I did well in Accounting 2 because I had help from 2 other students and because another JCCC teacher, Dave Krug, posted his lectures for Accounting 2 on YouTube. Thank you, Dave! One night for Accounting 2, Sasha Gluhovsky had to sub for Anthony. I wish she could have taken over the class because she was amazing. She's the reason I got an A on the 1st test in Accounting 2.

I needed to take an econ class, so I enrolled in Microeconomics with Frank Syracuse. Frank wasn't just knowledgeable about Microeconomics. He had a passion for presenting the info in a way that the students will understand and appreciate it. Listening to him explain diminishing marginal utility using Whoppers from Burger King as an example was awesome. I took Managerial Accounting with Robert (Bob) Henn. He was an amazing teacher. He can explain complicated Accounting concepts in a way that makes it so much easier to understand. I had no idea Accounting could get this complicated when I started this journey, but having teachers like Robert makes it less intimidating.

I also took an online class during my last semester that I enrolled in at the last minute because I was short 3 credits to complete my degree. It would have been nice if the people keeping track of that warned me before I started the last semester. I ended up taking a Microsoft Office class to refresh my skills in Office, to fulfill the credit requirement, and because I knew Excel is often used in Accounting offices. However, I did not enjoy the experience. This is not the fault of JCCC. I enjoy doing many things online, but I discovered that I prefer to take my classes in a classroom where I can talk to the teacher face to face and study with other students.

The very first department I interacted with at JCCC was the Academic Advising. Each time I enrolled in classes for the next semester, I always talked to an academic advisor to see what classes I needed and what they thought would be good. That helped me a lot, and they were always happy to help. I didn't utilize the Career Development Center until was I close to graduating. They did a great job of helping me update my resume. I loved that I was able to order the books I needed online ahead of time and pick them up at the bookstore. I didn't love the college textbook prices, but they are expensive everywhere. The library and the computer labs were great places to study and get work done. The cafeteria also had a nice selection of food.

I was only there 1 year (2016-2017) because I was able to transfer my college credits, but I really enjoyed my time at JCCC, and I highly recommend that high school students consider attending JCCC instead of jumping right into a 4-year college. A 2-year degree might be all you need for your career. Even if it's not, you will be able to transfer credits from JCCC to another college and save a ton of money on tuition. Shout out to Charlene Collins, Deana Sturd, and Joanna Georgiana for helping me get A's in my classes!", 'Best community college since it opened in 1969! I graduated from there in 1998 and have three kids going/have gone. Affordable, especially when you see the campus and realize how many amenities there are, which are included in the tuition price, including free tutoring.']

He calls my son to say he doesn’t want him to play at St. Mary’s.
From my understanding of what he told me he already spoke to Jadin about this. Unprofessional and unnecessary.

I will highlight that the other people from this college who I reached out to replied back instantly were very helpful and understanding.

Obviously, this is my personal experience with the University.
I’ve heard good things about this school.', "If you plan on attending this school for gen eds, it's pretty good. The professors and class sizes are great for that. name: Wichita State University-Campus of Applied Sciences and Technology
reviews:
["Currently enrolled in the AMT (Aircraft Maintenance Technician) program. While I go to school, I also work in the tool crib. Got to say if you're a hands-on person, this is definitely a great school to attend. At this NCAT center has programs from Welding, Composites, Design, Airframe & Powerplant and more than I know. It's got the same Academic Credentials as Wichita State University. Grinding out the general requirements is tough but once your past that classes become more hands on. Got a full ride scholarship from Kansas Promise Scholarship. For the Cost and time it takes to complete a program this facility will become one of the top leaders in producing Future Work Force individuals. Very diverse culture men and women. Staff is young and old with a lot of knowledge and wisdom.", 'If you want to become a pilot or learn how to construct and build a plane, I recommend you come here for experience.', 'My son got his certification for CNC programming here at WSU Tech. Everyone was very helpful in getting us through the enrollment process.  My son said he really enjoyed the classes and his teachers. They also took the students to job sites and had them speak with employers.', "Outline of review. Location- area, contacting, cleanliness, food, bookstore. Employees- front desk, business office, financial aid, advisors, professors. NDT program - Cost, Professor, courses, in-class, access to the field

LOCATION
Area is nice and clean with lots of parking. Has great airways between the buildings and a nice sitting area and bbq in the central court.
Contacting the location is a struggle. Part of this is that most of us contact during high call times like the beginning of school or as school is starting. Those are rush times in colleges. GO INSIDE OR EMAIL ADVISOR OF THE PROGRAM or call during office hours but remember they take lunches too. So 12 to 2 may be spotty depending on who is on lunch break.
>Cleanliness:Great! Bathrooms are always clean, the whole place is shiny. The parking area,lawn, and sidewalks are well maintained.
>Food: Bleh meh... it's all vending machine stuff and over priced. Pack a lunch or grab something on the way. 4 hour classes without a snack can get difficult.
>Bookstore: A tiny university bookstore with little in it. Best to buy from walmart for things and order books online unless you have financial aid

EMPLOYEES --- remember during rush times they are swamped don't wait until the last minute. Plan at least a month ahead before school starts preferably 2.
>Front desk: Great and mostly you can self assist with the tablet at the desk.
>The business office: Good. There are payment plans, financial aid, and direct. You can pay online after you go to the business office in person and signing the agreements.
>Financial aid: A wreck (0 stars!). I do not know why they  are so bad here. I use to do this job and it was not like this group. Research online and you'll probably be better off.
>Advisors: Great. I've met a few and they all are passionate about their jobs. Most important thing. It is your job to contact your advisor if you have issues. Take the initiative with them. They are there to advise. They are not there to babysit.
>Professors: I've had the pleasure of meeting a few in the programs. My direct is NDT professor John Saunders. They all are positive and funny and have been in the field. They know what they are talking about. Ask questions and take notes because what they say is what is out there.

NDT PROGRAM associate degree
>Cost:payment plans, financial aid, grants, scholarships, and high school access are best.
Otherwise it's $14,277.00 + fees and books which is about $3,000.00. Around $19,000 total. ( cheaper at other colleges but further away from me)
>NDT Professor: John Saunders is a great teacher. A lot of hands-on for students. He tells you exactly how it is and what it will be like in the field. With most programs it is YOUR job to take the initiative. YOU want to know more and learn more YOU need to ask more and do more.
>Courses: All classes are classroom hour classes. This isn't the same for all programs but it is for this one. There are some filler courses which I think WSU forced on to (WATC) WSU tech for credit requirement and required credit hours for a degree. For now that won't change. Try to make the most out of them. ORDER YOUR BOOKS ON ASNT and get a student membership. Way cheaper.
>In-class: Again you make the most of it.
If you want to learn you will. A professor can teach you the basics but for in field work you need to take initiative and the professor's here expect that front you. If you don't you will not be equipped for the field and that's on you.
The classes are about 60% reading and studying and 40% using tools and materials.
It can be fun. Talk to your classmates, interact. They will be your peers in the field.
>Access to the field:I'm close to graduating. I know students who graduated last semester and were in the field within the month of graduation. I've had offers almost. Can't wait to hit the field.
If you want the field-help yourself and the professors will help you. No one wants slackers in the field including the professors and the university. You want a reference. Show you deserve one.
It's legitimate.", "Went to this school in 2018-2019 through the Wichita promise scholarship. I had financial aid and it was a long and tedious process to get it. Teachers were great, but they never gave us enough time on the computer videos to learn from them. Also, never really learned any type of hands on things with sealer... I was there for aviation sheet metal classes, but they only touched on sealer things vaguely. When I left the class it was optional to attend the graduation ceremony due to covid starting at that time. I chose not to attend and did not get my certificate in the mail or an email notifying me to pick it up. In the end, I only had to pay for the book for the class, but I guess if you only pay $50 you get what you pay for. I now work for textron and am going through their training classes and am shocked at how much information that wsu tech left out. Also, I had to apply multiple times for different entry level sheet metal jobs for them to deny and then finally hire me. If you ever have to say where you got your experience from do not list WSU Tech as a source, since most aircraft people don't even know that they changed their name to WSU Tech and also because the companies are on the fence hiring people from that school. Final take aways, you get what you pay for, so don't expect to go in and learn something life changing because most of the teachers are there to do their job and go home. They don't want to answer extra questions or give extra help to students that need it."]
