name: Brescia University
reviews:
['I wouldn’t recommend Brescia University to any student of color — especially Black male athletes — because the environment is not culturally safe, supportive, or inclusive. My boyfriend, Damond Jordan, is a hardworking student-athlete who has consistently contributed to the athletics program, including stepping up to fix broken team equipment and showing up to support university events. In return, he’s been stereotyped, mistreated, and unfairly scrutinized.

One example: the Athletic Director, Mr. Purdue, approached him in a bathroom and made a degrading and unnecessary comment implying he was taking too long — a moment that felt more like profiling than leadership. There was also a situation in 2023 involving the cheerleading team that has been twisted and used to damage his reputation, despite no wrongdoing on his part.

Damond has been made to feel like he has to defend his character constantly while white athletes are protected, comforted, and believed without question. The culture within the athletics department, especially under Coach Karn, lacks structure and fails to show real cultural awareness or fairness.

What makes this more heartbreaking is that current staff members, including his guidance counselor (who is white), have acknowledged privately that the environment is toxic and discriminatory. Even former coaches who have left Brescia have agreed with that assessment.

If Brescia wants to uphold its Catholic values, then it must live them — not just preach them. No student should have to navigate a space where they’re unsupported, unheard, or judged because of the color of their skin. I hope this review helps other students make informed decisions.', "Brescia U has been a great institution for our family! Situated within a few blocks of the Riverfront and many museums, it's also a lovely place to visit.", "It is a nice quaint little college. I and my daughter enjoyed our visit. Offered many things I didn't expect to see at a small school. I would be proud to send my daughter, if thats were she chooses to go.", "Visited the campus yesterday. What a great atmosphere! Everyone was SO friendly! This small town is only a few hours from several  large cities (Nashville, St. Louis, Louisville, Cincinnati and Indianapolis)! If you're looking for a Catholic liberal arts education, check out this university!!!", 'I love the family feel at Brescia. The atmosphere is fun. Education is top notch.']

name: Campbellsville University
reviews:
['My experience at Campbellsville University has been deeply disheartening and stands in stark contrast to the values the institution claims to uphold. It presents itself as a Christian community grounded in compassion, academic excellence, and student support, yet my reality reflected rigid policies, indifference, and a troubling lack of humanity. Despite being a hardworking, high-performing student who faced unexpected and documented personal hardships, I was met not with grace or meaningful assistance but with dismissiveness, making it clear that financial interests outweigh student wellbeing and future success. While the university proudly promotes a mission of Christ-centered servant leadership, integrity, and a caring environment, those ideals were absent when I needed them most, revealing a glaring hypocrisy that reduced its promises to little more than marketing slogans, because upholding academic standards should never exclude reasonable flexibility or basic empathy, especially at a faith-based institution, and until Campbellsville University reevaluates how it treats the students who invest their time, money, and trust, its claim of putting students first will remain empty, leaving me to caution prospective students to look beyond promotional language and carefully consider the level of support they can realistically expect when challenges arise.', 'Honestly the school itself is not overly bad! I’ve only had one professor who was an absolute ass..that was Scott Rasnic! He is in the English Dept! Chances are you will fail his class..he is very hard grader and very condescending!

Also a lot of the classes have a boon you are required to buy plus you have to buy like 6 months of “access” to an online portal to the assignments on. It’s not enough to buy just the book..nah, they make you buy the access too. I pay a $125 technology fee every semester to access moodle but to then have to pay for another place to do the assignments on. 🤷‍♂️

My only other complaint is the financial
Aid dept!

1) they NEVER answer the phone.
2) Student refunds happen practically in the middle of the semester and sometimes later. Last year I didn’t  receive my refund until December. For fall, it was December and for spring it was April. This forced me to buy books and supplies for my classes out of my current wages that are sufficient for me to survive but not incur large expenses. These books are not $1-200 they are closer to $3-400 and you don’t get to keep them , you only “access” them for up to 6 months.
My previous school you had your student load money 2 weeks before class started!

Also they switched to “workday” ! It takes about 2 days to get 1 thing done and be happy if it “ goes through”

I definitely won’t pursue my masters degree with them!', "I attended a BB game at a tournament in which their team was participating. If I had not known previously that it was a Christian university, I certainly wouldn't have known that by the actions of their coaches..the players were just following the leadership and the leadership behavior was sad to see.", 'Wonderful "500 years through the Bible" exhibit and presentation!!! Really just LOVED IT!!!', "My rating is based solely on the incompetence and unprofessionalism I experienced with the Student Accounts office at CU. All other departments at the university have been courteous, understanding, and helpful—but unfortunately, my dealings with Student Accounts were the complete opposite.

I officially disenrolled from the university in October 2024, yet I continued to be billed without my knowledge, as I was no longer attending. When I eventually became aware and contacted the office, the representative I spoke with was rude, dismissive, and offered no meaningful assistance. They denied my claims and applied a number of questionable charges to my account.

Each time I attempted to speak with the director to resolve the issue, I was told she was either unavailable or would call me back—yet no return call was ever made. As time passed and I became busy with work and life, I suddenly received an email stating that my account was being sent to collections. I called immediately, and a note was added indicating that I would pay the balance once the invalid charges were removed. Despite this, they continued to pursue the full amount until I was finally able to involve another department that confirmed and removed the incorrect charges.

Unfortunately, this intervention came too late to prevent the account from being sent to collections. I never heard back from the director until the situation had already escalated. The entire experience felt like coercion—an attempt to force payment for the university's own billing errors under threat of collections.
0 STARS"]

name: Bluegrass Community and Technical College
reviews:
["I'm have almost completed my degree at BCTC and it has been a great experience. The tuition is very cheap, and as other have stated, nearly all of my instructors are UK instructors and carry the exact same course work to BCTC. As a veteran the VA reps they have are considered a 3rd party, but I have never felt it to be that way. Very helpful.
As for the negative reviews....
If you have financial issues, it is typically your own fault. A college is assuming you are an adult and understand how to take care of your responsibilities. One user said the school isn't accredited? Not sure where you got that info, but it is very wrong. The school has a very close connection to UK and actually have direct transfer options for 4 year degree students to most large colleges done in house.
I would recommend anyone at the very least to do your Gen ed courses here and save a lot of money.", "I think like any other school, BCTC has many benefits and drawbacks. When I went there, I found the professors to be fantastic (both online and in person). Many were understanding and helpful,  which was great as I worked full-time while in college and often times needed to either move ahead in the work or turn something in later than expected. Either way, they were more than fair and accommodating.

The tuition is not cheap. Sure, it's cheaper than your average University, but what they end up charging you when they try to keep some students behind another semester here and there to fulfill additional requirements is outright wrong. Many of my fellow students complained most about the lack of guidance they received, or inaccurate information they were given about their degree class requirements. We would be told one thing - this is what you need to take in order to get this degree. When the time came to collect on said degree, they would change the terms and insist you needed to take something else in order to fulfill the requirements. Then some other red-tape would come into play later on. I knew many students who fell into that trap and ended up attending a year longer than necessary.

I'd say for meeting your gen-eds or focusing on vocational-training specific programs (dental hygiene,  nursing aide, etc.), than BCTC is more than suitable. I would be remiss if I didn't caution students on the guidance and financial aid. Know what you need coursework wise before you start - AND know what it is going to cost you. I can't speak to their current operation. I can only hope the aforementioned departments have improved in the student experience.", 'Worst experience with a school ever. A lot of people pick them because they’re cheap and you get what you pay for. I had one meeting to register for classes. No one met with me again or tried to communicate with me. I was never assigned an advisor once class started. I did online classes for 2 weeks and did not like them. Professors were difficult to get a response from. I withdrew from class and apparently missed deadline by just days which I was unaware of. My Pell Grant was taken back all but 180 some odd dollars because of this, meaning I now had to pay the rest of my account. I called to discuss payment plans I could afford and they weren’t good enough for them. It was then turned over to dept of revenue who gladly accepted the payments I offered bctc before. Over half has been paid off in just the past 6 months. I called to discuss a meeting to potentially try to go back in the spring and was told I would not be allowed to attend because of the partial balance regardless of me still paying on it with no late or missed payments. Horrible experience. Do not plan to try and go back at any point in time now. Waste of time and money for classes I didn’t even do. Definitely research and spend the extra money to go elsewhere if you can.', "No one knows anything here I've been trying to enroll and  keep  throwing me around from person to person you email somebody they don't ever answer you back the student center is absolutely no help all they're going to tell you is go hunt down a professor because they don't know anything about the subject that you're applying for I also gave up trying to find professors because they do not keep their office hours. The school needs to train their staff better I'm actually going to drive out of my way now to go to a school in Louisville so I won't have to deal with these people ever again", 'I haven’t even made it to scheduling and this is already the most trouble I’ve been given by any academic program. And I’ve went to “better” programs. I’m stuck due to a terrible work accident that has left me 100% physically disabled until my surgery soon. I will not be recovered until mid 2025. Due to this I had to relocate a while back to my hometown to have help being taken care of. I can’t stop my life. I have to continue with my credits. I can’t work. I’m a liability. I cannot study ON campus for an unknown amount of time. On top of that I have been diagnosed and treated by a psychologist and clinical psychiatrists for autism and ocd with learning disabilities. I have had so much trouble for months just trying to get to an advisor. The school lost the electronic transcript I paid for. It took months to get that squared away. It was escalated so many times and no one could find it though I have proof that it was received by them. Every day is a new day of hurdles. No one I’ve spoken to seems to be on the same page with anyone else. Everyone has their way of doing it and it’s usually not working then the next person says that’s not the way to do it and it keeps going. Mind you, I was warned by others that it’s not a simple process getting started here. It’s hoops and hurdles and then they scramble the last week to fit you in places. I finally was given an advisors number. I left a message. They did not respond but sent a personal email and it felt rude, short, unhelpful, and basically a big fat I can’t help you. That was David Beckman. I desperately expressed the issues back and how hard it’s been and how I just need to get my classes together and I can’t go in person and everything for me is 4 steps behind compared to able bodied and intellectually abled students. I still haven’t heard from anyone in the disability office there. I explained I cannot do math online and have had to drop it in the past. I’m terrible at it and it has to be done in person so it HAS to wait but everything else should be no problem to get started and whatever obstacles can be overridden. I know because better universities agree. Freakin’ Columbia told me it could wait while working on my cybersecurity until I can get in person and be able to live in a math lab with on campus tutors and professor hours to get through it. My mind does not work that way. I can’t just do it. I have tried numerous times and can’t afford to fail out over and over but he was upset that I reached out to him wanting to know who sent me to him. It was one of the MANY people who you speak to over the phone at bctc. You can’t keep up. Even when you’re not calling them, they have someone calling you who has no idea the struggles you’ve been having wanting to know why you haven’t set up your classes yet. I’m sorry but I don’t have an hour to keep repeating this situation to each random caller. That’s how I keep ending up with a different answer to my issues every other day. I have no one to just go through this with me and help me get to where I need to be. I thought an advisor was that person. Another person I spoke to who works for the college personally apologized for that advisor and said they were going to get me scheduled with someone else. That was all it took to get an appointment with an advisor after months. It’s weeks out and pretty much, nothing can go wrong at that appointment as we won’t have time for that. Not quite sure how I’ll go about making sure everything is done in time. The page on disabilities is so confusing beyond anything I’ve read academically. I don’t have tests. I was diagnosed as an adult. I’ve been medicated. I can get letters, sure, but testing? I was treated in NYC and was told there is not proper adequate autism testing for adults but I was diagnosed without a doubt and given medications for symptoms. As well as OCD/ADHD which overlaps a bit. Either way, if you can go somewhere else, just do so. I’m seriously considering saying forget this and going elsewhere where I’m not such a problem.']

name: Centre College
reviews:
["It's great to see everyone at homecoming. I was very impressed with the new stadium and fieldhouse constructed this year. Nice to see that Norton Center for the Arts continues to offer such a great variety of opportunities for the students and community. Congratulations to the college for their continued recognition for outstanding academics and study abroad.", 'I am sharing this review based on my personal experience as a former student.

During my time at this school, I experienced serious issues related to student safety, discrimination, and the way complaints were handled. I was subjected to harassment by my roommate, including theft and being told to “go back to where I came from.” Disturbingly, this same language was later echoed by members of the school administration when I was threatened with being removed from the program for not responding to emails.

I was also physically assaulted by another student. The school’s response to these incidents was deeply inadequate and caused severe harm to my mental health, with long-lasting consequences.

I understand that not everyone will have the same experience, and the school is not without its strengths. However, my experience was serious enough that I feel a responsibility to warn prospective students to carefully consider whether this is an environment that can truly support them—especially if they are vulnerable or in need of institutional protection.', 'Beautiful campus and town. We were in Danville for another reason but decided to walk through campus since it was a beautiful day and a Centre alum friend recommended it. The glass sculptures on the campus grounds were such a treat to see!', 'Everyone is kind and welcoming! The campus is super clean and easy to navigate.', 'Class of 1994
My time at Centre was extraordinary. The education was top-notch, the faculty were all there for us, and the student body were, simply, wonderful people to whom I owe much gratitude for helping me to become a more civilised and productive member of society. There aren’t many such places. I truly thank our lucky stars that I landed so well.']

name: University of the Cumberlands
reviews:
['The University of the Cumberlands is a great place to study, especially if you’re looking for a supportive and friendly environment. The professors are approachable and genuinely care about students doing well, both academically and personally. Whenever I had questions or needed help, I never felt ignored.

The campus is peaceful and well-maintained, which makes it a good place to focus on studies. Class sizes are reasonable, so you don’t feel like just another number. I also appreciate how the university tries to keep education affordable and provides good resources for students.

It’s located in a small town, so it’s quiet and not very busy, but that can actually be a positive if you prefer a calm atmosphere. Overall, it’s a solid university with caring faculty, a strong sense of community, and good academic support. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a focused and student-friendly college experience.', 'I had a great experience with the University of the Cumberlands. It is a well-respected non-profit university that truly prioritizes student success over profit. The university focuses on delivering quality education at an affordable cost, making higher education accessible to many students.', 'Excellent school, the campus is well maintained (unlike some of the community colleges I toured in my hometown), most the professors are super nice and willing to help me with anything, very accommodating for my disabilities, and while it is a Christian school they are not that strict and there is no real dress code. They also have a lot of stuff on campus like pin making machines, 3D printers, free printing, a pool, clubs and sports, and they make all kinds of activities for students which is pretty cool. Maybe 1-2  of the professors I’ve had my entire time going here weren’t my favorite, but the majority are chill. Also they have free counseling for students, free gym for students, etc. by one price promise they really meant it, once you pay that initial tuition they don’t give you any surprise fees. Definitely love going here and will probably come back if I ever further my education.', "My husband drives for AAA/Boltons and so far we have met nothing but respectable kids and young adults that go to this college. Let's your young adults know we appreciate them being polite and respectable when we come and help them. Love your college", "I absolutely love this campus! It's such a great place to be, surrounded by nature and beautiful hills. The views here are absolutely breathtaking, I can't get enough of them! The only thing is, it's a bit isolated from the airport and shops, but that's not a big deal. Overall, it's a friendly and amazing place to study."]

name: Elizabethtown Community and Technical College
reviews:
['Former student, I needed my Student ID and called a few times with no pick up. The number on google seemed to be acting up if you select any option, so I waited until I was sent automatically to the operator. Wherever I ended up was where I needed to be, she gave me my Student ID after verifying me, and was able to give my start and end dates for my application to my second masters. Good and professional service from ECTC.', 'Cannot find anything about how this school operates. All the important information is so secretive. I hated attending this place. Terrible!!
EDIT - IGNORE THAT REVIEW!! I was upset because they charged me a fee for not returning my books. Even after two weeks and after Christmas break, I came back with the books and they refunded me about 90% of my money! They were so sweet and understanding about it too! ECTC is a lovely start for anyone. I’d recommend it. All the professors are very nice. The school is very clean. Lots of helpful information everywhere! They’re helping me build a better future.', 'Beautiful campus. Lots of updates to the college. Only seen the main part but it is very impressive. If I was returning to college that would be great for me. Instructors and staff along with students very friendly.', 'Staff was extremely professional and very friendly & helpful including the custodian who took time out of her busy day to ask how we were doing and if we needed any help when touring the campus with my foster daughter prior to her starting classes in a couple of days.
The campus was very nice and well maintained.', 'Based upon Veterans services
The college itself is a perfect transition between high school and college or if you are just getting back into school. The veterans service department is one of the worst I have ever had to deal with. I have dealt with them at 2 other universities and never had the issues that I have here. They don’t care about their veterans or helping them succeed. They will tell you to call people they know aren’t in the office (without telling you). They make it as difficult as possible to even speak with someone about their programs. They don’t put out information about veterans events happening on campus until the day of the event. And the coordinators question everything without giving the veteran the benefit of the doubt. The people have job security so their care of the people they are helping is none existent. If I was just the college I was evaluation I would give it 5 stars.']

name: Georgetown College
reviews:
["I don't work at the college, nor am I a student there. I live close to the college.
I walk by there on a daily basis as part of my exercise to help keep me active.
This is what I see when I pass by;
The grounds are very well kept. I see the landscapers out mowing the lawns on a regular basis.
The road has been black topped just this past summer.
There are fresh new cross walks painted on the road for students, faculty, and other pedestrians to cross the road safely.
There are a number of parking lots for students and faculty to park their cars.
There are cross walks leading from the college to the parking lots.
I see the college security making their rounds all the time.
Whenever there is some kind of activity going on at the college, the roads around here are blocked off to help ensure everybody's safety.
the college and surrounding grounds
are well kept, and maintained.
Please like and share.
scott-", "A beautiful campus that inherits such a rich tradition of academics, and success in the NAIA Division.  I feel welcomed every time I am blessed with the opportunity to take pictures, which assist in my introspection into life, and I'm never bothered by the campus security which is there to protect the student from harm....Thank you!!!", "Campus Townhouses are indeed one of the worst I've seen for the amount of money that's being paid especially since you have 6 kids living in them and after the entire summer you go to move your kids in only to see that not only their townhouse but numerous families we talked to moving in saw no cleaning was done and walls need patched and painted not to mention a massive water leak in the one the closets. $55,000  a year and this is the living conditions you offer.  I'm sure like every other complaint that the college will not address any of them. Here I thought UK was bad for putting 3 kids to a room this year but it seems Georgetown would much rather give you plenty of room and never fix any issues where you live. I hope everyone else that has kids here brings a cleaning crew and a mold inspection kit with them before they chance letting their kids stay here.", 'If you care about your child’s well being at all, DO NOT MAKE THEM LIVE ON CAMPUS. You’d be sick if you saw what the actual living conditions look like. They never clean the rooms, ever. There’s graffiti, nail clippings, and everything else. Seniority doesn’t matter, they will have you live in a Greek life dorm- even if you aren’t part of Greek life. They are awful at communicating as well. Do not put your child here.', 'I cannot in good conscious recommend this school to anyone who can’t afford it on their own (through scholarships, grants, etc.) However, if you can afford to go there, it’s a great institution. Unfortunately, I know too many grads who took out too many student loans, and didn’t realize the negative impact that would have on them in their 20s.

Georgetown afforded me many opportunities as an undergrad that had I attended a larger school, probably never would have happened. I can honestly say, that Georgetown had a positive impact on me. Based soley on my experience, I would give it 5 stars.

With that said, if you can’t afford to go there, please attend a less expensive school. You can get a degree that is just as good elsewhere.']

name: Henderson Community College
reviews:
['Hate seeing the negative reviews on a place that is obviously doing great work in the education world. Beautiful campus, nice facilities, but most importantly EXCELLENT staff members.

I’m a very non-traditional student, and coming here for a chance to reset and work on my career through a local college with ties to a University is first and foremost a gift to the area. The campus itself is very accommodating and lots of upgrades are being installed and built out.

The team at HCC along with the Murray State staff are accommodating and incredibly helpful. An added bonus, the Kentucky Career Center is based here, and for folks like myself who have gone through life changes - it’s a hidden gem.', 'I had the unfortunate experience of going to an event and the college is not up to code for the disabled.  No one was directing traffic for the event which was a madhouse for the guest speaker David Pelzer the author of a Child called It and people were parking in spots that blocked the side walk.  The lecture hall we went into did not have a disabled button to automatically open the doors.  We had to go out of our way to follow a strangely placed sidewalk in 19 degrees weather to come back around to where the stairs ended.  This college is not set up for the disabled at least in the area that we were in.  I was so disappointed!  The lecture hall had minimal seating for the disabled but we were able to get a spot where I could set my wheelchair and watch the guest speaker.  I will not be returning for any future events at this time.  Because the side walk was not right I was forced to get out of my wheelchair to get back on the parking lot and almost fell down.  Something needs to be done for the disabled at this college.  I feel sorry for anyone that requires adaptive equipment or accessibility that attends events or the college.  I will be reaching out to the appropriate company or individual to address this issue.  This was my first time attending at event here and I am so sorry for anyone that had or has the same experience.', 'Worst nursing school ever. Majority of Staff read power points. They let you have rap battles like on 8 mile. Better yet you can have a professor who says, "I seen," every 5 seconds. High failure rate, no advocate for the students.', "Henderson Community College library staff are always willing to help out and if they don't know anything about the topic you're working on, they will get you to someone who does.", 'Great place for graduation today.']

name: Jefferson Community and Technical College
reviews:
["You'll be forced to complete 20 applications before you're able to enroll in classes. Don't waste your time.", 'Dont waste your time especially when it comes to the advising center everyone working there is lazy and terrible at their job sat there for 2 hours waiting then all of a sudden told to form a line so even though i was there first was put to the back of the line because all the ladies would rather talk their nonsense than actually do their jobs, you are only a paycheck to them they do not care about any of you', 'Troy works in enrollment, when I called after returning back to school 11 years after last being enrolled and having you discontinue because my sons father fell ill to terminal cancer I reached my top enrollment because they had been leaving messages to call on my voicemail. I had enrolled and did my placement exam and had my official transcripts sent. Troy told me he didn’t know why they call me and he didn’t have any answers and there was nothing he could tell me. I have voicemails I had explain asking me to call back this number.  I ask him his name he said Troy I explained that I had an email where they also said they didn’t have my transcripts. When I ask for his agent ID he refused and told me he would be disconnecting the call. My concern is as a woman that is middle age returning to school while I have to college students one at U of L and one at WKU , being treated so poorly in Louisville Ky where us wanting our youth to have quality resources is very much of concern. It would be good for Troy to take some culture diversity classes and understand that how he treats new and returning students can be the determining factor whether a person gives up or says forget school all together. His dismissive approach and no resources or redirection to someone that could help me is and was very discouraging. I would say our community deserves better and Troy whether a veteran at deterring people or a veteran at turning people away should be held accountable and taught how to resolve conflicts or circumstances that he isn’t familiar with. I don’t know if it was the end of a work day bc I work out of state and am on central time or if it was the attitude of having to explain and go a loyalty beyond the call of duty to offer me the same respect and dignity the other specialist offered me. But in our community that we are losing many to senseless gun violence and drug overdoses as well as poverty and lack of education I would hope that someone his position would be more fluid and concern of the lasting impact he has on those that are depending on him to help find the answers sought and make it is duty to help Louisvillians to return to school or be enrolled timely.', "ONE OF OUR CITY BEST

name: Kentucky State University
reviews:
['⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Kentucky State University (KSU) is an incredible place of learning, offering students a nurturing and supportive environment to pursue their academic and professional goals. The campus is beautifully laid out, with plenty of green spaces and state-of-the-art facilities that make it an ideal place to study and grow. Whether you’re attending for undergraduate or graduate programs, KSU offers a diverse range of educational opportunities that set students up for success.

The faculty and staff at KSU are always there to help, creating a welcoming atmosphere where students feel supported in every step of their academic journey. The university also has an active student life, with various clubs, events, and activities to keep things exciting outside of the classroom.

As Kentucky continues to grow in many ways, one of the exciting developments has been the expansion of the legal cannabis industry. As the owner of a licensed, verified dispensary, I’m proud to be part of this growing, regulated market in Kentucky. Our dispensary focuses on providing top-quality cannabis products in a safe, professional environment, and it’s great to see the state embracing this industry in such a responsible and regulated way. For students or visitors interested in learning more, I highly recommend exploring the legal, safe cannabis market in Kentucky.

Kentucky State University is not only an excellent place for education but also a great community that connects students to the wider developments happening in the state, including the evolving legal cannabis industry. Whether you’re a student, prospective applicant, or visitor, KSU is a place that welcomes growth and opportunity for everyone.', 'Becoming a leader starts here!!!!

The Kentucky State University ROTC program develops our future leaders in the US Army and in our country.

We provide students/cadets 3, 2, and 1 year scholarships to those who are eligible and are willing to take the next step.

Come visit us!!!!', "Kentucky State is not somewhere i will ever send my child back too! They have no concern or care for out of town students! They claim they help the out of state students but they don't.  They are putting the students out 3 day before the assigned date. Again no concern for out of state students. Save your money! name: Kentucky Christian University
reviews:
['My wife and I took our son here for a football college visit. From the start, the staff treated us with love and appreciation. The campus is small and has a tight nit community. Everyone we encountered had a genuine love.  This is a good Christian College and I would NOT be disappointed if our son decided to go here for college.', 'Why did Kentucky Christian University NOT support Kim Davis when she was jailed for not issuing marriage license to a same sex marriage couple? I spoke with students at their location, to determine if / how I might assist, and was told  they were warned by the college admin NOT to attend the protest, with threats of expulsion! Also at the protest I saw zero advertisement / support from Kentucky Christian University faculty or students.

Exactly what type of religion does Kentucky Christian University claim?', "I'm a 2014 Alumni. When I was there, the first year was a bit rough, but I got in the swing of things.

In my sophomore year I had fantastic grades.

However, in my last 2 years I started getting sick of KCU. Why is that?

First off, I am furious that you spent so much money on your sports programs. We came here for the Word of God, not football, basketball, volleyball etc.

Your athletes were obnoxious to be around. They have all the attention of the university, and if one of your many workout machines broke, I got stupid emails raising money to replace it.

Meanwhile, the hot tub remained completely broken for the vast majority of the time I was there, and the pool table lost its balance, and you did NOTHING to resolve the issue, as readily as you did that workout equipment.

To make things worse, you forced all the athletes in the library at 7pm regularly, where they would constantly disrupt other students and make lots of noise, despite numerous reprimands.

Basically, your rulebook had no teeth whatsoever. It was nothing more than arbitrary. Students were vaping in the dorms, and nothing was done about them.

And chapel: let me discuss that. In my freshman year I attended every time no problem.

However, by the time of my junior year, I noticed students leaving chapel early against the rules, going on their cell phone, and nobody was openly reprimanded for dissing mandatory chapel.

In direct response, I started sneaking out in the middle, knowing I could be put on chapel probation if caught. Why would I do that? Because I didn't want to be there.

Nobody else was following the rules or wanted to be there. Why should I care? You don't squeeze God in a busy schedule: you find quiet time, away from everyone else, to reflect on the Word of God.

And to make things worse, going to Church on Sunday did NOT count towards mandatory chapel attendance.

How are you going to encourage adult students to follow Christ wholeheartedly, if they are penalized for normal church attendance,

and forced into chapels full of young people who are much more concerned about the giant lunch line and their next class, compared to the sermon?

And last but not least: the students were NOT the most godly individuals, especially the freshman students and student athletes. They were foul mouthed, blasphemous, and did not properly represent the Christian faith and sound doctrine.

In fact, during your talent show performance in the evening in either 2013 or 2014, you had a guy openly proposing to another guy, and announcing first gay marriage in KCU, while everyone else cheered.

Despicable! That's a blatant violation of both OT and NT. If he had done that 10 years earlier Kris would have arranged to have those 2 wolves in sheep's clothing expelled in a New York second, and now they're flaunting their blasphemy and past affiliation with KCU on Facebook.

By the time of my senior year, I was so sick of KCU, that I didn't care about my slipping grades. I just wanted to graduate and move on, and sure enough I did.

And don't expect me to donate money to your university. You mismanaged the university finances so badly, that staff had to move on after I left.

Support a university without more solid, Christian values and stupid rules that are arbitrarily enforced? Never!

As Jesus Christ said in Revelation to the churches: Repent, or I will remove your lampstand from its place.", "The perfect school if you are looking for a small Christian university, but it isn't perfect for everyone. The facilities are nothing special, but the people are. Anyone who wants to have a unique, Christ-centered college career will fit in perfectly. Those looking to let loose and have a crazy time probably won't enjoy it here.", 'I attended this school from 2005-2010. Most of the professors were kind and well intentioned educators who took an active role in the lives of their students. Sadly, many of these people have retired. This university is in the middle of no where. If you live in Ohio, West Virginia, Kentucky, or Tennessee, you may enjoy attending school here. If you are outside of this geographic area, you may struggle to fit in and find things to do, as Grayson, the city the school is in, is a glorified truck stop. I graduated with $35,000 dollars in debt and want to strongly encourage any student to consider how much debt you may leave with at the end of a four year degree. This was after the GI Bill and a few thousand dollars of payments each semester. I think it is deplorable that KCU straps ministry students with this kind of debt. If you happen to marry someone from the university, like myself, you will most likely marry someone else with an exorbitant amount of debt. Please think through the ramifications of signing up for this debt and how it will impact your life, ministry, and personal finances. It is possible to serve God and attend another Christian school without incurring this kind of debt. Liberty University is a strong Christian school and they are growing. Ultimately, KCU was a great place for me. The best decision I have ever made, outside of following Christ, was marrying my wife. This school provided me with an opportunity to meet her. In hindsight, I would do it all over again. Pros: one on one with professors, solid Christian education, and the opportunity to practice ministry. Cons: small campus, leave with thousands in debt (think 35,000), meal quality, and lousy living accommodations for on campus students. Best of luck to you in your search and God bless.']

name: Lindsey Wilson College
reviews:
['As a parent, I want my kids to have an awesome experience but also have fun and BE SAFE! Well, I couldn’t be more thrilled of my son’s choice to attend Lindsey Wilson College this Fall!

Madison Bryant - has successfully done her job when recruiting my son to LWC! From the beginning she has been an excellent representative of LWC with her kind and fun personality, really opening up and sharing her love for LWC from her days as a student. Reilly came home from school one day stating he filled out an info form because the girl seemed nice. Then the hand written notes kept coming and Reilly’s name was always spelt correctly; that’s an important detail where many other colleges failed. Madison even started the process of roommate assignments asking questions to find a roommate to match with Reilly. He has worked hard to get to where he is now and I am so thrilled he found a college that really resonated with him. Thank you Madison you are a key reason Reilly chose Lindsey Wilson College. Go Raiders!

Bradley Karnes - went above and beyond by airing my tire up and informed me it wasn’t going to hold air. He the offered to change my tire and put on a spare! Definitely makes me feel like safety is a top priority for LWC!

The entire staff was kind, friendly and helpful during our visit! Our Tour Guide, said friendly hellos, greetings said by name to each other is really welcoming and homey feeling!

#classof2025 #LWCRaiders', "I'm out in Bolivia right now, but plan to come back, only spent one year here and it was super fun, loved being a part of the singers and cant wait to come back for 2027!", 'Daughter is starting school here today.  Love everything about it so far.   Everyone is so helpful and nice.', "I believe this could be the best University to Grad from, my journey was impeccably amazing with the syllabus and the professor and staff of this school is marvellous I'm proud to be called as a blue raider All thanks to the Creator and my family specially my friends who helped me complete this Achievement with joy and happiness.", 'Dropped off our Freshman kiddo last week (Aug 2023) & learned a few good things ...
1) If arriving early to campus (many athletes do), there's not much guidance on where to go/how to start.  So.....
-  1st:  Admin Bldg (LR McDonald), 3rd floor & get Student ID.
-  2nd: get room key (housing info on MyLWC Portal) at Residence Life Offices (small round-hut-bldg just down from water tower).
- if you kid needs a sport physical, the Campus Nurse does these at the Biggers Center, her email is on LWC Site.
2) Our son met his RA & he was really great.  Important - it's a DRY campus & NO smoking.  EITHER ONE can get you ejected from your sport-team (not sure about academically, but they are REALLY strict about these rules).....some kids last year tested this & were immediately excused from their teams.
3) In most girls dorms, RA will get male visitors ID upon arrival & return it only when they leave (no overnight guests/boys after visiting hours).  Same visiting hours with boys, but don't think they check/get ID's like girls dorm?
4) Rooms are small!  They have a mattress, bedframe, desk & dresser (3-drawer) & a short (4-foot?) closet bar/pole & a shelf above.  Walls (in his) were cream painted cinder block.
- Bring plastic bins for under-bed storage, you can fit 3 x 66-qt (you could also use plastic drawers, but our son wanted airtight bins, which is smart in a male athletes dorm!).
- *bed was a twin NOT twin XL* (Horton Hall Freshm.Dorm) **bring a mattress encasement unless you don't care about germs at all**  We also brought a mattress foam topper.
- you mite want an office chair, the chair they provide is metal folding chair type.
- there is room for a mini-fridge & microwave, we also brought a Keurig AND an air purifier (recommended by his Advisor).  We also brought a smaller air-tight bin (20 qt?) to keep food items in, these buildings are older & probably have critters!
-**bring at least one surge-protector that is 10-ft long, bring TWO if you bring refer/microwave....the dorms don't have many plugs & they are old.  We found a great "surge-bar" at WMart with 6-8 plugs spaced apart & had a 10-ft cord.  Perfect for all small appliances to plug into. Then we had a 2nd one for his PC equipment. BE SURE to get NEW surge protector strips - this area gets brown outs & surges & it will kill electronics QUICK.  Surge Protectors only last about 1-2 years!
- a nice bonus is to get them a LifeStraw Pitcher or Bottle
- Horton Hall, Laundry (get them laundry pods!) was on 1st floor & bathrooms (each floor) are community bathrooms, so shower shoes & a bath-caddy are def helpful!
5) Freshman do NOT need a car!  Everything on campus is SUPER close.  Our son found friends within 24 hours he could catch a ride to WalMart with for incidentals.  So while it might be nice for them to have it, it's certainly not "needed".

Hope this helps!']

name: University of Louisville
reviews:
['First time visit to campus.

First impressions.  Smaller than I imagined.
feels modern and safe. Nice facilities.

might be a challenge on busy traffic days.

Louisville is nearby, and what a fun city it is.', 'University of Louisville is where I am doing my PhD. I really love what I do and my supervisor, professor Sharp, is a great person both in research and personally. I learnt a lot from him. I am in mechanical engineering school. They have been spending a lot of money recently to renovate all the instruments in the mechanical workshop. For example they added five new 3d printer for students to play with. For the measurement lab, a couple of new instruments have been purchased that are really awesome. Fluid mechanics lab also has new facilities to explore different aspects of the fluid mechanics concepts. Being a lab TA, I can tell for sure that all the ME students are enjoying the new facilities.
They have also been hiring top ranked new faculty members. I know some of them, they are from very top universities and can add to the reputation of the ME department. So if you are thinking about joining the engineering group in University of Louisville, do not hesitate to do that. Good luck with your study and have fun.', 'Attending UofL was the worst mistake of my life. Hit with many hidden fees, invalid & uncontestable charges, being taken advantage of and pressured the entire time I was there/before I had even started attending. My life has only gotten worse.', 'It’s very average. The parking department is absolutely the worst of them all. Grass growing high everywhere. reviews: ["40 min wait for chic fillet not enough seating even if I stayed which I did not their food isnt worth wasting my time iam not a student with nothing to do all day c'mon sodexo step it up ???", 'Cost, fees, and everything they can throw at you constantly change. Lie to students about help they will receive, deny all credits coming into college. Refuse to send transcripts that were paid. Accept loan & pell grant money on students behalf that no longer attend.', 'Nice athletic facilities, campus as a whole, just average', 'I am a transfer student that transferred over from Alabama and only spent one semester here. name: Northern Kentucky University
reviews:
["Very bland campus. All of the buildings look the same from the outside, but most of the buildings are pretty nice on the inside. The main reason this campus is getting a 3 star is because there are geese just walking around and they relieve themselves where ever they want. And the university doesn't seem to care at all. If you walk anywhere near the Business college or the Math building there is a 99% chance you step in geese poop, and if you get lucky and don't you will spend your whole walk trying to avoid it.", 'Beautiful campus, love the Student Union and Rec Center. Looking forward to taking our Bachelor Bound Students on our 3rd annual campus visit.', 'Grandfather passed away and the school sent me to collections after I dropped my classes. For a school that only cares about money surely education is good right? Nope! Go anywhere but here.', 'This would be one star had it not been for my professors who, for the most part, were pretty great people who were/are great at their jobs and who had to deal with the same administrative BS as I did. They all need raises for dealing with admin as long as they have.

To get right into it, The top administration here is a mess. There is a mandatory campus recreation fee that you can't opt out of even if you have never been to the the rec center. What happened was they wanted to build a rec center but no one was buying memberships to get in. Their solution? Require their students to pay for a membership every semester. By the time I graduate, I will have paid $1000 for a rec center that I've not been to once. I don't know why they decided to invest millions in a new rec center if they didn't know for sure that their students would use it. Another example: one of their last presidents was straight-up abusing school funds and instead of firing him and suing him, they paid him $1,000,000 to leave?!? Like go get your money back and stop charging us fees for breathing on campus!?

Additionally, their policies are out-right awful. For example: I'm a student that receives tuition assistance through my work; it takes a while to get to the school and NKU knows this. Do they provide the itemized bill earlier in order to apply for TA sooner? No. Do they make is easier for my work to contact them to let them know my TA is on the way? No. You have until the first day of classes to pay your entire bill or you get kicked from your classes and the reinstatement fee is $100. To avoid this, you can get on the payment plan which is $90; I literally have to pay them money for me to be able to pay them more money. To avoid getting kicked out of classes my first week I have to pay $190. There used to be a two-week grace period but they removed it for whatever reason. Another example is their parking pass policy, it's annoying that they increase the price every year, but with the cost of yearly maintenance it at least makes sense. The thing that particularly bothers me is that they charge their teachers to park. They literally have to be there, and unless they want to walk a half mile every morning they're stuck buying a pass. When I started going to NKU, parking was $286 a year for students and they charged their teachers $400...

Things constantly don't work on campus. There are the usual vending machines and school computers not working which isn't that big a deal, but the most frustrating example is the "NKU All Card". You have to pay $45-$60 bucks a semester for a mandatory food budget but whenever you try to use it at the student union or any of the vending machines, the All Card gets declined. This happens even if you have enough money on the card to cover what you're getting.

If something goes wrong (as it most likely will), dealing with the staff is hit or miss. Sometimes you'll get the most condescending Karen who looks down on you because you don't know the myriad of the school's useless policies. Other times, you'll talk to a talk a genuinely kind person that understands your frustration and really tries to help. One example being that at my last major, I couldn't get into any classes because I was kind of behind on credits so I was in one of the last groups to be able to register for classes. Now, this part was my fault and I totally accept that, what wasn't helpful is when I reached out to my adviser and department head for help, they sent me nothing but platitudes, no solutions. If I had stuck with that major, I would have graduated two years later than I originally planned.

At the end of the day, going to school at NKU is like getting your groceries at the dollar store. It's not the best option, heck, it's not even a good option, but it will satisfy the basic need at hand. If you want to open up more options in your life, try a trade or community college first, don't assume that you need a college degree to be successful in life. It's not worth the fees and the headache to deal with administration of a college like NKU.', "NKU is a fantastic university and I'm proud to day I'm an alum!!!!  My latest experience, though, was for the GRAD Cincinnati Summer Institute.  We were able to allow 30 high school students from Cincinnati Public Schools to stay on campus in the dorms and immerse themselves on campus.  The students were there for 3 days and 2 nights, experienced several academic programs, and ate their meals in the dining hall.  The GRAD Cincinnati Summer Institute was a great success, and we are lucky to have such a great partner in NKU.  They really are a first class institution!!!!!"]

My son has an issue with his classes and they were very helpful also with financial  aide', 'Went to University of Louisville Dental practice they were extremely nice people and are gonna help me fix my teeth. So grateful to find a place close that accepts Medicaid. So for any adults who have had trouble in dealing with that check them out and give them a chance. I think they might surprise you.', 'Be aware that WKCTC makes all students take FYE 105 even though it is not required for AAS students and is not a degree requirement.  This is a huge money maker for WKCTC and they offer this class to high school students in order to count them in their enrollment to make it sound like they have more students for awards, etc.  This is a scam!  My FYE teacher required a 10 page plus paper and closed the class 2 weeks early.  My experience at Murray State was like daylight and dark from WKCTC.  Also, I was locked out of my online blackboard class during my finals week one semester and I tried to talk to someone on campus and they just kept giving me the run around sending me to a company that is not associated with KCTCS who did not know what they were doing.  All I needed was to have my password changed and it took multiple days causing me to almost miss my final.  Finally, my math class was nothing more than Mymath lab.  I am not even sure why they had a teacher teaching the class.  My guess is that they pay their instructors so little that they cannot find proper instructors. Several of my instructors were great, but one did not teach me anything and was constantly on a smoke break.  Again, my time at MSU was a much better experience even though it was much more expensive.  It is definitely worth it!']

reviews: ["Visited the Combs Eye Clinic today.  The staff, doctors, and students were great.  All through the eye exam they took time to explain what they were doing and the results of the tests. name: Big Sandy Community and Technical College
reviews: ["I wanted to join Big Sandy's nursing program, with my previous history at another KCTCS school I thought it was going to be an easy process. name: Somerset Community College
reviews: ['I went for two separate state exams where if taken courses online and it was easy in and easy out. name: Spalding University
reviews:
['I had the opportunity to interview for the PsyD program at Spalding University, and although I was not offered admission in the final decision, I truly want to share how positive and respectful my experience was throughout the entire process.

From start to finish, the communication was clear, professional, and thoughtful. A special thank you to Elizabeth, the administrative coordinator at SOPP, who was incredibly supportive, responsive, and kind from day one until the final decision (even the rejection 😊).', "I would even give 1 star to this graduate university. name: Sullivan University
reviews:
['Waste of my time and money! The workforce grants did not cover enough for the tuition. Financial aid informed me that they could use part of the workforce grants to cover the technology fee. Then, later I got surprise saying I had to pay it in full. What a joke. Also, the instructor was not helpful and harsh in grading. Too many writing assignments in all my classes. I would never go back to this school. The tuition is way too much for the poor quality of the online courses. Definitely not much of teaching and had to learn mostly on my own. AVOID if you are nearly homeless like me', 'I'm writing this about Sullivan's College of Technology and Design, which has shut down, but you should know about the parent organization Sullivan and how it operates, the people involved and it's business practices.

SCTD was an awful experience. Let me start with saying a few of the instructors were OK, did a good job. However, this school is very expensive when compared to other schools, and the "lifetime job placement" is a joke. They won't even respond to you after a few years, beyond doing anything above simply responding. Add to that, any person who's gotten the itch to learn a trade can otherwise find a mentor/employer and learn from youtube videos. That's gotten me 10x further than the extraordinary student loans that I'm still paying on to this day (grad 2009).

About those bad instructors: my "Networking" class instructor was clearly RACIST. Read that again. RACIST. Day in and day out, he would give the 2 black students easy questions "what color are the clouds" while the other 8 of us white students got "explain thermodynamics" EVERY DAY. This instructor laughed at me when I told him that wireless-N is a networking protocol, and that modern cell phones have IP addresses. Read that again. My NETWORKING instructor laughed at this knowledge to his student (me) and said "that doesn't exist" and "phones don't have IP's!" RACIST. He never spoke with this kind of arrogance and disregard to the 2 black students, ever! He was always kind, super gentle and never telling the 2 black students they were wrong, even if they had answered totally wrong like "the clouds are purple". When I brought this treatment to the Dean, she completely threw my complaints in my face with super nasty attitude, she did not care or follow up on this.

Now about the A+ class instructor. She literally knew nothing at all about computers. She rambled about God and some Christian band with one student who liked her, for months. She talked about mostly nothing to do with technology for months. She would generally just read information from a paper or book, but steer the class discussion clear of any deeper inquiry into any subject. Because she didn't knew actually nothing about the subject beyond the words should could read.

Do your homework before you think about going to this place.', 'My experience at Sullivan University has been one of the most rewarding chapters of my academic journey. From the very beginning to now, as I graduate with my master’s degree and pursue my Ph.D., I have felt supported every step of the way.

The professionalism, dedication, and encouragement from the instructors and faculty have been unmatched. I truly believe I would not have made it this far without their guidance.

For anyone considering going back to school or just starting out, Sullivan is an excellent choice. With the resources and support available, success is not just possible......it’s expected.', 'I have called multiple times to the bursar’s office to pay my last payment. Every call went to voicemail and after leaving a message and call back number I never was contacted back. Now I’m sent to collections for a payment I have been trying to pay for 5 months now.', 'After reading, I had to say something good, and with reason.

You are going to have to pay, or take debt. And I failed a class due to mental health and had to pay 450$ for a class. I wasn't mad, I could have failed, and not got it,. And they were so nice! Dwayne said it was so low that I could be steady with payments, but try to increase. He was smart, and knew we don't wanna relax and pay the bill we wanna be smart and efficient.

I graduated here once for Cannabusiness, it's a very open minded program, not a lot of exact knowing, unless into the science side you want your facts. The teachers even to call out Professor Renfro for the society side of things, and then Professor Dean for making sure you don't get a lose win situation, and know how to really be professional. Both with military backgrounds! AND THEY WORK IN CANNABIS HA!

I have had the most supportive team in my experience here, it's not so crowded like colleges. Which I like. I want that private, and just more ideology, than to have the trend of people you know. That's everywhere.

I will say, if you're going to go, I want to let you know I'm a Alumni, with tattoos on his face , and hands and neck. I am currently in Web Developer certificate path in their system again, and going to double graduate. I only am spending about 16k for both. That is hilarious, a new car is more, but I got 2 career fields for less.

If you're smart, it's about how you play the system that is offered.

And when I say that, they give career advisors, don't think you know it all about your field. You're the learner. Go to the career fields even if you don't get what you want. I "want" Microsoft to show up, but imagine getting a gig at a restaurant setting up IT and working POS and having more fun, just due to them needing it that time and heard your background and seen how you are.

You have an advisor, check up on them and tell them how you're doing and failing, don't call the teachers 12am at night. If you email them, explain, and follow up with a call that helps mostly, then you can get everything cleared and resolved, they also can find resources, so you're not sinking more, there's more hands and buckets for it.

IT support is educated and very professional. I have had a good time in intro to programming and principals of tech with Professor Tran, and Bratcher. I've taken computers as a job, and reduced my time on it to a complete hault. All I do is go to typerracer.com, use pandora, and singe-player games now. This made me having more security in future, and current. It's not cyber, but knowing how things work made me evolve into seeing more. And the books aren't just random, you get almost everything you need and why for your career, not just do and code.

I wish the campus was more live like. We lost a lot due to Covid, so if you are hoping to have this "University Experience" that you usually pay tons of money to live at a college. Then maybe look at Lexington if they are more lively, or something else. This is the "School of Doing", and I realized it's not busy because people are doing things.

- Hunter Ingram
(Sullivan Alumni)
lokicoding98 - Github']

name: Bossier Parish Community College
reviews: ["Awesome experience and tour with Sydney and her team! Highly recommend anyone who's interested in attending here.   BPCC has so much to offer.", 'Definitely a mixed bag. Let me first say that for a Community College, it’s pretty good. The cost, classes and flexibility are decent. From my experience and the experience of my friends and family, the faculty and professors are extremely burnt out and can be very unprofessional at times. The biggest issue I had during my time here was the fact that the faculty had changed my major to a transfer student without my permission. I have no idea how this was even possible, as I’m fairly certain a student has sign off and document when changing their major. When I asked the faculty how this happened, the worker just shrugged and said “I don’t know”. Some of my advisors were also very rude and I would get different answers to the same question depending on who I asked. Overall, I would recommend this school to people if they know for certain what they want to do and if they have a plan.', "Haven't had any issues yet. Professor's are pretty friendly and pleasant to talk to. Classrooms are kept clean and everything is well maintained. Parking is eh, spaces are limited and pretty tight even for people driving smaller vehicles. Bathrooms seem to be a little ancient but they work for what they are.", "I went to BPCC for one semester and hated it. The teachers I had didn't give clear information and I was lucky if any of them knew what they were doing while teaching. The campus is really nice and clean but the people are not  friendly. I had to transfer today and I talked to 3 different people, 2 of the 3 were very rude. The other person genuinely wanted to help me and was interested in the wellness of my future.", "I have had nothing but wonderful experiences at this school.  I've gone to three different colleges in my life, and I can say from all that experience, this is hands down the best school I've been to.  Now I can't say that all degree programs are great because I personally am only taking communication classes and art classes, but I haven't heard anything horrible from anyone else either.  I really feel they're the least money hungry college I've been to because they actually CARE if you graduate or are doing well in your classes and your well being in general.  Most schools couldn't care less if you flunk out, they have your money and are happy about it.  But here they follow up on everything and are very pushy (in a good way) to get you to talk to your advisors and counselors to help you through anything you need help doing.  I'd highly recommend."]

name: Centenary College of Louisiana
reviews:
['Had Fun at Football Game I have Been to Every Home Game. Since they Started playing 3 Years Ago', 'Easter Sunrise Service was really beautiful at Centenary College’s Hargrove Memorial Amphitheater.', 'LONG REVIEW INCOMING: I mostly enjoyed my time here as a student. being such a small school, your time here will 100% be what you make of it. faculty and staff were generally great, save for some minor and isolated complaints i have with those who i never had to interact with much in the first place (looking at you psych department and admissions office). i will not feed you a lie that it is all sunshine and rainbows, as there have been times where i was quite angry as a whole with centenary as an institution but for me, the good definitely outweighs the bad. students are generally tolerable in my experience, there are absolute gems of people you can find if you are open and kind. it is hard for me to make a statement as a whole about the student body, but I can say that they tend to be either "rich" students who come from financially well-off families that or students who come from poverty who managed to be able to afford to attend thanks to scholarships funded by generous donors, lots who are even homeless and would have no place to go if not for the dorms. in my experience, there's been few genuinely "in the middle" students who come from situations that don't fall in those categories. I have also noticed that perhaps students like to gossip and "word travels fast at centenary" is generally accepted as common knowledge, though i am unsure if that is genuinely a 'centenary thing' or if it is consequence of something else like the small student body or the general age range of young undergrad college students. those who attend centenary tend to be 'traditional' straight-to-college-from-high school students, which can cause upset if you are someone with a non-traditional education path. i entered centenary as a 19 year old freshman in 2019, due to turn 20 that academic year and it honestly ended up getting quite annoying how often my peers would remark upon it, with some even seemingly being genuinely shocked i was a college freshman at 19 despite how normal that is. if you are entering centenary as a freshman and don't fall within the age range of 17 ~ 18, do be prepared to deal with some people (a small amount, but there nonetheless) genuinely being shocked by it or looking down on you for it. in my experience, being selective at first about who you tell your year and letting yourself first be judged based on your character when possible has been helpful as the "ew freshman" mindset of upperclassmen that is quite prevalent in high school is still going strong at centenary.

As someone queer, i feel LGBT students are  generaly safe with and respected by staff&faculty, though, do not expect a feeling of camaraderie amongst LGBT students since the campus's LGBT-centered club for students is lacking in attendance+interest, with only a tiny dedicated group of students keeping it alive. The general campus climate for LGBT students is okay, and I do not feel that lgbt students are in any particular danger of being maliciously targeted due to their identity.

there is more, but i cannot fit it all here so...

HIGHLY recommend if: you're interested in studying abroad (the opportunities are unmatched), want to study in a setting where you will be in the presence of professors who tend to generally care about your success, are a student who will thrive in classes of small size, interested in rigorous academics, open minded and willing to embrace new people+information&experiences with respect, are a STEM student (bio&neurosci profs are great and cent's engineering 3/2 program is unique) who wants to be well-prepared for post-grad studies, want a school that can leave you well educated on topics in many areas', 'This is a very old liberal arts college. Once on the outskirts of town, it is now at the heart of the city. With a lovely walking path garden full of trees and flowers from around the area, each noted and described with small placards, this campus is very pleasant. A small radio station (KSCL) gives students and locals some experience in local broadcasting as well as a small voice for unusual music.', 'CENTENARY IS AN AMAZING COLLEGE.  THEY REALLY CARE ABOUT their students. SAMANTHA will be travel to Paris for 3 weeks.  It will be a amazing experience for her. Starting a new journey in her life.  Please pray for her às her college journey will so']

name: Delgado Community College
reviews: ['Someone took out a student loan under my name at this school. According to aidvantage and recent reviews it seems this happens a lot at Delgado. I’m not sure why they’re not being held accountable or being investigated. It’s beyond me how this is allowed to happen. Lots of people are struggling dealing with student loan fraud. It took endless amounts of phone calls from me and aidvantage to pry the information out of them. It took a total of 8 months for them to complete their investigation. They will be in no hurry to help you. Maybe they should start checking fraudulent applications closer so it doesn’t happen in the first place. The investigation department at this school sucks and they don’t care.', 'This place has gone down hill. I have degrees from another college and never had the problems with financial aid that I do here. I now go to their sister school (which gave me absolutely no issues). The financial aid office is joke. I was approved with fasfa on my end but Delgado denied it on theirs. I had to pay out of pocket for two semesters and enough was enough. They then took out financial aid and I was paying cash still. I just reported them to the Department of Education this week because I am not paying for that loan when at their sister school they are actually using my Pell. I have never accepted a refund because I don’t want the debt and Delgado has not done a thing to help me in the financial aid department. I wanted to come here for Spring but once again was denied financial aid. Credits from her transferred to their sister school and I now attend there. Do better!!!?!', "Apparently this place gets hits with loan fraud a lot according to Aidvantage. I never went to this school but was a victim of identity loan fraud here. It's unfortunate no one does their due diligence to check on the application, they just take the money. The picture is the address they put on the fake loan application. The last time I got a little bit of help from them to get this corrected was in August. It is now December.", 'I love it here! This school and its education have always been underrated. I can’t thank them enough for the doors they have helped me open along the transfer path. I am just one semester away from graduating. All I can say is the classes might be a little expensive but they definitely make up for it. If you ever find yourself struggling make sure to reach your closest professors. They are always pleasant in welcoming to help.', 'So, the financial aid counselor straight up lied to my family and I. We were told that I do not have to pay ANYTHING, and will not have to pay anything for school because of fasfa & scholarships. Yeah, wish I didn’t listen to them. $1800 in debt for classes I didn’t even get a chance to take. When you call the school and let them know that there must’ve been a mistake they practically fuss at you. Then tell you pay it asap or it goes to collections. Been fighting this for months and nobody will take accountability for this.']

name: Nunez Community College
reviews: ["I got accepted into this school about 3 weeks ago and can not register for classes. I have been trying to contact the school going on a month without any success. At this point I just want to go to another school, but cannot register anywhere else due their system showing that I'm enrolled there. I was told to contact Nunez from the other colleges so that I can get enrolled, I can not cancel my acceptance because NO ONE EVER ANSWERS THE PHONE!!!!! I guess I will have to travel 9 hours to the school to request a cancelation. Hopefully, it's not an abandoned building once I arrive.", "I'm obsessed with Nunez. After being out of traditional education environments for 20 years, I would not have been able to navigate college without help. The staff and faculty are invested and kind and brilliant!", 'This school so far is unprofessional. I can’t get into contact with ANYONE about my ebook that’s aid for with finaid. I emailed them a total of 40 times, called, left voicemails, wrote on their FB, and contacted the instructor who can’t even help. I have to navigate through the course without a book lmao I refuse to pay for it when it’s already paid for but they just not putting it on my course. I suggest you find another school because if I knew it was going to be like this I would’ve found another school who has the program I’m enrolled in. I don’t live in Nola so it’s hard to go there. My classes are online.', 'This is a great school to attend.  While they may not offer as many programs as some of the larger community colleges, they still offer a lot. And all the classes I ever took there were small in size and taught by excellent professors.', 'I came for a celebration of the Battle of New Orleans where there were lectures about the battle here. Everything was clean and friendly. Great time! Plenty of parking.']

name: Grambling State University
reviews:
['The staff and cafe workers are very nice; and, they make guests feel very welcomed.', "I didn't get the full experience because school was out for Christmas break.

A smaller campus situated in the heart of the city, this town & it's school is proud of it's heritage.  Campus police were very chill. Thank God for that. Nobody wants to be harassed by the folks when they're trying to enjoy themselves & their surroundings.

I'm a huge sports fan & thus attracted to the campus by the legendary Eddie Robinson. His aura & his  legend remain omnipresent throughout the campus & the city itself. Home of the Fighting Tigers", 'I ', 'My son wanted to go to a HBCU so badly and chose this college, the beginning process was horrible, nobody answered the phones nor responded to my emails. But he still insists on going, we finally recvd information after finally talking to someone after like 2 months, that email came through I went in his room woke him up and said, "ARE YOU READY TO BECOME A TIGER?" I just Pray and hope when we go visit everything goes smoother than the process before and that I can afford it bcuz I don't want to go in debt signing up for a bunch of loans, seeing that you have to pay for them to accept your application, registration and other things which is crazy to me. I just hope that when they visited college day at University of Texas that they keep their word on things they told us. After we visit April 2024 I will update my review!!!', 'I’m excited for her but I wasnt impressed with the dorm furniture. My daughter didn’t have a mattress, broken drawer in dresser, had a half broken outlet cover (very dangerous) and a ripped up dorm chair. I know they can hire folks to help fix some things, but overall I enjoyed the campus. There are a lot of buildings in process of being replaced and they have some nice buildings and a lot of dorms. name: ITI Technical College
reviews:
