name: Louisiana State University-Alexandria
reviews:
['My experience with this institution has been extremely frustrating, and I’m posting this to warn other students before they get caught in the same mess.

Despite paying all of my tuition in full, the school failed to provide an accurate 1098T. My statements and receipts clearly show the amounts I paid, yet the school only reported part of it and completely ignored several payments. When I contacted them, I was given incorrect information and told everything was already included, it wasn’t.

Their unwillingness to fix their own reporting errors, acknowledge missing amounts, or provide a corrected form has caused nothing but stress, delays, and unnecessary complications with my taxes. I had to rely on my own bank statements and receipts because the institution wouldn’t do its job.

If you plan to attend here, keep every single receipt, statement, and record, because you may end up needing them when the school fails to report your tuition correctly. The lack of accountability and poor communication is unacceptable, especially when it directly affects students’ financial and tax situations.

I strongly recommend future students proceed with caution. This level of disorganization should not be happening at a university.', "I am a potential student seeking an online degree. I am also a veteran.

No one will answer your calls. You will get transferred around campus multiple times to multiple people, leave voicemails, and nada. No callback...not even an email....It is so awesome to be ignored repeatedly.

If I had not already gone through all the red tape with VA just to get here, I would be attending another school. Supposedly, the VA rep was on a parental leave, which is fine, but NO ONE in the office picked up the slack. I missed my 2nd half of fall enrollment, because I couldn't get a call or email. When I finally did get communication, it was literally MONTHS afterwards.

Absolutely horrendous response on any question from this school, which is in stark contrast to all the happy people you talk to when getting started. Go elsewhere. I am going to attempt to talk to the school president to address these concerns.", 'This review is strictly for the online program at LSUA. If you're currently googling online programs and uncertain which to choose from, please read this.

The online program at LSUA needs to be revamped. Between the program itself and the professors "teaching" it, it needs to be thrown away and redone from scratch. All of it.

Here are the various reasons you should NOT choose LSUA for your degree.

Money. Even if you have a grant, scholarship, whatever, you will be paying for so many unnecessary fees. Fees that don't even apply to you as an online student. Why am I paying a technology fee? An educational fee? A sports fee? On top of tuition, you are required to pay for the online access codes and all of your tests, including the one at graduation, which lets LSUA know just how well they are doing (none of these are included in tuition). It's a survey basically and you have to pay for it. Every test you take for your classes, you're paying for it. $13-50 depending on the class. Do the math. That adds up. Access codes are a joke. I just paid the school for a professor to teach me, yet I'm paying $150 extra for McGraw Hill to teach me the entire class (again, not included in tuition).

Curriculum. I haven't learned anything in this program. The professors don't teach. They reuse videos from COVID years. They barely interact with you and when they do, it's strictly via chatGPT. The curriculum is basically the same across the board. Answer forums, take 1,000 quizzes and then cram for the midterm and final. Walk away learning absolutely nothing.

Professors. In my 3 years at LSUA, I have had a handful of professors who actually have cared about the student's learning and well-being. Most act like you're inconveniencing them. Because god forbid an online student pop out of hiding with a question. Many professors are on a power trip. "You will call me doctor." "You won't make it very far. Might want to rethink your major." "I won't be hosting a review this week." Which also happens to be the last week of class, project due, final due and a thousand other assignments due. Yet the professor can't be bothered to spend one hour of their time to go over the material. (This professor only held 3 reviews in a 7-week class.)

Lack of administration oversight. Despite contacting administration/various department heads about different issues, no one acts on anything. Should you contact anyone about an important issue, you'll be met with, "it's being handled" or "I guess that's how that professor operates" or even straight up lies, just to shoo you away.

ChatGPT. Your professors and faculty will communicate with you only through chatGPT. Even though you'll spend thousands of dollars at this university in hopes of a professor teaching you, it'll all just be funneled through the infamous A.I. platform. An absolute joke, if you ask me.

In the end, I suggest you go with a different university. This one is a complete waste of time. I guarantee, at the end of the program, you and all of your classmates will be saying, "This program did not prepare me in the slightest for the real world. I have learned nothing." You also won't find any jobs because I'm pretty sure everyone knows that LSUA's program is a sham.', "I earned my Bachelor's degree at LSUA and loved the four years that I spent on it's campus.  The professors were great, and the campus was very clean.  I worked as a student worker, therefore I met a lot of the faculty and staff. Almost all of them were very kind and helpful.", "A Great Community College in Central Louisiana. They've now added on Dorm Room/Apartment's, A Pond with 2 huge fountains, and a Baseball field.
The College is small enough that you don't really need a vehicle to travel. You can walk on one of their several shaded 'walk paths' through out the Campus.
They have a Dog path here as well, which is very clean and shady. It also includes a water drinking fountain for dogs, as well as one for people to drink from, especially when the heat ramps up during those summer months.
This place is great for a first time Highschool graduate that maybe can't afford a big College like LSU or Southern Miss. I went here for 2 semesters and had a great time. I also walk my dog here on occasion and use the gym facilities as well."]

name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
reviews: ['College tour but for a very smart kiddo. Not too into sports so we worried...however I can say we were all pleasantly surprised. There is something for everyone here and hopefully gets all of pur kids out of their shells a little', 'LSU is a beautiful place and this is where I finished my first masters in engineering. II had always feel like my heart is attached to LSU Tigers. I went back after nine years for a visit and was taken by how much the university has changed and her beautiful is the new Patrick Taylor hall, and the school of engineering long life Tigers!', "One of tge beautiful and open campus you'll ever walk through and of course you see Mike the live mascot with all the beautiful oak trees all through campus", 'I’m truly enjoying the Grow Louisiana Seeds to Success  purse for Beginning Farmers at LSU. Today’s class was on Food Safety taught by Dr. Achut', 'LSU’s online accounting courses initially seemed like a flexible, self-paced bargain, but don’t be fooled—the savings evaporate when you realize they force you to take Accounting Information Systems as a prerequisite for Auditing, a cash-grab requirement other universities don’t impose, and my state doesn’t mandate.  Worse, they don’t even offer Tax Accounting II online, a core course every CPA candidate needs for business entity taxation.  Their marketing team even hedged with a suspicious “your credits may or may not count” warning, leaving you to gamble on CPA eligibility.  As Jocko Willink warns, “The shortcut is the longest path.”  Avoid.']

name: Louisiana State University-Eunice
reviews:
['Don’t waste your time or money attending this school. The communication is terrible and completely unorganized. They constantly ask students to complete tasks, yet they haven’t done their part on their end. Whenever you try to get information, they send you in circles and no one seems to have a clear answer.

If you’re waiting on financial aid money, good luck. Everyone in the financial aid department will tell you a different date for when funds are supposed to be disbursed, which makes it obvious they are not on the same page. Even knowing that students are having issues receiving their money, they still don’t provide updates. Instead, they’ve added telephone prompts that make it almost impossible to get through to someone in financial aid to ask questions.

If you’re looking for a school that actually communicates with and supports its students, this is not the place.

I feel forced giving this school one star because they don’t even deserve that!', 'My daughter attends this college and the experience with LSUE has just been extremely frustrating. The level of communication and support provided by several departments are definitely lacking. Advisors are practically non existent and don’t always provide complete and detailed information to students. My daughter was unaware with her degree plan and issues with classes that the institution told us that the advisor is supposed to help students with. My daughter’s advisor has never brought up important information to her and is practically useless unless there is a hold that needs to be removed off account. It often feels like she is left to figure certain things out on her own which defeats the purpose of having an advising department. The financial aid office is another problem, they consistently give out false information. It genuinely feels like the staff aren’t qualified or they lack proper training. Maybe they simply do not care about the students they’re supposed to be helping. Classes started almost 2 months ago and my daughter is still waiting for her funds to be released but yet they have all of their money from us. The financial aid office has no information regarding why the process is taking so long, all we’re told is that it’s being worked on, what do they do all day in their office? I wish that I was able to stop right there but we also ran into the issue of inaccurate information being given by the registrar’s and the admissions office, LSUE needs to get it together. This school has a new record for enrollment every semester, many students are attracted to this college for the programs that are offered but can students not feel like they are in the dark? If all these new students can be accepted at least make sure that they can be properly accommodated.', 'Do NOT waste your time trying to enroll in their respiratory therapists program or ANY program if you are someone of color. The students are NOT advocated for, simply prosecuted for any little to anything. I was fine and comfortable prior to starting this program and from the moment I got into this program my mental has gone down the drain. You speak up for yourself and they label you disrespectful. You try to defend yourself against false accusations and it falls on deaf ears. I’ve had professors stand in my face and tell us that some of us took the spot of someone who actually deserved it. I’ve heard professors sit there and express their dislike for other faculty members. They all will smile in your face as if all is well and behind your back it’s something completely different. There’s no punishment for certain students who bully and play “mean girls”. I should’ve known better when another student who graduated from the program told me about the hell David and Kathleen put her through, a black student that is. The program had NO structure in the four most crucial weeks of the semester! Some students felt like we were the guinea pigs of the year! It’s beyond crazy to me how Holly sits up there and talks about the program director and her dislike for him yet acts as though she’s his right hand man. I earned the right to be in this program and today they showed me that I was nothing more than disposable. Remember this when you’re applying there. Actually, save the time and just apply to the LSU in Baton Rouge or their Health Science Center in New Orleans. I was in their nursing program for a year and NEVER encountered such drama and turmoil. God sees all though and I know his plans me will come together with or without LSUE!', 'Amazing and beautiful school
Top athletics and all ways in championship contention

The campus is so beautiful!!', 'The customer service in the admissions department is unacceptable. They do not respond to emails & today when I called to verify they received the email. The lady who answered I spoke with today seemed to be annoyed when responding to my question.']

name: Louisiana State University-Shreveport
reviews:
["LSUS is an outstanding academic institution. The smaller class sizes are amazing, and they're made even more effective by the incredible faculty at the school. It's also an affordable school, allowing students to graduate with little to no debt. Highly recommend!!", 'The MBA program at LSUS is solid and AACSB accredited.
Yes, it is a lot of work, and really a great deal self-taught. That said, it is not high school or even under graduate studies so what you put in, you get out. If you are not prepared academically that is on you...
And, if you really need that much help with administrations and have no patience, again on you!
Really no reason for some of the negative reviews here, as it does not reflect the school or programs offered. Guessing they are just the type of people to complain (or be negative) in general.
In sum: Overall MBA experience was good, and recommended for those seeking an affordable, accredited program.', 'LSUS offers an outstanding online MBA program—affordable, flexible, and academically rigorous. Professors are knowledgeable, responsive, and truly care about student success. The support system is excellent, and real-world learning is built into every course. Highly recommend for working professionals.', 'Once you apply and pay the fee, communication ceases. Then when you do finally get an answer, jump through even more hoops. It is frustrating if I have repeated courses from one college at another due to timeline, I should not have to pay for transcripts over and over. Was a waste of time and money. Very frustrating. Will look elsewhere to complete my MHA.', 'A great education for an affordable price.  The MBA program like many online programs require a lot of self learning but it’s a perfect match for me who prefers this online format to strict class times.  Courses have been easy to register for and provide quality content while also including textbooks for free.  The pacing of the classes are pretty quick given the accelerated nature of the courses so those attending definitely need to make time in their schedule to sit down with the materials.  The software for classes work fairly well with Moodle being the learning platform and Proctorio being the exam proctor.   Though some less technologically inclined professors might not use all the features Moodle has to offer and Proctorio might not work well for those that like to take exams last minute.  Overall, I’ve really enjoyed my time in my program and look forward to learning more and hopefully graduating in the Spring!']

name: Loyola University New Orleans
reviews: ['I transferred to Loyola and absolutely loved my experience there for undergrad and graduate school. The school felt safe, was filled with friendly people, and the teachers were very approachable and helpful. The library is really nice as is the rec. The business school could stand to be updated I enjoyed my teachers there. I lived right off campus and could walk or bike to class. I had debated between Tulane and Loyola but what I got from Loyola was incredibly valuable. The academic supports helped me to learn how I best learn and it gave me a lot of confidence that helped my success in life. I am forever grateful for that.', 'Choosing to attend Loyola University New Orleans was the best decision that I have ever made. Here you will find that there is a true community of compassion for students. Additionally, the faculty is approachable and always willing to go the extra mile for their students. Loyola wants to see its students succeed and because of the care and compassion that we receive here, we do succeed. Thank you Loyola. Best 4 years :)', 'I am currently a graduate nursing student. This has been the profound educational experience I have had in my life. The professors are impeccably knowledgeable and well versed in their areas of expertise.   I went back to school to become more marketable in my profession.  My impending degree from Loyola will give me the confidence in my career that I am seeking along with speaking volumes to potential employers who welcome an employee with a Loyola degree..', 'Several friends that have attended and that are currently employed at this institution of higher learning. The campus is beautiful as is everyone I have ever come in contact with while there. The City of New Orleans is a gumbo of cultures and foods it-self. Some of the best cafes are within walking distance of the campus and you will by no means be disappointed.', "I loved going to Loyola. Small university so you really get to know your classmates. Some advisors are really helpful in pointing you in the right direction. Don't be afraid to seek them out if your assigned one isn't a good fit for you. I learned a lot from this university, and I grew as a person as well."]

name: New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary
reviews: ['Loved living on campus w/ my wife & our 4 small children Spring2019-Summer2021.  Missed having a garage ;) but the graciousness of staff, faculty & neighbors / fellow-students & fams made up for that easily.  Obviously not perfect and everyone stays incredibly busy, but it can be a very sweet time to huddle together and grow as a family as you study the Word.  We are grateful for our time & experience there & recommend it if Father God is leading you there.', 'One of the only positives of the seminary is the homeschool group and all the support if you decide to homeschool. Other than that, there’s plenty of negatives. The list is LONG. But I’ll only name a couple. Most of the seminaries activities are geared toward the single teens and young twenties crowd. And if you work on the campus? It depends who you work for, and if they have your back. Make sure your beliefs match theirs. Because they’ll turn their back on yours to save their own hide. Like when one of the campus police, now known as campus security, went to enforce the rules upon the wrong people, and got fired. Rules for thee, not for me (or my buddies). Even looking at their “rule book” online it says nothing about who the rules apply to. If there’s a different handbook they should have been following, they should have been given it. But, it was all “we just don’t discipline those folks”. Only the students. Administration and department heads only looked out for each other.  So many more reasons besides the ones listed why we left after four years. We’re glad to be gone from the city and the seminary.', 'The campus is gorgeous, the people are kind and godly!', "This review is on the Seminary as a whole, not on one individual person, as there are flawed people and great people every where. My husband went back to get his doctor's degree very late in life. NOBTS has been very helpful in his staying the course through the encouragement of the various professors. He has learned much to help him in his field of preaching and helping others.", "They have a security guard, I don't know his name but he has dark skin and dark hair. Maybe it was Daniel? He's so rude and I tell my friends from now on to go out of state for a seminary. I believe the people working at the campus should be godly and therefore show God's love.. he does not."]

name: Nicholls State University
reviews: ['After being there 4 and a half years (I graduated December 2024), I must certainly say, I loved this university! All the instructors were nice, the course content was understandable, they have a cafeteria, a fitness center, places to hang out and/or do your work, etc., and just like every other college, it’s where you can go and make new friends! After graduating, it just comes to show you how great college life can be. If there was a way to put 10+ stars on Google Maps, then I would. For those of you that are looking for colleges in Louisiana, I highly suggest for you to choose Nicholls State after reading this review. I promise you that you won’t be disappointed!', 'Great School!!!I Love It!!💯 And, Love it for My Child!!!💯 I Feel that They are Safe and Secure! I don’t regret attending college but I do regret who I placed my trust in for guidance. I regret not having more of a back bone when saying no or I don’t agree with what you’re saying about possible degree options.\n\nThe environment is very nice. It’s a well kept campus. It feels safe. The technology is well updated. The professors are nice and do try to accommodate the students. The major thing I’d change is when students come in with concerns over their majors / degrees it’s taken more seriously and not brushed off.', 'Beautiful, friendly, peaceful.....I  love it here and my son does too.', 'Cute campus, great parade!']

name: University of Louisiana at Monroe

name: Northwest Louisiana Technical Community College
reviews:
['Great place to learn.  I received my practical nursing training there back in 2009 and am now the Allied Health Coordinator. Come visit to see what the college has to offer.', 'Tried giving this school a chance more than once and kept getting the runaround. I should’ve been in the nursing program by this fall, but for whatever odd reason they said I had to wait until spring 2025 to apply for classes and on top of that, they keep trying to get me to take the associates degree route, which I told them I wanted to do the technical diploma route since I would not have to retake my accuplacer for the TD. Not sure what their agenda is with that, but I’m pretty much done with this school (which is sad because I heard a lot of good things about their nursing program) and the nonsense they keep presenting.', "So far attending this school has been one of the increasingly worst decisions I've made, and my course isn't even over yet. My teacher quits for a better position else where, and if that doesn't say something about the school then the fact that after several months, they fail to find a replacement, and proceed just move the classes to online even though there's supposed to be a hands on portion to the classes.

Then I get an email saying I have 3 days to make a payment or I will be removed from the course even though I was previously told my FAFSA had covered everything. Making the payment is no big deal, I needed to finish the course, but with only 3 days of notice!!!??? That is crazy to me.

But, another question I have if I'm not even getting the hands on experience that is essentially THE ONLY REASON I decided to take the course, then why am taking this class anymore let alone paying for it myself now? If here is no legitimate teacher or education why am I taking this class? It has been nothing but one problem after another. To the point it feels like they are trying to force students out of the course instead of actually assisting them.", 'I graduated with a  4.0GPA in IT from this school. The teachers are amazing, the staff is terrible. People in the office either sleep at the desk, have no idea what to do, or just be there for a paycheck. Never in my life have I had to deal with the office for their shortcomings in my life like I have here.', 'I’m extremely honored to be a graduate of NWLTC. The skills I learned and the people I met along the way helped make me the Chef I am today. Chef Chris Hayes']

name: Northwestern State University of Louisiana
reviews: ["The new construction of the Math and Science building is winding down the landscaping was completed on June 30, 2021. Treys landscaping Service out of Ruston Louisiana has created many modern views around this new addition to the university. Northwestern State Universities visitors students alumni and staff will enjoy their creation that turned the barren red clay busted concrete chunks sticks twigs and other debris of a construction site into a lush lawn with red tailed cypress and oak trees also maintenance free ornamental grass raised beds bordering the main entrance. What a transformation and compliments the architecture which is quite impressive itself I must say! The down spouts (chains) are my favorite 😐 don't judge it's the little things...\nFurniture and interior design decor is being moved in and systems tested soon the doors will be open and students eager to learn will be satisfied in a state of the art facility with an awesome landscape. Wish it would rain so I could experience the down spout chains in action🌞but it's just a beautiful day with the closest thing to rain here in central Louisiana you'll find is the high humidity lol 🥵! I'll add more photos when I figure out where I put them 🙄", 'My oldest grandson runs track and cross country for the university. He really loves it there. He graduates this next year.', "My sons first semester so excited for his future can't wait to see what life n college has in store for him.", 'Someone I know registered for classes and ended up not going to a single class and dropped out and ended up going to the military and deploying to the Middle East. 3 years later he gets served papers saying he is getting sued for not paying the semester for classes he never went to. Total he owed $9,000. After interest and fees, now he owes $15,000 for classes he never attended. He tried to contact people to help him and they were very rude and said if he went to the news station that they would sue for “spreading lies”(slander). This is a very crooked college who only just wants money. Very unfortunate about what happened to the football student as well. God bless his family. This college is a waste of time and money do not recommend.', 'Coming from a student, this is an averagely mediocre school. There are some select professors that are great, but the real kicker is the security issues and the financial aid. Generally the beginning of school there’s always people who break into cars, and just do very sketchy activities. The financial aid office is abysmal. This isn’t anything to any specific worker, but rather how things are done. From random charges to things being lost, it really is a headache especially when you’re a broke college kid and the fifth day of school they’re posting bills at your door and threatening that you can’t continue school because they need their pay. The medical and psych programs are great though, absolutely some of the best in the state. Just be warned if these issues']

reviews: ['Terrible , the staff refuse to do the job that they are paid to do especially enrollment. No one ever answers the phone, and your information is never updated in a timely manner. reviews: ['Jaguar Pride!!! I always have a great time tailgating on campus. reviews:

A highlight of my journey was working under Dr. Julius Codjoe, whose mentorship was both inspiring and rigorous. His guidance helped sharpen my analytical thinking and research skills, especially in transportation engineering.

The faculty’s dedication, the supportive academic environment, and the university’s commitment to innovation made UL Lafayette an excellent choice for graduate studies in engineering.', "Every year tuition goes up 400$ and mid semester adds another 200$ if you only have pell you probably should well go look up a tree and pick apples. 15 credit hours is 6700$ as a sophomore. I owe 2k every semester because they don't even have enough scholarships or the ones they do have suck.", "Join UL Federal Credit Union - you'll get great service!", "I recommend that if you want to cater to disabled students with the 'UL Life Program'.. maybe be a good idea to allow guardians or assisted guardians to drop off or help the students (in-nees) without harassing them about parking fees or tickets.", "The campus is beautiful and very safe, the people are friendly and hospitable and the weather is nice and warm. The University is great, the quality of education is excellent and the professors are top-notch. There are several programs and research areas that are truly world-class. name: Tulane University of Louisiana
reviews:
["I went here so I do have some thoughts. Graduated in 4 years, no mean feat in a town with as many distractions as New Orleans. To me, going to school in here felt a bit like Pinocchio might have when on the first day he was heading to school and got distracted to Donkey Island instead, with all its gaudy joys.

Plus, my four years coincided with the protests and conflicts over the Vietnam War, civil and women's rights, MLK and RFK assassinations ... lots going on in the world around us. At times classes were disrupted by protests on Tulane's campus and the term called off a month early in 1970, just after the shootings at Kent State. I remember going to Washington DC to participate in the national protest going on then.

I will say Tulane did present me with the opportunity to learn quite a bit and I did occasionally take advantage of that. Many of us who went there know we learned how to party and how to stop. Otherwise, there is no way we are graduating in four years, if at all.", 'Very happy my kids picked Tulane! We have had a wonderful experience here even traveling from Chicago to visit multiple times. The dorms are fantastic as well as the off campus living. The school itself is amazing I feel that it has set both my kids up for a prosperous future.', 'Beautiful university! I have had the privilege of working on a few research projects at the center and the staff are very knowledgeable. I feel good about the future of this world with Tulane on our side.', "Tulane University is an absolute gem! The campus is breathtakingly beautiful, blending modern facilities with historic charm seamlessly. Walking through the campus feels like exploring a vibrant community filled with lush greenery and stunning architecture at every turn. I think what truly sets Tulane apart is its connection to the vibrant culture of New Orleans. The fusion of academia with the rich local culture creates an unparalleled experience for students. I had the pleasure of visiting during parents' weekend, and it was an incredible immersion into university life. The energy, the warmth, and the hospitality of both the faculty and students were remarkable. The city's influence on campus life is palpable, enhancing the overall educational journey. Tulane University not only offers top-notch education but also celebrates diversity and embraces the spirit of New Orleans, making it a truly exceptional place to learn and grow.", 'One of the best universities in the U.S.A., it definitely competes with Ivy League universities. Moreover, Tulane has a gorgeous campus and is located in one of the best cities in the world!']

name: Bates College
reviews:
['My student had the most amazing experience at Bates. She was with people who were interesting and interested. The professors were fantastic. She learned so much and gained confidence by talking to her profs and getting to know her cohort. Tons of activities. The campus is lovely and compact, with something new around every corner. The surrounding countryside is stunning with great walking, hiking, water activities and much more. Can’t say enough great things about it. She has a wonderful job and is a successful adult thanks to Bates.', 'I signed myself up for a calculus class and god it was one of the worst decisions I’ve ever made. You know it’s bad when you’re trying to solve an equation and there’s more letters in it than numbers. I was so lost. All the other students were lost too. The professor was actually a really good teacher and a nice person. It wasn’t her fault, we were just dumb. Sometimes, while she had her back to us writing on the whiteboard, students would climb out of one of the back windows and escape into the forest.

The dorms were a pretty unusual setup that I didn’t like very much. I think at other schools, you get an assigned room with a roommate. Here, it was just a free for all, first come first serve. Each night, students were scrambling to get whatever bed was empty. And there weren’t enough beds for everyone. I’m bad at keeping track of time and tended to come home late, which meant the beds were almost always already full. So I had to sleep on the floor most nights. The dorm setup also meant that none of the students had many possessions. It just wasn’t practical. I kept a few books, a change of clothes, and some toiletries in a small backpack that doubled as my pillow on the nights I couldn’t find a bed.

One night I was trying to find a place to sleep, and I couldn’t sleep in my favorite floor spot by the window, because this guy who was a football player and a known creep around campus was sleeping in the bed right next to it. There was no way I was gonna shut my eyes in the same room as him. So I climbed the stairs to the fourth floor to find another spot.

At the top of the stairs, I looked out the window, and the sky looked really weird. The clouds were glowing green, and there was this huge dark mass of roiling clouds off to the east, moving horrifyingly fast. Oh god, it was a tornado! The tornado was absolutely ripping towards us at full speed, tearing apart cars and trees and shredding the siding off of houses. All this junk was flying through the sky at top speed. I was paralyzed watching it, it was headed straight for the dorm. Last second, it swerved course and dropped a huge boulder right in the middle of the train tracks down the road. And I looked down the tracks and there was a train, coming right for it. Oh no. I was like, I need to warn them, people are gonna get hurt! So I sprinted down the stairs and out of the dorm and I was running as fast as I could towards the train waving my arms yelling BREAK!!! But I wasn’t fast enough. The train smashed into the boulder. It buckled and ripped apart at the connections, cars broke loose and went careening off the tracks. They tumbled down a hill, crashed into the forest, and exploded in flames.', 'Bates is a great choice of college! Acceptance rate is 14%.
We loved seeing it inside, too! Gorgeous college!', "I never went to collage here. But I did have a Big Sister and 2 Big Brothers that had graduated from this collage. I grew up in this area from 5 untill 38 when I left the state never to come back. Personal reasons. Anyway the Big Brothers and sister I had here were the best thing that has happened in my life as a kid. I'm so much more educated because of the program and I really hope they still have one.", "This is one of the best colleges in Maine, i've only heard good things. Campus has a mountain and a great pond. Love jogging around there its good to look at. I super appreciate everyone there."]

name: Bowdoin College
reviews: ['Nice campus.  Walked around the campus on a Sunday afternoon. Buildings appear to be be locked as I saw students using a badge/fob to open the doors.', 'Beautiful campus! We visited the bookstore and chatted with staff. They were very friendly!', 'Hands down one of the best small liberal arts schools in our nation that is quietly producing effective leaders. Values, community, academics, tradition rooted in pragmatic Maine problem solving and common good orientation, founded before Maine was a state!', 'Avoid if you don’t go to an elite private boarding school in New England', "This is a fine college by almost any standard.  Our son graduated in 2007 with a major in biology, minor in economics, and had a wonderful experience.  His only regret is not taking full advantage of the great outdoor club.  We moved nearby the college after many years in England because the school plays such a positive role in the quality of life in neighboring communities.  Visitors are welcome on campus for nearly all cultural and sporting events, at no cost, very unusual.  In recent years the women's basketball team has been one of the best Division III teams in the country, always fun to watch.  Field hockey and ice hockey teams are also of note.  The college has wonderful programs for auditing classes and for local families to serve as host parents for students from far away, both of which we enjoy a great deal.  High quality food is served on campus and a fine learning experience for the right students.  A bit too liberal for my tastes but that's the direction many schools have turned in recent years.  Overall it's a wonderful school turning out fine young people, including superstars like Reed Hastings, co-founder and CEO of Netflix."]

name: Maine College of Health Professions
reviews:
["My Son and I visited today, as he is a HS Senior and is passionate about entering the medical field. We were warmly welcomed by Tammy who sat with us, was attentive, kind, informative, listened to all of my and my Son's questions, and presented a lot of very valuable insight and information in to their curriculum and processes. We had a nice, casual tour of the facility (which is beautiful corner to corner, top to bottom) meeting other staff, students, and instructors. We came away excited about the possibility of my Son potentially attending, but more so, we came away very impressed by the care, professionalism, and warmth we were shown by every single person that we interacted with. I'd leave 10 stars if I could.", "Unfortunately, I found Tammy in admissions to be very discouraging. While she is trying to be upfront, she was very vague about the questions I had and just kept pushing that I couldn't work and do school... That I wouldn't be successful if I did. While I appreciate the honesty, that seemed to be her main focus. I wanted information about classes, scheduling, financial aid etc... Outside of school is for me to worry about. I wanted to make sure I was making the best  decision which in turn was hard to do because my questions were brushed off or barely answered and the main focus was my ability to complete the course. I really just wanted information about the above and so I could decide what was the next best steps for me but I was really just shot down from the moment I picked up the phone call. I don't expect sugar coating but I expected my questions to be answered. When spending that type of money it's the least that could have been done.
Ive heard such great things about this school. My friend graduated from here and also went back to get her bsn. She highly recommended this school to me. But, first impressions are everything and the impression I got today was not a good one. I ended the call discouraged and feeling like I wasn't meant for this.", "I don't go here, but my wife does, and she loves it!", 'For Ms.Murphy', 'I really wish I could leave a better review. Let me start by saying that the reason I’m leaving two stars is because I had a couple of really amazing, supportive professors. I was beyond elated when I got my acceptance letter into the sonography program, as sonography was my dream since I was in middle school. The first couple of weeks went great. I was a little off put when I realized that MCHP does what’s called a “flipped classroom”, where students are expected to learn all material outside of class on their own. I’ve always been a hands-on learner, so I quickly started falling behind. There wasn’t much academic support, so it wasn’t easy to pass classes (even with “support”).
Secondly, there is a strict attendance policy. I understand fully having to have a strict policy for a school that is difficult to get into, but there should absolutely be excused absences for illness or family emergencies. You are allowed to miss three classes. Anymore? You fail the class regardless of your grade. I missed two days of my A&P Lab due to my entire family having cryptosporidium (I offered to provide a doctors note), and they told me they wouldn’t excuse my absence because it was not a long term health issue. You would expect a medical school to excuse absences for something like that. Mind you, I was still turning in all the work while I was gone.
In November, I had a family emergency that required me to go out of state. I communicated that with my professors. My A&P professor told my advisor (Kim Emery), who demanded we met over this. I explained that I had a family member who was at the end of life. Instead of being understanding and empathetic, she asked if it was possible for me to stay home and Zoom my dying relative so I wouldn’t miss any school. This honestly put the nail in the coffin.
I have always and will always be a hard worker. I have a really difficult time giving up on things, but this school quite literally drained me mentally and physically. By the end of the first semester, I had completely lost my passion for the career that I had been dreaming of since I was young. I felt so disrespected and unsupported. I feel like I wasted thousands of dollars just to teach myself and end up hating my career path. If you want to go to a school that is going to teach you, be supportive and not make you feel like your life needs to revolve around academics, this isn’t the school for you.

Sincerely,
An upset former student']

name: Central Maine Community College
reviews:
['I attended Central Maine Community College, and I can honestly say it was one of the best decisions I’ve made. The instructors really care about your success, they’re down-to-earth, and willing to take the time to help you figure things out. You’re not just another student.

The programs are solid and practical, and there’s a wide range to choose from, whether you’re going into a trade, business, or planning to transfer to a four-year school later on. The campus is really nice, small enough to feel personal but big enough to have everything you need. Plus, the view of Lake Auburn is hard to beat.

CMCC is also incredibly affordable, and the support you get for financial aid, advising, and other departments makes the whole process way less stressful. It’s a place that genuinely sets you up for success, whether you’re just starting out or coming back to school after a break.

I’d definitely recommend CMCC to anyone looking for a college that’s welcoming, affordable, and focused on helping you reach your goals.', "If I could give this school zero stars I would. I went to this college when I was a teen and it was great. I guess my parents are the ones that dealt with all their crap. I decided to go back as an adult, completely remote, because I work. My major was medical coding and electronic health records. I had to take bio classes, normal, I know, but do I really need to know the ins and out of cellular mitosis and cellular respiration? Anyway, I should have run for the hills when they couldn't even sign me up for classes and give me info on financial aid until the three days leading up to the start of the semester. Then they told me they did not want to go into the paper records to check my transcripts from high school. So my high school did it for them and sent them again. My classes started and one of my classes was titled medical coding, but was all about financial stability while in college and was all you tube videos from local colleges. Quality education right there. My bio class was all you tube videos geared towards high school students from Covid times, and the lectures were all done by the TA from a few years ago. I only heard from my teacher when I emailed her to tell her that her labs were wrong. One of my other classes was so poorly set up that the dates were all wrong and the teacher would not change them. I finished the semester and was moving on. I tried to get a hold of the financial aid department for question for three weeks, no answers. I finally emailed my advisor, again in the days leading up to the start of the semester. I also asked her why I was missing a class. Her response was that I got a C- in my Bio lab class and did not pass. A C- minus is passing. Even the dean of the school said it was, but not in this particular class. Never one was it communicated to me that I needed a C or better to pass. Yes, I talked to the Dean of academics, all the good it did. He decided to stand with his teachers that don't teach their own classes. I commend him for his loyalty to his teachers, just not the students who actually pay their salaries. I was told I have no recourse except to retake the bio lab class. No one could explain to me the financial package that was offered either. They wanted me to take out a 9500 dollar loan for two semesters. Even when I screenshot the page and sent it to the dean he kept saying I was misreading it and that would be for 2-3 years of school. Mine was only a 2 year program. I maintain that I passed and should not have to retake the class. Do not go to this school, it is not worth your time or frustration. Do not even get me started on the platform they use for classes. There is obviously more to the story but this is as short as I can make it. Thanks for reading.", 'i’m going to attending CMCC next fall & i toured this summer, this is such a BEAUTIFUL campus with a small university feel in a small town. coming for the south seeing a community college with on campus housing is amazing, i have heard great  about smcc and i ended hating it so im so glad i found CMCC. auburn is such a cute small town with nice restaurants. super exited to start school here!!!', "Went for the Class B trucking class. I explained from day 1 that I was an ex Marijuana smoker from the start and was truthful since the 1st email. I was told they can still work with me to get my license. Spent 3 weekends in class, passed my permit test. I spoke with the instructor about the dot test he told me not to worry that he didn't care how long it took for me to be able to pass a drug test and to take over the counter drug tests and to call him when I could pass. I done as he instructed and when I was able to pass a DT I reached out and was told the class had ended and to contact his boss. I reached out to her immediately and now after numerous back and fourth emails, waiting for responses I was told the class has ended. At first before starting class I even requested a later class so I had time to pass a DT I was told we are not holding spots. I was refused any information about the class or the processes and was told to fill out paperwork. I filled out the paperwork and rushed into a class on May 17th with no time to be able to pass a DT. Here I am Aug 12 with no class B license only a permit and an email refusing my 30 hours of drive time. Granted this was a free class offered at CMCC. Now I have to come up with $4500. for someone else to do drive time with. The instructors were great I did learn alot but it's a shame the school wouldn't let me complete the hours after I done everything I was told to do. They got the funding from the grants or wherever they received it from and I got no license all for doing what they told me to do. I even reached out to the president of CMCC's office and still no reply.", "This review is targeted at the testing center.  I would STRONGLY advise against taking any tests at this center, as my experience was extremely negative.  The test was started without my consent or presence and had timed out by the time I had sit down to take the test.  This is not Pearson Vue's fault, but took absolutely no accountability after being on the phone for 2 hours, and speaking to 6 different people.  I will never be back to this testing center and will be filing an official complaint against the organizations testing center."]

name: Colby College
reviews:
['Colby College is one of my very top favorite colleges so far, along with Brown University. I fell in love from the first sight with its wonderful look and extremely comfortable athmosphere, a charming tiny coffee shop (which was closed in the summer, of course), a great bookstore, full of all kinds of stuff, all these beautiful sitting areas outside... everything here is done with love and to make the best experience for students. I also love that it is so old and has a great history.

The acceptance rate is 10%.

Any student will be not just lucky to get in, but also happy here, no doubts.', "Colby stands as one of the preeminent liberal arts colleges not just in Maine, but in all of New England. It's unique 4-1-4 plan enables students to take intensive courses in January, while the curriculum encourages intellectual curiosity. If you are ever in Waterville, be sure to check out Colby!", 'Photos of an amazing fall sunrise from Mayflower Drive in the parking lot of Colby College. Very well maintained campus, great sights and plenty of opportunities for scenary and nature photos.', 'Great college, fantastic facilities, awesome people
And I met these two cool people from new jersey
The father was in the waste management business and his daughter fielder was super kind and caring', 'Took my elderly mother-in-law and my 6 year old son to sit by rhe pond. Had comfortable benches and a nice lawn to play on. Saw a little muskrat, 4 turtle sunning on a log, and tons off different size fish! Wonderful place to explore!']

name: Eastern Maine Community College
reviews:
["Oh god where to start.... Eastern Maine Community College has been the absolute worst experience I think someone could ever have. I went to Eastern Maine Community College because I needed a College based Algebra class in order to go to Umaine. When I first went there to figure out how to apply and I will say I was running out of time to get in for the fall semester but the staff in admissions were very rude and made it seem like they didnt want me to go to their college. Don't bother going to talk to anyone in that department area if you dont wanna be felt judged upon or treated terribly. After I finally got in I even tried meeting the finichial aid person and she turned me off and talked to me about how im the least important person when all I wanted was to figure out my finichial aid. (I never got my finichial aid until the semester ended. If that's not saying something to anyone then idk what else) It was very painful getting admitted. Accommodations were sweet but I also still felt very unheard when asking for a break from class accommodation and because they didnt see it was reasonable I had a mental breakdown in class and I couldn't leave without being penalized in a lab. The buildings were so worn down and felt not well take care or cleaned and always needed to fight to find a place to sit down that at least had a charging station. Not to mention I experienced alot more judging/bullying at school and not really being able to do anything about it. There was really only one of my teachers that made the college worth it which was my math teacher I had to drop chemistry because one they have no support systems in place or tutors for the chemistry program but they teacher straight out didnt know how to help me and recommended I dropped which I ended up doing. I was left being too scared all the time to go there because of the discrimination and judgement I felt I had and cried most days at school and at home because of how scarred i was with how they run things there. Im not having to file a claim with the courts because the school is negligent to give the student resources on how to get there 1098T.
The food there at the college is very mid they dont seem to meet healthy standards well and the food was always very low quality.
I was a transfer student and I was treated like crap. If you need to go to a college for credits please find somewhere else so you dont meet the same experiences I did there. And dont let them use the excuse “Were using a new system” to give you any shit if you have to go there and stick up for yourself because unless you talk to them with persistence they wont care. Also one final thing staff were very discriminatory to my transgender partner not cool so even thought theres a lgbtq+ club the school staff and administration there show lots of discrimination. One final thing I would have said something but how could I with all of that happening…. I hope eastern maine when you read this that you can kindly do better.", "This is for those trying to get into the RadTech program. After you pass the tests, there are other meetings where they get a feel for who you are. It's no doubt that they favor extroverted people over introverted people. It's basically a talent show. Also, they take in probably over 40 people for this and only 20 will make it into the program. I'm not sure if your test scores even matter.", "I'm a current student here, and I love it. The professors are absolutely amazing and I've learned more in 1 semester than I did in all 4 years of high school. Every aspect is solid, from classes to food to the staff around campus. Getting an education here is a no-brainer", 'I am currently in the Human Services program at Eastern Maine Community College. I am in my Junior Year, but went to this school starting my sophomore year to get the basics and learn more about Human Services. This college (from the human services standpoint) gives you an amazing example and head start within the basics of the mental health field. The main teachers in the program are Deb & Edmond. They are fantastic. They are hardworking and driven to provide student success. Multiple times when I was struggling, they were there to help me. I recommend this college to anyone who needs more one on one support. Especially straight out of high school or wanting to come back to college after a year or many years. The teachers help you feel like you are successful and provide a safe and comfortable learning environment. The pro is definitely the free college for some of us who graduated in a specific year. That is so wonderful and has seriously helped my success tremendously!!! The only downfall I would say is there is not many online classes for this field, which could be an addition to making the college more successful for those who are online learners. My only complaint for the college in general is some of the bookstore staff (not all of them).. but some have been a bit disrespectful to students. I understand it is a hard job and overwhelming when students are packing in to get their books during the start of a semester, but hiring more staff or switching off would be beneficial for these staff to reduce burnout and stress overall making it a healthier environment for the staff, and so they are kinder to students. Overall a wonderful college.', "The enrollement staff here is really unorganized. Over the summer I called everyday. Everyday I would not get a response. The business office likes to get you to pay more money than you owe. The bookstore has ridiculous prices. Definitely go to amazon first. The food is the same thing every day, and you are only allowed to have one plate.

That's the bad. The good. Very beautiful campus, teachers are willing to help with anything you don't understand. The classes are more hands on then out of a text book. Professors are easy to get ahold of."]

name: Kennebec Valley Community College
reviews: ["I am part of the class of 2019 here at kvcc.  I graduated with an associates degree in liberal studies.  After struggling at the university of new England in Biddeford I came to this school to try again at receiving a degree.  Almost everybody you meet, including the students, are fantastic.  Trio, a program here at kvcc, helped me get through and graduate college.  It took me 6 years to get a degree, but I did it.  You know, a school can have all the amenities in the world and still not be the right fit.  Kvcc may lack in amenities however they helped me get through college and get the education I always hoped for.  I took 2 to 3 classes a semester.  It was hard and long, but I'm thankful for my professors and the staff here at kvcc who helped me succeed.  And the crazy part was: I graduated while struggling with my mh issues.  They knew I was trying to get diagnosed and get on the right meds, and they didn't hold that against me.  Thank you so much, all of you, for helping me get the degree I worked hard for and deserved.  Maybe some day I'll come back for my bachelor's.", "Currently enrolled in the Electrical Technology program and on track to graduate in May. KVCC offers a well organized curriculum that is designed to engage and educate both a novice or a professional. The trades programs give students a hands-on approach that reinforces the classroom knowledge. Being able to work in the field while in the program is definitely beneficial! This is made easier & incentiveised thanks to the fact that some of the labs can be signed off by a boss or supervisor holding a master's license. Only reason for the 4* rating instead of 5 is that the ET program could definitely use a few more online and evening class options. Overall great community college with a friendly and helpful staff.", 'I love my school and the TRiO Push days even though I could only attend one day, was very encouraging', 'A great little community college. Everyone is close and friendly since it is a smaller campus. Would recommend for undergraduates.', 'Love my new college KVCC!  Awesome staff and professors!']

name: The Landing School
reviews: ["I attended the Landing School Small Boats program in 2001.  It was amazing!! If you are even just considering going to the Landing School don't think about it, just do it.  You will learn more than you can even imagine no matter what your entry skill level.  I was only 19 when i went and there were other students in their 70's and we worked together for 10 months and had the absolute best times and learned so much.  I went on to get a Mechanical Engineering degree after the Landing School and what i learned about boats helped me all all through my 5 years at college and has helped me in my everyday and work since.  I would give the Landing School a 100 out of 5 starts if i could!"]

name: University of Maine at Augusta
reviews: ["I transferred here after attending a private college that wasn't a very good fit for me. I absolutely loved my time at UMA online. I felt 100% more welcome and respected and I felt like a valued part of the UMA community. I truly enjoyed my time here and if I knew this college existed earlier I would have choose UMA instead of my last college anyday. I'm a proud UMA alumni. Great school, very affordable, good quality professors who care about students success!", "I was an aviation major at UMA and could only deal with a year of it. The Aviation department is fairly new and while the flight school they are partnered with is very proficient the university side of things is still a mess which makes things very frustrating. There are no dorms which means that if you live outside of Central Maine you're basically forced to commute or find an apartment which is incredibly inconvenient. Student Life is practically nonexistent. You can get a much better experience for around the same price at Vermont Tech. I opted to transfer to the bigger more expensive aviation schools where there are better career connections, an actual campus life and residence halls. Best decision I've made so far in my college career was to leave UMA.", "I attend UMA and I love it. I don't know what one of the other comments was talking about when they said there's no student life. There's literally a department for it that plans TONS of awesome events (we even had a ball last year) and tons of trips. Boothbay, Bar Harbor, Boston, Salem, New York. It's a great school.", 'Great university that is welcoming to all students.', 'I am freshman at this school i play ice hockey here']

name: University of Maine at Farmington
reviews: ['I have gone here once, twice in the future, for competing in the Geo Bee at the state level. This campus is amazing, with great food, great hospitality, great classrooms, and great people and setting overall. This might be some back road farm college for you, but for me, this is an amazing campus. 5/5.', '#1 liberal arts college and one of the best colleges in the country. All nestled in a 222 year old town. This is my home. Farmington is a rare gem.', 'Hiram Sibley treated my family and I horribly.  Was beyond rude at the campus.', 'We had a lot of help moving my Daughter in to her Dorm', 'Small and quaint campus, loaded with plenty to do?']

name: University of Maine at Fort Kent
reviews: ['This university turned out to be one of the best decisions I ever made in my life. I worked hard and all my instructors were very supportive as well as helpful. The town can be lonely and depressing but I always remembered why I came here. I enjoyed studying in the library and TRIO, the staff in those places were very professional and polite. There’s definitely no reason not to succeed when everything is working towards supporting your education. Those who decide to smoke weed and sleep around can do that all day and night. You have yourself to blame and years of regret await you in the future. You have to decide to wake up everyday and show up for your future it’s only a few years for a forever career. When you go down in the dumps, don’t forget to reach out to a trusted adult or counseling services. You are not alone, you don’t deserve to feel overwhelmed by how different the life in this town is. All the services to help you transition and adapt are in place; please use them.\nSincerely\nKayla BSN RN', 'There is a paradise for book worms, library mongers and people who care to use study rooms or the writing center. Absolutely stunning interior décor of the rooms and coziness, love it.', "Very accommodating people and an unbelievably awesome dining commons!  Some of the best smoked roast beef I've ever had!", "Very unorganized. Professors don't care to answer any questions. Certain professors (ex. Mariella Squire, World Cultures) don't even assign work and students have to chase after them in order to get help, assignments, and/or answers. The school with take extra money from you for no reason. The town sucks. All you can do is smoke weed and get drunk honestly. You'll love it if you're a hillbilly hick. There's a moose tick class where you have to count the number of living ticks on freshly killed moose... oh and yes, of you don't have your tick shot you are still expected to take part. Disgusting huh? Hm what else? It's expensive and there's nothing really good about it. If you make it out you'll have a good laugh. If you live in Crocker dorms they don't turn the heat on in the winter either. Even though it gets below freezing. Oh, and if you bring your own heater for your room the dumbass RA's will take it away from you AND charge you $50 for it. all for trying to stay warm. Oh but the RA's are allowed to have dogs in their rooms. Nice! Don't come here. Just don't.", 'Beautiful campus both during winter and fall']

name: University of Maine
reviews: ["Going to UMaine has to be the worst decision I've ever made. The facilities are old and uncomfortable (about a billion dollars in deferred maintenance). The Bangor area is depressing with nothing to do. The academic standards are not as thorough as I'd expected so everybody just uses AI without consequences. The university has a problem with retaining professors in many departments, leading to a bad academic experience. The mathematics department is a good example where my professor resigned a week before classes started and his replacement was horrible. The school does a poor job at engaging students without much of a community sense. The party scene was very disappointing. Do not join the Honors College, it is a waste of time. Nobody really cares about varsity sports and there's no school spirit. Housing screwed up my application so I got paired with somebody that wasn't my requested roommate. There are a few positives of the school, but I cannot wait to transfer out of here.", 'If you want $45k of debt as a in-state student with nothing to show for, go here. Good luck even getting a printed diploma. All these reviews are from people who attended a couple shows at the Collin’s Center. Try attending as a student in the 2020s. I’m sure your five stars will change.', 'Home of the greatest college mens hockey fans. The new facility is amazing.', "I've only gone to Umaine a few times, but it seems absolutely amazing. I definitely want to go there when I go into college, and I am very excited. My parents went there too, and they also had an amazing experience. My father did landscape horticulture, and my mother did physical education and teaching. I go there for homecoming with them, and I definitely recommend at least checking it out. (Also, good food.)", 'Here to see a show. Parking great. Staff very friendly and helpful.']

name: Maine Maritime Academy
reviews:
['not only one of the best maritime academy the in the global world also the best sport program like soccer now i was working with one of the great soccer player of MMA (15) here in San Diego Ca. General Dynamics. very hardworking lady thank you. GO MARINERS salute. MMA strong', "Great school, the classes are awesome and (most of) the teachers are really knowledgeable and helpful. However, this place is in the middle of nowhere, the administration for the school is horrible and doesn't prioritize what the students want, you must stay in the dorm until you are 21, the school is 90% guys, so the guys can be really creepy and the girls are super outnumbered. The first 2 weeks and the last 2 weeks of the year, the weather is good, and you can go sailing, swimming, kayaking, hiking... A lot of nature experiences! However, come early September to like mid May, it is a frozen, desolate, wasteland. I was grading this University off of the 'college experience' alone, I would give it 0 stars if I could. However, the academic side of the academy is that good that it deserves 3 stars.

It comes down to this: if you value immediate happiness over long term happiness, DO NOT go here. If you can see a little farther into the future, this school might be for you, but you will not enjoy it.", 'I remember my time fondly here, while I decided to go with another career field, the time I was there I found the community to be kind, and very supportive. The regimental life was different, but wasnt as extreme as other places ive seen (The Citadel, Annapolis and Mass Maritime). Great place to visit as well, and cool history!', "MMA is a niche college with a clear connection to the sea. The faculty and students are mariners -- from ocean science to maritime shipping. There are great benefits to this education and a clear path to a satisfying career. The location can't be beat -- beautiful coastal town with plenty of opportunity for boating, hiking and soaking up history. And the views from the campus overlooking Penobscot Bay are spectacular!", "Beautiful commencement and fantastic men's lacrosse championship.
What a weekend to be a Mariner."]

name: University of Maine at Presque Isle
reviews:
["I'm a non-traditional student, getting close to completing my BA in Psychology. The YourPace program has been amazing. The classes (at least for psychology) are more demanding than you may anticipate. I have become a stronger writer and better researcher. My professors have been excellent, kind, and responsive. I have had very few administrative issues, and the ones I did have were resolved quickly.

This place is wonderful if you're self-motivated and want to go at your own pace, however fast or slow that may be. Even if you go slow and pay out of pocket, it is still reasonably affordable.

The campus seems lovely, if remote, and I hope that one day I will get a chance to visit.", "Horrible experience. From the start, I had issues. I was told the orientation would take 2 hours; it took 8. Not only was it not helpful, but half of the true/false only had true as an option. This took countless emails to resolve. One of the classes was even worse regarding organization. In that class, I could not find the teacher's name and email, and my Academic Advisor seemed clueless. She finally just gave it to me, and then it took a week for him to get back to me. The issues just continued. This one session is it. I'm done. I emailed my advisor to take me out of the next session. Now, today I logged in so that I can work on finishing the two classes, and one of them is wrong. Somehow, my comp class now has a new teacher, and no work done when I am almost done. If you have a ton of patience for no and poor communication, tech issues, poorly designed online classes, and questionable curriculum, with tons of time to send emails trying to fix issues, then this is a school for you.  I am looking elsewhere and do not recommend.", 'The staff was incredibly rude. My first contact to the school was great, but once accepted, it was a different story.

Financial aid never communicated with me after receiving my info. I called to ask about the fafsa form I filled out and ask about loans and other options and Lynelle told me to "figure it out". Later on I spoke with another financial aid person, Sarah, who was quite rude as well. Killing them with kindness wasn't effective. I had to pull teeth to get information.

I was assigned to Chelsey for enrollment. She sends all her calls to VM. I had to put a lot of time into getting in contact with her. Once I did, she put together a few options, none of which are a fit for me. I tried calling her again to discuss that and went straight to VM. She claimed I never called, but my call log and recorded call prove differently. This game playing crap isn't necessary. She has some growing up to do and lacks accountability. I requested another enrollment specialist after she lied, as we are unable to having a working relationship when she avoids accountability and lies.

I was sent to Jessica. I scheduled an appointment with Jessica for a call. She never sent her phone number to me. Again, they lack basic communication skills. I had to chase her down for her phone number. Once I got the number, I called and she was defensive from the start. I ended the call and decided this isn't the right school for me.

I've read other reviews of this school with a similar experience as mine as well as discussed it on social media platforms and many have reached out sharing the same experience. I've heard the excuses that they are overwhelmed with students. That's an excuse!!! If they can't handle the number of students they accept, they need to limit the number they accept.

My experience with these people was a nightmare. I've been to college before and graduated. I know what college is supposed to be like and what their roles are. I think this college falls under "you get what you pay for".

It's so bad that there is a lady making money off helping students navigate their system because the school really doesn't want to help their students in the process.

Everything with this school was a secret that you had to drag out of them. They have my transcripts. I had to pull teeth to get them to tell me how many classes I needed. Any other school is more than willing to offer this. I had to pull teeth to get financial aid info. Apparently that was some big secret too. It's exhausting trying to get info from the school to make decisions.

I strongly recommend others consider another school. Look at reviews, read what others say on Facebook, Reddit, Discord, etc. Nobody should have to experience what I did with these people.', 'The gym is small with older equipment but it had everything I need for a workout.  The indoor track and pool are nice options to have. All the desk workers are kind and welcoming.', 'In reflecting upon the Master of Arts in Organizational Leadership (MAOL) through the University of Maine at Presque Isle’s YourPace online format, I completed the degree within six months.  The YourPace model delivers precisely what it advertises: an affordable, fully online, competency-based pathway allowing self-directed learners to progress as they demonstrate mastery.  Its flat per-session tuition and asynchronous pacing permit acceleration where prior experience aligns with course competencies and a slower approach when needed.  The program’s three-domain structure combined with regional accreditation through the New England Commission of Higher Education, situates it firmly within the framework of legitimate competency-based education.

Affordability is among UMPI’s strongest assets.  The flat-rate tuition per eight-week session allows students to control overall cost through accelerated progression.  Completing the MAOL in six months produced substantial savings compared with traditional per-credit models.  This design supports adult learners who can sustain weekly study routines and appreciate direct performance targets.  For disciplined professionals, YourPace offers an attractive, outcomes-based, and financially accessible structure.

However, operational inconsistencies muddy these strengths.  My assigned Student Advisor never contacted me during the entirety of my enrollment.  In online graduate education, proactive advising and academic coaching, particularly during onboarding and key assessment points, are essential for student persistence and satisfaction.  Without outreach, students must self-navigate institutional processes and troubleshooting, which undermines the model’s intended support framework.

Faculty interaction proved similarly inconsistent.  Response times and grading practices often deviated from institutional timeline guidelines, and feedback frequently lacked reference to rubric criteria.  Competency-based models rely on transparent evaluation anchored in rubrics to ensure reliability and formative guidance.  Without timely, rubric-linked commentary, students cannot easily identify or address performance gaps.  For instance, in OLS-530 – Globalization and Diversity, my rubric reflected scores of 4 across all categories, yet the overall course grade was a 3 without explanation or detailed feedback.

Course organization further demonstrated irregularity.  Some modules contained broken links, unclear instructions, or sequencing misalignments between outcomes and assessments.  Such design inconsistencies increase student load and erode the efficiency YourPace promises.  Effective CBE design depends on coherence between learning outcomes, activities, and evaluation artifacts: elements that, when disjointed, hinder learner momentum.

Despite these operational shortcomings, the MAOL program proved transformational.  It reshaped my understanding of leadership as an adaptive, ethical, and relational process rather than a positional one.  The coursework honed my capacity to analyze structural barriers in complex systems such as healthcare and crisis intervention.  I gained the ability to apply evidence-based leadership frameworks to foster inclusivity, transparency, and trauma-informed collaboration within interdisciplinary environments.  The program also reinforced the value of reflective practice, self-awareness, and moral accountability in leadership, which are now aspects that shape my overall experience.

Overall, the accelerated timeline cultivated discipline, endurance, and self-efficacy.  Sustaining momentum through overlapping projects requires deliberate time management and intrinsic motivation.  Thus, for self-motivated learners capable of independent navigation, the program can yield significant personal and professional growth.  For those valuing consistent mentorship and structured interaction, its success depends upon UMPI’s continued commitment to strengthening program execution and student support systems.']

name: University of New England
reviews:
['Pretty university by the Atlantic Ocean, the view from the library is eccentric, the cool breeze, a perfect atmosphere for learning definitely!!', 'Visiting my son during his first year here. The campus is beautiful and he really enjoys being here. Great classes and lots of programs available for students. Very nice facilities.', 'I'm a 60 yr old grandma looking for my beautiful 17 yr old granddaughter to deliver a McDonald's dinner to her. The grounds are nicely done and the views are breathtaking.. I was to meet her at the Commons, but I had NO idea how to get there and no experience with UNE 😂🙄  So after turning around multiple times (we saw a beautiful garden geared to attract Monarch butterflies), a wonderful gentleman who had to do with financial and admission stuff told me I could park where it said "staff only", pointed me towards the Commons and said "enjoy your granddaughter!".
The people were friendly, the buildings are amazing and I can't say enough about the campus grounds. Awesome visit!!! ❤️❤️❤️', "It's a beautiful campus on the Saco river near the ocean.", 'Pompous administration lead the admissions process.
Someone once told me they wouldn’t send their dog there….. now I know why.

The e-mail showing our application had been received was followed 30 SECONDS  later by the rejection e mail.   They never even read the application essay that took months to assemble.

They had no problem cashing the attached check!!

What a joke.   I still get pissed when I see their TV commercial saying how much they care about Maine’s future and students.']

reviews: ['Tried multiple phone calls to jeff Butterfield about the diesel program but never got a call back, would not recommend this school because of it', 'Best school ever!
