name: Maine College of Art & Design
reviews:
['I love being at Maine College of Art & Design. I applied and was accepted when I was 51, the same time my youngest kids were applying for schools. I have thoroughly enjoyed all my classes, majored in painting and minored in writing. They have all been challenging. I have taken such a variety Art History classes as well as others not necessarily associated with art. I thought the Pirates class last spring was one of the best. This semester, Chinese Painting and Calligraphy looks fascinating. Now that gatherings are back in person, the school is also having more Continuing Education classes on the weekends and during the breaks, getting back to normal.', "Just want to throw out there that they had a review rating that was much lower 6 months ago with many reviews being 1&2stars and now they've disappeared 🤔
Anyways-
Mother of student. Faculty are horrible to deal with. There is no communication. They avoid emails and questions about billing as much as possible but have no problem getting a hold of you right away for late fees. They will say one thing and do another like agreeing to make a payment plan then the following month after getting hit with late charges, the same exact person we talked to said they won't do a payment plan. When you do speak to someone, they sound annoyed and act like they dont want to help. The first year was awful. I thought we would be ahead of the game for the second year. Every time our daughter went to guidance with questions and to get set up for the following year, they were never in office, canceled apts they set up with our daughter. She never received info for a dorn. Now we can't get a dorm. During the first year,  one of the teachers called her out in front of the class, making a mockery of her animation and calling it racist. A gray scale animation about aliens on a planet, but the aliens were dark in color. Had nothing to do with race. She was treated horribly that her fellow students wrote statements and went with her to a meeting. Even they felt bad for what happened to our daughter. Very supportive. Either the Dean or assistant Dean, not sure who we talked to, said he'd take care of it, then decided there was nothing wrong with what happened. They only care about money and will find any way to add on more fees. You don't get to choose your dorm or room mates, and there's a set rent payment.  my daughter had 2 roommates and 1 left so they received an email they would have to compensate the rent for the roommate that left or agree to take another. Obviously they agreed to another roommate but not sure how they can be charged for the one that left  I could write a book on the crap we have dealt with. If my daughter didn't love the other teachers and the classes so much I would have had her leave. That being said, she had classes all day until 6pm and did homework until 11 or 12 and would pass out and get up early for class again. She stopped coming home on the weekends and missed easter because of all the school work she had. Id drive almost 3 hrs to see her on sun where she would show my what she was working on then would get right back to work. Almost 6 hrs of driving for a 20 min visit. She was behind on work and when asked for extensions was told no. They have unrealistic expectations. Some, not all, teachers act like they are the only class the student takes. She didnt get a chance to make friends or really enjoy portland other than check out nearby stores when she had to buy supplies. My other daughter goes to a different private school and they are so helpful and communicative and nice. It's amazing. I wish every school could be like that.", 'Amazing College of Art. My review is based only on my experience as a viewer and not as a college student.

While touristing around in the streets of Portland, we came across this awesome College that features amazing art galleries (open to the public + free of charge) with all of the amazing work of the talented local students.

Coming here on the weekend wasn’t too crowded, we even went up the stairs and explored some more art work and some of the cool art rooms. Some students were working on their art and we even got to see the really dope photo room with its own dark room. So so dreamy!

The art and talent of these students truly reflects on their art work. Can’t wait to come back in here and check out some of the newer art work. The galleries and art work changes constantly so make sure to stop by and check it out. Everyone is welcome!', 'Great open house. This is a very unique art school with friendly staff and students. I hope my daughter goes here.', 'Lovely art school with great facilites and tools un Portland Maine. A must yo visit']

name: Saint Joseph's College of Maine
reviews:
['We are wrapping up a great run at St. Joe’s!! Our son is completing his MBA after receiving his undergrad last spring while having played for the mens soccer team throughout. The entire experience was excellent! From the quality of the education, caliber of the athletic program, friendships made, growth as a person, support of the coaches and admin staff, and last but not least the beautiful location. I would recommend St. Joe’s to any student seeking these attributes. Go Monks!', 'Love everything about this school! Such a welcoming and supportive community with an absolutely beautiful campus.', "Our daughter transferred to Saint Joseph's for her sophomore year from a large university out west. She chose SJC because it offered the major she was interested in and gave her the ability to participate in a Division III sport, alpine skiing. She has had nothing but a positive experience! The academics have been a great fit for her, she has made great friends and has enjoyed the camaraderie of the ski team. The overall atmosphere of academics and athletics has exceeded our expectations. The professors are very attentive, and the ski team coaching staff has been amazing. To top it off, you can't beat the beautiful close knit campus on Sebago lake.", "We have a daughter who is currently a sophomore on campus. Our son now has decided to attend St Joe's next September. Once we walked on campus, met staff and current students, both our kids decided right then that's where they would be attending. Both play LAX, and after meeting with Coach Keenan for the girls and Coach Cosentino for the boys, both our kids felt welcomed. They had found a second home to play LAX and get a great education . As parents, we love the safety the campus offers and the close knit community, so we couldn't have been more pleased when our son decided to attend also! Such a beautiful campus on the lake makes visits enjoyable every single time.

Sincerely,
Kevin and Richelle Wesley
Massachusetts", "St. Joseph's College strikes a great balance of providing their students with a top notch education along with an outstanding athletic program. I can't say enough good things about the family orientated, student first culture the College, Athletic Department and specifically, the Women's Alpine Ski and Lacrosse team coaches provide our daughter and her teammates. We strongly recommend Saint Joseph's College to anyone looking for a great education while pursuing their passion for top notch athletics!"]

name: Southern Maine Community College
reviews: ['Not great… The campus itself is good, but the administration could be better. The dorm buildings don’t get any sort of regular cleaning in the common areas, and some instructors are quite… interesting. I probably would not choose to go here again.', 'Nice outdoor antique auto show. Food truck. Small show but very pleasant. Some unusual cars. Some beautiful restorations. To keep it short I'll say I personally cannot imagine finding a better school at the junior college level. I have found that whatever range of learning someone is in, or whatever their level of understanding is the school will match that and work with them to help further their education. The people that work and also go there, are extremely great!!"]

name: University of Southern Maine
reviews:
["A school with an exceptionally beautiful campus centrally located. What's not to like? It's the deception and deciet that seems to be threaded into the marketing approach. All these pop up costs and fee increases that are not mentioned as well as ridiculous fees for books in a digital age. It doesn't leave a favorable first impression as a parent. Being upfront on costs can go a long way on not creating negative energy/feelings toward the University that inevitably arise with the emerging truth.", 'Do not go here. The University hires and supports professors who misgender students. Disability accommodations are a joke. Lastly, the parking situation is TERRIBLE. Plan to spend an additional $100-200 on parking tickets per semester and trust me, they won’t dismiss them.', 'UMaine student here. I’ve been trying to get summer intern housing for a month. Housing never picks up the phone. My application was submitted a month ago. Was told I was guaranteed a spot but now they’re telling me they don’t know if they have availability. Ridiculous. They should genuinely be ashamed.', 'I find the low scores interesting because you are essentially rating yourself. If you have any reference at all it is because you had an experience at another school that you had an obvious reason to transfer from. This school is ripe to provide a student with exactly what they work toward. The administration is very accommodating and the professors provide the students with the opportunity to think for themselves. The core requirements promote a well rounded student who can think critically and make decisions based on that judgment. I would highly recommend this school for traditional as well as non traditional students. This review is provided by a non-traditional student who went full-time and graduated.', 'You are better off going to another University if you are set on the city of Portland.  While Portland is a great city, the University is one big disaster that is apparently getting worse with massive layoffs due to "budget shortfalls" even as much of the administration at the top get raises (one financial officer got a 40K raise bringing her salary to 250K)...figure that one out. Which brings me to my next point, if you are coming to this place for an education, think twice, this is run more like a business, it is an embarrassment to higher education.  Great faculty members have been laid off left and right in certain majors deemed "unneeded" by the current higher ups.

Even if you find a major you want that is not being downsized or terminated, there is still the issue of money.  No one from the business office will help you.  They are unsympathetic to the average students needs.  Because of that, and other reasons I will explain, you will likely graduate here with debt.  Even if you try to find ways to make the experience more affordable as it should be, you are likely to meet with denial.  For example, and from my personal experience, I lived in Maine for 3 years.  I rented there, worked and paid taxes there, got mail there.  By all accounts I was a resident of Maine but the University never granted me instate, after several pleas, they still rejected me with no reason given.  I went to the financial aid office, the only advice I got was "take out more loans".  Great advice to give a 20 year old.  No advice or attempts to help me find scholarship I might be eligible for by the financial aid office.  I did try to look on my own but there are so many scholarships, especially ones that are under the radar that nonetheless might be suitable to me, that I find it hard to believe that avenue was never explored with me when I visited the office.  They just want a quick, easy fix/response to students with legit questions (on how to make UNI more affordable, etc.) - like take out loans.  Great, but USM offers little help after graduating with job placement which is not good considering the advice you got for three years, "take out loans".  Considering the money you pay, this is not acceptable.  But considering the advice I got from fin. aid and apathy I got from the business department I guess I should have seen it coming!

This is one bloated bureaucratic mess.  Greed at the top with tons of unjustified raises while the talent "below" (great teachers) are axed because of "budget issues".  Learn elsewhere!']

name: Thomas College
reviews: ['Sweet twin turf fields...field hockey is actually not like watching paint dry..it is actually exciting...who woulda guessed that.  Thomas College has done this right!', "The Athletic Center was nice we had a good event but there didn't seem to be any fans or air flow so it was tiring. If it had better air flow or AC it would have been a 5 star", 'Was there for a conf this week. Alot of classrooms was hot. The food was ok nothing to write home about. Dorms where ok. I went to the room and found throw away towels. This was a green confereance.', 'Great school always doing things for the entire community. So much more then just a college. Lucky to have amazing schools locally. Do what you can to support them when you can.', "As an institution of higher learning, this college isn't a bad choice.  My review isn't about the entire school, or the school as a whole; this review is merely my perspective based solely on my experience working there from 2015-2019.  As the Director of the Theatre Program, I was repeatedly disappointed by the lack of interest in the theatrical arts here.  The people in charge of activities would constantly toss the drama club aside.  I would literally show up for rehearsal, and be told that another activity was happening in the auditorium and my rehearsal would have to be canceled.  One time, an activity was scheduled on a Thursday night just before Opening Night of my show!  Talk about feeling marginalized and unimportant. The idea of this being a big deal was foreign to the Activities Coordinator, but if I felt marginalized, how do you think my student/actors felt?  My first year there was phenomenal and the play that I wrote and directed was a SMASH HIT!  As my time at Thomas moved along, I began to realize that most of the students are just too busy with trying to pass their classes, and can not handle extra curricular activities of the artistic nature.  In 2019, no one showed up to join the club, no one showed any interest in acting at all.  I even tried to adapt the program and make it a Comedy Club, to no avail.  My take away is that Thomas is not a bad place, but if you're interested in the arts (at least the dramatic arts) this is probably not the place for you.  It's a great business school and has an awesome criminal justice program; however, theatre is definitely not a priority."]

name: Unity Environmental University
reviews:
["Unity Environmental University has been extremely disorganized and unresponsive on the administrative side.
I've already been enrolled here for over a year, but requested a stop‑out for this past January term multiple times. I was still enrolled and billed for the January class I never attended. I then clearly stated I wanted to start in February, made my payment, and set up a payment plan — yet the advisors confused my request for the stop out that I requested in January, removed my course from Canvas that I was originally given access to, deleted my schedule, and left me without access on the day before class opened..the one I already began payment on. The last 2 days, I made several attempts at contacting at least 5 different departments with no response. I sit here at 5am wondering if I'll have class or not.
Being fully prepared for a new term, only to have your class ripped out from under you the day before it starts, is unacceptable and incredibly stressful.
To be clear, I have loved every professor I’ve had here. The faculty have been excellent. The problem is entirely with admin.
The repeated errors, lack of communication, being texted by advisors and told I was emailed about some communication only to find an email never existed (several times) and failure to manage basic enrollment functions have made it impossible to trust this institution. I am now actively exploring transfer options because Unity has shown zero accountability.
If you’re considering this school, be prepared for billing mistakes, ignored requests, and major administrative failures — even though the professors themselves are great.", 'I started at Unity in 2023 and just graduated in 2025. Unity is the most holistic and environmentally focused university one could strive for. Their online program is balanced and effective at giving one the ability to have a life and pursue a degree. I wholeheartedly support anyone with a passion for the environment or animals to join. Everyone may run into their issues with certain things during their college experience but if you email your advisor consistently they will figure out how to help you! I love this university and may consider a masters degree with them too.', "NEVER go to this school. They constantly encourage the use of AI on assignments, despite it destroying our environment. Not a great look for an environmental school. And it's not only students, professors will clearly be using AI to grade and respond to assignments. This is obviously inaccurate but if you bring it up with your professor, they will use AI to respond. Do you know how pointless it is to argue with an AI chat bot?

Their use of AI is not their only weak point. They constantly switch professors to teach new classes, but the new professors don't make new content. I doubt they even know what content they're supposedly teaching. They will still use the videos of lessons from previous professors, as well as their instructions and rubrics for assignments, often times without proof reading. Yet, they grade the assignments on what they personally think it should include, meaning you practically have to read their mind if you want a good grade.

I strongly discourage anyone from choosing this school, it is full of incompetent leadership and professors who clearly have no idea what they are doing. I am currently looking at other schools and hoping to switch soon.

Editing my review to include that their loan policy is OPT OUT, not opt in. I had 12k in loans I never knew about or agreed to, and I did not need them. But since I never opted out, it was automatically applied. Now I can't afford to pay them in full so I'm out a ton of money from interest. I don't know if I signed without realizing it or what, but they never made it clear that over half my tuition was being covered by loans. I thought I was paying in full each term, there is no mention of loans on the payment screen. If I could give this school negative stars I would. Such a bad business and educational institution it's unbelievable.", 'I am currently going to Unity Environmental University using distance education to get a Bachelor of Science in Animal Health and Behavior, and I absolutely adore the school! Teachers are prompt when you need help they are just an email away and your advisor is also always quick to reply if you have any questions or concerns. Great school 10/10 recommendation.', "I took one online class and had a terrible experience. I was sold into being able to learn at my pace only to absolutely overloaded with homework. None of the staff seems to talk to each other. The orientation video says you aren't expected to complete assignments on your first 2 weeks but my teacher gave us 3 homework assignments recently right at the beginning and the student advisor was completely useless and in now way helpful."]

name: Allegany College of Maryland
reviews: ["To go to this college you have to submit to completely invasive digital surveillance inside your own home.  You will be required to take tests at home because professors are too lazy to proctor their own tests, so use AI to proctor tests (you're not allowed to use AI for anything, but your professor will use AI for everything, including assessing your work).  You are expected to use HonorLock, which requires you to submit your biometrics, a photo of a government issued license, and video of your home (yes, an actual video of your home; to make sure you're not cheating, but of course someone stores that video and now a recording of your private home is made public to the university).\n\nGovernment run schools are preparing to accept invasive digital surveillance inside your own personal, private spaces.  Never forget that a lot of what government run schools are is to prepare you for the dystopian plans they have to monitor you at all times for the purposes of control, while accepting those in authority are not subject to the same monitoring and control.", 'Had my teeth examined exrayed and cleaned. They are students so they are a little slower. They must ck in with their teachers. It may take more than 1 visit to get your wk completed. However, were very kind and worked to try to make the process comfortable. Great price! They charged $30 or $40. My Dentist wanted $400 after insurance.', 'The Allegany College of Maryland campus offers an exceptional academic environment and supportive community that empowers personal and intellectual growth. Its faculty is a notable asset, with professors who are both renowned experts in their fields and dedicated educators who prioritize the development of well-rounded individuals through comprehensive learning experiences that extend beyond the classroom.', 'I have visited so many colleges. This is one of the very few I would consider attending (and I currently am). I chose this school because the professors and staff actually help the students. The campus is smaller, but in no means lacking. I always feel so welcomed here. This college really is what you make of it, you can have the full college experience if you want tom', 'This school nursing program is racially profiled. All white board of nurses is laughable. Upload your picture to your profile for a grade… huh? Why? Your pictures are not on the website! Their nursing program is a joke failing student because of clinical skills, when they are literally passing academically. What a money scam. The nursing bag that is almost $100 bucks does not have enough supplies to complete a skill with. So, basically make believe all the way through. If you are black and dark complexion like me, don’t waste your money and time here. Go traditional!']

name: Anne Arundel Community College
reviews: ['The staff were all very friendly and accommodating! I had a pedicure complete with a neck warmer and hand massage. This pedicure included hot booties with paraffin wax. It was the most relaxing pedicure I’ve ever had. My nails were polished expertly and my feet felt great! A complimentary glass of prosecco was an added bonus!!', 'Highly recommend Tipsy Nail Bar. Their customer service was fantastic. Walking in the place was beautiful and I was greeted warmly & offered a beverage, then promptly seated for my pedicure. Holly was AMAZING! Thank you for doing such an amazing job on my pedicure! The thought and care put into my visit was greatly appreciated. I also had my eyebrows waxed & tinted, as well as my eyelashes tinted. They look so good and natural. I am not a big fan of makeup and this will allow me to not have to apply any for the next few months. I highly recommend their services & will be back!', 'I was very pleased with how nice the techs were (both for my nails and for my pedicure) at the Tipsy Nail Salon on College Pkwy in Fort Myers FL.  I felt like they did not rush and were very accommodating. They did a fantastic job!!! The facility was very clean and cute inside. I thought that offering complimentary drinks and a gift of the hand lotion at the end was a really nice way to show appreciation to your customers.   Continuing  with that mindset and customer service and I would choose to go no one else. I have already recommended this place to friends. Thank you for a really pleasant experience today.', 'Diane is always so nice and friendly and her work is the best. The salon is beautiful and very relaxing. I would recommend Tipsy to anyone', 'If you are thinking about taking online classes at this college, I would not recommend taking ENG 101 with Marjorie Paoletti. During my time in the class, I was accused of using ChatGPT on an assignment, and I was told that other students had received similar accusations. This created a stressful and discouraging learning environment. In addition to my experience in the class, I also had issues when contacting the front desk. When I called for assistance, the staff were often rude and did not seem willing to help or answer questions clearly. It made resolving concerns much more difficult than it needed to be. Overall, my experience with both the course and the administrative support was disappointing. I hope the college works on improving communication and professionalism so future students have a better experience.']

name: Baltimore City Community College
reviews:
["To discontinue use of the Virtual Help Desk without any notice to students (and very little notice to staff it seems) less than a week before the start of semester is beyond careless and it seems like complete disregard of students and education as a whole is the motto of this institution. Even besides this, getting a hold of somebody actually helpful is a almost impossible task. I spoke with three people yesterday (and took everyone's names) and am in the same place that I was before, only more upset by not only the lack of resolution but the absence of class and couth from staff members and work studies students working at the front lines of communication for the offices of this institution. I got nowhere with everybody that I spoke to on top of being met with such unprofessional and unnecessary attitudes. It almost feels like somebody is sabotaging the institution with how poorly it is run and the utter lack of competency and communication. It is a shame the magnitude of such egregious lack of consideration for students that overshadows the select few astounding professors and other staff I have encounter.

Teaching in my personal opinion, is beyond a labor of love and I will always have respect for educators but even more so for those select few wonderful people working under such poor leadership. For them, 5 stars; for the institution 0!", 'I’m a veteran and was interested in using my GI Bill  to enroll for spring semester. Was told I have to send an email to make an appointment. No answer! I emailed again & no answer. I drove to the school and was then informed to CC THE DEAN and then I should get a response. Guess what?! STILL no response. I also attempted to call multiple times and no answer ONCE AGAIN. Went to CCBC and was helped immediately. I would give this community college 0 stars if allowed', 'Very rude workers. I called the Registration office and Teresa Clayton was who I spoke with. I called because I was trying to register for my classes. I told her that the class that an advisor told me to register for was giving me an error message.

She asked did I speak with an advisor, I told her “yes.” She then proceeded to ask me “so what the problem is?” What representative speaks to a student like that???? Very rude. The workers act as if they hate their job.', "As others have stated, this place has no interest in assisting prospective or current students. No replies to messages and no answered calls. They clearly don't care and don't want your money.", "To be honest this is the worst school I been to. The professors that I've had struggle with communicating so it leaves everyone confused.  On top of that waiting 3 months and counting on financial aid disbursement is unheard of."]

name: University of Baltimore
reviews:
['I would consider donating to them after their desperate ads if they didn’t fire my late grandmother that worked there for several decades over an impersonal email which ultimately fed into her early death. Good luck', 'I am a current student, and I can confidently say that this university is declining in both academic quality and institutional focus. Leadership and staff appear more invested in self-promotion and distributing politically charged messaging than in supporting the academic and professional advancement of their students. Unfortunately, this shift in priorities has become increasingly visible across various departments.

Poor communication has become a persistent issue. Emails go unanswered for weeks, and students are often left in the dark about course updates, deadlines, and policy changes. When responses do come, they are often vague or dismissive, leaving students feeling unheard and unsupported. This unresponsiveness is not only frustrating but also deeply discouraging, especially for those of us balancing work, family, and graduate-level coursework.

Classroom environments have also suffered from a lack of strategic planning and engagement. Courses are frequently reorganized mid-semester with little notice, leaving students scrambling to adapt to new formats, assignments, and platforms. These chaotic shifts reflect a troubling lack of foresight and consideration for the learning experience.

If you are a working professional seeking a structured, student-focused academic experience that respects your time, effort, and investment, I would strongly recommend looking elsewhere. The university needs to urgently realign its priorities and refocus on the needs of its tuition-paying students, the very individuals who sustain its operations.', 'I love everything about this university, from the advisor to my professor and also the staff in the various offices such as financial aid, registration they all help to make my time at this university very pleasant.', 'I transferred here after finishing at CCBC, that transition went smooth for the most part. I liked my time here and I graduated. The location is good, right at midtown. Its not all the way into the city which made the drive less intense as a student that commuted. The class sizes were small to medium, not very large which I liked. Evening classes worked well with my full time work schedule. Most of the professors I had were great and also like how they offer career search assistance and workshops both as a student and alumni so some of the services dont stop because you no longer go to that school. The new library looks nice. By the time they redone that building I already graduated so not sure how nice it is inside but from the outside it looks great.', 'The Professors are great!! The administration, not so great. I don’t not understand why it is so hard for them to just do their job. I have to literally follow up everyday in person (I’m a online student), just for them to process anything. Then, they have the audacity to have an attitude as if I have done something wrong. This has not made for a great experience. I want to finish here so bad, but I’m transferring. It’s stressful!']

name: Bowie State University
reviews:
["My daughter was a student at Bowie for the Fall 2025 semester and the whole experience has been an absolute nightmare. She is leaving after finals. We can't take it anymore.

For staters, Bowie State is very unorganized. The right hand doesn't know what the left hand is doing. The housing and financial aid offices constantly send out notifications with dates they never keep. I've received four emails saying she has balance and it is going to collections only to log in to her student account and see the balance is zero. Emails to the financial aid and billings offices go unanswered for months and the people who answer the phones don't work for the school (African call-center), so they never know how to help. Scholarship/grant money is never properly posted to student accounts, leaving parents having to pay cost that should be covered by scholarship/grant money. My daughter had 3 scholarships paid directly to Bowie in September and October 2025 and Bowie still has not posted them to her account even though the semester is now officially over. We had to pay $12,000 out of pocket because Bowie is delayed in applying scholarship money. At this point, we don't know where the money is.

The housing situation is even worse. My daughter was in ELLC this semester and we spent a whopping $5,300 for her to be on campus for the Fall term, plus an additional $2,400 for her meal plan. The rooms in ELLC are freezing and the windows don't open so the ventilation is poor. The bathrooms have mildew in them and whenever students complain to the RA's/DA nothing gets done. Even though the meal plan is required to be one campus the food in the cafeteria is horrible (frozen pizza and chicken nuggets). Most of the students are resorting to ordering from DoorDash or UberEats because the cafeteria is closed on the weekends. The school is in the middle of nowhere with no grocery stores or food places close by. All and all, Bowie was the worst $12,000 I've ever spent. I want to support HBCUs but Bowie is terrible.", 'I visited Bowie State University to explore the campus and facilities. It had a very welcoming and organized environment and was easy to navigate through. There were also some interesting statues, murals, and historic buildings on campus that were enjoyable to look at. I would highly recommend going here.', 'NIGHTMARE!! Someone needs to investigate Bowie’s Financial Aid Department, their unprofessionalism, lack of communication, and disorganization. My daughter no longer goes here and if you’re reading this, don’t go here! They currently are stating that my daughter has a $10,000 dollar plus bill for the Fall 2025 semester, stating that her funds were reversed back to FASFA. Yet FASFA has not been made aware of this reversal. Not to mention that it  was nothing but problems from the very beginning since my daughter moved into her dorm. I have called countless times and all they say is “we have to escalate this and someone will follow up within 24-48 hours, only they never follow up with you.', "The campus is improving,but they charge building construction fee as part of your tuition. They're also far behind in many ways, especially technology. Professors are not always available during their office hours making it difficult to reach them with any questions or getting assistance.", 'The State of Maryland needs to do an audit on their financial aid department. They are taking money from 3rd party institutions (scholarships/grants) and not disbursing that money to the student accounts.']

name: Capitol Technology University
reviews:
["Great university good people and staff with great opportunities such as scholarships and you don't need a super high goal to go I would recommend and this is the place I would chose for a university 😁", 'Great place. Very open to working with their students.', 'Had my first class here staff is friendly. Will have to update at a later time.', 'Forever in life of those whom they gave a chance!

I have chosen to pursue my academic journey with Capitol Technology University because it stands as one of the most innovative schools, not just within the United States of America. The Capitol Tech crosses the borders, offering education and hope around the world! It breaks the status quo, shatters barriers, and offers opportunities to those who may have felt lost in life, society, or in their thoughts.
I believe that united by the recognition that the status quo is not getting the job done, academia, experts, readers and all who care, can and will change the world to better place to live, create and give back to communities!
The status quo is inviting attacks on digital world every second of every day. The status quo is a slow surrender of centuries long discoveries, talents and responsibilities.
We all want that to stop. Therefore, I invite you to join me in the privilege of fighting for the right to stand together in our mission to educate, mentor, and enhance the skills of future talents.

Dr. Ludmila Morozova-Buss', "Outstanding university geared towards the education of today's technology. This is our son's second year at CTU after transferring from 2 years at Frostburg State University. He wants to work on computer programming, robotics and drones; and Capitol Tech has the programs for these technologies which are far more in depth than just regular universities. They have very helpful and friendly staff both in administration and professors. It is a small university so there is a lot of one on one help, if need be. It has a moderate size campus that is very welcoming and quiet, especially being so closely located to the Baltimore/Washington Parkway. CTU is reasonably priced for tuition and on campus housing. And although it seems like it is in the middle of nowhere, it is halfway between Baltimore and Washington DC within the suburb of Laurel. It is affiliated with several government agencies and therefore has many internships within them. For students who are highly intelligent with technology and like the comfort and quiet of a small university, I highly recommend Capitol Technology University!"]

name: Cecil College
reviews: ['When to a graduation. It was nice. Its was long, the speakers need to have they speeches less than 3 minutes. We came see the students, not hear a lot of no never mind stuff.  Some people may want to get babysitter next time. To much crying and loud talking or yelling.   The staff need to get more control. At one time I could not hear the students name. And cell phone going off.', 'Community college is a great thing to have in a county so I’m happy Cecil has one. I think it’s a good stepping stone to go to community college after high school and before university. It gives you a feel of what college is all about without having to leave home right away. They have extremely good prices for classes. Ruth from the bookstore was always nice and helpful. Professor Cohen was my favorite professor I had when I went there. He was always funny and nice. If he ever saw you on campus he would always come greet you and ask you how you were doing. It’s remarkable that Cecil has a free food option across from the cafe if you forgot your wallet but still wanted a snack. The only thing I didn’t like about Cecil was that the way the advisors set up my classes I graduated on the wrong year because no one told me the way the graduation deadline worked especially with my classes (when I got close to finishing there). Having the wrong year really upsets me and they said they can’t fix it now. I would give Cecil 5 stars instead of 3 if I would have been able to graduate on the correct year like I wanted to.', 'This college is in the business of manufacturing conflict at the expense of student welfare. There are quite a few good people working at this college. Unfortunately, the minority of folks at the top poison the well. The college suffers from the typical lack of education training in most of their professors, and this does result in severe deficiencies in the quality of the company\'s services, but this appears to be a problem common in all community colleges. This college appears to be operated with a "nothing to lose" attitude towards students, which means they don\'t appear to act in the best interest of their customers, namely, students. Leadership from the top appears to be nonexistent from my perspective. I wish I saw a more hands-on approach from the college\'s President since the faculty and staff appear to lack unified purpose and vision. Accountability is very lacking at this college and there is no clear information on chain of command when there is an issue. The college\'s private security force, Public Safety, appears to often be used to escalate peaceful, but tense situations into highly distressing situations without probable cause of suspicion for any potential for actual harm to anyone. This is not the fault of Public Safety itself, rather, the faculty and staff who make students feel unsafe by needlessly involving Public Safety in otherwise docile situations.\n\nI give two stars and not 1 star because of the many people at this college who act in the best interest of student at least most of the time. A lot of good things happen here. However, I think that the negative aspects are more material to the functioning of the college as a whole and for that reason I don\'t give it more than 2 stars.', 'Well maintained college in cecil County. Wonderful staff, great security in the campus.  This college needs a good cafeteria, though. I see food truck on some days', "Signed up for Electrical courses at cecil college. Was supposed to start tonight. Just found out from another student that they had canceled the course. Do unprofessional. Now I'll have to wait another entire semester to sign up for a course some where else, because I will NOT waste my time with Cecil College ever again."]

name: College of Southern Maryland
reviews:
['There is an extreme lack of communication between advisors. One will tell you one thing and another will tell you another completely different thing, advisors are also extremely difficult to get in contact they seem to all be working with other students when I call that may just be bad luck on my end but I’ve called 3 days in a row and I still have not been able to get in contact. I work all day so it’s hard for me to make it up to Campus to meet in person.', 'A visiting student wanting to take a few prerequisites. Would not waive my English and math placement test with my bachelor’s degree (taken 3 college level English class , and three math classes) but requested me to provide the full syllabus per class (assignments ,due dates,topics), everyone I spoke to and my alumni school found this insane . I provided  course description for all my classes to facilitate the process for them and an official  transcript (very high GPA) which is considered documentation but they still couldn’t figure out if I was college ready. I sent them a professional email expressing my confusion and frustration which I received no response( from transcript coordinator or the president). I have so much respect for community colleges because they are open to everyone from different  backgrounds and I would think they would be the most understanding and accommodating to everyone’s different needs. But I was very wrong with this school.', "The only reason this is getting two stars is because of the amazing teachers from the paramedic program. Almost every class I too here the teachers were awful and unhelpful. I just dropped an online class because the teacher posted things that didn't line up with the material and included questions in her tests that weren't covered in the chapter, power points or extra learning material. Most of the teachers do not care about their class and act miserable

The disabilities office isn't great from my experience either and I ended up not using them again due to how hard it was to get in touch with them sometimes.", "This was a great school because it was way much better than Prince George's Community College. The problems are that the Dance Department is not very organized, have professors that are terrible teachers of teaching the Dance Ensemble and Ballet Dance courses. Plus, they do not offer contemporary, hip hop and tap dance, which is needed. There are also poor administrations in the Dance Department that needs improvement. Plus, some of the students including the teachers try to bullied me on social media, but I do not tolerated because I am too rigid for that. But at least I graduated in 2012 with a 3.80 grade point average and receive my Associate's Degree in Theatre and Dance. Now, I can move forward, move to another state to pursue my dreams including doing my dance careers, operating a better, successful dance company than College of Southern Maryland and other dance companies I had issues with in the past, get married, start a
family and live a healthy long life. I would highly recommended students to attend to this college, but not get a degree in Theatre and Dance. If you want to get a degree in Theatre and Dance, go to Towson University because their dance department is much friendlier than College of Southern Maryland Dance Department. Good luck to all students and have a bless life.", "CSM is a corrupt academic organization that has an incompetent Bursar's office.   We tried to drop a class within the deadline and were unable to due to multiple system errors.  After multiple phone calls we were told to call back the next day and that all would be well.  We did and were told all was taken care of.  One month later we receive a letter saying we are denied our refund with no explanation.  Multiple calls and emails to the Bursar's office go nowhere.  Very unfortunate for such a small academic institution to build their Bursar's office on dishonesty, lack of integrity and lousy customer service.  Be warned that they are unorganized and incompetent and it will require numerous phone calls to achieve absolutely nothing.  A totally disgraceful office."]

name: Washington Adventist University
reviews:
["Washington Adventist University, located at 7600 Flower Ave in the serene environment of Takoma Park, is frequently highlighted in my social and professional circles as a distinguished pillar of values-based higher education. From numerous insightful conversations with alumni and healthcare professionals in the DMV area, a clear consensus emerges regarding the institution’s exceptional ability to integrate academic rigor with a profound commitment to service and character development. My colleagues often point to the university’s substantive strengths in nursing and music, noting that graduates emerge not just as skilled professionals, but as compassionate leaders who are highly respected in their respective fields. In frequent discussions about the Maryland educational landscape, those I trust repeatedly emphasize the faculty's unique dedication to personal mentorship, creating a supportive atmosphere that my acquaintances describe as a transformative intellectual home. I am particularly struck by the university’s strategic proximity to the nation’s capital, which provides students with a sophisticated array of internship opportunities that bridge the gap between faith-based learning and global impact. It is evident from the collective feedback of those around me that the administration manages the campus with a clear-eyed vision, successfully balancing modern academic demands with a respectful nod to its historic Seventh-day Adventist heritage. Many of my friends who have seen their children thrive at WAU highlight the small class sizes and the inclusive community as decisive factors in fostering both professional confidence and technical moxie. Reflecting on these overwhelmingly positive sentiments from a trusted network, I view Washington Adventist University as a prestigious and dependable institution that fulfills its educational mandate with undeniable class, integrity, and a heartfelt dedication to the public good.", 'This school is one of the worst school I have seen, the administrative staffs are nonchalant about one’s future and keep running the business to the ground, they neglect their responsibilities and the school gives no career assistance. Good employees with excellent communication skills had their contract terminated since the school downsized. Also, foreign students are neither offered relief, grant or scholarship funds. In addition, one can never get in touch with a contact person either through calls or emails as they will never respond. I will advise one invests in a better school especially if you are an international student as you will benefit from the outcome. Attending this school is a big regret, since they’ve continuously proved me right, they waste time in preparing immigration documents, never respond to emails or calls and you might end up losing a good job offer.Lastly, the administrative staffs have no God-like characters and forget they were once immigrants. This is my experience therefore, I won’t advise international students to attend this school since we are seen to be non-existent. Nevertheless, the academic staffs are really nice.This is my awful experience, can you guys try and improve especially during this COVID season.', 'I'm writing this review on behalf of my husband and everything he's gone through. WAU has not handled my husband's issues professionally since the time he started there in 2010. He graduated in December 2014, after his professors cleared him to graduate. It was only four years later, when he went to renew his teaching contract and was receiving an "intern" pay salary that we discovered WAU was not releasing his transcripts because they had him in their records as not graduated. He was missing a 100-level BIO class. This was the first time we had heard of it, and his advisors as well. After trying multiple times over the course of a school year to contact people and resolve the issue, we still aren't in the clear, even after he passed a CLEP exam.

WAU has been extremely difficult to work with. He has not received timely responses to his phone calls or emails, he's often left in the dark over the paperwork he needs to complete or have completed by other departments, and this whole situation should have been avoided in the beginning by the registrar's office not clearing him to graduate if a 100-level BIO class was the issue.

Unfortunately, this is not unique. We both have had friends who have "graduated" from WAU to find out, when their transcripts are needed, that they have not graduated because they were missing basic level courses not relevant to their careers. WAU will not pardon this, even though it is clearly an institutional issue, so past students are left without diplomas until they finish the courses YEARS later.

I do not recommend WAU, and have been so highly disappointed in their lack of professionalism, timeliness, and attention to detail every time I or my husband has worked with them.', 'This school is REQUIRING ALL STUDENTS AND ALL STAFFS TO BE VACCINATED with NO WAIVER that’s terrible people have medical issues that they cannot get the vaccine because it will causes serious reaction and what happen to my body my choice I would not go to a school that does not premier choice! ‼️‼️‼️‼️‼️‼️‼️', "A former student had to leave Washington Adventist University  because they were being discriminated against their race. They went to a different Adventist University. I am glad that Washington Adventist University did not receive the rest of money since they went to different Adventist University. They are pretending to be Christian while doing the work for the devil. They are all about money. They are liar, selfish, wicked, ungrateful, and jealous. They refused to help the students. I am looking forward for them to be punished on Judgement's Day."]

name: Frostburg State University
reviews:
["If you are a student considering a future career in mathematics, computer science or any other STEM field, I would not recommend Frostburg State University to you. The mathematics and computer science curricula are so far out of date that it is becoming increasingly more difficult to get the proper education and training needed to pursue careers and perform jobs in these fields at a standard level based on today’s standards, tools and expectations. Rather than preparing students for graduate study or industry, the program leaves them underprepared and discouraged.

In addition, the lack of any type of effective support structure at Frostburg State University is not only an additional problem, but also creates an environment where students are expected to do well in hard technical subjects without any form of meaningful instructional guidance, mentorship or department investment. The absence of support in a field that relies heavily on precision of clarity, structure and involvement from the faculty is truly a detriment to students (especially) of the department.

In my experience, several faculty members within the department actively contribute to these shortcomings. More specifically, Christopher Boyer, Michael Flinn and Stephanie Boggs have shown through their lack of commitment to ensuring student success through their teaching, responsiveness and commitment to assisting struggling and motivated students that they are light years behind any level of standard expected of public universities. Rather than fostering growth or competence, their approach often creates unnecessary barriers that hinder academic progress.

It is difficult to understand how a program can expect to succeed when students are met with indifference instead of guidance. Universities exist to educate and prepare students for the real world, yet this department appears stagnant and disengaged. It is not unexpected that an institution will continue to experience an ongoing decline in both funding and enrolment due to a lack of support and respect for its students.

For serious academics (mathematicians/computer scientists), Frostburg State University is going to be of little benefit to you because the mathematics/computer science department does not offer you the level of challenge, cutting edge technology, and faculty support that you'll need to succeed in either area of study.", 'hello yest I went hear for univesrsity and i got an epic degree here/./.. name: Goucher College
reviews: ['This is an excellent college with outstanding professors who want to know that you understand the instructions/lessons, retain what you were advised, and use what you were taught. The campus is breath taking...you don\'t mind studying while laying outside on the grass and listening to music or just the winds. The grounds are immaculate. The food is even great. Want to wonder off campus??? Well,  feel free but security is "always at the entrance" to assure that students (and associated staff/faculty/friends) are the only ones on campus. It is not only a safe campus but you truly feel secluded from the world when you are there. Top Security, Top Academics, Top buildings, Nice rooms, Great people, Outstanding professors, Wonderful activities, Great events. It certainly will "spoil" you. Class of 1990.', "Visited for a Parent's Weekend since my son is going there... I'm impressed by what seems like an authentic commitment to diversity and inclusion that might even trace its roots all the way back to the founders of the school.\n\nSo far it is turning out really well for my son. And he also vouches for the vegan and vegetarian options in the dining areas. :)", "In business department of Goucher, the professors are wonderful at providing support. They expect you to work hard but are fair. Administration and faculty can be hit or miss, but they are almost constantly understaffed so that makes sense. I didn't stick around for clubs because I work at the same time as attending full time, so I can't review those. I do reccomend the college getting a marching band though, especially to help with school spirit and interaction. My grad date is spring 2024, I'm unsure if that's important. But the school is usually very clean.", "Horrible institution. DO NOT SEND YOUR CHILD HERE. The entire college is just a money making scam. They don't care about your education here or your rights to an education. The administration is awful and has no clue what they're doing. If they don't like you for one reason or another they will begin targeting, harassing and attacking you until you get out of their school because they don't actually want you there. They aren't innovative or friendly, all they do is falsely advertise these things. Half of the people who enroll here as a freshman want to GTFO and transfer someplace better at the end of their first semester. This college depresses the students who live on campus. Only send your kids here if you want to waste your time, money, and degrade your child's mental health. Your time and money could be going to a better school that actually cares about the well-being and education of your child. Any school that you choose WILL be better than Goucher College in every aspect, even a community college. Again, DO NOT GO HERE if you don't want to waste your own valuable time and money. There are plenty of better options around. If I had the option to rate Goucher as 0 stars, I would.", 'Great location and quiet campus; friendly security guards, maintenance & cafeteria workers. But...Dorm doors are not always locked. Security gate is a joke. Technology is outdated. Grass not cut as often as it should be. Scarce parking. Classrooms are a lot like high school. Cafeteria has large selection, but like all cafeteria food you will get tired of it and since this is a small school there are no on campus alternatives.']

name: Hagerstown Community College
reviews: ['Dental Clinic wasted my time. The student was nice. Went to have my teeth cleaned never happened. The Doctor was not knowledgeable felt like I was going to have a major operation. Terrible experience!', "Reporting from the trenches in Fall 2025: Low energy place. Students are painfully underfunded, while the college itself seems to be thriving financially. HCC is exploiting the students by allowing them to use their financial aid money at their store which sells laptops and tablets for WAY more than Amazon. Federal Student Aid is meant to cover these costs, including transportation, clothing, etc, but HCC has made it so Financial aid is delayed on purpose in an attempt to retain the students past the middle of the semester so they can maximize their profits (past the refund deadline). The graduation rate speaks for itself. This place has almost ZERO of the amenities of any 4 year school, so what are they doing with all of the money? These poor kids think this is college, when they're missing 90% of the college experience here. I'm seriously considering reporting this place to the Department of Education for scamming these kids. College bound students, this is my advice: Apply to a technical school like JRTI or else a 4 year college. Most of the students at HCC were so disengaged that they just sat in class like zombies. College isn't supposed to be a miserable experience.", 'Good school for local kids in Washington County. Only three stars because trying to get a hold of anybody during regular business hours like the operator, admissions, or registrar when calling is horrible. You just get answering machines to call somebody else which nobody answers and you have to leave a message. This is unacceptable for a local College.', 'Very prompt and thorough on the snow / ice removal!!!', 'Great classes, great programs,and well educated professors.']

name: Harford Community College
reviews: ["I love this College! All the people and teachers are so nice and helpful. I've never been somewhere that I've felt so welcomed and cared about. If your thinking of community college this is the one to go to", "I only wish I could give zero stars. I'm a 60-year old, white, disabled male, who's being both discriminated and retaliated by HCC Senior Administration (age, race, disability) to include financial aid, printing of my degrees, as well as allowing me to take classes. I currently have earned eight associate degrees; however, I only have received six. One of them doesn't even list my major. In December 2025, I will earn a ninth degree (A.A. in Sociology - Social Work), but HCC refuses to award it to me. HCC currently has a policy where any student 60 years of age and older can take as many classes as they wish for free, but even though I'm of age, they refuse me classes. The U.S. Department of Education, Office of Civil Rights is currently investigating my allegations. That office previously investigated HCC approximately ten years ago for the same disability issue and HCC had to change their policy. HCC even refused a request from Harford County Government for mediation, and as of this email has not responded to the U.S.D.E. (OCR) for a request of mediation. They have zero intention of an amicable resolution to this matter, and I have zero doubt it's due to Dr. Theresa Felder. I have over 120 credits, eight associate degrees, I'm a 41-year old member of HCC's elite Phi-Theta-Kappa, and a cumulative GPA of 3.55; however, on more than one occasion I've been on academic probation for no reason whatsoever. HCC has done everything in their power to discourage me from continuing education, but I will not give up! Please do not allow your child or loved one to ever attend HCC, for their experience will be MISERABLE! Oh, a week ago, HCC canceled a grant issued to me by the Maryland Higher Education Commission for no reason, and there's absolutely NOTHING I can do about it! The entire administration is filled with people who discriminate, retaliate, and punish me for no reason whatsoever. Oh, and most important of all, don't seek Student Services, for I was denied disability accommodations, Student Emergency Assistance for no reason as well.", 'They claim to be community based but honestly while I was there I never felt more alone than anything. The teacher barely teach and if you’re major isn’t one of the common ones good luck with getting classes when you need them.', 'Beautiful campus! I enjoyed my time there very much.', 'Graduated from their nursing program and all graduates in my class passed their state boards on the first try. This speaks volumes of the Nursing program here. As a veteran they provided guidance on navigating the use of my GI benefits as well. Definitely glad I attended Hartford!']

name: Johns Hopkins University
reviews:
['A great campus to work, stay, and collaborate—comfortable and reliable regardless of moisture, temperature, or darkness.', 'My daughter enrolled in Geometry and it went very well initially, She did 50 % in 3 months. At that time the technical platform changed in the middle of the course and got a new link, while the old link remained. My daughter got stuck with the old link, could not get help when she contacted the teacher which caused a lot of frustration. When I understood what happened and tried to assist my daughter she had given up. She did not complete the course, got stuck at 50 % completion.', 'I never went to John Hopkins now cause I’m still in high school, but I went there for my uncle’s graduation. It was a lot of fun. He was the last one because he did the masters of public health was also raining for us and cold, but we had our jackets. We’re ready to support him and all that stuff I fell asleep for a little bit in the middle of some of the graduation part, but got to watch it. It was nice to miss school for it. Everything was cool although the speeches some of the speech parts was boring. Very very cool though and the homewood field was cool. I talk to my teacher that was at my uncle‘s graduation here in that college and he said he’s been to the field before for a baseball game. Also, some of my teacher said that is a really hard school to get into.', 'Johns Hopkins University stands as a global benchmark for excellence in education, research, and innovation. From its founding principles to its modern achievements, the university consistently demonstrates a deep commitment to advancing knowledge and improving lives around the world. It is widely respected for setting the standard in higher education, particularly in medicine, public health, science, engineering, and international studies.

One of the greatest strengths of Johns Hopkins University is its strong research culture. The university encourages curiosity, critical thinking, and interdisciplinary collaboration, allowing students and faculty to work on real world problems that have a meaningful global impact. Its research facilities, laboratories, and libraries are among the best in the world, fostering an environment where groundbreaking discoveries are not only possible but expected.

The quality of faculty at Johns Hopkins University is exceptional. Professors are not only experts in their fields but also dedicated mentors who genuinely care about student growth. They bring real world experience, cutting edge research, and a passion for teaching into the classroom, creating an intellectually stimulating and supportive academic atmosphere. Students benefit from close interaction with faculty, which enhances learning and inspires confidence.

Johns Hopkins University is also known for its rigorous academic standards. Courses are challenging yet rewarding, pushing students to think deeply, analyze critically, and develop strong problem solving skills. Graduates leave the university well prepared for leadership roles in academia, industry, healthcare, policy, and beyond. The reputation of the institution adds significant value to the degrees it offers, opening doors across the globe.

Beyond academics, the university provides a vibrant and inclusive campus life. Students from diverse cultural, social, and academic backgrounds come together, creating a rich and dynamic community. There are numerous student organizations, cultural activities, and opportunities for service and leadership that help students grow personally as well as professionally.

Johns Hopkins University also shows a strong commitment to societal impact. Through its medical institutions, public health initiatives, and global research programs, the university plays a crucial role in addressing some of the most pressing challenges facing humanity. Its work in healthcare, disease prevention, policy research, and innovation continues to influence lives far beyond campus boundaries.

Overall, Johns Hopkins University represents excellence, integrity, and innovation. It is a place where ambition meets opportunity, where knowledge is transformed into action, and where students are empowered to make a lasting difference in the world. For anyone seeking a world class education grounded in research, purpose, and global impact, Johns Hopkins University is truly outstanding.', "A world renowned university and medical system on a beautiful campus that is always clean and well maintained. The campus both the university and medical campus are situated in areas where petty crime can be an issue so always be vigilant but the university has extensive campus security and campus police on patrol. It's such a great campus and a great place to work or learn."]

name: Loyola University Maryland
reviews:
['this is the worst school, starting from the administration all the way down to the underwhelming campus life and trashy dormitories/food. i regret letting them bribe me into going here everyday and remember why it was my last choice. if you’re a graduating senior please consider the nearby universities.', "Update: My original review is still true but changing to 2 stars. After investing close to $300,000 in education, their follow-through with career placement was grossly unacceptable. Return on investment simply isn't there...

Original review:

Loyola Maryland is an excellent school -- really top notch faculty and great environment for students to learn and grow.  Other posts here are way off topic.  The school itself is fantastic and the campus is beautiful.", 'Lovely people, beautiful campus, top notch academics. Looking forward to my son starting in August!!!', 'The school has made honest effort to be less racist and take bias reports seriously. Still it feels as though horrible people still get away with a slap on the wrist and don’t learn anything. Also the school does not care about the quality of the engineering department. They have some great and caring professors there but the quality isn’t consistent throughout and you can get some really poor quality engineering education. Go elsewhere if you can for STEM majors. I had to teach myself an unacceptable amount in order to learn material.', "My son is graduating this May and we were extremely pleased with the college. The campus is like a park! My son put a great deal into the College and got back what he put in,  a great education, great experiences, a great professional network and great friends.
The private school setting adds the lifetime camaraderie. It's small enough that you can actually get to know your professors, yet big enough for professional opportunities. Being in Baltimore and so close to DC, you cannot lose for internships and jobs.  Good luck to all! It was a great fit for our freshly minted college grad, best wishes to those just beginning their ventures. FYI - you will get out of any college what you put into it."]

name: University of Maryland Global Campus
reviews: ['Don\'t go here. The classes are mostly fine other than professors mostly just handing out As for very little academic rigor, but it has just been one problem after another and I\'m done. One issue is that they billed me, then sent it back, then requested it from me again all in not enough time for me to actually receive it. So I had to pay twice for the same class, or they would disenroll me. They would not work with me on this at all, despite admitting that something had gone wrong. It took a month, getting a state senator and a lawyer involved, and countless phone calls to finally get my money back, and they sent it to the wrong payment method even after all of that. They had claimed they sent it a long time ago but could not provide any proof or anything, which makes me think I was penalized for some kind of computer error on their end. My "success" coach also withheld information from me that would have prevented me from taking 4 classes in a semester (full time is 2 classes) by giving the dean the wrong email from me, and she had been trying to get into contact with me for over a month. I applied for financial aid and instead of applying it to my semester\'s balance, they applied it across three semesters, two of which had a $0 balance, which generated a negative balance on those two semesters and an unpaid bill on the one I was actually enrolled in. They refused to apply the negative balances to the unpaid one, and wanted me to pay again (the second time this happened, if you\'re counting). It\'s just dumb stuff like that. The classes are out of order on the website for the bioinformatics masters, so you have to figure out prerequisites yourself under the "take the courses in the recommended sequence" section because the order is broken. They run all these ads constantly which just makes them seem like a scam and takes away from any kind of reputation this school would have. I wouldn\'t do it again, that\'s for sure.', "DO NOT ATTEND!!!! This by far has been th most stressful experience of my life. My deployment to Iraq was less stress. The financial aid department is an absolute joke. My first semester was summer 2025. VA is paying for my classes, cool. Since I didn't know how the process worked for chapter 31 I applied for a Pell grant. 3 weeks into the semester I get a check from UMGC for overpayment for the semester. That was first week of June. July comes and I have to submit  a statement of educational purposes, notarized. Done and mailed in. End of August comes and they need proof of spousal income. We are separated and not on good terms, UMGC wants a signed statement from her to include proof we are living separately. After back and forth sending copies of county property tax records, my deed, her tax records, 3 copies of income taxes as filed, and signed statements attesting to the fact that she refuses to sign anything. I am told I own the money back that UMGC sent as an overpayment and its due in 30 days. Then starts the back and forth of what changed to cause it. Only explanation I got is Pell Grant was wrong and that's it. No, this is how to fix it, let's go over it nothing!!!! This lasts til November when they say, you statement of educational purposes needs to be redone cause the West Virginia notary is not in the Maryland Notary Registry. After a heated phone call still no admission of fault she searched the WV Registry and still couldn't find the notary at the UPS store. I searched 95 pages only to find out that the name they were searching was not the correct name. For some reason McInturff looks like McIntyre when you don't care about your job. The corrected information was sent in by both phone call and online case. Was the response you're good to go? NO! UMGC response was we couldn't verify the information provided. To get the point across I submitted 20 online cases with screen shots of the WV Registry site indicating the correct name. By this time I had already registered for spring 2026 classes and had them lined up. The first week of December I call and confirm that it's settled and am told that the VA Chapter 31 voucher expired and they sent an email to the counselor on November 11th. DURING THE GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN!!!! It's now almost December 11th a month later. Not once did anyone email me and advise me of this. Not once when I called about the Statment of Educational Purposes did they say anything. I reached out the the counselor and 3 days later it was settled and resolved. Now that it's getting close to the start of the Spring semester I find out that I have been disenrolled from all my classes after the VA sent the voucher for payment. As a combat veteran with PTSD, this experience is frustrating to the point I am giving up.", 'I’m so frustrated and upset with UMGC. I changed degree paths from Phycology to Business and was not informed that I needed 6 credits to “qualify” for federal aid but was not offered to take another course, was not made aware the process as this was my first time. After completing the course, I tried to enroll my next classes when I’m then informed that I could not register for my next classes because of a balance. After getting the run arounds, Bobby Grady emails me to explain the situation about federal aid and how it was dropped because of the 3 credits but needing 6. Every email was repeated about how there is nothing they can do and it’s not their staff’s responsibility to let students know. When I ask to speak to someone else, they can’t give out that information because it isn’t part of the procedure. Im a mom with a full time job so this bill was very unexpected when federal aid was approved. I guess I’ll be doing more research on another online program.', 'I recently signed up for the Fall Semester, which my employer Amazon Web Service (who is a major partner of UMGC) sent over a 100% tuition payment upon enrollment with confirmation back in May. Roughly 2 weeks prior to start of semester, I noticed that I still had a balance of over $1800. Called and was told that I had to pay the balance. I provided confirmation that the balance was supposed to been paid, which an advisor told me that "no payment was sent". Provided the tracking information and was told that it will be applied. I looked into my employer\'s career choice portal and noticed that UMGC never applied the payment to the balance. Called again a couple days prior to semester and was told that they can\'t locate the payment. Went through the process all over again and was told that it will be applied. Day before, haven\'t been applied. Called again and was told the same thing. I withdrew from the semester at that point as I shouldn\'t be responsible to pay a balance that AWS is willingly ok with paying but UMGC doesn\'t want to accept.  Since the day that I withdrew, I\'ve received a number of calls almost daily from admission that I haven\'t answered or returned as I shouldn\'t have to go months having to explain that all UMGC needs to do was accept the tuition payment.', 'This is not my norm, However, I have just gotten off the phone with the UMGC tuition representative, (I wish I knew her name to share), who, sadly was extremely rude and dismissive as she spoke as if I can\'t quite comprehend the English language. I had a previous conversation back in September with an advisor (really great & helpful), that made me think,  feel and consider positively that going back to University of Maryland and now discovering their Global Campus on-line program would be a good fit starting in the Spring 2026 term.  I would actually give 3 stars, to balance , for the initial conversation but this last convo unfortunately has tainted even that. I attempted to explain to her that I was speaking to the advisor on the phone and  I didn\'t complete the application (which she said it was, unbeknownst to me) ...I was not aware of it since the notices I received said it was not complete. I expounded  I needed to do due diligence for the Financial aide process before continuing. I am HIGHLY DISAPPOINTED in the manner that the fast talk happens in order to Get FUNDS from you and when needing to know  why you\'re being charged for what  has not occurred you\'re handled with rudeness, that I \'Should have known\'. I was not aware that I had completed the application in order to be charged an application or "any"  fees as of yet.  Very frustrating and not helpful when the rep would rather belittle than listen. I would  Not recommend . Truly disappointing. My search for school continues.(']
