name: Maryland Institute College of Art
reviews:
['This is not a museum per se, but is an art college. The building is beautiful and is worth the trip alone. The resident art works are a collection of student creations and permanent pieces. Since this is not really a museum, don’t expect the associated infrastructure like cafes and shops.', "We are parents who emptied our retirement account to send our kid to this school under the idea that it had a great reputation and was small enough that they would get individualized attention and support in building a career network. None of this has happened. Mind you our kid is SUPER motivated, organized and bright. Their high school GPA was 3.9. They are double majoring and have a 4.0 at MICA. They have applied every summer for internships and gotten NONE. They have approached professors to ask about any work experience that would be available, even unpaid and have not been able to get anything substantial at all (a few hours here or there). They are about to graduate next year and have no inroads for any art-adjacent jobs at this point. I hate to think that we turned down an offer from SAIC to go here. I have heard that this used to be a great school but things have changed. All I know is that in the past 3 years our kid has not gotten any guidance or support that would prepare them to get a job when they graduate. This school promises a lot and does not deliver. We are INCREDIBLY unhappy about this and I can tell you if our super motivated, diligent, serious kid can't get much out of this program, no one can. I advise you to look elsewhere, even if they promise you scholarship money. The market is flooded with people with degrees these days, even from fancy schools, so your best hope of getting a job right out of college is to have had some internship experience or at least have the backing of some faculty who can help you make connections. Our kid has none of this and will just be one of 1,000 applicants for a job where the applications are being read by AI. That's a grim future.", "Very high quality smallish private art and design college. Been rockin' it for 200 years. My daughter is finishing up her freshman year, and absolutely loves the place. She's from Kansas, so the adjustment to Baltimore was a little intense, but now she's off seeing shows in DC, and enjoying all the area has to offer.
I know Baltimore sometimes gets a bad rap, but every time I'm there it's been an absolutely lovely experience.
ROCK ON MICA !!
And visit the Edgar Allan Poe museum and house while you visit. Very cool!"]

name: University of Maryland Eastern Shore
reviews: ['The University of Maryland Eastern Shore needs to be in the conversation of top HBCUs in American. The growth of the University over the years with the addition of new schools (e.g. Schools of pharmacy,  engineering & aviation, agriculture, and veterinarian) makes it an ideal institution for advanced education.', 'Even though it is a huge campus, everybody in the HR building(Bird Hall), were extremely nice.', "As both an proud alumnus and a satisfied client, I can confidently say that the University of Maryland Eastern Shore has played a pivotal role in shaping my life and career. The university’s commitment to academic excellence, innovation, and community engagement is truly inspiring. The faculty are highly dedicated, supportive, and passionate about helping students succeed—creating an environment where learning goes beyond the classroom.\n\nAs a client, I’ve experienced firsthand the university’s dedication to service and community development, which reflects their core values of integrity and excellence. The campus atmosphere is vibrant, welcoming, and enriching, fostering lifelong connections and growth. Whether you're a student aiming for success or a partner looking for a trusted institution, UMES stands out as a beacon of opportunity and positive impact. I am proud to be part of the UMES family and look forward to seeing its continued growth and success!", 'Excellent B S Construction Management Technology program. Only accredited program in the State of Maryland.', 'UMES is absolutely great. Classes are definitely competitive for those there to learn. Programs are wonderful along with the people. Food can have some improvements though but its not disappointing. My experiences were awesome, even for an introvert like me I had a blast. Piece of advice though, go there to learn so you can represent the University. If graduation rates are low is due to the fact many people are not willing to put the effort. name: Montgomery College
reviews:
['I was a photography student here and quite enjoyed my time.  Professors were generally solid and the place was overall nice.', 'I went to the Robert Parilla Performing Center. Easy check-in with QR code on my phone. Seating was comfortable. There are no bad seats. You will see the stage great from any seat', "3rd semester here. I wouldn't say it's all perfect but it's still a decent school. Cafeteria could use better food options and the prices seemed to have risen but the Classrooms are nice. I understand that their schedules of certain classes all comes down to maybe an understaffing issue but i do wish they had more available times and teachers for some of the CMSC courses here and Germantown. Rate My Professors has been my go-to for signing up for classes here and it has been extremely accurate so far. IT is actually the most useless thing here though they were helpful 1 out of the 10 times. The Parking lots are a nightmare between 9am-1pm parking garage is your best bet and just getting there early enough to walk to your class. i honestly haven't had any Big issues here though and the few advisors i have talked to other than one were actually fantastic.

Ooo side note the College Central Network. Please i beg find more Cybersecurity internships. There's 1 and it's over an hour away 🙃", 'This is yet another review about the VETERINARIAN ASSISTANT PROGRAM.

As another student has shared about the lies and apathy of the internship coordinator, I’m sharing yet another distasteful correspondence with the program manager: TRACY SINGLETON. I emailed her asking about the logistics of taking the exam. No response. I emailed the program coordinator John, who responded to me and CC’d her. I asked him 2 follow up questions. She accidentally, I believe, replied to me instead of him. As you can see from the screenshot, she was disrespectful and rude about me - someone who has been nothing but curious and polite in my emails, and is excited about the program.

She is the program manager, someone who has a “PhD” as an accolade, yet speaks like a thug with no regard or empathy for potential students‘s logistical issues.

I have a high paying corporate tech job. I want to learn skills to help animals in my free time. I’m not even desperate for a job. So I can’t even imagine how others who truly need these skills to earn a living feel when they are regarded as UNWORTHY of her time and attention - something she is PAID to do.

If anyone with authority from Montgomery College reads this, I sincerely hope you take a good hard look at all the staff under this program. They seem not to be helpful, passionate, or respectful towards those who need help. If this type of people work in education, this country is going down.', 'Bijon and Ms Camille gave me awesome service. I’m super excited to move here. The community is also awesome and clean. I’m super excited I love the Montgomery team!!!']

name: Morgan State University
reviews:
['I, Ms. Tabu Winslow Morris, MBA, was on a University tour with the Upward Bound Catonsville Scholar at the Community College of Baltimore County, all Baltimore County Public School scholars, on Monday, October 20, 2025.

The campus was well-maintained, and the tour guide and admissions officer were friendly. Our scholars gained knowledge to help them make informed decisions in the college application process.', 'Homecoming was awesome and peaceful. Congratulations Morgan State  University is a great university.', 'This has to be one of the most unprofessional universities I have ever come across...mainly due to it's operations. From admission, to financial aid, to each department.

ANY high school student or potential transfer student interested in coming here...DO NOT.

1) No one ever answers the phone. They also have representatives as the first person you reach and they "do not know" anything so everything has to get escalated which can take multiple days rather than an immediate transfer. This tells me that staff want advanced notice (3 business days) to do their job.

2) Timeliness is not a thing here so if you are a current student or have no choice but to attend, I would suggest doing everything at least a month in advance.

3) Probably the biggest thing of them all is  the Senior Comprehensive Exam. Not only do you have to spend 4 years taking classes to get your degree...you have to take a final exam based on the content from your major from freshman year to senior year...and they will not let you graduate if you fail. So you will have to constantly retake it until you pass.

4) Writing and speech proficiency exams are also required so another test you must take in order to graduate.

I seriously do not know how they keep getting all these accolades, funding, and recognition...this is a horrible school! It's a shame. You would think since it's an HBCU they would want better for their students but they don't.  They are in it for the money and press.

Again...DO NOT go here. You are better off at Towson University!', "Morgan State has the only Interior Design program in Maryland. The professors are passionate and qualified. The coursework is challenging and engaging. If you're considering pursuing a design degree and live in MD, do not hesitate to attend Morgan. The tuition is cheap and this college is very supportive of transfer and non-traditional students (I'm both). It's the best academic move I've done for my career and my future. I will forever be proud to be a Morgan Bear :)", 'Morgan State University needs serious administrative reform.

My experience there was deeply troubling. From freshman year, I was told by professors that the school “wasn’t for me” because of my neurodivergency — extremely discouraging and inappropriate, especially for an HBCU that should uplift all students. I experienced degrading treatment, including a professor throwing a paper at me for not stapling it and faculty discussing confidential information in class.

While in the architecture program, I endured ridicule, intimidation, and public embarrassment from professors. A tutor made an advance toward me that triggered past trauma, and the following semester I was physically assaulted on campus and reported it. Instead of support, I was accused of manipulation, told I was crying “crocodile tears,” singled out in class, and discussed openly among faculty and students.

I pushed for a grade appeal after a professor admitted bias in grading me but felt discouraged and intimidated out of completing it. Faculty later criticized me for not finishing while ignoring that influence.

The counseling center was also no help. The most disturbing part was the J.D. assigned to my case. When I reported the assault, she documented it as retaliation rather than what it was. That was shocking and devastating. The handling of my case was eye-opening and deeply upsetting.

I also overheard staff referring to me as “crazy,” which felt like an attempt to discredit me simply for reporting, asking questions, and advocating for myself.

I attended believing this university would nurture and protect its students. Instead, I often felt targeted and unsupported. I genuinely hope leadership and culture have improved, because no student should go through what I experienced. Morgan has the potential to be a powerful institution, but that requires accountability, professionalism, and real care for student well-being.']

name: Notre Dame of Maryland University
reviews:
["To Monisha S, the name was changed back in 2011 which is when you would have attended.  I truly don't see the purpose of your review when it's clearly outdated.  I graduated from NDMU in 2016 undergrad, and 2020 Graduate program.  You gave zero reasons why you disliked the school so I'd like to ask exactly what was your issue when you only attended for a short time.  Your review seems to be your anger speaking and your issue is from 2011.  It's time to move on Monisha S - it's 2025 and a lot can happen in 14 years, just sayin.  Your review is from two months ago, so it's actually laughable.", 'I went to this school when it was called "College of Notre Dame of Maryland," and I only stayed during my freshman year before I transferred to another school. Transferring was the best decision I ever made. The administration and staff were rude, disrespectful, unhelpful, and racist. The student body was awful as well. I was miserable the entire time I was there, and couldn't wait to leave. Worst college experience ever!', 'Completed my Masters in 2012. I had the best experience at this university, at the time I was working  mother with 2 children, and the
evening and weekend courses made it flexible with my busy schedule. Highly recommended !!', 'Attended Baltimore Chamber Orchestra event at Leclerc Halll. Pretty campus, beautiful Fall day.', 'I remember my time at Notre Dame of Maryland and it was the worst college experience I could have imagined.

When I look back on my time there, I am truly happy I transferred schools to better my education. The teachers were careless and tried their absolute best to tear down certain students.

I had a business professor publicly humiliate me in front of a classroom, because I missed an event. She didn’t talk to me privately or gather information on the reason I missed the event and she didn’t speak with other students in the classroom that missed the event as well.

Another professor had expressed, in a classroom, I should become a housewife. A math professor laugh at me when I questioned my results on an exam. The  same math professor laughed when I questioned her teaching methods earlier that year, because I learn better NOT using a calculator 90% of the classroom.

Their administration is unorganized and their teachers are too busy NOT uplifting their students.

Please do not waste the beginning of your career on a school that doesn’t care about your future.']

name: Prince George's Community College
reviews:
["PGCC offered me an opportunity I never knew I could get. I've always wanted to go back to healthcare, and was so discouraged because everyone else was asking for things I could not give (day classes when I work full-time, too many unnecessary classes and courses, very expensive tuition). PGCC became my saving grace and worked for me in the exact way I needed, and gave me everything I needed for success. Workable class schedules, low-cost tuition, and the opportunity to graduate as soon as possible. Thank you, PGCC, and you, Ms. Nicole Stubbs!", "Sent my transcripts in November and they still haven't processed them, and probably never will. I asked my professor for office hours and he just left me on read. I'm on track to fail my class despite working for hours on it every day, because there's no support. I might as well just be doing khan academy videos. Not a supportive or effective environment. I regret coming here.", 'This campus looks and feels so dead omg I’m scared to go to this school. No warmth at all. I didn’t feel like I was entering a college campus it felt more like a Medicaid social security government office. The people that work here have no knowledge of nothing at all what so ever. They aren’t able to support any of the questions you have. They rely on the internet and links to give you information. They always say you can go on the website repeatedly with no information to actually be effective in helping you not even provide information that can help you navigate where you need to go on the website. Omg. They just want to sit around and do nothing all day I could go on and on.', 'If I could rate separately, I’d give the professors a solid 5 stars — they’re great. But the 1 star is entirely for the faculty and administrative staff. They almost never answer the phone, and on the rare occasion they do (maybe 1 out of 10 times), they’re completely unhelpful.

I’ve been trying to get a refund for over two months, and all I’ve gotten is the runaround. They told me I’d have it by a specific date, but that’s come and gone. Now they keep bouncing me back and forth between the school and Nelnet — the school says to contact Nelnet, and Nelnet says to talk to the school. No one seems to take responsibility or provide a clear answer.

It’s been an incredibly frustrating experience, and it really takes away from what would otherwise be a great academic environment.', 'As a student trying to get my life back on track, I expected at least a basic level of support and transparency from this institution—but PGCC has repeatedly failed to provide that.

I’ve submitted multiple appeals regarding my financial aid and still haven’t received proper updates or resolution. What is the point of offering an appeal process if students are going to be ignored after doing everything that’s asked of them? This feels not only dismissive, but unethical.

Students shouldn’t have to chase down resources they’re entitled to—especially when they’re trying to better themselves and continue their education. PGCC needs to do better, especially for students who are genuinely trying to move forward in life.']

name: Salisbury University
reviews:
["After a few tours, my daughter chose Salisbury University and has been attending since fall of 2024. I've been pleased with her stories about the culture and classes, plus I appreciate the resources for parents to ensure she's keeping up. Though she started out wanting to pursue a pre-med track, she took a chemistry class with Dr. Heimann and found a love in science. I appreciate the mentorship that has been given to my daughter. Looking forward to her graduation and her life after college!", 'The first issue is academic advisors! How do you tell a new student that if they repeat a class it’s free from tuition to take class over? That’s a lie! An advisor is suppose give you the correct information and help guide you along the way! Second, if a student is failing why is no one of advisory status telling the student the truth. Hey, this may not be the major for you and let’s look into your other interests. Instead you encourage them to be in debt by repeating classes as if school is free. And telling them this professor is hard. What kind of advice is that? Would you like you someone to encourage your child in that way? A different kind of conversation should be had. Just to be clear it is definitely the students responsibility to uphold their academic standards.

Housing, terrible! The amount of money an out of state family pays for tuition the dorms in particularly Martins Hall should be decent and clean. The shower had hair in it and the bathroom was completely dirty. I guess students stayed over the summer in this dorm. On freshman move in day I had to file a complaint on how nasty the dorm was. Remind you this is the first impression. The whole in the bathroom door of 307 was still there from a previous video someone did of dorm room in 2019, on YouTube, SERIOUSLY! I complained about that! They basically scold you in the parent ‘s orientation about what not to complain about and that’s how you hand over a dorm! And yes it’s a choice to have your kid attend the school! Please do better! I guess now Martin Hall is receiving a long overdue makeover.

I know no college, university or whatever you chose to call it isn’t perfect but effort for change is way more feasible and understanding. And please listen to your students comments negative or positive. It’s no way different students who attend different years  at the college complain about the same professor and no adjustments are made. Just because you have a PHD In biology should not give you the right to teach first time students as if they are in med-school. Its setting them up to fail. Be all means I’m not saying make it easy. Make it understandable and relatable to at least give them a shot. If a whole class fail a test, it’s it the students or the professor? I’ll wait!', 'I love the small campus life, because everywhere is like a walking distance, when you live on campus their is stores nearby like CVS and Dollar General to by needs and you get to walk their, no need to get behind the wheel, and also I was glad their is a church nearby to I get go on Sundays.', 'I am deeply saddened by the experience I had with this institution. As I was excited to actively pursue my degree at Salisbury, I was not encouraged nor guided enough to make it to the start of classes. I believe this had to do with discrimination of neurodivergence and race, as well as ageism. I unfortunately had to withdrawal due to lack of support and feeling devalued as a student.', "We toured Salisbury University with our daughter. Our tour guides were lively and energetic and were sincere in their appraisal of the university. The library is gorgeous and a testament to the school's small, but well though-out, campus. Between the Purdue and the Guerrieri families, this is the university that chicken built. Don't understand the reference, look it up! My daughter is looking at business and economics, so we were happy we got to see the Business building, which was quite impressive. Salisbury is part of the University of Maryland System, but is a Division III school, so unfortunately, there's not a lot of energy around their sports programs the way you would find at a larger school. I did watch their football team practice a little, and they looked decent. Housing looks like it may be at a minimum on campus, though I believe they are building more student dwellings. The biggest negative was South Salisbury Avenue. With its nail salons, vape and cannabis shops, food shops, etc., it looked like suburb that was being run-down by cheap businesses - similar to Baltimore Avenue at UMCP. Salisbury itself is also a bit of a dodgy town, but a lot of campuses are in similar situations. Always best to stay with a group of people when galivanting about!"]

name: St. Mary's College of Maryland
reviews:
['Specifically reviewing the Commemorative to the Enslaved Peoples of Southern Maryland, which was created by the college on its campus. The commemorative does not appear on Google Maps but it is located near the athletic fields next to the stadium.

Sitting prominently where cabins for the enslaved once stood, the Commermorative is a multilayered  beacon that calls the visitor to literally reflect on the lives of the enslaved and the legacy of chattel slavery in our own lives. Its structure is inspired by the “ghost cabins” in nearby St. Mary’s City.

The mirrors contain the text of erasure poems by poet Quenton Baker. “The erasure poetry that covers the structure is adapted from historical documents related to the Mackall-Brome plantation — one of three known plantations located on the land around St. Mary’s City. These documents include slave property and runaway slave advertisements, newspaper articles, and slave depositions of the Mackall-Brome family.”

Recordings of Baker reading the poems are available on the website for the memorial. I recommend listening as you visit; his words bring the Commemorative to life in a profound way.', 'Situated adjacent to Maryland’s first capital, St. Mary’s College of Maryland is in a location steeped in history. I could write about the small class sizes and the quality liberal arts education, but you can read all about that on the SMCM website. You’re here on Google maps, so you probably want to know what you’ll see when you arrive.

The campus is beautiful and facilities such as the Performing Arts Center offer a variety of programming that is open to the public. You can also spectate at athletics events at the stadium and at the gymnasium. They host quite a few swimming events also. In the summer, the River Concert Series is a significant attraction (especially for the 4th of July performance).

St. Mary’s College of Maryland is definitely worth a visit. There is a reason so many alumni make it a point to come back every year at Alumni Weekend. Make sure you stay long enough to catch a sunset over the St. Mary’s River!', 'Beautiful campus, plenty of parking..come down here few times a year for swim tournaments. Clean athletic facilities.', 'Great liberal arts school with strong programs in computer science, math, and physics. Outstanding performances at Didge Center. Attended free River Concert Series performance at their outside amphitheatre this evening. Great fun!', 'One morning just sitting in my car,I noticed how beautiful was the morning sky.
Just caught my eye 👁️it was breathtaking ❤️']

name: St. John's College
reviews:
["St. John's University’s Manhattan Campus at 101 Astor Place is frequently lauded in my professional circles as a masterfully positioned academic hub where Vincentian values of service meet the sophisticated demands of the global insurance and risk management sectors. Based on countless conversations with alumni and local industry leaders, it is clear that the campus offers a substantive, high-caliber environment where the intimate class sizes and direct access to Manhattan’s corporate heart are cited as transformative for career trajectory. It is genuinely impressive to see how the institution maintains such a transparent commitment to ethical leadership and social mobility, qualities that my acquaintances often praise for creating a community that is as compassionate as it is competitive. In the broader public consensus, the Astor Place campus is held in high regard as a distinguished boutique-style university experience, proving that a mission-driven education can thrive with elegance and academic rigor in the center of New York’s most dynamic district.", 'Nice modern building of St. John University. Nice area to sit and people watch.', "St. John's Manhattan Campus located on East 8th Street and 3rd Avenue.

The campus is in a relatively new building.  The building was probably finished and ready for occupation a few years back.

The building is a commercial property with lots of office spaces.  The ground fflooe have a CVS Pharmacy.

All around the campus is your historical neighborhood of East Village.", "New York is beautiful, there are a lot interesting places to visit, with wonderful people to know. I loved to study at St Johns university. There you study and practice hard. The classes are fantastic, with dynamic professors. St. Jonh's, I'll miss it a lot!", "The St. John's Manhattan campus is home to the school of Risk Management, Insurance, and Actuarial Science. It is also home to the Davis Library. A very nice building and staff overall."]

name: Towson University
reviews:
['Clean campus, modern buildings, no issues in my 3 years there. Professors were very easy going and understanding while being knowledgeable in their fields. SECU arena is crazy nice for a small school venue.', 'After spending $70,000 in tuition, at my daughter’s graduation, the security guard made my 70 year-old mother throw her water away at the door so they could sell her one on the inside. Absolutely disgustingly greedy behavior. The employees of the college should tell whatever administrator ordered the action that they are not going to harm other humans with greed.  FIRE THE JERK THST MADE THIS DECISION', "Towson University is a public university located in Towson, Maryland, United States. It is one of the 12 member institutions of the University System of Maryland. Established in 1866, Towson University has grown into one of the largest universities in Maryland and is known for its comprehensive academic programs, research, and community engagement.

Here are some key points about Towson University:

Academic Programs: Towson University offers a wide range of undergraduate and graduate programs across various disciplines, including arts and sciences, business, education, health professions, fine arts, and more.

Campus: The main campus of Towson University is situated on a suburban campus in Towson, Maryland, just north of Baltimore. The campus features a mix of modern facilities, historic buildings, and green spaces.

Student Life: The university provides a vibrant student life with numerous student organizations, clubs, and activities. There are opportunities for sports, arts, community service, and leadership development.

Athletics: The university's athletic teams are known as the Towson Tigers. They compete in NCAA Division I sports, primarily as members of the Colonial Athletic Association (CAA).

Research: Towson University is involved in various research initiatives and projects across different disciplines. Students and faculty collaborate on research activities that contribute to academic advancement and real-world problem-solving.

Community Engagement: Towson University is committed to community engagement and service. It often partners with local organizations and businesses to provide students with real-world experiences and contribute positively to the surrounding community.

Accreditation: The university is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE), which ensures the quality and standards of its academic programs.

Rankings: Towson University has received recognition in various national and regional rankings for its academic programs, campus facilities, and student engagement efforts.", 'If you're an in state student that doesn't have benefits, hard pass. They look for reasons to "academically remove" local students just for the money. I had a gut this was a bad choice and, was correct. Coming from an engineering/physics major parent.', 'Terrible experience overall got screwed over by the initial academic advisor and by the billing office. Professors were good but all around experience was very poor. Kind of wraps up my whole experience at the school.']

name: Stevenson University
reviews:
["We have taken several college tours lately, Stevenson University's tour was by far the most informative, relaxed and inviting. Our guide, Mary-Kimberly, was OUTSTANDING!!! She tailored our tour to meet the needs of my son field of study. Of all the schools Stevenson University was the first school to talk to us about finances, would our son qualify for any scholarships, how much is the meal plan, and the cost of the dorm. A few of the colleges just said that they talk finances once you are accepted. I did that exact thing, got accepted and then talked about finances. I was heartbroken when I got into my 1st choice school only to find out I could not afford it. I do not want that for my son.
It was very exciting to see all the new facilities and equipment. The technology is what you would want in the field that you are going into. The studios blew us away.", 'I just moved my baby girl in for her freshmen year and I love the spacious clean, and modern looking dorms. The school is very quiet.

Update 10/5/25: Well, its been almost 2mos since move in and my daughter is loving her time in school. She has quickly made friends but some of that is due to her being on the danceline of the marching band and meeting her roommate and one of her suitemates before school started. Attending the "welcome accepted students" events and orientation is a great way to make friends before starting school. And getting engaged in the different activities helps a lot too. My daughter had a great group of friends before band camp was over.

Because Stevenson is not a party school, they do a great job of bringing the fun to the students. They even offer bus trips like Field of Screams in PA. Day trips to places like NYC, and Bush Gardens.

The kids seem very comfortable in their dorms, they also seem to enjoy the north campus dining halls more than the main one in Rockland Center, and my daughter is enjoying her classes so far. I particularly enjoy the small classroom sizes. I definitely feel we found the right fit for my my daughter!', 'My son decided that this was the place he wanted to soar in & I decided to support his journey!
He’s a junior now and the happiness I’ve ever seen him.
Honor student in 3 different clubs and really working hard on building the kind of life that he deserves!', 'We had the pleasure of touring the campus.  The facilities are modern and the classes appeared to be well suited to learning in the 21st century.  We could not go inside the dorms but the buildings looked new.  Three dining halls along with a few coffee shops cover a campus that is larger than it seems from the main entrance.  Athletic facilities were nice as well.', 'I have been a student at Stevenson for the past two years and will be a student for the next two years to come! Before being enrolled at Stevenson, all of my experiences had been positive. When it came to applying, the turnaround time for the application was faster than any other school I had applied to, and my admission counselor was extremely helpful in answering all of my questions concerning transfer credits and scholarships. I am currently in the nursing program, and it has been a wonderful experience! They do a great job preparing you for going into clinicals and knowing what to expect with the workload/time commitment. Academics aside, I love the campus. I feel like there are so many great study spots on campus and many food options, so I rarely find myself getting bored with the food on campus. If I did have to give a complaint, it would be that I wish some of the study spots were open longer and did not close so early as it can make it so the late-night study spots can become more full, especially during midterms and finals.']

name: Washington College
reviews:
['What a pretty campus and stadium. We were there for a field hockey game. There is a lot of staff and facility parking in front of the stadium. These are open on the weekends. The bleachers were nice and clean. The turf is new and according to a few players plays very slow.', 'This is a college with about 900 students. Small enough to find your fit and large enough to have access to anything you could envision for your education.

We often visit the dining hall for dinner and we very much enjoy the food and fellowship.  The place is happy.  It’s Chestertown- what’s not to like?

Don’t park any old place - it will cost you. Safety is a serious matter here and the campus provides plenty of safety features throughout the buildings and facilities.', 'Really enjoyed this journey with my daughter.  The school is definately top notch.  Very safe and spirited atmosphere with excellent teaching and leadership.  These are photos of a dorm with 4 b.r. and 2 bath.  With a common area.', "Maryland is full of tiny ancient small-town colleges that are an integral part of their surrounding communities.  There are McDaniel College (Westminster), Hood College (Frederick), St. John's College (Annapolis), Mount St. Mary's College (Emmitsburg) and, of course, Washington College.  Washington College is a real liberal arts college, meaning that there is genuine interest in liberal arts and pursuit of truth and critical thinking.  It's not so much about pre-professional training.  Chestertown is a real feature of studying here.  It's a beautiful town and Washington has a beautiful historic campus.  Think of Chestertown as a miniature version of Annapolis and you'll get the idea.  The town has gentrified in recent years and that helps to contribute to its vibe of a nice college town.  The college itself is also gaining popularity and becoming more selective.", 'The college is wonderful for hosting events. I have been to conventions on campus several years. The food and event facilities are top notch. The staff always work to make guests comfortable, and everyone is friendly. Thank you all!']

name: McDaniel College
reviews: ["Went here for my B.A in Biology (class of 2024). Overall I'd say if you like small campuses with good student to staff ratio and small classroom sizes this is the way to go. Has a good honors program with research opportunities if in the honors program. Only critique would be student life programs. On weekends the campus is pretty much a ghost town with most students going home for the weekend. If you like fraternities or sororities it does have a lot of good chapters at the hill. I would say I feel the campus would benefit with a esports program or even a gaming club. Am sort of shocked there is no said program or club at the Hill already.", 'Just started my journey at McDaniel! Kinda nervous but mostly hyped 🟢⚫ Campus has good vibes so far. Let’s see where these 4 years take me', "Love, love, love this place, but it's certainly not for everyone.  This is a beautiful small college in a small, historic Maryland town about 40 miles west of Baltimore.  This college is a private liberal arts college, so you can expect intentional focus on liberal arts over pre-professional training.  The idea is to graduate with critical thinking and advanced communication skills, not just the vocational skills necessary to get a job.  Tuition is expensive, which is typical of a small, private liberal arts college.  There's plenty of housing for students who want to live on campus, but dorms are only practical.  There's no attempt at luxury.\n\nThe campus is idyllic.  The emphasis here is on quaint and peaceful, not diverse and bustling.  And while the campus is really beautiful, it's also small and somewhat isolated.  Westminster is a lovely historic town, but it's not a party town by any stretch.  For any kind of real cultural activity, you'll need to drive to Frederick or, even better, Baltimore.  As is the case with Frederick, Westminster is becoming more and more suburban as the Washington/Baltimore metro creeps in.", 'Excellent school and beautiful campus. Faculty is also top notch!!', "I like this place, but the souvenirs are expensive and the dorms don't look to good."]

name: Hult International Business School
reviews:
["I graduated from the part-time, Global Online MBA program with Hult (Boston timezone) in 2024.  I was very hesitant at first about enrolling in an MBA. With a busy job, two young kids, and lots of personal & professional travel, I wasn't sure how I would carve out the time for school. I was also nervous to go back to the academic environment since it had been many years since my time in undergrad. However - I couldn't be happier that I did it. The structure & flexibility of Hult's part-time program allowed me to balance school, work & family (for the most part!), and it was reassuring to be part of a cohort of other working professionals who were also juggling the same. It's amazing how well you get to know your peers.  The program may be online, but I formed strong connections with my classmates both in & outside of the classroom, as we cheered each other on through the tough times & celebrated successes along the way.

I gained many skills and experiences throughout the program that have already helped me in my career. Perhaps the most important has been the ability to take on new professional challenges that otherwise might have seemed too daunting. I needed to push outside of my comfort zone more frequently, and in doing that, Iearned I am capable of more than I realized. I credit my professors and my classmates at Hult for inspiring me and pushing me to be my best.

Looking forward to meeting up with former classmates one day at one of the global alum summits!", "I did my Undergraduate program at Hult in London and just started the Postgraduate Business Analytics program in Boston.
Hult has some great professors who really know their stuff and come from industry. Sometimes we have classes led by instructors who aren't traditional professors, but these people come with such strong backgrounds and experience and deliver amazing classes and best thing is that you can connect with this people and that opens doors to opportunities. You learn a lot, discuss real cases, it's just amazing.
The teamwork aspect is great thing that you might not like because you end up in uncomfortable situations when your team isn't doing their best, expectations and goals don't align, and you're honestly pissed about it. You have to figure out how to give feedback, whether to leave the team, or report people who aren't pulling their weight. It puts you in real-world situations while you're still in a safe environment to experiment, because at work there's way less room to mess around and try things. At Hult you can actually try and experiment.
My only issue with Hult is that some people who get in really shouldn't get in. This is mainly for undergraduate, the master's is a bit better.
So I'd say Hult undergrad is great and really preps you, and postgrad is great for me as well as it's completely new things that we go over and profs are just great.
Hult has students that are very spread out in terms of their abilities, there are some amazing people and some people that simply just shouldn't get in.
But it's totally understandable from a business perspective. It's a business that needs to earn money, and now with declining birth rates and deglobalization, universities are in tough spots.", "My experience at Hult has been nothing short of transformative! Studying here has been an incredible journey of growth, both academically and personally. The dynamic curriculum perfectly blends theory with real-world application, and the global perspective embedded in every course has expanded my understanding of business in ways I never imagined.

What truly sets Hult apart is its vibrant, diverse community. Collaborating with classmates from over 150 nationalities has enriched my learning and broadened my cultural awareness. The professors are not only experts in their fields but also passionate mentors who genuinely invest in students' success.

From the cutting-edge campus facilities to opportunities like the Hult Prize and Global Campus Rotation, every day feels like a step toward a brighter future. If you're seeking a business education that challenges, inspires, and connects you to the world—Hult is the place to be!", 'It’s a school with different people coming al over the world. And it’s not just about studying, you will always get chance to connect with new people and their culture in a more friendly ways. Quite a good choice to go and learn things Internationally.', "As a former student, I don't recommend it at all.
Choosing Hult is one of my biggest regrets in life.
It hasn't added anything to my life or my career.
It's a university that has no pedagogical project.
The professors are unprepared, with very few exceptions.
It's a university that has no physical laboratories.
The study rooms are insufficient for the amount of work they have to do. In other words, there are no rooms for everyone.
There is no physical library.
The career area is a fake. They don't have any projects to help, especially international students, find a job.
When I had a health problem, not only did they not support me, they made it even more complicated.
The academic leaders are always ready to give you any excuse.
In other words, they are very good at marketing strategies, sales, and creating reports for the rankings.
They pretend to be Non-Profit, but at the end of the day, they are 100% For-Profit.
If you still have time, look for one with a better reputation. Don't be fooled by false promises."]

We found the vibe to be rather low key, as opposed to some of the Ivy's we spent time at. The amount of money in endowment at this school (and some competing schools) also tends to indicate a lot of graduate loyalty.", 'good college but why are we honoring the inventor of american biological warfare who suggested giving smallpox infected blankets to native people? look it up', 'Amherst College was once a number one Liberal Arts institution in the US before Williams College']

name: Babson College
reviews:

Its reputation as the world’s leading institution for entrepreneurship is well earned, and the programs consistently deliver both academic rigor and practical application.

The executive education offerings are tailored to the needs of leaders. Courses are designed to provide actionable insights into managing complex organizations, driving profitability, and navigating global markets. Every program emphasizes strategic thinking and innovation, ensuring participants leave with skills they can apply immediately.

Babson’s focus on financial leadership and P&L mastery is unmatched. Executives gain hands‑on experience analyzing financial statements, optimizing profitability, and making data‑driven decisions. This practical approach ensures graduates are not only knowledgeable but also confident in leading their organizations through financial challenges.

Beyond the classroom, Babson fosters an entrepreneurial mindset that encourages creativity, resilience, and adaptability. The college’s global network and diverse community provide executives with invaluable perspectives, helping them think beyond traditional boundaries and prepare for the future of business.

The food at Babson was truly beyond five‑star, with every meal feeling like a gourmet experience, and the endless ice cream fridges scattered across campus made it feel like a dream come true always stocked, always available, and the perfect treat while working around the clock; combining that with the vibrant atmosphere for studying made the entire experience nothing short of amazing.', 'Babson College is an outstanding institution, particularly for those interested in entrepreneurship and business. name: Boston College
reviews:
['Boston College tends to run on a clear sense of structure and expectation. The academic environment is deliberately shaped, with an emphasis on mentorship, writing, discussion, and accountability that keeps students visibly engaged. Faculty interaction is not abstract; it is built into the experience, and students are expected to articulate ideas, defend their reasoning, and show steady intellectual growth. The culture signals that education is something you actively participate in, not something that simply happens around you.

UC Davis, by contrast, can feel like an institution whose size and reputation do much of the talking. The campus is vast, the systems are complex, and undergraduates can find themselves navigating bureaucracy and scale rather than being consistently challenged by it. Instead of a tightly guided academic push, students often have to create their own direction in an environment that can feel diffuse. Critics describe a disconnect between the confident image the university projects and the uneven intensity students may actually encounter, arguing that prestige and presentation sometimes overshadow day-to-day rigor.

At Boston College, the framework is designed to keep students on edge academically.
At UC Davis, it can be easier to disappear into the machinery and mistake motion for momentum.

The difference is between a university that actively shapes the student experience and one where students may have to fight the scale of the place to shape it themselves.', "It's certainly one of the premium college of this region run by Catholic church. It's very beautiful and lovable place. The library is a lovely place and one of the best in the country. Most of the students are aspiring achievers, get influenced to become one.

Limited number of parking. So plan to go using other mode of travel or check before leaving.", "This review is just the physical campus and has nothing to do with the school's curriculum or getting accepted into the University.  That said, this is the most beautiful campus I have ever seen in my life.  It was a complete surprise and got me completely off guard.  All of the buildings have the same gothic, sandstone color vibe.  The campus was spectacularly clean and pristine.", 'Boston College’s financial department came across as extremely aggressive in their collection tactics. I was contacted in ways that felt intimidating and impersonal, despite the school’s public claims about helping students through the payment process.

The clearest example of this was when Mr. Theodore Hilli told me, “You’re not getting out of this one, Kyle,” and, “You may have a debt collector come to your house,” as I was trying to explain why it felt unreasonable to charge me for a class I attended once and couldn’t continue due to personal circumstances. He even mentioned that the call transcript would be sent to a collections agency.

I had just lost my closest friend in a boating accident, and I tried to explain that I wasn’t asking for special treatment—just basic understanding. This school makes millions, yet their representative suggested sending debt collectors to my home over $1,500. Does that really seem reasonable? I didn’t even receive the product I paid for, so it’s not as though I cost the school any money. It felt like pure greed from a supposedly “holy” institution.

Isn’t that a little much? His LinkedIn profile states that he “works with students to help them through the process of paying their college costs,” yet most of his prior positions appear to have been in debt collection. It’s hard to imagine how such an approach aligns with genuinely supporting students who are barely of age and sense during an already stressful process...', "It is one of the most beautiful places in the area. If you're visiting Boston, you should definitely take the green line or a car to Chestnut Hill to see Boston College and the area. The pictures speak for themselves. Note that there are not many places to eat around just by walk, but a few min of driving or bus and you can find many places. There's also Playa bowls, just near the T station with great bowls and smoothies."]

name: Boston University
reviews:
['Boston University, stretching gracefully along Commonwealth Avenue, stands as a masterclass in urban higher education, seamlessly weaving a global research powerhouse into the very fabric of one of the world’s most intellectual cities. From several high-level discussions with alumni and local professionals, it is clear that BU operates with a merytorical intensity that challenges its students to think far beyond the limits of traditional textbooks. My peers frequently highlight the university’s unique talent for blending a sophisticated, cosmopolitan atmosphere with a genuine sense of intellectual grit, noting that its graduates are exceptionally prepared for the high-stakes demands of the modern economy. In frequent conversations about the Boston academic landscape, the public consensus consistently praises the institution's Questrom School of Business and the College of Communication as world-class benchmarks of professional readiness. I am particularly struck by the faculty's impressive ability to act as mentors and industry gatekeepers, a sentiment echoed by many families I know whose children have moved into prestigious careers immediately after graduation. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages this sprawling campus with a transparent and visionary hand, ensuring that "Terrier" pride is backed by serious academic substance. Friends who have engaged with the university’s research centers often describe a high-performance environment characterized by intellectual moxie and a deep-seated respect for interdisciplinary collaboration. The general sentiment among the community is that BU represents a prestigious and dependable pillar of progress that continues to elevate Boston’s status as a global hub of learning. Reflecting on these consistently positive and well-grounded testimonials, I view Boston University as a distinguished institution that executes its complex educational mission with undeniable class and an inspiring dedication to excellence.', 'Boston University is an incredible place to visit! The campus is full of energy, diversity, and inspiring architecture right along the Charles River. The atmosphere feels vibrant and intellectual, with friendly students and passionate professors everywhere. I loved exploring the mix of modern buildings and history — truly one of the best universities in the U.S.!', 'Boston University doesn’t wait for the world — it helps define it.
In the heart of a city built on innovation and intellect, BU turns ambition into action. From global business and biomedical engineering to law, journalism, and the arts, Boston University thrives on motion — academic, cultural, and professional. Here, you don’t just learn about the world; you live in its center.

At BU, excellence isn’t theoretical — it’s practiced. Classes demand critical thinking, professors expect originality, and the city itself tests your adaptability. The competition is constant, but it’s constructive — a challenge that sharpens instead of discouraging. Every lecture, every lab, every late night adds up to one thing: capability that counts.

The Boston University network is as global as its mindset. Alumni dominate fields from medicine to media, tech to diplomacy. A BU degree isn’t a paper credential — it’s proof you’ve thrived in one of the world’s most rigorous academic ecosystems. When you leave, you carry not just credentials, but credibility.

And then there’s UC Davis.

UC Davis markets the dream of innovation — but delivers the reality of inertia. Bureaucracy replaces agility, and students often wrestle with systems instead of ideas. Speak out, and you risk standing alone; stand out, and you’re told to blend in. The culture prizes compliance over creativity — a quiet campus that rarely makes noise in the arenas that matter.

Even the outcomes tell the truth. UC Davis’s 10-year ROI struggles to justify the tuition, offering returns that barely keep pace with the cost of living in California. The brand says “prestige,” but the experience often says “plateau.”

At Boston University, you evolve — intellectually, professionally, globally.
At UC Davis, you endure — bureaucratically, academically, slowly.

If you’re choosing between the two:
Go where excellence is earned, not advertised.
Go where the city fuels your growth, not the system stalls it.

Go Boston University. UC Davis just drifts.', 'Fantastic educational institution with dedicated, caring faculty and staff.', 'I’ve studied at many universities in the past and I have to say this was the worst one. Their dorm staff/supervisor and management are deplorable. They have racist and discriminatory attitudes. Beware of your privacy if you go there. They’re allowed to come into your dorm room whenever they want and search it.']

In frequent discussions about the regional academic landscape, those I trust repeatedly emphasize the faculty\'s genuine dedication to student mentorship, which many families I know describe as the decisive factor in their children’s professional confidence. I am particularly struck by how the university has transformed its campus with state-of-the-art facilities like the Dana Mohler-Faria Science and Mathematics Center, reflecting a visionary strategy that is highly respected by the community. It is evident from the collective feedback of my network that the administration operates with a transparent, student-first philosophy, ensuring that social mobility and academic excellence go hand in hand. Many of my friends who have collaborated with BSU graduates point to their impressive work ethic and sophisticated problem-solving skills as a direct testament to the university\'s rigorous "active learning" culture. The general sentiment among those familiar with the institution is that it remains a prestigious and dependable pillar of Southeastern Massachusetts, skillfully preparing the next generation of leaders with integrity and class. Reflecting on these consistently positive testimonials, I view Bridgewater State University as a distinguished institution that executes its complex mission with undeniable academic moxie and a profound respect for the individual journey of every student.', 'I have very little good things to say about BSU. name: Clark University
reviews:
["Why You Should Reconsider Clark University: Must Read

I graduated from Clark University in December 2023. This is my second time posting a review; the first one was removed (when I posted my review on USNEWS.

Here’s why I believe students, especially international ones,
should think twice before choosing Clark:

No Career Support or Campus Placements: Clark does not offer any structured placement support. No major companies come to campus to hire students, and the university makes no effort to follow up with graduates on their employment outcomes. The few companies that do visit are often local insurance firms hiring for commission-based sales roles—far from what international students expect when making a significant financial and personal investment to study in the U.S.

Overcrowded Classes: Some MS-STEM classes have over 60 students, with more than 90% from India, limiting diversity and cross-cultural learning. Imagine the kind of international school environment you can expect from a business university with such limited representation.

Inexperienced Faculty: Many instructors are recent MS graduates themselves, with little to no teaching experience.

Biased Grading: I gave honest feedback in a course evaluation and received a noticeably lower grade, which felt retaliatory.

Pre-Recorded Lectures: Several courses are offered as pre-recorded videos rather than live sessions. Many students come to the U.S. expecting in-person academic engagement, not simply to watch recordings. I was even required to take one such pre-recorded course. Despite raising my concerns with multiple people, including the dean at that time, I was still compelled to attend the class in this format.

Safety Concerns: The surrounding neighborhood regularly sees incidents of gunfire, robbery, and other safety issues. It does not feel like a secure environment to live or study in.

High Cost: Even with a scholarship, tuition is still significantly higher than that of better-ranked public universities like Texas Tech.

Poor Classroom Environment: Facilities are basic. The furniture and classroom setup feel more like a budget training center than a graduate-level university.

Alumni Outcomes Speak Volumes: If you're considering Clark, check the LinkedIn profiles of recent international graduates. Many are either unemployed or working in fields unrelated to their studies, clear evidence of weak career support and outcomes.

This is my honest experience, and I’m sharing it so future students can make an informed decision. If this review is removed again, I will continue to repost it. No student should come to the U.S. full of dreams, only to be let down by a university that overpromises and underdelivers.

09/23/2025: Update – My USNEWA review has been removed again.", 'Campus is lovely. Students committed to improving the city and the world around them. A curriculum that moves across disciplines allowing students to engage with academics more personally. Write. Write. Write. We just want more of it here within the undergraduate and graduate curriculum. This cannot be overstated.', 'I had some very abusive professors. People outright didn't believe I'm an immigrant because of my excellent English, what irony. They didn't even get my name right during graduation (called me by a woman's name). Imagine being laughed at, at your own graduation by these woke hypocrites. Despite being born in a foreign country and growing up bilingual, one of the deans told me, literally, "X [my ethnic background] or whatever is not a real country" and I was forced to take a foreign language. I couldn't believe it, and this was back in the mid 2010's. I was discriminated against, judged, and treated as subhuman because of my gender and background.

A handful of good professors, but they all left.', "To be fair, this is the best school I've ever got to know well, and I've known quite a few schools, including some highly regarded ones that get their stellar ranking by focusing on growing endowments and grabbing the hottest research fellows whilst ignoring students' needs. Clark is the opposite of that; most professors are focused on providing the best education experience as well as providing undergrads with opportunities to engage in research. This is the school that has absolutely exceeded all my expectations.", 'I vibed well with Clark. I visited the campus a few times, hung out with "Clarkies" and applied (& got in), BUT, I was VERY "small LAC" focused in my college endeavors. Therefore, I was gravitating less towards universities at the time I was applying to schools as an undergraduate.

I did like Clark though, but in the end, Hampshire College in Amherst won out. It was more: "academically flexible" then a LOT of the other places I'd looked at and applied to, and Clark fell into that more: "academically traditional" category. Clark has a VERY NICE campus though. Worcester isn't my favorite place in MA overall; and I felt the Amherst/Northampton area was a nicer placer to go to college (and to potentially live in after graduation); so it won me over.']

reviews: ['Beautiful campus- clean and well kept lawns', 'Beautiful safe secure campus.', "I graduated from Emmanuel College in 1982, so it has been some years. However, I recently visited the campus with a niece who is exploring Boston-area schools, and my impressions were the very same as when I first explored Emmanuel in 1978. The college is exceptional.  I can think of no other that offers so much for such an economical investment. Geographically, you are immersed in America's favorite college town -- Boston. And by immersed, I mean you can hear the Fenway Park crowd, walk mere blocks to Kenmore Square, and take up an internship at a Harvard-associated institution just next door (I did!). You have that gorgeous gothic architecture with ivy clinging to brick, which captures the ideal image many have of a college, but at the same time, students are welcoming, authentic, and as interested in your achievement as you are. What has changed about Emmanuel, besides enrolling men (a wise step forward), is that, due to smart business decisions made by its president, Janet Eisner, S.N.D., the school is now an impressive state-of-the-art academic facility. But even as I marveled at the beautiful learning environments, I felt the same pang of belonging I felt decades ago... this is a school that cares about its students and encourages them to grow and move among areas of study until they've found the one that's just right. And it's a fun place to be for four years. If I could only go back for another round, I would.", 'I applied to this school over a decade ago. name: Hampshire College
reviews:
["I wouldn't trade my time at Hampshire for the world. Rating or highly because if it's the right fit, it will change your life. (Also to offset some of the right-wing review bombings of people who've never even gone here) If you want to go to Hampshire though, you really need to ask yourself: Do you have what it takes to motivate yourself when you have no restrictions?

This college is EXPENSIVE. EX. PEN. SIVE. Seeing the current government situation, I don't see that changing, either. During my four years, I'd often look at my classmates and realize that there were 2 kinds of students who go here: Intelligent, hard working individuals making real changes getting the best educational experience for experimental minds that they could hope to get, OR spoiled rich kids and people so depressed and miserable that they could not bring themselves to do any work whatsoever, burning 70k+ every year just to fail classes because they liked the sound of a no testing school on paper. If it's the depression, I'd recommend taking time away, 70k is WAY too much to pay for an experience you're not enjoying. But there will always be people here who have never felt the fear of the real world and grift it in the most expensive college in the area because it's marginally easier, and that's a bit demoralizing for those of us who do have to work. Still, if you are a passionate person, if you want school to work with you on projects instead of against you, if you hate school because there's something you'd RATHER be working towards, not because you think effort is too hard to sum up ever, this is time and money well spent. (Also, they have some great scholarships that really helped me!)

Hampshire has a unique set of challenges, but no more or less than other colleges. You trade fraternities and high assault rates for disorganized management and an occasionally volatile set of peers (always bound to happen on small campuses that collect people with strong morals.) Its structure asks you to apply yourself. If you don't apply yourself to your studies, your community, your values, you are simply wasting your time and money. If you *do* apply yourself, getting involved in advocacy, independent studies, clubs, learning collectives, you will be getting the chance to learn life skills by doing in an environment which is still safe to fail in. I consider that infinitely more valuable than studying for tests.

If you feel like you belong at Hampshire, here's advice from a very proud alum and former RA: if you need help? Don't stop asking people until you GET IT. Staff on this campus want to help you, ALWAYS, but they're such a mess and so overworked it might take some effort to find the right people to help you in the way you need. You're paying them to be there. You are OWED that support, and then you can direct other people to it later.

Also, if you read this far, check out my Div III project online! It's a comic/prose hybrid novel about the AIDS crisis in Last Vegas, called Dirty Vegas Dogs!", 'The key to understanding Hampshire is that, above ALL else; the college expects the student WILL step up and take charge of their education and chart their own individual academic course and direction. I watched peers flunk out of/withdraw/transfer out of Hampshire left and right over my four years there because they had the notion that Hampshire was somehow going to be "easy" because the Divisional system isn't traditionally "exam and grades-oriented" and that is a COMPLETE & UTTER FALLACY!

IF you intend to graduate from Hampshire, you'd better have a VERY clear idea of what you want to study and concentrate in, and how you're going to do it. Hampshire REQUIRES you have an academic plan, and a vision. You will HAVE to fulfill concentration requirements. AND, you will also HAVE to push yourself to study extensively on the other four campuses, otherwise an Ivy League (or any) grad school program isn't going to happen unless you have a well-maintained EXCELLENT weighted GPA from Amherst, Smith, Mt. Holyoke & UMass/Amherst. Hampshire evaluations alone will NOT get you into grad school.

I was REALLY happy that I figured out that academic caveat BEFORE I even got to Hampshire. I was ready to take Five-College courses from the get-go, & CASA (Hampshire's Center for Academic Support & Advising) will advise first-years not to take courses off campus (which I found EXTREMELY academically limiting) until their second semester. Therefore, I took my first Five College course at UMass/Amherst during the Fall semester of my first year.

Hampshire IS therefore VERY difficult and challenging for students who enter college not knowing what they want to do, BUT, if you do choose Hampshire (for me it was my #1 college choice) then it means you feel you are ready for the challenges and the experiences of being a Hampster.

I chose Hampshire over a number of other colleges/universities that I'd applied to, (including some that surprised even me like Emerson College in Boston & NYU/Tisch as a Theater/Film student) but that was just one of the (MANY) things that further convinced me I was DEFINITELY "ready" for the Hampshire experience. IF I was turning down Emerson College & NYU/Tisch in favor of Hampshire's Theater/Film Programs, I REALLY wanted that "specific" experience that I KNEW Hampshire would offer me.

You just have to KNOW that Hampshire is for you or not. After a semester or a year, you'll just KNOW. Once you complete Division I, and file your Division II that's usually a pretty good indicator you'll keep on attending. Your residential life experience at Hampshire is also CENTRAL to your academic one, so choose VERY carefully with whom (& where) you'll live with on campus. I lived in two different Mods once I left the Dorms. #65 in Enfield (pretty good) & #81 in Prescott (EXCELLENT!) SO, sorting that out is also key to having a good overall experience at Hampshire. 👍

Luckily, in my case I was from an academic family: my parents were both accomplished English Professors and Writers in the NYC Academia/Literary world. Therefore, I had researched colleges EXTENSIVELY and even took two "gap years" in between high school and college to decide EXACTLY where to apply, and Hampshire just kept getting "top priority" when it came to my college choices. The fact that they thought also thought Hampshire was exceptional was definitely a plus -- they attended the University of Chicago & Columbia respectively, so I respected both their takes on Hampshire as academics.

Hampshire is NOT therefore an "easy" college, and it will test and challenge even the most rigorous of students. When it first opened in 1970, it was the MOST selective and competitive liberal arts college to get into in the entire country. I ❤️'d Hampshire because it was the "right fit" for who I was as an individual and as a student. And that's WHY I chose it. I needed a "safe space campus" where I felt TOTALLY comfortable being out and open as a gay man. 🏳️‍🌈 Otherwise, don't even bother, because you'll just end up hating Hampshire and wasting a WHOLE LOT of 💲💲💲💲.', 'What an incredible college experience my child is having at Hampshire. As a self motivated and directed learner they are getting all the resources they need to complete a truly remarkable undergraduate degree. I am impressed with the facilities and professors. Only drawback I’ve seen would be the difficulty getting into classes at the other 4 colleges', 'I had a good time and learned a lot in the classes, but other than that it was a bad experience.
-It's way too overpriced for what you get.
-For a school that says they offer constant feedback throughout the year including with midterm and final evaluations,,,, have fun opening up to few to no notes on your projects and papers, and copy and paste evaluations. "___ did a good job in class and did their work." Okay..and?? That gives nothing to future employers. Waste of money and time. All my evaluations were 4 sentences long. Really glad I worked my butt off in your classes only to say that I did my work and didn't  talk in class.

Onto the little stuff:
-bad food, few options, small portions, and too expensive.
-everything closes at 4 on campus.
-bathrooms are disgusting.
-Gross dining comms in dorms.
-make sure to make friends  DURING orientation!!!!!
-I recommend taking a college writing course at another school freshman year.

Positives:
-can wake up 10 minutes before class because everything is very close by.
-can be good if you're the right type of person I guess.', "i attended their admitted students day so i will be writing from that perspective. yippee!
- i feel like the majority of the student body is gay and neurodivergent, and they're all super cool actually
- the psychology class i attended was pretty interesting and the dude teaching seemed to be well-liked by the students as they were joking around and such
- super unorthodox, but probably a bit too much for me tbh 😭 so not really for me"]

name: College of the Holy Cross
reviews:
['This school does absolutely nothing to help students find employment. Most of my twins graduating class friends are either still searching 6 months later, or working in low end service jobs. Save your money, they only care about tuition collection. State colleges are better connected to employers.', 'Went here for a campus tour; the guides, staff and organization were tremendous and very helpful. So good, in fact, that my son applied and went for the interview - which was insightful and very professional. My son was so blown away by the experience that he ended up bypassing the "expected" schools to attend The CHC. We are so glad he did - he loves it and we, as parents, love it for him.', 'You climb that Worcester hill, and before the Gothic spires, before the manicured quad, something stops you cold: Enzo Plazzotta’s bronze hand—68 inches of oxidized metal thrust skyward like a prophet’s warning or a drowning man’s last reach. It’s called The Hand of Christ, but it reads like accusation. That’s Holy Cross in miniature: beauty on the surface, uncomfortable truths murmuring underneath.

The campus dazzles. Mount Saint James earned its nickname—The Hill—through topography that doubles as metaphor: you are always climbing, always reminded of hierarchy, always breathless. The 175-acre arboretum sprawls across dramatic elevation changes. Fenwick Hall’s twin spires (added 1868–1875) puncture the sky with Gothic ambition. Eleven Rodins live here. The architecture shouts permanence, prestige, and a very specific strain of American Catholic aspiration.

But here’s what else they own: a founding story steeped in the economics of enslavement. Thomas Mulledy, Georgetown’s former president, became Holy Cross’s first president in 1843—fresh off being censured for selling 272 enslaved human beings. When fire gutted Fenwick Hall in 1852, the largest rebuilding gift came from Patrick Healy, using $2,300 from his father’s estate—money earned by selling 51 enslaved people. Patrick and his brother James (the school’s first valedictorian) were themselves legally enslaved but passed as white their entire lives—an American arrangement of terror and silence that this institution both enabled and depended upon.

You cannot separate the spires from the ledger. You cannot admire those Rodins without asking who paid—and how.

Today, the college is aggressively selective—21% acceptance rate, down from 43% in 2022—more applicants competing to inherit this gorgeous, compromised space. Controversies swirl like weather fronts: a $25 million donor suing over broken promises, the student newspaper abandoning “Crusader” because it shared a name with a KKK publication, a dispute with the local bishop over Pride flags. In 2019, they ended need-blind admissions. The wealthy climb easier now.

What does it mean to visit? It means confronting American Catholicism’s glittering façade and bloody foundations at once. It means understanding that elite education has always been about who gets to forget and who is forced to remember. From the hilltop, Worcester spreads below—panoramic, possessive, perfect for an institution that spent its first decade debating whether proceeds from enslaved children’s sale were acceptable fundraising.

Go see it. The hand reaches up, the spires reach up—everything here strains toward heaven while rooted in earth that remembers everything. That tension is the American story, and Holy Cross tells it with startling clarity if you look past the purple banners and polished bronze.

The art is world-class. The view is breathtaking. The history is what it is: ours.', 'Save yourself $10,000 a year in vehicle suspension repairs by not going to school here. The number of speed bumps in the parking lot will destroy your car', '[My niece Katie and I had the chance to join a tour this morning, and it was such a great experience! Our tour guides, Ava and Maddie, were fantastic—so friendly, enthusiastic, and interactive. They answered every question and made the tour both fun and informative.

The admissions staff was warm and welcoming, and the campus is absolutely beautiful. The energy and positivity we felt throughout the tour really stood out. Highly recommend this tour to anyone considering the school!']
