name: Lasell University
reviews:
['Do not attend this school if you are a Criminal Justice major. Even without being a CJ major, the school advertises courses that you can’t actually take and there isn’t much help around that stuff. Also, the school isn’t as diverse as you’d think it is with students often being targeted or harmed with staff saying “freedom of speech” and if your abuser has money, nothing will get solved. The food at the dining hall is known to give students food poisoning and one Staff member who works there denies any wrong doing and blames students saying they got food poisoning elsewhere. The housing looks nice but there’s big infestations and some of the dorms are known to have mold in it. On the outside, the school looks pretty but please talk to actual students before going here, don’t talk to the students giving you the tour; they have to lie to you and sell the place to you. The school only wants money and doesn’t help with anything. The wifi constantly breaks down on students and they’re often left feeling stuck. Please try to go somewhere else. It’s not worth being here for the cheap price.', 'I previously attended Lasell for an earlier degree and decided to return to pursue my MBA. During the admissions process, I was explicitly told that any combination of nine credits across split-session semesters would qualify me as a full-time student. This distinction was critical because I planned to use my Veteran benefits.

Unfortunately, this information turned out to be incorrect. As a result, the Registrar’s Office repeatedly mishandled my VA certification, which ultimately caused me to incur a debt with the VA through no fault of my own.

I made multiple attempts to resolve the issue, working with both the graduate program office and the Registrar. While the graduate program office made sincere efforts to help, the Registrar’s Office consistently failed to communicate or correct the problem—even after involvement from the Academic Vice President.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this school to veterans. Lasell is not veteran-friendly, and errors in handling VA benefits can have serious financial consequences.', "Lasell has a lot of housing around the campus yet they always seem to be wanting to purchase more properties every time a house nearby comes up for sale. There is a concerted effort in the community to not sell property to Lasell and rightfully so. Who wants a grand Victorian house built in the 1800's to become a dorm that houses anywhere from 13 to 38 students. To Lasell's credit their dorms are very nice.

Lasell was a girls only college until 1997 and them becoming coed was not an issue, the issue came about 10 years later when for whatever reason there was an influx of kids from the inner city of Boston that started to go here. It was not a good time in the history of Lasell as there were cops at the campus all the time. Thankfully that time has passed and things are back to normal around the neighborhood.", "I can't wait to tell people about my experience here at Lasell College once I graduate! It has been an honor to meet everyone here on campus and get to know them on personal levels. I truly feel ready for the working world because of the classes I've taken and the professors help. The dorms that I have lived in for the past four years have been fantastic! They really made me feel safe and at home here on campus. I played a sport here on campus too and that even made my experience here even more enjoyable. Traveling around the MA area is also great. We are in-between two T-stations which is a quick and easy train ride into Boston which allows for a lot of fun activities. I give this school a grading of an A because it was truly an amazing experience and I will miss it dearly when I graduate.", 'Very positive experience with students helping seniors being abused at facilities outside of Lasell University campus.
If it wasn’t for Lasell students being honest seniors in other cities at other senior facilities wouldn’t know that others are trying to help them.']

name: University of Massachusetts-Lowell
reviews: ['The University of Massachusetts Lowell, anchored at 220 Pawtucket St, is consistently characterized in my professional and local circles as a pragmatic powerhouse that expertly bridges the gap between traditional scholarship and the high-tech demands of the Merrimack Valley. From several substantive discussions with engineering and nursing alumni, a clear consensus emerges of an institution that offers a merytorically rich environment where the faculty’s industry experience translates into a tangible competitive edge for its students. My colleagues often remark on the university’s unique ability to foster a culture of "work-ready" innovation, noting that its graduates possess a sophisticated technical moxie that is highly prized by regional employers. In frequent conversations about the Massachusetts educational landscape, those I trust repeatedly emphasize the university’s strategic transformation into a top-tier research hub that manages to maintain an incredibly supportive and inclusive atmosphere. I am particularly struck by the university’s dedication to hands-on learning through its extensive co-op programs, a feature my acquaintances describe as a decisive factor in their rapid career advancement. It is evident from the collective feedback of those around me that the administration operates with a transparent, forward-thinking vision, ensuring the campus remains a prestigious yet accessible pillar of economic and social progress. Reflecting on these consistently positive testimonials, I view UMass Lowell as a distinguished and dependable institution that fulfills its mission with undeniable class, integrity, and a profound respect for the practical success of its student body.', 'The psychology department cares more about money and reputation rather than actually helping disabled people. No one who works there really understands real psychology from real experience; they only know what the textbooks say. There was this study they called "great" which I can tell is ridiculous, when they tried to make kids not touch guns by giving them guns and saying "don\'t touch" which I already know has the opposite effect on kids. It makes kids want to touch it more. The teachers only pretend to know what they doing, and convinced themselves into believing they know what they\'re doing, and they haven\'t changed their teaching materials in 50 years. They teach ideas like using torture methods to control autistic kids, thinking that autism is some kind of "disease" that needs to be "cured." When I took a class there, I emailed the professor Richard Serna about how I struggle with school because of mental disabilities and he didn\'t take it seriously at all. He was condescending. He went into early retirement instead of doing anything to change the school or take responsibility for teaching hateful opinions about autism.', 'They lost my transcripts after I submitted them in person at their office that I got from overseas and did absolutely nothing to help me find them after I followed up asking for next steps since I did not hear back from them for weeks. I cannot speak to the quality of education there, but the graduate admissions department is incredibly horrible to deal with. I would not use my GI benefits here, I have since decided to look elsewhere and wondering if I should take legal action given that sensitive documents with my personal information and academic history is just floating around without any document control.', 'Great education and people however some departments could benefit from refinement. Overall, I would recommend this University to anyone looking for quality education.', "This insitution, law enforcement, and specically JULIE CHEN handled this emergency situation on south campus terribly. I don't feel safe having to attend class in person and I don't feel safe being an on campus student right now in general! Don't send your kids here. Sure some programs here are good and are getting recognized, but none of that matters over your life and safety"]

There are kids using their phones talking and texting.", "I Love Participating And Studying Compassion And Working Hard Writing Fractions In March 10,2014 Earning A+ Plus helping My Teacher Mrs.Hesier And Believe I Can Become A Businessman For his Co-Workers At Wendy's 303 Central Street, Natick Massachusetts,01760.", 'Financial aid department is completely incompetent with zero communication skills, and will cost you thousands. Best to avoid this place at all costs']

name: Massachusetts Bay Community College
reviews:
['I’ve had a couple experiences at this school that honestly left a bad taste in my mouth.

One time, I asked a gym teaching assistant a simple question, and he literally turned his head away and ignored me instead of answering. It wasn’t even a big ask — just a normal student question — so being completely dismissed like that felt disrespectful and unprofessional.

Another situation happened with one specific white student. I was just walking where I needed to go, minding my business, and he went out of his way to point me out and make it seem like I was “doing too much,” almost like he was trying to get other people’s attention. He could’ve simply walked past me the whole time, but instead he chose to make a small scene. It felt unnecessary and weirdly targeted.

What made it worse is that, as a minority, moments like that carry a different weight. When someone who doesn’t know me at all singles me out like that, it starts to feel racially charged, even if it’s subtle. It makes you wonder why you’re being treated differently for simply existing in the space. That kind of behavior doesn’t feel accidental — it feels intentional, and that’s uncomfortable.

At the end of the day, though, I don’t take their opinions personally. You can’t judge someone you don’t even know. If you’ve never spoken to me or taken the time to understand me, your assumptions don’t mean anything. It just shows a lack of awareness and maturity on their part.

I just expect basic respect. School should feel neutral and professional, not like you’re being dismissed or singled out for no reason.', "I've been taking classes here and there since 2021. I'm currently in their nursing program and set to graduate in the spring. I've enjoyed my experience at MassBay. There are tons of resources they have for students. I've always gotten the impression they really care about students. They really want you to succeed and make sure you have the tools necessary. Great school to get started at if you want to further your education! Will always recommend everyone I know to Massbay", 'I am writing this review to document a deeply troubling experience I had at MassBay Community College involving violations of the ADA and the creation of a hostile learning environment.
After disclosing my ADA accommodations, I experienced repeated bullying and harassment from an instructor, Dr. Singh. When I formally complained, the situation escalated rather than improved. In a lab setting, a student helper repeatedly clapped at me to rush my work under the hood—an action that is neither standard practice nor appropriate in an educational or lab environment. When I clearly stated that this behavior was not acceptable, Dr. Singh dismissed my concerns and made excuses to justify the conduct instead of addressing it.
Despite raising ADA-related concerns, no meaningful corrective action was taken. Instead, I observed retaliatory behavior. After I began providing documentation and statements from other students to the Dean, staff then approached students and discouraged them from speaking to me. This contributed to a hostile and isolating learning environment, which is unacceptable in any academic institution.
During this time, I was also dealing with an extremely vulnerable personal situation, as my mother was on hospice and has since passed away. Rather than receiving understanding or support, I felt further marginalized and dismissed.
MassBay promotes itself as an institution that supports diversity, equity, and accessibility. Unfortunately, my experience did not reflect those values. As a student of color with documented ADA accommodations, I did not feel protected, respected, or heard. To date, no apology or accountability has been offered.
I am leaving this review so that my experience is on record and not forgotten. I hope MassBay takes serious steps to address ADA compliance, faculty conduct, and the treatment of marginalized students so others do not experience what I did. I have also contacted the federal and state offices with my experience so this school stop begging for funding for equity when they don’t practice it.', 'Gorgeous campus and friendly staff.  I just wish it had better labeling for wheelchair users.  The floors are super confusing!

I was there for a training in room 420 something.  The person in the office told me to take the elevator to the south floor (logical).  Unfortunately this building is NOT logical.

Most of the floors are divided by this dipping hallway that simply goes down a. Inch of stairs and right back up!

I could not reach the room I needed from the elevator I was in.  I went down a floors:  same story.  I finally went down to the second floor and then took a different elevator, but it was very frustrating.  Then I couldn’t figure out how to get back out, as most of the doors said “fire alarm!”

Just… better signage.', "I’m reaching out to express my deep frustration with the advising ( AMAKA) I recently had. I was made to wait for at least 40 minutes, only to be told at the last minute that the advisor couldn't help me at all. This was incredibly disappointing and unprofessional, especially since I was depending on that support to move forward with my education.

Unfortunately, this experience has left me feeling like I have no choice but to leave the school. I expected guidance and assistance, and instead, I felt dismissed and disrespected.

I hope steps are taken to ensure that no other student has to go through a similar situation"]

name: MCPHS University
reviews:
["I graduated from the PharmD program in 2014 and truly loved the school. It was not an easy program, but that’s part of what made it great. I believe many of the negative reviews come from students who struggled academically and were unable to pass or graduate. If you're smart and willing to dedicate 5–6 hours a day to studying, it's absolutely worth it. I highly recommend this school.", 'Thank you MCPHS for allowing me to take supplemental courses online for my degree so that I may graduate on time. If anyone is considering trying their online courses and unsure, go for it! The platform is user friendly, I never had an issue once and I took two separate semesters of courses. Without MCPHS I would have needed to stay at my current university for an extra semester, I am so thankful that this was an option!', 'Really proud of MCPHS. If you are ready to succeed, the professors are ever willing to help you achieve your goals.', "4 star because parking is impossible if you have a 10a to 12 noonkind if a class. After 12, metered parking eases a bit if you have patience to go round a few times.
There's garage parking but $20 to $40 for a 2 hour class. Do the math if you have 2/3 morning classes.
Otherwise, the school is great. Am in yr 2 Healthscience/ Public Health. My professors have been great so far except 1/2.
They are understanding and will work with you if you reach out to them early before due dates especially for adukt learners with many other obligations. I love it here.
Ill recommend MCPHS - Boston as your college. Thank me later.
They will work with you on payments too. You just have to let them know whats going on and early too. Not when due dates are up or they've passed.", "Hey guys, good for all the students giving great remarks. I don't know if the school has paid you. I must say i was in the nursing program , ( the set that started 2005) the teachers were very bad.  Everything was very difficult, out of 50 students that got into the nursing program only 15 students or even less that graduated from the program. Judy Murphy was very racist, no room for improvement. It was a very bad school. I will recommend another school any day any time as matter off fact the school needs to refund money back to students that paid for tuition. All they care about is your money and not the students. It was a very traumatic experience. It was one of the worst decision i have  ever made in life to attend that college. I Owe up to 100,000 in debt with no  nursing degree to show  for. I thank the Almighty God i got my degree from another school with no stress or frustration. Guys open your eyes and look for another school. I wish you all luck in your careers endeavors."]

name: Massachusetts College of Art and Design
reviews:
["It's a good school. I studied there for a while. The teachers will convert your comic books into digital versions and teach you many techniques, such as how to format, draw shapes, and add shadows. If you think you like drawing or have a talent for it, I highly recommend studying there. And the food in the cafeteria is pretty good too.", 'Very good, Very informative and answered any and all questions pertaining to transfer from a university to  this school. Staff even conferred to director of admission electronically and got back to my granddaughter via telephone. I was impressed with the help they are willing to go to make sure any questions are answered.', 'Interesting art college, went there for an exhibit called nothing is edible that I saw online. Security guard was extremely rude, sent us to another building where a friendly employee told us the main building we went to was the right place. Went back and the guard confronted us again, asked me why I was signing in as if he wasn’t going to give us entry. Generally acted as if he looked down on us instead of being helpful with information on how to find the exhibit.

The exhibit was open to the public, don’t know what his problem was but he needs more interpersonal skills training.

The student exhibit was great, we loved it! Def very creative and executed skillfully.', "There's an AA Meeting there on Saturday Night from 8 to 9:30 pm.", 'I only walked around outside but being an art college there were a lot of interesting pieces around the building. Go check them out!']

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
reviews: ['M.I.T., thank you for keeping parts of your campus open to the public. Truly a gem among universities. So happy to step inside and experience the beauty of M.I.T., both inside and out. The backside view with the tomb is absolutely worth visiting, and the downtown lights in the background make for stunning pictures ✨ My kids loved walking in and out!!', 'The campus is beautiful and has a long-standing tradition. It’s spacious, with lots of trees and green lawns. While the exterior has a classic, historic look, the interior is very modern. There are always police officers on and around campus, so it feels quite secure. Don’t forget to check out the MIT Coop to grab some souvenirs!', 'Really cool campus. There are tons of things happening including free events. I usually just go to the dome and take a picture but there is so much more to explore including free art museum.', "Tour there for future education. It's just simply an amazing campus.", 'gorgeous university and very spacious to explore. I would recommend anybody to come here and at least take a picture in the big dome (the icon of MIT). Also, if you know anyone from this school, it would be better to have them accompany you and perhaps introduce you to their campus. It is a huge campus and it would be impossible to explore all of them if your time for visiting boston is limited. I would suggest go to harvard university too on the same day.']

name: Massachusetts Maritime Academy
reviews: ['Anyone whose children are looking for an academically strong marine science and maritime focused centered curriculum could not find a better place to tour for their future college students. So impressed with the list of degree programs, and they are adding certifications and liscensing classes all the time. The campus is self contained, professionally managed but student led studies abound, and the upgraded buildings and design, plus the new facilities coming (plus a new amazing sea faring Vessel) are gorgeous and State of the art for students moving out into the real world. NCAA div 3 sports abound, and hopefully, they bring back the winter cycle to add even more, with training facilities any SEC team would be excited to use!  The structure of the military type schedule is manageable without being overwhelming, and the students never need to worry about what to wear except on downtime. Beaches and shopping are minutes away, but you feel like you are on your own little island. Look them up. It is a true diamond in the rough.', "We went to watch my son's football game against the MMA. It is a nice clean facility. It was MMA's homecoming game and Canal day, which made it very crowded and busy, but it was an organized miss, the logistics and resources were well organized and deployed. I interacted with campus police while waiting inline to find a parking spot, they were friendly, accommodating and had everything under control.", 'A very difficult and time consuming experience that set me up for success in graduate school and life. The views cannot be beat and it was the most fun I have ever had playing sports.\nGo Bucs!', 'My cousin’s son is really enjoying his graduation from High School in Newton,!MA', 'Very nice academy. Was on a small but nice campus. The food was really good but the dorms were not the best, and looked like I was in the 1500s.']

name: Massasoit Community College
reviews:
['A very good Community College trust me!', 'Very disappointed with this school. There was constant misinformation and almost no communication during the enrollment process. My student was told multiple times that financial aid would cover the course, only for the school to suddenly send a $1,400 bill and give just 30 days to pay before threatening collections.

I would not recommend this school to anyone unless you get every single detail in writing. They charged outrageous fees for a student who took an online-only course and never even stepped foot on campus — yet still billed campus fees.

Overall, the experience was frustrating, misleading, and completely unacceptable.', 'If you're looking for a good nursing program, look else where! Program is all over the place; too many unnecessary/expensive materials  from corporations that you're "required" to have but they hardly use in exams or helps you in your studies. Clinical instructor(s) that "targets" students during clinicals, especially if you are a minority, male, a working parent, or a LPN. The nursing faculty will turn a blind eye and will make sure that it's a "you" problem and not theirs. The college is good in general, but the nursing program was very disappointing.', 'Great community College great place to save couple years of tuition they have competitive sports programs all types of classes for academics and then you can transfer to 4 year schools with two years less debt win win in my book', 'Went for the covid test.  Covid staff is well organized, very quick. But to enter the line you have to have a luck and Police dont make it easy to enter the line. Seriously you have to have a luck to enter and you may have to scroll multiple times around the street. Make sure you have enough gas in your vehicle to idle about 3 hrs.']

name: Merrimack College
reviews:
['Awful school. Charges 60k a year and is not worth it whatsoever. It is basically just sports washing and for-profit education at this point. Merrimack has an acceptance rate of over 70%, showing how lackluster its academics are. The college itself is in a suburb with many ordinances against university life, and is not nearly as accessible to Boston as described. The school offers nothing you can’t find at your local state university, but charges 6 times more in tuition.', 'Very well kept campus and well laid out. Was here for an event at the Rogers Center which was very impressive. Staff was friendly and helpful with parking.', '- Will never see me in that dining hall
- got food poisoning from the den
- don’t salt/plow walkways and roads nearly good enough
- overpriced', "Great school academically. Athletics and Esports are good and getting better. Where this campus falls short is in the food, lack of dorms, and lack of transportation. The food available on the required food plan is sub par. There are no longer any off campus options either. One cafeteria, one small cafe, two Dunkin, and a smoothie/sub shop. That's it. The food is often undercooked, dry, or otherwise poorly prepped. Plan on buying a food plan with microwave meals, as there are no longer ovens or other cooking options available in the dorms. The dorms are basic. Clean, nice RA's, etc. They simply don't have enough of them. Forced quads and triples in rooms that do not fit that, are a regular thing here. Plan on limited space, or paying extra, or living off campus. If Merrimack could ditch the food company preparing the food, and sign a reputable one. If Merrimack could build more dorms. If they could offer transportation options to the mall, the beach, and local towns. If. They would be a destination school.", 'Their Tuition-Free Teacher Education Fellowship program is harmful. You could work and make 40-50k as a sub teacher, covering the full cost of your degree and living expenses (and completing your practicum). Merrimac wants people to work for free for the year, covering 20K in tuition and no living expenses. Super helpful to the underprivileged. They also are extremely unhelpful and money oriented as an overall agency.']

name: Middlesex Community College
reviews:
['Went here this summer to do placement testing before fall classes. When I walked into the testing center the really old overweight Caucasian lady with white hair in the testing center was SO nasty and mean. I didn’t feel welcomed at all. This was one of my first interactions and impressions of the staff here. I walked in and greeted her saying I communicated with enrollment and advisement via email so I could do my placement testing before I register for classes. She acted completely shocked and immediately began taking her anger out, for whatever reason, on me. She wasn’t even doing anything besides sitting there when I walked in. She was like, “Oh well do you even HAVE an appointment? Who did you even speak with and when?” In such a degrading and hostile tone. She talked to me as if I shouldn’t be here and that I was ridiculous for even asking to do the testing. Even some other women that worked behind the desk with her looked uncomfortable, but of course didn’t speak up. This is NO WAY you treat students especially new ones. She was speaking very loudly and giving attitude when I had a question where the pencils were. She then went on to say as I walked into the testing room, “Well whatever, good luck.” I mean seriously?! I don’t care how bad of a day you’re having you don’t take it out on innocent people. I asked both the advisement and the enrollment office if I needed a specific appointment and they told me via email for the summer to just walk in and take the test before 3pm. So I did exactly what I was told to do. Nobody seems like they’re on the same page and unfortunately I got the brunt of it.', 'Unfortunately they have no teachers and the ones they do have don’t even teach. You’re basically teaching yourself and giving a teacher a free paycheck . Edison received all this money and instead of utilizing for supplies and enhancing the school district it decided to build a stadium. It makes no sense. No quizzes, no homework, no books in some classes. Science labs missing equipment and using outdated equipment. Some teachers don’t follow the syllabus. You are on your own. Most students drop their classes. The class goes from 20 to 6 and the teacher don’t care. They don’t even realize it’s because they are horrible. They only have one teacher per subject. So instead of finishing in 2 years you’re stuck doing 3/4 because they have no classes or teachers. Or you failed because the teacher is horrible. So now you’re paying more to take the class again somewhere else.. save yourself!!the counselors are clueless and not helpful at all! Students are teaching themselves using YouTube teachers. .. You are truly teaching yourself!! Maybe they should pay the students instead of the lazy teachers.', 'i hate this college. No one knows anything. I have to constantly ask 6-10 people for one question. The people you need are never around. The librarians cant even help with a lockdown browser and they dont even know anythiny. Im tired of walking to EVERY SINGLE building for ONE question that the PROFESSOR I HAVE SHOULD KNOW!!!!!', "I thought I put Edison on the GPS but accidently got to East Orange since the police is always there 24/7 monitoring students and THIRSTING for tickets and that makes it feel awkard and seems like there's lots of crime in Edison!

NO PARKING SPOTS AVAILABLE AT ALL! They consolidated the parking to only ONE SMALL SPOT area thats always full and they will still issue you tickets on permitted spots which is absolutely does not make any sense! and you have to walk at least 10-15 mins to get to your class even on raining days and bad weather conditions.

In short, if you are not disabled with parking permission, it's not a good option for you to go there!", "I've been waiting to get accepted and start classes for a year!
This school acts like it's Harvard University with the acceptance terms when it's just a regular community college like all others.

They required so many documents to submit just to get accepted that I was never asked for those documents at other colleges in NJ!

Advisors are very strict and really tough with the rules!

They have been still processing my application since Decemeber 2024!

I don't feel nice welcomed to that school and still deciding:
Is this the right school for me with the way they act?"]

name: Montserrat College of Art
reviews:
['If I could give this place zero stars I would. Let’s start from the beginning.

On my first tour to Montserrat in 2021, I was told many things that would soon be turned to lies. “Your guaranteed housing in the student village your first year” “We are very generous with aid to ensure our students can attend school” “We are always here to help and answer questions”. What they make seem is a very positive portray of the school is a facade. After touring the school and applying in 2022 I was accepted at their acceptance day. News flash: Everyone at acceptance day is accepted because the school has such an incredibly hard time getting people to apply, so they’ll take anyone who shows an ounce of eagerness.

After being accepted I had requested to view the dorms since I am disabled. I was given some stupid excuse that they were being cleaned or renovated. Of course I didn’t fight that and just went on my way. Thankfully I was able to hunt down current students on instagram who graciously sent me photos. It was nothing but alarming. However, I still decided to take the chance since the room were not from my building.

I lived in the Abbott location and didn’t even find out I was living there until a week prior. Found my suitemates maybe 5 days before and had to scramble to get to know one another. It was an absolute hell since none of us got along (they really don’t pay any mind to your preferences in the survey for rooming). Thankfully my roomate was nice and we got along okay. I moved in on the day that was listed for me and was left to wait over an hour since no one wanted to show up on time to help us. The day was nothing but chaos and was extremely inaccessible.

Once we were finally allowed to move in, the place was filthy, shower coated in mold, water brown, lots of belongings left behind from previous people. The rooms are actually a joke. They are smaller than an average single for a double and try to force three into one of these as well. You’ll usually have 8 suitemates in the house dorms (there’s like 7 houses) if you can’t get the village. The worst of it all was the trespassing issue. Constantly strangers from the town of beverly would try and break into our fence. There was even a homeless person living right under my window at a point. When I brought the is all up to the school the president sort of laughed it off time and my parents and had no interest in doing much. He even referred to these trespassers as the schools friends. When I tried calling law enforcement they wouldn’t come out to a house that I was paying to live in, because someone was trying to break into my property. I finally said enough was enough and left. The facilities of the school it’s self of nothing to bat an eye to. All the teachers I’ve had are just purely rude and have no interest to teach. I’ve been degraded multiple times by several and was able to receive any help from an advisor to assist me.

In the end I left and transferred to MassArt and I have truly never been happier. I actually feel like my needs are put first and my SAFETY. Unlike Montserrat, MassArt actually answers their security line and they get there in a minute. I’m not told that “it’s not big deal”. I’m actually cared for and treated with basic decency. Please be very weary about attending this place. They’ll probably delete this knowing their track record but this is true information that needs to be known.', "At the time that I was there, there was a woman directing the financial aid office that was renowned for the terror she caused, and had not only failed to remove extra charges on many student's accounts (art kit, mostly) but gave false information about loans and financial aid. (This means they were burdened with student loans THEY DID NOT NEED) There was also several safety concerns around the ventilation, issues with the lack of a decent meal plan, and student safety issues. The head of the animation department (Blyth) is another person well known for acting unkind and almost vindictive to her students. On several accounts she was caught lying, manipulating, and pitting students against one another.

All in all, there were maybe three good, professional professors at this college, who themselves were limited due to the number of fresh-out-of-high school students who seemed to care very little for their professors, the rules/safety concerns (don't put turps in a water bottle, the teacher tells us TEN TIMES) or for any of their fellow students. I saw most of my class year leave this place for better colleges, I saw students in tears over the additional and unnecessary loans added to their bill, I saw students being treated with uncalled for disdain, and I saw teachers being treated much the same. This college is a mess, to sum it up nicely. They fool you with their tour, and the gallery spaces, and their programs to get students out and working in their field of choice. Perhaps one out of three succeed, but the rest either don't care enough, or are smart enough to move on to another college as quickly as possible. Perhaps, in the few years since I have left, they have somehow managed to fix up everything nicely, but somehow I doubt it. At its core, Montserrat College of Art is rotten.", 'Fantastic school with a very personable staff. The professors are accessible and invested in their students: they go above and beyond to help their students succeed. There are tons of resources available to students who need it. From what I’ve seen,  most of the complaints come from students who don’t put much effort into their work or do things at the last minute - no institution can magically fix a poor work ethic. A successful art career and art education is rooted in time and effort spent, but some people seem to think they can skate by with minimal effort and succeed, which is unfortunate. That said, some of the technology, such as the printers, could use some updating, but overall im very happy with my education here so far.', "It's a beautiful campus in a great community. The staff is so friendly and caring. I'm so glad my daughter picked here to go to!", "Very similar experience as the user 'Chris Pine' stated. The head of the Financial Aid Office was often unhelpful and mishandled my Veteran Benefits, leaving me no choice but to utilize loans. I left after just two years due to dissatisfaction with how things were managed.
I attended in 1998-2000."]

name: Mount Holyoke College
reviews: ["Moving in my God-daughter for her freshman school year. It's a gorgeous campus. All staff have been extremely helpful.", 'I remember when Dr. Houseman sent his daughter “Baby” here to study Economics of Underdeveloped Countries. Money well spent!', 'Best place!!!! One of the most beautiful colleges I’ve seen', 'The entire Mt Holyoke system was personally traumatising, from the interdisciplinary degree I could create to the social connections, insufficient lack of support with career, internships and counselling. My sports teammates were bullies, and the coaches enabled that. The Residential Advisor department is horrible. I left mid-way to graduate early in my final semester - a fellow RA in the same position was placed in the nicest dorm, and I was placed in a basement room with clunky pipes. The World Peace class was taught from a white colonial perspective. The student body was international but not diverse in the true sense of the word. The only saving grace were some of the kind professors, and that I got to take better classes at other colleges.', "As an alumna, it is good to see the old place as well as check out what's new"]

name: Mount Wachusett Community College
reviews:
["A good college as any community college is to take your credits and transfer to a 4 year.
Professors and admin are hit or miss.
I was deeply reminded of this. when I saw this AI generated ad. If Admin is lazy enough to use AI like this it's just as lazy with placement credits etc. as they were with me.
School feels weird because i did a lot of tasks but didn't learn much in all.", "so far not a good start. i transferred all my college credits, and high school diploma. did the 101 tutorial.. tried to call an advisor to sign up for classes but they never answer. my student portal email isn't working either. what a mess!", "I am just toying with the idea about taking some classes next year. I went to MWCC to talk with an admissions rep.  They were super friendly and very informative. They went over many possibilities and options for me. They even gave me an impromptu tour of the area where the classes I am interested in would be held.
I'm still not sure if I will be taking classes, but the rep I talked with gave me a lot of information and gave me all their contact Info in case I had any more questions. It was a very positive experience.", "Perfect place to get a degree. If you're serious about getting some work done (not partying for years) then this is the place for you.", 'Just just joined so far staff seems very nice. Everything seems well laid out, I will update in the future if anything changes but seems like a place to work out. No one bothers you.']

name: The New England Conservatory of Music
reviews: ["II'd say the New England Conservatory is really a cornerstone of music education. It's one of the oldest independent music schools in the U.S. and a pretty iconic place. It's a hub for classical music, jazz, and a whole range of talented musicians.", 'Brand new facility just in the last month. Very nice location in Boston across from Northeastern University . They are in process of redoing the dorms as well. Prestigious music college.', 'Took in a program of student compositions as the first in-person concert since the start of covid.  Themes were scarcity, anxiety, and terror.  Artists were talented and convincing.  The hall was full of character and sustain.  It was a particular joy seeing the subtle nods, cues, glances, and inhales exchanged between chamber musicians.', 'It was great to meet friends and enjoyed the concert orchestra night.', 'Performers are well trained, good sound qualities, nice and clean hall. You need to come early as you can to find parking. They have paid parking, but if you come early enough you can find street parking nearby Shawnut St or Tremont St. They need to update their bathroom.']

name: Nichols College
reviews:
["I've only visited it twice now (and have been accepted), but I am absolutely blown away at how awesome this college is! Great campus: I love how everything is so close and is on one main road. Great people: I have yet to meet someone who has had a bad experience or someone who just doesn't like the college. The overall feeling of the college is welcoming, and their philosophy that they get to know their students is great! I even heard that they actually take attendance for each class and pay attention to it, something other schools don't do! And to make it better, their programs for business are great! It's my number one choice now, and I don't think that'll change.", "Another beautiful sports complex featuring a baseball field that has natural grass and dirt infield. Has a softball field that has a dirt infield as well. Full football/soccer field, tennis court and volleyball court with sand. They keep this place immaculate. Also has an Olympic size track around the football field. There are plenty of seats for watching all the sports events. Parking lot has plenty of space too. There are plenty of restrooms available. The only thing I thought was weird was that the baseball field doesn't have a backstop. They must lose a ton of baseballs. All in all an excellent experience. Would definitely recommend and return", 'The best dedicated business education for the dollar.
Excellent preparation for ever growing and changing

Each prospective student should interview an alumni from 10 -15 years ago and ask how his BUSINESS education compares with other employees in parallel positions.', "The president of this school, Glenn Sulmasy, should not be working at all, and especially should not be working in academia. He had inappropriate relationships with students at the Coast guard academy. Don't support any businesses that will support this man. His behavior was so egregious, he is banned from the campus of the Coast guard academy. Not the kind of person you want in charge of anything.", 'Five years later, I can safely say they like to lie to students about their earning potential post-graduation. You’ll be lucky if you see $40k/yr with a Nichols degree, and they’ll constantly beg you for money while you’re still paying off your loans.']

name: Massachusetts College of Liberal Arts
reviews:
['After transferring a few times I ended up here. This is the only place the Professors and staff did not abuse their authority. The places I had been before the staff abused authority for petty reasons.
I’d recommend steering clear of the drug scene it’s really lame and I saw a lot of people wasting their potential…but that’s every college. Definitely don’t feel like you need to compromise your values or sobriety to fit in, people will respect it or they’re not your people. There’s definitely that element that just abuses drugs for fun and it’s really boring. There’s so much more interesting constructive things you could be doing.

Build a good relationship with your professors and communicate it really helps.
The Students here are all awesome individuals, everyone has something to contribute to the community and conversation. Music department could use more funding but the Professors are golden, they genuinely want to help you succeed and will take time out of their lives to help you learn.
Food is a low point but the staff working at the dinning common aren’t to blame the college just buys cheap stuff. Staff were always friendly and their efforts made a huge difference. Plenty of times somebody would go above and beyond for no reason and that made my day.

Start a band or do some kind of cool project you only live once 🤘🤘🤘', "The other reviews can be very critical of this place.

Here's the experience that I had:

I have graduated twice from MCLA.  First with my bachelor's degree in mathematics. Second was my master's degree in education.

Both times I learned a considerable amount and the professors prepared me for my profession.

Aside from my education, I met a beautiful woman that is now my wife!

Lastly, I graduated the school with only $18,000 in debt. I would like to see other colleges be able to do that and still provide the education I received.

I'm a firm believer education is what you make out of it. What you put in is what you get.

With that stated Massachusetts College of liberal arts has given me everything I could have asked out of it.", "Toured this school and it is a nice small-medium sized liberal arts college. Student to teacher ratio 12:1, with class sizes having up to but typically no more than 17 or 18 students per class. The students seem to all know each other one way or another, and are all very friendly. The only downside for me is that it's on a MOUNTAIN!!! The twists and turns getting there were a little nerve racking for me, but the sites were pretty nice to see, and the location itself is pretty quiet. Definitely a great option for performing arts and education majors!", 'I applied to MCLA, (back when I applied in the Fall of 1992 it was still named North Adams State College) but I chose to go to Hampshire College over in the Amherst/Northampton Five Colleges area instead, because it was a bit less isolated there with more academic resources than North Adams itself was.

Although North Adams and MCLA's campus is fairly close to Williamstown, and the academic resources of Williams College & the Clark Art Institute, it still couldn't offer the same level of academia that the combined Five College consortium did. I was coming to college up in New England from NYC, so I wanted to choose a college that wasn't "too" isolated.

That aside, I genuinely liked MCLA, I enjoyed visiting the campus and sitting in on classes, and spent one weekend in Berkshire Towers (in a suite with all first-year students to get a sense of an entering students experience) and then another weekend staying in Flagg Townhouses with a group of upper-class students, to get a feel for being a returning student.

That gave me an in-depth feel for MCLA's residence life (which was VERY similar to Hampshire's actually because I'd done the EXACT same kind of "residential life" visits there in the dorms and the mods) and the campus is VERY "cliquey" because of it's small size and how you are housed, but that's typical of most small LAC's whether they are public or private colleges. Although MCLA ended up in my "safety school" category, it was my #1 safety school.

MCLA's  location in the Berkshires however, is STUNNINGLY beautiful. For a public institution, the campus is INCREDIBLY safe, modern and well-maintained.', "Hokey as it sounds, I truly became the person I am today at MCLA. The school is really a village within the city of North Adams, and everything you'd expect of a village - good, bad, and ugly - is never far from hand. If this sort of tight-knit ecosystem is your bag, MCLA rocked. I thrived in small classes that allowed students the ability to have challenging discussions, and the professors by and large recognized when to lead and when to assist. I never would have gone on to pursue a graduate degree in history had my profs at MCLA simply spoon-fed me facts; they seemed to love their jobs and they clearly loved interacting with students. Socially, the quiet town necessitates making friends on campus; rather than finding this limiting, I met amazing people, many of whom I still see regularly a decade later. Last but not least, MCLA is located smack in the middle of the Berkshires, a landscape of rolling hills, valleys, and moss-draped waterfalls that probably inspired the first nature postcard. Seriously - Google Mt. Greylock"]

name: North Shore Community College
reviews: ['I love NSCC. I earned an associates of liberal arts and an associates of science in nursing. Plus, its the only college near me with a funeral service program 😉', "I wish this was a four year school, I would continue on the my Bachelor's here if I could. name: Northeastern University
reviews: ['I visited the campus with my sister (her alma mater). It is a great place to study, with a diverse culture, many learning opportunities, and many smart Indian students.', 'Big campus, feels cold outside but also safe and lots of history everywhere.', 'Do not waste your time or money! They are unorganized and try to withhold your money. I have been calling for weeks trying to me money that should have been refunded a month ago! I will my lawyer involved if money is not in my account by this week. I should not have to constantly call about money that is owed to me! You all are quick to charge a late fee for students, but can take your time with giving our money. The entire cohort was not given credits that were promised.', 'Northeastern University, anchored at 360 Huntington Ave, stands as a masterclass in experiential learning, having effectively redefined the modern educational paradigm through its world-renowned co-op program. From numerous substantive discussions within my professional circles, it is evident that the institution operates with a merytorical precision that grants its students an incredible head start in the global job market. My acquaintances frequently highlight how the university seamlessly integrates rigorous classroom theory with high-stakes professional practice, a sentiment echoed by many families I know whose children have returned from placements at top-tier firms with impressive maturity. In frequent conversations about the Boston academic landscape, the public consensus consistently praises Northeastern for its sophisticated ability to evolve alongside the tech and healthcare industries, ensuring its curriculum remains perpetually relevant. I am particularly struck by the faculty\'s commitment to mentorship and innovation, which many of my peers describe as a transformative force in cultivating a truly entrepreneurial mindset. It is clear from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages the campus with a transparent and visionary hand, fostering a high-performance environment that still feels deeply inclusive and supportive. Friends who have navigated their graduate programs often point to the university’s global network as a decisive factor in their career mobility, proving that a Northeastern degree carries significant weight far beyond the East Coast. The general sentiment among the community is that the university represents a prestigious and dependable pillar of excellence, skillfully balancing its ambitious research goals with a profound respect for the individual success of every "Husky." Reflecting on these consistently positive testimonials, I view Northeastern University as a distinguished entity that executes its complex mission with undeniable class, academic moxie, and an inspiring dedication to real-world impact.', 'Currently a high-school student and Im considering this as my university, we did a tour and the campus looks lovely and the amount of opportunities they have is so extensive it almost feels like too many choices (also there were bunnies)']

name: Northern Essex Community College
reviews: ["Has some sauce. This is where I met the one and only Coach Foley. Brought my cross-country 8k time from 31:46 to 28:56 in one season. Absolute legend. Honestly it might drop to 4 without him. I'll have to ask coach first.", 'Visited the VES mobile office, West of the Technology building. Fantastic service.', "Great facilities and staff. Perfect launch pad for anyone looking to gain an associate's degree, and transfer to a state school. Great location right off of the highway with easy access to the Winnikini State walking trails. Thanks to NECC we were able to earn our Associate, and Bachelor degrees from Northeastern and U Mass.', 'If it were possible to leave this facility zero stars, I would. There was an issue with my account. When I reached out to make contact and try to address and resolve the issue, the staff was extremely condescending. I received nothing but negativity and crude sarcasm from the two females. In my personal opinion, they should not work with people, especially young adults that are trying to further their career. Spend the extra money and go to a different establishment for your education.']

name: College of Our Lady of the Elms
reviews:
["Honestly, I think Elms College is cursed. From the moment I started, nothing seemed to go right. The people were rude and unhelpful, making the environment really toxic. The dorms were in terrible shape — uncomfortable and poorly maintained. The dining hall was hardly ever open, which made things even more frustrating. Trying to get any help was a nightmare because no one answers the phones or responds in a timely manner. The tuition is outrageously high, especially for the quality of education and facilities they offer.

They talk a good game when it comes to enrollment, but once you’re there, the reality is completely different. What’s really disappointing is how poorly the athletics program is run. Most colleges have strong support and trust in their division III athletics, but at Elms, it feels completely disorganized and uncaring. They are lowly ranked in pretty much every sport and proud of it. It also seems like everyone just gets a handout instead of earning their way, which lowers the standards overall.
To make matters worse.

Nancy Davis, Assistant Dean of Academic Student Success, openly talks about student's education needs and grades to other students, which is unprofessional and breaches privacy.
On top of all that, the whole experience seriously affected my mental health. I felt unsupported and stressed throughout my time there. Even after I left, I dealt with lung problems that lasted for months, which I believe were related to the dorm conditions.

Overall, this place just sucks. Save your money and avoid it if you can. There are so many better options especially in the state of Massachusetts.", 'I transferred to Elms from HCC and was pleasantly surprised by my experience there. I loved that the campus was small and I loved that because of that, each student got more one on one help. The dining hall is beautiful and new, the library is comfortable and the people there are helpful, and the professors are all amazing at what they do. I wish I could have stayed there to continue my education!', 'Why does nobody answer the phone at all hours of the day? Admissions goes straight to a voicemail? Operator never at their desk? What a clown show', 'I love Marie or Maria in student accounts. She is the best. So helpful and humanistic.  When I think of Elms College, her incredible customer service is what I think of first. What a great employee!', 'The staff in each office is completely unreasonable and passive aggressive not to mention the final Aid office and student account. If you can I. Would find another place to go to school.']

name: Quinsigamond Community College
reviews:
['Never been inside. The outside of this place is beautiful. I love the nature here! It’s a wonderful, peaceful place. Till they cut down some trees. It looks awful. Sorry, I love this place.Some of my pics below…', "I would absolutely advise anyone with other options to seek a valuable education elsewhere. It’s concerning that a college can operate this dysfunctionally without any repercussions, and it’s a shame the stress they put on their students.
Financial aid, business, and administrative staff are, more often than not, rude and dismissive. Treating people like they're ignorant and don't understand how things work. School recently raised prices, and my child wasn’t notified until just shy of six weeks before the program started, even after they had already made arrangements to return to Worcester. Financial aid has been a hot mess three years in a row. Not sure how they are the only school that never has anything done on time. Students completed every checklist well before deadlines, only to be told that aid may or may not process in time, meaning she would be responsible for thousands in fees if it didn’t come through. On top of that, payment plans close well before aid is processed, leaving students stuck with no options.
Facilities are equally disappointing. Parking lots are full of crater-sized potholes (good luck in the winter), bathrooms are frequently out of order, and nothing ever seems to get repaired—yet tuition keeps going up. Their accommodations for students who need support are also troubling, showing a lack of care for accessibility.
At its best, this school feels like a community college pretending to be something more. A few staff members have been kind, but unfortunately the overall culture is spoiled. Unfortunately their time and money has been wasted and taken a toll on their mental health for going thru this and saying for anyone else child who has another path available, don’t waste your time here.", "Great school offers night classes and very informative on appointment expectations for waiting. School is up to date and we'll vested in helping students succeed", 'Where do I even start? This college is just a mess. If you need to get a degree and it’s your only option that’s the only way you should sell education here. I don’t even know how their rating is so high. The school is extremely low budget and unorganized. When you first sign up most people are not informed of what they need to do. Your financial aid will come in 6 different checks and will have discrepancies. The school does not keep up with online communications and transparency. They wouldn’t put merit list and Dean’s list students in the list till the middle of summer from spring. They are making the “bookstore” more complicated. You will no longer be able to retrieve your books there. Everything is online based and their tutoring demands that you must go into the school or fit into the small online schedule they have. Most schools in mass have unlimited online tutoring. They are only giving 15 hours of thinking Storm no matter how many classes you have(which is for 15 weeks).', 'there communication is bad i seen financial aid twice in person emailed them multiple times for an update to see if im suppose to do anything on my end. come to finally find out today after calling again i was suppose to get a form to fill out but no other person mentioned this to me before and im hear waiting and wondering if im going to be approved or not, supposedly the lady i saw should have told me to fill out the form she did not. upon ending the call now i gotta wait for someone else to resend a form out so its up in the air just waiting.']

name: Simmons University
reviews:
['The whole application process from start to finish was great. Simmons reached out regularly and connected us with tours and current students and were very welcoming. I work with several nurses who had a great experience there so I am very excited for the fall.', 'Unfortunately, I began this process with very high hopes of starting classes at Simmons, but I was met with repeated and significant barriers throughout the application experience. The persistent lack of communication, transparency, and basic respect for my time as an applicant was deeply discouraging and ultimately left me without any desire to pursue an MSW. The process was not only frustrating, but genuinely devastating, and it left me feeling unwelcome and undervalued.

Because of this experience, I would strongly caution others against the MSW program, as well as Nursing. I did not come to this conclusion lightly. I entered with optimism and enthusiasm, and it is profoundly disappointing to feel compelled to leave a review like this.', 'Simmons University is a private, women-focused university located in Boston, Massachusetts. It offers a range of undergraduate and graduate programs in the arts and sciences, as well as professional fields such as business, education, and nursing.

One of the standout features of Simmons University is its commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. The university has a strong track record of supporting and empowering women and other underrepresented groups, and it has a welcoming and inclusive community.

In terms of academics, Simmons University has a number of highly ranked programs, including education, nursing, and social work. The faculty are experts in their fields and are dedicated to supporting students in their academic and professional endeavors. The university also has a strong focus on experiential learning, with opportunities for internships, co-ops, and research.

In addition to its strong academic offerings, Simmons University has a vibrant campus life. The university is located in the heart of Boston, providing students with easy access to all the city has to offer. There are also numerous extracurricular activities and organizations to get involved in, including sports teams, clubs, and community service opportunities.

Overall, Simmons University is an excellent choice for students looking for a high-quality education and a welcoming and inclusive community. It is a great option for those seeking a women-focused education in the heart of a vibrant city.', "I did the online Social Work Master's for only one term. The entire program is very poorly organized. I did not receive a financial aid check until 11 or 12 weeks into the term. The format of the online classes was terrible, class sessions would oftentimes crash or I would lose audio connection. Attempting to speak with financial aid, or advisors was nearly impossible. Even if I had something urgent, the earliest I would receive a reply was a week, sometime I never even received a reply back. If you value your education and an efficient academic process, please do not waste your time, effort, or money on this school. The only positive things I have to say about this school were my interactions with professors, who were very nice and knowledgable and my academic support specialist. Aside from that, everything is mismanaged, poorly organized, and caused more stress and effort than necessary.", 'Nice. My cousin been studying here lot of praise from her.']

name: Bard College at Simon's Rock
reviews:
['I applied to Bard Academy at Simon's Rock (coming from having done my "Junior High School" years abroad in the UK at two public schools in London) for the pathway into finishing High School quickly/starting College early. Simon's Rock philosophy and concept REALLY appealed to me ESPECIALLY since coming from the British Public School system meant being FAR ahead academically of my American peers coming back into the U.S. system where I was more suited for a private high school setting.

This is back when SR's early college programs were ALL based at the Great Barrington, MA campus in The Berkshires; which I ❤️'d. The campus is just ABSOLUTELY beautiful. I'd also applied to Saint Anne's School, The Berkeley-Carroll School & Packer Collegiate (in NYC), The Putney School, Vermont Academy (in VT), Northfield/Mt. Hermon & Deerfield Academy (also in Western MA) for all my other private school choices. In between public and private schools, I applied to a total of 16 High Schools.

As a student from NYC, LaGuardia was ACTUALLY my TOP overall choice (even though it's public) out of ALL the schools I applied to, with Edward R. Murrow (where I ended up going), Stuyvesant, Hunter College High School, High School of Art & Design, Harvey Milk/Hetrick-Martin Institute High School (where I actually taught for a bit when I was a post-graduate student at NYU Steinhardt later on during my grad school years), John Dewey and Midwood High School rounding out my other top NYC public school choices.

LaGuardia is INSANELY tough and competitive to get into (even harder than Stuyvesant and Hunter College HS are), and so, I got wait-listed. Murrow was my immediate LaGuardia back-up, because it offered a lot of the same Performing Arts 🎭 based programs that I'd chosen LaGuardia for. Although I would have VASTLY preferred to go to school in Manhattan instead of Brooklyn, but Murrow is a solid school. A high school peer of mine from Murrow transferred to Simon's Rock after our Sophomore year, and I was always a bit jealous that she'd gotten to leave and go up to school up there. I also had another college peer that I met during my fourth year at Hampshire (who was also from the NYC/NJ area) who'd attended SR for her Associate's Degree and then transferred into Hampshire to finish her Bachelor's.

I EVENTUALLY got to leave NYC and head to college at Hampshire College in Amherst, Massachusetts after I'd graduated from Murrow and then taken a couple of "gap years" having different experiences working, travelling & studying at a few different CUNY campuses (and studying abroad in Israel and the UK) and working at CUNY City Tech for two years.

In the end, my route into private residential New England LAC life was MUCH different than my peer from Murrow (and from Hampshire) who had gone to SR, but at LEAST I eventually got there. 😅', "SRC was an amazing experience for me; it allowed me to broaden my horizon, start college at an early age, meet amazing people, and interact with so many brilliant professors. There are so many fond memories I have about this place. I'm proud to call this place my alma mater. ❤️", "I would Like to explain my situation a bit, by the time I applied I wanted to get into Bard college due to my academic strengths, later there is this one lady named Danielle in their admissions staff, I was forced to attend there new stupid Bard academy program; the reason is that they need more students in this new program, when I was interviewed they reassured me that I will be assessed for college as well, I had emails and everything to verify this statement, I was accepted not into college but academy, after that for some reason to torment me more they sent an official email from BARD COLLEGE saying I was accepted into the college program, they were literally forcing me to attend academy, I thought maybe it was fine but when the scholarships and everything came, They were literally asking me to pay them 71,000 dollars a ridiculous amount for this small high school program that would not even make me successful.

DONT APPLY OR GO TO THIS BARD COLLEGE OR BARD ACADEMY AT SIMON'S ROCK!!!!", "If I could give it 0 stars, I would've done so, their admissions staff are the worst they will not assess your aplication on the basis of your intellect or qualities but to increase the space in their new programs, they just want money from you and nothing else. DONT OPT FOR THIS STUPID INSTITUITION!!", "I didn't go to Bard Academy and therefore shouldn't be writing this, but I feel the need to let potential applicants know about their financial aid awards and admissions. I put my heart and soul into getting into Bard, and for months I stressed and worked myself to the bone. And it paid off, I got in. I was elated, but of course, the financial aid grant was far from what my parents could make work.  When Coronavirus 'arrived' and schools and businesses shut down, my mother lost her job, and my dad's business was hanging on threads. We tried explaining this to the Admissions/Financial aid team our situation, but instead of a response, were met with a couple thousand dollars knocked down from the massive price tag. We were very grateful for them to give us more, but were confused at the initial kind and welcoming admissions, to indirect communication and overtness. It became clear to my family and myself that as we waited and hoped for them to award us more money, that they don't usually get families coming from my financial background. I was heartbroken and frankly depressed for most of this summer. This was my dream school, I envisioned myself relating to all of these amazing experiences other students had, I envisioned myself thriving. It may have been naive on my family's part to apply to a school like this knowing where we came from. Either way, I can see where their priorities are, and unfortunately, my family wasn't the highest bidder."]

name: Smith College
reviews: ['We visited in July and it was so beautiful and green. The walk by the river and the botanical garden. So serene', 'Proud Ada Comstock Scholar, Class of 1998. She's a sweetheart.", 'Smith College has been turning out educated young women for quite some time now. name: Springfield College
reviews: ['This school had me interview in the wrong cohort and did not allow me to have a second interview in a graduate program. There appears to be inconsistencies in expectations of this college with admissions, and how applicants are dealt with. I would advise future students to constantly follow up with admissions to ensure you are placed in the correct cohort and interview cycle. No corrective action was taken.', 'A historic and vibrant campus with a great sense of community. The facilities are modern, and the grounds are perfect for a stroll.', 'This review is solely based on the library, which is open 24 hours of the day. The library comes with a Starbucks, and four floors providing ample amount of seating. The furniture is quite nice, and relatively comfortable. There are a great deal of computers to be used by students, and it comes with a gender inclusive bathroom on each level. All in all it provides a nice environment for study.', 'In my experience, many of the staff are very rude, does not provide good and timely response, let alone horrible customer service. Let’s talk about the lack of quality work and the lack of academic advising performance. There isn’t any quality in that area at all, no “attention to detail” No one Seems have a clue or worse, they don’t focus on the older online students. The main focus is on the young students, and no one else seems to matter. For the amount of money we pay to attend this private school the service they provide does match our money at all. Let’s talk about some of the Professors. They might have PhD’s but they certainty behave themselves as not having no education at all in the way they communicate with students. Rude, unprofessional. For many of them it’s just a title and nothing more.\nStudents surveys really need to be considered to possibly improve in certain areas that continues to lack in professionalism and “attention to detail.”\nPlease start with the academic advising for the online students. Certainly needs plenty of improvement.', 'Great school and football team']

name: Springfield Technical Community College
reviews: ['I am set to graduate in May 2025, and I am so grateful for the opportunity provided by Mass Reconnect at Springfield Technical Community College. The campus has a supportive atmosphere, and I’ve had some amazing professors so far, particularly Professors Tetrault and Meccouri. Their teaching styles and dedication to students have made my experience truly enjoyable. I highly recommend STCC for anyone looking to further their education!', "State Street U is amazing. I attended 22 years ago and stopped by for the first time since then and I was amazed to find, updated buildings, a beautiful store, and a whole new feel. The professors and professionals were mostly great when I was there and though I don't attend, I had a chance to talk to administrators and they are still amazing. It is a fantastic education at a great price.\n\nIf you are looking for a great community college, look no further than STCC. I'm proud my children and family are attending to make their lives better.", 'We were on the grounds for the Knox Cannon celebration put on by the Springfield Armory. A great day in the snow with oxen, horses, cannons and Veterans.', 'Great local school, I completed my 12 month program in IT last December with lots of knowledge. The professor was providing excellent materials, and it was easy to follow and understand every detail. I highly recommend online learning, which helped focus more on studying quietly.', "The place where you're supposed to feel safe turned out to be the opposite. My bicycle was my only mode transportation, and it was stolen from campus, even though it was securely locked. When I reported it to the police, they checked the security footage, but unfortunately, the video quality was poor. They have footage of someone stealing the bike, but it's not clear enough for them to take action. I'm deeply disappointed that, despite paying for college and expecting a secure environment, I experienced this"]

name: University of Massachusetts-Dartmouth
reviews:
['As a commuter I’m disgusted. With all of the educated people here and nobody sees how the parking situation across campus is a punishment for the poor. How many lots do commuters have vs. students who live on campus?? How many of the supposed commuter lots have shared parking between both groups?? Looking at those lots you’ll see a disproportionate amount of parking; commuters scouring for a spot meanwhile students living on campus have ample spots. Today I was extra mortified to see that tractors were parked in commuter parking, taking at least 8 spots when there was so much resident parking available. I get what you’re doing Umass; I pay $256 for a parking pass I can barely use. And you purposely don’t have ample commuter parking because how else would you make up the lost income from me not living on campus, if not through parking tickets… the system is gross and sets commuters up for failure, deterring them from attending class but I’m sure you all know that as a money-making machine. Truly gross.', "I'm a CVPA Alumni, Class of 2020, and the art professors I had at UMass really helped me to develop my own personal style, which is something that I struggled with in high school. They listened and they cared. Shoutout to Bruce Maddocks in particular, he was the best! Loved that I could also join the 2 campus drama clubs, which IMO absolutely made my college experience because I landed leads in both my freshman and senior plays/musicals. Don't overlook this place.", 'The University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, anchored at 285 Old Westport Rd, is frequently celebrated in my local and professional circles as a hidden gem of the South Coast that masterfully synthesizes artistic creativity with high-tier technical innovation. From numerous substantive discussions with alumni and regional business leaders, a clear consensus emerges regarding the institution’s unique ability to provide a merytorically deep education that remains grounded in the practical needs of the Massachusetts workforce. My colleagues often remark on the university’s exceptional prowess in marine science and engineering, noting that the faculty demonstrates a sophisticated level of expertise that is highly respected on a national scale. In frequent conversations about the regional academic landscape, those I trust repeatedly emphasize the campus's brutalist architectural charm as a backdrop for a community that values both intellectual moxie and social mobility. I am particularly struck by the university’s dedication to student-led research, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their children transform into confident, job-ready professionals within the school’s inclusive atmosphere. It is evident from the collective feedback of my network that the administration handles the university’s growth with a transparent and visionary hand, ensuring it remains a prestigious hub for critical thinking. Many of my friends who have collaborated with UMass Dartmouth graduates point to their remarkable resilience and sophisticated problem-solving skills as a direct result of the school’s rigorous "active learning" culture. The general sentiment among the community is that the university represents a dependable and distinguished pillar of the Commonwealth's intellectual infrastructure, especially through its impactful School of Law. Reflecting on these consistently positive and well-grounded testimonials, I view UMass Dartmouth as a premier institution that executes its complex educational mission with undeniable class and an inspiring dedication to the individual success of every student.', 'I do not recommend.

Kids went to the school and graduated. From admissions to orientation to advisors are incompetent. Go to a community college. At least if staffing messes up there you can blame lack of funding.

Orientation, there was hazing like activities. Advisors are useless after sophomore year. Almost like they forgot how to communicate to their students on what classes are required or missing for graduation. So then it's not a surprise that a large portion of the computer science students need to take summer classes and delaying their graduation. Then they "forget" to send degrees out.

I've never seen such ineptitude from what I assume are smart people.', 'Beautiful University & always plenty of parking! Easy access to get too n deffenitly recommend checking it out.']

name: Stonehill College
reviews:
