name: Tufts University
reviews:
['I’ve been here for 10 days as I was on a study trip and I enthusiastically enjoyed my stay here. The facility has everything one needs and one thing I really appreciated is that the campus is completely smoking-free. Moreover, the cafeteria was excellent.
The campus is located 15 minutes away from the nearest subway station, but one can easily walk to it, so it is a good choice for commuters.
Without further ado, everything was great; the only negative thing I feel to point out is the cleaning of the rooms and shared toilets: they need an efficient daily cleaning.', "Tufts, located in Medford just outside of Boston, has one of the most beautiful campuses I have stepped foot on. From the monumental engineering building to the luscious green quads in the summer, any where you look Tufts never disappoints. I recommend checking out the roof gardens if you're in town!", '🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
Tufts University is an incredible place to visit! The campus is beautiful, filled with historic buildings, green spaces, and a welcoming atmosphere. Students and staff are friendly and passionate, and you can truly feel the energy of innovation and learning everywhere. It’s a perfect blend of academic excellence, diversity, and community spirit — truly inspiring!', "The campus is okay but not the best y'know.  It's also too hilly for me and so walking or biking to get around is a hassle. It's all good though, still nice.", 'Tufts University is a private research university located in Medford, Massachusetts. It is known for its strong academic programs and diverse campus community.

In terms of appearance, Tufts University has a beautiful and well-maintained campus. The university is located on a picturesque, tree-lined campus that is spread out across several neighborhoods in the Boston area. The campus features a mix of modern and historic buildings, including several LEED-certified buildings that are designed to be environmentally sustainable.

One of the standout features of the Tufts University campus is its green spaces and outdoor amenities. The campus is home to several gardens, parks, and natural areas, including the Tufts University Arboretum, which is a beautiful and serene place to walk, relax, and enjoy nature.

Overall, Tufts University has a visually impressive and well-maintained campus that is a pleasure to explore. Its beautiful green spaces and outdoor amenities make it a standout choice for higher education.']

reviews: ['The grounds here are so beautiful! I enjoyed a walk on the dirt path along the lake. There are a few platforms where you can sit and enjoy the view. name: Wentworth Institute of Technology
reviews: ['Seems nice. Mainly sat in the parking lot while my relative was moving in. Buildings were classic Boston back Bay meets a bit modern college vibe. Most people were nice and kept to themselves.', 'Was a graduate in 2016. They have sent me emails and now a letter for a $1 past due amount. The letter threatened collections LOL. Multiple attempts to contact them have been ignored.', 'Pleasant and clean campus. From what I’ve heard from colleagues who have attended Wentworth, it sounds like a great career focused engineering and technical design college!', 'I was blown away by this school. I had low expectations being it is a very small school with a very high acceptance rate. I had never heard of the school and my daughter put it on her list as a "safety school." After attending the open house I hope it rises to one of her top choices. The campus is very quaint and comfortable. Felt very safe. It is surrounded by 5 other colleges. Very short walk to any class. Great program offerings, staff seems genuinely interested in the student\'s success. Great hands on learning and resources. Greatest concern is lack of student life b/c it is so small. Not much going on for students.\n* If someone from the school is reading this... I can tell you, you would draw a lot more students to Wentworth if you worked out an agreement with Northeastern in terms of student clubs and activities. An example of this would be how Syracuse University allows SUNY ESF students to join/participate in the clubs and activities (Not the official D1 sports teams, just the intramural teams). This is the only concern holding back my child back from committing and I am sure she is not the only one who has hesitated or turned away for this reason. I am not talking lack of parties. I am strictly talking about fun and interesting clubs and activities. Wentworth works with the other small schools surrounding the campus but that is still lacking enough choices.', 'Wentworth offers small classes, hands on experiences and good faculty. It’s a small school that is not struggling like other small schools, so you can get one-on-one attention and get a good job. They actually care about faculty’s well-being which means faculty can focus on teaching and students can have a better experience in the class.']

name: Western New England University
reviews:
['A highly efficient and quiet alternative to the larger regional airports. The terminal is easy to navigate, and the overall experience is very low-stress. It’s a great choice for travelers who value convenience and a quick check-in process.', 'Great School. I Graduated from Western New England and we do moving jobs there we love it!', 'Cute campus but small dorms.  Tour guide was helpful.', 'This is a great small university. It is a small tight knit campus. My daughter is finishing up her freshman year and loves it.', "I've attended schools from Syracuse University to Holyoke Community College and AIC and STCC and Umass and no one can touch WNEU. AMAZING school. Insane involvement from faculty and staff. Career focused education. Professors that will challenge you NO MATTER who you are and what department you're in.

I majored in Electrical Engineering, but took courses outside of Sleith (the engineering college). I enrolled in Spanish courses, Math course and Chemistry, which are all outside of the Engineering umbrella. I was astounded by how ubiquitous WNE's focus on high standards is. I earned a 3.9 GPA and was challenged in every course. Nothing was easy, but nothing was impossible.

I highly recommend the university. Sure, rural Springfield is a bit of a let-down for things to do. The university does a great job of creating trips and events for students every weekend. Thanks for a life changing experience."]

name: Wheaton College (Massachusetts)
reviews:
['I attended Wheaton in the 1970’s. It was an outstanding experience that prepared me for graduate school and a career in library science and archival management. The quality of the faculty and the academic opportunities offered were stellar. Wheaton has continued to offer an excellent academic program to both women and men in the decades since I graduated.', "I attended a performance in the Arts Center. I noticed that the front of the building facing the main parking lot does not have handicap accessible ramps or doors. There also wasn't any signage directing someone with the need for the accommodations of where to go.", 'As a recent grad, I would really like to say that I am proud of where I went to school and that I had the positive experience that was promised to me as a prospective student. But all of the positivity to be found on this campus-- which is held by the students, faculty, and student-facing staff (not their three-degrees-removed management)-- is clearly the lowest priority at this institution. This has been exemplified through recent senseless layoffs. With no warning to the current students (many of whom depend on their professors for major completion, advising, and course offerings) and inadequate notice for the faculty and staff (many of whom depend on the college for housing and tenure), the current Administration at this college has gone ahead with terminating numerous faculty employment without regard to the impact on campus climate and course offerings.

All of this of course is being done in the name of a very passive culprit: "financial troubles." But the firing of professors-- who at this school earn $82k on average if male and $77k if female-- is a misguided, if not malicious, "solution." According to the Chronicle of Higher Ed, professors at Wheaton have not seen a raise in many years and were in fact paid more on average in 2012 than they are today. Management has seen a different financial reality, with an average yearly salary of $132k that has increased each year that I have been a student. According to ProPublica, the office of President at Wheaton has seen an approximately $100k increase from 2022-2023 alone, receiving a salary of $499k in 2023. These pay raises were not necessary if Wheaton were truly in such a fragile position that they would have to reduce such "privileges" as student club budgets, printers in the library, and professors.

Students are paying more (dear prospective students: when your tuition goes up, your scholarship won't go up with it) while receiving less from this school, as professors who offer unique coursework are being terminated without replacement. Since I'm not an invisible bureaucrat making six figures in a management position, it's unlikely Wheaton cares what I have to say, but here's my two cents anyway: why not fix the pipe that is actually leaking?', 'The staff and professors are extremely helpful and care a lot. There is a lot of help available. The campus is also beautiful.', 'Mold in the residential walls inspired a campus-wide gaslighting campaign instead of actual repairs, food on offer is not substantive enough to justify the cost (and becomes more limited as meal plan costs increase), gyms are puny, transfer credits are not respected and student jobs on campus are fickle. Classes and deals offered to you when you agree to enroll will NOT continue to be available through all your four years. "Student-run campus" = admin kicks most of what you take for granted on a campus onto the plates of RAs and club exec.']

name: Alma College
reviews:
['My experience at Alma College was defined by a toxic environment that failed students on every level—academically, culturally, and morally. Prospective students should be fully aware of what lies beneath the glossy surface of this institution.

1. Failure of Academic Integrity and Faculty Discrimination:
The official 4-year graduation rate for my cohort was alarmingly low, near 33%, symptomatic of poor curriculum and advising. The academic environment was compromised by a prevalent, unchecked cheating culture (via Greek test banks) that rewarded connections over merit.

More personally, I experienced overt classism and gender bias from faculty. I was told by one professor that I "did not belong" in an advanced STEM course because of my gender, and was criticized for wearing simple clothing due to my low socioeconomic background. Other faculty displayed shocking ignorance of life below the poverty line, forcing students to educate them on basic survival economics. The environment is actively hostile toward students who do not fit the college's expected profile of wealth and privilege.

2. Profound Failure in Student Safety and Administration:
The most grievous failure of this institution is its neglect of student safety. After reporting instances of sexual assault, I was institutionally discredited and actively silenced by the administration—essentially told to "sit down and shut up." This created a known environment of impunity, where my aggressors and others were aware that nothing would happen to them. This institutional negligence resulted in further victimization.
Conclusion: Alma College Was Wrong.
I am now a highly successful academic, holding a Master's Degree in Statistics (3.8 GPA) and having first-authored 17 academic papers. The faculty and administration at Alma College systematically underestimated, judged, and endangered me based on bias and prejudice. The college's judgment of me was categorically incorrect, proving that its culture is fundamentally flawed and incapable of accurately recognizing or supporting capable students.

I strongly caution anyone considering attendance here. Alma College is an institution where your safety will be compromised and your academic potential will be actively discouraged if you do not fit their privileged mold.', 'Wonderful program! Enjoyed the variety and high quality performance. They delivered!', "Class of 2016.

Don't go here. Dorms are terrible. The food is bad. If you are able to find a way to live off campus or get out of the meal plan, they cut your financial aid.

They treat their most loyal community members poorly. I just found out they are no longer allowing Mr. Trent to take photos at live events anymore. If you've graduated from Alma in the past few decades, you probably have a Mr. Trent picture framed in your home. He would take photos for no charge for the broke college kids.

SAD.", 'As an Alma alum, the student and faculty ratio was a greatest benefit to my learning experience. You’re able to forge relationships that will last a lifetime given the small community atmosphere on campus. If larger colleges aren’t your style and you want a liberal arts education, consider attending Alma College. Feast your ears for bagpipes and prepare to randomly shout “Go Scots” and “Plaid Works”!', "I'm a sophomore, and I absolutely love this college. They have provided me with every opportunity I was looking for in a college, such as travel, good academics, and professional experience, all while the support from the faculty has helped me be successful and actually be able to receive said opportunities. I couldn't imagine going to any other college, Alma is truly my home away from home!"]

Kudos to "my girls"!!!']

name: Carnegie Institute
reviews:
["I completed a communications and leadership program with The Carnegie Institute, and I couldn't be more impressed with the experience. The program was incredibly well-structured, insightful, and above all, practical. It provided me with tools and strategies that were not only applicable in my workplace but also enhanced my personal relationships.

The focus on effective communication was transformative, helping me navigate challenging conversations with confidence and clarity. The communication techniques I learned have made a very noticeable impact on my ability to lead and collaborate with my team.

I highly recommend The Carnegie Institute to anyone looking to improve their communication and leadership skills, strengthen relationships, and achieve personal and professional growth."]

name: Central Michigan University
reviews:
["Central Michigan University (CMU) in Mount Pleasant, Michigan, is a renowned institution of higher education that has been shaping the lives of students since its founding in 1892. Nestled in the heartland of the state, CMU offers a vibrant and inclusive learning environment, fostering academic excellence, personal growth, and a strong sense of community.

At CMU, students have access to a diverse range of programs and degrees across various disciplines. With over 200 academic programs, including undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees, students can explore their passions and tailor their education to suit their individual goals. From business and education to the sciences, arts, and humanities, CMU provides a comprehensive educational experience that prepares students for successful careers and lifelong learning.

The campus itself is a hub of activity, boasting state-of-the-art facilities and resources. The Charles V. Park Library serves as a focal point for research and study, equipped with extensive collections and advanced technology. CMU's distinguished faculty members are renowned experts in their fields, dedicated to nurturing students' intellectual curiosity and providing mentorship and guidance.

Beyond academics, CMU offers a vibrant campus life with numerous extracurricular activities and organizations. Whether it's joining one of the many student clubs, participating in intramural sports, or attending cultural and social events, there is always something happening on campus. The university's commitment to diversity and inclusion is evident through its multicultural centers, where students from all backgrounds can find support, engage in dialogue, and celebrate their heritage.

Mount Pleasant itself is a welcoming community, providing students with a safe and supportive environment. The town offers a lively downtown area with restaurants, shops, and entertainment options, creating a perfect balance between academic pursuits and recreational activities.

Overall, Central Michigan University in Mount Pleasant combines academic excellence, community engagement, and a vibrant campus life, making it an exceptional place for students to pursue their educational and personal aspirations.", 'So far very impressed with the atmosphere and friendly people. Our daughter is just starting her Grad degree in Psychology. The affordability and convenience of her apartment at The Reserve Mt. Pleasant from the school is great. She is feeling supported and hopeful from day one. The campus is beautiful and the town is equally impressive. Looking forward to more visits.', 'More of the Central Michigan way. At graduation spent 100k on a degree for our son. And zero signs tell parents where to go for graduation. Don’t believe the billboards', 'Will be our son's new home for the next few years.  Wonderful, welcoming,  comfortable school environment.  "Big college with a small town feel" fits this college PERFECTLY.', "This place is a disgrace.  The many of the professors refuse to meet outside of their office hours, even when their office hours are during another class.

As of now I can count no less than 10 broken vending machines on campus, some that haven't been fixed in 4 months!  I've called both CMU and the vendors, and neither one wants to fix the machines.  I guess they don't want to make money.

The parking meters aren't maintained. I found one of the only available parking spaces near the Univerity Center. It was filled with quarters so much that it couldn't accept any more, so I was unable to pay my meter.  You supposedly can pay with an app, but it's only available for iPhone, and I have an android, so i want able to pay that way either. I came out to find I had been ticketed for not paying for a space (I didn't have a student pass at the time).  This is an absurd business practice.

The bathrooms smell like urine all the time, especially in Pearce Hall and Engineering Technology buildings.  I have found the same filth left on the toilets in the bathrooms several days in a row.  Considering the volume of traffic, those bathrooms should be cleaned twice a day, but at least once a day.

The engineering building is the most frustrating sight on campus.  When it rains heavily multiple buckets are used to catch the leaks inside the building.  There are almost no places to plug in your phone or laptop because there aren't enough electrical outlets in the common areas, and of the ones that are present, many aren't working or are broken.  The only reprieve is an extension cord that someone plugged into the cooling of the first floor to access from the common area on the second floor.  Otherwise, in order to charge your phone or computer, you have to sit on the floor like a child playing with his toys because the only outlets available are in the middle of a hallway and are meant for maintenance for cleaning rather than students.  Basically, you will not find working electrical outlets in the same place as seating areas on campus.

All of the sectional furniture in engineering should have been replaced 5 or more years ago, it's all stained and broken down or torn to the point that goodwill probably wouldn't accept it.  There are no study rooms in the entire building, making it hard to find places to work on group projects without leaving to make room for a class.  The printers in this building are a joke.  Most of the ones in the classrooms are blinking because they are out of toner, paper, or just gave up on life.  When they are working they often aren't accessible to student accounts and I have to go to the front office to print, except that I have to convert whatever I need to print into a pdf because that's all it accepts.  I guess it's too much to expect when they don't even know how to install the door stops in the correct place to...eh...stop a door.

I will amend this review when I see that my tuition dollars are being used effectively demonstrate basic maintenance and upkeep on campus.  Since no one is interested in fixing the problem, hopefully posting here will make this more of a priority for Central Michigan University."]

name: Mott Community College
reviews:
['Went here for some testing. Campus is absolutely beautiful. Lady at the library was extremely helpful in telling me where to go. Even let me know where restrooms were. The people who gave me my test were extremely friendly, and made the whole experience as stress-free as possible. Only thing I didn’t like was having to search for parking, but there was a lot of construction going on that was taking up some of their parking area.', 'Most Professors are awesome. I’ve been going here longer than I care to admit, as a full time student. Only to be wronged by a bruised ego power hungry “Professor” and
poorly judged/overlooked by a Dean I’ve never met or seen. With so many rising issues with the school’s safety and faculty, I have never felt so irrelevant and disrespected in my life.
Choose your school wisely and never give up the fight. Especially if you have to fight for yourself against people who share the same circle.', "My experience at Mott has been great! I am going to be graduating in the Spring and I couldn't be happier with my decision to go to Mott. On top of the great education I am receiving I will be able to transfer all of my credits to U of M Flint. Mott partners with several universities to allow their students to continue on to their bachelor degree after graduating.", 'Speak to your counselor before signing up for classes (they will set you right) and actually study the material. The nursing program is by far the best in the county.', "The staff is not trained in their position or in common courtesy. They treat you terribly. They have to check their ego!!!
DON'T USE AN ADVISER IF YOU PLAN TO TRANSFER!! My adviser had me taking classes that didn't transfer to the College that I planned to attend, so now I plan my own schedule. I feel like some professors use this platform to push their agenda. I had quite a bit of coursework based on inequality with gender and race, which is beneficial in the proper class, however it wasn't relevant to my classes at all. I had 27 credits that didn't transfer to UofM, that my adviser said was required. Keep up with the College Course book that you plan to transfer to because nobody at the school does!
Psychology department is amazing especially Professor Ruffin!!"]

name: Cleary University
reviews:
["As a veteran utilizing the GI Bill and a transfer student, I have never encountered such disorganization and incompetence from a college’s financial department. My experience with this school has been nothing short of infuriating. I have repeatedly missed my BAH payments because of paperwork the school failed to submit on time. I also haven't seen grant funds because of the schools delays and failures.
Now, despite fulfilling all academic requirements, the school is withholding my degree over funds that are the responsibility of the VA to disburse, funds I have no control over. Preventing me from applying to jobs that my degree is required for,. This is completely unacceptable.
If you are a veteran or rely on financial aid, I strongly urge you to reconsider attending this institution. Their lack of accountability and failure to properly support student veterans isunprofessional and deeply disappointing.", "I couldn't have more positive things to say about my experience thus far at Cleary. The classes are interesting and applicable to my job as a supervisor. I was at first intimidated with the idea of returning as an older student and perhaps having to compete with younger students, but I quickly realized that my life experience is an advantage. Lastly, the staff are knowledgeable and very accommodating. Overall, I am extremely satisfied and excited to continue my educational journey at Cleary.", 'I recommend Cleary University.
I am absolutely satisfied with my experience so far.  The staff is phenomenal and my teacher (Ms. L. Ellis) has been very attentive to my needs.  Mr. R. Bacon has done a wonderful job assisting me along the way and I am grateful for the consistent support that I have received.  It is a wonderful feeling to know that the staff as a whole is dedicated to my success.', 'As a full-time husband, father and working professional, the professors and support staff at Cleary University has made being an adult student, a challenging yet pleasurable experience. I am greatly appreciative of the constant and inviting communications. Highly recommended!', 'I LOVE Cleary University. It offers great flexibility and wonderful professors. The professors are very understanding and helpful. I truly recommend this school to anybody who has been trying for some time to complete a Bachelor Degree in Business Administration!!']

name: Concordia University Ann Arbor
reviews:
["There are some professors who are amazing. They treat you with respect and don't drop your grade from an 80 or 90 to a failing grade over very small mistakes on a couple assignments. It is insane to me that this school allows this. It does not make sense at all. You can't even talk to them about it because you will be gaslit and not heard. I thought Christians or children of God were better than this. These kinds of people that are who make students leave and never come back to school.", 'Bullies!! Your campus police tried to intimidate and follow me home for briefly stopping to pick up a family member on a PUBLIC road near your campus. Fervently policing and harassing your neighbors. No wonder this school has bankrupted themselves. A COMPLETE WASTE of money!!

I am glad to see Concordia will be closing for good. Bullies Be Gone. Bye bye!! 👋 👋', 'I love my nursing school! All the instructors are so helpful and truly care about the success of their students. The friendships, experiences and opportunities I have had here at CUAA are such a blessing!', 'The criminal justice program is taught by professionals in the field or whom have recently retired.  Minimum rank of Sgt with at least a dozen years experience.  Legal studies utilize the knowledge of true professionals such as prosecutors and lawyers.
Studies use NO TEXT BOOKS, rather the program uses the experience and knowledge base of its professional educators.', 'The campus is beautiful, the Church is beautiful and the people were extremely nice. I am enrolled and working on the last few last few pieces of paper to be enrolled in February.']

name: College for Creative Studies
reviews: ["The open house for prospective students was very welcoming, informative, and exciting. I'm not sure we can afford it but we were amazed and happy to see what is on offer here. Hopefully we can come back one day!", 'This school didn’t treat me well at all . Experience  alot of discrimination on campus from staff Professors .a school I dreamed of going to just to experience racism and mistreatment on campus. You have to pay for lockers .little to no help when asked. Everything is over price. Couldn’t afford to go here .it’s upsetting that no one tried helping me when I asked for it .', 'The summer camp for teens is great and there are so many different options. My kiddo tried pretty much all of the options through the years. There are classes that include field trips to the DIA which is pretty cool. Staff and volunteers are great!', "I must admit, through pure ignorance, that I did not know of this college until my daughter wanted to attend. Not because I wasn't interested, but rather, life choices did not necessitate the need for such a school. But, after visiting the campus during open house, I was blown away at the curriculum variety this school has to offer.\nNow, my daughter does not have a vehicle yet, so she commutes every day via myself or her grandfather, of which I am truly thankful. When I drop her off, I feel that the campus is very safe for her. I haven't heard of any crime on campus yet, at least, not during her time there.\nAs with any college/university, tuition is not cheap. But I know that with the many choices my daughter has, I'm positive it will be money well spent.", 'Great school,  little bit expensive but classes offered are top notch.']

name: Davenport University
reviews: ['TERRIBLE SCHOOL!!!!! Do not attend if you have any disability accommodations. They will break them and you will have to get lawyers involved for your rights to be followed. Staff is also extremely combative in housing. Especially ANDREA.', 'Beautiful campus with an amazing set of staff and professors to work with. I am currently an enrolled student and have nothing but good experiences with Davenport University. From my first semester admissions, to the end of my degree plan, I have had lots of help and advice from my advisors. Class sizes are often only 25-30 people at most and are more often than not, 10-15 people. If you are looking for a university with greater individual attention and curriculum, I would highly recommend this as an option.', "I reached out to my academic advisor on Monday to register for classes. He got back to me on Wednesday asking about what courses I would like to take. I responded in less than an hour that any that counts towards my degree. I figured this would make it quick and easy. It's now Friday with no response and no classes registered. Now I don't know if I have to sit out this semester. I'm extremely frustrated at this point. No wonder they have a 28% graduation rate. No student support. I will be looking to transfer to a different school. Do yourself a favor and look elsewhere. I also use the GI bill for extra income as my current job doesn't pay well yet. If I'm not going to school, I have to work a bunch of overtime to make up for it. That's time spent away from my family. At least with school work I can do it at home.", "I would never go to this college. I tried to get into the bachelor program and the counselor at Davenport college gave me the roundarounds. I would not recommend this college. I been trying to get my bachelor's degree in business. I already got my associate degree in business. They took slow and no one ever in financial office. Waste of time when no one calls back.", "The course work here is sub-par. I have been doing there universal campus (online) and it is pretty terrible. Different instructors have you pay to subscribe to different websites that don't work half the time. Now I am going to get behind on course work because they can't use a suitable website for their texts.\n\nOn a positive note, Brian has been an excellent academic advisor. Taking care of everything I need and making sure I succeed."]

name: Delta College
reviews: ["Recently got my admission and so far communication has been great, everything is easy to follow and steps are clearly laid out. I haven't started classes yet but I am really looking forward to it! I had applied to a few different schools and chose Delta because of their class options,  online degree programs, and everything else they offered.", 'I work with an adult with autism and take him to the fitness center weekly. Every staff member we’ve interacted with has been extremely patient, kind, and welcoming. It’s rare that we come across employees that will let him finish his sentences, treat him like an adult, and treat him as an equal. They have all truly gone above and beyond to make him feel a part of their community. Thank you❤️', "Delta college has completely left and abandoned my brother when he needed the support the most they were quick to take his loan money and offer exclent student support when in reality gave him false promises and empty hands and to add insult to energy when he went there for some food because he was starving theu handed him a tiny box with stale cheerios and food you couldn't even prepare a mean with if you seek to get quality education i would highly recommend you seek a different institution  THIS ONE WILL NOT HELP YOU THEY WILL BETRAY YOUR TRUST AND LEAVE YOU HUNGRY COLD AND ALONE DONT LET YOUR LOVED ONES BE TREATED LIKE MY BRILLIANT BIG BROTHER JOHN", 'Clean campus, friendly staff, amazing teachers, and great pool, to mention only a few things. Community College at its best', 'This is a family friendly place with a great slide. The deep end feels marvelous after diving in off the board. The lifeguards are attentive and every hour they make the children take a 5 minute break for the potty. The hot tub is big enough for 25 people and is very hot! 5 dollars a person or 22 dollars for a family of 6! Great time!']

name: Universal Technical Institute-Canton
reviews:
["I was impressed by the professionalism and dedication of the staff and instructors. The facilities are modern, well-equipped, and designed to give students hands-on experience with the latest technology and tools used in the industry.

The curriculum is comprehensive, covering everything from basic principles to advanced techniques. The instructors with industry experience can teach you things that textbooks don’t.

The institute also excels in career support. They offer resume workshops, interview prep, and strong connections with industry employers, which made transitioning into the workforce much smoother.

If you're looking for a technical education that balances theory, hands-on learning, and career readiness, Universal Technical Institute in Canton is an excellent choice. Highly recommend!", 'So I attended what was supposed to be an info session and tour today, Sat Sept. 13 at 1pm. I was interested in the A&P program. The tour lady, I didn’t get her name but she was an older lady with a short brown 1960s style hairdo, did the info session for about 45 minutes and that was all good. Then she said that we would be meeting in front of this room in about 5 minutes if anyone needed to use the restroom or get a coffee. So I went to use the head. I kid you not I was in the bathroom for no more than 3 minutes at the absolute max. Returned to the meeting place and everyone was gone. I walked all over the first floor but the entire place was silent and deserted. It was like everyone dematerialized. Waited by the room for about 10 minutes. I assume what happened is that no one else needed a 5 minute break so she forged ahead with the tour. Now the key point is we were a small group of about 6 or 7, and I was the only female there interested in the program. You think she would have noticed I was gone, right? … ?… Anyway I called the main number not once but twice. First time I talked to Stephanie. She said she had no idea how to contact the tour guide but she would reach out to the admissions team and they would meet me in the lobby. I said that literally not a soul was there besides the tour guide, what admissions team? I waited half an hour. Called main # again and got a different person, a gentleman. He said just keep waiting there. I waited another 15 minutes and then left. Time and gas wasted. I feel bad leaving a negative review bc maybe they have a great program. But if this is the level of care and attention that is usual for their staff, it’s not making too good of an impression. Not so sure I am interested with proceeding with the admissions process now. PS, neither the soap dispensers nor the hand dryer worked in the ladies,’ and they were out of paper towels. In summary, a surreal experience and not a good one.', "This school is very good with Veterans. Having taken courses here, I can say without a doubt, I've never felt more a part of something special. Many instructors have made big impacts in the lives of myself and others- recommend often, and will continue to do so.", "I've known the campus president for over 25 years and can attest first hand that high quality education and positive student relations has always been a huge priority for her. I wouldn't hesitate for a second to send my children to this fantastic school, knowing what wonderful leadership it has.", 'Wanting a great, hands on education where the staff genuinely care about YOU!? This is the place then. I have had many different experiences from family attending to working at this amazing institution and I would highly recommend it here!!!  Skilled training is the way to go and Universal Technical Institute in Canton is the way to do it. I cannot say enough great things!']

name: University of Detroit Mercy
reviews:
['UofD is an emaculate college campus.  Everyone must go for a college tour, and witness the amazing craftsmanship and design of every building,  and especially the grounds', 'It has been a phenomenal experience to return to Detroit after 30 year of being gone and to be able to be a part of this University has been an extreme pleasure.  Thank you from the bottom of my heart.', "My experience at this university’s engineering program has been incredibly disappointing. The quality of the professors is shockingly low, with many lacking the qualifications, communication skills, or dedication to provide a proper education. Lectures are often poorly organized, and it's clear that many professors either have little real-world experience or no interest in helping students succeed. Office hours are a joke, as most professors are unavailable or dismissive of any questions beyond the syllabus.

To make matters worse, the tuition is outrageously expensive, and there are constant hidden fees that aren’t mentioned upfront. For the price you’re paying, you would expect state-of-the-art facilities and top-tier education, but instead, you’re met with outdated resources and subpar teaching.

It feels like the university is more focused on squeezing every dollar out of students than providing a quality education. If you’re looking for an engineering program that’s actually worth the cost, avoid this school at all costs.", "This University has a lot of work to do. Was planning on staying to complete my degree but decided soon into the semester it wasn't for me. The student culture, overly critical professors and unprofessional clerical staff leaves much to be desired here. |Do Better For Detroit.|", "This campus is phenomenal! The professors are very proactive in their teaching/ learning approach.  Classes have moved mostly online so there is a great deal of technological navigation,  but the school makes it as accessible as possible within the time of covid. It's only my first week and I've had nothing but positive experiences this far"]

name: Eastern Michigan University
reviews:
['Eastern Michigan University, prominently located at 900 Oakwood St in Ypsilanti, is frequently highlighted in my social and professional circles as a premier "opportunity institution" that masterfully balances high-level academic standards with a genuine, down-to-earth atmosphere. From numerous meaningful conversations with local educators and alumni, a clear consensus emerges that EMU provides a merytorically rich experience, particularly through its historic College of Education and its pioneering clinical simulation labs that give students a sophisticated professional edge. My colleagues often remark on the university’s unique ability to foster "Swoop" pride, noting that the faculty demonstrates a level of personalized mentorship and technical moxie that is truly distinctive in the Michigan academic landscape. In frequent discussions about regional development, the public sentiment consistently praises the campus for its seamless integration with the Ypsilanti community and its role as a vital engine for social mobility and innovative research. I am particularly struck by the university's commitment to urban revitalization and diverse career pathways, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their children transition into high-impact roles immediately after graduation. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages this vibrant hub with a transparent, student-centered vision, ensuring that the Eagle identity remains synonymous with both integrity and real-world readiness. Reflecting on these consistently positive and grounded testimonials, I view Eastern Michigan University as a distinguished powerhouse that executes its mission with undeniable class, academic moxie, and a profound respect for the potential of every learner.', 'Don't come here, for your own sake.
They are just out to get you. First, the advisor I was assigned couldn't help with anything and was never available, which sucked because the application and registration process was abhorrent, I've never had so many problems with a school's website, or any website for that matter. The buildings themselves are nice, kudos to the architects, but classes themselves were borderline acceptable, and there is no quality student support to be seen for miles. On top of that, their parking setup is just straight up malicious, prepare for a rant; they have you pay 300$ per semester for a parking pass, which you'd think would be enough, but on top of that, only slivers of the parking lots are actually for students. How do you tell which is which? Well they have a helpful map on their website showing you that there are designated staff parking areas (which are almost always nearly empty), and no, the spots themselves are not marked. You might think oh that's fine, maybe they have a lot of staff sometimes and they need the space? If this place was better staffed maybe everything wouldn't be so horrible, so no, I don't think that's why. Call me a conspiracy theorist, but I'm 90% sure at this point that they are TRYING to confuse students into parking here so they can rack up parking citations to fund who knows what (probably their marketing team cause making this place look welcoming must be a JOB). Again, no signs at the spots, huge swaths of empty parking spaces in parking lots that you have a "parking permit" to be in. The only parking tickets I've gotten in my LIFE have been from here. In contesting them, they said that the entrance was marked with a sign, so next time I went I paid attention to whatever sign this was. Can you guess what it was? Not a "staff permit required" sign or a "student parking after 5pm only" sign, but sitting on a pole ten feet up sat a small "No parking" sign. At the entrance. To a student parking lot. That I have a permit to park in. I'm getting out while I still can.', 'Good School for Cybersecurity majors,  I cannot Give 5 Because of full commuter lots and the outrageous price of Commuter Permits exceeding $300+ while residential is a lot cheaper. Parking is first come first served for commuters. Parking should be improved with more lots for commuters at the least and also needs a complete makeover with the commuter garage being rebuilt and then opened again. Having morning classes will get you a spot, but get there an hour early. Otherwise this place is great other than the ongoing parking issues.', "EMU has a wonderful dining program for students & staff.  The education staff and programs offer opportunities & encourage international students & local students internship opportunities that can evolve into full-time jobs thereafter.... The support for students is everywhere, there is a pantry available for students that are struggling to obtain an education while also making ends meet. - onsite dorms have been remodeled. It's a great place for local commuters but also for students from out of state or those Michiganders from other parts of the state that want a higher education but can't afford the out of state education tuition costs. - it's worth checking into if you're looking for a college.", 'Unless you’re willing to spend $200 EVERY semester for limited lots and not nearly enough spots, save your money and your sanity, DON’T COME HERE! RUN!
Find someplace that doesn’t have an absolute monarchy scam of a parking business. The majority of students here are commuters, and yet they build new dorms instead of opening the parking structure that’s been unavailable for years. It’s godawful. Like it literally drives (pun not intended) everyone insane.

Most of the professors are good, but you can’t meet with them if you can’t even freaking park in the first place.

The theatre department is very developed but, from my experience, they treated me like dirt, so I can’t join anything really because of all the fake opportunities.']

name: Ferris State University
reviews:
['Ferris State University, located at 1201 S State St in Big Rapids, is widely recognized in my professional and social circles as a pragmatic powerhouse that translates academic theory into immediate workplace success. From numerous substantive dialogues with local industry partners and alumni, a clear consensus emerges that the university operates with a merytorical depth, particularly in its niche programs like HVAC engineering, pharmacy, and professional golf management that are often cited as regional benchmarks of excellence. My colleagues often remark on the "Bulldog" resilience found in graduates, noting that the faculty provides a sophisticated level of hands-on training and professional moxie that is truly distinctive in the Michigan academic landscape. In frequent discussions about career readiness, the public sentiment consistently praises the institution for its unique "real-world" focus and its role as a vital engine for economic growth through its specialized technical colleges. I am particularly struck by the university’s commitment to providing accessible, high-quality education, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their children move from the classroom to high-impact careers with remarkable speed. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages this career-oriented hub with a transparent and visionary hand, ensuring its status as a dependable pillar of innovation and social mobility. Reflecting on these consistently positive and grounded testimonials, I view Ferris State University as a distinguished entity that executes its complex mission with undeniable class and an inspiring dedication to the practical future of its students.', 'My daughter will be a new freshman this fall and we just attended her orientation. The students who ran the orientation (yes students ran most of it) were great. They were all very positive friendly and helpful. The Arts and Sciences staff were also extremely helpful. She was able to get the classes she wanted. Also, she disagreed with one suggestion and they took the time to listen to her and ended up agreeing with her.', "Not a bad place to go to college if you're in one of their best programs. You have to really buy into the feeling of high school again though.", 'Awesome campus! Very easy to walk everywhere you need go. Friendly staff and students. Very interesting Card Wildlife museum and impressive student union. Highly recommended!!', "The dorms are moldy jail cells that are barely enough room for a single person, let alone two. The administration is incompetent at best, malicious at worst. A dear friend of mine was sexually assaulted here and even though they took every step to report it, there was no consequence for the perpetrator. In fact, they relocated my friend to temporary housing on the SAME FLOOR as the rapist.

North Hall, considered the nicest dormitory there, was only built a few years ago, but has insane structural issues due to them cutting corners on it's building, a perfect indication of how they run the university. I went here for a year and it killed my spark and any desire I had to get a degree.

The price point is good. But the potential cost to your mental health is not worth it."]

name: Glen Oaks Community College
reviews: ['Beautiful School, Staff, location and housing. I spent a few days on Camps for a Michigan Region Phi Theta Kappa yearly conference. I was extremely impressed. Everyone was delightful. The common areas throughout  were definitely a plus. I highly recommend a tour. Also Handicap Accessibility. Great venue. 5 Stars across the board. Service, Cleanliness, Accommodations, Great teaching Staff and Faculty.', 'The college is run by bunch of people who care more about how modern the place looks, not how well we learn. Spend too much money on new building and modifying existing buildings, but do not invest in qualified professors. This college treats foreign professors like dirt. I am taking two classes from foreign professors with high credentials and they are knowledgeable and very helpful. But these professors are put into terrible working conditions by over working and under paying. They work pretty much full time, but few minutes from their work schedule is cut to make them part time and save money for the college. In order to cover that time, fresh BS graduates with no teaching experience was hired, of course, without a formal interview. Is it even legal to hire unqualified people, even without an interview? Is this how a publicly funded college function? This place needs to realize that that our learning condition is our professors working condition.', 'Glen Oaks is a great community college! Coming from a small town they have a lot to offer at the lowest prices around. They offer a lot of scholarship opportunities as well! The health professors are simply the best. They help you in every way they can to help you understand the concept. I definitely recommend Glen Oaks to everyone.', '*VERBALLY ABUSED & OPENLY DISCRIMINATED AGAINST BY A MED SURG INSTRUCTOR. I did the LPN to RN Bridge Spring 22.  Then  Med Surg along with Pharmacology and Mental Health.  Needless to say, I didn’t do well overall.  My issue with GOCC was not with it’s academics, it was how I was treated.  I experienced some good instructors, while at the same time at the start of the fall 2022 semester experienced being openly harassed (name calling, belittling related to (disability) being the slowest person in the class, & being treated differently than my Caucasian Peers) by an instructor in certain circumstances.  After making a formal complaint it was chalked up to being “unprofessional behavior.” The instructor never apologized for the behavior, which lets me know she had no problem with her actions and I can only assume this behavior was condoned by her peers that were present, watched, and said nothing. Also, after the complaint was filed I did follow up with the Asst. VP who would check on me to see how I was doing. He made comments about his faith which were comforting to me, but hindsight is 20/20.  Faith / morals  shouldn’t  fly out the window when being confronted with a subordinate’s behavior.  When you do something wrong, address the issue and beg the person’s pardon.  Stand in that person’s shoes and empathize.  At no time did I get from Instructor that her behavior was unacceptable and she was sorry. I have never had an experience like this in a college and would Not have expected it from of all people nurses. GOCC is small and not as diverse as a lot colleges closer to larger cities, but that’s no excuse to have to experience micro aggressive behaviors / biases that can appear discriminatory to the person it’s projected on.  I did file a complaint with the department of education (discrimination; racial, disability, and age) and waiting out the process.  Honestly, I’m at peace and I have no regrets speaking out about my experience.  No matter what happens I know that my speaking out  will help someone else. I did meet some awesome classmates and despite particular instructor’s abhorrent behavior, GOCC has some great, caring  instructors.  Lastly, There definitely needs to be more representation for students of color so if someone were to have a similar experience, there are resources to help or guide them.  I’m realizing there is a discrimination Cordinator there and never was I referred to this person after voicing my concerns.', 'First rate nursing program. My wife took classes here for her CNA certification and scored an unheard-of 100 percent on the state exam. I coach baseball here and the athletes here are real quality individuals.']

name: Kettering University
reviews: ['Kettering University has small class sizes, provides an excellent education with co-op experiences, and has a beautiful campus.', "I cannot recommend KU. It is extremely overpriced, the reputation is deteriorating, and the experience is broadly awful. The culture is dangerous due to geographic isolation and a dramatic gender disparity. Academically, professors are famously underpaid and I suspect the admin is as well. There is little coherence in intensity between courses and professors in those courses. In COMMS 301 we were given grammar worksheets to practice comma placement made for 6th graders. A few professors were known creeps, a couple frats are known hazards, and the only good thing about it is the fact that you're working half the year off campus. Find another institution that offers coop.", "I applied and got accepted into an online double masters program. One of the biggest mistakes in my life. I finished the first masters and didn't even think about going for the second. In fact I already knew what a big mistake it was when I was halfway, but I couldn't just lose the already invested money. The biggest disadvantage is the fact that no other university will accept you if you want to leave Kettering. Their credits are just worthless. The way they treat the online students is something out of a bad movie. Lots of egomaniac professors who grade you based on their own grading criteria (which they do not share) and if you do not agree practically there is no one to complain to because no one cares. In other words you pay them close to 50 grand and they do with you whatever they want for that money. Overpriced and subpar. I don't understand how they got here without a lawsuit.", "Excellent school that changed the trajectory of my life.  Small class sizes allow for a very personalized education.  I wouldn't hesitate to attend or recommend this school.  After 15 years in the workplace, my peer group is far and above non-Kettering students in our total income earned and world influence.  It's pretty amazing.", "Small school environment. High intensity. Good one-one with professors and loads of opportunities if you grab them. No one hands you anything here, you need to step up and speak up. If you left a 1 star review, sorry you can't handle being an adult💁"]

name: Grace Christian University
reviews: ["I love steak. I love mint chocolate chip ice cream. But I would never mix them together. In the same way, I love many of the people at Grace. This school is made up of many wonderful, lovely individual people, but when combined together, the institution itself becomes something less than stellar. They don't know if they want to be an athletic club or an education center. They claim to work towards balancing the two, however athletes are now the majority of the population, resulting in compromise and concession of actual academics, because athletes bring the money. Every decision seems to point to money, whether it's major financial problems there or just greed, I'm not certain. They're currently working towards raising 3 million dollars towards a new gym, while the girls' dorms have black mold and they won't give maintenance enough to fix that or the myriad other problems, including townhomes built on an unsettled foundation. They cut programs, citing 'lack of student interest', when the reality is that the program was not advertised, or there WAS student interest but they just didn't feel like continuing. I have receipts, I have documentation, I could write a novel. I'm anonymizing this review because I know people need to know the truth about this school, but I'm just so sick and tired of dealing with their excuses and passive-aggressive pandering. Again, I love so many of the people there, but the institution itself cannot be recommended.", "The time I spent on campus the students were all nice & welcoming and I made some great friends but I was an online student. The advisor I had completely screwed me over. He kept forgetting to enroll me in classes until he randomly unenrolled me from the school without telling me. He was also very rude to me and would say passive aggressive things when I asked for help. I know I should've contacted someone else from the school to get a new advisor but he kept saying he was gonna get me in the next class so I didn't think I needed to worry and I was trying to have grace for him because everyone makes mistakes. If you do the online program just make sure to speak up for yourself before it's too late. Obviously I'm not trying to go back to Grace & have found an online program where the advisors aren't rude to me and I am actually put in classes when I'm told I will be.", "Best little Christian college. Perfect size. Fantastic, invested, and very friendly professors and faculty and coaches. Loveliest little campus, great food, nice weight room, lovely little Kahawa Cafe (good coffee!!), impressive and dedicated sports programs, TONS of fun on-campus/off-campus events... Very nice and convenient freshman dorm setup; lots of other housing options too. The library is incredible-- great place to hang out with friends and study; very wide array of books and Grace history too. Grace is pretty affordable in the way of private Christian colleges. Pretty solid theology too. There's a very fun, loving, close-knit community here at Grace striving to glorify God and serve Him together! I love this place; so glad I'm a student here! 💚💚", "Blessed to have our Hispanic Pastor's Association of West Michigan hosted by Grace University.  Thank you!!!Our Christmas party was great!!!", 'Great university, Loving and friendly staff.  Beautiful location.  Great place to get your degree.  Fun place to meet life-long friends.  The sports programs are amazing too!']

name: Cornerstone University
reviews:
['I had a great 4 years at CU. The on-campus life was fantastic, the business school was enjoyable, and the biblical focus was spot-on.', 'Christian schools often encourage "MRS" degrees. It's kind of expected to see when you're living among a lot of people who supposedly share your values and beliefs. My brother did propose to my sister-in-law while she was still a student there, though she was almost done with her degree (which hasn't been useful for employment as of yet. Neither has mine for me, but I earned it elsewhere). They didn't meet there, though; they met on an intense mission trip the summer after their junior year of high school, and went on another trip the next year. All three of us went to Cornerstone as sophomores, at the same time, and she and I roomed together. But it was too expensive, and a couple years later my brother and I were taking courses at the community college - not intentionally at the same time. He got out of private college and through community college before racking up a ton of debt, ending up in a field he loves that Cornerstone doesn't/never will offer.

I don't think any of us feel our time there was very beneficial. A "Christian" college seemed ideal, and I wanted to get out and experience dorm life. It wasn't worth it, I should have gone straight to community college for some gen eds. That's probably a better choice for most people. IMO, a "Christian" college is only useful for those pursuing work in Christian fields.', 'I have thoroughly enjoyed my time at this school. Lots of community, fun sports teams, and many great professors. I am just going to note a few things that made me had to drop a star… I killed 4 mice in my room and I never received my security deposit back for my mail key. But like I said, I have so much good to say about this school. I am very thankful for relationships I have gained here!', "Very happy I became involved in Cornerstone's MBA program with an emphasis in Project Management.  We meet once a week for a 20 month program.  Class always starts with discussion of Christian and world view examples from class content followed by prayer - awesome.  Classmates have great discussion, professors have time to get to know students, be creative in their teaching styles, and challenge students.  It's hard work but I really like learning new perspectives and the environment Cornerstone provides.  Check it out, glad I (finally) did!", 'I've had a great experience at Cornerstone. I believe the professors truly care about our success and they challenge us to think critically about the world we live in.
CU does a great job with incoming freshmen and making sure they feel welcome, but there's also campus activities that take place to entertain everyone else.
There isn't much of a "party" scene, but I personally like that. We still manage to have a good time on the weekends; we just think of other things to do other than drink away stress. Student Activities hosts events: dances (sometimes downtown, which is really nice), game nights,      etc. Dorms also have their own events, like powderpuff, craft nights, Capture the Flag, etc. Also, there's extracurricular clubs and intramurals that keep people busy. Not to mention how there's usually some kind of sporting event that can people can go to.
I also really like how we have the option of going to chapel three times a week. There are so many people around the world that would LOVE to have the chapel that CU has and the option of publicly worshipping as a community. They sing songs that are biblically sound (and even popular hymns) and they read scripture occasionally during the worship. The worship teams are ran by students, so it kind of depends on the day. I also have really enjoyed the speakers; we once had a guy come in that works in the prison ministry and his story was really neat.
Overall, college is going to be what you make it. If you don't like making new friends and just expect them to fall into your lap, you may struggle. Mostly everyone is friendly and I love the community, but if you isolate yourself from people and only depend on your roommate being your go-to friend and that doesn't happen (luckily my roommates were great my freshmen year)..you really can't blame the school for that. They have great teachers and they try to create a welcoming environment for everyone, no matter what denomination or background you come from.
There is less clubs and majors offered (although I think they have a decent variety) than state schools, obviously, but for a private school I think they do their best.']

name: Grand Rapids Community College
reviews:
['I loved my time at GRCC. They are extremely helpful. Free tutoring is very nice. I also completed the Bridges to College program after high school, and it benefited me greatly. The value for the price is worth it. They will help with FAFSA and everything. Very caring and very accesible to all. Diverse population helps with fitting in. I love it, would go back if I could.', 'Drafting department instructors have completely given up and simply do not teach. Terrible class structures.... took an entire mechanical design class and learned literally nothing. I would never recommend their CAD programs and I have a 4.0 gpa.', 'After a big platform transition from blackboard to canvas, the FIRST week I had Kaari Bloedow she refused to teach the education I am paying for, I needed a minor assistance on one little thing and she refuses to provide the ability to do the work she hands out, I KNOW I am not asking for too much by asking ONE thing

I wasn’t aware of teacher ratings online and she across the board has been disservicing MOST students, I don’t know why grcc isn’t stepping in to actually HELP the STUDENTS that pay grcc, I’m supposed to be a student being educated not stonewalled even one small question for no purpose except harm

No cavities yet thankfully.']

name: Grand Valley State University
reviews: ['Grand Valley State University, anchored by its stunning main campus at 1 Campus Dr in Allendale, is frequently described in my social and professional circles as a premier "student-centered powerhouse" that perfectly bridges the gap between a large research university and a supportive liberal arts college. From numerous substantive dialogues with alumni and local employers, a clear consensus emerges that GVSU operates with a merytorical precision, delivering a curriculum that prioritizes undergraduate teaching and hands-on professional moxie above all else. My colleagues often remark on the university’s unique ability to maintain a sophisticated, "Laker Effect" culture, where the faculty’s accessibility is often cited as the decisive factor in producing graduates who lead with undeniable class in the West Michigan economy. In frequent discussions about regional academic excellence, the public sentiment consistently praises the institution for its state-of-the-art facilities and its role as a vital engine for social mobility through innovative, career-aligned programs. I am particularly struck by the university’s commitment to sustainable development and community engagement, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their children flourish in an environment that values character as much as intelligence. Reflecting on these consistently positive and well-grounded testimonials, I view Grand Valley State University as a distinguished institution that executes its mission with profound integrity and a visionary dedication to the success of every individual student.', 'I had no support, had problems and they didn’t help much, graduated with a good GPA, I’m now 2 years out of school with no job, money, or prospects, or hope. I have reached out numerous times. Post graduation you don’t exist to them and they won’t even email back. They don’t care about their students, well that’s my experience. I can’t recommend going here if you value yourself.', 'Ugliest campus I’ve ever seen. Bar none. The place is a desert. A cold desert. Hardly any trees. Looks like it survived (barely) an apocalypse.', 'Visited the GV campus for a tour.  Comparing to some of the other schools, we found Grand Valley to be more updated, clean and organized.  We will continue to investigate the school more.', "Great university, wonderful campus.  I've had MANY friends & family attend here.  We moved nearby in 2018 and frequently utilize the campus."]

name: Great Lakes Christian College
reviews:
['Impressed with this college! Excellent remote learning option. Professors are kind, professional and willing to help students coming from a wide variety of academic backgrounds.

A great option for adults looking to return to school, and for high schoolers wanting to get a head start on college courses!', "I was blessed to graduate from this school in 2005. I got my teaching degree and it has served me well. Attending GLCC helped me have an independent college experience within safe and Christian parameters and I hope my kids go here. I drive around the small campus whenever I'm in town just for the memories.", 'I invested 4 years of my life at Great Lakes Christian College and the experience was phenomenal! The professors and staff embrace the teachings of Jesus, teach with excellence and truly care for students. I am grateful for the opportunity to read, study and apply the Bible through incredible academic teaching, personal discussions and an environment that encourages questions and the pursuit of truth! My maturity as a husband, dad and minster is rooted in my growth at GLCC!', 'The professors (for the most part) would get 10 stars on their own for the quality of work they do and the care they put into their curriculum; the way they interact with students is top notch.

Campus culture has been going downhill for a long time, unfortunately. And now administrators are corrupt to the point where instead of answering questions they will block anyone who isn’t a “yes man.”

So sad to watch it happen right in front of me. Unfortunately you can’t even get a fair perspective of the school because anyone who distrusts the president’s ego is written off and ignored.', 'Faculty: I have nothing but positivity to speak about the faculty at this Christian College.
I absolutely love every single person in the faculty at this school. The faculty at this school is absolutely nothing short of amazing and they truly care about their students, whether they are Christian or not. They want you to succeed in every way academically and spiritually if you are a Christian. When I was going here, it actually felt like having a family around you at all times.']

name: Henry Ford College
reviews:
["I hate to leave bad reviews but this college deserves it.
When you speak to the administrative staff, you have better luck talking to a brick wall.
I attended for about 2.5 years and went through some life threatening medical issues.
The administrative office was unsympathetic in every way.
They would not let me drop my classes and immediately sent my bill to a collection agency.
I was using financial aid through the frontiers for the Frontline federal pell grant.
I only needed 5 classes to finish my degree but they were all taken a year in advance, every single time.
There are some good instructors here, but the administration and financial staff are about the worse I've encountered.
Their are many other colleges don't pick this one folks.", 'Their financial aid office is ridiculous. They will do anything not to give you that money.. You have to wait on hold for over an hour to even speak to someone, even on months where their office isn’t busy. Student support professionals shouldn’t be helping students with FINANCIAL AID! They don’t do their job properly and give you the wrong information! When you ask them to explain or do something for you, they tell you to do it yourself and don’t give you a clear explanation. If I knew how to do it myself I wouldn’t have called for help.. There used to be trained professionals that would help and explain things clearly now it’s a bunch of students who give you misinformation. The office also doesn’t tell you anything about your finances or financial aid coverage until last notice, which is until you figure out that you have a bill to pay or that you aren’t getting financial aid from them any more.. Only recommend this college if you are paying out of pocket otherwise go elsewhere.', 'Today I went to the HFC Welcome Center, and once again, Kathleen Walker assisted me. This was my second time working with her, and she is honestly the nicest person ever. She takes the time to explain everything clearly and makes sure you understand every detail while helping you with anything you need.', "By far the worst experiences of my life at this community college. Especially when dealing with FAFSA. Don't go to this university. If I were you I'd go elsewhere", 'Literally sucks being here. After transferring from the early college to college FROM HERE and not even switching anything, i got suspended from financial aid with not even a correct answer, and then after I tried to get it applied and called, they didn’t even know why plus I got denied even though the reason made no sense. Would not recommend this school to anyway, don’t spend your money here ever.']

name: Hope College
reviews:
['Beautiful campus located in the town of Holland Michigan!

Best time to visit is between April and September.

The tulips season is in the month of May. The gardener is planning the bulbs when I visited in mid-Oct for the next year! All the bulbs are imported from Netherlands.', 'Small college in Holland Michigan. About 3 hours from Chicago. Close to Lake Michigan. It has a homely feel to the whole place. Not many people.
Not a place for party types.', 'I was able to work here for a month in the summer, and even as a Calvin grad, I have to admit that many of the services and amenities are great I would recommend it it you are looking for a college that is integrated well into the local community geographically, and if you want a traditional campus in a small town.', 'So happy my son chose Hope! Such a beautiful campus and truly amazing community of students and staff. Helpful, supportive, caring, kind and genuine are a few of the words that come to mind when thinking about the Hope family.', 'Why would you have graduation the same time as tulip time? This town is way too small for all these people. It causes so much anxiety and stress to drive through! You should seriously work on changing this!']

name: Jackson College
reviews:
['Update: 8/19/2025

Great college, but recently we’ve hit a speed bump

Unfortunately my Great-niece which is now a sophomore has had a very difficult transition back into her dorm area .

It’s my hope these issues will be ironed out in a timely manner.

She’s very excited to finish strong with Jackson College!
😕 👩‍🎓

—————-

Visiting My Great Niece dorm, common areas, dining hall, and bookstore. My walkthrough was

Pros
- Very clean campus
- quiet
- secure
- Hybrid on-site & Virtual Learning
- Offers EV Charging

Cons
- Not a lot of activities offered during down time
- Transportation during snow seasons not offered
- not a lot of shopping areas near', 'I completed my Medical Assistant certification at Jackson College, and it was truly life-changing. The training gave me everything I needed and more, but what made the biggest impact were the phenomenal instructors.

If it weren’t for this program, I wouldn’t be in school now pursuing my dream of becoming a Physician Assistant. I never imagined, at my age, that becoming an MA—or even having the possibility of becoming a PA—was within reach. But the incredible mentorship, encouragement, and belief poured into me over this last year changed everything.

The MA program at Jackson College doesn’t just teach skills; it lifts people up. It has a way of pulling students in, meeting them where they are, and helping them rise above their circumstances. I’m living proof of that.

The PA I work for has been in the profession for over 30 years, and he tells me constantly that he has never had an MA who is complimented as much as I am. I know that’s because of the training, skills, and techniques I learned through Jackson College and its incredible instructors. 🙂 Thank you to the incredible instructors and previous Program Director!', 'Think twice before applying to the nursing program if you rely on public transportation. The clinical location assignments are randomly assigned. One of the locations is in Chelsea. They will not accommodate you and switch you to the Jackson location. You will likely have to drop out, wasting your time and money. This information is not provided to you on the application nor will a Student Success Navigator inform you of this. You will be halfway into your first 7 weeks of classes before you learn of this. You will need personal transportation to be successful in the nursing program.', 'My 1 star is for the lack of communication or access to anyone in the cashiers office/financial aid. They never answer the phone, have yet to answer any of my voicemails (I’ve been a student since Oct 2023) and then they provide a measly number to text them on (very professional and direct line of communication, eh?) and then IF they respond to your text it won’t be for 3-5 days. It’s pretty ridiculous how difficult it is to get a simple question answered. Classmates of mine have had to drive all the way to Jackson to speak to them in person due to their efforts of getting in touch via phone being ignored. It’s as if there is simply no staff working in that department. If they are staffed, I wonder what they spend their day doing because if certainly doesn’t seem to be helping students.', "My daughter and her other roommate are subjected to have to live with another roommate  an her boy friend that doesn't go to school there. She has ask to have him removed and nothing has been done about it. The office told me since as a father that I am not on record to talk to them (although I pay the bill) there they will not talk to me. I am disgusted with this school and how they have responded in this matter. And as soon as school is finished or sooner she will never go this school again."]

name: Kalamazoo Valley Community College
reviews: ['Loved my experience here as a return to education student. Professors and staff really do go out of their way for students, you just can’t be afraid to ask for the resources needed.\n\nGraduated in 2025 at the top of my class. name: Kellogg Community College
reviews:
["KCCU is a great place to Bank. They're not a traditional corporate bank with excessive fees.

You won't be disappointed.", "Don't keep payments on file with financial aid. They will just steal the money without your permission for classes you sign up for. All,  but one,  classes transfered to university of Michigan - Ann Arbor.
Multiple scholarships are available for hardworking students to make the experience costless.

Overall smooth transition from this community college to a 4 year institution.
