Affordable tuition, great community involvement and awesome on campus clubs to join! Great staff of counselors and advisors!! Im so thankful for my amazing professors! After 2 years I will move on to University, but I will always be a Bruin at heart']

name: Kirtland Community College
reviews:
['My 1st time going since it was built.  I thought it looked wonderful and beautiful! My son and I went for their event, E-sports. Plenty of vendors. Very nice environment.', 'Do not go here they are all about the money and let instructors harass you repeatedly. I filed a formal complaint about the instructor then dismissed from the Surgical Technologist program with no refund. Go to Delta! If I could give zero stars I would.', 'This is a "fake it til you make it" school for many degree paths.  They are more worried about building facilities (like dorms at a community college) rather than paying teachers and buying training aids for the supposed curriculum they offer.

If you are thinking about going to Kirtland for Medical or Art or maybe even Law Enforcement, you might be alright.  At least they seem to have their stuff together at least for those fields.

The buildings are very nice, as they should be for new buildings.  The staff for the most part is nice, although I did not have a single teacher that wasn't vocal about school policies they weren't on board with.  Which would only reaffirm my growing criticism for this school overall.

I was in a renewable energy class that had the entire class of 20+ standing around one machine (that had a foot print of maybe 2 & 1/2 feet by 4 feet) the entire semester.  Even the professor was visually upset multiple times throughout the class about the lack of equipment and training aids, many times calling it a joke.

I went to 95% of my classes, did 99% of my homework, and failed 95% of my exams but still got a Degree that says "cum laude" on it.  You tell me how that works because I barely passed Algebra.  Keep in mind that I graduated H.S. in 1998 so my expectation of education is completely different from younger generations.  Quite honestly I am not impressed with today's definition of education.  If I grew up today I wouldn't have had to work as hard to be an Honor Student from primary all the way through H.S..

I graduated with an Associates Degree almost a year ago (2023) and waited until now to do any type of review.  I was hoping that my anger of being ripped off would go down over the year but as I write this it only returns.

Be careful, yes I am mad and anger can be reflected in my words but I tried to be critical without being too bias from my experience.  If they had a few right people working in the right places there, the school could actually be amazing for all students and not just some of them.

I gave 2 stars and lower because they do have good people there and have plenty of potential they just need to harness it for the student over the school.', 'I went into the salon to have my sister in law Molly do a treatment and cut on my hair. I was very impressed by everything there. At one point a client had some issues and had to have an ambulance called, and every one there was very professional about it and handled it very quick. I also love my hair💗', "I do not recommend their online classes, you are literally paying money to teach yourself everything. Professors are there to give out assignments and grades, absolutely no teaching at all. One would think they would at the least record their class lectures as you're paying for the same thing as someone sitting in the class. Not everyone has an opportunity to attend a classroom setting when they're also working to take care of their family...."]

name: Lake Michigan College
reviews:
['The school itself is wonderful, I would have given 5 stars had my experiences with the bookstore not have been so bad, but because of my horrible experience with the bookstore; If you go here, try to find an alternative way to get books.', 'There's only 1 calc teacher in the entire college, he's very nice but I don't prefer his teaching style. Also, the coffee/hot chocolate machine on the lower floor in front of the library was out of everything, I clicked every button, but it just said, "Please select another item" as a college student coffee is my life force', "Lake Michigan College trail is a nice trail that can either start behind the athletic field or start behind the back of the Mendel Ctr. It takes you in the pines and oaks along a winding little path with small stream waterways and to a place that takes you away from the hustle and bustle of college life. Enjoy the cleared paths and if you get tired take a break on one of the wooden benches. It's a public trail, free parking, I think it is dog friendly, and nature friendly as we saw and heard many birds. Go out and explore and happy trails.", "Its the cheapest college in the area and you get what you paid for.

The staff in the financial aid, business and student advisory are some of the most incompetent people you will ever meet. Time and time again they ask for documents because they lose them every semester. Several times I had to straighten out financial issues after the geniuses had assured me it wouldn't be an issue, then the idiots deny it.

The housing director for the dorms is exceedingly callous and cold, if you have a personal issue with your housing or you want to leave early because a job - she wont care. Prepare to have an apathetic housing staff give you the run around, not mean what they say and then deny it if you bring it up, same with all the staff.

If I wasnt borderline homeless I would have never come here.

Ask any student the competency level of this barely functioning organization and you'll get the same answers.

The teachers are decent, every thing else is a big heap of stinking garbage that can care less about you, and their actions reciprocate that.

Enter at own risk.", 'The school is very up to date and clean. They also have a lunch area that serves hot food. Very compliant with COVID.

On behalf of a program, I was in the nursing program. I was always a straight A and B student until I applied here. The program is very fast paced to be only a ADN. They also try to cram in knowing basic nursing skills instead of requiring a CNA class. You will go through so much stress and agony. They recommend not working in which I did and relied on support. We did study groups also which they also recommended. They want you to teach yourself half of the material. The point system for the program is terrible. We were all passing barely until we got to the skills final which they select your two skills and you have to be perfect doing them or they will dock you so many points to the point you fail. You will do so much work, clinicals, check off of skills and get to the end to be nit picked over a simple skill. Also, if you have issues going on in life do not vent or disclose anything to them because I honestly think their judgment of you at the end effects your points during skills final. The skills final is a point final that they observe you do. No feedback or nothing. So you cannot defend your skills final until it’s to late and grades are submitted. If you have the money and patience go for it, but definitely not worth my mental health.']

name: Lake Superior State University
reviews: ["I went here during the 1960's when it was Michigan Tech and a number of ex Marines went there as well and they taught me about  fighting a war in a triple canopy jungle. You learned not to complain about anything and you stand by your buddies. The teaching straff were great !", 'Great university. Very small. Good student to faculty ratio. They have all of the student help that larger universities offer (tutors, health center, class study groups, counseling center, etc). Went all four of my years here.', "Definitely wouldn't recommend this place.  Unprofessional and ineffective professors seem to be the norm.  But, those unprofessional professors will scold you for being unprofessional yourself, because apparently trying to have any amount of fun in college (or just generally acting like a normal human being) is unprofessional.  Showing up 5-10 minutes late to every class they teach, complaining about how they don't have enough time to get through the lecture material, running class 15 minutes over the limit, setting up improper schedules then getting mad at students who have a scheduling conflict in reality but not in the registrar's system, and (on occasion) wearing seemingly the same clothes for a week straight, however, are all some of the wonderful and totally professional examples they set.", 'I do not recommend this college as a 4 year program.', 'My daughter is enrolled there through dual enrollment from her high school, and the college nor her high school know how to communicate with the family or the student in sufficient and efficient time frames before things begin for the students.   My only suggestion for other parents who have dual enrolled students at LSSU is to contact LSSU yourself if you have not heard anything and you know registration has begun.  This could save you the frustration we are having getting things straight.  The whole thing could have been avoided with communication from the time of registration began until now, but there was NONE!  At this point, due to miscommunications and some communication mess ups, I’m still not sure if our problem has been corrected?  I really wish I would have been on top of things when it came to this, but I had it in my mind the high school and LSSU knew what they were doing and would do what is best for the high school student who drives 45 miles one way...']

name: Lansing Community College
reviews: ['they announce themselves as a very good college that will help you succeed, "its free take advantage of it", "we will help you" , to high school kids. I never received this notice, and it wasn't enough time but they surely deleted my email and all the vital important documents I've used as a disabled veteran over the years.  Unbelievably irresponsible and unforgivable.", "Lower Columbia College doesn't have adults with. Degrees working there. The students try but when they don't know what their doing they arent very effective."]

name: Lawrence Technological University
reviews:
['I love this disc golf course! Just wish they had cement pads!', 'The "Technological" in Lawrence Technological University is a misnomer unless you probably only go for their bread and butter of engineering and architecture disciplines. Whatever reviews you see of it 10 years ago still applies today, and the facilities are anemic if you want to get work done. I've graduated within the last couple of years and the support I get during and after acquiring my degree makes me doubt that it was money well spent.

The best thing I've probably done for myself attending there was going to other universities on competitions or study meets without the support of LTU, and finding out that their faculties and student organizations are more proactive and accommodating in terms of research and collaboration. I was originally considering completing a Master's at LTU, but after collaborating with other students at out town competitions and learning about new technologies that is not even mentioned here, made me think twice even with the added Alum discount.

The only saving grace here is that the math department is better than Oakland's, and that there are a FEW amount of professors here that makes the LTU experience almost worth it. Although they have a new president, I anticipate that my review will still be valid 10 years from now, as their only prime employers seems to be focused on automotive and automotive related accessories.', 'A great school for graduate studies. I hear a lot of complaints from undergraduate students, especially about the way the teachers treat students. My experience was that there were some very condescending professors but, the majority of the professors and instructors were very approachable and knowledgeable. Classes were small. The teachers were also involved in the local businesses and taught what they were doing at workplace. I did my MSIS and a graduate certificate in Project Management. Everything I learned was immediately applicable. Unfortunately, we were still in a ressession when I graduated so there were no jobs. So, I had to keep my old job. But, I can still use the knowledge I gained there. I am planning to do my MBA there in near future. It is pricy but, I think the experience is worth it. The only downside was the library. A local community college has a better library. I had to use another university library to do my research. The cafeteria was great. Parking was free and parking spots were plenty. The campus was safe. There were times when I was on compus at 2 am trying to complete my assignment. The program was very demanding but, doable. They do not challenge you for the sake of challenging you. They challenge you based on what is expected from you. They take your success very seriously. I missed two classes because of the weather and lost 1 level grade in each class. The staff were very friendly and professional. The food and coffee were great. I really had a great experience and would do it again. But I would not do an undergrad there. For one, it is expensive and classes can be larger. I recommend their graduate programs. I was going to do a DBA but, they discontinued it unfortunately.', "Absolutely one of the worst universities to attend. First of all, they delete/hide negative Google reviews with any type of text in it. Don't believe me, sort by newest and you'll notice very few recent reviews.

I would avoid this university at all costs.

I was a student here for 5 years. A vast majority of the professors are great and I wish them the best. They truly try their hardest to make their students succeed. However, the administration on the other hand...

Since about 2016 the school has shifted it's priorities away from students and into athletics and focusing on money/profit. They've removed numerous academic scholarships to go towards sports scholarships. This isn't even a D3 school and yet they take pride in their athletics like it's U of M. Since these priorities have changed, there have been limited class options for non-athletics students, less & less facilities for non-athletic students to use, and more.

Last year (2022), they notified all alumni that you can no longer store data or access some basic Google services (like Sheets, Docs, and more). Before I attended LTU, this was a service I was looking forward to. Being able to keep all my schoolwork, projects, and more on the cloud and I don't have to pay for it? Now, this is a Google policy at the end of the day - not an LTU policy. But the fact that no back-up plan provided by LTU for alumni to continue to use is what is extremely disrespectful.", "LTU is a great school. A bit pricy, but if you put the time in, most of the program will help you get to where you want to go. It is not a diploma mill, but I've seen students that should not have been admitted. It makes you wonder if the high tuition opens more doors than it should. Only wish the cost was lower, but you do get real teachers from real world jobs, and some of them are brilliant scholars besides being just instructors. Overall, I'd rate the school very high. better than Wayne State, Oakland, and comparable to U of M and Michigan State.
No, it is not MIT or Cal Tech, but it is close to Michigan Tech. The availability of classes is better than 95% of universities out there."]

name: Macomb Community College
reviews: ['Amy Babcock is an absolute gem! 🌟 She’s always super helpful, kind, and patient, and she makes navigating Records & Registration so much easier. Her positive attitude and friendly personality make even the most confusing processes feel manageable. Honestly, she makes admin stuff almost fun—who knew that was possible?! I really appreciate all her support and would recommend her to anyone in a heartbeat.', 'This school played with my time for over 2 months, I registered November 30th 2025 and never got past the application process to register for classes. Finally, with 4 days left to register this month, the information input into the system is wrong.\n\nPut on hold and transferred through multiple incompetent employees to only find myself back to square one, is this place even real?', 'Always smart people around campus', "I have absolutely no idea how this college is so highly rated on Google.  When I went here, I found that many of the professors maintained an adversarial attitude towards educating their students.  It wasn't like this for all teachers (Dr. Flemming is, was, and will always remain my favorite all-time professor) but it was quite obvious that the adjunct faculty was doing it for the side money while their methods of teaching were archaic at best.  Further, when I began transitioning into my career, most professors were indifferent to the fact that I was having to balance work and school together.  I didn't succeed thanks to Macomb, I succeeded in spite of Macomb, and I would recommend people to either go to a different community college or simply start their academic careers at either Wayne State or Oakland University instead.", 'Can’t afford heat with the thousands for tuition apparently, it’s 50° or cooler in here every day of the week during the winter no matter the classroom in m building']

name: Madonna University
reviews:
['One of the biggest regrets in my life was wasting my time and money on their nursing program. I attended this nursing program with high hopes, but my experience was extremely disappointing. Students were not treated equally, in my experience. I do not recommend this nursing program. Policies seemed to be applied inconsistently, which, in my experience, directly affected grades and progression. Communication from administration often felt dismissive, and there seemed to be little accountability when concerns were raised. Overall, the program felt more focused on money than supporting students, and the environment was stressful and unfair from my perspective. Prospective students should be aware of these issues before enrolling.

Also, I personally found that Professor Patterson created a challenging learning environment. In my experience, he sometimes seemed to show favoritism and could be sarcastic or dismissive in front of others. This behavior affected student performance and well-being, making an already challenging program more stressful. Students deserve fairness, accountability, and support, which I often felt were lacking.

Do not rely solely on the advertised 16-month timeline without fully understanding how the program operates. While it may be marketed as 16 months, in my experience, many students including myself experienced delays due to failed validations or very narrow grading margins. When large portions of a class were unsuccessful at the same checkpoints, it made it difficult for me to believe this was simply about individual performance. Also the traditional nursing program is not any better. The result was that some students fell behind, repeated courses, paid additional tuition, and, in some cases, left the program without the outcome they expected.

Prospective students should ask detailed questions about progression rates and speak to former students. Do your research.', 'The beautiful, and well kept grounds of Madonna University. The fall colors are starting to appear and it was gorgeous weather for football!', 'Best experience! Here for BS (double major in Math and Spanish, College of Arts and Humanities), MBA (School of Business, accredited), and now as an employee (College of Nursing and Health, accredited). The profs really care about you. Excellent community, I even started an on campus volleyball league! Writing Center is extremely helpful. Would recommend to all.', 'The organization and administration of this place is awful. Tuition is a mess, outrageous amounts, and the financial aid department is a nightmare. Improvement needs to be made, transparency needs to be added.', "A great tour! We would love to thank the staff and students for being so friendly during our first college tour experience. This was a great way to begin our daughter's college search, and Madonna will be marked number one on her list. Keep up the great work keeping Madonna University a great place to be.

Lillian and Parents"]

name: Rochester University
reviews: ['The University of Rochester is one of the most beautiful, uniform, and well-maintained campuses I’ve visited. Every building — from the iconic Rush Rhees Library with its stately dome to the modern Wegmans Hall — is thoughtfully designed, blending classical architecture with contemporary function.\n\nThe campus layout feels intentional and cohesive, with red-brick facades and mature greenery lending both historical character and harmony. It’s the kind of place where every corner feels picture-perfect. The walkways are clean and inviting, framed by shady trees and trimmed hedges. Even statues like George Eastman’s are tastefully placed, adding personality without clutter.', 'We had a brief visit from outside and looks like a great university with a lot of research related activities. There are many historical buildings. Rates high and a great university to attend. Neighborhood is very nice too.', 'Quality educational institution with a not looking campus when the weather is nice. Solid sports facilities and school spirit.', "I went to Eastman Dental Emergency & had a molar pulled out. It was absolutely painless and quick. Also I didn't have to wait at all. Sometimes you get lucky and today was my lucky day 👍👍", "Feels clean, and safe. Especially at late hours because I delivered food here. Great school.  For example the security is on top of things. There's no one roaming the campus that doesn't go there during late hours."]

name: University of Michigan-Ann Arbor
reviews:
['My daughter, entered this school, has found a new direction and dream in her life. I feel so grateful to see her once passive personality transform into a more proactive one, and to see her constantly taking on challenges. She enjoys spending time with good friends and is passionate about her studies.
My daughter often tells me
" i'm so happy "she is attending
this school.

I couldn't have asked for a better place to call home—both academically and personally. The student vibes and sense of camaraderie made the experience truly unforgettable."]

name: Michigan State University
reviews:
["The botanical gardens at MSU are definitely a great place to visit with the family, kids included! Hundreds of plant varieties and lots of knowledgeable staff. The elementary school program my kids and I have been attending is awesome. It has been super fun for all ages, and very educational. Our lettuce is growing well and We all can't wait until our next visit!", "Campus is waking up from a winter's sleep. Beautiful campus. Lots of great memories here. Picked up a Master's degree and my Ph.D. I met my wife to be here. Our 2 sons earned 3 degrees from MSU. Great people and a fantastic campus!", 'All photos are taken and distributed by Be Photographed.

Michigan State University’s campus is always a beautiful place to photograph, especially in the spring. The area near the vet school is filled with stunning apple blossoms, fresh mulch, and colorful flowers that make every shot come to life. Across from the Spartan Statue, the tulips are always a standout, and the entire campus is impressively well maintained and litter free.

During graduation season, the long line for photos at the statue moves smoothly — every student is patient and respectful, which makes the experience even better. MSU truly shines this time of year, both in spirit and scenery.', 'I like their research. They provide great education. I am glad I could finally go to my school of choice for a year and a half.

They have wonderful regional and supportive farming. I wish their farming skill and knowledge was physically in Northeast, Florida to help with looking into if soil quality can be increased and specifically if more variety and better produce could be made in overlap with University of Florida partially perceived zone eight. What are lasting conditions?

There are also some good, old beef cattle in Monticello, Florida I wish the very best life. I wish they could check on them.

Could they help keep up and support the culturally unique, colorfully beautiful Hawaiian produce like the pineapples and especially sugar cane to support the famous Dole plantation to help create heartier plants? Would they start by partially looking at the soil and creating long term sub-sequential support routine and process? Who could help with some Hawaiian food quality like their shrimp and salmon? How could they easily only pull the most quality and then easily keep them fresh? I wish for easy and clearly clean process and environment.

I am so very thankful for what they take care of and help produce.
🏫 🔍 🐄 🍍 🍃 🍤 🍣 ✨🤗 🌺

📚✂️✏️📖🖍️📎', "I have sporadically over the last few years reached out to multiple admissions and academic counselors to ask questions, and the best I've gotten is an automatic reply with a canned response and then nothing. MSU has so many students because of degree inflation that they don't have to care about their jobs, and they clearly know it. How you do one thing is how you do everything, so if this is the experience just trying to talk to someone, how do you think the education is?"]

name: Michigan Technological University
reviews:
['Great university for engineering especially mechanical engineering. Faculty help students and there is a clear focus on helping students learn and grow.

The graduate certificates in engineering are excellent, and I have enjoyed my experience with the aerodynamics certificate. Attending Michigan Tech has helped me with my career and I recommend it.', '★★★★★ Outstanding Experience with Russell Stein, Staff Engineer w/ MTU’s MSE Department

(100)"]

name: University of Michigan-Dearborn
reviews:
['The University of Michigan-Dearborn, anchored on the historic grounds of 4901 Evergreen Rd, is widely regarded in my local and professional networks as a formidable catalyst for regional innovation and personal growth. Based on substantive dialogues with various alumni and industry partners, a clear consensus emerges that the institution operates with a merytorical depth, effectively distilling the prestige of the Michigan brand into a focused, practice-based curriculum. My acquaintances often highlight the university's exceptional ability to cultivate professional moxie, noting that the faculty’s integration of real-world challenges directly into the classroom provides a sophisticated edge in the competitive job market. In frequent discussions about the Detroit metropolitan academic landscape, the public sentiment consistently praises the campus for its robust engineering and business programs, which many describe as a gold standard for social mobility. I am particularly struck by the university’s commitment to inclusive excellence and community partnership, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their loved ones transition seamlessly into leadership roles within global organizations. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages this "metropolitan university" with a transparent and visionary hand, ensuring it remains a dependable pillar of integrity and intellectual advancement. Reflecting on these consistently positive and well-grounded testimonials, I view UM-Dearborn as a distinguished institution that executes its complex mandate with undeniable class and an inspiring dedication to the future of its diverse student body.', "I thought my education (CASL based) was of good quality, and most of my professors were excellent. However, 9+ years later, I find it extremely disappointing that in spite of a great C.V. and letters of recommendation from faculty, over the years UMD consistently refuses to grant me an interview for even temp/part-time adminstrative positions.

Meanwhile, I have climbed the corporate ladder. I can easily find other full-time corporate work, but with starting a family, I'd prefer something closer and part-time.

I wish I knew the university doesn't value its own graduates as a freshman. Maybe this will help someone undecided regarding where to apply/attend.", 'I have studied in 3 universities and this by far my favorite one! The campus , the activities they do in the campus for the students , GISO, inclusion , and how they listen and care for the students and help them !', "It's -19F right now with windchill. My car won't start, but I have to find a way in because they won't close. Other schools, including the one next door, closed for their students safety.

I'm editing to add months later: this school never told my loan servicer that I'm still in school. I'm now being asked to pay hundreds of dollars by my loan servicer because of this!", 'The campus is a nice and clean environment, friendly colleagues, and helpful professors. The library is a good place to study, quiet and neat. As an Alumni to the university myself, I strongly encourage students to attend, as it offers multiple degree programs that cater to diverse interests. U of M is definitely a place that sets you up for success, number one choice, go blue!']

name: University of Michigan-Flint
reviews: ['The University of Michigan-Flint, centered at 303 E Kearsley St, is frequently discussed in my professional and civic circles as a resilient powerhouse of urban education that brings the prestige of a world-class degree directly into the heart of the community. From numerous substantive dialogues with local professionals and alumni, a clear consensus emerges that the campus operates with a merytorical precision, especially within its high-demand nursing, physical therapy, and management programs. My acquaintances often remark on the university’s unique ability to offer a personalized, "small-school" experience while maintaining the elite academic moxie associated with the UM brand. In frequent conversations about the regional economic landscape, the public sentiment consistently praises the institution for its role as a vital engine for social mobility and its commitment to the revitalization of downtown Flint. I am particularly struck by the faculty\'s dedication to community-engaged research, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their children benefit from hands-on clinical and business internships. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages the campus with a transparent and visionary hand, ensuring it remains a dependable pillar of innovation and academic integrity. Reflecting on these consistently positive and grounded testimonials, I view UM-Flint as a distinguished entity that executes its mission with undeniable class and an inspiring dedication to the future of its students and the region.', 'As a student, I enjoyed the relatively small campus size. This made the majority of my classes within walking distance of each other. Depending on the courses, class sizes can range from twenty students in a class room to seventy students in a lecture hall. I highly value my education from this university.', 'I have been going here since Fall of 2014, and my experience has been good so far. They have a good selection of programs to choose from. My academic advisers have helped me stay on track with completing courses that align with my program. I do like that I have to meet with an academic adviser before registering for classes for each semester I attend. It helps me remain mindful of my program responsibilities. Class sizes are desirable; they have not been too big, as teachers are usually able to meet with students one-on-one for in-class help. Teachers usually care to make students feel like an important part of class. There are a lot of campus organizations and activities to be involved in, so students are bound to find something interesting to join. The campus works to ensure that students have a culturally inclusive and safe experience with them. On the other hand, I sort of feel like the campus partially lacks a strong community-focused presence. Maybe this is because it is a commuter school.', 'The faculty and student safety are all very kind, friendly and willing to help. I feel good knowing how much support my son will receive while attending. Go Blue!', "School of Management -\nGreat instructors, small class sizes  (average:18-30).  The instructors care about their student's success, and regularly make themselves available for students needs.  Also, very non-traditional, as most students are the University work full time, have families, and other priorities.  Great college."]

name: Mid Michigan College
reviews: ["Mountain biking. A really nice trail system. Well marked. Generally easy with some sandy areas. This system has an outside loop with many ancillary loops. Very well kept. There is a changing area and restroom at the red loop trail head. This is around the left side of the building and is not easily seen or found if you don't know it's there.", 'By far the worst instructors, Dean, and curriculum I have ever dealt with. They don’t care about their students just the grant money they get from students. Bought a book for 200 good luck selling it back if you do you’ll get 5 bucks for it. Biggest racket I have ever seen. Instructors don’t even have teaching certification. Their not held accountable. They base grades on their feelings about their students not on the students actually work. If I had a chance to do it all over again I would avoid this school like the plague.', 'Absolutely one of the worst schools you can go to. Very socialist and liberal ideological agendas.  After the death of my grandma, I was told i can’t make up my attendance grade for the classes i missed because she “isn’t immediate family”. The teachers are not real professors and have no certificates. They tell everyone to “wear masks!” But their whole administration office doesn’t. Rules for Thee for not for Me. absolutely a terrible school. NEVER GO HERE', 'Worst school ever. Online classes are supposed to help those that cannot complete in-class requirements so what do they do? Require even harder requirements for classes. They state that they are family and children friendly and that the classes are self paced online, but it is far from true. Spent nearly 4 years spending money on this college for a degree that shouldve only taken 2 years. Good luck yall, Ill have my degree through UofPH.', 'We went on a 3.5 mi walk on their beautiful hiking trails']

name: Monroe County Community College
reviews: ['Very poor experience here.  I have taken many other online courses. I enrolled at mccc  for an English course online, I received the most confusing syllabus and we were to have no online classes or pre recorded lectures. By the time I realized what I had paid for was trash , I only qualified for 1/2 refund for a dropped course.  I was willing to accept that refund and the school said I would get it . After 1 month I still do not have a refund .. buyer beware unacceptable !!\n\nOnce you pay your tuition Alex from admissions will not return your emails or calls.  I am waiting for a call back from the campus Dean.  The overall attitude of those at this campus is that they do not care about the students.', 'This is fine college of higher learning.  They care about their students and stay at the lead in science.', "Don't expect a good education from here. The staff here is absolutely useless. I took one class last winter(2023) and was told the last time I was physically in the office registering, picking classes and talking to financial aid that everything was going to be covered by financial aid and that I had $600 to spend in the book store. When I bought my books it was just over $300. Then I get a bill in the mail about a month ago in 2024 saying I owe them about $120. When I called them the first time in January 2024 I had to leave a message and they never called me back. Weeks later I call again and am told that I owe them for my books. That the pell grant covered the tuition and fees but there was not enough left for the books. But when I bought my books I was never even given an option to put a credit card in to pay for anything. Now they're telling me that the Michigan reconnect only covers tuition and fees and that's why I owe for the books. When I asked why I was not told any of this when I was in the office speaking with them before the class in 2023 I was told it's because they are understaffed and everyone that year was new. Seriously?!? So basically I have a bill unexpectedly because they're understaffed and nobody knows what they're doing? I asked the financial aid office this she said yes basically. Absolutely useless. Why was I told everything would be covered and that I had $600 in the bookstore? And now I'm being told that was a lie and their excuse is that they don't know what they're doing and apparently do not train their new staff.", 'My husband and I went to get our Covid vaccine. All of the Workers and Medical personal were all very polite and helpful. It was very organized and went smoothly. They are doing a great job. Thank you for your Service to your community.', "Health Dept was organized for vaccines but workers were not patience with older people. They were very short with me when i asked again about paperwork or couldn't see small print. They are dealing with 65-100 year olds. Be nice please. Do your job!"]

name: Montcalm Community College
reviews: ["Don't go here. They withhold scholarships if you get loans, test to the point that whole cohorts fail, then upper management will stand by them. Don't waste your money.", "MCC has been nothing but wonderful. The building is always exceptionally clean, staff is always friendly, and it's a nice campus!", "It's a great challenging course.  A long course compared to other courses in the area. Signage needs updates but bring your A game . I enjoyed the challenge and can't imagine how tough this will play in spring and summer.  I will definitely make time to play in the summer.  Had a lot of fun today and that's not easy with this crowd.lol", 'New student housing is looking amazing!', 'Save your money and go to a real school. Poor instruction and almost no guidance from instructors. Very unprofessional conduct in classroom. Instructors were more interested in flirting with each other than teaching. Go anywhere else']

name: Muskegon Community College
reviews: ['Everyone here is extremely rude and unhelpful you will be your own advisor and much more. If I could give zero stars a would. Do not recommend attending here.', 'We went to the planetarium with our son for one of the Tues/Thurs free shows and it was wonderful! What a great benefit for the community. Parking lot was well lit, buildings were very clean and well kept.', 'This is where I go to school, it’s a good place, great professors, nice fitness center', "ALL THEY CARE ABOUT IS MONEY.  THEY WILL STEAL YOUR TUITION MONEY!!!! SOME OF THEIR CLASSES ARE SO BASIC, THEY ARE QUITE RIDICULOUS!  TUITION KEEPS GOING UP, BUT CLASSES ARE LACKING.  THEY DON'T CARE ABOUT THE STUDENTS AT ALL!  I WILL BE DROPPING IN THE FALL AND FINDING A BETTER SCHOOL.", 'MCC is a wonderful community college that provides excellent facilities, educators, and amenities. If you are looking for a quality college education without going into massive debt check out MCC.']

name: North Central Michigan College
reviews: ['This college is beyond unprofessional. I’ve been locked out of my account multiple times and IT averages about four weeks to contact you to fix the problem. The semester starts tomorrow and now I can’t get books, view my schedule, I don’t know when or where my class is. Literally no one answers the phone or checks emails except Kathleen (she’s great). I just transferred here and I am extremely disappointed so far. This college has been a terrible experience and no longer feeling confident that I chose the right school.', 'Horrible experience. Go back 3 years, I try to attain a business degree, they send me my class materials a week into the class. I can’t manage to get caught up and drop the class. Fast forward, I’m interested in pursuing HVAC. I apply. Denied because I owe them $1,200. $1,200 for a class I couldn’t complete due to their inability to get materials to me in time? No thank you. Never recommending this place! 0 stars.', 'I know nothing about this college for its educational merits but they have a nice quad area with statues.', 'This will be my first semester at North Central. All of the staff that I have encountered each time I visit are welcoming, helpful and supportive. The student employees have been just as helpful and welcoming. So far my experience has been more than expectations', 'The people working for this college have been wonderful to me. I am returning to school as a non-traditional student, and they have helped every step of the way. Thanks NCMC for all you have done and continue to do!']

name: Northern Michigan University
reviews: ["I applied for a graduate program at NMU and never heard a decision from them. I emailed to ask what happened: they apologized and put my application back in the pool for the following term. They somehow misplaced it or forgot about it again. Between the first application and second application I fell homeless due to some bureaucratic rigmarole. So I emailed and said: forget it. Please just withdraw my application. But can you refund the application fee? I am homeless. They lied and said they would and I spent the next three months checking at the post office every day. I recommend not working with these folks. They don't seem to care at all.", 'Took our Daughter back to NMU for the start of her Sophomore year. Beautiful campus, great Faculty and Staff, all set in a UP wonderland.', 'Graduated from NMU in ‘08 and it was one of the most impactful and wonderful experiences in my life. The area is breathtaking and the size was just right between knowing lots of people and always meeting someone new. Would be very happy if my kids went here.', 'Beautiful campus with a bonus backyard view! Great friendly community.', 'I got my bachelors of science at Northern Michigan University and my advice for any young  person considering going to school at NMU is go somewhere else because the only successful people I know of who went to that school and got their degree from there are former students who landed jobs with the university after graduation. Go to a more reputable school whose name is more widely recognized.']

name: Northwestern Michigan College
reviews:
['College campus is beautiful, sure. People are friendly enough. My only issue with the school is the lack of communication. The lies of "oh I did send you this email" and they never sent me an email to begin with. Or, I ask for information over and over and I never receive a response back. It's very frustrating. You can't be a school that only gets good stars from how 'clean' the college is.
Instructors let bullying happen to students from teachers, other instructors send the rudest email.
The experience has been a real struggle. You can't get any communicating done in this place and I can't wait to be graduated.', 'I am only giving it 3 stars because I am sure outside my experience of problems it is a nice establishment. However, for me they make becoming an registered nurse so insufferably difficult that if it wasn't for NMC... I know for a fact I would've been not only a RN by now but doing so for a many years by this point, having a great paying job and better living because of that too along with doing what I like (medical). But nope. That is not the case. All because of NMC and it's dumb "point" sheet stuff. Utterly discouraging. As if we didn't already need nurses and medical professionals badly enough... Then we have NMC making that much more difficult than need be just to have a "chance" to get into a medical class. Absolutely egregious. That aside, I will say the rest of the place seems decent enough though. As my gal was taking a few classes there and I would go with her and keep her company and then chill in the library or be on my laptop outside of her class and so as it pertains to the actual establishment it's nice, clean, and looks fresh. The classes seem to be pretty decent too from what I had observed. Hence why I am giving it a 3. If I was to base it off my experience alone I'd give it a 1. 0 if I could. Because of how badly NMC screwed me over. As such, if I lived in a bigger and better city this wouldn't even be an issue since their colleges are superior and don't proactively hold back people from the careers they want to get into such as nursing and so on.', "WARNING--DO NOT LIVE ON CAMPUS. No A/C, No refrigerators and if your room is missing something good luck getting a replacement.. You're basically living in a sweat box for months on end. The staff is extremely up tight and obviously have never been anywhere but Traverse City and who hate their lives and have nothing else better to do than to kick people who aren't from the area out. A student was just kicked out of the dorms for a leaky Capri Sun juice pouch that was left unattended in the dorm hallway. Apparently this student will be facing carpet damage repair fees along with not receiving a reimbursement of nights that weren't spent there. Everything you do is on camera, this place is like big brother. You can only enter and exit one way in the dorms so they can watch you every time. Don't plan on driving around the campus at night unless you want to get pulled over by a rent-a-cop and get the 3rd degree on whether or not you live in the facilities no matter how many times you show a room key and ID. After all the harassment from the staff/ security and sleepless sweaty nights spent here I honestly cannot recommend these facilities to anyone looking to get a nice nights sleep, even if you are only staying for a weekend summer course, it's not worth it. Not to mention its $750 per month-- this again is no A/C, no fridge, no kitchen, its just your desk, bed and your sweat. For around $600 a month you can live in an apartment, get much better accommodations and have the comforts of sleeping at night with A/C.", 'Medical accommodations are horrific to obtain here. I moved on to a different school, U of M Flint where I was treated with respect and dignity. Unlike the person I felt with here.

In fact, I didn’t have any problems at U of M with staff or medical issues. The Veteran rep was great, but being a vet was a negative when dealing with accommodations.', 'Great school. Campus is beautiful and safe, easy to navigate']

name: Northwood University
reviews:
['I entered Northwood with genuine enthusiasm. The student body is exceptional, and classroom discussions are strongest when students are fully engaged. That aspect of the experience has been a highlight and speaks highly of my peers.

Unfortunately, my overall experience has been undermined by what I perceive as a lack of consistency, care, and follow-through among certain faculty and staff, particularly in relation to the values associated with The Northwood Idea. I raised multiple concerns through appropriate channels, including during the previous semester regarding the course Philosophy of American Enterprise. Despite escalating these concerns, including communicating with senior leadership, they were not meaningfully addressed.

Over time, it became clear that the process was less about resolving issues and more about discouraging further inquiry. That realization was disappointing, especially given my academic performance and commitment. I currently maintain a 3.9125 GPA, and I take my coursework seriously. I expected that same level of professionalism and accountability in return.

I am grateful for the relationships I formed with fellow students and for the guidance of a small number of faculty members who demonstrated genuine engagement and care. However, based on my experience, I do not intend to pursue graduate studies here. While I value what I gained from my peers, the overall experience has fallen well short of my expectations.', 'Very unorganized and radical. They write their own text on philosophy that represents only a specific demographic as moral beings and still reference humans as man. The book I read in my Fall 2025 semester was for class, Philosophy of American Enterprise, and was written in 2014... American Enterprise has significantly shifted since Covid, an unaddressed elephant in the room for us students feeling grossly ripped off. Due dates didn't match my syllabus and resources for major assignments were "forgotten" about until 4 days prior, I could go on 🤦‍♀️', 'When here for a total of four months, was non stop bullied for not being a part of the clique group. Had kids banging on my door at 3 am and when I told security they had me file a report and then proceeded to do absolutly nothing. Classes sucked. They market very well to new and excited students and then rip the fun in learning out of it. But yet still expect that almost a half a millions dollars is exceptable for this level of education. STAY AWAY', "Grad student -- you will have to fight every step of the way to make sure your education and information is correct. Was overcharged for tuition, tried to bring it up with my advisor for weeks and was repeatedly assured my total was correct despite numbers not matching their website tuition. Reached out to their accounting department to confirm and they found that I had been overcharged by over 10% of my tuition for the semester. Took multiple follow-ups to be refunded. Grade book had strange results that did not match my classwork -- when I reached out again, advising told me there was nothing they could do and that I cannot access old classes or view my grades despite paying for them.

Seems that they are much more interested in your money than your education. Wouldn't recommend.", "From my first day of visiting campus, all the way to graduating with my Bachelor's. Northwood treated me like more than just a number. They are the best college I've attended. And the Veteran services are top notch. Now pursing my Masters degree . Thank you Northwood!"]

name: Oakland Community College
reviews: ['THIS school is TERRIBLE , first you could never contact a counselor without an appointment then only come once the week for walk ins. Yall finally change it and Sheila is on the phone being rude saying she can’t help me with anything and that they are closed at 4:20pm when they close at 5. Don’t get my started on the FASFA ladies that’s a different story. I can’t even call the school because the system won’t let you get through. I’m trying to contact the lady who I JUST spoke to, to get out of my RECORDS so I can REGISTER FOR MY CLASS I don’t have all day for her to click a “X” that’s ridiculous!!! I’m not done either yall will hear about my story at this school. The DEAN, THE COUNSELORS and “PROFESSORS” and FASFA.', "OCC-Royal Oak Campus is home to many, many students who aspire in many, many ways. I'm truly grateful to Photography Instructor Rob Kangas, who's retiring soon. What a gift!\n\nMany, many other instructors have taught and inspired many, many students. Thanks a million!", 'Recently started back going to school during the summer semester and did 100 percent online courses ..I haven\'t been to college in over 14 years so working the d2l site was a challenge and then some teachers uses Proctor for exams ..I must say the grading scale has changed alot since I went to school in 2011..you can get 100 percents on all your course work and still fail the class or come close to it and the professors are anal they\'re heartless they\'re not understanding nor do they care to help you , I understand that it\'s college and we\'re all adults but these professors are anal and they have no compassion..I\'ve had to drop a few courses due to reading syllabus for courses and some teachers were so rude and blunt they basically cursed us out in a nice way and they have a negative demeanor..rude and arrogant the way they talk in the syllabus and some are not realistic..they expect a three page paper , 20 pages of mind tap homework plus listen to 15 chapters of lectures at once plus a quiz all in one week and some teachers will put the quiz date up on a Saturday that\'s to be taken by Tuesday way too much work and they basically tell ya "oh well" "there\'s no extra credit during this semester " one teacher was so rude in her syllabus I think her name was Johnson..she goes " if you earn a 89 percent in my course , don\'t bother asking me if I can bump it to a 90 for you , answer will be no! I mean she was very aggressive in her syllabus I dropped her course like a bad habit..I am not understanding why these teachers are so damn rude cocky and arrogant ..how are yall teachers but don\'t want to help and assist your students so that they can succeed? I\'ve never seen so many teachers that were unwilling to help their students succeed in my life ...I also got behind in one class due to the death of my manager , got laid off of work plus going thru alot of excruciating things and they had me write an appeal just to deny it on purpose ..even with proof ..this school and these teachers does not care about you ..all they care about is the money..I have decided to go to another college and dropped this one ..very ignorant professors and staff', 'The facility is very nice and accessible. NOTE: Google maps takes you to the college building itself. The correct place to park is in the parking garage across the street.', 'The building was clean. Multiple entrances and bathrooms. Easy to find. Hidden space for peace or alone time.']

name: Oakland University
reviews: ['Oakland University, elegantly situated at 201 Meadow Brook Rd within the rolling landscapes of Rochester, is consistently identified in my local and professional circles as a sophisticated intellectual hub that masterfully balances a research-intensive mission with a highly personalized student experience. From numerous substantive dialogues with local business leaders and alumni, a clear consensus emerges that the university operates with merytorical precision, particularly through its world-class engineering and health science programs that serve as critical pipelines for Michigan’s major industries. My colleagues often remark on the institution\'s unique ability to foster "Golden Grizzly" pride, noting that the faculty demonstrates a level of accessible expertise and professional moxie that is rarely found in institutions of this caliber. In frequent discussions about the regional academic landscape, the public sentiment consistently praises the campus for its safe, state-of-the-art environment and its strategic location that facilitates elite-level internships with top-tier corporations. I am particularly struck by the university’s commitment to community engagement and the arts, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who view Meadow Brook Hall and the campus as a cultural cornerstone as much as an educational one. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages this sprawling campus with a transparent and visionary hand, ensuring that academic integrity remains the bedrock of every degree awarded. Reflecting on these consistently positive and well-grounded testimonials, I view Oakland University as a distinguished powerhouse of opportunity that executes its complex mandate with undeniable class and an unwavering dedication to the success of its diverse community.', 'As an OU alumni, I was thrilled when my daughter wanted to attend Oakland University. I remember how strong my education was and how much the professors genuinely cared about their students and wanted them to succeed. It is sad to see that this level of support has disappeared. I am now watching my daughter try to teach herself the math she needs to learn because of the lack of instruction and support from her professors. Unfortunately, I would not recommend attending this school any longer.', "I have no real complaints about Oakland University. It is a super nice campus with an amazing library, student center, and programs. I have loved my time in the film program and have had amazing professors and met great people. The clubs are nice and the facilities are simply the best. It's nice and big and I can go on plenty of walks and theres amazing scenery. The community is great and I have loved my time here.", "Had a bad experience with a woman in the Financial Aid office. She didn't give her name and was not helpful at all. Calling them is a complete waste of time. I was trying to ask a question and she kept telling me to go to their website and pull up the calendar. I told her I had already looked at the calendar but didn't understand what was meant by one of the notes on an upcoming date but she wouldn't explain it and wanted me to look it up myself. I was asking about a medical withdrawal and the affect it would have on financial aid but without having any information from me regarding the circumstances, she told me that type of withdrawal wasn't necessary!", 'Here for a blood drive and there is ZERO handicap ♿️  parking spots that make it easier for handicapped individuals to park close enough to get in to the main door for blood drive. Inexcusable and HIGHLY prejudice.  I dont even know how thats legal honestly.']

name: The University of Olivet
reviews:
["I’m not a student or employee, but I’ve visited the University of Olivet countless times. The student body is incredibly proud, and you can really feel their passion for the school every time you're on campus.

​It’s been great to see the recent growth, especially the new Cutler Student Center. The new food options there, like Tu Taco, are a fantastic addition and give the campus a much-needed modern 'living room' feel.

​As with any small private university, the cost is a factor to consider, and the value really depends on which specific degree program you’re pursuing. However, the sense of community here is genuine, and the new facilities are making the campus experience even better.", 'My son freshman year in college I love love love this campus!!!  Very intimate all so about an hour away from home.', "The sports complex was not impressive and a little outdated in my opinion. It's a D3 college facility, not a park n rec playground.", 'I wouldn’t recommend this place to ANYONE as long a Steven Corey is President. No respect for staff or students. It breaks my heart as an alumni to be writing this, but what’s the point of keeping quiet as the place is being destroyed.', "I love this college. The classes are very small with a 17:1 student to teacher ratio and a roughly 1,100 student campus. Everyone is super friendly, the professors actually care about your education and take the time to get to know you and know your name. All of my professors know me by name and address me by name and they say hello to me in the halls when they see me because the recognize me. The campus itself is gorgeous in all four seasons and it's so small it takes roughly 5 minutes (give or take a few) to get anywhere for classes and they offer an all you can eat breakfast, lunch, and dinner facility for meals and right down the street on Main Street are many mom and pop type stores, so even the regular population of Olivet, Michigan is very welcoming. I would, with everything in  me, recommend this college to anyone and everyone because it is just wonderful. (that is if you don't mind small)"]

name: Kuyper College
reviews: ["As the husband of the temporary coach bus driver for Kuiper College's women's volleyball team, I've had the privilege of witnessing firsthand the incredible team spirit and dedication that these young women bring to the game. From the moment they step onto the bus, there's an infectious energy and enthusiasm that fills the air. They're always laughing, joking, and supporting each other, and it's clear that they have a genuine love for the sport and for each other.", 'Great Christian college with excellent faculty and staff, great community life.', "I've Been Here Probably 10 Different Time's To Work On My Son's Car And Meeting Different Students That Attend Here That Have Been Second To None As In Personalities And Attitudes! I've Had As Many Of 5 Different Students That Have Helped Me Out With Getting A hold Of My Son, & To Showing Me Where His New Residence Is As He Moved Without Informing Me.\nGR-8 Student's With GR-8 Personalities!\nVery Impressed!", 'Mr Wilson my coach friend/buddy who coach’s basketball is amazing I will go to that college', 'Solid community, academics, faculty and staff. Smaller community insures no one gets forgotten, creating a more focused and personalized educational experience.']

name: Sacred Heart Major Seminary
reviews: ['SHMS is my alma mater and is a wonderful institution with a rich history and a star-studded faculty of world renowned professors. The campus is beautiful and the buildings are majestic. The location is in a group of thriving neighborhoods, but venturing out further shows the degradation that Detroit has been suffering for several decades. The academics are rigorous and the spiritual program is demanding. It is a great place to discern and grow for the priesthood or earn an MA in theology to help serve the Church as a layperson. I highly recommend the institution and visiting if you are interested. Prepare to be challenged and to grow in your faith!', 'I attended SHMS Certificate Program in Youth Ministry years ago. These over-the-weekend courses were amazing and attended by like-minded Youth Ministers, enthusiastic to learn, share and participate. Courses ranging from catechesis to multiculturalism were as diverse as the as the faculty and attendees. The setting of the Seminary offered a great learning experience for each weekend as it not only included the classroom experience, but room & board, offering a relaxed setting for learning, discussion, meditation as well as fellowship with staff with seminarians. All of this takes place on the beautiful campus and chapel in Detroit, MI.', 'Very traditional building and very peaceful setting. This is so nice of a place to learn. The curriculum is outstanding and the professors are very good.', 'Our 30th College Reunion dinner held there.  Great people to deal with.  Great food, service.  Members only.', 'Beautiful chapel and great reception facilities.']

name: Saginaw Valley State University
reviews:
['I went to SVSU for five years. It was the best experience and choice I have ever made. The teachers here for the most part are incredible. I spent $35,000 over five years, which is not too bad comparatively to other schools. This school gave me a wonderful education with great educators and wonderful support. The first year dorms were pretty great too- then I moved off campus. Wonderful school! Shoutout to Professor Cohle, Professor Mellema, and Professor Shiva for being amazing at their careers!', 'All photos are taken and distributed by Be Photographed.

Saginaw Valley State University has such a clean and well-maintained campus — it’s a great place for graduate sessions and portraits. I’ve photographed several grads here, and every part of campus offers something different, from open walkways to beautifully landscaped areas that encourage you to explore.

It’s a peaceful, welcoming environment that photographs wonderfully year-round', 'What a beautiful campus! We were there for orientation and everything was top notch; the staff; the grounds; the residential halls; classrooms and labs; athletic areas and the food!', '5 star university, not much more to say. Dorms are incredible, cost is a reasonable as it gets, and the proffesors and class sizes are stellar aswell. Only gripe I have is some hiccups with financial offices but im entirely sure thats an issue everywhere. Happy to spend all 4 years here.', 'Great beautiful school that my daughter goes to my daughter got a full ride for free first year. Filled with great people great teachers, beautiful campus and great community. I highly recommend.. always driving to expand and make better']

name: Schoolcraft Community College District
reviews: ['I enjoyed my time at Schoolcraft College. I went for the name I was starting a curriculum company. My 20s were fun it was all going to workout till things went another direction… The people were nice. I enjoyed the friendships from my time spent there. I got hold of something interesting and someone interfered. It was taken away.', 'It’s all about the money!!! My daughter was kicked out of online class by the professor. She called advisor and was told they never do that .  She was kicked out after 2nd class, the third class tried to sign on and was already kicked out. Made a claim and of course they denied it and kept her money. It’s always the students fault. , never the schools fault.', 'My son is dual enrolled. They have been so helpful along the way. Great school', 'Played a game in the trinity elite sports center. Directions took me to the library and tech center on the other side. So if you’re looking to play in a tournament you’ll want to go to the sports center. It’s not in the actual college but it is on the school campus.', "This school is fantastic. They have the resources for when you struggle, the teachers are very knowledgeable on the material they teach, and the labs are truly amazing. The only thing I hate is that if you don't live in Livonia, you have to pay extra to attend. Overall, great school! Radiology Technologist program is very organized."]

name: Siena Heights University
reviews:
["It's Graduation time, I highly recommend all future graduates get your cap and gown at the collage book store don't waist your time ordering on line, read reviews first Oak hall!

It was a great 5 years the staff is helpful, many times, it's a family oriented school I seen great bonds developed, I think my son will take many good things from here the professor's have been there for assistance, growth and career development.

They have a great program for freshman first year, to help them along the new stage in life,The dorms are a bit on the older side but great experience the first couple years, with options to move up or out local over the years.  I was very excited for the soccer years but that turned out to be a bit disappointing, were a huge soccer/family and fans, never the less we supported our team the whole way through!

Go Saints!!
Thank you for the past five years and memories made.", 'Great Venue for Basketball Tournaments

This is a solid spot for basketball tournaments. Be sure to pack plenty of food—especially protein-rich snacks—since concessions can be hit or miss. The venue can get quite warm during the spring and summer months, so dress accordingly. Thankfully, the foyer is air-conditioned if you need a quick break to cool down. Bathrooms are decent and maintained as well as can be expected given the steady flow of event attendees.', 'This is a beautiful campus! What a shame they are planning to closes this university, it is a pillar in the city of Adrian, MI.', "Not surprised it's closing. I received my bachelors degree in accounting in 2008. I applied and applied and applied and applied to places once I graduated. I was NEVER able to get a job. I ended up becoming a stay at home mom for a few years then started a photography business. I had to move states and still can't get a job with the degree I received from this worthless school. I'm glad it's closing. If you don't help the people you service then you shouldn't be in business! TERRIBLE COLLEGE!", "I was unable to go to Siena, as I took up nursing in the 70's, but I fondly remember visiting my two sisters and best friend over the years they were there. I am sad it has to close."]

name: St Clair County Community College
reviews: ['Absolutely a Hidden Gem in Port Huron, Michigan!\nAside from providing excellent higher education opportunities to Thousands of individuals, SC4 offers free art shows, free exercise in the 188 step climb to the top of the McMorran Tower, free admission to one of the finest Museums filled with fossils in all of SE Michigan, plays, concerts, And the only Challenger Learning Center in All of Michigan!', "New student I'm having issues already with financial aid and covering classes, this school really is giving me a hard time after giving pell grants and a small scholarship they still want more money. I decided that this isn't for me will be finishing my classes and moving on to another school closer to the city.", 'The only one even helpful there was some guy named Scott... But he was running around like a chicken with his head cut off doing the work of five people. If you ask me the place has too many chiefs and not enough workers helping students..', "As a graduate of this school in the 2010's, I must say that any body that attends here will never regret it. Everything from the atmosphere on campus to the actual instructors, it is a really wonderful place to attend. I ended up meeting a lot of cool people here, a lot that I talk to a lot. My favorite instructors were Donna Parkhurst, Rob Richardson, William Pilkey, and last but certainly not least Michelle German. I could easily write a 10 page paper on this place, so I'll just leave it at this: one of my favorite life experiences sprouted from this place. Thanks again for all the great memories SC4, and faculty.", 'For the most part, SC4 is a decent school. However, I have not even finished my first semester here, and I have ran into many problems with the Michigan Transfer Agreement courses. My English course that I am taking is required for the transfer, and the teacher does not do anything. She does not teach anything, she does not grade anything, and it seems that she is a habitual liar. I am wasting my money on a school that does not do anything for their students. If you end up going here, do not go for the Michigan Transfer Agreement, because it is a waste of time and money.']

name: Southwestern Michigan College
reviews: ['The campus is nice and quiet, the professors and staff are where this place shines though. I cannot sing the praises of the professors enough!', 'Excellent college - the professors I had did everything in their power, to help  me pass each class I took. Oh, and the Learning Center, at the back of the library, was amazing! Some of the tutors took some getting used to, but others I loved right away, and was sad, when they left the main campus, to go tutor on the other, smaller campus. Of course, just like most people, I had my favorites, among the tutors and among the professors I had. (I only took one class at a time) Sadly, though, I had to drop out, due to having my financial aid suspended (for a second time), and not wanting to appeal it (again).', "Amazing college for starting right out of High School. They helped me set up my classes and got all of my financial aid figured out really fast. The teachers are very nice and actually care about what they're teaching. I would definitely recommend this school for anyone thinking about going to a community college. Very clean campus too and has pretty nice dorms. I would also hit up the SAC.", "Very good beginner college. I loved my time there. Most of the teachers were so thoughtful and understanding. One thing I didn't like was the financial aid office and the counselorsthat scheduled classes. They almost made me take a couple extra classes I didn't need. Be careful when you go to them!", "This is an outstanding local community college with a diverse student body with people coming from all over the world. Thousands of interestin and unique  stories have been told on that campus, and thousands more have yet to be told. I'm enrolled here and so far I've loved every moment. They offer a wide selection of courses and majors in many subject. A well rounded and friendly staff who are open for consultation makes this my favorite school."]

name: Spring Arbor University
reviews:
['Attending the spiritual conference with our church at Spring Arbor University was an unforgettable and deeply moving experience. The weather was beautiful throughout, perfectly matching the warmth and joy we felt during our time there. The university campus itself was not only stunning but also vibrant with a variety of uplifting activities that kept us engaged and inspired.
We had the opportunity to grow spiritually and deepen our relationship with our Savior, our Lord God Jesus Christ. The teachings and sessions were rich with wisdom, truth, and love, helping us reflect more on our faith and purpose. One of the highlights was the music—the songs and hymns were powerful and filled the atmosphere with worship and praise. It was a true blessing to sing alongside so many devoted believers.
The people we met were kind, welcoming, and full of the Holy Spirit, making the entire experience even more special. Each day felt like a gift, filled with joy, peace, and spiritual renewal. We left feeling refreshed, encouraged, and more united as a community.
Truly, our days at Spring Arbor University were blessed, and we thank God for this incredible journey', "I love this place! The campus feels like home- like a small city all it's own. My niece attends here and I enjoy coming to visit her. The food in the cafeteria is very good (particularly good pizza). They have worship services and Bible studies and lots of activities going on every night. The only complaint I have is I've heard some of the professors teach very liberal ideology (this is supposed to be a Christian college). I'm not surprised, just disappointed. You can't escape it, even at a place that is supposed to be a sanctuary from that kind of indoctrination. Thankfully those kinds of teachers are the minority. I think it should be a rule that teachers just teach their subject and leave their personal opinions/ideologies/beliefs out of their classrooms. It's not appropriate and the students didn't pay for that. Once my niece completes her degree, I think I will bring it to the attention of the school about these teachers. Other than that, I recommend this school. Just make sure you're kids are well established before sending them into any classroom these days.", 'Love this College! And everything about it! Staff & students all very welcoming during our 2 visits.', "Walked down from my airbnb and looked around the campus, quiet, very clean, lawns manicured and school hadn't started yet, they were setting up for assembly looked like. Huge trees on this property. Very nice small campus.", 'Nice campus.  Excellent gyms.  I think there were five or six basketball games all going on at once with no space issues. Stadium is really nice for a smaller school.']

name: Washtenaw Community College
reviews: ['The automotive program is top tier. Hands on learning is exceptional, teachers are awesome, and the Veteran coordinators actually know what they are doing! Administration is still pushing DEI bs, so I removed 1 star.', "This college ruined my life and any chance I had at ever finishing college in just one semester! The professors are extremely lazy and just use AI to grade assignments and never read them themselves! Don't bother using proper grammar or they'll accuse you of using AI! Not to mention they straight up lie about these class descriptions, I signed up for an online class and it ended up being a mandatory in person attendence class???????? and if you miss a class, the professors treat you like you just committed a crime even if you wanna make up work they just ignore you and they just continue to read their slideshow that's not even about the class I signed up for. Then to make it worse the transfer out process they make it impossible to withdraw from their college without you basically transferring to another college and the other college has to do everything, all this college wants is your money because for the first 2 weeks of class they make it very easy, seems nice right? Their drop with refund deadline is two weeks, after two weeks the workload and schedule for even a 12 credit hour student turns into 45+ hours of time you need to dedicate to these damn entry level classes and if you're like me and have to work to support your family outside of school, good luck because I was getting if I was lucky 3 hours of sleep a day for 3 months, and in return they do not help you at all if your situation is not great which is the OPPOSITE of what I was told by advisors and the admissions office of WCC. Im now super far behind because of ONE semester at this college and it could take an entire extra year to fix the damage. To anyone else who even thinks about coming here, please really consider your options", "The most unhelpful unorganized unprofessional process inconsiderate system ever. Trying to help my stepdaughter understand her financial aid request denial financial services payment plan qualifications. We were moved around from student services to five other window apartments. No department knew what the other one had or didn't have, it was an hour and a half of walking back and forth only to be sent back to the place we started student services. And still there was no resolution and everybody acted like there was no supervisor no management no accountability. Just a waste, just a waste and I felt everyone was just incompetent and uneducated. Then get a supervisor then get that person supervisor or director You don't keep sending me from one window to the next ridiculous", "Offers a variety of classes. Most professors are really good, kind, and help you succeed. Take David Erwin and Michael Quail (the older one) if you're going into Math. The campus is very well maintained, lots of parking, and there are a lot of different programs to help your career. There are some clubs (club sports, intramural sports, academic clubs--join women in STEM!) but the social scene isn't very active, but I guess that's good if you're an introvert. The application process and registering for classes is also very easy--just make sure you register for classes ASAP. Overall, a good school to go to (and much more affordable than universities).", 'Apologies for any triteness. Democracy runs well w an educated populace. A few hallmarks of a Democracy are; Quality of Life, Education, Freedoms and the Civil Rights of All. Universal Healthcare, Access, Education and Trades training, why not? If we are able to pay one man millions of dollars, then why not provide for millions of people? How often does corporate welfare, “trickle down” and subsidies to huge corporations translate into savings? Educated, critically thinking humans are one goal and Community Colleges are gateways and answers to improving and increasing Democratic values. How naive, ignorant and misinformed I was as a young adult, to snub and look down on Community Colleges. As the decades passed and the Grace of wisdom was given to me, I began to realize the value of CC. Mistakes made can be the process in which we grow and improve, if those mistakes don’t kill you.
