One of the most meaningful aspects of my journey was receiving the Herzing University grant on two separate occasions. These grants were a tremendous blessing and played a critical role in helping me continue my education without interruption. Knowing that the university believed in me enough to support me financially gave me renewed motivation and reassurance during challenging times. It allowed me to stay focused on learning, clinical practice, and becoming the best nurse I can be.

Herzing University did not just provide an education it provided opportunity, encouragement, and hope. I am incredibly grateful for the academic support, financial assistance, and sense of community that carried me through this journey. I am proud to be a Herzing nursing student and confident that the foundation I gained here has prepared me to serve patients with competence, compassion, and professionalism.', "I love Herzing... The staff is amazing and truly loves to see their students succeed. Professor Raulston, Professor Bammert, Professor Kova, Professor Conlin, Dr. Hegland, and Professor Baumann have all been the kindest, most genuine people throughout this journey. They make school fun (thanks, Professor Bammert!!!), relatable, and an overall positive experience. The Dental Hygiene Program is INTENSE, but the professors really make it worth it. I've learned more than I could have ever imagined, and look forward to being the best dental hygienist I can be. The BFF center has also been such a blessing. It's a great bump of support for families working hard to better themselves. Some resources are available upon request, and it remains an entirely judgment-free zone, which I appreciate immensely. The parent/child play area is well-maintained and inviting. I couldn't stay afloat if not for the BFF center/program!", 'Normally the process of getting into a college is very hectic and stressful, but with Herzing University, the staff was wonderful and very helpful! When I applied for more information about applying for Herzing I got a phone call almost immediately and was able to set up a meeting for Admission. Ali Krueger was amazing to work with and very helpful with my journey of applying to Herzing University.  My experience with the staff has been amazing so far and I am excited to start my education at Herzing University!', 'I am a full time student in the nursing program of Herzing University (accelerated nursing program).
The school has  seasoned and very helpful faculty.
The administration is extremely devoted to the professions  and are very approachable ( open door for everyone).

The school also supports the working and / or student parents by giving free money, foods and diapers not to underscore the free day care services that are available.
The campus is clean and provides free snacks and hot drinks.
I have been to many other institutions  such as the university of Minnesota, UND, Mayo Clinic Rochester. No Student accommodations can exceed the one here at Herzing University (twins cities).
I would recommend this institution starting with my immediate family members and others .
I started with a simple tour and did not go back since. I graduate  in the Spring of 2026(God willing).', 'My experience at Herzing University has been positive. The classes are well-structured and engaging. The workload is manageable for those who want balance between academics and personal time.']

name: University of Minnesota-Duluth
reviews: ["I've attended UMD from 2019 to 2025, and the entire experience was incredible (even during the COVID years). Already miss the campus, the students, the faculty, and the opportunities that were provided. Highly recommended to attend here for a nice, small-town feeling. Just be prepared for the winters up here.", 'Wonderful faculty, Great facilities, visionary leaders, and views of the lake. Their U Spatial GIS program is exceptional.', "I really enjoyed my experience here overall. I graduated in the spring of 2017. Although there are some noticeable issues with the multiple charges to your account and a major parking problem, I feel the instructors I had the overall education I received made up for it. It's not a perfect school, but I would recommend it overall. In addition to enjoying campus life at UMD, you can also enjoy the beauty of Duluth.", "UMD is a great school, it just doesn't deserve five stars. The business school, LSBE, deserves five stars. UMD wide, some of their professors are needlessly political which can lessen their credibility as objective educators. The liberal arts school is comical is some of their class offerings, however there are decent programs within the liberal arts school that should not be overlooked, such as anything related to world languages. The hockey team is great. The weight room is great, would be a lot better if you are on a sports team and have access to their better facility. It you want a commuter campus, this is the college for you. The food on campus is subpar but some days it can be pretty good. Only department I heard a lot of complaints about was the physics department (at the time of writing they may have improved but be wary). Would be four stars if it was a wet campus. Would be five stars if the University system cared about this campus but they give the impression of only caring about the Twin Cities campus.", "I've been on this campus since I was a little kid. My family members have taught here, I did music camp here, robotics, met with the diversity teams and the students in the intercultural center, speech meet, many of events and courses. I have yet to come here as a UMD student but I always feel welcome and included here. Amazing campus!"]

name: University of Minnesota-Morris
reviews: ['I loved the university. The campus is beautiful, people are friendly, and I felt welcomed everywhere in Morris.', 'So far so good, just moving our son in.', 'A good school to learn math and stats. Faculty are very good—only had a few professors ever who I didn’t jive with.\n\nDefinitely would go again, if I were ever 18 and needed a BA degree again', 'Impressive university in a small-town setting.  The people, professors, students, and staff are all working together to make the place better.  Like any genuine endeavor, this is a work in progress and they are not perfect...but its a great place to learn and be authentic about who you are and what you want to do with your life.  I felt welcome and engaged in challenging and positive ways.', 'I attended this University years ago! It was awesome and weird at the same time. They have some really caring professors, the counselors could use a bit of a touch up on understanding and relating to the student needs. This is definitely a college town and everything is far away. So be careful when traveling to the nearest store which was like 7-11 or a gas station convenience store. My dorm was in a coed building and lucky my room was near the bathroom. Dorm size was pretty cool.']

name: Minnesota State University Moorhead
reviews:
['Yall are done for. Your WiFi is complete abysmal trash. I’m sitting here tryna hop on a game with the goat but he can’t connect cause you disabled peer to peer connections. Count your days', 'Administration does not care about their students and only cares about saving money. Geoscience program is struggling with understaffing and underfunding. Multiple programs don’t have any staff. They limit their students to counseling because they won’t hire any more counselors. President downs is the downfall of this school. Bless the professors and staff that care about their students because without them, this school would be useless.

The campus itself is really nice with a good wellness center, dining center and library.', 'I had an incredible experience at MSUM. The political science and international relations programs were a perfect fit for me. Dr. Conteh was my first advisor, and I later switched to Professor Paul Kramer, who was an amazing mentor. His guidance and support were invaluable, and I wouldn’t have been able to graduate without him.
I also met my best friend there, and I loved the diverse international student community. Experiencing different cultures and perspectives helped me gain a broader understanding of the world.', 'Spent a year at the MSUM in Moorhead.

Pro's: The Sociology program is fantastic. Dr. Vigilant is very knowledgeable and willing to really explain the 'nitty gritty' of what you are learning. Most of the other teachers are very nice and willing to help. Nice campus, the advisers are friendly and mostly available.

Con's: The administration is horrible. Worse than horrible. I have been out of school for over 5 years and they still find ways to screw me over whenever I have to deal with them. From key administrative aids being out of the office for weeks, to the purposeful and never ending runaround you get from every single person from billing, to academics, to student aid, to the school board. They impose random holds on your account and never take them off, even after bringing in at least 3 people to resolve the issue. Its the poster-child for bureaucracy.

Never trust anyone when they say they will "leave a message" and "I'm sure it's fine."', "Good school. Excellent film, theatre, and education programs. A decent price for the full university experience without having to walk a mile to you next class. Knocked a star off because of the numerous classes cut and horrible decisions made by the last president. The dorms, and other campus facilities are undergoing numerous needed renovations. I would recommend this place to prospective students.

Kise Commons on the other hand, best to avoid eating there for every meal. Trust me, you won't go #2 for days.

Advice for new students… watch out for the squirrels. Seriously! Watch out for the squirrels! They'll ruin your day! Every long term student and staff member here has a personal story or two to tell you about MSUM's squirrels. I was once walking to class and a squirrel took a Dairy Queen blizzard cup up into the tree and dropped it on a girl's head in front of Ballard Hall and the library!"]

name: North Hennepin Community College
reviews: ['I was a straight-A student in the PTK Honor Society here, and I say this with my whole heart: going to this school may have been one of the worst decisions I ever made in my life. I would strongly encourage you to attend a different college. I will go a step further and say that you may want to specifically avoid Minnesota State schools in general. I am willing to revise this review if and when I feel things have improved, but this is how I feel for now.', 'The college has a spacious parking area with ample parking available for visitors and individuals with disabilities. The reception was warm and welcoming, and the advising team was very helpful in providing the guidance and support I needed.', "This collage is the best, most affordable option in MN. The teachers and students are incredibly friendly. If you haven't applied yet, you're missing out!", 'From the front doors of NHCC to Security, they all were efficient in their positions, spot on with prompt service and friendly energies.', 'The college is equipped for the vast learning experience of the adult learning because of the welcoming environment. It is a place with many resources and staff that are committed to student progress and growth.']

name: Normandale Community College
reviews: ['I encourage staff at Normandale College to maintain professionalism online. For example, Paul C. should consider keeping personal political opinions off public social media, as it can reflect on the institution.', 'This is Minnesota,s hidden gem, best community College in USA, the campus is so clean, user friendly, with a Japanese garden to disconnect from the outside. The staff is so helpful', "This is not a school that doesn't caters to students with disabilities!!!! I have dyslexia, and is deaf and hard of hearing. Becuase they refuse to pay the teacher 1 more hour of work I can't get the extra help I need to take classes to get things explained to me properly. Goodbye dreams of being in Healthcare or anything else becuase  this school too cheap 😡😡", "I was extremely happy about my experience at Normandale despite having to back out for family reasons. On the preparation side of college, you get so many resources and helpful staff if you show up in person. My academic advisor Njia Lawerence-Porter was great and my friend's relative Lori York are great people!", "If you need a question answered be sure to call or email ahead and check that they have full fledged staff members available. Oftentimes it is just students working, and while I respect that, it is very difficult to get any sort of help.\n\nThe Student Services professional staff I have met will always try to get you an answer- even if they don't know it themselves- so save your own time and make sure to visit when they are working!"]

name: North Central University
reviews: ['took a tour of this college campus and it was amazing we had a luncheon and got to meet the faculty and staff the lunch was awesome really good food really nice people this is definitely the place that I went all of my children to go to college my daughter does not want to visit any other place to go to school she has her mind set on graduating from North Central University we are so happy for her and happy that we know she will be somewhere where Jesus comes first Amen to that', 'Everyone from the staff to the students were very friendly and helpful.  We had vehicle issues,  students walked 2 blocks with a cart to help move the 3 kids into their dorms that our families were helping their kids get set up.  We were all having a rough day and they helped make it so much better.', "Never been there but I've spoken to a graduate and she just got her pastoral license. She told me how the staff is amazing and overall a welcoming place. I could feel it reading these reviews and listening to her speak. For sure where I want to go and I don't want to go anywhere else. Keep yall updated on if I go or not!!", "Great school to work on personal development.  However, their general education classes are abismal and I would say there have been about 8-10 classes that hold substantial value.  Their systems are very bad.  I've been here three years and every semester I need to look over all my bills and classes and spend hours meeting with people in different offices to fix my billing and class rosters.  Make sure you look over your bills because they likely are not right.", 'North Central has a welcoming atmosphere with wonderful professors. Its price is a bit much in my opinion. However if you want to learn more about religion, Christianity, and have an atmosphere to get closer to God in new ways its worth it.']

name: Northland Community and Technical College
reviews: ["This is the most joke of a school ive ever seen / attended. They lied to me about a multi-million dollar football stadium they were building along with a state of the art training facility (all a lie). I was told I would have somewhere to live (stuck me on a couch inside the apartment of 3 other people after flying from Florida with all my things. The school's teachers were a complete joke (besides the art teacher, he was cool but was still a joke). The office staff was very flirtatious with the football players, kind of disgusting. The whole school was a complete joke, from the way overpriced school store all the way to the teachers/football coaches partying with the college kids. The football program was so pitiful, the football coach was child that new nothing about football. They will take you money and give you the worst education in the world. Avoid at all cost.", "The nursing program has fallen apart. Don't expect any in-person class, up to date educational material, or support from college administrators.", 'I always get greeted with friendly, welcoming staff. The atmosphere is always so nice. Has nice Holiday season decorations with Christmas trees decorated beautifully along with the beautiful fireplace too!!', "If you care about your schooling, consider the program that you are going here for. They put more care into their nursing, ota, pta, welding, drafting, computer science, and other full blooded programs. The rest of their school seems to be just fluff. A large portion of their money goes into sports and propaganda. If you decide to go here to explore college career options or start with a two year liberal arts degree I caution you. While there are a few golden eggs, many of the teachers here are very poor. From being graded arbitrarily for watching a movie then to be tested about it a week and a half down the road, to being given random rubrics on writing down what you learned (even at the beginning of the semester). I don't know if the Deans know of this problem or if they just aren't paying attention but there are problems in this school right now. Be very careful of the teachers you choose. You may not learn anything if you don't remain vigilant and cautious. With all of that said, I just want to reiterate that there are some very good and praiseworthy teachers here. You just need to do your research first. I would suggest talking to them and getting a feel for what they are all about. Also, be very wary of the science department. There was where I had some of my worst experiences with teachers. Looking at you Mr. Robert Jung.", 'Relaxed and very quiet good places to eat and enjoy outdoors🌈 Excelente Ciudad de TRF MN']

name: University of Northwestern-St Paul
reviews:
["University culture is very strained and split down the middle. You either have friends or you don't. I didn't even know my neighbor next door in any way. One class (Leadership for Transformation) reliably informed me that as a white person I'm inherently bad and must go out of my way to appease others who are not white. Administration walks a fine line and makes both conservatives and progressives unhappy simultaneously. There is a literal communist party and a pro-life group there too, deepening the sense of uneasiness and social tension. My experience was rather poor, but most of that was due to my own mental incompetency and stage of life I was in. I spent the entire semester playing Minecraft because the social environment was not worth my effort. I went for one semester and do not miss it at all. It has a truly beautiful campus though, full of rich history. Make sure to visit in the springtime when the trees are in bloom.", "Any college experience will mostly be what you make of it, and who you choose to spend your time with. Northwestern provided excellent resources for academic and spiritual growth (legit professors, excellent dorm community, daily chapel opportunities, and local outreach ministries). But, the professors you take will change your experience a lot. So, choose carefully, ask for advice from older and more mature students, and spend time planning your schedule. Don't expect your advisor to help you pick the best profs who might change your life.

I went through the engineering program, which was amazing. Wouldn't want anything else. The academics are good here. But I also invested my life in the community, hall ministry, leadership opportunities, spiritual growth, and God did great things. It is incredible all he did in spite of all I am not.

Northwestern provides an environment for much potential, but it isn't everything. Rooting yourself in a local church will be of the utmost importance and it was equally important in shaping my time at Northwestern. Finding godly mentors and role-models is also a top priority. Last note, if you have godly roommates who are zealous for the gospel, living on campus will be an equally life-changing experience. It's worth the extra cash.", 'I graduated from Northwestern a few years ago. The art department is excellent! I couldn't have asked for more knowledgeable and caring professors. The only thing that discouraged me was that as a student of color, I felt completely out of place. I found myself conforming to the culture there, which consists mainly of white, conservative, upper-middle class folks. I felt a very strong disconnect between the other students and myself, sometimes even between the professors and me. Sometimes I'd ask myself, "What am I doing here? I don't belong here." I was an art major and it was only within the art department that I felt at ease. Everyone there was different, creative, expressive and open-minded. It was a little community of artists and I am forever grateful for that experience.', 'The MEL puts out great music, keep up the good work!', 'This place taught me that people who call themselves Christians hate you almost as much as they hate reading their bibles. If they call themselves a Christian, just turn around and walk the other way. They will lie cheat and steal just to have fun. This place is not a religious institution- it is a predatory system eaiting people with faith. They hate and steal here. Nothing else.']

name: Oak Hills Christian College
reviews:
['My experience at Oak Hills revealed a serious disconnect between the school’s stated commitment to Christlike love and the way it treats actual human beings, especially when it comes to sexuality, relationships, and gender. Their policies may be written with the confidence of dogma, but what they communicate in practice is something very different from the compassion Jesus modeled.

One of the defining moments for me was when the school expected me to kick out my fiancée—even after she sold her house—just so I could attend their program. That alone speaks volumes about their priorities. Rather than supporting students with real lives, real relationships, and real challenges, the institution seemed more invested in enforcing ideological conformity than in embodying the grace they preach.

The doctrinal statements sound pious and polished, but the lived reality is this:
their policies do not reflect the love of Jesus.
Not the Jesus who ate with sinners.
Not the Jesus who defended the woman caught in adultery.
Not the Jesus who touched the unclean, welcomed the rejected, or challenged the religious gatekeepers of His day.

Instead, these policies create an environment where fear, shame, and exclusion are masqueraded as “faithfulness.”

The school’s stance on sexuality and gender identity is not merely conservative—it is punitive. It reduces complex human experiences to violations of “community standards,” and the result is predictable: people feel judged, unsafe, and unwelcome. The language of “compassion” in their policy is overshadowed by the real-world consequences of their rules.

The irony is thick: they claim to “teach students how to think, not what to think,” yet they have already predetermined who is acceptable and who is not—who is allowed at the table and who must be disciplined or removed for failing to conform.

In my experience, Oak Hills did not demonstrate the grace, hospitality, or humility that marks the life of Jesus. Instead, they demonstrated an agenda that elevates institutional purity over human dignity.

A Christian school should be a place where people encounter the love of Christ in action—not a place where policies push vulnerable people out the door.', "Absolutely beautiful! The workers there are very nice! The students are wonderful! Felt God's presence there! He is certainly working through their lives !", "Classes are mid at best. Currently I don't like most of my classes.  More than makes up in a good christ following community.", "A really horrible place. Please don't attend. you will regret it.", 'I love the school. It has been a major blessings great people and learn a lot .']

name: Saint Mary's University of Minnesota
reviews: ["St. Mary's is a beautiful campus inhabited by a poisonous administration that is driving the school into the ground. In my three semesters there my experience at the school involved my advisor registering me for classes in a major I did not choose (as mine had been discontinued)just to keep me on campus and making up the numbers. At the same time, they discontinued several programs including all Arts, Theatre, and Music. The school has no trouble silencing dissenting opinions in order to control their own narrative.", 'Do not recommend. Saint Mary’s has changed, sadly for the worse. I still owe thousands of dollars, years later. Despite Saint Mary’s lying to me about affordability. I was told the same story everyone was. Go to college. Take out loans. You’ll get a high paying job and easily be able to pay them off.\nPlenty of support applying and attending, but where is the support after graduating? I haven’t seen any. And now? My major is defunct. My degree rendered meaningless.\nDo yourself a favor and find an affordable option that has real connections in the real world.', 'I attended this school briefly for a graduate degree is psychological sciences and I do not recommend this school to anyone. One of my professors was rude and made fun of students. I mentioned this to the board and they said they would look into it, they did nothing. I didn’t feel supported at all. Now after dropping out, they added a bill to my student portal, which I no longer have access to, and didn’t notify me. 5 months later, they finally send a bill to my house with late fees added each month. I reached out to the Student Accounts Specialist, and he didn’t even acknowledge what I asked about. This school is run like a business and they do not care about you as an individual. Consider elsewhere.', "If you are going there And are wanting to join Athletics I would truthfully recommend looking for a different college. This college Is struggling financially with athletics and had to cut programs in order try and make the other programs better which has not worked. Even when being on saint mary's campus things seemed rubbed down. When I would go to the dining area to grab gluten-free stuff the fridge that had all of the allergen food would be empty, so a lot of the time I would either have to buy my own food or I would just end up not eating at all. The campus is very old And if you like the old kind of scenic vibe then you might like this campus, but the thing I only really found good about this college was the scenery and the  bluffs, the rest was okay but not really the best, and now switching to a different college has showed me a different side of what Saint Mary should have been like.", "Great school! This review is for the Winona campus so keep that in mind if you are looking for info about the Twin Cities campus. Honestly, I loved the school--it is quite small but has a great supportive and positive learning community. I can honestly say that I enjoyed the vast majority of my professors and I also really liked the campus. It is small but located in the bluffs on the west edge of Winona. There are a lot of really great hiking trails on/around campus and the local beauty is hard to beat. While I attended a couple of other schools (UW-L, University of Minnesota) St. Mary's is by far my favorite!"]

name: St Olaf College
reviews:
['We went to see one of the many free concerts that St Olaf offers to students as well as private citizens. It was their Bell choir and it was extraordinary and wonderful. It was in a great venue on campus and made for a great evening of beautiful music.', 'From a parent's perspective.

For months now we have been getting ready for this day to tour the campus. We have jumped through every hoop and supplied everything asked for.  Every time we talked to them, it's "great, we can't wait to see you here", or "judging by everything provided, you shouldn't have any problem getting in".

Fast forward to night before tour day. We've already purchased St Olaf swag, took time off work for both my wife and I, traveled from out of state, rented a hotel room and spent money checking out the area. 19 hours before we are set to tour, our child receives a call informing her she didn't get in, no explanation, our child said but I have a tour tomorrow, they responded back "well, you can just cancel it".

First off, she is still a minor and that call should have gone to her parents. An explanation should be a must.

Second, they have been telling us all along how she shouldn't have any problems getting in, to the point that we didn't apply anywhere else.

Third, now here we are in Minnesota, sitting in a hotel room the morning of the tour that we were just informed to cancel hours before. We have spent over $1000 to travel and check out the area. All of us took 3 days off work/school and now we sit here confused.

For a college to be unorganized enough to be making these decisions hours before their big tour day and to be so arrogant as to call the night before and act like it's now big deal. Completely unprofessional and unethical.

I expected better from you!', 'I visited this college in 2016 and noticed that only European flags were displayed. I didn’t see Middle Eastern or African flags, and I wasn’t sure what the message was. I hope we can continue moving toward greater inclusion and representation.', 'Took our boys here for a campus visit. The campus is beautiful. Architecture is gorgeous with all buildings letting the outside "in", with lots of windows, natural light and stunning views for any season.

It is a smaller school with a close community feel. The class sizes are smaller with a great faculty:student ratio. Music programs available for all. Study abroad opportunities as well. Very nice athletics building with indoor track, tennis and volleyball courts, workout facilities and even a rock climbing wall!

Definitely one of their top picks!', 'St Olaf is everything it says it is. Many colleges and universities try to live out their promises; St Olaf actually lives it out!
I am so glad that my kid is able to attend this college!']

name: The College of Saint Scholastica
reviews: ['They have snazzy hiking trails. The anatomy, stats, and anthropology teachers are awesome. Jack the chef is snazzy too', 'My time at CSS warrants a zero-star rating if I could. name: Rasmussen University-Minnesota
reviews:
['I just finished my first week of general classes. It was stressful to think about going back to school but both Rasmussen and Admissions Advisor Gavin were a huge help in getting me started with my classes, explaining what to expect, and making me feel welcomed. Overall the enrollment process was simple and clear and all questions I had were answered clearly. My first week of classes at the Bloomington campus was a success and the instructors are very helpful and communicative with what they expect. I enrolled at Rasmussen because of their structured and accelerated nursing program and so far it has been good.', 'This is the second time I re-enrolled to Rasmussen in 5 years and Edward made it such a comfortable and easy process for me throughout it all. He’s been nothing short of helpful and kind to me while I was applying. The semester has started and it’s going so well for me.', "The enrollment process at Rasmussen was very smooth. I worked with Ed Knowles and I highly recommend him as an admissions advisor. He is very knowledgeable about Rasmussen, the nursing program, and what students need in order to begin the program. He always returned phone calls and emails quickly and was so helpful. It's now 5 weeks into the semester and I've had to reach out to him twice. Both times he was ready to help me. I cannot express enough appreciation for him!

Classes have been going well. Professor Sherry Hemauer has been exceptional. She is holding our quarter together! She has provided so much support and so many resources to us first quarter nursing students. Dean Frank has been around to meet students and visit classes. It's nice to get to know her. I have really enjoyed going to most classes and have had a great experience so far.", "This is a fantastic institution with career-focused programs. The Bloomington campus has an amazing group of faculty and staff who truly care about your education and success. The BSN and Medical Assisting programs both have strong outcomes. In 2024, 90.7% of Rasmussen's BSN graduates in Minnesota passed their NCLEX on the first attempt. Impressive! The BSN program is CCNE-accredited, and the Medical Assisting program is ABHES accredited.", "I just started Rasmussen's ABSN program earlier this month, but so far, I'm very happy with my decision.

My admissions advisor, Edward K., has been so kind and helpful. He guided me through the admissions process and made sure that all of my questions and concerns were addressed in a very timely manner.

As far as instructors go, Dr. Sherry is one of the best college instructors I've had. She truly wants every student to succeed and loves what she does."]

No one is coming to save you but yourself.
And nobody cares.
So, pursue whatever you like without fear or shame.
That's the real world for ya.
I'm currently in Florida where I live and running for public Offices and still miss SMSU's small caring environment.
Hawaiian Night and all of those fun stuff won't fade.", "Online adjuncts are constantly causing work to be harder than it needs to be. If you are doing online be aware that you will be on your own as they do not actually answer any of their phones. It took 7 days for a professor to get back to me I've had a professor who's had 3 months to get their syllabus right and constantly changes it. Whatever hiring practices they are using to hire adjuncts for the educational department is incredibly poor. The only professor that I have not had an incredible problem with is my history professor. Online adjuncts are clearly given no oversight or requirements and often barely can use the online portal themselves. Two of my professors were hired a week before classes started and one of them couldn't even be bothered to remove the other person's name from the syllabus. You will also be required to join a union to do any of the field experiences in the educational department. I am incredibly worried about not being able to pass the state boards because of the lack of actual learning that is going on in the online classes.", 'The best school compared to other!! Love it', 'Graduated in 1994. Set me on a path to success. Still support the place.']

name: Dunwoody College of Technology
reviews:
['The following review is in updating process.

I am a 3 generation alumni at Dunwoody.
My grandfather graduated here around 1940, my father graduated around 1970, and me and my brother vack in 2007.
This school was top notch for refrigeration from day one till around 2000. Hoping that this school and course improves to top in usa like years ago...
Personally my schooling at Dunwoody was only valuable from Two instructors "Denny Steinquest and Tom Klimin " vs more than 8 i had.
The classes it required for my degree i earned at Dunwoody was good: except for a few of the unnecessary elective classes required. I refused to be part of several movies in class we were required to watch to pass the class. It was a movie that my religion does not support.

Looking forward to this school improving and getting back to being top in usa as it was years ago. This review is the experience i had and a opportunity to improve.
Please take this review as a opportunity to improve and not brush under the Carpet.

12-17-2025 Was blessed to have Bill from Dunwoody out to my shop to discuss how to improve Dunwoody HVAC program and look over possible donations id like to make to boost the school.

1-8-2026 I toured the current course and was impressed. The things that impressed me were the passion that I seen from the Instructors especially Bill. I think Dunwoody is on the right course to getting Dunwoody back to being best in the world for Tradeschools!', 'The administration and financial departments are extremely difficult to deal with. Five months after graduation, the school closed my email account while I was still searching for a job. Career services offered little to no support for employment in my field. Career fairs largely involved companies collecting resumes with no apparent intent to hire students from Dunwoody.', 'Waste of time and money if you are wanting an architecture degree for residential design look somewhere else. They focus on nothing but commercial design with nothing being remotely realistic to in field experience. They just give you 16 weeks to creat a commercial design based off a location and certain requirements with unlimited “imagination and budget” there has been no residential design or architecture related classes and 1/3 of the classes are not pertaining to architecture. The only thing i am taking home from this college is the diploma and liscence accreditations but nothing from this program will help in a future of residential design', 'Would have had a better experience if they didn’t recommend I move into THE QUAD ON DELAWARE I have been suffering ever since while they cared very little about it. I have since dropped out of Dunwoody just because we’re in college doesn’t mean we should live in terrible living conditions. stop using college as an excuse to trick students into giving you money. This school costs so much and yet they chose the most cheapest option for student housing…', 'As I reflect on my professional journey in the electrical contracting industry, I can trace my success back to one pivotal decision: enrolling in Dunwoody (Dunwoody Institute at the time) College of Technology's Electrical Construction and Maintenance program in 1990. This program laid the foundation for everything I've accomplished in my career.

What set Dunwoody apart was their perfect balance of theoretical knowledge and hands-on application. The instructors weren't just teachers – they were industry veterans who brought real-world experience into the classroom. They taught us not just the "how" of electrical work, but the critical "why" behind every connection and system. The rigorous curriculum covered everything from basic electrical theory to advanced troubleshooting techniques, all while maintaining strict adherence to the National Electrical Code.

The lab facilities were impressive even by today's standards. We worked with actual equipment and systems we would encounter in the field, giving us confidence and competence before our first day on the job.

Beyond technical skills, Dunwoody instilled professional values that proved essential when I started my contracting business in the Twin Cities. Integrity, quality workmanship, and attention to detail weren't just buzzwords – they were principles we lived by during our training.

When I launched my electrical contracting business, I found myself thoroughly prepared for the technical challenges. Dunwoody translated directly to business success.

Today, as I look at my electrical contracting business serving the Twin Cities area, I'm grateful for the solid foundation Dunwoody provided. Their program didn't just teach me a trade – it launched a successful career and business that has provided for my family and contributed to our community's infrastructure for decades.']

name: Ridgewater College
reviews:
['Staff is very helpful and the campus has several programs including automotive, nursing and CDL training.', 'Ridgewater is a great place to do schooling and as a hub for testing. The proctor pleasantly let us know that there was a communication issue with the vendor of our tests, and that we would need to reschedule at no additional cost. Tried college again in 2024 and I love Ridgewater College, I love the atmosphere and the support I receive from my teachers, faculty, and administration. I'm having so much fun that a year of my two year program flew by in a heartbeat. And I can tell you what, when I graduate, I am gonna miss being here so much.

Jon, Kevin, Tutor Eric, My Advisors, all have been amazing and support me throughout my academic career. name: Century College
reviews:
['If you prefer clear information, communication and assistance for virtually any process (enrollment, financial aid, business office), Century College is not for you. It’s impossible to get any help unless it’s automated text messages. Emails & calls? Forget about it. Don’t understand something? Too bad. It has been by far the worst experience I’ve had when trying to accomplish something so important…and expensive. If you read info on their website, it might be correct, but good luck trying to actually figure it out as no one will answer your call. You’ll just get hung up on. Not to mention, IF you ever get in contact with someone, take the info they give you with a grain of salt…it’s probably also incorrect. Pick a school that will actually be responsive and helpful. It sounds like a small thing, but it’s not.', 'For Spring Semester I met with my advisor to make sure I took the correct courses to graduate in the spring of 2024. I was made aware that I only needed two art courses left. I decided to use the rest of my GI Bill on a third course so I can be considered a full time student. I passed all my classes and was made eligible to walk on Graduation day. However, months later I received word I needed two more art electives on top of that and did not receive my Art Degree. I am disappointed because now I have to use another semester to finish, when I should’ve been done already. Now I have to postpone my plans for four months just to go back and finish.', "This is the best Community College in the State, maybe even the Universe. The students here are very inclusive and open minded and the staff is genuinely interested in making things easier and accommodating.
The average price of a semester is the lowest I've ever seen, and the quality of education is very high.
I recommend this College.", "It's a yes from me. Choose century college. You won't regret it. Be sure to always contact your academic advisors. You will face challenges if you ignore their input. Sit and discuss your challenges and goals with them. They were and still are very helpful to me.", 'My academic advisor deserved a 1/5, my professors deserved 5/5s. Some professors phoned it in, others were amazing. I received a high quality education for little to no cost and had a full time job as a software developer before I had even transferred to UMN Twin Cities.

Always try to speak primarily with a transfer advisor at the institution you want to transfer to rather than an academic advisor at Century. They will often leave out information that could result in serious delays. Many of the transfer programs at Century only apply to Minnesota State schools and not University of Minnesota as they are part of different academic systems.']

name: Belhaven University
reviews:
['Belhaven has been such a great fit for my college years! Throughout my time here, I have witnessed how the professors and students are truly committed to helping me achieve my goals. From weekly chapel to Reformed University Fellowship (RUF) meetings to student-led Bible studies, the Bible clearly lies at the center of Belhaven University. I would definitely recommend Belhaven to anyone looking to grow in their faith, gain knowledge, and become a more-well rounded person!', 'I’ve genuinely enjoyed my experience at Belhaven University. From the beginning, I felt supported not just academically, but personally as well. The professors are knowledgeable, approachable, and truly invested in their students’ success. They don’t just teach the material they take the time to connect it to real life, faith, and professional growth, which has made my coursework meaningful and practical.

What I appreciate most about Belhaven is the sense of community. Even in an online setting, I’ve never felt like just a number. Communication has been clear, help is always available when needed, and there’s a consistent encouragement to grow both intellectually and spiritually.

Belhaven has challenged me to think critically, strengthened my confidence, and helped prepare me for what’s next. I would absolutely recommend Belhaven to anyone looking for a quality education grounded in Christian values and genuine care for students.', 'A Supportive, Values-Driven University Experience

Belhaven University truly stands out as an institution that cares about its students both academically and personally. The faculty and staff were welcoming, knowledgeable, and genuinely invested in student success. Professors are accessible, supportive, and bring real-world experience into the classroom, making the coursework practical as well as engaging.

Belhaven’s Christian worldview is thoughtfully integrated into the curriculum, creating an environment that encourages integrity, critical thinking, and personal growth. The smaller class sizes make a big difference—students are known by name, questions are encouraged, and mentorship feels authentic rather than transactional.

If you’re looking for a university that combines strong academics, personal attention, and faith-based values in a supportive community, Belhaven University is an excellent choice. I would highly recommend it to anyone seeking a meaningful and well-rounded college experience.', 'I absolutely love this school! The schools security is so amazing! All of the professors that I have had here have been so wonderful when it comes to caring for their students and having a genuine will to serve the students in whatever way they can. I have learned so much about God here. There are not many clubs but the ones we have are great! The food could be better but overall not bad. I have furthered my relationship so much with God here and I am so grateful for the opportunities I have been given.', "Belhaven University is one of the flagship schools of christendom in the U.S. Committed Belhaven students are involved in many clubs and organizations that aim to encourage the search for Truth and the furtherance of God's kingdom on the individual and global scale. Staff are ready and willing to serve and seek to provide students with all the amenities they deserve. If you are looking for a warm welcome, effectual encouragement, and spiritual growth, put Belhaven at the top of your list!"]

name: Hinds Community College
reviews:
['I am an online student. I came to this location to pick up my books and figured it would be best since it is the main campus. I had my toddler in a stroller. I walked all the way across campus to make it to the book store. Once I did, I picked up my books and headed across the hall to the actual book store. I had my toddler in a stroller with a diaper bag because thats what you do when you have kids; you go everywhere prepared.

Upon entering the book store, I wanted to look around at merch and see if they had anything else I needed. I was greeted by racist workers profiling me. They never took their eyes off of me from the time I entered to the time I left. Once I made a loop around the store and made it to the laptops and started to look at pricing, one staff member comes and stands at the door and ask me if I need any help. I tell her no because her tone was very clear. She then holds the door open for me to leave as if the laptops are near the door; they are not.

As I was leaving, she tried to crack a joke with me and I kept walking because I know exactly what they were doing. I called the book store once I got in the car and told her everything they did and that I was going to file a complaint. She goes, "ok," and hung up in my face because she knew what they were doing no apology, no empathy, no misunderstanding  a simple ok and click.

Not everyone who attends college is 18 and childless. I am almost 30; I am not a kid wondering around campus. Why was I profiled for bringing my baby and diaper bag with me while handling business on campus? I am strongly considering transferring schools. I have had bad experiences at Raymond and Jackson campuses; staff are awful and barely want to work. Raymond library staff are racially profiling students in a book store. I attend Pearl campus to suit all my needs; I live in Rankin, its closer and convenient. I thought I would give Raymond a try with it being the main campus. I will never return.', 'The campus doesn’t look to “bare minimum” nor “quality” standard at move in. Landscape is terrible. The elevators need repainting and bathroom showers need some attention. The university is making enough to have these matters resolved.', 'Financial aid department has drained me of my patience. I don’t know why I always get the inexperienced associates. I attend Hinds the entire year of 2024. Unfortunately for 2025 Spring semester I must now pay out of pocket again ( I can’t afford it). I was told by two associates in financial aid that my government loans were concisely filled out and they were being processed. Jokes on me because now I’ve been told that my promissory note wasn’t completed. At the time I was told it was. To add insult to injury the school doesn’t have a payment plan. God bless the two party system for creating laws to prevent citizens from obtaining a decent education.', 'All of the reviews are correct!!!! especially with the financial aid I was told I owed money and did not I had to turn in documents. I transferred over to the Rankin campus thinking it would be better. It is not I am probably going to miss my graduation because they have not informed us of anything and claim they know nothing not even the day of graduation!!!!! This is ridiculous you have to do everything by yourself because they will not take initiative until it is too late!', 'I don’t go to the school in Raymond I go to a different campus. The financial aid counselor has a weird schedule at my home campus so, I usually just talk and fax things over to Raymond. Just because it’s more for convenient for me..  When it comes to  financial aid, you have to be careful who you speak with. Some of them are not experienced, I would assume. I was told I owed thousands of dollars. Then I called the business office and was told that’s untrue. She told me that I needed to speak to someone different. So I call again and I speak to someone else and they figure everything out. I actually didn’t owe anything.. I just had to turn in certain documents. PLEASE be careful who you speak with… I still have issues with some people I speak with over the phone. I just don’t think I should have to speak to 5 different people to figure out my financial situations. That alone is extremely stressful. I guess I’ll stick with my home campus..']

name: Millsaps College
reviews:
['Thank you, Millsaps College. You gave me a chance, the stability to grow, to learn more than I had expected, to expand into fields I had dreamed of but thought impossible to plow. You were the base to launch my career far beyond the limits of my imagination. Did I achieve what I wanted? Honestly, so much more than that. 50 years later, I am grateful as ever. This is not the forum for me to catalogue my achievements, wealth and satisfaction, but to say thank you to the professors of bygone days, the administrators for their patience, the abundance of knowledge showered upon me. When I doubted, friends lifted my head, eye lids and spirit. When I fell, friends picked me up and showed me the path. I loved you, and I still do.', '[Short version: I am a gay trans man who was facing abuse by my family in 2016 when I joined the college. The abuse was perpetuated and made worse by the Millsaps administration because they spied on us and told us they would report any "rule breaking" (i.e. dating someone whose parents didn't approve of same sex relationships) to our parents, in addition to reporting our counseling information and other personal matters.]

When I went there in 2016, they had me in an office room with an abusive family member and a counselor (I don't know what her if that was her actual position but that's what I registered her as). I was 18 and the counselor was helping my family member force me to sign some kind of personal information release because my family did not want a gay, trans kid and were doing everything in their power to change that. I had a partner at the time, and my Southern Baptist family and their Catholic family wanted us to break up (their family did the same thing and forced my partner at the time to sign the release of information).

Brit Katz and others said they would be watching me and they would report anything to our parents. They watched us in our dorm building, they watched us in the cafeteria, they watched us walking on campus. They made calls and emails to our parents. They made us go to counseling to "process the breakup" and then they gave our parents access to our mental health records. At one point, Patrick Cooper called out to my partner when they were walking with a group of people during trick or treating in the dorms and wouldn't allow my partner to go down my hall even though they weren't going to my dorm. They controlled us, they spied on us, they took away our freedoms and rights, and they use "family values" to justify it. We continued our relationship in secret, as it was our right to do so, but we hid it in public spaces. One day we were separately headed from the cafeteria to our shared dorm building (I was farther behind and they were farther ahead) Dean Katz passed by us and was smiling and acting friendly and said hello to both of us separately. When I shortly after had a panic attack and chased him and said "It's not what it looks like. We live in the same building. We eat in the same cafeteria. We are going to cross paths at some point." He turned to me and he was frowning so deeply and his face was so drastically different from his friendly demeaner he normally held. He told me he had better never see that again and he would be considering contacting our families. I continued to have panic attacks for weeks in fear that he was going to report it to them. There is so so much more, and this is only a sampling of what we went through. We had to stop going to eat in the cafeteria, stop going to clubs, stop existing in public spaces, etc. We could have broken up, but us together was the only way we were able to escape the abuse.

Millsaps is not pro-LGBT like they say they are. This is not a safe space. They only care about the parents paying them more money. Do not go to this school. They also have a student organization whose sole purpose is to spy on students and report back to the administrators. They draw eyes all over campus and make statements that they're watching you. It behaves like a cult, and it destroyed my mental health and I almost did not make it out with my life.

I would have sued them if I knew I could, but I was an abused teenager with no other support system and had to endure it for another year and a half before I had to drop out of school, flee my family's influence, and lose housing. If I had to choose between visiting/attending Millsaps again or being homeless again, I would take being homeless any day.', 'Terrible. Racist, Discriminating, Injust. Students have been outed for performing black face and calling fellow students racial slurs. With no consequences. While the abused face suspension. Tweeiblw School. Terrible Board. Terrible students. Terrible.', 'Beautiful architecture at this university. Friendly staff and fun atmosphere for a football game. Home side bleachers are shadier midday, but cramped bc it is TIGHT seating area. Visitors side much roomier.', 'Give Dr. James Bowley his job back, he is award winning and all he did was share his opinion with three students just three over an email, GIVE THIS TEACHER BACK HIS JOB!!!']

name: Mississippi College
reviews:
['Well I attended MC for two semester in attempt to received my BS degree could not finish because of an illness but my classes I had there help me to be employee of the month three times at Raytheon Aerospace in Madison learning new software and my data base class was extremely helpful so thanks for the best experience of my life Godspeed', 'I wish I could say I was proud of where I graduated, but years after the fact, I can't. It wasn't for lack of involvement--I was heavily involved in several student organizations, worked on campus in Residence Life, and academically excelled every year of my experience. I was well-liked and popular with students, faculty, and staff alike. My experience itself was golden. However, the college has morphed into something I can't in good faith promote to others.

Mississippi College values image over all else. Don't be deceived--the values it purports to uphold mean nothing to its administration. "Integrity" and "respect" are vain buzzwords. In reality, they mean nothing when it comes to the student body and faculty. Pursuing knowledge and truth only matters when those versions match MC's narrative. And to civilly disagree with or share opinions against this narrative means excommunication from its community and losing your livelihood. MC has loudly and proudly shown what it truly values: conformity, silence, and compliance.

Don't misunderstand me. There are wonderful, kind, Christ-centered people at this institution. They model critical thinking, analysis of ideas, and civil discourse to their students. But if you're looking for a college where you, too, get to grow and become a part of that community, this is not the place for you.', 'Very glad my niece chose this college over Ole Miss. I like both, yet, when it comes to education, safety and laying the foundation for excellence Mississippi College is better.', 'Lovely historic liberal arts school and ca.pus', 'I had a great experience, though several of my friends did not. name: Mississippi State University
reviews:
['I do not recommend Mississippi State University based on my enrollment and administrative experience.

I applied in August 2025 and was accepted within a few weeks. I was told I would be assigned an advisor or enrollment counselor to help me get registered that never happened. After several weeks of no contact, I personally reached out to the head of the program I was trying to enter, and she was able to get me enrolled. I believed that resolved the issue, but unfortunately it did not.

Shortly after, I noticed three $50 course change fees and three $50 Bulldog Bundle charges on my account. I had not changed any courses, and I did not want the Bulldog Bundle because I had already purchased my books. I contacted the Registrar’s Office, which was extremely difficult to work with I was transferred multiple times and given conflicting information. I was told the course change fees were charged by the department and the Bulldog Bundle was handled by Barnes & Noble.

Barnes & Noble informed me that an opt-out email should have been sent to me but confirmed that I never received it. They even contacted the university on my behalf to request a waiver since the failure was clearly not mine and the university refused.

I then contacted the head of my department regarding the “course change” fees. After investigating, she informed me they were actually late registration fees not course change fees — even though I only registered late because the university failed to assign me an advisor as promised. The fees were still not waived.

To make matters worse, my official transfer credits were submitted months ago, and as I am now approaching my second semester, those credits still do not appear in my degree plan.

This has been an ongoing pattern of administrative failure: missed communications, incorrect charges, lack of support, and a refusal to correct mistakes that were not mine.

I genuinely like the instructors, and I enjoy the academic program itself but the administrative side of this university has been unprofessional, disorganized, and frustrating. If these issues are not resolved, I will be transferring to another institution such as Arizona State University.

Mississippi State University needs to do better.', 'Everyone was so nice and helpful.
The room was clean and looked good
I felt comfortable leaving my loved one there to continue her education.
Loved Mississippi State.', "Rescued a sweet pitty mix with a cherry eye. Got a Morgan's Pocket procedure done. Easily the best veterinarian experience I've ever had. 5 stars is not enough. From the first day we ran in during a storm and someone immediately offered us a towel to dry off, to checking on our progress post  operation through text and calls to the last day of follow up exam was nothing but excellence. I don't see it getting any better than this.", 'This place is the worst. I’m paying forty dollars to stay early and can’t even check in every winter and the food might as well be purina. Only go here if you want to hate yourself', 'The BEST college campus ever. It’s so clean, beautiful, and the people here are so friendly. The traditions are amazing and sporting events are awesome! Look for another place or you will encounter the reality in your own life.', "The people comment's about the lack of commitment and profissional behavior are completely true. name: Mission University
reviews:
['We have a grandson going to school here. He really likes the school.', "Graduated with my BA from here in 2017. Great school for learning some ins and outs of ministry. Thankful they allow college kids to be college kids and not dress like they are going to an office job all day. I was apart of the band for 2 years and have some of my most fun memories traveling for Breakaway. Don't let the old boomers scare you from attending ;)", 'I’ve attended BBC off and on for a few years now, both in-person and online. I recommend them for anyone considering ministry within the Baptist Church. Their emphasis on biblically based doctrine is something you don’t get at a lot of modern Christian schools. The Professors there actually care about each student, and go out of their way to help them succeed. The admin and student life departments are the same way. I know a lot of students who have come and gone, and many have gone on to have successful, God honoring ministries that reflect what they learned at BBC. The school has come a long way in recent years, developing championship level sports teams, remodeling and updating facilities, and ministering to students in churches across the country through camps and worship teams. Like any college, if you aren’t committed, you won’t succeed here, but if you’re looking for a community that’s Christ-centered, wants to see you succeed in your calling, and will help you grow, this is the place to be.', 'When I attended BBC it was still on the Old Paths. I loved my time at BBC back then. I met my Husband there and have been serving with him in the Ministry for 30 years. Now I see girls wearing ripped jeans and short shorts.  They do praise and worship sessions that look like a rock concert. I wish they had not changed. My children went to different Bible Colleges that still are on the Old Path. I believe in a Biblical View from the King James Bible, I believe that Women should dress modestly and look like a Lady. The Old Path is the right Path.', 'My wife and I have ambivalent memories about attending and graduating from BBC back in the early '90s. I enjoyed the challenges of learning theology from Mr. Pratt and Dr. Dell, as well as history from Ray Adams and Eli Harju. I really didn't care much for Dr. Dowell, Jr.. He seemed pretentious to me. Then there was Richard Bemarkt (sp?) and Dr. Sherman, who really opened my eyes when it came to Bible versions, especially when considering the biblical languages. I no longer exclusively use the KJV, even though from time to time I'll reference it in whatever studies I might be doing.

Life on campus was, eh, okay. Shirt and tie to class was something I had to get used to. That said, I remember my wife wearing her nurse's slacks to work one day and me getting called into the office for that. Back then the women were not allowed to wear pants, even though after that episode, it was understood by BBC that that stricture cannot always apply in all situations at all times. It is my understanding that BBC has now gone way off the deep end when it comes to dress requirements and now pretty much allows anything to be worn, which I don't think is wise, if it is true.

One other thing I've noticed recently about BBC is how expensive it is to attend. Six hundred dollars a credit hour for bachelor's work!? What happened? Did the churches quit supporting the school? Back when I attended, it was $55/credit hour, mainly because the churches were committed to supporting the product it was turning out and helped to subsidize the student cost. I guess BBC officials found it more lucrative to go the way of the world in that respect. Oh, and I see that student housing fees have skyrocketed through the roof too. Since my wife and I lived in C and then B dorms, our rent was like $150/month. But now it's around $800+/mo., which means that if we wanted to attend today, the cost itself, between tuition, rent, and some ridiculous fees that are being charged would make it prohibitive. Frankly, I don't think Jesus Christ himself would approve.

A few years ago I spoke and emailed back and forth with a BBC official about possibly teaching at the school. But, the more I thought about it, the more it just did not seem like a good idea. Since graduating from BBC I've gone on to earn an MA in Christian Apologetics, the MDiv and ThM in New Testament, and a PhD in Theology, all from accredited schools, both in the US and abroad. So, I would be more than qualified to teach whatever courses BBC had in its curriculum. The main sticking-point, though, would be theological inconsistency in what I've read in the BBC Statement about what it claims to believe. Therefore, it would not be long before I would be pointing out things like "free will" when it comes to salvation and how it does not jive with God's sovereignty, OR, how the whole Rapture doctrine cannot be defended, once the Scriptures are consistently exegeted using a sound grammatical-historical hermeneutic. So, all discussions and email exchanges simply ended by my choice.

BBC was an interesting time during our life's journey, but given what I know now that I did not know then, I could not repeat it. I will not go so far as to call it a "cult," like some have, because that is sheer ignorance, not knowing what a theological cult is, much less what the Scriptures teach about "wolves in sheep's clothing." I will simply say there were some good and bad things that happened, just like there are in pretty much all situations and walks in life, and if the Lord is leading you there, good for you. Make the best of your time, be wise with what little money you'll have while attending, and think critically about what you're going to be taught. Because once you leave, and if you're discerning, as you should be, you will learn that your education has only just begun.']

name: Central Christian College of the Bible
reviews:
["The School atmosphere is very negative and spiritually drained. During the chapel people don't have the desire to even be there. School has very poor leadership. They offer very little help to students who struggle academically and spiritually. It has zero activities for students to connect and make the school experience miserable.  The school spends great amount of energy arguing about theology differences rather then seeking unity of Christ-ship and fellowship. Although, there are few students who has very good experiences there are many who has very negative experience and later ending up walking away from the faith. I would not send my kids to this school!!!", "The ABHE is a national accrediting body, but the accreditation that really means anything comes from the regional accrediting bodies. Most regionally-accredited schools (that is, any traditional university) won't want transfer credits from a nationally-accredited program.

Degrees from places like this are essentially worthless outside of the fundamentalist circles where they're popular. In fact, in some cases, they're worse than worthless, because they speak lowly of the students who pursue them.", 'My time at Central Christian College of the Bible was excellent. I received an education that was both theologically challenging and ministerially practical. I was able to engage in ministry opportunities, including being a Residence Assistant, leading worship in chapel, spending two summers on a camp team, and even being the Youth Minister at a church. You can't beat graduating college with 4 years of experience leading in your area of study!
In addition to ministry opportunities, there were lots of ways to connect. One of those during my time was a group of us that met every week to discuss youth ministry. This was led in the home of our youth ministry professor at the time and gave us an outlet to discuss what was going on in our ministries and grow in our understanding of ministry in general. Which leads to the next thing....
The professors at Central are personable and helpful. They don't just care about teaching content, they care about the mission of the school, "to develop servant-leaders for the church." I couldn't tell you how many times Mr. Reese would say something like "down at the old country church..." in order to connect what we were learning with real situations in real churches.
All of these things, especially coupled with the opportunity for a full-tuition scholarship, makes Central Christian College of the Bible an excellent choice for Biblical higher education.', 'When my wife and I first came to Central we were drawn to the passionate focus the community and college had on raising up servant leaders. What we found when we got here was students living out that mission. Students here are committed to serving and leading beyond the classroom. I am thankful that this is a college where students can have an experience where they are noticed and where they are able to be used to their full potential.

Since I didn’t graduate from Central I like many new students I experienced everything for the first time myself. I was blown away that the college was doing so much to control student cost trough their full tuition scholarship program. It is one thing to say you have a goal of graduating students debt free. It was another to see that happen in front of me as my niece completed her education debt free at the college.
I am thankful to have spent the past seven years serving with passionate students who don’t just talk about making a difference but who actually put this in action. I am also thankful to work with and around a passionate community.

This is a great college and I hope you get a chance to come visit and share the experiences I have had!', "For those of you seeking to get a biblical degree and expand your understanding of the Bible, Central offers everything you will need.  Great teachers, amazing student body and overall great place to learn and grow in your walk with Christ.  Central offers learning opportunities outside of the classroom through plenty of different service opportunities for those who are interested in gaining practical experience.
It's affordability makes graduating debt-free a reality as it was for me.
One of the best decisions I've made in my entire life."]

name: Culver-Stockton College
reviews:
['I would not recommend this program to anyone seriously pursuing a master’s degree in education—especially if you expect adequate advising, mental health support, or basic transparency.

From the start, I was misled about the course load expectations. I only realized much later that I’d been enrolled in half the required number of classes each term, delaying my progress significantly. When I raised concerns, I was met with defensiveness and finger-pointing instead of ownership or help.

Despite reaching out multiple times about personal struggles—including tech issues accessing assignments and a close family member actively dying—I was essentially told “policies are policies,” and if I needed emotional support, to “talk to the counselor.” I wasn’t asking for a handout. I was asking for basic human decency, which this program seems to lack entirely.

This experience has left me emotionally drained and questioning whether this program was ever invested in my success at all. In grad school, I was told they “expected me not to need guidance,” which is ironic given how much I had to chase basic answers.

⸻

Post-Appeal Update

After submitting a formal appeal explaining that I had just lost my grandmother and was grieving while still trying to complete coursework, Culver-Stockton still upheld my suspension.

I’ve attached screenshots of the actual suspension letter and appeal denial for anyone who thinks I’m exaggerating. They acknowledged her passing in writing but said I “had not established a sufficiently strong case” to overturn the suspension. Let that sink in.

They claim below to have “reached out to me directly,” but no one has. I waited—gave them the benefit of the doubt. Still nothing.

If this is how they handle student support after a public review, imagine what they do (or don’t do) when no one’s looking.

This review reflects only the graduate education program, not the college as a whole. But if this is how they treat graduate students in crisis, I can’t stay silent. Others deserve to know before investing their time, money, and emotional well-being here.', 'A great local place to obtain an education. The educators and staff are friendly and knowledgeable.', 'The College is very unorganized. We have had problems at every step. The admissions office is mediocre and unorganized. They do not take care of their students. No doctor or nurse practitioner on site making it very difficult to get health care. The urgent care close buy is constantly closing early or closing due to being short staffed. The air conditioning is turned off in 84 degree weather, with old buildings and most windows not opening it’s miserable to visit let alone sleep there. The food is so processed, unhealthy very few items that taste good.  They have too many athletes on their teams, leaving so many students unhappy with their experience that if they don’t transfer they have definitely looked into transferring. However some credits will not transfer to other Colleges. Having a daughter at another College really enforces how unacceptable and inadequate this college truly is. I will note the professors  are caring and do a good job. Student-life is another problem.', 'I enjoyed and appreciated my time at
C-SC. Professors & administrators teach at a level higher than your average institution. Culver encourages students to learn and grow. The small campus has grown exponentially since 1987, however, still gives Alumni the same warm & fuzzy feeling. I’m not sure how anyone could not benefit from matriculating from C-SC; it reflects the “real world” and prepares students for that said world. Thank you for the degree & so many life lessons!', "We always stay at the Oak Hill Inn and Suites. Just off of 61 and at the entrance of CSC. Very clean, friendly staff, breakfast eggs  sausage  waffles  cereal, juice, coffee
CSC easy to get around. We came to watch quarterfinal women's soccer."]

He teaches on software the industry doesn’t use, the taught us the pure basics and nothing more, treats us terribly, the lab we work in’s AC and heat barely works, I’ve been yelled at by a security officer while I was sitting and working, and I’ve had to learn most of everything I have done myself.\n\nThis school was the worst investment I’ve sunk money into and good riddance when I’m done with it.']

reviews:

Since I've been out of college I've come back to sing and I regret nothing and I cannot wait to be more active in this program again.

If you love music and want to learn - come join any class he has", "I'm sorry, but this college almost ruined my life. reviews: ['Evangel university a small Christian university private school ranking in niche B+ in general my personal experience with Evangel  we my older son was totally awesome  I totally recommend!', 'Evangel is a great university to further your education and grow your relationship with the Lord!', 'The quality of the education, the helpfulness of the staff and instructors, and the Christian environment are, in my opinion, exemplary.
