Do not ever go here, they will screw you over a thousand fold if you even dare to leave after joining.", 'Beautiful campus and always clean. It has grown so much over the last few years.']

name: Four Rivers Career Center
reviews:
['Was a student in the automotive Collison Repair class, over all the class was amazing the instructors was amazing however Administration not so much.

In the 2 years I was at the school I was the victim of bullying which staff refused to do anything about, it wasnt the instructors faults by no means they both tried to help but were not backed by their superiors. I was told I was the issue that I should have to hide hats and jackets in small locker as well as my PPE and backpack (Side note: Lockers arent big enough for that) rather than punish the people doing it.

Another student in one day had over $350 of cash stolen from their wallet which was inside their backpack (put away) meaning the student took the time to search through their bag and stole the money, once again was told it was the victims fault.

To make things even worse, the Principal of the building when I posted my original review mentioning this and putting him on blast for not defending his students during the school year pressured me into deleted the original review, and did so infront of my Instructors.

Patents your kids will learn amazing skills at this school however be prepared to fight administrators to hold other students accountable for their actions and to protect your child.

Administrators you might want to rethink who you want incharge of your school as pressuring someone to take down a negative reveiw is textbook infringement of the 1st Amendment.', "The residents that live in the apartments directly next to the school are sick and tired of hearing the engine revving, tires squalling, AND FLYING BY LIKE WE DONT HAVE TO PARK ON THE STREET WHERE THEY'RE DOING ALL THIS.
I have an elderly mom who is bed ridden and has to hear this every day of the week just about.
We have enough noise from the street alone, and a factory directly across from us with big rigs coming and going all day long.
I have talked to a student from there and she has told me that the students have been warned about this.
I was a high school student obviously, and I remember what it felt like when school is out. But I've never seen and heard this many custom vehicles at one school. Some cars are louder than diesel trucks!!!  (Like the burgundy Jetta with the stack coming out the hood).  Police sit and monitor traffic right in front of the school off hours all the time. Never during school to monitor the students. If we have to follow the law while driving, they should be made to be a little more conscience too.
Kids will be kids. I have a system in my car that definitely would exceed city ordinance in areas that enforce it. But I try to be mindful with it. PLEASE have your students try to keep this in mind.", "This place reminded me of 8th grade allover, I was a student in the machinest program and I learned a lot. It was excellent, mostly hands on and verry little bookwork. But having said that,, the place was remineciant of 8th grade, a few of the students were rowdy and acted like children which made it more difficult for the rest of us who were there to learn. You learn by doing, not by misbehaving!  The school should have weeded out these juviniles: Instead; they threw them in with the rest of us.  Anyway, I guess  you meet such immature people in industry as well so that's part of the learning process . All in all this brings me to what I wanted to say: Through the years manufacturing things is not what we do  in this country anymore. It's cheaper to offshore the manufacturing jobs.   Most jobs today are in the medical field  technology and other service industries. The kind of jobs that you can't outsource to other countries. So, if I were a student I would concentrate on computers, medical or the construction industry. Rather than in manufacturing ;however unfornatuletly, you'll still haft to deal with juvenile behavior there as well.", 'The nursing program is a joke and continues to decline. Run while you can do not waste your time or money. There is ONE good instructor who knows what she is doing and talking about. Their fail rates are increasing each year. School is money hungry', 'Went to school here a few years back enjoyed every second of it. Staff was awesome. Teachers were very passionate about making sure everyone learned as much as they could in the time they had.']

name: Kansas City Art Institute
reviews: ['Wonderful place to visit. Beautiful campus and talented students.', 'I went there for a summer program, and I loved the campus and the rooms! I absolutely hated my professor, though. I was in the animation program, and for our final project, I had lost sleep and skipped meals just to get it done. In fact, our instructors had us sit down with them and pre-approved our concepts before we started them. A day before it was due, I showed him what I had done so far (that he pre-approved, mind you), and he simply said, "That\'s all?" Like... what? Yeah, alright. This animation you pre-approved, yeah, that\'s all. I don\'t know what else you were expecting, but at least it wasn\'t a fake tree that people breathe into. Like, what even is that? (That\'s was one of his projects for his college.) It just felt like him, along with some other professors, were really negative and underappreciating of the hard work students put in. I get criticism, and I thrive off of it. But simply saying, "That\'s it?" is NOT what I paid for. Not helpful, not positive, not even constructive. It\'s just terrible. The food was also kinda mid. Anyway, I hope this helps. I hope whoever goes avoids that professor because he\'s just way too full of himself.', 'Very clean buildings, beautiful landscape, community activities, great teachers', 'Great small school with caring staff and professors.', "Beautiful facility with alot of diversity and green space. My daughter currently attends school here and couldn't be happier."]

name: Lindenwood University
reviews: ['Lindenwood used to be a great school, but over the past two to four years (COVID-19, economic issues, changes of presidents at the school) it\'s gone downhill tremendously. The recurrent cancellation of courses, issues with the cloud that the school uses (i.e., Amazon Web Services) which leads to the shutting down of the education portal (called Canvas), poor leadership from deans, and hihring low-quality professors, have all exploded in this timeline. More work is put on adjunct professors with no pay increase. Full-time teachers seem to only care about keeping their positions by ingratiating those "in charge", but not keeping the trademarks of education or of the university at the forefront of their practice. Tenured professors no longer have a grip on their mission statements and appear to only want to "make it to retirement" (I have actually heard an English department professor say this to a student). The university increased prices for credit hours, yet the quality has decreased so significantly that it\'s astounding. I have two degrees from the university already and am working on a third. However, staying on track to graduate with them is nearly impossible, due to repeatedly dropping the ball, not offering courses that they affirm they have available, and cutting courses down, appeasing primarily the undergraduate course catalog. The value is low, and even in graduate courses, the professors give assignments that I have assigned to high school students in the past... They appear to also be infatuated with busy work, which many of us teachers know is a time-waster and not conducive to proper scaffolding. Generic responses from administration, such as “Please reach out to your academic advisor so we can address this,” are unhelpful due to slow response times on issues that require quick assistance. Additionally, the staff are not always sharp when it comes to decision-making and problem-solving. They give off energy that screams "I\'m just hear for the paycheck". Please think very hard before applying. Lindenwood is simply not the institution it once was.', 'I received my MFA in Writing from Lindenwood. Outstanding university committed to rigor and craft tools needed to be successful.', 'Beautiful campus and they offer great degree programs. This particular visit was for a football game.', 'Keeps calling me about an environmental survey and won’t take me off their list despite asking multiple times.', 'It is one of the oldest institutions in Saint Louis and the Mid West. The architecture is very attractive, likewise, the campus is very large.']

I stood up for a bullied student and confronted a bully the school counselor said i shouldnt do that. There is a process for that behavior.', 'I use to come here for my morning work outs. Lots of gym equipment/basketball courts, food court etc', 'the teachers here are jokes. it kinda just seems like the school is as well with how much they back their teachers up even if they know they are in the wrong. there are so many other colleges and programs save yourself and look elsewhere', 'Do not go here for aviation, it used to be the staple of this school way back when but now it is just a money grab. Actually having a teacher stay to teach Aviation has been struggling for the last 2 years and actually get “qualified” teachers to teach this trade. Don’t waste your money here, spend the extra money on a school that actually has a structure and good atmosphere. One more problem is the actual school will barely fund this program. All they focus on is other programs and aviation gets the bad end of the stick.', "I feel it is crucial to bring attention to the concerning atmosphere at this school. Over the past few years, I have observed troubling behavior from certain teachers that raises significant concerns about their mental health and ability to manage a classroom effectively.

Several teachers have exhibited tendencies to lash out at students for seemingly no reason, creating an environment of fear rather than support. This kind of behavior is unacceptable and detrimental to the students’ well-being and educational experience.

It is imperative that this school be thoroughly investigated to address these issues. Our children deserve to be in a safe, nurturing environment where they can learn and grow without fear of being treated harshly by their educators. I urge parents and the community to advocate for change and ensure that the mental health of teachers is taken seriously, as it directly impacts our children's education and safety."]

name: Metropolitan Community College-Kansas City
reviews:
['I have had terrible experiences with this college on almost every level. Administration will mess up your paperwork and then make you jump through hoops to correct it. They will overcharge you on tuition, drop you from your classes without notice due to their incorrect billing, and then refuse to place you back into the classes that you’ve already purchased materials for (which is a large nonrefundable expense). I had already completed the first two weeks of class when they dropped me from the course without notice, and then they stated they were unable to place me back into the class because the start date had passed. Then, they will offer to assist you enrolling in a course again next semester, as if you have any desire to return to their college after they just charged you hundreds of dollars that you won’t get back and made the process difficult. I transferred from this college and had a much better experience, as well as completed my degree, at the other college. I returned to this college for one specific online class and I immediately regret that decision. Save your time and money, go somewhere else.', 'I’ve always felt that this college offers classes that are a great fit for older students and those who work full-time, flexible, accessible, and generally supportive. Unfortunately, the administrative side of things doesn’t always reflect that same reliability, and today was a perfect example of how a single weak link can bring the entire system to a halt.

I was trying to get in touch with someone who could help me obtain a syllabus for a class I took here in 2022, a simple, routine request. Instead, I found myself calling the information center eight times and speaking with a few different people, only to end the day without a single step forward.

To be fair, a couple of the staff members were kind and genuinely tried to help. The first representative even tried two different methods when the first one didn’t work, and I appreciated the effort.

But the rest of the experience? Needlessly frustrating. One staff member barely said a word before immediately placing me on hold. Another call dropped the moment they picked up. And the last representative I spoke to, someone I had actually spoken with earlier, flat-out refused to help further after I explained that the previous transfer attempt caused the call to drop. She apologized, but then dismissed me, entirely refusing to try anything again.

I understand that technical issues happen. Truly, I do. But for every call to drop, all eight times, right after (or during) an attempted transfer? That stretches well past “technical glitch” territory and into something that reflects poor systems or poor processes, neither of which should be the customer’s problem.

What should have been a five-minute request turned into an hour-long exercise in patience. I sincerely hope the college takes a look at its phone system and training, because students and former students deserve better than this.', 'Worst school ever to deal with. The financial aid department has no idea what they are doing I have watched them screw up multiple student accounts last semester and this semester. The advisors keep saying the are busy and don’t know what to do Financial aid has stopped taking calls because they know they screwed up and there’s no way to speak to anyone higher up to get your issues resolved.
Run as far as you can from this school!!!', 'Not bad if you’re needing to start fresh in a career and they offer great courses for a degree or a trade certificate.

Good luck trying to get help by calling that number. I had some books that I bought but never used but I didn’t have the receipt. I called and explained my situation and the lady on the phone told me “you can try” When I asked, if its possible to return books without a receipt. Oh yeah.. if they say you need “x” book for a course you’re taking.. 9/10 You won’t ever use it. Instead they make you pay more for third party software on top of the courses you’re already paying for! Great! Spend more money!

Sometimes staff are unhelpful. I had failed a math class in my first semester (yeah I know, I was never an egg head in math) and my counselor either didn’t know or didn’t care and put me in an advanced math class I was never supposed to be in. I had asked the professor about it and he told me I was never on his roster so I went down to student services and met with a different counselor who told me “You were added in there by mistake. You were never supposed to be in that class” oh really? Thanks!

I’d also recommend using “Rate My Professors” before committing to a class because some of these professors are unnecessarily hard asses, don’t explain things well or correctly and never reference the syllabus after the first day.

They need to re-open the cafeteria and stop supplementing it with fast food joints and vending machines with sub-par “food” options.

In my opinion and experience, I’d use MCC as a base for a trade program rather than college itself, there’s much better college options out there if you can afford it.', 'They changed the policy for this semesters refund dates without notification and are now threatening to drop me from my classes and make me pay 4k for them anyway. This kind of corruption is disgusting. Previously you could drop a class for refund almost halfway into the semester. Now you have 5 days after classes start allegedly. The vast difference just screams scam. Especially having to pay such a large sum of money for literally nothing if they drop me from the classes.']

name: Maryville University of Saint Louis
reviews:
['I was robbed of my freshmen college experience going here. I come from Kentucky for the direct PT entry, but even that couldn't make me stay. I knew I wasn't going to a school that wouldn't have great campus life, but I didn't know the college experience here is this horrible. If your not on a sports team or in a program that you love don't go here.

1. NO SOCIAL LIFE: this school is for people who are instate and just all about the school side of your college experience. Everyone leaves on the weekend they provide no reason for people to stay and make campus life fun. They offer poor excuses of "activities" and clubs are stressful and annoying to be apart of.

2. The food is terrible for the price they offer. You can't not survive on a meal plan here without being hungry all the time. The food is horrible and maybe you could survive on the best meal plan but why spend all that money on campus bad food when you can spend it on better options.

3. For a school that prides themself on their e-sports team the internet is very mid. I had many times where my assignment take forever to load and using any console to play games was horrible.

4. They make you take require classes that don't provide you any value, but just for them to earn some money off you.

5. 96% acceptance rate is really evident.

Again if your not here for a sports team or your fine with not having a campus life and being bored then go here. BUT, if your outstate don't even think about it. I really regret coming here now I can't get back my Freshmen college experience that I wished for.', "THIS SCHOOL SUCKS!!! Horrible online structure, leaves students in the dark about where to even start or go for information. I WAS SWORN UP & DOWN AT INTERVIEW I'D RECEIVE ASSISTANCE WITH PLACEMENT FOR CLINICAL!! NOPE I ended up paying thousands to an online site to find clinical placement. Professors (except Prof. Aaron Langford) are completely useless. They post instructions for am assignment only to later turn out to be incorrect thus affecting your grade. Oh, they also make you take extra classes that you've already taken to get extra money! Not worth the money or stress! STEER CLEAR!", 'The in-seat classes here are alright, but the online classes are very bad. The online classes barely have any of their own course material, and send you to complete LinkedIn courses, or to watch random YouTube videos. When they do have textbooks, they don't tell you what to read. They use online discussion boards for every assignment and act like that's teaching or learning something. Feedback will be "Good job" or "didn't write enough", which teaches you nothing. Their online option feels like checking a box and will not prepare you for a career.', 'I have attended and successfully completed 2 other online programs at other institutions. I started the NP program at Maryville and quickly regretted it. They use so many different programs and apps. I always felt I was missing information. The exams are heavily weighted and the preparation for them are terrible. They provide study guides that encompass the entire content! This program was terrible. It’s definitely not designed for working parents. It’s more for those that can devote time chasing information. I learned more from YouTubes than the “lectures”.', 'The masters program part time for the nurse practitioner program was so intense. The school made you believe that you can work and still be a full time mother in the program, WRONG. I went through 4 classes and the fifth class I was required to study hours a day because nursing exams are required. Unfortunately, I can’t get my money back. I wish the school was more honest and not sure if I’m going back next semester. There was no way I was going to do a 16 week course this summer where I had to study nonstop and my children are on summer break. It was impossible to do, so I had no choice but to withdraw. Program is costly as well, costing around 6k a semester. I’ve decided to not go back for my masters, too expensive.']

I highly recommend this shop to anyone looking for reliable and efficient car service!']

name: Missouri Valley College
reviews: ['It’s a nice, small college. I’m majoring in Elementary Education and I love my professors. The only thing is that if you don’t participate in a sport or activity on campus you will feel extremely left out. I’ve been here 3 semesters and I’ve never been able to make friends or fit in on campus. It’s great for athletic students and they often get scholarships, but if you’re not planning on participating in activities on campus then it probably isn’t for you.', 'DO NOT GO HERE. This school is a sad excuse for a university. My sister went here for two years and nothing good came of it. The school makes you bring your own A/C unit for your dorms, and their housing contract basically makes the student liable for anything that goes wrong in the dorms. My sister had a brick thrown through her window during the winter and housing had no urgency to the situation. It took two weeks for them to come to “fix it” by simply putting up a  piece of cardboard and some tape. The Vice President of Student Affairs, Heath Morgan, refused to do anything about the situation and hung up in my face multiple times when I addressed concern for my sister’s safety. I asked to set an appointment to meet with him and he refused, even though it is his job to meet with concerned students and family. The lack of professionalism among faculty and staff is sad and disheartening. If you are considering going to school here, don’t waste your time or money. You’re better off going to a state university, with actual regards for student well-being and professional faculty, for less money.', 'Awesome place and coaching staff!!! Felt like family.', 'Absolutely a perfect College Football weekend. Thank you, for a wonderful weekend. Thank you, Dr. Humphrey & your entire staff for making our 1966 Hall of Fame Baseball team feel special. Everyone was so nice, it made for this a very special moment for all of the team members. name: University of Missouri-St Louis
reviews:
["I visited this campus in Fall of 2025 to assist my daughter with moving in and settling on dorm. She had chosen UMSL as her place to shine and prepare for the next phase of life. This selection was made from a pool of over 20 universities all covering varying degrees of scholarships. UMSL checked all our boxes and was not the least expensive, however our daughter's and our peace of mind was not to be compromised. Communication with her Recruiter/Advisor, Matheus was seamless leading up to and after making the choice.  Matheus even visited our island as part of his recruitment strategy and it was in one of those sessions my daughter's was enagegd. Discussions with other members of staff were warm and cordial leading up to and after arriving at UMSL.Dan in the Financial Services Office at the MSC with whom I spoke several times provided valuable information. Dr. Stallings who is my daughter's Academic Advisor was lovely in person as she was on the phone and Dr. Jordan who attended to us in her absence on 1 occasion when we got to UMSL for Orientation week designated herself as my daughter's on campus Mom😊 Dr. Jessica was full of energy and vibrant and met the students where they were. On to campus...it's clean with lots of green spaces which I absolutely love. Tgere a couple geese and squirrels too! At the time we got there, construction was ongoing however you literally can see and feel the capital expenditure and reinvestment in the university. There were charging and sanitization stations throughout the MSC where all Orientation activities were based. The campus is huge and has 2 train stations (North and South campus) and a police post on site. The Nosh has a couple options for dining and seating appears adequate as it can get busy. The dorms are consistent with normal dorm size and are equipped with bed, study table, closet, dresser, microwave and fridge plus retractable blinds. You do not share dorm room (which was HIGH on our list of requirements) but bathroom is shared among 4 suite mates who are responsible for cleaning. Freshmen must reside on Oak Hall if living on campus and it is has a kitchen, wash room, pool area, game room, garbage disposal etc. Can you tell yet? We loved our selection and generally have been satisfied with our daughter's settling so far. She has confirmed that she too loves her university and campus. Very satisfied Mommy...go Tritons!!🧡💛 If you're ever scouting for universities in the US, check UMSL out, they're highly recommended!

P.S. It's rated in the top 5 for safest campus in the US and commute was fairly easy via metro or UBER when I visited over the 12 days. We also had no incidents of theft, violence or crime and the people are warm and friendly....pretty laid back.", 'Let me just preface this by the fact that I am not actually a student here yet, but not for lack of trying on my part. I started this application process in January and it is now March and I still do not have an admissions decision, even though I have done everything they have asked me to and more. I’ve reached out multiple times to my admissions specialist without a response. There seemed to be some confusion between my maiden name and my married name which I made sure to point out to them from the get-go, but it still caused a ton of issues.  When I reached out to UMSL via Facebook messenger because I wanted to see if there was someone else I could work with, I was told that my admission specialist had been sick and that she would get a hold of me.
It is very frustrating to send continuous emails and have some not be responded to, but at the same time still getting the automated emails that say “we still need your transcripts.” I submitted my additional transcripts on 2/18 and was told that they would be updated the next day, yet I still continued to get automated emails stating they needed my transcripts.As a non-traditional student waiting over two months for an acceptance decision when another local university responded to me within a week and sent me my acceptance letter, school email, online log in, etc. coupled with the severe lack of communication, tells me about all I need to know about attending this school.', 'My child transferred from SIUE to UMSL this semester; tuition/fees is 42% higher; “automatic scholarships” are much more restrictive—can only be used for tuition not other university expenses and definitely not refunded; Financial Aid awarded a scholarship then revoked it & charged us a late fee & interest because they mistakenly awarded aid. They don’t care about the students financial wellbeing…consistently encouraging him to get a loan he doesn’t need. Overall, this was the worse decision he could have made.', "UMSL doesn't like unconventional students. If you are taking classes at two schools at once, (which working adults often have to), UMSL refuses to sign a  consortium agreement. They give the excuse that if they offer the class, you should take it with them.  In my case that would mean delaying my graduation an extra year!

Now let's discuss financial aid. Now for a state school UMSL is a little higher than some of the surrounding states, but they'll give you a merit scholarship if you have a high GPA (which I did). Your financial aid page in myview will show that you are awarded the scholarship before classes begin. Then 7-14 days later, the financial aid office will tell you that they are revoking it, because you are a part time student (even if a consortium agreement would prove otherwise; see what they do? :) ).

But wait! It's only 10 days into the semester so you'll have to pay for half of your classes, it's their drop policy. So they hook you with the promise of scholarship for being a top student, and then they pull the rug out once it's too late to avoid paying for classes. Very classy.

So they don't offer classes when you need them, get uncooperative when you do what's best for your education, and if you are a working adult taking a healthy course load and still maintaining a 3.8 GPA, they will not give you a scholarship for this excellence.

Do yourself a favor and walk around the campus. Ask yourself, is this school thriving or dying? UMSL knows the answer. They've tried nothing to solve it, and they're all out of ideas.", 'Attending University Of Missouri St. Louis is financial money pit designed to drain your wallet and to fill your life with student loans that you can never pay off. When I attended they refused to honor half of my 64 credited courses that I passed at another credited university in the area. For the degree that I was completing I was required to participate in an internship program on campus despite the degree being offered one hundred percent online. Missouri Has outdated educational requirements requiring certain " core" classes to graduate. UMSL would not accept one of those core classes due to a low but passing grade.

Financial aid and student support services Is a joke. You don't get financial aid assistance unless you are a full time student and what money you do get is based off of income. In today's society with the high rising cost of living it simply isn't worth attending collage and even if you do it doesn't guarantee you a Job.']

name: Moberly Area Community College
reviews:
['I recently had a very disappointing and unprofessional experience with a staff member in the financial aid office. I went in to get assistance applying for my last student loan and to confirm there were no holds on my account as well as other questions. Normally I work with Jordan, who is always extremely helpful, but she was on lunch so I was directed to another staff member.

From the moment we began this staff members tone and demeanor were condescending and dismissive. When I explained I needed help with the loan process and checking for holds, I was told, “You could have looked that up online.” I tried to explain that I had already attempted this and was having issues, but instead of offering assistance, she continued to make me feel like I was inconveniencing her.

When I politely said, “I appreciate your help, but I would prefer to wait for Jordan,” she said “Well I was going to help you!” and even followed me out into the hallway. I heard her talking to the front desk about me right when I left. I felt so uncomfortable by this staff member I waited in my car.

This behavior was completely disrespectful and unprofessional. I was polite the entire time and only wanted help to ensure everything was processed correctly. I would have gladly worked with her if not for her attitude, rudeness, and unnecessary comments.

Students deserve to feel supported and respected, especially when dealing with something as important as financial aid. This kind of conduct does not reflect well on the college, and I truly hope this is addressed so other students don’t experience the same treatment.', "I have had a great experience at MACC I loved the teachers! It's a great school to start out at and the classroom size is smaller making it easier to get acquainted with your classmates and get help if needed. The cost is also very affordable compared to a University or private school.", "I had a decent experience. Some of the teachers were very great, while others were not. Artie Fowler and Diane Tigner were very rude and condescending to me most of the times I needed help with academic advising. My credits didn't transfer very well into Truman State, but I still don't regret starting with the community college. I was a straight A student at MACC, and I am a straight A student at Truman as well. Life is what you make it, I guess. MACC can be an excellent opportunity.", "I enjoyed my time here. I will be graduating in December with my Associate's in Psychology and I will be transferring to UMSL for Spring semester. I definitely recommend Michael Johnson as an advisor because it seems like he is the only one who knows how to actually be an advisor. Work hard and the work pays off. The ones giving bad reviews are the lazy ones.", 'Always great experiences .zhad many good times here and oldest daughter went to college here too.  Great sports events, been Greyhound boosters for yrs.  A great college.']

name: Truman State University
reviews:
["I never attended Truman but I know someone very close who does/does. Although this school is beautiful, please don't overlook safety. This school is a massive security risk for any women who attend. The percentage of people who are stalked is very high and I can confirm that the numbers match reality. Within 2 months of my friend attending their first year they were texted from an unknown number describing them and the things they had done previously. This person knew where they lived inside campus and supposedly peeped through their window. The victims let the school and the university police know  . The school and police proceeded to do the bare minimum with just escorts to and from work and after 2-3 weeks the police without doing any investigating had dropped the case. The school could have reviewed cameras facing the parking-lot, but never did. ( also there are very limited amounts cameras inside the actual campus walls). If you or your daughters saw this school as a good option please make sure that safety is one of your main concerns because obviously it wasn't Truman's.", "The parking situation is pretty bad. That's gotta be minus at least 2 stars. The main freshman dormitory is ryle hall where there isn't enough parking for the residents so they overflow into commuter and staff parking. This causes commuters and residents to inevitably get parking tickets all the time. Its ridiculous that they are charging broke college kids for parking tickets when they don't have enough parking. You'd think they'd have scavenged enough money from students at this point to pay for additional parking or something.", 'I graduated with a B.S. in Communication back in 2018. I loved my Truman experience, and I think it runs analogous to Kirksville's motto "where the people make the difference." I love the professors and students that I met throughout my collegiate career. I also enjoyed serving in the local community and stayed away from the party scenes. Plus, I did all of that while working a great on-campus IT job that helped bolster my resume and allowed me to graduate debt free.', 'Fantastic place to get your degree! Beautiful campus!', 'International Student here. Thought sky was the limit when I transferred. I was a D2 athlete for the school when they decided to cancel the athletes program.
Pros: cheap.
Tuition is affordable.
Staff is easy to talk to and they do what they can to help students.
Cons:
False advertisement; no where near what they call ‘Harvard of Midwest’
Cheap; basically too cheap to a point that they have no resources. Students and their mental health are never given any proper attention. Look up what happened with AKL and what Truman did to follow up.
Good professors leave for better paid programs and some of the professors don’t understand or try to understand kids. There is a clear language barrier. I thought I was the international student but some professors here don’t understand English. There are some professors like Dr. Gillette who are literally carrying the university on their backs.
There are limited resources and almost everything has to be student funded. My school that I transferred from took us to Paris for a conference and took care of everything. During my time as a student athlete, the coach told us that we basically are responsible for our own even when it comes to traveling.
Look up how many people finish their degree in 4 years!
The school constantly reaches out to its alumni network for funding but the minute you graduate, there are no resources for jobs. And if you are an international student, you are doomed. You have to be the very best to get good opportunities.
Many graduates from my batches are working jobs that didn’t require a degree.
They say Truman prepares you for the world. It prepared students for poverty and depression.
In all, it’s not a bad school if you are a nerd. It’s not a bad school at all. Just nothing as advertised and not even close to Mizzou, SLU or washu. Just be careful']

name: Northwest Missouri State University
reviews: ['As a graduate student, I applied for their Master’s program in Special Education with certification. NWMS  partners with a 3rd party for their online programs. This information is not divulged to applicants. It was a fluke that I found this out. The call center from the 3rd party is useless. The employees are not trained to do their jobs and each person will tell you something completely different. It was quite a disappointing process to be accepted, enrolled in class and then have this experience. I have decided the application fee is a wash and to go somewhere else. Please, do you research prior to enrolling in their online programs.', 'I completed an online certification program at Northwest Missouri State University. The university is a highly affordable option, particularly suitable for those seeking a compressed academic schedule. However, prospective students should be aware that courses are delivered in intensive 6-to-8-week intervals, which demands very strong time management skills and a high degree of self-motivation. While tuition is low, the compressed format can sometimes compromise the depth or quality of the education received. The academic advisors, who are often professors, may have slower response times. It is also important to note that, as of this review, the business school does not hold AASCB certification.\n\nNWMSU is a solid choice for highly disciplined students prioritizing affordability and speed.', 'If you are unsure, go for a visit. It was our best campus tour of 4 universities', 'Beautiful campus and great school.', 'Beautiful campus and nice people.  I absolutely loved it. It felt down to earth and like we were at home. We traveled around 13 hrs from East Kentucky to get there. It was so well kept, clean and beautiful buildings and facilities.']

name: Ozark Christian College
reviews: ['Shalom! This is a place to be, a valley of brokenness where life is molded into vessels for use in the kingdom of God. Some he (Jesus) made them "pastors and teachers" I feel it and I hear it, here all around everyday, as I move about my studies. Where else can be besides serving Jesus. The staff and students give great care into the comfort and enjoyment of their guest. It is always a pleasure to attend anything OCC offers to the public.', 'I deeply loved everything about Ozark Christian College--the classes, the professors, the camaraderie between students, the chapel services, the integrity and humility of its leadership, and the push beyond academics for everyone to pursue closeness with God and excellence in ministry.  Everyone down to the custodians showed a godly example and helped me grow in my faith and ministry ability.']

name: College of the Ozarks
reviews: ['What a pleasure!! Great atmosphere, great food, excellent service by young, polite and respectful collage students working for their tuition at what is known as Hard Work University!! We'd enjoy more products from the mill like a high protein flour."]

name: Park University
reviews: ['The school itself isn\'t bad, but the classes are absolutely horrible. The assignments do not match up with the course material because they are "being updated," instructors are almost impossible to get ahold of, maps in geography classes are blurry, end-of-course survey questions are irrelevant, case studies are old/outdated, instructors do not unlock units/materials on time, the lectures have many spelling/grammatical errors in them, there is not a standard process for accessing course materials, their "first-day" program does not let you read any textbook material early, they make you download spyware to complete some final exams, and the some instructors seem like bot programs which makes students drop the class. FUTURE STUDENTS: Do not pay money to an organization that is this disorganized and of poor quality. Ironically a class about quality control had many course content errors. PARK: You need to do a serious audit of your academic\'s programs. Yes, I am an on-line student with Park and I regret staying this long with them. There are a lot of better options to choose from, both in the local area and on-line. I would give them zero stars if possible.', 'Completed my Bachelors here in 2023. 10/10 recommend. I am active duty in the Marine Corps and completed this throughout multiple deployments and travel abroad. This college offered enough flexibility to balance my career in the military, and educational pursuits. The staff is friendly, and I never had any troubles navigating the online student portals or learning environments. Every professor was a star in their craft, and aided immensely towards the betterment in their students.\n\nFollowing this positive experience, my drive has increased to further my educational pursuits, and I am now pursuing a Masters program.', 'I had a great experience with Park. This school is great for full time workers like myself with the flexibility of doing 8 week courses. Many of the programs are fully online so if you can’t make it to campus this is a great option. I graduated this past December and I have no regrets', 'I have been a Park student from my time in the Army and continuing after retirement. I have completed two degrees and now working on my masters degree. Hand down best college I have ever experienced and had the pleasure to communicate with. Amazing staff and advisors. 100% recommend.', "Park has allowed me to go full time to do my undergrad and graduate degree while still supporting my family, and I'm not almost certain that traditional university environments would have allowed me to spend my time at home working at my pace throughout the week and getting to still be with my family. Even though they allow you to have flexibility, the courses are rigorous and professors are there to answer questions when necessary. They respond quickly, and I have had a professor call me when I got confused on something so that he could help me through it right away rather than waiting until later and emailing. Everyone, including advisors are always ready to help, and there is tutoring available for when you have trouble with something in a class. I am almost done with my MBA, and I am so grateful to Park because I don't know if I'd be this far along in my educational journey if it wasn't for their online programs. I definitely recommend this university for anyone who is looking for a legitimate university with the ability to accommodate a career professional in an effort to further their education."]

name: Stevens-The Institute of Business & Arts
reviews: ['I went there back in 2005-2007 for Paralegal Studies. I loved going to school there! I was able to find a job in my field within a year, and I still work in the legal field.', "I absolutely love SIBA! They have a  supportive, nice, accommodating, and informative staff. A large number of their staff currently work in the fields that they are teaching in and they keep the curriculum interesting and current. As an older student who has done college before, I knew that I needed to get a better education and find a better job to take care of myself, but I also didn't want to invest in 4 years of schooling. I love that you can earn a bachelor's degree in less than 2 years and be set up for success in the field that you're studying!!", 'Do not let the size of this school fool you. It may be small, but it is a powerhouse! My sister recently graduated from here, is doing fabulous, and has already landed her first job!!! She only had positive things to say about her program, her instructors, and the quality of the education she received. The school invested in her and helped give her direction, which is not always a given. I am so proud of her and what she has accomplished. I am thankful that SIBA provided the opportunity and guidance to get her there!', 'The most amazing college I ever attended. Its more than just a school. Its a huge support system that becomes your family. They push you to your full potential and will stay on you till you succeed.', 'I am beyond grateful that I found this charming school 3 years ago! It is small and personal with the most welcoming "Siba family"! Not to mention it\'s in a renovated loft space, making it trendy and fun! I was so hesitant to go back to school until finally I found this GEM and felt like I was at the right place at the right time! Fast forward...... I\'ve now graduated at the top of my class and the opportunities just keep unfolding as we speak. Thank you to my Siba family!!!']

name: Ranken Technical College
reviews: ['I am a parent of a student that attends this school for plumbing in the evening. From my understanding it is never an instructor available. Ranken makes evening students complete a worksheet when staff is unavailable that is not graded by anyone. I think that it is very sad to have people drive all the way to the school to have no one to teach or (Haines an instructor teach to classes at the same time) People are paying for education that Ranken is not providing. How can a student achieve the necessary hours for graduation? Why does Ranken expect to collect funds and not providing anything but a hard time. This school is nothing like it once was and I feel that the government funding for student loans need to look into this practice more. Sad', 'This is literally the worst school. From the administration to the faculty. If you have mental health issues they will target you, retaliate against you, and like to try to cover up their tracks. Do not go here if you want a genuine education. They tell you to advocate for yourself, and when you do, the school will go to war with you. There is nothing consistent about the teaching or the “punishments.” They pick and choose who they want to target and dock points based on how “they” felt. If you’re thinking of enrolling your child or yourself in this program, please look elsewhere. They may have had a good reputation in the past, but it is not the same culture now. The things they have done are despicable, underhanded, and truly mind blowing. A lot of the faculty are bullies.\n\nUpdate after the generic reply from the “owner”: the Office of Education is one of the biggest culprits in my complaint. They give 0 crap about the students. They bully/intimidate their students and don’t care about student safety in the slightest. That includes the VP of Student Success. She should have been fired immediately for the things she has done. There have been MULTIPLE complaints of bullying by faculty and the office of Student Success, but nothing has ever been done. A student is going to end up hurting themselves because of the treatment of the faculty and administration. The president of the school needs to clean house and take these complaints seriously.', 'Don’t go for electrical automation or control systems. Field is over crowded. The union does not respect the degree only highschool grades. There are no apprenticeships and the biggest lie ranken ever told was that the companies are willing to train people. Avoid maintenance technician jobs at all cost if you do get this degree. Same with any job that sounds too good to be true. Build job experience no matter what. 60% of jobs out side of school are ruthless resume destroyers that will fire you with in 3 months. Avoid the job title maintenance technician at any/all factories like it’s the plague. AND FOR THE LOVE OF GOD. LOOK UP WHAT THE IEC. TAKE MY ADVICE GO TO THE IEC AND NOT RANKENS ELECTRICAL PROGRAM IF PAYING FOR A DEGREE. YOU WILL BE IN A OFFICAL GOVERNMENT SPONSORED APPRENTICESHIP. WITH A JOURNEYMAN CARD AT THE END OF IT!!!! A JOURNEYMAN CARD!!! THAT YOU CAN USE TO FORCE YOUR WAY INTO THE IBEW!!! DONT END UP LIKE ME!!! IF YOURE IN THE ELECTRICAL PROGRAM LEAVE AND JOIN THE IEC IMMEDIETLY!!!!!!!!!', 'No instructors are ever there in the day, or evening. Jake Moehlenbrock is a joke and has no idea what he’s doing with hvac and could not teach basic math. My Instructors cant answer questions regarding basic electrical concepts', 'I would not recommend this school to anyone especially veterans  like my self who have fought for this country to keep our way of living and freedoms. This school will take your money and not work with you. I’ve had medical difficulties and the school will not excuse my absences even with my medical conditions and doctors notes.']

name: Rockhurst University
reviews:
['This is an exceptional institution dedicated to servant leadership and that adheres closely to its core Jesuit values.  The campus is gorgeous and the professors and staff are thoughtful and considerate.  RU consistently ranks as one of the best universities in the Midwest.  I am an alum (2004) and I have two daughters that are as well (2021).  I have one daughter that is an ER nurse and another that is a Doctor of Physical Therapy.', "Rockhurst has a beautiful campus in Kansas City.  It is a smaller college campus and it is located close to the Plaza.  Although I haven't personally taken classes, I have been told it is a good experience.  They are partnering with St Luke's for the nursing program. The security officers that I've encountered have been super friendly and helpful.  I would definitely recommend checking out this college.", 'Rockhurst‘ S ARRUPE Hall provides a wonderful venue for the Midwest Poet’s
series', "Rockhurst University, located in Kansas City, Missouri, is a vibrant institution known for its strong emphasis on Jesuit values and academic excellence.

One of the university's standout features is its commitment to a holistic education, combining rigorous academics with a focus on service, leadership, and social justice. Students are encouraged to engage in the community through service-learning opportunities, fostering a sense of responsibility and compassion.

Academically, Rockhurst offers a wide range of programs across various disciplines, including business, health sciences, humanities, and more. The faculty are dedicated and supportive, providing personalized attention to students and fostering a dynamic learning environment.

The campus itself is picturesque, with historic buildings and modern facilities coexisting harmoniously. The university's small size fosters a close-knit community where students can form lasting connections with peers and faculty.

Rockhurst's location in Kansas City also provides students with a wealth of opportunities. The city's vibrant cultural scene, internship possibilities, and thriving job market offer students a well-rounded college experience.

Overall, Rockhurst University stands out for its strong sense of community, academic rigor, and commitment to Jesuit values. It's a place where students can grow intellectually, personally, and spiritually, preparing them for successful and fulfilling futures.", "Great place to walk my dog. Security is very present. The staff that I've met are very decent. And some of the students I've met are very decent, kind, and just seemingly okay. The campus itself is laid out very nice. Also their architect is interesting as well as their landscaping.

My understanding is that they offer a great business degree. Five Star"]

name: Saint Louis University
reviews: ['I had a great learning experience here as a graduate student. I loved my department and its community. I made fantastic friends, and I think my career was greatly benefited by attending SLU. I only give 3 stars because dealing with administration was difficult, and I found being a parent while a GA unsustainable. I got a job as soon as I could (once I passed comps), and worked for 3 years while dissertating. Once I had a job, it was hard to stay connected, but I still checked my email regularly. The actual process for graduation through the registrar has been a nightmare. I defended in August, and then was shut out of the system. I could not communicate with the registrar except by phone, and it took numerous phone calls and emails to all sorts of administrators to finalize my graduation. All because they locked me out of my email unnecessarily. I told the provost while I was a student, and I say it again now: this school was designed for celibate men who live on the campus (i.e., seminary). They have not figured out how to work with student professionals who have families. Again, the actual faculty are lovely. I have no complaints about them, just admin.', "DO NOT go here as a transfer student. I transfered right when they changed their core curriculum which sent me back to registering with the underclassmen. Hopefully there decided on what they're going to do for the core so that other years do not have to deal with what I did. This place totes around their diversity and inclusion all over campus but they're not any better than any other university.", "Well I can finally say I been to college. Honestly I was working in the city and I needed to run by US Bank which is also there so I went inside to do some quick banking. Place seemed nice enough. Bank lady was super friendly although probably a little suspicious of me more than likely. Didn't interact with anyone else so not much to tell. Thanks for the super easy banking experience SLU. I will definitely root for you all next March madness (sadly, I'm not much of a college sports fanatic truth be told; but always a hometown fan anyways.) 😉", 'I graduated from the School of Professional Studies in May 2021 with a 3.04 GPA with a Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Information Systems. I have requested my transcripts numerous times through the National Student Clearinghouse for personal reasons and also for admissions to various graduate programs at other institutions. SLU has issued transcripts with inconsistencies and discrepancies over the years. It was only recently that I discovered this. As a result I have lost application fees and was denied admissions to some programs because my GPA was WRONG! I was a B student but sometimes they had me on paper as a C almost D student. It was only my most recent application where the admissions office at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville (SIUE) was transparent enough to compare the official transcript they received from SLU in June 2024 to an official copy I had received in September 2021. SLU corrected the error and issued a new transcript free of charge but that does not fix the embarrassment and disgust I experienced when it caused issues with my admissions to New York University (NYU) and The University of Texas Austin. SLU can\'t refund me for those application fees or turn back the hands of time to make it right. I went through rigorous appeals processes where I was not allowed access to my admissions files at these schools but they both stated that they had "academic concerns" (e.g. the transcript from SLU). It\'s insane that I paid $64K in tuition and people in the office can\'t click a correct button or the institution can\'t invest in software that isn\'t faulty to automate this for them. I would advise anyone who has graduated from SLU to check their records thee times after requesting them, even if the records are sent directly to another school, call the school who received it to inquire. The hard part is many schools will not disclose what they have received.', 'Hello, I just gave 5 stars. I live in Türkiye. I will be graduating from this university next academic year. How can I come from Türkiye?']

name: University of Health Sciences and Pharmacy in St. Louis
reviews: ['We came to my baby girl’s tour after being offered an athletic scholarship and she said yes. What an impressive school but the staff, professors and coach made it so easy for her to decide to leave me in Miami and come join the UHSP family in the fall. I couldn’t be more proud of her! They truly exceeded our expectations!!', 'A clean, crisp, professional, state-of-the-art institution! The vibe is amazing as students are gathered in many study spaces either collaborating together or simply hanging out. And their rec center/ gym is top notch. How cool for competitive gym to be sunken in three floors? We were very impressed with Jordan Laird, one of the admissions personnel, who took over 2 hours with us going over all aspects of the college, the tremendous amenities, and discussed all the fun campus life opportunities. And then she took us on an extensive tour of all the facilities, professional buildings, and residential offerings. And can’t say enough about Starbucks and Chick-fil-a steps from class or dorm. This school is amazing!', 'My name is Yeongmi Park and I am from South Korea. I have previously studied in Illinois and Boston, Massachusetts. I have never experienced such a loving and caring environment in any American school before. However, at St. Louis College of Pharmacy, I could feel that the faculty members really care about their students. They want us to be happy and successful, and are always willing to help us with anything they can. Additionally, the students are very kind and compassionate towards each other. They support each other to survive and flourish together. Come to UHSP, you will not regret to.', 'Very nice campus, I enjoy working with the staff.', "Beautiful Campus. They always to an awesome job on the up keep. It's a quiet place to sit and reflect. It's always quiet and peaceful. I love how it is nestled in the Central West End. I love how I can sit and reflect. Still beautiful"]

name: Saint Louis Community College
reviews:
['Reading the reviews before hand (mainly looking for WHERE the testing center is) I was like oh boy here we go…
Worst part was parking. People don’t know how to park. That aside, I walked in and was greeted by the nicest security officer. Robinson maybe? Anyways he knew I was there for testing (maybe the profuse sweating) and was very very kind. Got the elevator told me where to find the testing center and there was a restroom nearby haha!

So my fears of wandering campus in searching of the testing center were for nothing.

Arrived 20mins early for my test and was seated right away.
Testing dude was cool. Straight forward. No watches, jackets, water etc. you read over it.

Took the test (if you’ve read this long and are vested, I DID pass)
So really, no issues on my side whatsoever', 'Literally impossible to get ahold of an advisor. And when you do get ahold of an advisor, they don’t even know what they’re talking about. When I was finally able to get ahold of an advisor last spring to speak about transferring to this school, and what other prerequisites I would need for the Rad Tech program, the advisor recommended I take classes over the summer to ensure I had all my prereqs ready for the coming fall program. I spoke to her so many times on the phone from March-now and told her so many times my biggest worry was just needing to graduate as quickly as possible. Out of all of the conversations we had, she assured me I would be on track to start the program this fall and would take Anatomy 2 while starting the program. I did my job shadowing, sent her the information she needed, she submitted my application. A day later I receive an email from the rad tech department saying the waitlist to enter is 2-3 years??? So I should have applied to the program before even starting any prerequisites? This is devastating news to me and it’s insane that the advisor I spoke to for months wouldn’t ever mention this. I haven’t even started this school yet and it’s clear how little staff cares about its students. I gave up my summer in order to ensure I would start this fall. I relocated to STL per my advisors recommendation in anticipation of starting this program this fall. I am sitting here with 2 years of prerequisites for a major that has a 2-3 year waitlist, in a town I moved to specifically for this. This is devastating to me.', 'Getting ahold of anybody is a nightmare. I reported them to the VA because I have yet gotten to even speak to a veteran representative. If you are a veteran I highly advise using your benefits elsewhere.', 'Your “wanna be” campus police officers are some of the most unproductive people I’ve met in my life. Instead of focusing on people speeding in front of your campus next to the CDLC, they would rather ticket parents running inside to pick up their child after a long day because you parked in a “no parking zone” for less than 3 minutes. You folks are the laughing stock of “cops”. Instead of giving parents the safety of having room while they do construction on Oakland they would rather park sideways in the pick up area to force parents to park on the street and take their kids out in harms way. There’s no compassion or grace, just authority and power tripping campus policing. So many other things your security should be focused on but nope, we need to ticket parents parking incorrectly and waste multiple hours at the end of the day sitting in their cruiser to block traffic. I’ve watched multiple people speed past me and my son because of the construction and the location of where we are allowed to park. It’s frustrating when your security officers just watch and continue to kick back in their cruisers and do nothing about it other than block your safest entry to pick up your child. Do better.', 'Everybody who works up at the school is very embarrassing, including the professors, the advisors The people who work in the student advocacy office, even the people who work in disability services when it comes to helping you in class… And especially the phone concierge People. Unless you just love online classes, this is the worst school ever']

name: Southwest Baptist University
reviews: ['Went to the 4th of July celebration. It was very good!', "The 18 hole disc golf course is nice, a few of the tee pads could use some help but it's fairly clean.", "Love SBU!  During our 1st visit, I asked who would be teaching the classes (at other schools so many grad students often teach today). I’m very pleased with the theologically conservative direction of the university. Knowing that all the professors affirm the Baptist Faith and Message is extremely encouraging. If you have a student nearing the end of his or her high school career, then you must schedule a visit to this great university.', 'We recently visited to check out the college for an upcoming student. We had a great time. We were treated very kindly and enjoyed their nice campus. We especially enjoyed the professor we met in the intercultural studies department. name: Missouri State University-West Plains
reviews: ["So far from my first semester in this college, I've learned that the experience online is horrendous, most professors online don't seem to actually actively teach. The math is especially tasking because the professor I currently have hasn't offered help when I emailed him about an issue on the Pearson's website. I genuinely wish I could do in-person college but with my situation and placement, I can't do anything. I wanted to further my education and find a career that would fit me but instead I'm possibly in debt to a school that wouldn't give two pennies of thought to me. I feel lied to and I feel hopeless. I hope that something changes but for now I wouldn't recommend this college.", 'Missouri State University-West Plains lacks effective and decisive leadership at the top. Therefore, it will continue to have a decline in enrollment unless and until a chancellor and academic dean are selected who can move the institution forward. The faculty, staff, students and community are amazing and deserve much better. The lack of nontraditional students on this campus is a telling sign of a failure to respond to the workforce needs of local business and industry. No two-year college can sustain itself on dual-credit (tuition-free) enrollment. Unless these and other issues can be resolved, I would highly recommend exploring another two-year college in the area such as Three Rivers College, Ozarka College, Ozarks Technical Community College or Arkansas State University-Mountain Home. These institutions are much more responsive to the needs of the region.', 'Nice campus. My daughter loves going there.', "This school doesn't even deserve a star. I wasted my time coming here for a semester for them  to never apply my financial aid or A+. I was constantly in and out of the business department even months after the semester ended fighting with them to have my education covered and to come back, but no one cared enough to help me. They Always sent me to a student for help and they couldn't even help me. They continued to send me the same paper work I had already turned in. They screwed my fiancé over the same way, repetitively sending him the same paper work he had sent in until he finally dropped out. He didn't have time to fight with them between his work schedule. The only time they wanted him to come in was when he was working and no other time would do. This school has screwed over so many people that I know. They have billed my friends for things they advertise as free and no one seems to know how to do their job, seeing as students run the whole operation. They have great teachers here, but unless you're paying out of pocket for your entire education here, I'd advise you to go some where else. I made 100 mile round trips four times or more a week to this place and have nothing to show for it but an empty wallet and a tore-up car. I didn't have the money to begin with to even DRIVE to college let alone the bill they sent me at the end of the samester for over $2000 or the $800 I had to spend on books from this place. This is a sad excuse for a school. It's a rip off and I wish I never would have even started school here and just went straight into the military. It's sad when an 18/19 year old girl thinks it's easier to go into the military than to go to college.", 'STAR Orientation was great. Very informative. Friendly, helpful staff. Overall good university. Now in my second semester and things are pretty much the same. Would recommend.']

name: Southeast Missouri State University
reviews:
['A well-organized university that opens its doors to talented and studious students, offering a wide range of academic streams from Bachelor’s to Master’s level. The dedicated staff ensures a disciplined learning environment through proper and consistent assessments. One of the university’s unique highlights is the President’s Academy, which focuses on leadership and practical application of knowledge. The surrounding community is deeply supportive of the student body, even offering scholarships from their own local funds. In fact, Cape Girardeau, the nearest city, is known for its unwavering commitment to serving the needs of university students.', "As a 1990 graduate of Southeast Missouri State University, I am writing to express my profound disappointment regarding recent administrative decisions made by the university. While I support the dissolution of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) programs, I am deeply concerned by the decision to reassign associated staff to other departments rather than proceeding with their termination.

Given the university's current budget constraints, it is difficult to justify the continued employment of these individuals, particularly in academic or subject-matter expert roles where their primary background is in DEI. I believe these reassignments risk lowering institutional standards and undermine the academic integrity expected of a discipline-specific education.

Due to these concerns, several fellow alumni and I have decided to discontinue our financial contributions to the university indefinitely. Furthermore, we will no longer refer family or friends to SEMO, as we believe other institutions now better align with our expectations for academic excellence and administrative fiscal responsibility.

I hope the university will take this feedback into serious consideration as it evaluates its future policy and staffing decisions.", 'Worst School  I ever been to, no communication and no support for international student athlete. No communication between services which make your life hell since you need to do everything yourself.

For a big school, this is alarming, I never seen this in my 5 years in the USA. I will not recommend to my worst enemy.

The athletic office will not support you, and would let you stranded if your need they help. Any International student athletes if you have an offer apart if it is to play football, run away from this place !!!!!', "I know they have great faculty that care about student success!

Beautiful campus but being a car or electric scooter, it's hilly.", 'I absolutely love my time here at SEMO. The staff and students are so nice and there are so many opportunities to expand my horizon. There are so many international students here that you get so much culture and amazing experance.']

name: Missouri State University-Springfield
reviews: ["Beautiful campus, but some classes are taught in a more roundabout way that can make it confusing, and parking is difficult. Most buildings claim they are handicap accessible, but are still very difficult or impossible to get into without help. Look forward to future marching events.', 'I had an amazing conversation with an academic advisor named Sarah . name: Washington University in St Louis
reviews: ['The campus is beautiful. The updates since the last time I was here are incredible. The student body is very fortunate for the kind of facilities available. Both at the undergraduate campus and medical school campus changes abound.', "The campus is full of architecture that shows the roots of the university. Buildings that represent what the foundation of knowledge stands for at this school. Sucks that the underground parking-lot I went to was being finicky for no reason and a line built behind me. I had to move out the way for others to go through, who had no issue, before I could redo my exit. There also weren't too many students outside despite it being beautiful weather outside, come on guys. I know school is hard but please take the time to go outside. I also heard a student was expelled for calling out the schools administration for ignoring racism and discrimination. Sucks to see a school like WASHU in decline.", 'Washington University in St. Louis, anchored at the iconic 1 Brookings Drive, is consistently portrayed in my professional and social circles as a premier bastion of Midwestern intellectual rigor where a substantive focus on interdisciplinary research creates a truly elite, yet surprisingly collaborative, academic atmosphere. Through numerous insightful exchanges with medical professionals and successful alumni, it is merytorically evident that "WashU" provides a high-caliber environment, frequently lauded by my acquaintances for its exceptional ability to merge world-class biological sciences with a deeply respectful, student-centric approach to liberal arts. It is heartening to observe how the institution maintains such a transparent dedication to regional excellence and global innovation, a quality that the broader public recognizes as a vital catalyst for the impressive influence its graduates wield across both the scientific and corporate landscapes. Ultimately, in the collective view of informed observers, the university stands as a distinguished hallmark of private research, rightfully respected for its elegant synthesis of historic architectural beauty and a forward-looking mission that genuinely empowers the next generation of leaders.', 'Beautiful campus! Amazing university with some of the best programs across many disciplines.', 'Great school. My friend just graduated and I’m proud of him.']
