name: William Jewell College
reviews:
["I first visited William Jewell twenty five years ago and was positively impressed with its reputation and grounds.
Last year I toured William Jewell with my daughter as we were college shopping for her. We were impressed with the quality of the place and the friendly, helpful and open people that we met.
We were surprised at how small the student body is. We were scared by the cost of tuition. Fortunately they worked with us with academic scholarship and athletic scholarship, making it still costly, but tolerable.
My daughter has now been a Cardinal for five months and is very happy. Her largest class has 25 students. Her classes, dorm friends, classmates, professors, teammates and coaches all have been great.
Because of it's petite size, William Jewell isn't for everyone, but we highly recommend it. Quality over quantity.", 'My grandson played in a baseball tournament. One of his games was at William Jewell baseball field. It was nice and clean, and we had a 90-minute rain and lightning delay. Bleachers are great because you can put your seat on the bleacher or use your chair on them.', 'Sadly, like many formerly church-related colleges, Jewell has abandoned historic Christianity and its identity as a Christian and Baptist college.

When I attended there, many years ago now, it was a wonderful, solid, mostly faithful school. I got a great education from caring professors and even was able to attend Oxford for a year. All this at a cost the same or lower than KU or MU at that time.

Now it has become much more expensive, and much smaller, with the enrollment having declined by over one third as it has abandoned its Christian identity. I never considered it for my own children for those reasons.

It certainly has much nicer facilities and lawns now. But I much prefer the old, humbler, Christian Jewell, which was affordable for ordinary middle-class kids. I would choose a mind and heart for God over fancy buildings and lush landscaping every time.

Ironically, Jewell and its neighbor across the river in Kansas, Benedictine College of Atchison, have switched places. BC has re-emphasized its Christian identity and become more faithful to its church and heritage (Catholic), and has seen great growth and renewal. (And it also has a beautiful campus.)

Jewell has done the opposite, abandoning its churches, heritage, and faith (Baptist), and enrollment has plunged. Jewell has about 800 students now and Benedictine 1400. In my time it was the opposite.

I hope Jewell would do what Benedictine has done, and see the same revival and renewal. But I am doubtful that will happen.', 'Don’t go here. I have never met one person who has genuinely enjoyed their time at Jewell. The RA’s are trying to get everyone in trouble which is why most of the school leaves during the weekends. Decent campus, decent education (very easy), awful experience. Did not feel like a “college experience.” It felt like I was in middle school or high school.', 'I Would never recommend this college to anyone. They are not the college they use to be years ago.
Reasons I give such a low rating.
1. Dorms are very expensive and required the 1st year. Heaters and airconditioner broke down numerous times. Water heater not working and only cold showers available.  Brown water coming from faucets.
2. Advisors do not do their jobs. Will not return calls or emails for days, weeks if ever. Will not help you with selections to best map out your course to your major. Recommend changing your major even though it is the only thing you want to do.
Will even recommend going to a different school if you dont.
3. Make you take classes that are not transferable.
4. The teachers do not care about the students. Just there to collect a paycheck not actually teach.
If this does not make you look into other colleges and you choose to go here. You will soon experience what a lot of others have. I have heard more bad than good from others I have discussed these issues with that have had very similar experiences']

name: William Woods University
reviews: ['My review is not helpful for those who attend college here, but I will say this, every summer I attend this university for a student council summer camp and they go ABOVE and beyond to help us out! The kitchen staff feed hundreds of hungry mouths, and the admin always take time to attend and thank us for coming and welcome us! We love the ducks!!!', 'I recently made a visit to William Woods as an accepted student. The very personal and caring treatment is amazing! All the staff was more than delighted to see me and were so excited I was there! This is a definite choice for anyone who wants that personal touch with their school.', 'I’ve been trying to re-enroll in the Legal Studies program at William Woods and keep hitting walls. I followed every step—submitted the re-entry form, made payments, reached out to multiple departments—and still can’t get clear answers on when the next term starts, what classes I need, or if my tuition rate is still locked in. Instead of answers, I’m passed around or ignored. Advising, financial aid, and other staff either deflect or don’t reply at all. I’m trying to plan my finances and coursework to stay on track and graduate, but the lack of support is making that impossible. I’ve maintained a 4.0 GPA and stayed committed through personal setbacks, but this has been frustrating and discouraging. At this point, I’m seriously considering transferring. The school claims to support adult learners, but that hasn’t been my experience. If you’re looking for responsiveness or structure, I’d be cautious.', "I couldn't have chosen a better place to spend the past four years. William Woods University was not only the university I received my degree from, but a place that became my second home. Whether it's the staff, faculty, coaches, or other students on campus, everyone there is tremendous. Ever since I stepped foot on campus on my first college visit, I could tell that each professor and faculty member was passionate about what they did and genuinely cared about each student that crossed their path. I would not be the person I am today without having had such a great collegiate experience, and William Woods University is to thank for that!", 'A wonderful university. We attended for an equestrian event and the grounds were beautiful and the staff we interacted with were friendly, knowledgeable, and helpful!']

name: Blackfeet Community College
reviews: ['Moxie (Xolo Maridueña) × Papa (Angelina Hathaway) = Blackfeet Community College Campus (Community college in South Browning, Montana) @Blue Shoe Podcast (Our Family Owned Shoe store in New York)', 'I went to school here and tried to get my Associates Degree in Carpentry. 1 year through they drop the carpentry classes and tell us they will give us a 1 year certificate and so I would  have to sign up for different classes the next year so  I couldn’t get an Associates like I had planned  I ended up dropping out and had to pay back my PAL Grant and tuition or a portion anyway because the college did help us. Be careful if you go here things change fast.', 'I love the library! It has so much history about the Blackfeet and the staff is always ready to help you!', "This place is getting more and more courses and degree options. GO CHECK OUT STUDENT SERVICES! See what's available and how to get started on your future. GO, SUCCEED!!", 'Excellent local college, friendly knowledgeable staff, great place for research and learning']

name: Highlands College of Montana Tech
reviews: ['They discriminated against me because of my past DUI convictions. They did not accept me until there were no longer any spots open in the classes I was seeking. name: Carroll College
reviews:
['I just started working here to get a few free courses. This campus is AMAZING!  The library has so many neat workshop areas for public media, podcasting etc., and there is a 3D printer lab as well.  It would be neat to see one of those 3d puzzles some day.  The food is great and looking forward to learning to earning my next degree(s).  God Bless', 'Very pretty campus. It was a great place to eat a to go sandwich and puts around with a new camera/lens.

But seriously, who ever heard of a college that closes their library at 4:30pm when classes are in session?!?', "Beautiful campus, the crazy speed bumps that were there could've broken exhaust or other parts on your car even going over them from a dead stop but thankfully they have been removed.

For the most part everyone is polite and kind.", "Love this small Catholic college. The Holy Spirit is really doing something here. Our daughter's in her third year and loving it", 'Carroll College has been a warm and welcoming place for our son and family. Our son is super happy here with his professors, coaches, and administrators. The friends he has made are great people. We feel comfortable and proud having this be his home away from home.']

name: Dawson Community College
reviews: ["We celebrated Veterans Day with DCC. They are amazing and I look forward to their womens' basketball games this season. Thank you so much for celebrating and loving us. The VFW is absolutely grateful.", 'Great tour today with the Softball coaches. Small, family atmosphere with excellent programs. Classrooms are close by along with the dorm rooms.', "There is something wrong when a community college costs $40,000 for a 2 year degree, and you get zero face time with your teachers, zero guidance, and if you ask questions they just brush you odd like you're stupid, if they even respond at all. And if you point any of that out they say you have a bad attitude and imply that your just not cut out for college. I can definitely see why no one feels college is worth it and young people are rejecting it in droves. The quality of what you get is no where near worth the amount of money they take from you.", 'What an awesome facility! I wish the community college I attended in western Montana had this kind of infrastructure. Guest wifi, a library (with a huge telescope! And an art gallery!), a cafeteria, workout equipment.', "Hello, My name is Luis I from Venezuela I 19 years old\nI am interested in getting a sport schorlarship, will you have places available? reviews: ['Nice comfortable environment. Computers are accessible and up to date. Welcoming staff.', 'Great place to go for a small learning experience.', 'Awesome. Services and good food.', 'Great coffee and chili dogs!', 'none of them are the sharpest knife in the cupboard']

name: Montana State University Billings
reviews: ['Fantastic food and exemplary service is the daily fare.  All FRESH INGREDIENTS and tasty sauces.\nI highly recommend this establishment  !!!', 'Msu billings is a great college in my opinion. The staff is amazing.', 'Checking my son in was so easy. The staff and all volunteers were amazing.  Highly recommend going here', "Nothing fancy or flashy but a good college all around. As long as you're going for a STEM degree or something in the trades rather than a pointless liberal arts degree, this college is a good choice. I left after three semesters but it had nothing to do with the college and had circumstances been different I would gladly have finished out my four year degree here.", 'A college campus that I thought I\'d never see. They have a really generous acceptance rate so if you are just sitting shy of a few credits and want to finish your degree, talk to them. They have a great staff to help plan things and the chancellor very strict on keeping the campus tidy and free of ice and snow. And the price isn\'t that expensive compared to a lot of other universities. The only complaint I have is the general feel. It seems like I\'m going to some school slightly above a community college but not quite a "college".']

name: Flathead Valley Community College
reviews:
["Both of my kids went here, one is still going and the other transferred to Montana Tech for engineering.  They both told me it is a good school and the engineering stuff prepared one well for MT.  I'm so glad that they make it affordable for local residents!", 'One of the best Community Colleges in the whole state. I went their for there Land Surveying program. It has been completely update to be online and local.', 'Great college, tons of opportunities. Word on the block is the engineering department is good.', 'Never experienced worse college/university/continuing education admissions. Took a class here years ago and had to call Disability Services to register for classes.

The class itself was enjoyable, especially because of the varied student population. It was interactive and included essay exams.

FVCC sponsors a weekly speaker series on world topics, featuring speakers from across the nation. Apologies for the cuss word “world” if that offends anyone’s religion. These series focus more on the Golden Rule and honesty than on pressured conformity.', 'Wonderful staff and opportunities to learn and pursue academic goals! Helped me through the process greatly, and is a good start for anyone looking to stay in the valley for education.']

name: Great Falls College Montana State University
reviews: ["The adult learning classes in school is the most phenomenal experience. I've ever had when it comes to learning mathematics. And other subjects, the teachers, Bobby, Melissa and Christie are so phenomenal. It was quite the experience, amazing staff down-to-earth, people. And just the knowledge, these folks have is unreal. If you're studying for the asvab highset or just wanna brush up on any mass skills or other extracurricular? Scholastic skills definitely. Definitely. I need to check them out. They don't judge you based on how while you read or anything like that.Just pure love and joy in these folks is hard.And they are willing to give you the time and day", 'Our daughter and two sons attend the college readiness Hi-Set courses.  The teachers and staff are helpful and supportive. What an amazing program.', 'Great Falls College is located in Montana. That offers programs to choose from. Students who study for a higher in-depth learning of education will accomplish a standard degree of self-worth, and they will know that hard work pays off.', 'Clean facility with very helpful faculty. The Bookstore cafe is a great place to go for very good coffee.', "Admissions, testing, and advising are great. I was going to take a summer class, but I didn't because my school wouldn't accept the transfer. Then I get a $30 charge from the school. When I went today to see what the charge was explaining I didn't even attend a class there they told me it was a non-refundable registration fee. After I already paid the application fee in addition to this. The gal couldn't even give me a payment due date, but told me I would be sent to collections if I didn't pay it. So be aware of the fact that this college takes money any way they can get it even if you do not actually attend with them. Student Accounts shows no empathy or solution seeking options. Not impressed at all. All other departments are great, however.\n\nMoved from 2 stars to 1 star because they used to offer free proctored tests, and now charge $15 each time I go. As a non student, who take online classes I'm giving your school way too much money to plug a test key into the computer each time I visit. Way to use your monopoly."]

name: University of Providence
reviews: ["Staff doesnt know how to treat veterans and when telling them you want all classes covered by you're va benefits they cant even do that simple thing. Would highly not recommend going to this school if using a gi bill this school go somewhere else.", 'UP was my alma mater back in the days when it was still called CGF (College of Great Falls).  I’m in my late 70s now but my 4 years there live on in my memory as some of the best of my life.  The phrase “small but mighty” always comes to mind when describing the school and I think it has maintained that feel and reputation over the years. At any rate, I loved every minute of my time at CGF (UP) and will cherish fond memories of it for the rest of my days.', 'The Staff was very friendly, and at exactly helpful very knowledgeable.', "Being a transfer student from ISU I'm impressed . The latter statement was 4 years ago. I graduated this year with plans to go to graduate school. The school has issues that, are not taken seriously or are ignored. Many changes, though minor can improve and help student learning at no additional cost. Even with the multitude of problems the university has,  they will never be solved unless they hire a mediator to work with students and staff. Such person must have a likable personality and known among the students, professors and staff to properly retrieve information to suggest changes. Our new President is a very likable and devoted individual.  But such a position prevents him actually to see what is taking place on campus. The university has provided me an excellent education I could not have gotten from a more prestigious university.  The staff and professors go above and beyond what is required of them to help struggling students. The university is very humble in their devotion to students and provide a one on one.service to students. But as I mentioned there are many things in need of change. For example;  this is the only university I know that has banking hours for a study environment.  The library is the primary place of study but opens at 730 am and closes at 10pm. If you are in need of more studying time your out of luck. They graciously extend the hours by 2 during midterm and finals. Though the the library is over staffed and only one librarian has a devoted concern towards students, beware if you bother the others for help and interrupt their online movies and other activities.", 'I ATTENDED THE  UNIVERSITY OF GREAT FALLS READING FOR AN M.A. DEGREE IN LIBERAL STUDIES. I ENJOYED THE PROGRAM, FACULTY AND THE OTHER GRADUATE STUDENTS. I WAS MOST WELCOME AS A CANADIAN. PETER J.M. PALLESEN.']

name: Helena College University of Montana
reviews:
['Best school ever!! My kids love coming to interact with the college kids.  Staff is awesome, helping you always to find a path towards a career.', 'The high success rate of graduates in the HiSet Program is obviously due to the amazing staff members. After attending today for the first time, I feel motivated and feel like I have a clear path ahead of me. Thank you for being amazing 👏', 'Although a small College, Helena College offers a wide range of programs and courses. The staff is incredibly helpful and nice. The classes are small which makes it easier to get individualized attention. The campus is well maintained and easily accessible for all.', 'I am about 70 years old and deaf so consider this source.    I wanted to sign up  for a small engine mechanics class (to learn to maintain an ATV).    When I went to admissions they told me they would send me the necessary literature and I gave them my mail address.  "No problem",    she said.

That was the last I have "heard" or seen from them.      Perhaps they dont want old deaf people as students.

jus'   sayin'

P.S.      I have a masters degree in science from the University of Nevada at Reno,   but I am not a real doctor (ha).   So college has been no stranger to me until  I dealt with the admissions lady here............', 'No one is ever online to help you. Even when they’re supposedly open no one ever answers your calls. Good classes, if only their website ACTUALLY WORKED SO YOU COULD ACTUALLY REGISTER FOR CLASSES. Terrible service, horrific support system.']

name: Little Big Horn College
reviews: ['I received my AA in Human Services from here, great place to learn! Awesome staff! Ask for Eric Tiner if you want to pursue anything to deal with Human Services and tell him Monty sent you. Yes!', 'We were there for delivering a post-flood aid for the Little Big Horn community. We were greeted with such a welcoming hospitality. Thank you, Aldean!', 'Very fine institution. The Apsaalooke people are friendly and accepting. They actually thanked me for learning their language.', 'Very nice studying environment for the pursuit of my major and very caring for their students.', 'Classes are a bit lacking, but what they do have, they do well. Also a bit tough to get comfortable and relax for long periods of time.']

name: Miles Community College
reviews: ['The best food in town all from scratch, the coffee is fantastic and the people there make the experience that much more amazing!', 'College is nothing fancy compared to other colleges I have attended, but it has everything you will need. Miles City is a terrible place to live, nothing but churches, bars, and small casinos. City has almost no diversity. Though the Bucking Horse Sale in the summer is super fun. The summers are scorching hot and the winters are bitterly cold. Living here for two years was torture, but I received a grade A nursing education from them that began my nursing career 13 years ago. Thank you Miles Community College.', 'Not the fanciest place, but still a great place to further your education. Staff is awesome!', 'Love this place. I work in the kitchen. I cook dinner so come on down.', 'Great place and great people I completely recommend, anf the cafe is excellent']

name: Montana Technological University
reviews: ["Great campus, fantastic staff, looking forward to my daughter's college career days", 'I came put to watch my buddies son play. What a nice campus!!! Too bad the football coaches cant control the teams poor sportsmanship and swearing at the crowd. What a disgrace to talk to another team and their parents. Hope #80 gets his mouth cleaned out and #31 stops flipping the crowd off when his teammates make good plays while he stands on his cruches. #12 seemed to be the only one out there with some positive sportsmanship. Go sports team!!!', 'My son graduated in this school. Great school and landed him a great job! He had a little difficulty thriving the first year, he is a California boy, but bloomed to be a great student and embraced the beauty of Montana by fishing and hunting. You want your kid to have a great job, skip liberal arts. A skilled job will do your kid good. He graduated with a Engineering degree.', "My time spent here has been an amazing advancement towards my career and I have created everlasting friendships. I have been able to complete all my classes on time  and have had the opportunity to work one on one with the professors. They are very understanding and the small community provides a family like atmosphere that can't be beat. You get to know most of your fellow students and create contacts that come from all across the world. The rowdy crowds are always a great support for our teams and the town of Butte has so much history that I feel honored to live in such a close knit town. This school provides careers right after graduation and honestly, I could not have chosen a better school to attend if I wanted to. This place has been a home to me and challenged me in ways I never thought I could overcome.", "Currently attending and it's exactly what I paid for; an engineering campus with renowned rigorous classes. The other review posted by the helicopter-parent isn't true. The campus is great and the staff are very reliable. However, the classes are/will be hard! This parent was obviously lied to by their child who didn't put enough effort into their academics. If one wants to succeed at Montana Tech they have to put in some hard work. This is why Montana Tech DOES create many internship opportunities. Companies realize the dedication students must commit to complete their education at Tech. If the homework for the classes are completed, a student can definitely expect success and job opportunities in their chosen field.\n\nP.S. The food isn't great, but they are currently working on Grill options and are definitely improving."]

name: Montana State University
reviews:
['MSU does not only charges students to park, but also does not and cannot guarantee parking to individuals with parking passes. Students often have to show up significantly early to get parking and cannot leave during the day without losing their spot. There are more students with parking passes then there are parking spaces.
The campus also does not provide adequate ice removal despite shaded areas and high foot traffic.', 'I have gotten 4 degrees at msu my first on having credits from 3 other colleges as I was in the military while working on it. Msu is by far the best university  i have attended. Does it have problems? Like any large bureaucracy yes. But generally  it is still personal and you can usually  find an actual person that will directly  help you with whatever issue you are having. Also the vet support center is the best in the country.', 'Such a beautiful campus. Visited the bookstore for some Cat gear... which I highly recommend! Walked down to see the ducks and up to the tailgates section. Go Bobcats!', 'I graduated from MSU in 2014, and I had a good experience. I remember the professors were impartial and fair, with nothing standing out in my memory to the contrary.

I visited again recently this year (2025) and the campus has grown a ton. There are several new buildings and renovations that have been completed since my time there.

The only issue that I had was there was a program for people that lived in Washington and Idaho to attend the school and not pay out of state tuition. I recall that I was initially charged the out of state tuition, but it ended up being a moot point I did not have to peruse due to attaining an ROTC scholarship.

I received my degree in Psychology, and while this school has a stronger agricultural and engineering focus, I still found that the psych program nested well as a scientifically focused degree, and it seemed to be well run.

MSU will foster your education, and you will get out what you put in.', 'This university does not care about its students, it just cares about making money and beating record enrollment.']

name: The University of Montana

We went to the game last night. It looked packed and all the students and band made the surrounding mountains ring with cheers. Such a great atmosphere for a night game. Wish they had another video screen on the other end though. Also it would be great if you could have a beer in your seat. Still it was a great place to see a game.', 'Nice collage campus in a somewhat historical area. Easy walkabout or bike riding location.  Many trails, although the "M" trail is a bit tough, other sections and river bridge to the old City near by.  Hidden road trails on the back side on the "M" to car ride. Small town feel with all the amenities needed in a modern Era.']

name: Montana State University-Northern
reviews: ['I attended the diesel program at MSU-Northern and it was very disappointing. If you are an engaged person that actually wants to learn something, this is not the school for you. The only reason I am giving it 2 stars is because I liked the campus and I had one teacher that was absolutely awesome.', 'My husband has been waiting for his books in the mail for the trades program in Plumbing for 5/6 months now. He has paid for them and we have spoke to multiple people in admissions office and then get sent to a voicemail of the registration office who never answers and won’t call back! We have been told his books are on the way and then told they don’t have any information on him and each time it’s a new excuse! We’ve even had email contact with registration and admissions saying the books would be sent and they have not. I am shocked by the lack of care, it’s been MONTHS! He could have been onto new coursework by now yet hasn’t gotten his first book? We are simply just a family trying to better our lives and education, please make this right.', 'Beautiful campus, rich history, excellent profs, great facilities in a quiet, safe community.', 'Great programs, small class sizes, many ways to get assistance no matter what kind of student you are.', "The academic office has no clue on what they're doing, and have made it very difficult for transfer students. They are not attentive and are very disorganized. Not satisfied."]

name: Rocky Mountain College
reviews: ['Staff is great! Nice friendly atmosphere...\nI visit campus once a month to speak with students and staff about The Navy. I am a Navy Recruiter and live to hear stories from past service members/ veterans. Also to hear of the students who have questions about joining the Navy.\nCampus is great and I would recommend their aviation program.', 'The only saving grace this college has is the genuine kindness of it academic professors. The higher level individuals and pro staff that run the, Housing, Cafeteria, and Sports departments make living at and working for Rocky a nightmare. The majority of the student work jobs are a sad joke, one where students work too much for little to no pay or feel as though their job is pointless. Rumors of not only students, but staff alike, actually affect the reputation and way the rest of those on campus treat you, whether those rumors are true or not. Rocky claims to have a great community and top notch everything. Living, working, and going to school here made me feel like a slave in prison. Save yourself time and money by not even visiting.', "The campus and staff are very helpful in every aspect. It's a beautiful campus. My granddaughter is enjoying new adventures in college", 'The counselors have been so helpful in getting me set up as an incoming freshman - truly helpful staff and remarkable teamwork! A great experience thus far.', "There is no consideration for people who want access but are not students. Don't even try to use the place as they don't want you. Parking is hopeless and finding the place on Google Maps ... they don't have the data. This place is for their students only. As an outsider it is not worth your time or effort."]

reviews: ['Disc Golf Course is alot of fun for new players and families.', "I don't have the time or space to say all the good things I want to about this place. name: The University of Montana-Western
reviews: ['The block schedule is great and makes it easy to balance work and school. The professors I had were amazing! Small class sizes made it easier for more one on one time with professors without having to go to office hours. If you’re reading this and aren’t entirely sure what you want to study, Western is both a great place to start college because of low tuition, and a terrible place to start too. If you’re looking for unique weirdly specific classes that broaden your perspective to give you a better idea of what’s out there, you might find them here but definitely not as frequently as other educational institutions. Big shoutout to the Biology, Education, and Math departments.', 'Delightful University. Excellent group of Professors. Custodians are awesome people. They keep Western spotless', 'The X1 program at UM Western is great. Received a BS here and I loved the block schedule. Some really cool classes spent in Yellowstone, Craters of the Moon, and Moab. Great school.', 'Great University in a Home Town Setting! Come for the outdoors lifestyle.', 'Gotta be one the most poorly run schools out there.']

name: Bellevue University
reviews:
["My advisor takes a minimum of 2 weeks to get back to me and then gives me the wrong information. I'd like to finish my degree, please find someone competent to assist students in their pursuit to actually graduate.", 'I pay thousands of dollars in tuition, yet Bellevue University only provides a paper student ID without a photo instead of a proper plastic one. On top of that, I have to print it out myself online as a student. I tried to use this ID to get a student discount at a local business, but I was refused — because anyone could easily make a fake one. It was truly embarrassing.

I contacted Bellevue University, but they said they have no plans — past, present, or future — to issue regular photo student IDs. Future students considering Bellevue University, please take note: you might end up feeling the same embarrassment I did.', "Emails: Complete the setup of your Student Email Account

I already have a Bruin account with you guys because I'm alumni. I just wanted info on another degree program, but instead of just showing that on the website, you're forcing people to click on the 'Request More Info' button. I still haven't received info on the program either. All I'm getting are these stupid emails wanting me to setup my account, which I do not need to do. I already have one, but others shouldn't have to setup accounts and jump through MS Outlook hoops and all of that, just to get info on a program.

Are you trying to scare people away? You did with me. I am no longer interested in returning to Bellevue University now, and I guess I'll just need to block everything coming from you, since it's all spam and contains nothing of which I requested. Sad!", "I inquired about their social sciences program and made it known to please call during certain times as I work full time in a doctor's office and can't step away to answer. They ignored that and were calling and texting me nonstop every day for a week and a half. I finally got ahold of someone in admissions and requested to only email me because the calls becoming too much and they weren't trying to work with my schedule. Sabrina Buls started to help me, and we both were guilty of playing cat and mouse. I had an abrupt family situation happen and I imagine she had many other potential students reaching out for information. She finally told me that we could do my professional college advisory session via email and sent me some questions to answer. I replied back to her and never heard from her again. It's been almost 3 weeks and classes start September 8th. I will go somewhere else. Clearly this isn't the college for me as they're super unprofessional.", "I am graduating with my Bachelors in August. My advisor Nakita was great and extremely nice. She will do everything she can to make sure you succeed. All the teachers give good feedback and they will work with you. You get what you give. Time management, learning the material given, and being able to follow instructions will set you up to pass.

I had a few bad grades back in 2022. I took a year off and came back stronger, changing my major, and getting all A's and B+ for the remainder of my undergraduate.  If I get all A's with my Kirkpatrick Series this summer than I will graduate with over a 3.0 overall GPA and my major GPA is 3.7. Point is you are the master of your own education. I will be able to pursue my master degree. I have grown so much from college in the past two years.

I had my eldest daughter when I was 18. I was in poverty but I always tried to make it out. I went to trade school then I decided to get my degree. It was an adjustment going back to school when I was 25. I had my youngest daughter in the end of 2020 and wanted to go to school while I was a stay at home mom. It was trying to say the least. I had so many personal issues because life will always be life.

I have become someone I can say without a doubt, my daughters could be proud of. I have become someone I can be proud of. No one else in my entire family has graduated college. I am able to confidently provide a future for myself and my family. I suppose not everyone has the same experience or likes the school but I will always be grateful to this university.

I guess this was long compared to other reviews, but I really wanted to share my gratitude."]

name: Clarkson College
reviews: ['Unimpressed in the Masters program. Some professors are uninvolved. The classes are pre programed, timed to post. Responses to some professors are delayed. name: Bryan College of Health Sciences
reviews:
["After intimately researching over 50 colleges in the last year and a half, I found Bryan College of Health Sciences. Ranked 15 in the nation, last years graduates had a 100% pass rate on their ARDMS exams. I moved my family halfway across the country to attend this college. Why? Because I know that I will obtain my degree, with student debt attached. However, debt and a degree does not get you registered (or in some states licensed). You have to be able to pass your board exams. With Bryan's excellent pass rates, most of the time at 100%, I am confident I will be able to pass my board exams as well, and that is what is most important at the end of the program. I have already passed my SPI physics exam for sonography, the first time. Additionally, the college does not only accept low/high GPA students, and they do not turn away students who have transferring credits from another institution. I transferred in with a 4.0 cumulative GPA, with an exponential amount of transfer credits. The college accepts a whole host of diverse students. I made an excellent choice, and will graduate in two more semesters! Go Bryan!", 'There is very little that can be said about Bryan College, at least nothing good.  The academic culture mixed with poor management have diminished this program to a second rate center for education. Of course I am only pertaining to the nursing program, other programs may be fine and well, but the overall entity is still managed by the same group of inept individuals.
Speaking strictly about the BSN-Nursing program:  There always appeared to be some disconnect with the instructors and the students, as if the professors were almost burned out. I'm sure the professional burned was not helped with a vast majority of the professors focusing on ascertaining their own Doctorate in Education.  Other professors, for a lack of better works, were just too old or incapable to changing with the times. It seemed that there would always be a technological issues or they teach from their own outdated point of views. literally not teaching the science of the practice, but sharing minimally applicable stories of the "good ole days".
Bryan does a pretty good job of selling individuals on how  they are Great and Wonderful, and that here we are all family! This only holds true if you if you a willing to sacrifice a majority of your own identity. You see, if you voice your concerns or professionally speak your mind- they will can make your educational experience hell.  For example, I was in a clinical situation bearing witness to a  medication being, it was not me who administrated the medication. Afterwards, I received an Unsatisfactory for the clinical week for asking my clinical instructor what ramifications would have ensued if I were to admin the medication under RN supervision.  Furthermore, after each clinical week you a required to  write a self-evaluation, providing your strengths and weakness, what you plan to do differently next week, and express any personal concerns that you had during your clinical experience. Not once, but three separate times I was reprimanded for voicing my concerns. Additionally, I would say that 50 to 60% of clinical experiences is extreme hand-holding and the clinical sites don't provoke much intellectual growth- as if the course of the day was not very well thought out.
Classroom lectures were lack luster at best. The educators were rarely engaging, missed several key concepts needed for NCLEX, and boy-oh-boy did they love showing movies. I found that if you missed a class it really did effect you on the tests, you would have to learn the material on your own anyhow. The educators did a poor job of teaching at a higher level of quality. I would think for 20+K/year a professional should provide better education or at the very least prepare the students for their future careers.
In summation of my own personal experiences: It is most certainly not worth the money, the education provided is substandard and you will have a strong sense of being prepared for saving lives. Lastly, a large majority  of the individuals that attend the college are fresh out of high school, so if you can't deal with teenybopper gossip and drama that constantly encompasses the environment then I HIGHLY recommend looking into another college. At the end of the day all your employer really wants to know is that you care about your patients, your jobs, and every action that you perform is well thought-out and causes no harm AND not where you went to school!
I hope this helps any potential candidates, its most certainly is not in favor of Bryan College of Health Science , but I can not in good conscience go without voicing my serious concerns.
Take everything with a grain of salt, but understand that I am a nurse and know few things especially speaking from first-hand experience.', 'This is a top notch Health Professions College.  The Nursing programs are the best around. They are cutting edge on what they teach and how they teach.  You receive from the program what you put into the program.', "It's beautiful campus, gives exceptional training for medical support staff", 'Fantastic private college providing instruction in Nursing and other health professions.']

name: Creighton University
reviews:
["Fairly certain people attend school here, so that's neat. Has at least fountain on campus. Various trees and little plant things. Access to other fun activities such as walking and skipping about. 5 stars.", "If you’re a Paramedic hoping to advance with Creighton’s Critical Care program and you earned your medic through a hospital-based, NREMT-accredited program, save yourself the trouble. I met every requirement, yet the enrollment office fixated on the lack of a “traditional transcript” — as if modern healthcare education hasn’t moved beyond paper trails.

My program, based at a Level 1 Trauma Center, sent the documentation directly. I personally reached out to the EMS program multiple times. They stated they had their hands tied. I even contacted the President’s office. The result? Silence. Indifference. A complete unwillingness to engage.

For a university that markets itself as forward-thinking, the rigidity and lack of responsiveness are incredibly disappointing. Having been stationed at Offutt and having earned my Bachelor’s from Bellevue, I expected Creighton to rise above bureaucratic box-checking. Instead, they’ve shown they care more about outdated processes (or perhaps they think the pennies I'd bring to the school just aren't shiny enough) than about advancing today’s healthcare professionals.

:-(", 'Creighton  has a beautiful campus.  The students are bright and friendly and it seems to be a very inclusive environment.', 'Great staff and students, the future is bright', 'SUPER FRIENDLY AND GOOD ATOMSPHERE']

name: Doane University
reviews:
['Doane University is a pretty small college located in Crete, NE but the campus is so green and beautiful. Students can walk all classes no needs to ride on bike or e-scooter. Also, each class sizes are pretty small between 5 to 50. Students are easily able to communicate to their professors during class. Of course, the location is very local and it might be hard to access there but it would be valuable for students studying at a small & beautiful campus like Doane.', "Do NOT bring your dogs to any sporting events held here. We have brought our 2 well-behaved smaller dogs to all of our Sons games this season, and every location has been very welcoming of our fur babies being there.
We did not have the same welcoming vibe as we did with other colleges
Upon arrival, we weren't sure where  to sit , we decided to walk all the way to the farther bleachers, assuming that was the side for the away team fans, we reached the bleachers only to be told that we couldn't sit there
Ok, so we walk all the way back to the opposite side & we decided to stand by the fence and wait for the current game to end , seconds after standing by the fence a guy on a golf cart rushes up to us to tell us that dogs are not allowed in the stands ok fine rules are rules but he did not need to be so rude and grouchy about the situation .
This same man watched over us the entire game, giving us dirty looks
We just wanted to watch our Sons game.
My husband said that the mens bathroom 🚻 floor had urine all over the floor. Maybe less attention on guarding empty bleachers and families with dogs and more attention to the nasty bathroom.
We are  so grateful that other college campuses have been so welcoming & and friendly. We  could NOT wait to leave THIS campus !", 'Beautiful campus in Crete, and top-rate facilities! name: University of Nebraska at Kearney
reviews:
['Good enough, parking is ridiculous for the cost of a permit. What does $100 a year get… not convenient parking. Oh there’s a game your permit is no longer valid. The UNK crew parks all over the side of the road I’m sure to get valuable fixes done but makes the parking lot very dangerous.', "Nice looking campus.  Very nice gym.  (The popcorn at the volleyball tournament was so incredibly salty, we couldn't eat it and had to return it)", "A campus bathed in beauty and sunlight.A Campus Bathed in History and Sunlight
Stepping onto this campus is like stepping into a living postcard.  Ancient oaks, their branches heavy with years and wisdom, drape intricate shadows across the sun-dappled lawns.  The buildings themselves seem to whisper stories of generations past, their weathered brick facades and ivy-clad walls echoing with the laughter and debates of countless students.
A gentle breeze carries the scent of freshly cut grass and blooming flowers, mingling with the soft murmur of conversation and the distant strum of a guitar.  Students lounge on the grassy slopes, their textbooks open beside them, while others hurry along the paved pathways, a sense of purpose in their stride.
The heart of campus is a bustling hub of activity.  A grand fountain, its water sparkling in the sunlight, serves as a meeting point, surrounded by benches where students gather to chat or share a quiet moment.  Nearby, the library stands tall and proud, its towering windows hinting at the wealth of knowledge contained within.
Beyond the central hub, the campus unfolds like a tapestry of diverse spaces.  Modern science labs hum with the energy of discovery, while cozy coffee shops offer a warm respite for contemplation.  Hidden courtyards invite quiet reflection, and vibrant murals add splashes of color to unexpected corners.
This campus is more than just a collection of buildings; it's a vibrant ecosystem of learning, a place where history and modernity intertwine, and where the pursuit of knowledge is woven into the very fabric of its being.", 'Parking is a bit of a mess and challenging if your visiting from out of town but the stadium is really nice.', 'First time even calling, lady in admissions VERY rude.']

name: Nebraska Methodist College of Nursing & Allied Health
reviews: ['I attended an event and I was very impressed both by the people and the facility! What a gem for Omaha ❤️', 'Super friendly. Fun and exciting. Definitely the school where my child will be going.', "This review is for the phlebotomy course at NMC, NMC's teaching, and my clinical experience. The course is broken up into 2 weeks in the classroom and 3 weeks in clinical rotation. I rate the classroom teaching as exemplary. Professor Di Lorenzo is passionate about what she teaches and very knowledgeable about phlebotomy and lab work, as she is an industry veteran. One would think that as a NMC student, being sent to Methodist Hospital for clinical rotation would be a good match, as the hospital and school are linked (students are sent to non-Methodist sites as well). There was no organized training program or trainer, thus no consistency. We were assigned daily to phlebotomists that were working the floor on that day. Overall I trained with at least 8-10 people. There were only 2 people I worked with where I sensed he/she trusted me, had patience, and was willing to demonstrate skills and answer questions, and treat me with general respect. Otherwise, I dealt with poor attitude, at times being abandoned by the trainer (where did they go?), and a general lack of interest in training and responsibilities that go along with it. The person promoted to the training coordinator position towards the end of our clinical rotation is a good phlebotomist. However unfortunately I wouldn't be surprised if this person's severe demeanor puts potential new employees off. During the time I spend with this person, I sensed I was being brow-beaten. I didn't feel welcome at Methodist Hospital as a student, and sensed the students were a burden to be dealt with. As a non-employee, one could also sense the malcontent between employees and management. Said management seemed to take very little interest in our training (i.e. asking how training was going, what our overall goals are, asking how did we did in classroom training, etc.). NMC is a great and reputable college and has a great teaching staff. The clinical portion, which is a large portion of the course, was a disappointment.", 'Very nice very     Tubby very big']

name: Metropolitan Community College Area
reviews: ['Metropolitan College of New York at 60 West Street is frequently described in my professional circles as a pioneering force in Purpose-Centered Education, where the curriculum is uniquely structured to turn classroom theory into immediate social and economic impact. From numerous conversations with alumni who have utilized its accelerated programs, it is evident that the institution provides a substantive, results-oriented environment that many of my acquaintances credit for their rapid transition into leadership roles within the city’s public and private sectors. It is truly impressive to observe how MCNY maintains such a transparent and respectful focus on empowering working professionals, a quality that is widely praised for making a rigorous degree both attainable and deeply relevant to the challenges of modern urban life. In the collective view of New Yorkers, this college stands as a distinguished pillar of civic engagement, rightfully celebrated for its sophisticated ability to merge professional development with a profound commitment to social justice and community service.', "Metropolitan College of New York (MCNY) is a private institution located in New York City. Founded in 1964, MCNY offers a range of undergraduate and graduate programs focused on preparing students for careers in business, education, human services, and public affairs. The college emphasizes experiential learning, community engagement, and social responsibility, providing students with practical skills and knowledge to succeed in their chosen fields. With a diverse student body and a commitment to serving non-traditional students, MCNY provides flexible scheduling options, including evening and weekend classes, to accommodate working professionals and adult learners. The college's urban campus is situated in the heart of Manhattan, offering students access to internships, networking opportunities, and cultural resources in one of the world's most dynamic cities.", 'Great private school, professors are helpful, offers a great variety of online courses, campus is beautifully designed and decorated, very inviting atmosphere. This picture is the silent room comfortably furnished right next to a very inviting lounge. As a student I very much enjoy studying here. The level of diversity is amazing, and everyone is helpful and kind.', "I am your neighbor in Battery Park City and MCNY is a TERRIBLE neighbor. The HVAC on the top of your building is SCREEEEEEECHING horribly and is causing noise pollution throughout the entire Batter Park City area. I've asked, emailed, called, begged and pleaded for someone to care - and they don't.\n\nNot sure if this attitude carries over to their college - but I'm betting it does. Don't go here until they can figure out how to tighten their HVAC belt.", "I hold a BA in Human Services from MCNY... The way they set up their curriculum makes the probability of graduating on time very high. If you apply yourself you will leave that institution with a lot of new knowledge & beliefs. It has changed me as a person for the better. When I first began MCNY I did attend orientation & was informed that the students who attended have a higher chance at graduating, I can't say how true that is but I did attend orientation & I did graduate so... I would never forget Micheal Molina who said you will not leave this school the same person you came in as. He was right! I left a human service professional (HSP). I always knew I possessed the compassion, morals & understanding that one needs to become a HSP, but what I left my school with only enhanced my abilities & added much more to it. This school literally changed my life. It helped me look into the person I was. It has helped me in my personal life. While you are attending MCNY it may be hard to appreciate but as I graduated as this new person I have to say my money has been well spent! A lot of money!!!!!!! Lol but my education at MCNY was the best investment I ever made & I mean that from the bottom of my heart!"]

name: Midland University
reviews:
["I can't speak for others, but I can speak from personal experience. I recently graduated from Midland University Spring of 2023. This is a solid university for those who apply themselves, like anything you get what you put into it.  I attended for my bachelor's degree in Art Management.  The professors care about the students and their success. The school is very active with engaging the community and various societies on campus. Midland may not be for everyone only because it is tucked away in Fremont Nebraska and very community oriented. All my instructors had an open door or was always available for meetings if I needed instructions. The hybrid option is great for those who require it and when needed. The acceptance from everyone, be it age or whatever is none like I have encountered, and that is an amazing part. It is hard not to feel judged, but here I never was as a returning adult to the classroom. I have made lifelong friends and countless networks from my attendance. If you have questions, all you have to do is just ask they will tell you or they will find the answer.  Midland University graduate 2023, Suma Cum Laude B.A. Art Management.", 'Although the sticker price is high...most students do not pay that amount.  Like many colleges...you get out what you put in.  I found the business instructors to be a nice mix of career professors and real world business professionals.  This provided a blend of learning/understanding and applying concepts; they always had time for me and questions I had.

The facilities over need attention across a variety of elements which they are working on.

The student body is filled with great people.  Many of the people I met still talk daily despite living states and even continents away.', "Living Hell. Attending Midland was one of the worst experiences of my life. I have only been attending the school for almost a semester and I can tell you that I wouldn't wish this place on anyone. There are too many cons to write about so I will focus on the major ones. Firstly, if you are trying to live a healthy lifestyle, forget about it at Midland. The caff has the worst quality of food I have ever experienced. The caff workers are rude and dampen your mood. My dorm room has gashes in the walls and is in a general state of disrepair. I haven't had a stable connection to the wifi in my entire time being here. The quality of this school amounts to a community college. If it were 4k a year, then it might be worth the quality you'll receive here, but instead it's 35k. On top of that, you will have to pay for the damages that the neighbors on your flood committed. If you are considering going here for athletics, I would advise against it. The coaching staff here is awful. I came for soccer, there are many players who feel degraded and have lost their love for the game. My friends on the other sports teams have only negative things to say about their respective coaching staffs. Most of the classes I have taken seemed pointless. DO NOT LET THEM PULL YOU IN. Going to Midland was the worst decision of my life. It set has been a great waste of money and has set me back. I cannot even explain how horrible it is as Midland. There are many many more cons to write about, but I don't have the time. Learn from my mistake... DON'T GO TO MIDLAND!", 'Careful about sending your kids here, these people are frauds sometimes- I was a student enrolled in Music Education. Coming from an underprivileged background, I knew I needed a public service job with tenure, benefits, and loan forgiveness, and I felt it went hand-in-hand with my passions for music, teaching, and helping kids.
They gave me high-interest, private student loans to help pay for their ridiculous tuition while I was a music education major. My grandpa cosigned my student loans, because he believed that music education was a good investment for me.
When this administration took the campus over, they cut the entire music program, fired the faculty, and dropped all the music education students (it was only me). They told me I didn't have a choice, I could either get a *worthless* performance degree because it was the only thing my credits were still good for, or transfer to a new school and add years to my education. This was a lie and it was fraud. They were legally obligated to finish the degree I started and signed up for and paid for. It's called a "teach-out" and their failure to finish my education degree was fraud.
But because I was a trusting kid, I didn't know I had to have a lawyer in the room with me when I talked to these executives, when they told me my major was canceled, so I took them at their word.
Fast Forward, it is now past the statute of limitations when I realized what criminals they were (and are, these same people still run this campus). They even took white-out to their records and erased the record of me being an education major. They are telling me I was never enrolled in the program, and that I just coincidentally happened to be taking education classes for no reason, that there was no fraud, and that I am harassing them with slander.
I've defaulted on my student loans, there are no jobs that I can use to pay all my bills and these loans besides. The cost of this school's fraud isn't just on me; my grandpa is paying out of his retirement on the loans he cosigned, that were used to pay for my music education. This campus is siphoning my grandpa's retirement money, today, to pay on the fraud they committed on me 12 years ago.
If you're looking to pay top dollar for a private school, I'd recommend going to one that isn't run by frauds who lie to and take advantage of their students. Graduating in 2009 with a worthless degree that was forced on me, that I didn't choose, and a mountain of debt, ruined my life. Permanently. They burned my chance at a future to line their pockets with criminal fraud and got away with it.', 'My son attends Midland and is in his Junior. I have nothing but good thing to say, the faculty and campus is wonderful. My son has really enjoyed his experience there!
Best decision we have ever made for our sons education.']
