name: College of Saint Mary
reviews: ['Amazing college.  Supportive and caring faculty. CSM will always have a special place in my heart!', 'My daughter is a current freshman at CSM and is having an amazing experience! The people on campus are welcoming so much that it feels like a family. She enjoys her classes, athletic coaches, and meetings with her advisor. There are many opportunities for scholarships which makes it affordable. She gets lots of attention at this small college. A+++++', 'This school is more than just a school. The support from the faculty is unparalleled especially for me as a single mother. I graduated the LPN program here in May 2023 and love the campus so much I decided to stay to further my education. What I will say about the nursing program is that while it can be incredibly challenging, there is a reason for that. Everything from the assignments, the exams, to the clinical paperwork set me up for success not only on my NCLEX, but in my practice as a nurse. You don’t want to be learning the important interventions and contraindications for the first time when you’re out in the field especially if you are involved in direct patient bedside care. I couldn’t ask for a better education. This campus makes a point to educate students on diversity and  prepares them to serve people from all walks of life. The only thing I would like to see different is awards and scholarships for mothers on campus who may not be able to participate in as many extracurricular activities.', 'I have to admit. I didn’t vet this school prior to attending the LPN program. I just got in with little effort. And No TEAS required. To sum it up, it was a hazing experience, my opinion. In talking to other classmates, their primary reason for attending, excluding returning students, was because CSM doesn’t require TEAS. Please, just go take the TEAS and get on a waiting list elsewhere. This program has a lot of hoops and is ripe with control freaks. If you’re thinking of coming, all I can say is don’t. The completion rate is a failure (27-38%) for a reason. Let that be your best warning and save your time, effort, money and academic record. And while the school boasts about a 100% NCLEX pass rate, so do the other LPN programs in the region, except this school hasn’t always and doesn’t tell the entire story. MOST people passing failed out of the program (failing one class, means a mandatory repeat…the following year; not semester) the first time, then must wait nearly a year, if they come back at all, to return to complete the program (which isn’t the best in Omaha) and then sit for and pass NCLEX…2 years after initially enrolling a 1 year LPN program elsewhere. Graduation classes are made up of returning students, as the norm. Many of the people in my class were students that failed the LPN program the prior year, and were returning (set up to make you feel as though you have no other option) or they left or failed out of the BSN program and dropped down to the LPN program…prior experience…and still struggle), teaching is ineffective and testing is worse (not enough time, a deliberate attempt to cram everything into a single exam and poorly written…plus, you can’t use a back button to change an answer…and more) they dominate your time, the staff is not diverse, there are only, literally, a few inexperienced NEW first time teaching instructors, MUCH of the grading is subjective, clinicals we’re primarily about how complete a single report sheet was filled in, not patient care, the school needs professional test writers, labs are barely used, student concerns are dismissed or ignored and the costs, financially, are burdensome. And you risk financial aid. Students are afraid of speaking up out loud. As you can tell, there’s no way I’d come back. Don’t do it. Go elsewhere, MCC (the best school), Lincoln, Columbus or Iowa.', "This school seems to have great academic programs. But I will say that it is not a very welcoming campus. As a transfer sophomore student, I have gone to many of the events to meet people but people are not welcoming. Many- not all- of the girls are rude and it's like no one knows the decency of a polite conversation. I will be staying at this school because of my program but the people here are stuck up, rude, and the school lacks helping new students fit in unless you are on a sports team. Screw people who are just here for academics I guess. Because they aren't going to have events that people can go to to meet people on their floor or who live on campus.\nLet's just say it is a very lonely campus and while I enjoy my classes, the people are stuck up and do not appear to have manners."]

name: Southeast Community College Area
reviews:
["Southeast Community College is the best Community College in Nebraska. I love the infrastructures,  all the courses,  especially Computer Science and Nursing.  The administration and faculty are excellent. My  daughter, Martha,  is on the women's wrestling team, the Bobcats! Five stars🌟 for SCC 🥰", 'Dropped a class 5 days after it began and they refuse to give any refund. Somebody may respond and say their drop policy is posted but most would agree it’s not right to pocket 100% of the money when the consumer received less than 10% of the product. The UI on the hub is extremely outdated and looks like it hasn’t been updated since 2007. Also compared to other community colleges they are pricey. Other comments on here claim they are only $363 but I paid $600 for one online class. Go to metro instead especially if it’s online', 'I will start off by saying this school has potential and I feel like it really depends on what program you’re going into. That being said, I feel like the health science department is a joke. I was a transfer student and the very first time I met with my assigned advisor she more or less told me that I wasn’t going to make it in the field and I should quit now and find a different career. When it came to taking the next steps I was given some misinformation and when trying to figure out what I needed to do, I was met with a lot of rudeness, push back, and being passed around not getting straight answers of who I needed to contact. I got tired of it and went directly to the head chair member. When I got a response it was worded VERY harshly and basically told me I was SOL. I’m not upset about not getting the answer I was hoping for, I’m LIVID that I wasted 2 years of my life being told I was able to do something when it was never a possibility. I could’ve already been done with the program somewhere else. They REALLY need to work on their communication and people skills. I honestly wouldn’t waste my time if you have ANY self-respect.

I also had a MAJOR issue when filing for FASFA. I had sent ALL of the required paperwork in months before the semester started, and they LOST one of the forms. I understand mistakes happen, but I ONLY found out when I contacted them on why it hadn’t been processed. This led to me not being able to sign up for classes until after they had already started and I had to play catch up.

That being said, all the individual professors and most of the supporting staff were great and I loved being in their classes.', 'Had a campus visit today as an option for my daughter for college. Appreciate the opportunity to talk with a staff member and a tour of the campus. Absolutely amazing facilities.', 'Advisors do not care about students; difficult to get anything done regarding signing up for classes. If you have a IEP make sure you register every freaking semester because it does not automatically transfers']

name: Union Adventist University
reviews: ['Very good quality education at a very affordable price. Great staff and student success team. Highly recommend!', 'Union is a great place if you are looking for a private conservative Christian college with quality education.  Their nursing, PA and education programs are some of the best in the region and nation.  Their pre-med program for many years had 100% acceptance to medical schools.  I had to work part time to help pay school, and the alumni gave back with scholarships and helped pay about a third of my tuition and room and board!  Many teachers would pray before each class and would even pray with you individually.   It’s a small college which means great teacher-student ratio.  Unlike public university with one teacher per 200-400 students, at Union, if I’m not mistaken it was one teacher per 12 students or something around that.  Again, it’s a private conservative Christian college, so if your values are on the opposite spectrum, this is probably not the best match for you or your children.  It’s worth noting that friends of mine who held different values than Union but chose to be mature, realistic and positive, most were able to graduate well, got great jobs and reported great experience.  If you were raised expecting everything to go your way, there is no college or workplace good enough for you or your children.  Union is a great place for college and I def highly recommend it.', 'Hard pass. Dont pay that much money for a degree that won’t get you a job.', "Came here to consider whether I'd want to attend their school for college, and it was a wonderfully whole experience. The students and staff were all very friendly, and were willing to answer any questions or concerns I had regarding the campus. Their facilities were mostly up to date, and the campus is also a short distance from convenience stores and restaurants, which was also a plus. Although I may not end up attending this college, I thoroughly enjoyed my experience at Union and would encourage any unsure students to visit it and see if it's the place for you!", 'I attended the Union college Bachelor of Nursing program and I absolutely loved it. This school is very prestigious, prides itself on not just helping students through their education journey but assisting them in their spiritual journey as well. It definitely does a good job of achieving this. I am glad I attended Union and I highly recommend it.']

name: Nebraska College of Technical Agriculture
reviews: ['Very welcoming. Very friendly. Very hands on. Very good choice for future vets. Many animals including pigs and goats. Perfect choice for future horse riders.', "I chose NCTA because of the friendly, home-like atmosphere on campus. I love the fact that I know almost everybody on campus. The instructors are always willing to help you with any questions that you may have.  NCTA has offered me several opportunities to learn more about the agriculture industry. My participation in several clubs and traveling on the livestock judging team have helped me to make the necessary connections to succeed in today's industry!", 'My experience at NCTA is an extremely large reason behind my career and social success. The social networking that NCTA\'s small but friendly campus offers is one of a kind. The approachability to professors and faculty is exceptional for a busy, growing, college of it\'s size. The faculty and staff at NCTA are advanced in their teaching techniques and approaches all while maintaining the caring and family like culture that is trademark of rural Nebraska. The transition was easy coming from high school and my experience at NCTA aided in my transition to a four year university, with all credits transferring. NCTA offers a large variety of agricultural majors and opportunities for those who are willing to work towards improving themselves and the agriculture industry. "You can lead a horse to water, but can\'t make it drink". NCTA will provide you with the necessary skills, knowledge and professional relationships to make an impact in the agricultural industry, if you choose to take advantage of the great opportunities that await at NCTA.', 'This school is great if you want hands on learning and if you like small class sizes and a small student population! Professors work with students one on one and never leave you behind! At NCTA you are not a number like at a big university! If you want to transfer to UNL, NCTA makes that easy for you to do!', 'I know I made the right choice by coming to NCTA for the first half of my college experience. The hands on learning and smaller class sizes were something I looked for in choosing colleges and I found NCTA offers both of those things and so much more. The teachers here want to see you succeed in college and life after and they are ready to help you get to where you want to be!']

name: Wayne State College
reviews:
['🖤 CD Douglas and Alicia Doresey — True Champions of Student Success at Wayne State College

I can’t say enough about how much CD Douglas and Alicia Doresey have meant to me during my time at Wayne State College. Their support went far beyond the usual “student services” — they genuinely care about each person who walks through their doors.

CD has been a steady source of guidance, always listening patiently and offering thoughtful advice tailored to my struggles and goals. It’s rare to find someone in a busy college setting who takes the time to see you as a whole person, not just a student ID number — but CD does exactly that.

Alicia’s kindness and encouragement have been like a light during some of my toughest moments. She has this way of making you feel seen and understood, and her dedication to helping students navigate challenges is inspiring. Her support helped me stay focused and motivated when things felt overwhelming.

Together, CD Douglas and Alicia Doresey create an environment where students aren’t just pushed through the system — they are truly supported, uplifted, and empowered. Because of their care and dedication, I’ve been able to overcome obstacles I never thought I could.

Wayne State College is lucky to have them. If you’re a student struggling to find your path, they’re the ones who will help you find it.

Thank you both for believing in me when I needed it most.

🖤', 'Cheap can walk everywhere small school can meet everyone  foods not that good', "Awesome environment!  People are so friendly and welcoming. The professors are like our parents. So caring! Small class size, easy to build a good professional relationship with professors. Overall a complete package of quality education you will get here at an affordable cost.

Strongly recommended for both international & domestic students.

Institutional graduation requirements: 120 credit hours
On-campus employment opportunities are available!

Tuition fees: Less than $3000(12 credits)
for international students, if you qualify for the Nebraska Access Tuition scholarship. Other departmental scholarships are available.
For domestic students, I think it's a big win to keep your educational cost lower.

N.B. As a freshman, you are required to live on campus. In that case, the living cost will be around $7000-$8000.

Living cost: It depends. Generally, the rent is $250 -$350 if you live with your roommates including a utility bill, wifi the overall cost will be around $350 -$500 on average. ( for an individual)

Graduates Employment Rate:100%(might vary based on majors)
Lots of clubs such as ACM, WSC International Club, etc.", "This is a great place to come or to send your kids-- predictably safe small Nebraska territory town with all the amenities you need and none you don't.  It is a public school, so plan to be exposed to some ideologically driven teachers in the humanities.  The dorms are close to classes, and the entire campus is well laid out.  It is a fantastic investment for a four year degree college and they have excellent working relationships with the University system should you pursue post grad work.  I found my four years here were fantastic and made good acquaintances with many on the staff.  It's an easy place to get involved and to become a leader.  Drama free environment for the most part.  Alcohol, the bane of most college campuses, seemed to me the only real caution.", "WOW we've been to several college visits this one was impressive. The physical School is older but it has a lot of history.  And it's been renovated it's the Staff and what school offers that impressed us. Google had the entrance at the wrong location. It was down the street but signs for visitor parking made sense so we found it."]

name: Western Nebraska Community College
reviews: ['Has great tech programs taught by instructors who are at the top of their field. They have all come from industry where they practice what they teach. These career areas are in high demand with good pay.  Great Collision Repair/Auto Body program with many options to fit the students needs. Lots of hands on learning. Also has great Automotive, Diesel Welding, Aviation and Powerline programs. Low cost for a great education that makes you job ready in 2 years or less for students who are motivated and apply themselves to learning their trade.', 'My family and I attended the Family Fun Day on April 1st, 2023. We had so much fun. The booths were great and the atmosphere very welcoming. My kids loved the mascot. I wish I could have had his vest he was wearing! We had a lot of fun.', 'This school is a joke. If you are a student that is paying for your own schooling...go somewhere else. They do not communicate with their students about payments, bills, etc. none of that! They are horrible communicators and really do not seem like they have the best interest of their students at mind. They are very disorganized. Most of the classes they make you take don’t even transfer over to most four years. If you are thinking about going to school there, don’t stay In the dorms if you can, they are a waste of money. Due to the some factors like, the WiFi is horrible and the beds suck. I’m trying to do my homework and the WiFi doesn’t work most of the time. Your advisers don’t check with you to see how you’re doing throughout your time there. I was never even told who my adviser was until the next semester to pick classes! During my time there I didn’t not feel welcomed as a student. If I could go back I would have not enrolled at that school. Many times I would call the main campus for questions about statements on my account and they never answered my questions. They just danced around them. They would send me to another department and I’d get sent to voicemail, I’d leave a message with no call back! I’ve gotten attitude from many of the staff there for no reason! As a new student whose never done this college path, you think they’d be more helpful. Some of my teachers never Got back to me about assignments. Honestly, I could just go on with now awful this school is.. if I could give them a 0/10 I would. If I could go back and not enroll at this school..I would. If I were you, I’d take my money elsewhere if you have a choice!! This school may be “cheap” compared to others but wouldn’t you rather pay a little more for a school that cares about you? Cares about you succeeding? Is attentive, listens, and respectful?', 'This will be my first and only good review. Great communication between students and teachers helps to excel any student. I have visited several other colleges; however, none compair to the comfort of WNCC.  In addition, the price of tuition cannon be beat for the amount of knowledge revived.', 'I have received one assiociate degree from this school, and I am working on another. This school is great all around, but especially to our veterans. The student veteran organization is top notch. Along with many other benifits for regular students. Their PTK program is recognized nation wide, not a common thing for community colleges. There are many recourses on campus that help you succeed, ie. the math and writing center. Every teacher I have had has put enormous amount of effort into helping students succeed. The work load is not too bad, but challenging enough to get a good education. The cafeteria has good food all the time, I have not found anything that I did not like. The library has an excellent selection of books and resources. They even borrow books you need from other places if requested. The admissions office make enrolling very easy, they also have people there to help fill out a FASFA . During tax time they have people that help fill out students taxes for FREE. Hands down one of the best community college in our state!!']

name: York University
reviews:
['This university is a great educational institution! Very well known in Southern Ontario and if you live in the GTA, its a fine choice.

Very good campus grounds with a cozy, village-like feel that is easy to get to as it is located on the subway line, has several bus stops, and several parking lots. There are also several anemities on campus if you need to buy food, miscellaneous goods, or use the bank.

The campus is quite insulated so everybody you see will also be a student and because of the college system at the university, socializing can be easy in spite of York being a commuter school.

York has strong humanities programs, a growing engineering faculty, and high quality professors.

The only downside I would say is the risk of frequent striking, but outside of that, it really is not a bad school contrary to what arrogant high school students and others believe.

If I had to go back and pick again, I would still pick York!

Good experience.', 'Visited York University for a program and was quite impressed. The campus is well-organized, and it seems to have all the necessary facilities for students and visitors. A welcoming environment with great infrastructure.', 'York University has been an extremely frustrating experience and is deeply disappointing overall. The biggest issue is the complete lack of organization and accountability across administrative departments. Simple processes like registration, academic advising, or getting clear information take weeks and often involve being sent in circles with contradictory responses.

Communication is poor and inconsistent. Important updates are unclear, delayed, or buried in confusing systems, leaving students stressed and uncertain. When problems arise, there is little transparency or urgency to resolve them.

Academically, the quality is very inconsistent. Some instructors care, but many courses feel poorly structured, outdated, or unclear in expectations. Grading can feel arbitrary, and meaningful feedback is often missing—especially considering the high tuition costs.

Support services are heavily promoted but difficult to access in reality. Long wait times, limited appointments, and generic advice make it feel like students are just numbers rather than individuals who need support.

Overall, York fails to deliver the organized, supportive, and student-focused environment it promises. Prospective students should seriously consider other options before committing.', 'Attended the Canadian Tennis Open tonight and every year I am amazed at such a great job that they do. The staff and volunteers are always friendly and helpful and it is a delight to attend. We attend every year for the last 5 years and have nothing but praise and admiration for the organizers. A good Tennis game becomes the 🍒 on the top.', 'One of Canadas top leading University’s is York University. With a diverse platform, Internationally recognized and acclaimed programs, professors and scholars make York what it is. York a university has the largest politics department along with the only university that offers a full Political Science degree unlike most universities.']

name: College of Southern Nevada
reviews: ['I am very disappointed with how this college handles financial aid. Students are supposed to receive their aid a week before classes begin, but instead we now have to wait until after we’ve already been in class for two weeks. This is the second time the school has done this.\nMany of us rely on financial aid to cover bills, rent, food, and basic living expenses. Delaying these disbursements puts unnecessary stress on students who are just trying to focus on their education. It feels like the school is playing with our money, and it shows a lack of respect for students and their needs.\nThis situation is unacceptable, and unless changes are made, I cannot rate this school any higher than 1 star.', "I had a bad experience with this school and it resulted in me not wanting to continue. I don't feel like it's worth the money that I paid. Unresponsive student government who were never at their stations whenever I showed up to pick up the ID that I paid for. I received emails for months telling me that my financial aid was about to be canceled if I didn't send in my transcripts, and after I resolved the issue I continued to receive these emails throughout the semester and they said it was a glitch. I contacted, made appointments with, and worked with multiple different departments for help with class selection and still was given the wrong answer, resulting in more money out of my pocket and nothing to show for it. Maybe it's a sign from God before I wasted much more money. The only good thing that came out of this was their affordable living agreement with NSU. I did meet some staff that truly wanted to be helpful. But this really turned me off from this school.", "This place completely screwed me over. I'm from California and I started college out there. Came to Nevada to be with family and wanted to continue my education. I enrolled in my first semester and got set up with financial aid. I thought all was good until I went to buy books and they said i couldn't use my financial aid for the books. I would have to pay out of pocket and be reimbursed later... In California, financial aid does not work this way and this absolutely baffled me. I don't get help from family as my family is poor. I work to try to help pay theirs and my own bills. I cannot just afford $800+ worth of books without notice. So I dropped out of the semester with W's. I received no financial aid, but I had been approved for it. Somehow, despite not having received any financial aid, I now OWE them what I got approved for...??? I couldn't even afford my books so of course I couldn't afford to pay a couple thousand in financial aid that I never received. So naturally, the school sent it to collections and it is now ruining my credit. No education, no financial aid. Just debt.", 'CSN is a joke. I had put a course I was looking at taking in the cart but did not proceed to go through with it. Fast forward to September of 2023 where I get a bill from CSN for one online course for around $300. Not once did I know they had finalized me into that class. Never received any emails or phone calls regarding this class so I received an F for a class that I didn’t even know my login to the CSN email or to take that course! Tried to dispute but since I don’t have any “proof”, it was denied and sent me to collections. Not sure how to give proof of something that I never received any notification about a class. Now I’m out a few hundred dollars for a class I didn’t even take.', "The campus is pretty nice and some of the people in the registrar office and financial aid were friendly and helpful. The bad thing that made me really dislike there offices was the financial aid process, I finished my paper work and then they told me it would take 2 to 4 weeks for them to scan my paperwork and then give me my aid. It was awful, I have attended two other community colleges and they had my paperwork done within a week or less. I almost couldn't keep my classes because  not only were they making me wait to do something simple but they didn't even try to find a way to help me keep my classes. Basically in short there offices are awful when it comes to getting things done, but the campus and my teachers so far are good."]

name: Las Vegas College
reviews:
['I’m a former student who ultimately withdrew because the environment became unbearable due to ongoing unprofessionalism within the program leadership.

Ms. Soto, the program chair, consistently created a toxic learning environment. She regularly spoke negatively about other instructors in front of students, shared personal business that had nothing to do with class, and openly dragged her coworkers and even her superiors during lectures. As a student, I didn’t come to class for workplace drama — I came to learn.

There was clear favoritism shown, particularly within the MA program. Certain students were treated better than others, while the rest of us were left confused and uncomfortable. She would frequently switch to Spanish during class discussions, excluding non-Spanish-speaking students entirely. That alone made many of us feel dismissed and out of place.

What really crossed the line was witnessing openly racist remarks. Ms. Soto stated that a student only passed exams because she was Asian — completely dismissing the fact that this student studied hard and earned rheir grades. That comment alone told me everything I needed to know about the lack of professionalism

On top of that, she was extremely difficult to talk to. She’s just not a safe person (as a student) she loves to try to make you feel stupid. Anytime I needed help, I avoided her like the plague and tried to get assistance from literally anyone else because of her attitude and how uncomfortable she made students feel. Many of us had — and probably still have — complaints about her, but most are too scared to speak up due to fear of retaliation. I actually still have a friend in her class today & she’s still complaining about the same things I complained about!

As for Mr. Cadiz (who is apparently no longer there), his behavior made students uncomfortable, and it was known among staff. He was literally sleeping with students. The fact that leadership was aware and did nothing speaks volumes about the culture at this school.

Honestly, the only positive thing I have to say is this: the Intro class was the best experience I had, and that was when Ms. Lima was teaching. She was thorough, professional, and actually cared about students learning. The difference was night and day. I genuinely miss her teaching style and wish the rest of the program reflected that level of quality. If it had , I would still be there.

Overall, I did not leave because the coursework was hard — I left because the environment was toxic, unprofessional, and draining. I would not recommend this program unless serious changes are made to leadership and accountability.', 'The college is a joke. I unfortunately have to go here for my RN because no other “in person” college will take their credits. I came here 2+ years ago for my LPN license. When I was coming here for my LPN license, The LPN director singled me out because of my sexual orientation. In the beginning, I could care less what she thought of me, but then it got personal. I won’t say exactly what she did, but it was bad. She did quit midway into my LPN course, which I and the majority of the school was happy she was gone. Well, guess how’s back as the Dean…. Now that she’s back as the Dean, I question if she will single me out again, and if she will jeopardize me getting my RN license. I spoke to corporate about this shortly after finishing LPN school but they obviously couldn’t care less.', 'I had an appointment with Suzie some time ago because I was interested in the nursing program. Initially, she was very helpful and professional. We discussed various important aspects of the program, and her demeanor was quite pleasant.

However, everything changed when I started asking questions about attendance and grades. It seemed odd, but the only thing she could tell me was that if I failed two exams, I would be automatically expelled from the program. She insisted this wasn't a school decision but a federal regulation the school had to comply with, leaving no options for students. While it seemed a bit extreme, I accepted it at the time.

Later, as I continued researching other schools and gathering information, I discovered that no such federal regulation exists. This left me wondering: why would Suzie say something like that? I understand that any school can set its own rules, but I don't believe it's necessary to lie to potential students about non-existent regulations to justify the institution's policies.

I honestly don't know if this "two-exam failure" rule is an actual school policy or if Suzie simply misled me, perhaps because she didn't want me to enroll. It's truly difficult to say, but such an experience doesn't inspire much confidence in the school right from the start.

What a shame. This really seemed like a good school. But after reading some reviews, it doesn't seem like a good idea to enroll here.', 'Being the last student in the Business Digital Marketing program at Las Vegas College was truly a unique and memorable experience. Although the program has now come to an end, I’m grateful to have been a part of it and to represent its final chapter.

The coursework was detailed, engaging, and provided me with a strong foundation in digital marketing principles and strategies. I owe much of my success to the incredible instructors, especially Mr. Jordan and Mrs. Gomez, who played an integral role in my education. Their dedication, support, and passion for teaching made a lasting impact on me.

I also want to recognize my externship coordinator, Tammy Brown, who was nothing short of amazing. She was professional, personable, and incredibly patient throughout the entire exiting process. Her guidance and support made the transition from student to graduate feel smooth and well-supported.

My time at Las Vegas College was both rewarding and empowering, and I’ll always look back on it as a key step in my professional journey.', "From the very first day, I felt supported, encouraged, and truly seen. It’s rare to find a school where students are treated with genuine care and respect, but LVC delivers just that. The atmosphere is positive and uplifting, and the faculty go above and beyond to ensure you not only succeed but thrive. One of the biggest highlights for me was learning under Professor Ms. Soto Her dedication, passion, and patience made a real difference. She took the time to explain things thoroughly, pushed us to do our best, and celebrated every win with us! LVC is a community where students can grow, feel empowered, and leave with a sense of pride in what they've accomplished."]

name: University of Nevada-Las Vegas
reviews:
['The University of Nevada, Las Vegas carries a distinctly practical rhythm. The setting is energetic and career-focused, shaped by a city built on industries that move quickly and expect results. Students are often balancing academics with real-world experience, and that dynamic creates an environment where adaptability and initiative matter. The atmosphere encourages figuring things out by doing, so graduates tend to leave with a sense of how to operate in fast-changing professional spaces.

UC Davis offers a very different tone. Its presentation is polished, the campus is serene, and the messaging emphasizes tradition, research, and community. While that can make for a comfortable academic setting, the pace can feel less tied to immediate application, leaving some students to create their own urgency if they want to stand out. Critics sometimes point to the university’s high cost of attendance and argue that the financial investment does not always align with the outcomes students expect, particularly when measured against more career-driven environments. In those views, the experience can seem shaped as much by institutional image as by measurable preparation for competitive job markets.

One university leans into hands-on momentum shaped by its surrounding economy.
The other projects the calm of an established academic brand.

The choice comes down to whether a student prefers an environment defined by direct engagement and practicality — or one centered on a more traditional, carefully cultivated campus experience.', 'Apologies for being a  grumpy pants, I was attatched to a bench for a day and a half without food or water and worse lmao...
Looking forward to a successful semester.
Thankyou to the staff for all of your hard work and co-operation.
During the break, I had an opportunity to discover how unique this university is. Welcome back REBELS! Also look out for the new lounge area at the SU! If you see the construction guys say thankyou! Smile #WhatATimeToBeAREBEL', 'I just got off the phone with an employee who advised me to escalate the issue to the Rebel Success Center. I was also told not to register for the payment plan because it would result in a 10% late fee and I did the wrong thing setting up a payment plan. As a veteran who is also using ch 35 as a spouse, I have a code on file that should prevent late fees. This is all new information to me, and the lack of clear communication has been extremely frustrating. As an alum who completed my undergraduate degree here and is now in graduate school, I expect better — frankly, this has been the worst customer service I’ve experienced.

It may be time to consider hiring new staff in the cashiering department.', "This school didn't take to account my disabilities affected my previous school grades in which I had no support because the disability services were understaffed they didn't care and just denied me I won't recommend this school or Colorado State University to anyone with grades affected by disabilities there are way better options that do take your disabilities in to account and help these places suck.", 'Rather not say.  Great school.']

name: University of Nevada-Reno
reviews: ['This post is rating the campus ambiance, not the actual educational opportunity. The campus is beautiful, high tech, and provides a lot of extra curricular activities. They are home to the Nevada Wolfpack football team, so students can catch the game with their friends on a Saturday night. There are also a lot of on campus shops for food, coffee, etc. such as, Starbucks, Panera Bread, Panda Express, Mexican food, sushi, cheeseburgers, and more. It’s a campus worth looking at and provides a strong sense of community.', "Best fitness center, hands down. This place really knows how to take care of it's students. Definitely worth checking out campus too, it's beautiful", "I'm a charter bus driver, and we took Sacramento State University football team to UNR, for a game. The atmosphere was electric. Tons of food trucks, and LOTS of foot traffic. UNR did provide a police escort to get us on to campus.", 'Clean, well equipped and stately. This gave us a great feeling of higher education and professionalism.\nWe came specifically to look at the Davidson academy.', 'The campus is a wonderful place to take a Sunday morning walk especially during a pandemic.   Animals and fowl were claiming the walks and the lake their own.  And how in the world did the coyote know he was safe  during  his morning walk!']

name: Great Basin College
reviews: ['Met with a guy named Gertrude "baba" badingaling there, greatest guy i\'ve ever known and he also helped me with my studies. Hope you succeed in your future endeavours in college football.', 'I have attended this college for the last two years and absolutely love it! Everyone knows your name and you really get one on one time with professors if you need it! The library and Academic Success Center are always open and offer tons of help! They provide student tutors in math, science and english free!', 'It’s a decent place. Currently doing  kids robotics classes.', "And I love everything about this college. name: Truckee Meadows Community College
reviews:
['By Far the BEST Community College anywhere! My daughter went here for her Junior and Senior year of High School Dual Credit Program as well as the college side. She was able to complete her High School Honors Diploma as well as earn her Associates Degree, both in 2 years at TMCC! We can never say enough about how stellar this school, teachers and professors are. RateMyProfessor is very helpful in picking the right Professor for your classes, that fit your style and needs. The Campus is always clean and feels safe. We are super Appreciative of all the support my daughter has received over the past few years. Thank You ~ Thank You ~ Thank You !!!', 'Came here to review the cafe, absolute gem of the school. Amazing food (especially the specials) and friendly staff. Always excited to see what will be on the menu for the day!', 'I visited Financial Aid in person to address what I believed to be a discrepancy between my attempted credits and my earned credits. I brought with me my transcripts and was accompanied by employees from Admissions and Records who were willing to help clarify the matter.

Unfortunately, the experience I had with the Financial Aid staff during that visit was extremely disappointing. Rather than listening to my concern, I was told, in a dismissive manner, that they would not run another report. Even as the Admissions and Records staff attempted to engage with them to resolve the issue, the Financial Aid staff continued to refuse. The tone and demeanor felt not only unhelpful, but also unnecessarily rude, as though my bringing up a concern was an inconvenience. The student individual and the (coordinator?) refused to look at emails sent to me the day before and the transcript that Records and Admissions printed out and brought over to Financial Aid.

As a paying student and an Iraq War veteran, I expect to be treated with professionalism and respect when seeking assistance from TMCC. The interaction left me feeling frustrated and undervalued as a student. In fact, the experience was so negative that I briefly considered leaving TMCC altogether. The only reason I did not was because of the kindness and professionalism shown to me by the Admissions and Records team, who demonstrated that not everyone at TMCC treats students in such a manner.

I hope that this feedback will be taken seriously, and that steps will be taken to ensure students who raise concerns are treated with respect and given a fair opportunity to have their issues addressed.', 'This is my first time going back to college enrollment process and it was absolutely terrible experience. I had an appointment with an advisor it’s my first time back in quite a while I asked the student workers at Welcome Center (an older lady and a colored short hair girl) the older lady just gave me an rude look like why did I interrupt their conversation? Then I asked her where academic advising is. I arrived to academic advising the 2 girls in the front very loud and talking about their personal life not acknowledging me anyways got checked in. I met with an advisor it was delayed about 15 mins anyways he wasn’t knowledgeable about my appointment he asked “how can I help you today?” I mean didn’t we speak over the phone about why I’m here? Isn’t it on the notes? Anyways he was very rude he said if you sent them on last week we don’t have them yet but yet you found them in your system. TMCC said found out that my classes aren’t accredited to TMCC standards which is ridiculous because other nursing schools are accredited (might not be the same accreditation) but have students graduating and working with nursing degree and license in Reno but yet TMCC won’t accept my previous credits. That’s crazy I thought coming to TMCC would be good experience but seem like it isn’t.', "I've liked it so far. You need to be proactive and treat college seriously. This isn't high school where things are spoonfed to you. It prepares you for real life where deadlines matter, effort matters, and sometimes, you need to use critical thinking skills to figure something out. I've mostly had fantastic teachers who are really passionate about educating. It's very online friendly which is what I do with an occasional trip to campus."]

name: Western Nevada College
reviews: ['Outstanding school, WNC’s dual credit program allowed me to get my associate’s degree while still in high school. If you’re a local with kids, I’d highly encourage them to do JumpStart so they can get an associate’s as well.', 'Contrary to some of the negative reviews I have read, I have had one of the best experiences in my life attending Western Nevada College. I have never had a substandard class nor an inadequate instructor. In fact, my mentors have gone above and beyond to ensure my continuing success. The counseling department has always been available whenever I needed assistance. The tutoring department and the library,  proved to be invaluable resources. I would highly recommend Western Nevada College to anyone pursuing an education. Thank You, William Gilroy', "Taking CNA classes with Kendal Valdez. She's an amazing Teacher. Very fair, very patient, and willing to listen. Can't say enough! I'm hoping my future teachers are this good. She sets the bar high!", "Honestly unless you are taking available classes. You are fine but if you need independent studies good luck trying to get that threw the tech side and when they do give it to you. It only lasted a couple months and not the full semester. I was also referred to go to tmcc. What's really funny about that is they are trying to kick up enrollment and here they are trying to send me away. I'm so unhappy and done with this school not to mention this is my second semester straight of problems with the same people. They make you pay for the full experience but barely help you along the way. When you voice your concer they brush it off like it doesn't mean anything, and then barely listen to you when you ask for help. I'm dropping my classes and won't ever come back unless it's under different management. I was told the issue would be resolved but still hasn't even happened yet.", 'Some professors are good, and others like to be on their phone on social media during lecture time which is close to 3hours mind you. So the time she could be using to teach us each part of the human anatomy she spends on instagram and Facebook. Along with her inconsistency of teaching and rude habits she had not only wasted my time at this school, but takes no regard in how the material actually comes out. Sad that this isn’t the only teacher, one before her the class had to remind him to add assignments to the canvas days before being due and graded. Really decide who you want teaching you bio, anatomy 223 before picking the class because you may just have your time wasted as well as you money taken with no regards for you education.']

name: Colby-Sawyer College
reviews: ['We had a wonderful tour led by Gabriel and Yas. Both were absolutely fantastic! They were knowledgeable, welcoming, and made the experience enjoyable and informative. The school itself is beautiful, and the grounds are truly impressive. We had the chance to meet some of the staff, and I left feeling very confident that my daughter will be in great hands. We especially appreciated the emphasis on small, interactive classes, and the nursing labs were state-of-the-art and incredibly impressive. Overall, it was a great visit!', 'Colby-Sawyer College was a "Game Changer" for me personally & professionally. I was a 4-year student, basketball player & graduate with a degree in Business (BA). The professors care deeply and I felt it. The Hoops Team, they want to WIN! I loved that and I still talk to my coaches & teammates, 20 years later.  Each year the school helped me build social skills, professional skills, confidence, communication & community living. I had a job set up in Boston months before I graduated. CSC campus is beautiful & New London is charming. Worth the visit!', 'A very beautiful and well-maintained campus.', 'Beautiful campus and athletic facilities.. with a great field hockey team to boot..', 'Amazing nursing program with great athletics. Low tuition.']

name: Dartmouth College
reviews:
['Dartmouth College stands as one of the most remarkable institutions of higher education in the world, blending academic excellence, deep tradition, and a truly unique sense of community. Nestled in the serene and picturesque town of Hanover, New Hampshire, Dartmouth offers an environment that is both intellectually stimulating and personally enriching. The college’s beautiful campus, surrounded by lush forests and rolling hills, creates a peaceful yet inspiring atmosphere that encourages learning, reflection, and creativity.

One of Dartmouth’s greatest strengths is its commitment to undergraduate education. Unlike many large universities, Dartmouth places students at the heart of its academic mission. Professors are not just distant lecturers but mentors who genuinely care about their students’ intellectual growth and personal development. The small class sizes allow for meaningful discussions, close interaction, and individualized attention, making learning a deeply engaging experience rather than a passive one.

Academically, Dartmouth is exceptional across a wide range of disciplines. Whether in the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, or business, the college maintains rigorous standards and encourages interdisciplinary exploration. Students are encouraged to think critically, challenge assumptions, and pursue knowledge beyond the classroom. The college fosters a culture of curiosity and innovation, preparing graduates not just for careers but for thoughtful and impactful lives.

Beyond academics, Dartmouth offers a vibrant and inclusive campus life. The strong sense of community is one of its defining features. Students form deep friendships, collaborate on projects, and support one another through their academic and personal journeys. The college’s traditions, such as the Dartmouth Outing Club and seasonal events, help create a shared identity that connects generations of alumni.

Dartmouth also provides abundant opportunities for leadership, research, and real-world experience. Students can engage in cutting-edge research, participate in internships, study abroad, and contribute to meaningful community initiatives. This holistic approach to education ensures that graduates leave Dartmouth as well-rounded individuals with both intellectual depth and practical skills.

In addition, Dartmouth’s alumni network is exceptionally strong and supportive. Graduates of the college are known for their loyalty and willingness to help fellow Dartmouth students and alumni, creating lifelong connections that extend far beyond campus.

Overall, Dartmouth College is not just a place of learning but a place of transformation. It nurtures intellect, character, and creativity, shaping individuals who go on to make significant contributions to society. For anyone seeking a world-class education in a warm, close-knit, and inspiring environment, Dartmouth College is truly an outstanding choice.', 'Went to Dartmouth a million years ago for medical school… I’m sure it’s changed since the dark ages. I loved it though!', 'Dartmouth is a really nice campus. Hanover, NH. Beautiful. Took the tour given by students. Well worth it!', 'Always a good trip! Scenic campus and lots of things to do in town as well.', 'Absolutely amazing experience take the trip it is worth the visit go to bones gate frat and see the man on the couch']

name: Franklin Pierce University
reviews: ['Franklin Pierce needs to do something about the water. Video taken Jan 22nd at 5pm. Having students pay to live with water thats dirty is insanity. RES Life has done nothing but swept everyone concerns under the rug and not dealt with the problem.', 'Updated: June 2019: (3) 🌟: I returned here to attend the graduation ceremony of my kid. I felt it was a money grab for the school administration to ask for the graduating class to join the alumni association and immediately start giving to the school. Really..?! Give the graduates a chance to live first. I have come to understand the disappointment with the teachers in the university by my kid. The program my kid originally came to the school to explore was discontinued after a year or so and my kid was left adrift to find her way out of school with what she needed to graduate. My kid started helping other kids who arrived to the school in need of help and guidance. My kid choose to get into extra programs to focus her skills and allow her to shine as an individual. My kid enjoyed living in the townhouse for almost (3) years.\n\nAugust 2015: (4) 🌟:  I came here to drop off my daughter for classes.  The school arranged for help for incoming students to have assistance getting the bags taken upstairs to the dorms. My daughter really enjoyed her initial visit to the school and the teachers she encountered. I liked the fact that the teachers know the kids who attend the college. I went to the cafeteria to with my daughter to sample the food and it was not bad. I had an opportunity to meet with the college President while at the school meal and was impressed with the possibilities he discussed. My kid had an issue with roommates in the dorms, but she eventually moved into another location that she enjoyed much more. My kid has enjoyed most of her time in the college with the small classes and felt that she has benefited from the smaller classes. This campus has bad cell phone service. This campus is secluded in a wooded area. This campus is not near a major city or shopping areas. There are town houses on campus.  This school is expensive and small classes and different from the larger schools.', "Visited here for the Halloween trick or treating and was not disappointed! I would gladly take kids back here for that. Lots of the homes and dorms were decorated and handing out candy. Lots of people were dressed up and festive. The shuttles we're really nice to use to get back and forth. This college also employees intellectually disabled adults and should be recognized. Definitely worth a visit! I've heard from lots of people that their food is really good.", 'First off, this campus couldn’t even get me water without any brown sludge running through the pipes. That res life director Heather is a real pain in the rear end! Worst director of a campus I’ve ever seen. Could barely keep her emotions in check while managing the other res life staff. A four year old toddler has more composure than this so called “director”. I pray to any god, or deity that this school closes, and that no young future leader of this country attend this institution, and to see the hypocrisy, and favoritism within the campus.', 'Very nice experience. Everyone very helpful and polite.']

name: New England College
reviews: ["Started my educational journey at NEC around 2017 so some information might be dated. Multiple programs completed here over the years, and have been considering enrolling in another one. There isn't a class I disliked. Most professors are extremely professional and exceptional educators, easy to get ahold of. Over time experiences seemed to improve. Liked their old system with Bisk a bit more for online student payments and admin tasks, however Blackboard has become more user friendly over time. Folks have asked me if this is a real school as it's not as well known- and I'm glad to say it's very real, with a very lovely campus right next to Pat's Peak where I personally learned to snowboard over the years. If you've seen info somewhere for the school's online programs: book an intro call. It'll be worth it :)", "location is terrible and dead nothing to do. only go if you're ready to be bored out of ur mind and freezing everyday", "Do yourself a favour and avoid this school!!!!! It doesn't exist for students, they just want to exploit international students of their money.\nWow and their tuition payment policy is absurd, you have to pay in full within the first week of classes else all your access and records will be terminated. Schools that actually have the students interest in mind give you until the next semester or session to balance your account. This school will threaten and harass you with calls and emails even when partial payment has been made. They only want your money. Beware!!!!", 'Gorgeous small liberal arts college where the professors and administrators work hard to give every student skills to succeed.', "We're a retired couple with no connection to NEC. We just love to eat there, whether it's dinner or brunch.  It's one of the very best dining commons of Southern NH colleges."]

name: Southern New Hampshire University
reviews:
['From admissions through fully understanding how the online program works, the entire experience has been clear, organized, and professional. As a full-time Project Manager balancing work and school, I value structure and efficiency — and that’s exactly what I’ve received.

The program is straightforward, well communicated, and I appreciated the immediate sense of connection with peers right from day one.

Working with my admissions advisor, Tonya, has been exceptional. She has gone out of her way to streamline the process, answer every question thoroughly, and speak to me like a real person — not just another enrollment number. In a short amount of time, she’s made this transition feel manageable and genuinely exciting.

I can’t recommend this school enough. Well done.', "I had an awesome experience at SNHU, from the day I requested information on pursuing my MBA to register for classes.  I was financially responsible for my classes. My advisor Devon Hirsch is an awesome person. We communicated about everything, even with challenges with a class she got involved in and helped me through it. She follows up with me every semester to know how I was doing. She's a great listener!  The instructors I had was very involved with making sure assignments were completed.  Dr. Robert is a very dedicated instructor. I love this guy! I would recommend students to take his class. SNHU courses are designed to help students reach their goals and the instructors are in the field for the classes they teach.  Thank you SNHU.", 'I’m a current Computer Science online student and my experience has been very positive overall. From the very beginning, I received help making sure all my documentation was in place. I also get text notifications when it’s time to submit FAFSA for the current term, or simply how am I feeling about the semester, which really helps me stay on track. Whenever an issue comes up, whether after a phone call, someone always follows up with me.

My academic advisor regularly checks in, follows up, congratulates me on progress, and clearly explains things when I have questions. My professors have also been great. Some are very direct with assignment feedback, which pushes you to improve, while others recognize strong work and offer encouragement. I appreciate both styles because they help me grow and do better.

The only challenge I’ve noticed is with textbooks. After purchasing books through the bookstore, they are not always located in one consistent place, and it can vary each term. Aside from that, assignment directions are clear, even though many of the courses are challenging which is expected.

Overall, my experience has been strong, and I would highly recommend the online program here to anyone considering it.', 'SNHU is a wonderful university geared towards working adults! I have earned my bachelors and masters degree from their online programs and cannot recommend them enough. The instructors are caring and compassionate. The degrees I have earned while at SNHU have set me apart from my coworkers and made me competitive in the workforce.', "I had an incredible experience at SNHU! The university truly awakened my potential, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to pursue my Bachelor's degree in Psychology with a concentration in Mental Health. The journey wasn't easy, but with focus and dedication, I was able to push myself to new heights and achieve my goals. The professors at SNHU were marvelous, supportive, knowledgeable, and passionate about helping students succeed. I'm looking forward to commencement and can't wait to apply my skills and knowledge in the real world. If you're considering SNHU, I highly recommend it."]

name: University of New Hampshire-Main Campus
reviews: ["It had me at hello!  Great atmosphere. Great campus. Everyone you spoke to was genuinely passionate about being there. Can't wait for my girl to be a wildcat in the fall!\n6/13 Back for orientation. Stayed over night in Adams Hall. Nice, clean comfortable room! Campus food is excellent! 🍀📚", 'Genuinely so funny how much money this school takes from the students. The Tuition itself is already wack. But be prepared to also pay hundreds of dollars in parking tickets because the school doesn\'t have enough pay to parks (very intentional on their part). Also, be prepared to pay an extra $50 to be let back into your room if you get locked out...not like the campus police are supposed to HELP students out of the goodness of their hearts???! No, lets charge students $50 for being locked out of their room without their phone in a BATH robe. Nice! Oh, and you cannot forget about the $35+ you\'ll be charged every year for the "damage" to your apartment (when the damage was there when you moved in!!!). All in all, get ready to be in major debt, become sick from the dining hall food and enjoy your daily hikes to mount Everest as you walk 25 minutes in the snow...(again...because there is no where to park if you drive to class). Save your money, don\'t park on campus and never get locked out of your room :)', "Proud son of Louis A. Wiesner Foreign Service Diplomat, and Elizabeth P. Wiesner, Episcopal Church ordained minister.  I transferred from Plymouth another fine campus and interesting different dining experience to the good.  Had 4.0 GPA but only got credits not GPA transfer.   Also attended Lisgar Collegiate Ottawa, Canada. (SNL there then P. Akroyd) (JA also there Ambassador Kaukenan ). UNH Class of 1981.  I continue to come to Durham for laundry at DLC.  Live in Dover next to a Cleary.  The atmosphere in Durham, and the water,  welcomes a diverse population of students and occasionally folks whose machines broke at home.  Now for sale I was pleased to see UNH hold a class downtown this week as DLC and Hayden Sports up for sale $1.2 mil. each.  In 1981 Burger King, Weeks and Youngs were the gems and Pettee Brook market.  The Mill Plaza recently set to redo the layout was defeated by the local townsfolk but was to address the loss of the bed spaces on the main st.  Parking is a huge issue in back of the laundry center.  Two happy tenants will need space-Barbers, and Franz food.  Without a tear down some how a laundry/Franz/Barber shop with apts. above and parking below ground or part of the lot.  Burger King wanted a drive through and may have been denied.  I also would like to see a traffic circle may be in front of the Post office.  The future is bright!  New England Center was a great conference center restaurant but apparently the glass used in construction is not sufficient and heating the building is overly expensive.  My housing on Strafford ave., 2, corner of, 8 b/r house rented from Bayside, a frorority of sorts.  Concerts with legendary artists Muddy Waters, Taj Mahal, Frampton-40 + in 4 yrs. Face to Face played Franklin Ballroom, live cafe music at the Tin Palace (now Subway).  Potentially a steep decline in enrollment forecasts may force high end condo's to be considered.  Budget cuts at the University as revenues decline. The waterfront development in Dover next to Newicks may inspire.  The business owners on Main st. very approachable on this subject.  Our family includes Frank Bolles who donated 200 acres to Nature Conservancy at Mt. Chocorua where we spent many happy summers on the lake. His owl collection at Spaulding Center. Priscilla Phenix lived in Durham, announcer for the tv station and choir member, my aunt.  Shout out to my roomies from Madbury rd. ( and our landlord  L-C H. Kuo and Dr. Hitchcock) now Dr. R. Cooney, NH Engineer Mark Kirouac, Dr. Hubie Karreman DVM.  And to my lady Dianne L.G. I met summering at AGR fraternity-we were just brave strangers.  Joy is when WUNH play songs you were thinking of and also when you hear your name and the song-Jill, Sue, Russ, John P., Ken, CC, Joe,  some from archives and when Jeff's Kid was a kid.  Fair winds and following seas to Roger H. retiring and leaving Hayden Sports and DLC to find new ownership to redefine Main st. already seeing changes after Cio left.  New Feb. '26 deal in making to sell both buildings on Main st. and replace with 4 story.  Coldest winter in 20 years still smiling.", 'This is a university with poor student support; the needs of the institution come first over student safety, well-being and success.', "I didn't get accepted...but my daughter did!\nBeautiful school & campus!  Visit!"]

name: Keene State College
reviews: ["Our son is starting his 3rd year here and loves it. Smaller college but has a great atmosphere where you're not just a number. Has met all his needs to be a successful student.", 'Very nice school.\nBeautiful country setting with small town Main Street and all the local shopping centers nearby !', "Beware people who just want to take a class or two! Not only are the classes exorbitantly expensive, but the financial department is really sneaky about costs. You only have 7 days from the start of the course to drop and not incur a charge, but they don't bill you until after the 7 days are up so you're screwed. They make no exception even when they admit they misled you", 'We had a wonderful time visiting our son at KSC!! A beautiful day to walk around and enjoy the last of the foliage.', 'Amazing college with amazing faculty and staff and beautiful landscapes']

name: University of New Hampshire at Manchester
reviews: ['Massive Place and plenty of parking. Well light. History is alive and Well. Place of Higher Learning. Very scenic and many Activities.', 'Good luck getting ahold of someone. I was trying to inquire about attending here and giving them money but every email I send gets ignored and calls get put on hold and never picked up. Weird..', "Let me start by saying the admissions and student services faculty assistant  manager Kaitlynn were soo unhelpful. The  student services including financial aid were sooo helpful. When admissions told me no, Student services said yes. They didn't try to go out of their way at all to help me at all being a new student. I applied in March, and admissions or Kaitlyn didn't do their job until a week before school started. They are only trying to set me up to fail, and believe me when I get in contact with the Dean I will be talking with him or her. I can't believe they are allowed to be employed, it was that bad. Even Deborah in admission rolled her eyes when I was trying to get enrolled. There is no student experience other than being difficult. When I was able to finally become a student and expressed I am in training for work all week, they weren't cooperative at all, and didn't try to work with me at all. I will be trying to find another school. If I can give this school 0 stars I would. Not happy with the school at all.", "I'm going to own UNH and I think my old business law professor from NECC taught that Chemistry class I took there in 07-08 that I received a D in. Other students in the class had all the answers to the final but no one gave them to me and Constantweirdo called me during a class. Can you say lawsuits?", "I graduated from UNH Manchester in 2019 with a B.Sci. in Biotechnology, and I loved every second of it! UNHM is a phenomenal school, and much better for Biotech than the UNH Durham campus. Everyone here is super nice and always willing to help you with whatever you need. The in-house cafeteria is great, and there are an endless numbers of places to hang out and study or chat with friends. The building itself is an old mill building, but the refurbishments are practically brand new and make the campus both culturally authentic and technologically modern. The professors are great, and the small size of the campus means that you are more than just a number to your instructors. You really get to know each one of your professors personally, which is great because they're all good people.\nHonestly, the only downside is the shortage of parking from 9:00am - 3:00pm on Mon - Thurs. Few classes are held on Fridays, so it is a lot easier to find parking then. But if you get there before 9 each day, you really don't have to worry about finding a spot. Even if you can't find one, there is back-up parking next to the WMUR building and in the parking garage 1 block down.\nOverall, I give UNH Manchester a 5/5! I am so glad I chose this place for my undergrad, and I am thankful for the great experience! :-)"]

name: Plymouth State University
reviews: ["all i have to say is, get ready for the food. I'm surprised there's other schools that are #1 on the Princeton Review for best dining. although it does send me straight to the bathrooms for a quite a jiffy. overall, a worthy experience. :)", 'I\'ve gone here for almost a year now and I love it. I do not like to party. I know it\'s known as a big party college but it\'s nothing you can\'t easily avoid and there are plenty of people who do not like to party as well. Beautiful campus with a great view. "cheap" compared to other places and has a great Computer Science department', "My son's football team had a game there. It was one of the cleanest games I ever watched. The Panthers, players, coaches support staff and spectators were a class act.", "Plymouth State seems to find a way to nickel and dime you at every turn. If you're hoping to earn a degree without running into countless hidden fees, you'll be severely disappointed", 'Graduated from Plymouth State.  My experience at Plymouth State was wonderful.  Excellent education with caring professors.   Dorms were always maintained.  Excellent Business, Education and Meteorology departments.  Great friendly student body with a lot of outdoor activities.  Excellent choice for college if you do not want a large sprawling overcrowded campus.']

name: NHTI-Concord's Community College
reviews:
["Everyone seemed nice on the phone. There's just no easy way to find the entrance. You go in the building only to see there's a map on the wall that tells you your in the wrong place. Outside there's no signage to direct you where to go and impossible to find. I ended up leaving pissed off after 15 minutes of futile attempts to find the place. I'm sure they do great work if you can find the place and get in there. One and done for me. I won't try going there again.", 'As a student, let me tell you about this school. The buildings are in disrepair, but just enough so you don’t notice on your first few days. While there are a few awesome teachers, many either don’t care about students or are completely delusional. Most of the homework given by the teachers this semester was written by AI. The amount of students, both in the dorms and commuting, that are struggling with depression and thoughts of ending it is staggering. The RAs are crying, because of the unnecessary workload from the school (sooo many useless meetings). Dining hall is barely edible, Campus security will screw you over in ways you can’t even imagine, and everyone is miserable.

DON’T GO HERE.', "I can't say enough about the dental students at Concord Community College! I have been going here for years and love being a part of the dental school as a patient. This is a wonderful place where you will always be well taken care of and help them to become the best dental hygienists!", 'Attended a new student orientation last year with my child and spouse.

No signage anywhere telling us where to go.  No people standing around to help find our way.  We randomly entered the one unlocked building and bingo.

Who is running this campus?  Poorly run and rundown looking.  My kid is going to GBCC this term', 'Went for a Chamber of Commerce meeting.  What a great school and staff!']

name: White Mountains Community College
reviews:
["Pro:
If looking for a great environment to learn, this is definitely the place to be. With my instructors, lol---i love because I am thinking of class yesterday; I really enjoy my classes. With my instructors, I am loving school again, feeling excited and truly enjoying class. From interactive environments, stimulating discussions and a strong push for guest speakers supporting what we are learning, everything feels relevant and deserving of my full attention, no matter how tired I feel. And believe me, I do feel tired by the end of my day.

Another pro:
Great people, from the staff in administration, to my peers, to the instructions, it's an all-around friendly community. Everyone is helpful, from Ronnie and Asemina, to Mike in Admissions, to Annette and Amanda in the Registrar's office, to Diane and Melissa in the library... To the security guard, to my classmates!! Everyone is awesome.

Improvement needed:
The only drawback is the cafeteria closes long before I end my day. My last class doesn't end until 7:30p at night. I have barely 30min between the end of the class (if we end on time) and the beginning of the next class, so no time to leave and get a real meal. Plus the cafeteria is closed before my second class of the day (which starts at 2pm) ends at 4:30pm. I eat lunch after my first class ends at 1230pm. So nothing for many hours. Further, I drive an hour each way to get there. By the time I get home, I'm starving, dead tired and struggling to stay awake. So not having the chance to refuel with a good meal between my last classes is detrimental. From what I hear from my other classmates, I am not the only one feeling this way.

Yesterday, I was told by the security guard to grab from a table in the student area. I felt very grateful...there was mainly only food that was highly processed and heavy salt. I grab miniature boxes of cereal and ran back to class.

Update: DO IN PERSON CLASSES!!! So much better than the online. Just heads up. If you must do online, do hybrid!", "Thank you WMCC for letting us conduct our auditions for 'The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark' in your lovely Bistro.  What a beautiful college and I love the pride one senses when just gazing around at the decor, style, and beautiful art collection. I am excited to meet all of you later!", "Great teachers, great experiences, and great location. It's a wonderful place to attend college.", 'Great place to go to school']

reviews:
["I've watched 25 graduating classes at Rivier. I've watched Rivier grow from an all girl's college to a coed college, and from a college to a university, from typing classes to computer classes and from graduate programs to doctoral programs. I've taken classes at Rivier and had the opportunities to change my mind for the better. I've worked in Housekeeping, Public Safety, Grounds, Maintenance and the Mail room. I can honestly say that most of the workers try to go above and beyond the call of duty by taking care of all the little details for students, staff, faculty and administration.

We cater to our students and that's what we do. Rivier is like a place your mom taught you the world is supposed to be like. Sincerely,
Fred Tappan", "Rivier University is the biggest regret I've made thus far for a secondary education institution. The Student Financial Services have let me down more than once, resulting in missed opportunities for financial help or gave me no notification if I owed the school money until I did/do. They sent my financial aid refund to me then three days later contacted me stating they needed it back, that they had made an error sending it to me.
