name: Eastwick College-Hackensack
reviews:
['I attended Eastwick College for the Clinical Medical Assisting certification, and my experience was extremely disappointing. There were multiple moments of clear unprofessionalism throughout the program. One situation that still bothers me to this day was during a certification test — the dean (or whoever he is — bald head, glasses, I honestly don’t even want to remember his name) walked into the testing room twice asking when the student was going to finish. It was rude, distracting, and made me feel rushed during an exam that should’ve been treated with focus and respect.

To be fair, thanks to God, the professors I had were amazing. They genuinely cared, they taught extremely well, and they helped students succeed despite everything. If it wasn’t for the professors, that school would not be running. The administration, on the other hand, was a completely different story. When I went through the long and stressful process of trying to schedule my Medical Assisting exam, I never heard from the dean at all. No communication, no support — nothing. But this same person had the audacity to interrupt my exam in person.

I’ve spoken to many other students who feel exactly the same, but they’re nervous to say anything publicly. I’m writing this review not only for myself, but for those who feel intimidated or unheard. When you spend a lot of money on your education, you deserve professionalism, communication, and respect — not disorganization and disrespect.

To anyone reading this review, please choose wisely before committing to Eastwick College or any of their New Jersey locations. And honestly, those banners on the highway saying Eastwick is “one of the best schools” should be taken down, because from my personal experience, that statement is far from the truth.', 'The biggest problem I have with this school is the dishonesty during enrollment. When you're signing up, they tell you there is no exit exam -but that's not true. There is an exit exam; they just call it the  NCLEX Prep Review. The name is misleading because there's no actual review or teaching going on.
In reality, students must take nine ATI specialty exams including Med-Surg, Peds,
Fundamentals, and Maternity - plus a four-hour comprehensive exam at the beginning and another at the end. You must score a Level 2 on the comprehensive, and even though your first attempt grade is recorded, you only get two more chances to reach Level 2. On top of that, you must maintain an 80% average across all nine specialty exams to pass. If you don't, you fail the class and don't graduate even though this is
your final term.
What makes it worse is that the so-called "NCLEX Review" class is just sitting for exams while the instructor watches. There's no review, no prep, no guidance. Other nursing schools like Jersey College and Berkeley College don't operate this way they offer actual review and support before graduation with one exam The comprehensive exam.
Before enrolling here, think carefully and ask for all policies in writing. I wish someone had warned me about this before I signed up.', 'Thank you faculty members and proffesor Ari
For your patience, commitment & dedication to us your students . I’m so glad I chose Eastwick College Hackensack campus . Where Directors (Dr. Simmons , Dr. Guirguis and professors go above and beyond for their students to ensure academic knowledge & success. Thank you  all
For all your contributions. Dolores L  🙏🏼🫶🏻', "It's currently 2026 in the beginning, they make you feel like they're going to help you with certain things. And once you're in, don't expect to receive help.You practically have to beg them to help you. I do not recommend the school at all, especially if you have a learning disability. This school is not for you.", 'My visit to Eastwick College in Hackensack was nothing short of frustrating and disappointing. My daughter and I had a scheduled appointment at 5 PM, and actually got there by 4:45, yet was forced to wait nearly 45 minutes before being seen—by someone other than the admissions director, Miss Monica Laina. Instead, I was informed me that Miss Laina was in a meeting, even though I saw her walking past us multiple times, engaging in conversations, laughing, hugging, and socializing rather than attending to prospective students.

When Miss Laina finally addressed us, she mistakenly began speaking to the wrong person despite me clarifying that my daughter was standing beside me. Her demeanor felt indifferent, as if she had more important matters to tend to. After just a few seconds, she vanished and never returned. Nearly 20 minutes later, after asking for assistance, the kindest staff member there, Patrick, stepped in. Miraculously, another worker Rosa Cruz appeared within seconds—after we had already waited almost an hour.

During our walk towards the admissions office, I observed another young woman sitting at a table visibly upset, nearly in tears, due to being ignored. She told me that none of the staff would lift a finger to help her until a student eventually stepped in to assist her, highlighting a concerning lack of staff attentiveness. I stopped and tried offering some type of assistance to her, but couldn’t because now I was being rushed into the office. Additionally, when inquiring about the student-to-teacher ratio, I was told it was nearly 40:1, which raises concerns about individualized support. The graduation rate was stated to be over 95%, yet several students I spoke with felt they were wasting their time and money. Some even mentioned that certain teachers taught material that wasn’t relevant to the exams.

Ultimately, I spent 90 minutes at the college, yet only received about 10–15 minutes of actual conversation—and no satisfactory answers to my questions. Based on my experience and observations, Eastwick College would greatly benefit from hiring staff who genuinely care about students, rather than those simply collecting a paycheck.']

name: Bergen Community College
reviews:
["I really love the environment here at BCC. This is currently my 2nd semester here, and I have nothing but great things to say. My professors and bosses have all been wonderful, and every time I'm on campus, I feel a sense of community and belonging. 😊", 'Everyone is very nice , its like a tight community and professors make you feel like at home. College itself might feel old stylish but they have dunkin and the cafe, huge library with tutors. Plus they have different buildings for IT, Medical professions.

Parking is always available and security is always around. Honestly if i had extra income I would go for another degree in this college, people are very welcoming.', 'I give a 3.5. I graduated last year after going back and forth for years. Most professors are excellent, but there was a moment it seemed like they were desperate for professors. I had one who admitted she was recently fired from PCCC yet got a job at BCC. They do provide adequate resources for students to help you pass. My main issue with Bergen was the counseling department. I wasted thousands of “free” government money at Bergen and was given the run around for years for one of their healthcare programs. During my time there, I had courses “expire” for my program that I had to pay to retake, even though I got an A the first time. I also had the curriculum change for the program change while I was doing prerequisites making me have to take a whole different (but it was really the same) course, which I also had got an A on originally. I feel your experience at BCC will differ greatly based on your support system. I was young, inexperienced and didn’t have any or parents to come with me when I started Bergen. I genuinely thought all the people in the counseling department wanted to help me get into my programs and graduate, but I was wrong. I think staff was overwhelmed, and since I was a young girl alone, they didn’t  feel the need to treat my situation with the same urgency they would those that werent alone. I don’t believe I was offered the same information for certain things people who were accompanied by experienced and educated adults got. There were some good counselors, especially Larry (? Black man with glasses) but by the time I graduated he wasn’t even counseling anymore. I would get passed to different ones and given all vastly different information every time. They have excellent healthcare programs and some classes taught me things I will never forget, but I do resent the amount of money I wasted due to miscommunications from the counseling department and my naivety. PCCC & ECCC definitely caters to working adults and first generation college students more than Bergen does.', "Great local 2 year college! Lots of choices to help you get your associates degree. Affordable prices and lots of help if you need it in the financial aid office. Good option if you still don't know what you want to do, but want to at least get your basic classes done so when you go off to another college you can transfer most of all of what you did here.

Nice campus, friendly students and staff. Easy parking and lots of spots. Also plenty of busses to get you to and from here.

They have a good cafeteria upstairs, but they are also building a new cafe downstairs right next to the entrance which will be nice!", 'I'm a first year student and am wrapping up a couple classes to finish my first semester. I liked my professors but Ms. Datema- forget about it!!! She's genuinely one of the worst and most confusing teachers I've dealt with- coming from someone who had a 4.0 GPA in HS.

Anyways, due to some personal reasons I wasn't able to go to one of my classes consistently. I filled out a form to withdraw even though it was past the deadline, thinking they'd be understanding considering there was a major death in my family. But no, they have zero regard for what's going on even though they claim they "want the best" for their students. Nothing but ten sets of attitude every time I deal with these people.

The only reason I came here was because I heard good things about it and thought it was an affordable way to start my college career. Save yourself the time, money, and stress by enrolling elsewhere. I'm starting to think PCCC in Paterson would've been a better alternative LMFAO.']

name: Rowan College at Burlington County
reviews:
["I don't know where to fathom of the gaslighting, victim blaming and indifference of concern, I experienced of THE MOST ordeal worst way possible.

Last semester, in October. There was an extremely serious incident of an off campus field trip, to Six Flags Jacksonville, where there was a straight up negligence of being left behind, without a headcount, let alone no contact number form everyone and worse, it was after 11pm, where its a dangerous  place to be stranded, with  the park being in the heart of a forest and temperatures  were dropping. Fortunately  and miraculously, a school from NYC(that was extremely more meticulous and compassionate,  than my own), was extremely  compassionate  and  faithful and generous  to get me out of the ordeal, in going to a busy well lit area, where I can contact a rideshare  back, who was also generous.

This is something this institution must know, before it happens to someone else,who may be less fortunate and having no cash for a backup rideshare.  What kind of chaperoning  group would just callously leave a student behind like that, without  at least making sure, they at least have an alternate ride back to their destination. The irony of this is the NYC bus had 2 loaded busses of people, while my own had less than 25- 20 people and still somehow never saw me. Nobody even bothered to be on the lookout. Reported this to Student Activitiesand so far, got no response and concern. Unbelievabl, truly wicked more than Madame Morrible.", 'To whom it may concern,

I’m writing to express my deep disappointment regarding a recent interaction between my daughter and a staff member named Craig. As a mother, it was upsetting to overhear how he spoke to her—his tone was condescending, dismissive, and frankly, rude. When I stepped in to address the issue, he hung up the call. That level of disrespect is shocking.

My daughter is 19 and preparing to start school this fall. This is a critical time in her life, and she deserves guidance, not hostility. We expected professionalism and support—not to be made to feel small or unimportant. This experience has shaken her confidence and left us both questioning the values of your organization.

I urge you to look into this matter and take appropriate steps, including retraining Craig on respectful communication and customer service. I’d appreciate a response outlining how this will be addressed no later than Friday afternoon.

Sincerely,
Mrs. Jones', "School is so fake. My calc professor was horrible gave the review 2 days before the first test and HW problems sometimes weren't related to what was in class. So I failed the first test. This college doesn't care about students passing they just want to take our money.", 'Like many others mention here, no one answers calls and no one wants to do their job there. Does not matter how many phone messages or emails you send. No one will ever call you back and when you go in person - because that’s the only choice you have - you get an attitude. The student center might look nice but looks are deceiving. The advising department is particularly inept. What they do there is push you from one person to the next, no one knows whats going on they just can’t figure it out, so you won’t get an answer to anything. They’re all tangled up there and will just send you in circles. They should be embarrassed.', 'Since Covid the staff service has become terrible. The advisement and financial aid staff does not like to help the children. They purposely give you a hard way to go to discourage you from taking certain classes like nursing, it’s almost as if they are redlining to keep certain nationalities out of the program. They make mistakes with paperwork and it is on the students to fix. They are lazy and it is frustrating. The staff is condescending and it’s almost as if it brings them joy to deliver discouraging news .

I will be reaching out to the state with several audio recordings ( because they this is New Jersey and you can record conversations) -  via 1 party consent

I will also be writing the dean and emailing audio, now they more than likely will not car but at least it will be on record. If more of us do this maybe we will see significant changes!!!!!!!.']

name: Caldwell University
reviews:
['Extremely disappointing food quality and declining value
Unfortunately, I have to leave a very negative review regarding the food services at Caldwell University, especially in the new cafeteria.

The quality of the food is extremely poor. Taste, freshness, and overall standards are far below what should be acceptable at a university. On top of that, the number of meal credits continues to decrease, while the quality of the food keeps getting worse instead of improving.

It feels like cost-cutting is happening at the expense of students. For those who rely on campus dining, this situation is frustrating and simply unacceptable.

I sincerely hope the university takes this feedback seriously and makes meaningful improvements to both food quality and the fairness of the meal credit system.', "This is a very good size, good population mix school. We are touring for our son, didn't know that they were Division II NCAA but seeing the facilities and some of the athletes there i am highly impressed. Strongly consider visiting..", 'I hate doing this but it has to be a change on how this College operates.

If it wasn’t for the love that I have for my child, I would have insisted that he stayed at the University he left because he was doing so well and made the National Honors Society as a Freshman.
This is where our troubles started when he wanted to transfer to this University.
My son is very different and when I make this statement it’s because at 17 he was drawn to his faith in his Christian values as a young person and because of that and how close knit Caldwell University is leaving that impression on my son and being a small school my son was ready to embark on his new journey.
My son transferred and was accepted to this university in June/July timeframe and from that time  until now as I write this review we never received a financial aid packet home. So as a concerned parent of coarse I was concerned

This is not my first child I put through school so I’m very familiar with the process, we visited the school in late July and I’ve expressed this same concerns to Financial Aid with only one person working in the office and was told that they were having some trouble receiving students federal aid but not to worry about it I should receive something soon once they process it.

So I waited and waited August rolls around and it’s still nothing and please can I also add that I’ve called in between the waiting, left voice messages and no one ever called me back and that small act within itself lacks courtesy, when it’s the parents which support their kids that need to know this information before school starts.
My middle child is in school and every time I have questions about her financial aid, her Financial Aid department always call me back and ready to break things down.
But Caldwell University Financial Aid department lacks that,the day I moved my child in the dorm he didn’t have a schedule for his classes and he had to wait on getting that, it’s now November going into the next semester and I still haven’t gotten a breakdown of my sons federal aid and the expected amount that I would have to pay.

Lastly the part that really got me is when they added late fees on my son’s account and wanted to hold us responsible when they are clearly the ones who dropped the ball from the time my son transferred in got accepted, no financial aid packet home no return phone calls from this department no nothing  when we did our part from the beginning.

But I will say when I call the admissions office someone there heard my frustrations and tried to assist me in my concerns and for that I appreciate it.
Again had it not been for the love I have for my kid, I would rather for him to transfer back to which he came from or transfer somewhere else because if this is how you handle new students/ students period then there is something wrong with this picture and it’s very much about the principal of all of this from start and not the point.', "DO. NOT. COME. HERE.!

When I first came here as a freshman I was a Nursing major, everything was great until it wasn't. I can only say that I had very few good professors; after that A MESS. I'm actually concerned that some of these professors got hired to teach. And as a student naturally you try your best to have patience with these professors, because everyone has different ways of teaching but certain things are considered okay and not. I had to withdraw from two different classes because of how difficult and non-flexible those professors were; and of course as a student, you don't want to risk your GPA or have bad grades in general. Some of them don't even follow the school's policy, and will fail you if they wanted to. I even had a professor who did not give your grade until you finished the course, and did not even give the grade on the platform your supposed to give them on; which is blackboard. This school will literally fail you, and mentally drive you insane. And the list literally goes on!!!", 'The university is beautiful, and being here gives me a comforting feeling, as if I’m back in my hometown.']

name: Camden County College

name: Centenary University
reviews: ['Had to write something after seeing some odd reviews that seemingly had nothing to do with the school itself.  My child is a freshman and has had nothing but a positive experience so far.  It is a small school and that is perfect for their needs.  The staff is attentive and everyone that I have met truly wants to be teaching there.  Not everyplace is for everyone, but this is a great little school!!!', 'Please do NOT consider boarding at this University if you are planning on attending Sussex CC. Yes it great they give the students a place to stay, but it is an on going hassle. My son moved in at the end of Aug…. He was all moved in ( also plays BB) practice started.  After a mth or so… his door is being  banged on daily that he needs to pack his shit up and move to different room!  -  got that straightened  out and now a email is sent to kids on Friday that they have to move to a different building! Like who does this???  These kids don’t have help moving all their stuff????? They are in the middle of studying , practicing etc…. Just horrible Don’t do it save your money and rent an apartment with some buddies or something - This department is not ran well and the RA’s on campus are just as bad!', 'My experience with this university is trying to interview the future, Lieutenant governor and not one person had anything positive to say about him running. Not only was I redirected to his campaign, but I was also asked why was so curious. Then I had to take a second look at the reviews and it no longer baffles me why. Nine reviews for an alleged well-known successful university, If that doesn’t concern you please enroll and find out yourself.', "This is a great university. The small setting with less than 1000 students makes extra help easy and close relationships with professors. The programs are great and the professors are fantastic. They all are dedicated to the success of the students. The library is cosy and the staff is phenomenal. The Writing Collaboratory is extremely helpful and I'd recommend it to anybody. The campus is easy to navigate. There is a variety of clubs and organizations to get involved with. The cafeteria food is delicious. Most students are dedicated to their education. Programs make it easy to find careers after college and classes are designed to careers early on. The campus is in a great location and four blocks from entertainment and restaurants. It's only two blocks from the train station. There is also a wonderful theater and students only pay $5 a ticket. Students thrive here. I would recommend this university to anybody.", 'This is a beautiful college in the middle of a great town. The main building has a goldfish roof that make it look very nice.']

name: County College of Morris
reviews:
['The Vietnam Memorial Moving Wall, a half scale replica of the Vietnam Memorial in Washington, DC had a stop at County College of Morris this week. An emotional and educational experience, to say the least. They also provided a mobile "VetsCare" which provides on-site support for veterans. Thank you County College of Morris for hosting this event.', 'County College of Morris has engaged in unethical and harmful practices. In 2018 I enrolled briefly, paid for my classes, and was forced to withdraw due to personal family financial reasons, within 2 days. I was told by staff that I did not owe anything further. Despite this, months later they falsely claimed I owed around $1,416. I disputed this in writing with their Bursar’s Office in 2019, and the debt was later removed from my credit report after a formal dispute.

Fast forward to 2025 — more than six years later — CCM resubmitted this old, disputed, and legally time-barred “debt” to the State of New Jersey’s Set-Off Program. As a result, $1,401.84 was wrongfully seized from my 2024 state tax refund. This action was not only unfair, but a clear abuse of state programs meant for legitimate collections. It is outrageous that a public college would weaponize state tax systems against former students for balances they know are invalid.

I have now filed formal complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, the NJ Office of the State Comptroller, and the Better Business Bureau. Their conduct shows a disturbing lack of integrity, accountability, and fairness.

Students and families should be aware: if this happened to me years after leaving, it can happen to others. CCM’s practices are predatory, dishonest, and highly unethical.', 'Graduated from here back in 1998 and my son graduated here in 2025 now my daughter is going to start school here now. Truly is a wonderful place to begin your journey.', 'Went for a Pearson test. Love how they used solar panels to cover the parking lots.', "Is there any other audio playback besides kurzweil.  It's not good at all . I need something more.
Im special kurzweil is too robotic for online courses . I need more than this for paying 620 a course . This is ridiculous. I need help to get my books on audio . Kurzweil isn't cutting it.  I don't know what to do . I am an iep student . This college doesn't cater to iep students. how does an iep student get audio books without the word being mispronounced?????it .does not pronounce the words correctly.  Omg .  Im smart enough to even realize this . Why . ?? Why ??!?!"]

name: Rowan College of South Jersey-Cumberland Campus
reviews:
['My son recently joined the Men’s Basketball Team, and his experience at this school has been completely unacceptable. After being recruited from over 45 minutes away, he faced blatantly unfair and discriminatory treatment from the head coach, Mr. Stalling. We are aware of other athletes who reported similar treatment in previous seasons, many of whom were intimidated and chose to leave the team rather than voice their concerns.

Mr. Stalling often spoke to his assistant coaches in a degrading manner, despite the many contributions they bring to the team.
As the only Hispanic player on the team, my son was the only one denied the opportunity to participate in practices or games. Even after several attempts to request a private conversation, Mr. Stalling refused to meet with him. The fact that no explanation was ever offered is alarming and entirely unprofessional.

Due to these experiences, my son is now transferring out of the school. For any families considering this program, I strongly recommend thorough research before committing. Our experience was completely unacceptable, and I hope serious improvements are made for future students.

I could give this school zero stars, I would—but unfortunately, I had to select one in order to submit this review.', 'As a college student here I can believe that Cumberland County College is a great community college to go to. The college has a wide variety of people of all different ages and ethnicities. The professors and staff of the college are always friendly and helpful. The college campus it self is beautiful and well designed. Creative art is spread throughout the Campus. There is always fun clubs you can join all over the Campus. Some clubs are academic others not as much. What ever you are looking for in a college you can find here at a affordable price in CCC', "I originally went to this college as a kid and I did not take it seriously. As a result, I failed and went out into the real world. I learned a lot of life lessons that I didn't have to. After I got fired from my job of ten years, I went back. I was focused this time and college changed my life for the better. I made some good friends and I am on a career path that I really enjoy. I know the professors aren't the greatest, but you can still learn from them and be a self starter. Stay humble and have an open mind. Don't let anything distract you from your goal. Keep on top of your financial aide, apply for grants and scholarships, do your classwork and go out of your way to make your portfolio better. That's the mantra I followed and it worked. I'm going to be graduating soon and I'll be going to Rowan in the fall. College is like everything else in life, you get what you put in.", 'Great looking campus lots of buildings Green Space', "A mixed bag. It's very possible to get unlucky and have a terrible experience, but for the most part the staff at least meets status quo. If you're lucky like me, you'll be surrounded by great professors, bosses, advisors, etc. to help you achieve more in a four year college. Bottom line is this: to get the best experience here, ask everyone you know about professors you've had. Its important to know about each professor in order to maximize your success.

Also, try to avoid online classes. It might work for you, but I had a terrible experience with all 3 of my online courses."]

name: Drew University
reviews: ['My colleagues and I attended an Open house. Friendly people in admission office and answered all our questions. Cozy, beautiful campus.', 'Amazing town and beautiful campus.  Our child loves it there!', 'one of the best places I’ve ever been to. drew is it’s own little world. beautiful campus beautiful people, reminds me of the smell of fall leaves. so many amenities on campus- accessible radio station, instruments, gym, food, etc.', "I met some good people here. It has a beautiful campus and passionate faculty. The only issue for me was housing. Given the general condition of the room and building, I wasn't sure whether it was worth what I paid. And sometimes the inconsiderate, tactless attitude of the staff made the whole experience much less enjoyable than it would otherwise have been.", 'Agree with the review about housing below. I once discussed some highly delicate issues with the housing staff and the person was tactless and combative all along. I didn’t expect personal friendliness, but there wasn’t even anything that showed some formal professionalism that I’d normally expect from a professional staff at a school. No “I see what you mean, but…” or  “I understand it may look that way, but…” or “Regrettably,…”, just a couple of curt sentences that basically conveyed the impression “you’re wrong, and you’re doomed.” How unprofessional.']

name: Essex County College
reviews:
["I'm here everyday.The campus idms beautiful. Always clean.The staff is attentive & helpful.They play a very vital role in the community.", 'Fantastic place and wonderful people. Felt welcomed the moment I walked in.', 'To be literally honest, ECC is an affordable college. I love few professors here because they are great, I hate most professors here because they are not really up to the mainstream of academia.', '“Our very own — there’s truly no place like home! Every school has its ups and downs, and ours was no exception, but through it all, we stood strong, we grew, and we made it together! 💪🎓❤️”', 'My experience at Essex County College has been nothing short of horrible. The lack of professionalism, guidance, and support from staff has left me extremely disappointed and frustrated.

I began attending this school in September of last year. Right from the start, there were red flags. I was mistakenly registered for the wrong major, which I had to correct myself once I noticed the error. Still, I gave the school the benefit of the doubt — something I now regret.

During my second semester, I had to drop a class due to circumstances beyond my control. I spoke with my advisor, who assured me it was okay to drop it. The professor of the class even encouraged students to drop if they were having difficulties. What no one told me, however, was that dropping the class would bring me below the 6-credit minimum required for the grant I was enrolled in. As a result, I was hit with a charge of over $2,000.

When I contacted the Financial Aid office to understand the charge, I was met with rudeness and unprofessional behavior. I was told that I "should’ve asked" about the credit requirement — as if new students are expected to come in already knowing all of the fine print. At no point did anyone inform me that dropping to 5 credits would make me ineligible for aid. This was a major oversight on their part.

I reached out to the president, vice president, and dean. Eventually, I was directed to Dean Kirkland, who was dismissive, nonchalant, and unhelpful. He told me he would look into it, but I had to follow up multiple times just to get a response. When he finally got back to me, he said the best he could do was remove the charge for the class I dropped — ignoring the much larger issue of the financial aid adjustment and lack of proper guidance. He wouldn’t even let me finish explaining my situation during our conversation.

Now, I’m stuck with a bill of over $1,300. Because of this balance, my transcripts are locked and I’m unable to access any official documentation showing that I attended or which classes I took. I also cannot register for the next semester, leaving me completely stuck in limbo through no fault of my own.

In short, this college does not care if you succeed, drop out, or fail. If you’re looking for a supportive environment with professional, caring staff who want to see you thrive, look elsewhere. Essex County College failed me in every possible way, and I would strongly advise anyone considering it to think twice before enrolling. Don’t waste your time, energy, or money']

reviews:
['We certainly enjoyed ourselves at the Felician Family Day. My son appeared to have a wonderful time. Perhaps I will have the opportunity to teach and mentor the new nurses or attend more events in the future.', 'Connor is the worst. 0 help whatsoever he doesn’t reply to emails . name: Georgian Court University
reviews:
['Georgian Court University is one of those hidden gems in Lakewood — a beautiful, peaceful campus with a real sense of dignity and class the second you pull in. The grounds are kept immaculately, with those classic, elegant buildings and a calm vibe that feels more like a little oasis than a busy school.

Every time I’ve been there, the staff and security have been pleasant, organized, and helpful — you can tell they take safety and structure seriously (yes, you check in, but it’s smooth and professional, not a whole production). Directions are clear, people are respectful, and the overall environment feels welcoming.

What stands out most is the atmosphere: quiet, clean, and well-maintained, with a sense that students can actually focus and grow there. Whether you’re coming for an event, walking the campus, or just visiting, it feels like a place that’s run with thoughtfulness.

If you’re in the area and haven’t seen it, it’s absolutely worth a visit — a classy campus, well-managed, and a really nice presence right here in Lakewood. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️', 'If you are a transfer student I would avoid coming here. It’s always a struggle to register for classes and the registration office is never willing to help or work with you. Every transfer credit they claim they accepted still needs an override and advisor to sign off. The lack of communication is a real problem too. I wish they do better. I wish they would advertise that to future students because it should never be a struggle to register for classes EVERY semester.', 'Ken is very approachable and always quick to respond. He takes the time to answer all my questions clearly and without delay. He is professional, insightful, and committed to education and growth.', 'Incredible grounds. Office staff and professors are very nice and warm. Very accommodating', "I had the misfortune of attending this university, and I must say it was a complete waste of my time and money. The treatment I received from the professors was nothing short of appalling. I was subjected to verbal abuse, disrespect, and was consistently talked down to whenever I asked for help.

The professors at this university seem to take pleasure in belittling their students (Dr. Egan and Dr. Nash - Nursing).

When I asked for help, I was met with resistance and disdain. The university's lack of support and resources is staggering. This university's ratio is woefully inadequate, and it shows in the lack of attention and support provided to students.

The amount of money spent on tuition is simply not worth it. I can see why this school is unheard of - it's because it's a subpar institution that prioritizes profits over people.

In conclusion, I would not recommend this university to my worst enemy. The verbal abuse, disrespect, and lack of support are just a few reasons why I would advise against wasting your time and money here. I hope that prospective students will take heed of my warning."]

name: Rowan University
reviews: ["Notice how all of the recent reviews from students are terrible? Thats because Rowan University in itself is garbage. The parking is atrocious. The parking office knows how the student body feels and has not done anything to fix it for YEARS. The school continuously funnels money into new projects instead of addressing its glaring issues. Not to mention the state of multiple buildings (elevators may become stuck or remain unfinished) and reek.  Also, the inability to use the library. Most staff will lie to your face and redirect to avoid any accountability. You can get a mediocre education here at best. The campus isn't safe considering the fights, drug use, and assaults that are consistently reported. Rowan will try to scalp you for any money that you have to offer. Rutgers has a better reputation for a reason. It's not worth settling for Rowan.", "It has downgraded a lot. I think people that tend to like the university have settled for less. Students of color are treated differently. There are barely any parking spaces, it's been like that when I first came here in 2021. I am looking forward to transferring, I find some of the professors or most even to be ignorant. I think there is an illusion that people are happy here. When you are going through something or do not have the support, they lack understanding or empathy. They failed to remove a student in a timely manner who threatened to harm other students. The food options offered is nasty, not all but most in my opinion. You are waiting approximately over an hour for food. I feel many students are here because they had made the decision to settle. Rowan's music department is amazing. They refuse to improve things around the camps.", 'Rowan is amazing. My daughter is in her third year there. Her first two years she lived on campus. Her freshman year was rough ONLY because she had to live in Holly Pointe and the kids were constantly disruptive and pulling fire alarms. The University did not discipline enough in my opinion.  Her next year in the Townhouses was AMAZING!!!! As for the college, I love it and my daughter loves it. There is so much there for them both academically and non-academically. My quiet shy daughter is doing something new every day on campus. There are themed nights and lots of clubs. Everyone has been so kind and inclusive.  It is also very safe. Rowan has their own police department that also works together with the Glassboro Police department.  Their presence is noticeable without looking like a police state. There are many shops and stores that the kids can utilize.  The student center and recreation center are open early and close late. There are plenty of crosswalks that have flashing lights. I truly am happy my daughter chose to go to Rowan over the many other offers she had for colleges.', "I'm reviewing as a student. There is no library and bot enough spaces or areas for student study, especially quiet. You walk all over just looking for a place to study or a printer. Fees are the same without library as with.", 'Date of first-time visit was Easter Sunday 2025.  I toured the campus after photographing the Hollybush Mansion and I was very impressed.  Since it was a holiday the only living things I saw were the ducks which was fine by me.  The campus is divided by a road that leads into town.']

name: Rowan College of South Jersey-Gloucester Campus
reviews:
["I had the pleasure of meeting with Dr. Raja today, after being referred by another provider. The office was very clean and organized and the exam was well lit with information to keep you engaged while waiting. The front desk staff and medical assistant who took my vitals where very pleasant and an overall joy to work with. Dr. Raja was very well versed. He took the time to sit and allow me to share my history, my concerns and my goals with him. I've met with other doctors who made me feel rushed and even got mad when I advocated my needs. Its important that I am a good fit for the practice, but also that they are a good fit for me! He answered all my questions confidently, and provided clarity for things that I was unsure of. The most important part to me is not finding a doctor who knows all the answers, but also a doctor who doesn't mind consulting with colleagues in areas of uncertainty. Although I wasn't able to commit to any treatment today, I really appreciate him going above and beyond to coordinate care with a doctor who may be more versed for the conditions I deal with. I could tell that I mattered, and that is a priceless feeling! I now look forward to meeting with Dr. Cox at my next appointment and exploring any options that may be available. Upon leaving, Jill went above and beyond to ensure that my medical records where all ready and avaliable, and was sure to call me prior to the end of the day to schedule my next appointment. Overall, it was a wonderful experience, and I wouldn't hesitate to refer him to anyone in need of care and services! Job well done Dr. Raja! You really are a gem.", 'Sunday morning practice. It is nice to see the young kids playing.', 'This is a pathetic college that is completely disorganized from the top to bottom.

First, the administrators and faculty need to stop using the excuse that they updated their "system" as the reason why there's conflicting information regarding programs as well as provide ACTUAL HELP for their students.

Second, advisors should lay off the caffeine (mines was literally shaking and stumbling across every word) and become knowledgeable of the programs their students want to pursue. My advisor told me to take classes to "fill up my schedule" even though I didn't need them for the program I wanted to apply to. When I asked for more help, he simply stopped responding.

Third, BE CAREFUL WHAT YOU PAY FOR. I paid for a test that was not required even though it stated it on one of the countless "resources" that I needed to take it before I applied. Now they won't refund me because it is policy. Is this a way to generate extra income? Did Rowan not give you enough funding already?

Finally, the professors I've had here are laughable. My A&P professor spent half the class misreading off the powerpoint and the other half telling us about his past patients and their medical history. I came here to learn and not to hear about your daughter and your career background.

Coming from someone who was returning back to school after already graduating from a four year college, I did not expect such a drop off in quality. If you are considering a career change, AVOID THIS DISORGANIZED COLLEGE AT ALL COSTS', 'DO NOT GO HERE. Cannot apply to graduate because the student portal is down; either all of the staff is uninformed or is lying to students about the portal. I emailed the graduation office TWICE over two weeks and no one responded to either of my emails. Cannot access necessary paperwork for financial aid and was told I did not need to fill out anything for it. May not receive a $4,000 refund because I could not access the paperwork in the portal and it may already be too late. Cannot apply to graduate and may not receive my $4,000. Staff is rude and untrained.
Edit: the staff told me I wasn’t allowed to file to graduate with paper in-person at the college because the portal would have been live last week. It never became live. So when will I be able to graduate?? Why do they keep lying? I am moving soon and this whole situation is completely disrespectful to the years I was at this institution.', "Genuinely the worst experience I've ever had with any school. Almost every semester had a different issue. During the summer before the fall semester of 2024, the whole website was down for months. This made it nearly impossible to register for classes or even meet an advisor for months. The spring semester for 2025 there surprisingly wasn't any issues. For a summer class I took for 2025, I had a financial aid problem. I kept getting told I owed money even though I had paid for my class. It took 2 phone calls, 2 visits to the college itself just to get them to fix a problem that should've taken 10 minutes at most. Now, as I try to register for fall classes, their website is awful. For the last month and a half I have tried to get people to fix an issue I was having registering for a lab science I need to graduate this upcoming fall semester. Instead of getting fixed, now there are no lab sciences other than ones that are for specific majors because this horrible school can't fix a problem. The class I wanted that had two courses for the semester is now full. On top of that, since I don't have this class, I may now lose my NJ STARS scholarship because I'm not a full time student. I hate this school. While the teachers may all be pretty good from my experience, good teachers doesn't help when I have a problem nearly every semester."]

name: Eastwick College-Ramsey
reviews:
['Throughout my time at the institution, I have observed what appears to be a lack of consistency, transparency, and organization in several areas that directly impact students’ education and success.
There seems to be inconsistent application of policies, which results in students feeling that they are not treated equally or fairly. Additionally, some instructors appear to struggle to effectively deliver course material or provide sufficient clarification when students ask questions. When concerns about instruction are raised or requests are made to change instructors due to learning difficulties, students are often told that staffing shortages prevent any adjustments. This leaves students feeling unsupported in their academic progress.
I have also experienced difficulty obtaining clear information about financial obligations. Students are not always informed of outstanding balances or financial requirements in a timely manner, sometimes only learning about these issues late into their program. Greater transparency and proactive communication regarding tuition, fees, and financial aid would help students plan responsibly and avoid unexpected challenges.
Furthermore, clinical placements and simulation labs have often felt disorganized. At times, facilities have not been prepared for student arrivals, resulting in lost learning time. On-campus lab sessions have also occasionally lacked the necessary supplies or equipment, forcing students to substitute materials and limiting the effectiveness of hands-on training.
When these concerns are brought to administration, including leadership, students are frequently assured that meetings will be held or issues will be addressed. However, many of these concerns appear to remain unresolved, which contributes to frustration and the perception that student feedback is not being meaningfully considered.
I share these observations not simply to criticize, but in the hope that they will encourage reflection and improvement. Students enroll with the expectation of receiving a structured, supportive, and transparent educational environment. I believe that addressing these concerns would greatly improve both student outcomes and institutional reputation.', 'First, let me start off by saying this school is absolute garbage. Anybody who just has “experience” in the field of ultrasound or any of the other “majors” can just get a job here and teach 40 plus students. There’s no certification needed to teach there so that goes without saying how unprofessional and unorganized that place is. The front end of the school is absolutely terrible. You need help or a tutor? you’re on you’re own. Yet in the beginning of starting there, they scam you into believing how amazing the school is and how much they have to offer, how many tutors they have to offer and all the other lies they tell. The amount of money spent to go here, you get a terrible education and “teachers”  who don’t give a care in the world for your education or well being, it’s disturbing. Never would i EVER, in a MILLION years recommend anybody to attend this school. I have never ever seen a school so unorganized and horrible like this one.', 'Just so everyone is aware. Eastwick is not accredited by the CCNE or ACEN as of 2025-2026, meaning if you want to apply to obtain your BSN or MSN.. it will be very hard to do so. They want you to waste your money and time at their facility. Not only are they hindering their students from moving onto better but the lack of proper education for nursing students is poor.', 'WARNING Please Read
1. Do your pre requisites(ex. math, english, anatomy) some where else! THEY DO NOT TRANSFER CREDITS
2. The people in the front offices are the most unorganized and un knowing college reps I have ever met. Especially in the financial aid department, be ready to hear I don't know and if you call you will most likely get hung up on!
3. The financial aid department tries to charge you early for the next module when you haven't even completed the current one or got a new schedule. You also have to pay attention to your account because multiple people get letters in the mail saying they owe money when you really don't!
4. If you want to go for CVS(cardiovascular sonography) DON'T!
The teachers are not qualified to teach, they did not get a teaching degree! The school just hired students that have graduated in the past. They do not teach you properly they just read off the slides they send you and you will literally get " I don't know" when asking the teacher a question. You also don't get homework and most classes don't even count attendance as a grade.
5. The dean and program director don't care about your success! Multiple students had went to them to voice their concerns about the teachers and they were yelled at or told to "change the way you study". They also don't treat all students the same, some students get their grades bumped up to pass while others don't, even when they are only a point away from the requirement.
6. Lastly students needing to repeat a class for the third time due to terrible teaching were given the run around as to why their appeal was denied like "attendance and participation" which aren't required for most classes.

Overall I do not suggest going to this school. They do not care about your success and would rather side with their "teachers". If you do decide to take the risk please do your pre requisites somewhere else and attend at your own risk!!', 'I came here to post a negative review but I see there are already so many. Currently the director wants to go on vacation so she has allowed students to take the exam at home unsupervised. She move up exams and deadlines for other students to accommodate her vacation needs. Is it not a conflict of interest for the director of a program to sell study materials online. The abuse of power and retaliative practices is outrageous. The director intimidates students and other professors. She implements and bends rules when she sees fit. And often changes things with less than 24 hours notice. Would not recommend do not do it.

I am not a disgruntled nagging student. I am not failing courses. Trust me when I tell you do not come to this school. If you think the president or CEO will do anything about it the director has made it clear and his lack of action or intervention has certainly made it clear that bullying, intimidation, and disorganization is a common and welcome occurrence at Eastwick college campuses. In the community while Eastwick is known by hospitals for once having great surgical technology students the terror and abusive practices of Karen Chambers is also well known.']

name: Hudson County Community College
reviews: ["Having been none too moved by the class based education (however limited,) I'd received from a competitor some years back, I dare not compare this more popular rival. I lack the experience of its facility's offering.\nSo why am I reviewing this? Simply because, I was parked outside.\n*Building looks reasonably clean and inviting.", 'Do not attend this school they are scam artist, I attended this school for one semester simply because I was being charged so much money with no explanation of why. I was given a book by advising that listed all the prices of the school, when I called the bursar office the women was saying a completely different price then what was listed in the book I was given. When I would try to talk about the fees she would get on the phone talk real fast cut you off every second and still give no legitimate explanation as to why you where being charged all this money, just would keep on repeating that I lived out of county or talk about a bill that you where not inquiring about. Also the professors try to fail you with again no legitimate reason, out of the one semester I took both the professors I had where terrible. I had to cc the department to have my grade corrected, I was accused of using ai, and had to drop one of my courses from receiving an unjustified 0 on an assignment.', "First, I would like you to consider the type of people you hire and take their values into account. This happened around 9:45 a.m in JSQ location.I was waiting my turn to have my car parked, and they asked me for my ID, which is fine, I showed it to them, and they asked me to leave. And the reason? The reason was that I didn't have a sticker! They asked me for my ID but not for a sticker! The man didn't even dare to say, “Show me your schedule,” or even comment, “We'll keep your car until you come back with the sticker.” They didn't say anything to me at all, and they didn't say anything to my face. All I said was that I was late for class. The worst part? The worst part was having to leave that parking lot ALONE! The street is very narrow, and backing out of that parking lot is difficult. I didn't even receive instructions or help to get out of there! I hit my car, and what did they do or say to me? NOTHING! I left there totally angry, crying because at some point, maybe it was my fault, but no one deserves to be treated the way they treated me.As I said, maybe it's my fault for not having a sticker! But you know how hard it is to find parking outside! How was I supposed to move my car, find parking, and come back? It was impossible since I had already looked for parking. And as I said at the beginning, what angers me the most are the VALUES, the way those people who worked this morning treated me. It would have cost them nothing to wait for me to come back for the sticker and leave my car there for 10 minutes, it would have cost them nothing to give me instructions on how to leave the parking lot, they did absolutely nothing! I am an immigrant student who, unfortunately, has been paying for college for over a year, and situations like this simply make me want to leave. I emphasize values because I work in customer service. I have never treated people this way, and I never will, even if I have a thousand people on line. ALWAYS TREAT PEOPLE WELL!  And I don't want to think that just because I'm Latina, they treated me that way.", "I decided to apply here after highschool. I came here in person for orientation day after taking a bus AND a train. Only to meet a staff member who eventually told me it was better if I went to my own town's community college.(My town doesn't even have a community college). I was so excited and looking forward to attending only to feel unwanted. My mental health was already a bit low and this helped it get worse. It took me a bit more than a year, to finally feel better and decide to continue education. I don't regret not attending this place and am currently checking out another school.", "This location has some of the rudest staff and faculty I’ve ever encountered. From the security guards, to a few (not all) of the lunch staff. Many have poor attitudes, especially if you have questions or need assistance. They  make you feel like a burden simply for asking. While most of the professors and classes are great, the school needs to improve how they hire and manage their faculty. it took months for a complaint I filed to be addressed, after I had to reach out to everyone in HR just to get my case heard and be dismissed in the end. It's clear that the Journal Square campus doesn’t prioritize or care much for their students. If you want to be treated with respect, I’d recommend the North Hudson campus instead."]

name: New Jersey City University
reviews: ["New Jersey City University is frequently celebrated within my community as a vital engine of socioeconomic mobility, where the historic campus on John F. Kennedy Boulevard serves as a substantive cornerstone for both academic excellence and urban renewal. From many insightful conversations with local graduates and families, it is clear that NJCU distinguishes itself through a profoundly respectful and inclusive atmosphere, with many praising the university's unique ability to provide a high-caliber education that remains authentically attuned to the diverse needs of its student body. It is truly heartening to observe how the institution maintains such a transparent commitment to fostering practical leadership skills, a quality that my acquaintances often highlight as the primary reason for their successful integration into competitive regional industries. In the broader public consensus of New Jersey residents, the university stands as a distinguished beacon of opportunity, rightfully respected for its sophisticated yet accessible approach to empowering the next generation of professionals within a supportive and dynamic environment.", "I'm student and I love my experience. My only not so bad thing to say is. I wish they weren't merging with Kean. However, a degree is my goal it the institution shouldn't matter to much.", 'Beautiful campus, powerful mission. If universities were measured by service to their communities, NJCU would be Ivy League.', 'This university  is  the  best,  especially since they  always care about all students , and it is a safe place.', "My orientation at NJCU was nothing short of amazing! The staff was super friendly and helpful, making the entire process enjoyable and stress-free. Everyone was attentive, ensuring that all students felt welcome and supported. The breakfast provided was nice, adding a pleasant touch to the day.I highly recommend everyone to attend NJCU's orientation – it's definitely worth it. I managed to get everything done in just one day, which was a huge relief. A special shoutout to my advisor, Crystal, who was absolutely fantastic! As a re-admit student, I felt completely set up for success. Crystal not only helped me apply for my fall classes smoothly but also discussed and planned my spring 2025 schedule. Her guidance was truly invaluable. Kudos to Crystal and the entire NJCU orientation team for such a wonderful experience!"]

name: Kean University
reviews:
["I attended Kean University from September of 2023 until August of 2025. I was a remote student, so I do not have any comments on living accommodations or community events. However, there are many other things I can comment on.

Firstly, the classes here are very limited, so finding any interesting courses that do not pertain to your major is difficult. The classes that are available are perfectly adequate and allow you to earn your credits. I did find it hard to register for classes on time, as the second they all open up, it's basically the Hunger Games. If you aren't able to get into the classes you need, I hope you're prepared to spend even more time here.

Secondly, getting in touch with staff is nearly impossible. They do not answer the phones (I'm aware they're busy people, but having to wait over a day sometimes for a call back can make you a little grumpy), and they also rarely answer their emails. I've been communicating with the graduation department since mid-November about my missing diploma, and it's basically like talking to a brick wall.

Lastly, a huge shout-out to Mrs. Kristina Jones, my former EOF counselor. She was the only one of my counselors to answer her email and phone whenever I needed her. She made sure I had all my credits completed on time and supported me during my mother's hospital stay in February of 2025. I couldn't have graduated without you!", "I originally applied to Kean University, maybe 3 years ago now. I did not register for classes because I decided on a different major. I then applied again because I saw they had a 3-year nursing program. There was so much miscommunication on how I can switch my major and get everything I needed in time for the application, since missing out on that application, I asked how I could be on track for this year's application. Because it was summer time, I was told the head of the nursing department was out, but would be in at the beginning of the semester, maybe if i tried emailing her she would answer prior to being back in office. She did not which was anticipated. I was eventually told by the nursing department itself to switch my major to public health to make up time for classes like A&P, microbio, and stats. I switched my major, retook my anatomy class I was told needed to be retaken and was enrolled in the class as the nursing application opened. As I was applying I realized I didn't qualify as an internal applicant because you need to be full-time and already have a full-time semester (which I was NEVER told). So I called and got many different answers (last one being told to apply and then I reminded the nursing staff member of the application requirements and was then told I cannot apply at all) I got the email of the head of nursing again expressed my frustration of the misinformation I was told by her department just for her to ask for names of the people i spoke to and is not sure why im taking nursing classes under a non nursing major or why i am in a&p 2 when i need to retake a&p1. I am not sure why i would write the names of the people im supposed to trust when I call for information, so I told her that its not a sufficient result to retrain her staff and that her department specifically instructed me to change my major and retake the 1 class. She stopped answering which is completely unprofessional in my opinion. So I took matters into my own hands and asked for a meeting with the dean of health professions to investigate my matter. I got a reply within less than an hour. But it took over a week to get back to me, so I decided I no longer wanted to attend Kean University at all. Still expressed my disappointment with the assistant dean of health professions, where she then told me to at least look into pubic health careers (which is not why I attended the college at all) she then emailed me shortly after our meeting to just drop the class, and I can get a 100% refund. It just seems like nobody knows anything and just say anything, or just dont answer your calls and emails. College is not an easy process at all, and if you need help or any sense of direction, this school is definitely not where you want to be.", 'How can you trust this place when they go back on their word like it means nothing? I was told I could keep my email after graduation!! Something I trusted and linked many important accounts to this email 😡', 'Just received a notification that my alumni email address is abruptly being discontinued. New students, steer clear of this university. Once you graduate, they will toss you aside like trash.', 'If you are an education or music major, I’m sure it’s great. For anything else, I STRONGLY suggest going elsewhere, ESPECIALLY as a transfer student. I have talked to others who agree as well.
It’s a relatively nice, small campus and there’s only a handful of professors I liked or wanted you to succeed. The biggest problem lies in the system and faculty relating to administration, registration, and finance. There have been multiple times the school didn’t allow me to take certain classes or be able to further progress my degree, claiming I didn’t take the prerequisite when I did and the system says I did. But they never fixed it permanently, setting me back multiple semesters. Also, you need to meet with your guidance counselor before registering for the next semester. Mine didn’t answer me in time once, and a class I needed booked up. Even though it wasn’t my fault, they refused to not do anything about it. I went to upper administration for both issues and they were rude and didn’t help or answer eventually. They are way too expensive for what they represent and how they treat most.']

name: Mercer County Community College
reviews: ["I'm extremely proud to have gone to Mercer. They set me up for great opportunity and the West Windsor campus was easy to navigate and had everything I needed. I used to be able to get good coffee and tea there during class.", "Advising and transfer services are a disaster at the moment.  booked virtual appointment with transfer services and no link sent in confirmation email.  when i called transfer services, they told me that i do have an appointment but there's not a link to send at the moment and that i need to go in person and ask for the link. how incredibly unorganized. deadlines for transfer are soon and i need help.  mercer does NOT set you up for success.", 'The best of the best but pricey']

name: Middlesex College
reviews:
['Went here this summer to do placement testing before fall classes. When I walked into the testing center the really old overweight Caucasian lady with white hair in the testing center was SO nasty and mean. I didn’t feel welcomed at all. This was one of my first interactions and impressions of the staff here. I walked in and greeted her saying I communicated with enrollment and advisement via email so I could do my placement testing before I register for classes. She acted completely shocked and immediately began taking her anger out, for whatever reason, on me. She wasn’t even doing anything besides sitting there when I walked in. She was like, “Oh well do you even HAVE an appointment? Who did you even speak with and when?” In such a degrading and hostile tone. She talked to me as if I shouldn’t be here and that I was ridiculous for even asking to do the testing. Even some other women that worked behind the desk with her looked uncomfortable, but of course didn’t speak up. This is NO WAY you treat students especially new ones. She was speaking very loudly and giving attitude when I had a question where the pencils were. She then went on to say as I walked into the testing room, “Well whatever, good luck.” I mean seriously?! I don’t care how bad of a day you’re having you don’t take it out on innocent people. I asked both the advisement and the enrollment office if I needed a specific appointment and they told me via email for the summer to just walk in and take the test before 3pm. So I did exactly what I was told to do. Nobody seems like they’re on the same page and unfortunately I got the brunt of it.', 'Unfortunately they have no teachers and the ones they do have don’t even teach. You’re basically teaching yourself and giving a teacher a free paycheck . Edison received all this money and instead of utilizing for supplies and enhancing the school district it decided to build a stadium. It makes no sense. No quizzes, no homework, no books in some classes. Science labs missing equipment and using outdated equipment. Some teachers don’t follow the syllabus. You are on your own. Most students drop their classes. The class goes from 20 to 6 and the teacher don’t care. They don’t even realize it’s because they are horrible. They only have one teacher per subject. So instead of finishing in 2 years you’re stuck doing 3/4 because they have no classes or teachers. Or you failed because the teacher is horrible. So now you’re paying more to take the class again somewhere else.. save yourself!!the counselors are clueless and not helpful at all! Students are teaching themselves using YouTube teachers. .. You are truly teaching yourself!! Maybe they should pay the students instead of the lazy teachers.', 'i hate this college. No one knows anything. I have to constantly ask 6-10 people for one question. The people you need are never around. The librarians cant even help with a lockdown browser and they dont even know anythiny. Im tired of walking to EVERY SINGLE building for ONE question that the PROFESSOR I HAVE SHOULD KNOW!!!!!', "I thought I put Edison on the GPS but accidently got to East Orange since the police is always there 24/7 monitoring students and THIRSTING for tickets and that makes it feel awkard and seems like there's lots of crime in Edison!

NO PARKING SPOTS AVAILABLE AT ALL! They consolidated the parking to only ONE SMALL SPOT area thats always full and they will still issue you tickets on permitted spots which is absolutely does not make any sense! and you have to walk at least 10-15 mins to get to your class even on raining days and bad weather conditions.

In short, if you are not disabled with parking permission, it's not a good option for you to go there!", "I've been waiting to get accepted and start classes for a year!
This school acts like it's Harvard University with the acceptance terms when it's just a regular community college like all others.

They required so many documents to submit just to get accepted that I was never asked for those documents at other colleges in NJ!

Advisors are very strict and really tough with the rules!

They have been still processing my application since Decemeber 2024!

I don't feel nice welcomed to that school and still deciding:
Is this the right school for me with the way they act?"]

name: Montclair State University
reviews:
['i spend like 6k every semester to go here, a lot of stuff is broken and professors either call out or get their information from google ai. I wish the material were more challenging and less like high school 2.0, I do enjoy the views and parking deck, I’ve only eaten here a couple times and it’s nostalgic but I haven’t eaten there recently so I don’t have much to say on that topic.
