I love going to class so it’s 3 stars.', 'My sister graduated there as a commuter. She finished w a psychology degree. She works as a caseworker making great $$$. Her experience at Montclair State was beneficial for her future.', 'My daughter got various external scholarships. She also got a scholarship from Montclair to cover some of the cost. Halfway through the first semester they decided since somebody else gave her a scholarship they will deduct it from what they gave her. So basically they're taking money away from her. When she contacts the financial aid department she gets no no emails returned. The communication is terrible. It's really disappointing that a university is run this way. Trying to get a call back or an email reply is non-existent. It is a total scam. It is called "displacement" and is illegal in New Jersey. Don't believe whatever amount of money they offer you is what you will actually get. Makes me very angry.', 'We went there for a sports clinic .
Nice facility and staff.
The campus seems well maintained and up dated.
The training was professional.
I’m not certain about the academics, as we were not there to take a class.
The campus is a bit sprawling and it took a bit to figure out where we needed to go...all in all- the road signage is adequate.
There is a Yogi Berra stadium which looked interesting.', 'Left the accounting masters program after realizing I was being lied to. They wanted me to take out a 10k student loan (x 4 semesters = 40k) for a “career changer” degree that would not have yielded value.']

name: JFK Muhlenberg Harold B. and Dorothy A. Snyder Schools
reviews:
['I’m reporting this school’s administration to any department I can report it to. They are an absolute joke and HIGHLY unprofessional. It is December 10th and I have not received my financial aid nor an update as to when it’s will be disbursed since I am now carrying a balance. It is impossible to meet with personnel as they make you wait for hours only to tell you they no longer have time to take students who have signed in to meet with them (and it’s impossible to schedule an appointment). They hound you for tuition payment while you are WAITING for financial aid to be disbursed. I have been to 3 institutions and have NEVER been given the run around as much as I been by this school. I even missed out on a GRANT because they filed THEIR paperwork late so now I am only eligible for the spring semester grant. They should honestly be ashamed how they are treating students given how EXPENSIVE this school is. No sympathy and no sense of urgency whatsoever. Extremely upset by how this school is being ran.', 'I am a current student. I would NOT recommend anyone to this school. The teachers are amazing, however administration is completely HORRIBLE. It is Sep 30th no one has financial aide yet, but they are asking for tuition payments. No one answers the phone, emails, or listen to VM. If I wasn’t so far in I would absolutely transfer to another school. Please find another program or make this your very last resort. -JF', "Completely unprofessional and incompetent teachers like Marie Taylor who curse in class, cannot spell correctly, humiliate and bully students, and gossip about them with others. Additionally, it's hard to reach anyone in the main office if you ever need help.

Please save your money and go elsewhere. Stay on a waiting list if you have to. Or else--good luck!", "School is so hostile for no reason. Even just trying to get information from administration the security guard harrasses you to leave the parking lot that is literally in front of the school. They threaten to tow you and expect to to find street parking. Plus the school can't be bothered to post the hours so you can talk to anyone. You call and no one answers the phone. It says 24/7 which can't be true. It is not inviting to anyone who wants to get information and there is no way anyone should pay 50,000$ plus for that kind service.", 'Kianna Spaulding has been such a huge help throughout my nursing school journey. Anytime I had questions or needed guidance, she was always patient, supportive, and quick to help me figure things out. As you may know, nursing school can be overwhelming, but having Kianna there made the process so much smoother.
I’m really grateful for all the time and effort she put into helping me, she truly made a difference in my experience. Thanks again!!! C/O May 2025']

name: Eastwick College-Nutley
reviews:
['I DO NOT RECOMMEND COMING HERE!!!!! Professors are unprofessional and create an environment that makes it uncomfortable for students to learn. They all give off an “I’m just here for a check” energy and don’t care if you need help or are struggling.

Cardiovascular labs have 55 STUDENTS with 1 INSTRUCTOR, so be ready to fight for an ultrasound machine or be forced to sit on a bench with the other students who couldn’t get a machine to practice scanning—something we PAID $48K TO LEARN TO DO!!

Parking is terrible. My car was hit in the lot because students and staff literally box people in due to how small the parking area is. There is NO HEAT in the WINTER and NO A/C in the SUMMER—it gets so cold that the sink faucets freeze! Way too overpriced for the amount of suffering students go through.

But the absolute worst is the FINANCIAL AID DEPARTMENT. They will come into your class and broadcast your financial situation in front of your peers.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND COMING HERE—especially if you’re interested in the Cardiovascular program. You’re better off applying elsewhere. Even if another school is competitive, keep applying until you get in.', 'My experience at Eastwick College was absolutely unacceptable. The level of unprofessionalism from the professors was shocking, and the administration was even worse. The Dean of Academics is completely unhelpful. Instead of supporting students, she wastes time, avoids responsibility, and offers no real solutions. Dealing with her was beyond frustrating and felt like a dead end every single time.

The registrar’s office is a mess. Some of the employees clearly do not know what they are doing or even what their job responsibilities are. I was given incorrect information, run in circles, and forced to deal with delays that could have easily been avoided if the staff were properly trained or organized.

Students deserve respect, guidance, and professionalism. Eastwick College failed in all of these areas. I would not recommend this school to anyone.', 'This school does not work with students who have jobs at all. The Registrar makes your schedule and will not change it for any reason. If you work or just limited availability this school will make things very difficult.

There is no heat in the winter and no AC in the summer. Communication with professors is extremely poor. Professors don’t respond to emails, and lecture slides are also sent very late—sometimes only a few days before exams—so students are forced to cram.

When you get into core CVS classes, there will be at least 45 students in one lab with only one instructor. Before core classes, the school requires Medical Assistant and Phlebotomy classes even if you don’t want those certifications or already have them, which wastes time and money.

There is never parking! If you are late on payments, financial aid staff will come into your classroom and call you out in front of everyone, which is embarrassing and unprofessional.

This school causes unnecessary stress and anxiety. Save yourself the headache and go somewhere else. If I could give zero stars I would!', 'I took a tour not that long ago and it seemed like okay School. I took it upon myself to do more research and what they do not tell you of that this is a private college, so that means your college credits will not transfer if you want to pursue further education beyond the programs they offer. For the route I am trying to go this was a extremely important piece of info.', "Warning! It's important to be aware that the Anatomy and Physiology classes are currently taught by an instructor whose English may be challenging for some students to understand. If you have concerns about the effectiveness of the teaching in this foundational course, it may be worth discussing these issues with the administration. For instance, I reached out to Dr. Elmiry, the dean, regarding the hiring decisions related to this course, but unfortunately, my questions were not addressed. It might be beneficial to proceed with caution and consider additional support while taking this class or another school."]

name: New Jersey Institute of Technology
reviews: ["I was placed into adv. math and programming courses, which is ridiculous given that the comp sci grad cert program was advertised for career changes. I was overwhelmed out of the gate, which should not have been the case. One prof didn't even lecture! He just told us to read the textbook. In my opinion that's unacceptable. Additionally, my advisor was completely unavailable, AND is the one who set me up with inappropriate courses in the first place. I truly regret my time at NJIT and their program and/or advertising needs to be revisited.", "It was nice! Very popular and extremely busy campus. The school has great curriculums. PARKING IS A DIFFERENT SUBJECT! Parking is scarce even with a parking pass. It's because you have the live-in and the outsiders parking in the parking lots. I know the dorms have separate parking spots but I guess if they don't feel like walking they will drive a block just to park in the lots.", "Was here this morning for Salesforce training and I could not have been more pleased with the outcome. Andrew McDermott is the truth! He guided me through what he believes my strengths are and showed me excellent networking opportunities. NJIT allowed us to use their spaces for this trailblazer meetup and for this I'm grateful. This is a hidden gem in Newark NJ.", "I would give it a 0 star. This school has highly impersonal, indifferent environment: this is a weed-out school. Natural interest in learning is not encouraged here, everything is about how to fail you. No-one cares about students. No-one helps. Professors don't care. Tutoring sucks too. This school's goal is to be making students into soulless corporate-machines. I have studied in other universities and got degrees in other places. I have never seen such unhelpful, arrogant, power-seeking, miserable, terrible professors. Enrolling to this school was one of the worst decisions I have ever made. The campus is really bad too.", 'Great campus! Beautiful. Also, visit the makerspace and schedule a tour!']

name: Ocean County College
reviews:
['Does not answer the phone. I’ve called admissions “the hub” 15 times and they just don’t answer…. they clearly don’t care about their students', 'I had a deeply unsatisfactory experience with Ocean County Community College. I was charged for a course I never attended, and despite reaching out multiple times, I received no help or resolution.

In May, I was contacted two days after the course began and informed the representative that I would not be participating because the class did not meet the qualifications I needed for my education. I was locked out of my OCC account and couldn’t disenroll myself, but the woman I spoke with assured me she would process it on her end. I confirmed this with her and trusted the matter was handled.

Months later, I was shocked to see a charge for that same course. I called the admissions office on January 11th and explained the situation, including that I was unable to access my account or view any billing info. I also mentioned that I was misinformed about the course transferring to my current school — it turned out to be pass/fail and therefore not valid for graduate programs.

I emailed OCC with a detailed explanation and request for help — and got no response. I called multiple times trying to get assistance logging into my account or disputing the charge and got nowhere. I was completely ignored when I needed support the most.

I would not recommend this institution based on how poorly they treat students who run into problems. No one should have to deal with this kind of negligence or lack of accountability.', "Such a fantastic school so close and affiliated with so many wonderful four-year programs.  I was able to transfer to Ramapo and eventually get my masters degree from Fordham and a supervisor certificate from Kean University. I also studied some sign language here and other classes. I'll always remember my art classes though because I met friends I'll have forever.", 'OCC is a very beautiful school with a lot of nature surrounding it which is nice. My only complaint is that a friend of mine graduated from here and her parents missed seeing her walk across the stage for the graduation due to how far the parking lot was from the actual spot was commencement was her mom struggled getting up the hill supposedly because all the other parking lots were full that were closer and there weren’t any carts escorting people anymore either.', 'Are ya’ll short staffed?  I keep calling and no one answers.  Almost day after day.  Did you need help in the admissions office?  I just wanted to confirm that I only need two more courses to graduate.  I loved this school, but lately no one picks up the phone.  I think I’m about to move back to New Jersey to work in the administration’s office LOL.']

name: Passaic County Community College
reviews:
['The old white lady in the student services desk date June 25 9AM was so snippy and disrespectful to my family and I. For an institution that serves a diverse demographic, I’m surprised they still have employees like this. She keeps on being sarcastic and assuming what we’re trying to say before we can even finish. God forbid someone with no support approaches her, it will definitely not put them on a right start for their college success.', 'I’ve been a student for a good amount of years. This year has been my first time not receiving financial aid and because of it, I’ve noticed something awfully infuriating. For my next semester, I am taking 4 credits. 3 of those are online, the other 1 on zoom. Now, what I want to ask is this, why am I getting charged for the full amount per credit, when for online classes, I am simply teaching myself the material. Now, I have taken other classes online and let me tell you, they are all the same. $932 plus other fees to teach myself? I’d figured I would at least get a discount neither I nor a professor are going to be taking time and space on campus…', 'I called in for information about ESL placement test

at 3.03 PM on Tuesday December 13 / 2022 on the phone number that end with (973)-***-5582!

It was the old women who picked up the call.

Did not give me any useful information and end the conversation “ okay ? Bye! “

How professional the staff at this college handle!

No longer want to continue to to study with the college.', "All of the professors I have experienced were extremely outstanding, hardworking people who truly care about their students and the state of people. They strive to create outreach programs for students such as, The Men's Initiative and have powerful speakers and leaders who are always available to help. Programs such as EOF and the honors society Phi Theta Kappa, are great to join if you feel a bit lost and need some guidance and fun. Great opportunities to excell and lots of scholarship offers. You have to be involved and talk with your professors in order to be successful. They have so much to offer. Go to this community college and don't waste your time here. Keep GPA about 3.5 and above and you will get accepted and transfer over to your next choice. Stay on top of deadlines. You can do it! Be a doctor. Why not !", "I personally am okay with this School. Employees there (in the Financial Department, Academic Advisors) are somewhat mediocre. It's as if they just started working there. Overall, what saved my experience while attending that school, were the professors. I was extremely blessed to have received great ones. Professor Masri, Amanda in particular. It would be better off if they allowed students to reenroll while simultaneously paying off any debt owed. They don't let you do it unless it's all paid off which blows."]

name: Princeton University
reviews: ['Princeton University is absolutely beautiful and a pleasure to visit. The campus is well maintained, peaceful, and full of classic architecture and history. It’s very walkable and easy to explore, even later in the day.\n\nA truly inspiring place with a welcoming atmosphere. Highly recommend visiting if you’re in the area.', 'One of my best places to take photos for architectural photography :).', 'Gorgeous campus for a peaceful stroll. A few gentle hills and plenty of beauty all around. If you are visiting and want to explore, you cannot go wrong with an aimless meander. Many excellent food and shopping choices in town. Definitely one of the most beautiful American college campuses.', 'I really love the entire atmosphere of the universe and the area. You have have a nice set of shops and parks nearby the school offering a great place to visit (or possibly going to school). I think Princeton is one of the best Ivy League schools due to is location and academics. Go Tigers!', "Really beautiful campus. I stopped by here and don't regret anything. I loved walking around and seeing all the different buildings and dorms. It was actually gorgeous. There is a gift shop as well. I recommend !"]

name: Rabbinical College of America
reviews:
['I attended the Winter Program of Tiferes 2025 !

This was my experience:

I got better at Davening. The commentary during davening helped me understand the flow and the meaning behind it.

I learned alot about Halacha, Chumash, and Mishna.

I learned about a book I never knew about, the Tanya. I wish to learn this book more. Never knew about kelipot nogah.

I never really learned about the rebbe before and I finally got to read his Sichos during Shabbat.

All the students were very welcoming and excited to offer their knowledge and friendship to new students.

We had alot of Farbrengens, which were very fun and the Rabbis spoke about their unique experiences with different Jews around the world, and answered alot of our questions.

Really recommend this experience!', 'A beautiful campus for Jewish studies. Wonderful atmosphere with warm hearted bucharim, rabbis, and staff. Tiferes is fantastic - come and stay for a while.', "Beautiful campus very smart built and we'll maintained! We stopped in for sachris was really uplifting", 'Some of the wisest and most intelligent people in the United States of America learn and/or teach here.', 'The best yeshiva I have ever been. In one week you feel like you live there. In a month you make others feel like they live there.']

name: Ramapo College of New Jersey
reviews:
['We are truly honored and grateful that our son has been accepted to Ramapo College of New Jersey. As parents, we feel incredibly fortunate and proud. The campus is spacious and beautiful, surrounded by nature and a peaceful environment that is perfect for learning and growth.

We once attended one of the college’s presentations, and we were deeply impressed by the professors — they were knowledgeable, passionate, and inspiring.I want to express our heartfelt appreciation to Ramapo College for giving students such a wonderful opportunity and environment to pursue their dreams.', 'I am disappointed with the extent to which this institution has embraced a liberal approach. The school should endeavor to become more competitive and selective in its admissions process in order to enhance its reputation through a lower acceptance rate. If it aspires to compete with other in-state schools, it is essential to attract higher caliber students.

Also a commuter school, unless you join greek life or a sport, making friends may be challenging.', '“I lived there for years" ...and in 1986 "Ramapo We Sing To You" an Alma Mater was written for my voice, by alumnus Michael Alasá & by whom in time became my dear friend Dr. David Welch professor of music at Ramapo College.

..I had a dream come true and conceptual Bliss & the Collage finally and forevermore have a song they call their own!

Voice Performance Major & Psychology Major (mid 1980ś)

2023 Marquis Who's Who
HONORED LISTEE

Biographee | 77th Edition

edit: graduated and still no EV stations']

name: Rider University
reviews: ['This review is not on the academics or admissions of Rider University, only on the grounds and walkability of the campus. The campus is large and mostly flat with few trees and mostly low level buildings which means plenty of sunshine but not a lot of shade. The buildings are neat and orderly but basic and certainly not architectural masterpieces of any kind. Overall, a nice place to get your 10k steps (or earn a degree, you’re choice.)', 'Genuinely horrible administration. They seriously lack communication skills, and won’t solve problems until it’s too late.', "The school is great, genuinely. Most of the staff aside from a few outliers are very kind and clearly want to foster an environment conducive to learning for the students. However, there is one thing that no one really accounts for that is very impractical -- the number of electrical outlets. In every place on campus that students go to study -- Crans, the SRC, the BLC, residence hall lounges -- there are so few electrical outlets. There are maybe four electrical outlets for every 50 people in a space and realistically when everyone is trying to do school work or study on their computer, it just doesn't work. Great school though!", 'I am here for my masters and honest the campus is huge and totally green…. The maintenance is very good', 'What kind of school bans Chick-fil-A because they believe something different than some people at the university. Even though the students wanted it they still said no. That’s pitiful.']

name: Rutgers University-Camden
reviews:
["Something strange happened when I went here...

I went to get a degree to get a job; instead, the place taught me how to start and run a business that generates 7-figures annually. I didn't even study business! Strange, right?

I started here fresh out of the military, and wanted to be a doctor. I had no friends, so I joined a veteran group, and created a benefit run for a fallen student who was recently killed in combat (Jeremy Kane).

The school actually helped us set it all up, and gave us $20k to pull it off (we needed permits and police to shut down streets in Cherry Hill). Yes, my professors and coursework was great, but people like Mary Beth Daisey and Fred Davis all helped shape me into the employer I am today.

So when you go there, don't have an agenda. Instead, seek out your deepest passions, and what gives you meaning. For me, it was doing charity, which taught me I'd be pretty good at creating something and managing people. Who knew?! Yes, you can just get the degree, but if you dive into campus life, groups and activities, you can leave with a lot more than that. Oh, and the gym and library are awesome!", 'Rutgers Camden is a pretty small campus but it has a lot going on for how small it is. It makes people feel at home, no matter what background you come from. There’s a variety of culture on this campus, and it’s a lively campus. Students and faculty are both very friendly and willing to help if you ask, we’re all here to help each other! College is tough, but at Rutgers everyone is here to make sure you succeed and become the best person you possibly can be.', 'Very happy and proud that my daughter is attending this school very safe also , 5 stars for my childs saftey , security picks her up from the transportation center and gets her back to the dorms safe.', "I work on Campus at the CC Library so I'm in the area quite a bit. It's very well kept and the staff security are rather friendly. I like the events they host for the community here, Camden Comic Con being one of my fave. I bring my son every year, he loves it!", 'Low-key one of the best universities in the Philadelphia/South Jersey area! The biggest selling point is the amazing faculty. Faculty at Rutgers-Camden are held to the exact same hiring, tenure, promotion, and research standards as the faculty at the many-times-larger Rutgers-New Brunswick, so they are truly top of the line. Unlike almost any other state school, the faculty at Rutgers-Camden only teach 2 courses per semester (rather than 3 or 4), and thus they have enough time to do cutting edge research and are expected to, but they also have more time to interact with students. The campus is also surprisingly peaceful and beautiful and gives you the feel of a small, elite liberal arts college. This is kind of the best of all worlds - a small, intimate campus with small class sizes and lots of interaction with professors plus the cutting edge research and training of a large research university. And all just a 5 minute train ride from downtown Philly!']

name: Rutgers University-New Brunswick
reviews: ["Rutgers NB houses the oldest Queens College campus. It has 3 campuses in close proximity. Building style ranges from old Victorian to modern glass. Kirkpatrick Chapel, the Gothic Revival chapel on Old Queen’s campus, is another type that can be found. It’s a pretty open campus but if you're close by, you might want to check out Princeton. The architecture will take your breath away!", 'This university acknowledged my unaccompanied homelessness and that my apartment styled dorm was the only space preventing me from being on the streets.  Yet the residence life office, despite being one of the two offices that verified my homelessness, still demanded I declutter the space in a short timeframe, and they sided with my apartment mate who not only called the RA and staff on me just for crying in my room, but he also later yelled at me directly and ragequit because I was crying.  Said office also referred me to student conduct instead of helping me with basic needs.  The financial aid office interviewed me about my homelessness and yet still demanded third party documentation I couldn’t get, and even suggested I take out a private loan to cover the balance.  I am so sad and disappointed that I have to drop out for the sake of my safety.  If this university claims it’s inclusive and diverse, my experience was anything but that.  It was a very traumatizing experience that left me heartbroken and shattered.  If you are a nontraditional student in any form, please RUN FAR away from the dorms at this university.  And if your a nontraditional student under 24, don’t bother with this school until the FAFSA automatically considers you independent at age 24.', 'The best university in New Jersey and one the top public institutions in country. So big that there are 5 different campuses in the New Brunswick/Piscataway. A lot of great days on College Ave and Douglass and there is bus service to each part of campus which offers different things according to interests. Loved the football stadium as well', 'For 4 years Rutgers was our home, and the center of our family life.  Our eldest children grew up here and the youngest was born.  It was a wonderful life experience as a family, as people and students.  Life at Johnson apartments was happy, with difficult moments of adaptation but definitely a great challenge.  Being a family programmer on campus was an amazing  experience where we enjoyed many moments with families from all over the world.Thanks Rutgers for those years!!', "Rutgers does not seem to care about finding Mortimer Wortman, a missing student who goes to Rutgers University. They have not acknowledged or made an effort to help find Morty and only made a comment after deleting comments from their students. Before attending this school, just know if you go missing, it's up to your family to find you."]

name: Rutgers University-Newark
reviews: ['As a someone looking for a good school, do not come here. Admissions is a joke. Financial Aid has no one reliable. No one is here to help you. Their One Stop gives bad information. Save your time and money and go somewhere else.', 'I was going to try and enroll and coming from another school I wanted to know what was my process. I called the school and the first person I spoke to said I needed to reach out to another department which he gave me the number to. I tried to call twice and when finally someone answered I was told I would need to email for any questions I had. I then emailed and it took a day for someone to get back to me. I asked in the email if someone could’ve reached out to me, to please call me to help direct me as I am older and still new to college but that was not even possible for them to do. I’ll be trying to go to another school that actually takes the time out to guide new students who don’t know where to start and help them get to where they need to be!', "I don't have no problems with the clinic the only problem is the emergency room the worst emergency room ever seen", 'Quiet & there is high police patrol. Do not speed!', 'Very frustrating experience.  Impossible to reach advising or other important departments.  Not by phone, not in person.  Kid will likely be dropping out after first semester.']

name: Saint Peter's University
reviews:
['I expect to much for the study biology in this university expect all others university ! Yesterday i had a first class and its cancelled that’s not a way to secured our future planning! Last semester had a same shits i had a 5 days classes in a week and it’s canceled mostly ! How can you teach students with this cancelled classes! I had a bad experience and I already paid fees for this
semester ! I also complained to the Mr Singh main principal and he also didn’t take any actions on this complaint idk how can you run this university with this all things !', 'My son enrolled at Saint Peters University for Fall 2025 and moved in on August 24, 2025. Due to unforeseen medical circumstances, he had to withdraw on September 10, 2025—just seven business days later.
Before his withdrawal, I was explicitly told we were within the timeframe for a full refund. I had paid a $2,500 down payment, and to this day, I have not received it. Instead, I was informed that my son is being charged $3,415 for a full semester meal plan—for meals he never consumed.
When I reached out to the Dean of Residence Life, I was told there was nothing they could do because my son signed the housing agreement. I then contacted the Dean of Students and the President of the University, and have yet to receive any response.
I am deeply disappointed and shocked that a Jesuit institution, which promotes values such as community, moral and ethical behavior, compassion, and cura personalis (care for the whole person), would choose to exploit a family in this situation.
Charging a student $3,415 for food they never ate—especially under compassionate medical circumstances—is not ethical, moral, or in alignment with the Jesuit mission this university claims to uphold.
I am still waiting to hear back from the university’s leadership, and I truly hope they do the right thing.', "The worst school ever. Canceled day1CPT program overnight at the beginning of semester leaving nightmare to hundreds of students with no choice but leaving the country and the decision was supposed to be released one month in advance. And the tuition was NOT REFUNDABLE which is probably why they are holding the news.
Worst International student service as well.

This lady Alison Jackson, so arrogant, so rude, never answer your question directly always using either robotic or sarcastic tone...
I wonder whether she ever went to school for an education. Actually I won't be surprised if she graduated from SPU. So funny that is the service you get after paying 20k a year.
PLEASE choose other school.", "Nice Display of Hard work and dedication... Go St Peter and the peacocks let's go peacocks", 'Like with most colleges and universities, you need to do your research BEFORE deciding where you want to apply. Don’t take their brochures at face value; if on a weekday tour of any school, try to walk around after the tour and see if you can find students in the major you want to study and ask for their honest opinions. Make arrangements with the departments to shadow freshmen level, mid level, and advanced classes to see what it’s like. Don’t just look at the tuition price and say “too expensive, I’m going elsewhere” or “too cheap, classes are probably poor quality”.

Honestly, I think Saint Peters is a solid mid level school in terms of programs. I started with a major and minor in two departments that I ultimately switched to a major and minor in two other departments, but between those four departments one thing was common between them; there was opportunity in each. The science majors have the opportunity to do big or small research projects, art/theater majors have the opportunity to do performances, education majors have opportunities to TA at area schools, so on and so forth for most majors. A lot of schools will boast about students having opportunities, but what Saint Peter’s has is the ability to push a larger volume of students into obtaining those opportunities. Jersey City is a large city minutes away from NYC; most motivated students won’t struggle to find large or small internship roles as long as they don’t suffer from a fear of missing out on hypothetical “better internships”.

Unfortunately no school is exempt from some negative aspects. While the school has a lot of great professors you’d love to study under, just like any other school it does have its fair share of ones you don’t want as your advisor or professor. Other than that, most of my other complaints would revolve around the quality of the dorms during the time I attended. Dealing with the billing department can also be a pain (even if they are the ones who owe you money).

All in all this school won’t radically change the lives of every student for the better and put everyone on the path to becoming billionaires, but it’s programs are solid and reliable and will get you the foundation you need to have a long career in your field. And although I’m not a Christian, I do appreciate that they try to instill into their students a sense of giving back and helping others rise above.']

name: Salem Community College
reviews: ["I love this college. It's very small and close knit.  The courses I took here as prerequisites were great.  I'm currently enrolled in the ADN program. It's brutal and intense but any good ADN program is.", 'Loved going to school here, it was perfect for really preparing me for college and getting my B.A', 'The Christmas concert was truly exceptional, bravo!', 'I would like to express my satisfaction as well as my dis-satisfaction with certain programs at Salem Community College. The business program is an exceptional program that provides adequate support to aid and assist the students to not only pass the class but to be successful in their many endeavors to grow. Whereas the nursing program is the opposite. The nursing program do not have an organic approach to aid and assist students in providing the necessary tools needed to pass and to be successful in the field of nursing. It’s all about exams and the grades you acquire from those exams. Nursing is all about treating patients from a holistic approach. It shouldn’t be predicated on exams and grades like they teach you in the nursing program at Salem Community College. Nursing is all about caring, communication, problem solving, willingness, commitment, time management, and problem solving to say the least. And, to add insult to injury, the school circulates a message indicating that exams and grading is what makes a good nurse. It is in my opinion, that the leadership of the nursing program should become more proactive in providing a quality education for ALL students by hiring and training better educators who interacts and engages the students in knowledge of the lesson. By doing this it will help the students gain a better understanding of the lessons taught and not feel discouraged, disheartened, and dispirited. Nursing is not about how well you take an exam, and this is what Salem community college program is about so they can rank number one school for pasting n-clex.', "If you are interested in scientific class technologies, there is literally no better place in the United States to learn. I use literally quite well in that sentence, it is the only school in the United States that teaches this as a degree program. This place is it. That doesn't mean that they skimp on the quality. My interactions with SCC glass staff and administration have been nothing but stellar. Every single person there knows what they're talking about. And they are eager to teach you. You need to do something, times tools and resources are made available for you to do it. The lab is open to you as long as you're a student, any good to do almost anything. The instructional staff is nothing less than world class."]

name: Seton Hall University
reviews: ["As a student from the Carolinas, I have loved Seton Hall and would undoubtably call it my home away from home. I've had amazing professors who care for my success. From ESPN to NBC Sports, I've had amazing internship opportunities and I'm only in my second year. The friends and memories I've made are the cherry on top and I can't imagine myself anywhere else.", "The academic offers and experiences I've had as a student at Seton Hall have been beyond my expectations. I am an English major in my second year at Seton Hall; the one-on-one experiences with my professors have given me opportunities to do academic research and publish multiple academic articles. I appreciate Seton Hall's dedication to students and opportunities they present to individually grow each and every student! I love it here!", 'Going to give good and bad things: Seton Hall has some teachers that will grade you unfairly and be a bit rude but most are very kind. You won’t really get the college experience, you can’t really have too much fun or have late nights out, as you need to sign people in with ID’s and not past 2am and also no opposite gender or any overnight guests unless you do a form 48 hours before, so you can’t have friends over spontaneously. The RA’s are too invasive, they will walk into your room, laugh, all while you are sleeping when it’s an hour before you have to leave to break. Unlike at other schools, you have to leave at a certain time before break, and if not you have to pay $45 a night which is a lot of money. Parking is extremely expensive too, for a year just it’s like $1k and for overnight it’s $18 and textbooks can be around 500$ and you need to pay for additional programs that isn’t included in tuition that can run about 100$ each, so if 3 classes had them you would have to pay 300$ along with the 500$ for textbooks. In you billing you will see random fees that are expensive like 700$ and if you don’t pay them you can’t register or see transcripts. Good thing about Seton Hall is they offer lots of scholarships but also have many fees and costs. The dean and area coordinators are very kind and caring though. Also, you can’t doordash anything to the buildings so you have to walk to the nearest gate which can be like a five minute walk but it’s not fun in negative degrees in snow. Also, you cannot have a car on campus if you dorm unless you win some type of lottery, so you can’t really have a job or go anywhere, jobs on campus are impossible to get and they barely hire any students. Also compared to other schools, rooms are extremely small and showers are so tiny. The best upperclassmen dorms look much smaller and less modern than the freshmen dorms at other schools. You can’t really enjoy the college experience, it’s not really a party school at all you would have to go to NYC to go out. Train station is a bit of a walk and shuttle won’t take you there. A 30 minute walk is definitely not fun in the cold. By not having cars and for going out, you have to spend a lot on transportation to the city, going out in the city, doordash, and ubers. Though some teachers are unfair, most are extremely professional and all the administration in each specific school is very professional as well, whenever I called an office for help, they have always been extremely kind and supportive. The school itself is good and you can have fun especially in the city since it is close and there is a train station nearby. If you like a smaller school it’s definitely a good choice.', "I couldn't imagine being at any school other than Seton Hall! Throughout my two years being here I have gained so many valuable life skills. The small class sizes give me the opportunity to connect with my professors and peers, helping campus feel like it's own little community! If you are seeking a school that will set you up for a future full of success Seton Hall is the perfect place for you!", 'Seton Hall University offers a welcoming and academically strong environment with excellent faculty and supportive staff. The campus is beautiful, well-maintained, and equipped with modern facilities that enhance the learning experience. Students benefit from small class sizes, strong community values, and great internship opportunities. The university focuses on personal growth, leadership, and career readiness. A great choice for students seeking quality education in a friendly and inclusive atmosphere.']

name: Raritan Valley Community College
reviews:
['I would like to express my sincere gratitude to Mesonas Leonard, the Director of the Financial Office. I had a complicated situation with my documents, and he was incredibly helpful throughout the entire process. He always maintained communication, was happy to assist, and, despite his busy schedule, he always ensures that matters are resolved thoroughly and efficiently. I truly appreciate his support and dedication.

I would also like to highly recommend Jennifer Berry. If you have any questions regarding HESAA, she is always ready to help. She responds promptly and approaches her work with responsibility and care, making the process smooth and reassuring.

Additionally, ESLS instructor Lindsey Hageman is fantastic. She not only helps students understand grammar but also assists in selecting the best classes for your major. Whenever you have questions, she provides clear guidance and directs you to the right resources.

Overall, I am very grateful for their support and highly recommend reaching out to them for any guidance or assistance — their professionalism, kindness, and dedication make a real difference for students.', 'This school serves two counties but has one location...? Brookdale and Middlesex County College has multiple locations for their one county, but RVCC has one location, in the middle of nowhere, to serve two counties.  Does anyone see the problem with that? 2 counties, one of which is the wealthiest county in Jersey. RVCC... Expand and do better! Also, they never answer their phones. They make people drive ALL THE WAY to their campus just to ask and answer one question. Yes, you can email, but that takes a while for them to respond. Horrible school and I do not recommend it.', 'The absolute worst community college to ever exist in New Jersey.

Let me start off by saying, I went here for one semester before dropping out and moving to another college. I went in person.

My experience has been nothing short of a complete nightmare. First off, the registration and applying here is absolute hell— nothing is clear and there is no help from any academic advising. Phones are busy and the actual academic advising building is always full.

When classes began, The staff already were incredibly rude and non-helpful. I’ve watched in class and in hallways how teachers and staff (in general) have blandly disrespected/humiliated/mistreated students with disabilities or certain accommodations. This school in general is filled with rude people and they aren’t very welcoming. You have to learn almost everything you are taught, on your own. Me and my friends along with others in the past have made multiple complaints about the staff’s rude behavior but the complaints are definitely ignored.

The lunch here is way overpriced and most students choose to just starve which is a huge problem with hours of classes ahead.

Overall, save your FASFA money and go to another college. This school greedily takes all of your FASFA and drains you out with stupid charges. But when you ask for help or needing something like a document/transcript/credit moving, they immediately UP CHARGE YOU UPFRONT.

PLEASE DO NOT TO HERE!!', 'Head of security harrassed me for looking like one of his workers, even after changing clothes he still felt the need to come up to me and start a commotion making me feel very uncomfortable.', 'Nice evening at the zephyr show.  Venue is good, easy in and out, fairly small so no bad seats.']

name: Aviation Institute of Maintenance-Teterboro
reviews:
['PLEASE READ. STAY FAR AWAY!

I don’t leave negative reviews without a valid reason. Unfortunately, my experience with this school was extremely disappointing and misleading.

MISLEADING ADMISSION PRACTICES:
Before enrolling, admissions was very attentive and checked in constantly. Once I signed up, that communication stopped almost immediately. They will tell you whatever they need to in order to get you enrolled, including claiming you can walk away  freely within 30 days if the program isn’t for you. This is not true. Despite dropping the program and confirming multiple times that I was no longer enrolled, penalties were still applied and a loan continued in my name which I am now forced to fight off. They (Erick Madan) will pretend to not know they had said conversion and then they will say it’s a misunderstanding to try to scrape any kind of money from you.

FINANCIAL AID ISSUES:
The financial aid department offers very limited help beyond pushing you through FAFSA. When issues arise, responses are vague, generic, or avoided altogether.

LACK OF SUPPORT AFTER ENROLLMENT:
Once enrolled, student support drops off significantly. Staff who were previously responsive become difficult to reach and you are left chasing unanswered texts and emails. While there may be a few good individuals, there are also toxic admissions reps (Erick Madan) who negatively affect the experience.

POOR EDUCATIONAL VALUE:
The cost of this program is not justified. They poach on people wanting to jump into the aviation world by being the only known school in North NJ. The other schools are either in Queens NY or Upstate NY, both hours away and with wait times to get in. Much of the instruction consists of material that can easily be found for free through YouTube, Dauntless, Prepware, and other self-study resources. Paying around $50,000 to sit in a classroom and watch youtube is not worth it.

MY FINAL ADVICE:
I strongly recommend looking into an apprenticeship before considering this school. You’ll gain valuable experience / knowledge and get paid while learning. With proper logbook sign-offs, you can test for your A&P license after 30 months (or 18 months for one part of either the Airframe or Powerplant license). You’ll come out of the apprenticeship with a SOLID 30 months of real world experience rather than the 21 months of school debt and no guarantee of getting your license if you simply don’t pass your exams which you have to pay out of pocket and they are not cheap, they are at least $1000’s of dollars altogether if not more.

The opportunities are out there and I am lucky enough to have come across one thus my reason for dropping the program. Please take your time to research and reach out to companies about taking on an apprenticeship opportunity.

Don’t let this FOR PROFIT school SCAM you. Yes few students have come out of the program licensed and into great jobs in the field BUT they are the exception not the rule.', 'I want to share my experience in Block 3, Instructor Karim is one of the best teachers I’ve had. He explains everything in a simple, easy way and always makes students feel comfortable asking questions. I struggled in the hangar at first, but he took the time to repeat the hands on projects with me until I got it right, and I felt really proud and confident. His hangar projects are fun, safe, and help us get comfortable with tools. He also makes helpful handouts for Aviation Laws, Regulations, and ATA codes, and he teaches extra skills like safety wire. He’s always early, prepared, respectful, funny, and very easy to talk to. I have seen many students go to him during breaks because they trust him. I’m really happy I had him as an instructor, he encouraged me to keep going with my A&P and focus on building a good career in aviation.', 'I am currently a student in Block 10, and I have learned so much during my time at this school. I will never forget my first week when I almost decided to quit. On my third day, I met the Program Coordinator, Ahmed, who encouraged me to stay and assured me that I would receive the support I needed to succeed. He also recommended that I attend tutoring, which helped me prepare for my written exams. Thanks to the guidance and support of Ahmed, Edgardo, and Mr. Jordan, I have been able to stay motivated and continue progressing in this program.', 'I am concerned about the behavior of certain individuals, particularly Ahmed, who seems to be operating with an unprofessional attitude and appears to be on a power trip. This kind of conduct creates an uncomfortable environment. The treatment I have received from some instructors, who instead of providing constructive guidance, seem to target or provoke students.

I’m honestly dissatisfied with the quality of education and overall experience of this school. I feel that the tuition fees I have paid do not reflect the value of the education being provided. The lessons are often insufficient, covering only the bare minimum or, in some cases, not providing meaningful content at all. This lack of substance is frustrating and does not meet the expectations that were set upon enrolling.

As paying students, we deserve a more respectful and engaging learning environment where we can expect quality teaching and support that aligns with the tuition fees we are paying. I respectfully request that the institution address these issues and work to ensure that we are receiving the education we are entitled to.', 'The school is not worth what you are paying. Like other reviews stated; it’s a mess and staff are obviously on a power trip. The staff smoke in the shared environment, they are on their phones—I am not paying 50k worth of tuition for staff to be on their phones; do better. When issues are addressed, the staff will put a target on your back for simply speaking up. While I was outside the dean was literally yelling like a lunatic. Where is the professionalism. I’ve been harassed by grown adults. The list goes, on and on. This behavior is highly distasteful.']

name: William Paterson University of New Jersey
reviews: ["Excellent diversity of students and teachers for those willing to actively seek out and see-through to a first class education within an accessible and inclusive institution. But when it comes to tuition, it does feel a bit steep for what you get. For in-state students, you’re looking at around $16,748 a year for tuition and fees, and if you’re from out of state, it jumps to about $24,464. That’s not even counting room, board, and other expenses, which can add another $13,000 or so. While the facilities are decent and the campus is pleasant, I feel that the overall experience and resources don’t always match up to the price tag, especially compared to other state schools. Financial aid helps for many, but the sticker shock is real if you’re paying full price.', "WPU's motto is Willpower, which has caused me to challenge myself in ways I didn't think were possible. While I am only online, I plan to attend the campus full-time in the fall. If you are not ready to challenge yourself, you'd not be a good fit for the school.", 'I love this school. I have attended 3 other institutions and WP is by far the best school. I love the culture, the atmosphere of it. I never had problems finding parking so I am not sure what people are talking about. I am attending evening classes and have taken day time classes a few times. The staff is always very helpful and respond in a timely manner. The professors are wonderful and are always there to give you that extra support you may need. It is also located in a such a nice area.']

name: New Mexico Highlands University
reviews:
['I had a highly positive experience with New Mexico Highlands University. Having attended multiple colleges and universities to obtain various degrees including two masters and certifications, I would confidently recommend NMHU. Currently residing on the East Coast, I earned my BSN from NMHU. Although the initial process was somewhat challenging, particularly in coordinating transcripts from seven different institutions, the enrollment process, class registration, and academic quality were outstanding. The IT support team was very responsive and efficient. My nursing professors demonstrated a high level of expertise and were very supportive; they responded promptly to any questions and were always willing to conduct meetings via Zoom or video chat. The workload was manageable, even for full-time working students. Overall, I had a very positive experience and strongly recommend the RN to BSN program, regardless of your location within the United States. The program is excellent and provides good value for your time and investment. Class of 2024.', "I have had a great experience at NMHU.

Each and every person I have interacted with at the university, from the registrar's office to the technology help desk to the staff at my local branch campus seem to genuinely care about the success of student.  The professors are knowledgeable, and add real world experience to the curriculum.  They go out of the way to ensure the each student gets everything they want to out of the class.  They also crave feedback, and appreciate ways to improve what they are teaching.  That was a refreshing change from academics who are certain they already know everything.

The best part for me, as a self employed mother and serial volunteer, is the ability to complete upper level classwork in an online environment, without sacrificing the quality of the education.  The ability to replay a lecture, get instant feedback with online testing and submit work electronically has made this a far superior learning environment.", 'Despite being originally apprehensive about the small campus, I was almost immediately won over by the friendliness and support of NMHU School of Business professors and staffs. Almost all of the classes are infinitely interesting and professors here genuinely care about their students. Online classes give a great opportunity for non-traditional students to pursue higher education in a more accessible way. The department on the main campus gives off a warm and friendly feel where professors, staffs, and students know each other and that we are a part of this great community. I am given so many opportunities here that I would not be able to acquire should I have gone to a different university. For that, I am forever grateful.', 'The undergraduate business program at NMHU is a hidden gem. It is also one of the most affordable programs I have found. The staff is so knowledgeable in their fields and extremely willing to answer questions you may have regarding what classes to take in order to best prepare you for your future goals. Classes are small within the department, allowing for a great learning experience. Professors have wide ranges of expertise and experience in the business field and are always willing to give guidance regarding education and career goals. I was incredibly lucky to find it.', "NMHU has offered an exceptional program to it's students (particularly the school of business).  I have had great experiences with almost all of my professors and fellow classmates, and learned more than I had expected through taking online courses.  The school is very diverse which is something that is rewarding to see as a student, and the incorporation of that into student programs makes this school very profound in its own way."]

name: University of New Mexico-Main Campus
reviews:
['UNM’s check-in process is unnecessarily inefficient and actively works against patients, and staff appear just as frustrated by it as patients are.

Patients are not clearly instructed how early to arrive for appointments. At my first visit, I checked in 20 minutes early, only to arrive 15 minutes late to my appointment — entirely due to UNM’s own process. The delay came from waiting in line to check in, repeatedly signing the same paperwork, and then having to walk several minutes to a different building after check-in.

To make matters worse, there is a second check-in at the actual doctor’s office, which consists solely of informing staff that you’ve arrived. This adds another redundant step with no apparent benefit.

On two separate visits, reception staff at different clinics openly discussed how frustrating it was that they are not notified when patients are delayed coming from the main hospital check-in. In other words, patients arrive late through no fault of their own, clinics aren’t informed, and both sides are left frustrated — a clear coordination failure.

Patients are also routinely required to re-sign multiple consent forms at every visit (HIPAA acknowledgment, communication consent, permission to be seen), even when these were signed recently within the same system. I was incorrectly told this repetition is “required by law.” It is not. This appears to be a system or workflow failure being passed off to patients as a legal necessity.

The cumulative effect is predictable: long lines, delayed appointments, unnecessary stress, and breakdowns in communication — especially harmful for patients dealing with medical or mental health issues. You can arrive early, follow instructions, and still be late through no fault of your own.

This is not a front-desk staff problem. It is a leadership and systems problem. Until UNM streamlines check-in, integrates records properly, and improves interoffice communication, patients and staff alike will continue to pay the price for institutional inefficiency.', "Since becoming a patient within the UNM system, I have repeatedly encountered situations where I was directed to seek care outside the system because services were not available. For example, my primary care physician told me that I would need to find treatment elsewhere for my PTSD and Major Depressive Disorder because UNM’s psychologists and psychiatrists were largely functioning in administrative, teaching, or supervisory roles rather than treating patients directly. As a result, my PCP attempted to manage my psychotropic medications using trial-and-error adjustments. That approach led to severe emotional instability, including periods of intense anger and depression. In such circumstances, the potential consequences could have been catastrophic, yet the system offered little meaningful support. I also experienced a misunderstanding with an eye surgeon, after which I was told that the surgeon would not perform the procedure and that I would need to find another specialist outside the UNM system. Without that surgery, I risk permanent vision loss. Once again, the responsibility for locating necessary medical care has been placed on me.  I am currently dealing with a serious medical issue that requires an ultrasound for diagnosis, yet the earliest available appointment was six months away. I previously had to wait five months for an initial appointment with sleep medicine, even though I already had a diagnosis of sleep apnea.

While the University of New Mexico Hospital continues to expand and renovate its main facilities, many patients are struggling to access basic medical and behavioral health services because of severe provider shortages. I understand that some funding is restricted to capital projects. Still, from a patient’s perspective, the emphasis on physical expansion and modernization can feel disconnected from the realities of care delivery.

Buildings do not treat patients—clinicians do. When patients face long delays, fragmented care, and limited access to specialists, it raises important questions about priorities. The result is a system that may appear increasingly modern, yet is becoming harder for patients to navigate and less humane for those who depend on it.

To be clear, I do not believe the frontline staff is the problem. Many of them are dedicated professionals doing their best under difficult conditions. The issue appears systemic and reflects institutional decisions that prioritize expansion and infrastructure over accessibility, continuity of care, and patients' practical needs.

For those of us who depend on UNM for medical care, the current situation raises serious concerns about whether the system is fulfilling its fundamental mission to provide timely and humane treatment.

**** Medicare's rating of UNM Medical is 2 out of five stars. That speaks volumes about the quality and quantity of care available to seniors from UNM Medical.", 'Working on getting a kidney transplant. Everyone on the transplant team is great.
Friendly, courteous, and on the ball.
Making all the hoops easy to jump thru.', "I needed a break from the hospital one evening.. so I decided to take a walk on campus ad found this gem. Duck Pond, but really the whole campus is beautifully landscaped. You're in an oasis far from reality at times here. Perfect medicine", "This is a nice large clean campus. reviews:
['Lot of great things happening here.t The conference coordinator is a great guy!', 'Regarding the CONTINUING EDUCATION DEPARTMENT: I have signed up for two continuing education courses. Low efficiency and so out of touch with what the world is advancing in education. SFCC student website is poorly designed and the worst student portal I have ever used. If I had a choice, I wouldn’t even try to attend this school. CNM is way better; my gosh.', "This place is a great local resource. If you are interested in the arts, visit the art studios. Sculpture, welding, woodworking, painting, ceramics, photography, etc. all have great instructors. Plus, it's affordable, and I've heard that it's even more so for seniors.
Degree programs here help the school stay in biz while adding to your list of accomplishments so sign up for one. If you are a returning student, you've probably already fulfilled many of the requirements and will only be taking electives anyway, so it's not going to cost you more money than if you just pursued your interest anyway. You'll help keep your program going by doing so, because The Man loves to cut funding for education and is more likely to do so if programs don't have a lot of graduates. So you are helping other students have access in the future.
I'm going for an associates degree in the art department and am having a blast. I've already got a degree, so I'm just taking what I would have wanted to take without a seeking an additional degree. It's really helping me accomplish work I wanted to be able to do outside of the school.", "Despite what some may say, the Santa Fe Community College is an excellent school. Especially for those of us who can not afford and expensive University.The staff and facilities are awesome and there are many degree options for you to pick from. There are also many extra circular classes that seem like  a lot of fun! Sure it's not perfect but no one should expect it to be as they are just a small college. I can say from my own personal experience that I enjoy coming to school here. Everyone is really friendly and most of the teachers are helpful and caring towards their students.

As for the previous reviewer, I work at the bookstore and I can tell you that we would never purposely sell you a used book for full price. If that was really the case, you should have come back the the Bookstore with your receipt and shown us the mistake. We would have refunded you your money if what you said was true."]

reviews: ['I have been an advisor and supporter of the geotechnology program here for over 20 years. I have great respect for the faculty and their physics, robotics,  earth  science, geographic technologies, CAD, and other labs are as good or better than in many major university research institutions that I have visited.  This is an absolutely top-notch institution.', "Delayed directions.. also I think I could've used a different exit.. so I wouldn't have to do a Uturn", "Best Early Childhood Education program ever. The staff is great. They work hard for their students. I graduated from here and I'm way more qualified and was ready for my career.", "I graduated in the Spring of 2006, it took me less than two year's to earn my Associates in Business Administration.  Many of my Instructor's/Professor's taught at UNM and CNM, which mean's I got the same education at a fraction of what I would have paid attending those institutions.  I also got more quality time with my educators as opposed to being just another face or number amongst a larger class setting (and my teacher's knew my name!).  I had the opportunity to transfer into the Anderson School of Business at UNM to earn my Bachelor's and all my credits were viable, but I chose a different path.  I now attend the Institute of American Indian Arts, where I am 6 credits shy of earning my Bachelor's Degree in New Media Arts. I credit SIPI for being my stepping stone in pursuing a higher education for myself, my family, and community.  I have utilized much of the education I acquired there in my life and within a school setting, which has allowed me to maintain a 3.5 cumulative GPA and above. I never experienced any physical harm or have ever felt endangered at the school and I am recommending both, my 20 year old cousin and 16 year old niece to attend there in 2012.  Thank you for your time....also I am using my full name for this rating, because:  I truly believe it is a great school!", 'This is an amazing community college! name: Western New Mexico University
reviews:
['I was enrolled in the Online Master’s program in Vocational Counseling at Western New Mexico University and had a 4.0 GPA while working full time as a Vocational Development Specialist with the Anaconda Job Corps Program. I genuinely enjoyed my coursework and was committed to completing my degree.

At the time, I was paying my tuition directly rather than using student loans. After completing a part-time semester in 2020, I knew I owed a balance and called the university on three separate occasions to make a payment. Each time, I was told that my account showed “in good standing” with nothing due, even when I expressed concern and attempted to pay anyway.

A week later, I received a notice that my account had been sent to collections.

When I called, I spoke with the same staff member who appeared confused, blamed COVID-related issues, and could not clearly explain what happened. Her supervisor was abrupt and told me I “should have checked my emails.” After carefully reviewing all of my emails, I found no billing notice or warning from WNMU.

When I called back to address this, the supervisor avoided my calls and only responded after I escalated the issue to her supervisor. At that point, I was told the error was “in the system” and that nothing could be done, despite the fact that I had repeatedly tried to pay. By then, significant late fees had been added. My request to have those fees removed due to the university’s error was denied, and no apology was ever offered.

Ultimately, I chose to withdraw from the program rather than continue giving my time and money to an institution that would not take responsibility for its own administrative mistakes.

This experience was deeply disappointing and stressful, and it permanently impacted my educational plans. I strongly caution prospective students—especially online students who pay out of pocket—to document everything and be extremely careful, as billing errors and lack of accountability can have serious consequences.', 'Really beautiful campus! And the people I asked for directions etc were super nice. The museum on campus is awesome 👍', 'Fabulous collection of Pueblo pottery from southwest New Mexico. Free! Helpful staff. Go soon!', 'I enrolled in the online Master’s in Mental Health Counseling program at WNMU, and unfortunately, my experience was largely negative. The assignments felt repetitive, and communication with professors was extremely limited—emails often went unanswered, and there was no alternative way to get clarification. While the program is affordable, the lack of support and overall disorganization made it a frustrating experience. Education is too important to me to compromise on quality, and I wouldn’t recommend this program to those seeking meaningful engagement and guidance in their studies.', 'Great school. Small campus. Fantastic dorms.']

name: Vaughn College of Aeronautics and Technology
reviews:
['review here from an actual student. I attend this school, and tbh it’s very good you get lots of help and opportunities within the school including guidance with courses one on one. Free parking and lots of benefits including a free gym membership at bqe. many in campus clubs I feel like the ones who write bad reviews are the ones who miss class and arrive late, (Two absences and you are dropped from a class) I recommend this school. The best part about it is that the professors are actual employees in the industry Many work at LGA and JFK.', 'If I could give 0, or even negative stars, I would. I officially withdrew from this institution on September 2nd, 2025. Today is November 20th, 2025, and despite paying over $7,000 in tuition, the school has failed to process and issue my refund, which is now three months overdue. Most competent educational institutions process refunds within two weeks.

The administrative incompetence and lack of financial transparency at this school are staggering. I strongly urge all prospective students to reconsider enrolling. I am surprised of how competent my high school was compared to an accredited college.

When I withdrew, I was simply told to "wait for the refund to be processed." After waiting significantly longer than is standard, I contacted them and was then informed that I needed to complete several other administrative steps. These steps should have been communicated to me immediately upon withdrawal to expedite the process.

Staff members are unresponsive. Multiple emails regarding my outstanding $5,000+ refund were either completely ignored or met with unhelpful, non-committal replies that did not address my core issue.

The administrative department repeatedly provides the same, false assurance of "Wait two weeks." This stalling tactic has been used every time I have called over the past three months.

I initially understood that the 90% refund policy would apply to the $7,000 I paid, yielding approximately $6,000. I was later informed that the 90% applies to the total cost of the entire semester, resulting in a much lower refund of approximately $5,000.
This means I paid nearly $2,000 to attend classes for only TWO DAYS, an unjustifiable expense given the quality of the administration and services provided.

This ongoing failure to issue my legal and rightful refund has had a direct and punitive impact. I was wished "good luck" at my new college, yet the school is actively preventing me from using my own money to pay my tuition there.

Do not trust this school with your money. If you have any administrative or financial issues, you will be met with silence, stalling, and utter incompetence. They prioritize holding onto student funds over providing basic, professional service. Absolutely unacceptable.', 'I. Jing zhao came to USA for 6 years. Currently working in the travel agency . I has been visited this school on May 2018. Mr Domenic Proscia met up with me and my colleague . He showed us around the whole campus. He made a vivid tour and explained every thing in detail. Also I could feel he has good sense of humor. Personally speaking, I felt The staff is very helpful. Through talking with Proscia. I would like to say he is so friendly and helpful. 😊Even though I am too busy to continue summer camp plan for this school. But if I had students want to study abroad. I would like to recommend this school. Thank You 🙏 Domenic proscia. 😊💫🌟', 'Tried several times reaching out to several faculty members to inquire about a Masters in Airport Management. Weeks have gone by and no one responds. I have left phone messages too!!! So I have to look into other sources.', "Terrible institution. The good reviews definitely have to be investors/board members because every student can tell you a negative experience they had. Incompetent administration that never resolves your problems when they themselves caused them, hop you from person to person instead. It's very expensive and the cost is not worth it. There are only a handful of good professors keeping this school alive. I'm shocked they don't have a plethora of lawsuits. Save yourself the money and headache, pick another school."]
