name: SUNY Adirondack
reviews:
['Pro: Low costs for a degree, campus is clean, many classes were the same quality as ones I took at SUNY Plattsburgh and SUNY Albany, admin offices were helpful and more accessible than the other schools I mentioned.

Cons: I was forced to withdraw from a Writing About Film class I took. The teacher spent 3 months using the class to express his political hatred for George Bush. I disagreed with him once and I was forced to withdraw because he was threatened by my opinion. Hostility towards conservatives is something I noticed at SUNY Plattsburgh (main campus) as well. But overall most professors didn’t discuss politics.', 'This is the school of failure. If you love failing over and over again this is the place to be! If you struggle your first year of college like any normal student normally does you get to be put on academic probation and then guess what happens!? You get academically dismissed yayyyyy! Then you send in an appeal it gets approved then they control how many classes you take and what you take even better! 😆 Then they have you taking up to just 2 classes for the next 2 semesters because they said so! Which ultimately makes you graduate a year late! Which means more semesters to take which means more money you have to spend! I LOVE THIS SCHOOL SO MUCH! In all seriousness this school is horrible the graduation rate is 28% for a reason.', 'I attended this school for a year before leaving. the teachers did not care about what they were teaching. they showed up later then students and left class early. 80 minute classes turned u to 40. Aside from the teachers. my dorm was broken into and and my medication were stolen. the campus security didn’t care to help find who broke in and help me get my stuff back. instead i was lied to and gaslighted by the officers. trying to make me think no one broke in. i don’t recommend this school. it’s filled with kids that don’t even attend the school and live on students couches dealing drugs.', 'I enjoyed this college a lot. I went before they built the dorms back in 2013. Reviews weren’t as popular back then and I see some mixed reviews so here is an honest one.

The people in the financial aid office are amazing. They help you and really explain things to you if you don’t understand. They really educated me on financial aid and how it worked since it was all new to me. I did work study and working in the gym/sports events was great. I met a lot of cool people and coach Haskell who oversaw most of the athletics at the time was amazing. If you do work study opt for the gym!

My professors were pretty good. And if you needed extra help you just ask. I’ve forgotten her name but my history professor was very intelligent and genuinely cared about her students. My music teacher (I got stuck taking that class) was HARD but I learned a lot. There’s also a tutor study section in the library many people don’t take advantage of that.

Go to orientation and to sporting or events even if you aren’t social it’s a great way to meet people and learn about the school.

The campus is beautiful and if you don’t want to live on campus you can most likely find something near by. I commutes from VT at the time so it was a long ride but I loved the school.

The only bad thing I would say is that they need to have a better disabilities area, because not everyone has the same disability.', "Suny Adirondack, one of the worst experiences of my life honestly. The dorms are mostly the reason for the cause of trouble on campus. Don't get me wrong ,the staff are great (most), but for the other 80% of the campus, I would say avoid. If you can afford to go somewhere else do so. We could not really do anything without being told no, or being questioned on where we were going or what we were doing. Public Safety constant;y was in your business or inviting themselves into rooms to room check. Also not to mention tension built between students would lead to violent crimes on campus. Vandalism here is an all time high, and there is corruption in the student body as well as officers on campus. A note to take as well is, that almost anybody can get into this college, and with dorms comes mixing NYC kids with Upstate country kids, does not go well. This really was not a good place to be. My friend almost died in the lobby (while choking on his vomit officers put him on his back?!). Amazed me of how untrained they are to deal with an OD situation, because some spiked my friends what ever that night. I made a few good friends, but refuse to go visit due to public safety honestly. They give me the hardest time trying to go knock on my friends dorms to see if they were home. It was like high school mixed with a prison here. Also the cops are right in the dorms, hope you sleep well if you go here. Probably not though because how loud everyone had there music. This college was not a college and never will be.

P.S. I'm sorry to my past professors whom see this, this had nothing against the program I was in. Honestly this is a good school for Adventure Education though being located right under the Adirondacks, just don't get mixed up in the riff raft of the under belly of the school."]

name: Bryant & Stratton College-Albany
reviews:
['This school has truly been a wonderful experience for me! I have never felt so genuinely supported by the staff and administration, who consistently go above and beyond to help us overcome any challenges we face and to stand up for our needs. Dean Kayla makes it a priority to connect with every student on campus, greeting each of us by name and fostering a sense of belonging. Melvina, one of the administrators, is always just a text away, ready to address any questions or concerns we might have. The college radiates a student-centered atmosphere, and this positive energy is evident in every course we take. It truly feels like a community that cares.', 'I am deeply grateful and incredibly proud to have been part of this institution. Throughout my time at this college, I gained not only quality academic knowledge but also valuable life lessons, discipline, and friendships that have left a lasting impact on me.
Thank you to every professor, staff member, and fellow student who made this journey so meaningful and rewarding. I leave not just with a degree, but with a sense of confidence and purpose for what lies ahead.
I will always carry the name of this college with pride and remain forever thankful for everything it has given me. Forever Bobcat 💙', "This truly is an institution centered on its students - the support systems are amazing, and the career focused approach helps students beyond the classroom. The instructors care deeply about not just academic success, but the wellbeing of their students. It's an honor to be part of this amazing team.", 'With being a student from Bryant and Stratton I can truly say attending this college and taking courses this school is so welcoming as well as so understanding when it comes to personal life being in the way! There is so many opportunities and different paths you can take while attending this college. Each and every single person here is so nice as well as so inviting to have a conversation with. I’m truly happy to be a Bobcat!', 'The staff at Bryant and Stratton are the best.  These fabulous people supported me, and kept me on track from the beginning to the end. I can honestly say without them I don’t believe I would have made it.

If your planning to continue your education and are nervous, Bryant and Stratton is definitely the place to start.']

name: Alfred University
reviews:
['Cool little town and beautiful campus. Check out the “castle” on campus. Museum of Ceramic Arts is small but very interesting. Well worth a visit.', 'This review is not about the school itself or the beautiful music center.  It is about the horrible parking situation during a big event at the music center.  There is not enough parking.  No shuttles, no one directing which way for additional parking, very long walk just to get to the facility.  Very disappointed.  But the building is great and all county was well attended and the kids did great.', 'Honestly speaking, the university has a nice scenery and many resources but the people here are just!!! The food also is mid, not good, not bad, I have gotten sick from the food more times then id like to admit. For the amount of money they charge and the fact that they keep increasing each semester payment by about $1000, you would think new things or better quality would be introduced.

They lure you in with a seemingly nice scholarship but then the semester payments make you have a mini heart attack. Even with loans and financial aid, they still have me paying about $4k for the semester payment. Absolutely ridiculous and not worth the money.

The financial aid office lacks accountability sometimes aswell, if something needs to be updated/done or if something was updated, they won’t even let you know, you have to find out for yourself and sometimes have to dig deep with them.

Again, not worth the money. If you come to this school, I advise you to join off of HEOP or know that you will be able to afford thousand dollar semester payments (2k - 5k+).

Alfred University, please do better. Your financial aid office and their process/effort.

School Rating: 4/10', "Best college I've ever attended!", 'Amazing school. I don’t go here but my girlfriend does and, minus the stress that obviously comes from school, she seems to love it here! Obviously pricey, but you’re really getting what you pay for.']

name: The Ailey School
reviews:
["Just an absolutely wonderful experience. If you add up my dance experience across the 31 years of life I've lived, it sums to precisely 0.

As an absolute beginner, I really appreciated both the challenge as well as the judgement free attitude of the absolute beginner instructors.

I've loved taking ballet a few times a month, and it is an incredible deal. 1.5hrs of high quality instruction, with a live pianist, on both bar and on floor.

Highly recommend, truly one of the best parts of nyc", 'After-work dance vibes @ The Ailey Studios

Highly recommend dropping by The Ailey Studios after work for a dance class — it’s such a warm and welcoming community, with  professional teachers.

I used to do more “structured” ballet, but  I tried West African dance for the first time — barefoot, heart open, completely swept away by the live drumming!

The space here is clean and well-maintained, which makes dancing even more enjoyable.

What’s amazing is — you can learn literally any style of dance you’re curious about. From ballet to West African, contemporary to hip hop — they’ve got it all.

Plus, the class levels are clearly structured: absolute beginner, beginner, and beyond. So it’s really easy to find the right class for your level and grow at your own pace.', 'Wow. Came to the Center to get some information and the security desk was the most unfriendliest, unwelcoming and quite rudest thing I have encountered in all on NYC! People are on the streets are nicer! To think they get paid for this attitude is mind blowing!

All I wanted is to get information on booking & classes & she almost threw me out of the building repeating „Come back at 5. we have you your information. You can leave now.“

Very sad, because I do not step into places & leave money in which THIS is my first encounter.

Disgusting! And I was truly excited to enter this school!', 'I am sitting at the performance in DC and I am so disappointed.  I have supported Ailey since the 90s so I have seen the history of this company.  It no longer celebrates African American culture.  It’s not soulful, costumes are cheap and dancers are average.  Don’t waste your money.', 'This is a professional dance school in a beautiful building and location in midtown. There are classes available for all levels and motivations, whether you’re a novice just starting, someone looking for a fun way to improve fitness, or a professional training in the different techniques. I took many classes here, and because I am by no means much of a dancer, embarrassed myself a lot. It was a wonderful experience and opportunity to take world-class, professional dance training though.']

reviews:

name: American Academy McAllister Institute of Funeral Service
reviews:
['I attended AAMI from 2018-2021 it was a really unique experience I gained so much knowledge that I didn’t have going in. It wasn’t always easy but I learned so much. The classes were challenging and interesting and they prepared you for the boards and the profession in general. The instructors being funeral directors as well was something I appreciated. During my time there covid happened. I could say the school adapted and handled it all very well. Overall I would say if you put in the work at AAMi and with the support from your teachers and classes you’ll be confident and prepared for the future after you graduate.', 'I’m a proud graduate of the American Academy McAllister Institute of Funeral Service. My experience there was challenging but incredibly rewarding. The instructors really know the profession and care about preparing students to serve families with compassion and professionalism.

The online coursework is intense — from embalming and restorative art to psychology, ethics, and funeral law — but it gives you the knowledge and confidence you need to succeed in the field. I also appreciated the flexibility of the online and hybrid options, which made it possible to keep up with work and life while studying.

I left well-prepared for the National Board Exam and ready to begin my career. If you’re serious about funeral service, AAMI is a great place to start your journey.', "After working as an assistant at a local Funeral for several years, I realized I wanted to get into professional funeral service work. I was in my 60's and enrolled into McAllister Institute. The application process was simple, I transferred
some credits from a previous degree I had. The staff at AAMI helped me get some financial help, and I began my journey.  The educational process was very understandable, AAMI staff was very supportive, and I graduated 2 and a half years later!  I had no problems with the final exam, the National Conference Exam, nor the State Law exam.  I'm very happy with my progress. I've been licensed for 5 years now!", 'I graduated from AAMI in 2019 and had a great experience. The instructors were knowledgeable and the program prepared me well for the licensing exams and for working in funeral service. The online format was convenient and well-organized, making it easier to balance school with everyday life. I’d recommend AAMI to anyone looking to enter the funeral profession.', 'In 2012 was already working for a funeral home and decided to go to school to get my mortuary license.  Living in Kansas, working full time and raising a young family I needed to attend online.  I researched and compared all of the schools offering all online at that time and decided to go to AAMI- the deciding factor being - I had the opportunity to go to NYC for 2 weeks.

There were some things I didn’t care for, mostly not having a good support structure with the school for online students.  It’s more here’s  the syllabus, watch the class, take the tests with no hands on help or study structure, however that was 10 years ago so hopefully things have improved on that since then.

My other major concern was Little to No help with travel arrangements, where to stay, how to use the trainst systems etc. but in the end it was an awesome experience that I’ll never forget.

All in all AAMI did provide my education, fit my basic needs and I worked hard to be successful.  I was prepared (even if I didn’t think so) for my National Board Exam and passed on my first attempt in 2015.']

name: American Musical and Dramatic Academy
reviews:
['My daughter has had a fantastic time at this school and their year end Performance was fantastic.', 'I know three Portuguese people who graduated from AMDA.
One of them is the most famous musical star in Portugal:
Sissi Martins, who graduated as Silvia Martins.', 'I’m currently studying at AMDA.
It’s really the best decision I have ever made.
The teaching method is really good, I’m in my second semester and I feel that I already learned and developed a lot of skills.
Besides that, the teachers are amazing, they are really from the industry and are giving us the real training to be there.
The conservatory is intense, but that is really why Amda have a lot of amazing alumni now working in the industry.
As an international student, Amda’s support from the beginning was always really important for me, and the friends that I’m making here are really the best.', 'I joined AMDA NYC back in 2021 Fall. This school has changed my life. Incredible staffing who are all working professionals within the acting world and all are incredibly motivated, fun and inspiring. My time at this school has been nothing but positive thus far and, the school continues to get better and better. I have done my own reading into reviews and the bad reviews have definitely changed. I have seen things change here, I have seen things become progressively better for the students here at AMDA. AMDA has become much more of a supporting and safe environment for not just me but for everybody who needs it. You certainly learn a lot here, develop great connections with your teachers and get plenty of opportunities out here. I myself, am certainly glad that I chose this school. Great friends, great classes, great locations, great teachers and all around an incredibly exiting journey.', 'My daughter just graduated in Sept 2017 from NYC in dance.  She had a very positive experience from start to finish!  Starting with Elliott Kerr, Assistant Director of Admissions.  Elliott did a nice job of answering all our questions and helping get all our paperwork completed.  Our daughter loved all her teachers and has said through out her program, "this is the right school for me."  I feel like the program and the school prepared her for auditioning and the life of a performer!  THANK YOU AMDA!']

name: Barnard College
reviews: ['I literally walked hours from downtown to the campus... the first time when I visited the campus many moons ago. Such a fun memory!', "While I do not attend Barnard, I am always on the look out for their events! The have some amazing free events with fabulous speakers though out the year and anyone can attend. It's a pretty cool campus, makes we wish I had gone there.", 'No way to reach them by phone--they all hide behind insipid "phone trees".', 'Wild to me that we pay all that tuition, room & board money, and my little sister doesn’t have AC in her dorm or hot water in the bathrooms. Don’t even get me started on the gulag-looking facilities…', "Barnard is great. It is really pretty, but the campus is sooo tiny. I know it is part of Columbia and all, but still the campus is miniscule. I would totally go here though if I Penn and Columbia weren't options."]

name: Berkeley College-New York
reviews:
['I think I went to the Berkeley College because I wanted a way to build my credit in the society and it does not stop here. By the knowledge having learnt here, it always led me to the next and a better journey. When there are so many colleague graduates graduate every year, Berkeley is a place for you to take the initiative to learn, to observe and to compare where is the destination that you want to go thereafter and while enjoying the journey because what you have input.', "I've had an amazing experience at Berkeley College. The staff is incredibly supportive, always available to help, and genuinely guides students in the right direction. The professors are knowledgeable and excel at teaching real-world scenarios, which allows students to apply what they learn directly to their careers. Berkeley College encourages a strong focus on career development from start to finish. I earned both of my Bachelor’s degrees here, and the accelerated programs have been a significant advantage, helping me advance toward my career goals in no time. Highly recommend!", 'I was warned about Berkeley college but I didn’t listened and  now I have learned my lesson.

I was naive when I first started and they took advantage of it.

Attending this school the school cost were almost $13k my financial aid would cover atlease half and the rest of 6,000 would be cover by students loans.

6k per semester is very expensive unless you can really afford it and I was considered low income.

Keep in mind and don’t make the same mistakes I did even though I was warned. This is a “for profit” private school so they are operated for a profit.

Early in my attendance I was told that I will get 50% off my next degree (Bachelors) once I completed my associates degree with them and naive me fall for that. Until after I completed my associates degree and was told I didn’t qualified for the 50% off since I did not meet the criteria which was never mentioned to me at the time.

If you are going to mention a discount atlease mentioned the criteria. If I would have known those criteria I would have transferred to a CUNY college which would have penciled out cheaper. I only continued attending hoping to get the 50% off and my aid cover most of the other 50% eventually having little to no loans or outstanding balance. But that wasn’t the case since I missed a semester not knowing that semester would exclude me from the tuition discount.

Please please !! Get a statement of accounts for each semester and view the break down cost for the semester and proceed wisely.

Some colleges would take advantage of you if you dont know your info.

I wasn’t able to complete my bachelors and I have been distressed ever since. However, I’m glad to be moving forward with CUNY. Although I have accumulated thousands of dollars in loans from Berkeley.

I only found out today that Berkeley college was sued for deceptive behavior.', "The worst mistake of my life was accepting a call from their admissions call center and signing up. But I was new to this country and had no guidance. The admissions are money hunger, and once they get you inside, they trap you. Leaving you with a massive student loan debt and the degree they offer is useless. To all prospective students, run away and don't sign up to this college", "Berkeley College was a wonderful experience for me, even though it is a very expensive school. But they made me feel like I was home, very good professors, I enjoyed all my classes, and my professors. I recently graduated with my associates degree and it was a wonderful experience. I would totally recommend this school. Wish I had the nerve to take out more loans but I've had enough with the loans I have. Thank you Berkeley College for making me feel like I was home, and doing everything possible for me to graduate. I truly appreciate it."]

name: SUNY Broome Community College
reviews: ['This school is falling apart academically and physically. Buildings are run down, parking lots are not kept up with. The programs are outdated and they try to squeeze every penny out of the students. Most of the professors in the fringe programs are adjuncts and not committed to the curriculum, making more of a gripe session about the course material than a lecture on the actual topics. I am appalled that this school is in the Suny network, it is the lowest quality education I have ever received.', "SUNY-Broome is one of the best schools for students to get an excellent education. Just understand between transfer and non-transfer programs. Academic Advisors are really helpful and make sure to listen to your advisor. Really listen. Sometimes they have insight into things you wouldn't know. For example, I thought my computer security and forensics AAS was a terminal program. It actually could transfer. If you choose a program, look at our articulation agreements, understand if you want a terminal program, cert, or transfer. If you want a transfer talk to both schools about credits that will transfer with both schools, so you're not surprised. Understand what won't transfer. Trust your advisor to know how to advise you as well. Thank you, SUNY-Broome, for your warm hospitality during my time as a student here. I appreciated it.", 'Had a great day last week!', 'Great School, excellent staff. Awesome environment to learn. Looking forward to this learning experience.', "Attention  homeschoolers!!!!! Do not even try to go to this school unless you are a member of HSLDA. They will ghost you, stall the process, give you bad information, keep needing more paperwork, and then tell you that you will have to talk to someone else. They make it so complicated that you give up. They might ask me to take this down, but my wife has been trying to get in for 7 months. When she compares the process with others who weren't homeschooled, everyone she talks to had a very easy experience. So I say be prepared for a fight if you are a homeschooler."]

name: Bryant & Stratton College-Syracuse North
reviews:
['I was very hesitant on starting college again but when I toured Bryant and Stratton I felt at home. The process of getting started was smooth and easy as you have many people that will guide you through the starting process. The person that helped me get through my 2 semesters was my advisor Dominic!! He has helped me through my courses and has answered all my questions to the best of his knowledge. He is an amazing advisor and certainly supportive of all the students he works with. It was a great honor to be one of the students he worked with and it was a great honor to attend the college itself. If you have Dominic as an advisor please don’t hesitate to ask questions. He is very respectful and responsive and he cares for all the students😊As for me, I will be continuing with my journey at Bryant and Stratton college but online. I can’t wait to graduate and I’m glad to be back in school.', 'Very happy with the decision I made to go to Bryant & Stratton! Professors and staff are extremely helpful and nice!', 'Don’t bother applying here. The only thing acceptance depends on is a copy of your high school diploma. Admissions tests won’t matter, letters of recommendation won’t matter, ability to pay/FAFSA approval won’t matter. They will let you get knees deep into the process and be like “oh sorry, we couldn’t do our jobs properly and get a copy of your high school transcript so you can no longer go here.” I’m still waiting on someone named Amanda in admissions to tell me why they had my sister to go thru this entire admissions process only to tell her a week before classes start (and assigned to classes) that she’s ineligible to attend since the high school she attended over TWENTY years ago shut down. Shocker! A 40 year old’s high school no longer exists. I’m sure this happens every single day to people over 18 looking to attend higher education. So is this a racial thing because my sister is a woman of color? Or are they really that incompetent. Both ideas are scary.

So now after taking their stupid exams and jumping through hoops to get ready to go back to school, my sister can’t attend because these people are either extreme racists or extremely incompetent. Take your pick.

Shameful.', 'Do not go here! You will come out with massive debt, I almost signed on the dotted line, after going for a tour, but I said let me go home and think it over, because while I was there, I could feel the pressure, and that they wanted me to sign on so bad! My recruitmant person, kept calling me, trying to convince me to sign up, they must get commision, I had to stop answering her phone calls! It is a scam, go to OCC or BOCES!', 'The people running this place have ties "behind closed doors" in the republican party and funnel money from the staff and students. I do not have hard evidence, but when it cost $5,000 for 1 semester of a meal plan (for 1 student) and the kitchen staff is limited to less than $4 a plate and you have a Republican politician randomly show up and steal the spot light from students during their graduation ceremony, it speaks for itself. They are VERY good at making this "college" seem like a beautifully painted picture, the dorms are pathetic considering what the students have to pay for.(its cheaper to rent an apartment than to dorm here and this includes what you will spend on food) Also, they FORCE all dorm students to have a meal plan. The network here for students to use is HEAVILY throttled and some ports are blocked (good luck streaming movies and playing video games on your off time)
James street also is not that great of a neighborhood, there is an abundance of registered sex offenders in the neighborhood, students WILL NOT have access to the dorms directly and will have to wait for a security guard or RA on duty to open the main front entrance doors at night. (assuming they are even at the desk since they have other responsibilities to attend to)

My suggestion, don't make my mistake. STAY AWAY.
Note: My observations here only reflect the Syracuse, Downtown campus.']

name: Bryant & Stratton College-Buffalo
reviews:
["Bryant & Stratton College has truly changed my life for the better. As a single mom with limited time and a lot on my plate, I was nervous about going back to school. I’ve struggled my whole life with dyslexia, ADHD, and a learning disability that made reading and comprehension extremely difficult. I didn’t learn how to read until high school, and growing up, I was bullied, passed along in school, and made to feel like I would never amount to anything. Because of that, I spent years being ashamed, scared, and convinced that college wasn’t for someone like me.

Talking to the recruiter at Bryant & Stratton was the first time someone in education made me feel like I could do this. With the encouragement of my son, my family, and my friends, I took the leap, even though it was one of the hardest decisions I’ve ever made.

From day one, my instructors and my student advisor went above and beyond for me. They were patient, caring, and incredibly supportive through my depression, anxiety, and the challenges of being a full-time working single mom. They were flexible with my assignments and deadlines when life got overwhelming, and they always made me feel seen, understood, and capable.

The tutoring program is phenomenal. They helped me break down material in ways I could understand, and for the first time in my life, I felt like I wasn’t “behind” I was learning. I was growing. I was succeeding.

This college didn’t just teach me academics. They helped rebuild my confidence, my self-worth, and my belief in myself. They showed me that having a learning disability doesn’t mean I can’t achieve great things. They worked with me every step of the way, no matter how busy or chaotic life became.
I was honestly heartbroken when I found out I couldn’t continue here for my bachelor’s degree because it isn’t offered in Ohio. If I could stay with Bryant & Stratton for the rest of my education, I absolutely would.

I highly recommend Bryant & Stratton College to anyone, especially single parents, people with learning disabilities, or anyone who has ever doubted themselves. This school is supportive, flexible, compassionate, and truly life-changing. I am forever grateful for the way they helped me transform my life.

Sincerely.
A new graduate!!

(With an associate's degree in human and social services. Overly excited, and I'm proud of myself! If I can do it, so can you!!)", 'I’m truly shocked by the negative reviews because I recommend Bryant & Stratton to anyone and everyone. My experience getting my associate’s in ECE online was the best schooling experience I’ve had in my life.

The advisors selected all my classes so I didn’t have to worry about anything, and they were ALWAYS responsive when I had questions. I graduated in 2024, and now in 2026 I reached out through the chat on their website for past syllabi. The advisor immediately sent what they could and followed up with the rest the next business day after contacting the registrar.

The professors were also responsive, friendly, and supportive. The courses were easy to follow and engaging, and I genuinely liked my professors. Some left positive remarks on my work, which was very motivating for me.

Even though it’s online, you absolutely can connect with people. At the beginning of each course everyone introduces themselves, and you regularly read and respond to classmates’ work.

I really loved this school and have had no issues applying to other schools as a transfer student with my Bryant & Stratton degree. I would give more stars if I could!', 'I do not recommend this institution! I was informed that I was an active student, but after numerous assurances, I discovered that this was false. I accidentally learned from a different advisor that I was not enrolled as a student. Additionally, it took over two months for them to release the hold on my FAFSA and Pell Grant, causing me to miss opportunities at other colleges during that time. I have called countless times and spoken with many representatives, but each conversation provided a different story. My funds are still not accessible!', 'I do NOT recommend this school to anyone. First of all, the medical billing and coding program is insanely over priced for the lowest certification possible that most employers don’t even recognize. Secondly, they do not care about you. I had so many issues going through this program with having issues contacting financial aid for some important issues. They don’t care about your education you are getting, I had to out source alot of information cause it seems like they just hire anyone to be an instructor (i had a few good ones though). There was many different times with different Instructors where i had corrected them for false information. And lastly, the “life long career services” you get after graduation is furtherest from the truth. During my closing interview right before graduation, my resume was supposed to be reviewed by career services. Its been 3 months and have not heard anything. So I attempted to send out a email recently and still have not heard anything. THIS SCHOOL DOES NOT CARE ABOUT YOU. I cannot stress enough to look at better options, this place just want you money and thats it.', 'This college just pushes students through like a rotation as fast as they can. The online is 7 weeks, too fast to retain any information. After a year I still couldnt code to save mt life. They ask you to do a survey about the course and teacher only the 2nd week in not allowing for an honest actual survey when it is only week 2!! Because after the survey is when professors and class goes badly but you already did the survey. I regretted my choice of going here. Almost 20,000 after 1 yr wasted']

name: Bryant & Stratton College-Greece
reviews:
["My experience at Bryant & Stratton College has been nothing short of exceptional, deserving a perfect 10 out of 10. From the moment I stepped onto campus, I was warmly greeted by the staff, who consistently demonstrate friendliness and genuine care for every student. There has never been a moment where I felt judged or overlooked; instead, I encountered a nurturing environment that fosters growth and learning.

The campus itself is meticulously maintained, reflecting a commitment to cleanliness and organization that enhances the overall atmosphere. It's refreshing to be in a place where I can focus on my studies without distractions or concerns about safety, as I feel secure and valued in this community.

The faculty members are truly outstanding, not only in their expertise but also in their dedication to student success. They go above and beyond to ensure that we grasp the material, regularly checking in on our progress and offering assistance anytime I face challenges. Their approachability and willingness to help create an enriching educational experience that I greatly appreciate.", 'I do not recommend the Bryant & Stratton College – Greece campus nursing program.
My experience has been a consistent lack of instruction and accountability. Despite the cost of attendance (roughly $50,000 for the program), students are routinely expected to “teach ourselves,” and questions/concerns are frequently redirected back to the handbook instead of being addressed with clear guidance, remediation, or consistent teaching.
Leadership influence appears to be centralized, and decisions feel predetermined rather than student-focused. Communication is poor, transparency is lacking, and students who raise concerns are treated like the problem instead of the process being examined.
The schedule/clinical expectations also make this program extremely difficult for anyone with children or significant responsibilities. There is little flexibility and minimal support for maintaining a realistic school-life balance. Clinical rotation hours and placements were another major disappointment.
If this program had stronger instruction, clearer communication, and leadership that prioritized education over control, it could have potential. As it stands, I would encourage prospective students to seriously research alternatives before enrolling.', 'My one star is cause i know several people that are in the last class and they said it is a very hard course cause teachers don’t teach what they are quizzing students on. And there’s no support like they claim they have in orientation. It’s a lot of money to teach yourself all the material and that’s a huge chance to fail. Orientation they make it sound like they care about their students and how much easier it is cause classes are smaller. Well that’s not the experience people in the last class said.

I can’t imagine how scary that is to take out a huge loan with the belief that they mean what they say about caring about their students success. I pray everyone who goes here gets better support than the last class received .

I never hear good things about their nursing program .', 'Highly don’t recommend if going for Nursing School, very unorganized & self teaching is the way they do things. Nothing good to say , you’re teaching yourself after paying $50,000 in the end ! They don’t care as long as the monthly payments still rolling in.', 'Call center says that they do evening classes for nursing they do not.
It is a full-time daytime program Monday through Friday not flexible
46,400 for 4 semesters.
Teas test for admission
30 student class sizes
3 starts a year January, May, and September they are 16 month programs.
Staff is nice, facility is clean.
Is accredited and you can sit for nursing boards if you go here.']

name: Canisius University
reviews:
["I went to Canisius for a 4 year triple major and I really enjoyed it. The classes are small and the professors actually care. It has a great business program, but there are a lot of gen-ed prereqs that you need to take which is somewhat of a shame. Highly recommend getting involved with groups and clubs though. Networking is one of the best things you can do. You will have some professors taking attendance, and I know, sounds a bit weird for college (especially because you are the one paying), but it only furthers the fact that the professors care. All of the professors have their doctorates and many have real-world business experience which is a big plus. Since graduating, I still keep in-touch with a few professors. You'll get as much out of it as you put in. If you try and sit back and be invisible, you won't get as much out of it. If you're actually active and participate in class, you're going to have a good and positive experience. I would recommend Canisius. Have made many life-long friendships with students as well as professors. Get involved though!", 'I am a Canisius graduate of 2013 and I do not regret going to this school. To get the most out of this school, you have to know certain people. These people are the professors, your classmates, and maybe the staff that make the food ;).

In all seriousness, the classes were small and the professors were willing to help. This college has resources at your disposal so do not be afraid to use them. Now, it is an expensive school so keep that in mind, but the programs are fantastic.

Just keep in mind that it is near the East Side and some neighborhoods are not so good. During the day you will be fine walking through them but at night I would keep an eye out and check your surroundings if you are walking around them. Other than that, have fun!', "Spent 1 year there and it was the best of my 5 years in university. They offer tons of awesome classes (in litterature and history at least, I can't speak for the rest), the library is super modern and everything is done to make the students feel good. A few teachers were so-so but on the average they were really helpful.", "Campus is looking good day or night. I haven't been there since I was like 12 through 15 years old.  In my youth I was among the very few people capable of swim a full length & a half underwater.", 'From the day I stepped on campus I knew Canisius was going to be my home for four years of undergrad. The small classes helped me get to know a lot of my teachers on a personal level. I was able to be very involved in campus programming and I came out of my shell throughout my four years on campus. I was able to balance clubs, school and work study, while enjoying all of the activities that the school offered throughout the week.
Being in the heart of Buffalo provided a great opportunity for me to learn about a new city. I enjoyed the ability to take the subway into the city or drive a few minutes to Niagara Falls for a visit.
Go Griffs!']

name: St Paul's School of Nursing-Queens
reviews:
['Ms. Tucker is an amazing advisor and truly supportive. She is someone students can rely on not only academically but also personally. If you need resources, guidance, or support with everyday life challenges, she is always willing to listen. She is impartial, thoughtful, and provides honest, well-grounded advice. If you are feeling concerned about your grades or think they may be too low, she offers clear direction and helpful strategies to support improvement and help you reach your academic goals. You can tell she genuinely cares about her students’ success and well-being, and it truly shows.', "The negative reviews are 100% REAL! My experience with this school’s admissions process was unprofessional and bizarre from the start. I requested information online at 9:00 PM, and instead of a follow up during regular business hours, I received an immediate call just to be told “Did I request information because they were closed.”
The representative was dismissive and gave 'mhm' responses to my questions, showing a complete lack of interest in helping a prospective student.

The caller scheduled a meeting so I can get actual answers, but it was NOT a meeting. Upon joining and simply saying “How are you, good morning,” I was immediately muted. It wasn't a consultation it was a GROUP session where they muted all students. This lazy assembly line approach for recruitment is completely inefficient. For a field like nursing, you expect a program that values communication and professional standards but this school shows neither. I highly recommend looking somewhere else  for a program that actually respects its applicants. Trust me!!

*also to note they sent me a link for the zoom with a message that said “Don’t be late.”
I asked if these are automated messages and they never responded. Very weird and unprofessional never seen that sort of message before.", 'I am happy I chose St. Paul’s School of Nursing for my degree. Like all Nursing programs, it was a challenge at first that required commitment, late nights studying and occasional tears (lol) but it is well worth it.
The Professors in class and clinical are knowledgeable, supportive and approachable, which truly prepares you for a professional nursing career. Success in this program depends on the work you put in, you must do your part.
So if you are serious about nursing and willing to work hard, disciplined and motivated, then this is the school for you.', 'Well many people may have different experiences with them. But me as freshman I can say it might be difficult to talk to them on the phone,but all the staff were always accessible, whether through scheduled appointments or prompt email responses. they treat me with respect ,patience and show empathy. Ms Willis The Advisor she is very nice when talking on the phone even when meeting her in person she’s very approachable,very polite. her title is definitely a good example of . I can’t wait to  get started .', 'Jayne Kier is the WORST professor ever!! she uses content outside of the textbook provides and is a complete liar! states she will test only on content thats covered in class yet completely side blinds you on the exams! If you ask her 1 simple question she responds with a nasty attitude as if you are bothering her! she needs to pack it up and be replaced with a professor that actually cares!']

name: Cayuga County Community College
reviews:
["Love the nature trail behind the college. They have ample parking. They have trails behind the college. Several small ponds,lots of nature too see. Never seems too be too overcrowded whenever we go.  Nothing too virgerius, they don't have any up or down hills. Just twisting graveled trails. Definitely recommend checking it out. It can get kinda muddy especially if it has rained in the last several days. So you may want to bring your hiking shoes if you have any. Last time we walked the trails we saw bunnies,frogs/ toads and deer.", 'I attempted to take a couple of pre-regs for another degree and thought this would be a good option. After a two week interaction with Cayuga where they could not even locate my account they assigned (even with me providing their assigned username) I had to withdraw so that I could take the classes elsewhere. Ten months later, I receive a bill for tuition and am told that I am responsible for the balance. I am forced to fill out an "appeal for refund" and establish a "mycayuga" account for an institution who could not accept my money at the time? No one will speak by phone. No one (apparently) reads my emails as I am providing documentation to support my statements.

tl,dr: Do not attempt to take classes here online unless you are forced to do so. There are so many student friendly options out there.', 'Classes haven't even started yet and things have already been such a headache! The process of enrolling and getting things in order is far different from when I first attended. Technology is supposed to improve things I get but, there are so many "apps" that you are supposed to sign into to figure out what you are supposed to be doing and or what you might need. I cant even log into the main my Cayuga page majority of the time because the authenticator app that you need to get a code from when you log in doesn't even work half of the time so then you have to contact the help desk to reset everything all over again! And talking to anyone to get help is almost a joke ! The answer I get the most is "it should all be in the app" great isn't it when you cant even access things half of the time?! Oh and classes are all over the place not much at the college itself it seems. This is going to be a very trying time I can see it now!', 'Best place to study and earn your degree. Qualified and seasoned staff', "It's pretty cheap for a college about 2k-5k a semester if you're living off campus, layout is pretty ok to get around, although the professors can be very hit or miss and they also dictate how well you do for the class

A super nice professor who knows what they're doing? Guaranteed pass

A professor that couldn't care and focuses on just the textbook's work for you to do on your own? Ya just drop out of the class it's not worth it

Anywhere inbetween is usually good as well as long as you know what exactly the class is about, like how Discrete Math isn't math, it's essentially coding translation"]

name: Circle in the Square Theatre School
reviews: ['The musical JUST IN TIME could have been better directed, blocked and staged by the HS DIRECTOR OF GLEE. He is good but not Tony award level. The script needs tightening and there was too much filler. They had a chance to end this on a bang but the ending dribbled. Costumes were good, the seating was so so, the band was very good especially the woman who played several wind instruments and the TROMBONE PLAYER. Both players were exceptional. I have never seen such poor casting in my life- what a hodgepodge. The worst thing was the cost of the ticket. Let’s see what Netflix can do with this mess. Out of towners loved it but you didn’t see the enthusiasm at the closing as you do at DEATH BECOMES HER ETC.', 'Like this theater. Spacious, yet intimate; perfect for the musical we just saw, Just in Time... Spectacular! Johnathan Groff is a force to be reckoned with! What a performer. He gave it his ALL in that place.\nAnd though for some reason my aisle seat was drenched, which soaked my jeans from my bottom all the way to the back of my knees, the staff quickly addressed the situation and gave me two cushions and a towel. During intermission, three different members of the staff, came back to check on me and asked if I needed another towel. They all said it was "the first time that has happened" 🤷🏻\u200d♀️ At least it wasn\'t beer, (or something worse). I didn\'t let it ruin my evening. Will definitely attend other shows there.', 'A wonderfully intimate theater. Would imagine great views of the stage from any seat; although ours were Center Stage. Loved how Jonathan Groff and cast were easily able to interact with the audience.', 'was our 1st time in the "basement of Wicked".   we saw Just In Time - what a great performance.   But even better - the theater staff was incredible - from Will Call to security, ushers, to bar staff - they were all just welcoming inviting, answering a couple of questions we had about the theater & how it\'s a teaching facility as well as being a performance theater.   What a great time.   we had floor seats - right next to the tables for the  just in time layout.  But I can easily see how other productions can take advantage of this wonderful space.   Cannot wait to have another experience at this theater.', 'The play Just in Time was excellent.  Even the most affordable seats were good given the size and layout of the theater.  The theater  was decorated  in a way to make it an immersive experience.  The drinks are very expensive, the only down side.']

name: Clarkson University
reviews: ['Clarkson has a nice campus set in quiet Potsdam NY. It is a STEM focused university that facilitates a flexible approach for students to explore the bounds of learning.', 'Today is the time to leave Clarkson. I had my wonderful two years in Clarkson and Potsdam. My research career will continue in NJ, but I will not forget this place along with the local people I have made friends with. I will be back some day in the future. Ciao!', 'Beautiful surroundings, nice size classrooms. Inside buildings are nice.', "I only visited this school when growing up. I sat through a recruiting trip with the Men's lacrosse Head coach. He seemed generally interested in accepting me as a student, and I my application was accepted. They were originally my first choice of school, I was generally impressed. It wasn't the only engineering school I looked at, RPI Engineers, completely overwhelming. I ended up going elsewhere because of their differences in majors, schools and what I already knew I wanted to study. My commitment just wasn't enough for me because of the coursework, and so I don't regret graduating from another school. If they have the exact major I was looking for I would've committed to this school no questions asked.", 'Excellent engineering school - my son and daughter in law  both loved it there. It was their home . They were involved in many clubs including pep club and dance clubs. They graduated and remain very involved alums! . He went on to a fast track masters program. She a fast track nursing program. Now our daughter is attending Clarkson and she loves it!!']

name: Clinton Community College
reviews: ['They got me a job as a Computer Lab Assistant through FAFSA work study, participating in 3 clubs, 1 sport, and working as a full time student. Overall best experience in my life. Met the love of my life there at the newer Moore building.', "I attended my first semester fall of 2016 and enrolled for my next. I'm not the typical high school student just stepping out. I'm a single mother of 2 girls.  It has been a great experience. I'm so glad I chose Clinton. The teachers are amazing and the environment makes all the difference. Keep up the great work!", 'Fantastic view, fantastic staff, historical building!', "I've only been going there for 1 semester, but already feel right at home. Ps, whenever I walk into the Moore Building, feels like the Overlook Hotel from Stephen King's The Shining. Just a compliment.", 'Don’t waste your time. Buy self help books and/or go to a trade school. I was told I competed the course and 2 months later I needed more credits because they didn’t honor the required courses I took my first semester. The staff I met was mostly unmotivated and one of them taight and went to the school  so they didn’t have to pay back loans.']

name: Colgate University
reviews:
['My son was recruited by the soccer coaches at Colgate University and invited us to visit the campus. The coach was very engaging, responsive, and seemed eager to have my son join Colgate’s soccer team — until they met me in person, a covered Muslim woman, during our visit.
After the visit, they stopped responding completely, which was very surprising and disappointing. My son was deeply upset because they never followed up, not even with a positive or negative response. It’s okay to say no, but not responding at all is unprofessional and feels very discriminatory.', "Many of my smartest and most accomplished friends have passed through the hallowed halls of Colgate University. They have the finest of amenities and an august faculty and staff that rivals any other four-year university in the state. Dan McCoach is easily one of the top Facilities Managers in his field, and Kip Manwarren is an exemplary Manager of University Printing and Mail Services. It's no mystery why Colgate is among the 100 most selective colleges and universities in the United States.", "I graduated in '09. Wonderful, rigorous education. Freshman year will be a wakeup call (in a good way) for many. Students are nice, jolly, and sharp as hell. Small classes. Professors are invested into your education. Exactly what I was looking for in a college. Cold in winter, but it makes it kind of fun. Especially if you're like me and coming from a year-around warm climate like Southern California. Wouldn't change a thing!", 'Nothing else could have better captured the idea of an American liberal arts education. Truly phenomenal as a 2014 grad.', 'A sleeper education and experience. The people, activities and education were all good but it was the combination the created a foundation for the rest of my life. Just as alumni from 40-50 years prior to my class told us at reunion when we were finishing our freshman year (advice we didn’t appreciate at the time), Colgate lays out a way of thinking more than a particular set of disciplinary skills.

Teaching was superior (in 80-90% of courses) to my years at Harvard, something I hear from other grads. But it was the conversations, arguments and debates with classmates from diverse backgrounds that stick with you. Yes, this is a student body that is largely upper middle class and dominated from Northeast states, but what these students shared (at least during my time there, graduating in 1976) was independence, curiosity and intellectual abilities (again, not everyone and as appropriate for 18-22 year olds).

Finally, as with every experience, you get out of it what you put not it. I’ve never found a college graduate who didn’t regret not taking advantage of more opportunities. Colgate has more opportunities than anyone can capture, and way more today than when I attended.']

name: Metropolitan College of New York
reviews: ['Metropolitan College of New York at 60 West Street is frequently described in my professional circles as a pioneering force in Purpose-Centered Education, where the curriculum is uniquely structured to turn classroom theory into immediate social and economic impact. From numerous conversations with alumni who have utilized its accelerated programs, it is evident that the institution provides a substantive, results-oriented environment that many of my acquaintances credit for their rapid transition into leadership roles within the city’s public and private sectors. It is truly impressive to observe how MCNY maintains such a transparent and respectful focus on empowering working professionals, a quality that is widely praised for making a rigorous degree both attainable and deeply relevant to the challenges of modern urban life. In the collective view of New Yorkers, this college stands as a distinguished pillar of civic engagement, rightfully celebrated for its sophisticated ability to merge professional development with a profound commitment to social justice and community service.', "Metropolitan College of New York (MCNY) is a private institution located in New York City. Founded in 1964, MCNY offers a range of undergraduate and graduate programs focused on preparing students for careers in business, education, human services, and public affairs. The college emphasizes experiential learning, community engagement, and social responsibility, providing students with practical skills and knowledge to succeed in their chosen fields. With a diverse student body and a commitment to serving non-traditional students, MCNY provides flexible scheduling options, including evening and weekend classes, to accommodate working professionals and adult learners. The college's urban campus is situated in the heart of Manhattan, offering students access to internships, networking opportunities, and cultural resources in one of the world's most dynamic cities.", 'Great private school, professors are helpful, offers a great variety of online courses, campus is beautifully designed and decorated, very inviting atmosphere. This picture is the silent room comfortably furnished right next to a very inviting lounge. As a student I very much enjoy studying here. The level of diversity is amazing, and everyone is helpful and kind.', "I am your neighbor in Battery Park City and MCNY is a TERRIBLE neighbor. The HVAC on the top of your building is SCREEEEEEECHING horribly and is causing noise pollution throughout the entire Batter Park City area. I've asked, emailed, called, begged and pleaded for someone to care - and they don't.\n\nNot sure if this attitude carries over to their college - but I'm betting it does. Don't go here until they can figure out how to tighten their HVAC belt.", "I hold a BA in Human Services from MCNY... The way they set up their curriculum makes the probability of graduating on time very high. If you apply yourself you will leave that institution with a lot of new knowledge & beliefs. It has changed me as a person for the better. When I first began MCNY I did attend orientation & was informed that the students who attended have a higher chance at graduating, I can't say how true that is but I did attend orientation & I did graduate so... I would never forget Micheal Molina who said you will not leave this school the same person you came in as. He was right! I left a human service professional (HSP). I always knew I possessed the compassion, morals & understanding that one needs to become a HSP, but what I left my school with only enhanced my abilities & added much more to it. This school literally changed my life. It helped me look into the person I was. It has helped me in my personal life. While you are attending MCNY it may be hard to appreciate but as I graduated as this new person I have to say my money has been well spent! A lot of money!!!!!!! Lol but my education at MCNY was the best investment I ever made & I mean that from the bottom of my heart!"]

reviews: ['Best atmosphere ever and the service is very attentive and kind. Pim P was my server and she did an amazing job. I think it’s a good place for dates because the atmosphere allows for conversation and the food is nicely portioned. Their soy sauce is good too.', 'I visited Columbia University just to walk around and explore the campus, and I was truly impressed. The architecture is stunning, the atmosphere is full of academic energy, and the campus is much larger than I expected. It’s amazing to see such a historic and prestigious institution right in the heart of New York City. As a graduate of the MPA in Environmental Science and Policy program, I gained invaluable knowledge in sustainability and policy through a rigorous, hands-on curriculum. Beyond academics, the campus is breathtaking - historic architecture, tree-lined walkways, and iconic landmarks like Low Library make it a perfect place to learn and reflect. An incredible experience all around!', 'Colombia university is an incredible place, not just because of its academic excellence, but because of the people and its location. The community is welcoming, diverse and inspiring -students, faculty and staff genuinely care and support one another being local located in New York City. It is a huge advantage the campus blends beautifully with the city energy while still feeling like its own world. The campus is very well kept and sprawling with space for learning and discovery. The student body is very diverse. The university is easily accessible by public transportation whether that be by Bus 🚌 or train. Thank you for reading this review. Cheers 🥂.']

reviews: ["My mother's Alma mater................she got a degree in Elec. name: Cornell University
reviews:
['It is one of the most beautiful universities I have been to. Looks like I am standing in the sky watching downside hills, rivers , buildings; also like standing on the buildings hundreds years ago, feels how the past people think and learn in the university. The waterfalls is great to watch and it’s free parking after 5pm. The only bad thing is that when I am passing the walking road , one young people just drive until he sees me , and yell on me which is his fault not yield on the walkers on the yielding sign of walkers. Be careful if you walk over there , seems some young divers there is careless driving.', 'A quiet, historic campus perched on a hill above the small town of Ithaca. The stone buildings are beautiful but feel a bit tired—roads are rough, parking is a nightmare, and the campus, while scenic, feels somewhat isolated and less alive than other major universities.

Highlights:
•	Uris & Andrew D. White Library: Gorgeous, especially the cast-iron stacks in White Library. Feels like walking into a magical archive.
•	Sage Chapel: Breathtaking interior. We walked in as a student practiced Bach on an instrument that looked like a piano but sounded like a pipe organ—absolutely heavenly.
•	Café Jennie: Tucked inside the Cornell Store. Great macaroons, cozy atmosphere, and shelves of books by Cornell authors.
•	Morrison Dining Hall: Modern, clean, with a good pasta bar.
•	Cornell Dairy Bar: A hidden gem for fresh, creamy ice cream.

Worth a visit for the views, the libraries, and the intellectual charm—but be ready for hills, potholes, and a sense of quiet detachment.', 'We received a very nice prospective students tour. I guess I will be updating this review if we get accepted :)', 'Cornell University and UC Davis can share space in rankings tables, but the environments they foster often feel worlds apart.

Cornell is built around sustained rigor and unmistakable expectations. Courses are demanding by design, faculty engagement is direct, and students are routinely required to prove what they know through visible, high-level work. The culture is competitive in an open, academic sense — ideas are challenged, standards are enforced, and progress is tied closely to demonstrated ability. It is not designed to be comfortable; it is designed to make students sharper, more disciplined, and professionally credible by the time they leave.

UC Davis, by contrast, is shaped heavily by its scale and institutional confidence. The campus is large, the messaging polished, and the reputation strong, yet some students describe a gap between that image and the day-to-day undergraduate push. Instead of a tightly structured environment that consistently applies pressure, the experience can feel diffuse, with students responsible for creating their own momentum inside a complex system. Critics argue that navigating bureaucracy, fitting into existing structures, and managing perceptions can sometimes matter as much as — or more than — raw academic performance, which can frustrate highly driven students expecting a purely merit-focused atmosphere.

There are also concerns raised by some observers about whether the cost of attendance aligns cleanly with outcomes, especially for students seeking a clearly defined pipeline from classroom to career. In such views, the institution’s strong self-image may not always translate into equally strong, uniformly experienced preparation at the undergraduate level.

At Cornell, intensity is embedded into the structure.
At UC Davis, intensity can depend largely on how much a student generates independently.

The distinction is less about labels and more about philosophy: one institution tightly engineers challenge and accountability, while the other offers breadth and reputation but requires students to carve their own path through a much larger system.', 'In the area for a work related event and stumbled upon Cornell! Absolutely gorgeous campus with so much history! I loved walking around and admiring the architecture and vastness among the incredible nature of Ithaca!']

The professors truly care about your success as a student and go above and beyond to help you succeed. So many talented students, faculty and community members were part of the show. Blessed beyond belief. Thanks to all.']

name: Culinary Institute of America
reviews:
["Always a great time no matter how professional you are.  I took just one cupcake decorating class here a year ago and well.. I'm starting a full program next week! Such supporting staff and experiences professors", 'I had a great experience here in a night school program for classic culinary arts.', "I am currently a student on the 6 month intensive French Culinary Arts program and I really love it.

Being British-Lebanese (I'm an international student), I had initially planned to go to culinary school in London. However after visiting and looking at multiple courses all over the UK I just knew that this was the place for me. The course is the perfect amount of time for a career changer like myself not feel like I'm wasting time. The facilities are the equivalent if not better than anything you'll find in the industry, the chefs are admirable in both their skill and their professional demeanor, and the vibe is one of enthusiasm and support.

Don't be fooled, this course is no joke. Get ready to work hard and learn about every aspect of food and the industry that surrounds it. Here we are taught in both practice and theory of all the different cooking techniques, how to apply them to french cuisine, and how to practice this knowledge in the professional world. Plus we get some really great visiting chef demos (often because the chefs are alumni. Perks.) and unique volunteering experiences like the New York Culinary Experience and The James Beard Awards. The opportunities and support of the school and its wonderful student and careers services teams are there for us during our time on our course, as well as after we graduate.

This is the place to go if you want to learn how to work in the food industry and still love food. I will seriously miss it when I graduate.", 'One of the most scams in NYC they promise you great things. And plus the chefs on level 5 and 6 they treat you worst then the US army. Plus wen you go in for a job in any top restaurant they don’t care if you have a culinary art certificate from the French culinary institute . They mostly care how many years of experience you have in the profesional Kitchen. You better of going straight to a restaurant start as a prep and learn in there then going into debt of more then 50k$ if you can’t get a good job all of that will start killing you specially your credit score. You better off going to college then spending money in this institute. I’m college you will not go I to that much amount of debt at least farsa and scholarships will cover your college tuition. If you fail a level you have to pay huge amount of money to retake that level.  You better learning from YouTube all there culinary techniques. Anyone can cook you just have to put the love into the kitchen and you don’t need this institute in order to cook good food.', 'Great experience to learn the foundations of cooking. Excellent instructors and amazing facility. Hard work and diligence required. Not the same as a restaurant experience but very supportive stepping stone. The library is an amazing resource as are the librarians. The student services are extremely helpful and will find you an opportunity any time, any place.']

name: CUNY Bernard M Baruch College
reviews:
['Baruch is a good college. I am a transfer student and is dealing with issues created by the Bursar’s office. I cannot pay the commitment fee online. The tech service and admissions office cannot fix the problem so I paid cash in the Bursar’s office. I asked the senior lady if she updated in the system. She said it’s already updated. When I came back and checked online, it’s not updated. I spent tons of time with the admission’s office. I was kicked around between the offices. No one thinks it’s their job to update the information even if I provided screenshots or payment history. My admission process is on hold now. Baruch never contacted me with updates regarding my admission which is very disappointing.

I am considering dropping the admission. There is so much trouble and so much anxiety from the admission process. I wish I have chosen a different college. My money and time will be wasted.

I highly recommend future students to choose another college at the same time even if Baruch accepted you. You may end up like me wasting time and money and with no college to go.', 'I have had a great experience as a graduate student! It’s definitely the best bang for your buck 👌🏾', 'Stay away from this university they make classes so difficult for no reason this school will stress you out. The smart kids basically do adderall you have to do that or else it impossible to pass the hard classes its terrible place.', "Baruch professors are outstanding and knowledgeable. Most of them enjoy what they do and want their students to learn.  Unfortunately, the administration tells a very different story. I have seen students denied enrollment in required courses, leading to unnecessary delays in their graduation. I have witnessed students approach department heads in the MBA programs for help, extend a hand in greeting, and get ignored. Moments like these send a clear message: students are not valued or respected.

Baruch is meant to help its students, yet it often feels like the opposite. Administrative staff seem more focused on protecting strict processes than on supporting the people the institution exists for. This gap between the professors' dedication and the administration's indifference harms both the student experience and the school’s mission.", "I liked my classes and the professors, but it was hard to find classes that matches my schedule. Countless times there were classes available but wouldn't let students register reserving them for specific groups. Scheduling was very challenging. The staff doesn't care if you need help. They would find a reason to say no. Their superiors are even worst. They frown at students."]

name: CUNY Borough of Manhattan Community College
reviews: ["I love BMCC. They provide so many resources for their students, they have many wonderful professors and the overall experience feels like a real college experience. I recommend this school to anyone looking to start their career no matter the age. I will be graduating this June with my A.S in Early Childhood Education and I couldn't be prouder of where my journey begun!
