I highly recommend Bmcc to anyone who’s interested studying in a community college.', 'Good college to start or simply get your associates degree!']

name: CUNY Bronx Community College
reviews: ['Bronx Community College located in the University Heights section of the Bronx is the former home of the NYU College of Arts and Sciences as well as its Engineering school.\nThe Hall of Fame for Great Americans is located there. The latter surrounds the historic Gould Library designed by Stanford White. It is a classic double domed and columned building with beautiful bronze doors. (Think Florence)\nThese buildings are worth the visit. Remember the campus is part of City University and you may have to show ID and have packages inspected.', 'This is the WORST SCHOOL I’ve attended in my life. EVERYTHING is a scam for more money. It’s literally a hustle. No help from guidance counselors, they don’t know how to work technology so they can’t help you. Blame everything on the influx of students that “need help too” yet ALL OF US are confused and without guidance. We of course still need to uphold our end of meeting deadlines and paying for this garbage without seeing change. I cannot wait to leave this miserable institution.', "Got accepted, did everything i needed to months before spring semester. They told me to come in to register my classes when i called them, so I commuted to the college in the 7° weather, just to be turned down over a language error in my last years application. Even after I cleared it up, she told me she can't over look it and said I'll have to start in 2027 (when I'll be almost 27, im 25 right now, my years were wasted). She told me to take an english test ( mind you i grew up in new york) bc there was a language error in my last years application. I just left crying. They had so many chances to tell me this year and last year that that error was gonna be an issue but didn't. They wanted to wait until I come into the office thinking I'll be starting college and then tell me I can't start. This was my first choice both times bc of the online classes and how pretty the campus is and for the first time in years, when i saw i was accepted I felt excitement  and had something to look forward to. Sad, angry, frustrated, depressed isnt even enough of a word i can use for this. Even if i can go back in the fall, nothing will feel the same for me anymore being almost 27, starting this late and this horrible experience my last straw. I wont bother trying to attend college anymore. Even applying here was a hassle. Really wish beautiful places like this hired beautiful people. PATHATHIC SUPERVISOR and staff.", 'Visited Bronx Community College today for the First time. Living in the area for years and never knew this was here by the trees of the Major Deegan. The campus is exquisite so much history in the architecture. You really can’t comprehend this is in the Bronx. This use to be the old NYU Campus many years ago. It’s like time stops here the chaos around you just stops doesn’t even feel like you’re in the Bronx for a second. I’m so happy my son chose this school for his College. The College feels very safe and that’s very important to me.', 'Busar\'s office always has an attitude when called on the phone, as if they don\'t want to do their job. Answering the phone by simply saying "Busars" with no greeting is not acceptable customer service, if you ask them any information about your account they will try to give you the service level answer that you already know and won\'t want to do the leg work on issue.']

name: CUNY Brooklyn College
reviews:
["I attended my wife's Graduation ceremony here . She worked hard during covid with only online classes . And during a part of that time she was laid off as was most people . We walked in prospect park for exercise and sanity . She earned her bachelor degree and when the world opened we were invited to this joyous occasion. I was proud as I watched her walked down the aisle. She was a little reluctant but her uncle was able to convince her and me. All staff tried hard to make this special as it was !", 'Lovely campus—Brooklyn College is a hidden gem in Brooklyn! The architecture is stunning (those Gothic buildings and clock tower feel classic and grand), the quad is peaceful with green space and benches—perfect for studying or relaxing between classes. Great for arts/performing arts students with the Whitman Theater and music hall.
Campus feels safe, diverse, and community-oriented—lots of events, good library, and easy subway access. Not as flashy as some schools, but solid value and chill atmosphere.', "A nice traditional college campus, definitely loved it although some halls and rooms of the buildings definitely feel overlooked and poorly maintained. Can't tell when was the last renovation but it's nonetheless a beautiful campus and I love it quite a bit. The surrounding area makes it really easy for a quick bite to eat too and I had no trouble getting in.", 'December 2 — Brooklyn College BSA event.

This was by far one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had with event security. Even with our RSVP confirmed, we were denied entry for no valid reason. The security staff’s behavior was completely unprofessional — rude, disrespectful, and outright insulting. They acted more like thugs than trained personnel.

I’ve attended and performed at many events, including performing at last year’s show and participating in multiple BSA and outside events. I have NEVER been treated this badly anywhere. The way the Brooklyn College security team handled the situation was unacceptable and embarrassing for a CUNY institution.

I genuinely hope the Brooklyn College security supervisor takes this seriously, because the level of disrespect and unprofessionalism we experienced should never happen to anyone. Until they fix their security management, I won’t feel comfortable attending or performing at their events again.

Highly disappointing and completely unacceptable.', 'Beautiful campus and one of the oldest in Brooklyn. College has been renovated in the last two decades. It is very pleasant to walk around the beautiful campus. College has pipeline high school, which funnel students into 4 years of college.']

name: College of Staten Island CUNY
reviews: ['This is an amazing college with wonderful professors. I am grateful to be a part of the CSI family. There are many excellent opportunities, and people are very friendly and approachable.  I have raised my GPA, received an honor, and also gained a research opportunity. Thank you all.', 'I’ve had a really positive experience with the College of Staten Island. The campus is beautiful and offers a great environment for learning. Most of the faculty and staff are helpful, and there are plenty of resources available for students. A solid 4-star institution!', 'CSI OPEN REC SPORTS: Open gym volleyball at College of Staten Island is the highlight of my week. Clean courts, well kept nets, and friendly staff. Players range from beginners to seasoned hitters, yet everyone shares sets and cheers good rallies. there are speakers that plays music which keeps energy up without drowning court talk. There are lots of balls, rotation system runs smoothly(with one sub) , and wait time is minimal. Best part is the vibe. competitive but welcoming, with encouragement after every spectacular dive. Whether you crave cardio, volleyball improvement or community, this session delivers. Come early spots fast, and you’ll want every minute on that court.', 'Beating college, build on huge area. Buildings are pretty far away from each other. It takes too much time to walk from classrooms to library or other classrooms. The staff is low and due to Covid-19 canteen is closed as well. Miscommunication is at peak, along with the teachers and students. Parking is very nicely provided for students to park their cars inside the campus, which is great. Overall about 3 to 4 🌟 stars.', 'Shout out to the campus security supervisor, Micheal. The sweetest person ever, so so kind. He let me on his go cart because my next building was very far, truly appreciate him. Thank you!!!']

name: CUNY City College
reviews:
['Depending on the professors, you will be provided a good education. Some professors will scream and won’t even let you present properly. They don’t care about you or your education. There are good professors, and I had a good experience my first year.

I strongly recommend checking Rate My Professor. Be extra careful when it comes to advising and classes. I had a serious problem where they made me take a class that didn’t count toward my degree, and at the end I found out that I didn’t even need that class. Instead, I needed two others to complete my degree.

They will try to blame you, so please be careful. It shouldn’t be like this, but that’s how it works here. You should always double check everything with different advisors and please document everything,', 'So far as a freshman being at CCNY is great. Many resources, academic and mental health support, scholarship, fellowships, research opportunities by the college itself, connections with ivies, MSKCC, etc. Rigorous. I consider CCNY the ivy among all CUNY colleges because of its highly rigorous academic curriculum. It is extremely a great college, cost efficient, resourceful, and gorgeous campus. Lots of chilling out area inside the building, study spaces. And even outside. As a student interested in biomedical sciences. This is a great option. If you aren’t able to pay for expensive out of state colleges. Professors are great!', "Asinine school with overcrowded classes, a misleading class description, and a crappy science department. E permits take 3 centuries to process, which are required if you're an engineering major, considering you can't even register for your preferred time schedule because the classes are full. Job prospects for 90 percent of majors are poor post-graduation.", 'I love the location of CCNY in the New York on Hudson edge, it has big parks and grounds compared to other colleges which are like just look like any other buildings not like a college.', "It is very much like a community college. It's very diverse, tolerant, peaceful and affordable for middle class students. 😎In fact, many well-known people, such as Woody Allen and Colin Powell, have gone to this college. Plus, there's a lot of guidance involved for those whom wish to find their passions and study abroad. So, for those who wish to explore, this is definitely worth it."]

name: CUNY Hostos Community College
reviews:
['I graduated from Hostos in 2020. It was a great school however,  I noticed that people in office now are not really interested in Spanish students anymore.  They try to make it difficult specially to entertain any science majors.  I had all my prep for Radiology completed since 2020,and when I try to come back a " black " advisor make it really impossible for me. While Lehman college never asked me to repeat anything in science since my science were all A and -A minus from the same Hostos. However ,I had done 6 writting intensive classes that I don't need just as a way to jold me back because of my race and age I guess. School should be the same rules for everyone not for on group. That is not honest!!! Some people they don't even require so much writting intensive, sometimes none,even when they can rarely communicate or write properly in English.  But if you are Spanish, now they make you take classes that you don't even know to hold you back. This is a Cuny practice nowadays because life is all about who is incharge or have the magic stick on hands.', 'Amazing professors, great mental health counseling available and supportive staff. Plenty of additional support for students like the writing center, office hours, food pantry, etc. Enrollment was the most difficult part but once I was admitted and enrolled in classes, it was smooth sailing ⛵️', "It provides an on campus college experience in one of New York's most urban municipal arenas for economic opportunity and economic stability; unmatched without a discussion of what a metropolitan cost of living engages.", "I accidentally tried to withdraw from my math course, but instead I withdrew from the classes I wanted to remain enrolled in. I then attempted to reverse this change, and it took the registrar two weeks to reinstate me. The problem is that they re-enrolled me in my math class, which I had tried to “drop” before the deadline of November 5. I stopped attending the class, but if it isn't officially removed, I will receive an F. The registration office doesn’t seem to care; I’ve gone to them three times already. I also asked to see the registrar’s email, but it turns out they gave me the wrong one. Now I am trying to get them to remove the math course from my schedule. The registration office will say anything to get you out of their face. Once you’ve admitted to Hostos, they stop caring. Even the technical support staff look at you unfavorably. After this semester, I plan to transfer.", 'My experience as a parent with Hostos Community College (Forensic Science Program)

I’m very disappointed with the lack of organization and responsibility shown by some professors at this school. My son studies Forensic Science, and professors often fail to notify students when class is canceled. Many times, students arrive on campus only to find a note on the door saying the professor won’t be there or is at another class event. This happens far too often—teachers get sick or are absent without prior notice, and students end up wasting their time and losing motivation.

It’s frustrating to see an institution that should be training responsible professionals fail to set an example of commitment and reliability. I truly hope the administration takes action, because students deserve respect, clear communication, and consistent classes.']

name: CUNY Hunter College
reviews: ['I was extremely disappointed with the condition of the school auditorium. It was, quite frankly, disgusting. The floors were taped up, the walls were cracked, dusty and dirty. There was a dirty tissue left for who knows how long. Loud alarm kept turning on, and so much armed security. Felt more like a prison than a school.\n\nA facility meant to host students, parents, and guests should be held to a much higher standard. It reflects poorly on the school and detracts from the overall experience of any performance or assembly. I hope the administration takes this feedback seriously and invests in at a thorough cleaning and renovation. The students and staff deserve a clean, safe, and welcoming environment especially if you charge for renting this horrendous place to other schools.', 'For being a commuter college Hunter isn’t very commuter friendly for all students. They don’t have an indoor area for electric bikes or scooters not to mention outdoor bike racks. They have one at BMCC. There is all this renovation being done but not for this. In the winter the cold kills the battery, which can be the difference between being able to make it home and not. If you have to take the six it’s almost always packed and often delayed with stops skipped. And you aren’t allowed to bring them inside so how are you supposed to charge them? Do better Hunter', "The buildings are crumbling, rats are common occurrence, they will find a way to make your schedule hellish, counselers don't respond (have been waiting on mine to answer my email for 4 months) and when they do respond they don't know how to actually do their job, best part is that it doesn't get better. I beg you, for your own good, go to city college instead", 'Do not come here if you\'re pre-med. They have this system where you can\'t take gen chem 1 and gen bio 1 in the same semester, you can only take gen chem 1 for first semester and then gen chem 2 and gen bio 1 next semester. I haven\'t started any math/science classes as a freshman because they\'re all full and i have none for next semester either. Might be affordable but if you have to take multiple classes in the summer just to stay on track (not covered by financial aid) then how "affordable" is it really?', 'It’s a pretty good college among all the CUNY schools. It’s the main campus of Hunter College, the other two big campus are in uptown(for social work major ) and east village(nursing school ). The library and classrooms are nice. However, the office services are really bad, and some people who work there are not nice, sometimes they’re really mean!!!']

name: CUNY John Jay College of Criminal Justice
reviews:
['If you’re thinking about completing your four-year degree at John Jay whether you’re a freshman, a CUNY student, or transferring from a two-year college don’t walk, run. John Jay is an amazing university.

When it comes to academic support and resources, the staff and faculty truly make sure you understand the material, the workload, and the expectations. They also connect students with helpful resources when needed. There are numerous support groups available, which makes a big difference in student success.

While it’s not an easy university and you definitely have to put in the work, the support system makes it worth it. Overall, John Jay is a great college, and I would absolutely recommend it. Proud blood hound alumni!!!', 'I’m genuinely surprised. This has always been my dream school, which makes the lack of response to emails and phone calls even more disappointing. It’s difficult to reconcile this level of communication with their reputation as the number one Criminal Justice school in the city.

I expected a higher standard of professionalism.', 'John Jay is a unique school with a rooftop garden and a 'bougie' feel right by Central Park South. The campus is top-tier and the unique classes have prepared many for law school.

However, my experience with a specific instructor, Ms. Lu, in the physics department was unacceptable. Despite being a peer-reviewed, federally-funded researcher, I was told I was 'not academically qualified' after correctly identifying that the 'box question' on gravity is not counterintuitive—a fact backed by physicists like McCloskey. I was also told that Ms. Lu heard a lot of "talk" on my end about science. I got a 93 on the first exam despite the exceptionally poor instruction, but the minute my scores dipped due to documented personal struggles and this instructor's hostility, I'm somehow incompetent? Excuse me? I paid to hear this from an adjunct without even a PhD or tenure?

More concerning was the unprofessional environment; I was repeatedly targeted, interrupted, and berated despite being the only hijabi in the class. No student paying out-of-pocket should be insulted for their identity or their academic background. I have officially lodged a formal discrimination complaint (Complaint #599) regarding this treatment. I would advise prospective students to look elsewhere for science instruction after this adjunct's conduct. CUNY has a lot of schools.', 'Even though I’ve never been here, I’ve been in several Zoom meetings with one of the advisors, Brianna, and she is the most sweetest and supportive person I’ve ever met from John Jay. I told her about something traumatic happened to me on social media two years ago, and she understood.

My banker told me that his wife went to John Jay, and majored in Forensic Science. Crazy how something like this can be impactful!

If you’re fond of any degree related to Criminal Justice, New York, Affordability, and likely winters! Then this place is for you.', "I'm going to have classes here so I went to check it out and it's huge! It has 10 floors and is super clean. The lecture halls and the classes look cool and they have lots of places to sit and eat, and the ppl are nice and friendly :)) I'm not the best at reviews but I'm glad I chose JJ"]

name: CUNY LaGuardia Community College
reviews:
['The fact that they even have a 4-star rating is worrisome. Because HOW?
Teaching wise, yes, I would give a 4 star rating, because I have encountered some amazing professors. Others not so great, so there they lose a star.

I decided to go back to school after 13 years, and I can’t believe their system is as bad if not worse than it was then.

The way that LaGuardia treats you when you need help!!!! I felt like a mouse in a maze. They literally throw you around from office to office and in each office nobody can help you.
The advisors I spoke to, spoke to me like they had no time to explain anything, and the other one spoke like she was annoyed at all the valid questions I had.
The financial aid department took away my FAFSA help, and then I was granted a scholarship and they took away a $1000 from $2600 that I got granted. Like how? Why? Just why?
I clearly need the help, and they could care less, taking away money that was granted to me.
I went to look for help in something regarding admissions and there is no face to talk to, I was told that they only work remotely. I really hope they take that away from them soon. Because how is it that I need to speak to someone in person and there is no person to talk to. Not even a video call, not even a decent phone call, all through email.
And lastly, I will not be able to start at a four year program because the schedule interferes with LaGuardias winter session. Like how did you not think about this when making the schools schedule? So I need to be backed up for over six months because of their schedule.
I am beyond disappointed with all the runarounds and the no help.
The only thing that has make it worth to go back to school are the majority of great professors I have.', 'I truly appreciate LaGuardia CC, the college has helped me incredibly in my aim to advance my career and education. I took a class in the Adult Continuing Education department last year and I was hired directly from my internship. This year, I just enrolled for Spring 2026 semester as a 39 year old woman getting my first degree. The college is a beautiful campus, there are many programs to support all different kinds of students. I look forward to finally getting my first degree at LaGuardia.', 'I want to warn future students about the Radiologic Technology program at LaGuardia Community College. The program is NOT accredited by JRCERT (Joint Review Committee on Education in Radiologic Technology), which is the national standard for radiology programs.

This is never clearly explained to students during the admission process. Many only find out by accident from other people, not from the school itself. While the program is institutionally accredited and graduates can still take the ARRT exam in New York, the lack of JRCERT accreditation can limit your job opportunities — especially in hospitals outside of New York State, federal facilities, and some specialized programs.

However, professors are great, I appreciate everything they’ve done for me. Professors are kind, caring and supportive, they want you to know something, not just getting grades. In addition, many students don’t realize that, but LaGuardia Community College has a very, very, very good staff. Administrative staff is very caring about their student, they try to help everyone and make you academic life much easier.

In conclusion, I can definitely recommend this college, but only if you’re 100% sure that they have all of the accreditations you need for your future career.

Good luck!', 'Every single "professor" I had at this college was a left wing radical. When did it become a requirement that college professors have to be left wing radicals. And why don't colleges hire any professors with conservative values. It seems like the educational systems hiring practices are extremely discriminatory towards conservatives.', 'One of your middle aged Bengali security officers needs a lesson on manners. We were there for an event and a Bengali security officer/guard spoke SO rudely to my friend for sitting on a bench! She was clearly feeling unwell and waiting bc I went to the bathroom. I understand if people are supposed to leave after an event but we needed to put on our coats and it was so rainy AND my friend had a hugeee migraine and looked sick! There is no need to try to usher her out w pure rudeness and inconsideration. We were preparing to go! We both regret not calling your supervisor but we remember your face well. Ik you thought you could get away w talking to “unimportant” Bengali woman that way but funny thing is she works for cuny and she could definitely make sure you answer for your behavior. Both of us will be looking for your boss next time we come by so make sure you learn some manners by then. Ik you talked to her like that bc you talk to alll Bengali women w disrespect. Absolutely abhorrent behavior.']

name: CUNY Medgar Evers College
reviews:
['Some professors are really hands on and make the experience great. The administration is trash. The seek program is helpful. If you plan to do nursing, I would say pick another school. I plan to transfer. No one can ever give direct answers and will lead you astray.', 'You can start at medgar and go anywhere. It’s such a stepping stone to its many students most of whom are living in poverty and trying to make a better live for themself, their families and communities I am medgar made!!! That school will always have a special place in my heart ♥️', 'Congratulations for strengthening cultural diversity and including salsa from Cali, Colombia, in this event.', 'Let me tell you—Medgar Evers College is a hidden gem that deserves way more credit than it gets. If you’re looking for a school that actually invests in its students, provides countless opportunities, and fosters a strong community, MEC is where it’s at.

First off, the professors who care, REALLY care. Shoutout to Professor G. McMillan, Professor X. Rose, and Professor A. Okereke; they don’t play about making sure students get the knowledge and put in the work. The coursework? Challenging but rewarding. If you apply yourself, you’ll walk away sharper, more prepared, and ready to take on the world.

Now, let’s talk about campus life, because MEC does not let students just come and go without offering experiences that make college worthwhile. The activities? Endless. Whether you’re into sports, Greek life, leadership programs, or student organizations, there’s a space for you to grow and thrive.

And let’s not forget the trips. I’m talking about all-expenses-paid, knowledge-packed, fun-filled trips, both in and out of state, where you get to learn, connect, and explore in a new setting. And if you’re a foodie? The school is always throwing down with brunches, luncheons, dinners, and breakfasts that give students a chance to network while enjoying a good meal.

The resources are consistently on point, both on and off-campus. Need financial assistance? There are scholarships and programs constantly being offered and awarded. Need motivation? MEC brings in influential Black leaders from high and low places to drop gems in powerful lectures. Need a community that respects and acknowledges your values and beliefs? MEC has that, too.

And when it comes to big events and functions? MEC knows how to plan and execute for the benefit of its students. Whether it’s professional networking, academic enrichment, or just a celebration of culture and achievement, they show up and show out.

Now, no school is perfect so some departments can be a little unorganized and some staff might make things more difficult than they need to be. BUT, there are many who step up, correct mistakes, and do their best to guide students in the right direction. The dedication from those individuals makes a huge difference.

Final verdict? MEC is more than just a school, it’s a whole experience. If you take advantage of everything it has to offer, you’ll walk away with more than just a degree. You’ll walk away with knowledge, connections, experiences, and a stronger version of yourself.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Highly recommend.', 'One of the best colleges ever. They have many programs that will help you succeed. They even have books in the library that you can use to study if you don’t have your course textbooks on hand. Great advisors my advisor when I went to Medgar was Ms. Glenda W……… They make sure students graduate before time and on time.    They offer many things. It was a virtual graduation . Dr. Lashley knows we well . I even won my traveling suitcase from them now I’m throwing it out it has water damage']

name: CUNY New York City College of Technology
reviews:
['This college is horrible, but professors are truly amazing — they care about students, always remind you about tutoring and office hours, and try to help as much as they can. They are the only good part of this place.

The administrative staff is awful — rude, unhelpful, and passive-aggressive. They don’t care about students at all, and communication is a nightmare. It can take up to 3–5 business days to get a reply to a simple email. Almost every student I’ve talked to feels frustrated and disappointed.

The building is old and in terrible condition. Bathrooms are dirty, not available on every floor, many don’t have soap or paper towels, and even the boxes for napkins and tampons are broken and always empty.

And the worst part — the college doesn’t tell students the real waiting times for programs. After finishing prerequisites, you often have to wait another year to even start the program, and no one warns you about it. Many students feel scammed and end up leaving for other colleges.

Professors are great, but everything else is a mess. I would never recommend this college to anyone.', 'The worst transfer office ever. I went and stayed there from 10 am to 6 pm. Nobody is willing to help. I get it most of us get to go to college for free but how can some places can hire employees like that. First they called my ticket number around 4 pm then I went upstairs and these stupid people didn’t even transfer my credit. Being an employee somewhere is a big responsibility doesn’t matter what job or in what position. They should take do their responsibilities nicely', 'I’m extremely disappointed with how administrative issues are handled at City Tech.

On a random morning during this winter break 2026, two of my enrolled classes were canceled without warning. A hold was placed on my account from ASAP/ACE, which prevented me from enrolling in replacement classes.

Attempts to contact offices for help were unsuccessful, and I was told to email an advisor who is no longer active on the hold description. With no clear point of contact and no immediate assistance available, my degree progress is put at risk through no fault of my own.

This lack of communication and accountability creates unnecessary stress for students who are actively trying to plan their education.', 'This is a review for the cafeteria inside citytech. The food is terrible. Empanada is misshapen, look at the display. That's not a crossaint, it's a "empanada".

There are raisins in the beef empanada, I asked if it's supposed to be there, and the worker said yes. The meat smells rotten and I almost threw up from the stink. 0/10 would not recommend their empanada ever. Cheap management padding their beef empanada with raisins so they can increase the calories and lower costs while charging 5$ for a single one.

When I bite into a beef empanada I don't want to see or taste raisins inside.', "DO NOT COME HERE! I am an upper level senior who only needs one more class to graduate. I've been trying to get an ePermit to take the course at another college during the winter semester because the times that City tech offers the course conflicts with my work schedule. However, after weeks of contacting different departments they are all giving me the run around or telling me to wait until December 1st when the ePermit department begins processing again. The problem is that all of the classes are filling up. THE COMMUNICATION AT THIS SCHOOL IS HORRIBLE. STAFF NO HELP."]

reviews:

name: CUNY York College
reviews: ['Lovely campus and easily seen from the street. The school is close to public transportation.  The campus houses a high school and an elementary school.  The grounds can use some work and some more public art installations.  The cemetery is gated but plenty of history ardorns the head stones. The indoor exhibit of The Tuskegee Airmen is worth visiting the campus.  The stundent art galley is the best.  Ask security for accessibility for people with disabilities.  Security at the gate will ask of I. D. He is very pleasant and awesome with directions.  Most staff/faculty are helpful too.  Better to get assistance from the more experienced staff.  They are quite knowledgeable.  The food is pricey for college life, but the chicken Marsalis, peas & rice, Mac & cheese and green beans with show string beans cut carrots was a tasty pleasant delight.  The logistics of the buildings are identified in letter quadrants to help navigate your way through the buildings. For example 1B 106 would be on the 1st floor in the "B" section.  The Art department is quite amazing.', 'Very few people were actually capable of helping me. For the most part I was walking around the school from place to place looking for what I needed. And no one could give me the right answer for the longest time. I even had to get short with some people, because of the runaround. The staff needs retraining badly.', "I spent a semester here before transferring out several years ago as the classes at this school do not have actual equivalencies to other CUNYs or SUNYs. There are good programs in the economics/finance/law departments, but cost wise it's not worth it.", "Professors are ok. Howerver, most of them have Big classes,  less time to answer  questions and emails. Bathrooms are filthy. Elevators are out of order most of time.  The service System does not run as well as other schools, specially financial aid office who misled you to take 12 selfpaid credits and admition office, where they charge you commitment fee in case you don't take class there. Disappointing experiences!!!", 'I’ve always had great experiences here and all offices are very clear and helpful. Classes and professors I have encountered have also been great.']

name: Daemen University
reviews: ['As a senior at Daemen, I can say it’s been a great experience overall. The small class sizes make it easy to connect with professors, and they really care about helping you succeed. The coursework is challenging but rewarding, and there are plenty of hands-on learning opportunities, internships, and career support.\n\nThe campus has a welcoming, close-knit feel, with lots of clubs and activities to get involved in. While some areas could improve, like expanding certain programs or updating facilities, Daemen has definitely prepared me for my future. If you’re looking for a supportive, career-focused school, I’d definitely recommend it!', 'If you’re planning on pursuing a future in writing for social media or marketing, this is the place for you!', 'Attended Daemen College basketball. name: Dominican University New York
reviews:
["I am a photographer and I did a Graduation shoot on The beautiful Campus and id like to share my experience, The Campus is absolutely gorgeous tons of sunlight and much provided shade with all the beautiful trees surrounding the campus. The staff were very helpful & Super welcoming from the moment I arrived till my exit I was restricted at any location which was amazing, If you'd like your grad photos taken by yours truly please feel free to reach out here are some shots from that day", 'Dominican College is about whats on the outside and NOT the inside. Beautiful campus with even more beautiful opportunities, presented at the door. As a student you learn not everything that glitters is gold. The overall well being of the students as far as academics is poor. Students will fail and be left alone to fail because that means they will continue to generate income for the college. Administration only looks for students when there is a bill on their account, never to actually “assist” the situation at hand. I do not speak for the colleges administration  entirely because their are individuals who strive for students’ success as much as the student themselves. I do find some professors at Dominican college to be caring yet unable to help due to the colleges “rules“ and abilities to manipulate the system for financial gain. Information is kept from students to keep them from graduating at a timely manner CONSTANTLY. The professors assigned to advice their students sometimes have no idea how to ADVISE A STUDENT, therefore leaving obvious room for error. This college has mislead me multiple times with no remorse for their “mistakes”. I quote this because it almost seems planned when it resorts back to financials. I went to Dominican College seeking a specific degree and left with something completely different trying to avoid the financial strain the college itself would have caused me. I was prepared for a 4 year college nothing more, nothing less. The education that is given in Dominican College is mediocre and could be learned for a lesser price in community colleges(depending the degree type of course), where you can actually achieve what you set out to achieve. Not just the “next best option”. As a recent graduate of the school I can honestly say, they do not promote graduating at a timely manner being that it is a 4 year college. They promote staying in college as long as there is money to pay for classes to graduate. I also want to end my review by saying before attending this college , several alumni gave me this SAME ADVICE and I chose to attend anyways. I will say I do not regret the experiences and people I met during those years. I do wish I took the advice I was given as far as academics and a school which genuinely cares about their student bodies overall success.', 'Dominican College does in fact challenge the mind and spirit. The programs available at the college are indeed challenging but, rewarding with hard work, effort and determination. They offer a wide range of community oriented services that provides aid in the community and around the world from El Salvador to France. The colleges athletics program is well established and their Athletic Training staff are superb. Dominican College has definitely succeeded with providing students college wide services. For example, career services, onsite counseling, academic success are extraordinary services that the college provides to students. Knowledge, friends, networking and lifelong skills are often fruits that may be obtained from these initiatives. Overall, this college continues to meet the student needs. Proceed with their vision to make the campus community oriented, safe and a great experience for students and families. Especially, with the implementation of the new turf field being constructed and the Hennessy center being renovated. This college is going on the right path.', 'Where to begin... Do NOT fall for the "Actuarial Science" program listed that is advertised - you will take the exact same classes as general math majors, nor do any of the classes prepare you for the actuarial exams.

Staff? Completely hit or miss. I have wonderful relationships with a handful of staff members here, but the rest of them do NOT belong there.

Academics? Prepare for a high school environment where some teachers will deduct your grade for petty reasons such as not bringing a textbook to class, not providing a doctor's note if you are sick, etc. Similar to staff, about half of the teachers are amazing, while the other half simply go through the motions.

Bottom line - There are plenty of other schools with a superior education at a more affordable price.', 'Awesome school, amazing opportunities. Proud mom of a son that attends. Class of 2018. Criminal Justice Major. Small caring school, where everyone know each other and you feel comfortable that your child is safe and learning.']

reviews: ['Wonderful campus! Founded as a college for women in 1855, it is the oldest existing college granting degrees to women that were the equivalent of those given to men. Elmira College became coeducational in all of its programs in 1969. Nice place to wander around, visit the Mark Twain Study, bookshop, fountain. Well-kept grounds. Impressive collection!', "I parked here while my kid got something from one of the buildings.  She's getting a great education", 'Good college and very good campus.', 'Cool architectural designs.  Nice town.', 'Yes the school is small but a great looking campus( yea-to much purple) but it is charming and I loved living on campus. at the school leading me in circles and they couldn't fix my problem so I had two assignments late because they coudnt help me", 'This college has the worst employees. Every time you call them someone is rude and you are re directed to a website to do it yourself. They should just let go of all of the staff since they tell you to do it yourself anyways. Horrible.', 'i did online classes at this school and i thoroughly enjoyed them and all my professors, however, every. single. time. i had to call the bursars office or the registrars office or any office for help it was a terrible experience. everyone i spoke to was so rude and condescending to me and acted like i had no idea what i was talking about. i was dropped from a class on accident by a professor and it took me HOURS and multiple roundabout phone calls to get it fixed. everyone i spoke to asked me if i was “actually doing any work in the class” which i was, but they were just very dismissive of everything and just blamed me. come to find out the professor dropped the wrong list of people and it was never my fault. i have continued to have all of these same issues every time i call. like i said, great classes, but the staff are extremely unhelpful.', 'ECC North Campus is an excellent place for locals to get access to a quality education from a community college. One of the nicest things is the class size and average cost of going there for an associate degree or some other kind of certifications. The smaller class sizes means it\'s far more likely you\'ll be able to get more personal attention from the professor when you need it, having fewer classmates sometimes makes for much fewer distractions, and the professors really do care very much about the students they\'re educating. The average cost for an associate degree in one of the various programs is often considerably less than one of the larger SUNY system colleges like Buff State or UB. I\'m very pleased with my experience going to ECC as what they called a "hybrid student." That basically means I decided which classes I\'d be taking online and which ones I wanted to do in-person because I felt being in an actual classroom with a professor right there to assist me as I go was just a better fit for me. You of course do have the option to go fully in-person or fully online should you find that\'s the best way for you to proceed. If you have any questions about a specific program, I\'d urge you to get in contact with one of the department heads or advisors in that field. They are incredibly helpful people who are very happy to help you make the very best decisions for your educational journey. They even have special advisors on staff to help you decide if transferring to a four-year university, and will guide you through every single step of the way. Like I said earlier, I couldn\'t possibly be happier with my experience going to ECC, and if I ever needed to go through another associate degree program for whatever reason, I\'ll begin my search at ECC.']

name: Fashion Institute of Technology
reviews:

Whether you’re a prospective student or a design enthusiast, FIT is an incredible place to explore!', "I don't go here but this is my dream school. I am almost 17, and a junior in highschool. reviews: ['Great collage for your kids to go to very nice people ,very professional', 'Great school! Professors know you and will take time to help you. Most of them have experience in that field. name: Fordham University
reviews: ['Good tour and in the running for schools for my daughter.  Looking forward to visiting Lincoln campus as well.', 'I had never been on the campus of Fordham University before, and I was pleasantly surprised to discover such a beautiful college right here in the Bronx. It’s so green that you just want to breathe, breathe, and breathe — surrounded by a million trees. They  have tennis courts and so much more. If you ever get a chance to visit this place on a tour, I highly recommend it. A truly wonderful place to visit!', 'Fordham had a big impact on who I’ve become, both professionally and personally. The professors challenged me, the NYC setting pushed me to grow up quickly, and the overall experience felt grounded in something deeper than just academics. Being part of the water polo program was a highlight and will always be one of the best memories of my life. I’m grateful for the friendships, discipline, and perspective I gained there.', 'I toured Fordham last Friday, and was really impressed. Our tour guide Emily was chill and very attentive to the groups needs. A couple experiences that added to my impression: The buildings are mix of old and modern, but all clean light and airy. We were also invited into a seminar style class, and I had the opportunity to ask real students and professors questions of their experience. Many down-to-earth people here, cannot wait to apply!', 'As a U.S. Army veteran, I’ve experienced Fordham University as an exceptional supportive community. The professors are deeply committed to student growth, and the #RamVets Connect team made my transition from military to college life seamless. The Rose Hill campus is warm and inviting, and Fordham truly upholds its Jesuit mission of educating the whole person—mind and body.']

name: Fulton-Montgomery Community College
reviews: ['I attended classes here after graduating high school back in 2013, and I wasn’t the least bit impressed with the college as a whole. The teachers aren’t the most helpful with making sure you understand the material; while others are a bit ill-tempered and oddly acting; to say the least. Sure the tuition is reasonably priced, but it’s a community college; you can’t expect much. The vibe felt a bit off then (of course I can’t speak on behalf current state of the school) in terms of student spirit and I’m sure it is now. I stopped attending classes in 2015 to pursue full time work, and I’m glad I did. The guidance counselors weren’t of much help or cared either. Nowadays, college and academia as a whole aren’t needed to make money and perform at a professional level, unless you plan to specialize in a field that needs it, I.e the Medical field. Long story short, don’t bother with this school. I’m glad I didn’t give it more time and money from me.', 'Place is ok, staff and teachers are very helpful. Pay your tuition bills immediately or expect bursar office letters for the rest of your semesters.', 'Took a programming class here. It was a great class and the staff was fantastic. I enjoyed learning and working with others here.', 'Watched our amazing granddaughter, Charity, graduate.  We are very proud of her.', 'They werevery very nice when I came in to get the Moderna Vaccine...']

name: Genesee Community College
reviews:
['Batavia philharmonic orchestra plays there for the Christmas season.  Wonderful venue!', "98% precent of the employee's who work at Genesee Community College are amazingly wonderful!  My teacher's are great. The Campus Safety Officer's are kind as ever, & the kitchen employee's are nice as ever.
The one part I am not fond of is how expensive the food in the kitchen is. Genesee County is Upstate, NY. It shouldn't be nearly as expensive as it is here for a slice of pizza, etc. Ridiculous.
Other than that it's wonderful here.  😄", "It never too late they say, well I went here in the late 90's and it was a huge waste of time.   The curriculum was so far behind the industry it was a complete joke.  I had one professor for the whole major.  I spent half my day in front of the same teacher and in hindsight the guy was a dope.  The curriculum was based on old out dated practice, the professor could hardy use computers at the time and that was where the industry was surly headed.  The professor, Dennis Shine, failed me for Pictorial Drawing 101 because he didn't like how I did the shadowing on my final project, he was the failure, teaching that course in the first place.  The outdated course was only offered every other semester and was required to get the degree.  I passed everything that had a right or wrong answer and failed the one thing that was subjective.  I felt it was personal, he definitely didn't like me by that point.  I'm 90% sure he kept a book of mine on purpose.  I left it on my desk, last day of class,  front of the classroom, I was one of the last person out of room, I realized I left it a few minutes later, went back for it and old Dennis played dumb didn't see it.   It was a physics book, It was the only course that was worth anything.  I would still have the book had I not left it.
So to sum up, great campus if you don't know any better.  You may be subjected to a single professor for all the required courses.  Your professor may be out of touch.   People who can, do; those who can't, teach.", 'Got my AS in general studies in 1997. Great college to help launch a student towards their major. Great campus and library. I am forever grateful to GCC.', 'Increased tuition costs with enrollment having decreased each year since 2010, they even increased the cost of the cafeteria plan that is forced upon your tuition bill from $560-$590 all while not increasing the amount of meal swipes. Small portion sizes and the food is always out before their hours of 11am-2pm. They continue to increase prices because enrollment is decreasing but can not offer enough food from the hours that students pay for regarding the meal plan.']

name: Hamilton College
reviews: ['I graduated from Hamilton in 1978.  My time there was educational,  inspiring and fun. Classes were generally all interactive rather than lecture-based, which made a huge difference to my interest in, and commitment to, learning. It is an insitution with an amazing history and a curriculum that guides one to critical, rather than rote, thinking or just technical "training". I was sorry to see the fraternity system later abolished for politically correct reasons, but my experience at Sigma Phi earned me lifetime friendships and another avenue for learning.', 'Beautiful campus. Cold, but beautiful.', "Beautiful campus with awesome buildings and if you're lucky enough to go to school there do it", 'Beautiful school.  Great place.', 'We went for a football game. It was pretty easy to find parking and the stadium. Pretty campus and drive to hamilton.']

name: Hartwick College
reviews: ['Hartwick College is a not just a place of learning, but somewhere that prepares you to truly be ready for the world. As a student at Hartwick College I have gotten an education steeped with opportunity to truly envelope myself in my interests. I knew going into college that I wanted to get actionable experience within my field, and I have always been supported by the amazing team here to be able to do soo. Whilst hartwick might not have the monetary support of Harvard, it has the ability to truly know your professors and academic team that rivals any school', 'As an alumna, I knew how important it would be for my son—now a senior—to take advantage of Hartwick’s incredible J Term courses. He’s traveled to Spain, Central Europe, and most recently, Greece, and each experience has truly been life-changing. Hartwick goes above and beyond to make these opportunities possible, offering generous scholarships that open the world to its students. We are so grateful for the transformative learning and global perspective Hartwick has given him.', 'Alumn from back in the day here, I was recently reminded of Hartwick and decided I\'d leave my two cents. Basically they didn\'t help me out at all during my time there (07-11); there are no resources to help students with internships or job hunting, there are very few majors and minors to choose from (don\'t get me started on the "build your major" scam), there\'s really nothing going on at Hartwick or in Oneonta, the students are rude and unfriendly, the faculty and staff are largely apathetic, the tuition is ridiculous, the dorms are cramped, old and unclean and even the food sucks. But, to be fair, the campus looks pretty so I guess that makes up for everything else according to some. My advice is to stay away unless there have been some major improvements since 2011.', 'This was just a visit by my daughter, a Hartwick graduate and her father, to remember a bygone time.', 'Hartwick College - The Life Balance College, reasonable cost and high scholarship for international students 🎉']

name: Hilbert College
reviews: ["Is a great school my daughter she's about to graduate next year", 'Had questions on my daughters account and financial aid. name: Hobart William Smith Colleges
reviews: ['Neo Gothic, Ivy covered halls full of rich ceremonial traditions preserved by an empathetic administration with an impressive network of supportive alumni who continue to value their affiliation and time spent at the prestigious colleges of Hobart & William Smith.  The President is an inspiring and impressive person who has demonstrated her prioritization of fostering academic exploration, independent and critical thinking, diversity of thought, international partnerships with ancient institutions abroad and the management and preservation of the high esteem of the colleges.', 'My oh my was our visit here just fantastic. I came here with a buddy of mine who attended this fine institution many moons ago. He showed us around all the main attractions of this place of higher learning. Movie theater. Library that has books and stuff. Courtyard. Art. Place where some guy named Tommy ruffled some feathers. Big ol party with lots a young fella and misses havin a ball soaking up the last bits of summer and bouncing around a castle. We looked at the math and science buildings but not for long because our pal didn’t really do much of those harder subjects. Real beautiful everywhere we looked so much so I started telling my old lady that we should go back to college, maybe even at this place itself. Thanks for the memories!', 'We live near these great colleges. Pre-pandemic we attended sports, student plays and performances and walked in their field house. The campus is beautiful and essential to the health of Geneva. If our grown children were of college age I would send them here in a heartbeat.', 'We loved our visit with our daughter whom is seriously considering HWS for the Fall of 2021. Campus was especially beautiful this time of year (early Fall). Our tour guide Michael was very well versed and articulate and the admissions crew (Jessica and others) were very knowledgeable and helpful. The town of Geneva is a great college town and being right on Lake Seneca is a huge bonus. Absolutely visit if you are even considering applying.', 'School is amazing. Campus is wide open . Fairly small campus and could do more for the community and students. Should integrate community and service to the community.  Seems like a separate entity from the city it is in. Reminds me of a cheap Fordham university.  They also seemed separated from the bronx.']

name: Hofstra University
reviews: ["I only went to the auditorium so I can't speak about any other buildings. They cleared most of the nearby parking areas of snow. The place has good security and is kept clean.", 'At first, I thought that everything was going to be fine for my first semester. It wasn\'t. Professors are incompetent and aren\'t flexible with office hours for students whether it is in person or virtual. Michael Scott Heiss who was my instructor for WSC-001 insulted me by saying " you\'re not the best writer" as if to say that I\'m terrible at writing and he is not, thinking that he knows it all when he doesn\'t. It brought my self-esteem confidence down and enthusiasm so much that writing was one of my hobbies and I may not want to pursue it after i heard those words. The only good thing that came out of Hofstra was meeting a few good people especially my best friend who I now consider to be a part of my family. Everything here is disorganized all over the place and not structured the way it should be. Facilities are so filthy to the point that you can see black mold festering everywhere along with dust building up which is what has compromised my asthma and chronic bronchitis along with my allergies. Homework assignments and or projects are not spaced out evenly which hasn\'t helped me set enough time to study. The cost of everything is way too much for me to afford which is why I will be furthering my education at CUNY over the next few years. Not only did Hofstra ruin my life completely it has put an enormous amount of stress on my mother as well as myself. It has pretty much destroyed my chances of becoming an educator author and journalist. I was never able to have peace and quiet on campus due to my sensory issues of noise being that I\'m autistic and have adhd. If professors spent less time talking about nonsense and get classes started on time, then everything would be done in a timely fashion. Tutoring is very limited, and it only runs during the week not on the weekends which was problematic. Food is the worst of all especially the buffets which has gotten me ill to the point where I almost had to throw up. You can\'t even have piece while using the bathroom whether that be by someone playing music so loud or two people having a tryst in the shower to the point that you hear loud moaning as a result of it. Trying to sleep at night was terrible knowing how loud everybody was on my floor. People in general are rude obnoxious loud and don\'t have a care in the world if something serious were to happen to you. The entire area surrounding the campus and the campus itself is very dangerous knowing that it is considered a high crime area because it is in Hempstead and Uniondale which is the ghetto and the hood. How can anyone let alone myself be safe over there knowing that someone has to make sure that my safety is in check by escorting me to every building I have to be in for class? Every building is falling apart to the point where it\'s on the brink of collapse and complete structural failure and the elevators inside that help people get to their designated location are failing every second hour and minute of each day. However, you put it Hofstra will continue to get worse and worse as time passes by. SAS would always wait until the last minute to tell me when my time was up for taking exams which made it all the more frustrating. Hofstra will most likely not reach the goals it has set out in its strategic plan for when the centennial comes up in 2035 which is a decade from now. Hofstra is the way how it is because of the incompetence of the all the leaders especially those who are at the senior level including President Poser who is just as bad as the rest of the team is. As I move on to the next chapter to accomplish my goals to being an educator Hofstra will continue to go downhill and be the biggest embarrassment disappointment and joke in the history of higher education and academia that anyone has ever seen. I am proud of my best friend for earning his Bachelor of Science degree in mechanical engineering from HU and looking forward to seeing what the future does hold for him which is what made me proud of him above everything else. Avoid coming to Hofstra at all costs.', 'Excellent campus with a high level of academic rigour. Feels very inviting and has a very tight-knot community. Feels like “family”. I’d definitely recommend this university to parents.', 'Went there for 2024 Long Island FRC regionals, was also there earlier for hackathons. Although the university may seem bad in terms of ranking, all the facilities and faculties are very nice.', 'Hofstra University was a deeply disappointing experience—while the campus is beautiful and Public Safety is outstanding, almost everything else fell short. Accessibility services were disorganized and unhelpful, accommodations weren’t enforced, and the campus itself is not disability-friendly. Jewish life is practically nonexistent, the kosher food options were severely lacking (especially during COVID), and the Hillel community was cliquey and unsupportive. I was bullied, ignored by Title IX when I reported it, and shuffled between counselors, including one who was unprofessional and dismissive. Everything on campus is overpriced, and the support systems don’t justify the high cost. Unless you can hand-pick your professors and fend for yourself in every area, this school is absolutely not worth it—look elsewhere for a better, more supportive college experience.']

name: Houghton University
reviews:
['Transferred after spending 2 years here. Wouldn’t recommend it.

Here’s my breakdown:

45% of people are not truly Christians and are there just for the decent price or sports programs
45% of people consider themselves devout Christians but are judgmental terrible people
5% of students and faculty are truly great people and inspirational Christians

Unfortunately the 5% doesn’t make up for the terrible food, few course offerings, outdated and small dorms, and overall draining atmosphere. Most of my peers agreed that Houghton is steadily going downhill.

The administration is terrible too. Horribly strict rules that will suffocate you.', 'Wasted a year here. Such a backwards place in the middle of nowhere. So close minded and controlling. Such a traumatic place for LGBTQ people, whom many of my classmates were. Not a safe place for young adults to explore who they are. Poor student life activities. Music program was also very very limited and no musical theater or jazz programs. No dancing allowed and no visiting with friends of the opposite sex in dorms.', "We stayed at Houghton for a week of camp with our church's Student Ministry.  The staff was incredible there right down to the dorm cleaning staff, who would take the time to stop and have a meaningful conversation with you.  Some of the food was incredible. The campus is beautiful, and just the right size. Both of my kids have talked about going there when they graduate.", "Graduated in 2003, loved everything about Houghton. Please consider graduates' reviews of this school, most of the negative reviews are from people who did not attend. I don't know current enrollment stats, but it would be a good idea to call the office with questions before writing this off. I do agree that the town isn't much to behold, but this is NOT the place to go if you want a bustling metropolis nearby. It's a beautiful area, has a supportive faculty and cohesive student body, and you will love it if it is right for you.", "Houghton is such a great college! I'm thinking about going there in the fall. Not only is the campus beautiful but the professors and admission counselors are very helpful and care about you. At this college you will not only be able to further in your career, but with your walk with Christ. I would recommend anyone to go to Houghton or at least, take a tour and visit."]

name: Hudson Valley Community College
reviews: ["Having been none too moved by the class based education (however limited,) I'd received from a competitor some years back, I dare not compare this more popular rival. I lack the experience of its facility's offering.\nSo why am I reviewing this? Simply because, I was parked outside.\n*Building looks reasonably clean and inviting.", 'Do not attend this school they are scam artist, I attended this school for one semester simply because I was being charged so much money with no explanation of why. I was given a book by advising that listed all the prices of the school, when I called the bursar office the women was saying a completely different price then what was listed in the book I was given. When I would try to talk about the fees she would get on the phone talk real fast cut you off every second and still give no legitimate explanation as to why you where being charged all this money, just would keep on repeating that I lived out of county or talk about a bill that you where not inquiring about. Also the professors try to fail you with again no legitimate reason, out of the one semester I took both the professors I had where terrible. I had to cc the department to have my grade corrected, I was accused of using ai, and had to drop one of my courses from receiving an unjustified 0 on an assignment.', "First, I would like you to consider the type of people you hire and take their values into account. This happened around 9:45 a.m in JSQ location.I was waiting my turn to have my car parked, and they asked me for my ID, which is fine, I showed it to them, and they asked me to leave. And the reason? The reason was that I didn't have a sticker! They asked me for my ID but not for a sticker! The man didn't even dare to say, “Show me your schedule,” or even comment, “We'll keep your car until you come back with the sticker.” They didn't say anything to me at all, and they didn't say anything to my face. All I said was that I was late for class. The worst part? The worst part was having to leave that parking lot ALONE! The street is very narrow, and backing out of that parking lot is difficult. I didn't even receive instructions or help to get out of there! I hit my car, and what did they do or say to me? NOTHING! I left there totally angry, crying because at some point, maybe it was my fault, but no one deserves to be treated the way they treated me.As I said, maybe it's my fault for not having a sticker! But you know how hard it is to find parking outside! How was I supposed to move my car, find parking, and come back? It was impossible since I had already looked for parking. And as I said at the beginning, what angers me the most are the VALUES, the way those people who worked this morning treated me. It would have cost them nothing to wait for me to come back for the sticker and leave my car there for 10 minutes, it would have cost them nothing to give me instructions on how to leave the parking lot, they did absolutely nothing! I am an immigrant student who, unfortunately, has been paying for college for over a year, and situations like this simply make me want to leave. I emphasize values because I work in customer service. I have never treated people this way, and I never will, even if I have a thousand people on line. ALWAYS TREAT PEOPLE WELL!  And I don't want to think that just because I'm Latina, they treated me that way.", "I decided to apply here after highschool. I came here in person for orientation day after taking a bus AND a train. Only to meet a staff member who eventually told me it was better if I went to my own town's community college.(My town doesn't even have a community college). I was so excited and looking forward to attending only to feel unwanted. My mental health was already a bit low and this helped it get worse. It took me a bit more than a year, to finally feel better and decide to continue education. I don't regret not attending this place and am currently checking out another school.", "This location has some of the rudest staff and faculty I’ve ever encountered. From the security guards, to a few (not all) of the lunch staff. Many have poor attitudes, especially if you have questions or need assistance. They  make you feel like a burden simply for asking. While most of the professors and classes are great, the school needs to improve how they hire and manage their faculty. it took months for a complaint I filed to be addressed, after I had to reach out to everyone in HR just to get my case heard and be dismissed in the end. It's clear that the Journal Square campus doesn’t prioritize or care much for their students. If you want to be treated with respect, I’d recommend the North Hudson campus instead."]

name: Iona University
reviews: ["Great university, strong spirit and love the small footprint.  I got a great education here and job opportunities through this school many years ago. Would be 5 stars if pricing didn't get as high as it has. Something needs to be done about the escalation of university costs for sure.", 'I guess not really a bad school and the area is cool.
