We greatly appreciated the day and the campus is a nice small homey campus with everything you need around in a Short distance.  Felt safe and great worth. Only non-Ivy in the north east that has a rowing team (walk on!) how neat is that. Consider this beautiful college when searching for a place for your young adult to call home for a few years.', 'When i came here; I saw Iona, but when she saw me she ran away.\nNever coming back, you embarrassed me.', 'Very nice institution lovely campus']

name: Island Drafting and Technical Institute
reviews: ["I just learned the school is closing. I attended the school in 1988 for Mechanical Drafting...at the time it was for traditional drafting...yes, on the slanted tables using paper, pencils, T-squares and triangles. It was one of the best places to go for drafting and was well known among the industries that employed their graduates (Grumman, Raytheon and many other defense contractors). Keep in mind, in the 80's getting a job with those employers was like hitting the lottery. At the time, the school was just beginning to roll out CAD traing programs and acknowledged the future of drafting will be CAD - but the current environment in the industry was still very much traditional hand-drafting. I did get a drafting job but due to that type of drafting being phased-out, I ended up working as an electrician and then designing low voltage, network and data systems for the same electrical firm. I came full circle and as part of my design job offered to go back to Island Drafting at night to learn AutoCAD, which my employer thought was a good idea and paid for. While I was never employed solely for CAD work, my design jobs had me using it often and to this day 37 years later I use AutoCAD regularly. Sad to see it close. The school was very good and I remember Mr. DiLiberto always being a visible presence at the school. The staff were all industry veterans and the classes were small and personal. I suppose the school's closing is more due to it being a family business because CAD work is still in demand.", "Sorry to hear This tech college closed. I graduated in 2004 with an AOS which served me very well into retirement. Its like everything else. You get out what you put in. You show interest and want to learn, They went out of their way to help you. It was a Great experience and I'm better for it. I would seek out 5towns for the follow up on this area of education. Thank you Joe", "Fun so far. People seem genuine and interested in you. Connections you make with your peers are meaningful. I will update my review as I progress through the school and beyond. So far I'm excited and it feels rewarding.", 'Great place did alot for me in life. Front desk  guy will go to bat for you allday everyday', 'This school is nothing but a scam and should be shut down immediately.']

name: Ithaca College
reviews:
['I was impressed by the staff when we visited, they were very welcoming and eager to help, we even got to meet with a department chair with a phone call when we realized we had signed up for wrong tour. Of course the beauty of the school is impressive as well.', 'Freshman move in day!! The staff and students were so wonderful and helpful! Made the entire experience go smoothly and alleviated all our worries.', '1. Education wise I feel that my student made good choices when possible when talking to instructors and fellow students who had advise on which instructors are worthwhile.
2. Cost: as others have written, the cost keeps increasing and now is getting to be at the same level of a University.
3. Meal Plans: "Spendy" with questionable value.  As time and experience moved on, we moved to more basic option, when it offered a quick solution without having to travel off campus.
4. Housing is dated, and in some cases not well ventilated.
5. FEES: This place is like a HOA which will fee you to death.  Besides having to pay for parking, even if you help peers move and leave the car for 5 mins, a ticket, from what I have heard from others the campus police seem to focus more on ticketing then anything else.
6: FEES: Part 2.0. Late fees, even a min late to a day late, there is ZERO flexibility, now they will not even consider a post mark.  Funny the IRS will even give you that bit.
7.Finance office is useless:  On many occasions myself, student, or former wife will call or email, and seldom get any response.
8. Overall my student is happy with most things, but keep in mind my and other reviews when considering this choice.  Spend your money wisely...', 'At its best Ithaca College is serviceable and at worst Ithaca College needs to seriously rethink its strategy to attract prospective students.

1) The dorms are outdated and often lack any ventilation in the rooms leading to the room to either being freezing cold or sweltering hot. The heaters in the rooms randomly decide when they want to work and electrical outlets are in places no one can normally reach. The bathrooms also need work as do the students that use them.

2) The dining halls lack real variety and are mostly closed on weekends meaning good luck finding food like all the other 4,900 odd students. Even with recent changes, it feels like a bandaid to the problem rather than a step towards a solution.

3) The instruction and instructors can be a hit and miss with some who are too good at their job and others make you wonder why they even got the job. Some courses have no reason being optional while others will make you question whether a gap year looks cool. If you are doing business, film, journalism, photography, theater, or performance arts. this is your school. If you are doing anything else, it can be a hit and miss.

4) The rising cost of Ithaca College ( as with most institutions right now) makes community college and state universities look more and more favorable. If there is no quality of life improvements, there is no need to have a net cost slowly creeping up on Cornell’s net cost.

The school is plagued by a history of questionable choices, over-expansion, and poor management. I can only hope the best for those who have to work here and don’t have a choice.', 'We enjoyed our time at Ithaca College during their Fall Open House. The campus is beautiful, the people are amazing and welcoming, and the music facilities are incredible. The landscape was gorgeous on our long drive to the college. Would be great for someone who likes a remote location.']

name: Jamestown Community College
reviews: ["I hope all international students who read this review will not apply to this garbage school, or you will regret it, just like I did not heed the warnings of many people online. My friend and I applied to this school two years ago, and after being rejected for visas, we requested a refund of our dormitory deposit. The school initially replied that they didn't know, then denied and refused to refund it. After two and a half years of negotiations, the school still hasn't fulfilled its obligations. We asked many teachers at American community colleges and students who were rejected for visas, and none of them had encountered this situation. Moreover, many school officials believe that Jamestown Community College's actions are both unreasonable and foolish.\n\nFurthermore, their response was that our dormitory deposit was one day late. If you can accept a one-day delay, why can't you refund it? The school principal even personally wrote back, rudely warning me to shut up. I want to make this public so that everyone will not apply to this school. I've seen many negative reviews mentioning refunds, and I believe this isn't the first or second time they've done this. People should act with a conscience; aren't you afraid of retribution?", "This school has a serious problem with the lack of knowledge in the financial aid office. Not only that if I have a question about financial aid, I get bounced between financial aid office, Student success navigators, and registrar's office. None of which can answer any questions and have no knowledge about what they doing. Even just transferring coursework in from a different college and petitioning to have it counted as a course equivalent is a chore. I've done that got it approved by a dean/chair of that particular dept, then when I forward that approval to the registrar, I get a new story on why it can't be accepted. The instructors / professors are great but the administration at this school lacks knowledge, and they really sound like a bunch of work study kids who don't know how to do their job. I was warned of this. Do your own research. If you're military applying for Veterans tuition award, or gi bill benefits go elsewhere. This college has no idea how to handle them. If you are a TAP student have a semester in cash saved up, as again they don't know how to use them. They also have no clear drop/add dates listed anywhere.", 'As an International student I attended JCC from 2022-2024 and it truely was my home away from home. I have since graduated from JCC and moved between some other universities and have not experienced anything even close to how wonderful my time at JCC was. The support from professors and the International Student Services was top tier. The dining hall food was always fantastic, and there was always something for my taste even when I didnt want what was being served (im not big on fish). I never went hungry and always felt welcomed. I often miss my time and friends at JCC and hope to visit one day again in the future.', "If you haven't seen a play at JCC I recommend that you do. A fantastic theater dept at a small local college.", '. Great school overall I rather enjoyed my three years there. the only problem I had there was constant issues with the financial aid office. it was a pain trying to concentrate on my studies when I was always putting out fires at the financial aid office to ensure that my tuition and everything was paid. most of the professors were good but I did have what you would call a few professors from hell the issues with the financial aid office combined with the professors from hell is why I give this school only 3 out of 5 stars']

name: Jefferson Community College
reviews: ["Me, a 13 year old, went to the college for a tour not expecting to be able to due to covid, but a nice guy named Collin gave me about a 20 minute tour of the jules center and from the looks of it the college is very nice, I can't say for sure though because I don't go here. From the looks of it, 5 stars, but just in case I'll give it 4. Images uploaded are by me under CC0.", 'How long do students need to suffer under instructors who do literally the bare minimum possible? What are we even paying for? I can buy a textbook and read it. I don\'t need to pay this school 600 to do it. We are paying to be TAUGHT. How many bad class reviews need to be received before these in-it-for-the-check professors are let go? L.Cov is terrible for students every single semester. And yet... still "teaching." I had him, and he was non-existent, not even a single message, contradicting due dates, syllabus full of errors, and everything in the classes made from a third party website like Cengage. And every semester, I hear other students having the same problem.\n\nDo better Jefferson Community College.', 'Clean facility, free parking, and sheltered bus stop.', "They are very helpful. I'm finally in my email.", "After this summer semester I had taken a BUS Law course with L. Covell. This is by far the worst class I gave taken. He doesn't respond to emails, you ask a question trying to figure something out and you are left clueless wondering about what to do or where to go with no direction. I feel as if this Professor is checked out and is only there to collect a paycheck without assisting the students. Someone needs to look into this as it will more than likely become a Continued issue. I will be willing to edit and change my review once someone reaches out to address the issue."]

reviews: ['That job don’t pay at all I’m security officer it pay 18 an hour and it right next to Columbia University there guards get more money than us I don’t recommend anyone to come to apply for this job very unprofessional I will never ever come to this school ever again work you like a slave', 'Gorgeous building, amazing learning opportunities']

name: The Juilliard School
reviews:
['I’m just gonna make it clear-
I have not stepped foot in or near this building.
But I already know it’s amazing.

Hi, I’m Parmida Alizadeh and I am a 13yr old overachieving girl with a dream. A dream to pursue my dreams of being an actor against my family’s wishes of it because it’s “not a stable career” 🙄

My research shows (yes, I’ve done countless research about the best performing arts schools in the world what can I say, I’m a nerd 🤓), and this one is BY FAR superior to everything else. Even though I live in Sydney, I really hope I make it here. Because even though I’ve gone behind my parents back and scheduled interviews with many talent agencies such as Munchkins Talent and Starfish and Bubblegum Acting, (I got into Munchkins on the spot after the director interviewed me, and I got into Starfish) it’s still “not a stable career” and I should use my talent for science to become a doctor.

…Asian parents am I right 😔 I know y’all can relate.

So, I guess I just wanna put this review out there for future me.

Future me, if by all these obstacles and challenges you still make it Juilliard, pursue your dreams.

For everyone out there, all the kids my age (yes I’ve read all the reviews on this school), all the people out there with a dream, never stop because other people tell you no. Never stop because you doubt yourself.

Because you can do it.
Because you are amazing.

I hope I inspired some of you, to hopefully follow your dreams.

Hopefully, I’ll maybe post another review on this place when I apply here.

Don’t let ANYONE tell you what is best for you. Follow your dreams, and your gut, and the universe will work everything out.

Thanks for reading this review (can it even be called a review lol) to the end.

I hope I inspired some of you.

- Parmida Alizadeh ⭐️💖🫰🏻🎉', 'All sorts of concerts from talented students, including Juilliard Station, a glass recital box right on Broadway at 66th, where you can see the concert, while in turn being watched by people headed toward the #1.
Arrive a bit early to check in.', 'Amazing experience. It is a beautiful place. You can enter into some areas or halls of the school with pictures of great artists and dancers. The area in front of it is amazing, with seats where you can admire the view, rest and have great time with your friends, as nice pictures. It is worth visiting it if you like dance and know a little about the school. It is well-know and many times appears in hollywood movies. It is New York so I think it is best to get there by metro (subway), if you are by car, you have to find a park-in-lot and pay for it. Well located too, close to many other touristics sites, stations and restaurants.', 'I attended Juiliard Pre-College division from 1956-1968 and enjoy all of Juiliard Student Concerts now. Wonderful concerts to attend there.', 'Always amazing and awe inspiring not to mention these wonderful students!']

Go Wolves 🐺!', "My niece goes there and the dorms have not been cleaned before the student moves in. The room was filthy. Cobwebs, walls and the floors are filthy. Paint peeled off the walls. My daughter said it's a beautiful area and college, her only grip was it was a rather long ride, more so that she spent the whole ride back home on her phone, with no wifi and in silence, Her best friends family speaks primarily Spanish..lol but all and all my daughter is hoping to have her license in a couple months to make the drive herself (I will be definitely going with her,  hahaha).", 'Visited my sister here. Beautiful area with lots to do in the local towns. I brought my drone with me']

name: LIM College
reviews: ['The Financial lady name Sharon is one of the most rudest, evilest people I have ever encountered. When you call them it’s for help and she is everything but help. She’s extremely insensitive and talks to you like she hates her job or you don’t know what you’re talking about. I was extremely nice when I got on the phone and she was pure evil. My tuition was nearly 20,000 and I explained to her my situation, I was actually calling to be transferred to someone that was helping me figure things out but she decided to add hate before doing that. She told me “Well none of the stuff you sent over matters, you’re still going to have to pay that” What college student has 20,000 hanging around for fun? And what kinda of human let alone one older than college students talks to college students like the bottom of the barrel. It’s unbelievable LIM College allows people like that work there and not doing anything. I called for help and guidance and all i got was shame and hatred.\n\nOn top of that, as I got accepted I kept getting new advisors at least 3 realistically because THEY KEPT QUITTING. Literally was sending me emails that it was their last day and good luck. So my experience was absolutely ridiculous, I decided to not go. If school was that stressful via phone imagine how unprofessional they are in person.', 'I regret going to this school so much and I wouldn’t recommend it at all. Their financial offices alone are a complete headache to deal with and I had ran into countless issues and mistakes with them. The cost of the schooling overall is extremely overpriced for the curriculum they provide. Most of the classes are a complete waste of time and aren’t conducive to the degrees at all. And you’re required to complete like 3-4 internships just to graduate which is absolutely absurd. Please do yourself a service and don’t ever go here. It’s not worth the time and money at all.', 'Good luck getting in contact with anyone at this school if you have an issue. Emails go unanswered, the staff is unprofessional and rude, and you can’t get in touch with anyone. I honestly wish there was someone above the people who work here that I could contact, because it’s impossible to get help from anyone. Because of this, I have transferred, and I would not recommend this school.', 'Literally everyone in this school has the NASTIEST attitudes! Especially student financial services! They are so dismissive, condescending, and just nasty! I’m so happy I made the decision to leave! For the younger generation that might read this review, please go to a RESPECTED university and take up Marketing or business and I promise you you will get that same kind of jobs for a much more affordable education with counselors that care and guide u through! LIM is not even respected in the fashion industry, good jobs would rather see university experience. I got that straight from networking ON MY OWN within the fashion space and rubbing shoulders with CEOs. It’s what ultimately helped me make my decision to go to an in state university. I no longer have to deal with the nasty attitudes of LIM employees!', 'I do not recommend this school. It’s a waste of money and if you are out of state it’s an even bigger waste of money. All you get are loans and barely any funding. Also, you need 2-3 internships which are required and there’s not much help given to help you achieve those. I never heard of a school forcing students to take that many internships. Usually it is one internship and if you are working you can get credit from your job. Not here they will keep you from graduating if it means they can get that $6,000 from you. Another thing which really made me regret coming here is how inconsiderate some of the staff can be. I recently lost a parent and was told to contact the assistant Dean to get an extension on coursework. This individual called me at 6pm and started asking me personal questions. Then proceeds to ask me why I needed off from school if I wasn’t burying my parent that week. That was when I realized this school wasn’t my dream. I shouldn’t have went to a for profit school when I had amazing schools in my area where I would have had everything paid for.']

name: Le Moyne College
reviews:
['This university is fantastic.
Callum Matthew Is perhaps the best tennis player on the planet.
Earl makes the best bacon and cheese omelettes in the state.
FINS UP
EEE-EEE-EEE-EEE-EEE', 'Really enjoyed my visit for family weekend. So happy my kid chose this school for sooo many reasons.', 'The campus is so beautiful in the winter.', 'Cozy and lovely college*

*Non-student review', "Almost unilaterally, professors truly care for you and your future. Most staff do what they can to help, too. The Madden School of Business is ranked highly for a reason. Note: Le Moyne seems to be handling the pandemic crisis fairly well. I don't think I would be able to come up with a better way. One challenge, though, is the WiFi and cell reception in their library. In order to attend classes virtually, getting on Zoom can be difficult with unreliable/no connection to the outside world."]

name: Long Island University
reviews:
['Even though this isn’t a review for LIU as a whole, I still wanted to leave feedback for Gourmet Dining. LIU’s Gourmet Dining has been recently good, but one cook who really stands out is Amy, I noticed her name on her nametag while she was on break. On the days she’s cooking, the food is fresher, better seasoned, and clearly made with care. On the days she’s not there, it’s obvious from the food that she isn’t in; the meals feel more mediocre. The dining area is clean and organized, but Amy’s skill truly elevates the overall experience. If she sees this review, thank you for the great food, my friends and I always look forward to eating when you’re cooking!', 'If you’re considering enrolling here  don’t. This is not a school built for learning; it’s built for chaos, burnout, and frustration. The administration has no regard for student time or wellbeing. Exams, quizzes, and workshops are announced with little to no notice sometimes less than 24 hours and then scheduled outside of class time, forcing students to miss work and personal commitments. When you raise concerns, the response is essentially “too bad.”

The teaching quality is abysmal. Lectures are disorganized, instructors read directly off slides, and when an exam is open-note, it doesn’t even help because the material is taught so poorly that you still have no clue what’s going on. The program creates an environment where survival replaces actual learning. And then they wonder why their pharmacy licensing exam pass rate is 60%!

There’s also a rampant cheating problem that the administration refuses to address. Instead of investigating or improving exam integrity, they make tests harder and pile on even more assignments  punishing the honest students while rewarding those who cheat. It’s demoralizing and unfair.

And the tuition? Around $50,000 a year for what? Outdated facilities, overworked professors, and a cafeteria that charges a dollar for a plastic fork. Every part of this place screams exploitation rather than education.

If you care about your mental health, your time, and actually learning your profession  look elsewhere. This school does not care about its students; it cares about appearances and tuition checks.', "Long Island University's Brooklyn campus, situated at 1 University Plaza, serves as a significant private institution offering a variety of undergraduate and graduate programs within a dynamic urban setting. The university is primarily known for its commitment to career-focused education and its role in providing accessible education options within the New York City metro area. The most frequently highlighted positive aspect of LIU Brooklyn is its exceptional location, which provides students with direct access to numerous internship and career opportunities throughout the bustling borough. Overall, LIU Brooklyn maintains a stable presence in the regional higher education landscape.", "Damn great venue. First time here. Robert Plant in concert. What a great place first tier service and amenities. Parking was easy I used spot hero. 25 dollars. Then don't forget to tip.", 'LIU promised you would succeed and get a job within one year of graduation. That was a lie, I reached out to the school for assistance, and they responded with check indeed. I didn’t pay four years of tuition for them to tell me that, you don’t need a college degree to know how to do that']

name: Mandl School-The College of Allied Health
reviews:
['BEWARE! Money hungry organization. They don’t care about admissions, what credits you took or if you even qualify. They only ask about money and how you can pay. My first meeting with them they wanted me to pay that same day. They tell you spots are limited and rush you so you can pay them. And now they call me every day asking if I’m ready to make a deposit for this school. Absolutely not! For the price of $20,000 you would think everything is included but it’s not. You still have to pay for uniforms, textbooks, state exams and your cpr cert. Total waste of time and horrible institution.', 'As a graduate from the Surgical Technologist Program, I can say without a doubt Professor Hicks was phenomenal in preparing her students for the professional field. From vocabulary, instrumentation, sterility, and even real life operating room simulations she was absolutely spectacular. I have only great things to say and nothing but gratitude towards her ability to teach while showing compassion for the learning students.', 'To :Director of Student Services & Operations
Dear Jhonatan Aybar,
Thank you so much for your effortlessness to always help us students to succeed in this
journey!
Indaia M.', 'As an HR consulting firm dedicated to professional excellence and equity in education, Lean On Me HR Solutions is deeply concerned by the alarming conditions reported at Mandl School.

A valued client and aspiring clinician has expressed ongoing frustrations with the lack of instructional quality—including repeated open-book quizzes due to what appears to be insufficient teaching efforts. When students are forced to self-teach in a hands-on healthcare curriculum, that’s not education — that’s exploitation.

Moreover, reports of poor facility upkeep and rodent presence in an institution meant to prepare future healthcare workers are not just unacceptable — they’re unsanitary and unsafe.

If Mandl expects students to become respected professionals, they must first respect their students by providing clean, functional learning environments and educators who actually educate.

We urge Mandl to step up — your students deserve better!

— Brenden Johnson, Founder & CEO
Lean On Me HR Solutions LLC', "In 2016, I wasn't sure exactly how I can make a difference in my community while having a great career in helping people. I was on the bus one day & saw an advertisement for Mandl School for Allied Health. It offered a variety of assistance training in healthcare. I had to start somewhere so why not here. I was nervous when I started, but Dr. Seginy was the first professor I met & wound up being all the support I needed to continue my education as a medical assistant. He tutored in between classes & after school every week. Dr. Seginy even counseled students through hard times. He even helps students make up exams convenient to their work schedules, so no student was left behind. I've thrived on my scholastic duties because of the dedication of this Dr. Seginy at Mandl. I graduated Mandl in 2018 & deeply thanked him in my graduation speech. Today, I am studying to become an RN & he still keeps track of all my progress to date. He is a wonderful teacher & I am thankful to have him by my side for life! If you don't give up on yourself, Dr. Seginy will not give up on you."]

name: Manhattan University
reviews:
['I graduated from here in 2013. They have more new stuff now, including a student commons building (that was under construction during my time there).

The reason I picked Manhattan is two-fold—I had family who attended and loved it, and I liked how friendly and helpful the students were the rainy day I came to tour the campus. The campus itself is lovely—not too big, not too small. The old buildings have “character,” and they give you that Ivy League feel without having to visit Boston.

Most of my professors were caring and passionate, and I liked the small class sizes. The core curriculum was not my favorite—I had to take three science classes even though I majored in Communication. I minored in English so I also took a few classes which happened to have some pretty salacious material on the syllabus. Something I learned—the “Catholic school” label only applies in that some of the Lasallian brothers teach here and there is mass every Sunday.

The college is mostly known for its engineering program and 5-year teaching program, so it’s great if you want to study engineering or education. If you want to go into another field, particularly in the arts…there are probably more robust programs at other schools. But that may have changed since my time here. The Communication department was just starting to get off the ground.

There were plenty of social events during my years here, and I’m sure that hasn’t changed. I acquired several free T-shirts. Lots of extra-curricular opportunities as well, and there is something for everyone. I joined the WRCM radio club, wrote a bit for The Quadrangle, and I was on the staff for Manhattan Magazine.

As a commuter, the FOMO was real, but I do recall the food on campus was subpar. They switched from Sodexo to Gourmet Dining when I was there, which was a step in the right direction. I’m not sure who the caterer is now. (Manhattan College, if you’re reading this: you should find some students who are excellent cooks and offer them work study jobs!)

Overall, college is what you make of it. If you want to go to a school that has a nice campus, decent proximity to the city (the 1 train is right there), and a sense of being known as opposed to “being a number,” check out Manhattan College.', "As a student at Manhattan College, one of my favorite aspects of this college and how tightly knit of a community it is. Everywhere you go, you see a friendly face. The staff and workers are all around great people who love the students and strive to make personal connections with them. The campus is so pretty- something that a lot of NYC school don't have. There are so many ways to be who you are and express yourself at this school through clubs and sports and overall is a great academic institution.", "Recently visited my family and my niece was telling me about her time here, and how gender studies class here is 'hating on men and it's all full of women, and it's just really cool'...

Like we just allow bigotry in New York now huh?", 'Manhattan College is a private, Roman Catholic, liberal arts university located 4513 Manhattan College Parkway and Waldo Avenue, Bronx, NY 10471. They offer excellent educational programs, have a beautiful NYC campus and unparalleled career opportunities. They ranked #16 out of 181 Regional Universities North', 'Beautiful campus, hilly and lots of stairs, nice fitness center, and highly ranked in multi categories for academics. School is also a D1 university in sports.']

reviews: ['I don\'t know where to start. As a freshman in the nursing program completing my first semester I wish I knew the benefits of enrollment sooner. They just want your money, they’ll require you to retake gen ed courses even if you already have a degree that don’t even relate to the program. Nobody knows what they’re taking about so get everything in writing! If they don’t have an answer they result to ignoring you or giving you snarky remarks. Admissions sucks school sucks R U N they’re so many better opportunities that actually have your best interest at heart', '12 years ago, I applied to the nursing program at this school and was rejected because of one low grade in an anatomy and physiology class (which I was taking at this school) because I had a terrible professor and like other more recent reviews have noted, no support from administrative staff when I tried to get help and report the professor for not actually teaching. I had A\'s in all my other pre-requisites. 12 years later, I graduated with a bachelor\'s degree and two master\'s degrees with a 3.98 overall GPA from an esteemed university in the south. Yet this school felt I wasn\'t "good enough" for their ADN program. Here\'s my "Pretty Woman" moment. You work off tuition, don\'t you?', 'Great place to get a degree in the nursing or healthcare field.', 'This school did not prepare me at all for what I have encountered in the real world providing occupational therapy. They just wasted my time with arts and crafts and not teaching me how to transfer patients and stroke recovery and PNF patterns and ESTIM and ugh. name: Marymount Manhattan College
reviews:
["RUN.
This is a school for rich white people, and even then only a certain type of rich white people. You will be paying ridiculous amounts of money for an experience worse than being in high school. If you are not in a theater or adjacent major your education will not be worth a damn and you will be completely ostracized by other students. If you are queer, disabled, neurodivertent, POC, alternative, etc. there is unfortunately no place for you here. The social environment is just horrible, the dorms and campus are filthy and nothing works, there are NO resources for students who need off campus housing, and many of the professors shouldn't even be employed here. My single year here was a complete waste of time and money. Do not repeat my mistakes I'm begging you.", 'This is a fantastic school for anyone with passion in the arts. Welcoming, fun, beautiful, fantastic professors. Transferred here from hunter, best decision of my life thus far. So grateful to attend such a university. Small classes so you get the education you deserve.', 'PLEASE READ IF YOU ARE APPLYING TO THIS SCHOOL

I attended the biology program as a transfer student and it was the worst mistake of my life. Marymount Manhattan puts up this facade that their small class size sets them apart from any other college in the city. Let me be clear: this school has more downfalls than advantages. This school requires their students to take general education courses as a freshman and then again at junior and senior levels. I was a biology major taking dance, film and painting during my junior year. Just another ploy to make more money.

I was told by an advisor that I would have to graduate a year late to take one single class in spring semester that was only offered every other year. If a class is mandatory for graduation, it should be offered every year. The shortage of staff to teach classes sets an automatic disadvantage for students. How can they expect a student to return to one of the most expensive cities in the world to take one single class?

The adjunct faculty is laughable. I took a painting class and had to buy everything out of pocket. I do not come from money as most students at this school and was told by my professor that my brushes were "too cheap". The courses from this college are impossible to transfer as they are considered a joke at even community colleges.

As a freshman my friend failed her first biology exam. Normal, not everyone is able to adjust to a college style exam right away. She immediately went to see her professor about improving her grade and she was told to change her major and her aspirations to go into medicine over her first ever college exam. Is that pushing your students to be successful?

Maybe the BFA programs are better, but I have only heard negative aspects about them as well. The majority of my anatomy class was failing and nothing was done by the staff to improve lessons regardless of the countless complaints by students.

The graduation rate is laughable. The advisor and bursar offices are laughable. They are quick to take your money for a transcript but never send it out. There is so much more to say about this college but it cannot be done in a single review.

Please do your due diligence before committing to this school. Countless people can tell you the many other options in the city you can choose from.', 'Great school! The location is fantastic and the teachers really do care about helping students succeed. The staff are all very kind and everyday will greet you with a smile when you walk in the doors.', 'Marymount Manhattan College is an amazing college that pushes students to be the best. The faculty at this school is fantastic and are experts in their field. From the moment you walk into Marymount Manhattan College, you automatically feel at home and like you belong there. My time at this school thus far has been wonderful and I would not trade my experiences here for anything in the world. I highly recommend this school to all.']

name: Mercy University
reviews:
["I wouldn't recommend this school to anyone; the staff are very unprofessional.  First, they told me over the phone that I could learn English from scratch, but then they put me in a class with people who had already been studying for six months and already knew the language. When I approached them and asked to be placed in a class for beginners, they refused and simply said that if I wasn't satisfied, I could leave.  And on top of that, you have to pay almost $1,000 every month for this, even though they don't teach you anything from the very beginning.", 'Mercy University’s Manhattan Campus on West 34th Street is consistently highlighted in my professional circles as a transformative urban academic hub that masterfully bridges the gap between high-level theory and the pragmatic demands of the New York job market. Through numerous conversations with graduates and current students, it is evident that the institution provides a substantive, career-focused environment where the faculty’s real-world expertise is frequently cited as a primary driver of student success and upward mobility. It is truly refreshing to observe how this campus maintains such a transparent commitment to accessibility and personalized mentorship, qualities that my acquaintances often praise for making a large-scale educational journey feel both inclusive and exceptionally well-tailored to individual goals. In the broader public consensus among New Yorkers, Mercy is held in high regard as a reliable engine of opportunity, proving that a centrally located university can foster a respectful, high-energy community while remaining deeply dedicated to the holistic development of its diverse student body.', 'Faculty members are approachable and genuinely care about student growth and achievement.', 'Still remember when I had to drop a course after the first class, due to an emergency unforseen situation. I went to my PACT counselor and filled out paperwork to drop the course. I checked a week later on the portal and it said I was still enrolled. So I checked in with my counselor again who ensured that it was in the process of being removed and that it took some time. I trusted her to do the job while I was dealing at home with an emergency situation.

I get my transcript and see a FW as a grade for the course. This meant I was never withdrawn and an F was averaged into my GPA for that semester. Because of that my GPA dropped below a 2.5 even though I received As in all other courses. That was unfair and significantly impacted my overall GPA at graduation. The school said they could do nothing about it.

I still graduated in 2017 with a 3.7 GPA but had yet to hold a job over $17 an hour over 4 years later. After graduation I tried to contact the school to ask for help and job resources and network opportunities. They told me to use the job networking website they offer students but there were literally 0 options for careers in my field of study after months of using the portal I contacted the school again for more opportunities and was told "we don't know how else to help you, sorry".

I ended up going back to a CUNY for my Master's but I really wish Mercy did more for their students. I'm left with 40k in debt and barley any way to pay it back. I feel terrible', 'A pretty good college with a wide range of programs. Has options for a mix of in-class and online classes, which allows for flexibility based on different personal circumstances and schedules.
The best advantage is that many of the bisiness teachers are or were executives in the private sector and they bring this real experience to the classroom.
The admin side could benefit from some fine tuning, but overall a very good experience, never had issues with payments, processing or graduation. Recommended and the Manhattan campus is very well located, both in terms of  access and being near center town.']

The staff are lazy, rude, and highly incompetent. I am embarrassed and ashamed to say that I went here. If you are a parent or student please do not chose this college, it will only lead to stress and turmoil.']

name: Molloy University
reviews:
['As a former student and a single mother on a fixed income, my experience with Molloy University regarding my outstanding balance has been extremely disappointing.

While trying to complete my education to build a better future for my daughter, I trusted the financial aid process and signed documents that were never clearly explained to me. At no point did anyone from financial aid or the bursar’s office thoroughly review what I was committing to in terms of loans and repayment obligations. Looking back, I truly did not understand the full financial impact of what I was signing.

Now, despite explaining my financial hardship and going back and forth with their collection agency, there has been no willingness to negotiate or offer any reasonable consideration. As a single mother doing everything possible to improve her circumstances, being repeatedly rejected when trying to resolve the balance has been discouraging and disheartening.

For an institution that identifies as a Catholic college and promotes values of compassion and community, I expected more understanding and support — especially for students who were simply trying to better themselves through education.

I hope the university takes a closer look at how financial aid obligations are explained to students and how hardship cases are handled. No student should leave school confused about their financial commitments or feel unheard when trying to resolve a debt responsibly.', "I hope this help.....I actually would give 3.5 stars overall, 5 stars for safety, 2 stars for campus food, 2.5 stars for club activities, 1 star for dorm life and 5 star parking on campus. Majority of students commute. If you don't have a car to get around, do not go to this school. Basing the review mostly as a nursing student. The main campus is in Rockville Centre. If you're a nursing student, you will have to do a class, a semester that I know of, at their off campus site in Amityville. There is a parking lot at the off campus site. At the office campus site, there is a fridge & microwave to use. You start your clinical sophomore year. 1st year clinical is at a hospital the school is affiliated with. You don't get to choose which hospital and the school will not allow you to change location. Clinical always start at 7am. First semester clinical it's once a week from 7am-1:30pm (no break, possibly you can't have your belongings there, whatever you can fit in your pocket). Sophomore 2nd semester, clinical will be 7am-7pm. Possibly twice a week junior year. You need a 77 and above for all science and nursing classes to consider passing. You get 2 chances to pass. If you still don't pass, you're kicked out of the nursing program. They have an intense nursing program so you need to be on top of your work and studies. Do Not Recommend last minute studying. The school offer shuttle bus from the main campus from/to LIRR station at Hempstead and Rockville Centre stations. There are  places to eat by the stations that are nice. Since there is nothing close to the campus, the school should make an effort to serve good food to students not rely on students driving out or getting GrubHub. The closest place that have pretty good food is Hollywood Deli on the corner of Hempstead Ave & Marshall Street which is couple blocks drive but about 15 min walk from the North Gate entrance. If you turn on the corner of the deli on to Marshall St & Peninsula Ave, they have decent price gas (paying cash or debit) at Mobil there. At the station, there's a Tim Horton. It would have been nice if Molloy would have a shuttle bus from their main to the off campus site. On the weekend, they provide a shuttle to Roosevelt Field mall but no shuttle to their off campus??!!! Dorm life....null. The school doesn't put any focus on encouraging some type of social gathering events for the poor students who dorm. They do have nice, spacious dorm rooms. If you like to be fit and want to squeeze in a gym workout on campus. The hours are open in the evenings. Each day have different hours. What do we pay tuition and fees if you don't have full access to their facilities like the gym. Most students are there during the day. They thrive on offering small class settings which sounded great but when you try to get classes you need it's full so quickly. They should offer a few of the same class at the same time slots. Registering classes online is brutal. Experienced glitches on each registration so far. If you get an assigned counselor that's not helpful, be proactive to request a different advisor. Don't settle. You're with that advisor til you graduate. Tuition....I'm going to put it in terms of 2025 Fall semester rather than discuss it for the year 2025-2026 (just double what I mention to know the year cost). So fall semester tuition is about $19,800. What I didn't realize are all the additional fees you need to pay with the tuition that they don't mention at Open House. You have the option in paying in full or 5 month payment plan. Medical insurance coverage is mandatory. If you have you can waiver it by a certain time. If you need insurance it's about $2800. I thought enrollment fee occur when you 1st enroll but it's not. It's every semester, about $400. There's a fee for the major you chose and the amount varies by major. Nursing fee $936. Academic technology fee $345. Student activity fee $135. Science classes have fee. 1st yr clinical expense @$800. The school do have some fun events. Wish they were more frequent.", 'I loved going here but the issue was that Ben Molloy did not not actually attend this university hence the loss of 1 star.', 'Me and my school Martin Van Buren came here in march of 2024 and I had a blast can’t wait to attend the open house march 7th!!', "my mother went to Molloy 20 years ago and raved about it and I have been a nursing student for 3 years now and all i can say is this school is now filled with the most incompetent people from teachers to the people in the bursar office. they do not care to help or advise their students, and the bursar office will straight up lie to you about owing money and then freeze your accounts without warning and without any type of notification to you (this has happened to me in 4 semesters where I couldn't register for classes because there was a hold on my account- after speaking with them weeks before and them saying that I'm all caught up with grants and loans). nursing is a very hard field of study and you do not want or need this added stress of incompetency, honestly i know many people that went to Adelphi and i really wish I had gone there, and i advise you to do too. don't take this review the wrong way, i am passing my classes it's just the mediocracy of this entire school has finally pushed me over the edge and i feel it necessary to warn anyone thinking about going here.
These 5 stars reviews are all made by staff or people who attended molloy over 10 years ago, in 2023 do not go there!"]

name: Monroe University
reviews:
['While attending, I was assisted by Ms. Virgo, and unfortunately, I did not find the support I expected. When inquiring about the program of interest, the information provided seemed incomplete, and she asked why I was asking certain questions related to the program and potential experience there. I found this approach concerning, as asking questions is a fundamental part of the learning process. As someone ready to enroll, this interaction left a negative impression and ultimately influenced my decision not to move forward. Given that this is a private institution, I expected a higher level of professionalism from staff who serve as representatives of the school. I recommend reconsidering how staff engage with prospective students to ensure that applicants feel informed, welcomed, and supported.', 'Everyone is so willing to help you achieve e your goals. No dept. within the university leaves students to fend for themselves. From admissions, to career counseling and advising in between and go above and beyond. I have in my four years of studying at monroe not only attained a BA starting at barely a high school diploma but have had the opportunity to engage with professors with different backgrounds, expertise and networks. I look forward to pursuing my masters at monroe in 2026', 'I am a current student. The admission process was great. Olga M. walked me step by step through everything and explained everything I needed to know. I will never forget how nice and helpful she was.

The advisors and professors are excellent. They give me options each semester for days and class hours, and most importantly, they are there for anything I need, anytime. I see people saying that the school is not accredited, which is not true. The Nursing program is accredited, and students sit for the boards right after graduation. The DMS program is accredited with ARRT; after the ARRT registry, graduate students can sit for ARDMS.

I don’t see any problem with this — anyone who wants success has to work hard. I have been here for three semesters, and I have already learned a lot. Nobody has been unprofessional or rude — quite the opposite. I am truly enjoying my student life at Monroe, and I will graduate next year.

Update: I graduated in 2023. I got an amazing job and am now doing my master’s degree at Monroe University.', 'Monroe college offers various degrees. Easy admission process staff are professionals and care about all there student current ,pass admission and new ones. Friendly environment and home feel. I would recommend to all my friends and family to attend this place . The staff really cares.', 'BEWARE! Terrible communication, extremely rude, terrible instruction. With many high hopes for Monroe college, especially nursing program, it’s such a waste of time. You will be expected to self teach 99% of program, told if you don’t understand it’s your fault and not the sleeping professor (even if you’re a 85% average).
Spend your money on a cheaper program as you will not have a greater experience going private.']

name: Mount Saint Mary College
reviews: ['MSMC is not aligned with modern nursing education models. I highly recommend students to attend Mount Saint Mary College, and get as involved as you can!', 'From an educational standpoint, my experience at The Mount was one of a kind. name: Nazareth University
reviews:
["A great place to go to school and a wonderful place to visit.
The students here are almost all very kind, sweet, accepting, supportive, and open-minded people. They are slightly diverse in terms of demographics, and quite diverse in terms of personality.
The college offers a diverse range of majors and excellent classes. It has particularly great music, performing arts, nursing, and physical therapy programs. Class sizes are not very big, with very few lecture hall-style class settings. The teachers are mostly very kind and care greatly about what they do. Tuition is very high, but depending on your program, it might be worth it.
The campus is beautiful! It's full of nature and a mix of collegiate gothic and more modern buildings. It's small and dense, but not crowded. It's also very safe; risk of theft or damage to property is very rare, but the latter is more common among lowerclassmen. There's so much history to uncover! It's located close to good places to shop, eat, and visit in Pittsford.
The academic buildings are clean, well-lit, and mostly fitted with modern amenities. Bathrooms in some buildings are very clean, some are quite unclean. The lowerclassmen residence halls can be somewhat loud, are typically slightly unclean, but have many events to attend run by the RAs. There are dorm or suite-style living choices. Upperclassmen residence halls are mostly clean, almost always very quiet, and have dorm, suite, apartment-style living choices. Living arrangements are for full-time students only. Can be hard to find parking near them.
The food in the Dining Commons is pretty good. It has a pretty diverse menu with some options tasting decent, some great. Other food locations around campus have a somewhat limited menu range and the food is mediocre. Some alternative dietary accommodations are met, and more might be made if requested.
Facilities staff are mostly not friendly, but not unkind. The staff in the Dining Commons are mostly pretty friendly and very kind.", 'I attended my Daughters commencement at Nazareth on Friday, May 16, 2025. Beautiful campus & very enjoyable Commencement ceremony.', 'Very bad neighbors, very noisy both from sports events and late night fireworks.  It appears that those along with the constant bell ringing,  like it is 1800s,  every half an hour are the reason so many kids , and parents,  accept to go there for a mediocre, at best, education.  The college students are harrasing people walking on campus and security bans the people walking and there are no consequences for the students.  Littering on campus is also a big problem.
This college is preparing very low quality citizens for our future generation.  I reccomend you look somewhere else for a good education.', 'The campus is really pretty all year round and overall a decent experience. The professors are really great and all the staff here are wonderful. Great atmosphere and close to a good amount of nice places!', 'One of the best schools in Rochester coed. We live right behind the sports fields and enjoy watching all sorts of games baseball lacrosse hockey and even rugby that was great fun to be so close to the young people and enjoy their sports.']

name: Neighborhood Playhouse School of the Theater
reviews: ['Walking around midtown East today after bagels at TAL Bagels. Passed by this small  actor training school which has been here for over 90 years. I believe some rather famous people attended the school.  Often we see the students out during the day for breaks. There is a difference between being an actor and being a famous actor. Some entertaining teachers...I wouldnt take acting as a full time job.. GUYS: wake up and smell the coffee.', 'Went to my first show here tonight and loved it ! Talented actors in a great venue that’s been here nearly a 100 years .  Proof is on the walls highlighting the many now famous actors that have studied their craft at this neighborhood playhouse .']

name: The New School
reviews: ['The New School has been an amazing college for my son to attend. While we worried about sending him to school in the heart of NYC, we have discovered our fears were unfounded as the school works hard to acclimate students to the big city and makes use of the diverse, creative opportunities it provides in classes, assignments, and inspiration. My son often had class in one of the many museums or parks or other interesting places. The school is truly dedicated to mixing art, design, history, story, social justice, and community building - learning is often hands on, research driven, and provided with context. The assignments are rigorous but teachers work very closely with students and the school offers many types of equipment and resources to document, create, and display projects. The New School is great for aspiring writers, journalists, philosophers, musicians, actors, students interested in community planning, architecture, social justice,  and artists of every kind. There is a great mix of students from all over the country and around the world which has provided my son even more ways to learn first hand from the new friends he makes. We have been grateful for the generous merit scholarships which help pay for 3/4 of his tuition. Learning in the heart of a thriving city and working with outstanding faculty who are using a progressive, integrated curriculum has motivated my freshman son and inspired him to reach even higher in his artistic endeavors. This school is not only for fashion designers - my son is an artist and not pursuing fashion in any way. His roommate is a writer and he has friends studying philosophy. I highly recommend The New School.', "Classes stopped for a whole month last semester because the administration refused to give their faculty a reasonable contract, forcing them to strike. At the end of the strike, they were threatening to cut healthcare for all striking workers and the union filed an unfair labor practice charge against the school. This school's leadership cares more about money than the material and working conditions of their teachers and the education experience of their students.", 'Came here for a presentation for extra credit from Hunter College (better school btw) and the security has attitude I also don’t feel bad for the people that go here that want to spend thousands a semester would never come here again even if it is for a class', 'Garbage school with garbage faculty when they actually show up for work. Don’t waste your time or money here, unless you enjoy being disrespected and ignored.', 'This school is a disaster! dont come!']

name: New York University
reviews:
['A few years ago, I participated in the Career Edge Program. This week-long program was amazing as I was able to live on campus, attend events with other students, and learn in the classroom. Amazing school!', "NYU is not your traditional university with miles of green acreage and beautifully manicured pathways connecting academic buildings. This university basically surrounds Washington Square, a small park filled with eclectic personalities, which acts as the school's common area, while the university itself spreads out in a 2 block radius in each direction around that same park. Given its compact size, the university has tons of people passing through, most of which are a mix between students, tourists, and locals. In a city of over 20 million people, that can be exciting or intimidating, depending upon your temperament. The school itself has around 28,000 enrolled students. If you like the excitement of a big city married to the concept of a college campus, NYU is your vibe. We toured here, and my daughter loved it. I thought it strange that we didn't get to see any classrooms, dining facilities, or living quarters on the tour, and I think this would have enhanced our overall experience. This is one of the only college tours we've been on that left out all three. There is a lot of emphasis on academics and research opportunities for students. NYU stands as the premiere educational institution in New York City next to Columbia.", 'Fantastic school that teaches and goes above the standards. A student goes in expecting academics, they go out ready for the world.', "i heard someone called riley didn't get to keep his air frier. so stingy. they didn't even let him keep his electric scooter? if u leave that outside its going get stolen because its new york city. if he doesn't have it in his dorm or with him he's not going to be able to get anywhere, because it's new york city.", 'Beautiful architecture old style building.
Water fountain was so beautiful.
Went there to check out Nyu for my daughter
She loves that University.🤞']

name: Niagara County Community College
reviews:
['I am a first year returning non traditional student at SUNY Niagara, this is the 3rd college I’ve been enrolled at over the years and I will say it’s probably my favorite of them all including over a 4 year private institution I went to. The professors are all really great that I’ve had, you can tell they care about their profession and the success of their students genuinely, so it makes me want to work harder to give it my all. The support systems they have in place here are also amazing! So many people that check in on you just to ask how things are going and about your mental, physical and financial wellbeing, which makes you feel like you’re not just a number or a paying student body to satisfy requirements. In my short time here I already feel like I belong here and I know I made the right decision to come here even if I have to commute almost an hour during winter months during rush hour, it’s so worth it. Very thankful for this opportunity to get another chance to fulfill my life goals now that I finally know what I want to do the rest of my life. I honestly cannot say one bad thing about my experience here.', 'What kind of a school makes a correspondence student studying abroad from an English speaking country get an F1, $10000 bank statement and English proficiency test. Maybe Canada can start asking Americans for English testing', 'Sketchy school
- school computer systems got hacked and took a month to get back
- advisors don’t really care about students (lack of information/guidance) doing everything on your own is better. Don’t rely on any of the advisors
- gym closes too fast
- random school shuttle time/not following the schedule
- dinning comm food is the same thing over and over again but overpriced. $12 for salad', 'This college misguides students frequently. Be careful what your advisor tells you and they tend to swap your own major without your permission.

I’ve lost thousands of dollars due to the unmanaged people that work here. This place has a low tuition cost for a reason.

I’m disgusted how they treat students and the sad part is they can’t own up to their own mistakes either. I’d give it zero stars all day if I could.', 'Great school! I graduated as a dual major from this institution and have since transferred to University At Buffalo. The professors and staff were great and helpful! Highly recommend beginning the college journey here.']

name: Niagara University
reviews:
["I was lucky enough to visit Niagara University today with my daughters for a Volleyball clinic run by Vilis Ozols.  The clinc itself is a 3 day 'camp' format and day one was exceptional.

In speaking with some of the athlete coaches that attend the university they boasted about how much they loved the university.

Safety Campus Office do a good job of looking out for students and staffs. They drive around school to make sure everything/everyone is okay. Lectures and professors are super helpful and friendly. Just a little too cold in winter there but summer time is much enjoyable around the campus', 'I was there only on my phone. Imagine that. name: North Country Community College
reviews: ["I've attended this campus twice. Once in person the second online. The food service workers at the connector were always friendly polite and conveniently efficient. The book store is a little pricey yet they will help you out on deals. This is an excellent junior university experience because grades are usually raw as opposed to curved.
