There are no bounds at NCCC in either your future ambitions or the extent everyone associated with this college will go for you.\nBut in the end, it's your choice and we will stand by you and your decission until, and even after, your decision is completed.", 'Stopped in to check out out the pool and stayed for a swim. Had a great time, and the facility is taken care of by a wonderful and friendly staff.', 'Water aerobics was fun and a good workout.', 'Beautiful campus. Navigating the campus roads are tricky.']

name: New York Institute of Technology
reviews:
['The New York Institute of Technology’s campus at 1855 Broadway is widely recognized among my tech-oriented peers as a premier launchpad for digital innovation, where a career-centric curriculum effectively translates high-level technical theory into practical market leadership. Through various exchanges with alumni and industry professionals, it is evident that the institution’s location near Columbus Circle serves as a strategic crossroads for networking, with many acquaintances specifically praising the faculty’s ability to bridge the gap between classroom learning and the rapid evolution of the global tech sector. It is truly commendable how NYIT manages to maintain such a transparent focus on "maker" culture and interdisciplinary collaboration, qualities that local residents often highlight as key factors in the university's reputation for producing highly adaptable and socially responsible graduates. In the general consensus of New Yorkers, the campus stands as a sophisticated and reliable pillar of professional development, rightfully respected for its commitment to providing a substantive, future-proof education in the heart of the city’s cultural and economic hub.', 'This institution has lots of choices with every aspect of fields !
Advance library and practical knowledge with high Tech labs !
Atmosphere is so vivid and peaceful!
Every faculty has very nice mentor and professors!
I had my Masters in Environmental Technology and it was fantastic experience in my life !
Thanks very much to Professor Stanley Greenwald and team 😇
Best wishes', "*Content warning for yapping* (Continuous updates)
I am now a third year at this school, and so far, I'd honestly give it 2.5 stars.
As with all schools, some staff are nice and some are not. Security tends to be friendly. However, the teachers have such a wide spectrum of horrible and amazing. The math and physics department seem to definitely have the short end of the stick. One of my math classes has an unavoidable (advanced math) professor who honestly bullied me throughout the entire semester (not to mention she's also the department chair). The chair (and unavoidable teacher) of the physics department is also not good. He is narcissistic and is very non-tradition. I won't say he isn't smart, but he is not a skilled teacher -- which is a very common theme at this school.
Another slight issue is that the school has a vast majority of some majors (especially computer science) and a huge lack of others. I am a physics major, and the program has maybe 15 students (if you include majors as well as minors). However, more people are enrolling in my department so this may not be a consistent problem. But an ongoing problem is course cancellations due to lack of enrollment. Still not enough students.
However, having a small department isn't particularly bad. The school, in general, has classes of up to 40 people. 40 is not a very large number compared to the 100 some other universities face. But for me, 40 is still a lot — so having small classes is a huge bonus for me. The classes that the entire school doesn't need have less than 15 students, with some of my classes having only 3 students.
Even with education aside, the last issue with this school is the accessibility. While there are elevators in each building, they absolutely suck. The elevators work sometimes, and other times, you have to climb up a plethora of stairs (where in one building our school only has access from floor 6 which means you will be climbing a minimum of 6 floors). So if anyone reading this can not be prepared to randomly take the stairs, consider a different institution. Lastly, the total cost is always rising. The dorms are getting more expensive, and the cost of tuition is also getting more expensive.So honestly if you are considering coming here, unless this is your absolute dream uni, save your money for a cheaper place that probably has the same quality of professors -- if not better.
That is it for my review as a 3rd year. Thanks for reading my yap session.", 'Got my masters from NYIT 2 decades ago! Great place to be in. Very convenient location, right in the middle of NYC', 'This is a general review and it doesn’t mean everyone here is not good. Some staff are very nice, same as the professors, but this school is not for good and smart students. This school is for the ones who wants to get a student visa to come to the US. If you are already here in the US don’t go here. Also if you care about your money and you want to learn something don’t go here. Specially for higher education such as masters, for me it was a waste of time and money!']

name: New York School of Interior Design
reviews:
['Barbara, the woman who runs the entire school… told me I’d make a good bartender when I graduate. After spending over 200k on attending this HORRIBLE waste of money school. You absolutely do not need their degree to do interior design. They teach you the skills to become an intern, not become a designer. They don’t believe in THEIR OWN students. They will make you hate design and art because they do not appreciate creativity. Do not waste your money or your years here.', 'FAFSA STUDENTS / AID REQUIRED PLEASE READ:

This school is very challenging for anyone who is a financial aid student or requires financial aid to pay for the education.

Your refund checks are paid towards end of each semester not prior so all textbooks, required materials, housing and food will be on you.

Your refund checks are sent via USPS in the form of a written check. I have had multiple missing and will take another week from the disbursement date.

The bursar office and financial aid office with just bounce questions back and forth from each other rather than just answering your questions.', 'Applicant who loves that school', 'Classes Are Big Enough !!', 'Great school']

name: Onondaga Community College
reviews:
["I like the outlay of Onondaga Community College. The teachers and staff are friendly, nice, helpful. It's easy to be able to concentrate and get that degree. In the summer there are track and field meets and they are fun to watch. It's really easy to sign up to get enrolled. There are dorms.", 'I just want to shout out to the president, Dr. Warren M. Hilton. Since taking on the presidential role at OCC this school has nothing but improved. From how the faculty respond to students to the overall quality of your education. All it takes is one stroll through the campus and the proof is in the pudding. Dr Warren continues to allocate funds into the correct places allowing the school to continue to grow where needed. Also special shoutout to Coach Piraino who has made many junior college young men turn D1-D2 . This school gives you what you put into it. Lastly treat others how you’d like to be treated the staff here work tirelessly to ensure the operations run smoothly and effectively for all alumni’s to succeed. My first semester has been a dream at OCC and I can’t wait to continue my learning experience.', 'Small but mighty place good price if you’re looking for something more or just want to get in or back into something professors are top notch for this kind of college', 'Charged me for an entire semester that I never attended all because I told them two days late that I wasn’t able to attend this semester and nobody did anything to try to help, lady on phone was rude and dismissive. Beware once you click register now they will do nothing to confirm whether you are going or not, they will give you random classes and charge you full price. How ironic the place that is supposed to be affordable will charge you for not going, and will make no exceptions to try to help you remove charges for services you never received. Guess I just made a $1600 donation 🙃', "Graduated here a bit ago. Overall, this place is aesthetically beautiful. The wildlife, overview of the city, and sunsets while having headphones make you enjoy your free time there.

However, there are a lot of things I wish could be improved here. For one, the dining experience is interesting. None of my friends enjoy it, there is occasional food poisoning, and the allergy/diet accommodations are few to none and staff are only given a seven minute training for accommodations through video. I warn anyone who plans to live on campus with allergies have a good lawyer and doctor or connections at school that will care about your health because the meal plan is mandatory and I have been told by my friend with celiacs  that it is complicated to get accommodations without getting mistakes in their food that is life threatening. There is a food bank that can provide meats and veggies but Wegmans/Aldis nearby will be your best friend. Also, there is no food available on Sundays/Saturdays until 12pm.

Living on campus without a car is a struggle, but I have heard Veo scooters are now on campus. Nevertheless, unless you have a friend who lives on campus with a car, each week will grow increasingly frustrating if you're stuck on campus. Parties are abundant but can be frustrating if you study diligently. Only building B has a kitchen in the room and I don't recommend using the public kitchens in A or C. The dorms are way better than other SUNY dorms, but make sure to document any problems and contact maintenance, unless you want to pay extra fees. Make sure you have friends to dorm with you and get a single room, because you could get ANYONE. I have had nightmare experiences with suitemates using my things without permission, and unfortunately a lot of my friends have had that problem.

There are lots of good staff, and there are staff who do questionable things. Look at RateMyProfessor and definitely ask people for info on previous professors. I'm lucky to have had most of my instructors, since they are amazing people. One concern I have is the amount of stress they have from the workplace, which means stress on students. Expect this to be commonplace and understand they are people too. Micron is making big changes and it's overwhelming staff and students.

Transferring and financial aid have been frustrating. I had to figure out everything myself on how to transfer because the transfer services are frustrating to reach out to and bring more questions than answers, so you'd be more in luck asking for help from the transfer institutions in the college you're transferring too. With financial aid, all I can say is make sure you look into it every week/month in case miscellaneous fees are charged and make sure to apply for TAP and FAFSA if able. There is a joke here that everyone has problems with financial aid here.

Near the end of my last semester, changes were being made to the program I was a part of. Beforehand, a lot of my classes I needed to graduate with were cancelled and I ended up with credits I could not transfer with, classes I was overqualified for, and courses that ended up being too crowded. As a result, I will have to take another year at my new institution. Some courses are cancelled without reason, so do be wary. One of my friends had to confront the dean to fix this problem or else they would not graduate. Overall, talk to your professors once you get screwed over like this and they will help. I am lucky to have had the professors I had, but I felt there was more stress than there should've been with my college experience.

Overall, I enjoyed my time here and made countless connections, but I question if I would be better off at a 4 year. I would suggest coming here if you would like to get back on your feet, like me, or take a few courses or just imprive your GPA. If you expect to go to a 4 year college and you want to save money at a community college, I recommend you do more research.

On the more good side of things, you will definitely find amazing people and friends here."]

name: Orange County Community College
reviews:
['I am extremely frustrated with my experience at SUNY Orange regarding the Financial Aid Office and the Student Accounts Office. Today at approximately 4:20 p.m., with offices closing at 5:00 p.m., I received an email stating that my Spring 2026 registration was dropped because my financial aid had not been processed.

I want to be clear that my financial aid has already been approved for the full amount, but it has not yet been processed due to a required form change. This form change was completed and submitted two days ago, as instructed by the Financial Aid Office.

Immediately after receiving this notification, I attempted to contact both offices and called repeatedly, but was unable to reach anyone before closing. The delay is due to a backlog within the Financial Aid Office, not because I failed to submit documentation.

As a result of this administrative delay, I am now being told that I must make a payment of $1,256 in order to remain enrolled, a payment I am unable to make at this time. This situation is both unfair and distressing, as it is outside of my control and directly impacts my ability to continue my education.

Students should not be penalized or dropped from classes due to internal processing delays, especially when financial aid has already been approved. I hope this issue is resolved promptly and that my Spring 2026 registration is reinstated while my aid is being processed.

Adding to this review -  Spoke to this Sweet woman named Juanita from Student Services Central. Who was able to give me more information and was so caring. Thank you Juanita for the wonderful service you provided and for assisting me through this nervous break down I had.', 'This experience was satisfactory as a student. I had extremely good professors that enticed me to go deeper and learn more to the extent that I went from here to a four year college well prepared.   This is written as thank you card to THEM ! The administration at that time was pleasant and respectful.
If it is four stars only  it is because the  administration situation got to be quite different later on but this is another story completely.', "Advising staff is so so rude and unhelpful. Really recommend going to a different school. It's worth the drive for a better atmosphere. I even moved to go to HVCC, where I've had only good experiences with all areas of staff.", 'Internet never works on Middletown campus, and when it does work it’s absolutely horrible, making it impossible to even get any work done on campus .', 'This College is A Scam, Students Be ware, I signed up for 2 classes this summer, but because my financial aid never got approved I withdrew from their classes before the they even started. Now 3 months later they send me to collection for the full amount, even after I withdrew. This college is a scam & you can’t even go & talk to someone in person, everything is online. & they’re online system are always down.']

name: Pace University
reviews: ['"I\'m so grateful to University of PACE for shaping my future! 🎓 The professors are experts in their fields and genuinely care about student success. The diverse course offerings and state-of-the-art facilities helped me discover my passion and excel 💡. I love the collaborative environment and extracurricular opportunities that made my uni life unforgettable 🎉. If you\'re passionate about learning and growth, University of PACE is the perfect fit! 🚀"', 'A good university (definitely NOT the best in NYC!) offering undergrad and grad programs with reasonable tuition costs. As an alumni of Lubin school of business, I highly recommend its business programs as the majority of its scholars are either business owners or top level managers/directors in Wall Street.', 'I was researching the school\'s programs and was surprised to see "Go Further" as a logo. It should be "Go Farther".\nBest regards from far away (as in mastering the distance between knowledge and skill,\nVi Ryerson', 'The campus has some really cool buildings. The layout of the university is smart because all the buildings are nearby each other.', 'I went to Pace University for the event the campus was beautiful. The staff were very helpful to us for anything. The cafeteria was spectacular. They took us on a tour to the campus. I will definitely come back again in the future.']

name: Paul Smiths College of Arts and Science
reviews: ["Beautiful campus! PSC students are kind, gritty, and hardworking. Come breathe some fresh Adirondack air! Don't sleep on the Paul Smith's College VIC, this is a must check out if you enjoy beautiful trails and getting out in mother nature :)", 'Gorgeous!! Went here to visit with my son and it was amazing. Not THE MOST handsome friendly walk with cobblestone, potholes and mud but boy did I love this school.', "Paul Smith's is not only beautiful (if you've ever listened to a loon calling while looking across the lake at St. Regis Mtn., you know what I mean), but it has given me a wonderful community to be a part of.  From day one, I have felt the camaraderie and openness that the college fosters, not just in its students, but in their faculty and staff as well.", "Only gonna give 4 stars cause, unfortunately, we didn't get to tour the whole campus, our fault, not theirs.  But the experience we had was 5 star worthy. My daughter is looking at Colleges, and Paul Smith is one of her top choices. The Saturday open house was very informative, She's interested in a business degree and pairing that with a culinary/baking degree. They had great activities for the current students and for the guests to partake in. Hoping she may want to visit in warmer weather so we can walk the grounds and tour more of the complex. She is very excited about the possibilities.  I know if I would of known Paul Smith existed when I was coming out of High school, they would of been a top choice college for me also.", "Paul Smith's College is a phenomenal school if you love the great outdoors!  You receive  an educational experience surrounded by the gorgeous Adirondack Park with lakes, rivers, mountains and forests.  Take advantage of fishing, hiking, skiing,  climbing and so much more.\n\nGraduates have gone on to be some of the most respected and knowledgeable professionals in their chosen field."]

name: Plaza College
reviews:
["Plaza College's Allied Health program has been amazing. I am so grateful that I applied here.

From the first phone call with admissions, I was provided a holistic review of my academic experience and given a very supportive push to have all of my documentation submitted within the required time frame.

This program provides the necessary prerequisites and gives you an excellent foundation for success. I have never been part of an academic organization that supports its students so much. During my entire experience with prerequisites and required exams, I have continued to be impressed with Plaza College. Throughout my journey, I've felt a consistent sense of guidance and care every step of the way.

The professors and faculty are incredibly kind and encouraging. They really make an effort to know every student individually and connect very often. At any given point, I felt comfortable reaching out and getting clarification or simply to express my gratitude.

Applying for financial aid was made so simple, where it had previously been such a painful process.

If you are looking for a school that will challenge you to be the best student you can be, Plaza is the way to go.

Overall, Plaza College’s Allied Health program has exceeded my expectations, and I’m truly grateful for the support I’ve received.", 'I first enrolled in Plaza College back in 2011, where I entered into the Medical Assistant program. I graduated in 2013 with my Associates degree in Allied Health and was able to successfully gain employment as a Registered Medical Assistant. Every step of that journey was absolutely amazing. I was able to flourish within the program thanks to all the support and the resources the school offered.

Just this January (2025), I discovered that Plaza college was now offering a 16-month accelerated program to obtain a Bachelors degree of Science in Nursing (BSN). It is a very well-known fact that any nursing program in any school is a very competitive program to enter. What I most like and appreciate about Plaza College is that they prioritize their students first for entrance into their nursing program. This shows how much they value their students, and how much they want to see us succeed. With this in mind and with such a great initial experience at Plaza, I had no doubt that I wanted to rejoin Plaza college and transition into their nursing program.
I knew that it had been some time since I had graduated, and that I would have to retake some classes, or take some for the first time in order to qualify for the nursing program. I was admitted into the allied health program in May to complete my prerequisites (Chemistry, A&P 1 & 2, Advanced Composition, Microbiology, Statistics, and Bio-Chemistry). I am currently in my last semester of prerequisites, I have successfully passed my HESI examination, and was recently accepted into the January 2026 Nursing Cohort. I couldn’t have done it without the help, support, and encouragement from the professors I have had the privilege of having so far. I am looking forward to the many new experiences and the knowledge I will obtain from the nursing program. I am looking forward to working hard to make my dream of becoming a nurse come true.', 'I recently completed the A to Z class at Plaza College, and I genuinely had a great experience. Even though the course was only four days long, I learned so much more than I expected. Mrs. McMahon was an amazing teacher  she made the class enjoyable, easy to follow, and kept everyone engaged the entire time. I’m really glad I decided to try out this class. If you are thinking of committing to court reporting or aren’t sure and want to see if you enjoy it, definitely take this class!', 'Taking my Allied Health prerequisites at Plaza College gave me a great head start while I was applying to the nursing program. The professors were very supportive and the coursework lined up perfectly with what I needed to transition into the nursing program. I highly recommend the Allied Health track to incoming students who want a clear pathway into the nursing program.', 'I had just found about court reporting not too long ago and was looking for schools that practiced stenography. Plaza college has given me the opportunity to talk with teachers, advisors, and senior court reporters to further explain the career and what benefits it brings you. I recently just finished the A to Z classes with Mrs. Cindy McMahon and I can honestly say it was one of the greatest and eye opening experiences I’ve had to go forward with this career path. Everybody has been super helpful and has given me all the information I’ve needed for this.']

reviews: ['Good place to study medical science. Bigger class size. Supervised Apartments are available at nearby CCNY towers. Down side is no cafeteria on campus. I take my hat off too those enroll at this school. If you're breathing, then must be achieving. Strive to best the best individual you can be. Hold your head and be proud of who you are.", 'met some great people', 'It is so beautiful!!', 'Awesome environment']

name: Pratt Institute-Main
reviews: ['I graduated from Pratt.\n\n17 years later I was in the UK, and randomly, some woman asked me "where did you go to school in the USA?"  I told her "Pratt."  She blasted out laughing.  Apparently \'pratt\' in the UK means a really stupid person.  Remember that if you are aspiring to come across as intellectual and educated when you come to study here.', "Going to Pratt was one of the best decisions in my life. As with everything in life, it's what one makes of it.", 'I know several people who went to Pratt including an architect that I worked with in the 1980’s and my daughter and her classmates. Let me just say that both my professional associate and my daughter are extremely successful in their fields of endeavor and are generally happy, well adjusted human beings. I loved the campus because it reminded me of Harvard Yard where I attended school back in the dark ages. I did hear that the Pratt Cats were relocated during the pandemic and have not returned to the campus, which is a great loss. Here’s to reinstating the Pratt Cat tradition as soon as possible!', "Got my b.arch here. Not really worth the amount of money spent. If you're financing, know that you can get the same accredited education for less in another school in the city.", "We went on a campus tour today. My daughter and I loved the campus. It's not too big or too small. Nice old buildings and an engine room. My daughter wants to do animation and film. The facilities for them are up to date and student to professor ratio is 12 to 1. Dorms seem good. We weren't able to go into any of them but from the outside and description they sounded nice. All in all this school has jumped to number one on my daughter's list of schools."]

name: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
reviews: ["I go here so I'm obligated to give it a 5 star review. This is a very good STEM school, but if you want to go here for a non-STEM major, you may want to reconsider, since the best courses and professors here are in STEM. This college is also very expensive, so apply for financial aid! The coursework is very difficult but also rewarding. The community is very tight-knit and close. This is a smaller college in Troy, NY, so there is a lot to do on and off campus (barring COVID times). The campus is quite pretty and safe from my experience.", '0 star if possible. Shirley Ann Jackson was the worst president and the administration could not be any worse. Very expensive, professor smart but doesn’t know how to teach (at least for my major), doesn’t care about students mental health, arch program is a scam, troy is a pothole, reconsider your mental health, social life and student loan before apply and prep to transfer. I don't know why RPI's ranking is so low, it should definitely be in top 100 schools in world.", 'Love this school so glad my son decided to attend college here', "We go to Black Families Technology Awareness Day every year and my son has a great time. It's student led it could be more timely but due to the storm we were late but didn't miss anything."]

reviews: ['Excellent University. Excellent campus. They  Dont care about people or students. Seriously, take your college tuition elsewhere please dont go to this abomination of a school!', 'It was a great experience, but some other times I went through some roadblocks, I had huge up and downs just like a roller coaster all the years I had in my life, some may not show great days or cut short times a outgoing person I really am, absolutely grateful I live close & loved gratefully, I hope it stays in business 🙏🏻', "It's changed over the past two years. Professors have been leaving or secretly fired left and right without giving reasons to students taking said classes. The vibe has shifted noticeably. Most staff and professors are still very sweet and helpful, however I'm concerned about the future.", "I graduated from Roberts last year and I had a great experience.  I do agree with some reviews that communication is not always great, but as long as you are proactive and take an active approach to your education here, you'll do wonderfully.  The staff and students are very respectful and the professors seem to really care about you and your overall success.  It is a nice size campus, not too busy and not too small.  Finding a parking spot during busy times was a challenge.  Food is AMAZING"]

name: Rochester Institute of Technology
reviews: ['I would not recommend applying to this school. My experience here has been very disappointing. I feel like many of the professors and staff do not truly care about their students or support them the way they should. I’ve also personally experienced and witnessed unfair treatment toward students of color, which made the environment feel unwelcoming and uncomfortable. Because of this, I’ve decided to transfer as soon as possible. I hope the school takes these concerns seriously and works to create a more supportive and inclusive environment for everyone.', 'Absolutely beautiful campus!  Over the weekend, we went for an Open House. The entire presentation was very nicely put together. Everyone we talked to had a genuine love for the school. Students were helpful wherever you walked.  Can’t wait to go back!', 'Focus on your degree and your life will follow. Best university to get an engineering degree and stay focused as it is pretty isolated (least distractions). You will be happy you went through RIT after you leave(not when you are studying) for the rest of your life.', 'Great school for all major interests. This school also offers great education to Art majors as well (glass, jewelry, ceramics, Industrial Design, etc). I really enjoyed attending art exhibit shows and demonstrations in this school :)\nAlso, the school hosts "Imagine RIT" each year which cannot be missed.', 'Beautiful and lush green campus. The sports training facilities are pure classy. The university shuttles have great connectivity to nearby markets. The library has some of the best collection of books, journals, magazines and very comfortable seating on a the floors. On campus dining offer great food with frequent visits by outside chefs offering Indian, Japanese, Columbian food items.']

name: University of Rochester
reviews: ['The University of Rochester is one of the most beautiful, uniform, and well-maintained campuses I’ve visited. Every building — from the iconic Rush Rhees Library with its stately dome to the modern Wegmans Hall — is thoughtfully designed, blending classical architecture with contemporary function.\n\nThe campus layout feels intentional and cohesive, with red-brick facades and mature greenery lending both historical character and harmony. It’s the kind of place where every corner feels picture-perfect. The walkways are clean and inviting, framed by shady trees and trimmed hedges. Even statues like George Eastman’s are tastefully placed, adding personality without clutter.', 'We had a brief visit from outside and looks like a great university with a lot of research related activities. There are many historical buildings. Rates high and a great university to attend. Neighborhood is very nice too.', 'Quality educational institution with a not looking campus when the weather is nice. Solid sports facilities and school spirit.', "I went to Eastman Dental Emergency & had a molar pulled out. It was absolutely painless and quick. Also I didn't have to wait at all. Sometimes you get lucky and today was my lucky day 👍👍", "Feels clean, and safe. Especially at late hours because I delivered food here. Great school.  For example the security is on top of things. There's no one roaming the campus that doesn't go there during late hours."]

name: Rockland Community College
reviews:
['BEWARE!!! This school drags their feet on processing your paperwork. The academic advisors are not helpful, telling a student " I don't really know what to tell you. or I don't know is not an actual helpful answer". They do not return phone calls in a timely manner, and when you speak to different staff members they give different or incorrect information. They do this to a degree so after a certain point you are 100% financially responsible. THEY SET YOU UP FOR FAILURE! The famous school line is they are here to help when in fact they are not. The stress that is added to countless phone call and emails to no avail, They really only care about money and do not care for the success of the students. They talk to you condescendingly and place the blame on you (The Student) for a system they have set up designed for you to fail. PLEASE Find another school, this may be a cheaper option as far as colleges go but cheaper does not always mean better. Financially don't do it to yourself and put yourself through the extra stress of trying to navigate this poorly managed excuse for a college.', 'Our kids practice soccer here for travel soccer. It is a massive indoor venue with multiple "fields" all occupied concurrently with large "curtains" separating the fields. There is parking in the front and the back. For whatever reason, Waze brings you to the back, and the parking there is on dirt, can be on a steep incline, and just isn't great. Google maps, however, will bring you to the front / main entrance, but then you have to find your way over to the field house. 4 stars because it isn't in perfect shape and could use a refresh, but it is definitely perfect for what we need it for and on par (or maybe better?) than other community college arenas.', 'I was here for a gymnastics meet and while the facility is large it is also a little dated. It has seen better times. The walk to the field house is almost dangerous especially for disabled people.  The college itself seems nice. I have not had any interaction with students but the security guards are very nice and helpful.', 'This is my first time ever attending college, and I chose Rockland Community College because of its proximity and the SUNY Reconnect program. I currently work at a hospital with a demanding schedule, and I needed to drop an Anatomy & Physiology class.

Before dropping the class, I went to the financial aid office with another student to ask if dropping would result in any penalties. A staff member assured us that there would be no penalties if we remained enrolled in the flex-start six-credit program. Based on this guidance, I dropped the class and enrolled immediately in the flex-start program.

Shortly after, I discovered a balance of over $800. I contacted financial aid, and a director, Marilyn, kindly explained that the front-desk staff member had given incorrect information and advised me to appeal, which I did. Despite following financial aid guidance, my appeal was denied, with the school claiming it was “not at fault.”

I contacted student accounts to request a payment plan, explaining my situation, but was told no plan could be offered because the deadline had passed. I even attempted to escalate by leaving voicemails for the supervisor, Brian, and emailing Marilyn again, but received no responses.

As a single mother and a first-time college student, this experience has been incredibly frustrating. The school’s lack of support has prevented me from registering for classes and has forced me to consider other institutions to continue my nursing education. Following advice from financial aid should not result in a financial penalty, and students deserve better guidance and support.

It is disappointing that Rockland Community College chose not to assist me in resolving this issue or providing a reasonable payment option, despite the circumstances. I hope they reevaluate their policies and train staff appropriately to prevent other students from experiencing the same unfair treatment.', 'Show is getting smaller and smaller every year. Not alot of hunting stuff.']

name: Russell Sage College
reviews: ["This my daughter's first year there, and right from the start we got a really strong positive vibe from the students, staff and campus!", 'Teachers are absolutely wonderful. I feel they do a wonderful job with curriculum and really give great opportunities to grow. Unfortunately if you stay in dorms...Food is awful!  They charge so much but you definitely don\'t get quality. It became a joke that they offer mystery meat and only when visitors come do they "play up" the experience to impress. Security is worse. As you will come to find the neighborhood is very dangerous and the school encourages the buddy system when leaving campus. Well..On campus I was being harassed by boys and when I went to tell security they treated me like I was lying and offered no protection. I traveled an hour and a half home every Friday after classes because I did not feel to stay the weekend.', "I knew I wanted to attend Russell Sage since I came to see the campus. It's a small campus, but that's why I like it. All the teachers get to know you and that is why they are willing to help. The College has many activities, tutoring, and clubs to join. It's also big on empowering women. There are certaintly downsides to the College, such as some teachers. However, I think every College has downsides.", 'By far and hands down the best educators and education!\nMy daughter is receiving a wonderful education! Smaller classes = more one on one. If you fail here, your doing something wrong. EVERYONE is so helpful!\nHighly recommended!!', 'The campus is located in my favorite area of Troy,  along River Street and the adjacent streets. As a visitor it is a great place to find a nice spot outside to sit and read.  There is also a guest Wi-Fi signal available.']

name: St Bonaventure University
reviews: ['Gorgeous campus. I did a presentation there, had a tour and lunch. Students are welcoming and friendly, they held the door, said hello, and made a great impression.', 'The nation’s first Franciscan university, St. Bonaventure University is a community committed to transforming the lives of our students inside and outside the classroom, inspiring in them a lifelong commitment to service and citizenship. In 2020, St. Bonaventure was named the #2 regional university value in New York and #3 in the North by U.S. News and World Report. The occupational therapy program that launched in August 2021 has outstanding faculty and state-of-the art facilities. Go Bonnie’s!', 'Beautiful, nice campus and wonderful staff and friendly students.', 'Great walking or biking trails with good parking.  The only complaint I have is that while the signage is nice,  none of the birds or animals depicted were sitting or standing nearby.', 'Always a great time watching a game at the Reilly Center!!']

name: St. Francis College
reviews:
['Our daughter went to St. Francis College and graduated.  She loved her time there. We were very happy with the support she received  especially from her water polo coach, Carl Quigley.', 'SFC is a small college but don’t underestimate the professors here. Most of the professors I’ve had are some of the most patience, sweet, and inspiring people. They are all unique in their own ways and genuinely care about your grades and your education. The new campus location is also very spacious and refreshing.', "I'd say it was a pretty good experience while it lasted. I was only there for a tour of the place. I'd say the place is pretty good for cheaper tuition than most universities and cheaper prices for food if you're buying any in the lounge/cafeteria. Definitely a place to go with friends though. Doesn't seem as welcoming if you're alone, introverted, or not as outgoing.", "I am going to be a Sophomore this year and I couldn't be happier with the school. All the faculty and staff made the transition from high school to college very smooth. The faculty and staff care about how your are doing both academically and personally. From the minute I stepped through the door at my open house, I was automatically welcomed with open arms to the St. Francis College family.  Everyone from the students to the faculty members are friendly as well, it is really easy to find a solid group of people who will be by your side for a long time. Its also the perfect school for students who want to be highly involved on campus. There are lots of opportunities from department jobs, to research assistants, to clubs and sports teams. I myself am a member of two of their 21 NCAA Division 1 teams, as well as a handful of other clubs and organizations on campus, from Student Government to the Latin American Society. This is the perfect school for someone who wants to be an individual and find themselves, rather than just be one of a few thousand. In just one year I have felt myself grow so much and I can't wait to see what else SFC has in store for me.", 'i visited for a couple hours in September for an immediate decision, and i got in!

everyone from the front desk/security to admissions counselor himself were very friendly! the school itself is small, but the building is small and compact and everything was clean, nice, and updated!

i am so tremendously excited to be a SFC student and in the class of 2024!']

name: St Lawrence University
reviews: ["May be the worst college ever. Go here if you're weird and dont want to have any fun!", 'Beautiful campus, friendly and helpful staff.', 'I went to SLU many years ago. I’ve lived all over the country. And who are the folks I keep up with? My SLU friends. It is truly a family.', "The worst part about St. Lawrence University is that a lot of people will never get to experience it. This school is truly special and fosters a specific mentality of work-hard play-hard. The school is ranked #3 in the country for alumni-callbacks (behind Harvard and Yale) and it is apparent why it is if you go here.  People here are extremely extraverted and friendly. The entire school does stuff with each other due to the tight-knit community here. The wet-campus policy allows nightlife to be vibrant and inclusive to all students. There is truly no other school like SLU in America if not the entire world. I highly recommend taking a tour and experiencing what SLU has to offer to you or your children. You won't regret it.", 'I couldn\'t wish for a better "onward and upward"experience for my daughters. The campus is doing everything they can to preserve as much as they can despite COVID, and they must be doing okay because my daughters were dying to get back to stir up more of their weirdo trouble.']

name: St. Thomas Aquinas College
reviews: ['We visited for one of their barbecue tour days. It was awesome. You will have the chance to talk directly with the Director of Admissions. She is incredibly knowledged. Do not hesitate asking anything, she will not go around and will give you a sincere answer. Talking to her after the tour is the best part of the visit. We visited many colleges and this is the first time that someone dedicated so much time to us. Go and visit ... you will be surprised of how well they treat you ( and feed you).', 'St. Thomas Aquinas College provides opportunity, and space to excel in your major of choice. I highly recommend going to this school to prepare your future careers in the best way possible. As for the Computer Science majors, this school is by far the best choice.', 'Great campus..Great school..', 'Smells']

name: Sarah Lawrence College
reviews:
['Hands down the best Liberal Arts education in the US - awesome faculty that goes above and beyond', 'Love Yoko & Everything She Dun 4 Jon 💝', "I visit this college on Google maps and I like it most and I want to study in this college but I am poor and I can't reach here", 'I figured since the top review is from some guy who didn’t go here, that I would leave a review too. Since I’m a guy who didn’t go here.

Great school! I didn’t go here, I dropped out of CUNY John Jay. But I’ll say bronxville is pretty nice!', "Chose Hampshire College over both Emerson College in Boston and SLC in the end, because being from Brooklyn, I wanted to go to college up in New England FOR REAL and I needed the COMPLETELY interdisciplinary academic structure Hampshire offers. I figured the Amherst/Northampton area & Hampshire were more indicative of that then Boston or Bronxville would have been. 😁 Still, I ❤️'d all three colleges pretty equally, and for awhile it was a toss up as to where I'd go. They were my top three college choices after all. I also applied to nearby Manhattanville College (now Manhattanville University) & SUNY Purchase.

I REALLY ❤️'d SLC's Theater & Film Production Departments, because of the affiliation SLC has with the British American Drama Academy (BADA) & Yale School of Drama. Had I gone to SLC I probably would have had an easier route into BADA for Field Study as an undergrad & then Yale for grad school; but I still managed to get there via Hampshire, since Hampshire and SLC do have a fairly good connection with each other as well."]

name: Schenectady County Community College
reviews:
['So far not a good experience because of the lack of communication with the ADA office and my professor. My online class is not user friendly. My grades and assignments are not being posted and I am worried my class work is going to suffer.

The handicap buttons on the doors DO NOT WORK!! I broke both my legs and use a walker so it is hard to open the heavy doors. There are no handicap buttons on the doors at Center City at all either. Which is NOT HANDICAP FRIENDLY!

In all ,this experience so far has not been stellar because I thought the standards at SCCC were high. I was hoping for a second chance at this college because first time was rough too! I was wrong again this time!', "Overall it really depends on what program you go to school for that will determine your experience. I went for Criminal Justice and had a lot of good professors, had Advisor Buffardi who was a very pleasant man to know and study under.

Costs were generally cheap, except for the textbooks (those you should buy online for MUCH less). It can be a pain getting started because many of the different admin departments don't communicate well and the general advisors don't know what they're talking about. Once you get by the starting gate though things are much clearer and easier. Overall I was happy with my choice to stay local and get my degree through SCCC.", 'Great value for young ones pursuing a degree.  Several great degree programs that can get working right away.', 'Schenectady County Community College is a wonderful institution. Two of my children and my wife are alumni. The school is well known for their music and culinary arts programs. For young people just graduated from high school this is a great school as the campus is compact and they have housing available, which is rare for a community college. The school also would be good for adult learners as well.', "SCC was the worst experience of my life and was a waste. I dropped out due to personal issues and the school was just not helpful (granted I was so confused on what I wanted to do and had no help to figure out what would be best for me) my counselor was HORRIBLE! I told her all my issues and she was absolutely rude I told her I was scared of my ex at the time and scared about not being able to feed my cats (I always managed to do it no matter what) and SHE TOLD ME TO GET RID OF MY CATS! WHAT KIND OF COUNSLOR SAYS THAT HONESTLEY THE WORST! I would give this place a 1 star but I did like SOME of the professors there. But overall don't waste your time."]

name: Siena College
reviews:
['After being accepted to Binghamton and other universities, my daughter chose Siena University—and it has been the best decision she ever made. The campus is beautiful, safe, and easy to navigate. Small class sizes allow professors to know their students personally, offering guidance and support every step of the way. The education is exceptional, with dedicated professors and outstanding resources. Because the community is close-knit, students quickly form meaningful connections, and everyone is welcoming and friendly, creating a truly supportive environment. Siena provides a top-notch education that is hard to find at other universities. For anyone seeking an education that fosters growth and builds a strong foundation for future success, Siena University is the perfect choice.', 'I was a vendor at the Siena Career & Expo 2026 Job Fair, and I have to say they were the BEST hosts!! They offered a glorious spread, featuring a variety of the freshest fruits, veggies and cheeses, in addition to their scrumptious buffalo chicken dip served with crispy homemade tortillas and kettle chips. Everything was fantastic.
The students were even more amazing! They arrived on time, completely polished, and so eager with enthusiasm.  It was a true pleasure to partake in this event at Siena. I almost wanted to go back to college!', "I graduated from this college in 1987.  I visited campus and toured the math and computer science departments recently.  I was very disappointed.  One of the professors said there is no point in doing research.  The faculty had students explain their projects.  I felt bad for the students, since it appeared the faculty provided little actual support.  It sounded like they were doing REU projects, just to say they do undergraduate research.

The cost has gone way up.  Not many courses are taught by friars, as opposed to the 1980s.  I'm not surprised, since the two friars I knew when I went there, both left the priesthood and married students.  It was offensive to listen to a former priest brag how he married my former RA and left the priesthood.  I went on to obtain a Ph.D. and publish 40 papers, but they had no interest in any of the research I did.

While I was visiting campus, one of the professors who has been there since 1987, explained how he contacted a former student to try to get a major donation.  He said the former student agreed to donate millions.  I could tell where the story was going.  The former student overpromised and did not have the ability to donate what he promised.  It was obvious the professor told this story several times and it was difficult to hear.", "Good parking, good seats, women's basketball.", 'Great university, close to Albany but still very open and welcoming.']

name: Skidmore College
reviews: ["Beautiful campus but far too controlling according to our niece who attended Skidmore. Didn't stop us from getting her a graduation brick.", 'We drove around campus to take a look for our daughter. As we were there on a  weekend, we were not able to take a tour.  The campus looks lovely.', 'Absolutely gorgeous scenery, generally pleasant architecture with some decent student amenities.', '😊❤️👌👍', 'Awesome education and culturally diverse events.']

name: St. Joseph's University-New York
reviews: ['St. Joseph’s University in Brooklyn is consistently highlighted by students and alumni I know for successfully combining a personalized, supportive learning environment with the immense practical advantages of its NYC location. Friends often emphasize the small class sizes and the accessibility of dedicated faculty members, which fosters truly meaningful mentorship and academic growth. The campus provides a strong sense of community, a quality often hard to find in larger urban institutions, while still offering robust professional opportunities in fields like nursing and education. This institution genuinely focuses on student success and ethical development, making it an excellent choice for those seeking both individual attention and career readiness.', 'Students receive guidance, mentorship, and practical experiences that enhance their learning.', 'I absolutely love this school. If I’m picking knits, they’re a smidge understaffed depending on your major, but if you put in even the slightest effort, you can get as good an education here as just about anywhere else.  I’d steer away from the online courses personally, but to each their own. Any criticisms I have, however, are monstrously overshadowed by the location alone. It’s a dreamy place to ponder the arts, and minutes away from a nearly infinite array of legendary locales. You can get a life’s worth of educating without even attending a class.  The collegiate experience is like a super bonus. The classes are generally fine, and some are phenomenal, like poetry and music in cinema, and pretty much all my history courses were awesome. I had one “bad” class, but that’s a pretty standard college experience no matter where you go…so I’d go here again and again, if for nothing else, the location alone.  Brilliant pubs and restaurants right around the corner, so if you have a terrible professor, again pretty common no matter the school, just pop out for a beer and a snack to take the edge off.  Good to go. Go Bears!!!', '9/10 times  Professors are great. Every school has a couple of poor professors. Scheduling is terrible. Not enough classes offered. They will most likely not accommodate. You must accommodate to them sometimes feels like the school will not work with you. Very Frustrating. Classes themselves are mostly good. Parking is usually not a huge issue. School has potential to be 5 stars but lack of classes available and consistent poor schedules block that potential. I put 3 but I would give it 2 1/2', 'As far as the graduate nursing program goes, to say the least, there is room for improvement.  Although most of the teachers were knowledgeable, there was one instructor who was both disorganized and maniacal.  She single handedly ruined the experience and many of my classmates grades because she was unable to provide consistent instruction for multiple semesters.  Her ineptitudes and inappropriateness were brought to light however the program continues to struggle under her instruction.  Additionally, the behind the scenes aspects like health clearance are also wildly disorganized, last minute and rude.  WHAT A MESS!']

name: St. John Fisher University
reviews:
['If you are a student you must find an internship on your own

Do not wait to start looking

Website is not truthful and the internship course does not place you somewhere

Handshake is not that good either for searching for opportunities

Applied to 1200+ positions with very few replies and less than 15 interviews

Professors are great, career services could be a lot better

Found out about local employer events after I graduated and was not eligible for any of their internships. Should be advertising this to students in main foot traffic areas.

Did not find out about scholarships they offer until it was too late. Should be advertised as well.

Summer research opportunities available but not advertised

Very disappointed in my experience. Feels like I wasted 100k and 4 years.', 'Going to the Mental Health Counseling Graduate Program here is the first decision I ever made that I knew was a "100 percent yes" decision and it is, to this day, one of the most fulfilling decisions of my life. The campus is beautiful and peaceful. The professors helped me learn and grow in ways I couldn't have even fathomed at the time of choosing the university. I feel that the relationships made are lifelong ones and I consider it one of the most positive and integrative and uplifting choices I've ever made. I cannot recommend it enough and think fondly of my education and relationships made there every week. It started a path which has led to a meaningful and purposeful career. I can say with assuredness that I am now making a wonderful living doing something I enjoy because of the education I received at St John Fisher 🙏🏼✨', 'THE FOOD IS A LIE, they say it’s the best in New York but they lost that ranking 6 years ago! I’ve been here for 4 years and each year the quality and selection only got worse and worse, the food you see when visiting is not what they will actually serve 99% of the time. The only decent thing is that they added occasional halal food options which taste better even if you’re not Muslim. Parking spaces are non existent for residents, you have to park 10 minutes away in the far lot. You don’t get climate control until your sophomore year, even then it’s fake and barely actually impacts the temperature. They choose which days it works and which days “we can survive” without it. They set whether you get to heat or cool the rooms, switching heat/cool modes doesn’t actually do anything. When it’s hot outside and the thermostat is set to 60, the room never gets below 70 degrees. The rooms are tiny and shared, unless you’re physically severely handicapped good luck ever getting a single room.
Now on the academic side, it doesn’t get much better, the science courses are shallow and don’t go in depth to prepare you for the benchmark exams like the MCAT/DAT or the real world. You’re forced to take 50% “core classes” which are just pointless boring liberal arts courses that heavily push an agenda on you. 95% of them are things like “gender studies, LGBT in education, race and social justice”. The more moderate classes are very rare and are immediately taken up by upper class men so you’re forced to go into those classes. If you have ADHD, run away because good luck ever getting the motivation to turn in their depressingly boring and long frequent assignments. I’ve excelled in my major science courses but nearly flunked out because of their “core classes” which couldn’t be easier if they weren’t so long and boring. I have to give it to them that at least the security team got better recently, previously they had major power trip issues and they would take out their frustration out on you. The scholarship offer is what sold me on this place and honestly I wish I had gone somewhere else even if it cost thrice as much. Most science classes have been cut down further since and it’s less deserving of the title “university” than it has ever been. They waste our budget on stupid things like rebuilding a library that worked fine previously instead of giving us decent food, or actual climate control, or parking lots, or a better core class variety, at least. I have to give it to them, most* of their science teachers are good people and the only reason I survived this place so long. Even with nearly a full ride, if I could go back in time and go anywhere else I would. Don’t let the scholarships fool you, it’s more of a corrupt high school than a college. Cough up the extra buck for a better place! I just hope my academic record is salvageable after these “core” classes that I refused to do. God forbid I don’t want to be force fed an agenda that has nothing to do with my major!', 'Had a great day watching the Buffalo Bills practice. All the staff were friendly and helpful with directions', 'Went for Bills practice camp. It is well organized and enjoyable. But very hot.']

name: St Paul's School of Nursing-Staten Island
reviews:
['Great school .. had a blast at grad fest ? Thanks to Chaturi De Silva the Student Success Coordinator. She did a great job with the planning and everything went smoothly. Can’t wait for graduation and pinning !', 'I just started as a Medical Assistant at St. Paul’s after my sister has been a part of the program and I have to say I enjoy the curriculum that they have to offer here. The program is fast pace and as much difficulty as it may offer, it is enjoyable. The staff are very dedicated to what they teach here and care about both Nursing and MA students. They take consideration in feedback or suggestions to their program so it’s an overall good experience for everyone.', 'Just graduated in august and passed my NCLEX this october! Professor Gallotta was the best teacher and mentor, she really made my experience at st. paul’s so much better!!! Nursing school is tough and she was always there with the best advice and guidance. Her stories and encouragement really made me so excited to start my career in the field! ♥️', 'It’s been 13 years since I earned my ASN from Saint Paul’s University, and I can confidently say it changed my life. The program provided an incredible foundational education: the quality of instruction, clinical experience, and faculty support prepared me not only to pass the NCLEX on my first attempt, but also to excel in my BSN and now APRN journey. It also instilled in me tools of excellence which rewarded me several nursing excellence and patient satisfaction awards, board certifications, and financial success.

I’m especially grateful to the Registrar’s Office, Silvy and Danya, who recently went above and beyond to help me with transcript requests for graduate school. Their dedication and responsiveness made a meaningful difference.

Saint Paul’s gave me the strong start I needed, and I’ll always be proud to be a graduate. My professors were amazing and left a lasting impression in my life. We were a community of student nurses who I still stay in touch with. It was the best years of my life. Thank you!', 'I am truly grateful for the support and guidance I received from the Dean at St. Paul’s School of Nursing. He went above and beyond to help me achieve my goals and even supported me in securing a great job after graduation something that was a very big deal for me and my future. His dedication to students is clear, and he is genuinely committed to our success both in school and beyond. I couldn’t have asked for better leadership during my journey at St. Paul’s -']

name: St. John's University-New York
reviews:
["St. John's University’s Manhattan Campus at 101 Astor Place is frequently lauded in my professional circles as a masterfully positioned academic hub where Vincentian values of service meet the sophisticated demands of the global insurance and risk management sectors. Based on countless conversations with alumni and local industry leaders, it is clear that the campus offers a substantive, high-caliber environment where the intimate class sizes and direct access to Manhattan’s corporate heart are cited as transformative for career trajectory. It is genuinely impressive to see how the institution maintains such a transparent commitment to ethical leadership and social mobility, qualities that my acquaintances often praise for creating a community that is as compassionate as it is competitive. In the broader public consensus, the Astor Place campus is held in high regard as a distinguished boutique-style university experience, proving that a mission-driven education can thrive with elegance and academic rigor in the center of New York’s most dynamic district.", 'Nice modern building of St. John University. Nice area to sit and people watch.', "St. John's Manhattan Campus located on East 8th Street and 3rd Avenue.

The campus is in a relatively new building.  The building was probably finished and ready for occupation a few years back.

The building is a commercial property with lots of office spaces.  The ground fflooe have a CVS Pharmacy.

All around the campus is your historical neighborhood of East Village.", "New York is beautiful, there are a lot interesting places to visit, with wonderful people to know. I loved to study at St Johns university. There you study and practice hard. The classes are fantastic, with dynamic professors. St. Jonh's, I'll miss it a lot!", "The St. John's Manhattan campus is home to the school of Risk Management, Insurance, and Actuarial Science. It is also home to the Davis Library. A very nice building and staff overall."]

name: Sullivan County Community College
reviews: ['Great experience, wonderful staff, I went to the Fall Festival and it was great', 'We went to SUNY Sullivan grounds for kite flying festival. Went with my grandson and thoroughly enjoyed. Lots of people with colorful kites. Weather was sunny and nice. A memorable kite flying experience !!', 'The Biology Professor is horrible at teaching despite her knowledge and does not seem to care much about her students. other than that the school is pretty nice. i commute but the dorms are a plus for some.', "Great College and amazing professors. I grew up and learned how to be an educated young man with the professor's being my mentors. I will especially miss Dr.  Tom Lambert,  and Dr.  Tom Martin.  Amazing Professor's and People.. My life will never be the same. And especially with Jim Windrle benig the best Financial Aid Director ever to help a student graduate. Thank you all.... I'll miss my friends most of all. My heart is heavy when I know I'll never see them again.", 'The best college to start off your education to a brighter future']

name: SUNY College of Technology at Alfred
reviews: ["as a kid from nyc coming here was one of the best decisions of my life, the nature and quietness of it has been one of the best things in my life over the last 4 years. The partying is also crazy around August & sept. You gotta have a good friend group to pass the time though. Most professors genuinely care about you and your future, I recommend this school a lot especially if you've been in a big city your whole life and need a break", 'Great place. Beautiful plac3 in the fall season. Small school in the middle of the mountains. Safe and quiet. Not a party school which will allow you to concentrate on your studies. Although Alfred Village is a short walking distance away the closest town with amenities and stores like Walmart, Aldi, is 14km away.', "The service was good, but the english muffin and toast was not toasted all the way.\nThe home fries came out with bell peppers that were not advertised and The home fries weren't cooked enough and came out Really greasy. The scrambled eggs didn't come out scrambled. Hopefully next time we go, they have all these problems fixed.\nAnd to add-on, they don't offer you water when you first get there.", 'My name’s Big Strong Eric, and I love Alfred State (especially the Darth Vader statue). Great place to hang out with my bro Matty B Raps and lift weights.', 'The welding program is good. Helped me go from nothing to being able to stick weld in this moment in time. The distance from everything though is annoying at times']

name: SUNY College of Technology at Canton
reviews:
['This school is great. Professor Wang specifically, and all his colleagues are the best. Both myself and my daughter not only earned degrees in Cybersecurity, but we have learned so much.

Professor Minhua Wang is dedicated to the success of his students. It is obvious that he is relentless in the pursuit of education. I can only hope in the future, I have professors like him.', 'Not a student but I have benefitted from their Small Business Development Center (SBDC). If you’re in the entrepreneurial spirit, definitely reach out to them. They’ve also started to offer summer camps for local kids.

That’s already more than what another university nearby does for locals.', 'I’d rate zero if I could, the people in the one hop shop are hardly useful, food stinks, and the job acceptance rate is terrible. Even if you get state aid, you’ll likely still end up paying nearly $80,000 for a 4 year degree. Some of the faculty are helpful but most of them give up on their students very easily.', 'The financial aid office is a mess. Nice people who help when they can but end up messing it up in the end causing you to either owe more money or dropping your schedule. If I could find another school in NYS who had my program I would gladly transfer immediately. Not worth the time or money.
Update:
They do not fix their pot holes all year and it creates bathtub sized pot holes that ruin your wheel bearings.
Do not go to this school.', 'This school was nothing but a nightmare for me. The Financial aid office screwed me up. I did a whole semester, fine and great. Come second semester I’m in class for over a month and they pull me out in the hall to tell me something is wrong with everything and that I shouldn’t have been coming to class and everything I did for the month didn’t count. Took me years to pay back that loan for absolutely NOTHING. Every time I needed some help, they’d make me an appointment, and I’d trek through snow a mile away just for them to cancel on me. Just beware. I should have sued them for doing me like this.']

name: SUNY College of Technology at Delhi
reviews: ['I would not recommend suny Delhi due to the sheer amount of sickening food, greed, dishonesty, and lack of consideration for the students. The few programs that make your time there worth while are over shadowed by the horrible attitude of both staff and administrators. The food has gotten worse every semester, yet somehow has also become more expensive. School has been purposely over enrolling students which resulted in some students having to sleep in the lounge or being absolutely cramped into a triple room that isn’t big enough at all. And when all those extra students drop out, guess who keeps the money?', 'They have awesome advisors and professors. One of the best professors there is Steve Calabrese! You can really tell he is genuinely passionate about his job,  and his students success.', 'SUNY Delhi is amazing.  I went for 4 years and loved every moment of it.  My professors for the most part were consistently respectful and supportive within my academic endeavors.  The culture of student life and clubs is amazing, I was able to dive into so many different areas of campus life and get involved in many different spaces.  Some highlights was my time spend with the college players, a remarkable theatre arts club that’s is very loving and inviting. Being able to be a founder of a now very successful organization being the Environmental Studies and Sustainability Club (ESSC). As well as my Professor and in many ways I consider a mentor Dr. Jack Tessier, he is phenomenal and not only created and over sees the Sustainability B.S program that I was the first ever graduate of. But also allows and encourages my to continue to be involved as an alumni and allows me to come and speak to upcoming graduates about a career in Environmental Education.  All in all wouldn’t have done anything differently.   Graduate of 2020 and 2022', 'Awesome experience for the ages...very serene, spectacular, and beautiful mountainous views.', 'I went on a tour today for this school and from everything that I heard they have everything I needed in a school. They allow freshman’s to have cars on campus for a $168 fee (that covers the whole year). They allow you to stay on campus all four years of college and have specific dorms for upperclassman like juniors and seniors. The school and view is beautiful. The school it’s self seems to have a great support system. Everyone seemed friendly and welcoming. The food tasted good from my experience. I recommend this school for anyone in New York looking to go away from home but still be in their home state. I enjoyed my tour here and hope to enjoy my four years here.']

name: SUNY College of Agriculture and Technology at Cobleskill
reviews: ["While our son currently attends the college and enjoys the College, as a parent I feel that SUNY Cobleskill in the Agricultural Department needs to distance themselves from working or being affiliated with United Ag and Turf which is at the very essence is the John Deere Corporation. The Company itself is at the center of an FTC investigation which is proving that John Deere is guilty of violating Right To Repair Laws with its tractors among other investigations that don't paint the Company in a good light. A College of higher learning should be also instructing it's students in how to conduct themselves in an ethical manner and having students to an internship within a Company that is being investigated isn't a good look for a College.", 'I went to SUNY Cobleskill for a education workshop. Found the place to be extremely clean and quiet. They also have a shuttle to take you around the campus. Well organized, clean and quiet. Go SUNY!', 'Amazing place. Love walking through center of campus especially fall time!', "Beautiful and large area for taking long walks. It's a pastoral and scenic campus.", "We went for the trick or treat festival they had there tonight.  It was a great time for all the kids. Trick or treat y'all. I give them a 🎃🎃🎃🎃🎃 rating."]

name: Farmingdale State College
reviews: ['As I am a transfer student, I felt professors are more friendly and helpful compared to Nassau Community College I attended. I FULLY RECOMMENDED YOU TO APPLY TO THIS SCHOOL!!!', 'I’m not even attending this school…I called about 20 times in a single day to ask about admissions, which led me to the reviews because I believe if they cannot simply answer the phone then there has to be something wrong…All the high reviews are probably fake and made up by the facility. Thank GOODNESS I am a review reader, besides the unprofessionalism there is clearly a lot more I do not want to involve myself in. I will not be applying here.', '2025 graduation lasted from "doors open at 5:30PM" until nearly 11PM, 5.5hours of graduation ceremony. Arguably the slowest, most disorganized, and rowdy graduation ceremony I\'ve ever been to. Very disappointing and unbecoming of a school thats been around for over 100 years, you\'d think this would be more streamlined by now, but you\'d be wrong. It took so long, most of the graduates left after getting their degree and missed the ceremonial hat toss.', '1star for WiFi…i can’t tell how disappointed about the WiFi connection. name: Stony Brook University
reviews:
["The high reviews for this school is why I attended the university for a few semesters, but after circling back to those same reviews I am convinced they live in an alternate universe where the school is actually wonderful! Spoiler alert! It's not! Food is awful, professors don't care for the most part and actually nobody cares about you besides your depressed friends trying to survive along with you. 3hrs+ to drive here from Queens just to realize there's no parking as the alternative is commuting by train, which takes 2hrs+ from Jamaica and Long Island as the useless diesel trains are probably still in use and keep breaking down/ have delays. If you want to actually learn and be happy, go elsewhere!", 'Stony Brook University is an outstanding institution that combines excellent academics with a supportive and engaging campus environment. The faculty are highly knowledgeable, approachable, and dedicated to helping students succeed both academically and personally.

The campus is spacious, clean, and well-maintained, providing modern facilities that enhance learning and research opportunities. I particularly appreciate the university’s focus on innovation, career readiness, and extracurricular activities that foster personal growth and leadership skills.

Whether you’re pursuing academics, research, or community involvement, Stony Brook University provides a vibrant and nurturing environment. I highly recommend Stony Brook University to anyone seeking a high-quality, well-rounded university experience.', "It's just a research school. reviews:
['My experiance is limited to reviewing an article regarding

Dean', '2023 November 18. Visited 6 pm on tour w SUNY SA Fall Conference....so, dark out.

name: SUNY Brockport
reviews: ['As a transfer student who had attended 2-3 schools before this I cannot in good conscience recommend a school that is so incredibly disorganized, a student could run it better. Every department you email (give or take a few good professors) will send you in a back and forth loop with no solution in sight. Check it out!', 'I can\'t say I\'m a fan of this school, and if I had it to do over, I would start a different degree somewhere else rather than transferring to this one as the only school available that would take under half my credits. reviews: ['I graduated with Bachelor’s Degree from Buffalo State (Class of 2015& Masters in 2018). Buff State is One of the best SUNY schools for Criminal Justice. Thank you.', 'I love Buffalo State it’s a university not a community college so you get top tier education here one of the best in the country in my opinion']

name: State University of New York at Cortland
reviews:
['SUNY Cortland feels less like a student-centered institution and more like a revenue-driven operation wrapped in a college brand. The parking situation alone speaks volumes. There are clearly not enough spaces for the number of students, staff, and visitors, yet enforcement is immediate, aggressive, and unforgiving. Instead of meaningfully expanding parking or improving clarity around policies, the system seems built around rapid ticketing and strict penalties.

Tickets are issued quickly, sometimes for overlapping or confusingly worded violations, with no meaningful warning system or grace period. The volume and speed of enforcement make it hard not to question whether revenue has become a priority over fairness and common-sense solutions.

What makes this more frustrating is that leadership has the authority and resources to address the root issue — lack of adequate parking — but enforcement appears to be the primary response. When top administrators are compensated at high levels, it raises reasonable expectations that systemic problems like this will be solved rather than monetized.

The so-called parking appeals process and review board do little to restore confidence. The process feels procedural rather than impartial, with outcomes that seem predetermined and little room for real discretion. Instead of functioning as an independent check on over-enforcement, it comes across as an extension of the same system.

Beyond parking, the campus culture often feels more focused on social life than academics. A noticeable party atmosphere and inconsistent oversight contribute to an environment that can feel chaotic rather than scholarly. For a school that promotes academic excellence, the overall atmosphere doesn’t consistently reflect that mission.

Once tuition is paid, accountability seems to fade. Concerns are met with bureaucracy rather than solutions. Visiting your student shouldn’t feel like navigating a system designed to extract additional fees. Prospective students and parents should carefully consider whether this is the environment they want to invest in — financially and academically.', 'Very friendly admissions staff. Great tour guides.  Be prepared for a lot of walking.  Be prepared for hills. Appreciated our tour guides comments regarding their experiences as students at Cortland.', 'I was here teaching for a day and supporting faculty students and others. The students faculty, administrators and facilities are magnificent. They are innovative and forward thinking. The buildings are beautiful.', "Great athletic/sports facilities. There's something for everyone's interests,  including games, Xbox, pool tables, etc.", 'Nice complex... field turf']
