name: SUNY College at Geneseo
reviews:
['Last week I visited a dreamlike place as a guest, at an event being held there, an unimaginable place, something like a paradise for young people with super-gifted brains.
Young people with a heightened spirituality, as if emerged from a portal to a parallel universe.
And the wonderful thing is that I was there, sharing the same environment with those amazing young people.
Then confirm the truth of the proverb of the most famous physicist of the twentieth century, albert einstein, which stated "imagination is better than knowledge".
I close my eyes and imagine being next to einstein himself at the university of zurich, in his younger years, or the tesla in graz or stephen hawking in cambridge.
They all stated  as a fact the professions they would practice, with unquestionable certainty, despite none of them being older than nineteen years old.
They did not know the future, but they were creating it guided  by divinity and like the great men that history has produced, they already imagin themselves, practicing the profession they chose out by vocation, to make our planet a better world.
This place is geneseo university, located in the center of the city  of the same name, in livingston county in the finger lakes, region of new york.
It's currently the cradle  of this  new generation of gifted brains.
With a well-earned academic reputation, it's undoubtedly in that place , the future is being woven, for a better present.', 'I would not recommend this school for families with a child who has Type 1 diabetes. The nearest emergency room is over 20 miles away, and there is no program in place to support students with this specific medical condition. Although my daughter loves the school and plans to major in Accounting with a minor in Data Analytics, I am not willing to risk her health being jeopardized. SUNY Plattsburgh offers better support and has an ER located just two minutes away.', 'The campus is beautiful, a lot of green and you get to see the sunset as well. Its just the waether seen it can get cold at night.', "Ya can just lay-back on the campus or sit in the library, and dream about life in WWII. That's cause the National Warplane Museum, is in the background.", 'Beautiful campus, cute shops, and an amazing event for the eclipse! Thanks for the great time.']

name: State University of New York at New Paltz
reviews:
['I had to drop out after just one semester because of bigotry from a few faculty and staff members, and the school's refusal to take it seriously. It got worse over time. I couldn't even finish one of my classes because of it

I was subjected to hate for my assigned gender, less fortunate financial status, both real and not real but assumed disabilities, for being transgender, for being older than most other students, and for being an abuse survivor

It included things like being told I'm not welcome on campus, being told I have to hide signs of a physical disability because it made a faculty member uncomfortable, having my gender identity policed, being told I should only take "easy" classes and not challenge myself academically, being told I have to take exams in a different room than other students - for no reason, being mocked based on a disability I was assumed to have based on misogynist stereotypes, being victim-blamed, being stared at excessively in a hateful way, being singled out and humiliated in class in front of other students, and more

This was limited to a few people. I got along with the other students, and everyone who wasn't part of the group harassing me. I can see how some people have positive experiences at this school

But the school really needs to work on making inclusion more than just a superficial part of their brand, and instead make it real. I took all the right steps to respond to what I was dealing with - met with the people involved, contacted the DEI office, contacted the Title IX office. Things got worse and not better

For context, I didn't do anything that would provoke a reaction. I did dye my hair different rainbow colors, but otherwise, I just showed up for class, acted like any other student, didn't wear anything controversial, didn't say anything controversial. There was no reason for me to be treated this way. And it started at orientation, before there had been any interaction at all

I had been excited to finally get to go to school and study what I had always wanted to study - after a lifetime of not having had those kinds of opportunities. And I probably won't get to go back and try again

Also: The Hudson Valley, being rural, was not a diversity-friendly place in general. I also dealt with hate off campus at my job and in other places. This made everything worse. I think the school should be aware or this, and make more of an effort to be an exception', "I visited the New Paltz campus for the first time on Wednesday September 18, 2019.  I enjoy visiting colleges and take pictures.  What surprised me is how dated the campus looked.  It reminded of the school I attended in the early seventies. Almost like going back into time. I did ask someone if there are any new buildings or on going construction and she said yes but I didn't see very much activity.  I visited the campus art gallery it was wonderful.  The campus has a couple of lakes but other than that, the SUNY New Paltz campus is as dull as dishwater.", 'My years at this university were nothing short of transformative. The quality of education exceeded my expectations, and the faculty’s dedication to their students was inspiring. The programs are well-structured, combining theoretical knowledge with real-world applications. Beyond academics, the community spirit and cultural diversity enriched my perspective in countless ways. I am proud to be an alumna of such an outstanding institution. The only drawback during my time here was ending up in the older dormitories without air conditioning - a challenge in the warmer months - but it certainly added to the memories and stories I cherish today.', 'Always a warm welcoming visit when I stop by the professors are all amazing and the views around the campus are incredible', 'I love my old school 🙃 Kathleen from the international student office is doing a great job; she was always helpful. I send my greetings to her. Also, I loved going to the theater performances at school. They are very successful 💯']

name: State University of New York at Oswego
reviews: ['During my full fall semester at SUNY Oswego, I had an enriching and multifaceted academic experience. I enrolled in courses such as Intro to Global Studies, Foundations of Sustainability, 20th Century World, Cultural Anthropology, and participated in the College Community Orchestra. These classes offered a comprehensive understanding of global issues, environmental sustainability, historical contexts, and cultural dynamics, while the orchestra provided a creative outlet and a sense of community. The faculty’s commitment to personalized mentorship and immersive, hands-on education greatly enhanced my learning experience.\n\nBeyond academics, SUNY Oswego’s vibrant campus life and supportive community stood out. The university offers over 200 clubs and organizations, fostering an environment where students from diverse backgrounds can connect and grow. I joined around four or five clubs during my time there, and one of my favorite activities was ice skating—it was not only fun but also a great way to bond with others and enjoy the beautiful winter season. The picturesque lakeside campus provided stunning views and an inspiring setting for personal and academic development. Additionally, SUNY Oswego’s emphasis on affordability ensures that students can pursue a world-class education without excessive financial burden. Overall, my time at SUNY Oswego was intellectually stimulating and personally fulfilling, offering a well-rounded college experience.', 'My daughter attends school here and has had a great experience. The campus is beautiful and the school is constantly improving the facilities.  The administration is very proactive and for a small college I’m impressed with how much they do for the students.  Campus life is welcoming and they offer many things to do outside of the classroom.  Winter can be tough with winds off the lake but school is not in session during the worst part of winter.  Fall and spring are nice and summer is beautiful.   The town is small but they had recently been awarded a huge amount of money by the state and the results are stunning, they have really done a great job improving the downtown and port area and are currently working on a new marina.', 'My son is in his first year at SUNY Oswego and he is absolutely thriving! From the moment we arrived, the campus felt welcoming and full of positive energy. He’s made amazing, lifelong friends and genuinely enjoys his professors, who are supportive, approachable, and clearly passionate about what they teach. The balance between academics, social life, and campus activities has been incredible. As a parent, it’s such a relief to see him so happy, independent, and engaged in college life. SUNY Oswego has truly exceeded our expectations and I couldn’t recommend it more highly for any student starting their journey!', 'Drove north, a little over an hour, to SUNY Oswego to enjoy the day and the performance of SQUONK!  They did not disappoint! Interesting and wonderful musical journey; a crowd pleaser and encouraged crowd interaction of all ages. It was a fun time!  Will go again to spend more time in Oswego!', 'Beautiful setting on Lake Ontario. Seemingly laid back atmosphere, small student-teacher ratio, high tech, great amenities like a stone fireplaces in the dorm lobbies. Modern and contemporary architecture.']

name: SUNY College at Potsdam
reviews: ['A solid campus with good community presence. I like the gym; it’s well-equipped and easy to access. The school also offers programs and events around town that keep things active and connected. Overall, it adds value to the area beyond just academics, making it a good local resource.', 'Thanks to the SUNY Potsdam folks for welcoming so many people and putting on a great SOLAR eclipse yesterday. Such a beautiful and welcoming campus, staff and student body!!!', 'Great school with lots to do for students.  Pretty campus!', 'We just had a conference here. The accommodations and food service were fantastic', 'I went here for a bachelors in criminal justice during Covid. Their program for that is a joke. Open book midterms but the questions were out of chronological order. Professors played favorites with class curriculum then hot button subjects. You would get foreign emails of 3rd party people trying to con you then lock out of your account. I got locked out of my classes then ability to contact professors through outlook. Whenever I tried to get anything fixed it was automated emails giving you the run around. They are impersonal it feels like there’s a huge communication barrier between the instructors and minority students. I felt overworked with the homework assignments writing the same ideas redundantly. They have you redo it if you don’t use the same nomenclature they like. Everything is graded by a TA. It’s the oldest 4 yr school in NY but it’s a joke. If you’re a half decent honor roll student it’s worth a try but it felt like a repeat of everything from prior schooling.']

name: SUNY at Purchase College
reviews: ['I attended a college open house with my daughter today, and it was an exceptional experience. I was surprised by the number of parents and aspiring students at this event. This was my fourth visit, and I must say that this college has much more to offer than I had previously thought. The new president has a unique, down-to-earth personality, which is refreshing. It’s no wonder this college ranks among the top 10 public colleges and eighth in the nation for liberal arts.\n\nI strongly encourage all high school students and their parents to visit this college with an open mind. Ask questions and explore the wide range of curriculum options and opportunities available, as well as the beautiful, open campus environment. Best of luck!', 'I had the privilege of watching the Ethical Culture Fieldston School win the NYSAIS High School  championship on the SUNY Purchase College field. The  turf field itself is magnificent and is the equivalent of any Division 3 college. It has approximately 10 rows of seats for fans around the 1st to 3rd base lines, a good Press box with live announcements, and real dugouts for the teams. In addition, it has enclosed bullpens for pitchers and catchers and a scoreboard. It is wonderful especially for High School  teams.', "I spent a year here before transferring. Terrible quality school with a depressingly negative social scene. Skip Purchase and set your sights higher if at all possible. I've never met a graduate who thinks fondly of Purchase. I have come across many over the years who have had their lives permanently twisted, damaged, and ruined by their time at Purchase. If your future ambition is to work in a cafe or tattoo parlor you might be able to make some worthwhile connections.", 'Very beautiful campus, great presentation, and a great amount of value if you come here. Just not for me', 'In the Fall of 1980 I attended SUNY at Purchase and it was like being in another world. All my life I continually yearned to be at this college because going there was the right choice. The people at this college accepted me for who I am and not,"who I am supposed to be". Where I live now,the people have high expectations of me and constantly expect too much saying that my career just isn\'t good enough. At Purchase, I worked for CIR and I could take my learning step by step. A liberal minded college makes me feel free. I would also read much of Sigmund Freud and this opened my eyes to a world I had never known. No, I don\'t want to go to San Diego or Arizona or even Florida. I consider Purchase my second home. Someday I would like to go back to Purchase and work at CIR, Center for Industrial Resources, in my senior years.']

name: SUNY Old Westbury
reviews:
['It’s a very good school and especially if you don’t want to spend lots of money Suny Old Westbury is a great school for that. The food here is also really good,they have a really nice boba place and also a really delicious ghost kitchen. The best part about the ghost kitchen is that it stays open really late so that when I needed food and had to stay very late for internships, I didn’t have to worry about not getting dinner. The ghost kitchen has many options such as chicken sandwiches and fries and wings and tenders. My favorite order would be a grilled chicken sandwich with fries. It was always fresh and the ingredients never hurt my stomach which says alot about their oil and how much they clean their fryers. They have the best art gallery that always has something new for its visitors and students. The gallery is the Amelie A. Wallace Gallery. They sometimes throw big events that offer food and amazing artwork. Professor Yi who manages the gallery always does a great job and I recommend that any one who visits the SUNY Old Westbury campus should check out the gallery. Lastly all the professors are very enthusiastic and care about their students. I have met so many great people just in those 2 years than I have met since high school. People don’t expect that from a SUNY school but I can say with certainty that you will meet some of the best people here and you will have some great experiences without needing to spend a fortune.', 'It has been a very long time since I visited a University. Now , with my grandchildren entering this world, I thought myself as holding their hand through these doors, instead they held mine as I walked slowly to their new beginning. I'm not going to lie, it was very emotional moment for me. To my surprise the school staff was prepared even for that. Very supportive, kind and understanding. I was not ready to walk long distances during the orientation due to my breathing difficulties/allergies, but they made sure I was informed of all that I "missed" and brought back together with the group when they returned to complete the event. Today, at the end of second week, I see my grandchildren so happy to be a part of this school and looking forward to all it has to offer.  May God's blessing surrounds everyone at this Campus so they can all arrive at their destination, SUCCESS!', "It was raining heavily today. The school's large parking lot is almost always full every day, so I can only choose to park in a farther parking lot and then walk to the classroom. So I brought an umbrella with me, otherwise my clothes would get wet. When I was almost at the classroom, I chose to go to the bathroom to put my umbrella away, because I didn't want to dirty the classroom floor with my umbrella. Because of this, when I came to get my umbrella after class, it was taken away. To be precise, it felt like it was taken away by the cleaner. After all, no one would be so poor as to steal an umbrella. Then I went to the library, hoping that the staff there could help me. But they said that they didn't know or have any contact with the cleaners of the new academic building. I also expressed my understanding, and then I asked for the phone number of their cleaning department, and they said they didn't have any. This surprised me a little that the administrators of a school had no contact information or communication channels with each other. Although this umbrella is not worth much even if it is new, this experience made me realize that if you leave some valuables in the classroom or bathroom or somewhere in the school in the future, the school may not be able to find them for you. This experience made me very disappointed. From now on, I will bring my umbrella into the classroom no matter how dirty it is.", "SUNY Old Westbury My 2nd Home from 89 to 93! I don't know where to begin all I can say is this place was 100% instrumental in my lyfe! I have the greatest memories and resilent past times..93!!!Rho Rhose Angie", "The bad reviews are outdated - the school has done a lot to improve the campus for both residents and commuters. I transferred here 2 years ago from a different school, and am really so happy with my decision.

The campus is beautiful and makes you forget that you're still on Long Island. You'll find some professors you don't love anywhere, but to my surprise I've met some of the best I've ever had (better than the private school I transferred from)

Making friends as a commuter could be hard for some, but the people I've met here are kinder and friendlier than anywhere else I've been.

Yes, some of the buildings are a bit run down, and yes the school doesn't have an A++ reputation. But it really defied my expectations for a lesser known SUNY school.

If you're debating it, just know a bunch of people in your position were also just as skeptical - it's not that bad :)"]

name: State University of New York at Plattsburgh
reviews: ['What a wounderful campus and facilities.  Met with Coach Nedbalski and his assistant coach Chatt this Morning/afternoon.  My Son loved the experience and I felt the same.  Definitely a contender.   Thanks and had a really good time.', "Don't waste your money and time at this awful college. I went here from 2017-2018 and was bullied horribly by other students for bigotry related reasons which led to me dropping out. Most of the students are from Long island and are stuck up, rude, and bigoted. Staff don't care about students. Food is terrible, There is never anything fun to do on campus. Go to literally any other school in New York you'll thank me later", "Well, I just want to say that this school is suitable for those who already know each other or are members of a group, because most individual students are very lonely and introverted or undisciplined. Even if this school takes most of the accommodation, it is still difficult for you to get effective social interaction, and the transportation in this place is almost by car. If you don't have a means of transportation, You're going to be miserable,And most of the time if you're not actively looking or exploring, you're just sitting around in one place, and the weather is really bad, especially in winter.", 'We only saw the outside, where there was a fountain with stepping stones, some pretty cool metal sculptures, benches for sitting. We found it by accident and thought it was a wonderful place to read a book, breathe in the fresh air and have fun people-watching.', "After completeing my Bachelors of Science at Suny Plattsburgh, I'll say this. The faculty at Suny Plattsburgh are passionate and well informed in their fields, and they want to see their students succeed and will meet them halfway to do so, sometimes even further. The students at Suny Plattsburgh are difficult to live with and connect with. A lot of them are from NYC or Long Island and they are loud, rude, and entitled. The student body uses the IPhone app Yick Yack to anonymously communicate across campus. This can lead to false rumors, and private information being spread very quickly across campus, and if you dont have the app, you dont even know until it is too late. This caused a safety concern for a student in my senior year there."]

name: Empire State University
reviews: ['SUNY Empire State University is better than CUNY, in that you can at least enroll, but once you are enrolled, the momentum ceases. I inquired about study grants, and they told me that they will not entertain anything that does not align with their research agenda, basically a glossy way of saying they don\'t want to sponsor students in any activity that they themselves don\'t find personally beneficial, and will turn down funding a deny a student a study opportunity if this is the case. When they say "non-traditional" students, what they really mean is low-performing students, meaning that if you nearly flunked out of school, this is the school for you. But if you took a non-traditional route and are looking for a high quality education, I suggest you look elsewhere. If you are just looking for the paper saying that says you withstood interactions with low quality people over and extended duration of time and can do this in a career as well, may be for you.', "Empire State University's Manhattan location at 4 Park Ave is consistently recognized by working professionals I know as an invaluable resource for highly flexible, non-traditional education. The most compelling aspect is their dedication to adult learners, allowing students to transfer credits generously and receive credit for prior professional experience. Friends emphasize that the curriculum is structured to accommodate demanding schedules, making it genuinely feasible to earn a SUNY degree while maintaining a career and other obligations. It truly stands out as a pragmatic and career-focused pathway to advanced education in New York City.", 'I enjoyed my experience at the school, substantially. I attended numerous schools outside of ESC (at the time) and this one of the best schools I had the pleasure of going to. I attended schools like UB aka University of Buffalo where I saw and experienced bullying and racism and York College where there was an insane amount of rude and unhelpful staff coupled with not so friendly attendees. At BCC where I recently did an e-permit because I am doing a post-bac degree a second time around, and it resembled much of both UB and York. This school on the other-hand was a breath of fresh-air. Although it may not be as academically challenging as I may want, it was a great starting point for someone doing and completing college for the first time. People were helpful and friendly, and most importantly mature. The only issue I recall having was finalizing my degree with Costello (I believe) it was quite the trip, but it worked out at the end. I should give a shout-out to Malongze for being such an amazing mentor through the course of my BA. She is genuinely such an inspiration! Thanks Malongze and another professor (he was a really nice old man) he retired a few years later. You are both the best!', 'I am a recent graduate of SUNY Empire State University, and I must commend the institution for its exceptional quality. The faculty and staff demonstrate a genuine commitment to the success of their students, providing invaluable support throughout the academic journey. While I encountered some initial challenges with my first two advisors in terms of responsiveness and assistance, the transition to Mrs. Buzick proved to be transformative. Her outstanding guidance and support were instrumental in shaping my academic experience over the course of three years.\n\nI am now preparing to pursue a graduate degree in school counseling, a milestone that would not have been possible without the foundation laid by SUNY Empire State University. I wholeheartedly recommend this institution, particularly for individuals with demanding schedules.', "I earned my BA degree from ESC. I loved my mentor and I had excellent professor who all ways genuinely wanted to help. I was a hybrid student, meaning I took classes both in person and online. I don't have anything bad to say. It was enjoyable. I only wish I could earn my masters degree there too."]

name: Swedish Institute a College of Health Sciences
reviews:
['I thoroughly enjoyed the in-person continuing education course at the Swedish Institute this past weekend.

As a former Swedish Institute faculty member and someone who currently assists in teaching the Medical Massage CE Certification program, I deeply appreciate well-run, thoughtfully taught CE courses and the Swedish Institute consistently delivers.

This weekend’s Fundamentals of Ortho-Bionomy: The Extremities course was a true pleasure. The subject matter was engaging and immediately applicable, and Rosa, our instructor, was outstanding. She is deeply knowledgeable, warm-hearted, and passionate about the work, and she held space beautifully for learning, questions, and exploration. Studying with her was genuinely enjoyable, and I absolutely plan to continue with more Ortho-Bionomy courses as they are offered.

Over the years, I’ve taken many in-person CE courses at Swedish, and the quality has been consistently excellent with diverse offerings, skilled instructors, and a learning environment that truly supports hands-on, in-person learning.

And finally, a big thank you to Tania and her team for making these courses so seamless and accessible. They do a wonderful job facilitating continuing education with excellent faculty, making CE feel less like a requirement and more like a gift.

Highly recommend to any practitioner who values learning, connection, and excellent teaching.', 'I attended Swedish Institute for the Surgical Technologist program and graduated earlier this year. The teachers for this curriculum were great. I have to especially mention Mrs. Hicks who was also my Clinical Instructor during my rotation. She’s absolutely amazing, knowledgeable and talented. She really had our back during clinicals and made sure we were treated with respect. While I feel the teachers for this particular curriculum were all great, I think the administrative staff could have done a better job.', "I graduated from the Swedish Institute in 1986. Of course things were very different back then, since it was a largely family owned entity. I had some of the best instructors on the planet then and have taken continuing education courses periodically over the years, including an upcoming course I'll be taking this year.
From past to present, they've offered an excellent education and continuing ed opportunities for both new grads and alumni, to deepen knowledge and skill levels, add new techniques and maybe take some different in-depth career paths with an array of very advanced workshops.
Highly recommend them!", 'I was genuinely considering attending this school, and my experience with my advisor started off very positive. Over time, however, the communication shifted. During several phone calls, the tone became unexpectedly harsh, and after I sent one detailed message explaining my situation, I did not receive any response for about a week. When the advisor eventually called, I missed the call due to an important commitment but returned it as soon as I could. The conversation that followed felt dismissive; I was told not to send long messages because “she didn’t have time,” even though it had only happened once.

I also received text messages from the advisor around 2 a.m. on more than one occasion, which I never complained about, but the overall attitude in our later interactions left me feeling discouraged and unwelcome. I attempted to continue communicating with short, brief messages, but the tone remained the same. I was eventually advised to try a different program or even a different school altogether, which was disappointing considering how hopeful I had been at the beginning.

I’m sharing my experience not to be harsh, but to be honest. I think constructive, respectful communication is important—especially for students who are trying to make big decisions about their education.

Edit: A representative at Swedish contacted me shortly after my review being posted. He helped clarify things , and addressed my concerns. This significantly improved my experience , and I’m extremely grateful they took the time to reach out to resolve this. My new admissions advisor has been extremely helpful and responsive. He took the time to understand my situation, corrected the issues I was experiencing, and is now doing his best to get me into the program I want by the month I’m hoping to start. I really appreciate his support and the effort he’s putting in to make this happen.', 'As a recent graduate, I unfortunately cannot recommend this school. For the amount of money students pay, the majority of the learning ends up being self-taught. During my work-study experience, the only truly supportive connections I made were with certain lab instructors and a few genuinely kind staff members. The lab team is the strongest part of the program--they care, they teach, and they want students to succeed. Because of them, the program could have so much more potential.
However, the academic side of the program is extremely lacking. Most professors do not actually teach, and online didactics should really be held in person. Students consistently feel dismissed or disrespected by some members of leadership. In my personal experience, Ms. April often spoke to students unprofessionally, and Ms. Peralta, the clinical coordinator, regularly made the clinical process stressful, disorganized, and unnecessarily difficult.

Clinical placements are very delayed, communication is poor, and professionalism is inconsistent, as she is disrespectful and racist. This affects students and their ability to progress on time.

Despite the challenges, the lab instructors truly work hard and create a positive learning environment. If you do choose to attend, rely heavily on your textbooks, build a strong personal study method, and be prepared to advocate for yourself. For the tuition cost, students deserve better structure, support, and respect.']

name: Syracuse University
reviews:
['Gibbie Clinic: Syracuse University has a wide variety of programs known worldwide.  The Gibbie Clinic, which is a speech and audiology program is run by professors that are well-versed in their subjects.
In my case, it was hearing. I realized that I was not hearing things the way that I should and so I went up there for a hearing evaluation.   Rana, who has two more years to go in her program (and is from Saudi Arabia) and Olivia (1st year student and shadowing) ran my hearing test.
We went over the results of the test, which found that I was having trouble hearing. We went over my options and we decided to try hearing aids. At no time where we pressured into buying hearing aids.   My wife and I left to discuss the results and went home.
We decided eventually to purchase the hearing aids with the understanding that we had 45 days to return them if we were not happy with them or felt that they were not appropriate.
The process has been great. I’ve been seeing these two wonderful young ladies that are with the hearing aid program along with their professor.  The professor stays off in the background and lets Rana run things and only interjects when needed.
I would recommend Gibbie Clinic to anyone that needs a hearing eval.', "The great university offering plenty of academic courses. It's among top 50-60 university of USA. I have given 5 star rating because my son has graduated from here. His experience was great. He got right guidelines from the professor as well as administrator from the concerned department. My has  pursued in Masters in Computer science, been one of the topper in university & got placement in very good company there is US. I had been there to attend his convocation ceremony and met to his Professor..Was nice meeting with him. Overall good experience. Worth spending time and money to achieve higher education here.", 'Visited Newhouse, it was excellent! Fantastic place for students to get inspired by their professors and state of the art facilities.', 'Graduated 2015. They suspended me for a year before I could graduate. After 10 years, they permanently disabled my email address that they promised I would have for life. Avoid.', "My daughters second year and it's still a nice safe place, good views for jogging nice small locations for picnics and a lot of positivity in the air"]

name: Tompkins Cortland Community College
reviews: ['TC3 has become a beautiful campus with interesting opportunities.   I appreciate touring the TST BOCES PTECH program.', 'Very glad I chose TC3. It was the most welcoming school with professors who truly cared about not only knowing your name, but doing their best to help you succeed. People are quick to judge those who go to community college, but it was the best education I received. I recommend everyone start here or just go here depending on the degree they are looking for. Not only will you be saving lots of money, you will receive the best college experience. I wished I could have stayed here for my full four years. Not to mention they offer free tutoring, which saved me when I had to take the required statistics course.', 'This is a great school. We have some really amazing community colleges in upstate New York and this is one of them if you get to go to one of the schools you’re going to get a very high-quality education for a quarter of the price of somewhere else. My suggestion is get your first two years out of the way and then transferred all for your school that is the way to do it to not have all of your future earnings going into loans.', 'The administration here is very apathetic to the struggles of students trying to get an education. There is almost no support for financial aid, let alone transfer and career planning. Besides this the professors that I had were subpar and focused more on your attendance than your class performance. There was no understanding or flexibility for those who were working to support a family and had periodic shift changes. One might imagine that the faculty would see someone working 60 hours a week and still striving to get an education as worthy, but that was not the case.', 'Excellent environment, the staff is really friendly, a lot of resources for you to improve on classes, lived on campus and it was the best experience! A quiet and peaceful place.']

name: Touro University
reviews: ['Touro University has increasingly become a centerpiece of conversation among my peers, recognized as a dynamic institution that masterfully aligns its academic curriculum with the evolving demands of the New York professional landscape. From the insightful feedback shared by several acquaintances who have pursued degrees there, it is evident that the university provides a substantive and nurturing environment where student success is treated as a collective mission rather than just a metric. It is genuinely refreshing to witness how this campus, situated right in the heart of Times Square, maintains such a high level of cultural integrity and personal attention, qualities that are frequently praised by local families for fostering true career readiness. In the broader public consensus, Touro is viewed as a vital educational partner that champions both inclusivity and high academic standards, making it a highly respected choice for those seeking to integrate rigorous study with real-world application. Reflecting on the consistent stream of positive testimonials from the community, it is clear that the university stands as a reliable pillar of opportunity, distinguished by its commitment to empowering students from all backgrounds to achieve excellence.', 'Touro GST has provided a very supportive and engaging academic environment. The faculty are approachable, and the coursework in data analytics is practical, hands-on, and aligned with real industry skills. I’ve genuinely benefited from the learning experience here as a Data Analytics student.', 'Touro offers a positive learning environment with supportive faculty and practical coursework. The programs are well suited for students who want hands-on experience and real-world exposure. I’ve had a good experience here and would recommend it.', 'Touro University Graduate School of Technology is for individuals seeking a rigorous, forward-thinking, and professionally relevant graduate education in technology. The school’s emphasis on real-world application is evident in its project-based coursework, internship support, and preparation for industry certifications.', "As a graduate student from Touro University myself, I'll state that this is one of the most welcoming and kindest schools one can enroll into. So many people here want the best for their students and offer many opportunities to help boost their resumes for future job offers. It is an amazing environment to be around for grads and undergrads, and I believe stands as currently one of the best universities within the city."]

name: Trocaire College
reviews:
["I had the displeasure of attending this college my freshman year. I was in the very first hospitality program (2008) . A semester was about $5,000, over 10,000 per year. Books were very expensive, over 800$ per semester. This is 2008 money!   My professor Brandon Supernaught was a complete joke, all we did was watch videos and chatted about current events. This was his first year at the college and he was very unprepared. To make it look like he had a incredible and challenging curriculum, he had to fail a student. This student was me! Brandon failed me in both classes I had with him. When I asked why, he told me it was because I didn't do a bonus assignment. I aced every test with him and attended every class, But I still get a fail.
got kicked out of the program because I failed those two classes. Spent near $15,000 and was able to transfer one! English credit

I happened to know a friend who took his program a few years later And he brought up my name and proudly said he failed me in front of the class.  (This should be looked into)!

Would not recommend this program to anyone.

The college also had a massive data breach , to be honest they probably willingly handed it out  for money. Wouldn't trust these people.", "I graduated from Trocaire over twenty years ago.  At that time this institute was the gold standard.  I received an excellent education from the former staff, they were all long time seasoned teachers. I have talked to many students who are current or recently students and have heard terrible stories.  If you hear one or two you don't necessarily believe it, I hsve heard many more than that. Its very sad to know this school has deteriorated.  People think everything needs change,  change is good,  that is not necessarily true, if something is not broke,  dont fix it and that's what they did.  To the people complaining about what they have to give up to be a nurse,  that is part of the process.  If you want to be a qualified nurse you will put things to the side to make that happen.  If you just want the title and paycheck then you'll just get through it. Nursing school requires discipline,  nursing school has rules,  grade cut offs for a reason.  Too many people blaming the program or a teacher for their lack of discipline or for failing by 1 or 2 points. You will be taking care of human  beings,  saving lives,  you shoukd be required to meet the scores .", 'I had a frustrating experience with the admissions process. My Google meeting was rescheduled to a different advisor, but when the meeting time came, no one showed up.

When I called admissions to find out what happened, I was given the new counselor’s phone number. After contacting him, he told me he had no idea we even had a meeting scheduled. This lack of communication and coordination made the experience feel very disorganized and unprofessional.

First impressions matter, and unfortunately this made me question how organized the college is.', 'I applied in mid-November of 2025 online solely because of my employer offers a tuition-based scholarship. So I would just come out of pocket for the remaining balance with the help of financial aid. Its now January 2026 this place is a nightmare. I haven't even started and let me tell you how bad it's been. I went to the wrong location to drop off my college/ high school transcripts. I thought I applied for the Williamsville location come to find out that I have to go down to South Buffalo instead. I live in Niagara Falls let me tell you that is a far drive just to hand in papers. When I get there I thought that I could park in this certain spot that read "Trocaire Visitors". The security guard walked past me to place a piece of paper on my car windshield saying that if I park there again I would be towed at my own expense. I waited at the desk for the security guard to return. Instead another member of staff ushered me back to the right department. My college and high school transcripts were the first things that I submitted. I was accept to the college a few days later. Then I received an email saying that I had to upload my vaccinations records to a website called Castle Branch. I had a very hard time trying to upload my records to the point where I had to email someone to do it for me at the college after a few dozen tries. I received an email about a week later stating that I needed to turn in my college/high school transcripts for approval. I kid you not I received this email for about a month. I also received a letter in the mail stating that I needed to turned my transcripts in and take the HESI exam. I finally email the admissions office and asked why I was receiving this over and over again? What a coincidence the notices finally stopped. At the end of December I received an email stating that I needed to schedule an appointment for Financial Aid. After Christmas vacation maybe around January 2nd I received an email saying that I didn't need to schedule any appointment that I can simply do it online by myself. And that I shouldn't have waited for a response from Financial Aid because it takes about 2 weeks for it to be approved!!! On January 6th, 2026 I received a phone call so I can get my schedule. I still haven't been approved for financial aid! And I still haven't uploaded my second vaccine to their Castle Branch website. But I'm getting a schedule for classes bc the semester starts January 26th, 2026. I have worked in healthcare for several years and I've heard nothing but negativity about this college it's honestly not hard to see why. It is very unprofessional and disorganized already and I haven't even stepped into a classroom yet.

UPDATE: On January 30th 2026 I received a phone call from John from Admissions asking me again for my Bryant & Stratton College transcripts it was the first thing that I provided to this college. I'm already in classes and I'm being asked for the same document that I have provided multiple times now. On February 2nd, 2026- I had to pay $10 for my college transcripts to be sent electronically to Trocaire because my previous college did not sign the official transcript. Which made the transcripts unofficial, I purchased my transcripts back in 2017 for ECC but never went. The packet was sealed when I handed to Admissions on December 2, 2025.', 'A data breach at this already terrible excuse of an institution leaking my social security number. For the amount of money this "college" makes you wld think they wld have better security measures in place. Subpar instructors... does not care about students. Better, more affordable options EVERYWHERE.']

name: Ulster County Community College
reviews:
['A lot of benefits and scholarships . Food and clothing for the needy it’s a very good school. I have received a Lot
Of financial support from this school , my thank you to the account department particular Joe , carol from the scholarship department and the admissions support unit .
It’s a great school', 'SUNY Ulster is a great place to start your career path.
Helpful, friendly available staff is always there to answer questions point you in the right direction and be the compass that you may need at any time.

I am a graduate from there as well as two of my daughters and now a third will be attending.', 'Wish I could give 0 or even negative stars. SUNY Ulster ruined college for me! The staff and a good portion of the professors here are extremely rude. I drove to my high school my first semester to get some paperwork I needed for the registrar office and the lady told me she wasn’t accepting it because I got it from the school rather than having it faxed and that it had to be faxed. She was quite rude about it too. When I was behind on getting text books for class the professors were really nasty and were not at all understanding of the fact that I had very little money which was why I depended on financial aid I would even go hungry some days because I couldn’t afford food at the dining hall and didn’t always have a lot of food I could bring from home, I had to drive 45 minutes there and 45 minutes back to attend classes and did not know what I needed until the day of classes because as a new student I had no access to blackboard right away to find out. I switched my major because I struggled with the vet tech program and everything was fine the following semester but then my third overall semester I was overwhelmed and struggled to find balance between school and work and I was also battling some mental health issues I was having and had to leave school. Because of that the school decided that I owe them nearly $2,000 for leaving despite my appeal letter that I wrote to the dean explaining my situation!!! I will never recommend this school to anyone! If you struggle with mental health or you struggle financially DO NOT ENROLL IN SUNY ULSTER OR THEY’LL TRY TO ROB YOU!!! THEY DON’T CARE ABOUT YOU OR YOUR STRUGGLE! JUST ABOUT MAKING MONEY! There were only like 3 maybe 4 professors that were actually nice and understanding the whole time I was there. The rest of them were rude and uncaring', "If I could give this school zero stars I would. I have had nothing but problems since I've started here. I wasn't informed I was accepted, about courses being cancelled, what my major was, who my advisor was, or that they didn't have my major when I transferred in. I also was not informed of fees I had to pay or the deadline to pay them so instead of being informed and paying they unregistered me from the courses I was supposed to take. They drag their feet to let you know anything and when you try to get information you get nothing but attitude and rudeness. Two faculty members go well above and beyond what they had to in an attempt to help me but I wouldn't recommend this school to anyone.  This college made me absolutely despise college and learning which is a first for me. Avoid this school at all costs.", 'Peaceful environment, helpful teachers! A lot of newer students complain that they are not handed information or being informed of certain aspects of their semester. I felt this way at first until I realized... this is college! It takes a lot of work and effort to keep up with emails, the portal, etc. You have to really bust your ass to make sure you have all your paper work in and take the time to make calls. Although it may seem like it takes forever, financial aid is processed and you are able to access the portal to seek important news and advisor information. name: Villa Maria College
reviews:
['I pulled into Villa Maria on a bright weekday morning expecting a quick walk-through and a stack of brochures. Instead, I got Esther. From the first handshake she was less “tour guide” and more trusted producer—setting pace, hitting beats, and giving me the kind of context only an insider who cares can deliver. We stepped out onto a campus that feels intentionally human in scale—closer to a great high school than a sprawling university—and within minutes I understood the advantage: you can see the whole learning journey from almost any point on the map.

Esther threaded us through the neighborhood story first—how Villa Maria exists for the students who live right around it, how the college acts like an on-ramp to a different trajectory. We passed clusters of small classes where professors actually knew who was absent, who needed a nudge, who just landed an internship. It’s mentorship disguised as everyday teaching. “We coach, not just credit,” Esther said, and then introduced me to a professor who, unprompted, described a sophomore’s portfolio like a creative director defending a pitch.

Renovations can feel like lipstick if they’re not tied to a purpose; here they read like strategy. Esther walked me through the refreshed commons—bright lunchrooms that feel more café than cafeteria, a library that invites you to linger, labs where the tech isn’t just new, it’s used. You can smell the fresh paint and also the ambition; it’s top-notch work executed with restraint, the kind of polish that says, “We expect you to do your best work here.”

The digital shift is real. In studio after studio, I saw the bones of a modern creative education: marketing fundamentals, content and design workflows, and the tools today’s teams actually live in. It’s not theory-first, it’s portfolio-first—make something, ship something, learn why it worked. As someone who hires for this world, I felt the curriculum tilting in the right direction.

Halfway through, Esther handed me off to senior leaders who were refreshingly candid about where Villa Maria is and where it’s going. They spoke about access with the humility of people who do the work, and about outcomes with the urgency of people who know they’re measured by them. The plan is clear: protect the intimacy, expand the opportunity, sharpen the pathways into real jobs—especially in the digital and marketing tracks where momentum is obvious. I left those conversations encouraged; the destination matches the mission.

I’d be less than honest if I didn’t note the tradeoffs. Some programs—game design in particular—face a tougher local runway. Western New York isn’t exactly bursting with studios, and graduate placements can be a heavier lift. But the team didn’t soft-pedal that; they reframed it. Build stronger portfolios. Stack internships. Leverage remote work. And remember you’re in a city that quietly rewards builders—if you’ve got an entrepreneurial itch, the market gap is also an invitation.

What stuck with me more than any single room or piece of gear was the throughline: this is a small college by design, delivering one-on-one attention you can feel. Students aren’t left to wander a course catalog; they are guided—as if a capable hand is on the small of their back—through the whole experience. Esther made that philosophy visible simply by being Esther: present, precise, relentlessly student-first.

By the time we circled back to the entrance, Villa Maria had told a complete story. A mission rooted in the neighborhood. Facilities renovated to serve that mission, not overshadow it. A digital, marketing, and advertising focus coming into its own. Leadership that knows where the gaps are and is building real bridges. And value—frankly hard to beat—when you weigh the cost against the attention and momentum on offer.

I came for a tour. I left with a clear picture of a college lifting people up the right way, one small class and one guided step at a time—and a renewed appreciation for how much difference the right guide can make. Thanks, Esther.', 'Stop Spending Money On Renovations and Taking Away Our Lyft Credits and Just Fix The Wifi

name: School of Visual Arts
reviews:
["I'm graduating this year from the Illustration department, so I want to express my appreciation to SVA! :) The professors I had were really nice and helpful—they gave honest critiques and helped me network. I'm very into picture books, so I took classes like silkscreen book making, children's literature, Picture Book with Eugenia Mello, and senior thesis class with my favorite artist, Doug Salati! The campus is nice and located in the Gramercy neighborhood. However, the illustration dep has very limited spaces, we only have 2 floors in a shared building, and the elevator is always crowded. I hope we can get better classrooms and a bigger print lab.

Overall, SVA is a very business-oriented school—they really prepare you for the industry. So if you're thinking of becoming a commercial illustrator, I definitely recommend it!", "I graduated from BFA Design at SVA two years ago and still think choosing SVA was the best choice for my undergrad study! The location is convenient, surrounded by a lot of nice restaurants and groceries, and it's in MANHATTAN! Facilities in our department are always the latest, and the instructors I had were nice and professional, they always have tons of news from the industry and make sure your work catches the latest trend in the field (at least in the graphic design field!). SVA is a relatively small but warm community, students are close to each other and I made my best friends here. If you are looking for programs that help you look for jobs and get into the industry easier, go for SVA!", 'This school has many buildings spreading in blocks in a busy but quite nice area in Manhattan. We went to the admission office and were received very friendly by the staff. We were given a lot of booklets about the art school.

Both the main building and the admin office looked bright and neat. The art gallery at the main building has some artworks displayed.', 'The Branding program at SVA is one that I highly recommend. The curriculum is rich and highly practical, covering all the essential branding skills you need. The faculty members have impressive backgrounds, and the courses maintain an exceptionally high standard. The professors are dedicated and meticulous, carefully evaluating and refining each student’s work to help us apply our knowledge effectively to real-world cases. Additionally, the program provides strong support for students’ career development after graduation, whether in building connections or planning career paths. It is a program worth studying, regardless of your background.', "I’m a current senior in SVA’s BFA Illustration program, and I wanted to extend my gratitude to this school. Over the past few years, I’ve watched myself grow as both an artist and a person, and I owe so much of that growth to the faculty at SVA. The professors here are some of the kindest and most knowledgeable/skilled people I’ve ever met in the industry, and with their support, I’ve been able to come out of my shell and create a graduating portfolio I’m truly proud of. I’ve felt nothing but encouragement to explore different subject matters, mediums, and approaches to my work. Both my studio and humanities professors have bolstered my character and career.
Aside from academics, I’ve also been provided with incredible opportunities to get involved on campus, whether that be through on-campus working positions or student engagement events. SVA has given me the tools to communicate effectively with others, both in business and interpersonal settings.
If I had to name an area of improvement for the school, it would be the amount of space provided to the illustration and comics department. Illustration is the largest major at SVA and it is currently occupying two floors shared with the comics department. I feel that future students would benefit from more space, especially additional spaces to explore traditional media.
With that being said, I couldn't have chosen a better place to achieve my bachelor’s degree. SVA is truly a dream school for any illustrator."]

In this realm, authority is the flipper and you are the ball, so saddle up, bcuz you're gonna be here a while.

The average waiting time on the 6 or 7 occasions I've gone to see them was one hour, and the conversation is never longer than 5 minutes. name: Yeshiva University
reviews:
['At Yeshiva University, the academic structure is intentionally demanding and personal. Classes are generally smaller, faculty interaction is frequent, and students are expected to engage directly with both professors and peers. It is difficult to remain anonymous. Participation, analytical thinking, and consistent performance are visible in day-to-day coursework. The culture often reinforces the idea that progress is demonstrated through intellectual contribution and measurable academic output rather than simply being enrolled.

The experience at University of California, Davis can feel structurally different. Its scale alone changes how pressure is distributed. With tens of thousands of undergraduates and highly decentralized departments, the intensity of the academic environment can vary widely depending on the major, the instructors, and the initiative of the student. Rigor certainly exists, but it is not always uniformly embedded in the everyday structure.

Critics argue that this scale can create a gap between the university’s strong public reputation and the consistency of the undergraduate academic experience. Because the institution is so large, motivated students sometimes report needing to create their own pressure—seeking difficult courses, research opportunities, or honors tracks—rather than encountering it as a built-in expectation across the board. Some top students faces backstabbing from professors and peers because they can not adjust to top students’ level and cognitive demands. The gap is so large that sometimes staying becomes self-destroying just like  the fish in Oldman and the Sea can bitten so that only bones can be left once at home.

Outcome statistics also appear in discussions about institutional effectiveness. Critics sometimes point to figures suggesting that a portion of students who begin at UC Davis remain enrolled for very long periods before finishing. In those discussions, examples are cited where individuals may spend up to 10 years enrolled while accumulating around $58,000 in costs or debt before graduating, raising questions about alignment between cost, pacing, and student expectations.

At Yeshiva University, pressure is embedded in the culture and reinforced through constant academic visibility.

At UC Davis, the level of pressure can depend much more on how much intensity a student creates for themselves.

The contrast is less about labels or rankings and more about whether the institution itself supplies the friction that pushes students forward—or whether that responsibility largely falls on the individual.', 'The ugliest college campus in the United States. Why won’t they renovate it? Beautify this campus.', "They are terrible at explaining loans, didn't approve my financial until 3 weeks before starting school. If you are not from NYC they don't help with housing or anything. My 2nd Program: MLT

The school labeled it as “poor performance” without acknowledging the health challenges I was facing. Despite my efforts to explain and seek support, I was not given the opportunity to re-enroll. Instead, I had to start over at a new school (Halifax Community College) and repeat my entire final year. HCC took me with open arms and was a far better school. I hope future students are treated with more empathy and understanding, especially when facing legitimate medical concerns. I found another school, repeated my final year, and not only graduated—I went on to earn my CLS bachelors degree, as well.
