name: Elizabeth City State University
reviews:
['Went to vote, mostly empty. Everyone is nice and friendly! Have your IDs ready!', 'Atmosphere was awesome. Beautiful campus.', "We went to go to the planetary and it was great it's also great for family and adults if you get a chance you need to go it's outstanding if you like that kind of thing The narrator was great and explained everything even some of the old history on how star clusters had got their name", "I had the opportunity to attend ECSU a few years back in an attempt to refresh my math skills before attending graduate school.  I won't go into details but consider the fact that an Elementary Calculus for the Social Sciences text was used for MATH MAJORS!!!  In the preface the author stated it was to be covered in 1 semester or 2 quarters.  The math department at ECSU in their infinite wisdom used it for all 3 semesters for their MATH MAJORS.   Betty Crocker math ring a bell?  That is but the very tip of the iceberg.

Students go there, make straight A's, and then wonder why they can't score high enough on the GRE, MCAT, LSAT, etc. to be accepted to quality graduate schools.  This school has and continues to do a disservice to its students.  ECSU graduates are unprepared to grasp the skills needed to learn their jobs if they happen to be hired for a job.  ECSU has the reputation among the academic world as being the worst school academically in the state of North Carolina and it has lived up to that reputation for decades.

Think about it ... this is a school that has the lowest admission requirements of any school in the state and accepts 50% of its applicants!  If you think you will be surrounded by an intellectually stimulating environment, you need therapy.

If you are reasonably bright, want to learn the skills needed for a career and want a degree worth more than a blank sheet of paper, avoid this place at all costs.  Even if they pay you to attend (which is how they get most of their warm bodies), it is a waste of your life.

One last thing:  There are numerous reviews here telling you what a wonderful education you can get there.  Also you get out of it what you put in.  Sadly they are clueless and have never attended a competative division I school.  You can learn 100% of the information you are exposed to at ECSU and still be in the bottom 25% at any other major university in North Carolina.   I wish I  was incorrect, but sadly I'm not.", 'Many Students Build their future here']

name: Elon University
reviews:
["This is the most underrated university in America. Elon University gave me amazing opportunities to study abroad, take a wide range of classes, land amazing internships and a fulltime job, write an undergraduate research thesis, have some really unique on-campus jobs, launch three businesses on campus, play club sports, and spend a ton of time outdoors on the amazing campus.
If you've never been to campus, take a tour (or a virtual tour on the admissions website) and you'll get a great feel for the energy and culture at Elon. It's hard to describe.
Take a look at their fantastic honors and fellows programs as well, I have great things to say about my time in an honors program. It's only a matter of time before Elon University is a top-20 university in this country.
If you need more proof, look at some of the amazing rankings including #1 for undergraduate teaching, #1 study abroad, and #1 most beautiful campus!", 'Makes you wish you were college bound again. Took a tour of Elon, today. A young man named Britt was our guide. He was knowledgeable and gave extra attention to our questions and concerns. I love how he was patient with our son. And we all felt very welcome. Many young people smiled as we walked around. I can see why the students seem so happy. This campus is a dream. Everything just felt right. It’s like they have thought of everything. Every detail is impeccable. The great part: Many choices in good food, we’ll never have to worry about our son.
If I could give more than 5 stars, I would.
Thank you for a memorable visit.', "Academically it's a Ivy League competitor!  The campus is well designed, manicured and comfortably built for living.  There is plenty of green space for College life experience without having a City or community intertwined but close enough to 2 larger cities, Greensboro and Raleigh.  The faculty are well educated and very good at leading this group of young adults into the workplace and world.  There's an emphasis on Study Abroad and allows the students to explore the world in a safe learning environment!  Once you get to explore what this location has to offer it's extremely difficult to consider any other option, seriously the University is top notch!", 'Incredibly welcoming. Fabulous campus and tour. Accommodating. Working on campus diversity. Active campus atmosphere.', 'It’s pretty. Although, the tour and the overall vibe of the school wasn’t my thing at all.']

name: Fayetteville Technical Community College
reviews:
['I have went to FTCC originally for IT back in the Spring 2022 Semester, after finishing that semester I realized it wasn’t for me so I decided to change my major to Business/Marketing for the following Fall 2022 Semester and that was one of the best decisions I made. The marketing program in FTCC was so enjoyable and I was very engaged in all the business and marketing classes. I then graduated after the Spring 2025 semester which was my last semester there finishing the program ending at a 4.0 GPA, my Associate as well as 3 certificates. I admit I miss going to the school, it was a big part of my life from 2022-2025/early adult years, I recommend this school to anyone that was me at 18/19 years old, who don’t know what’s next in life and don’t want to go to a big University but just a college to get a degree in something you’re passionate about.', "FTTC failed to notify me that my financial aid had been pulled and my account needed attention. Now all my plans are screwed up so I don't know if I'll finish. Definitely won't be coming back to FTTC though. I cannot recommend this school to anyone", 'The school is an absolute joke, The Faculty here absolutely sucks and is zero help. Trying to get signed up for school here is unreasonably difficult because the people that literally get paid and are there to help, dont want to do their job. Do better, your whole purpose working at a school is to help students yet they get zero assistance. Disappointing and unbelievable', "Going into my second year. The campus is really nice and I'm enjoying the environment so far. However my advisors are very neglectful and sometimes just don't answer questions or contact me at all before something causes an issue.

I've had an experience where my advisor accidentally scheduled me for a class under a major I wasnt associated with and now I have to fully commit to another degree plan I never actually planned to get.
This added another year to my progression...

I understand advisors can make mistakes but often they don't try to fix them.

Theres also a ongoing issue with the Microsoft authentication system and the college Microsoft accounts. The student email will sometimes shut off if the authentication app updates or if you switch phone numbers. You will be locked out of your own account until bypassing the verification process under the school campus wifi. This I feel can be extremely dangerous for multiple reasons.

1. Hackers. If my laptop is stolen and used to take my account to information.. all that person has to do is connect to campus wifi and they have all my information.
2. Students schedules. Scheduling is tight for everyone and having to go to campus to fix your login is a waste of time and can mess up how people can get help.

I think its a major problem and I have multiple peers that have experienced the same thing. Yet. Administration & IT do nothing. Nor Microsoft.", 'Well, I have nothing but great things to say about Fayetteville Technical Community College (FTCC). If you want to further your education or learn a trade, this is the place for you. Stop by and see us!!']

name: Fayetteville State University
reviews:
['As a student at Fayetteville State University who is also a working mother, my experience has been mixed. Fayetteville State is a large university with a lot to offer academically and socially, and there are many opportunities available for students who can fully engage on campus.
However, accessing basic assistance has been extremely frustrating—especially for off-campus, working students. Reaching anyone by phone is consistently difficult, if not impossible. Issues that could easily be resolved with a simple phone call often require unnecessary trips to campus instead. This creates a real hardship for students who are balancing work, parenting, and school responsibilities.
If you are an off-campus student, be prepared to make multiple in-person visits for matters that should be handled remotely. While the university has many resources, prompt, personalized, and convenient support is lacking.
Overall, Fayetteville State University may be a good fit if you have the flexibility to be on campus often. But if convenience, responsiveness, and accessible communication are important to you—especially as a working parent—this may not be the best environment.', 'I wish that I would have done more research on the university. I came to this university on the strength of a tour as I was going to be a transferring student from Pitt Community College. My cousin attended FSU and I got to stay on campus with her as a child. That was years ago and that’s why I wanted to give FSU a shot. It’s been hectic ever since I have started especially registration. I have even had to talk to my husband about it because I just feel like giving up and going someplace else. I can believe the reviews on staff, organization, administration, getting the run around I mean sheesh!! You can’t hardly get anybody on the phone. SMH I think I made a mistake choosing this university.', 'I am currently a transfer student at UNCFSU, and I have been struggling with both the registrar and advising center to transfer my classes!!!

Its been two semesters since I've been attending this college and I am still missing classes that I already took at my university.

Everytime I try to get in contact with a faculty member in the registrar or advising center, they send me on a "wild goose chase" just for the final person who answers  the phone to NOT be able to fix my transcript or answer my questions appropriately.

It's giving they are either super understaffed and they don't know what they are doing at all. I have no idea if I am going to be able to graduate next year at this rate because there are over 30 credits missing from my transcript that was never transferred properly or picked up at all. Including classes I took my first semester at this college.

The way my situation is being handled is absolutely ridiculous! Leslie Tukes is a terrible advisor!!!', 'Don’t waste your time trying to find parking, YOU WONT!! There are several parking lots closed for “construction” during school hours and you will get a citation for parking elsewhere. This school makes money off parking citations but they wont give you any reasonable parking especially for someone who is Handicapped like myself. I have to walk the length of a football field on my disabled foot just to get to class everyday.', 'all the nursing school professors are great but Dr. Vogt goes the extra mile for her students. She is a wonderful and caring instructor']

I recommend traveling further to another community college, but if you decide to waste your time and money with Forsyth tech then double and triple check everything because they are not looking out for you.']

name: Gardner-Webb University
reviews:
['Our daughter chose this university for three reasons: it is a "Christian" school, it had the major/minor she wanted, and for its location. I'll start with the positive. The location is beautiful. And we were thankful that the two degrees she was seeking were both offered at one university. Unfortunately, we were completely disappointed with the lack of Christian elements. We simply didn't find the Christian components we had hoped for. Even during the orientation week, meetings with parents didn't involve an opening prayer, and the focus wasn't directed towards a daily walk and relationship with Jesus. Our Christian life shouldn't be reserved for just Sundays; our hope that Jesus would be honored in what was happening on campus simply didn't materialize. Maybe this is just the state of our world, but as an example, we were very unhappy to find out that at the time of registration, the university had a lesbian in charge of housing. Additionally, one of our daughter's professors was a lesbian. While they were both kind, we disapprove of that lifestyle based on the teaching of Scripture. By hiring these women to play significant leadership roles, the university seems to be condoning that lifestyle. How is this an appropriate choice when choosing leaders for a Christian university? Our daughter also shared with us that in a different class, the professor asked the students about where they thought they would end up after they passed; not one person other than our daughter said "Heaven" because of salvation through Christ! Sadly, our daughter had great difficulty finding quality Christian friends. We also had issues with the billing procedures of the university. The bill we received to start her sophomore year omitted her housing charges. After taking a significant loan out to pay for what we thought we owed for the school year, we were advised of this mistake and had to pay the amount out-of-pocket. It was $6,000 in total! Though it was their error, there was no compensation on our behalf. Additionally, though she should have been given priority regarding her housing location due to her disabilities, due to this error, her room wasn't assigned to her until shortly before she arrived for her sophomore year rather than early in the summer months. The disabilities department was disappointing as well. Rather than go to bat for her, she had to advocate for herself in many instances. In one specific situation, a professor expected her to attend class regularly while our daughter believed she could do the class virtually. When those wires got crossed, the disabilities department would not play the role of advocate for our daughter and she received a failing grade; she had to retake the class the following semester. We were also disappointed in learning that on long weekends, the campus pretty much shuts down, including the dining options. Unlike many students who live nearby, our girl was stuck alone on campus (we live many states away) without the provision of food. One time she was alone during the aftermath of a hurricane with a ghost town of a campus and without power. We could share more, but needless to say, she had a terrible experience. She is no longer enrolled in GWU and is much happier doing her studies online with another college. If you are seeking a university that will saturate your son or daughter with God's Word and provide a rich Christian education that challenges their relationship with Jesus, we would encourage you to look elsewhere. Should you choose to enroll your son or daughter at GWU, we hope your experience is better than ours.', 'We had a tour this summer and although the campus was practically empty, the students that arranged the tour and gave the tour were professional and informative. Very friendly to us and answered all our questions. Campus was beautiful with a lot of outdoor green space. They have an indoor rock climbing wall and a lot for the students to do in their free time without having to leave campus.', 'Excellent school with a quality education!!

Gardner-Webb offers an ever-growing, wide selection of academic programs.  And between the Tucker Student Center & being centrally located between Gaffney, SC & Shelby, NC, students have everything they could ever need within a 10 minute drive.

As for Homecoming 2022,  my family had wonderful time attending the Alumni Tailgate, seeing the Homecoming Parade, & even going to the football game (which we won!)!!!', "Amazing place. Such a beautiful campus. Women's lacrosse team is fantastic especially #19", 'Always great to spend time on campus. Got to the see several alumni at the presidential search which had Nate Evans giving us his plans forward for GWU!']

name: Greensboro College
reviews: ['Gboro College: paying homage to my alma mater. The college offers both undergraduate and graduate opportunities for international students. The campus is centrally located and offers all you need to pursue your career. It was great to be back and visit the bookstore as an alumnus now.', 'Beautiful little campus. Quite the hidden gem. The grounds offer a variety of scenic buildings with well maintained greenery.', 'Such an amazing "hidden gem" college.  The campus is beautiful and has some great history, as the college was founded in 1838.  The faculty and staff truly care about the students and you have to sincerely try to fail at anything at this institution, because everyone wants you to succeed.  While the small size will lead it to likely never being a nationally ranked "ivy league" institution, there are many alumni who have had success in a variety of fields.  As a private college, everyone is afraid of the price tag - but the reality is, with a combination of campus-based scholarships and bringing in your own scholarships - this can often be better on your wallet than many state schools.', "It's a beautiful campus with tons of events happening all the time. I even got the chance to visit their cafeteria and they have a buffet for the students that only cost $8.50. Then I got a chance to talk to some of the professors who were really nice and they also offer a middle college program for juniors and seniors in high school. Those teachers were even nicer.", 'Let me start off by saying, this school isn\'t what the representatives claim it to be. $40,000 a semester is not worth it. This school has some of the rudest and incompetent staff I\'ve ever seen. They have professor\'s that don\'t teach and advisors that encourages the student to quit. Seems as if they couldnt careless as to whether the student pass or fail, because they will get their money one way or another.This school is definitely here for the money. Instead of a degree, the parent and or student will get a bald head from stress and student loan debt.']

name: Guilford College
reviews: ['Guilford is an amazing place with a bucolic campus, active student government, social justice focus, great academics, and wonderful student community.  I am proud to have graduated from there and they prepared me for the life I am now living as an entrepreneur, clinician and meditation teacher.   They taught me how to write well, how to think clearly, and how to care for others.  I could not be happier with my college experience at Guilford.', "Great place to get an education and I feel very fortunate that I attended here. Classes are smaller, the professor's I had here were great, and the campus is beautiful.\n\nIf you're older then the adult education program is perfect for getting you're college degree while fitting to your work schedule. The parking situation is also perfect compared to most other colleges. One other standout is the excellent library. Don't rule out Guilford because you've never heard of them. It's a great school period.", "I was attracted to Guilford College because of its Peace and Conflict Studies degree as well as the small, close-knit community, beautiful campus, and absence of Greek life. Guilford was such a life-changing place that I can't even imagine what my life would have been like if I'd chosen a different school. The professors are top-notch and they actually care about you and whether you show up for class or turn in your homework and I knew I needed that kind of personalized attention to succeed academically. What truly makes Guilford great are the people. The friends I made while I was a student will be with me for the rest of my life and I keep in regular contact with them even though it's been almost 10 years since we graduated. People do really try to live up to the core values of community, diversity, equality, excellence, integrity, justice, and stewardship.", 'Beautiful campus and incredibly friendly students and staff', 'Guilford College was a fantastic experience for me and a life changing experience. I received what I feel was the best liberal arts foundation and education in my major I could get. The school is tight nit and people know each other from students to staff. The atmosphere is very progressive and "family" like. The time there I did not only "learn" my courses, but my mind was opened to life in a wider world view. I looked at the world and problems differently. I learned to think critically, to analyze, to be logical and to approach the problems of inequality, for example, by not just individual charity, but by structural change in society. Psychological change in how people perceive liberty, "wealth", and freedom. The whole American myth of oppression and opportunity and then the \'Me" concept is so rampant the country is devolving and students are losing site of these ideals because student loans are driving them to the private sector, where creativity is crushed and debt is making them robotic. Now have  PhD in Psychology [although told I would never even make through a MA] and a PhD in Philosophy.']

name: Guilford Technical Community College
reviews:
['If you’re a CCP student hoping to get ahead, please read this — my experience at GTCC actually pushed me backward academically.

I’m 16, have always maintained a 3.91 GPA, and was a year ahead in school. I joined GTCC’s CCP program hoping to stay on that path. Instead, GTCC confused me with another student for over a month, which completely derailed my enrollment. Because of that mistake, I missed the first 8‑week semester and was forced into the second one with almost no course options left.

Since I needed online classes, the only choices available were Art and English. I started the semester already behind, rushed, and stressed — all because of delays I didn’t cause.

The biggest issue happened in my Art class: Canvas, the online program they used, locked my instructor out of one of my major assignments, and I wasn’t allowed to redo it. That single assignment was a huge part of my grade, and because no one fixed the issue, my GPA dropped to a 2.0. For someone who has always worked hard to stay ahead, that was devastating.

I filed a grade complaint, hoping someone would help. GTCC didn’t respond for an entire month. When they finally emailed me, they required a same‑day reply — on a Friday — even though I had already withdrawn and moved to another college by then. I wasn’t checking my GTCC email anymore, so I never saw it in time.

Overall, GTCC’s disorganization, slow communication, and lack of support directly harmed my academic progress. I hope future CCP students get a better experience than I did. Honestly, I would give zero stars if I could.', 'I was crazy excited together back into college. When I got there and did everything I was supposed to do and send, to be truthful, I came across people was helpful because they seen the excitement on me. They kept telling me that, " they didn't get emails ".And I'm showing them everything I've sent So I traveled all the way back home and thank God, I caught the mall man to get more information. Make a long story short, I came across this lady in making sure I could get in my classes. This lady look me in my face and said, " No you can't come in this semester but you can start in January 2026, and I'm sorry". I'm like , you don't even know because she didn't even ask. She didn't smile or make me feel like I was going to be re assured. I'm was seeing if I could pay on the spot. My classes started on the 16 of October and I go to figure out my financial aid. I just packed my information and left. I guess its a standard to meet in community colleges now. I feel like, never mind because I'm going to get my degree. And to everyone that's trying to come back to college to better their self, don't give up. It's always some stepping over people out there.😇🥰', 'Guildford Technical Communit (GTCC) is a nice College with good Specified and Tetiary Lecturers who help in Technology and good Healthcare for a brilliant future for students and other family members in Healthcare needs such as dental care at North  Carolina (NC, USA 🇺🇸)', 'I was super excited to register for classes. I had already set up my student email , sent over my transcripts , finished my fafsa application & my new student orientation. My last step was to stop by and register for classes. So that’s what I did.
On Friday I got my self and my two children ready and drove up to the campus so that I could register for classes.  And ask them questions. I was so excited to go only to get there and get dismissed.

The admissions lady that was supposed to help seemed to be annoyed with my questions and was speaking to me with an attitude. She didn’t answer any of my questions just  told me to come back in December for the next semester. Instead of encouraging me or trying to help me out now.

Actually before I even drove up to the school I had looked on the school page  to see when  the deadlines were and if I even could sign up.
The deadline for some classes was on August 8th which was the day that I stopped by the school. She could have helped me but instead she dismissed me and now it actually might be too late for me to registered **sighs** so  I got my hopes up for nothing. But nonetheless I had also stopped by the campus because I had some questions about college and was so startled by the fact that the admissions lady didn’t even try to help me she just shut me down almost kicking me out of her office telling me to “try again next semester “
I thought we were gonna make a plan and see what classes I needed to take. But instead got almost kicked out of her office….

Why work here if you’re not truly passionate about watching students succeed? I thought teachers like to see their students succeed? If my questions were annoying her she could have pointed me in the direction of someone that would’ve helped me. Instead of belittling me. I literally left crying and my 9 year old son was in the car trying to comfort me. In the parking lot of the campus. I’m still upset about this encounter.
I’m so shocked that a teacher/ administrator could speak to me in such a way. Especially because my son was with me and I was being very respectful towards her.
Now I don’t know what to do or what college to attend anymore because I always heard good things about this college and I was excited and was really hoping to go here.
I’m super bummed out and  I’m looking to register somewhere else in the next semester.wish it could have been here. This is the school I wanted to be at.

Thanks for nothing GTCC.
What a way to help a student mother out.', "Hello! I am here to let you know my story through the school for the CNA class. The teachers are not there to help you at all. Literally will make it impossible for you to succeed in the class especially if you even miss ONE assignment. You can email and call everyone you would like and no one would be of any service or valuable help. I had the teacher  Sara kilibreth solodow. I emailed her several times, on different platforms and she got back to me days later and wasn't even any help then. They just want to take your money. Please go find somewhere else if you can. My experience with this school was honestly the worst I have ever had in my life. Not even the dean seemed to care. This was just honestly awful. I would give zero stars if I could."]

name: Halifax Community College
reviews: ['Called to inquire about a student email not working and was completely brushed off by front desk. She stated that “I’m just front desk”. Lets live in 2019 and be united.', "Southern Soul Valentine's Day concert"]

name: Haywood Community College
reviews: ['I went here for a driving course in buildings 1600, for escorting oversize,over wide, over height, overweight, and wide loads.. immediately after entering the door, it was clear to me that this place was a autobody class and maybe a mechanic class. inside the building was very clean for one the restrooms, and all the vending machines was neat, with access. And the instructor was great. She was very thorough with her job and talked about everything made sure that everyone in the room understood and knew exactly what we were trying to learn. So thanks Haywood community college my experience there was great.', 'I am currently attending college at Haywood community college. The staff has been very accommodating to me in spite of this being a rural area. I have issues with accessibility and they have gone over and above to work with me. For the first few weeks, I needed help getting to classes. I am totally blind and the campus is rather large. A member of the staff was willing to walk with me every day until I could learn the route. The advisers are also very considerate of students needs. They have been wonderful. If there were an award for community colleges, I would definitely recommend Haywood community college.', "I went to my niece's graduation.They have several graduations because the auditorium is too small for all the graduates and families but ample enough to accommodate a fairly large crowd.\n\nThe campus is beautiful. It has a walking trail around a pond. That area is famous for high school prom pictures.", 'The campus of HCC is a beautiful place to walk in the spring. There are many nature trails and gardens on the grounds of the college. The administrative staff was very helpful in giving me the information that I needed about continuing education courses.', 'I attend college here. There are many things to do including hiking, Frisby, walking, ect. There is a pond, complete with a small water wheel. Also, if you like geocatching, there are two on this campus. Beautiful trails, helpful staff, and who-hoo a library! Our mascot is the Bobcat.']

name: High Point University
reviews:
["I have mostly fond memories of studying at HPU debate camp for one summer. It's a lovely, if small, campus but the facade of the immaculate model-home, manicured topiary,  curbside appeal is alluring and appropriate, since there is a soulless aspect to its campus life and (lack of) school spirit.

It certainly doesn't help that there are literally no students at all in the campus photos, above
No people at all. It's creepy, but telling.

However, the admin, profs and staff were very kind, helpful and extremely prepared to facilitate learning.......even if they all seemed like they wish they were at another university.

Western? UNCG? ASU?

Dare to dream, eh?", 'Went for a visit to High Point University to encourage kids to seek higher education.  The campus was well taken care of.  Would like to visit again.', "It's like no other school I've visited before. Their marketing should be studied! Beautiful campus with lots of amazing resources... the food isn't bad either. Experiential learning at its finest. So far, I have nothing bad to say about High Point.", 'This is a comment on the type of students you might run across at HPU:  After retiring from public education, I worked at HPU for two years as a study hall monitor in the athletic department.  The students I met during my time there were courteous, disciplined and hard working.  99% were great kids!  In truth, I believe they bucked the stereotype that "all HPU students are spoiled rich kids.". They have demanding academic and practice schedules.', 'High Point University has been an amazing experience for my daughter! From the moment she started, we’ve seen incredible growth in her confidence, academics, and leadership skills. The campus environment is beautiful and welcoming, and the staff and faculty truly care about the students. The opportunities for personal and professional development have been abundant, and it’s clear that HPU is dedicated to student success. We are beyond grateful for the positive impact it has had on her life!']

name: Isothermal Community College
reviews:
['This is an excellent place to take the kids for a picnic.  There is a fantastic picnic area next to the pond at the entrance.  It is cleaned and maintained on a regular basis.

I love taking my kids for a short visit to feed the ducks.  We always bring rolled oats to feed the ducks instead of bread, because it is much better for them.  They love the oats!

There are also some beautiful large fish and turtles in the pond that you can feed as well.

There are some fun steep hills and large oak trees for the kids to play on too.

This is an excellent community college with a nice picnic area for visitors!', "My son and I spent time at Imogene Lake to feed the ducks. It's was a beautiful fall day. There are picnic tables for a quick bite or to take a seat and a trail to walk off your food. Fair warning ⚠️ the ducks are not shy!", 'This is a great place to go take college classes and get exercise as well. The staff and teachers were very knowledgeable while I attended and now, being finished with college, I still love to go and walk around the campus for exercise. There is a beautiful pond in the front to walk around as well as lots of walking trails. Lots of pavement so you can take the kids to ride their bikes.', 'Whatever you do, do not take online courses here! Its a complete debacle and totally horrific. You will get nothing but extreme amounts of busy work that will not teach you much but how to feel overwhelmed with nothing but busy work. Viewing and understanding the grades page is almost impossible and extremely difficult to read. Then when your course is done you will not be able to see any grades or info on that course as the info will be removed. These courses are expensive to begin with. Go to Pheonix. Its the obvious better choice, even though I figured that out too late. This school is not worth doing anything online. My spouse has a masters degree, and even she agreed this course was horrific.', 'Did my graphic design classes here. Also has one of the best Radio & TV Broadcasting programs in the state. The Small Business Center (inside the Foundation building) is phenomenal at connecting potential and current entrepreneurs with the resources and guidance they need to succeed. I teach classes through the SBC. Great experience as a student AND as an  instructor. College is a huge asset to the community.']

name: James Sprunt Community College
reviews: ["The school is great overall. However anytime I call I have a hard time getting in contact with anyone and no one returns my phone calls. Registration is almost over and I've been reaching out to my advisor since the beginning of last month to register and still no response. I know that I am not the only student and there are many reaching out for help but it is just ridiculous that I haven't received a response in a month now.", 'Great small town college, good variety of courses online in person. And hybrid. Awesome instructors who work with you and want to see you succeed. Many programs avaible like the spartan table,, tutoring,, designed to support the diverse population of a community College. As a working parent, their flexible classes and support was amazing.', 'Best school. Instructors are humble, cordial and understanding expected for one Maths instructor but other than him all of them are great. I will recommend this school to anyone.', 'Greatly enjoying presenting a series on social media marketing for here at the small business center. It is a beautiful campus to walk around. If you are a small business owner make sure to check out the outstanding services offered by the small business center including training and consulting for no charge.', "I attended the Small Business Center's class last night for the first time. This is a great resource for local business to take advantage of. Just because they don't charge you anything doesn't mean the classes aren't worth anything. Every small business owner should be in attendance."]

name: Johnson C Smith University
reviews: ["All though the dorms aren't the best the classrooms also might be small but it is the attitude everyone has they are all so happy to be there it seems no one is judgy or mean.The teachers are sooo nice and understanding,Mr Gregory took an assignment that was 2 MONTHS! late its insane i'm happy to be a graduate at JCSU CLASS OF 2024!", 'My son is enjoying his time at JCSU. He loves his new school, and I love that for him. He’s found a place where he’s growing, and I am happy with his decision to go there.', 'HBCU Proud, JCSU Bound!!! Moved my son in... Class of 2028! Had an excellent experience even if the GBA orientation was a tad bit chaotic. It was still great seeing the campus and JCSU leadership/faculty.', 'My daughters enjoyed the guided tour with Daniel from Admissions. They learned a lot (and so did I)...Gaming & Gaming Management is a thing! By thing, I mean a minor. This school seems to really be invested in the future of their students.', 'Visited for an event for Congresswoman Adams. Nice  campus. Clean inviting.']

name: Johnston Community College
reviews:

name: Lees-McRae College
reviews:
['Beautiful campus and everyone is so nice. reviews: ['Nice college. reviews: ["Amazing! I love the place as I'm a student there currently! Love all the professors and Perks is amazing! name: Martin Community College
reviews: ['This was a successful B2B transaction as we worked with Martin Community College to fabricate and install their EMC/monument signs! Thank you for your business!', 'We were there for FFA horse judging. The equine program is AWESOME  with great facilities.', 'This review pertains to the equestrian program specifically. I have not been a student personally  but was intrigued by the notion of an equestrian program  at a community college level. Having attended a community college myself, I can see the value in offering programs that are more financially accessible. My understanding was  that the students work with professionals  to learn about and eventually get to start young horses. Bearing this in mind,  I indulged the request to  use a young horse of mine  as one of the ones to be started by  a student  with  professional supervision. The director and instructor, Tammy Thurston is the individual who teaches the Colt starting class. Upon the return of my filly, she could walk, trot and Canter both directions in an arena. But, she also had girth sores resulting in scarring from the training methods used and her feet were overgrown despite having been told she would be trimmed every 4 weeks. Anyone with any sense knows how important maintaining correct hoof balance is in overall development. Furthermore, when I arrived to pick her up I noted she had a runny nose with yellowish green discharge. It was later noted that she had an accompanying cough. When I asked about the duration of symptoms I was told that several of the horses had had a runny nose recently from allergies. A week later after a vet visit and plenty of antibiotics her respiratory symptoms have improved. Because of my concern for the well-being of the horses in the program I brought my concerns to the director. Initially, the position of the director was that the college was not responsible for the care of the horses in that class because the students had signed lease agreements with the owners to use for the class. My concerns were belittled and more or less blamed on the student that had used the horse for the class. What\'s worse is that the instructor/director further stated that she and her husband train 20 to 30 horses a year and that 75% of them develop girth stores and white hairs AKA scarring. It says a lot about the mind of my young horse that she didn\'t retaliate because of the pain and cause serious injury. While the program may be a good price, I\'m afraid you get what you pay for as a student seeking an education working with horses. Hopefully, my concerns will not be dismissed and something will be done about the choice of farrier and the involvement of the instructors in the care of the horses beyond "training" them to be ridden.', 'If you are a small business you need to check out their free Small Business Center free small businesses resources. It is a delightful campus and I was told they have one of the states leading equestrian programs. You can see the horses at the side of the school.', "I was at a free Bookkeeping Seminar at Martin Community College. We received great information from the instructor and valuable networking time also. I'm so happy to be part of this community."]

name: Mayland Community College
reviews: ['At this community college they treat you like you’re back in high school. Probably because half of the school’s population is early college high school students, since most adults would rather go somewhere that treats them like actual adults. The instructors also seem convinced they are teaching at an Ivy League university. I guess some people never got enough validation during their own school years, so now they prove their academic worth by making simple prerequisite classes  miserable for everyone else. The best part is that more than ninety percent of these classes have absolutely nothing to do with what you are actually going to school for. So, get ready to waste your time and money! Oh and God forbid life happens. Work, kids, emergencies, you know… normal adult responsibilities, apparently do not exist in their world. These people the school likes to call “instructors” are more like robots who make no mistakes. Except they hate robots because they can’t get through one lecture without mentioning AI and how they don’t like it. It’s like if they don’t talk about it the dean is going to fire them or something. Which hey… might not be a bad idea. Good luck trying to get in touch with an advisor too. I guess they have better things to do like tweaking their assignments to be only achievable if you sever your leg and post it to the Moodle form.\nAnyways, go Mayland Community College Highland Cows!', 'Wonderful campus in a beautiful setting. It was a real joy to offer training here through the small business center to the entrepreneur class.', "I have enjoyed taking classes here at Mayland. I couldn't ask for better instructors, they all show that they care about us students and are willing to help if needed. I am also part of the National Honors Society of Leaders and Success and in the S.O.A.R. program. The faculty as well as the instructors all go out of their way to help students achieve their goals and to be successful in life!", 'The most outstanding Community College you will find. Seriously, they are very forward thinking and are making a huge impact in the community. what other community college can boast a 3D printer, telescope, observatory, green houses, full scale welding center, and is undertaking a massive hotel/ convention center project. They are doing more than lots of university systems.', "It'd a fun school with nice teachers and people. Some of the teachers are nice. Get to hang out with people . Its a fun place in life skills and work skills class."]

name: McDowell Technical Community College
reviews: ['Tech is the best!  Great college with great instructors.  Small classes allow the student to get all the help they may need. The campus is easy to navigate and the walking trail that leads to the fishing pond is awesome.', "Hannah Berthelson in the financial aid department is amazing to work with, I highly recommend every student to go see her! I was lucky enough to work as a work study in student services and that was hands down the best job I have ever had. Kim, Lisa, Debbie, Kelly, Sharon, Briana, Dr. Gossett .. They were the best!!  I miss them all so much!!', 'I absolutely love it I got a facial Samantha Calderon I loved it. That was my first facial but it want be my last. AMAZING.thank you']

name: Meredith College
reviews: ['I loved touring Meredith college with my dad and Dr. Lisa Rouff! It was so much fun and shout out to our tour guide Lizzy Sevilla!', 'My daughter just graduated today.   It was a beautiful ceremony.  She has been VERY happy attending school here.  The campus is amazing and the small-size classes and tight-knit community feel is amazing.', 'Drove there and walked around today. It was spring break but I did get to check out a few buildings and athletic facilities. Beautiful softball field and a nice soccer/track complex. The people I know who went there loved it.', 'Beautiful campus! My daughter starts going this fall. She is blessed with this opportunity and I came wait to see where it takes her', "Our daughter is a sophomore student and she loves her College. The teachers are very professionals and are available to help.  The staff is very friendly. If the student doesn't have a car, she can rent one inside the college. The place inside and around the college is very safe; if somebody lose anything, it always appears. We were welcome since the first day.  She feels that Meredith is her second home and we, like parents, are very happy about that."]

name: Methodist University
reviews: ['Wonderful opportunities to be gained here!  The campus is self contained but connected to the local community.  The Music and PA programs are top notch.', 'PA graduate here— wonderful education and still see how my training has paid off 5 years later. The school is well recognized in the medical community.', 'The campus Police and Security DON\'T KNOW THE LAW here.  NC Statute states § 14-269.2 section (K) if you have concealed carry handgun holder, you can keep your handgun in your car.  These officers have made statements that "No one can have guns on campus, to include federal officers and deputies."  The security here is power hungry and it is scary because they will call the police on you for legally carrying a firearm in your car... Legally...  If you don\'t know, when the police hear "firearm on campus" they come guns out and ready, regardless of the law.\n\nI saw the other comments on here about security and it\'s true.  Be careful around the security and law enforcement on this campus.  The clerk at the police station stated the same thing "No firearms on campus! Even if they are licensed or with another agency."  Which again, is not the case.', "The campus was nice, small intimate.The class sizes from what I seen were small. The staff is very helpful and friendly. It's a private College so the students to staff ratio is good. Not alot of food places to eat on campus,  but they do have Starbucks and Chick fil a😋. Classes are not that far apart you can walk to class from the dorms that's a plus for me.", "Let me start off by saying there are some awesome teachers and staff here, BUT you do have that slim group that makes the overall experience not so pleasant. I've always heard rumors around campus that some ethic groups can be treated a little unfairly, but I had not experienced it first hand until recently. I was treated very rudely by a staff member and I did report it. Of course I was given the standard apology in which I expected, but I felt like everything else was followed up with fluff about policies of the campus. I'm sure do to confidentiality I would not be told whether this person had any disciplinary action or not. I'm sure nothing happened and that is just my personal opinion. This was not the first time I had been encountered with an unpleasant response from this same person. I would not even go as far as saying do not attend this campus, because it is some positive things and people at the campus. BUT make it a last choice if you other options. I am here for one purpose only and that's to obtain a degree in which I will Do, but it is always nice to be respected by employees of an organization where lots of money is being spent. At the end of the day if there aren't any students they would not be getting paid."]

name: Mitchell Community College
reviews: ["Great experience! Winter choral concert was festive and wonderful. Best of all, it was Free!! Mitchell needs to do more sharing of events on social media, not saying they don't, but just more. The community is missing out.", "As a staff member I just wanted to clarify the review by Trudy. We do not ask for proof of residence to use our library. All community college libraries are public. Also, our computers are available to all our patrons for however long they would need to use them. In the event of all of them being used and a student needing to get on one we would probably ask a public library patron to accommodate the student. However we do have an adequate amount of computers that we haven't run into that problem yet. : )\nIf you want a nice quiet place to study, we are your library! It is especially quiet on days when school is out but we are open. The staff are friendly and willing to help with research and computer needs. We also have many interesting books and movies. Come on in and check some out! : )", 'Have used the library and computers on numerous occasions. Open to non-college folks with proof of city residence. Student employees helpful when needed. Computer time limited if not a student. Great resource, though! This college is growing fast! Lots of programs not normally available to those not looking for a degree. Short programs/training for those wanting additional information for better jobs, etc. Finally knocked down old hospital on West End St and a new nursing school will begin to be erected soon according to press releases. Will bring more traffic to area but learning facilities are always a boom to the area.', 'I was a senator at MCC . Going to college here was amazing. So many great memories !', 'Highly recommended, very affordable. Professors very knowledgeable and care about their students grades. Former graduate 👩\u200d🎓']

name: Montgomery Community College
reviews: ['Montgomery County Community College is a nice and good place to learn. They have a huge Campus at Blue Bell and several majors available.', 'What a wonderful experience. Earned my Associates degree here. If you pick your teachers and meet with them before taking thier class, you can earn a University education with top notch teachers who do teach in Universities also.', "Very nice and friendly community college. One of the best such colleges in this area, famous for their liberal arts programs  but now has become equally good in stem branches and other professional studies. Modern and rapidly expanding facilities, newly built huge science, health sciences building, labs and theater along with a huge modern auditorium with new building for culinary arts coming up, all in the middle of a colorful expansive campus, that changes color according to the seasons, dedicated friendly staff, faculty and eager students, all from diverse and talented background, really caring, it's been a pleasure teaching mathematics there for the last six years! This place has really and fundamentally converted me from being a skeptic to an ardent cheerleader for the community college system, you will be surprised to find out what are programs they run, and at an affordable price point also. Really gets you ready if you either want to go on further towards higher education or simply want to get a head start with an associates degree in a myriad of disciplines. I have a past student that is going to go to NASA!", 'Was charged over $1000 for classes I tried to unenroll from several times WEEKS before the deadline. My counselor took every opportunity to slow down the process as much as possible and was extremely difficult to work with and generally had a bad attitude. He made it clear that any unenrollments need to be made through him, yet my multitude of emails stating that I had no intentions of attending another semester and demanding that I be unenrolled either went unanswered or were met with half-assed responses several days and sometimes even weeks later. Despite several documented instances of me attempting to unenroll before the deadline the school doubled down and passed off the $1000 to a debt collection agency.', 'Due to unforeseen circumstances that had happened to me, I had to withdraw from two classes. I had a medical letter written from a Doctor to provide documentation of my withdraw yet it was rejected. I’m being charged $1600 because I could not attend my classes due to medical issues I had during the time. It seems they will make no exception if you decide to withdraw past the due date no matter the reason.']

name: Montreat College
reviews: ['We attended a high school baseball game on your campus on Friday evening.   First I will mention the fact that the field is not accessible for handicapped persons.  secondly, there were no restrooms for anyone to use, not even a porta John.   You have obviously poured $1000 into your Astra turf field, but can’t afford to have operating restrooms.   Shame on you!  Montreat you can do better than this.', "I was a student at the university for a year, and I left a year ago. They've been writing to me and sending me emails for a month asking me to pay a $16 fine, according to them, hahaha. It says a lot about a university to ask for $16 a year after I left 👏👏", 'We toured during the summer when the campus was undergoing some upgrades and most buildings were locked. Our tour guide was unable to get into several buildings such as the cafeteria and male dorms. The tour was brief and not very helpful. The campus is crowded, there is very limited student parking so students are asked to park in town and shuttle to school. The dorms are in terrible condition. I wouldn’t wish that on anyone. There is a smell of campsite restrooms in the one we toured, urine with dampness. The dorm room model was cramped and dirty. They had made it a three person room and removed all but one desk saying most students study on their beds!   Clearly they added an extra bed to these once double rooms to accommodate more students and make more money. Every student needs a decent workspace. This did not make sense to us. And the model bathroom was dirty. The carpet in the hallway was threadbare and everything smelled damp. The rock and marble work of all the buildings is pretty but unfortunately causes a dampness. Montreat is not gated and very close to the town. People and tourists were walking all around nearby and it would be very easy to access the grounds at any time. They do not have full time security.', 'BEWARE: "Surviving off ancestors work & reputation" stage of deprecation. $40k/ Semester to find your own YouTube training and get a little paragraph from adjuncts as "education". A couple courses have actual educational provisions. Otherwise it\'s just you, the book, and the test. Free courses on YouTube have multitudes better training. They hide behind "you\'re not Godly" as retaliation to any feedback. Only survive by using religion as gaslighting and an epic campus handed down by ancestry far greater. Sad. Truly sad and pathetic literally the worst by far of any education I\'ve ever had. Flee like Sodom and Gomorrah. Probably have been infiltrated by Marxists to destroy a Christian institution. Tragic. I really wanted to enjoy this place.', 'Awesome small liberal arts college (former alumnus). Several, world class rock climbing locations within an hour drive, snow boarding close by with weekday student rates for weekdays in winter, 15 minutes from Asheville!! Loved the small class sizes and hard to beat the location on the East Coast.']

name: University of Mount Olive
reviews: ["We attended our grand daughters first college softball games yesterday! They won both games! More importantly, what a great program - great leadership - great values - great education - we are so happy for our grand daughter and our family - its funny how God makes everything work out. Long story! University of Mt. Olive is just a wonderful setting for a true education, values, morals, life skills - I'd also like to thank my grand daughters assistant softball coach - Jason - what a great leader - passionate - kind - giving and really a great leader & role model for Cadence and the team - keep up the good work! Thanks again! Bob & Diane", 'This university is beautiful, quiet, and has an overall inviting atmosphere. They have exceptional staff! When I toured here, I was amazed at the professionalism and the thoroughness in which everything was explained. This is a Christian based university with a variety of degree options, mainly liberal arts based. However, they have agricultural degree options and facilities that are well maintained. This includes their farm and arboretum. I was highly impressed by what I saw.', 'I was pleasantly surprised when my daughter and I visited this campus.  It is a small University, but it is spaciously laid out.  I think this gives it a bigger appearance. The campus has beautiful large trees that line the campus.  Overall, it had a nice hometown feel.', 'UMO is a Liberal Arts University in Eastern NC and is one of the most unique private educational institutions in North Carolina. The University of Mount Olive was founded by the Original Free Will Baptists as a liberal arts institution with defining Christian principles for more than half a century. To top it off, Mt Olive is the home of the famous Mt Olive Pickle Company. Education and pickles, quite the combination.', 'This is a great college with a small town feel with small class sizes I loved it there class of 2006']

name: Nash Community College
reviews: ["This course plays very nice,and it definitely has tight lines you have to hit,open shots and the wind plays a factor as well on the right day. I really enjoyed playing there today and would definitely make the drive again to have some fun at this course. I recommend it to anyone and am looking forward to another tournament out that way at that campus! I had one of the Best cards I could ask for,these ladies were fun and great attitudes and funny and knew how to throw some plastic,hats off to them,and I'm honored to have met them and play 2 rounds with. All around 4.5 stars for this place in my opinion and food was close by in case you didn't bring anything during the break. Very satisfied and had a blast out there today,go get some rounds in everyone!", 'Nice campus. Seems like they have a programming to over based on review of courses from their website', "I've been here for 5 years (2010-2015) and I must say it's been a pretty good experience. The teachers are really nice and are helpful..most of the time. The only complaint I have is the high prices of food and drink..$1.49 for 1 cup of tea?!?! But other than that this is a good place to learn.", "My husband currently goes here to receive his Class A Trucking license through the SAGE program. The registration process was so easy, and during our first meeting they gave us the complete class schedule with a breakdown of the cost in an easy to read format. There are no hidden costs or fees. Everyone we spoke to was extremely helpful and polite. The cost covered the physical, driving records, all materials (pens, paper, printed book for the test), and the test itself. Everything is done at the school aside from the physical, and they even have an app to help you study for the test. We researched many schools, and you really can't get your license any easier than this. Thank you Amy and Amelia for all your help!", "Today I went to my brothers graduation. I caught a cold a few days before the graduation but I couldn't miss this moment. The graduation is in progress and I'm trying my best to not go to the bathroom to blow my nose, but I can't. I go to the bathroom a few times because I needed to. It is towards the end of graduation and I had to go to the bathroom one last time. I'm approaching the door and the security guy (middle-aged, obese white guy with glasses) tells me that I went to the bathroom four times and if I need to go then I couldn't come back. I understood. What I disliked was when he stated his opinion towards me with an attitude behind it. I do not believe that it is that man's job to judge who goes to the bathroom! Nash needs better security fast! I will not tolerate this!!!"]

reviews:

name: University of North Carolina Asheville
reviews:
["Me & my wife went there for a college tour since I'll be transferring here soon within the next year. The person that gave the tour did a wonderful job and was very knowledgeable with answering all my questions. The campus is very beautiful ❤️ I had great fun just exploring with on the tour, they no have me sold on transferring to here with all the available things for the students! 😍 Can't wait.", 'I’m an alumni and prospective students should know that this school has turned its back on its mission of conservation and environmentalism. if you are considering enrolling in this school for its mission of conservation and dedication to the environment, as I was, then know this school no longer cares about the environment or the local community of which it is part of.
As an alumni, seeing this school trying to destroy a 40 acre forest after the devastation and mass tree loss from hurricane Helene, is extremely disappointing to say the least. Not only has the university refused to listen to the local community concerns and even its own students, but it went to the state government for a bill that would allow them to ignore city ordinances. My advice, if you care about conservation, natural splendor and environmentalism, go else ware.', 'If you want the best 'education' from their "Music Technology" program, just make sure your nose as far up Jude Weinberg as you possibly can get it and he knows that you know he is the greatest thing to ever walk the Earth.

I learned more in a few weeks from actual educators and a real studio for a few hundred dollars than I did in 4 semesters and thousand upon thousands of dollars at UNCA.

Universities are not what they used to be. This school is a joke. They spent millions on a basketball arena, the school has no athletics program worth speaking of. The SWIM TEAM is probably the best ranked team among the entire college.

Jude was THE WORST instructor pretending to be a teacher I have had throughout my entire life.', 'I was drawn to UNCA because of the natural beauty and enjoyed spending time in the contiguous woods. I graduated over twenty years ago and it is extremely unfortunate that a public school is considering developing the woods when the public does not want the development to happen. It is not fair for the few stakeholders at the top to presuppose that this misguided development will behoove the student body when considering their full life experience. The people who come to this area simply to spend time in these woods, including the writer herein, are deeply disappointed and the loss of their presence and benefit to the campus area will hurt the community. Both Warren Wilson and Montreat have thriving campus communities with a lot more preserved natural areas and it would be unthinkable for them to develop their natural areas as they know how beneficial they are. As a former UNCA soccer player I can attest that destroying the last remaining nature corridors in the area will not increase the competitiveness of the team and will only lower the health and wealth of the community and student body. Alumni and parents please consider sending your donations and adult children to a public system that serves the public and doesn’t embellish an appointed hierarchy of disregard. I respectfully and adamantly disagree with anyone who opines that Hurricane Helene-related damage can be fixed by destroying more natural areas that actually mitigate anthropomorphic climate changes to our environment. Nature does not exist simply to monetize. Moreover this decision disregards the swell of mental health issues facing society and the student body including the worst scenarios that have happened in the UNC system in recent years. Numerous studies link more time spent in natural settings with better overall wellbeing. Streamlining UNCA into another unsustainable developed area is not what the alumni want. People will now have one less convenient area to enjoy and the natural highlights of the campus will be forever lost. Good long-term planning and public sentiment should transcend the putative outcomes of this development.', 'Make sure to make your voice heard about keeping local zoning control local — oppose HB926!!! Leave the trees!

If it wasn’t being run into the ground by greedy dinosaurs and demogorgons, it could be a great school and asset to the community they claim to be apart of.']

name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
reviews:
['At University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, the academic environment often encourages active engagement and visible intellectual contribution. Many classes emphasize discussion and analytical thinking, and students are expected to interact directly with faculty and peers. Because participation and reasoning are central to coursework, motivated students often feel pushed to develop their ideas and defend them in a serious academic setting.

The experience at University of California, Davis can feel structurally different. Its very large scale and decentralized departments mean that academic rigor varies widely from course to course. Some students report that meaningful challenge depends largely on their own initiative rather than being consistently embedded in the system.

Critics also argue that in such a large environment, highly driven students may sometimes encounter competitive or unsupportive dynamics from peers or in group settings. Instead of being consistently nurtured, ambitious students may feel that they have to protect their work, navigate academic politics, or seek opportunities outside the standard structure in order to continue growing.

At UC Davis, professors tend to retaliate students who follow the facts but not do some theatre acts. Some very top students can face consistent interferences due to professors’ low ceiling and low quality of their TA and peers. Social manipulation and strategic flattering seem to be more important than learning.

In this contrast, UNC can appear to provide a more cohesive intellectual culture that encourages development, while UC Davis may feel more diffuse, leaving students to create their own academic pressure and pathways for advancement.', 'The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, legendary for its historic charm and academic prestige, remains the gold standard in my professional circles for balancing a "public Ivy" reputation with a deeply rooted commitment to the common good. From numerous meaningful dialogues with Tar Heel alumni and researchers, it is clear that the institution possesses a merytorical depth that elevates every student it touches, fostering a unique blend of intellectual curiosity and civic leadership. My acquaintances frequently highlight the university's world-class medical and pharmacy programs, noting that the level of clinical sophistication and research moxie found on campus is truly transformative for the entire Southeast. In frequent discussions regarding the nation’s top-tier universities, the public consensus consistently identifies Chapel Hill as a place where heritage meets cutting-edge innovation, managed with an undeniable class that honors its long history. I am particularly struck by the faculty’s accessibility and their passion for social impact, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their children flourish in such a culturally rich and academically rigorous environment. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration maintains a visionary and transparent approach, ensuring the university remains a dependable pillar of both tradition and progress. Friends who have navigated the humanities and business tracks often point to the institution’s powerful global network as a decisive catalyst for their professional success and personal growth. The general sentiment among the community is that UNC-Chapel Hill is not just a school, but a distinguished intellectual hub that nurtures the soul of North Carolina while competing at the highest international levels. Reflecting on these consistently glowing testimonials, I view this university as a premier institution that carries out its educational mandate with grace, integrity, and a profound respect for the future.', 'Went to the Smith Center for the UNC Duke basketball game. UNC won on a 3 point shot by Seth Trimble. Pregame there was a good luck message from Drake Maye. I am still celebrating.', 'We visited the UNC campus as tourists, and thoroughly enjoyed our visit. A supremely well manicured and well maintained campus with a number of buildings that are couple of hundred years old.

You can just walk randomly and still take in a lot of the campus, but it is even better if you have someone who knows the campus and can tell you why to take a sip of water at the fountain or a bit of history of the Old West building.

We recommend the Coker Arboretum, a calming oasis with some excellent fauna (tiger lilies!).', 'Academics are decent, not outstanding. Student body quite rude and stuck up. Faculty do not give proper guidance and support. Not worth it for out of state students.']

name: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
reviews:
["I am a junior going into my senior year in biology.
There are no classes outside of the common core available for me to take next semester. My academic advisor stood me up multiple times for email and Zoom interviews. The lab instructor / teaching advisor was insulting students and was on their phone constantly during class time. My cell biology instructor informed me that I make 'stupid mistakes' during my test review. My online LEADS class had multiple due dates listed for each assignment, almost every assignment, usually with grammatical errors. The tragic safety incident this semester involving a young woman using a campus-provided transportation method that goes into the city raised serious concerns about campus safety and the university's communication/security protocols, especially because she died of a violent crime.
Honestly, it has been a terrible first semester experience as a transfer student, despite my passing grades. I consider community colleges to be better staffed and better behaved than this university, and am considering if I would like to pursue a degree at a different academic establishment.", 'Thanks for making the graduation ceremony a truly miserable experience. Parking was a nightmare, and there was not enough seating for the disabled.  I ended up watching the whole thing on a screen next to the concession stand.', "Parking so bad its almost laughable. And the university would rather let in more and more students instead of accommodating for any of them by just building decks instead of parking lots. I've missed countless classes because I've had to park on the edge of campus and walk 20-30 minutes. This is what our tuition pays for??", 'Went to the College of Engineering here, plenty of opportunities to get involved in research, plenty of good professors. Maybe it doesn't have the funding of the "more reputable" universities - but that makes UNCC incredibly efficient at producing research results.

Student population knows how to turn up *when necessary*. Not really a party school - they get shut down pretty quick.

Chancellor takes pride on making himself available to the student population (but realize you're talking to a busy man, don't just e-mail his secretary to complain).

"It is what you make it" - I've heard this a lot at this university. That's generally true in life - so it shows people are learning.

Quality school - not MIT - but local and quality. Take it seriously and get serious results. If you don't.... well don't blame us. We done told you.', 'Was looking forward to the possibility of going to this school but the application and initial processes made it so horrendous that I wound up withdrawing my application altogether and looking elsewhere. Lots of improvements needed here.']

name: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
reviews:
['University of North Carolina at Greensboro was honestly disappointing.

Academically, it does not compare to schools like University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill or North Carolina State University. The classes didn’t feel very rigorous, and I wasn’t challenged the way I expected to be. It felt like the overall academic standards were lower, and there wasn’t a strong culture of pushing students to excel.

The campus vibe also wasn’t great. There are stereotypes about the school lacking ambition and professionalism, and from what I saw, that reputation didn’t come out of nowhere.

Dining was strange too. Having a whole “Fried Chicken Wednesday” tradition (with the Hellcats theme) being one of the big highlights just felt like the school focused more on gimmicks than actual quality.

Location is a problem too because the campus is located in the HOOD of Greensboro making everyday and night feel unsafe. There were times it genuinely felt like you had to constantly watch your surroundings.', "Went for a campus tour and honors tour. The staff and guides were extremely friendly, well versed and professional. There is a lot of growth and development with the school so that's a plus. The exercise facility was incredible. I only wished there would've been more information available about the offered majors... however, we did attend on graduation day so I understood.", 'Attended Admitted Spartans Day with my daughter in late March and we fell in love with this school. We have visited approximately 20 colleges to that point and none gave us the definitive feeling that this was HER school like UNCG. What sold us immediately was the academic program presentation for nursing. We loved that we had the opportunity to meet with about a dozen faculty, staff and  students who very clearly expressed their passion not only for the nursing profession but for UNCG during the Q&A and tour. The nursing school building itself is new which was also a welcome change as I have viewed quite a few nursing schools and they were very old and run down. They had state of the art facilities with numerous simulation labs and high fidelity mannequins as well as an anatomage table to practice dissection using 4D and I was excited to learn they will also be incorporating virtual reality into their program next year. Aside from the nursing school, we also enjoyed having a meal in one of the dining halls, checking out the dorms and walking around campus and meeting with other students along the way. Everyone was so lovely. Very excited for my daughter to start this fall!', 'I love UNC Greensboro! One of the most affordable and diverse public universities in NC :) The admin and staff are open to communicating and helping anyone with questions or concerns. You can tell they want their students to succeed!!', "I don't care if I can take anything, but I would really go crazy without food. I walk for 10 minutes and wait in line for 5 minutes and all I get is that they are out of drumsticks. They told me they ran out.  Then I get a piece of fried chicken with the skin all soft and raw inside. Then I threw away the plate of inedible garbage to get a burger which turned out to have mushy meat on the inside and black crumbs on the top and bottom of the bun and the whole thing tasted bitter in my mouth. Cups were unwashed 4 times a semester with sauce on them. Not to mention the chicken breast it was not cooked at all. We pay so much money to eat here and you give us garbage?"]

name: North Carolina Central University
reviews:

The sloping hills, the verdant green

name: University of North Carolina School of the Arts
reviews: ['Amazing campus and opportunity for a specialty education. Great programs for music, design, art, vocals, film, drama and dance for high schoolers and college-level students. Great to catch a show whether you like opera, drama, ballet, modern or film.
