name: North Carolina State University at Raleigh
reviews:
['This is a squarely mediocre university.

Support systems end up so-so:
The Military and Veteran Services are incredible.

Meanwhile, the Disability Resource Office can't help you with temporary accommodations for a broken wrist at all--Useless.

Advising is decidedly the worst I have ever experienced; They simply do not provide any worthwhile advice and encourage students to overburden themselves with classes as a quick fix to problems they caused, like putting you into the wrong major.

The on-campus clinic also repeatedly assures you your insurance will cover something and then the charge reliably ends up on your bill months later. "We'll waive it."--Charge still there.

Courses/Professors:
Shout out to Dr. Crume, an IBM Hall-of-Famer who comes to teach cybersecurity courses for the love of enlightening students. He's one of the few professors I've had who genuinely cares.

Meanwhile others will not accommodate for injuries, I had a broken wrist and a motorcycle accident in the same semester, zero deadline leniency was given.

Other professors pretend that their 1CH course is graduate-level and they require 10hrs/week of work for it--Totally out of touch.

Impressively NC State is a sub-city to Raleigh, everything a young adult could desire is on campus from decent food, to entertainment and plenty of makerspaces for tinkering and DIY. I think the only thing they are missing is a garage for DIY vehicle maintenance--I'm sure there are better ones, but campus is very nice.

The university also works with plenty of companies near and around the triangle to get students internship, mentor opportunities and the likes (at least for CompSci).', 'North Carolina State University, anchored in the heart of Raleigh, is consistently described in my professional and social circles as a formidable engine of innovation that masterfully translates "Think and Do" into a tangible reality for its diverse student body. From various substantive discussions with engineers and researchers in the Research Triangle Park, it is clear that NC State operates with a merytorical precision that places it at the absolute forefront of global STEM education. My acquaintances frequently highlight the university's exceptional ability to foster a sophisticated, high-performance environment, noting that graduates enter the workforce with a technical moxie that is highly coveted by the nation's leading tech firms. In frequent conversations about the North Carolina academic landscape, the public consensus praises the institution for its impressive Centennial Campus, which my peers describe as a visionary model for industry-academic partnership. I am particularly struck by the faculty's commitment to solving real-world challenges in agriculture and veterinary medicine, a sentiment echoed by many families I know who have seen their children thrive within these prestigious programs. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages this land-grant powerhouse with a transparent and forward-thinking hand, ensuring it remains a dependable pillar of economic growth. Friends who have navigated the school's graduate tracks often point to the high-impact research opportunities as a decisive factor in their career mobility, proving that an NC State degree carries significant weight internationally. The general sentiment among the community is that the university represents a distinguished hub of integrity and grit, skillfully balancing its ambitious goals with a profound respect for its heritage and its students. Reflecting on these consistently positive and grounded testimonials, I view North Carolina State University as a premier institution that fulfills its mission with undeniable class and an inspiring dedication to excellence.', 'As a former PhD student in Civil Engineering, it was such a nostalgic feeling to return to the main campus. So many nice memories here. I spent over 6 years at State (PhD and a few months of Post-Doc), and had so much fun. Both the staff and fellow students were so nice and helpful. My only disappointment (but a big one) was that there was no graduation ceremony for the year 2020 due to Covid. I have always felt incredibly lucky to be on Main Campus although I was in an engineering stream, so it was sad to see Mann Hall being demolished. Howling cow ice-cream tasted yum as usual. I will definitely recommend this university to anyone - one of the best in the country imo.', 'Great round of golf at Lonnie Poole with one of the best views in Raleigh', 'Beautiful school. Said tour was full just show up.  Arrived had no idea where to go. People on campus had no idea. No way tour full lucky if 30 people. 5 tour guides take all 30 instead of breaking up group.  Had to pay $2 an hour to park.  School does not give any vouchers. Toured many school this is the worst tour we took.']

name: North Carolina Wesleyan University
reviews: ['I went there in 1994 to 1995. The minute I stepped on campus I knew I wanted to leave. Back then tuition room and board were $12,000 yearly. I worked in the library and cafeteria. I ended up transferring to University of Tampa.', 'This is a great school for someone who wants small classes and wants to play sports. What needs to be noted is that no one is on campus on the weekends and there is not much to do off campus since it is a bad town. Finally the technology and facilities are lacking here, nothing compared to other local schools. But they are improving greatly over the last few years!', "The school has a very supportive faculty and staff. They go above and beyond and do the best they can to help there students. It's been a lot of fun being a bishop and I've learned and grown a lot.", 'Good place to stay at and it is not that big. The school has a moderately large campus and features a huge auditorium and a gym. The campus is very pretty and the dorms are what you would expect them to be. Other than the dorms the college is very nice.', "We went to my grandson's school band concert. It is great of them to allow it to be there."]

name: University of North Carolina Wilmington
reviews:
['My daughter is in her "Senior" year and what should be her best year. So far the ENTIRE experience has been horrific.  With what they are getting in tuition you would think the students would have better advising. Unfortunately, due to the lack of advisors she has been steered wrong multiple times. Then she gets penalized because she is told the wrong information.  The professors are no help and very rude. They are not leaders by any means.  They more or less treat students like idiots and offer no guidance. These young adults should be treated with a little more respect and guided in what should be a wonderful learning experience.  I have 4 biological children and 4 step children.  Most of which have, will, or want to go to college.  I will never again suggest UNCW to anyone as a good college.
My daughter will be graduating in May but will be considered an "Early Graduate" because some ill advised information when she started put her behind. She will have to take 1-2 classes during the summer. Now, because she is graduating in May as an "Early Graduate" she will not be on the commencement sheet, she will not get her cords or mentioned with her honors. If she waits until December to graduate she will be considered a "Late Graduate" and will have a whole other process to go through.
This is just the most recent experience with UNCW. There is so much more the has really caused difficulty and hardship for her. The amount of money that has been put into this school.  I will make sure that any child of mine or their friends who plan to go to college will not make the same mistake.
Do your research before deciding on a college. This was her dream college but has turned out to be a very BIG disappointment.', 'Just got off the phone with an advisor or financial aid person in charge of the “b”s and she basically told me to look into other institutions that offer “more” even though I said nothing about wanting more just wanted to know tuition prices..when I mentioned I was happy that my FASFA might fully cover costs. She then stated I was wrong and because I’m from Tennessee I don’t know what I’m doing. When mentioned I already have an Associates and I’ve used FASFA before she acted like I had no idea what I was doing cause I should get 14,000 (Thank you for assuming I’m in poverty) and was dumb when she knew absolutely nothing about me from a 10- 15 minute call. On top of talking over me! Do better with students considering your school! Makes me want to look elsewhere.', 'Pretty accessible campus. Stopped by for their surplus sale & it was busy, but very cheap computers, chairs, desks, and other furniture. If going for tech, make sure to bring a charger to test the devices before purchasing!', "Very charming campus, nice size, good quality teaching with good class sizes, great research in marine bio. That said, I can't speak to the undergrad, on-campus student life side. Also, with so many gorgeous beaches around, etc., I don't know how I would have gotten any studying done if I went here as an undergrad!", 'We took the exclusive Nicki and Patrick Angle tour of the campus.  Very knowledgeable and the singing was on point! Would recommend!']

name: Pamlico Community College
reviews: ['Mr. Mcadoo is Amazing! What a great set of fire instructors. The amount of knowledge these men have, can not be found in books!! Thank you Pamlico Community College for having such great instructors!', 'PCA Christmas Program was so good !! I believe everyone enjoyed themselves !! Thank you for allowing them to use your auditorium!', 'It is a nice school and I know lots of kids from rural areas go here and they are all great kids', 'I attended and graduated from Pamlico Community College College back in 1987-1989. name: William Peace University
reviews:
['We could not have asked for a more perfect family brunch at William Peace University the day after our wedding. The campus is stunning, providing a beautiful backdrop for our families to gather. Elsie Hernández was incredibly accommodating, helping us with every detail to make our day special. Our guests were equally impressed by the beauty and seamless organization of the entire event. We highly recommend William Peace University for any special occasion as well as a lovely photography opportunity as we had our engagement photos done her as well. Thank you for making our wedding weekend unforgettable. I highly recommend for anyone to reserve Main Parlor for their special event!

This vendor embraces inclusivity and is welcoming to the LGBTQIA+ community.', 'It has very good gafics were not talking about games really I like it and the kitchen.', "I'm in love with this school. It has provided me the tools for success, and overall has helped my confidence as a leader. The school may be  small, but has activities that are present throughout the week. This could be writing workshops, movie nights, sport games, musicals, dance parties, etc. The resources available on campus are all next to each other, so traveling from place to place is swift. Professors are also really nice, and there for the students. Overall it's been a great experience.", 'This is an amazing university! The faculty and staff do everything in their power to make sure the students are able to grow. Although it is a small university, there are still many events that can help improve your skills academically,  and they have countless events for fun too!', "From A Parent:

They are restricting ON CAMPUS students from parking in certain spots, because the commuters have no where to park. Now the residential students (More than 250 btw) have to somehow all park in less than 200 spots. HOW DOES THAT SOLVE ANYTHING. Its not a residential vs commuter issue, its a lack of general parking for everybody issue. THERE ARE LESS SPOTS THAN THERE ARE STUDENTS IN GENERAL. I can't believe some of the bone headed decisions that get made on this campus. One of many issues."]

name: University of North Carolina at Pembroke
reviews:
["I haven't been here for a sporting event since my son played football here. The athletic complex here is absolutely amazing! The state and school have done an amazing job with the entire campus. A great hidden gem here in North Carolina!", 'My niece goes to school here. She has complained about the roaches in her dorm room repeatedly for month. She came home for the holidays and returned to roaches in her dorm room. Unacceptable, especially for what students and their parents are paying to attend this University.', 'This is absolutely the worst school I have ever been to. Please reconsider before going here. This school is only good for the locals who stay around the school. They have tried to cover up several race wars and school shootings. You are much better off going to Fayetteville state or another school in the area. It’s not worth your college experience by any means. Administration does not care and will find excuses for employees. If you address any concerns then you will become a target. After 4 years I still have trouble getting certain things done because this school rather be petty than to just do their assigned job. I highly do  not recommend especially if you are of African American descent and advise you to reconsider.', 'Great facility and campuses area. I felt safe and streets were very clean everywhere. Excellent job, the town of Pembroke!', 'As an online student, I found the university’s Passport program to be poorly designed and almost entirely disconnected from the reality of remote learners. It seemed built around outdated assumptions about who students are and how they live, with little attention paid to working adults who manage full-time jobs, families, and coursework. Communication was another serious issue — emails very frequently went unanswered, and when I finally reached my assigned advisor, Mr. “Bowling Lane,” he offered no advice or follow-through, even dismissive. The entire system felt one-sided. For a university that promotes accessibility and inclusion, the lack of support and consideration for its online community was both disappointing and revealing.

Calls/Emails sent via remote students are as good as gone...loved a few professors, they make the pain hurt less lol.

Reach out for more info!']

name: Pfeiffer University
reviews: ["Today's visit was my 50th graduation homecoming. The buildings and grounds are extremely well kept and look much newer than their nearly 100 year reality. (Actually looks better than in 1975.) Caring, professional staff and faculty make visiting a joy. Great scholastic and sports reputation. Today's visit brought back a lot of wonderful memories, and helped make a few more.", 'Kind people and a beautiful campus! Wish they could do more online programs or courses over the summer and get over some regular classes and take a few classes on campus that you absolutely need. Most teachers don’t give very well feedback and some of them the way of teaching needs to change most of the students can’t engage in class if it’s the same thing everyday . Come up with new plans get students to interact more . Plan more fun lessons to keep us interested on the subject. Not sit there and watch PowerPoints and listen to the proffers speak and call it a day .', 'Cool small University with lots of satellite locations to serve a broader population. Beautiful historic chapel with amazing pipe organ and nice facilities for athletics and academics. Love how Pfeiffer has always been a part of the Northern Stanly County community.']

name: Piedmont Community College
reviews: ["CPCC needs some help in the IT department. It took me several days to get access to my account and each time had to wait at least several hours. Then today I can't login again. I decided to take classes from another NC community college - much easier process and HALF the cost!", 'Someone hit my vehicle in the parking deck while I was in class. Now there is a big dent in my vehicle and the school is saying they can’t do anything about it even though there are cameras that recorded the incident. Very frustrating.', 'Amazing school! Completing classes was easy, and I was very impressed with the modern campus and friendly instructors. As an adult student, working while completing the online programs was manageable. I recommend attending here before pursuing a four-year degree! This school helped me get my foot in the door with local companies looking to hire and made the transfer to UNCC very smooth.\n\nHowever, my academic advisor was nonexistent, and my financial aid advisor was rude and unhelpful. Also, some professors are better than others, but you can get all As in every class if you try.', 'Cpcc does not care about its students at all. After being here for almost two months I have run into so many issues already. I was trying to transfer schools and they were extremely unhelpful and had me pay for several documents that were of no use for my applications. I also have learning disabilities, and haven’t been able to get my needed accommodations even after two months of waiting, due to many careless issues with the cpcc system and disability team. Their help system here is a complete joke. I personally wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone especially if you plan on transferring from here or getting accommodations.', 'Need better student drop off and pick up, my mom picked me up from campus at the Elizabeth campus and some crazy lady tried to cuss me and my mother out just bc she had to wait a second for me to get in the car, where is campus police for these situations? I went through this twice and absolutely no consequences for others who chose to cuss and get angry at students while trying to safety get home not to mention cars will drive around cars waiting for pickup and I seen a car almost directly hit a student and had to slam on the breaks.']

name: Pitt Community College
reviews: ["Absoluetly WORST college! My daughter enrolled in classes through a scholarship,after she enrolled we realized the scholarship didn't cover her books. I'm a disabled  single mom. I didn't have the money for them and her FASFA didn't go through, so she withdrew. I've attended several colleges and have multiple degrees. Not one of those colleges didn't have a grace period to withdraw from classes without a penalty. Pitt however hits you with FEES if you don't withdraw from classes BEFORE they start. Nobody knows if every class will work out before it starts. This school is a MONEY GRABBER SO BEWARE!! They care nothing about the students and everything about making money.", 'I have attended multiple colleges over the years of different levels.  PITT is very impressive.  The campus is beautiful as well as laid out easier than others. The staff I have encountered has been amazing and extremely helpful. THEY ALSO HAVE A GREAT REPUTATION in the healthcare industry.  I drive 1.5hrs and pass 2 other colleges to attend PITT due to their amazing reputation and program outcomes in healthcare.  DEFINITELY look into PITT if your looking do do great things in your future and career.', 'I first went to PCC as a high school student back in 2023 and am now on the verge of graduating. I have absolutely loved my time here. The instructors are wonderful people, especially those in the math department. I didn’t think I was particularly interested in math before I started, but I was quickly inspired to pursue it further, and it has now become one of my favorite subjects and shaped my path in life. It has a beautiful campus too, with plenty of buildings containing comfortable study spaces. I’ll certainly miss this school when I transfer. I would definitely recommend this school to anyone who’s nervous about starting college, the people here are so kind and easy to work with!', "My son has been going for a few months, started during the summer & had no contacts for any support. Well all of that changed after the open house yesterday!! I've never seen my son so excited about the school! Heck we all had a great time learning about the different departments and meeting the amazing folks who make up the PCC community! Please make sure your freshman go to an open house!!", 'Can i please get a call back  i didn’t meet the deadline for last semester and i feel like i wont meet this one i called multiple time get transferred to voicemail leave name and number and details message but never get a call back my name is Roger Byrum']

name: Queens University of Charlotte
reviews: ["WARNING FOR SUMMER INTERNS THINKING ABOUT STAYING HERE:\n\nQueens will NOT refund your security deposit, and tries to stall out the dispute period of your credit card. The air conditioning broke for 3 days and the power went out, and we were not refunded despite this violating the amenities list they were contractually obligated to provide. I had to throw away $220 of groceries, and they did nothing about it. The kitchens are filthy and many of the appliances are not properly maintained, consistently broken sinks and faulty induction burners. The fridge on my floor had a toilet plunger inside, and was basically unusable due to the smell. Staying here is like paying for what you think is a regular hotel room, except when you get there you realize there isn't a bed and you need to sleep on a dirty floor. The two good things I have to say about this place is it is in a nice neighborhood and the gym is well maintained. Other than that, this place was horrible.", "It was amazing experience being able to drop off my god daughter and see how she's continued to blossom at this Queen's University in Charlotte. The campus looks amazing as well as the people were quite friendly and it's in a very amazing neighborhood. It is extremely safe area and I would definitely recommend to any college seeking student", 'Small classes, leadership opportunities and strong faculty - all wrapped up in a booming city!! Highly recommended!', 'I recently visited Queens University of Charlotte as a prospective student, and my experience was disappointing. Rather than focusing on academics, student experience, or campus life, the conversation felt entirely centered on finances. It became clear that the university prioritizes donations over genuinely supporting its students. I got the strong impression that their main interest in me was tied to what my family could contribute to their athletic program, rather than my potential as a student or athlete. A school should be built on education, opportunities, and community—not just financial contributions. This visit left me questioning the university’s true priorities.', 'Highly recommend for university/college experience. Classes are the right size, and the professors are extremely knowledgeable and helpful. Also, it is a beautiful campus only a few miles from uptown.']

name: Randolph Community College
reviews:
["Very awesome college to meet your educational goals! Excellent staff members who genuinely care about you and your education. RCC is a place that you will be guaranteed success in your chosen career. I graduate this May 8,2024 However, I'm staying for more majors. Plus being a part of the Student Government Association is totally fun and awesome! Never a dull moment at RCC.", 'The school is conveniently located right off the highway. Most of the teachers are great and will work with students to make sure they succeeded. One of the biggest issues I have with the school is the slow wifi. It can make getting homework done at school a slow process. Overall I enjoyed the school and believe it prepared me well for a University.', 'Great community college. Very nice staff', "I appreciate your timely response. This is a Cosmotology Junior College training our youth to access business skills. Which include managmenting an offie. These students need to learn telephone sills, answering/appointments/times, days, and dates of potential closings. The students need to learn to set up the voice mail with closure notices/dates and times. Opening and closind dates I was there early on the 18 th and you were closed. No sigh on when you would be reopened. The note on the window was a tad deceiving (closed Oct.25th). Did that mean you were closed from the 18-25? .or just closed Oct 25th.
I would post a photo but it won't let me.", 'The school facilities are clean. Rated individually, the staff in the welcome center were mostly friendly- but not very helpful. Collectively, the entire registration process was very confusing.
We we're sent to a room to set up our own payment plan on a computer- which was simple. What I wasn't told (or asked) is that the payment plan was not including her books. All  I was given was a paper with a circled number for the cost of the semester and that's what I entered into the computer. There was not a print out or a list of procedures given to us after the payment plan was initiated. We had to piece every part of the registration process together. I want to really stress the fact that there was not any guidance by staff or faculty.
After setting up the payment plan I went back to the welcome desk and confirmed that we set up the payment plan and she acted like we were done...She didn't even ask if we needed additional help or assistance. It felt like I had to plead for guidance from the young ladies at the front desk. What about books? We were sent to the bookstore- but there's not even directional signs telling you where the bookstore is. When we get to the bookstore we find out my daughter's books were NOT included in the payment plan (which was relatively easy to fix and was done so by phone by one of the staff). While standing in line, waiting for the payment plan to be revised we overheard another mother say to her daughter(that she had overheard someone else say) to go to the library to get a student ID. There were no signs, maps or directions given from staff on how to find the library. So, once again, we were back to the welcome desk to find out if my daughter needs a student ID?  Where is the library? Does the ID cost anything additional?
The librarian was the most friendly and helpful ( although she didn't have a campus map nor a list of any details to offer) she did direct us back to the welcome center - AGAIN- for the parking sticker. Prior to the librarian,  no one ever mentioned or indicate anything about a parking pass. The parking passes are given out at the Welcome Center (front desk) which is frustrating knowing that we had already been there at least three previous times for directions and information.
My daughter is registered and beginning the Fall Semester at RCC.
My biggest suggestion to the Faculty and Staff is to have a Welcome Packet with step by step instructions, maps and suggestions for programs.  It was by sheer chance we learned that there's an orientation happening over the weekend. It was also by chance that we found out about some of the extra-curricular activities and clubs that my daughter has an interest in.  Why aren't these simple directives and insight given to new students in a packet?  I know a lot of people who have graduated or enrolled their children at RCC- and they all have very positive stories and testaments regarding their experiences...and I'm sure we will too- but right out of the chute was a very frustrating experience. I suggest a more seasoned customer service/faculty member being at the front desk to steer the young ladies towards embracing their role as "Welcome Center" and "Information Desk" in a more pro-active, hands-on manner.']

name: Robeson Community College
reviews:
["A Wide variety of Skilled Labor Courses.  Exactly what we need now. If our youth are smart, they'll go blue collar Now. The industry is sucking right now. Much opportunity Now.", 'Today I visited the college to see the singing military personnel. Not exactly what I wanted to see as far as protecting the country and all but at least they can sing', 'An excellent place to continue your education or increase your employability. There are even classes to help you improve your basic skills or find a new hobby.', 'Found the me I did not know existed.
Love this college.', "As a normal student coming from high school, this school is probably not too bad but, as a veteran, I have not had a good experience and only three weeks into the semester.
They know I'm a veteran but they don't have me in their system as a veteran so I've been dropped from my classes twice while waiting on my GI Bill to kick in. They are suppose to wait and eventually they'll get their money from the VA. I was kicked out of my classes 5 days before the semester started. They didn't call or email me about it. I received a letter in the mail the day before school started and I had to call them to get them to fix it. Lucky, I got back in all of my original classes. Then, about four days into the semester, it happened again. This stopped me from being able to do any online work for the whole weekend. They had forgotten to put me in the system as veteran again.
And if that wasn't bad enough, they charged the VA for instate tuition but they charged me out-of-state tuition. That's a difference of about $2,000 that I'll have to pay if this doesn't get fixed. I'm in the process of getting that fixed mid-semester when I should be studying.
I feel a lot of this is due to a lack of communication between offices at the school. They fail to communicate with me and with each other. But as I said earlier, as a normal person, you probably wouldn't have so many problems but vets, I'd recommend going somewhere else."]

name: Rockingham Community College
reviews:
["I attended Rockingham Community College from Fall of '21 to Spring of '23 for my Associate in Science degree, and I can safely say that I had a fantastic experience at this college. Relatively small even for a community college, RCC has classes that rarely extend beyond 20 students. As a result, you have a lot of opportunities to interact with your professors during class. The professors themselves are friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable on their subjects, and they have a genuine desire to help you learn and succeed in the classroom. They'll make you work for your grade (this is college, after all) but they are there for you if you get lost or need help. And if for whatever reason you can't get access to a teacher during office hours, there's a tutoring center (called the ARC) in the Science building that can help you out as well (this place is especially helpful when writing those challenging essays). In addition, RCC's campus is very pretty, and almost has a private college look and feel. There are also some hiking trails that I highly recommend spending a lunch break on from time to time, as it's a very relaxing experience for anybody who loves being in nature, or just enjoys some peace and quiet. The main drawback I have is that I found the student life here to be somewhat lacking; I felt that most students just didn't want to get involved in extracurriculars. Overall, RCC is a phenomenal choice if you're looking to get your first 2 years of a bachelor's degree knocked out without getting swamped in student loan debt. I'm proud to call myself an Eagle and I highly recommend anyone in the area to trust the reviews here, give this college a visit, and consider attending!", "Rockingham Community College: Your Smart Start to Success.

If you're looking for a college experience that truly puts students first, look no further than Rockingham Community College in Wentworth, NC. My time at RCC has been nothing short of fantastic, proving that high-quality education doesn't have to break the bank or feel like a faceless institution.
What truly sets RCC apart is its incredible instructors. They're not just experts in their fields; they genuinely care about your success. I've been consistently impressed by their willingness to go the extra mile, whether it's staying after class to answer questions, offering detailed feedback, or simply creating a supportive and engaging learning environment. The small class sizes are a huge advantage here, allowing for personalized attention and a strong connection with both professors and peers – something you often miss at larger universities.

Beyond the classroom, RCC offers a surprisingly vibrant and welcoming campus atmosphere. From the moment you step foot on campus, you feel like part of a community. There's a real sense of camaraderie among students, and the staff are always friendly and happy to help navigate anything from financial aid to career planning. Plus, with a beautiful campus that includes walking trails and great facilities, it's a pleasant place to be.

Whether you're aiming to transfer to a four-year university, jump directly into a new career, or simply gain valuable skills, RCC has a program for you. Their diverse offerings, from nursing and welding to liberal arts and specialized programs like Brewing, Distillation, and Fermentation, mean there's a path for everyone. And let's be honest, the affordability makes it an unbeatable value, especially with scholarship opportunities like the Next NC Scholarship for eligible residents.

Rockingham Community College isn't just a stepping stone; it's a solid foundation. It's a place where you can learn, grow, and truly thrive, all while feeling incredibly supported. If you're in the Rockingham County area and considering your educational options, do yourself a favor and check out RCC. You'll be glad you did!", 'Great campus! Gives you a good country feeling coming to the school. Everyone wants to help you here which makes for great experience!', 'Fantastic college that provides good education in an incredible number of programs! Register today to ignite your successful future.', "If you need to change careers or are looking to find a place to start your education, do not pass up RCC. This is an excellent community college that cares about the students and wants them to succeed. From the business office to the classroom. Educators are devoted to their students. You'll leave feeling prepared for the future ahead."]

name: Salem College
reviews:
['I attended my freshman year here in 2002–2003, and it was one of the worst experiences of my life. I sincerely hope the school has changed since then, because what I lived through was toxic and traumatic. The student culture was viciously cliquish—steeped in classism, cattiness, and exclusion. Professors often carried themselves with arrogance and disdain. And my roommate? Diabolical. It was my first taste of what it means to live with someone who can twist reality, make you look unstable in front of others, and leave you questioning your own sanity. My first gaslighting. I still don’t know how I survived it and it has impacted my ability to trust others to this day.

The larger campus environment wasn’t much better. In the Rat, most if not all, member of the wait staff was African American, serving an overwhelmingly affluent, white student body. That imbalance was impossible to ignore, and it left an impression that something was deeply off. Hazing was another nightmare. I can still see myself hiding under my bed in the dark, shaking and sobbing, as students beat on the door so violently that light flashed through the cracks with each blow. I thought the door would splinter and collapse. That night is seared into my memory as pure fear.

I eventually escaped and transferred to the Florida university system, which felt like coming up for air after drowning. But even in that dark, suffocating year, there was one light: my English professor, Dr. Rose A. Sackeyfio. She was brilliant, compassionate, and unforgettable. Her teaching gave me the foundation to write countless A+ papers and, later, a graduate thesis that was returned with the rare note that it “need not be defended.” That kind of influence changes you forever. Anyone who has the privilege of experiencing her teaching is truly blessed. She was the single bright spot in an otherwise devastating chapter of my life.', 'I graduated from Salem in 2009. The campus is gorgeous and the student-teacher ratio is awesome. I did have my own personal challenges while I was there, but ultimately Salem gave me all the tools and resources I needed to continue on with a successful career. Salem’s goal of building strong women, though seen as a positive to those of us in the “adulting” world, has had its challenges within the institution. Being a small school, a small voice within the student body can gather traction quickly. Some issues from the past year (2017/2018) I would agree with, others I would not. Please do your research and remember that the loudest reviews are going to be the most negative. I’m looking forward to seeing how Salem evolves in the next 10 years. Proud alum here. 😊

Edited to add: the review about the “hazing” is dedicated to one night of the entire year, the same night, every year. It is a “senior wakeup call”. There is plenty of notice given to the student body and students may plan to leave the campus during this time (classes are canceled the entire next day for the greatest event of the year, Fall Fest!).', "This school has sucked the life out of me. This school has left me feeling sick and tired (quite literally, as they didn't fix the mold and water damage above my bed for months). I completely regret my decision to attend this institution. I do not believe that Salem College has the student's best interests in mind. I have seen this institution show more care for it's white alumna from 1967 than the current students. The facilities are falling apart, the hot water is sporadic at best, the only available food causes sickness, racist action on campus (from students and faculty alike) is swept under the rug, administration has not created a trans policy, claiming that policies 'take time', yet they were able to complete an extremely limiting protest policy after a week of demonstrations. My choice to attend Salem College was the biggest mistake I made in high school.", "This was one of the worst years of my life. They have a tradition that allows hazing of the underclass, in the middle of the night around 3-4 in the morning all the seniors run through the hallways pounding on the underclassmen’s doors with hammer, bats and other assorted items. It is has been a long standing tradition that is allowed by the school. With such a high rate of women be survivors of assault and other violent acts it is hard to comprehend why a school would allow just behavior. To wake up in the middle of the night and having 100 + people running, screaming and pounding on doors with large items is not an environment I would ever want to be a part of. They enforce strict rules about guests and micro manage the dorms yet they allow and support hazing on campus.  I was bullied by security on campus, they would come in and search my room, flipping things over and leaving things a mess. They never found any alcohol but still searched my room several times in a disrespectful manor. There was a major divide between legacy students and non-legacy students. Girls bullied each other on campus and staff would feed into it. Staff and campus leaders (president, student services) are MIA. I never knew anyone who ran campus, heard from the president, any department heads or other helpful staff. I was lost on campus and felt like there was no one to reach out to. There was no strong bond with the departments until JR or SR years. If you are looking for a women's college go to Stephens College. I ended up transferring and was so glad I did! Amazing community of female leaders and an environment that fosters innovation!", 'Salem is the first women’s college in this country, and it continues to provide innovative and exceptional education to this day. It is a small college, but that is it’s strength — small classes, leadership opportunities, and a unique community you won’t find anywhere else.']

name: Shaw University
reviews:
['I wish I could leave no stars. I strongly encourage anyone considering this university to do thorough research before enrolling. My experience has been extremely disappointing due to the school’s ongoing lack of organization, professionalism, and basic communication.
During freezing temperatures and severe storms, students were left without hot water or heat. This alone was concerning, but the school’s response made the situation far worse. Students were informed early one morning that they needed to move out of their dorms and return home because classes would be held virtually. Just a few hours later, that decision was reversed, and students were told they could return to campus—only to be placed in hotel rooms instead.
When students arrived back on campus, no hotel reservations had actually been made. As a result, students were left sitting on campus for hours with no updates, no clear instructions, and no communication from the administration. The lack of planning and accountability was alarming, especially during a situation that directly impacted students’ safety and well-being.
Overall, this university has shown a pattern of poor leadership and disregard for students. It feels as though the institution is more focused on collecting tuition than ensuring a safe, stable, and supportive environment for its students. This experience has been disheartening, and I would not recommend this school to anyone who values clear communication, organization, and student care.', 'My nephew returned to school the second week of January and has been living in a building without heat or running hot water. Shaw has not provided any formal notices or emails informing families of these conditions. As a result of students using space heaters to stay warm, a fire broke out in the building. Firefighters had to force entry into all of the room doors. Additionally, not all of the fire sprinklers were functioning in every room. Many of my nephew’s belongings were stolen because the RAs failed to properly secure the doors once they were opened.The university has only offered a small credit to our account, which we do not feel is fair given the circumstances. Students were instructed to vacate their rooms and remove all belongings within 48 hours of the fire.

As of today (02/16), we were told to report to campus between 10:00am - 4:00pm to be assigned a hotel room. We arrived at 11:00am, and it is now 4:10pm, and we still have not been assigned a room.

THIS IS RIDICULOUS!!!', 'Great HBCU school in the middle of Downtown Raleigh. Absolutely loved attending Shaw University. The people are amazing. One of my best experiences. The staff, the coaches, and the instructors care about the students. If I had to choose again, I would come back again.', 'Tour guide was nice and knew her information, really enjoyed my visit.', 'The mother of all HBCUs! Great university']

name: St. Andrews University
reviews:
['Our son, Kiro, studied Philosophy at the University of St Andrews, and as parents, we feel it is only right to share something of our experience. This is not a review of teaching methods or academic structures; we cannot speak for those, but rather a personal reflection on life as the parent of a student, and the joy we felt in discovering this remarkable place alongside him.

St Andrews itself is unlike anywhere else. Nestled on the coast, it feels both remote and timeless, with an atmosphere so enchanting that it seems almost unreal at times. Coming from London, each visit felt like stepping into another world, peaceful, picturesque, and steeped in history. The journey may not be the easiest by public transport, but perhaps that very distance is what has allowed the town to preserve its beauty and authenticity!

We visited Kiro often, and every time we were struck by how safe and welcoming St Andrews felt. We never encountered difficulties, and the town always gave us a sense of reassurance, a gift for any parent sending their child away to study. Walking its cobbled streets, exploring the coastline, and sharing moments of everyday life with our son there gave us memories we will always treasure.

We are deeply grateful that our son had the opportunity to study at such a distinguished university, in such an extraordinary setting. As parents, we too feel enriched by the experience of St Andrews, its charm, its history, and its warmth. It has been a privilege to know it and experience its magic.', 'Come and learn here.
St andrews is a historical place with lot of attractions.
Nice golf field, good hotels, many students and clean city. A nice beach is right there.', 'No golfer can resist a trip to Saint Andrews. But if you only go to the old course, you’re missing out on one of the loveliest towns there is and did the heart of it is the University of St. Andrews. The ancient university sometimes better known as the place where the Prince and Princess of Wales attended, but I prefer to think of it and remember it as a world class institution that just happens to be next-door to a bunch of world class golf courses. It was not term time when I visited, but the few people I saw deleted with the school were friendly. And the campus buildings and grounds itself, dispersed among the town, were impeccable. I’d be happy to see members of my family attend, this venerable institution.', 'We were visiting St Andrews for a day trip from Stirling and walked around town.   It was founded in 1413 (the oldest university in Scotland and 3rd oldest in the English-speaking world).  Prince William and Kate Middleton met here.  The architecture of the buildings were beautiful.', 'The university of St Andrews is a lovely, old, historic institution set on the seaside city of quaint St Andrews, Fife, Scotland. My wife and I strolled around it, during our free time on our bus tour of Scotland after exploring the oldest golf course in the world, ‘The Old Course,’ the ruins of the tragic St Andrews cathedral and the famous nearby beach, the Saint Andrews West Sands, from the movie ‘Chariots of Fire.’

What a unique and wonderful university to be able to attend! Founded in 1413, it is Scotlands oldest and most prestigious university. It is the third oldest English speaking school in the world.  It was founded by Catholic priest who were forced out of Paris, Oxford and Cambridge by politics. In 1876 they were one of the first universities to open to woman, but only by correspondence at first.

The university has had its struggles over its long life and at one time only had 100 students. Now around 12,000 students attend this prestigious university. There is also a statue of Prince William where he met Kate, while they were students here.']

name: Stanly Community College
reviews:
['I paid $2000 to take the nail technician program. We have to take state board examinations and one of the test requirements is a sealed product. The test itself is $80. We are given what the school supplies us with that comes in the kit we pay for. I get to the test site and they tell me what I have is not acceptable and another classmate had the same issue. The school is going to replace that item but will not repay for my test that I just lost out on $80 and a day at work. Ultimately it’s the schools fault that the items were not checked. We as students take what was given to us and it should have been checked by the teacher or whoever. We pack our state board box and don’t touch it until the day of the test.

Now on to the rules. We had a girl in our class who would clock in and leave. Which is a huge no no. The teacher brought it to administrators and they knew of her behavior and did nothing. She got the cops called on her one night for leaving her child in a running car parked in the handicap spot while she was in class with her man doing manicures. She didn’t show up for the mandatory final exam. What’s the point of having rules if you’re not going to enforce them? It was so bad our teacher quit.', 'worst staff to help you with anything, my girlfriend was applying and she said they made filling out her fafsa almost impossible and they kept on giving her looks as if she was dumb. stay AWAY from this school the curriculums arent even that varied and they send your balance to collects  A MONTH after completing a class which is absolutely incredible.', 'Avoid this school at all costs.

I was in a terrible car accident, had multiple surgeries, and was in and out of the hospital. I physically and mentally couldn’t keep up with my classes, and because of that, I failed. The school knew what I was going through but still forced me to pay back my financial aid—something they never made explicitly clear upfront. Like, who in their right mind is thinking about financial aid policies while dealing with hospitalizations, infections, and surgeries?

The teachers were useless. One of them (ACA 111) straight up told me, “You’re an adult, be responsible for your decisions,” as if I wasn’t recovering from major medical issues. The advisors? A joke. My assigned advisor, Garrett Allen, never reached out, and I had zero support navigating any of this.

And let’s talk about how outdated the curriculum is. They’re still teaching CompTIA Network+ N10-007, which was retired in 2021. A+ and CCNA courses are just as old. Why am I paying for courses that won’t even help me pass the current certifications?

The worst part? If you owe them money, they come after you fast. 15 days after the first notice, they start sending threats, and 30 days later, they send you to collections. What kind of school operates like that?

This place is a scam. They don’t care about students—just money. If you’re thinking about coming here, don’t. Find a school that actually supports its students and keeps its courses up to date.', "I was actually a student who who wore many hat's! I am a full time employee, proud mother of two, and successfully completed my Associate degree program online with Stanly. My professors and advisor were both attentive and understanding with any concerns I had. Furthermore, I was very well taken care of at this college. It was truly a wonderful experience and if they had a bachelor's program I would still be there now!", 'I would recommend Stanley Community College to anyone looking to further their education. I obtained my Associate’s Degree in 2015, and I couldn’t be happier with my experience. The staff was more than helpful and accommodating, and the instructors were knowledgeable and genuinely cared about the students in their classes.']

name: Wake Technical Community College
reviews:
['In my opinion, this school engages in highly fraudulent and deceptive business practices. Be extremely cautious if you are considering enrolling. Their program appears intentionally misleading, with a pass rate of only about 20% — nearly twice as bad as the North Carolina average. The exams contain subjective and grammatically incorrect questions, and they refuse to disclose which answers were marked wrong.

I am reporting these deceptive practices to the North Carolina Consumer Consumer Protection Agency & North Carolina Real Estate Commission, as it appears their intent is to induce students in with low prices, only to fail them so they are enougraged to pay again to retake the course. I have never encountered an educational institution so uninterested in helping students succeed or even explaining their mistakes such as what was incorrect on the test. This conduct strongly suggests fraud and deliberate deception. In my first class, I was informed that literally everyone failed the final exam — clearly indicating either inadequate instruction or intentionally deceptive testing designed to promote failure without accountability.

When I questioned one of the administrators about why they do not share which answers were incorrect, I was told to “go to the NC Commission.” One of the exam questions was literally missing numbers, and another shifted pronouns mid-sentence from “he” to “her.” The fact that a final exam contains such blatant errors and inconsistencies is deeply concerning and points to a much larger problem. I would not be surprised if a class action lawsuit is eventually filed against this institution.', 'Staff is very rude. All of a sudden my financial aid was taken from me without proper notice and a reason as to why when I have not had any lifestyle changes what so ever. name: Western Piedmont Community College
reviews:
['WPCC twice entered a grade of "F" by mistake.   I am stuck with one of them because I got the grade from the professor, didn't think I needed to check behind them, and years passed before I discovered it.  My daughter went two years to community college before going on to a 4-year and I would not allow her to step foot on WPCC's campus.  I will never give another dime to a school that would do that to a student.', 'I went to WPCC 11 years ago, I came as a solid C student. They truly do meet you where you are, to help you be where you want to be. The instructors and staff were invested, and I quickly became an A student. By the time I graduated I had a choices of universities and scholarship opportunities, all because of my time at WPCC. I truly believe community college is the way to start your post-secondary journey, and our hometown college is pretty special.', 'Great community College! The pond has some good fishing as well.', "What a beautiful campus. It's a real pleasure to come here and speak.", "We are opening a third Video Production office in Lenoir, and while we're waiting for the land to be cleared, we thought it'd be fun to take Terry Adams Excavator's class. Not only would it be a good skill to have for new land owners, but a good experience.

Coming from Charlotte, NC and previously attending classes at CPCC, I was skeptical of the facilities here. Not only was I wrong; I was extremely wrong.

First, let's start with the Instructors. Terry Adams is one of the best instructors that I've ever had the privilege of being in their classroom. Having never knew anything about heavy equipment, after the class, I now have the confidence of hopping on a excavator and moving some dirt.

The classrooms were well-equipped and easily accessible for students. I had contact with our Instructor during the entire time of the course. The technology in our class was impressive, in fact, some of the technology I didn't even know existed.

Finally, not trying to be cliché, I would be remiss if I didn't speak to the support staff here. Friendly doesn't even begin to describe them all. Any issue that you may have, the staff is happy to help you find a solution.

I would encourage any student looking to further their knowledge to attend WPCC. When people care...truly care, it shows. It's evident here. Education from a caring Institution, that's WPCC."]

name: Wingate University
reviews:
['This college has a sweet amiable feel to it.  I did not attend but I know someone whose daughter attended.  She felt like giving up a few times but stayed the course and graduated today. (5.12.19)  I am not sure if the school partners with other entities to offer summer internships but I wish she had that opportunity to do so.  Beautiful campus.', 'Great little school, mostly walkable. The students and faculty are friendly and accessable. And it has the largest Starbucks in NC!', "Wingate has a very personable and helpful staff many of whom have been there a long time it seems . Admissions staff was first rate. But once your student is enrolled, as a parent, you will need to be persistent to stay informed so you can help your student succeed.

Wingate's technology is antiquated. Difficult to do any business online as a parent. The school is paper intensive and sometimes the paper seems to fall through cracks. Wingate only recently came up with a way for tuition to be paid online. There is no parent portal yet that allows you to stay up to date with what is due when. Bills are mailed and the expectation is you mail checks or pay on site. If they have a payment plan, they do not advertise it. Most pertinent information goes through the student portal that the parent has no access to. This creates opportunities for miscommunication and missed deadlines.

The school is under-staffed. If you have to phone someone to ask for help or clarification, expect to get voicemail that states you will hear back in a couple of days at least. Email is a better option but don't expect a same-day reply.

Communication is not a strength here. During this last and very widespread flu season, the campus had a very big outbreak but no classes were cancelled and parents never received any communication regarding making certain your student had a flu shot.

Overall, I would say the school has its heart in the right place and most professors are engaged and want to see the students succeed. Still, the school has a ways to go in developing the kind of infrastructure that justifies its tuition costs.

Wingate rightly has a reputation as a collegiate Sparta, roughly one in every four students is some sort of athlete. Not necessarily a bad thing but if your student is not going to be playing a sport or chooses to leave a sport once there, be aware of what other options they have on campus to stay engaged. The student transfer rate accelerates at year two.

If campus surroundings are a consideration, know that Wingate is an exceedingly small town so that the campus is basically all there is. The neighboring town of Monroe is slightly bigger with more ammenities: small mall, Walmart and fast food options. Charlotte is a short drive beyond that. Uber is not allowed on campus, we were told. So your student needs a car or friends with wheels if he or she is going to leave campus or fly out of Douglas International.

Overall, Wingate has been a good experience for our student despite a bit of heavy lifting for the parents. Having proper expectations is important when choosing a college. Before you go, we wanted you to know what our experience has been.", 'This campus is so nice. I took my oldest daughter her for a college tour. The staff was amazing and the guide that we had was really nice and helpful. She was very knowledgeable and for the things she didn’t know she was able to get the answers to. Thank y’all for a wonderful experience.', 'This is a great university.  You can tell that the staff here for the most part cares and does all that they can to offer an affordable education in a field that will get people jobs and prosperity.  The actual campus is absolutely wonderful.  It is very scenic and laid out nice.  There area also some very quaint older buildings.']

name: North Dakota State College of Science
reviews:
['Unfortunately, my experience with NDSCS has been consistently frustrating. The bookstore routinely does not have required textbooks in stock at the start of the semester, leaving students scrambling or falling behind through no fault of their own.

Several instructors appear disorganized and assignments are misdated, course materials are copied and pasted from previous semesters without being updated, and there is little clarity after the second and third weeks of class. This creates unnecessary stress and confusion for students who are trying to stay on track.

On top of this, most interactions with staff, especially in the bookstore, have been unpleasant. Many employees come across as dismissive or rude when students ask for help. I can count only a couple of staff members who have been genuinely kind and helpful, and they were online instructors.

Students deserve better organization, clearer communication, and basic respect. At this time, I cannot recommend this college based on my experience.', 'BE CAREFUL WHAT YOU SIGN UP FOR!
They’re misleading to fill their classes, and get your money, but then don’t disclose that there will be 200+ miles of driving for “state mandated labs.” When signing up for this CNA class, they advertised a local Jamestown class with labs provided in Jamestown, with absolutely ZERO mention that there’s a chance a weekly commute to FARGO would be necessary. 200 miles a week, a full tank of gas in our car, for 5 weeks, and we were NEVER ONCE warned that this was a possibility. DECEIVING and unempathetic to students, their families, and their lives. I would HIGHLY recommend looking into doing your post secondary schooling or classing at any other school but here. This was on top of being bounced via email and phone for 3+ weeks. Absolutely ridiculous and after 3 weeks of reaching out to people, they still offered 0 help.', "It's not a good College to go to for electrical studies. Your much better off going to a trade school than going here for your journeymen's license or just thinking about doing electrical work. Some of the teachers either speak to silently or, get completely nervous or speak WAY to fast when trying to teach. 2/10 do not recommend for electrical studies.", "I'd recommend any and all who love to travel, but the winter's/fall out there is extremely Brrrrrr!!!!! So please be highly aware and prepare for the zero below, plus the ice and snow. Most important you'll need a block heater for your oil pan to stay warm while your vehicle is parked, with the zero plus below weather, your vehicle will not start if the oil freezes.", "I went here for a semester my freshman year and I wouldn't recommend it. Since it is a small school your opportunities are extremely limited. There are very few clubs with most not being  operational because not there isn't enough students. I would try to join clubs but would get turned down because no one was in them. I also felt like there was little support for any incoming freshman. Starting college away from family and being cut of from them due to bad winter conditions was stressful and adjusting and integrating was difficult when you don't know anyone. Also because this is 2-year, half of the student body will be gone when your done by spring. The options you have for making friends are very limited and the time you spend with them is extremely short. This put lots of pressure on me to try to make friends immediately, but the stress was to much and I ended up being alone in the end, which made the other problems of that come with college life worse. There is a therapist and she's great but it unfortunately wasn't enough. The four-ish months I spent here nothing but a cold, stressful, lonely, miserable experience. Overall I give this college a 2-star. Not everything was negative which is why this isn't a one star review, but so much could have been better. Hopefully they can make changes later on, but I don't know what those would look like."]

name: Williston State College
reviews:
['I did not go to school there but I had to rent from them and the foundation is not friendly and constantly harassed the tenants in the building. The building was very nice though. All though I was on the 4th floor the building did shake as it was built on a wetland.', 'Retrieving transcripts is extremely difficult, and the website is inaccessible for those who have not graduated. Additionally, professors at the University are unwilling to make accommodations for disabilities.', 'I absolutely loved my experience of attending my first two years of college here . All of the professors I had genuinely cared about the students . It is a community driven and influenced community college . Because of the small size , you are able to get the one on one help you might need . There are many opportunities for students who apply themselves and want to further educate themselves . Could not recommend more if you are considering going for a trade , continuing your education, or just trying to figure out a life and career path .', "Professer quality varies wildly- some do definately care and are fantastic at teaching, others are horrible and will blantently tell you to your face that they don't care if you pass or not. Others simply refuse to help you at all and insist you teach yourself ALL of the material.
The cafeteria is really hit and miss but I'm told it's been better recently. Sometimes the meal is downright fantastic and other times they serve you moldy food (yes, really. It depends on who is cooking that day.)
Their basketball team harasses people constantly and makes a lot of women uncomfortable, including myself.
I don't regret getting a degree here but I wouldn't recommend it if you have literally any other option.", "Williston State College is a place where students get individual attention in each of their classes, a stark contrast to the four-year schools on the eastern side of North Dakota. Every professor made it a point to know every student's name, which was incredible for me. I never went to class and felt unwanted, or as though I was a burden to my professors' research time. The college offers several interesting courses each semester, and, from my own experiences, the variety in the classes offers students a well-rounded two-year education for a very manageable price."]

name: Trinity Bible College and Graduate School
reviews: ['Trinity Bible College and Graduate School offers a vibrant and welcoming atmosphere that fosters both academic and spiritual growth. The picturesque campus provides a peaceful setting for students to engage in their studies, participate in community events, and form lifelong friendships. With dedicated faculty who are passionate about mentorship and student success, learners are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed for their future ministries. Overall, Trinity is a wonderful place to study, where faith and education come together harmoniously.', "I went to college there in 1987/88. Long time ago. I loved going to school there. people were so nice and considerate. You could feel God's love there. I miss it there. And I think about and pray for you all everyday. Thank you for giving me a great, and memorable experience.", "Sent my son for a year to Trinity. He had a decent experience, but housing was really bad and he hated hated the food.\n\nBiggest issue: they say they are accredited, but they did not explain that their credits don't transfer to a lot of secular colleges. After my son switched majors his first semester, his advisor assured him he should continue to attend and have credits transfer. We found out that was not true. Wasted a whole year and tuition.", "Spent 5 years at TBC.  Not a whole lot taught about real life.  Got a very rude awakening after I graduated and real life started. reviews: ['I am currently enrolled in the RN program, and as someone with zero background to college, and only a GED, ETI has really been a great experience so far. name: University of Akron Main Campus
reviews: ['Trash! The campus is trash! Everything is so overpriced! Please don’t fall for their we are so affordable now BS ads! The professors are so old they can’t even teach their subjects right, the learning atmosphere is so dry and dead, the food’s nasty and over priced, their staff workers and administrators are so incompetent and unsupportive, the academic advisors don’t even know how to advise you, the learning standards have completely fallen down to community college standards, it’s not even university standard anymore, the teachers curve grades a lot, students can hardly read or write, everyone is stupidly getting into student loan debt, and there are so much more! Please go somewhere else! This school is not worth your time and money.', 'Most of the buildings are old and run down. A lot of the classes are much larger than they need to be. I had several with 150-200 students and it is very hard to communicate with the professors in that situation. It’s often hard to find parking. The campus has a lot of non students walking around the outskirts asking students for money. There is often violent situations that I am alerted about from their text system. Aside from that the education is decent and the price is higher than I’d like but cheaper than some alternatives, but not all of them.', 'Although I absolutely loved the counseling services offered here, my professors at Wayne campus were awesome, the gym on main campus is awesome, although the housing is horrible. I lived on campus in Buglar here the heat and hot water is often out for DAYSSSS, 5 consecutive days during January winter all while I’m in out of state student with no support here, so I had no choice but to be in bed with 5 layers on. No one ever knows anything. I had to CC and forward emails from department to department, before getting clear answers. My biggest problem here is from department to department there are students responding to emails and answering phone calls. They lack the basic knowledge of the departments they work in as well as understanding or even people skills honestly to interact with the public or answer questions. Maybe it’s because I’m 29, so I look older. I just feel like regardless of age, it was VERY difficult getting support here, or finding consistent answers. Personally, I have a learning disability and due to not being in school for 10 years, I hadn’t had an IEP and I wasn’t sure how to get about getting one. My physical appearance doesn’t warrant for help, I seem independent, so when I would reach out for help, I would get confused looks, or just attitudes as if I just need to figure it out alone. Eventually I found Dr. Juanita at counseling services, and she was very helpful at the ending of my spring semester. Unfortunately I never got my IEP plan here just due to the frustration of not being heard in the mist of attempting to fix issues, so I chose to not re enroll. I will say, they WILL fix a problem, but all the hoops and holes you have to jump through is ridiculous. Especially considering the faults tend to be on thier end. I’m mentally exhausted. Being an older student returning to school after so long, I would think they would have some type of support group or something in place. I felt very lost and alone here. The underlying shame of having to return to school surrounded by young adults is already overwhelming, but to receive shameful looks or consistently deal with passive aggressive attitudes is a lot and makes the shame worse. I wouldn’t recommend main campus at all. Wayne campus is smaller, everyone is more helpful, and they help with a smile.', "Watched the Akron Zips vs Buffalo Bulls men's basketball game on ESPN+ last night and was appalled by the lack of professionalism of the two announcers. Clearly, no prep work was completed for this game.  Player's names were mispronounced throughout the game, no history of the opposing team's journey up to this point, and negativity toward any player who has played for multiple teams during their college tenure. Why throw shade on kids who transfer via the portal to better themselves? Many transfers are created by head coaches who recruit a kid and then leave for the big payday, and the players who remain are left in a precarious position. The post-game conference with the Zips head coach is evidence of the genesis of the arrogance that permeates this program. Yuk.", "Nice baseball field. We were there for my grandson's game. Dayton vs Akron U.  Dayton won 14-11.  Yeah!"]

name: University of Akron Wayne College
reviews: ['I live an hour away, it’s a long drive but, I am having a wonderful experience at Wayne Community College. The Professors that I have for my classes possess a Doctorate Degree and they are able to teach at my level of understanding. Not many doctorate Professors can do that. They make learning easy, they are very approachable, understanding and compassionate. They will work with you but, don’t take it for granted they are very stern! The advisors are wonderful because, they ensure you have the classes you need and don’t add “fillers”. I appreciate the staff in the library, and Smucker learning center, cafeteria, bookstore, even the IT Department. Just about everyone is easy to work with. This is my personal experience here at the College. If you’re thinking about returning to College from a long time away from school, like I did. This is the best place to start.', "If you're looking for a small college experience with all of the benefits of a big university, Wayne College is the perfect choice! The campus is beautiful and the staff is incredibly friendly and helpful. The academics are top-notch, and I've never had a problem getting the classes I need. I would highly recommend Wayne College to anyone looking for a great college experience!", "Wonderful, quiet campus. Excellent teachers and staff, who are very thorough with their work. The cost of education here is extremely affordable. My favorite things about this campus is the Student Union and the FREE 3D printing lab. If you're looking at going to Akron main, but live in Wayne County, I recommend you save some money and go here for a year or two, it is the perfect way to transition from High School to College.", "One of the best options for a high school student to consider - CCP classes are available at no cost through many high schools, and post-secondary options are still out there.  This college is directly connected to The University of Akron, one of the top schools for the sciences.\n\nAlthough there are those that put down the community college option, it is foolish to pay more when you can get the same high quality education that will provide you with a successful career pathway.  Don't turn your nose at such an economically wise option.  Employers certainly won't fault you for making a fiscally responsible decision.  Instead, it just might get you hired.", 'Beautiful campus. Great for CCP students to start their general education classes and first year college students to get a great college experience.']

name: Art Academy of Cincinnati
reviews: ['My 11 year old son just finished up a week long camp here. He had such a wonderful experience. We have done other art camps in the past and many feel more like a babysitting experience without a lot of clear instruction. This is the second time he participated at the Art Academy (first in 2023). He made a small patchwork quilt that he sewed by hand, played around with different mediums to create art and learned to work well in a group setting to make some larger pieces. He was a bit disappointed by the ratio of boys (4) to girls (20), but that is not something the school can control and moreso just a reflection of interests for kids his age. The communication from the school was informative and timely. Would definitely send him again.', 'You never know what new, dynamic things their students are going to come up with, far more exciting than your average art school. Great location as well, right in the middle of Cincinnati arts. Stop by to check out one of their Final Friday exhibitions.', 'The Art Academy of Cincinnati is THE Best SCHOOL. I graduated class of 2015 with my BFA (bachelors in fine arts) - easily the best four years of my life. The city of Cincinnati is an awesome place to be a college student there is incredible historic architecture and new friends around every corner and its on the rise, there are always new restaurants (great for students who need employment or who are hungry) and lots of cool bars if youre into that. I went to the art academy knowing a wanted to be an artist and graduated with skills and confidence.', "As a graduate of the Art Academy of Cincinnati, and now its Academic Dean, I couldn't be more proud of what this small college of art and design has been able to give to so many artists. As a private, not-for-profit art college in Ohio,  the AAC continues to teach young artists and designers to follow their hearts and engage the world on their own terms through their creative work. What makes the Art Academy of Cincinnati so powerfully vital, not just in Cincinnati, but in the respective worlds of contemporary art and design, is the commitment to provide what our mission statement calls for “To create and sustain radical, forward-thinking, contemporary visual artists and designers whose creative contributions make a substantial difference in all the lives they touch. ” We make artists who delight in imaginative expression because we know that imagination makes the world.\nMAKE ART, MAKE A DIFFERENCE.", 'I’m a current student at AAC and while the classes offered are amazing and the environment is mostly good there are some issues. For one in my current dorm, they did not change the upstairs air filter which caused my roommate to be sick. The air filter was caked in dust and had not been changed for over a year probably. Also the way they handle Covid 19 is horrible. They give out misinformation to those impacted by it. They treat their isolated students like prisoners with some staff being snide, rude, or downright disrespectful to those students. The isolated students are not given adequate housing or enough resources to quarantine. I love AAC but I am disgusted and disappointed with their actions. If I could complain to the city or sue AAC I would in a heartbeat. Do better AAC.']
