name: Belmont College
reviews:
['My husband and I both attended here. They cancelled both of my majors due to not enough students to fill the classes. That was after I had already completed Summer and Fall classes. My husband was in welding he ended up having to go out of town the last week of class for work. One week before end of the semester! They took his Pell grant and his loans the term was paid for in full!! They submitted a bill to the Ohio Attorney General Office stating he owes them $1500! Like how? They got their money. So no I would NOT suggest this school. You can’t tell me they didn’t foresee the closing of those two majors they got what money they could before they closed them. Not caring about the students getting shafted. Then to take all financial aid then say a student owes them because they missed the last week of class. They are crooks and will steal your money. Don’t bother calling because if someone does answer they are rude and unprofessional.', 'In all honesty this college could be great, in fact one of the best community colleges in the USA.
Unfortunately it’s not, not even close. The financial aid is not something I ever recommend dealing with, most advisors are dismissing and disinterested in their work(mostly because there is like 3 for all students in the college), the campus it self is cramped and unorganized, the student commons area is constantly rented out to college staff and others for personal use, and the newly installed cafeteria is so over priced that it’s worth the walk to Subway, or the BP to get a sandwich from their instead. The library is atrocious, almost no in depth study material is available and if you would want to get a book loaned out from and other library you might as well travel there and get it there. I wanna make a personal complaint here so this is just my opinion and not facts, the chairs here are AWFUL. I understand college is a place of learning and not relaxing but it feels as if the chairs are designed to make students uncomfortable and want to leave. Also you cannot find a public printer, do not use the printer in the study commons it is never working.
The only advice I could give to whatever individual working for this college is this:
1. Hire more student advisors. They are constantly overwhelmed.
2. Lower prices in the cafeteria and vending machines. We already owe you thousands upon thousands of dollars.
3. Get Couches.....', "The financial aid department is unorganized. It's as if they expect new students to know what to do. They do not offer assistance unless you beat down their door and demand it. The instructors who I have had are great. Very helpful. The way classes are offered is not so great. It took me 4 years of going part time to graduate from the LPN program. This was because the classes I needed for the night program were not offered consecutively. Good instructors. Poor management and financial aid services.", 'I would not recommend this school to my worst enemy! I had nothing but issues in the welding program. You are better off going to the union and letting them teach you the trade for free! A welding degree is a complete waste of time. It does not count towards hours if you decide to go union you have to start all over. The facility was terrible the directors of the program was a complete joke. Half the time the shop did not even have materials. I pretty much had to teach myself through YouTube because the teachers do not teach! Do not waste your time on a degree at Belmont. You will find it’s nothing but issues the whole duration of your college experience.', "In all honesty, I wouldn't recommend this school to anybody. I went through their CDL Program. name: Bowling Green State University-Main Campus
reviews:
['We stayed on the Bowling Green State University campus for a week for our youth conference. We had over 1300 youth in attendance. The campus is very beautiful and well taken care of. The facilities were very clean. The staff were friendly to work with throughout the week. The food at the dining halls was pretty good. Our youth had a great time in the campus.', 'Wow, they are serious about their Falcons. It is a beautiful campus that looks to be handicappedaccessible. It also looks safe.', "What a beautiful campus. We visited on the President's Day open house to do some tours with our graduating child. What an experience to visit on an actual school day and witness the university in motion. I now know why my kid has committed to BGSU! Every person we met, including the president of the university, were genuine and enthusiastic, making the experience that much more enjoyable. A huge thank you to all the students and staff that made for an amazing day.", "The professors and advisors are great which is why it even deserves one star, and they do a lot to make sure that you have what you need. However, when it comes to the universities procedures and policies its outright aggravating. My car was damaged in the parking lot, I reported it to the Campus police, they photographed the damage and said they would call me back. THEY DIDN'T. They have no cameras in the parking lot besides lot 5!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I pay $88 PER SEMESTER, to fight for a parking spot and even then risk my vehicle to damage. My car has got scrapes from doors, and had to buy a beater vehicle (WHICH ALSO GOT DAMAGED) because they damaged my BMW and even chipped the paint after the third time being hit by a car door and its going to cost me $200 just to get the dent out of my door!!!!!!! I have tried everything to even arriving at 7am in the morning and parking on the edge where only one person can park next to me, however. The laziness of the snow being shoved onto the back corner of the parking lot has prevented me from parking safely as well.

It gets better... I have a disability, so I was forced to walk pretty far despite paying SO much to park here and attend classes $650/mo WITH FASFA support!!!!!!!!!!. And despite the money they receive from us students, due to these cold conditions, they didn't really clear up the sidewalks, ice is everywhere, and they shoved all the snow onto the bike racks and not a single one is cleared up. Its got at least 6 inches of snow covering the bike rack if not more. I cannot walk that far to get to my classes especially in the cold and I cannot push my scooter through 6 inches of snow. I cannot get my electric scooter through any of this and it interferes with my heath conditions. No charging stations for the scooters (or you're not allowed to charge it there...).

They forced students to come to school on a level 3 that was issued in numerous counties, and caused me and some other students to succumb to illness due to the cold, I left early to go to the doctors as I was extremely ill and could not breathe from the cold.

I love the vibes of this university but they are severely neglecting the students especially ones who are not on-campus despite paying an arm and a leg to even be here. Commuter students be ware and FOLD YOUR MIRRORS.

And BGSU, please make this campus more accessible for students who cant walk all the way from their car in -1 degree temperatures, and allow them to be able to charge their bikes and scooters if they need it and PUT MORE CAMERAS UP. We are paying YOU TO PARK HERE. It is the least you all could do to prevent more reported vehicle damage... as the officers said it happens so often all they can do is take a report and check the SINGLE CAMERA YOU ALL HAVE IN LOT 5. COME ON.", 'As an alumnus of BGSU, I did have some great time and precious memories on campus, and even now I still appreciate this journey and all the people I met here.']

name: Bryant & Stratton College-Parma
reviews:
['I’m incredibly grateful for my time at Bryant & Stratton College. Over the years, I earned two associate degrees and a bachelor’s degree, and each step of the journey helped shape my career and confidence. The instructors were supportive, knowledgeable, and truly cared about my success—not just in the classroom, but beyond graduation as well.

What really stood out to me was the flexible learning options and the practical, career-focused curriculum that prepared me for real-world challenges. The staff was always helpful, from academic advising to career services. I felt like I wasn’t just a number—I was part of a community that wanted me to succeed.

If you’re looking for a school that’s dedicated to your personal and professional growth, I highly recommend Bryant & Stratton College. It’s made a lasting impact on my life and career!', 'I am currently a student at Bryant & Stratton College’s Parma Campus. School has always been a challenge for me, but everything changed when I enrolled at B&SC. The instructors are incredible—they’ve provided the support and guidance I needed to become the student I’ve always aspired to be. The staff is also outstanding, always there when I need encouragement or help during tough times. I’m excited to complete my program this December, and I’m already exploring what program I’d like to pursue next at the college. I wholeheartedly recommend Bryant & Stratton College to anyone looking for a quality education surrounded by people who truly care about your success.
– Brooke ❤️', 'Forever so thankful for my time at Bryant & Stratton College! I was apart of the PTA program and I felt so supported throughout my learning experience and prepared to work after graduating! I loved the smaller class size, hands on environment, and accessibility for any help I needed whether that was in the classroom itself, while studying for my licensure exam, resume writing, and even networking! Truly can’t recommend this program/school enough!', 'As a graduate from the Physical Therapist Assistant program I am beyond grateful for my experience at B&S! My instructors were always very insightful, supportive and helpful throughout my journey. I am now working in the career field as a PTA and couldn’t be happier. I enjoyed the smaller setting of B&S as it really made the experience more pleasant and I still keep in touch with my Instructors and former classmates.', "I absolutely recommend this school! The teachers were wonderful and helped me get through my classes with ease. At any time, I had a question or needed more time on an assignment they were very understanding.  I believe the staff did a great job helping all the students get on task to get to graduate. I got right into my job after graduation thanks to them! I'm excited to go back to further my career."]

name: Capital University
reviews:
["I attended from 2019 to 2023 and was not happy with the academic experience. While Capital offers a small campus near downtown and an accredited degree that can open up the path for further education and a career, there are serious issues with Capital’s academic policies.

Capital promises #capfam and one-on-one guidance from academic advisors, but this fell short. My advisor never once met with me to review future plans or go over my course load and went on a year-long sabbatical without notifying or meeting with me. I only learned of his trip from the department head.

The most crucial aspect of the university, its academics, is the one that is executed the poorest. For Signature Learning courses, professors take rich subjects and water them down for the weakest students. They benefit humanities students the least; it does not make sense for students whose entire course of study has been in the humanities to have to take UC320 - Humanities. A humanities major is generally more knowledgeable and has superior relevant skills than a non-humanities major. Imagine if there were a UC course for nursing skills or business management, those departments would not stand for it, as it would be a disservice to their students’ time and skills.

Semester-long group work happens often in the business school and in UC courses. While educators advocate that it fosters soft skills and prepares students for work in their field, this is a misnomer that forces top-performing students to make the choice of either doing more work or accepting an inferior product/lower grade. As a grad with corporate experience, I have to challenge this; in class, you’re not working with people who are specialized, the work is researching and writing and if you are the best at that, you will have to deal with not only trying to motivate your peers, but also having to edit their inferior work or just do it yourself. While there were great experiences that I had with some, the overwhelming amount of time, I was forced to do the lion's share of the work and I had to deal with a lot of dead weight.

Grade inflation is rampant, especially in BUS333 in Fall 2022, a 5-credit course designed for juniors and seniors w/in the marketing major. The professor allowed a 1st exam retake due to a class average of 58.9% with several scores in the 40s, threw out grading on an assignment, stated an extra 10% added to the final grade, added an extra 15% to Exam 4, and allowed the final exam to be taken home. I knew students who outright said they were failing the class and then ended up passing, others who said their final grade was a low D or C. Working backwards, their true final grade ought to be an F. While I love the professor and the material, I felt demoralized that apathetic students were rewarded with second, third, and fourth winds. My earned advantage was being eroded.

Other courses my senior year, BUS337 and 349, had open exams that were largely multiple choice; a monkey could copy the question into Google and select the correct answer.

It’s not that I have a different opinion on the academic aspect of the collegiate experience or that I wanted my peers to fail; it’s the fact that they did not do the work and, rather than face consequences, were rewarded with multiple chances to redo their failures. If they had truly learned from their mistakes, they would have put in more time after the first exam, but they did not and were rewarded.

Capital advertises a 21-27 ACT range, not accurate since 2019. Their most recent 2024 fact book reports the middle 50% is 18 - 25. Standards are low, and it shows in class.

I know higher education faces multiple challenges, but the academic practices at Capital are inexcusable and, while they are happening across all universities, Capital excels in how much it acquiesces to them. While I did have some great experiences, there are serious academic concerns. If you are a prospective student, I would seriously reflect on what you want your academic experience to be and would encourage you to pursue options other than Capital.", 'Beautiful campus and generally great students.  We just took a tour and really enjoyed the experience. The campus feels like a larger school than it is, but the classes and student/faculty ratio also retains that small school feel.  This seems like a great choice.', 'Son is a junior this year at Capital. He has lived two years on campus and two years off campus. He has gotten 7 parking tickets in 2.5 years attending the school. Doesn’t matter if he has a parking pass or not. This year he lives off campus and still gets tickets because he isn’t a visitor, so can’t park on the street or in the visitor lot. Even if he is just going to the trainer, they still ticket you. You get a parking pass for a lot and can’t park in said lot from 2a-6a (the lot connected to the dorms), but they want you to park down the street. The food is horrible, the dorms have mold everywhere, and the buildings are run down. For the money people pay to attend this school, you would think you would get more. Some of the best years is someone’s book of life are his worse years. It’s said, but he can’t wait to graduate and get away from Capital.', 'Pretty cool, needs even more sidewalks closed', "Students get out of their time at Capital University what they put into it. The classes are small, so students actually get a chance to know on a personal level all their professors, and there are many ways to gain leadership experience on campus if students actively look. The campus community is very friendly, accepting, and welcoming. Finally, Capital's campus is situated in a gorgeous and safe neighborhood. This area is also diverse with four synagogues being within walking distance of campus and many churches and a mosque within easy walking/driving distance."]

name: Cedarville University
reviews:
['Cedarville University located in. Cedarville Ohio is Christ-centered; providing academic excellence accredited BA and MA in various degree programs, plus a beautiful campus !', 'Visiting we were pleasantly surprised at how beautiful the grounds were. Many of the buildings have huge windows overlooking the lake. Excited they are getting new dorms as the old ones need to be replaced. Overall it appears the President and professors care deeply about students. Also the student body as a whole are some of the kindest students we have come across while visiting multiple campuses. Highly impressed!', 'Linda and I were eager to visit the Campus after 23 years when her daughter attended.

So much NEW CONSTRUCTION is in-progress!  Linda may recall the Student Center building may have been completed in her daughter's last year.

A new entire pedestrian-only area in the heart of all the classroom buildings has construction across, and south of the Student Center.

And, so many NEW DORMS!  In my opinion, the Campus is RIPE for a street level Monorail traversing the dorms to Engineering right through the pedestrian walkway with a bridge crossing the storm overflow and valley. This Trail is home based at the Student Center.  Another "Trail" line runs east to west with a lighted tunnel  north of the Student Center, and going under the north/south Trail.

But, the blessing to this University is there are only male and female students as our Living God intended- each with a unique Plan to RAISE THE KINGDOM!

We decided to go inside the Student Center.  The Dining Hall is expansive.  The Boarding Fee can be reduced with a significant  deposit to a spending account.
Scholarships can be $10,000 per semester even!

Upon leaving the Center, we encountered two young ladies doing homework.  Turns out, they are Psychology majors: the same as Linda received her degree in teaching.

God's blessings to all you Yellow Jackets.  Pray often in groups!

- Keith Carey
Psalm 1, 34, 51, 103', "Had a wonderful visit to Cedarville University.  The students and faculty we met on both formally on the tours and informally on campus have an passion and appreciation for the school, the vision, values, the leadership, their education, and for people in general.  Just an amazing culture there.

Update: Now after visiting again, I'm further impressed.  Very solid teaching, both academically and in the Biblical teaching.  The staff and leadership love God, love people, and really strive to help the students succeed not only in their future career, but in life.  When asked tough questions, the leadership does not give in to what people say or even try to walk a fine line trying to please everyone, but they stick to the Bible as the source of truth, and practice grace and truth.  I sat in a Bible class and talked to several professors and saw the passion first hand!   I encourage you to visit their web site and watch a few of the Chapel archives.", 'The most Bible based and purposeful university around. Solid as a rock in these turbulent times. My freshman is in great hands. Top notch professors, administration, student leaders, and 1000 day stewardship plan to help young people develop into adults who love God with all their heart, love their neighbors, and lead in their professions. Praise the Lord!']

What message are  they sending, that students that are foreigners,  plus size, or black is not what they want to represent their nursing program on their website or in their magazines..STOP IT 2025"]

name: Central State University
reviews:
['It is unfortunate that I feel compelled to leave a negative review.

I applied to Central State University in December after my previous institution closed and I relocated to another state. I specifically considered Central State because it is an HBCU. My application was submitted on December 7, 2025.

Initially, I communicated with Anauta regarding my transcripts. I questioned why transcripts from every institution I previously attended were required, as my most recent transcript already reflected my transfer credits. Nevertheless, I complied and submitted all requested transcripts on January 7, 2026. I emailed both Anauta and Tracy to confirm submission.

To date, I have received no acknowledgment, no response to emails, and no returned phone calls. I left multiple voicemails and escalated my concerns by contacting Teria, the Interim Director of Admissions, yet received no response from her either.

As of January 23, 2026, I have not received any communication regarding my application status—no acceptance, denial, or update of any kind. The complete lack of responsiveness reflects poorly on the admissions process and raises serious concerns about professionalism and accountability within the department.

Prospective students are entitled to ask questions and expect timely communication, particularly when making important academic and financial decisions. Unfortunately, my experience suggests a disregard for those responsibilities.

For comparison, I was accepted into another institution within days of submitting my application and was able to successfully transfer more than half of my credits. Regrettably, due to this experience, Central State University is not an institution I would feel comfortable being associated with!', 'Caught in the rain and then surprise-ambushed by a traveling tour of twenty 8th-12th graders from Maryland, but still grateful we have an HBCU so close to us in Ohio. I only wish our legislators were as appreciative and supported the school more as it seemed severely run down in places. I fear my daughter didn’t get the full experience as many of the doors were locked and inaccessible.', 'The campus is beautiful.  The staff that we saw today was awesome.  We were literally, just passing by asked a question of a young man and he took us on a tour.   Our visit was during the students during Spring Break and not many students were present but again the ones that we did encounter on campus were very welcoming and excited to talk about their experiences.', 'Football stadium audio is absolutely TERRIBLE and intelligible! Live stream to game was not working.

Student staff unhelpful to the point they couldn’t even direct us to a bathroom.  Everyone seemed very unorganized. But more importantly nobody was smiling or even friendly. This includes everyone we encountered. Parking lot attendant, admissions, concessions and stadium volunteers.

We have put several kids thru school and have visited dozens of universities with sporting events and we would never consider this as a potential university based on the awful attitude of everyone we encountered and witnessed. Just very low energy!
We were walking to the visitors stands and got all the way to the goal post just for a lady to tell us we had to go the other way because the band was coming. Well the band never came and we were made to walk 3/4 around the track the other direction to sit down. That was ridiculous.

Admission was $26 and parking was $11. No option for cash payment or tap to pay!

Now for the positive..the BAND ROCKS!!', "This was a very good parade. I'm a 63 yr. old black male. And it done me good to be around my people having a good time. I love the band. But the sistas were looking fine as hell. Keep up the good work"]

reviews:

2. Touch base with the school you want to go to after this and see what programs transition because college is a business, they only care when you as the right questions.', "Had the pleasure of meeting some very gracious and professional people and professors (not you, PAUL Weingartner). But I also had the misfortune of dealing with some of the most unprofessional and trashy people ever, who take their anger out on you because they're broke and miserable. As far as the curriculum, it taught useful things but felt a bit half-baked at times. Also Madeline Ndambakuwa can't teach her speech class to save her life, and I'm surprised she's even tenured.", 'So far so good. I have enrolled in the Associates HIM program and am enjoying it. I am only in the first semester but have had no real issues. The outgoing HIM program director was retiring and did seem to not really care too much, but the new one is great. I enjoyed my meeting with her. My one real issue, I am doing this totally online. No classes at the school. For an online degree, I sure have to go to the school a lot. In the first half of this semester alone I have had to go up there at least 5 times. To get books and I was required to make another meeting with my academic advisor for an intro to college class on top of the meeting I had when I first applied. This is online school, I should not be going onto the actual campus but maybe once just to check it out and meet with my advisor.

Other than that, nothing but good stuff. My professors are professional and competent, even if they are online. So far the work is challenging and they have made it pretty easy to use their online services. Registering for classes, checking on financial aid stuff, school tools like email are all easy to access. If you are looking for a 2 year program, this might be the place for you. Just make sure you do your research first, and do not just go off of Google Reviews. I see a lot of negative reviews on here that seem like its a personal problem, not a school problem. One review talked about "ghetto acting students" which alone is a racist comment. Ghetto? What do you mean by that? Just because someone is immature does not mean the campus is bad. A lot of people going here are fresh out of high school. College shapes you, college helps bring you into adult hood. Give people a chance. Don't go off Google Reviews alone. Go in and speak to the program director, to financial aid, to admissions and gage it for yourself.', 'I attended 2 semesters here which went well and allowed me to complete half of my credit hours. When I first applied to the school my first advisor assured me I could complete my program completely online, as I don’t live closer enough to commute daily. When I went to register for my third semester I was informed one of my classes would have to be taken in person which I was annoyed at since I was assured I would be fully online. I did find a way to make the commute for that class once a week, and was told the rest of the classes I would definitely be able to do fully online. The day before one of my classes was about to start, I noticed it was changed from online to in person. Then I noticed 2 of the classes had changed like that. I contacted my instructor but didn’t hear anything back so had to miss the first class. I knew I wouldn’t be able to complete my degree without these 2 courses but I wasn’t able to commute, so I looked into transferring and ended up having to transfer because I never heard back from the instructor. The day after I completed my transfer the instructor emailed back and said I might be able to take the classes online, which isn’t even a full answer and was too late at this point. I was also told I would receive CState Accelerate which would cover whatever balance is left after my financial aid. I kept waiting for my balance to be covered by them and contacted them multiple times asking when the remaining balance would be taken care of and they would never give me a date and it ended up showing I owed 1000 dollars which I couldn’t afford as I was told it would be covered. Also was a nightmare when trying to transfer as the school was withholding my transcripts so I couldn’t send them to the new school. After I dropped all my courses the school also told me I would owe a fee for dropping them which is ridiculous because it’s not my fault that the instructor made the courses impossible for me to take last minute. Overall horrible experience, the staff who answers the phone are some of the rudest and least helpful people I’ve ever met and the faculty likes to deceive students and potential students. They will tell you whatever you want to hear so you will go there and change it last minute with no remorse. Would never recommend for anyone.

Edit: They are also charging me money to drop my courses now even though the website says 100% refund the first week.', 'Best landscaping education you can get. I started an associates of applied business in Landscape Horticulture in autumn 2024 and have learned more than I could imagine about landscaping. Mark and Heather are the best instructors anyone could ask for, and are very supportive and encouraging. If you work hard in the Landscape Horticulture program, then the landscaping world is your oyster, which you with shovel will open.']

name: University of Cincinnati-Clermont College
reviews:
['I review businesses from a disability perspective. I love being a student at UC Clermont, the sensory room is very helpful.', 'I’m supposed to have my degree. Advisor of this school was completely incompetent and had me take incorrect classes. 2 years of school and I’m told I need to add an extra 2. Cost me thousands and he expected me to be cool with 2 more years and thousands of more dollars. I left and went to trade school. What a joke. Literally made my life more difficult and I got nothing to show for it. Thanks UC', 'Got my first vaccine shot here. No waiting and they were even able to take us early. Super nice people.
Update: got my second shot and was very impressed on how well organized they were. Lines moved smoothly and was happy to see more people here.', 'Lied to me about being able to get my VA benefits. Not even registered at this school as far as the VA is concerned. Not A fast process to get registered at this school. Told me I can get my E.M.T certificate here but threw it out and told me when it was to late to find another school. My point is this school does not care and will try to make a few bucks off you while getting sqrewed in the process. If your a veteran please do not come here and have your savings destroyed like I did.', "I am currently an IT major at the College. All of my Professors are extremely knowledgeable in their field of study and easy going people. Average cost per semester for my IT major has been $2650. (MUCH cheaper than the for profit Schools). I wasn't required to take SATs or ACTs for acceptance. I was required to take a Math and English Placement exam.

Campus is easy to navigate and is on top of a hill in beautiful Batavia. I'm extremely happy with the School and would highly recommend it to anyone. I've been out of School for approx. 8 Years due to Military Service and the Veterans Department helped me with all my transitioning.

Career Services has local and regional companies that come to the School to talk to Students for Internships and Job positions as well. Regardless of your age (and I've seen from 18 to 44) this is a great place to get back into School before transferring somewhere else after your Associates. (only one Bachelors Program is currently offered at the time of this review. But their are plans to add more.)"]

name: University of Cincinnati-Blue Ash College
reviews: ['A very nice campus!  I had some time this evening so I walked over here from Summit Park (about a 40min walk).  It was beautiful and there were paved roads or sidewalks the entire way.  UC Blue Ash was very clean with publicly accessible restrooms as well as outside seating.  (Note though:  There is no public "UC guest" WiFi.  At least as of September 2022, the only WiFi networks I could find on campus were all secured.  I\'m guessing you must have a student ID and password to access the network.)', "I attended UC Blue Ash for five semesters, and it was the best schooling and time of my life so far. From ease of access to resources like the math lab and social spaces that just aren't the same at other universities. The opportunities provided by this school are something you CAN NOT pass on, especially with the big school benefits from UC Uptown. This place is truly one of the hidden gems of higher education.", 'The Dental clinic has been remodeled, very spacious! The students, dentists and instructors are very kind and professional 😀 Great way to save money and they do a phenomenal job on your teeth cleaning!', 'This is a great experience.   It was a little weird at first.  The experience  is awesome. They try to make you feel welcome.  You learn your way around.', "UC Blue Ash has exceeded my expectations over and over. As far as I'm concerned, community college doesn't get any better. Great professors who are motivated to teach. Pleasant campus with some nice green spaces."]

name: Ohio Christian University
reviews:
['Not who I thought they were. I did all the online research and numerous conversations, but once I was actually on the campus grounds I saw how things really are. They only actually have about 100 students living on campus, barely 200 total. This means getting classes is take what THEY GIVE YOU when they tell you to. The limited professors cover numerous classes and degrees so a class is typically taught one slot per week. They seemed great from a far but in person it was SMOTHERING. I won't say cult, but horrible vibes. So after leaving I did more digging to find that transferring and accreditation would be an absolute problem with courses because how they have to combine multiple courses into their "curriculum" because they don't have enough professors and students for the actual course. They have no career services department to work on your internships or job placement after graduation. If the new President sticks around loooooong term, then maybe 15-20 years from now if they can get enrollment from 200's to around 1,000 they can get better accreditation and afford to diversify their courses with more professors and then get more accreditation and be recognized better by other higher learning institutions. Otherwise, you're wasting money unless you are planning on ministry or being a teacher. Be thorough before enrolling, save your money and get your associates at a Community College, it will at least transfer and you won't be retaking courses.', "I have been to 3 colleges and I must say OCU was an amazing online experience. The studies were in depth and the professors were wonderful. I also loved the staff I was always able to speak with someone if I had questions. My daughter wants to attend OCU we are praying on it but it's definitely the only place I feel good about.", 'If I could give this school 0 stars, I would.

I am deeply disappointed with my experience and strongly recommend that anyone considering enrollment read this fully and speak directly with former students (LinkedIn is a good place to start) before committing.

As someone who has worked in higher education for years and attended two other colleges, it honestly makes me ill that the first Christian institution I attended was also the most unprofessional I’ve ever encountered.

1. Enrollment & Onboarding:

Enrollment outreach was persistent (normal), but onboarding was disorganized. Orientation consisted of two required evening sessions where staff simply read minimal slides, which were emailed days later. Most concerning: critical attendance policies were not clearly disclosed until after enrollment. Missing a single assignment or discussion post results in an absence strike; the second is automatic withdrawal. This policy is extremely important for adult learners and should be emphasized before financial commitment. This was my first red flag.

2. Systems & Virtual Learning:

Students must juggle multiple disconnected platforms (Outlook, Sonis, Brightspace, Slingshot), which was inefficient and frustrating. Textbooks also suddenly switched from physical to digital without explanation.

3. Instruction Quality & Assignments:

Instructors:
I had one excellent professor. Most others were disengaged, slow to respond, and offered minimal feedback. One instructor was hyper-critical of minor formatting while posting unprofessional, unprepared videos (petting cat, graphic tee's, messy backgrounds, losing train of thought mid-sentence). Expectations for students were strict, yet professionalism was inconsistent.

Assignments:
The workload was ABSOLUTELY overwhelming BUT surface-level: multiple discussion posts (equivalent to short papers), 1-2 long assignments weekly, plus weekly final papers or presentations. Instructions were poorly written, typo-filled, and often felt mechanical. Many assignments amounted to watching basic YouTube videos and writing reflections - all something I could have done for free at home.

Overall:
- Lack of meaningful academic advising beyond enrollment
- No proactive student advocacy or escalation support
- No flexibility or grace policies for adult learners
- Minimal accommodation guidance despite strict attendance rules
- Tuition cost vs. instructional value mismatch

Faith Integration:
For a Christian institution, faith integration was shallow. Assignments rarely required meaningful biblical study, sourcing scripture, or deeper theological engagement. Reflection questions were basic and repetitive, like "What do you believe is God's purpose for you?"

Deadlines & Grading:
Student deadlines were rigid, yet grading was often late - sometimes weeks - making it impossible to apply feedback before final submissions.

4. Communication & Financial Aid (MOST Concerning):

Communication was CONSISTENTLY poor. Fin Aid was unacceptable: emails went unanswered, statements were REPEATEDLY incorrect, no calls were made to review issues when asked, and no accountability or apologies. I’ve also worked in a student finance dep before - this level of disorganization isn't normal.

Withdrawal & Compassion:
When I withdrew during a difficult personal time, the response was cold and transactional. There was no empathy, guidance, or support - something especially troubling for a Christian institution. Not even "I'm sorry!" or "How can we support you?"

Culture & Leadership:
I observed what appeared to be insular leadership and possible nepotism. Professional warmth, clarity, and responsiveness were often missing. Virtual learners felt excluded from campus culture, reflecting outdated views on inclusivity and technology.

This experience left me disillusioned, unsupported, and financially stressed. These were not isolated issues - they were systemic. If you are seeking deep faith-based education, professional communication, financial transparency, and compassionate leadership, I strongly encourage you to look elsewhere.', 'I really really enjoy this establishment. It’s super clean, comfortable, staff usually friendly, and a nice variety of foods to choose from.
The price for a senior to some is more than reasonable $5 and I want supposed they had to raise it a couple dollars. It’s still doable.
I’d like to make a constructive criticism:
Friday night some friends & I came to dinner then enjoy music & comedy over at the circleville Methodist church.
The lasagna could use a little more sauce. Was a bit dry. Perhaps something happened & that had to go minimal.
The pizza is usually pretty good better since I told them the crust was a bit difficult to chew.
A month ago the Tex mex broccoli dish on a Friday was difficult to eat as the tortilla strips Were quite hot, spicy wise. Even the college girls we heard commenting that it was way too hot. So maybe they could choose a little more mild.
I highly recommend this establishment.', "The young gentleman's that took us back and forth to the pumpkin festival were just awesome. I absolutely loved them so beautiful very proud of them ❤️"]

name: Clark State College
reviews:
['Easy ways to find the classes comfortable, the classrooms are equipped with everything necessary, this college also has a canteen where they cook fresh food every day you can safely come and drink any drinks soft drinks eat food all fresh,also here there are a lot of rooms where you can retire and read quietly many classes where exams are taken', 'Met the president of the school she has a great personality!! Nikki Woodyard was so amazing over the phone and in person getting my son set up!! I am excited about his future here!!', "I came here from my high school CCP classes. I figured the college would be pretty good considering my experiences with the CCP classes weren't bad. Boy was I wrong, it has been nothing but nightmares since I started here. They do not tell you any important information and expect you to be able to find out everything for yourself. A majority of the teachers I have dealt with are near impossible to get in contact with, and one even took an entire week to respond to a question about an important essay, causing me to fail. The classes are beyond awful. I have a major interest in cybersecurity, however i'm now having to turn to something else because the cybersecurity program was using textbooks that were 8 years outdated which made assignments require complicated workarounds. Financial aid and the cashiers office ended up screwing me out of 400 bucks because of a massive error on their end they neglected to fix. I had an assignment that required me to set up 2 more semesters of classes that barely ended up getting finished because the main student advisor was suddenly quitting. Quite frankly I feel bad for the advisors, they get paid like trash, only 20 bucks an hour. If you can afford Sinclair, go to Sinclair. Do not make my mistake.", "A majority of the positive reviews on this site are biased and are from the staff. Please, heed the warnings that you see here. Some of these positive comments come as a result of the staff coercing someone to post a positive review. Please, do not believe the positive reviews - for the sake of your wallet and academic progress. Coming to this college was nothing but a huge waste of time and money.

By far the worst college ON THE PLANET. Please, go anywhere else but here. A lot of the credits do not transfer, the staff is rude and doesn't care about you, and a professor at Sinclair told me that they consider these classes to be sub-standard. Don't waste your time or money. The only thing they care about is your money.

I understand that you may want to attend a community college because it's cheaper, but do keep in mind that you only get what you pay for and at clark state that isn't much! Low tuition fees = low quality institution. The professors are not here because they want to ensure the success of their students. They're here to collect a paycheck and enhance the appearance of their resumes.", 'The professors are awesome, I have learned a lot from them, and most of the time they are very accessible through email. But, the staff is incompetent and honestly haven't helped me in any way. Half the time they have students working in their offices and the students are not only rude, but have no idea how to help you if you have a question. I went into the cashiers office to pay for a semester of classes and was told "This is how much you will owe IF you pay on time" and got a dirty look. The people in the records and registration office are nice and I feel that they're the only office that know what they're talking about and actually want to help you.']

name: Cleveland Institute of Art
reviews: ['Horrible hours for the mailroom. I really wish it wasn’t closed ALL the time.', "Beautiful location, with a lot of careful planning gone into projection and sound. The selection of films from the past and around the world opens a lot of doors to you in terms of film as art and expression. I particularly enjoy their showings of cult classics around certain seasons, themes, or directors. Now, to explain the 4 stars. I understand this is an educational institution first, not an entertainment venue, but it wouldn't be a fair review if I didn't give my honest opinion. First, the seats are torturous. I'm a tall guy, the only other place that is so uncomfortable to physically exist in is an airplane. Lastly, no concessions that I'm aware of. Again, I know it's not that kind of a theater, but it would be nice. Especially if I could get a beer to numb the pain of those seats.", "This is the BEST place in Cleveland to go see classic, foreign, and cult movies. The theater shows projections digitally and on 35mm film. Just check their schedule and it will say if it's on film. The theater has a strict no cell phone policy, so please be respectful because some people (me) like to watch a piece of art uninterrupted. They often have have different series of films. For instance, they just finished a series on the films of Jodorowsky, which I was fortunate enough to see 3 of. To save myself from rambling, go see movies here and, if you can, become a member.", "After purchasing tickets online they then made us exchange them at the ticket counter so we could be registered for a $5  gift card. Very annoying. Security girl was worthless. She sat behind a counter and played a game on her phone the entire time. I don't think she ever looked up. Theater was clean, comfortable, and good leg room in the lower seating area. Well maintained restrooms.", 'The Cleveland Cinematheque represents the very finest film and tradition of respect for film available in the Midwest. John Ewing with the assistance of Mister God has created the finest independent film Society I have ever encountered. If you are not a member become one if you have not seen a film here do so immediately.']

name: Cleveland Institute of Music
reviews: ['Fantastic facilities and faculty!! Gorgeous Concert Hall too', 'Two extraordinary music halls (Mixon Hall and Kulas auditorium) feature the endeavor of the students and staff of one of the world’s finest music conservatories. Most of the students are taught and mentored by members of the globally renowned Cleveland Orchestra and students perform at least twice a year at neighboring Severance Hall.  Many students are featured soloists who perform at The Cleveland Museum of Art as well.  Most concerts are offered to the public free of charge.  Each and every concert, ensemble, opera, and solo performance is staged with artistry, skill, and passion. Every student selected to attend this world-class institution has exceptional talent; -most will go on to achieve world-class acclaim and success,  thanks to the dedication of talented faculty, staff, and the devotion of the CIM community.', "Amazing school with awesome facilities. I'm not a student of this place, but I felt this place was nice when I visited the school to watch the piano recital.", 'I had a opportunity to see one of the many free shows that they offer and all I can say is the show was excellent. A beautiful facility with many individual practice rooms for students. Will be attending different events they have to offer in the future.', "This was my first time seeing a concert at The Cleveland Institute of Music. The school is filled with some of the most talented musicians from around the world, taught by members of internationally reknown Cleveland Orchestra. Mixon Hall, where the performance was tonight, is a beautiful airy concert hall. It's visually stunning, the stage overlooks a lush garden. Acoustically it is clear, if not slightly dry. This is a great place to see world class music performed at a fraction of the cost (if not outright free). Check back to see what they've got on the calendar!"]

name: Cleveland State University
reviews:
["First off, apologies for the long post — just taking a stroll down nostalgia boulevard. ... While I only attended this University for a year in 1999 before Transferring to MTSU, my experience staying on campus at the converted Holiday Inn (now gone sadly) is one I'll remember and cherish for a lifetime.  There was comradery between the guys on my floors and the girls on Floor 5 like nothing I've experienced.   On Campus the profs were great, there were many extra circular programs to take part in (For me Fencing and news photography).     Also one of the hidden jewels of this University is being downtown.  Cleveland was one of the more underrated cities in America in the late 90's.  Exploring these lands as a young adult was  enthralling.  The Rock n Roll hall of fame was a short walk away.   Next to that was the abyss of Lake Erie.  From a Photographer's perspective the options were limitless.  I never felt unsafe, even venturing into abandon buildings to get a shot.   I was young and bullet proof back then. Maybe its all changed but the decision to go to this school is one I'll never regret.", "Got to tour the campus during their Fall Visit day. Parking was simple in the dedicated parking deck (free during visit). It was a short walk to the student center where we were given information about the school and it's programs. Lots and lots of walking and multiple parts of the tour were up and down several flights of steps. Excellent information and a wonderful tour and history about Playhouse theater. Close to home (an hour+ for us= local-ish!) Definitely recommend checking it out.", "Update:

This place is a complete joke now. I completed my undergrad here years ago and it was so much better. I used to love this college. So much has changed over the years. Not sure if CSU decided to cut half of its staff because it seems like there's almost never anyone available for questions. The enrollment center is not what it used to be. No one picks up the phone and don't bother leaving a message because they don't call back. When it comes to advisors, it's so difficult to get a hold of them or even get on their schedules for an appointment.

Additionally, each semester they enroll me in health insurance automatically when I already told them I do not need it. Then, they never want to pick up or respond to emails regarding the extra $1000 charge and fix it.

This is not the same university I went to years ago. So much has changed. The University needs better organization, management, and MORE STAFF!!!", "Not a college you'd want to go to. Everything is always broken, nothing works. They charge you to park there. The school is a joke. My daughter spent a week with no hot water, they were in no rush to fix it. Then the electric, no rush, then there was flooding. They are just in no rush to help these students. They let them suffer and stress about living there while they are in school!!", 'I came to this university seeking education, growth, and a sense of belonging. Academically, there are opportunities. Socially, my experience has been deeply disappointing.

A significant number of student-athletes were consistently rude, dismissive, and unwelcoming toward me. As an international student, I already carried the weight of being far from home - being treated like I didn’t belong only made that heavier. I wasn’t asking for special treatment, only basic respect and kindness.

No student should feel invisible, isolated, or mocked in a place that claims to value diversity and inclusion. I hope this university seriously reflects on how students -especially athletes - represent this campus and how newcomers are treated.']

name: Columbus College of Art & Design
reviews:
['While I can’t speak to the quality of the school and education. The school has a unique presence in Columbus, Ohio. While visiting the city it was centrally located near the Art Museum.', 'My 20yo Step-Daughter was just yelled at by a 60 year old man (student), saying "I will end you" in class and the school did nothing to address or correct the situation. The individual has already been reported for inappropriate advances.', 'as a student here, i can say that this school is horrible and the amount of cons heavily outweigh the pros. the faculty is terrible at addressing student concerns and do not meet the needs of the students at all. if the professor is good, they are really good -- but if the professor is bad, they are TERRIBLE. this school is extremely expensive as well, and most of the time it feels like you are not getting what you are paying for. theres numerous cash grabs and irrelevant, but mandatory, payments. with the amount of money this school makes, you would expect higher quality care, but not at all. the internet is terrible, food is not great... i would save your money and choose any other art school over this one.', 'Super friendly folks, providing classic art education in a focused and accessible location!

If you are an art focused student, looking to extend and/or expand your art, or art related career, do some digging into CCAD!  Great place do hone your art capabilities, as well as expand into classic "hands in/hands on" types of art that not every college can provide!', 'If you want to be a concept artist or character designer, don’t go to this school, it’s a waste of money. I graduated from CCAD in 2015, majoring in Illustration. The Illustration major was the only major that offered an entertainment design class, but it didn’t focus much on concept art techniques. Most of the professors come from comics or traditional illustration backgrounds, so they don’t understand how the concept art industry works or its standards.

We used Photoshop a lot, but I never saw an Illustration teacher do demo paintings in Photoshop. Every class felt like you just did one project after another, learning everything on your own. Even the basic drawing fundamentals classes felt more like hobby art classes. Only a few teachers actually taught and demonstrated techniques. Most of them were lazy, just standing there doing nothing or playing on the computer.

Critiques were basically useless. If your perspective was wrong, the teacher wouldn’t correct it or point it out, they just expected you to figure it out yourself. If you want to see what a good art lesson looks like, watch YouTube videos. If you want to see how a good art teacher grades students’ work, check out Proko’s examples. Having a good art teacher is crucial, but sadly, CCAD’s Illustration program failed to provide that.

Think about how much you’re paying for classes that don’t actually teach you. I regret not dropping out in my sophomore year. So if you’re a high school student considering Illustration or Concept Art, think twice. Do thorough research before taking $60k+ in student loans to attend this school, there are better and cheaper options out there. You can get better art education elsewhere without spending tens of thousands at CCAD.']

name: Columbus State Community College
reviews: ['I had a lot of issues with guidance counselors but overall I am very satisfied with the education I received from the MA program. Years later and I’m still appreciative of all the Ms. Stout taught me. It was an extremely thorough program and I was very prepared to start my first MA job.', 'As a current student of Columbus State Community College, I love the location of the school, all I have to do is catch the bus and I’m there. Ofc some people will say this school isn’t the best, but it depends on their own experience with the school. Mines has been okay, I did have a hiccup within my first year of being in college, but that’s was because of my mistakes. With not getting homework in on time and not having the proper identification for this semester, but overall the school is amazing. Smaller classrooms can help a student like me who had disabilities to get work done.', 'Health records office specifically needs more education on professionalism to the students. Not only is the office always closed but as a student I came back twice and my second time I seen the sign on the door still said closed and to come back at 12:15. I waited from 12:05 and seen an employee unlocking the door with food in her hands and heading back into the office at 12:13. Wanting to give the worker more time to put their lunch away and to open the door, I waiting until 12:15 to come inside (that’s what the time stated). I opened the door and the employee stated “you forgot to lock the door”. This off the bat was VERY rude to say and to hear as a student. The rest of the conversation did not get any better, I’m writing this review not about CSCC alone but the health records office employees who assisted me on this date.', 'I have enjoyed my education here but please find a better math program than Aleks. Aleks gives you a crazy amount of problems to complete per assignment and if you answer a question wrong, Aleks knocks down your progress rather than keeping it stagnant, thus making a one hour assignment into a two hour plus assignment. The explanations they provide aren’t always clear either. Columbus State Math Department, please find a program better than Aleks.', "Columbus state community college has no care for students. Students are just money to them. They don't care about students.\nThey have the worst nursing program in Columbus, Ohio. All they do in the nursing program is encourage students to drop the course.The moment that the 2 week period pass and they get your money, any help you need from that nursing department, all you hear from them is drop the course, drop the course."]

name: Cuyahoga Community College District
reviews: ["Attending Tri-C has been one of the best decisions I've made. and this Tri-C location is my favorite. It sits on top of a valley so you can see for miles on a clear day. It's right off the highway and is next to several restaurants (Chipotle, Chic-Fil-A, Buffalo Wild Wings...) The professors there treat you like an adult and genuinely want to see you succeed. They have TONS of online options for those who need flexibility. Sometimes communication with admin is frustrating but, overall a the school provides a solid experience. The education is top quality and the price is very affordable. To anyone considering bettering their life through education, Tri-C should be on your list. Check out the Eastern Campus.", 'Whoever plans to go to Tri C please hold yourself back from checking some of these online class teachers up here because they have the rudest attitudes for no reason at all sometimes even when you ask questions about the work in a nice way. It’s totally unnecessary to have a rude attitude when you don’t even get paid that much anyway', 'WOW !!! I can\'t believe the negative comments. I\'ve been attending Tri - C since the 70\'s.  I\'ve been at Eastern for the past  8 years.  My experiences have always been positive ...always!  I\'ve made lots of friends, Instructors make themselves available and not just for Academics..they help you out with personal issues to make sure life doesn\'t affect your success at school. From Administration to Instructors, Tutors to Support and Housekeeping Staff.....they all go beyond their job descriptions. I would question those who wrote negative comments  and suggest to that maybe it is the way you approach/ talk to people that might be the reason  you might possibly get "attitude" !    I\'ve been to all 3 of the major campuses and an off site campus and never have experienced anything like what has been said by the negative Commentors.', 'Rude staff. I don’t know if I’m going to continue my education here very discouraging', "Listen to the reviews saying that staff is extremely rude. I transferred to this school from Kent state and boy was it a huge mistake. While there are some extremely nice and helpful people that work here, overall compared to Kent staff seems like they do not want to help the students and get frustrated when you have questions. I'm not talking about professors and just the people that work in the information center and book store. They just don't seem to understand why a transfer student doesn't know every single thing about this school and don't seem willing to help. I have been asking about an access code for a website needed to complete assignments for my class or a few days now, and not a single person, except for my professor has been able to help me. First I was told to go to the bookstore where an employee there was very rude and even scoffed at me for not knowing the exact course number at the time I asked her about the access code. Overall, the professors are really good, but if you are a transfer student and you have questions, you will be met with lots of attitude."]

name: Davis College

name: University of Dayton
reviews:
["I'm disappointed with experience with Chemical Engineering program. There appears to be favoritism in certain classes where students from India receive noticeable more support and better Grades. name: Defiance College
reviews: ["There is nothing quite like DC. The library staff are phenomenal,  the registrar's office is extremely helpful, and the achedemic support is amazing for such a small school. The most difficult part about DC isn't the staff, the grading, or the community; the most difficult part about DC is manging your own time.", 'I am a graduate from DC and loved it. This school doesn't help students with planning or teaching them how the system works so students fail or have to stay an extra year. I strongly recommend to everyone not to attend this college. It will hurt you in the long run."]

name: Denison University
reviews:
['I recently visited this campus while passing through Granville and it is such a unique, quaint University. This small liberal arts school sits high up on a hill near downtown Granville. The atmosphere (especially in the fall) makes you feel like you’re exploring a small New England town. Walking around the campus is a workout on its own! Got to explore the student Union, the football field, and a few historic buildings. The culture is strong and vibrant here at Denison!', 'Denison University has beautifully manicured grounds. My wife and I spent an hour or so wandering about the campus as a break from a long road trip. A miniature wetland, meadows, a large field of zinnias, as well as formal plantings of flowers dot the campus.', "Great memories over four years at Denison University's athletic complex in Granville Ohio with WashU Swimming.

The complex is maybe ten years old, but looks new. It houses indoor track, tennis and swimming. My visits after Thanksgiving have been at their annual Denison Invitational Meet with my son. The school uses the opportunity to fundraise the local food bank.

My specific experience with the school is through swimming only. So the rating has nothing to do with academics, although I know from ratings and word of mouth it is a strong D3 school.

The pool is a looker. It's a 50 meter with diving wells. They also installed a very large spectator area to hold large events like conference and the Denison Invitational. However, a star deduction with air quality issues over the years. This makes competing much harder.

So long Denison University. My son has graduated out of this meet and it will be missed. Not just the facility, but the people and memories it holds.", "I enjoyed my time at Denison University, but most of all, I enjoyed my time spent at the Homestead at Denison University. Denison has a reputation for being a preppy, snobby school, especially in terms of student body (if not academics.) I did not find that experience to be universally accurate, especially because of the time I spent at the Homestead, the Bandersnatch, WDUB (the radio station) and the excellent English department. Denison is currently looking at closing the Homestead, after cutting support for it over the years. This is despite it being a unique student experience that can't be found at any other university. If this occurs, it's likely I will change my review to lower than a 4-star review.

edit: unfortunately, based on recent issues with the communication between the administration, the students, and alumni, including the mishandling of the future of the Homestead and communication around it, I have downgraded by review from 4 stars to 2 stars.", 'Denison University is a Beautiful campus! Lots of fall colors right now. I enjoy taking walks and photos here.']

name: Edison State Community College
reviews: ['Absolute garbage of a school.  My son took a class there, it had extra lab fees that we paid up front and they told were paid up. I would avoid this school and its business office like the plague. I call to make sure it was confirmed and they told me, the advisor had another 2:00pm appt. with another student and that my appointment was supposed to be at 1:30pm. Still didn't receive a phone call at that time. The classes I was hoping to sign up for are now waitlisted and full. My Fafsa and transcripts from high school and another college were already sent to this school; now I have to make a fafsa correction to apply to a better community college since they're very unorganized here. name: The University of Findlay
reviews: ['I just wanted to say University  of Findley has a superior Security team. We had a scary incident with not being able to locate my daughter who traveled in from out of town to attend her study group last Friday and they wasted no time locating her (where she was studying had no cell reception) . They took the call seriously and she was located in less than 20 minutes. Thank you to the team who located her quickly.', "The University of Findlay has a small pretty campus. Most of the architecture is beautiful red brick. The Science/pharmacy/teaching building and the library has it's own unique style. They have foliage producing trees in the fall and trees with nice blooms in the spring. They have flowers planted everywhere from Spring to Fall. They have cute clocks around campus. During the Winter they have so many beautifully decorated Christmas trees. One for the AMU student Center and one for the library. They also have a fire place in the AMU student center which is a great place to sit next to to study.", 'I was there. The most wonderful experience I ever had... I will always remember this college...', 'We watched youth flag football.  Beautiful field, great coaches', "Sue King is not someone to go to for the barn program. The horses are mistreated in the barn program. Half of them have mental and physical issues due to the lack of turn out, over riding, under feeding, and terrible medical care. I would not recommend bringing your horse into the program or even riding one of their horses in the program. There is a horrible retention rate in the program because the students are mistreated and beaten down, or they leave because they can't stand the way the horses are treated. The coaching is useless, they have no riders above training level, and the only decent riders they have are the ones assigned to one of the few decent horses. The majority of students will be overworked on terrible horses and severely injured through negligent barn managers or misbehaving horses. They do not quarantine sick horses, the vet on staff and the barn managers know nothing. The barn is incredibly dusty it will give you iron lung or spontaneously combust at any moment. Do not go."]

name: Franklin University
reviews:
['Too easy to qualify for acceptance. Classes are too simple. Many students who have been in classes for 2 years still do not know how to cite sources. Too expensive for the quality of the education & "professors." Flexible, yes, but it is not a quality education in many aspects. I would call it a degree mill with a liberal ideology that is devoid of true responsibility, accountability, & fairness.', 'Great university with many great programs from Bachelors, masters as well as PhD', 'not worth the time or money. curriculum is shallow to accommodate working/busy students. Grades are inflated, and the "hands-on" experience is merely an online module that you complete in person.

you may qualify for grants and scholarships to help cover the cost of tuition, but usually they wont take effect for a couple years unless you're destitute now. So expect to spend at least $30k for what amounts to a crappy high school education.

there is one small library that has a few rooms you can study out of, but for the most part there are no amenities despite a hyper-inflated tuition. And that's even after they reduced tuition.

The teachers are all adjunct except for a few key department heads that are compelled to teach a 100/200 level to fulfill some requirement or bc they couldn't staff the class. Some adjunct are passionate and are extremely effective at their role, but most are burnt out and just as financially destitute as the students.

For this education to have value, you must have someone else footing the bill, whether that be scholarships, company tuition reimbursement, etc. The education is not worth the sticker price.

For your degree to have value afterwards, you must have your OWN network and internships established. Franklin will not provide you much beyond access to connect with Alumni. Zero help with internships, zero help with company networking, zero help with career beyond shallow advice from similar failures.

So to conclude, Franklin University's education has value; if you're not paying for it, already have a career network established, and want to get an easy (but incredibly shallow) degree. For everyone else, it is an overpriced high school academy.', 'Whitney potter and Chris tyner  - cannot say enough about these individuals. While I’m sure there’s plenty more good hearted people here, these are the ones I encountered at the university. They don’t understand how much they’ve helped me stay on top of my academics even when I felt like I was alone and giving up! I commend you all. You may do this as your careers but you are truly working miracles and it doesn’t go unnoticed. Franklin is the best university I’ve attended. They hold you accountable and provide you tools to succeed. Though, online I still feel a part of the campus. Not all super heroes wear capes! Love 🥳☺️☺️', 'I have been a student at this University going on 2 years now after transferring from another school. This is an amazing University and definitely centered around supporting the working adults. Honestly I have never had an issues with any professors so far with 5 classes under my belt. Most classes are online with some on-campus if needed. My academic advisor has been very supportive and helpful. Overall I have had a great experience and I am excited to graduate hopefully fall of 2023. I highly recommend this school for anyone already in the workforce or have children and want to attend class in the evenings.']

name: Heidelberg University
reviews:
['The German’s oldest university and college town! So vibrant! Walking around the campus on the cobblestone streets was amazing.', 'Founded in 1386, this historic and highly significant place is the fifth oldest university in Europe. I wish I could have explored it more thoroughly, but since I visited on the day of the fair, I couldn’t see much around. I only managed to take a photo of its gate.', 'First off, i will just say that this a tourist review of Heidelberg University, not a review of student life.

31,000+ students come to this university and it is one of the most prestigious universities in Germany. It is the oldest university in Germany and one the oldest in the world, being the third of the Holy Roman Empire. Heidelberg university was founded in 1386 by Pope Urban VI. It has been coeducational since 1899 and has a very strong tradition of research and has an excellent reputation.

The architecture is Baroque, with Victorian and Gothic influences because of its age. Its stone is a reddish brown sandstone. Interesting statues and faces are set above doors and windows. The ground is covered in cobblestone and there are lovely green trees everywhere. Heidelberg is a beautiful, historic city and the university is at it’s center along with the castle.

Our tour group even met Heidelberg students and we had beer and lunch with them in a university pub. It was a lovely experience and we really enjoyed meeting and talking to our student, Prateek, a friendly, intelligent, international student originally from Delhi India. He was an excellent young man and we were very impressed with him and his English skills were outstanding. Our host explained his life as a student and his future plans.

Prateek represented the students, himself and Heidelberg university very well and we were very impressed. Meeting a student from the university left an excellent impression of the kind of educated human beings that Heidelberg university is producing.', "After leaving the Heidelberg Student Prison, we wandered into Heidelberg University's exhibition hall through one of the exits.

The first thing we saw was a long corridor lined with artworks and paintings. Among them were some early 19th-century paintings by Charles de Graimberg, which depicted the ruins of Heidelberg Castle as they appeared at the time.

We moved on to explore some university exhibits and eventually came to a glass door. We met a friendly staff member and, out of curiosity, asked if we could take a look inside. He invited us to follow him, although he explained that the university is normally not open to the public. He ended up leading us to the university's old assembly hall.

When we arrived, we noticed a young lady practicing a musical instrument in the hall. The staff explained that there would be a performance later that evening. Not wanting to disturb her, we quietly admired the beauty of the hall without taking any photos.

Back in the day, the hall was used for lectures, but now it’s reserved for ceremonies and performances. The entire hall is made of wood with a rich reddish-brown tone, giving it a warm and elegant feel. There’s a central aisle flanked by tidy rows of red chairs, with classical-style balconies on the upper floor. The walls and ceiling are decorated with carvings, paintings, and sculptures that contribute to the hall’s peaceful and classical atmosphere.

Later, we found out that Heidelberg University is the oldest university in Germany that is still operating today. It was founded way back in the days of the Holy Roman Empire!", 'Built in 1836 the oldest university in German. The wooden door , marble stairway shows the history of the building. Imaging this is an incubator for researchers and scholars cultivated many Nobel Price winners. Heidelberg university furnished with turreted buildings, stone bridges and baroque red-brick buildings.']

name: Hocking College
reviews: ['Deborah with their Financial Aid team is absolutely awful. I had a 504 plan in high school, I’m neurodivergent and needed assistance and she had the WORST attitude and zero patience to help explain and walk me through anything she needed from me. She speaks so fast while the phone chops her words and gets pissy because you don’t understand what she’s saying. Ryan campbell, and jim monroe were my contacts, and they were very helpful.', "Cheaply done, the whole place smells like a public bathroom, the food was rank.  Good sized drinks, lots of cool competitions and animals.  If you live far away, it's not worth the trip.  Got a nice weight room, though.", 'I am not satisfied at all with hocking college. If I could give them less than 0 stars, I would. The way they treat their horses in their program is absolutely devastating and abusive in many ways. They are not giving proper care to the horses. Care that is necessary for them. They refuse to retire the older horses who are tired. Hocking is a money hungry, pathetic excuse for a university. Anytime a student has a concern, it is ignored. The people in charge of this university spend more money on their petty needs than the university’s needs. The care of the students and the horses need to be under review as well as the people who are making the decisions for this university. I guarantee that anyone who inspects this university will see that the only people who are getting a benefit from this school are the people who are in charge. If you get nothing else from this review, please shut this horrible place down. They do not care for the students or the animals. They care about money and money only. If you are considering this university, literally run. Go anywhere else. You will not get a good education and you will not be properly cared for. The people they place in charge of dorms are even questionable. They cross boundaries with students and make them feel uncomfortable. The dorms have horrible mold. A pipe recently burst and flooded half the dorms and a lot of students stuff are ruined. The university is not compensating or doing anything for the damages done by the flooding. Parents, if you’re thinking of sending your child here, don’t. They will not be safe or taken seriously by people in charge. This place is overpriced even if none of these problems existed. If you have graduated from here, I pray you find the counseling and help you definitely are going to need after suffering through years of being here.']
