name: Hondros College of Nursing
reviews:
['Professor Hansen (NP),

I just want to take a moment to say thank you truly. Thank you for everything you do, for pushing your students, and for never lowering the bar. You expect excellence, and because of that, we rise.

When I first switched locations, I was honestly upset. But now I see it clearly God had a plan. I understand exactly why I needed to cross paths with you. You challenge us, you stretch us, you make our brains hurt (in the best way), and because of that, I know I’m becoming a stronger, sharper, and more well-rounded nurse.

You are truly the glue of the Maumee location. Your leadership, consistency, and dedication set the tone, and it shows in your students. I’m grateful for your guidance and for the impact you make every day.

Cheers to you, NP Hansen
(5 stars is personally for Professor Hansen)', 'Clinicals have been cancelled 4x and we have not heard from anyone. It’s been switched to a SATURDAY. A day I have work and if I don’t like it I’ll have to drop from the program. They’re still working on solutions 6 WEEKS in the semester and still nothing. But hey you can’t miss a day and you can’t complain otherwise they’ll harass you into leaving the school. Money hungry. Unprofessional. And the most uneducated school.', 'Recent Michigan State grad & very surprised how slow they are when responding to calls/emails. Emphasis on the lack of communication. Its 3 days before the semester start and financial aid have yet to contact me back about setting up payment plans to avoid enrollment cancellation. Not very convenient and could have been resolved months ago. I will be sending reviews updated as the semester goes.', 'The leadership at this school is extremely rude, unhelpful, and unprofessional. They wait until the very last minute to respond — if they respond at all — and then use that delay as a reason to say it’s “too late” to fix anything. Many students have sent multiple emails and made countless phone calls with no response, only to be told later that nothing can be done. It feels like they purposely wait for students to give up or drop out.

It’s heartbreaking to see how the Dean and other leaders handle things. Instead of supporting students who truly want to become nurses, they push them out of the program without compassion or fairness. The environment is discouraging and unsupportive.

Out of nearly 200 students, only a handful — around 9 — have actually graduated. That says everything about how this program is being run. Nursing is supposed to be about care and empathy, but unfortunately, the leadership here shows neither.', "Why is it that you have to pass all classes with an 80 percent or better. Most schools you can pass a class with 70 percent.  The grading scale is higher than any other schools. Maybe lower the grading scale to 70. At a community college when can even pass with a 65 percent.  Why is the school grading scale so high? Nobody isn't asking for a hand out.  Just help the students out. I thought it was about the students succeeding and not failure."]

name: Kent State University at Trumbull
reviews:
["It's unfortunately a community college in the ghetto misrepresenting itself. I had the crummy experience of Mr. Hazai, his inability to teach and a textbook that does not match the workbook which this incompetent makes absolutely no effort to clarify. It's like being handed all the materials and tools to build a house, being shown a photo of a house, told to lay the concrete foundation and he will be back to grade you tomorrow. He then sits back to watch the struggle and frustration of every person in the room who must hope they can get personalized assistance before they run out of time which was a daily struggle. To say he is incompetent is an insult to incompetent teachers everywhere. After 3 decades he still does not understand what a teaching plan is and how to teach!
There was no instruction or proper demonstration. When I understood him 2 minutes in he talked another 15 until he made sure you were confused!

This is well known by the other faculty, which some have discretely admitted to, and there are no shortages of other students current and past that share their dismay, frustration and anger with absolutely no reservations about this teacher and this outdated class virtually NO OTHER SCHOOL in the COUNTRY requires for their engineering program.
I have over a year into my engineering degree at another college so I know quite well what I am talking about as well as a lot of hands on experience designing and building analog circuits.

The other disaster is the new common core math and other computer based classes. Driving 70 minutes one way to do math on a computer that I could be doing at home is an absurd means to justify the cost and salary of a teacher. Not to say these are bad math teachers but the system is experimental and students are suffering.  Again, I talked to numerous other students that were extremely unhappy and frustrated with this experimental, sloppy system. When you need clarification of a math process for a problem you are working on and clicked on the E-book, it didn't actually take you to the necessary pages. To use the glossary or index was a tragedy because like the textbook and workbook for the engineering drafting, the assignment titles and categories are not based on the books content tables.
Until I mentioned it to the teacher the book did not open to the necessary subject you were working on. When I did, miraculously it started doing this the following week. Asking for help was a problem in itself because the issue was knowing what to ask to begin with. Finally after purchasing the textbook to avoid the strain of reading it on a computer, I realized just how poorly written the textbook was and this is the book the teaching software is written on!

Sloppy, jumping around, unorganized and nonsensical structure. If you're going to focus on plotting number lines, or whichever topic, do so systematically as opposed to leaping all over the place, fogging up the students ability to focus and requiring them to turn to a teacher who will need 20 minutes to explain something that should take 2.

Once I had enough units for my grant to pay for 90% of the costs, I withdrew and looked to our local community college which is a much larger, nicer school with tried and true methods as opposed to highly experimental in crude beta stages that SHOULD NOT involve charging students. If you want to experiment on people either provide the classes for free or outright PAY people to attend them.

This is truly a community college surrounded by ghettos in every direction you drive and unjustly bears the Kent State name. By the time I left I felt like I was at a vocational school for high school students and 30 something year olds wanting a trade certification. Most people are there for literary degrees, business, nursing, police academy etc. Nothing so complex or difficult as engineering.

The bottom line is if you're interested in one of their technology degrees DO NOT DO IT. They are not equipped with the staff to teach these fields just the equipment and facilities.", 'Many engineering students could have sued this place.  We were given the wrong schedule of classes for our major. No one knew until a professor noticed and told us. I took a whole year of classes that didn't even count!  The students all met a few times on saturday and we discussed our frustration but nothing became of it.  Moral of the story: the "advisors" suck.  Everyone I've spoken to says the same.  I tell everyone not to go there....you don't get a "full" college experience anyway.   There are no dorms so all the kids live with their mommies and still act like they're in high school. The few adults in the classes are looked down on by the kids.  If you're close to 30 years old, you're already the oldest in the class usually.  Also, when class is over everyone runs out to their car and speeds away.   There is slim to none extracurricular activities so finding people to hang out with is damn near impossible. I tell people dont go here...if you are so inclined to go to kent state, go to the main branch.', 'I graduated with my piece of paper, and that's about all the value there is.  If you go here just know that its a 4 year credential, nothing more unless you make something of it through self study.

Admin, "teachers", are terrible, but its a cheap (relatively) piece of paper that will help you stand out to the admin (H.R.) at bigger firms.', "Kent State University Trumbull is in my opinion the best place to get a quality education at an affordable cost. Smaller class sizes and the best faculty that actually cares about their students success are just a couple of it's many benifits.", 'Their math courses are a joke. You have to come in and do all course work from a computer program while the instructor sits in the back, and only does anything if he catches using a calculator. (For some reason they do not allow them)']

name: Kent State University at Tuscarawas
reviews: ['If you\'re thinking about going here please don\'t. Only reason it gets a star is because I can\'t give it zero. Athletes are treated like garbage and given no extra consideration whatsoever, the office people are all lazy and seem to never want to do their jobs, and worst of all they lie about financial aid and how "extensive" their services are. I attended for a year and hated every minute of it. Only reason I stayed is because of the lease I had on a house out in New Philadelphia.', "I went to school here now it's my daughter's turn 30 years later. Nice campus & plenty to offer at this branch", "Love the campus, started in 2019 and it's a wonderful place to study, learn, and the teachers are awesome.", 'Very Nice Place', 'Very nice facility and performance was great, put me in Christmas Spirit.']

name: Kent State University at Salem
reviews: ['If there was a lesser rating I totally would give this a ZERO star rating. I used to attend the BSN program at this location before I made the switch to the ADN program. If you are planning to attend the BSN program, DON\'T!! The professors here are emotionally ABUSIVE to NEW incoming students. Instead of helping the students learn they pick and tear down the students who don\'t do well on exams or classwork. I WAS struggling to the point of crying my eyes out because these professors are sooo beyond rude. I would ask for help, they would meet with me, and then help me study, and proceed to tell me that I shouldn\'t be a nurse. I\'ve even had students tell me that the professors would aggressively come up to their car during clinicals and falsely accuse them of giving them "attitude". These teachers don\'t want to help you and are only in it for the money. Don\'t go into this program if you want to get emotionally abused', "Nice little school. Freezing there, most of the time. Why isn't there a gym? How is a school going to be a medical oriented school, but no gym for weights or otherwise. Very strange.", 'Enjoyed my time there and received my undergrad, went on to receive my graduate degree. Teachers I had for my program were really great and was not as expensive to attend as YSU', "Love that it's a small campus all in one building and the class sizes are usually pretty small too.", 'I dont think they have very good completion rates.']

name: Kent State University at Kent
reviews:
['I was promised lifetime access to my kent.edu email, but I only graduated 4 years ago and they’ve already deactivated it. It was connected to my google photos so now every picture of every piece of art I made during my time there is gone. I have nothing to show for my time at Kent except the diploma. No portfolio, no pictures, nothing. For fashion and art students, this is so careless and disrespectful of our work that I cannot encourage anyone to attend here.', "Kent State University promised lifetime access to their university email accounts.

For the university to go against their word is a disgrace. It's a also a massive inconvenience for some alumni who have relied on their KSU email account being their primary email for years.

Retaining access to student email accounts is the least the university can do given the fact that most students pay an arm and a leg to attend it.

I will keep this review up as a reminder of the promise KSU broke.", 'I’ve known faculty here in geology and Geography for many years and recently taught there for two days. The faculty and students are all top notch… I highly encourage a visit or to enroll there. Kent is a very nice community as well and the regional surrounding landscape is beautiful particularly in the fall.', "Very helpful staff, actually riding around d on golf carts offering not only directions but rides. Elevators and carts available to help students move in, rounded environment, nice people, clean dorms. Surrounding area is somewhat secluded. A Walmart down tge street but no close Kroger that I knew of, lots of extra curricular activities for the kids, my daughter actually chose jujitsu! As time goes by I may update, if I don't its because nothing has gotten worse as we discover more about the university.", 'Also promised lifetime access to Kent State email, and was deactivated after 4 years. HUGE headache and waste of my time trying to fix all the problems this has caused.']

name: Kenyon College
reviews: ['Was here with the Photo Booth Guy doing a photo booth event and Kenyon college has such a beautiful  campus! Big trees, leaves on the ground, the buildings architecture all stone like old style design ....rustic and absolutely beautiful!!', 'Kenyon college is in very small town.  Beautiful college. We drove 1hour 20minutes from Columbus Ohio to get there little far from major city.', 'Seems like a really nice campus. Was there for regional tournament basketball game for Special Olympics', "Leadership needs to teach men's athletics about civilian etiquette when in public restaurants, poor reflection on your college .", 'Beautiful Campus❤️ love this school!!']

name: Kettering College
reviews: ["Kettering College has been a great place to work.  We try to make sure every student succeeds and learns their calling of healthcare. And while we aren't perfect, we work hard to make this place the best it can be for our students, faculty, and staff.", "A great faith-based college for a student interested in healthcare and getting 1:1 attention from their professors on a small campus. All programs have a rigorous curriculum, and the college is affiliated with Kettering Health to help students get connected to jobs even before graduation. It feels like family here, and yes, there's no football team or frat parties, but it's a unique college experience that will take you deeper and prepare you for the career you want.", "This college provides well-rounded, compassionate healthcare providers to the Miami Valley by modeling for students the care they should provide to patients. The professors provide curated, compassionate teaching to students, the staff members go out of their way to ensure student needs are met and that they are supported through tutoring, advising, and even with help with setting up off-campus support. I've heard of situations where they help students get bus passes and offer car rides to take on-campus students without cars to appointments off campus. Employees occasionally host students in their homes for meals and worships and provide one-on-one support because they care about their students as people, not just as numbers.", 'Wonderful school, faculty and staff! My 13 year old told me she plans to attend Kettering College because she just feels at home whenever she visits the campus. Faculty and staff are so professional and kind!', 'Kettering College is a great place to be. I appreciate the students, faculty, and staff in my life. The facility is state-of-the-art, and the student-to-teacher ratio is just right for students to be cared for.']

name: Lake Erie College
reviews: ['I graduated Lake Erie in 2008. I loved my time there! IHSA was wonderful with Bud Robert’s at the time. It was D3 and the football team started my Senior year. Many big changes have happened since, but it looks to be the same small school charm which is what I loved most. I believe I got more from LEC than any  large university could ever provided . I loved the small classes and my professors were excellent!\nI loved it and still cherish those memories 20 years later 😊', 'Beautiful campus in the Spring. Nice helpful administrative staff. Courteous students. 2/3rd student body play collegiate level sports.', 'It was a good D2 college. Small but friendly, tour guide was ok. But they where very welcoming.', 'Windy day and cool. Beautiful landscape and honorable history. Romantic getaway with family.', "This place is nice ,staff friendly grounds are amazing, can't wait winter to see the snow."]

name: Lakeland Community College
reviews: ['Even though life can get busy, there is something beautifully grounding about spending an evening at a civic band concert. For just $5 per adult, it’s one of the most elegant and affordable nights out you can find. The conductor thoughtfully selects unique pieces each time, creating a romantic and uplifting hour of music that feels both classic and fresh.\nWhat makes it even more special is the heart behind the sound. The band members range from dedicated music teachers to talented students and passionate community members who simply never stopped playing their instruments. You can truly see — and hear — the hard work and devotion in every performance.\nWhether you attend solo for a peaceful evening, bring a friend, or turn it into a charming date night, it’s always a lovely experience. They even offer two free summer concerts at the Mentor Civic Center and at Garfield’s House in Mentor, making it easy for everyone to enjoy. I wholeheartedly recommend going — it’s music wrapped in community spirit.', 'I was not impressed the first time I attended long ago. This time, they claimed I owed the state money…? And then again. And again. And again. 50 confused old ladies kept having me pay random amounts of money over and over and then claimed each time it was the last time. Thousands later my hold never did drop. They were profoundly incompetent and never had answers. I’d honestly guess they had a racket and were stealing from students. I signed up for their competition down the road instead. None of the bs.', 'I love this school! I just started this semester and I can reel you that every there is so welcoming and friendly.  the classes are very affordable! All of my classes were paid for by red cross this semester which I am extremely grateful for.  The school has everyone you need and looking for in a community college.. This school is very close to Mentor.', 'Wish I could give a negative number of stars. My daughter quit her classes because she found out they won’t transfer, they still charged over 1 thousand dollars with her never taking the class. The counselor she talked to lied and initially told her they would transfer. Now I get a threatening message that I owe yet more money 60 dollars , part of the breakdown was for books? That she never bought or used. You live and learn but I wouldn’t send my dog here and I have 2 other younger daughters who will never go here as well. Luckily we’ve had better luck with her transfer college and as big of a school as that is you can actually sit down and talk to a real person imagine that.', 'Great learning experience! Amazing staff. Lost and found only keeps things for 90 days, though, if anyone was wondering.']

name: James A. Rhodes State College
reviews: ['This college has frequent issues with their website when turning in or doing assignments. Return books to bookstore that you rent, and they "misplace" some, and charge YOU for it. No one fixes it.... Hard to get in touch with everyone. No way to work on a time frame with this college with issues with websites, and no way to get in contact with ANYONE you need to regarding logging in,  assignments, registering, financial aid etc. etc. Last time i signed up everything took so long classes had already started for a whole week while i was still trying to get set up for each class. The FIRST day i was on the class page to try to catch up the teacher gave me a 0 on my first several assignments... EVEN THOUGH... I stayed up late the day I registered and got my books and tried to work toward catching up... I want to go back to college, but I don\'t think this is the one to be in...', 'The bookstore is horrible.  The employees, not the student employees, were terribly rude.  They did not give me all the textbooks I ordered online and it took 3 people and yelling for them to finally understand that they did not give me the access code.  I even brought back the receipt and my actual order confirmation.  They lied and argued with me about my order being fulfilled and held for me.  I do not recommend getting textbooks from their bookstore.', 'Absolute joke of a college, good luck getting in touch with anyone until it\'s either too late or VERY last minute. Had 2 semesters left for my bachelors at another college but Rhodes is telling me i\'ll graduate in 2025! They\'re money hungry, good luck getting your classes to transfer from rhodes to another college, or even better rhodes doesn\'t "fax" over transcripts, they are the only college i know of that wants a physical copy of it sent in the mail! Advisors are probably the worst thing about rhodes, professors typically do genuinely care for their students so don\'t let them go unappreciated. Biggest joke of a college and everyone within a 40 mile radius knows it!', 'They have a sensory room. I went there to take my test and the nice women in the testing area let me check it out.', 'Got my teeth cleaned for free and they did a great job on my teeth']

name: Ohio Business College-Sheffield
reviews:
['Update:  So things seam to be getting better.  We have better instructors on staff & the YouTube videos seam to have gone down to a minimum.  They also seam to be trying to interrupt class much less, which is very helpful.  Glad to see the college is listening to concerns of students and starting to make the necessary changes to provide the education the students deserve.  Hopefully everything keeps going in the correct direction.

So last quarter we started with no tools.  No explanation on why we had no tools, just that they were on order.  This quarter we HAVE NO BOOKS!!  I cannot speak about other courses, but the electrician training offered at OBC is a joke.  Our instructor literally just shows us videos of people reading the book to us. Apparently they do not think people attending their school can read? These are videos that other colleges have put out to help with the covid pandemic or as part of their curriculum.  These videos are from YouTube & loaded with ads as well. We then have to do homework and since our instructor has not taught us anything, we have no idea what the questions are talking about. I do not even know where to begin when I read homework questions.  I think, if I only had a book to refer to I could do so much better.  This course is beyond frustrating because I actually want to learn but I am not being taught. Yes the class size is smallish, but there is non stop interruption from other staff members and other students in the building. When another instructor or staff member walks into our class they have a conversation with our instructor which disables our ability to clearly hear the video that is playing but nobody seems to care. This is on top of the hammering sawing & drilling from other rooms.  If you want to waste money and not learn anything this program at Ohio Business College is right for you.', 'The school is great although, I’m not appreciative of workers talking behind their students back because a student is told one thing and the student wants to make sure that it happens like getting out earlier than usual because we have lives and sometimes needs a break. Instead of talking to you like the adults we are, instead that rather talk about you behind your back in front of other students. So future students please be aware!', 'Stopped by to Chat with The Instructors and Students. Outstanding group of guys. They took the time to help each student and the students had great things to say about the Instructors. If your looking at Truck Driving Schools THIS IS THE ONE#!! Small classes and it  looked like everyone had a truck when I was there???
They had plenty of instructors on hand to help out any student in need too.', "in order to work at this school cuz I have a diploma from them I have 5 years experience with electrical yet it only requires 3 years and they told me I need to have a journeyman license Tim does not have a journeyman license Greg who teaches third quarter has never been an electrician I do not recommend this school I cannot get a job cuz I basically went to the school so if I didn't go to the school I would have had better options they lie to you it is no certification you get a diploma that is equivalent to a high school diploma cuz a diploma is a diploma so no unless you know why you're going to this school cuz it's not to be an electrician I truly regret going here cuz at this point I have to pay money back that I can't even earn I can't become an electrician at this point is what it's looking like and even if I do it has nothing to do with the school cuz I'm going to have to redo all my different training", 'A total scam. The teachers barely know anything and the other staff is even worse. Go to LCCC. Way better. I wanted to drop out and they pulled every card to try make me stay. The job placement is a joke. The lady said she could get me into best buy after I graduated. OH MY!! Best buy!!  ....I couldve applied and got a job there without her. Literally useless. This was around 2015.']

name: Ohio Business College-Sandusky
reviews: ["OBC is a wonderful college. The staff is wonderful and awesome to work with. They help you get through just about everything when something doesn't seem right. Love this college, just wish they offer more then just a diploma and associate degrees. Because if they offered more i'd definitely go back!", 'Teachers are amazing, always willing to help! Love their way of teaching and making sure you understand. I wish they had more to offer cause I would definitely go back! Highly recommended', 'Be careful- make sure your program is accredited. You may not be able to sit for a certification exam or even go out on internship because of the bad reviews this school actually has within the healthcare community.', "Love this school. Has a staff that truly cares about student's success.", 'yum food college 69']

name: Lorain County Community College
reviews:
['Beautiful sprawling campus. Large central Student Center with a Starbucks, bookstore and many other choices for food. Business and entrepreneurship building, culinary arts, theater, art gallery. Hands-On Innovation Center that partners with many community businesses. Free parking.', 'The fall and spring film series at Stocker Arts Center is a gem. The movies are shown on a large screen. They feature a broad array of topics, beautiful cinematography, and tickets are only $7.', 'Volunteered at the dental hygentist school. The school is well run and my teeth are nice and clean 🪥', "Communication is a HUGE problem here. Less people to talk to and far too many useless emails that give the wrong information.  It has been a huge inconvenience to myself and caused me to miss deadlines and push back my ability to join the program I signed up for.

Edit: 2/8/26

Joined the sterile processing program. It is not worth the headache.  Buy the hspa books online, self study. My previous review hasn't changed. I swear these people work against you graduating, not for you. This has been a horrible experience.", "My daughter's music program had a performance at LCCC. The food was catered by LCCC. It was delicious. It's also a very nice building"]

name: Lourdes University
reviews: ['Gorgeous setting. Beautiful buildings very tranquil atmosphere and beautifully landscaped', "Just enjoy the time I spent when I'm there.", 'Very nice campus. The University has expanded with a sports facility and dorms. Beautiful park like campus providing a safe environment for the kids. Small class rooms are an asset.', 'This university is terrible. The professors do not care about the students or if they learn any material. When students speak up they are not heard by the administrators. And the whole system does not have enough resources or money to pull in quality education!', 'It was here that I learned that life happens,  but you can happen to life too. Twas here, that I learned  that you can blame anyone,  and anything or you can grow up,  man up,  and get it done.\nTwas here, that I learned we live in an eclectic world to say the least.  Twas here, that I learned that you can go out and happen to life.  Twas here, that I learned that you need to look beyond your upbringing and where you came from.  Twas here, that I learned life\'s a B, grab a helmet.  Hold on tight and bring roses for your friends. You know that I come from small-town USA, where the locals aren\'t really friendly,  I come from "The Farmer City " of not Washington Coutt House but "WARshington Court House " as the locals twang it. Pictures the movie "Deliverence" in real life.  So to go from the 740 to the 419 shook me to my very core. Was the school founded by nun\'s? Yes. Is it a Great school? Yes. I would and will recommend Lourdes University every day of the week and twice on Sundays.  It\'s true, and this is year 29 for me.  I\'ve been blessed with longetivity to be sure, but I will always be a Greywolf. The only drawback is the economy of Toledo has taken a swan-dive to the very ROCC-BOTTOM. That\'s why I gave four stars out of Five. But I\'m beyond excited to return.']

name: Malone University
reviews: ["I was apart of Malone's first online MBA class in 2012 and it has changed my life! Great school. Great values. Great education!", 'I needed help navigating to the correct building, and called the number provided on the security booth at an entrance. The man who answered was extremely polite nice and professional. He went above and beyond and met up with me to guide me to the right place. Youre lucky to have a good man like that on your team!', 'By far one of the best places to ever receive and education.  The faculty and staff are always pleasant and are willing to help as much as they can.  Everything is well put together, students are great, with a lovely-expanding campus.  I would recommend anyone who is continuing their education to look into what Malone has to offer.', "I've been a student here for a good while. It's a great institution with a picturesque setting, ample parking and best of all a community of students, staff and faculty that is a real community of faith and caring.  Putting Christ's kingdom first and showing love to God and neighbor are Paramount to the Malone experience.", 'The staff was amazing for our high school/ junior high event held on campus. Very friendly, Christian atmosphere. I would recommend any high school student to check out Malone and take a campus tour!']

name: Marietta College
reviews:
["Marietta College overall is a beautiful campus all year round. I've walked and stayed on this campus many times in 10 years and the stores change, the food places change, even some buildings have changed and that's okay. However especially over the last 5 years, the beautiful bricks have gotten so bad on the Christy Mall and the streets surrounding the college, it's hard not to notice and I wish the college would fix this. Additionally, though they have made the campus more handicap accessible, there are many places that still need improvement.", 'We had a very enjoyable time visiting the Marietta College campus.

The surrounding town has a rich history. General Putnam was given a land grant by the United States for his service in the Revolutionary War.  He chose the area that is now the town of Marietta. General Putnam also sold lots to many former Revolutionary war soldiers in exchange for their land grants.

The school offers more than 50 undergraduate majors across the arts, sciences, and engineering, as well as Physician Assistant, Psychology, Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and Athletic training graduate programs. It has a beautiful campus that encompasses approximately three city blocks next to downtown Marietta and enrolls 1,200 full-time students.

The original school was Muskingum Academy which was started in 1797 by the citizens and General Putnam.  It was the first place of higher learning in the Northwest Territory and its first instructor was a Yale Graduate, David Putnam.
(Credit Wikipedia, 2022)', 'Just visited. Beautiful campus. Beautiful girls hanging in the library. People and place are both very attractive!', "My son toured the campus and fell in love with it! We had toured a couple other schools, that I thought couldn't be beaten, but he found his college!! He was accepted and sent in his registration payment!! He's going to be playing football for the college (OLB) and found a major he never considered which will be a perfect fit for him (sports management)! He received a great scholarship package and was on par with all the other colleges he had looked at and applied for FASFA (68% paid for through scholarships/grants). I'm so excited to see him so excited about going to college and getting to live out his dream to play football on a collegiate level!!", 'Loved it here. Best years of my life']

name: Marion Technical College
reviews: ['This college as a whole has been amazing. My instructors and the rest of the staff and faculty really care about your education. If I ever have any problems and I go to someone they either know the answer I am looking for or they will find someone who does. If I have any suggestions on how to make things better or easier for students they are always ready and willing to listen what I have to say and make improvements that will better students experiences. I wish I could further my education here farther than an associates degree because I have had such a great experience here. If you are on the fence, sign up! You won’t regret it.', "Amazing school. I graduated and walked already after my two years. Every teacher was supportive and there for me. You can just walk in to talk to an advisor (unless during semester start/end). Then it's by appointment. That is so much better than other schools. Osu only has very picky walk in times. MTC teachers put books in the library or I borrowed their copies so I spent nothing. They are friendly and the school is very pretty. Only a couple teachers were annoying, but every place has 1 or 2. I loved my time there.", "I have been going to this college 1 year and 9 months so far. I just started the Nursing program. I got put on a wait list last year because the program was full so just a heads up about that. That's not their fault though. My experience with MTC so far has been good. Of course there has been some minor issues, but you'll find that with any college. The staff and teachers have made my experience amazing though! I have loved the support and kind words that almost every single staff member has shown.", 'After being here for two years I can honestly say that this college is amazingly lit because of the support from the staff, faculty, and the administration. Marion Technical College does a great job giving you the resources (tutoring, resume building and more all for free)  to achieve your goals of complteting your degree. They also help push you to do better and they have personally helped me to get to next. Thank you MTC!!', 'Absolutely amazing experience! I am in the PTA program and have the most dedicated professors! All of the staff and faculty are very friendly and are invested in my success! Highly recommend this beautiful and uplifting campus!']

name: Mercy College of Ohio
reviews: ['My child was enrolled there in nursing school. The ADN program. The teachers and the lab instructors were unhelpful and had little empathy for students.  Most of the coursework was self taught.  And even if you self teach, and get good grades academically,  they can still fail you on a points system that faults you for things like not being immune to chicken pox (even if once you find out that you\'re not immune, you take the proper steps to correct it), or for not having a student to use as a patient in skills check off..all under a category called "professionalism" when my son said he hadn\'t made any friends to use as a patient, hoping one of the nurses in the lab would volunteer to be his patient,  their response was "you should\'ve talked to more people "  when other students that were present in the nursing lab at the time of my child\'s scheduled check off , but from other classes/another semester (further in the program) offered to be his patient,  he was refused because "it had to be someone in his class. "  since when is making friends a prerequisite to being a nurse? We are not there to treat our classmates or colleagues.  We are there to treat the patients. You do not NEED to make friends in school,  or on the job to be a good and professional registered nurse. As a RN BSN myself,  I recommend another school. Any otber school. I listened to my sons lectures weekly and assisted him with his homework and other assignments.  There are far better programs out there. Ones that have staff members who actually care,  and want to teach. Not to mention, about 1/3 of the students in my childs class were repeating their first semester because they\'d failed once already.  Why are so many students failing their first semester? It almost seems like they\'re setting them up to fail. This isn\'t the way GOOD nurses are made. Student nurses need compassion and empathy. The same as they should teach us to give our patients.  Nursing school is hard. We dont need the "eat your young" mentality that mercy college is bringing.   Go to a different school. Even if you get accepted right away at mercy, you\'ll be put back a semester  on some nonsense that will destroy your confidence. It\'s worth waiting a semester or two in order to wait for another schools seat.  You won\'t regret it.', 'Mercy is a great school! I just obtained my BSN degree from Mercy and although it was challenging, it was well worth it. Classes are small and teachers are always willing to help. I went on mission trips over spring break with the school and those experiences were unforgettable and irreplaceable. Anyone that is serious about obtaining a Nursing degree in Toledo should consider Mercy College.', 'My experience at Mercy was more like a nightmare. The students are treated like burdens, instead of the paying consumers they are. There is a huge lack of communication between instructors and lab staff, which leaves students unsure and ultimately unsuccessful. Educators are supposed to give students the tools they need to become successful, this is not what I received during my time at Mercy.  You can study hard, ace exams, and practice in the lab everyday, however one poorly proctored lab check off can fail you for a whole semester, and if you try to appeal, it is just your word against theirs.  I do not recommend Mercy if you hope to graduate , and get that RN behind your name.', "Don't be discouraged by the 1 star posters.  My daughter attended Mercy College and we couldn't be happier.  The staff is great.  The people that had trouble in school had several resources to help them do better.  My daughter constantly scheduled tutoring sessions.  Mercy prepares the student, but the student has to be prepared for the challenge of nursing school.  Remember nurses have human lives they are taking care of.  Does anyone want someone getting low grades to be their nurse? I don't.  No school prepares their student for the NCLEX (test to become a registered nurse) better than Mercy. We were so happy with Mercy that our son is now attending Mercy this fall (BSN program).  Great school!", 'Denise, I added to this review, please read if you see this.                                                             I graduated from Mercy a few years ago. It was one of the worst experiences I\'ve ever gone through. I did graduate and got what I went there for but students are repeatedly disrespected by teachers and the clinical instructors. The skills lab was a joke. I\'d go in there to ask questions and I was told several times to find a book and look up the answer instead of doing their jobs that they are paid for and help a student with their knowledge. If I couldn\'t find the answer, they\'d hand me another book to look at while they continued to have conversations with their co-workers. Most clinical instructors were mean and made you feel stupid, even in front of patient\'s. I may have a RN after my name but I regret going to this school. I\'ll never forget some of the cruel things several teachers have said to me and how unhelpful and unsupportive the staff was. After I graduated, several of the teachers got fired and I wasn\'t surprised. I don\'t recommend going to this school. Nursing school is hard enough and this school isn\'t worth the added stress.                                           EDIT: Hi Denise, not sure if you will see this, I appreciate your response. I just want to add that the teachers, clinical instructors, and staff, need to realize people are not only students but also paying customers. I feel Mercy lacks in customer service when it comes to students. This surprises me since having good customer service skills is an  important aspect in nursing for patient satisfaction. I agree with a previous review that stated, " students are treated like burdens." I never once heard words of encouragement from the staff at Mercy. A lot of negative and unkind remarks. I also got more help from the students working in the skills lab than the nurses who worked in the lab. I feel the staff at Mercy needs to be educated on the importance of customer service skills. If there are multiple student complaints about an educator, take it seriously. When I was there, one of your clinical instructors actually got me to cry in front several students and hospital staff. I felt I had no one to report this to, worried staff would turn against me.']

reviews:

reviews:

It was ok some parts are pretty steep but was a good walk for me and the dog.', "A Kafkaesque nightmare were hopes and dreams come to die.

I enrolled for the IMS program at the time was told to take these required classes to qualify. Fast forward four years later they changed the program and the classes I taken were null and void.

name: Mount Vernon Nazarene University
reviews:
['Class is 2002! Spiritually-focused, academically stellar, WNZR is a crown jewel among college radio stations.', 'While there are some very kind and Christlike professors and students here, I don't agree with how numerous situations were handled. Things were swept under the rug under the guise of Christian virtue. Reports taken to campus security or the campus pastors were hushed up or shooed away. The campus pastor cared more about plastering the school with diversity and inclusivity and "wokeness" then actually upholding Nazarene values. Funds are almost entirely funnelled into sports. While that is true that it makes them money, there have been ceiling panels in the science building that have not been fixed my entire duration at the school.

Additionally, not only have I heard of many of my close friends and classmates being lied to by the establishment and many within leadership, but I have experienced this myself.

I honestly wish I would have gone somewhere else. If going here, please do your research on what alum from your program say.

Edit: if going into chemistry, PLEASE GO SOMEWHERE ELSE. Since graduating, I have only discovered more and more of how professors are allowed to get away with clear violations of the codes of conduct the school supposedly has. I, as well as other students I know, have been bullied by a professor and when we brought these to attention, they were brushed aside. Recently, another graduate informed me that they were approaching the school about their work being plagiarized. The outcome has been extremely frustrating. The alum was told they were immature in getting upset with the plagiarism and that they were unlawfully deleting personal research from their OneDrive account after finding the professor directly copying and pasting from the documents. Until the school can own up to it's mistakes and rectify the situation, I strongly warn against this program I once loved.', "While experiences may vary depending upon each student's efforts, a quality faith-friendly education can be obtained at this University.  The campus is lovely in every season, the staff is friendly and helpful, the professors are knowledgeable and personable, and the extracurricular activities promote a strong sense of religious and civic duty.  In my personal experience, the History Department and the Thorne Library are top-quality.  Financial aid is often made readily available.", 'University is Very, very big very beautiful place professor is very friendly with staff is very friendly. I love it. My daughter carrier will be success.', "I first showed up at MVNU as a transfer student. There were problems with some credits transferring (to no fault of MVNU) and thus the amount of financial aid I could receive. I was ready to pack up and go home. They assured me they would help me get everything worked out, to go unpack get settled in and we would figure it out together. They held true to their promise and things could not have turned out better. My time at MVNU were the best academic and spiritually growing years of my life. I am very grateful for MVNU's level of care and commitment to their students and would highly recommend MVNU to anyone."]

reviews: ['I attended Muskingum University for an accelerated program for Special Education. I already had a Bachelors degree so most of my classes transferred over. name: North Central State College
reviews: ['The registered nursing program is a joke. Very disappointed I wasted my time and money going there. It’s pretty bad when the students know more than the “professors”. The people running the program were unprofessional and lazy to say the least. Paid for a certain amount of credit hours and they only had class half of the times we were scheduled. Lessons were taught per self by reading hundreds of pages per night because the professors were unsure what they were teaching. During class time professors had crying babies and barking dogs along with many more distractions. Spoke higher up and the dean was absolutely useless, wouldn’t take any responsibility for the low class education. The program does not equip students to become skilled nurses. If you have standards for your education I recommend going elsewhere.', "I was excited to get into nursing school. But I was lied to about my financial aid going up if I added a class and now I owe almost 300$ and had plenty of aid to cover it. I passed 2 classes with As and they told me I have to drop the one class to MAYBE get part of a refund! How can I be responsible for something I was advised to do and now I owe a late fee on top of it HOW BOGUSS!!!??????? I did an appeal and those people are a joke too they obviously didn't understand what I was saying! I will NEVER refer anyone to this school!", 'Worst College Ever. Tried taking summer classes here and it was unbelievable the amount of trouble I went through. No organization what so ever. Then I finally got the right classes registered a week before the semester starts. Then they tell me that I was suppose to pay for the classes the week before that even though they didn’t have the right classes. For online classes they cost more than in person lecture classes at AU. Would not recommend this “place” to anyone', "I would never go back to this school.  I was very disappointed in the teachers in medical program but also try to reach out to the dean and she was not very understanding and rude.  So many of the students in our class try to reach out to the teachers about not understanding the material they were teaching so we had to self teach ourselves .It seems like all the school wanted was money and not care at all about the students education.  It's pretty bad when you have more than 12 plus students complaining and them not wanting to do anything. This place is mostly money hungry ,and it's very disappointing . They should be caring for all  the students futures and do there best to guide them not break them down.", 'Great teachers. Everything else is terrible. They constantly cancel classes needed for graduation. Dont offer many classes needed all year (sometimes for a year and a half). name: University of Northwestern Ohio
reviews: ["Safety (or security) here is outrageous. Unlike a normal college dorm that's managed by student RA's and a couple housing managers, these dorms are managed by power hungry 40 year old men who wish they were police officers. They are constantly talking down to students and patrol the area like it's a prison. They have one of the most ridiculous guest policies I've ever heard of. If you don't drive to the center of campus and give them your driver's license even one time (you have to then drive on main roads without your license to get back to the dorms) they will lose their minds and threaten to kick you or who youre visiting out of school. Not to mention it's about a 5 minute drive to the center of campus and you have to wait at an office that is typically unmanned then wait for the glorified security guard to let you in, and sometimes they will sit in their truck staring at you for minutes while you wait. Genuinely some of the rudest college staff I have ever delt with. The school is great if you like racing, but you better have no respect for yourself if you're going to live in the dorms", 'Kicking out a student who was homeless before coming to this school, now has to find a place to live but still allowed to attend classes is a new all time low. His roommate’s played the race card to kick him out of the dorms but you all backed them up. Your predatory financial aid for students is something everyone needs to know about as well. You charge $2700-2800 every 6 weeks for some programs on top of the $500-700 dorm fees. Campus safety security who think they are law enforcement are always harassing students in the dorms especially Sherwood park area. Another reason to not send your kids here for a so called education…..parents and students beware.', 'I have been disrespected several times by our housing association, specifically Nathan Rowe, several times. he lets himself into your dorm and into your bedroom. how would you feel if a grown man let himself into your house and into your bedroom while you are sleeping? if thats not a good feeling, dont come here.', 'What to say about this place. Sherwood park dorms are a joke almost like section 8 housing you share with 5 other people(the dorm is Less then 1,000sqft). The office staff is pretty incompetent when it comes to collecting money, they threatened to withhold my degree because apparently I owed them money but they never mentioned it until 4 months after I graduated. Lastly it’s basically just a big high school you live at, lots of drama and kids acting out. They try to give you a professional environment but for the most part they get a lot of riffraff.', "I got my class A CDL here with a tanker endorsement and I've been a company truck driver for several years now. it's how I make my living. If I remember correctly I had Mr. Trammel as an instructor. And no, I don't drive for SWIFT, JB HUNT, or SCHNIDER. I got a job hauling grain for a local farmer, and used that for the required 2yr OTR experience all the companies want.\n\nI'm updating my review on 8/5/22 I've been saving my pennies, and bought my own big truck. I'm going to try and make it on my own with the help of some friends. I bought an old 87 International. Pre electronics haha I'm still out on the road driving every day."]

name: Ohio Northern University
reviews:
['Ohio Northern University at 525 S Main St in Ada is frequently discussed in my social and professional circles as a hidden gem of high-level scholarship that offers an intimate, focused alternative to the region's larger state schools. From several substantive conversations with alumni and healthcare professionals, a clear picture emerges of an institution that operates with remarkable merytorical precision, particularly within its highly-regarded pharmacy and law colleges. My peers often emphasize the "Polar Bear" community's unique ability to provide a sophisticated, private education where personal mentorship from distinguished faculty is the standard rather than the exception. In frequent discussions regarding career outcomes, the public consensus consistently highlights the university’s impressive placement rates, which my acquaintances describe as a direct result of a curriculum that balances rigorous theory with hands-on, practical application. I am particularly struck by the university's ability to maintain an elite academic standing while fostering a culture of genuine kindness and mutual respect, a sentiment echoed by many families I know whose children have thrived there. It is evident from the collective feedback of those I trust that the administration manages the campus with a clear, forward-thinking vision, ensuring that students are equipped with both the ethical foundation and the technical expertise required for modern leadership. Many of my friends highlight the institution’s role as a vital intellectual engine for Northwest Ohio, proving that its impact reaches far beyond the small-town charm of its geographic location. Reflecting on these overwhelmingly positive and consistent testimonials, I view Ohio Northern University as a prestigious and dependable bastion of excellence that fulfills its educational mandate with undeniable class and an inspiring commitment to student success.', 'This place transformed my life and I’m forever grateful. I have ONU friends that might as well be family, an outstanding career, and a broader perspective on life. Thank you.', 'The ONU College of Law is so pathetic that Dean Rose quit in the middle of his contract, during the winter break, leaving the class of 2026 without an administrative leader.  Congratulations!', 'Love doing my regular walks around the place, always clean, safe and greatly maintained.', "My sister held her wedding at this facility and it couldn't have been more perfect! Where do I start?
The facility itself is very nice. Modern, immaculate inside and out, and very well designed. It's located on the ONU campus, which is absolutely beautiful.
The rooms are sparkling and super comfortable.
The food is delicious and expertly prepared.
The Staff!! Where do I begin? From the moment we walked through the door we couldn't have been made to feel more welcome! It's not a huge facility, so everyone was aware of the upcoming event and was so welcoming.
Beginning with Heather at check-in, Gayle assisting all weekend with food/beverage. Carla everywhere!
And Tabitha, who coordinated the wedding; simply a masterful job!
So many others that all contributed to making this a truly exceptional and memorable event!
I'd like to thank the entire staff for taking care of my sister and new brother, along with the rest of my family and friends. You made this an occasion we'll never forget!!"]

name: Ohio State University-Lima Campus
reviews: ["I attended here right out of high school from 2000 to 2002. It was a good school to attend before transferring to another to finish out my bachelors degree in engineering. I recall the tuition was very inexpensive compared to other state or private schools and I was able to live at home and commute which saved money. With it being OSU, my credits easily transferred to Purdue Fort Wayne where I ended up finishing my degree. Most classes were very rigorous. I barely passed calculus and chemistry with a C+ there but when I transferred to PFW, my credits transferred but my grades didn't so I was glad for that. I took an art class at OSU Lima and we had to draw a naked lady that came in and derobed. Somewhat awkward but educational experience.", 'I went to speak with Tony Dickman in financial aid.   He was very knowledgeable and so helpful.   I had many questions and he patiently helped me through all of them.   Advised that if I had need for any more assistance to give him a call.   A very professional kind young man', 'Just took a tour. The daughter was considering attending next fall. After the tour, she claims she\'s "fan girling" lol.... She absolutely loved it and I think she made up her mind already! She\'s gonna be a Buckeye!', 'Do you like teachers that can speak English and know the subject matter? Campus is nice too though, even though it's pretty empty right now."]

reviews:
['I was on the phone with an IT team member I think his name starts with an M and hes an super nice guy and he helped out an lot can wait to be on campus. BEST SERVICE!', 'My only regret is that I wasted time, money and resources on community college.  I should have began my journey with university at the start. name: Ohio State University-Newark Campus
reviews:
['Nice campus, huge car park, large auditorium, decent classrooms but too many statues 😅. Some are scary.', 'Stray cats aren’t friendly, they will take your fingers!', "I like to stroll on the campus. There's a lot to see, fountains, a stocked pond with a bridge, ducks, Canadian Geese, and much more. Yes, you can feed the fish.", 'OSU football sucks. Ranked 73 out of 80 in schools in midwest.', 'Writing this review based on the campus.. nothing to do with the Ohio State education quality.
The campus is AMAZING. Very clean and tidy no matter where you go. If you hang out in the same spot for an hour, you're bound to see a janitor walk by a few times- they are working to ensure the campus bathrooms, hallways, etc. are clean at all times.
The size is perfect for getting around quick to any building. There are several parking lots located around campus. Parking is typically an issue for students during busy hours; often students will find themselves parking on the opposite end to walk to a morning class (but "opposite side of campus" is not far of a walk, don't be fooled by the negative connotation of the remark).
At the moment I am writing this review, there are 6 main student buildings and another is in the process of being built. The buildings are a mix of older and newer buildings- but nonetheless are well kept.
Overall, a huge plus for the city of Newark. Beautiful and practical small campus away from the madness of Columbus.']

name: Ohio University-Main Campus
reviews: ['Great. First time visiting Ohio University and thought it was wonderful. Loved the layout and the architecture very interesting. Impressive size and beautiful campus. Plenty of green space and probably amazing in fall and spring. Would definitely give it strong consideration for higher education.', 'Ohio University in Athens is consistently described in my professional and social circles as a quintessential American institution that masterfully blends historical prestige with a forward-thinking approach to modern pedagogy. From several substantive discussions with alumni and residents of the region, a clear consensus emerges regarding the university’s exceptional ability to foster a nurturing yet intellectually rigorous environment that truly prepares students for global challenges. My colleagues often highlight the Scripps College of Communication as a prime example of the university’s merytorical excellence, noting that its graduates enter the workforce with a level of sophistication and practical skill that is highly respected in the industry. In frequent conversations about the Midwest’s educational landscape, those I trust repeatedly emphasize how the stunning, brick-lined campus serves as a vibrant backdrop for a community built on mutual respect and collaborative innovation. I am particularly struck by the faculty\'s commitment to personal mentorship, which my acquaintances describe as a defining characteristic that sets this institution apart from larger, more impersonal state schools. It is evident from the collective feedback of those around me that the administration manages the university with great class, ensuring that the legacy of being the first institution of higher learning in the Northwest Territory is upheld through constant academic evolution. Furthermore, the university\'s role as an economic and cultural engine for Southeast Ohio is frequently praised in public forums, cementing its reputation as a vital pillar of societal progress. Reflecting on these overwhelmingly positive sentiments, I view Ohio University as a distinguished and dependable choice that fulfills its mission with undeniable integrity and a profound dedication to the success of every "Bobcat."', 'Beautiful Campus. A lot larger than I had expected prior to our visit. All the buildings pathways and some of the roads even are gorgeous bricks. The grounds are well maintained and landscaped. The lecture halls are a nice size. Everything seems well kept. Dorms are nice. Room sizes are pretty small but pretty standard in comparison. I had stayed in Jefferson Hall during orientation the dorm room I had was a double with built in drawers and small area to hang clothes. 2 built in desks. Microwave and mini fridge. The cots or beds if you want to call them that are these sort of camp style and they are extremely tall. I had to use a chair to get into the bed. I\'m only 5\'4" but still ridiculously high up. Also I would highly recommend if you have a student going purchase a really thick good mattress pad. As sleeping on that thing felt like a spring loaded rock. Bathrooms and showers were clean. Showers have glass doors that shut for privacy.', "Such a beautiful campus; it really is it's own little slice of Ohio. It's somewhat secluded with no other major cities around, but there's so much to do on campus that there really isn't a need to travel too far from campus. I came here for my MBA and I wish I would have gone here for my undergraduate.", 'Campus Police should be ashamed of themselves. Letting a peaceful woman be assaulted and letting a mob of rioters surround her truck. If the rioters were that overwhelming, Campus Police should have requested help from the Sheriff SRT.']

name: Trinity Health System School of Nursing
reviews: ['I had an excellent experience at Trinitas School of Nursing 🫶from my first semester through graduation. Throughout the program, I worked with a wide variety of professors and completed clinical hours at multiple hospitals 🏥 , which provided a well-rounded and high-quality nursing education.\nThe faculty were consistently knowledgeable, supportive, and genuinely invested in student success🙏. I am truly grateful 🥹 for the guidance, encouragement, and mentorship I received during my time in the program.\nI highly recommend Trinitas School of Nursing to anyone aspiring to become a Registered Nurse.🍀', 'I used to trust on my skills and passion to continue in the nursing program. After failing my first semester, Bonilla professor stop me to continue studying with all the recommendation and "motivations" to inspire her students. I would never recommend this school to anyone. If anyone take the risk, go ahead. That\'s my honest opinion.', 'I had a great experience at this school. I just graduated in 2025. Not easy at all, even up to the last semester I was always changing my study methods. I was lucky I didn’t have to work during the last part of the program, and admire anyone who was able to get through it while working. Very hands on learning, it wasn’t perfect, I didn’t love all the professors, some did stick out though like Bowers and Mojica, I absolutely loved and learned so much in their lectures and will never forget them.', 'I usually do not write reviews but due to the mistreatment I made time today to explain. This school needs to be audited/ looked into including every instructor they are disgusting to their students treated us like trash. They do not help at all their main goal is to collect your 9k every semester and fail you so you can come back and repeat the course and get another 9k. About half of the class  are re-admitted students. You reach out for help they do not help you but instead watch their students struggle, request office hours and you gain nothing from her. They are very discouraging especially the Nure 131 coordinator she doesn’t care about her students. They are unorganized the clinical instructors never know what’s going on we were always left in the blind. Forget about tutoring you reach out to them and no one wants to help after begging and pleading to get some kind of assistance..  UCC barely has tutors for the course .  Now the Exam reviews they do not go over the exams after you have taken them they place you in a room to go over the  50 questions  they rush you out of the room you can not ask any questions about what you did wrong or how you can improve. They encourage you to drop the course more than they encourage you to stay in the program. You pay all of this money sit in class for hours just to go home and be your own instructor because they spend more time arguing and bashing students during lecture then actually teaching us felt more so like a war zone then an actual nursing class. If you dare to ask them a question about material during lecture that you need clarification that they CANT  answer they get embarrassed and talk down on you in front of the class.  If your able to find somewhere else where you will receive better education than this I suggest you save yourself the trouble  from this unorganized establishment . Your mental health will be in shambles dealing with them. Please do something to help your students they are really trying to become nurses but you guys are very discouraging and bashful', "Before entering the school, please check the graduation rate. School grading is based only on testing, all the hard clinical work, and additional paperwork are not graded. Some tests include questions that weren't covered in the lectures. Testing is horrible. To me- waste of money and disappointment.  I will look for better nursing school, I should listen to students who failed TSON but succeed in other schools. However, I decided to give it a try. Big mistake. Do your research,  talk to students who already in this school."]

name: Ohio Wesleyan University
reviews: ['Ohio Wesleyan University, anchored at 61 S Sandusky St, stands as a quintessential example of how a private liberal arts institution can effectively harmonize traditional scholarship with contemporary global engagement. In my frequent interactions with the local Delaware community and various alumni, the consensus consistently highlights a substantive academic environment that prioritizes the "OWU Connection" as a transformative vehicle for real-world experience. My colleagues often remark on the university’s unique ability to blend rigorous classroom theory with high-impact internships and international travel, which in the eyes of many professionals gives their graduates a distinct competitive advantage. From what I have gathered through detailed conversations with those close to the faculty, there is a profound culture of mentorship here that ensures students are never just a number but are actively guided toward leadership roles. The public opinion surrounding the campus culture is overwhelmingly positive, often emphasizing an inclusive and intellectually stimulating atmosphere where diverse perspectives are treated with the utmost respect. I have heard many success stories from friends whose children found their voices at OWU, crediting the school\'s sophisticated approach to critical thinking and its unwavering ethical foundation. It is evident that the administration maintains the university with great class and transparent communication, fostering a sense of stability and prestige that resonates far beyond the state of Ohio. Ultimately, based on the collective feedback of a trusted network, I view Ohio Wesleyan as a premier educational landmark that fulfills its mission with academic moxie, ensuring its students are both culturally fluent and professionally prepared for a complex world.', "I am very impressed with Ohio Wesleyan's campus. The buildings are historic and well maintained. It's also easy to find your way around.", 'great place for walks if youre a flaneur that enjoys historic architecture.  has a peaceful calming atmosphere with some interesting buildings as long as there arent too many people walking around.', 'I graduated in 1987 and it was amazing to go back for my reunion and see how he school has grown.  It was so much fun to see my old classmates.  I am proud to say that I still have my hair and it is not grey like most of friends.  Guess living in florida all those years helped.\n\nThis was and is still a great college and helped me is so many ways.', 'Small school in North of Columbus with facilities to enable kids with learning, research and be ready for the future']

name: Otterbein University
reviews: ["You are my sigma, skibidi sigma. You make me looksmax, in Ohio. You'll never know dear, how much I orz you. Please don't take induction away. The other night dear, as I was mewing. name: Owens Community College
reviews:
["Never ever go to the school.
They are constantly telling you wrong information. I got told a lot of wrong information even before I went to my first class. Considering they charge over eighty five dollars per semester for administration fees for them to have that much incorrect information , total rip-off. The desk agent are extremely rude. I can't tell you how many times I was
Talk down to or talk to like I was stupid at the school. Mostly off the incorrect information they gave me. But still , I was talked down to all the time. And their classrooms are not fully equipped, even the teachers say that they're not fully equipped. What am I paying all this money for????", "I attended the Toledo campus from Spring-2012 through Fall of that same year. My philosophy instructor, David St.Aubin, didn't actually teach any philosophy and instead told us his economic theory about why we should abolish inheritance and why Mitt Romney was awful (he was, but that was irrelevant to the course). I'm 99% sure he didn't have any degrees in philosophy or any related field. He also expressed jealousy over not getting hired to teach at a university. He never cited the primary sources and instead gave god-awful outlines that were often incorrect.

My math instructor also went on rants (this time about how Obama was the anti-Christ) and I didn't learn any math at all as a result.

General vibes: I frequently heard loud cursing from the hallways during class, fights in the parking lot, and depressing buildings. The food options were very limited, and the career center was just there for show.", "This college could be better when it comes to advisors and having people to help you get started. I feel like I keep getting pushed to do everything online or myself and it's frustrating and the advisors barely reply to your emails . Both financial aid and advising has been this way and they take for ever to answer your questions. Other colleges were much better at this . I hope this improves because it leaves students feeling burned out trying to start", 'Campus was nice but the police are very shaky when they pull you over you can tell there in class also was trying to say they could’ve arrested me for a warrant I had when I was a juvenile that I was told was already expunged the other cop was really cool tho he helped me out with a situation.', 'My daughter who is 16 has had the worst experience with this school. To the point where she wants to give up. Graduated high school early and the staff at this school is rude and gives her no help. Had to find outside sources to help with tutoring. School staff and tutors are not helping will be contacting the dean or whoever is in charge because this is unacceptable.']

name: Professional Skills Institute
reviews:
["I can not say enough good things about the programs at PSI.  I graduated here last year from the lpn program and had a great experience with the teachers and staff.  I am now enrolled in the lpn to rn bridge and I have been very impressed with how organized they are (even better than before) I did have several issues that arose during my lpn program and it was always handled with professionalism and with a caring attitude. Is the program hard ? (YES). Is the program worth it ? (YES)  With hard work you will become a nurse in 12 months!  My biggest advice is don't fall behind on homework because you will have a lot of it.  If you are struggling to understand a concept you can find many nurse educators videos on you tube that will help.  Try to plan ahead, it is very difficult to work full time when you are in these accelerated programs.  Don't get discouraged.. YOU CAN DO IT !", 'This school has gone downhill. It’s another Hondros but I feel it’s worse. They changed the curriculum on the students so you now have to get a 76.5 average on all tests to pass the class. Even if you did all of your homework, they don’t care and don’t factor it in until after knowing you passed the tests. It sucks for us students because even if your homework would’ve helped your grade, they don’t include it. There’s no student support. So many people have failed out or got held back because of this. I wouldn’t recommend this school to anyone. It’s sad because it used to be such a good school. They changed everything and it’s not benefiting the students at all.', 'I do not recommend Professional Skills Institute. Throughout my time here, I experienced clear favoritism and unprofessional conduct from administration, including the Director of Nursing, clinical managers, and other administrators.

The environment feels discriminatory, and student concerns are not handled with professionalism or integrity. Due to these issues, I have formally reported the school to the Board of Education.

I regret spending my money here and would strongly advise prospective students to explore other options. I am highly dissatisfied with my experience.', 'As long as you take the time to read the material and study accordingly, the program was great. My third quarter there were issues with staffing one of my classes, but they were able to have a substitute finish this semester. Every nursing program has its flaws and bumps in the road, and this one is no different. But I enjoyed the staff and clinical teachers I had at PSI.', 'Money hungry . Teachers don’t lecture . You can go to the Dean & anyone in the program they don’t care. They tell you whatever you want to get you to sign up and enroll but the program you have to teach yourself . Fundamental teacher just curses all lecture and takes pride in failing students . Teachers teach from chat gpt and when you ask a question they tell you they’ll get back to you but there is no follow up . They tell you to read the chapters to learn but if that’s the case then make the school completely on line because coming in person is a waste of time. Started with 24 people and in the first few weeks were down to 18 with half of them failing . Changed the grading scale but waited until the second day of class to lets us know . GO TO ATHENA or Hondros . Save yourself the trouble.']

name: Fortis College-Centerville
reviews: ["I graduated from Fortis back in 2020 with my\nLPN. Decided to go back for my ADN and it was the absolute worse mistake. They do NOT care about students success but they care about their failures because the more you fail the more money it is for them. Not appropriate lab equipment or sims equipment to learn proper IV placement or other skills needed for nursing. Worse thing is that because of personal issues in life I failed a class due to low grade in HESI. Dean Tieman didn't approved my appeal but yet she did approved other students so there is favoritism. I submitted all paperwork even my mother and sister's personal information and records for them just to put excuse after excuse. I only had 4 classes to go to graduate with my ADN but unfortunately will not get to finish due to their excuses and policies they have and too much money I had to pay now due to their lack of professionalism or their care for students. All they care about is money. So my suggestion is to NOT go to this school. Never got to meet with the school president because they didn't allowed me to.", "Do not come here for the nursing program. It is a horrible school. Teachers are very overwhelmed and overworked. They are running short all the time. They won't make time for you for scheduled tutoring sessions. Clinical days are not put together. It will give you so much stress and no time to focus on studying for the RN program. Negative zero stars.", 'Do not recommend this school at all. The staff is unhappy. They get new teachers every term if not in the middle of the term. They tell you when you sign up that they work with your schedule and are flexible that is the furthest from the truth. This school honesty doesn’t even deserve 1 star. The RN program cost 52 thousand dollars for them to have teacher teach that do not know what they are teaching. They have clinical instructors that respond “I’m not sure I’ll have to look that up” for all questions. The school is strictly for profit! If you aren’t willing to teach yourself do NOT waste your time with this school. I’ve learned more from my own studies than more than half the teachers I’ve had. The night students are forgotten. If I could go back in time I would have NEVER attended this school. Knowing what I know now. This school is a joke and take your education as a joke. The more you fail the more they make so they are all for it !', 'Received a Criminal Justice associate degree in 2010, refused me job placement. In debt because of Rets/Fortis how does the government allowed this school to continue to be in business blows my mind!', 'Really wanted to go to this school to be a nurse but somehow they told me I was more likely to be a dentist assistant. I wish I would have stood my ground but I was young.. this was 11 years ago. I finished the program but never got a job out of this no one would hire me. In debt now with nothing to show for.']
